Draft: Tado Jurić

Draft text:
----

Tado Jurić (born 1979 in Orašje) is a Croatian demographer and political scientist. [ref: Demograf Jurić: Za 10 godina svaki 4. stanovnik - s migrantskim podrijetlom, Hrvatska radiotelevizija] He is an associate professor at the Catholic University of Croatia in Zagreb. [ref: ] His publications cover migration from Croatia and Southeast Europe and the use of digital sources in demographic research. [ref: Forecasting Migration and Integration Trends Using Digital Demography – A Case Study of Emigration Flows from Croatia to Austria and Germany, Comparative Southeast European Studies] [ref: Experts raise concerns over Croatia's migrant approach, Croatia Week]

== Career ==
Jurić received his PhD from Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen–Nuernberg, Germany in 2012. His doctoral and later publications examined migration policy and demographic change in Croatia and Southeast Europe. [ref: Tado Juric, scholar.google.com] He has held academic and research positions in Croatia and abroad, including a visiting professorship at the University of Graz. [ref: Gastprofessur am Institut für Ethik: Tado Jurić, theol.uni-graz.at]

Jurić has been cited by Croatian [ref: Demograf Jurić: Za 10 godina svaki 4. stanovnik - s migrantskim podrijetlom, Hrvatska radiotelevizija] [ref: Jutarnji list - 'Nismo svjesni što se događa. Studenti mi se žale da su izgurani s tržišta rada, a nisu svi pridošli budisti i hinduisti...', www.jutarnji.hr] [ref: Jurić: Demografija je postala pitanje nacionalnog opstanka, N1] [ref: Demograf Tado Jurić: Migracije će potpuno promijeniti Hrvatsku kakvu poznajemo, www.24sata.hr] and international media on migration and demographic issues, including Deutsche Welle, Die Kleine Zeitung, Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, Berliner Zeitung and Alfapress have cited Jurić on migration-related topics. [ref: Iz Hrvatske odlaze oni koji već imaju posao, dw.com] [ref: Tado Jurić: Političarima iseljavanje odgovara, dw.com] [ref: Exodus am Balkan: Tado Juric: "Kroatien wird zum Altenheim Europas", www.kleinezeitung.at] [ref: Exodus aus Südosteuropa: Kroatien & Co: Länder verlieren Kampf um kluge Köpfe, www.kleinezeitung.at] [ref: EU-Kommissionspräsidentin von der Leyen zu Besuch in Kroatien, FAZ.NET] [ref: Kann ein Land seine Demografie steuern? Kroatien probt den Ernstfall, Berliner Zeitung] [ref: Labor market/ Germany eager for workforce from our region, alfapress.al]

He serves as a special adviser on migration to the Croatian Minister of Demography and Immigration. [ref: Posebni savjetnici, mdu.gov.hr]

He has contributed to international migration and demographic policy research through the International Centre for Migration Policy Development (ICMPD) [ref: Tado Jurić - ICMPD, www.icmpd.org] and the Wilfried Martens Centre for European Studies [ref: Tado Jurić, Martens Centre], and is listed as an expert in migration and demography in the Migration Research Hub. [ref: Tado Juric Expert Profile, CrossMigration]

== Publications ==
Jurić has published books on migration, demographic change and digital demography. [ref: Prikaz znanstvene monografije Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije] [ref: Predstavljanje knjige "Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije", mdu.gov.hr] His 2017 article “Suvremeno iseljavanje Hrvata u Njemačku: karakteristike i motivi” and his 2018 book Iseljavanje Hrvata u Njemačku. Gubimo li Hrvatsku? have been cited in subsequent academic publications. [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com] His later publications in English and German have also been cited in scholarly literature, including research on migration, refugee flows and digital demography. [ref: xmed.jmir.org] Several of his books have been reviewed in academic publications, including Westbalkan-Erweiterung der EU, [ref: Westbalkan-Erweiterung der EU, PW-Portal] Gastarbeiter Millennials [ref: ] and Contemporary Migrations and the Survival of the Nation (Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije). [ref: Tado Jurić Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije, Politička misao: časopis za politologiju] [ref: Prikaz znanstvene monografije Suvremene migracije i opstanak nacije, Migracijske i etničke teme] [ref: Matica hrvatska - Kolo 1, 2026. - Cjelovito o migracijama, www.matica.hr]

Selected books:
* Jurić, T. (2018). Iseljavanje Hrvata u Njemačku. Gubimo li Hrvatsku? (Emigration of Croats to Germany. Are we losing Croatia?) Školska knjiga, Zagreb 2018.
* Jurić, T. (2025). Immigration Ideology. Europe's Demographic Survival. Verlag Dr. Kovač. Hamburg.
* Jurić, T. (2023). Big (Crisis) Data in Social Sciences and Humanities: Predicting Crises. Verlag Dr. Kovač. Hamburg.
* Jurić, T. (2021). Gastarbeiter Millennials. Exploring the past, present and future of migration from Southeast Europe to Germany and Austria with approaches to classical, historical and digital demography. Verlag Dr. Kovač. Hamburg.
* Jurić, T. (2013). Westbalkan-Erweiterung der EU, Europäisierungsprozess in Bosnien und Herzegowina, Serbien und Kroatien. Hamburg.

Draft: Delta Institute

Draft text:
----

Delta Institute is a Dutch think tank working on government digitization and innovation policy. The organization began in October 2023 as Recoding Government (), an initiative of Alexander Klöpping and tech entrepreneur Onno Eric Blom. It has operated under its current name since April 2026. [ref: 'Overheid digitaal zeer gebrekkig', Kamer komt met plannen, NOS Nieuwsuur] [ref: Commissie Digitale Zaken wil historische digitale hervorming van de overheid, iBestuur] [ref: Wetgevingsoverleg over de Jaarverslagen en Slotwetten 2025 van de ministeries EZ, BZK en JenV, voor zover het onderwerpen betreft die zien op digitalisering, House of Representatives of the Netherlands] [ref: Omdat de toekomst er niet vanzelf komt: waarom we verdergaan als Delta Instituut, Delta Institute]

== Founding and manifesto ==
On 9 October 2023, Klöpping and Blom published an opinion piece in the newspaper NRC which said that the Dutch government's IT infrastructure was outdated, and argued that information technology is a core government task. [ref: Het kan niet langer zo doorgaan met de ict-incompetentie van de overheid, NRC] [ref: Manifest over ict-onkunde wekt beroering, Binnenlands Bestuur] On the same day they released the manifesto Recoding Government, which called for better pay and more policy influence for programmers inside government. [ref: Manifest over ICT-incompetentie van de overheid wil politiek wakker maken, iBestuur] [ref: Manifest tegen ICT-onkunde overheid aangeboden aan 'volgend kabinet', AG Connect] The article reached the House of Representatives three days later, in a committee debate of the standing committee on Digital Affairs, where the state secretary promised a written response. [ref: Verslag van een commissiedebat, gehouden op 12 oktober 2023, over digitaliserende overheid, House of Representatives of the Netherlands] [ref: Reactie Manifest 'Herprogrammeer de Overheid', House of Representatives of the Netherlands]

The group presented the manifesto to members of that committee on 13 February 2024. [ref: Aanbieding manifest m.b.t. ICT-problematiek bij de overheid door de groep 'Herprogrammeer de Overheid', House of Representatives of the Netherlands] On 16 December 2024, committee members released the document Ons Digitaal Fundament (), which proposed a central Digital Service. NOS and iBestuur both reported that the document came out of cooperation with the foundation. MP Barbara Kathmann called the manifesto "the stone in the pond" and credited it with pushing the House to press the cabinet for major IT reform. Klöpping currently sits on the organization's advisory board, whilst Blom runs the organisation. [ref: Position paper Herprogrammeer de Overheid t.b.v. rondetafelgesprek Nederlandse Digitaliseringsstrategie, House of Representatives of the Netherlands] The coalition agreement of January 2026 announced a Dutch Digital Service, a competitive pay scale for IT specialists, mandatory review of IT projects above five million euros, and centralized digital procurement. [ref: Coalitieakkoord: Nieuwe Digitale Dienst moet regie pakken over IT Rijk, iBestuur] [ref: Coalitieakkoord: CIO krijgt meer sturing én verantwoordelijkheid, AG Connect] The Dutch Digital Service launched in the summer of 2026. [ref: Digitale Dienst gaat toch zelf aan de slag met eigen iters, Binnenlands Bestuur]

== National AI Delta Plan ==
The idea for a National AI Delta Plan came up over dinner with minister of infrastructure and water management Vincent Karremans at the Ministry of Economic Affairs, in Summer 2025. Six tech entrepreneurs and researchers, Blom among them, wrote the plan; the foundation covered part of the cost. Karremans received it in November 2025. [ref: Tijdens een etentje bij minister Karremans bedachten zes techbro's een AI-plan. Dat is nu regeringsbeleid, Trouw] [ref: Nationale AI Deltaplan: soepel ontslagrecht moet Nederland aantrekkelijk maken voor ai-hoofdkantoren, Computable] It runs to 52 recommendations, built with input from more than sixty experts. [ref: Beleidsmonitor: Het Nationaal AI Deltaplan van Nederland, Kenniscentrum Data & Maatschappij] [ref: Nationaal AI Deltaplan moet Nederland aan top van Europa brengen, BNR Nieuwsradio] The newspaper Trouw reported that the Jetten cabinet folded the plan into the coalition agreement "almost word for word."

== National Agency for Disruptive Innovation ==
The foundation was one of the outside partners in a Ministry of Economic Affairs study of a National Agency for Disruptive Innovation (NADI), envisioned as a Dutch counterpart to DARPA. Minister Karremans sent the findings to the House of Representatives in February 2026 and left the decision on whether to actually establish it to the next cabinet. NADI was subsequently mentioned in the coalition agreement. [ref: Beslisnota bij Bevindingen verkenning naar een Nationaal Agentschap voor Disruptieve Innovatie (NADI), Ministry of Economic Affairs / House of Representatives of the Netherlands] [ref: Bevindingen verkenning naar een Nationaal Agentschap voor Disruptieve Innovatie (NADI), House of Representatives of the Netherlands]

Draft: Yamamoto Kakuyoshi

Draft text:
----

Yamamoto Kakuyoshi (山本角義, March 3, 1914 – January 30, 1982) was a Japanese martial artist.
He was a direct disciple of Takeda Sōkaku, the reviver of Daitō-ryū Aiki-jūjutsu, and the founder of Mugenshintō-ryū Iaijutsu. [ref: 合気、その源流山本角義伝, 月刊秘伝] [ref: [https://www.aikidosangenkai.org/blog/aiki-rentai-conditioned-body-yukiyoshi-sagawa-part-2/ Aiki Sangenkai – "Aiki Rentai: The Conditioned Body of Yukiyoshi Sagawa (Part 2)"], retrieved 2025.]

== Biography ==
Yamamoto was born in Akita Prefecture under the name Yamamoto Tumekichi (山本留吉).
While working as a cook, he met Takeda Sōkaku in 1937, when the latter frequented the restaurant where Yamamoto was employed. Yamamoto soon began training under Takeda.

According to Takeda's records, Yamamoto formally enrolled in Daitō-ryū in 1941. That same year, he received the Hiden Okugi no Koto certificate, and in 1942 he was licensed as kyōju dairi (teaching representative).
Takeda Sōkaku died in 1943, making Yamamoto the final disciple to receive such formal recognition. For this reason, he is often described as the “last student” of Takeda—not simply in terms of chronology, but as the last to have mastered the art to the level of advanced transmission. [ref: Stanley Pranin, Conversations with Daitō-ryū Masters, p. 184 (Seigo Okamoto interview).]

After World War II, Yamamoto lived in Hakodate, Hokkaidō, and later established the Jūshinkan Dōjō in Tomakomai, Hokkaidō. There he taught:
* Daitō-ryū Aiki-jūjutsu (Yamamoto-ha)
* Mugenshintō-ryū Iaijutsu (sword drawing / real-sword methods)
* Ono-ha Ittō-ryū kenjutsu as transmitted through the Aizu domain [ref: [https://calgaryrakushinkan.com/mugenshinto-ryu Calgary Rakushinkan – Mugenshintō-ryū page]]

== Mugenshintō-ryū Iaijutsu ==
Yamamoto is credited with creating the style known as Mugenshintō-ryū Iaijutsu (無限神刀流居合術). [ref: [https://calgaryrakushinkan.com/mugenshinto-ryu Calgary Rakushinkan – Mugenshintō-ryū page]]
The system drew on Yamamoto's training in Ono-ha Ittō-ryū kenjutsu under Takeda, combined with the principles of Daitō-ryū Aiki-jūjutsu. Its practice centers on sword-drawing (iai) with an emphasis on real-sword methods (shinken tōhō), integrating sword and unarmed principles into a unified pedagogy.

The creation of Mugenshintō-ryū represented a continuation of Takeda's efforts to connect the sword traditions of Aizu with the aiki-based body methods of Daitō-ryū. The school has been transmitted through Yamamoto's successors, and remains part of the curriculum at branches of the Yamamoto-ha lineage. [ref: [https://webhiden.jp/master/yamamoto_kakuyoshi/ Web Hiden – "Yamamoto Kakuyoshi"]]

== Legacy and continuation ==

The Jūshinkan dōjō, founded by Yamamoto Kakuyoshi, continues to operate in Japan. [ref: [https://jushinkan.shin-gen.jp/ "柔進館 流派／伝承系譜／理念" – Jūshinkan official website]]
It is affiliated with the Shintō Jūshin Kai (神刀柔進会), an organization that maintains Yamamoto's martial legacy. The group emphasizes preserving what Yamamoto and his teacher Takeda Sōkaku regarded as the core of Daitō-ryū Aiki-jūjutsu—its grounding in bujutsu (martial techniques) and its orientation toward protection without unnecessary injury. [ref: [https://daito-ryu.jp/ Shintō Jūshin Kai official website]]

Martial arts historian Stanley Pranin recorded references to Yamamoto in his book Conversations with Daitō-ryū Masters. Katsuyuki Kondō stated that he studied with Yamamoto for two days in 1972. [ref: Stanley Pranin, Conversations with Daitō-ryū Masters, p. 165.]
Seigo Okamoto recalled participating in a demonstration with Yamamoto, referring to him as “the last student of Sokaku Sensei” and remembering his distinctive sword drawing methods. [ref: Stanley Pranin, Conversations with Daitō-ryū Masters, p. 184.]
Yamamoto is also mentioned in Kondō’s book Daitō-ryū Aikijūjutsu Hiden Mokuroku Ikkajo (p. 33).
Yamamoto is discussed in Satō Kinbei's 1991 memoir "Jū to Ken to Dō", where he is described as Takeda Sōkaku's “last disciple” and as an active participant in postwar Daitō-ryū demonstrations. Satō recounts correspondence with Yamamoto and cites him as a source regarding Takeda's training methods. [ref: 林檎プロモーション]

Nandinkhusel Nyamjav (born 9 September 2006) is a Mongolian basketball player who plays as a guard. She represents Mongolia in international 3x3 and 5x5 basketball competitions.

== Career ==

Nyamjav developed through the Mongolian basketball system and represented Mongolia in international youth competitions. She is a two-time champion of Mongolia's National Premier League, winning championships with Ulaanbaatar Amazons in the 2022–23 and 2024–25 seasons. [ref: Meet the FIBA WBL Asia 2025 teams: Ulaanbaatar Amazons, FIBA] [ref: Н.Нандинхүсэл: Монголоос өөр газар сагс тоглож чадвараа ахиулаад, улсынхаа нэрийг Дэлхийд гаргахыг хүсэж байна /ВИДЕО/, iSee.mn] [ref: Би АНУ-ын WNCAA-д тоглох мөрөөдөлтэй, News.mn]
She attended SPIRE Academy in the United States before beginning her college career. [ref: Nandinkhusel Nyamjav, Florida Tech Athletics] [ref: Нямжав Нандинхүсэл, MSports]

== College career ==

=== Florida Tech Panthers ===

Nyamjav played for Florida Tech during the 2025–26 season, appearing in 17 games and averaging 11.6 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.0 assists per game. [ref: Н.Нандинхүсэл WNCAA Division I-д тоглох анхны монгол тамирчин боллоо, iToim] Her season-high was 28 points against USC Beaufort, and she recorded a double-double of 16 points and 10 rebounds against Saint Leo. [ref: Women's Basketball Adds Seven to 2026-27 Roster, Tennessee State University Athletics]

=== Tennessee State Tigers ===

Nyamjav transferred to Tennessee State University for the 2026–27 season. [ref: Nandinkhusel Nyamjav, Tennessee State University Athletics] [ref: Historical step: Mongolian basketball player Nandinkhusel receives No. 10 in NCAA Division I, Open.kg] [ref: Монгол Улсын Гавьяат тамирчин Н.Нандинхүсэл NCAAW буюу АНУ-ын эмэгтэй сагсан бөмбөгийн оюутны лигийн D1-т тоглоно, iKon.mn]

== 5×5 national team career ==

Sema Kılıçkaya (also written Sema Kiliçkaya or Sema Kilickaya), born on 31 January 1968 in Antakya (formerly Antioch), Turkey, is a French novelist, translator, and teacher of Turkish origin.

Writing in French from what she calls an "in-between-three" position between Turkish, Arabic, and French, Kılıçkaya draws on an identity shaped by the Turkish–Syrian borderlands and the Antakya region. Her novels explore exile, the relationship to one's mother tongue, and the transmission of migration memory. She received the Prix Seligmann against racism in 2014, awarded at the Sorbonne, for Le Royaume sans racines and the France-Turquie Literary Prize in 2018 for La Langue de personne.

== Biography ==

=== Early life ===

Sema Kılıçkaya was born on 31 January 1968 in Antakya (the ancient Antioch), in the southeastern Turkish province of Hatay, near the Syrian border. According to a 2024 interview with the French research outlet Observatoire de la Turquie Contemporaine, she grew up in a household that was both Turkish-speaking and Arabic-speaking, reflecting the multicultural character of the Antakya region. In 1972, at the age of four, she emigrated to France with her parents as part of the Turkish economic migration of the Trente Glorieuses. The family settled in the Haute-Marne department in eastern France.

=== Literary career ===

Her first book, Anadolu. Contes, récits et anecdotes de Turquie (2004, Publisud), a collection devoted to the oral heritage of Anatolia, received extensive coverage in the Turkish national daily Hürriyet when it was released.

Her first novel, Le Chant des tourterelles (The Song of the Turtle Doves, 2009, L'Arganier), spans three generations of women and traces the fate of a Turkish family between Syria and Turkey. It was shortlisted for the Prix Senghor first-novel prize in 2009.

Le Royaume sans racines (The Kingdom Without Roots, 2013, In Octavo), drawing on her observation of a Turkish community transplanted to Haute-Marne, earned her the Prix Seligmann against racism in 2014. The distinction, awarded by the Chancellery of the Universities of Paris, was covered as a major event in the French-Turkish press by Hürriyet (which ran a front-page report and a follow-up piece on the Sorbonne ceremony of 5 February 2015) and by edebiyathaber.net.

Quatre-Vingt-Dix-Sept (Ninety-Seven, 2015, In Octavo) is a political family novel centred on Alèv, a young Alevi woman, and the memory of the 1937–38 Dersim events as transmitted to later generations.

La Langue de personne (Nobody's Language, 2018, Emmanuelle Colas) is set in a family of Turkish origin in eastern France in the aftermath of the Charlie Hebdo attacks. It won the 2018 France-Turquie Literary Prize. It was the subject of a scholarly critical reading in the peer-reviewed academic journal Hommes & Migrations, published by the French National Museum of the History of Immigration, and of an extended literary essay on Kedistan.

== Reception ==

The academic journal Hommes & Migrations has read Kılıçkaya's work as a fictional exploration of the "invisibilised stories" of working-class migrant families in rural France, arguing that her novels stage language itself as the central object of migration — both wound and shelter — and that her writing constitutes "an ethical inquiry into the possibility of a shared idiom."

The Turkish daily Hürriyet, reporting on the Sorbonne ceremony of 5 February 2015, described Le Royaume sans racines as a novel that "brings to French readers a face of Turkey that remains invisible in dominant narratives" and framed the Prix Seligmann as a rare recognition of a Turkish-born author writing in French about the migrant condition. An earlier Hürriyet report on the announcement of the same prize characterised the distinction as "a major recognition from France for a Turkish writer."

The Turkish literary outlet edebiyathaber.net devoted an essay to the paradox of Kılıçkaya's reception, noting that her prize-winning novel had, at the time, no Turkish edition and remained unknown to Turkish-language readers despite its critical success in France.

The online magazine Kedistan described La Langue de personne as "a language novel" in which the search for a shared idiom becomes an ethical and political question, and situated it within a broader French-Turkish literary field concerned with post-migratory identity.

The Observatoire de la Turquie Contemporaine, in a 2024 interview-portrait, presented her body of work as one of the most sustained French literary meditations on the memory of Turkish rural migration to Europe and on the specifically Anatolian, Turkish–Arabic-speaking origins of the diasporic experience.

Her novels have also been featured on national radio: RFI devoted an episode of its summer series Littérature sans frontières – Une terre, une auteure to her work and to the biographical trajectory that informs it.

== Bibliography ==

=== Novels ===

* Le Chant des tourterelles, Paris, L'Arganier, 2009; reprinted by In Octavo — shortlist Prix Senghor 2009
* Le Royaume sans racines, Saint-Pourçain-sur-Sioule, In Octavo, 2013 (reprinted 2018) — Prix Seligmann 2014
* Quatre-Vingt-Dix-Sept, In Octavo, 2015
* La Langue de personne, Paris, Emmanuelle Colas, 2018; paperback: J'ai lu, 2018 — France-Turquie Literary Prize 2018
* Les Pluies sauvages, Le Pythagore, 2020
* L'Affaire Benjamin S., 2023

=== Other works ===

Anthony K. Chow (Chinese: 鄒果慶) is a Malaysian-born businessman who has served as chief executive officer of Newegg Commerce, Inc. (NASDAQ: NEGG) since 2019. [ref: Honoree: Anthony Chow, Los Angeles Times] [ref: How did Taiwan help Newegg make its comeback?, CommonWealth Magazine] He previously held executive roles at Newegg from 2006 to 2011, and later worked at OTTO Group's China business and Haier Group before rejoining Newegg.

== Education ==
Chow holds a bachelor's degree in electrical and electronics engineering from the University of Toledo and an Executive Master of Business Administration from the UCLA Anderson School of Management. [ref: Newegg CEO Anthony Chow Receives the Los Angeles Times CEO Leadership Award, citybiz] [ref: Form 6-K, www.sec.gov]

== Career ==
Chow first joined Newegg in an executive capacity in 2006, overseeing North American operations and later the company's China operations, including its OZZO Logistics subsidiary, until 2011. [ref: Newegg’s CEO Unifies a Multinational Workforce, UCLA Anderson School of Management]He then worked as an executive at OTTO Group's China business and at Haier Group Corporation.

Chow rejoined Newegg as chief executive officer in 2019, when the company's annual sales had fallen to about $2 billion. He negotiated new supply agreements with Taiwan-based component manufacturers Asus, Gigabyte, MSI, and ASRock. Newegg reported sales growth of approximately 38 percent in 2020. In May 2021, Newegg completed a reverse merger with Lianluo Smart Limited and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol NEGG, at a reported valuation of approximately $3.9 billion. [ref: Electronics Retailer Newegg Goes Public, Los Angeles Business Journal]

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Newegg continued fulfilling customer orders while several competitors experienced shipping delays; trade publications attributed this to the company's geographically distributed supply chain. [ref: How to Buy PCs (and Parts) That Ship Now: Newegg CEO, Others Explain How They're Maintaining Stock, Tom's Hardware] [ref: The best alternatives to Amazon for buying tech right now, PCWorld] The company also reported increased customer demand during this period for products such as webcams and laptop computers used for remote work.

== Recognition ==
In 2021, Chow received the Los Angeles Times B2B Publishing CEO of a Public Company Leadership Award.

== Professional affiliations ==
Chow was elected to Newegg Commerce, Inc.'s board of directors on August 9, 2025, filling a vacancy created by the resignation of company founder Fred Chang. He is listed as a member of the UCLA Anderson Forecast Board of Advisors. [ref: Board of Advisors, UCLA Anderson School of Management]

== Corporate developments ==
Under Chow, Newegg repositioned its in-house Advanced Battlestations (ABS) brand of pre-built computers toward the gaming market. [ref: Newegg Reinvents the ABS Brand to Focus on the Gaming Community, TechPower Up] In 2025, the trade publication TechPowerUp reported that most of Newegg's initial stock of Nvidia GeForce RTX 50-series graphics cards sold within minutes of release. [ref: Newegg Sold Out Most NVIDIA RTX 50 Series GPUs in Just 5 Minutes, Entire Stock Cleared in 20 Minutes, TechPower Up]

According to the Chinese business publication PEdaily, Newegg's China-based subsidiary, the e-commerce platform SellingPilot, received an industry award in 2025. [ref: 新蛋SellingPilot斩获“2025 新锐奖”，以 AI 智能ERP领跑跨境电商数字化新赛道_行业动态, 投资界] Newegg's China operations were also named an outstanding cross-border e-commerce enterprise by the Shanghai Cross-Border E-Commerce Association in 2022, [ref: ] and received a foreign-trade enterprise award at a national cross-border e-commerce forum, according to a report republished on the Baidu Baijiahao platform. [ref: 新蛋斩获第三届中国对外贸易合作发展论坛 “对外贸易先锋企业”大奖, baijiahao.baidu.com]

Wayne Ngan (May 19, 1937 – June 12, 2020) was a Chinese Canadian ceramic artist and potter based on Hornby Island, British Columbia. [ref: Wayne Ngan, Telford, Toneff & Boyd Burial & Cremation Centres] He was known for his wood-fired stoneware and experimental glazes. [ref: Pottery by Wayne Ngan, Vancouver Art Gallery] Ngan also built his own kilns. He received the Saidye Bronfman Award in 1983 [ref: Wayne Ngan, Island Potter: A Portrait by a Friend, Luminare Press] and had a solo exhibition at the Vancouver Art Gallery in 1978.

== Early life and education ==

Ngan was born in Canton, China, [ref: Wayne Ngan — B.C. ceramics artist whose 'whole life is an art project' — has died, CBC] 19 May, 1937. In 1951, he immigrated to Canada. He lived with his grandfather on Mitchell Island near Vancouver, Canada. [ref: Richmond: Secrets & Surprises, Yorklin Associates]

He attended the Vancouver School of Art (now Emily Carr University of Art + Design). Ngan enrolled in the least expensive studio course, pottery. [ref: Wayne Ngan — Potter, Canadian Museum of History] Ngan worked at a shingle mill and later on sold homemade ceramic tea bowls to support himself. [ref: B.C. potter Wayne Ngan turned clay into objects of rare sculptural beauty, The Globe and Mail] He graduated in ceramics from Vancouver School of Art with honours in 1963. [ref: Obituary, Wayne Ngan: A life of magical art in ceramics and sculpture, Vancouver Sun] Ngan received the Marie E. Lambert Pottery Prize and the A.W. Tickle Memorial Award.

== Career ==

In 1967, Ngan moved to Hornby Island. There, he built a home and studio. He worked with Lloyd House to design his studio and kiln sheds. [ref: Builders of the Pacific Coast, Shelter Publications] Ngan's home included a firing studio, garden, sod roof and repurposed chicken coops into bedrooms. [ref: Towards a Good Fit, Architectural Design] At his home, he constructed three different kilns, for an array of firing techniques. He practiced hakeme, a hand-brushed decoration on pottery and salt-glazing.

Ngan utilized various techniques including raku, high-fired stoneware, salt glazing, and wood firing. He developed a ceramic practice that was closely connected to the island's landscape and materials. [ref: The Invisible Social Traces of Objects: Wayne Ngan's Ceramic Vessels, The Capilano Review] He experimented with local natural materials such as clays, ash glazes, seaweed, and driftwood. [ref: The Canadian Mantra: Reuse, Repurpose, and Recycle!, Studio Potter]

In 1978, Ngan lived in Japan for three months. He studied Japanese ceramic traditions with potter Yoichi Murakami. Ngan taught and led workshops on ceramics at different educational institutions in Canada and China. In 1984, after receiving a grant from Canada Council and inspiration from the Sung Dynasty, Ngan built a 300-cubic-foot wood-fired kiln.

In the beginning of the 2000s, Ngan spent more time on painting and sculptures.

== Work ==

Ngan's ceramics were functional and sculptural. [ref: The Doris Shadbolt Pottery Collection, Ceramics: Art and Perception] His work is associated with the West Coast ceramic movement influenced by Bernard Leach and Japanese pottery traditions. [ref: Thrown: British Columbia's Apprentices of Bernard Leach and Their Contemporaries, Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery] [ref: A Licence to Kiln, The Globe and Mail] Writer Joni Low described Ngan's vessels as restrained in form and emphasizing materiality and process over decoration. Ngan engaged directly with his materials and firing processes. He built and modified his own kilns and developed glaze formulas through experimentation with locally sourced materials.

Ngan's work was influenced by the pottery traditions of China, Korea, and Japan, particularly the work of Shoji Hamada. His techniques included salt glazing, wood firing and hakeme brushwork. He was also influenced by Sung dynasty ceramics.

Low and other commentators have noted that Ngan's house, garden, and workspaces on Hornby Island functioned together as part of his studio practice.

Artist and writer Amy Gogarty has argued that Ngan's work was distinguished by "his mastery of firing techniques and by his ability to integrate historical ceramic traditions with a distinctly regional West Coast vocabulary of materials and form".

== Recognition ==

In 1978, the Vancouver Art Gallery presented Pottery by Wayne Ngan, a solo exhibition curated by Doris Shadbolt. [ref: Pottery by Wayne Ngan, Vancouver Art Gallery] His work was later featured in the exhibition Thrown: British Columbia's Apprentices of Bernard Leach and Their Contemporaries, which examined the development of British Columbia studio pottery.

His work is held in the collections of the Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery at the University of British Columbia [ref: Search the Collection, Morris and Helen Belkin Art Gallery] and the Vancouver Art Gallery. [ref: Annual Report 2024, Vancouver Art Gallery] [ref: Highlights from the Collection, Vancouver Art Gallery] A collection of his pottery is on permanent display at the Canadian Museum of Civilization in Ottawa. [ref: Artists in Their Studios: Where Art is Born, TouchWood Editions]

In 1983, he received the Saidye Bronfman Award, for Canadian fine craft. In 2013, Ngan received the BC Creative Achievement Award of Distinction. [ref: B.C. Creative Achievement Awards honour artist Wayne Ngan, Georgia Straight]

is a Japanese architect and urban planner. He is the founder and chief executive of Kotaro Horiuchi Corp. (stylised KOTARO HORIUCHI; ), and works from Paris, Tokyo and Ishigaki Island across architecture, interior design, furniture and spatial design. [ref: X-Knowledge Includes a one-page profile of Horiuchi with several of his projects.] His early work in Paris was published in the European and Japanese design press, [ref: kotaro horiuchi architecture: salon du fromage, Designboom] [ref: Shōtenkenchiku] and in 2019 he was the only Japanese finalist in the international open competition to reimagine the roof of Notre-Dame de Paris. [ref: Forest Roof — The People's Notre-Dame Design Competition, GoArchitect]

== Biography ==

=== Education and early career ===
Kotaro Horiuchi was born in Nagoya, Aichi Prefecture, and studied architecture and urban design at the graduate school of Meiji University, completing his master's degree in 2004. [ref: Nikkan Sugoi Hito! The outlet's name translates roughly as "Daily Amazing Person!", a Japanese web magazine of interview profiles.] While a student he represented Japan at the 1st International Architecture Biennale Rotterdam (2003) with a work on Tokyo, "Tokyo Ring Project / Visible Area Map".

During the same period he gained experience at several European offices: in 2003 at Mecanoo in Delft, the Netherlands, led by Francine Houben, and as an assistant at the summer school of the Architectural Association in London; in 2004 at PPAG in Vienna; and from 2005 to 2009 at the office of Dominique Perrault in Paris, known for the Bibliothèque nationale de France. [ref: Dominique Perrault Architecture, Éditions HYX / Centre Pompidou Exhibition catalogue, Centre Pompidou, Paris, 11 June – 22 September 2008.] According to Nikkan Sugoi Hito!, this itinerary across the Netherlands, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, Austria and France left him working in six languages.

=== Practice ===
In 2005 Horiuchi founded his own practice, Kotaroo Architecture, in Paris. He incorporated the firm in 2009 as Kotaro Horiuchi Architecture Inc., reorganised it in 2015 under the name Kotaro Horiuchi, [ref: Kotaro Horiuchi, France News Digest] [ref: Kotaro Horiuchi, Japanese architect in France, French Code] and established Kotaro Horiuchi Corp. in Tokyo in 2020. [ref: JIA Bulletin Self-authored; used only for uncontroversial biographical detail.] He now works from Paris, Tokyo and Ishigaki Island, and holds a first-class registered architect qualification (, ikkyū kenchikushi); he is also a PADI Master Instructor.

One of his best-known early built works is the Paris cheese shop salon du fromage HISADA (2010), at 47 Rue de Richelieu. Working within an existing 18th-century building on a narrow site, he clad the interior and exterior in graded aluminium studs and arranged a ground-floor sales area beneath an upper floor used for cooking classes, wine-and-cheese gatherings and events. [ref: Bamboo Media] The project was published in the Japanese trade magazine Shōtenkenchiku in 2011. It was followed by The Roof Residence (2011) in Maintenon, France, where three dwellings and a restaurant are gathered beneath a single perforated roof that opens the interior toward the surrounding landscape. [ref: kotaro horiuchi architecture: the roof residence, Designboom]

=== Notre-Dame competition ===
In 2019 Horiuchi was selected as a finalist (second place) in "The People's Notre-Dame Cathedral Design Competition", an open, participatory competition organised by GoArchitect of the United States that invited the public to imagine the future of Notre-Dame de Paris after the 2019 fire. From 226 entries submitted from 56 countries, six finalist teams were chosen by a public vote of more than 30,000 people; the finalists came from five countries, and the only Japanese-led entry was "Forest Roof", a proposal to crown the cathedral with a garden-like canopy. [ref: Results of the People's Notre-Dame competition, Pragmatika] The finalist proposals, including "Forest Roof", were later collected in the book Top 50 Visions of Notre Dame (2019). [ref: Top 50 Visions of Notre Dame A compilation of the competition's finalist proposals, including the "Forest Roof" entry led by Horiuchi.]

=== One Sapporo Station Tower ===
Horiuchi provided design supervision for the main-entrance façade and common areas of One Sapporo Station Tower, a residential high-rise (48 storeys, about 175 m) directly connected to Sapporo Station as part of the Kita-8 Nishi-1 urban-redevelopment project. Completed in 2023, it is the tallest building in Hokkaido; its developers include Daiwa House, Sumitomo Realty & Development and Tokyu Land. [ref: Sora no Ma — Skyscape for All, Houzee Awards / Architecture Collection] The project received a Platinum award at the 2024 Houzee Awards [ref: Platinum Winner 2024 — One Sapporo Station Tower, Houzee Awards / Architecture Collection] and six Gold certifications at the 2026 Grands Prix du Design (organised by Agence PID, Canada), where it also received the jury's Grand Prize and the public People's Choice Award. [ref: One Sapporo Station Tower — Urban Thresholds, Grands Prix du Design (Agence PID)] In 2027 the project received a German Design Award from the German Design Council. [ref: One Sapporo Station Tower — Urban Thresholds, German Design Council]

The World Time Attack Challenge (known as the Yokohama World Time Attack Challenge or WTAC) is a multi-day time attack event held at Sydney Motorsport Park. It is a festival that also features a variety of categories in car culture such as drifting, demonstrations, straight-line racing, car show and a trader alley.

== History ==

=== 2008–2009: Superlap Australia ===
The origins of the World Time Attack Challenge [ref: https://www.worldtimeattack.com] can be traced back to the inaugural Yokohama Superlap event held in 2008. Conceived with limited resources and minimal event management experience, the event was organised within a matter of months and marked the beginning of a new era for time attack motorsport in Australia. With support from industry partners and grassroots workshops, the first Superlap attracted 65 competitors from across the country and was hosted at Oran Park Raceway in New South Wales.

The early format featured two primary classes—Open and Clubsprint—culminating in a Superlap shootout, which was won by Peter Lucas driving a supercharged Honda-powered Lotus Exige. Despite its relatively modest and experimental beginnings, the event quickly gained traction, supported by exhibitors and sponsors such as Advan Yokohama, Turbosmart, [ref: World Time Attack - A Walk Down Memory Lane • Turbosmart, Turbosmart] Haltech, and Royal Purple, many of whom would remain long-term partners of the event.

In 2009, the event expanded in scale and professionalism, introducing a Pro Class and attracting more competitive machinery, including Mark Berry's ADVAN/Hi Octane Nissan Skyline GT-R (R34) and the Tilton and Pulse Racing Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution entries. That year's outright victory was secured by Garth Walden in the Tilton Evolution. The 2009 event also marked the final running at Oran Park Raceway before its closure, adding historical significance to the competition.

=== 2010–Present: World Time Attack Challenge ===
Following the closure of Oran Park Raceway in 2009, the event relocated to Sydney Motorsport Park (then known as Eastern Creek International Raceway) in 2010. This transition marked a significant turning point, both in scale and ambition, as the event was rebranded as the World Time Attack Challenge (WTAC), reflecting its growing international focus.

The introduction of international competitors in 2010 elevated the competition to a global stage. Notably, Nobuteru Taniguchi piloted the HKS CT230R Mitsubishi Lancer Evolution, which set a new benchmark for time attack performance and secured overall victory. The presence of established Japanese teams and drivers signalled WTAC's emergence as a premier destination for elite time attack vehicles and engineering.

Throughout 2011 and 2012, WTAC continued to expand in both participation and technical sophistication. The Pro Class became increasingly competitive, with Australian teams rapidly developing their vehicles to challenge international entrants. Advancements in aerodynamics, tyre technology, and engine performance contributed to progressively faster lap times, reinforcing the event's reputation as a showcase of cutting-edge time attack engineering. [ref: In The Moment >> Smashing the 1:30 barrier, Speedhunters]
[ref: In The Moment>> Cyber Evo Dips Below 1:29, Scorch Breaks Down, Speedhunters]
[ref: Flash Result >> Cyber Evo Defend Their Crown, Speedhunters]
[ref: Behind The Scenes >> Life In The WTAC Pitlane, Speedhunters]

The event also grew beyond on-track competition, incorporating a larger motorsport festival atmosphere with trade exhibitions, car displays, and spectator engagement. By 2012, WTAC had firmly established itself as a globally recognised event, attracting leading teams from Japan, Australia, [ref: Australians Dominate At World Time Attack Challenge 2012, Drive] and other regions, and setting the foundation for its continued evolution as the world's premier time attack competition. [ref: WTAC 2012 - Archives Speedhunters, Speedhunters]

Between approximately 2013 and 2017, the event entered a period often characterised as an "aerodynamic arms race," with increasingly extreme vehicle designs emerging [ref: The 2017 WTAC Finals and Unlimited Aero Extremes, Headcount Coffee]
[ref: The Dust Settles At WTAC: Tilton Reigns Supreme, Speedhunters]
[ref: Welcome Back, WTAC, Speedhunters]
[ref: Flash Result: Tilton Evo Takes Third WTAC Title, Speedhunters]
[ref: The Speedhunters WTAC Wrap-Up, Speedhunters]
[ref: Open Wide & Say Ahh... The Engine Bays Of WTAC, Speedhunters]
[ref: World Time Attack Challenge 2016 - Shattering Records at Sydney Motorsport Park, DSPORT Magazine]
[ref: WTAC 2017 Starts Here, Speedhunters]
[ref: World Time Attack Challenge 2017 Is On, Speedhunters]
[ref: Why We Keep Coming Back To WTAC, Speedhunters]

Jarrett Bell is an American sports journalist and NFL columnist for USA Today, where he has worked since 1993. [ref: Staff Profile: Jarrett Bell, USA Today] He is a member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame selection committee and a recipient of the Pro Football Writers of America (PFWA) Bill Nunn Jr. Award. [ref: Bill Nunn Memorial Award Winners, Pro Football Hall of Fame]

== Early life and education ==
Bell was raised in Detroit, Michigan. [ref: Jarrett Bell (@[user]) on X, X (formerly Twitter)] During his youth, he worked at Olympia Stadium as an equipment manager for the Detroit Jr. Wings and as an assistant in the Detroit Red Wings public relations department.

He attended Michigan State University, graduating in 1981 with a bachelor's degree in Human Communication. [ref: USA Today Columnist Jarrett Bell On His 30 Years Covering The NFL, KUT Radio] In 1979, he studied abroad at the University of London under The Guardian's Contemporary Mass Media program. [ref: Jarrett Bell, posthillpress.com]

== Career ==
Bell began his journalism career as a staff writer for The Dallas Times Herald. [ref: Sports Journalist Jarrett Bell First Black Man To Receive Bill Nunn Jr. Writer's Award, blackenterprise.com] In 1989, he became the editor of The Dallas Cowboys Weekly. From 1990 to 1992, he covered the San Francisco 49ers for The Marin Independent Journal.

In 1993, Bell joined USA Today as a national NFL columnist, covering league games, business operations, and executive profiles.

From 2013 to 2017, Bell was a contributor for ESPN, appearing as a panelist on NFL Insiders and SportsCenter. [ref: 2020 PFWA Off-Field Award nominees announced, profootballwriters.org] He has also appeared as a commentator on CBS Sports, NBC Sports, CNN, and NFL Network. He was a regular guest on the Baltimore Ravens pregame show on WBAL from 2001 to 2018. [ref: Jarrett Bell: Getting personal with the NFL, iheart.com]

Bell was featured in two documentaries, “The Forgotten Four” and “Minister of Defense: The Reggie White Story.” He also had a cameo role in the movie Invincible.

==Author==
Bell co-wrote Reggie Williams' memoir, Resilient by Nature: Reflections from a Life of Winning On and Off the Football Field, released in 2020, for which he received an Outstanding Book Award from the National Association of Black Journalists.

== Committees and honors ==
Bell has served on the Pro Football Hall of Fame Selection Committee since 1997. [ref: HOF Selection Committee member Jarrett Bell joins the show, Pro Football Hall of Fame YouTube] He was a member of the 26-person Blue Ribbon Panel that selected the NFL 100th Anniversary All-Time Team and serves on the media panel that selects the Super Bowl MVP. The National Association of Black Journalists honored Bell with a Salute to Excellence Award in 2020.

In 2022, the PFWA awarded Bell the Bill Nunn Jr. Award for long and distinguished career contributions to professional football reporting. [ref: 'I got a story for you': USA TODAY Sports' Jarrett Bell wins prestigious Bill Nunn Jr. Award] [ref: USA Today's Jarrett Bell wins writers' award for service, yahoo.com] He is the first Black journalist to receive the award. He received first-place honors from the Associated Press Sports Editors (APSE) in 2020 and has received multiple writing awards from the National Association of Black Journalists (NABJ).

Daddy B. Nice is the pseudonym for Bruno Niceswanger (born November 2, 1946), an American writer and music critic who according to The Village Voice indispensably chronicles, reviews, and aggregates Southern Soul music's subculture from the inside. [ref: Southern Soul Guide: Sweet Angel, Mel Waiters, and Luther Lackey, The Village Voice] In 2005, he launched the website SouthernSoulRnB.com with the determination to "spread the word" about the genre of music. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] The Jackson Free Press has called Daddy B. Nice "The Apostle of Southern Soul," [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] and Jefferson Blues Magazine has described him as "The Southern Soul Oracle." [ref: STEVIE J / KÌNG GEORGE / SUMMER WOLFE / CURT THE COUNTRYMAN ft. COUNTRYBOII TYE, Jefferson Blues Magazine] Before his work in music criticism, he was an editor for underground newspapers and a participant in radical student activism at the University of Northern Iowa in the 1960s, and later published articles as a freelance journalist in Boulder, CO. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] [ref: Showdown in Boulder: Tate, Fuller and civic pride, The Rocky Mountain News]

== Early life, writings, and underground press ==

Niceswanger was born in Carroll, Iowa on November 2, 1946. [ref: An Apostle for Southern Soul, Jackson Free Press] While attending the University of Northern Iowa in 1965, he published a poem titled "The Way Bruno Feels About Writing" in the literary review Midwest. [ref: The Way Bruno Feels About Writing, Scholarworks.uni.edu] He was given an award and named an outstanding journalist by the university in 1966. [ref: Awards given to outstanding SCI journalists, IndexUNI] In 1968, he was recruited by publisher Doug Warrington to edit Campus Underground, an underground newspaper based in Cedar Falls, Iowa that Warrington had aspired to make a national newspaper. [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] Niceswanger was chosen to be the first editor after a search among interested students in the three Iowa state universities. [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] When that publication folded due to financial issues, he edited its successor, The New Prairie Primer, from 1969 to 1970. [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute]

The first issue of the The New Prairie Primer featured a highly popular, multi-page article by Niceswanger covering his experience of going to the Woodstock Music & Art Festival titled "Going Up to Meat County." [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] In the wake of the success of the first issue, the Primer received enough donations to make their second issue about the Vietnam War, free to readers. The Vietnam issue featured the first publication anywhere of the entire list of Iowa's war dead, and featured a story by UNI student, Dick Simpson, who was under indictment for refusing induction into the armed forces. [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] [ref: Underground Newspaper In Circulation Under New Name, Index UNI] The second issue of the Primer also brought attention to the notable cooperation that was happening between the anti-war hippies of the radical left and various statewide church ministries. [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] The paper did receive support from the United Christian Ministry and was headquartered in the basement of the Bethany House, which caused some community opposition. [ref: Everything You Ever Wanted To Know About The Primer, Index UNI] [ref: Underground Newspaper In Circulation Under New Name, Index UNI]

During his time as an editor, he participated in radical student activism, including the anti-Vietnam war movement and protests related to the "UNI7." [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] In 1970, he edited a tabloid exposé titled "Special Report: The Military-Industrial Complex in Iowa," detailing defense contracts held by local companies. [ref: Campus Underground [with] The New Prairie Primer (12 issues) [with] Special Report: The Military-Industrial Complex in Iowa, AbeBooks] [ref: The Crest of the High Wave: Radical Studnets and the Underground Press at UNI, Midwestern Marx Institute] Niceswanger also published "The Conspiracy To Undermine The Freaks" in The North American Review in 1969, which analyzed the systemic harassment of the counterculture. [ref: The Conspiracy to Undermine the Freaks, The North American Review] Sometime in the mid-1970s, Niceswanger moved to Boulder, CO, and as a free-lance writer was published in the regional newspaper, The Rocky Mountain News. [ref: Showdown in Boulder: Tate, Fuller and civic pride, The Rocky Mountain News]

Vincent J. Roscigno is a sociologist and Distinguished Professor of Arts & Sciences in Sociology at The Ohio State University. His research is comprised of topics ranging from social inequality to workplace discrimination, the sociology of work and education, collective behavior and social movements. Roscigno has served as the Co-Editor of the American Sociological Review, as President of the Southern Sociological Society, and as an elected Council Member of the American Sociological Association. In 2026, he received the American Sociological Association's Distinguished Contributions to Teaching Award. [ref: 2026 ASA Award Winners, American Sociological Association] [ref: American Sociological Association Announces 2026 Award Recipients, [www.newswise.com](https://www.newswise.com)]

==Education and career==

Roscigno received his B.A. in sociology from the University of Arizona in 1989. He attended North Carolina State University, where he earned his M.S. in 1991 and his Ph.D. in 1996. [ref: American Sociological Association. "Roscigno, Hodson Are Incoming Editors of American Sociological Review." Footnotes, July/August 2006, Vol. 34, No. 6. https://www.asanet.org/wp-content/uploads/fn_2006_06.pdf] His early scholarship, while at North Carolina State, included a co-authored study with sociologist Donald Tomaskovic-Devey on racial economic inequality in the U.S. South. [ref: Tomaskovic-Devey, Donald and Vincent J. Roscigno. "Racial Economic Subordination and White Gain in the U.S. South." American Sociological Review 61 (1996): 565–589.]

Roscigno began teaching at The Ohio State University in 1996. He was promoted to associate professor in 2001 and to full Professor in 2005; he was named Distinguished Professor of Arts & Sciences in Sociology in 2012, the same year he received the university's Distinguished University Scholar Award. [ref: Vincent J. Roscigno, Curriculum Vita (June 2026). The Ohio State University Department of Sociology. https://u.osu.edu/roscigno.1/files/2026/06/VJRVITA__6-9-26.pdf] [ref: ]

From 2007 to 2009, Roscigno served as the Co-Editor of the American Sociological Review alongside the late sociologist Randy Hodson. [ref: ] From 2013 to 2018, he was the founding Co-Editor (with Toni Calasanti of Virginia Tech) of Social Currents, the official journal of the Southern Sociological Society. [ref: Social Currents, and the Prospects and Promise of Sociology, Social Currents]

==Research==

Roscigno's research addresses inequalities through various methodological procedures ranging from quantitative, qualitative, and historical methods. [ref: ] As of 2026, his publications have accumulated more than 14,000 citations. [ref: Vincent J. Roscigno, scholar.google.com]

===Workplace and organizational inequality===

In one area of research, Roscigno's work examines how race, gender, and age discrimination operates within organizations and labor markets, through his 2007 book The Face of Discrimination: How Race and Gender Impact Work and Home Lives, which draws on discrimination complaints filed with the Ohio Civil Rights Commission. [ref: The Face of Discrimination: How Race and Gender Impact Work and Home Lives] His 2011 article "Power, Revisited," delivered as his Presidential Address to the Southern Sociological Society, presents a theoretical framework for understanding power within organizations. [ref: Roscigno, Vincent J. "Power, Revisited." Social Forces 90 (2011): 349–374.]

===Labor movements, music, and culture===

Roscigno's earlier research explored culture, media, and labor mobilization in the American South. His 2004 book The Voice of Southern Labor: Radio, Music, and Textile Strikes, 1929–1934 (co-authored with William F. Danaher) examines how southern textile mill workers used radio broadcasts and music to build solidarity, sustaining labor insurgencies during the strikes of 1929 and 1934. [ref: Roscigno, Vincent J. and William F. Danaher. The Voice of Southern Labor: Radio, Music, and Textile Strikes, 1929–1934. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press, 2004. https://www.upress.umn.edu/book-division/books/the-voice-of-southern-labor] The book was reviewed in both academic and government publications, including the Journal of Interdisciplinary History, [ref: The Voice of Southern Labor: Radio, Music, and Textile Strikes, 1929–1934. By Vincent Roscigno and William F. Danaher (Minneapolis, University of Minnesota Press, 2004) 177 pp. $19.95, The Journal of Interdisciplinary History] and the International Review of Social History. [ref: Roscigno, Vincent J. and William F. Danaher, The Voice of Southern Labor. Radio, Music, and Textile Strikes, 1929–1934. [Social Movements, Protest, and Contention, vol. 19.] University of Minnesota Press, Minneapolis [etc.] 2004. xxviii, 177 pp. $59.95, International Review of Social History] It was also reviewed by the Bureau of Labor Statistics in its Monthly Labor Review. [ref: Music for the people: the role of music in the southern textile strikes of 1929–34: Monthly Labor Review: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Bureau of Labor Statistics]

===Education and first-generation students===

William Thomas "Tommy" Beavers (December 14, 1949 – October 29, 2023) was an American drummer best known as a member of the Western swing band Asleep at the Wheel. He performed on the band's 1993 album Tribute to the Music of Bob Wills and the Texas Playboys and was credited by the Recording Academy with one Grammy Award win and two nominations. Earlier in his career, Beavers performed with Tommy Shaw in the Montgomery, Alabama-based band Harvest.

==Career==

===Harvest and Harmony===
During the 1970s, Beavers played drums in the Montgomery-based band Harvest with bassist Jimbo Jones, keyboardist Eddie Wohlford and guitarist and vocalist Tommy Shaw. [ref: The Quaz Q&A: Tommy Shaw, Jeff Pearlman]

In a 2011 interview, Shaw recalled his time with Harvest and specifically praised Beavers's drumming, noting his ability to control his dynamics while performing in the group's small venue.

After Shaw left Harvest to join Styx, the group continued as Harmony. Singer-songwriter Beth Nielsen Chapman subsequently joined the lineup. [ref: Tommy Beavers, Encyclopedia of Alabama]

===Asleep at the Wheel===
Beavers joined Asleep at the Wheel in the early 1990s, replacing drummer David Sanger. He was part of the lineup that recorded the 1993 album Tribute to the Music of Bob Wills and the Texas Playboys. [ref: Tommy Beavers – Biography, Discography, Albums & Expert Reviews, AllMusic]

Contemporary reference works on Asleep at the Wheel identify Beavers as the band's drummer during this period, alongside Ray Benson, Tim Alexander, Cindy Cashdollar, Ricky Turpin, David Earl Miller and Michael Francis. [ref: Asleep at the Wheel]

AllMusic credits Beavers with drums on A Tribute to the Music of Bob Wills & the Texas Playboys (1993), Still Swingin (1994), and Texans Live from Mountain Stage (1997).

At the 37th Annual Grammy Awards, "Blues for Dixie", performed by Asleep at the Wheel with Lyle Lovett, won the Grammy Award for Country Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals. The Recording Academy's individual artist record for Beavers credits him with one Grammy win and two nominations. [ref: Tommy Beavers – Grammy Awards and Nominations, GRAMMY.com]

===Later career===
Beavers later returned to performing primarily in the Montgomery area. His career and contributions to Alabama music were the subject of a feature by the Montgomery Advertiser following his death. The article included comments from Asleep at the Wheel bandleader Ray Benson, who discussed Beavers's contributions to the band's recordings, live performances and television appearances. [ref: This one's for The Beav: Memorial concert Sunday for Grammy-winning drummer Tommy Beavers, Montgomery Advertiser]

Beavers also participated in music education workshops organized by the Montgomery Area Musicians Association.

==Auto racing==
Outside music, Beavers participated in automobile road racing. His racing activities included competition at Road Atlanta and Daytona International Speedway.

==Recognition==
In 2017, Beavers was recognized by the Alabama Music Hall of Fame as a Music Achiever.

The Recording Academy credits Beavers with one Grammy Award win and two nominations.

==Death==
Beavers died on October 29, 2023. Following his death, musicians with whom he had performed participated in a memorial concert in Prattville, Alabama. [ref: In memory of 'The Beav': Fellow musicians hold memorial concert and fundraiser, Montgomery Advertiser]

Ashendye (Amharic: አሸንድዬ) is a religious festival celebrated in Lasta, Lalibela, and Gondar of the Amhara region of Ethiopia. [ref: Bete Amhara: A Journey Through Wollo’s Living Heritage, Landscapes, and Seasonal Festivals, Rex Clarke Adventures] In different localities of Amhara, the festival is also known as Shadey (ሻደይ) or Solel (ሶለል). It explicitly commemorates the Old Testament story of Moses and the reed basket in which he was saved. In contrast, Ashenda in Tigray (ኣሸንዳ) is a secularized civic festival that centers on female social autonomy, gendered freedom, and modern regional political expression. [ref: Tigrayans in North Texas preserve culture, tradition through Ashenda, a day to honor women, www.keranews.org/]

== Historical and Cultural Roots ==

The Amhara highlands of Bete Amhara and Gondar serve as the foundational cradle of the Ashendye festival due to the region's ancient roots in early Jewish tradition. [ref: Falasha anthology, New Haven, Conn.; London: Yale University Press] This deep Hebraic heritage is preserved through the historic use of the Tabot (Ark covenant replica) ceremony. This celebration predates the Aksumite Christian era and goes back before the spread of Christianity.

Girls participating in Ashendye traditionally wear fresh green Cyperus sedge grass, known as Ashenda (Amharic: አሸንዳ), woven and tied around their waist. This grass is prepared as a thick, layered belt or skirt and serves as one of the festival's most recognizable elements.

Within this historical framework, the connection centers on the symbolism of the reed basket. In Amhara tradition, the primary reason young women weave and wear the native green Cyperus sedge grass around their waists is to symbolise the papyrus reed basket that saved the infant Moses on the Nile. According to the Old Testament narrative, Moses's mother placed him in a basket hidden among the reeds of the Nile River to protect him from Pharaoh's decree. The fresh river grass used in the festival acts as a living monument to this biblical event of preservation and divine protection. [ref: Travels to discover the source of the Nile, in the years 1768, 1769, 1770, 1771, 1772, and 1773, Edinburgh, Printed by J. Ruthven, for G. G. J. and J. Robinson, London]

== References ==

Jarno Zaffelli is an Italian motor-racing circuit designer and the founder of Dromo Circuit Design. [ref: Jarno Zaffelli, un reggiano sulle piste di mezzo mondo, Corriere di Bologna] [ref: Jarno Zaffelli, progettista delle piste: 'Autodromi migliori grazie a noi', Il Resto del Carlino] His work has included the redesign or resurfacing of circuits such as Silverstone, Zandvoort and the Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps, as well as the original design of the Madring circuit in Madrid. [ref: Architect Zaffelli: 'Bouwen aan Circuit Zandvoort is als spelen in het zand', [[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting] [ref: El diseñador del circuito semiurbano de F1 en Madrid: «Que la gente esté tranquila; Madrid no será como Valencia», El País]

== Early life and career ==

Zaffelli trained as an industrial technician in experimental mechanics and briefly studied management engineering. In 2000 he began developing a proposal for a motor-racing circuit near Reggio Emilia. Although that circuit was not built, the research led him to travel internationally to study existing tracks and ultimately to establish Dromo Circuit Design. Italian publications subsequently profiled his development from the Reggio Emilia project into an international circuit-design career. [ref: Jarno Zaffelli, il progettista italiano che sfida Hermann Tilke, FormulaPassion.it] [ref: Dalla Malesia ad Abu Dhabi, progetti ad alta velocità, Gazzetta di Reggio]

Zaffelli developed a crash-prediction model based on eleven years of accident and circuit data. The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile reported that the model was used during Dromo's 2012 reconstruction of the Autódromo Termas de Río Hondo in Argentina. [ref: Crashing the numbers, FIA Auto+Medical] At the 2017 FIA Sport Conference, he presented the use of data analysis in circuit design and safety work. [ref: How the art of circuit design can improve safety while increasing the entertainment factor, Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile]

Following the cancellation of the 2018 British motorcycle Grand Prix because of drainage and surface problems, Zaffelli was appointed to take part in the technical investigation at Silverstone. [ref: MotoGP, Silverstone: Jarno Zaffelli condurrà l'indagine tecnica, FormulaPassion.it] Dromo subsequently worked on the circuit's complete resurfacing in 2019. [ref: Silverstone's Brooklands bump set to be fixed for MotoGP, Motorsport.com]

Between 2019 and 2020, Zaffelli led design work for the renovation of Zandvoort ahead of the return of the Dutch Grand Prix to Formula One. The project included the banked Hugenholtz and Arie Luyendyk corners. [ref: Development of the Zandvoort GP circuit, Professional Motorsport World] In 2021 and 2022, Zaffelli and Dromo worked on the renovation of Spa-Francorchamps, including changes to the three-dimensional geometry and surface of Eau Rouge–Raidillon while retaining its plan-view alignment. [ref: Jarno Zaffelli: «Il y avait l'option de changer l'Eau Rouge», L'Équipe]

In January 2024, Zaffelli was presented as the designer of the semi-permanent Formula One circuit planned around the IFEMA exhibition complex in Madrid. [ref: Why Madrid F1 critics have it wrong – 'It's a real test of driver & machine', [[Motor Sport (magazine)] In 2025, IFEMA terminated its implementation-support contract with Dromo and appointed companies from the German group founded by circuit designer Hermann Tilke to continue the project. In 2026, the Cologne Regional Court granted Dromo interim relief limited to Germany, prohibiting two Tilke companies from reproducing specified protected materials there. [ref: Landgericht Köln, judgment in case no. 14 O 62/26, following the hearing of 2 April 2026, pp. 1–4 and 61–64 ([https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Landgericht_K%C3%B6ln_judgment_14_O_62-26_(redacted).pdf redacted copy], in German).] El País reported that IFEMA maintained that the contract had been terminated because of documented breaches and that it was entitled to provide the material to third parties; Dromo disputed that account. The German order was preliminary and did not determine the wider contractual dispute in Spain. [ref: El diseño del circuito de F1 de Madrid desata un conflicto millonario con frentes en Alemania y España, El País] [ref: Ifema moviliza a la Comunidad de Madrid en su pulso millonario por el diseño del circuito de la F1, El País]

== Early life and education ==
Medy Renaldy was born in Jakarta on December 31, 1996. He is an alumnus of Trisakti University, Faculty of Industrial Technology, majoring in Industrial Engineering at the class of 2014. [ref: Profil Medy Renaldy: Biodata, Kekayaan, Fakta Menarik, dan Foto Masa Muda, Inilah.com]

[ref: Medy Renaldy: Bukan Sekadar Konten Kreator, Tapi Pengusaha Kreatif Inspiratif, kabarbaik.co]

[ref: Penghargaan Abang None DKI Jakarta Favorit, FTI Trisakti]

== Career and business ==

=== Illustrator and Entrepreneur ===
Before becoming a full-time content creator, Medy worked as an illustrator. He has enjoyed drawing since 2014 and often painted portraits of important figures and celebrities, such as Jokowi, Will Smith, Najwa Shihab, and Benyamin.

In 2017, he founded MR Creative Lab, a service for creating realistic face illustrations and for a gallery of his artworks. [ref: Instagram, www.instagram.com] Due to his talent in drawing, he was invited to appear on the talk show Hitam Putih on Trans7 hosted by Deddy Corbuzier in 2018.

In addition to digital content, Medy also founded a business into the culinary field by founding Soto Susu Bu Tin restaurant in January 2020, which serves Soto Betawi with a special recipe from his mother.

=== Content Creator ===
Medy has had a YouTube channel since October 2, 2011, but he became consistent in uploading content since 2020. He focuses his content on reviews, unboxing, and stories about expensive, rare, and high-quality toy collections from various franchises such as Marvel, Harry Potter, and Toy Story. [ref: Kronologi Medy Renaldy Dihujat karena Bulu Babi, IDN Times]

In September 2024, Medy had the opportunity to meet American YouTuber, IShowSpeed, during his visit to Jakarta, and Medy gave him a Cristiano Ronaldo action figure as a gift. [ref: 3 Fakta Menarik Action Figure Ronaldo yang Dihadiahkan Medy Renaldy ke IShowspeed, medcom.id]

As of 2 October 2026, Medy Renaldy's YouTube channel has over 5 million subscribers and 774 of videos that have reached a billion views total. [ref: Medy Renaldy, YouTube] His TikTok account also has over 11 million followers. [ref: Medy's tiktok, TikTok]

== Public attention and controversy ==

=== Customs Incident ===
Medy once became the focus of media and collector communities after he expressed his disappointment with the Customs and Excise authorities. [ref: Kemenkeu beri bukti kasus paket mainan Megatron bukan ulah Bea Cukai, Antara News] The incident occurred in April 2024 when a Megatron toy package, which was a gift shipment from the producer, was detained by the authorities and the toy box was reportedly damaged. [ref: Paket Mainan Megatron Milik Youtuber Rusak, Bea Cukai Beri Klarifikasi, Bisnis.com] Medy claimed he was asked to send an invoice for an item that was actually a gift. [ref: Influencer Medy Renaldy Respons Video Pembongkaran Mainan Megatron, ekonomi]

=== Appeal to Stop Playing Roblox ===
In October 2025, Medy once again sparked public debate after uploading a video on TikTok containing a serious appeal to the public, especially adults, to stop playing the online game Roblox. Medy expressed concerns about the psychological and social impact of the game. He presented three main reasons: [ref: Medy Renaldy Mode Serius, Ingatkan Bahaya Main Roblox: Stop Sekarang Kalau Mau Selamat, Wartakotalive.com]

* Potential indicator of a lack of social interaction, referring to study results linking internet gaming disorder to loneliness.
* The trend of mountain climbing simulations in Roblox was considered insulting to the nature-loving community.
* Potential for gaming disorder characterized by a chaotic lifestyle.

Medy's statement sparked pros and cons, and it emerged around the same time as a ban from the minister of primary and secondary education (Mendikdasmen) regarding the game Roblox for children, which also became a concern for the Deputy Minister of Communication and Digital Affairs. [ref: Indonesian government warns children, parents against ‘violent’ Roblox]

Nagarukhra (; ) is a town and a local government area in the Nadia district in the Indian state of West Bengal. It operates under the Kalyani subdivision and the Haringhata CD block. The town is share the part of the area covered by the Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority (KMDA) in the Region and is administered by two Gram Panchayats. [ref: Kolkata Metropolitan Development Authority, KMDA]

== History ==
The earliest known historical identity of the area is associated with Ukrah (or Ookra). Historical accounts connected with the Mughal administration, including references in the Ain-i-Akbari, indicate that Ukrah was documented as a pargana during the Mughal period. [ref: History of Nadia, Nadia District Administration]

During the early 18th century, Ukrah became associated with the Zamindari system of Bengal. Local historical accounts connect the Ukrah Zamindari with Raghuram, a descendant of Bhavananda Majumdar. Following the Battle of Plassey in 1757 and the East India Company's acquisition of the Diwani of Bengal in 1765, the region came under British revenue and administrative control. British geographic surveys associated with James Rennell recorded the name of the area as Ukhra or Aukerah, documenting its continued presence during the colonial period. [ref: Rennell and the Surveyors of India, The Geographical Journal]

The Jamuna River played an essential role in the development of the settlement by providing opportunities for transportation and agriculture. Over time, a local market (ganj) developed. It is historically suggested that as the settlement grew into an important local center, the prefix "Nagar" (meaning town) was added to the older name Ukhra, forming "Nagarukhra".

Throughout the 19th century, Nagarukhra and the surrounding Nadia region became part of the colonial economy, particularly noted for "Indigo cultivation" (neel kuthis). The partition of India in 1947 impacted the territorial status of Nadia. The district was briefly associated with East Pakistan in early boundary arrangements before the Radcliffe Award placed most of Nadia, including Nagarukhra, in India on 18 August 1947. [ref: Partition of British India, The National Archives]

== Geography ==
Nagarukhra is situated in the southern part of the Nadia district within the flat alluvial landscape of the lower Ganges basin. The surrounding terrain has minimal relief, characterized by fertile alluvial deposits and low-lying agricultural land. Groundwater and topographical studies identify the lowest recorded ground-surface elevation in the district near Nagarukhra, at approximately 14 metres above mean sea level. [ref: Ground Water Information Booklet, Nadia District, West Bengal, Central Ground Water Board, Ministry of Water Resources, Government of India]

The settlement is closely associated with the Jamuna River, a key geographical feature of the locality, and is located near the administrative boundary between Nadia and North 24 Parganas districts. [ref: District Census Handbook Nadia, Census of India 2011, Series 20, Part XII A, Directorate of Census Operations, West Bengal]

=== Climate ===
Nagarukhra experiences a humid tropical climate (Köppen climate classification Aw), typical of southern West Bengal. Summers are hot and humid, the monsoon season brings substantial rainfall, and winters are mild and dry. According to local climate data, the annual mean temperature is approximately 26.3 °C, with an average annual precipitation of 1,550–1,560 mm. July is generally the wettest month, while December is the driest. [ref: Climate Summary for Nagarukhra, Weatherbase.com]

== Civic and revenue administration ==
The civic administration of the wider town and its adjoining areas is managed by two rural local bodies: Nagarukhra-I and Nagarukhra-II Gram Panchayats. Law and order for the entire Nagarukhra area and surrounding villages are maintained by the Nagarukhra Police Station. [ref: Nadia District Police, West Bengal, Nadia District Police]

=== Revenue office ===
For land and revenue administration, the core central part of the town corresponds to the Ukrah mouza (Jurisdiction List or JL No. 77). This specific mouza houses the local Revenue Inspector (RI) office, which manages the land records and revenue matters for the immediate region under the state's land reforms department. [ref: Mouza Information, Land and Land Reforms Department, Banglarbhumi]

=== Postal services ===
The town operates a delivery post office serving the local residents and surrounding villages. It functions under the Department of Posts with the designated PIN code 741257. [ref: Locate Post Office: Nagarukhra, India Post]

=== Electricity board ===
The area's power supply and electrical infrastructure are overseen by a regional Customer Care Center (CCC) of the West Bengal State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (WBSEDCL). [ref: WBSEDCL Customer Care Centers, WBSEDCL]

== Demographics ==
Nagarukhra encompasses multiple mouzas (revenue villages) spread across the Nagarukhra-I and Nagarukhra-II Gram Panchayats.

Draft: Arunachal church burnings, 1968–1978

Draft text:
Between 1968 and 1978, Christian communities in the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA), renamed Arunachal Pradesh in January 1972, faced a period of persecution [ref: Christianity and social change in northeast India: a study of the role of Christianity in social change among the Khasi-Jaintia Hill tribes of Meghalaya, Vendrame Institute; Firma KLM Private Ltd.] [ref: The Illustrated Weekly Of India(january-july)1988] that included church burnings, [ref: Togo Basar's Articles from Arunachal Pradesh, India: The History of Untold Misery and Persecutions to Christians in Arunachal Pradesh India, Togo Basar's Articles from Arunachal Pradesh, India] a crackdown on missionaries, and arrests of pastors and converts, alongside standing Inner Line restrictions on missionary entry. [ref: Indian Christians Stopped an Anticonversion Law. Until Now., Christianity Today] [ref: Identity Crisis: A Law Banning Conversion Sparks Fears of Religious Divide, Global Press Journal] Journalistic accounts associate the crackdown with the tenure of K. A. A. Raja, the territory's first chief commissioner and later first lieutenant governor. [ref: Preach, Fifty Two] It has also been documented by the Government of Arunachal Pradesh including Bundle-Con-1970-73, titled as Confidential Files, which contains 16 files. Among them is a 1970 confidential file titled "National Integration, Protection of culture and religious faiths of the people of NEFA". [ref: National Integration-Protection of culture and religious faiths of the people of NEFA, Confidentials Files, State Archives of Arunachal]

== Overview ==
According to Christianity Today, police burned churches, looted homes, and attacked Christian families between 1968 and 1974, [ref: North East India: Combating the Converts, Christianity Today] with 47 churches reportedly torched in a single region in 1974. [ref: ] [ref: North East India: Combating the Converts, Christianity Today] A former Adi policeman, Takeng Taggu, later recalled having burned churches and arrested missionaries on government orders during this period before he himself converted. A 1990 dispatch by the Catholic agency UCA News, the main contemporaneous Christianpress account, reported substantially higher decade-long totals. [ref: Despite persecution, Christianity flourishes in Arunachal Pradesh state, UCA News]

The period overlapped with the founding of the Donyi-Polo revival among the Tani communities and the entry of RSS-affiliated organisations, developments later linked by scholars to the administrative climate of the time. [ref: The Institutionalization of Tribal Religion: Recasting the Donyi-Polo Movement in Arunachal Pradesh, Asian Ethnology] [ref: BJP and Donyi-Polo: New Challenges to Christianity in Arunachal Pradesh and Northeast India, International Bulletin of Mission Research] [ref: ]

In 1978, when Arunachal Pradesh was still a union territory administered directly by the central government, accounting for this incident, its legislature passed the Arunachal Pradesh Freedom of Religion Act, which prohibits conversion by force, inducement, or fraud. [ref: Philosophy for NEFA] [ref: A decades-old law and politics of religion in BJP-ruled Arunachal Pradesh, Deccan Herald] The period thus is also regarded as the culmination for the passing of the Arunachal Pradesh Freedom of Religion Act, [ref: BJP and Donyi-Polo: New Challenges to Christianity in Arunachal Pradesh and Northeast India, International Bulletin of Mission Research] which is an attempt to prohibit proselytism. [ref: State Anti-conversion Laws in India, Law Library of Congress, Global Legal Research Directorate] [ref: The Catholic Church in Northeast India: 1890-1990: a Multidimensional Study, Firma KLM]

==References==
