OnlyRoses is a British rose retailer founded in London in 2007 by Anian and Sabine Schmitt. It sells fresh-cut roses and preserved roses under the Infinite Roses name. [ref: The Roses That Might Last Longer Than Your Relationship, Vogue] [ref: London-Based Rose Retailer Opens First U.S. Location, Retail TouchPoints] In 2019, OnlyRoses supplied roses for the stage design of the 91st Academy Awards. [ref: David Korins' Renderings For The 2019 Oscars, Live Design]

== History ==
OnlyRoses began in London in 2007 as a retailer specialising in roses. By 2017, it had expanded through franchise locations in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Doha, Riyadh and Kuwait City. Trade publication FloralDaily reported that the company's Abu Dhabi store at Nation Towers was its largest at the time. [ref: A flower shop dedicated to roses only, FloralDaily]

In 2017, OnlyRoses established a retail presence in Beverly Hills, California. [ref: Madonna-Loved Flower Shop OnlyRoses Will Open Its First U.S. Boutique in Beverly Hills, The Hollywood Reporter] Interior Design reported that the approximately 550-square-foot boutique was designed by Italian firm Baciocchi Associati. [ref: OnlyRoses Debuts Los Angeles Outpost by Baciocchi Associati, Interior Design] A December 2017 feature in 805 Living described the boutique as the London brand's first United States location and reported that it stocked fresh Ecuadorian roses and preserved Infinite Roses. [ref: World-Class Weekend, 805 Living]

== Products ==
OnlyRoses sells fresh-cut roses and preserved roses marketed as Infinite Roses. Vogue reported in 2018 that OnlyRoses had introduced Infinite Roses in 2010 and sourced its roses from farms near Quito, Ecuador. According to the magazine, the preserved roses could last up to a year without water. Co-founder Sabine Schmitt told Vogue that the rose heads and stems were preserved separately before being reassembled.

== 2019 Academy Awards ==
Production designer David Korins incorporated approximately 40,000 red preserved roses supplied by OnlyRoses, marketed as Infinite Roses, into scenic elements for the 91st Academy Awards, including a floral interpretation of the Oscar statuette. Korins described the roses' role in creating a warmer stage setting in interviews with Interior Design and Galerie. [ref: Behind-the-Scenes Q&A with 2019 Oscars Set Designer David Korins, Interior Design] [ref: Go Behind the Scenes of the Dazzling Swarovski-Adorned Oscars Stage, Galerie] Ecuadorian newspaper El Universo reported that the roses came from Ecuador. [ref: 40.000 rosas preservadas de Ecuador adornaron el escenario de los Premios Oscar 2019, El Universo]

August H. Nimtz (born 1942) is an American political scientist. He is a professor of political science and of African American and African studies at the University of Minnesota.

His first book, Islam and Politics in East Africa (1980), based on fieldwork in the Tanzanian town of Bagamoyo, focused on the political role of its Sufi brotherhoods. Since 2000 Nimtz has written mainly about Karl Marx, Friedrich Engels and Vladimir Lenin. His books include Marx and Engels: Their Contribution to the Democratic Breakthrough (2000), a two-volume study of Lenin's electoral strategy (2014), a comparison of Marx and Frederick Douglass written with Kyle A. Edwards (2024), and a reply to Cedric Robinson's Black Marxism (2026).

== Early life and career ==
Born in 1942 [ref: August Nimtz: History and Contingency in the Making of a Black Communist, Minneapolis Interview Project] to a New Orleans family, [ref: Double Ring Ceremony Unites Nimtz-Towns In New York City, The Louisiana Weekly] Nimtz grew up under Jim Crow laws, attending schools that were segregated by law. [ref: "Black Marxism" Under Debate, 40 Years On, Cosmonaut] He took a Bachelor of Arts at Purdue University in 1963 [ref: Receiving Degrees, New Orleans States-Item] and a Ph.D. in political science at Indiana University in 1973. [ref: August H. Nimtz, jr. Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press. 1980. Pp. xvi, 234. $20.00, The American Historical Review] His doctoral research was based on fieldwork in the Tanzanian coastal town of Bagamoyo, where he lived in 1969 and 1970 and later visited. [ref: Islam in Tanzania - Islam and Politics in East Africa. The Sufi Order in Tanzania. By August H. Nimtz Jr. Minneapolis: University of Minnesota Press, 1980. Pp. xvi + 234, The Journal of African History] His first book was a shortened and revised version of the thesis.

Nimtz has taught at the University of Minnesota since 1971. He is a professor of political science and of African American and African studies there. [ref: August Nimtz, College of Liberal Arts, University of Minnesota] In 2002 he received the Horace T. Morse-University of Minnesota Alumni Association Award for Outstanding Contributions to Undergraduate Education. [ref: Distinguished Teachers Morse-Alumni, Scholars Walk]

Nimtz was a member of the Socialist Workers Party (SWP) from 1972 to 1995. He co-chaired the Minnesota Committee on Southern Africa from 1976 to 1978 and the Twin Cities chapter of the National Black Independent Political Party from 1981 to 1983. [ref: Voter's guide: City primary election, Minneapolis Star and Tribune] He twice ran for office for the SWP: for mayor of Minneapolis in 1985, [ref: Mayor, Minneapolis Star and Tribune] and the next year as running mate to Tom Jaax, its candidate for governor of Minnesota. [ref: Socialist candidate for governor wants public steel control, The Duluth News-Tribune]

== Works ==
Nimtz's first book came out of his doctoral fieldwork and was about Islam and politics in Tanzania. His later books are about Marx, Engels and Lenin, and several of them are about race and slavery in the United States.

=== Islam and politics in East Africa ===
Nimtz's first book Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania came out in 1980. It examines the political role of the tariqa, or Sufi brotherhood, in East Africa under German and British colonial rule and through independence. [ref: Review of Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania, The International Journal of African Historical Studies] Nimtz argues that the reason the brotherhoods grew was because they gave leadership roles to African Muslims, which they could not get within mainstream Islam. [ref: Review of Islam and Politics in East Africa: The Sufi Order in Tanzania, The American Political Science Review] The book ends with thirteen propositions meant to apply beyond East Africa. Norman R. Bennett reviewed the book in the American Historical Review and called it a major contribution that went well beyond earlier guesswork about the brotherhoods. Ibrahim Abu-Lughod called the book an important study in the American Political Science Review and C. C. Stewart wrote that the book opened a debate that had not been possible before in East Africa.

Bennet and Stewart felt the thirteen propositions at the end of the book were weak. Bennett wrote that they were commonsense conclusions from evidence and the latter called several of the propositions circular. Abu-Lughod wrote that the book stopped at the independence struggle and did not cover what happened to the brotherhoods afterwards. Marguerite Ylvisaker reviewed the book in the International Journal of African Historical Studies and wrote that she doubted Nimtz's claim that the split between "black" and "white" was the basic division in Swahili society. She also added that women's membership got only a brief mention.
[truncated]

Draft: Pidiya (festival)

Draft text:
Pidiya is a traditional Hindu festival celebrated in the Bhojpuri region of India and Nepal. [ref: R̥tugīta: svara aura svarūpa, Ayana Prakāśana] [ref: Bihar Ke Paryatan Stahal Aur Sanskritik Dharohar: Demanding Ebook Book, Prabhat Prakashan] It is observed mainly by girls and women for the well-being, longevity and prosperity of their brothers. [ref: भोजपुरी संस्कृति का अनूठा पर्व: पीड़िया धर्म, परंपरा और भाई–बहन के प्रेम का पवित्र संगम - peediya festival celebrating bhojpuri culture brothersister bond, Jagran] [ref: Pañcāmr̥ta: Bhojapurī lekha saṅgraha, Santosha Prinṭarsa] The festival begins around Godhan (Govardhan Puja) and continues for about a month. [ref: Bhojapurī bhāshā kā itihāsa, Loka-Sāhitya-Saṅgama] It involves making pidiya figures from cow dung, creating Pidiya paintings, singing traditional folk songs, listening to ritual stories, fasting and immersing the pidiya in a river, pond, or other water body. [ref: भोजपुरी कहावतें: एक सांस्कृतिक अध्ययन, Vaṇī Prakāśana]

In the Bhojpuri region, Pidiya is traditionally associated with the bond between brothers and sisters and family unity. The observance connects religious practice with traditional family values and customs. Traditionally observed after the paddy harvest, the festival has remained an important part of Bhojpuri cultural traditions, particularly reflecting the affection, respect and close bond shared between sisters and brothers. [ref: Bonded Labour (Kamaiya) in Nepal, Trilij Counselling Centre]

==Name and observance==
Pidiya is also known as Rudravrata. [ref: Trends in Social Science Research, Chitra Srivastava] It is traditionally observed by the Bhojpuriya people during the months of Kartik and Agahan. The observance begins around Godhan (Govardhan Puja) and continues until the second day of the bright fortnight of Agahan.

==Ritual practices==
On Godhan (Govardhan Puja), sisters begin the rituals by making pidiya from the cow dung left after the Godhan ritual and attaching them to the walls of their houses. [ref: Loka sāhitya, Prakāśana Kendra] In some traditions, cow dung from a female calf is also mixed with the cow dung used for making the pidiya. Sisters traditionally make sixteen pidiya for each brother, with the number of sets corresponding to the number of brothers.

The pidiya are removed and made again at different stages of the observance. The first pidiya are removed on Kartik Purnima and another set is made again on the same day. The pidiya are later removed on Agahan Shukla Pratipada, marking the end of the month-long period of their display on the walls. As part of the observance, two ritual stories are traditionally heard: the chhotki katha (small story) from Godhan to Kartik Purnima and the badki katha (long story) from Agahan Krishna Ekam (Pratipada) to Agahan Amavasya. They are narrated by elderly women of the family. The sisters traditionally listen to the stories after completing their daily activities and only then consume food and water. On Agahan Shukla Pratipada, the sisters observe the special Rudravrat Pidiya, a one-day fast associated with the concluding ritual and involving distinct fasting and ritual practices. On this day, both the chhotki katha and badki katha are heard. On Agahan Shukla Dwitiya, the pidiya are taken to a river, pond or other water body and immersed, marking the completion of the ritual cycle. [ref: आज मनाया जाएगा पीड़िया व्रत, जानें इस व्रत का महत्व और विधि- विधान, www.livehindustan.com]

The observance also includes exchanges between brothers and sisters. Sisters may give sweets and gram to their brothers, while brothers may give their sisters money, clothes or ornaments. Sisters also exchange ghee-based sweets and chiura (flattened rice) with one another, a practice known as mutth dalal. [ref: Indian Philosophy & Culture, The Institute]

The sixteen pidiya made for each other are associated with Shodash Maatri puja (worship of sixteen mother goddesses). [ref: Bihar Ke Parva-Tyohar Aur Khanpan: Bestseller Book by Subodh Kumar Nandan: Bihar Ke Parva-Tyohar Aur Khanpan, Prabhat Prakashan] The pidiya are also described as symbolic representations of Lord Shiva, resembling the pind-like form used to represent Lord Shiva in certain Hindu rituals. [ref: पीड़िया के भोजपुरी गीत - कवन फूलवा फूलेला अधि अधि रे रतिया, News18 India]

==Rudravrat Pidiya==
Agahan Shukla Ekam (Pratipada) is the main day of the Pidiya observance and is known as Rudravrat Pidiya. [ref: भाई के लिए बहनों के प्‍यार का त्‍योहार रुद्र व्रत पीड़िया - Know the importance of Rudra vrat pidiya, Jagran] It marks the principal day of the vrat and it's concluding rituals.
[truncated]

Draft: Lubna Speitan

Draft text:
Lubna Speitan is a British-Palestinian award winning contemporary artist and activist. She is a founding member of the Greenwich Palestine Alliance and a long-standing campaigner for Palestinian rights [ref: ] [ref: GREENWICH PALESTINE ALLIANCE, GREENWICH PALESTINE ALLIANCE]. She has been involved in a legal campaign concerning Greenwich Council's investments and Palestine [ref: Campaigner takes Greenwich Council to court over Israel investments, The Greenwich Wire].

Speitan is based in London and is specialising in Abstracts, Landscapes, Seascapes, Nightscapes and Portraits although she has put her painting career largely on hold for more than two years while undertaking activism [ref: Biography, lubnaspeitan].

== Activism ==

=== Greenwich Palestine Alliance ===
Speitan is a founding member of the Greenwich Palestine Alliance, a London-based grassroots organisation campaigning on Palestinian issues. The organisation has organised political education, demonstrations and campaigns directed at institutions in the Royal Borough of Greenwich [ref: ].

=== Pension-fund campaign ===
In December 2024, Speitan submitted a public question to Greenwich Council concerning support for Palestinian residents affected by the conflict in the Middle East. In 2025 and 2026, Speitan pursued a judicial review backed by the Public Interest Law Centre concerning the investment policy of Greenwich Council’s pension fund. By early 2026, the council conceded that its stance on lacking legal power for divestment was unlawful, leading to a policy review [ref: Greenwich Council concedes pension fund investment policy was “unlawful” following Israel divestment challenge: law centre, www.localgovernmentlawyer.co.uk] [ref: Greenwich Council admits pension investments in Israel are unlawful following legal challenge, Morning Star] [ref: Gaza activist taking Greenwich Council to court claiming it unlawfully invested £60m in Israel, The Jewish Chronicle] [ref: ].

The dispute concerned a clause in Greenwich Council’s Local Government Pension Scheme investment strategy that stated that the council could not exclude investments in order to pursue boycotts, divestment and sanctions against foreign countries and UK defence industries. According to data from the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, Greenwich’s pension fund has invested more than £61.8m in companies with Israeli interests. Following the legal challenge, the council accepted that the relevant provision was legally erroneous and agreed to remove it and consult on its responsible-investment policy [ref: Greenwich Council concedes pension fund investment policy was “unlawful” following Israel divestment challenge: law centre, www.localgovernmentlawyer.co.uk].

Speitan said that the campaign arose partly from her family’s experience in Gaza and the West Bank. In an interview with the Public Interest Law Centre, she described the campaign as an attempt to apply consistent human-rights principles to local-government investment decisions and drew comparisons with local-government divestment campaigns during the South African anti-apartheid movement: "Our own local history proves this: divestment from South Africa was a crucial, tangible step Greenwich council took against apartheid. It showed local government can be a powerful lever for global justice" [ref: ].

=== Art ===
Speitan is a contemporary artist whose work has been exhibited in London. Her website records participation in the FLUX Exhibition in London in 2023, an exhibition involving dozens of contemporary artists [ref: Biography, lubnaspeitan].

In December 2025, she held what her website described as her “final studio exhibition” at Thames-Side Studios in Woolwich. The exhibition presented remaining works from her artistic career, with proceeds intended to support her campaigning through the Greenwich Palestine Alliance and Trade Unionists for Palestine.
==References==

The first of a two-part adaptation of the 1986 novel, as well as the second adaptation following the 1990 miniseries. Gaetan Algoet

Gaetan Algoet (born 7 January 1964) is a Belgian author and maritime researcher known for his work on historical shipwrecks, piracy, and geographical reconstructions. His work is based on early historical and mythological sources. He has published works in Dutch, English, German, and French. He is active as an independent researcher based in Belgium.

== Biography ==
Algoet was born in Germany. He worked for the Belgian Air Force. He is also certified Dive Master.

His interest in maritime research began in the Dominican Republic, where he met Czech marine archaeologist Lubos Kordac. He invited Algoet to conduct archival research on the French shipwreck La Viette with the American organization North Caribbean Research (NCR). This led to their first collaborative publication.

In 2009, Algoet made his debut as an author in cooperation with Lubos Kordac. Their book Verborgen en verloren schatten in de Dominicaanse Republiek was published in 2010 by Free Musketeers.

Over the following years, Algoet published through various Dutch and Belgian publishers before establishing his own imprint, Algoet Publishing. His works cover maritime history, piracy, and historical geography, including studies on Hispaniola, the Spanish Plate Fleet, and medieval legends.

In 2026, Algoet received regional media attention for his independent geographical reconstruction of the location of Avalon. This is a legendary island described in medieval chronicles. His findings were featured by the Belgian regional broadcaster ROBtv. [ref: ROBtv. "Locatie van mythisch eiland Avalon na 1500 jaar gevonden door Gaetan Algoet uit Begijnendijk." 2025. https://www.robtv.be/nieuws/locatie-van-mythisch-eiland-avalon-na-1500-jaar-gevonden-door-gaetan-algoet-uit-begijnendijk-chatgpt-geeft-mij-98-tot-99-procent-kans-204211]

== Works ==
=== Dutch-language works ===

* Verborgen en verloren schatten in de Dominicaanse Republiek (2010, with Lubos Kordac)
* Avalon onthuld – Het verloren Koninkrijk
* De Rode Piraat
* De grootste kaperbuit aller tijden - Piet Heyn en de Zilvervloot (2026)
* Amerika onthuld
* Historische scheepswrakken rond Hispaniola
* Tussen Velt en Bergh: 200 jaar verbonden
* Het Piratenleven Onthuld (three-volume series)
* De Slag in de Baai van Maimón
* Het geheim van de broederschap

=== International editions ===

* A Hundred Giants: The French Huguenot Experience in Florida: 1562–1565 (2018, with T. L. Armstrong and R. H. Baer Florida: Signum Ops)
* Avalon Revealed – The Lost Kingdom
* Avalon enthüllt – Das verlorene Königreich
* Avalon Révélé – Le Royaume Perdu
* The Pirate Life Revealed – 17th Century
* The Pirate Life Revealed – 18th Century
* Battle in Maimon Bay
* Piet Heyn (2026 Florida: Signum Ops)

== Reception ==
Algoet’s archival research on historical shipwrecks, including the Nuestra Señora de la Concepción, is cited on the English Wikipedia in the articles San Miguel (1551 shipwreck) and List of shipwrecks in the 16th century.

His research was referenced in the Brazilian historical study A Profundeza Do Mar Azul (2020) by historian and archaeologist Dalton Delfini Maziero. He cited Algoet’s work on early colonial shipwrecks. [ref: Maziero, Dalton Delfini. A Profundeza Do Mar Azul. Google Books. https://www.google.be/books/edition/A_Profundeza_Do_Mar_Azul/f5r7DwAAQBAJ?hl=nl&gbpv=1&dq=Ga%C3%ABtan+Algoet&pg=PT91&printsec=frontcover]

Algoet is listed as a contributing author by Field Manor, a historical museum in Florida, which highlights his co-authorship of A Hundred Giants: The French Huguenot Experience in Florida: 1562–1565. [ref: Field Manor Museum. "The Ais People." https://www.fieldmanor.org/the-ais-people]

He is also included on the Signum Ops Authors Page, an American platform documenting contributors to historical and archaeological publications. [ref: Signum Ops. "Authors Page." http://www.signumops.com/authors.html]

A maritime researcher on the TreasureNet forum described Algoet as “a marine archaeologist and very reliable man,” noting his expertise in early Dutch script and archival interpretation. [ref: TreasureNet Forum. "Any early Dutch script experts here?" https://www.treasurenet.com/threads/any-early-dutch-script-experts-here.162427/]

Standaard Boekhandel, a major Belgian bookseller, published a redactional description of Algoet’s book Avalon onthuld – Het verloren Koninkrijk, summarizing his methodology and referencing regional media coverage. [ref: Standaard Boekhandel. "Avalon onthuld – Het verloren Koninkrijk." https://www.standaardboekhandel.be/p/avalon-onthuld-9789403850023]

== External links ==

Robert Van Gulick is a philosopher and professor of philosophy at Syracuse University. [ref: Robert Van Gulick, Syracuse University College of Arts and Sciences] His work is primarily in the philosophy of mind and philosophy of cognitive science, particularly consciousness, self-awareness and functionalism. [ref: Robert N. Van Gulick Curriculum Vitae, Syracuse University College of Arts and Sciences]

Van Gulick is associated with the Higher-Order Global States (HOGS) model of consciousness, which combines elements of higher-order and global-state approaches to conscious awareness. [ref: Higher-Order Theories of Consciousness] [ref: Consciousness] The model has subsequently been discussed in academic literature on higher-order and self-representational theories of consciousness. [ref: Same old, same old: the same-order representation theory of consciousness and the division of phenomenal labor, Synthese] [ref: Phenomenal consciousness with infallible self-representation, Philosophical Studies] [ref: The Oxford Handbook of the Philosophy of Consciousness, Oxford University Press]

== Education and career ==

Van Gulick received an A.B. in philosophy from Princeton University in 1970. He earned an M.A. in 1973 and a Ph.D. in philosophy in 1976 from the University of California, Berkeley. His dissertation was titled Functionalism as a Theory of Mind.

He taught at Rutgers University from 1976 to 1984 and joined Syracuse University in 1984. He became a professor of philosophy at Syracuse in 1995. From 2008 to 2010, he held Syracuse's William P. Tolley Distinguished Teaching Professorship in the Humanities. [ref: William P. Tolley Distinguished Teaching Professor in the Humanities, Syracuse University College of Arts and Sciences]

Van Gulick served as president of the Society for Philosophy and Psychology in 2002. [ref: Past Officers, Society for Philosophy and Psychology]

== Philosophical work ==

Van Gulick has written on consciousness, self-awareness, functionalism, intentionality, emergence and the relationship between phenomenal experience and cognitive organization.

=== Higher-Order Global States ===

Van Gulick developed the Higher-Order Global States model as an account of the relationship between consciousness and higher-order awareness. In contrast to standard higher-order accounts that posit a distinct higher-order representation of a lower-order mental state, HOGS treats the relevant higher-order content as arising within the organization of a larger global state.

The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy interprets Van Gulick's account as one in which globally available first-order states acquire a higher-order dimension through their incorporation into representations of the self and its relationship to the environment. It also notes some ambiguity in the theory concerning the precise relationship between the original first-order state and the resulting higher-order global state.

The HOGS model has been discussed in subsequent work on higher-order and self-representational theories of consciousness. Josh Weisberg examined the model in Synthese as a form of same-order representation theory and considered its combination of global availability and self-awareness. Chad Kidd considered HOGS alongside other self-representational models in Philosophical Studies, including whether its account of integrated conscious states addresses problems involving self-misrepresentation.

Tom McClelland discusses HOGS in The Oxford Handbook of the Philosophy of Consciousness, situating it within self-representational theories and describing the role that integration into a subject's broader mental economy plays in the account. Later authors have continued to compare aspects of HOGS with alternative accounts of higher-order representation and self-consciousness. [ref: Quotational higher-order thought theory, Philosophical Studies] [ref: Pre-Reflective Self-Consciousness: A Meta-Causal Approach, Review of Philosophy and Psychology]

Van Gulick later connected HOGS with Global Neuronal Workspace theory. In an editorial introducing a 2022 special issue on self-consciousness, Stefan Lang and Klaus Viertbauer describe his contribution as combining HOGS with the Global Neuronal Workspace framework and developing a virtual-self integration account of the conscious subject. [ref: Editorial: Self-Consciousness Explained—Mapping the Field, Review of Philosophy and Psychology]

J. M. Barrie and the Lost Boys (also published as J. M. Barrie & the Lost Boys: The Real Story Behind Peter Pan) is a 1979 biographical work by British writer and filmmaker Andrew Birkin, researched by Birkin and Sharon Goode, examining the relationship between J. M. Barrie, creator of Peter Pan, and the five sons of Arthur and Sylvia Llewelyn Davies, who inspired the character. The book grew out of Birkin's research for The Lost Boys (1978), his three-part BBC docudrama on the same subject.

== Background ==
Birkin first explored Barrie's relationship with the Llewelyn Davies family in The Lost Boys, a three-part BBC drama he wrote, broadcast in October 1978 and starring Ian Holm as Barrie. Drawing on the extensive research undertaken for that production — including Barrie's private notebooks, family letters and diaries, and recorded interviews with surviving members of the family and their circle — Birkin expanded the material into a full-length documentary biography, published the following year.

== Synopsis ==
The book traces Barrie's growing closeness to the Davies boys — George, Jack, Peter, Michael and Nico — from their first meetings in Kensington Gardens through Barrie's eventual role as their guardian following the deaths of both parents. Structured around primary documents and photographs reproduced alongside the narrative, it follows the family's story to the deaths in adulthood of three of the five brothers, and the shadow these cast retrospectively over the creation of Peter Pan.

== Publication history ==
The book was first published in the United Kingdom by Constable in 1979, and in the United States by Crown Publishers. Birkin later assigned his rights in the work to the Great Ormond Street Hospital Children's Charity, which holds the copyright to Peter Pan. A revised edition, with a new preface and additional illustrations, was published by Yale University Press in 2003, to coincide with the centenary of Peter Pan.

== Critical reception ==
The book received widespread critical praise on publication and on its 2003 reissue. In Time, Gerald Clarke's review, headlined "The Lost Man", called it "one of the year's most complex and absorbing biographies", [ref: The Lost Man, [[Time (magazine)] while Eve Auchincloss, writing in The Washington Post, described it as "a terrible and fascinating story". [ref: Review of J. M. Barrie and the Lost Boys, The Washington Post] In his review "Barrie, poet of death" for The Listener, the author Ronald Blythe called the book "a lesson in revelations. Having created one of television's masterpieces, The Lost Boys, Andrew Birkin follows it up, not with the now customary book of the programme, but with its documentation set out in another form but with an equally compelling artistry. It is indicative of the author's creative use of restraint that this astonishing history justifies his claim of 'love story' from beginning to end." [ref: Barrie, poet of death, The Listener] Blythe later nominated the book in The Guardian as being "my most unforgettable read of the year." [ref: Books of the Year, The Guardian] The writer and director Caroline Thompson wrote in the Los Angeles Times that "this stunningly constructed biography is a story of obsession and the search for pure childhood; touching, moving, charming, a revelation." [ref: Review of J. M. Barrie and the Lost Boys, Los Angeles Times] The Oxford Companion to Children's Literature calls it "the most candid and perceptive biography to have been written of Barrie". [ref: The Oxford Companion to Children's Literature, Oxford University Press] Writing privately to Nico Llewelyn Davies on 13 June 1979, the editor and biographer Rupert Hart-Davis called it "unquestionably the best book on the subject, and unlikely ever to be surpassed." [ref: Letter from Rupert Hart-Davis to Nico Llewelyn Davies, 13 June 1979, reproduced in facsimile at [https://www.jmbarrie.co.uk jmbarrie.co.uk].]

SpenDoe is an American hip-hop artist from Santa Cruz, California. His music draws on West Coast hip hop, including the Bay Area-derived mob music style. [ref: Spotlight On: SpenDoe, Crooked Forest] He has also released music under the name M. Aundre. [ref: Meet M. Aundre, Bold Journey]

== Career ==
In December 2006, the BBC Asian Network included SpenDoe's song "Unforgettable" in "Friction's Top Five" on Bobby Friction's program; the surviving page lists the song second. [ref: Friction's Top Five, BBC Asian Network] The song also appeared on the network's The Hype Show playlist in February 2007. [ref: The Hype Show playlist, BBC Asian Network]

In September 2019, SpenDoe was featured on the cover and interviewed in the first issue of 41510 Magazine. [ref: SpenDoe, 41510 Magazine] In 2020, the California Black Media article "A Deadly Mix: Hip Hop Mashed Up With Opioid Abuse in California" noted his collaboration with Sacramento rapper Mozzy on "Omertà". [ref: A Deadly Mix: Hip Hop Mashed Up With Opioid Abuse in California, The Observer]

During 2021, several music publications reviewed SpenDoe's singles. We Write About Music discussed the acoustic-guitar opening, bass, synthesizers and vocal delivery of "Foreign to Me", while Australian publication Stimulate Your Soul characterized it as combining a West Coast sound with Mediterranean-influenced instrumentation. [ref: California Artist SpenDoe Drops Fresh New Single 'Foreign To Me', Stimulate Your Soul] Italian publication Indie Italia and French publication Indie Chronique reviewed "Changing Lanes", describing its forceful flow and mixture of old-school hip-hop, funk and groove. [ref: SpenDoe 'Changing Lanes' - A testa alta, Indie Italia] [ref: Entre vrai hip-hop et groove avec SpenDoe, Indie Chronique]

SpenDoe and Sacramento rapper-producer C-DUBB released the collaborative project Professional Mobbin: The Cali Way. In 2022, Crooked Forest published an interview with SpenDoe centered on "To the Top", his collaboration with producer Sureet Sandhu and his West Coast influences.

Under the M. Aundre name, he released "Altered State" in 2023. Writing for EARMILK, Malvika Padin characterized the song as nostalgic, West Coast-influenced hip hop with introspective lyrics. [ref: M. Aundre makes a strong impact with debut single 'Altered State', EARMILK]

SpenDoe performed at the 2023 Juneteenth celebration in Drake Park in Bend, Oregon; The Bulletin used a photograph of his performance as the lead image in its coverage of the event. [ref: Juneteenth celebrated in Bend with photos, festival and memories, The Bulletin] In October 2023, he released the five-track West Coast EP, produced primarily by C-DUBB with an additional contribution from Vallejo producer the Slapmaster. Lyrics & Threads described the project as drawing from the Bay Area mob-music tradition and highlighted the reflective writing and relaxed delivery of "Rollin Up". [ref: SpenDoe Takes Us on a West Coast Journey with "WEST COAST" EP, Lyrics & Threads] That year, SpenDoe also appeared on "Official", from San Quinn and C-DUBB's collaborative album The Mob Hour Continues, opening the song's first verse. [ref: Official – San Quinn, C-DUBB, SpenDoe, Russell Falcon, Folded Waffle]

In 2024, French music publication Extravafrench reviewed "C.O.A.", a C-DUBB-produced track from Name 100, describing its bass-heavy trap production as drawing on the 1990s Bay Area mob-music tradition and emphasizing ambition and perseverance. [ref: L'Éclat d'un Artiste Entre Hustle et Floss: voici SpenDoe sur « C.O.A. », Extravafrench] Last Day Deaf subsequently reviewed the EP. [ref: Listening Now: SpenDoe - Name 100, Last Day Deaf]

Coverage of the Name 100 single "Smiles and Cries" appeared in PopFad, The Urban Juice, Korliblog, and LandonBuford.com. The reviews discussed its synth-driven production and themes of adversity, resilience and the contrasting experiences of life. [ref: A Brand New Release by Violet Jane and Another Single to Explore, PopFad] [ref: Santa Cruz Rapper Spendoe Explores Life's Duality in New Single 'Smiles and Cries', The Urban Juice] [ref: Hip-Hop's Hidden Gem: SpenDoe's 'Smiles and Cries' Single Review, Korliblog] [ref: SpenDoe reflects on life's highs and lows in 'Smiles and Cries', LandonBuford.com]

In May 2025, Sway's Universe selected "Name 100" for its weekly SU SoundWave feature, identifying SpenDoe as an independent Santa Cruz artist and discussing the track's West Coast production by C-DUBB. [ref: SU SoundWave Picks of the Week: Kevin McGee, SpenDoe, Maliibu Miitch and More, Sway's Universe]

In 2026, SpenDoe appeared on Day Day's "From the Bay", from the album My Elevation (M.E.). The track was produced by Funk Daddy. [ref: Day Day Drops "From the Bay" from New Album My Elevation (M.E.), The Urban Juice] [ref: North Cali's Finest: Day Day and SpenDoe Rep the Culture in "From the Bay", Fenomen Mag] World Wide Hip Hop credited SpenDoe as the album's executive producer. [ref: West Coast Rap Artist Day Day Releases New Album "My Elevation (M.E.)", World Wide Hip Hop]

Robyn Dixon (née Bragg; born March 31, 1979) is an American television personality, real estate agent, and entrepreneur. She is best known as an original cast member of the Bravo reality television series The Real Housewives of Potomac, which premiered in 2016. Dixon is also the co-host of the podcast Reasonably Shady with fellow Real Housewives of Potomac cast member Gizelle Bryant. She was previously married to former professional basketball player Juan Dixon, with whom she has two sons.

== Early life and education ==
Robyn Dixon was born Robyn Bragg in Baltimore, Maryland to parents Gladys and Guy Bragg. [ref: Who is Robyn Dixon? The Potomac 'Wife is Keeping Her Family Together, Bravo] She attended the University of Maryland, College Park, where she graduated with a bachelor’s degree in business administration in 2000. While in high school, she met basketball player Juan Dixon when his team played against her school. They began dating in 1996. [ref: ‘Real Housewives of Potomac’ Star Robyn Dixon and Juan Dixon’s Relationship Timeline: From High School Sweethearts to Rekindling Their Romance, Us]

== Career ==

=== Public Relations ===
Dixon began her career in public relations, working as a publicist and event manager for TAA PR, a Washington, D.C.-based public relations, marketing, and special events firm specializing in luxury lifestyle, fashion, and hospitality. [ref: Who Is Robyn Dixon? The 'Real Housewives Of Potomac' Star Is A Power PR Player, Bustle] She later served as the lead publicist for GLO30, a skincare company based in the Washington, D.C., area. [ref: Class Notes, Terp Magazine] [ref: Robyn Dixon’s latest corporate venture? A facial business in Howard Co., The Banner]

=== Real Estate ===
Dixon entered real estate investing with her mother, Gladys Bragg. [ref: RHOP Star Robyn Dixon Wants More Black Women To Invest In Real Estate, BAUCE] Bragg initially worked in real estate wholesaling, and after completing several wholesale deals, the pair began rehabbing properties. Dixon described their first rehabilitation project in an interview as a learning experience. In 2017, the two began renovating properties for resale with guidance from real estate investor Marcel Umphery. [ref: Robyn Dixon Just Revealed the (Not So) Glamorous Life of a House Flipper, Bravo] Their first renovation project was featured on The Real Housewives of Potomac during its third and fourth seasons. [ref: RHOP's Gizelle Bryant Apologizes to Robyn Dixon for Open House Fight: 'I Really Messed Up', People] Dixon and Bragg subsequently sold the property for a profit of more than $30,000. [ref: Robyn Dixon Reveals She Sold Her Flip House… and Made a Tidy Profit, Bravo]

=== She is Empowered ===

In 2017, Dixon founded She Is Empowered, a women’s entrepreneurship and professional development initiative that was part of the Visionary Events Group. [ref: Every Single One of Robyn Dixon's Business Ventures in Her Growing Empire, Bravo] The initiative hosted seminars and events in the Washington, D.C., area focused on entrepreneurship and developing multiple sources of income.

=== Embellished ===

In 2020, Dixon launched Embellished, an accessories and apparel brand featuring satin-lined baseball caps, graphic T-shirts, hoodies and masks. [ref: Here's Why Robyn Dixon's Embellished Hat Line Is So Good, Bravo] The satin lining was designed to protect hair from breakage. [ref: Satin lined fashion caps by Robyn Dixon, Embellished] The business was featured during the fifth season of The Real Housewives of Potomac, including an October 2020 episode in which Dixon presented the line. Following the episode’s airing, Dixon said the response was greater than anticipated, and the collection sold out. [ref: Robyn Dixon Shares "Amazing" News About Her Embellished Hat Line, Bravo] She subsequently expanded Embellished’s headwear offerings to include satin-lined ribbed beanies. [ref: Robyn Dixon Just Shared a Very Exciting Update on Her Embellished Hat Line, Bravo]

=== Television ===

==== The Real Housewives of Potomac ====

Dixon joined the Bravo reality television series The Real Housewives of Potomac as an original cast member when the series premiered in January 2016. [ref: ‘The Real Housewives’ Franchise Heads To Maryland And Texas, Deadline] [ref: Bravo Plots ‘Real Housewives’ Franchise Expansion for 2016, The Hollywood Reporter] Her early storylines centered on her relationship with former NBA player Juan Dixon, whom she had divorced but continued to live with while raising their two sons. [ref: ‘The Real Housewives of Potomac’: TV Review, The Hollywood Reporter] [ref: 'Real Housewives of Potomac' premiere react: Meet Bravo's latest big, bold personalities..., Entertainment Weekly] During the series, the couple reconciled and became engaged for a second time in the fifth season. [ref: Love Is in the Air: All of the Celebrity Engagements of 2019, People] They married in a private ceremony in Maryland in August 2022, with their sons and Robyn’s parents in attendance; the wedding was featured in the seventh season finale. [ref: Robyn Dixon and Juan Dixon Are Married Again! RHOP to Air Surprise Wedding in Season 7 Finale, People]

Phigros is a rhythm game developed and published by Pigeon Games. Phigros was initially released to the public globally in August 8, 2019. [ref: Phigros 开发者Q&A - Phigros综合讨论 - TapTap Phigros论坛, www.taptap.cn] In February 24, 2023, the official Bilibili account announced that the game had surpassed 10 million downloads. [ref: Phigros官方的动态]

== Gameplay ==
[[File:XING,and_Muse_Dash_collab_with_Phigros.jpg|left|thumb|The IN chart for the song XING simulates the gameplay of Muse Dash.]]
Phigros features several chart difficulties. All songs have Easy (EZ), Hard (HD), and Insane (IN) difficulties, while Another (AT) is available for some selected songs. Legacy charts consist of older versions of certain charts, while Special (SP) charts are used for certain hidden or event charts. [ref: Phigrosの評価とアプリ情報 - ゲーム一覧, GAMEWITH] During gameplay, notes approach judgement lines that can move, rotate, change opacity, or otherwise change position. There are four types of notes: Tap, Hold, Drag, and Flick, each requiring a different input when reaching the judgement line. [ref: 日常安利《Phigros》非定型音游~不安分的判定线, 3DMGAME] [ref: Phigrosの評価とアプリ情報 - ゲーム一覧, GAMEWITH]

Notes are judged as Perfect, Good, Bad, or Miss according to the timing of the player's input. Perfect or Good judgements increase the player's combo, while Bad or Miss judgements break it. [ref: Phigrosの評価とアプリ情報 - ゲーム一覧, GAMEWITH] The player's score is calculated from both their accuracy and their highest achieved combo. At the end of a play, the game displays the player's score, accuracy, judgement counts, highest combo, and a grade based on their score. [ref: Phigrosの評価とアプリ情報 - ゲーム一覧, GAMEWITH]

Unlike many rhythm games, Phigros features a dynamic judgement line and does not use fixed lanes. During gameplay, the judgement line can move, rotate, or disappear, requiring players to follow its position as notes approach it. The movement of the judgement line can also be incorporated into chart patterns and visual effects. [ref: 日常安利《Phigros》非定型音游~不安分的判定线, 3DMGAME] [ref: 「Phigros」官方宣传PV, bilibili]

== Development and publishing ==
Development of Phigros was started by Soullies, who was a teenager at the time. [ref: 因为“五块钱”捐款，一款免费发布且更新数年的独立游戏，被部分玩家冲了……, 搜狐] He subsequently assembled a team of rhythm game enthusiasts, which became Pigeon Games and continued development of the game. Pigeon Games distributes the game's songs without charging players individually for them and has released regular updates since the game's launch. [ref: 无广告又无内购！这款良心爆表的音游，却被玩家调侃为“屁股肉”……, 搜狐] The game has also released special charts for April Fools' Day.

The game's soundtrack primarily consists of electronic music and features compositions by numerous artists. These include composers who have participated in the BMS music competition The BMS of Fighters, as well as artists and labels such as SOUL NOTES. Phigros has also featured collaborations with other rhythm games, like Muse Dash. [ref: TGIF my friend. Drop everything you’re doing and get the new update!, Steam] Some charts incorporate references to their source material.

== Reception and community ==
Phigros has attracted a niche but active community. Following its release, the game appeared prominently on TapTap's "Hottest" rankings, and users on Bilibili have produced content featuring the game.

Reviews have highlighted the game's level design and its use of unconventional gameplay elements. Reviewers have praised the changes in gameplay and chart design for adding variety and surprise to individual songs. [ref: Phigrosをじっくり遊んで徹底レビュー！, スマホゲームCH] Other reviews have criticized the movement of gameplay elements for making charts more difficult to read and increasing their difficulty. [ref: [好游推荐] 快看，线条与指尖之舞, TapTap]

The game's visual presentation has also received attention. Reviews have praised its illustrations and their relationship to the themes of individual songs and charts. The soundtrack has similarly been highlighted for its variety and emphasis on electronic music.

The game's free-to-play model has also been discussed by reviewers. Some have described its lack of paid access to individual songs as lowering the barrier to entry, while other discussion has focused on the game's level-unlocking system. Some players regard unlocking charts as providing a sense of progression, while others have criticized it as limiting player choice.

Phigros's visual effects and interface have also influenced user-generated content on short-video platforms. In 2024, 36Kr reported on the use of effects inspired by Phigros in "beat-synced dance" videos on Douyin. [ref: 全网爆火的“卡点舞”，抖音竟然不是最大赢家？, 36Kr]

==Production==
Marc du Pontavice first read Listen to the Moon in 2017, when he was having a drink with an artist Xilam collaborated with, and he recommended it to du Pontavice [ref: 'Lucy Lost' Producer & Director Share the Secrets of Their Magical Animated Mystery (Exclusive First Look), Animation Magazine] and that he thought the "themes of family, love and memory against a backdrop of vivid landscapes, would translate beautifully to the screen". [ref: What we're watching at MIPTV, Kidscreen] After meeting Olivier Clert in 2022, he convinced him to make it into a theatrical movie instead, by deciding that they would tell Lucy's story and by uniting the different narrative strands of the book by bringing Milly, who exists in another plot of the novel, directly into the Lucy's world, which du Pontavice really liked, where Clert developed it by creating a complete storyboard, editing it with voice acting and music, making it look like a movie. [ref: How Olivier Clert's Storyboarding Instincts Cracked Xilam's 'Impossible' 'Lucy Lost' Adaptation, Cartoon Brew] Clert joined the project later, after seeing some early visual materials at Xilam, as he was drawn to their timeless quality. Originally, he was only going to contribute as a storyboard artist, but he soon became more deeply involved in developing the story.

Border (; also known as Bian jing) is a 2026 Mandarin- and Mongolian-language drama film written and directed by Ah Biao in his feature debut. [ref: San Sebastian Competition Title 'Border' Boards Reel Suspects for Global Sales, [[Variety (magazine)] [ref: Ah Biao, Fred Cavayé, Jesse Eisenberg, Amanda Kernell, Gabriel Martins and Tony Vahl also to compete for the Golden Shell, San Sebastián International Film Festival] [ref: Bian jing / Border, San Sebastián International Film Festival] The film stars Zheyan Li, Feng Qi, Han Sanming, Gang Zheng and Tao Guo.

According to the official poster billing block, the film was produced by Jenny Man Wu, with Lili Tong, Tyler Hill and Xue Ma as producers, and Yaohua LI (also credited as LI Yaohua; Chinese: 李要华), Jing Yang and Hao Zhou as co-producers; Dongmei Li, Nan Xin and Ning Wu are credited as associate producers. [ref: Borderless Films, official poster billing block for Border.]

Produced by Borderless Films as a Hong Kong–United States–South Korea co-production, Border was selected for the Official Selection of the 74th San Sebastián International Film Festival, where it had its world premiere and won the festival's Special Jury Prize. [ref: San Sebastian Adds Jesse Eisenberg, Fred Cavayé, Amanda Kernell Films to Golden Shell Race, [[Variety (magazine)] [ref: Jesse Eisenberg & 'Les Misérables' Added To San Sebastián Competition, [[Deadline Hollywood] [ref: San Sebastián: Mike Leigh's 'Tender Loving Care' Wins Golden Shell & Best Screenplay, [[Deadline Hollywood] [ref: 'Tender Loving Care', by Mike Leigh, carries off the Golden Shell at the San Sebastián Festival's 74th edition, San Sebastián International Film Festival] Paris-based sales company Reel Suspects handles worldwide sales.

==Plot==
In a forgotten town where men keep their feelings buried and speak little, a broke young miner drifts through a numb routine. His life is disrupted by the arrival of an enigmatic young woman, who awakens a dormant curiosity. He follows her onto a darker path, leaving behind the only world he knows, unaware that she is not who she appears to be.

The 2026–27 Utah State Aggies men's basketball team will represent Utah State University during the 2026–27 NCAA Division I men's basketball season. The Aggies will be led by first-year head coach Ben Jacobson and will play their home games at the Smith Spectrum in Logan, Utah as a member of the Pac-12 Conference. This will mark Utah State's first season as members of the Pac-12 Conference after spending the previous thirteen seasons as members of the Mountain West Conference. [ref: After nearly two years of waiting, Utah State's Pac-12 era begins, The Herald Journal] [ref: Utah State officially begins Pac-12 era, ABC4 Utah (KTVX)] [ref: Utah State celebrates its new era of Pac-12 membership, Deseret News]

==Previous season==
Utah State finished the 2025-26 season 29–7, 15–5 in the Mountain West Conference to finish first in the conference. As the top seed in the Mountain West Tournament they would defeat 8-seed UNLV in the Quarterfinals and 5-seed Nevada in the Semifinals to advance to the Championship against 2-seed San Diego State. The Aggies defeated the Aztecs 73-62 to win claim the tournament championship. [ref: SDSU busts in Mountain West championship, falling to No. 1-seed Utah State, The Daily Aztec] [ref: Utah State beats San Diego State to win the Mountain West tournament title, Deseret News] As a result, they received the conference's autobid to the NCAA Tournament as the 9-seed in the West region. [ref: Arizona withstands Utah State comeback to reach Sweet 16 Utah State proves its toughness in Round of 32 loss to Arizona, KSL Sports] [ref: Bradley scores 18 points to lead No. 1-seeded Arizona past Utah State 78-66 to reach Sweet 16, AP News]

Two days after the season's conclusion, head coach Jerrod Calhoun left to take the same position at his alma mater, Cincinnati. [ref: Cincinnati hires Jerrod Calhoun: Utah State coach leaving after two years to guide his alma mater, CBS Sports] [ref: Utah State's Jerrod Calhoun returns to Cincinnati as coach, www.espn.com] On March 30, 2026, the school named Northern Iowa head coach Ben Jacobson as the team's new head coach. Hygglo is Swedish Peer-to-peer rental marketplace for individuals to rent various items from each other. It was founded in Stockholm in 2016 by Ola Degerfors, Axel Hellström and Henrik Fräsén. Hygglo vill få folk att hyra grejer – nu ökar de efter uppköp: “Har lång väg kvar”, Impact Loop

Hygglo is part of the Sharing economy and has been used in many case studies in academic research regarding the environmental and social effects of peer-to-peer sharing. [ref: Assessing the Environmental Potential of Collaborative Consumption: Peer-to-Peer Product Sharing in Hammarby Sjöstad, Sweden, Sustainability] [ref: Ethics and Sustainability in Digital Cultures, Routledge]

== History ==
Hygglo was founded in Stockholm in 2016.

In 2019 and 2020, Hygglo was included in Swedish technology publication ‘’Computer Sweden’’s Topp100 selection of Swedish websites and online services. The service was included in the sustainability category in 2019 and the sharing-services category in 2020. [ref: Topp100 2019: Här är Sveriges 100 bästa sajter och nättjänster, Computer Sweden] [ref: Topp100 2020: Här är Sveriges 100 bästa sajter och nättjänster, Computer Sweden]

In 2022, Hygglo acquired British competitor Fat Llama. [ref: ‘A cricket bat to the face’: The story of one startup’s ‘gruelling’ road to acquisition, Sifted] [ref: Swedish Hygglo fattens peer-to-peer rental portfolio with Fat Llama buy for $41.5 million, Tech.eu]

== Academic research ==
Hygglo has been part of a case study in research examining both the environmental and social effects of the sharing economy.

A 2019 peer-reviewed study by Michael Martin, David Lazarevic and Charlie Gullström, published in the journal ‘‘Sustainability’’, investigated peer-to-peer sharing using transaction data from Hygglo in Hammarby Sjöstad, Stockholm. The authors researched the environmental effects of sharing consumer items compared with scenarios in which products would be purchased instead. The study found that product sharing reduces co2 emissions in the scenarios examined, main due to a reduced need for additional manufactured products.

Hygglo was also used as a case study by researchers Per Fors and Tina Ringenson in a book chapter examining the relationship between the sharing economy, social sustainability and local communities. The researchers examined how peer-to-peer sharing platforms could affect relationships between people in local communities. They discussed the potential for such platforms to strengthen local social connections while also considering limitations related to factors including user homogeneity and residential segregation in Stockholm.

In 2026, ‘’The Washington Post’’ discussed Hygglo as part of a examination of peer-to-peer sharing and community-based alternatives to purchasing consumer goods. The reporter used Hygglo while researching the challenges associated with sharing items between individuals. [ref: I wanted to buy less stuff. I ended up bonding with my neighbors., The Washington Post]

The market is located near the Mayiladuthurai junction approximately from the coast in Mayiladuthurai district. The market operates as a weekly market on Tuesdays and Sundays. [ref: மவுசு குறையாத மயிலாடுதுறை கருவாட்டுச் சந்தை, கட்டுரை] [ref: Decades-old dry fish market in Mayiladuthurai lacks basic amenities, The Hindu] [ref: 100 ஆண்டுகள் பழமைமிக்க சித்தர்காடு கருவாட்டுச்சந்தை: 60 நாட்களுக்குப் பின் திறப்பு, ETV Bharat News] [ref: தமிழகத்தின் முதல் கருவாட்டு சந்தை..! நூற்றாண்டு கடந்த மயிலாடுதுறை மண்ணின் அடையாளம்..!] [ref: தமிழகம் கண்ட முதல் பிரமாண்ட கருவாட்டுச் சந்தை - இது மயிலாடுதுறை மண்ணின் அடையாளம்! #MyVikatan, www.vikatan.com/]

Teneo Online School (also trading internationally as Teneo International School) is a British international online school headquartered in London, England, delivering Pearson Edexcel qualifications to learners aged 11 to 19. The school operates entirely online, with no physical campus, and serves families across the United Kingdom, South Africa, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Hong Kong, Qatar, Kenya, Nigeria, and other countries.

== History ==
Teneo Online School was founded by Saul Geffen, who also developed the school's proprietary Smart School System. The school initially focused on the South African market, operating at teneoschool.co.za, before expanding internationally under the brand Teneo International School at teneoschool.com. The school offers curriculum pathways aligned to South African qualifications including CAPS and IEB, as well as the Pearson Edexcel British International curriculum.

== Curriculum and qualifications ==
Teneo delivers the Pearson Edexcel British International curriculum from Key Stage 3 (Years 7–9) through to International GCSEs (Years 10–11) and International AS and A Levels (Years 12–13). Pearson Edexcel International Advanced Level qualifications are recognised for entry by more than 1,000 universities worldwide, including institutions in the United Kingdom, North America, Asia, and the Middle East. [ref: Teneo Online School offers global families more than ever, GlobeNewswire]

In South Africa, the school additionally offers the Curriculum and Assessment Policy Statement (CAPS), the Independent Examinations Board (IEB) pathway, and the South African Comprehensive Assessment Institute (SACAI) Matric pathway. Students sit final examinations in person at approved examination centres. Teneo holds Pearson Edexcel Centre Number 94897.

== Smart School System ==
The Smart School System is Teneo's proprietary learning platform developed by founder Saul Geffen. The system combines live teaching, real-time analytics, behavioural science, and artificial intelligence to monitor learner engagement and academic progress, generating alerts when a learner's engagement changes so that teachers can intervene early.

== Research and public interest work ==

=== School safety ===
In 2026, Teneo International School submitted Freedom of Information requests to police forces across the United Kingdom, seeking data on sexual offences recorded at school premises over three years. Of 35 forces contacted, 19 were able to provide offence data. The data showed that reported sexual offences at schools rose from 1,789 to 2,066 over the period, an increase of more than 15 per cent. The sharpest rises were recorded in Nottinghamshire (50 per cent), Devon and Cornwall (49 per cent), and Greater Manchester (31 per cent). Several forces, including the Metropolitan Police and West Yorkshire, cited the cost of retrieving the data as a reason for not responding. [ref: Sexual offence reports at schools up by more than 15 per cent over three years, Daily Mirror]

Taryn Jankes, Chief Marketing Officer of Teneo International School, told the Daily Mirror that a rise in reported offences did not necessarily mean more offences were taking place, and that increased reporting could reflect stronger safeguarding culture and greater willingness among young people to come forward.

=== Matric study resources ===
In September 2026, Tracey Clayton, Phase Head at Teneo Online School, was quoted in The Citizen regarding free study resources available to South African matric pupils. Clayton recommended past papers published by the Department of Basic Education, free platforms including Siyavula and Khan Academy, and small study groups as alternatives to private tutoring. She noted that while free educational material had narrowed the gap between learners who could afford additional academic support and those who could not, access to a device, data, and a suitable study environment remained barriers for many families. [ref: Writing matric? Here's where to find free study tools, The Citizen]

== Recognition ==
In 2026, Teneo was named a finalist in the Trendsetter Awards' Product or Service Setting a Trend category at The EdTech Awards 2026, the world's largest awards programme for education technology presented by EdTech Digest. Saul Geffen was simultaneously named a finalist in the School Leader category. [ref: Teneo International School Named a Global Finalist in the World's Largest EdTech Awards, GlobeNewswire]

Also in 2026, Teneo received the Educational Establishment of the Year award at the Education Resources Awards.

== Delivery model ==
Teneo operates through three delivery formats: live online lessons taught in real time, a hybrid model combining live and recorded sessions, and a fully recorded format. All live sessions are recorded and made permanently available for revision and catch-up. The school reports having educated more than 20,000 learners and produced over 4,000 graduates.

Klarita Gërxhani is an Albanian-Dutch interdisciplinary economist. She is Professor of Behavioral Socio-Economics at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (VU Amsterdam) School of Business and Economics, where she serves as Associate Dean of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion. [ref: prof. dr. Klarita Gërxhani, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam] She is a lifelong member of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) and holds the title of Knight of the Order of the Academic Oak, a state decoration conferred by the President of the Republic of Albania in April 2026. [ref: Academy selects 17 new members, Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]

== Early life and education ==
Gërxhani began her academic studies in Tirana, Albania, where she completed an M.A. at the Faculty of Economics, University of Tirana. She moved to the Netherlands, where she earned an M.Phil. and a Ph.D. in Economics through the Tinbergen Institute and the University of Amsterdam, completing her doctorate in 2002 with her thesis "The informal sector in transition: Tax evasion in an institutional vacuum".

== Career ==
Gërxhani began her academic career at the University of Amsterdam, holding successive positions as postdoctoral researcher, assistant professor, and associate professor. She subsequently held a full professorship in the Department of Political and Social Sciences at the European University Institute in Florence, Italy, from 2015 to 2022. She joined VU Amsterdam as Professor of Behavioral Socio-Economics in January 2023. From 2023 to 2025 she served as Head of the Department of Ethics, Governance and Society and from 2026, as Associate Dean of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion at the School of Business and Economics. [ref: Klarita Gërxhani, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam] She is also a research fellow at the Tinbergen Institute. [ref: New Research Fellow: Klarita Gërxhani, Tinbergen Institute]

Gërxhani has supervised fourteen doctoral students to completion, with one ongoing, and has mentored seven postdoctoral researchers.
== Research ==
Gërxhani's research lies at the intersection of behavioral economics and economic sociology, combining laboratory experiments, field experiments, vignette studies, and traditional surveys. Her work spans several interconnected themes.

Her early research examined the informal economy and tax evasion in post-communist countries, particularly Albania. Using surveys and experiments, she showed how a clash between formal institutions and rules on the one hand and informal institutions on the other drives informal economic activity, with tax evasion varying systematically by income source, gender, and institutional context.

A related strand of her work investigates how formal and informal institutions shape individual behavior and how social norms evolve and change over time. In the more than two decades since the start of her career, she has also studied norm compliance, institutional change, and the relationship between social values and collective decision-making.

Her most prominent recent work examines how competitive settings generate gender inequality. Her experiments demonstrate that men and women perform equally well when there is no competition, but that status-ranking competition against peers improves men's outcomes while worsening women's. This effect is observed even when men and women do not differ in ability; it is driven by gendered expectations. [ref: Academy selects 17 new members, Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences] This research was the subject of a feature interview in Het Financieele Dagblad, referenced on the newspaper's front page. [ref: Hoogleraar Gërxhani: 'Meritocratie is een fabel, weten we nu', Het Financieele Dagblad]

She has also studied employer behavior extensively, including how firms recruit workers, how social networks and contacts influence hiring decisions, and how gender and intersectional biases shape the evaluation of job candidates. This work combines laboratory experiments with field and vignette studies to isolate the mechanisms behind labor market discrimination.

An earlier strand of her research explored the role of social capital in post-communist societies, examining how trust and informal networks differ between Eastern and Western Europe and how they relate to economic participation, welfare attitudes, and political behavior.

Gërxhani's work has been covered by De Telegraaf, NPO Radio 1, [ref: Bar weinig vrouwen zijn hoogleraar economie, NPO Radio 1] ABC News Albania, [ref: Interview with Klarita Gërxhani, ABC News Albania] and A2 Business CNN Albania, [ref: Interview with Klarita Gërxhani, A2 Business CNN Albania] and she has been invited by corporations including KPMG and Heineken to discuss the application of her research to workplace inclusion. She has delivered keynote lectures at institutions including the MIT Summer School, the German Institute for Employment Research (IAB), the Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research (ZEW), and the European University Institute.

Draft text:
Zaery (born Amr Elrayah Abdalla October 1, 1998 in Sudan,Khartoum,Omdurman )is a sudanese organist, composer. [ref: Zaery: Taking Zanig Music from Omdurman to the International Stage, The Sudanist] [ref: Zaery, the Artist Who Will Take ZANIG Music to the World Stage – Weekly Music Vibes, weeklymusicvibes.com] [ref: From the Margins to the Mainstream: The Rise of Zanig in Sudanese Music, The Sudanist]

== Life ==
He was born in Omdurman and spent his early childhood in the Al-Murabba'at neighborhood before moving to Al-Abbasiya, where he grew up. He is the eldest of three brothers. Mazen is the middle child, and Muhammad Al-Mustafa is the youngest. He was raised in Al-Abbasiya and developed a love for music, inspired by the musicians Ayman Al-Rubu and Nijiri. [ref: ] [ref: أسطورة (الزنق) بالسودان “نيجيري”: لن أعود لدراسة الطب ودخلي الأسبوعي يعادل مرتب موظف كبير في شهر, صحيفة كورة سودانية الإلكترونية]

He became involved in Zanig music a Sudanese youth oriented musical style  associated with urban popular neighborhoods, pioneered by musician Ayman Al-Rubu amidst the working-class neighborhoods of Omdurman. [ref: Zaery: Taking Zanig Music from Omdurman to the International Stage, The Sudanist] [ref: لا يخلو أورغن من (صولاته) الموسيقية أيمن الربع.. رائد الكتمات!! - النيلين, www.alnilin.com]

He began performing live in 2012, marking his first steps in the music industry. At the time, the popularity of Zanig music among musicians stemmed from its style—dance-oriented, youthful, and contemporary—pulsing with youthful vitality. [ref: Miami City Weekly, www.miamicityweekly.com]

== Career ==
The real turning point in Zaery life came when he was personally requested to perform at a major public New Year’s Eve concert in Port Sudan in 2016. This marked his transition from playing the keyboard in working-class neighborhoods to performing at large-scale concerts in theaters and across various states. [ref: زنق, الرصّة] This large-scale public concert brought him widespread fame in Sudan. [ref: Zaery: Taking Zanig Music from Omdurman to the International Stage, The Sudanist]Subsequently, he performed at popular events across the capital's neighborhoods—ranging from private functions to rehearsals with other artists—which significantly shaped and enhanced his musical experience. [ref: Zaery, the Artist Who Will Take ZANIG Music to the World Stage – MusicTimes] [ref: ]

== His musical works ==

In 2019, Zaery recorded an African-style musical track at the Hajjaj Studio in Sudan and produced a music video in collaboration with a band. In 2020, he collaborated with Sudanese artist Noon Al-Ankaboota on the song "[https://www.facebook.com/share/v/1bmcFJgEFx/?mibextid=wwXIfr Kassar Samah]," which blended elements of "Zanig " and "Daluka" music. He later collaborated with Sudanese singer Wad Al-Jack and participated in live performances and a tour throughout 2021. [ref: Zaery: Taking Zanig Music from Omdurman to the International Stage, The Sudanist] [ref: ود الجاك يخوض تجربة أول حفل جماهيري في (اتحاد الفنانين) - تسامح نيوز]

In June 2022, Zaery moved to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where he joined the Sudanese band "Sequence" and performed Western and reggae music at various events and festivals. He also appeared on the Saudi television program "Ala Al-Wa'ad"—filmed at Rotana studios alongside artist Abdelfattah Grini. [ref: Zaery raises the Bar for Afro Pop music with ‘Rasta’, Sinusoidal Music] [ref: New Music Radar: 19 bands worth throwing into your rotation right now, Happy Mag] [ref: عبد الفتاح الجريني.. نوستالجيا نجم مغربي ولد بين أحضان الهجرة, Hespress - هسبريس جريدة إلكترونية مغربية]

== Zanig music ==
[https://nowvoyagermag.com/culture/city-beats Zanig] music is a modern musical genre in Sudan that gained prominence after its melodies captured the interest of Sudanese society and the youth. It is a fusion of African rhythms and contemporary Sudanese youth music. Furthermore, [ref: Zanig: The Story of a Music Genre Born in Khartoum, Sudan, Now Voyager Magazine]it features dance styles with an African sensibility, with the keyboardist often accompanied by a group of dancers who perform in highly choreographed unison. [ref: An Artless Artist: The Overlooked Genius of Ayman Al-Rubo by Al Rayah Al Rehima, Andariya]

Draft text:
----

VolDex is a family of financial indices measuring implied volatility, developed by Nations Indexes, Inc., a Chicago-based index provider. The principal index, VOLI, tracks the implied volatility of the S&P 500 over a 30-calendar-day period using at-the-money options on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (ticker: SPY). [ref: Vix challenged by new volatility index, [[Risk (magazine)] Nations Indexes calculates VolDex on a wide variety of underlyings including the Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000, Gold, Silver, Treasury Notes, Treasury Bonds, High-yield bonds, Volatility itself, Bitcoin, and several equities including Apple, Tesla, Microsoft, SpaceX, and others.

VolDex indices are most often compared with the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX). The primary methodological distinction is that the VIX uses a variance swap-based calculation drawing on a broad range of strike prices, while VolDex is a closed-form calculation using only options near the current market price of the underlying asset. [ref: Self-Regulatory Organizations; International Securities Exchange, LLC; Notice of Filing of Proposed Rule Change To List Options on the Nations VolDex Index, Federal Register]

==History==
Nations Indexes, Inc. was founded by Scott Nations, a former Chicago-based proprietary options trader. The company introduced VolDex in June 2013. Writing in the financial trade journal Risk, journalist Yakob Peterseil described the launch as a challenge to the VIX's two-decade market position, noting that VolDex "only looks at the implied volatility of a precisely at-the-money option due to expire in precisely 30 days," contrasting this with the VIX, which "prices future S&P 500 variance."

In August 2013, the International Securities Exchange (ISE) filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission a proposed rule change to list options on the Nations VolDex index. The SEC published notice of proceedings in November 2013 [ref: Self-Regulatory Organizations; International Securities Exchange, LLC; Order Instituting Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove a Proposed Rule Change, as Modified by Amendment No. 1, To List Options on the Nations VolDex Index, Federal Register] and approved the rule change on January 28, 2014 (Exchange Act Release No. 71365, 79 FR 4512). [ref: ISE Gets Green Light to List VolDex Options, The Wall Street Journal]

In 2018, Crain's Chicago Business identified VolDex as one of several products seeking to challenge Cboe's dominance in volatility products following controversy surrounding the VIX. [ref: VIX woes open up opportunities for Cboe rivals, Crain's Chicago Business]

In 2019, Nasdaq licensed the VolDex methodology from Nations Indexes to create the Nasdaq-100 Volatility Index (VOLQ). [ref: Nasdaq nearing launch of its own volatility index, S&P Global Market Intelligence] CME Group announced futures on VOLQ in August 2020 [ref: CME Group to Launch Futures on Nasdaq-100 Volatility Index (VOLQ), CME Group] and launched the contracts on October 5, 2020. [ref: CME to launch volatility index futures contract, Crain's Chicago Business]

==Methodology==
VolDex is a closed-form measure of at-the-money implied volatility. The calculation uses the first in-the-money and first out-of-the-money call and put options for expirations that bracket the target tenor. For the 30-day index, this means one expiration before and one after 30 calendar days (43,200 minutes) from the moment of calculation.

Forward prices for each expiration are derived from put-call parity. These define the at-the-money level; option prices are then interpolated to yield hypothetical at-the-money put and call prices, which are combined to produce the VolDex value.

The methodology can be applied to multiple tenors and asset classes. Tenors include zero days-to-expiration (0DTE), one day, seven days, thirty days, and periods through 360 days. Asset classes include the S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, Russell 2000, U.S. Treasury bonds, gold, silver, and individual equities. [ref: VOLQ: How to Measure Nasdaq-100 Volatility, Traders Magazine]

The component expirations for the 30-day index roll each Thursday morning to the Friday expirations that are approximately 29 and 36 days in the future.

==Indices==

===VOLI (S&P 500)===

VOLI is the original VolDex index, measuring 30-day implied volatility from at-the-money options on SPY, the S&P 500 ETF. It is disseminated in real time under the ticker symbol VOLI, and historical data maintained by Nasdaq covers a period beginning January 31, 2005.

A combustiologist (derived from Latin combustio = burn) is a physician who specializes in combustiology, the branch of medicine concerned with the diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation of burn injuries. [ref: Комбустиология чрезвычайных ситуаций: учебное пособие, Всероссийский центр экстренной и радиационной медицины им. А. М. Никифорова МЧС России] [ref: Ожоги термические и химические... Клинические рекомендации РФ 2021, MedElement] The term is almost exclusively used in Russian-language medical literature and in medical education in some post-Soviet / CIS countries (Russia, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Belarus, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Moldova, Armenia, Azerbaijan ). In English-language medicine the usual designations are "burn surgeon" or "burn specialist".  Poland – The field is called Kombustiologia, but it is not a recognised independent specialty. Burn care remains part of general or plastic surgery.  Latin America / Spain / Portugal – The forms combustiólogo / combustiologista appear almost exclusively in translations of Russian/Ukrainian articles. National terminology uses: Spanish-speaking countries → especialista en quemaduras, médico del quemado, cirujano de quemados. Brazil / Portugal → especialista em queimaduras, cirurgião de queimados.  Western Europe, North America, other regions – Standard terms are "burn surgeon", "burn specialist", "chirurgien des brûlés", "Brandchirurg", etc.

== Overview ==
Severe burns produce a prolonged hypermetabolic response that can last up to two years and involve multiorgan dysfunction, [ref: The hypermetabolic response to burn injury and interventions to modify this response, Clin Plast Surg. 2009 Oct;36(4):583-96. doi: 10.1016/j.cps.2009.05.001.] together with vascular leak, hypovolemic shock, and immune and inflammatory disturbances that predispose patients to sepsis. [ref: The pathogenesis and diagnosis of sepsis post burn injury, Burns & Trauma] Combustiology therefore overlaps with critical care medicine, plastic and reconstructive surgery, trauma surgery, and physical medicine and rehabilitation. [ref: Teamwork for total burn care: Burn centers and multidisciplinary burn teams] [ref: Burn Teams and Burn Centers: The Importance of a Comprehensive Team Approach to Burn Care, Clinics in Plastic Surgery]Combustiologists typically work in specialized burn centers or burn units. These centres commonly operate with multidisciplinary teams that include surgeons, critical-care physicians, nurses, physiotherapists, occupational therapists, dietitians, psychologists and other specialists. [ref: Burns, World Health Organization]

== Conditions treated ==
=== Burn injuries ===
Burns are commonly classified by cause and by depth.By cause:
* Thermal burn (flame, scald, contact, steam)
* Chemical burns
* Electrical burns
* Radiation burns
* Friction burns
* Inhalation injury(it is a frequent and important complication of fire exposure)

By depth:
* Superficial (epidermal; formerly first-degree burn)
* Partial-thickness (formerly second-degree burn), further divided into superficial and deep
* Full-thickness (formerly third-degree burn)
* Deep burns involving fascia, muscle or bone (fourth-degree) [ref: Classification of Burns, Stanford Medicine Children's Health]

Depth largely determines healing potential and the need for surgical grafting. Extent is expressed as a percentage of total body surface area (TBSA). Age, comorbidities and inhalation injury also affect severity and prognosis.

=== Severe skin conditions ===
Some extensive epidermal-loss disorders are managed in burn units. Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) present substantial challenges and are frequently treated in burn centres. [ref: Stevens–Johnson Syndrome and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis: A 15-year Regional Burn Center Experience, JPRAS Open. 2025 Feb 8;44:83-92. doi: 10.1016/j.jpra.2025.02.003.]

== Treatment ==
=== Initial management and resuscitation ===
Initial care follows trauma principles (airway, breathing, circulation) followed by early fluid resuscitation. [ref: Burn Fluid Resuscitation, StatPearls Publishing] The Parkland formula recommends 4 mL of lactated Ringer's solution per kilogram of body weight per percent TBSA burned in adults (commonly 3 mL/kg/%TBSA in children), with half given in the first eight hours and the remainder over the next sixteen.Formulas serve as starting estimates; rates are adjusted according to the patient's response (commonly urine output).

=== Surgical management ===
Early excision of necrotic tissue and wound closure is regarded as one of the major advances in the treatment of severe burns. Autologous skin grafting remains the standard for definitive coverage but is limited by donor-site availability. [ref: Advances in stem cell-based tissue-engineered skin substitutes for burns, Trends in Biotechnology] Skin substitutes include acellular scaffolds, temporary allogeneic-cell constructs and permanent autologous-cell constructs. [ref: Tissue engineering of skin and regenerative medicine for wound care, Burns Trauma. 2018 Jan 24;6:4. doi: 10.1186/s41038-017-0103-y.]
[truncated]
