The International Engineering and Technology Institute (IETI) is an international academic organization founded in 2015 and based in Hong Kong. It is involved in academic collaboration, research activities, conferences, fellowships and awards in science, engineering and technology. [ref: SSUET VC honored with prestigious global award, Business Recorder]

== History ==

IETI was founded in 2015. In 2020, the Department of Statistics and Data Science at Tsinghua University described IETI as a non-profit organization established in 2015 that promoted research and collaboration in science, engineering and technology, with activities extending into mathematics, statistics, economics and related fields. [ref: Professor Lijian Yang was Elected as Distinguished Fellow of the International Engineering and Technology Institute, Tsinghua University]

In 2026, the Pakistani newspaper Business Recorder described IETI as a non-profit and non-political academic organization founded in 2015 and reported on one of its international awards.

== Activities ==

IETI's activities include academic conferences, research collaboration, fellowships and academic awards. Universities in several countries have reported appointments and awards involving the organization.

In 2020, Tsinghua University reported the election of statistician Lijian Yang as an IETI Distinguished Fellow and described the institute's research scope and fellowship program.

In December 2025, the University of California, Santa Barbara reported that computer scientist Linda Petzold had been elected a Distinguished Fellow of IETI. The university described the fellowship as an honor recognizing Petzold's contributions to computational science and engineering. [ref: UCSB Professor Linda Petzold Elected Fellow of IETI, University of California, Santa Barbara]

In 2025, the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology reported that environmental engineer Irene Man Chi Lo had been elected an IETI Distinguished Fellow. [ref: Prof. Irene LO Elected Distinguished Fellow of IETI and Honored with Career Award at International Conference, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology]

IETI has also participated in the organization of international academic conferences. In May 2026, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University reported that IETI co-organized the fifth International Symposium on Big Data and Artificial Intelligence for Education Transformation (ISBDAI 2026). The event included a keynote address by Nobel Prize in Physics laureate Ferenc Krausz. [ref: Nobel Laureate Prof. Ferenc KRAUSZ shares insights at PolyU to shape the AI-Powered future during the ISBDAI 2026, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University]

== Fellowships ==

IETI operates a fellowship program that includes Fellow and Distinguished Fellow categories. The organization also has a Laureate Distinguished Fellow category. [ref: About IETI, International Engineering and Technology Institute]

The fellowship program has been reported by universities including Tsinghua University, the University of California, Santa Barbara, and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.

IETI's fellowship lists include academics who have received major international awards. However, the individual distinction of a fellow is separate from the organizational status of IETI.

== Awards ==

IETI administers academic awards and honors, including awards related to scientific research, leadership and young researchers. [ref: IETI Awards, International Engineering and Technology Institute]

In July 2026, Business Recorder reported that Muhammad Afzal Haque, vice chancellor of Sir Syed University of Engineering & Technology, received an IETI Global Leadership Award. The newspaper described the award as an international recognition for contributions to engineering education, research and international collaboration.

== International activities ==

IETI's activities involve academic institutions in several countries. Its collaboration with The Hong Kong Polytechnic University on ISBDAI 2026 was reported by the university in connection with a keynote presentation by Nobel laureate Ferenc Krausz.

The organization has also been referenced in university reports concerning individual academics and their appointments to IETI fellowship positions.

Draft text:
Jamelyn Ebelacker is an award-winning artist, entrepreneur, social activist and member of the Santa Clara Pueblo tribe. She has worked to elevate awareness of indigenous experiences in the United States. In 2022, she assisted in the creation of the "People of the First Light” parade float in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, the first ever permanent Native American float in the history of that parade. She currently serves as the marketing manager of the Santa Clara Development Corporation. [ref: ] [ref: Who, indigenousdirection]

== Education and Early Contributions ==
Ebelacker completed her Bachelor of Fine Arts undergraduate degree at the Institute of American Indian Arts in Santa Fe, New Mexico. After graduation, in 2017, she followed in her family's tradition of public service by serving in the Peace Corps in St Lucia and Dominica as an educator [ref: ]. Her work in the Peace Corps was terminated by the Covid pandemic in 2020 but not before she was nominated for the Franklin H. Williams award, which honors Returned Peace Corps Volunteers who exemplify an ongoing commitment to community service. Upon returning to the US, she began working for Indigenous Direction as an Associate Producer, Project Manager and Digital Artist where she helped create the first permanent indigenous float in the Macy's Thanksgiving Parade. In 2023 she enrolled in the MBA program at Arizona State University where her work led to her selection as recipient of Arizona State University’s (ASU) 2024 Martin Luther King Jr. Student Servant-Leadership Award. In addition to her MBA with concentrations in Consulting and Marketing, she earned ASU's certificate in sustainability. Ebelacker continues to support the Pueblo people through the Santa Clara Development Corporation as well as continues her heritage pottery craftsmanship through her family company Eberlacker Family Pottery. [ref: Native American Women Make Their Marks in Business While Honoring Their Heritage, Forté Foundation] [ref: Ebelacker Family Pottery, Ebelacker Family Pottery]

Draft text:
Cut the Rope: Magic is a puzzle video game developed and published by ZeptoLab. The fifth main installment of the Cut the Rope franchise, the game's plot involves Om Nom travelling inside a magical book after a spider wizard inside the book steals his candy supply.

== Gameplay ==
Like other titles in the franchise, the game's goal is to cut ropes in order to feed candy to Om Nom. A new feature in this game allows Om Nom to transform into different creatures, each with their own unique abilities, in order to solve certain puzzles. [ref: Zeptolab Goes Back To The Well With Cut The Rope: Magic, Now Available For Free In The Play Store, Android Police] In some levels, the player must face off against the spider wizard, who will forcefully attempt to bring the candy to his direction; the player will lose the level if the wizard eats the candy. [ref: Cut the Rope: Magic Review, Trusted Reviews]

== Development and Release ==
In October 2015, five years after the release of the first Cut the Rope game, ZeptoLab announced a brand new game for the franchise entitled Cut the Rope: Magic, which was slated for a December release, although few details of the game were given at the time. [ref: Om Nom is back, and still hungry: New ‘Cut the Rope’ set for December, GeekWire] [ref: Cut the Rope: Magic swinging into Android devices this December, Android Authority] The game was later released on December 17, introducing six different transformations for Om Nom, including a bird form, a baby form, a fish form, a mouse form, a ghost form, and a dragon form. The game was free for Android, while the iOS version costed $1.

== Reception ==
According to the review aggregation website Metacritic, the game has received "generally positive reviews" from critics. [ref: Cut the Rope: Magic Reviews - Metacritic, www.metacritic.com] Nadia Oxford of Gamezebo in particular praised the game for its graphics and blending of old and new mechanics. [ref: Cut the Rope: Magic Review - My Magical Om Nom, Gamezebo] Michael Crider of Android Police positively compared the game's addition of magical transformations to that of the Super Mario franchise and, while noting the game's use of in-app purchases and advertisements, stated that the core gameplay would make these flaws easy to ignore.

== References ==

Olivia Faith Liang (born May 11, [ref: ] 1993) [ref: Kung Fu's Olivia Liang on Reclaiming the Martial-Arts Stereotype, Popsugar] is an American actress. She is known for her roles as Alyssa Chang in the television series Legacies [ref: Legacies Recap: Another Saltzman Birthday Ends In Death And Betrayal, TVLine] and Nicky Shen in Kung Fu. [ref: ‘Kung Fu’: Olivia Liang Cast As The Lead Of the CW Reboot Pilot, Deadline] Liang has also appeared in television series including Grey's Anatomy, Into the Dark, and One Day at a Time.

== Life and career ==
Olivia Faith Liang was born on 11 May 1993, She grew up in Diamond Bar, California. [ref: Olivia Liang Is the Role Model She Wishes She Had, Cero Magazine] Liang became interested in acting at a young age and also trained in dance. [ref: Olivia Liang On How The 'Kung Fu' Reboot Rewrites The Show's Problematic Legacy, Bustle] She studied ballet, jazz and hip-hop and later described dance as her first form of storytelling. [ref: 'Kung Fu's' Olivia Liang Says She Struggled With Anorexia As A Young Dancer, Women's Health]

She attended the University of California, San Diego, where she studied communications. [ref: Heroic Hugs, Television Academy] [ref: Olivia Liang, The CW] After graduating, she attended an acting program at the University of California, Los Angeles.

Liang began her television career with guest roles, including appearances in One Day at a Time and Grey's Anatomy. [ref: Kung Fu: Gender-Flipped CW Reboot Adds Legacies Actress In Lead Role, TVLine] In 2017, she was selected for the ABC Discovers Talent Showcase. Thereafter, she appeared in Hulu's Into the Dark and The CW's Legacies. [ref: Meet Olivia Liang, star of CW’s new Kung Fu reboot, South China Morning Post] [ref: Interview: Olivia Liang Talks Into The Dark: Crawlers (Exclusive)]

In 2020, she was cast in The CW's Kung Fu. [ref: 'Kung Fu' Star Olivia Liang is Fighting on Her Own Terms – The Nerds of Color] [ref: ‘Kung Fu’: Olivia Liang Cast As The Lead Of the CW Reboot Pilot, Deadline] After more than 150 actresses auditioned for the role. At the time, she was appearing as Alyssa Chang on Legacies. [ref: ‘Kung Fu’ Rights the Wrongs of Its Ancestor, The New York Times] [ref: Legacies season 2 star lands lead role in The CW's Kung Fu, Digital Spy] Liang had not studied martial arts before being cast in Kung Fu. After being cast as Nicky Shen, she began training for the role. [ref: Why Kung Fu's Olivia Liang Was "Anti-Learning Martial Arts" Before Landing Her Role, E! Online] The series premiered in April 2021 and ran for three seasons, ending in 2023. [ref: ‘Kung Fu’ Star Olivia Liang Bids Show Farewell In Emotional Instagram Post, Deadline] In May 2021, Liang appeared on The Kelly Clarkson Show to promote Kung Fu. [ref: Olivia Liang to Appear on ‘The Kelly Clarkson Show’, Nerds and Beyond]

In 2023, Liang joined the cast of Paper Flowers, an independent film directed by Karan Soni. [ref: Kapil Talwalkar, Olivia Liang, Karan Soni & Tom Everett Scott Join Inspirational Indie ‘Paper Flowers’ Based On Viral HuffPost Article, Deadline]

== Personal life ==
Liang has spoken about having anorexia as a teenager. She said that her experience with dance contributed to the pressure she felt about her body and appearance. She later discussed the experience in an interview with Women's Health.

Bayou Boy is a 1971 American television adventure film produced by Walt Disney Productions. [ref: The Wonderful World of Disney Television, Hyperion Books] [ref: Disney A to Z: The Official Encyclopedia: Third Edition, Disney Editions] Directed by Gary Nelson and written by Louis Pelletier, it originally aired in two parts on NBC's The Wonderful World of Disney on February 7 and February 14, 1971. [ref: Bayou Boy (television), D23] [ref: Louis Pelletier; Wrote 500 Episodes of 'FBI' Radio Series, Los Angeles Times]

Filming took place at Pine Island Point at Caddo Lake, on the Texas-Louisiana border near Shreveport. [ref: Dynamite, cowboy boots, horse falls, and toupee hijinks with Steve McQueen's costar Mitch Vogel, Medium] [ref: Disney filming at Caddo Lake, Shreveport Times] [ref: Prehistoric Caddo Lake is Setting for Disney's 'Bayou Boy' Adventure, The Robesonian] [ref: Louisiana to be Spotlighted in Disney TV Series on NBC, The Marksville Weekly News] [ref: Page 28, The Jeffersonian] In one instance when a stuntman failed to show up, a local highway patrolman was asked to fall 25 feet in a lake. [ref: City Beat, The Mexia Daily News] After filming Governor Preston Smith made the cast of the film honorary Texas citizens. [ref: 'Bayou Boy' Cast Honorary Texas Citizens, The Salt Lake Tribune]

A $12,000 replica of the bayou was constructed at Disney Studio in Burbank for the alligator fight scene. [ref: Bayou Boy, Chronique Disney] [ref: Prehistoric Caddo Lake is Setting for Disney's 'Bayou Boy' Adventure, The Robesonian] [ref: TV Scout, The Index-Journal]

Co-stars John McIntire and Jeanette Nolan were married in real life, and often appeared in the same shows and movies. [ref: Husband, Wife Acting Team in 'Bayou Boy', Idaho State Journal] [ref: Behind the Scenes, The Daily Herald]

The musical score was composed by Buddy Baker. [ref: Norman "Buddy" Baker Collection, NYU Special Collections Finding Aids] The opening title song, "Bayou Boy", was written by Terry Gilkyson and performed by his daughter Lisa. [ref: Dynamite, cowboy boots, horse falls, and toupee hijinks with Steve McQueen's costar Mitch Vogel, Medium]

The Robesonian called it an “exciting two-part action adventure drama,” [ref: Percy Rodrigues Fights Alligator on 'Disney World' Bayou Drama, The Robesonian] and The Oneonta Star felt that it was “suitable family fare.” [ref: Top TV, The Oneonta Star] The Daily Herald referred to it as a “mystery adventure,” [ref: Mitch Vogel in Title Role for Disney's 'Bayou Boy', The Daily Herald] and the Albuquerque Journal wrote that “kids should eat it up.” [ref: TV Key Previews, Albuquerque Journal]

The film was rebroadcast by NBC in 1979 under the title The Boy from Dead Man's Bayou. [ref: The Magical World of Disney Season 17 Episodes, TV Guide] [ref: Bayou Boy (television), D23]

His Royal Highness, Alayeluwa Oba (Professor) Saka Matemilola (4 August 1964) is a traditional ruler of Nigeria, an engineer, and an academician who is known as the Olowu of Owu Kingdom in Abeokuta, Ogun State. [ref: Saka Matemilola: A New Beginning In Owu Kingdom, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News] [ref: Matemilola to succeed Dosunmu as Olowu of Owu Kingdom, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]. He succeeded Oba Adegboyega Dosunmu, who passed away on 12 December 2021, and became the 14th monarch of the kingdom. [ref: News Update – Owu Kingdom][b] He graduated from the University of Ibadan with a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering and holds a Ph.D. degree from the University of Cambridge.[a] Prior to his installation as the Olowu of Owu Kingdom, he was working as a consultant for reservoir engineering in the oil industry at Shell. [ref: Olowu warns traditional rulers against partisan politics as Falola Interview examines palace, power, Tribune Online] Additionally, Matemilola has also lived in the UK before relocation to Nigeria in 1996. [ref: Hunger Threatening Nigeria’s Future, monarch Tells FG, Daily Trust]

He has earned a name as Olowu from his involvement in the importance of traditional institutions within the democratic process in Nigeria. In this regard, he has observed that traditional rulers must be made a part of the form of governance without engaging in politics, and there must be a constitutional arrangement for their involvement. [ref: Nigeria’s Oil Woes Rooted In Decades Of Misrule, Say Industry Veterans, Platform Times] He has criticized the feeding scheme in schools by the federal government. [ref: Olowu visits burnt Baale’s residence, urges calm over alleged arson, Vanguard News]

The Olowu Hope Programme is a social intervention programme that deals with education, healthcare, business and environmental sustainability, and which includes daily meals for primary school children in Abeokuta. He is also the President-General of the Muslim Council of Ogun State. [ref: NSCIA seeks divine intervention, urges Nigerians to complement prayers with action, Muslim News Nigeria]

== Early Life of Alayeluwa Oba (Professor) Saka Adelola Ayokanmi Matemilola ==
Matemilola was born on August 4, 1964 and hails from one of the ruling dynasties that traces its lineage to the family of Ajibosin, grandson of Oduduwa. Matemilola is from the ruling dynasty of Matemilola of the Soke Compound. Matemilola has Bachelor of Science and Master of Science in mechanical engineering degrees from the University of Ibadan and a doctoral degree from the University of Cambridge. [a] He was active in charity work during his stay in the UK. His return to Nigeria in 1996 has been referred to as continuing his public service career.

== Career ==
===Petroleum industry===

Matemilola has worked as a reservoir engineering consultant at Shell Petroleum, Port Harcourt, between 2009 and 2011. In 2011, he was part of the group that set up the Centre of Excellence in Geosciences and Petroleum Engineering at the University of Benin. According to reports, he sits on the board of a number of corporations. The Platform Times referred to him as a former president of the Society of Petroleum Engineers.

=== Academic reputation ===
In The Toyin Falola Interview, the historian Toyin Falola referred to Matemilola as one of the rare individuals who combine traditional leadership and international scholarship, based on his background from Ibadan and Cambridge in engineering and energy.

=== Accession ===
Matemilola appeared after the selection of seven aspirants from the ruling lineages of Owu, following the performance of certain traditional ceremonies. Matemilola was to be crowned on 29 October 2022.. He has stated that his family had been preparing him for the position for many years and that he had received encouragement from his friends and colleagues to aspire to the throne. His throne name is Oluyalo Otileta VII, and his style is Alayeluwa

=== Reign ===
====Unity and Culture of the Yoruba====

Matemilola states that the unity of the Yoruba is the main goal of his reign. This will be done using programs such as the Odun Omo Olowu, which is an annual celebration in which he will send a message of unity to the Yorubas in and outside the country.

===Public Appearance===

Matemilola’s public appearances include the courtesy visit by the association of organizations such as Abeokuta North Chapter of NULGE (National Union of Local Government Employees) and the Agboole Akogun family. Also included among some of his public appearances is the 60th birthday celebration of the Olota of Ota, Oba (Professor) Adeyemi Abdulkabir Obalanlege.

===Political views===
====Non-partisanship====
In The Toyin Falola Interview, titled "Indigenous Education, Character Formation and Citizen Making," Matemilola maintained that traditional rulers cannot become apolitical in the process of governance but should desist from partisan tendencies. He posited that for a ruler to hold power, he must represent the entire community not a political party. He added that if a ruler openly supports a political party or any candidate, the stool becomes debased.

Draft text:
John Michael Faile II (born May 11, 2000) is an American professional baseball player in the Cincinnati Reds organization. He plays catcher and first base for the Dayton Dragons, the Reds' High-A affiliate. Faile played college baseball at North Greenville University, where he set NCAA Division II career records for home runs and runs batted in.

==Early life==

Faile was born in Lancaster County, South Carolina, and lived in Lancaster until the eighth grade. His parents are Michael and Julie Faile. The family later moved to Boiling Springs, South Carolina, because of Michael's work. Faile is the oldest of three children, with a younger brother, Austin, and a younger sister, Annalynn. [ref: Archdeacon: Epic Faile — The unbelievable story of a Dragons hero and his grandpa, Dayton Daily News]

Faile played baseball from a young age. His grandfather, Curtis Threatt, was an important part of his baseball career. Threatt played football and baseball at Colorado State University and later worked in education and athletics in South Carolina. He also regularly played catch with Faile when he was growing up.

Faile attended Boiling Springs High School. About 60 players tried out for the baseball team when he arrived, and Faile was one of three players who made the team.

Faile was named to the South Carolina All-State team in 2017 and 2018. He was also named the state's 5A Baseball Player of the Year in 2018. [ref: John Michael Faile - 2023 Baseball Roster, North Greenville University Athletics]

He attended North Greenville University after high school. Faile had not received a Division I scholarship and was overlooked by larger college programs. [ref: MLB draft within reach for North Greenville catcher overlooked out of high school, The Post and Courier]

==College career==

Faile played five seasons at North Greenville from 2019 to 2023. He was named Conference Carolinas Freshman of the Year in 2019.

In 2021, Faile batted.438 with 23 home runs and 78 RBI. He was named Conference Carolinas Player of the Year and the National Collegiate Baseball Writers Association Southeast Region Player of the Year. [ref: John Michael Faile of North Greenville named Herff Jones Conference Carolinas Male Athlete of the Year, Conference Carolinas]

In 2022, Faile hit.418 with 16 home runs and 86 RBI. He won the Conference Carolinas Triple Crown, leading the conference in batting average, home runs and RBI. [ref: 2022 Baseball Cumulative Statistics, North Greenville University Athletics]

Faile suffered a knee injury during the 2022 Conference Carolinas tournament, but he returned for the NCAA Division II championship tournament. He hit a home run in his first at-bat after returning from the injury against West Chester University. [ref: Crusaders Begin NCAA Division II Baseball Championship with Win Over West Chester, North Greenville University Athletics]

North Greenville won the NCAA Division II national championship that year after defeating Point Loma Nazarene University 5–3 on June 10, 2022. It was the first national championship in the school's baseball program. [ref: National Champions: North Greenville Wins NCAA Division II Baseball Tournament, North Greenville University Athletics]

Faile broke the NCAA Division II career RBI record during the 2023 season. He finished his college career with 81 home runs and 337 RBI, both NCAA Division II records. [ref: Dayton Dragons GameDay, Game Notes, and Roster for April 2, OurSports Central]

Faile also played summer baseball while in college. He played for the Savannah Bananas in 2020 and the Spartanburgers in 2021. [ref: 2020 Savannah Bananas Summer Statistics, The Baseball Cube] [ref: 2021 Spartanburgers Summer Statistics, The Baseball Cube]

==Professional career==

===Billings Mustangs===

Faile was not selected in the 2023 Major League Baseball draft. He played for the Billings Mustangs of the Pioneer League in 2023. In 54 games, he hit.353 with 21 home runs and 70 RBI. He was named Pioneer League Rookie of the Year. [ref: Cincinnati Reds sign catcher John Michael Faile, Reds Minor Leagues] [ref: Award Winners & All-Stars Announced, OurSports Central]

===Cincinnati Reds===

The Cincinnati Reds signed Faile to a minor league contract on December 19, 2023. [ref: John Michael Faile Signs Minor League Contract with Cincinnati Reds, North Greenville University Athletics]

Faile began the 2024 season with the Arizona Complex League Reds before joining the Dayton Dragons in August. He hit a home run in his second plate appearance in his Dayton debut and homered again the following night. In his third game, he hit a grand slam. [ref: Dragons 2025 Team Preview, Part 2: First Basemen, MiLB.com]

Faile played 91 games for Dayton in 2025. He hit.233 with 13 home runs and 56 RBI. [ref: John Michael Faile Stats, Age, Position, Height, Weight, Fantasy & News, MiLB.com]

In 2026, Faile hit.278 with 14 home runs and 51 RBI during the regular season. On August 30, he hit his 30th home run with Dayton, tying the franchise record set by Chris Williamson. On September 5, he hit his 31st home run with the Dragons and broke the record. [ref: Faile Breaks Dragons Career Home Run Record in Dayton Win on Saturday, MiLB.com]

Trevor J. Blank is an American folklorist and associate professor of communication at the State University of New York at Potsdam. His research focuses on digital culture and Internet folklore.

== Education ==
In 2005, Blank earned a bachelor's degree in American Studies from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County, where he became interested in folklore as an undergraduate after meeting Charlie Kemp, then the state folklorist of Maryland. Kemp encouraged him to pursue graduate study in the field. [ref: Notes on the Authors] [ref: Humor Makes Life More Tolerable. Interview with American Folklorist Trevor J. Blank, Folklore] He earned a master's degree in folklore from Indiana University in 2007 and his Ph.D. in American Studies from Pennsylvania State University, Harrisburg in 2011. [ref: AMST Alum Prof. Trevor J. Blank is this year's URCAD Speaker]

== Career ==
In 2009, he published the anthology "Folklore and the Internet: Vernacular Expression in a Digital World". [ref: ] He is an associate professor in the Department of Communication at the State University of New York at Potsdam. [ref: Trevor J. Blank, University Press of Colorado]

== Awards ==
In 2009, Blank received the Richard Reuss Prize for Students of Folklore and History from the History and Folklore Section of the American Folklore Society for his essay "The History of the Hoosier Folklore Society, 1937–2007." [ref: Richard Reuss Prize, The American Folklore Society] In 2010, he received the William Wells Newell Prize in Children's Folklore from the American Folklore Society for his research on children's folklore. [ref: Penn State professor's essay on farting takes the prize, pennlive]

== Publications ==
=== Author ===
* Spring Grove State Hospital (2008, with David S. Helsel)
* The Last Laugh: Folk Humor, Celebrity Culture, and Mass-Mediated Disasters in the Digital Age (2013)
* Toward a Conceptual Framework for the Study of Folklore and the Internet (2014)
* Maryland Legends: Folklore from the Old Line State (2014, with David J. Puglia) [ref: Blank, Trevor J, viaf.org]

=== Editor and co-editor ===

Catherine Lezer is an Australian local government politician, property investor, and businessperson who has served as an independent Councillor for the City of Perth since 2020. [ref: Elected Members, City of Perth Official Website] Alongside her council duties, Lezer holds roles in strata property advocacy and state heritage governance. [ref: Catherine Lezer Official Website]

== Early Life and Education ==
Born and raised in Perth, Western Australia, Lezer's professional background is in business and corporate governance. She holds a Bachelor of Business, a Master of Business Administration (MBA), and qualifications from the Australian Institute of Company Directors (AICD).

== Professional Career ==
Prior to entering local government, Lezer built a career as a property investor, mortgage broker, and advocate for inner-city and strata living. Since 2015, she has been involved with the Strata Community Association (SCA), previously serving on both the New South Wales and Western Australia boards. [ref: SCA WA President Report 2022, Strata Community Association] [ref: SCA WA President Report 2023, Strata Community Association] She remains active within the organization, including hosting and presenting at events such as the CHU SCA (WA) 2026 Owners Conference. [ref: CHU SCA (WA) 2026 Owners Conference, Strata Community Association (WA)]

In 2021, Lezer was appointed to the board of the Heritage Council of Western Australia, where she advises on state heritage planning and preservation. [ref: New Chair and members appointed to the Heritage Council of WA, Government of Western Australia] [ref: Heritage Council of Western Australia Annual Report 2025-26, Government of Western Australia] She has also served on audit and risk committees for both the SCA and the Department of Planning, Lands and Heritage.

== Political Career ==

=== City of Perth Council ===
Running as an independent candidate advocating for apartment residents and sustainable urban design, Lezer was first elected to the City of Perth Council in 2020, placing third with 6.34% of the vote under the first-past-the-post system. [ref: Lord Mayor Basil Zempilas unveils the team driving new-look City of Perth, The West Australian]

She was re-elected in 2023, being the first candidate to reach quota with 16.57% of the vote under the newly introduced optional preferential voting system, securing a term running until October 2027. Within the council, she serves as Chair of the Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee.

=== Mayoral Candidacy ===
Following the departure of Lord Mayor Basil Zempilas to State Parliament in early 2025, Lezer was the first candidate to announce her candidacy for Lord Mayor, running under the campaign slogan "independent, proven, ethical". [ref: Perth councillor Catherine Lezer first to put hand up to replace Basil Zempilas as Perth Lord Mayor, The West Australian] During her campaign, she completed the national Pathways to Politics Program for Women as part of the 2025 Western Australian cohort. [ref: Recommendations for your pathway to politics: Cr Catherine Lezer, Pathways to Politics] She narrowly lost the election by 70 votes.

=== Council Initiatives ===
During her tenure on the council, Lezer initiated and supported various urban policy proposals:
* 2021: Initiated targeted grant programs to assist strata complexes with sustainability upgrades, waste management, and building reports.
* 2021: Introduced an apartment recycling yellow bag initiative.
* 2022: Passed a motion to install a rainbow street crossing to celebrate diversity. [ref: Northbridge gets new bold rainbow street art, OUTinPerth]
* 2024: Passed a motion advocating for additional green open space and pocket parks.
* 2025: Initiated a program encouraging the conversion of vacant spaces into residential homes.
* 2025: Passed a motion regarding security enhancements on Central Area Transit (CAT) buses.
* 2025: Unsuccessfully proposed a motion to install playground fencing to enhance public safety. [ref: Request to fence inner city kids playground after anti social behaviour knocked back, PerthNow]
* 2026: Passed a motion for modifications and extensions to CAT bus routes to improve precinct connectivity. [ref: CAT bus route extension needed for struggling East Perth businesses, PerthNow]
* 2026: Passed a motion to install public lighting along Langley Park and Riverside Drive. [ref: Let there be light: call to install lighting along Perth riverfront, PerthNow]
* 2026: Unsuccessfully introduced a motion proposing a cost-saving budget review package. [ref: City of Perth councillor wants art project binned as $168m of projects left unbudgeted, PerthNow]
[truncated]

Draft text:

Pakka Limited (formerly Yash Papers and Yash Pakka) is an Indian packaging company headquartered in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh. The company was established in 1981 as Yash Papers and initially manufactured low-grammage kraft paper. It later expanded into moulded-fibre food-service products and other packaging made from agricultural residue. [ref: Prospectus: Yash Papers Limited, Securities and Exchange Board of India] [ref: How letting go brought 40-year-old family biz Yash Pakka back from the brink, Forbes India]

The company is listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange and the National Stock Exchange of India. [ref: Packaging firm Pakka gets listed on NSE, The Hindu]

==History==

Pakka was established in 1981 as Yash Papers Limited by K. K. Jhunjhunwala in Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh. The company began as a manufacturer of low-grammage kraft paper, with an initial installed capacity of 1,940 tonnes per year. Commercial production began in 1983.

In 1991, Yash Papers established a second paper manufacturing unit with an installed capacity of 6,000 tonnes per year. In 1992, the company made a public issue to finance an increase in its manufacturing capacity to 16,000 tonnes per year.

The company expanded its energy infrastructure during the 1990s. In 1997, it installed a 2.5 MW steam turbine for cogeneration of power. The company also began exporting its paper, with its first direct export order executed in 1999.

During the 2000s, Yash Papers expanded its paper manufacturing operations and moved into speciality grades. Its manufacturing infrastructure subsequently included pulp production, chemical recovery and power-generation facilities.

Ved Krishna, the son of K. K. Jhunjhunwala, joined the company in 1999 and later took responsibility for its operations. During this period, the company experienced financial and operational difficulties before shifting its focus towards higher-value paper and packaging products. [ref: From Ayodhya to 30 countries: how this sustainable paper business beat all odds to clock Rs 300 Cr turnover, YourStory]

During the 2010s, the company increasingly expanded from paper manufacturing into packaging products made from agricultural residue. It developed moulded-fibre products and launched CHUK, a brand of compostable food-service tableware made from sugarcane fibre.

In 2015, Ved Krishna stepped away from the company's day-to-day operational management. The company subsequently moved towards a more professionally managed operating structure while continuing to expand its packaging business.

In 2018, CHUK received design recognition including the Red Dot Design Award and the Good Design Award. [ref: How Yash Pakka is making sustainable packaging a reality in India, [[The Telegraph (India)] [ref: CHUK Delivery Containers launched; Solves Biggest Packaging Challenge, Food Infotech]

In 2019, the company changed its name from Yash Papers Limited to Yash Pakka Limited, reflecting its expansion beyond paper manufacturing into packaging products.

In 2023, the company changed its name to Pakka Limited and was listed on the National Stock Exchange of India, a listing that coincided with plans to expand its Ayodhya operations and establish a manufacturing facility in Guatemala. In 2024, the company's board approved an increased budget for the Jagriti project, an expansion of its Ayodhya manufacturing operations, with the revised project cost reported at ₹675 crore and completion expected in 2026. [ref: Outcome of Board Meeting held on 27 March 2024, National Stock Exchange of India]

==Products and operations==

Pakka produces paper, moulded-fibre food-service products and other packaging made from agricultural residue, particularly sugarcane bagasse. Its principal manufacturing operations are based in Ayodhya. [ref: Pakka Ltd: How 1 Son Took His Father's Dream to a Rs 400 Crore Sustainable Packaging Success, The Better India]

The company's product portfolio includes speciality paper, moulded-fibre food-service products and packaging made from agricultural residue. Its operations use sugarcane residue as a principal raw material, and biomass-based energy generation has been incorporated into its manufacturing processes. [ref: Yash Pakka: Packaging with Care Never Comes to an End, Food Infotech]

In 2022, YourStory reported that the company's products were being used by businesses including Rebel Foods, Haldiram's, Cafe Coffee Day and Chai Point, and that the company operated in more than 30 countries at the time. In 2023, The Telegraph India reported that Yash Pakka distributed its products in 43 countries and worked with more than 40 commercial partners.

==CHUK==
CHUK is Pakka's brand of compostable food-service tableware, developed as the company expanded from paper manufacturing into moulded-fibre products made from sugarcane residue. The brand produces food-service items including plates, bowls and containers, developed as alternatives to conventional single-use plastic and expanded-polystyrene food-service products. The Telegraph India reported in 2023 that CHUK formed part of Yash Pakka's wider expansion into agricultural-residue packaging alongside its paper operations.
[truncated]

Kristin Stoneking is an American Methodist bishop.

== Life ==

She was ordained a deacon in 1995 and elder in 1998 by Bishop Alfred Frederick Mutti in the Kansas East Conference. Okko The Exiled is an action-adventure platform game developed by Frozen Flame Interactive and published by Eastasiasoft Limited. The game was released for Windows and macOS on September 30, 2026, with console versions planned for 2027. [ref: Gorgeously animated 2D action-adventure Okko The Exiled is OUT NOW for PC, eastasiasoft]

The game is set in Kutala, a land inhabited by demons, and follows Okko, who sets out to defeat the Demon Lord Yalda and fulfill an ancient oath. [ref: Okko The Exiled, Steam]

== Gameplay ==
Okko The Exiled is a 2D side-scrolling action-adventure game featuring platforming, real-time combat and exploration. Players control Okko as he travels through Kutala, fighting enemies and bosses while acquiring new abilities. [ref: Okko The Exiled, eastasiasoft]

The game features hand-drawn pixel-art animation, combat abilities that allow Okko to stomp, launch and deflect enemies, and a hub area known as the Old Throne. Players can also collect Deevols, which unlock additional challenge levels.

Reviews have described the game as a 2D action platformer with some Metroidvania-style progression and an emphasis on exploration and secrets. [ref: Review: Okko the Exiled, Movies, Games and Tech]

== Plot ==
The game is set in Kutala, a land of demons ruled by the Demon Lord Yalda. Okko is a young horned demon who has spent much of his life isolated from the wider world. He eventually sets out on a quest that involves defeating the rulers of Kutala and fulfilling an ancient oath. [ref: Análise: Okko The Exiled não revoluciona, mas traz uma bela e satisfatória experiência de ação 2D, GameBlast]

== Development ==
Okko The Exiled was developed by independent studio Frozen Flame Interactive in cooperation with Eastasiasoft. Frozen Flame Interactive was founded by Matthew Strnad, who had previously developed the platform game Robozarro. [ref: Pixel art action platformer Okko The Exiled arrives on consoles and PC in late 2025, eastasiasoft]

The game was presented at the Tokyo Game Show in 2025 and subsequently featured a playable demo during Steam Next Fest.

== Release ==
Okko The Exiled was released digitally for Windows and macOS through Steam and GOG.com on September 30, 2026. The standard edition was priced at US$14.99, while a deluxe edition containing the digital soundtrack was priced at US$19.99.

Console versions for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S are planned for early 2027.

== Reception ==
Okko The Exiled received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its pixel-art presentation, animation, combat, boss encounters, progression system and musical score. Criticism focused primarily on aspects of its controls, platforming, puzzles and level design. [ref: Review: Okko the Exiled, Movies, Games and Tech] [ref: Okko The Exiled – Recensione PC, GameSource] [ref: Análise: Okko The Exiled não revoluciona, mas traz uma bela e satisfatória experiência de ação 2D, GameBlast] [ref: Okko The Exiled, Pizza Fria] [ref: Review – Okko The Exiled, Gamestic] [ref: Okko The Exiled Steam Review – Welcomed Home Or Sent Away?, Retro News]

Movies, Games & Tech and GameSource both rated the game 7 out of 10. Movies, Games & Tech praised its level design, secrets and boss encounters, while criticizing aspects of its controls and traversal mechanics. GameSource highlighted the combat system, progression and visual presentation, while criticizing the predictability of some enemies and aspects of the game's movement and Focus Mode.

GameBlast gave the game 7.5 out of 10, praising its controls, character mobility, pixel art, boss fights and story, while finding that some mechanics were underused and that certain levels were unnecessarily prolonged. Pizza Fria rated the game 6.5 out of 10, praising its visual presentation and progression while criticizing the long levels, repetitive use of the soundtrack and some platforming mechanics.

Gamestic gave a cautiously positive assessment, praising the hand-drawn pixel art, animations, character designs, soundtrack and boss encounters. The review criticized the controls during tight platforming sections and described several progression puzzles as unclear. The reviewer reported encountering softlocks that could be resolved by reloading the game. They also noted that the soundtrack is impressive, though could become repetitive because the same track is used across two full stages.

Retro News gave a strongly positive assessment, praising the game's level structure, secrets, difficulty curve, combat system, pixel art, animation and soundtrack. The review described the gameplay and presentation as excellent and considered the game a strong value for its price, recommending it to action-platformer fans.

Melon Sandbox (previously known as Melon Playground) is a free-to-play 2D physics-based sandbox video game developed by DUCKY LTD and published by Playducky.com, originally released in 2021. The game allows players to conduct open-ended physics experiments using ragdoll characters, weapons, vehicles, and interactive objects.

== Gameplay ==

Melon Sandbox is a two-dimensional ragdoll physics simulation in which players freely arrange characters, weapons, and objects on a map and observe the resulting physics interactions. The game provides no objectives or win conditions. Progression is entirely self-directed.

Players choose from a variety of maps, including open plains, mountainous terrain, underwater environments, and enclosed rooms, and populate scenes using an item menu that contains firearms, melee weapons, explosives, vehicles, syringes with status effects, mechanical components, and biological characters called Livings [ref: ]. Characters react to damage, temperature, electricity, and fluids through a layered physics model that simulates the effects of bleeding, burning, freezing, and dismemberment. A time-scale slider lets players slow or pause the simulation, enabling complex chain reactions and cinematic replays. Scenes can be saved, exported, and shared.

In 2026, version 36.0 introduced an in-game object known as the Lua Chip, which allows players to inject custom Lua scripts to program complex logic, custom timings, and dynamic object interactions within the sandbox environment, introducing coding to the game. Later that year, version 38.0 introduced multiplayer support [ref: Melon Sandbox Multiplayer Update Lets Four Players Build Chaos Together, Kicks & Grips].

=== Creator Ecosystem ===
Beyond its core gameplay, Melon Sandbox features a creator economy in which players design, publish, and monetize user-generated content (UGC) through an in-game Workshop [ref: Ragdoll Sandbox 'Melon Sandbox' Celebrates 5th Anni, DayOne]. The Workshop uses an in-game currency called Mels. Players purchase Mels with real-world currency to spend on community-created content. A portion of the payment is distributed back to the original creator. Creators can convert accumulated Mels into real-world currency through a cash-out mechanism [ref: Melon Sandbox: 150m installs and UGC evolution, www.pocketgamer.biz].

== Release and ==
The game was originally released on August 27, 2021 under the name Melon Playground. The developer aimed to adapt free-form, realistic physics experimentation to mobile touchscreen controls.

= Progressive Democratic Students' Union (PDSU) =
The Progressive Democratic Students' Union (PDSU) is a leftist student organisation in India. George Reddy is considered the founder of PDSU, [ref: 'PDSU founder George Reddy was AP’s Che Guevara', The New Indian Express] although PDSU's official formation happened after George Reddy's death. [ref: ‘George was fearless and continues to be an inspiration', The Hindu]

=== History ===
George Reddy, a student leader and activist, used to publish pamphlets under the label of PDS, which became a state-level organisation following his assassination in 1972. PDS formally changed its name in 1974, leading to the formation of PDSU. [ref: Keeping the Dream Alive: In Memory of George Reddy, Mission Telangana] PDSU is active in Telangana (particularly in Nizamabad and Khammam), Andhra Pradesh and New Delhi. [ref: Progressive Democratic Students Union holds 22nd conference in Nizamabad, Countercurrents] [ref: PDSU lays siege to Bhatti, Thummala offices over Rs. 8,200 crore student dues, Telangana Today] [ref: PDSU protests against privatisation of medical colleges in Andhra, The Hindu] [ref: PDSU alleges linguistic discrimination against non-Hindi-speaking student at JNU, theprint.in] [ref: JNU Student Alleges Linguistic Discrimination and Academic Harassment, dailypioneer.com]

=== Activism ===

==== 2024 protest against delay in release of scholarships and fee reimbursement ====
PDSU Telangana protested outside the State Legislative Assembly in Hyderabad demanding release of scholarships and fee reimbursements. The demands also included allocation of 30% of the state budget to education, justice for the victims of the NEET UG question paper leak, and filling up of the vacant teaching and non-teaching positions in the universities. [ref: Hyderabad: PDSU activists stage protests outside Assembly demanding release of scholarships, fee reimbursement, Telangana Today]

==== 2025 protest against privatisation of medical colleges in Andhra Pradesh ====
In 2025, PDSU demanded that the Andhra Pradesh government revoke the steps taken towards privatisation of medical education. It said that the increasing rate of privatisation of medical colleges would affect students from SC, ST and OBC minority communities. [ref: PDSU protests against privatisation of medical colleges in Andhra, The Hindu]

==== 2026 campaign against academic harassment and linguistic imposition ====
In 2026, PDSU accused an assistant professor at the Jawaharlal Nehru University, New Delhi, of academic harassment and Hindi imposition and demanded an impartial, time-bound inquiry into the assistant professor's actions to ensure a safe learning environment for students. [ref: JNU Student Alleges Linguistic Discrimination and Academic Harassment, dailypioneer.com] [ref: Delhi NCR News: जेएनयू में गैर हिंदी भाषी छात्रा के उत्पीड़न का सहायक प्रोफेसर पर लगा आरोप, Amar Ujala]

Draft: Murder of Jeanie Seton

Draft text:
The murder of Jeanie Seton, also known as the Ratho murder, was committed at Ratho in Midlothian, Scotland, on 16 April 1864 by George Bryce.

Bryce was convicted of murder at the High Court of Justiciary and publicly executed on 21 June 1864. His execution was the last public execution to take place in Edinburgh.

== Background ==
Jeanie Seton – also known as Jane or Janie Watt – born 1841, was a nurse (nanny), working for the family of the grain merchant Robert Tod and his wife Margaret in Ratho, Midlothian. [ref: Cowan H. Report of the Trial of George Bryce for Murder. Edinb Med J. 1864 Jul;10(1):76-92. PMID: 29646165; PMCID: PMC5311517.] [ref: Cunningham, S. (1899). Inverkeithing, North Queensferry, Limekilns, Charlestown & The Ferry Hills (1st ed.). Dunfermline: W. Clark & Son.]

George Bryce, born 1829, lived in Ratho and was the romantic interest of Isabella Brown, neighbour of Jeanie Seton. In March 1863, Brown distanced herself from Bryce. Bryce believed Seton was behind this.

== The murder ==

On 16 April, at approximately 7 am, Bryce entered the Tod's house. He asked the house cook for the whereabouts of Jeanie Seaton; the cook told him that Seaton was in the nursery and that he could not see her. Bryce ignored the cook, entered the nursery, and attacked Seton. Her screams attracted the attention of the cook and Mrs Tod, who attempted to intervene. The cook was bitten by Bryce while trying to help Seaton. [ref: The Ratho Murder, www.thegenealogist.co.uk]

Seaton escaped the Tods' house but was followed by Bryce. She was found outside the neighbouring house with her throat cut. She died from her injuries. Witnesses reported that Bryce had stomped on her body.

Bryce fled the area. He later asked an acquaintance, Davidson, to cut his throat, claiming that he had attempted to do so himself. Davidson refused and, having learned of the murder, pursued Bryce with a group of local quarrymen. Bryce reached the railway line near Ratho station, where he was intercepted by railway navvies. He was restrained and taken to Ratho police station.

== The trial ==
Bryce was tried at the High Court of Justiciary in Edinburgh in June 1864. His defence argued that he was insane; evidence was given that Bryce had been known locally as "Daft Geordie Bryce". The jury found him guilty, but recommended leniency, citing the "low organisation of his mental faculties".

Included in trial evidence was the razor used in Seton's murder. [ref: NRS Catalogue - browse - details of record, catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk]

The court sentenced him to death, with the execution scheduled for 21 June 1864. [ref: NRS Catalogue - catalogue record, catalogue.nrscotland.gov.uk]

== Execution ==
Before his execution, Bryce reportedly acknowledged that murder was a crime and that he should be punished.

Bryce was hanged at Edinburgh on 21 June 1864 at approximately 8:20am. His body was removed from the scaffold at about 9am. His execution took place on the corner of the present-day George VI Bridge and The Royal Mile, now the site of the French Consulate. [ref: The Maiden: The Scottish beheading machine, National Museums Scotland] [ref: The Hidden History of Public Executions in Edinburgh, www.escapethepast.co.uk] [ref: Site of the Last Public Execution in Edinburgh Historical Marker, www.hmdb.org]

The execution attracted a large crowd; contemporary reports describe disorderly behaviour among the spectators, including singing, drinking and fighting.
File:Post execution of George Bryce, the Ratho Murderer, by Dr John Smith.jpg|Post execution sketch of George Bryce by Dr John Smith of the Royal College of Surgeons, Edinburgh.
File:Brass tile of the site of the last public execution in Edinburgh.jpg|Commemorative plaque on the Royal Mile for the site of the execution.
File:The Death Mask of George Bryce, 1864.jpg|George Bryce death mask, from the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh archives.

=== Newspaper reports ===
The Dunfermline Saturday Press of 25 June, 1864 p.4 reported: ″On making the fatal plunge, the body remained in perfect stillness for the space of about thirty seconds, after which a slight tremor of the spinal cord, a clutching of the fingers, and a slight drawing in of the foot were the only movements perceptible. There was no struggle whatsoever indicative of suffering".

The Dundee Courier of June 22nd, 1864 reported: “The body fell three feet, and entirely disappeared from the view of the public.″

The Southern Reporter of June 23rd, 1864 reported: “Only the rope being seen, the vast crowd began immediately to disappear.″

“The Times of June 22, 1864 reported: ”The executioner drew the bolt, and, with a few slight struggles, the convict expired".

== Aftermath ==
Following Bryce's arrest, Seaton's mother had reportedly been so distressed by her daughter's death that she was taken to an asylum.

Jane Seton is buried at Hope Street Cemetery, Inverkeithing. Her memorial stone reads:JANE SEATON, aged 23 years.

I know O Lord that Thy judgements are right

Into thine hand I commit my spirit, Thou hast redeemed me O Lord God of Truth, Psalm XXXI, 5.
Erected by the children to whom she was nurse as a mark of their love.George Bryce would be the last person hung in public in Edinburgh. Hanging as a form of punishment continued in Edinburgh until 1954. [ref: hiddenscotland.com]

Pamela Lowell is an American licensed clinical social worker, watercolor artist, and author. [ref: BookShelf: Trauma Specialist Offers Ospreys As 'Gateway Drug' to Nature, SEJournal Online] She is known for her professional and creative work intersecting trauma psychotherapy, environmental stewardship, and wildlife art, which is the subject of her 2024 nature memoir My Summer with Ospreys. [ref: Meet Pamela Lowell, CanvasRebel]

== Education and Career ==
Lowell earned her Master of Social Work (MSW) from Rutgers University in 1984. [ref: Ms. Pamela A. Lowell LICSW, AAO Education Hub] She has operated a private psychotherapy practice since 2001, specializing in the clinical treatment of complex emotional trauma, anxiety, and depression.

From 2008 to 2015, Lowell served as a clinical consultant for Adoption Rhode Island, providing agency and state-wide training, program evaluation, and specialized supervision for complex foster care cases. [ref: Pamela Lowell, MSW, LICSW - Bio and Press, PamelaLowell.com] [ref: Pamela Lowell Profile, LinkedIn] For her contributions, she received the organization's Community Partner Award in 2008. She was also the clinical director at Turning the Corner Group Homes, where she designed and implemented agency-wide trauma-informed care using the Attachment, Regulation and Competency (ARC) framework. Additionally, she has served on the adjunct faculty at Rhode Island College.

== Art and Activism ==
As a visual artist, Lowell creates large-scale watercolor paintings depicting New England salt marshes and regional avian species. Her painting Breakfast on the Marsh (2023) was chosen for the Roger Tory Peterson Institute's juried exhibition Art that Matters to the Planet: Wild America, curated by ornithologist Kenn Kaufman. [ref: Art that Matters to the Planet: Wild America, Roger Tory Peterson Institute] In August 2024, the Cape Cod Museum of Art hosted her for a presentation focused on wildlife translocation and environmental art. [ref: Presentation: My Summer with Ospreys with Author, Artist, and Trauma therapist Pamela Lowell, Cape Cod Museum of Art] She volunteers for the Mass Audubon South Coast Osprey Project, assisting with nest monitoring and population data collection, and routinely donates portions of her art proceeds to environmental non-profits.

== Literary Works ==
Lowell has authored four books:

* Returnable Girl (Marshall Cavendish, 2006) – A young adult novel following a 13-year-old girl navigating the foster care and adoption systems. [ref: Returnable Girl Review, Booklist] The novel received the International Reading Association (IRA) Young Adult Choices designation and was named to VOYA's Top Shelf Fiction list.
* Spotting for Nellie (2010) – A young adult fiction novel.
* My Summer with Ospreys: A Therapist's Journey Toward Hope, Community, and Healing Our Planet (Stillwater River Publications, 2024) – A non-fiction narrative weaving wildlife monitoring with trauma therapy concepts, featuring original watercolor illustrations.

== Reception ==
Lowell's literary work has received recognition from major literary and conservation outlets. Kirkus Reviews praised Returnable Girl for its authentic, "convincing portrait" of troubled adolescents, citing Lowell's real-world clinical expertise as a family therapist. [ref: Returnable Girl, Kirkus Reviews] Booklist noted the novel sensitively captures the emotional reality of betrayal and longing within the foster care system.

Her 2024 memoir, My Summer with Ospreys, was reviewed by Tom Henry for the Society of Environmental Journalists, who described it as a "breezy, loose narrative" that effectively bridges mental health counseling with climate awareness. Rebecca Minardi of the American Birding Association commended the book's ability to frame environmental grief through the lens of trauma therapy while maintaining a heartfelt, human tone. [ref: Finding Community in Ospreys, American Birding Association] Additional commentary from the West Virginia Highlands Conservancy praised the integration of her watercolor artwork within the environmental narrative. [ref: Close-up with Ospreys: Book Review, West Virginia Highlands Conservancy]

Draft: Pagurixus jerviensis

Draft text:
----

Pagurixus jerviensis is a species of hermit crab in the family Paguridae. It was described in 1984 by the carcinologists Patsy A. McLaughlin and Janet Haig as part of their revision of the genus Pagurixus, and is known from Jervis Bay and other parts of the coast of New South Wales, Australia, as well as Lord Howe Island. Australian specimens had previously been misidentified as Eupagurus lacertosus, a distinct species, before being recognised as new. [ref: A review of Pagurixus (Decapoda, Anomura, Paguridae) and descriptions of new species, Crustaceana]

==Taxonomy==

The genus Pagurixus was established by Melin in 1939 as a monotypic subgenus of Eupagurus, with Eupagurus (Pagurixus) boninensis from the Bonin (Ogasawara) Islands as its only species. Several additional species from across the Indo-Pacific were subsequently referred to the subgenus, but almost all were known from one or very few specimens, and the group remained poorly understood.

In their 1984 review of the group, based on material from major museums in the United States, Europe and Australia, McLaughlin and Haig concluded that Pagurixus warranted generic rank. Alongside redescriptions of the previously named species, they described P. jerviensis as new. The species has since been treated as valid in the world checklist of anomuran decapod crustaceans. [ref: Annotated checklist of anomuran decapod crustaceans of the world (exclusive of the Kiwaoidea and families Chirostylidae and Galatheidae of the Galatheoidea). Part I – Lithodoidea, Lomisoidea and Paguroidea, The Raffles Bulletin of Zoology]

Australian material now assigned to P. jerviensis had earlier been reported in the literature as Eupagurus lacertosus or Pagurus lacertosus, for example by Pope (1947), Dakin and coauthors (1948–1960), Griffin (1967) and Healy & Yaldwyn (1970), but these records did not represent that species, P. lacertosus (Henderson, 1888).

The holotype is a male (shield length 2.6 mm) collected by P. Berents on 24 May 1980 at a depth of 18 m on the north face of Bowen Island, Jervis Bay, New South Wales; it is deposited in the Australian Museum in Sydney (registration AM P33836). Paratypes from Jervis Bay, Shell Harbour, Long Reef near Collaroy, the open New South Wales coast and Lord Howe Island are held in the Allan Hancock Foundation (Los Angeles), the Rijksmuseum van Natuurlijke Historie (Leiden), the United States National Museum and other collections.

==Etymology==

The specific name evidently refers to Jervis Bay, the type locality of the species.

==Description==

Pagurixus jerviensis is a minute species: the shield, the hardened anterior portion of the carapace, measured 1.0–4.3 mm in length in the material examined. As in other hermit crabs, the soft abdomen is protected by an empty gastropod shell. Like other species of the genus, it shows pronounced sexual dimorphism in the right cheliped: the right chela of large males becomes swollen or elongate and loses much of the armature seen in females and small males, with the corneous cutting teeth replaced by strong calcareous teeth.

Within the genus, P. jerviensis belongs to the group of species lacking rows of setae on the underside of the terminal segment of the antennular peduncle. It is distinguished from its congeners by the short, stout dactyls of the second pereopods, each with 7–10 corneous spines on the ventral margin, by the dorsal row of spines on the dactyl of the left chela, and by the telson, whose terminal margins are straight and armed with 2–4 strong spines, sometimes accompanied by a few spinules. Females have paired gonopores.

==Distribution and habitat==

The species is known from the coast of New South Wales, including Jervis Bay (Bowen Island and Boat Harbour), Shell Harbour and Long Reef near Collaroy,and from Lord Howe Island in the Tasman Sea. Known records span the intertidal zone to a depth of about 22 m.

==References==

Draft text:
Drag Syndrome is a British drag performance collective composed of drag queens and drag kings with Down syndrome. The collective was founded in London in 2018 by choreographer and artistic director Daniel Vais and developed from his work with performers with Down syndrome through Culture Device Dance Project. [ref: Drag Syndrome: A collective opening up drag for people with Down's Syndrome, Dazed] [ref: The Drag Troupe For Kings and Queens With Learning Disabilities, Vice]

The group's performances combine drag, dance, lip-sync, costume, movement, humour and audience interaction. Since its formation, Drag Syndrome has performed in the United Kingdom and internationally at queer nightlife venues, festivals, Pride events and cultural institutions. Appearances have included Glastonbury Festival, RuPaul's DragCon UK, Berghain in Berlin, Somerset House in London and the Münchner Kammerspiele in Munich. [ref: Line-Up 2023, Glastonbury Festival] [ref: Prepare To Be Blown Away By The Power Of Drag Syndrome, British Vogue] [ref: Drag Syndrome, Somerset House]

The collective has received media attention for its relationship to disability, sexuality, gender, artistic autonomy and queer culture. It has been profiled by outlets including Dazed, British Vogue, The Guardian, The Standard, PAPER, Gay Times, PinkNews, Vice and ITV News. [ref: Drag Syndrome: Inside the UK's first Down's syndrome drag night, ITV News]

==History==

===Formation and first performances===

Drag Syndrome developed from Culture Device Dance Project, an artistic company founded by Daniel Vais involving dancers and performers with Down syndrome.

According to accounts published by Vice and Dazed, the idea developed after Vais attended an event with actor and dancer Sarah Gordy where they saw drag performers. Gordy expressed an interest in experimenting with drag, and Vais subsequently discussed the idea with other artists from Culture Device. The performers began researching drag and developing their own stage identities.

Drag Syndrome gave its first public performance on 29 March 2018 at vFd, formerly Vogue Fabrics, an LGBTQ+ performance space in east London. Vice reported that the sold-out performance featured six artists. Following the response to the first event, the project developed into an ongoing performance collective.

A second event, Drag Syndrome 0.2, was held at Vogue Fabrics on 31 May 2018.

ITV News profiled the collective in June 2018, including performer Otto Baxter, whose drag persona is Horrora Shebang.

The collective subsequently became part of London's queer nightlife and performance scene and appeared at London Pride, the Royal Vauxhall Tavern and other queer cultural events.

Later in 2018 the collective performed at Alternative Miss World at Shakespeare's Globe.

PAPER published a feature on the group during its first year. Vais described the performers researching drag and developing individual characters rather than treating drag solely as costume. [ref: Drag Syndrome Shines a Light on Inclusivity, PAPER]

===International expansion===

During 2019 Drag Syndrome increased its activity outside London and the United Kingdom.

ITV News Wales covered members of the collective during a performance in Cardiff in June 2019. [ref: The drag act changing the way people think about Down's syndrome, ITV News Wales]

The collective also appeared at Montréal Pride in Canada. By November 2019, Dazed described Drag Syndrome as being on an international tour following performances in Britain and continental Europe.

The Dazed feature profiled Vais and performers including Horrora Shebang, Justin Bond and Gaia Callas and discussed the development of their individual drag identities.

The collective subsequently continued touring internationally, appearing at Pride events, theatres, festivals, clubs and cultural institutions.

===Michigan discrimination dispute===

In 2019, Drag Syndrome was scheduled to perform in Grand Rapids, Michigan, as part of a disability drag event organised by DisArt.

Peter Meijer, owner of the Tanglefoot Building where the performance was scheduled to take place, prevented Drag Syndrome from performing at the venue. Meijer said he had concerns about whether the artists were able to give "full and informed consent" to participate in drag. [ref: ACLU files formal complaint against Peter Meijer, Michigan Public]

DisArt and the American Civil Liberties Union of Michigan challenged the decision, and the ACLU filed a formal discrimination complaint.

Members of Drag Syndrome publicly rejected the suggestion that they were incapable of deciding whether they wished to perform drag. [ref: Drag collective Drag Syndrome kicked out of US venue after owner thought the performers didn't give their 'full and informed consent', Attitude]

The dispute generated international coverage and discussion about autonomy, sexuality and the rights of people with intellectual disabilities.

===DragCon and British Vogue===

In January 2020, Drag Syndrome performed at the inaugural RuPaul's DragCon UK in London.

Filmmaker Jess Kohl followed members of the collective during the event for a short documentary titled Drag Syndrome, commissioned by British Vogue for its 2020 Pride film series.

The film followed the performers preparing for and performing at DragCon UK and explored their individuality, gender expression and artistic practice.

Draft text:
----

Li–Campeau syndrome (LICAS) is a rare autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in both copies of the UBR7 gene. Reported features include developmental delay, intellectual disability, distinctive facial features, hypothyroidism, and variable heart and genital abnormalities. [ref: Li-Campeau syndrome (Concept ID: C5543068), MedGen] [ref: Eighth case of Li-Campeau syndrome in a Turkish patient caused by a novel pathogenic variant in UBR7 and expanding the phenotype, American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A]

== Signs and symptoms ==
In the original series, seven children from six unrelated families were evaluated between the ages of two and ten years. All had global developmental delay and intellectual disability. Low muscle tone was common, and some children had no speech. Six had seizures beginning in infancy or early childhood. [ref: Li-Campeau syndrome; LICAS, Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man]

Other findings in that series included cardiac abnormalities in five children, hypothyroidism in four, and short stature in five. All six boys had genital abnormalities, predominantly undescended testes; one also had a small penis. Two siblings had microcephaly. These counts describe the original cohort.

Reported facial features include drooping upper eyelids, widely spaced eyes, a prominent forehead, thick eyebrows, low-set ears, and a long philtrum. Strabismus, epicanthal folds, downward-slanting eyelid openings, and a high-arched palate have also been described. Less common findings include scoliosis, increased body hair, underdeveloped kneecaps, long fingers, a single transverse palmar crease, and gastrointestinal dysmotility.

Cardiac findings have included atrial and ventricular septal defects, patent ductus arteriosus, and patent foramen ovale. Brain imaging was performed in four children in the initial cohort. Reported abnormalities included enlarged ventricles, cortical atrophy, a thin corpus callosum, delayed myelination, and nonspecific white matter changes.

== Genetics ==
The condition is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in UBR7, located on chromosome 14q32.12. The variants identified in the original families segregated with the disorder in a pattern consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

Reported variants included frameshift, nonsense, splice-site, and missense variants, as well as an intragenic deletion. The investigators predicted a loss-of-function mechanism. Although variant-specific functional studies were not performed, cells obtained from three patients showed loss of UBR7 protein.

In an independent case reported in 2023, an affected child had a homozygous splice-site variant, while each parent carried one copy. The investigators predicted that the variant would impair UBR7 function.

== Diagnosis ==
In the original cohort, the genetic findings were identified through exome or genome sequencing. In the 2023 case report, exome sequencing identified the UBR7 variant, and Sanger sequencing confirmed its presence in the child and carrier status in the parents.

== History ==
Li and colleagues described seven affected individuals with biallelic UBR7 variants in a study published online in December 2020 and in the January 2021 issue of the American Journal of Human Genetics. [ref: UBR7 functions with UBR5 in the Notch signaling pathway and is involved in a neurodevelopmental syndrome with epilepsy, ptosis, and hypothyroidism, American Journal of Human Genetics] An additional case was reported by Edizadeh and colleagues in 2023.
==Research==
Experiments involving the Caenorhabditis elegans counterpart of UBR7 identified developmental defects and altered Notch signaling in germline stem cells, suggesting a role for the protein in developmental signaling.

In 2023, researchers generated an induced pluripotent stem cell line from blood cells of a seven-year-old boy with the syndrome. The patient carried two different UBR7 variants. [ref: Establishment of a novel human induced pluripotent stem cell line (SIPDi001-A) with compound heterozygous mutations in the UBR7 gene from a Li-Campeau syndrome patient, Stem Cell Research]

John O’Leary is an American business executive who is the President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Daimler Truck North America (DTNA). He assumed the role on April 1, 2021, succeeding Roger Nielsen. [ref: John O’Leary to Succeed Roger Nielsen as CEO of DTNA, Transport Topics] He is also a member of the Board of Management of Daimler Truck Holding AG, representing the North American region. [ref: Daimler Truck extends John O’Leary’s term on management board, FreightWaves]

O’Leary has been cited in national and business media in connection with U.S. manufacturing trends, tariffs, and the transition to electric vehicles. In coverage by The New York Times, he commented on the impact of tariffs on domestic steel pricing, noting that U.S. producers had “more headroom” to raise prices. [ref: U.S. Steel Producers Raise Prices After Tariffs Stymie Imports, The New York Times] He has also been quoted in The Wall Street Journal regarding infrastructure limitations affecting the adoption of electric heavy-duty trucks. [ref: Sales of Electric Heavy-Duty Trucks Are Hitting a Regulatory Wall, The Wall Street Journal]

O’Leary previously served as Chief Transformation Officer and Head of Mercedes-Benz Trucks in Germany from 2020 to 2021, and earlier was Chief Financial Officer of DTNA from 2012 to 2020. [ref: Daimler Trucks NA Names New CEO, School Bus Fleet] In 2024, he joined the board of directors of Portland General Electric. [ref: John O'Leary will join Portland General Electric board of directors, effective January 1, 2024, Portland General Electric] That same year, he co-chaired Oregon’s Clean Tech Manufacturing Task Force alongside Governor Tina Kotek and U.S. Senator Ron Wyden. [ref: Governor Kotek Releases Clean Tech Manufacturing Task Force Recommendations, Office of the Governor of Oregon]

== Career ==

O’Leary began his career in the commercial vehicle industry in 1989 at Paccar. He joined Freightliner (now DTNA) in 2000, where he held several leadership roles, including Internal Audit Director. He later served as President and CEO of Thomas Built Buses from 2002 to 2010, followed by Senior Vice President for DTNA’s aftermarket business from 2010 to 2012.

In 2012, O’Leary was appointed Chief Financial Officer of DTNA, a position he held until 2020. [ref: Daimler Truck extends John O’Leary’s term on management board, FreightWaves] In September 2020, he relocated to Germany to serve as Chief Transformation Officer and interim head of Mercedes-Benz Trucks.

Following the retirement of DTNA CEO Roger Nielsen, O’Leary was named President and CEO effective April 1, 2021. [ref: John O’Leary to Succeed Roger Nielsen as CEO of DTNA, Transport Topics] After the spin-off and public listing of Daimler Truck Holding AG on December 10, 2021, he joined the company’s Board of Management, representing North America. [ref: Daimler Truck launched on stock exchange as an independent company, Daimler Truck]

During his tenure, O’Leary has been cited in industry and business publications in connection with market transitions in the North American Class 8 truck sector, including supply chain disruptions, tariffs, and shifts in demand. [ref: DTNA’s O’Leary Reflects on Time of Transition for Company, Class 8 Market, Transport Topics] He has also been referenced in reporting on DTNA’s investments in electric truck development and engineering in the United States, including projects in Portland, Oregon, [ref: Daimler goes big on electrics in Portland, Portland Business Journal] as well as broader industry trends such as partnerships and acquisitions among truck manufacturers. [ref: Truck makers pursue acquisitions and joint ventures, Axios] Additional reporting has noted the company’s strategic focus on expanding its vocational truck segment in response to changing market conditions. [ref: As on-highway sales slump, DTNA sees opportunity for Western Star, FleetOwner]

In October 2023, the Daimler Truck Supervisory Board extended his management board term through March 2026. [ref: Daimler Truck extends John O’Leary’s term on management board, FreightWaves]

O’Leary’s tenure as president was marked by a focus on modernizing production and expanding technological capabilities. In August 2026, DTNA announced plans to build a new truck manufacturing facility in the United States. [ref: Daimler Truck plans to build a new truck production facility in the USA, FinanzNachrichten] [ref: Daimler Truck expands US business with new plant, Reuters] [ref: Daimler Truck Eyes New USA Plant, North American Orders Surge, Bloomberg] Following the announcement, O’Leary commented, “We want to have the best, most modern plants out there, because we know that will give us a best-cost position.” The expansion followed the company’s plans to upgrade technology across its manufacturing operations. O’Leary added that the new facility would “strengthen our ability to deliver industry-leading products while supporting long-term growth in the United States.” [ref: Daimler Truck North America Plans to Build New U.S. Manufacturing Facility, Daimler Truck]

In December 2025, he entered Forbes Italias ranking of Italian billionaires in 62nd place, with an estimated net worth of US$1.5 billion. [ref: Crescono i miliardari italiani: sono 79. Ferrero sempre in testa, Forbes Italia]

== Early life and education ==

Ghirelli was born in Rome in 1980. [ref: This Italian Entrepreneur Became A Billionaire Investing In India. Up Next: Space And AI, Forbes] He studied civil engineering at the University of Rome. [ref: Filippo Ghirelli, Confassociazioni] He earned an MBA and a master's degree in Financial Markets from LUISS Business School and completed a specialization at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.[ [ref: TEDxYouth@ISMonaco: Meet our speakers, International School of Monaco]

== Career ==

=== Infrastructure and Genera Group ===

Ghirelli began his career working as a project engineer on infrastructure projects in West Africa, including Guinea, Ghana and Mali, and Turkey for multinational enterprises such as Astaldi. He came back to Italy in 2006 for high-speed rail projects and became general manager at De Angelis Group in 2007

In 2009, Ghirelli established a construction and project development business, which evolved into Genera Group, later integrated into Mareterra Group Holding. He invested in projects in Italy, Morocco and Egypt. Political unrest in Egypt in 2013 affected those projects, and he shifted the company's focus to industrial energy efficiency in Italy. In 2013, he also co-founded the sustainable energy trading platform OV Energy in partnership with UniCredit and WWF's Officinae Verdi. [ref: Interview, YouTube]

In 2017, Ghirelli sold 49% of the company to the German investment group IKAV, but bought it back in 2020. He then sold a 75% share to the Swiss manager SUSI Partners. SUSI bought the remaining 25% in December 2024, after which Ghirelli resigned from Genera's board. [ref: SUSI Partners Acquires Remaining Stake in Italian Energy Service Company Genera Group, SUSI Partners]

=== Nayara Energy and Infracorp ===

In January 2023, Hara Capital (a part of Mareterra Group) bought a 24.5% share in Nayara Energy, an Indian company with a refinery in Vadinar. [ref: Hara Capital Sarl completes purchase of Trafigura's interest in Nayara Energy, Trafigura] The investment initially included plans to develop biofuel production for aviation, although these plans did not proceed.

In 2024, Ghirelli founded Infracorp, a global tech-infrastructure holding firm, and acquired Riviera Airport in northern Italy to develop it for private aviation and logistics. [ref: Villanova, aeroporto ceduto da Toussaint al gruppo Infracorp, Il Secolo XIX] [ref: Aeroporto di Villanova d’Albenga: Infracorp compra la maggioranza da Clemens Toussaint, Eco di Savona]

== Sport ==
In 2014, Filippo Ghirelli was in talks to buy the Mallorca football club. [ref: Filippo Ghirelli está dispuesto a comprar el Mallorca, MARCA.com] [ref: 'Quiero pensar que llego al Mallorca para quedarme', ELMUNDO]

== Personal life and other activities ==

Ghirelli resides in Monaco with his wife Daniela and their two children. [ref: Pictures: Venice collides with Monaco at Dreaming in Azur charity gala, Monaco Life] The couple founded the Venetian Arts Foundation, which held a charity gala in support of the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation.

He is a former vice-president of environment and energy at Confassociazioni. In July 2024, he was named co-chair of the Monaco Ambassadors Club alongside Christian Moore. [ref: Brazil in the spotlight at Monaco Ambassadors Club’s annual Summer Party, Monaco Life] An International School of Monaco speaker profile lists him as a member of the Prince Albert II of Monaco Foundation. He is also a TEDx speaker. [ref: ISM holds third TEDxYouth event, International School of Monaco]
