James Patrick "Jimmy" Sullivan, [ref: Powerless] [ref: See the Voices Behind Your Favorite 'Monsters, Inc.' Characters, Entertainment Weekly] often nicknamed Sulley, is a fictional character and one of the main protagonist of the Disney/Pixar's Monsters Inc. franchise, alongside Mike Wazowski. He is primarily voiced by John Goodman. Sulley was a former student at Monsters University before getting expelled, but was able to work at Monsters Incorporated, going from a mailroom worker, to the top scarer, to CEO.

Sulley has been generally well received by critics and audiences for his character, his kind-hearted nature from the first film, and Goodman's performance.

== Creation ==
Throughout production of 2001's Monster, Inc., Sulley had received numerous revisions. In an early concept for the film, Sulley, originally named Johnson, was an up-and-comer at Monsters, Inc., nervous about the possibility of him losing his job after his boss announces a downsizing. Johnson also feels envious due to another scarer, Ned (later renamed Randall), being the company's top performer. Throughout various drafts, Johnson's occupation went back and forth between scarer and some other position such as a janitor, a refinery worker or an assistant to Ned, until eventually given his final incarnation as the top scarer of Monsters, Inc. [ref: ]

Sulley had also received various redesigns. He originally had tentacles, but were scrapped due to them them being too difficult to animate for the time and to avoid distracting the audiences. [ref: Early Tests. Commentary by Thomas Porter, Steve May and Michael Fong, Monsters Inc. 2002 DVD.] He was also planned to wear glasses throughout the film, with test footage depicting the character with them already created. However, the creators abandoned the idea as they found the eyes were perfectly readable and a clear way of expressing a character's personality.

Bill Murray was considered for the voice role of Sulley. [ref: Bill Murray And the Roles that Got Away, Best Movies by Farr] [ref: 3 Comedians Who Screen Tested For Famous Animated Movies, VICE] While Murray had screen-tested for the role and was interested, Pete Docter, director of Monsters, Inc., among other filmmakers, were unable to make contact with him to formally offer the part. [ref: That Time Bill Murray Was Offered the Role of Sulley in Monsters Inc., TVovermind] [ref: Spotlight on Bill Murray & my Top Five Favorite Roles, FLIXCHATTER FILM BLOG] [ref: Monsters, Inc., Blonde Episodes] [ref: 10 Not-So-Scary Facts About Monsters, Inc., Mental Floss] The role for Sulley was ultimately given to John Goodman, who had previously appeared in a number of Disney-released films, including Hollywood Pictures' Arachnophobia (1990) as Delbert McClintock, and Disney Animation's The Emperor's New Groove (2000) as Pacha. [ref: Eight Legs, Two Fangs and an Attitude: ‘Arachnophobia’ Turns 35, Bloody Disgusting!] [ref: ‘We’ll Never Make That Kind of Movie Again’, Vulture] John Kahrs, animator of Sulley, found that the "bearlike quality" of Goodman's voice provided an exceptionally good fit with the character, while Goodman compared him to an National Football League player, describing him as an "seasoned lineman in the tenth year of his career," and a "total pro."

== Role in the Monsters, Inc. series ==

=== Background ===
In Monsters, Inc., Sulley's best friend, roommate, and assistant, Mike Wazowski, mentioned to Sulley that he [Sulley] had been jealous of his looks since fourth grade, implying that they'd knew each other since childhood. While Monsters University retconned Mike's statement by establishing the two first meeting in the titular university, an deleted scene for the film had shown that the two did met in school. The scene was originally set to be the opening for the film before getting cut. [ref: Monsters University Deleted Scenes, Behind The Voice Actors] Another retconed statement from the first film was from the teaser trailer, in which Sulley reminds Mike of one time at fifth grade when Mike was putting notes while Sulley and the rest of their class was studying geography. [ref: Monsters, Inc. Trailer]

=== Monsters University ===

Sulley was accepted into the titular university's scaring program. In the film, he was initially portrayed as lazy and careless about school studies for the program. Sulley was also initially accepted as member of the Roar Omega Roar (RΩR) fraternity after its leader, Johnny Worthington III, noticed his skills for steeling and chasing a pig mascot named Archie from another school called Fear Tech. He was eventually kicked out from both the scaring program and RΩR for clashing with another program student, Mike, during the final exam and was moved to can designs, along with Mike. The two decides to join another fraternity, the Oozma Kappa (OK), so they can compete in the university's Scare Games as a way to rejoin the scaring program. Throughout all the training the competing for the game events, Mike and Sulley gotten along better as time gone. Ultimately, the Oozma Kappa became the champions of the year's Scare Games after winning the Simulated Scare event against RΩR, giving Sulley, Mike, and the rest of the Oozma Kappa, the opportunity to join the scaring program. However, Mike discovers that his scare simulator level was lowed down to easy. Sulley admitted that he tempered the simulator to ensure that Mike can get a high score.

= Jamon Jordan =
Jamon “Baba Jamon” Jordan (born January 19, 1971) is an American historian and educator and is the official historian of the City of Detroit. [ref: Jamon Jordan, Detroit’s unofficial historian, is now its official one, BridgeDetroit] He is also the founder of the Black Scroll Network, a Detroit-based organization which offers tours of African American historical sites throughout the city, and is also a lecturer at the University of Michigan, teaching a course in the university’s Semester in Detroit program called “From the Underground to Motown: A Course on Detroit’s History.” [ref: ] [ref: ]

== Early Life and Education ==
Jordan was born and raised in Highland Park and developed an early interest in Detroit’s Black architectural history through stories his grandmother told as a child. He learned about places such as Black Bottom, Paradise Valley, Gotham Hotel, Forest Club, and the Flame Show Bar, all of which weren’t well-documented at the time, though the stories gave him a vibrant picture of the places and people that inhabited these spaces. He was also raised in a household that valued reading, being introduced to works such as The Autobiography of Malcolm X at a young age, which furthered his interest in Black history as a child. [ref: A Storied History: Detroit’s African American Architectural History Lives on Through the Tours of Jamon Jordan, Michigan Architectural Foundation]

He became engaged in the intersection between activism and education during his time at Highland Park High School, where he and other students recognized the inadequate education they were receiving from their teacher. He and these other students would protest against their teacher's poor teaching job in-class, and as a result of this experience, he realized that he wanted to be more proactive as a student. [ref: Jordan, Jamon, Voices from the Grassroots]

He triple-majored in Black Studies, American Studies, and Sociology at Western Michigan University, gaining a more comprehensive view of Black history in the United States and Detroit’s role in it. Outside of class, he challenged racism on campus, joining clubs involved in African American culture and African American resistance to white supremacy, and began a newspaper called The Black Scroll. He graduated with a Bachelor of Science in Black Americana Studies and Sociology.

== Career ==

=== Educator ===
Jordan's first teaching job after returning to Detroit, following a brief stint in Kalamazoo, was at the Ben Carson Academy, a charter school within the Wayne County juvenile detention facility. This position was short-lived though, as he and everyone else who worked there lost their job after the privately-owned school lost their contract with the county.

After working briefly at another charter school in Inkster, he turned to the Nsoroma Institute, an African-centered school. Having read about it in the Michigan Citizen in high school, he saw Nsoroma as a natural fit as he thought his own approach to education was similarly African-centered. While there wasn’t an opening at the time of his interview, he returned two weeks later to follow up, and after teaching a class for another instructor who thought he already worked there, he quickly earned himself a position as a teaching assistant, with a job as a full-time instructor following shortly after. He worked at the Nsoroma Institute for 12 years until it closed in 2013.

Jordan has been part of the University of Michigan's faculty since the Fall 2021 semester, teaching the course “From the Underground to Motown: A Course on Detroit's History," part of the Semester in Detroit program.

=== Black Scroll Network, History & Tours ===
Jordan founded the Black Scroll Network later in 2013 following Nsoroma Institute's closure after providing years of educational tours to students and parents, offering the general public the same experience with African American history in Detroit that his students received. [ref: Jamon Jordan teaches the hidden Black histories of Detroit, Detroit Metro Times] The Black Scroll Network provides guided, educational tours to sites important to Black history in Detroit, with popular sites being Black Bottom, Paradise Valley, the Berry Gordy House, the Motown Museum, and the homes of Aretha Franklin and Rosa Parks. [ref: Historian Jamon Jordan shares the legacy of Black Detroit: "I'm just telling their story" - CBS Detroit, www.cbsnews.com] In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, Jordan contracted COVID and lost his mother, promptly ceasing in-person tours. It later shifted to a virtual format [ref: Local historian relaunches Detroit tour company after battling COVID-19, losing mom in 2020, WXYZ 7 News Detroit], with in-person tours returning in mid-2023.

=== Historian of Detroit ===
On October 25, 2021, former Detroit mayor Mike Duggan and City Director of Arts, Culture & Entrepreneurship Rochelle Riley announced that Jordan would be named the first official historian of Detroit.

As city historian, he has been appointed with the job of scouring the archives of Detroit's history and educating people about the stories that haven't been told, as well as reminding the citizens of the importance of the city's history. [ref: Detroit's first historian appointed to tell city's story, FOX 2 Detroit]

Draft text:
Danphone A/S is a Danish telecommunications and hardware company that manufactures coastal radio systems, NAVTEX equipment, AIS shore infrastructure, and testing devices for the Global Maritime Distress and Safety System (GMDSS). [ref: [https://profiler.dk/13640378 Danphone A/S Unternehmensprofil], Profiler.dk.] [ref: [https://oceannews.com/news/defense/danphone-selected-to-deliver-navtex-solution-to-ccg/ Danphone Selected To Deliver NAVTEX Solution To CCG], Ocean News & Technology, 26 August 2024.] The company is headquartered in Nørresundby, Denmark.

== History ==
Founded in 1990 in northern Denmark, Danphone initially focused on radio communication technology and has since expanded into complete maritime communication systems. [ref: [https://elek-data.dk/artikel/kommunikation-iot-og-cybersikkerhed/danske-danphone-skal-sikre-verdens-lngste-kystlinje Danske Danphone skal sikre verdens længste kystlinje], Elek-data.dk, 27 August 2024.] Over subsequent decades, the company shifted its primary operational focus toward shore-based maritime safety infrastructure and GMDSS-compliant testing equipment.

The company operates on an export model, supplying coastal infrastructure and radio testing equipment to national maritime authorities through public procurement contracts and regional infrastructure upgrades. [ref: [https://nordjyske.dk/erhverv/claus-falk-navigerer-i-en-branche-hvor-forretning-er-som-at-kaste-med-terninger/ Claus Falk navigerer i en branche, hvor forretning er "som at kaste med terninger"], Nordjyske.dk.]

== Operations and systems ==
Danphone manufactures shore-based maritime communication systems, coastal radio infrastructure, and radio inspection equipment designed to comply with standards set by the International Maritime Organization (IMO) and International Telecommunication Union (ITU).

=== Coastal radio systems ===
IP-based GMDSS communication platforms configured for coast stations, ports, and offshore facilities. These systems support Voice over IP (VoIP), automated logging, and remote management across VHF and MF/HF radio frequencies. [ref: [https://automatik.nu/artikel/navtex-udstyr-sikrer-canadas-kystlinjer/ Navtex-udstyr sikrer Canadas kystlinjer], Automatik.nu.]

=== GMDSS test equipment ===
Portable test devices, such as the Futronic series, used by maritime radio surveyors during mandatory inspections of shipborne radio equipment, emergency beacons, and Search and Rescue Transponders (SART). [ref: [https://www.samsa.org.za/api/api/File/view/Uh7apBvciUWErMv55gbYgg%3D%3D Calibration and Battery Replacement – Futronic MKII GMDSS Test Box], South African Maritime Safety Authority (SAMSA), 2026.]

=== Maritime safety information & NAVTEX ===
Transmitter installations used by maritime authorities to broadcast weather alerts and navigational warnings to vessels. The company also produces NAVDAT (Navigational Data) transmitters operating in the 500 kHz band. [ref: [https://elek-data.dk/artikel/branche-og-teknologi/danske-firmaer-samarbejder-om-ny-teknologi-til-sfartssikkerhed Danske firmaer samarbejder om ny teknologi til søfartssikkerhed], Elek-data.dk, 4 November 2024.]

=== AIS shore infrastructure & VDES ===
Physical Shore Stations (PSS) for the Automatic Identification System (AIS) used in coastal vessel traffic tracking, alongside VHF Data Exchange System (VDES) technology. [ref: [https://digitallead.dk/viden/nyheder/dansk-maritim-foererposition-styrkes-med-nyt-projekt-for-sikkerhedsmeddelelser-til-soes/ Dansk maritim førerposition styrkes med nyt projekt for sikkerhedsmeddelelser til søs], DigitalLead.]

== Major contracts and deployments ==
The company supplies coastal communication systems and safety equipment to national maritime authorities globally:
* Canada: The Canadian Coast Guard (CCG) selected Danphone to replace Canada's nationwide NAVTEX infrastructure, delivering 24 1 kW transmitters and 21 automatic antenna tuning units along the Canadian coastline.
* Africa: The company has supplied coastal radio communication networks, port systems, and safety infrastructure under contracts with regional maritime authorities in several African nations. [ref: [https://www.electronic-supply.dk/article/view/1056930/nordjysk_kommunikationsspecialist_far_vigtig_afrikansk_ordre Nordjysk kommunikationsspecialist får vigtig afrikansk ordre], Electronic Supply DK.]

Arena Breakout: Infinite is a first-person tactical extraction shooter developed by MoreFun Studios for PC. The game is a PC evolution of the mobile shooter Arena Breakout; MoreFun studio head Hanjin “Enzo” Zhang said that the PC version had been in development for more than three years and was built from the original game. [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite devs on building a military sim for all gamers, GamesBeat] It is set in the fictional war-torn region of Kamona, where players enter raids to search for supplies, fight human and AI-controlled opponents, and attempt to leave through extraction points. [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite is a snack-sized Tarkov I can't stop playing, but has some awful monetisation, PC Gamer] [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite Early Access Launches Today, GamesPress] [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite Officially Launches on Steam & Epic, Delivering the Ultimate FPS Extraction Shooter Experience, GamesPress]

The game entered early access through its official website on 13 August 2024. [ref: How to get early access to Arena Breakout: Infinite, Shacknews] It was released on Steam and the Epic Games Store on 15 September 2025; Steam lists MoreFun Studios as both developer and publisher. [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite, Steam]

== Development and release ==

In a May 2024 GamesBeat interview, Zhang described the studio's aim as offering an immersive military-simulation experience to both casual and hardcore players. He told GamesBeat that "the most enjoyable part of military simulation games is that it can provide an unparalleled level of immersion which other games cannot provide," and summarised Arena Breakout: Infinite's core loop as "gearing up, fighting and extraction." Zhang added that the studio wanted a title players could pick up in short sessions, describing the design intent as "easy come, easy play, easy go."

Following the closed beta of the overseas PC version in May 2024, Arena Breakout: Infinite reached the top-two position among Chinese-developed games on Steam's global wishlist chart, according to a September 2024 Gamescom feature by Chinese trade publication Jinghe. [ref: ]

MoreFun announced on 7 August 2024 that Arena Breakout: Infinite would enter early access through the official website on 13 August. The company said that the early-access period would be used to optimize performance, introduce features and refine gameplay systems. The early-access build added the Armory map, weapons and equipment, Kill Cam and Spectate features, additional language support, lower hardware requirements and a season system. [ref: Arena Breakout: Infinite Early Access to Launch on August 13, Arena Breakout: Infinite]

On 2 September 2025, MoreFun announced that the game would release on Steam on 15 September. [ref: Tactical FPS Arena Breakout Infinite locks in Steam launch 2.1m wishlists later, PCGamesN] [ref: Steam Full Release Dev Blog, Steam Community] The company described the full-release update as adding weapons, accessories, Farm map areas, tactical items, supply stations and updates to the Trophy Room. Arena Breakout: Infinite became available on Steam and the Epic Games Store on 15 September 2025. [ref: Arena Breakout Infinite is out on Steam, and it's no longer pay-to-win, PCGamesN]

Elkington's work in sales technology was profiled by destinationCRM in 2017. The publication described him as a contributor to sales-industry thought leadership and technological innovation, and reported that he served on the advisory board of the American Association of Inside Sales Professionals.

The Capture of El Maragato is a real, historical incident that took place in Spain in 1806 A.D involving a notorious highwayman and dangerous prison escapee whose real name was Pedro Pinero, known by his moniker El Maragato. Pedro was born in the town of Andiuela de Somoza in Leon, Spain and worked in the charcoal industry before joining a gang of criminals as bandits. [ref: 250 años del nacimiento de 'El Maragato', el bandolero que inmortalizó Goya, La Nueva Crónica]

In 1804, he and several of his accomplices were captured and after lengthy trials El Maragato was sentenced to 200 lashes, 10 years of hard labor at the Cartagena naval shipyard and execution by hanging, but he received a royal commutation from King Carlos IV that spared him from the gallows while upholding the remaining sentences. In 1806 he escaped from prison.

After his escape, he spent about two months in hiding, committing robberies, stealing food and weapons. Later on, Pedro broke into the quarters of the Franciscan friar, Friar Pedro, to rob him and hold him at gun point. But the confrontation took unexpectedly dramatic turn. The friar maintained his composure and in a sudden move, lunged at the bandit and forcefully took the rifle from him after a violent physical struggle. As the bandit attempted to flee, the friar shot him in the leg to impede his escape then bound him securely with the help of local residents and handed him over to the authorities. The friar later attempted to help El Maragato obtain a pardon, but his pleas went unanswered. The bandit was swiftly tried and executed by hanging in Madrid. Meanwhile, Friar Pedro received royal praise, commendation and an annual stipend for his brave actions. [ref: ] [ref: ]

This incident captivated the Spanish public, inspiring the artist Francisco Goya to immortalize it in a famous series of 6 oil paintings that narrate the details of the event. To this day the series remains on display as a historical and artistic testament at the Art Institute of Chicago [ref: ] and a 10-minutes short film about him, directed by Luis Miguel Alonso was released in 1997 under the title El Bandido Maragato. [ref: ‘EL MARAGATO’: 250 AÑOS DEL NACIMIENTO DEL BANDOLERO CUYA CAPTURA INMORTALIZÓ GOYA – Real Asociación Española de Cronistas Oficiales]

Taylah Hasaballah (b.1994, Melbourne) is an Australian artist living and working in Paris. Her practice centres around the concept of entropy through chemically driven paintings that investigate transformation, matter, and time. Skyfire is an American financial technology and artificial intelligence infrastructure company that develops identity verification, authentication, and payment systems intended to enable autonomous AI agents to conduct transactions with digital services and merchants. [ref: Skyfire lets AI agents spend your money — with guardrails, TechCrunch] [ref: Experian's Chief Innovation Officer Gleams AI Gains With Startup Collaboration, InformationWeek]

The company was founded by Amir Sarhangi, who previously founded Jibe Mobile, a messaging startup acquired by Google in 2015 that became part of Google's implementation of the Rich Communication Services (RCS) messaging standard, and Craig DeWitt, a former Ripple executive. [ref: Google Buys Startup Jibe Mobile, The Wall Street Journal] [ref: Google says RCS messaging is now available worldwide, TechCrunch]

The company is associated with infrastructure for agentic commerce, including systems for AI agent identity verification and automated payment execution. [ref: These New AI Bots Will Do Just About Anything for You, The Wall Street Journal]

== History ==
Skyfire was founded in 2023 by Amir Sarhangi and Craig DeWitt.

Before founding Skyfire, Sarhangi founded Jibe Mobile, a mobile messaging company acquired by Google in 2015. Jibe's technology became part of Google's implementation of the Rich Communication Services (RCS) messaging standard.

DeWitt previously worked at Ripple in digital payments infrastructure.

In August 2024, Skyfire publicly launched infrastructure intended to support autonomous AI agents conducting commercial transactions, including programmable digital wallets and transaction controls. [ref: Skyfire launches to let autonomous AI agents spend money on your behalf, VentureBeat]

The company announced an $8.5 million funding round in 2024 with participation from Neuberger Berman, Coinbase Ventures, Brevan Howard Digital, Arrington Capital, and other investors. [ref: AI payment processing startup Skyfire launches with $8.5M in funding, SiliconANGLE]

== Products and technology ==
Skyfire develops infrastructure intended to support autonomous commercial activity by AI agents.

Its platform includes systems for:
* identity verification and authentication of AI agents
* programmable digital wallets
* policy-based transaction controls
* automated payment execution using methods including card payments, ACH transfers, wire transfers, and stablecoins.

In 2025, Skyfire introduced KYAPay (Know Your Agent Pay), an open protocol intended to support standardized identity verification and payment authorization for AI agents engaging with third-party services. [ref: Skyfire launches AI agent checkout to enable fully autonomous transactions, PYMNTS]

Skyfire's identity and payment infrastructure has been referenced in reporting on emerging agentic commerce trust frameworks involving organizations including Experian, Visa, and Cloudflare. [ref: The Trust Gap Holding Agentic Commerce Back, PYMNTS]

In reporting on Experian's Agent Trust initiative, PYMNTS described Skyfire as providing a standardized mechanism for exchanging AI agent identity information across platforms together with payment credentials that can operate within existing checkout systems.

In September 2026, Mastercard announced that it was working with Skyfire to incorporate Know Your Agent (KYA) identity verification into its Agent Pay infrastructure. The collaboration was intended to help financial institutions and merchants identify and verify AI agents participating in transactions. [ref: Mastercard expands Agent Pay with trust and intelligence services, The Paypers]

Reporting by Forkast discussed Skyfire's KYA technology as an identity-verification component of Mastercard's broader agentic-commerce trust framework, alongside Mastercard's transaction-level risk assessment capabilities. [ref: Mastercard's Probability Score Shifts the Agent Commerce Question From Identity to Trust, Forkast]

== Industry coverage ==
Skyfire has been cited in reporting on the development of commercial infrastructure for autonomous AI agents.

In The Wall Street Journal, Belle Lin described Skyfire as a startup developing blockchain-based payment systems for bots to make purchases under transaction controls defined by users.

InformationWeek described Skyfire as a technology partner in Experian's agent trust ecosystem, including support for identity and payment infrastructure for AI-driven commerce.

Draft text:
George J. Magovern Jr. (born March 4, 1952) is a prominent retired American cardiothoracic, vascular and transplantation surgeon [ref: Health Care Heroes: Celebrating Magovern's career of milestones, Pittsburgh Business Times] who spent 40 years at Allegheny General Hospital (AGH) in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. His career focused on cardiac and vascular surgery, transplantation, mechanical circulatory support, surgical education, and clinical research. From 1985 until his retirement in 2025, Magovern held a number of clinical, academic and administrative leadership positions at AGH and later Allegheny Health Network (AHN), including chairman of the Department of Thoracic and Cardiovascular Surgery and chairman of the AHN Cardiovascular Institute.

Magovern is a member of a family closely associated with the development of cardiothoracic surgery nationally, [ref: Mending hearts: Dr. Magovern had a healing effect on Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette] and in Pittsburgh: His father, George J. Magovern Sr. [ref: In Memoriam: George J. Magovern, Sr. (1923–2013), Texas Heart Institute Journal] (1923–2013), was a pioneering cardiac surgeon who, working with engineer Harry Cromie, developed a sutureless prosthetic aortic valve [ref: ] in 1962. In 1957, the elder Magovern and thoracic surgeon Edward M. Kent introduced open-heart surgery using the heart-lung machine to Western Pennsylvania. [ref: George Jerome Magovern, MD, November 17, 1923–November 4, 2013, The Annals of Thoracic Surgery]

Magovern's brother, James A. Magovern [ref: Obituary: Dr. James Anthony Magovern / Nationally known heart surgeon, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette] (1954–2007), was also a cardiac surgeon and conducted cardiovascular research at AHN until his death from cancer.

== Early years ==
George J. Magovern Jr. was born on March 4, 1952, in Brooklyn, New York, to George J. Magovern Sr. and Ann Magovern. [ref: Obituary: Ann Magovern / Longtime supporter of Allegheny General Hospital, Pittsburgh Post-Gazette] Both of his parents were born and raised in New York. The family moved to Pittsburgh in 1957, when his father joined the medical staff at Allegheny General Hospital, and settled in the Fox Chapel area in 1960. Magovern was raised in an Irish Catholic community, and attended the former St. Scholastica grade school in Aspinwall.

He was the oldest of six children; his younger siblings were James, Mary, Susan, Frances and Ann. James Magovern followed his father and older brother into cardiac surgery and cardiovascular medicine. Magovern attended Shady Side Academy in Pittsburgh, graduating in 1970. [ref: News Post, www.shadysideacademy.org] As a student, he participated in football, wrestling and tennis.

== Education ==
Magovern attended the College of the Holy Cross in Worcester, Massachusetts, where he majored in biology and graduated in 1974. He then attended the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine, graduating in 1978. While in medical school, he served as president of his class.

Following medical school, Magovern completed his surgical training at Johns Hopkins Hospital in Baltimore from 1978 to 1985. His training included general surgery, vascular surgery, general thoracic surgery and cardiac surgery. Upon completing his residency, Magovern returned to Pittsburgh and joined Allegheny General Hospital in 1985, beginning an association with the hospital that continued until his retirement four decades later.

== Career ==
Clinical practice and transplantation

During his career, Magovern performed several thousand cardiac surgical procedures. Most were performed at Allegheny General Hospital, although he also operated at West Penn Hospital, Forbes Hospital, Beaver Medical Center [ref: Jun 29, 1994, page 122 - Pittsburgh Post-Gazette at Newspapers.com™, Newspapers.com] and Westmoreland Hospital. His clinical practice encompassed the surgical treatment of coronary artery disease, valvular heart disease, heart failure and thoracic aortic disease, as well as thoracic organ transplantation [ref: Allegheny Health Network completes 500th heart transplant - Becker's ASC, Becker’s ASC] and ventricular assist device implantation. [ref: Jul 15, 2000, page 1 - Pittsburgh Post-Gazette at Newspapers.com™, Newspapers.com]

In 1987, Magovern established AGH's heart transplant and left ventricular assist device program. The heart transplant program launched in 1985 [ref: ] and received approval from the United Network for Organ Sharing (UNOS) in 1988 and became one of the country's longest continually approved heart transplant programs.

Magovern also performed AGH's first single-lung transplant in 1992. He subsequently served as director of the lung transplant program from 1992 to 2000.

Leadership at Allegheny General Hospital

In 1992, Magovern was appointed director of the Division of Cardiothoracic Surgery at AGH. Two years later, he became program director of the hospital's Cardiothoracic Surgery Residency Program. He was a member of the Thoracic Surgery Directors Association from 1995 to 2013. In 1995, he was elected to membership in the American Association for Thoracic Surgery. The following year, he was promoted to professor of cardiothoracic surgery at Drexel University College of Medicine.

Alejandro Cifuentes (born 6 June 1965) is a Spanish analytical chemist and food scientist. [ref: Quick Update: Foodomics Alejandro Cifuentes on how foodomics could lead to new ways of treating Alzheimer’s disease, The Analytical Scientist] He is a research professor at the Spanish National Research Council (CSIC). He is known for introducing the concept of Foodomics. [ref: ] He is an editor of TrAC – Trends in Analytical Chemistry. [ref: ]

== Education and career ==
Cifuentes received a Ph.D. in Chemistry in 1992 from the University of Valladolid. He held postdoctoral research at the University of Amsterdam between 1993 and 1995 through a European Union fellowship. [ref: Alejandro Cifuentes Founding Director of the Institute of Food Science Research (, ICBC]

Cifuentes has spent his academic career at the Spanish National Research Council (CSIC). He has headed the Laboratory of Foodomics since 1999 and directed the Metabolomics Platform at the Institute of Food Science Research (CIAL), a joint CSIC–Autonomous University of Madrid facility, since 2012. [ref: Prof. Alejandro Cifuentes and Prof. Elena Ibañez Appointed Editors-in-Chief of Exploration of Foods and Foodomics, Open Exploration] He was deputy director of the Institute of Industrial Fermentations before serving as CIAL's founding director from 2007 to 2010. He became a full research professor in 2007. [ref: Alejandro Cifuentes - Laboratorio de Alimentómica, www.cial.uam-csic.es]

He serves as Editor of TrAC – Trends in Analytical Chemistry, and Specialty Chief Editor of Frontiers in Nutrition. [ref: ] He has also served as editor of Elsevier's reference work. [ref: Comprehensive Foodomics, ScienceDirect]

== Research ==
Cifuentes' research focuses on analytical chemistry, separation science, food science and foodomics. [ref: ] His laboratory develops and applies high-resolution analytical platforms including liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS) [ref: Online Extraction Followed by LC-MS/MS Analysis of Lipids in Natural Samples: A Proof-of-Concept Profiling Lecithin in Seeds, Foods], gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS), capillary electrophoresis–mass spectrometry (CE–MS), multidimensional chromatography, and molecular biology techniques for the characterization of food composition.

He also introduced the concept of Foodomics. [ref: Foodomics: Analytical Opportunities and Challenges, Analytical Chemistry]

His group has investigated molecular signatures related to cancer, Alzheimer's disease, obesity, inflammation, and other chronic disorders, using metabolomic, lipidomic, transcriptomic and proteomic approaches to understand the mechanisms through which dietary compounds influence disease prevention and progression. [ref: Exhaustive Search of Dietary Intake Biomarkers as Objective Tools for Personalized Nutrimetabolomics and Precision Nutrition Implementation, Nutrition Reviews]

== Selected publications ==

*Foodomics: Advanced Mass Spectrometry in Modern Food Science and Nutrition, John Wiley & Sons
* Fundamentals of advanced omics technologies: from genes to metabolites, Elsevier
* Applications of Advanced Omics Technologies From Genes to Metabolites
* Green Extraction Techniques: Principles, Advances and Applications

* The role of Food Science and Foodomics in the implementation of One-Health, Frontiers in Nutrition
* In vivo neuroprotective capacity of a Dunaliella salina extract - comprehensive transcriptomics and metabolomics study, npj Science of Food

Christian Obi, known online as The Igbo Wolf, is a Nigerian content creator, comedian and actor. He is known for comedy skits featuring recurring characters such as Professor Uwa, an Igbo lecturer in a Yoruba school, and for a series of ironic "happy to be at work" selfies that spread widely on Twitter in 2022. [ref: Creator Spotlight: How the Igbo Wolf Became a Social Media Trendsetter, Zikoko] [ref: #BNCreativesCorner: Through Content Creation, Christian Obi (The Igbo Wolf) Lays Bare His Dreams and Utopia, BellaNaija] He made his feature film debut in the 2024 film Japa!. [ref: Glazing Hot With... Content Creator and Budding Actor, The Igbo Wolf, Glazia] Alongside his creative work, he works as a product manager in the finance industry in Lagos. [ref: How The Igbo Wolf Combines Content Creation With His 9 To 5, PiggyVest Blog]

== Early life and education ==
Obi grew up in a family of four boys. He took part in cultural dance in primary school, and in secondary school he directed and acted in school plays. He wanted to attend the film school PEFTI, but instead studied computer science at Igbinedion University. At university he joined the dance and drama group.

He completed his National Youth Service Corps in Yenagoa, Bayelsa State, where he worked as a teacher and wrote, acted and danced for the local cultural group, for which he also wrote a play.

== Career ==
=== Early career ===
After national service, Obi took freelance writing, graphic design and early UI/UX work, and was paid to write a television series for Africa Magic that was not produced. He later worked in customer support at a travel company before resigning in late 2019 to study data analytics, shortly before the COVID-19 pandemic. During the pandemic he earned income from brand campaigns on Twitter and posted a recurring news-style video series called "Twitter Happenings". He subsequently moved into strategy and then product management, focusing on financial technology.

=== Content creation ===
Obi posted his first Instagram skit in 2019 but paused because of his phone's poor quality. He resumed in August 2021 after buying a new phone, and a skit using an underwater mermaid filter went viral within days.

On 21 September 2021 he posted a skit on Twitter as Professor Uwa, an Igbo lecturer taking a roll call of Yoruba student names that carry unflattering meanings in Igbo. The character was inspired by a secondary school teacher who mispronounced a classmate's name. An improvised closing line, "Dazz ya name?", became a widely used meme on Nigerian Twitter, and the video passed 40,000 views overnight. The success of the skit led to his first direct brand partnership.

In January 2022 Obi began posting selfies of himself looking miserable with ironic captions about how happy he was to go to work. The posts went viral in February 2022, and users across Africa and beyond responded with similar photos of their own.

His other recurring characters include Work Chris, a frustrated employee; RonkeHR, a human resources officer; Mama Elo, a Nigerian reimagining of Maye Musk; Chimoney; Mama Chekwube and Chekwube. His style avoids slapstick, voiceovers and sound effects, and he writes, directs, shoots and edits his skits himself, usually in single takes. His stage name combines his ethnicity with the idea of a lone wolf.

=== Acting ===
Obi appeared in MTV Shuga and Getting Ahead before making his feature film debut in Japa! (2024), produced by Inkblot Productions, alongside Adesua Etomi-Wellington, Jidekene Achufusi, Mofe Duncan, Layi Wasabi, Seun Ajayi and Blossom Chukwujekwu. He has said he hopes to work in Asaba-based Nollywood productions.

=== Public engagements ===
In July 2024 Obi was a panellist at the Student Leader Launchpad held by African Women on Board at the University of Lagos, where he spoke on social media as a leadership tool. [ref: African Women on Board tackles youth Apathy; Hosts future Leaders at UNILAG, ThisDay]

Sync.me (originally SmartSync) is a caller ID and contact-management
mobile app developed by Sync.me Technologies Ltd for
Android and iOS. The app identifies incoming callers,
blocks spam and robocalls, offers reverse phone lookup, and
synchronises contact details and photos from social networks.

== History ==
The app was first released as SmartSync, a social contact-synchronisation app for the
iPhone that displayed a caller's latest Facebook status updates and photos when they
called. It was founded by Ken Vinner and Shlomo Unger with angel funding.

The company later renamed the app Sync.ME and, in November 2012, raised a US$4 million
funding round from undisclosed private investors. At that time it reported approximately five
million users and described itself as syncing more than one billion contacts each week, with
particular popularity in Japan after the addition of a Japanese-language search
algorithm.

The app subsequently added caller identification, spam-call blocking, reverse phone lookup and
spam-text filtering, which became its main focus. The company says
its caller identification draws on a database of several billion phone numbers together with
spam reports crowdsourced from its users.

== Features ==
On Android and iOS, Sync.me offers caller identification for incoming calls, including numbers
not saved in the user's contacts; blocking of spam and robocalls; reverse phone-number lookup;
filtering of spam and scam text messages; and contact synchronisation that backs up and updates
contact details and photos from social-network profiles. The
contact-syncing function, which originally drew photos and details from social networks, was
the app's initial focus before it added caller-identification tools.

== Reception ==
Reviewing an early version, TechCrunch described it as "the app that turns you into a
god", referring to the way it surfaced callers' social-media information during a
call.

Luigi Bruti (born 1960 in Montemonaco, Italy) is an Italian musician and electronic musical instrument designer. He worked for SIEL and Roland Europe before becoming involved in the establishment of the Italian digital-instrument company Dexibell. His work has included the Roland E-20 arranger keyboard and the Roland V-Accordion. [ref: Luigi Bruti, NAMM Oral History]

== Career ==

Bruti worked for the Italian electronic musical instrument manufacturer SIEL. A 1985 report in the British music newspaper Sounds described him as a SIEL demonstrator presenting the company's MIDI software and electronic musical instruments. [ref: SIEL, Sounds]

After SIEL became part of Roland, Bruti continued his career at Roland Europe. A 2018 article in Music Trades identified him as the designer of the Roland E-20 arranger keyboard. [ref: Bringing A New Style To The Keyboard Market, Music Trades] NAMM's Oral History program also credits him with contributing to the development of the V-Accordion series. [ref: Luigi Bruti, NAMM Oral History] Roland founder Ikutaro Kakehashi also identified Bruti, together with Francesco Rauchi, among the engineers involved in the V-Accordion project. [ref: An Age Without Samples: Originality and Creativity in the Digital World, Hal Leonard Books]

A 2008 report in Accordion USA on Roland Europe's V-Accordion production described Bruti as director of the V-Accordion and marketing divisions and discussed his role in the development of the instrument. [ref: A Roland is Born in Acquaviva Picena, Accordion USA]

After Roland Europe ceased operations in Italy, Bruti became involved in the group that established Dexibell. In a 2018 reportage following a visit to the company's facilities, SM Strumenti Musicali described Bruti as the figure who gathered former Roland specialists to form the new development team. [ref: REPORTAGE - DEXIBELL: IL PIANOFORTE ITALIANO, SM Strumenti Musicali]

In 2019, the American trade publication The Music & Sound Retailer reported on the history of Dexibell and described Bruti as a keyboard innovator who joined forces with Proel chief executive Fabrizio Sorbi to begin developing and manufacturing Dexibell keyboards. The article also identified him as a founder of Dexibell. [ref: The Music & Sound Retailer Visits Italy, The Music & Sound Retailer]

== Music ==

In 1981, Bruti composed Musette, which was included in the musical programme of Ettore Scola's film Passione d'amore. [ref: Società Italiana degli Autori ed Editori, Programma musicale del film Passione d'amore, 1981, line 25.]

In 2004, Bruti was one of the producers of Linda Valori, who placed third at the Sanremo Music Festival with Aria, sole, terra e mare. [ref: Concerto di Valori per…Linda, Riviera Oggi]

== Patents ==

Bruti is named as an inventor or co-inventor on patents concerning electronic musical instruments. These include a patent for a method of electronically reproducing accordion sound, developed with Demetrio Cuccu and Roberto Gaetani. [ref: Method for reproducing the sound of an accordion electronically, Google Patents]

== Awards ==

In 2014, Bruti received the Merit Award of the Confédération Internationale des Accordéonistes for his work in the field of electronic accordions. [ref: CIA Merit Awards, Confédération Internationale des Accordéonistes]

== References ==

Music for the film was composed by Franklyn Marks, including the song "The Four Seasons". [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse - Full Cast & Crew, TV Guide] [ref: The four seasons, Copyright Encyclopedia]

The film is available on DVD, Disney+ and Apple TV. [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse, Orange County Library System] [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse, Disney+] [ref: Justin Morgan Had a Horse, Apple TV]

Josh Spiegel of:/Film called the film “baffling”, while Common Sense Media gave it three out of five stars. Draft: John R. Woznicki

Draft text:
John R. Woznicki is a literary scholar and academic administrator whose scholarly work primarily involves twentieth-century American poetry and poetics. Woznicki is the author of Ideological Content and Political Significance of Twentieth-Century American Poetry [ref: John R. Woznicki. Ideological Content and Political Significance of Twentieth-Century American Poetry. Edwin Mellen Press. 2002.] and the edited collection The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. [ref: John R. Woznicki ed. The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Lehigh University Press. 2013.]

== Scholarship ==

Woznicki’s first monograph, Ideological Content and Political Significance of Twentieth-Century American Poetry [ref: John R. Woznicki. Ideological Content and Political Significance of Twentieth-Century American Poetry. Edwin Mellen Press. 2002,] is an interdisciplinary examination of politics and ideology in twentieth-century American poetry, drawing upon philosophy, sociology, literary criticism, and cultural studies. It examines the work of Ezra Pound, Charles Olson and the L=A=N=G=U=A=G=E poets, with particular attention to totalitarianism, utopian thought, and political consciousness.

He then edited a collection of essays and wrote the introductory chapter for The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later, [ref: John R. Woznicki ed. The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Lehigh University Press. 2013,] a collection of scholarly essays reassessing Donald Allen’s influential 1960 anthology The New American Poetry 1945–1960. [ref: Donald Allen ed. The New American Poetry 1945–1960. Grove Press. 1960.] Woznicki’s collection considers the anthology's formation, its modernist antecedents, poets and movements represented in it, and its subsequent literary and cultural influence. A paperback edition was subsequently published in 2015. [ref: John R. Woznicki ed. The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Lehigh University Press. 2015.]

== Reception ==

Orchid Tierney reviewed Woznicki’s volume in the Journal of Modern Literature. [ref: Orchid Tierney. “Back to the Future of Poetry? A Review of The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later." Journal of Modern Literature, vol. 40, no. 1, 2016, pp. 164–168. DOI:10.2979/jmodelite.40.1.09.]  Tierney characterizes the collection more broadly as an investigation of tradition-building and the reasons Allen's anthology remained relevant to poets, readers, and scholars of innovative writing.

Choice Reviews recommended The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. The review discusses aspects of the legacy of Allen’s anthology, including women poets, the British avant-garde, the long poem, and Language poetry. [ref: John. R Woznicki.The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later. Bloomsbury Book Page. Bloomsbury Publishing. https://www.bloomsbury.com/us/new-american-poetry-9781611462142/.]

Patrick James Dunagan reviewed The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later in the journal Your Impossible Voice. [ref: Patrick James Dunagan. Review: The New American Poetry: Fifty Years Later, edited by John R. Woznicki. Your Impossible Voice. ISSN #2327-381X. https://yourimpossiblevoice.com/review-new-american-poetry-fifty-years-later-john-r-woznicki-ed/.] Dunagan considers Woznicki’s introductory argument and the volume's attempt to move critical discussion beyond the original construction of Allen's anthology toward questions concerning its reception, cultural influence, and continuing relationship to contemporary poetry.

In discussing Donald Allen and the historical significance of The New American Poetry, Stephanie Anderson directs readers to scholarship concerning Allen's anthology and includes Woznicki's collection alongside work by Alan Golding and Stephan Delbos. [ref: Stephanie Anderson. “‘It's Only Vanity if It's Not Good’: Daisy Aldan and Women Midcentury Small Press Publishers.” Post45, 2024.]

In his book titled The New American Poetry and Cold War Nationalism, Delbos identifies Woznicki’s volume in his discussion of prior scholarship on Allen’s anthology, citing essays from the collection throughout his study. Delbos engages Woznicki’s own interpretation of Charles Olson. In the chapter “This Thing Is Most National: Nationalism and Assimilation in The New American Poetry,” Delbos discusses Woznicki's interpretation of correspondence from Olson as revealing Olson's conception of his American poetic identity in relation to the European cosmopolitan tradition associated with figures such as Ezra Pound and T. S. Eliot. Delbos argues that the passage can be taken further by examining the nationalism underlying Olson's position. [ref: Stephan Delbos.The New American Poetry and Cold War Nationalism. Modern and Contemporary Poetry and Poetics series. Palgrave Macmillan, 2021. p. 135.]

== Academic Career ==

22:11, 25 April 2026 (UTC)[user] Charles Lee Bevins is an American physician-scientist and immunologist known for his contributions to the study of antimicrobial peptides and innate immunity, particularly the role of defensins in epithelial host defense. His work on antimicrobial peptides has been described in independent scientific coverage as part of a broader shift in biomedical research that recognized endogenous antibiotics as key components of host defense.

== Early life and education ==

Bevins earned a Bachelor of Arts in biology from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County in 1976. He received both his MD and PhD in biochemistry from the University of Maryland School of Medicine in 1983 [ref: 1998 recipient of alumni award], where his doctoral mentor was Ralph M. Pollack [ref: Detection of a transient enzyme-steroid complex during active-site-directed irreversible inhibition of 3-oxo-delta 5-steroid isomerase, Biochemistry].

He completed residency training in pediatrics at the University of California, San Francisco and conducted postdoctoral research at the National Institutes of Health under the mentorship of Michael A. Zasloff [ref: LinkedIn Biography] [ref: Peptides from frog skin, Annu Rev Biochem].

== Career and research ==

Bevins began his academic career at the University of Pennsylvania School of Medicine, where he served as Assistant Professor of Pediatrics and Genetics. He later held a faculty research position at the Cleveland Clinic before joining the University of California, Davis in 2003, where he became Professor of Microbiology and Immunology in the School of Medicine and was later named Distinguished Professor [ref: University Website].

His research has focused on antimicrobial peptides and innate immunity at epithelial surfaces. Early work from his laboratory demonstrated that epithelial cells produce antimicrobial peptides, including tracheal antimicrobial peptide (TAP) [ref: Tracheal antimicrobial peptide, a cysteine-rich peptide from mammalian tracheal mucosa: peptide isolation and cloning of a cDNA, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A], supporting the concept that mucosal surfaces contribute actively to host defense.

Bevins’ work on antimicrobial peptides was discussed in contemporaneous scientific coverage as part of a group of discoveries that helped establish endogenous antimicrobial peptides as a major component of innate immunity.

Subsequent independent reviews of antimicrobial peptides have described these molecules as central components of innate immunity and host–microbe interactions, reflecting the emergence of the field to which Bevins contributed.

Bevins has also contributed to studies of defensins in intestinal immunity [ref: Paneth cells of the human small intestine express an antimicrobial peptide gene, J. Biol. Chem.] [ref: Defensin-6 mRNA in human Paneth cells: implications for antimicrobial peptides in host defense of the human bowel, FEBS Lett] [ref: Protection against enteric salmonellosis in transgenic mice expressing a human intestinal defensin, Nature], defensin function in the male reproductive tract [ref: A common mutation in the defensin DEFB126 causes impaired sperm function and subfertility, Sci Transl Med] [ref: Multifunctional glycoprotein DEFB126--a curious story of defensin-clad spermatozoa, Nat Rev Urol], the role of defensins in shaping the microbiota [ref: Enteric defensins are essential regulators of intestinal microbial ecology, Nat Immunol] [ref: The potter's wheel: the host's role in sculpting its microbiota, Cell Mol Life Sci], and host–microbe interactions [ref: Human α-defensin 6 promotes mucosal innate immunity through self-assembled peptide nanonets, Science], including research on Paneth cell function [ref: Paneth cells, antimicrobial peptides and maintenance of intestinal homeostasis, Nat Rev Microbiol] and inflammatory bowel diseases [ref: Reduced Paneth cell alpha-defensins in ileal Crohn's disease, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A].

== Media coverage and impact ==
Bevins’ research has been featured in independent scientific and general media. A 1993 feature in The Journal of NIH Research highlighted his work on antimicrobial peptides as part of an emerging field of “endogenous antibiotics.”

His research on the human defensin DEFB126 and its role in fertility was later covered by The New York Times in 2011.

== Honors and recognition ==

Bevins has received numerous honors for his research and mentorship, including:

* National Institutes of Health MERIT Award [ref: NIH Reporter]
* Distinguished Professor, University of California, Davis
* School of Medicine Research Award (University of California, Davis)
* Dean’s Awards for Excellence in Teaching and Mentoring (University of Pennsylvania, 1996 [ref: PENN Award]; University of California, Davis, 2007)

He has also served in leadership roles in the scientific community, including co-chairing a Gordon Research Conference on Antimicrobial Peptides in 2001 [ref: 2001 GRC].

== Selected contributions ==

Bevins is known for contributions to:

* Discovery and characterization of epithelial antimicrobial peptides
* Studies of defensins and Paneth cell biology
* Mechanisms of innate immunity at mucosal surfaces [ref: Inducible expression of an antibiotic peptide gene in lipopolysaccharide-challenged tracheal epithelial cells, Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A]

== Origin: How Peach and Goma Were Created ==
Peach and Goma are fictional cats created by Bu Jue Xiao Xiao, a Chinese artist inspired by her daily life and relationship with her boyfriend. [ref: Who Created Peach and Goma - Story Behind the Adorable Cat Duo, Get Bubu Dudu] First introduced to the world as a sticker series called "Peach Cat", Goma and Peach quickly earned many followings after their fame extended into not only WeChat (the first area they were used as stickers) but Instagram, Twitter (now X), and Youtube.

== Relationship with other characters ==
Despite being created by different artists, [https://english.mathrubhumi.com/lifestyle/who-are-bubu-and-dudu-the-internets-favourite-couple-m1olonjq Bubu and Dudu] are often compared with Peach and Goma. Because of their similar drawing styles and ways of expressing love, Bubu and Dudu are constantly confused with the cat characters. It is notable that the artists of the characters continue to sell merchandise in the same websites. Bubu and Dudu are sometimes expressed as "overshadowed by Goma and Peach" [ref: Why is Bubu and Dudu overshadowed by peach and goma] on media platforms such as Reddit.

== Media appearances/Merchandise (Daily Appearances) ==
This cat couple is often found on animated Youtube clips/songs or social media platforms. They were recently used in a yogurt ad for Chunzhen's Craving Yogurt (Nut&Berry Oat Crunch) [ref: Peach and Goma] and are available as memes on messenger apps such as Kakaotalk(recreated into a Korean version by a Kakaotalk artist, quan, on the app), WeChat, and Telegram. Peach and Goma are also found in online shops such as Peach and Goma Shop or Buy Bubu Dudu, etc. as plushies and mug cups [ref: About Peach and Goma Cat: The Adorable Cat Couple, Peach Goma Official Shop]. Even more than their simple drawing style, Peach and Goma are earning more and more fame from their everyday interactions that show humor and affection people can relate to easily. Couples continue to support and empathize to Peach & Goma, the everyday couple.

== About the Characters ==

=== Appearance & Personality ===
Peach is a fluffy white cat with large eyes and an energetic, playful, and mischievous personality while Goma has gray fur and a gentle personality that contrasts with Peach’s. [ref: About Peach and Goma Cat: The Adorable Cat Couple, Peach Goma Official Shop]

=== Relationship ===
Whether Goma and Peach are a couple or not is currently not revealed by the artist, whereas Netizens continue to guess the two cats' relation. Their relationship is often interpreted as best friends, roommates, or a couple from their humorous and heartwarming gestures and playful interactions. [ref: Are Peach and Goma a Couple? Peach Goma Relationship Explained, Get Bubu Dudu]

Leonhard Gregor Herten (born April 29, 1955 in Korschenbroich, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany) is a German physicist.

== Career ==
Gregor Herten studied physics at RWTH Aachen, where he received his doctorate in 1983
[ref: "Messung der Ladungsasymmetrie in der Reaktion e^+ e^- \to \mu^+ \mu^- mit dem MARK-J Detektor bei PETRA"]
under the supervision of
Albrecht Böhm.
He subsequently worked as a Research Fellow at the European Centre for Nuclear and Particle Physics, CERN, from 1984 to 1986. From 1986 to 1992, he was a Professor of Physics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Cambridge, MA, USA, first as an Assistant Professor and later as an Associate Professor
[ref: MIT LNS 1992 Symposium: On the Matter of Particles - L. Gregor Herten - The Future of L3 at LHC].
From 1992 to 2023, he was Professor
[ref: Experimentelle Teilchenphysik, Prof. Dr. Gregor Herten]
of Experimental Physics
at the Albert Ludwigs University of Freiburg;
he has been retired since October 2023.

== Research ==
Gregor Herten's research focuses on the investigation of the elementary building blocks of matter and their interactions using high-energy particle accelerators. He contributed to the discovery of the gluon
[ref: Discovery of Three Jet Events and a Test of Quantum Chromodynamics at PETRA Energies, Phys. Rev. Lett. 43 (1979), p. 830.]
and to the observation
[ref: Measurement of e^+ e^- \to \mu^+ \mu^- Charge Asymmetry, Phys. Rev. Lett. 48 (1982), p. 1701.]
of
electroweak processes
at the
PETRA storage ring of the Deutsches Elektronen-Synchrotron, DESY, Hamburg.

Together with his research group at the University of Freiburg, he developed and built
[ref: The ATLAS Experiment at the CERN Large Hadron Collider, JINST 3 (2008) S08003.]
large, precision
particle detectors for
muons for the
ATLAS experiment at the
Large Hadron Collider, LHC at CERN, which contributed to the discovery of the Higgs boson
[ref: Observation of a new particle in the search for the Standard Model Higgs boson with the ATLAS detector at the LHC, Phys. Lett. B, 716 (2012)].
Further contributions include measurements of Z boson decays at the
Large Electron-Positron Collider (LEP), as well as the search for new particles beyond the Standard Model and the study of heavy
quarks at the LHC
[ref: Gregor Herten: Complete list of publications on InspireHEP (Gregor Herten) (https://inspirehep.net/authors/1006125)].

In 2024, he published a textbook in german language together with Christoph Berger entitled "Elementarteilchenphysik"
[ref: Textbook: Elementarteilchenphysik, Springer Nature].
The English version of the book was published in 2025 under the title "Particle Physics"
[ref: Textbook: Particle Physics, Springer Nature].

== Administration ==
Gregor Herten served as Vice-Rector for Research at the University of Freiburg from 1995 to 2000 and received the Freiburg University Medal in recognition for his service to the university
[ref: Universitaetsmedaille/2000-2009].
He was the German scientific delegate to the CERN Council, and its Vice-President from 2007 to 2009
[ref: Presidents and vice-Presidents of CERN Council].
He was a member and, from 2005 to 2008, Chair of Commission C11 on Particles and Fields
[ref: IUPAP C11 Members]
[ref: Gregor Herten, Report from IUPAP-C11]
of the
International Union of Pure and Applied Physics (IUPAP).
From 2013 to 2015, he led the Section Matter and Cosmos (SMuK) and the Division of Particle Physics of the German Physical Society (DPG). In addition, Gregor Herten served as a scientific advisor on boards and committees of DESY, CERN, the
German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMBFTR)
and the
German Research Foundation (DFG).

Draft: Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo–Campeau type

Draft text:
----

Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo–Campeau type (SEMDGC) is an inherited skeletal dysplasia associated with pathogenic variants in ERI1. It causes pronounced short stature and abnormalities affecting the spine, pelvis, hips, and limbs. Fingers or toes may be shortened, underdeveloped, or absent, and facial features vary between affected individuals. [ref: Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo-Campeau type (Concept ID: C5882737), MedGen] The disorder follows an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. [ref: ERI1, PanelApp]

== Signs and symptoms ==
Skeletal manifestations include limb shortening and abnormalities of the hands and feet. Reported findings include short digits, joined digits, curved fingers, absent toes, restricted elbow extension, and dislocation of the radial head. Hydronephrosis and vesicoureteral reflux have also been recorded.

Radiographs show flattened vertebral bodies, irregular vertebral endplates, and scoliosis in affected individuals. Severity varies: two siblings are alive into their twenties, whereas three other individuals with the severe skeletal phenotype died in infancy or early childhood. These observations describe the initial series rather than an established survival estimate. [ref: Null and missense mutations of ERI1 cause a recessive phenotypic dichotomy in humans, The American Journal of Human Genetics]

== Genetics ==
ERI1 is located on chromosome 8p23.1. It encodes a 3′-to-5′ exoribonuclease involved in RNA processing. Reported severe cases have carried at least one pathogenic missense variant. By contrast, individuals with two null alleles have generally shown milder skeletal involvement. [ref: Congenital Bone Disorders Associated with ERI1-Mediated RNA Metabolism Dysfunction: Spondylo-Epi-Metaphyseal Dysplasia Guo-Campeau Type and Beyond, Current Osteoporosis Reports] The latter presentation, involving digital abnormalities and mild intellectual disability, is classified separately as Hoxha–Aliu syndrome (OMIM 620662).

== Diagnosis ==
The original study combined clinical and radiographic assessment with exome or genome sequencing. Candidate variants were investigated by Sanger sequencing and where parental samples were available, family studies.

== History ==
Guo and colleagues described the disorder in 2023. Their study included eight individuals from seven families with ERI1 variants; five individuals from four families had the severe skeletal phenotype.
==Research==
Cell experiments linked the missense variants to impaired exonuclease activity, abnormal 5.8S ribosomal RNA processing, and reduced histone messenger RNA degradation. Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells also showed impaired cartilage differentiation.

A 2025 review emphasized that the mechanism connecting altered RNA metabolism to the skeletal abnormalities remains incompletely understood. It also noted that Eri1-knockout mice do not reproduce the full human phenotype, limiting their usefulness as a model of the severe disorder.

== References ==

Draft: MT-ND4 m.11232TC

Draft text:
----

MT-ND4 m.11232T>C (also written 11232T>C or m.11232T>C) is a rare mutation in the mitochondrial gene MT-ND4. It changes one amino acid (leucine to proline at position 158) in the ND4 protein, which is part of complex I in the mitochondria. When the mutation is present in essentially all of a person's mitochondria (homoplasmic), it has been linked to a high risk of severe, permanent brain injury after sevoflurane anesthesia. [ref: Effects of a Mitochondrial Genetic Variant on Sevoflurane Hypersensitivity, Anesthesiology]
__TOC__
==History==
Starting in 2025 and 2026, doctors began reporting cases of previously healthy children and young adults who woke up slowly or never fully recovered after routine surgery. Many developed damage to the basal ganglia, movement problems, cognitive decline, or died. Almost all of them had received sevoflurane, and testing showed they carried the same m.11232T>C mutation. The patients shared maternal Venezuelan ancestry (often linked to the state of Carabobo). Because mitochondrial DNA comes only from the mother, the mutation is passed down that way.

Lab experiments with cells from these patients found that sevoflurane at normal anesthetic levels almost completely shut down the part of mitochondrial energy production that depends on complex I. Propofol did not cause the same sharp drop. A few patients who had already been injured by sevoflurane later had surgery with propofol-based intravenous anesthesia and did not have the same acute brain injury again.

Professional groups have responded. The American Society of Anesthesiologists and the Society for Pediatric Anesthesia recommend asking about maternal Venezuelan ancestry and considering avoiding all volatile anesthetics in those patients until more is known [ref: ]. The FDA has also issued an alert about the risk [ref: FDA Alerts Health Care Providers to Cases of Neurologic Complications from General Anesthesia Linked to Genetic Variant in Patients of Maternal Venezuelan Ancestry, FDA]. Targeted genetic testing for the mutation is now available from some labs.

Not every person with the mutation has been shown to react, and researchers are still working out exactly how high the risk is and whether other anesthetics are also dangerous. Before these cases, the mutation was listed as a variant of uncertain significance. The new clinical reports and lab data are what changed that assessment.

== References ==

Kiran Bhat (born 21 April 1990) is an Indian-American novelist, poet, short-story writer, literary critic and translator, who has written the poetry collections Autobiografia (2019), Speaking in Tongues (2022), [ref: Indian literature page-turners 2022, The New Indian Express] and the novel We of the Forsaken World (2020). [ref: Kiran Bhat's Book Launch: We of the Forsaken World, Global Atlanta] [ref: I like the idea of channeling the sorts of stories that humans like to come back to: Kiran Bhat, author, Girar, Kitaab] [ref: Author Kiran Bhat and Book: We of the Forsaken World, [[Khabar (magazine)] He is also the author of the ongoing serialized online novel Girar. [ref: Kiran Bhat Is Writing the Diversity of Our World, Electric Literature] In 2026, he received the International Writer of the Year award at the Peoples' Awards, held at the House of Commons in London. [ref: Kiran Bhat Honored with International Writer of the Year Award, Khabar]

== Early life ==
Bhat was born to doctors Anu and Subra Bhat and raised in Jonesboro, Georgia, United States, and partly in Karnataka, India. [ref: Circling the World: An Interview with Kiran Bhat, PRISM international] [ref: I try to compress our globe into a single narrative fictional space: Author Kiran Bhat, NRI Pulse] Bhat graduated from New York University. [ref: NRI writer's travelogue 'Tirugata' released in city, Star of Mysore]

== Career ==
In 2013, Bhat published his first book, titled Early Stories, which is a collection of stories written during his college years and subsequent time period he spent traveling. [ref: Traitor to Tradition, Resister to Remorse: A Conversation with Kiran Bhat, [[Asymptote (magazine)]

In 2019, he released the poetry collection Autobiografia and the Mandarin-language poetry collection Kiran Speaks.

In 2020, Bhat published a Portuguese story collection titled Afora, Adentro and his novel We of the Forsaken World. [ref: World traveling author makes stop at Edinboro, Edinboro Now] [ref: A Poetic Call for Peace, [[The Wire (India)] It is a short story cycle involving sixteen narratives based in four imagined places replicating the industrialising parts of our world. [ref: 'The Will to Survive Is a Force That Never Discriminates': Literature and Global Environmental Refugees and Other 'Forsaken' Peoples, Heavy Feather Review]

In 2021, Bhat started working on a new novel, titled Girar. [ref: With Girar, Author Kiran Bhat Is Reinventing Storytelling and Publishing, NRI Pulse] Girar is being released as a digital novel in monthly installments, with each story set in another country of the world. [ref: Kiran Bhat Interviewed, [[BOMB (magazine) 20 December 20 2022] [ref: Lounge Interview: Kiran Bhat, Author, Traveller and Polyglot, Kitaab]

Bhat published the poetry collection Speaking in Tongues: Poems in Spanish, Mandarin, and Turkish through the publisher Red River in 2022. [ref: Book Review: Speaking in Tongues: Poems in Spanish, Mandarin and Turkish, [[Outlook (Indian magazine) 12 November 2022] Bhat also contributed the poem "A Reporter Asked" to the poetry anthology Amity: Peace Poems, which was edited by Sahana Ahmed and published in December 2022.

Bhat curates for the Yatha Katha Literature Festival in Mumbai, and is co-chair of the Environmental Sustainability Subcommittee of the Global Indian Council. [ref: Kiran Bhat nominated for a Peoples' Award in U.K., Khabar]

== Awards ==
In 2026, Bhat was nominated for International Writer of the Year in the Public Life category of the Peoples' Awards, an annual event bringing together members of the diaspora community and Members of Parliament. He received the award at a ceremony held at the House of Commons; the organizers stated that he was the first person of Indian origin living outside the United Kingdom to receive it.

== Selected bibliography ==
* Early Stories (2013) [ref: Early Stories, eBookit.com]
* Accepting My Place (2017) [ref: Accepting My Place, eBookit.com]
* Tirugaatha (2019) [ref: Kiran Bhat, Cordite Poetry Review]
* Autobiografia (2019) [ref: Autobiografía - Bhat, Kiran, National Library of Spain]
* We of the Forsaken World (2020) [ref: We of the Forsaken World by Kiran Bhat, Dactyl Review] [ref: On the Page: The Novelist-Poet Questions in Kiran Bhat's Seminal Work We of the Forsaken World, Modern Diplomacy]
* Girar (2021)
* Speaking in Tongues (2022)

=== Book contributions ===
* Yearbook of Indian Poetry in English: 2020–2021 by Many Poets [ref: Yearbook of Indian Poetry in English: 2020–2021, Hawakal]
* The Best Asian Short Stories 2021 by Zafar Anjum [ref: The Best Asian Short Stories 2021, Kitaab]
* Amity: Peace Poems (2022)

== Personal life ==
Bhat is of Kannadiga origin. He has traveled to 177 countries and held residence in 25 cities. He currently resides in Mumbai, India, which he considers home. He speaks 12 languages, including English, Hindi, Kannada, Spanish, Portuguese, Mandarin, Japanese, and Turkish.

Rajmata () is a historical novel by Neelam Karki Niharika. This book was published on March 30, 2026, by FinePrint. [ref: Neelam Karki ‘Niharika’’s New novel Rajmata Released, SpotlightNepal] It won the Kabi Danda Puraskar, 2083 B.S. [ref: राजमाता उपन्यासलाई कविडाँडा आख्यान पुरस्कार, Ekantipur] This book is based on the life of the heroic women whom history overlooked or the state failed to recognize.

==Synopsis ==
Before Nepal acquired its present geographical shape, it experienced many ups and downs. At times it expanded, at other times it fragmented, and it had to endure the fate of being divided. During different historical periods, small kingdoms emerged and disappeared. The powerful conquered the weak, and many dynasties took control of the reins of government. They ruled either independently, jointly, as tributary states, or as semi-autonomous kingdoms. The names of the royal families that conquered these kingdoms and the records of their remarkable achievements have been preserved in history [ref: ‘अध्ययन गर्दै जाँदा थाहा भयो – महिला सवालमा इतिहास पनि पक्षपाती रहेछ’ – नीलम कार्की निहारिका, ‘अध्ययन गर्दै जाँदा थाहा भयो – महिला सवालमा इतिहास पनि पक्षपाती रहेछ’ – नीलम कार्की निहारिका]. Some women, too, found opportunities to have their names engraved on stone inscriptions, copper plates, or written in the colophons of manuscripts, alongside those of their husbands or sons. Occasionally, they are also mentioned in royal genealogies.

Over time, archaeologists unearthed historical documents through excavation and research, and historians carefully recorded them in books with great dedication and perseverance.

By weaving together those historical pages, while also giving due importance to certain heroic women whom history overlooked or the state failed to recognize, Rajmata presents a beautiful garland of interconnected stories [ref: निहारिकाको नयाँ कृति ‘राजमाता’] [ref: History, Memory, and Marginal Voices: ‘Rajmata’ Reframes Nepal’s Past Through a Feminine Lens, History, Memory, and Marginal Voices: ‘Rajmata’ Reframes Nepal’s Past Through a Feminine Lens]

==Award==
Kabidanda Akhyan Puraskar of 2083 was awarded to Rajmata. The award was given by Kabidanda Sahitya Samaj and the award money is 200,160 Rupees.

Draft text:
Glenn Richard Cohen (born October 26, 1964) is an American-Israeli psychologist and former officer of the Mossad (Israel's national intelligence agency).

Following the Hamas attack on Israel of 7 October 2023, Cohen was designated as the first mental health professional to meet returning hostages upon their release, and subsequently led the team of psychologists that debriefed the hostages released from Gaza captivity between November 2023 and October 2025. [ref: 'Resilience is in the Jewish people's DNA': The man helping Israel's freed hostages heal, The Jewish Chronicle]

==Biography==

Cohen was born and raised in New York City. He studied at Ramaz high school and was an avid basketball player. [ref: How do you debrief a hostage?, The Jewish Standard] In 1982, he made aliya to Israel. After a year studying at Yeshiva, he enlisted to the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) in 1984. [ref: What we know about captivity in Gaza – with Glenn Cohen, Call Me Back with Dan Senor]

=== Education ===
Cohen earned his undergraduate degree (B.A) in Psychology and Geography from The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and his graduate degree (M.A) in Clinical Psychology from Bar-Ilan University, specializing in combat-related PTSD. [ref: The Blogs: Ex-Mossad Chief Psychologist Delivers Message of Hope and Resilience]

==Military and Intelligence Career==

Cohen graduated from the Israeli Air Force flight academy and served for seven years as a search and rescue helicopter pilot. [ref: Glenn Cohen on Hostages, Trauma, and the Psychology of Survival, The Algemeiner] After his discharge, he was recruited by the Mossad where he served for 30 years, [ref: Glenn Cohen on Hostages, Trauma, and the Psychology of Survival, The Algemeiner] retiring as Chief Operational Psychologist. [ref: ] He retired from the Mossad in 2015.

==October 7 Hostage Crisis==

===Emergency Reserve Duty===

Following the Hamas October 7 attack in 2023, Cohen was called up to serve in IDF emergency reserve duty in the Hostage Negotiation Unit, serving for over five months. He was the first psychologist to meet returning hostages as they crossed back into Israel. [ref: 'Humanitarian intelligence': Debriefing head lays out protocol for questioning freed hostages, The Jerusalem Post] [ref: ]

===Debriefing Protocol: "Humanitarian Intelligence"===

Cohen authored the protocol for the psychological recovery and debriefing of returning hostages, and led the team that debriefed hostages released from Hamas captivity. He coined the term 'humanitarian intelligence' to describe an intelligence-gathering approach that centers on the trauma victim's wellbeing, contrasting it with existing US protocols that prioritize security debriefing immediately upon a hostage's return.

Cohen drew on lessons from the reception of Israeli POWs after the 1973 Yom Kippur War, noting that those POWs had described their treatment upon return as one of the worst aspects of their captivity experience.

Cohen has also written about post-traumatic growth (PTG), arguing that national trauma can serve as a catalyst for societal renewal. [ref: From national PTSD to national post-traumatic growth: Israel must turn pain to power, The Jerusalem Post]
