Kh. Asadul Islam, also known as Kh. Asadul Islam Ripon, is a Bangladeshi financial executive and capital-market professional. He has served as the managing director and chief executive officer of Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited since June 2014. His previous positions include chief executive officer of IDLC Securities Limited, executive vice president and head of brokerage at The City Bank Limited, and managing director and chief executive officer of City Brokerage Limited. [ref: ]

His professional activities have included securities brokerage, investment management, institutional investor services, and commentary on Bangladesh's capital-market development. He also briefly served as a non-executive director of Asia Frontier Capital in 2013–2014. [ref: Asia Frontier Capital (AFC) - Asia Frontier Capital, www.asiafrontiercapital.com]

== Career ==

=== Early career ===
Islam began his professional career at Premium Securities Limited before moving to Peregrine Capital Limited and Union Capital Limited. In 2002, he became a director of SES Company Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of Union Capital, where he remained until 2006. He subsequently joined IDLC Securities Limited, serving as its chief executive officer. [ref: Kh Asadul joins City Bank as Head of Brokerage, today.thefinancialexpress.com.bd]

In July 2009, Islam joined The City Bank Limited as executive vice president and head of brokerage, following his tenure at IDLC Securities.

=== City Brokerage Limited ===
On 24 November 2010, The Financial Express reported Islam's appointment as chief executive officer of City Brokerage Limited, a wholly owned subsidiary of The City Bank Limited. He was also described in subsequent reporting as the company's founding managing director and CEO. [ref: City Brokerage Limited appoints new CEO, today.thefinancialexpress.com.bd]

During his tenure, City Brokerage provided securities brokerage services to local and foreign investors. In January 2014, The Daily Star quoted Islam on the growth of foreign portfolio investment in Bangladesh during 2013. He attributed the increase partly to macroeconomic indicators and discussed the influence of interest rates, exchange rates, and international market conditions on foreign investment. [ref: ]

=== Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited ===
In June 2014, Islam was appointed managing director and chief executive officer of Alliance Capital Asset Management Limited, an investment management company operating in Bangladesh's mutual-fund industry. [ref: ]

In November 2014, Alliance Capital announced plans to introduce a Shariah-based equity index for institutional investors. The proposed index, developed using research from S&P Dow Jones Indices, was intended to help institutional investors identify Shariah-compliant investment opportunities. Islam discussed the proposed product and its investment objectives in an interview with The Daily Star. The announcement concerned a planned launch rather than a confirmed launch of the index. [ref: ]

In October 2022, Alliance Capital received second place in the asset-management category of the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission's Golden Jubilee of Bangladesh awards, which recognized market intermediaries for their performance in 2021. The award was presented to the company during Islam's tenure as its managing director and CEO. [ref: ]

== International financial activities ==
In October 2013, Asia Frontier Capital, an investment firm focused on frontier markets, announced Islam's appointment as a non-executive director. At the time, he was serving as the managing director and CEO of City Brokerage Limited. [ref: Asia Frontier Capital — October 2013 Newsletter, www.asiafrontiercapital.com]

In February 2014, Asia Frontier Capital's newsletter featured an interview with Islam concerning Bangladesh's economic conditions, investment environment, and opportunities for international investors. [ref: Asia Frontier Capital (AFC) - February 2014 Newsletter - Asia Frontier Capital, www.asiafrontiercapital.com]

In April 2014, Asia Frontier Capital announced that Islam had stepped down from his directorship for personal reasons. [ref: Asia Frontier Capital (AFC) - October 2013 Newsletter - Asia Frontier Capital, www.asiafrontiercapital.com]

His international professional involvement also included discussions of foreign portfolio investment in Bangladesh's securities market through his roles in brokerage and asset management. [ref: ]

== Contributions to capital-market discussions ==
Islam has participated in public discussions on Bangladesh's securities market, investment-product diversification, regulatory coordination, and the participation of institutional and foreign investors.

In December 2011, The Daily Star published his article "Stockmarket: what next?", which examined market instability following the 2010–2011 stock-market decline. The article advocated greater coordination between financial regulators, more transparent supervision, and the introduction of diversified investment instruments, including bonds and index-traded funds. Soren Johnstone is a Canadian filmmaker, cinematographer, editor, producer and screenwriter based in Vancouver, British Columbia. His work includes narrative films, documentary films, action-sports productions and television. He is known for directing the feature film Play with Fire and the documentary Hicks on Sticks. [ref: Hicks on Sticks, Film Threat]

Johnstone began making videos in the 1990s, initially filming skateboarding and snowboarding in the West Kootenay region of British Columbia. His later work has included the documentary Lost in Havana and the travel and action-sports television series Getting Amongst.

== Career ==
=== Early work ===
Johnstone began creating videos in the mid-1990s. His interest in filmmaking developed while filming friends skateboarding and snowboarding in British Columbia's West Kootenay region. According to his professional biography, he co-founded a production company in his early twenties and subsequently began producing professional video work. [ref: About, Soren Johnstone]

His early work was associated with skateboarding, snowboarding and other action sports. His action-sports productions include Attention Deficit, Under Exposed and Distortion. [ref: Soren Johnstone, Soren Johnstone]

This work garnered national attention when Johnstone received a YTV Achievement Award for Visual Arts. [ref: ]

=== Play with Fire ===
Johnstone wrote and directed the independent feature film Play with Fire. He also worked as cinematographer, editor and co-producer on the production. [ref: Play With Fire (IMDb), IMDb]

The film was completed in 2009. Contemporary coverage of the production by The Cascade reported that the film received a Best Cinematography award at an international film festival in Toronto. [ref: Play with Fire: Indie film premiere grips crowd at the Reach, The Cascade]

The film was shot in British Columbia and was produced independently. Johnstone worked with producer Michael Babiarz on the production.

=== Hicks on Sticks ===
Johnstone wrote and directed the feature-length documentary Hicks on Sticks, which documents a skateboarding and music tour through Western Canada. [ref: Hicks on Sticks definitely on a roll, [[Montreal Gazette]

The documentary originated with footage Johnstone recorded while accompanying the tour in 1999. The tour brought together four skateboarders and two bands and travelled through small communities in Western Canada with a portable skateboard park. The objective was to bring skateboarding and live music to young people in communities where those activities were not readily available. [ref: 2012 Action Sports Film Series, Newport Beach Film Festival]

The Newport Beach Film Festival presented the world premiere of Hicks on Sticks in 2012. Festival material described the film as a Canadian production directed by Johnstone and documented the tour as travelling approximately 1,800 miles through Western Canada while towing a 5,000-pound portable skateboard park.

More than a decade after the original tour, Johnstone combined footage recorded during the 1999 trip with later interviews with participants to create the documentary.

Film critic Scott Knopf reviewed Hicks on Sticks for Film Threat in 2012. Knopf commented positively on Johnstone's use of extensive footage from the original tour and described the resulting story as captivating.

The film runs approximately 115 minutes. Johnstone is credited as director, writer and producer, with Michael Babiarz also serving as producer. [ref: Hicks on Sticks, Rotten Tomatoes]

The documentary features skateboarders Josh Evin, Eugene Voykin, Mike Evans and Shane Wallace. The Newport Beach Film Festival described the original tour as involving four skateboarders and two bands travelling through Western Canada with a portable skateboard park. Apple TV also lists the film as a 2012 documentary directed by Johnstone. [ref: Hicks on Sticks, Apple TV]

In 2013, Johnstone was interviewed by Martlet, the student newspaper of the University of Victoria, about making Hicks on Sticks and the Canadian skateboarding culture depicted in the documentary. [ref: Canadian skate culture explored in documentary, Martlet]

=== Lost in Havana ===
Johnstone later directed Lost in Havana, a documentary centred on skateboarding and travel in Cuba. The film continued his work documenting action sports and the communities surrounding them.

Johnstone served as director, cinematographer and editor on the production.

=== Getting Amongst ===
Johnstone subsequently worked on Getting Amongst, a documentary television series created by Jon Caften, combining travel, action sports and local culture. Johnstone worked as a director, camera director and editor on the series.

The program follows participants travelling internationally and interacting with local communities while taking part in skateboarding and other action sports. The series was broadcast and distributed by Tastemade and was also made available through digital distribution platforms. The show is the intellectual property of Wildkind Media, of which Johnstone is the president.

Episodes of Getting Amongst were produced in countries including Slovenia, South Africa, Paraguay, Cambodia, Portugal, South Korea, Sweden, Lebanon, the Netherlands and Panama.

----

Gianfranco Conti is an applied linguist, language educator and author known for developing Extensive Processing Instruction (EPI), an approach to foreign-language teaching. EPI, sometimes described as the "Conti method", has been discussed in research published by the British Council and in professional publications on language education.

Conti has co-authored books with Steve Smith on language pedagogy, listening instruction and memory, including The Language Teacher Toolkit, Breaking the Sound Barrier: Teaching Language Learners How to Listen and Memory: What Every Language Teacher Should Know. His publications have been reviewed in journals including Applied Linguistics, English Australia Journal and Convergence.

== Career ==

Conti has worked as a language teacher and teacher educator in primary, secondary and higher education. His professional work has addressed second-language acquisition, memory, listening instruction, curriculum design and classroom pedagogy.

In October 2023, Conti delivered professional-development sessions for teachers from secondary schools and some primary schools in Guernsey. The Bailiwick Express reported on the training, which focused on EPI and the MARS EARS framework, alongside changes in French teaching at Les Beaucamps High School and increased uptake of GCSE French there. [ref: Metacognitive strategies prove successful, Bailiwick Express]

In May 2026, the Ballarat Times reported on a professional-development event in Victoria, Australia, attended by more than 100 language teachers, at which Conti discussed his approach to language teaching. [ref: Engaging students in language key, expert says, Ballarat Times] In February 2026, the Gorey Guardian profiled Conti ahead of a planned professional-development conference in County Wexford, Ireland. The article reported that more than 50 teachers had attended his previous workshop in 2024 and quoted French teacher Karen Murphy on his influence within language-teaching networks and the use of his instructional methods. [ref: World renowned language specialist set to return to Wexford, Gorey Guardian]

== Extensive Processing Instruction ==

Conti developed Extensive Processing Instruction (EPI), a language-teaching approach emphasising repeated processing of language patterns and multiword units, scaffolded practice and progression towards independent language use. [ref: Content and language integrated learning and extensive processing instruction: A useful partnership for language teaching?, British Educational Research Association]

The approach uses sentence builders and structured listening, reading, speaking and writing activities. It is associated with the MARS EARS instructional sequence: modelling, awareness-raising, receptive processing, structured production, expansion, autonomy, routinisation and spontaneity.

=== Commentary and professional reception ===

In 2021, Elisabeth Wallmann examined EPI in an article published by the British Educational Research Association, discussing its possible relationship with content and language integrated learning (CLIL). She considered potential benefits and limitations, including questions concerning vocabulary range and cultural content.

Sonja Fedrizzi described adapting Conti's MARS EARS framework for blended and remote language teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic in Scottish Languages Review. [ref: Modern Languages during a pandemic: how instructional videos, Conti's MARSEARS framework and strong routines have enriched my practice, Scottish Languages Review] The approach has also been discussed in Babel, the journal of the Australian Federation of Modern Language Teachers Associations, in practitioner accounts of classroom teaching. [ref: From Silence to Socialising, Babel]

In March 2022, Camille Robinson published an article on the French-language website of tutoring company GoStudent examining Conti's language-teaching methodology, professional background and associated classroom activities. [ref: Apprendre les langues grâce à la méthode Gianfranco Conti, GoStudent]

In the July 2022 issue of Languages Victoria, published by the Modern Language Teachers' Association of Victoria, Andrea Truckenbrodt cited Conti and Smith's work in an article about scaffolding writing with visuals. [ref: Scaffolding writing using visuals, Languages Victoria] The same issue announced a professional-development workshop on EPI and MARS EARS led by Conti. [ref: MLTAV Professional Learning, Languages Victoria]

=== Educational policy commentary ===

In September 2026, Ian Collen of Queen's University Belfast cited Conti's views on vocabulary selection in an article for The Conversation about proposed curriculum reforms in Northern Ireland. Collen distinguished the frequency of words in language corpora from their relevance to younger language learners, drawing on Conti's argument. [ref: Proposed curriculum in Northern Ireland would restrict children's language learning, The Conversation]

The Monastery of Saint Petka is a Serbian Orthodox monastery for women. It is dedicated to Saint Paraskeva of the Balkans and is located near the Pet Jezera urban settlement in Bijeljina, Bosnia and Herzegovina. [ref: „Манастир Свете Петке, Пет Језера у Бијељини“, Namjesništvo bijeljinsko.]

Ehrigite is a sub-microscopic bismuth telluride mineral with the chemical formula. Formally approved by the International Mineralogical Association (IMA) in 2024, it is a member of the tetradymite group of minerals. [ref: Ehrigite, a new mineral from the tetradymite group, Mineralogical Magazine] The mineral is named in honor of Dr. Kathy Ehrig, a prominent chief geologist at BHP, recognizing her contributions to geometallurgy and ore microscopy. [ref: New mineral named after BHP geologist Dr Kathy Ehrig, Mining Weekly] [ref: New mineral named after BHP geologist Dr Kathy Ehrig, BHP] [ref: World-first new mineral identified using electron microscopy, Microscopy Australia]

== Properties ==
Due to its sub-microscopic nature, ehrigite is rarely seen as discrete macro-crystals. Under reflected light microscopy, it appears opaque and pale gray, resembling other native bismuth and bismuth telluride minerals. Grains isolated by researchers are typically smaller than 100 microns.

== Discovery ==
The mineral was discovered by a research team led by scientists at the University of Adelaide, including Associate Professor Cristiana Ciobanu and Professor Nigel Cook. The type locality for ehrigite is the abandoned Good Hope gold mine in Hedley, British Columbia, Canada, where it occurs alongside other bismuth-rich minerals. [ref: https://resourcesreview.com.au/news_article/new-mineral-ehrigite-recognised-by-international-authority-honouring-bhp-scientists-legacy/]

Draft text:
== The Once and Future World Order ==
The Once and Future World Order: Why Global Civilization Will Survive the Decline of the West is a 2025 book by international relations scholar Amitav Acharya, [ref: ] published by Basic Books in April 2025. [ref: The Once and Future World Order, John Murray Press] The book explores the historical development of world order across different civilizations and regions, beginning with ancient Sumer and Egypt and extending through Persia, Greece, India, China, Rome, the Islamic world, Africa, the Americas, and Europe to the contemporary international system. [ref: The once and future world order: why global civilization will survive the decline of the West, Basic Books] The book examines the development of political ideas, institutions, and practices associated with relations among states and societies, including diplomacy, trade, political organization, war, and interstate cooperation, and concludes with a discussion of the changing international order and the implications of declining Western dominance.

== Contents ==
The book consists of an introduction and fourteen chapters, tracing the development of different world orders and interactions among societies throughout history, before turning to the contemporary international system and its possible future.

The book begins by underscoring that different ideas and institutions so commonly associated with today’s US-led “Western” world order emerged in non-Western civilizations thousands of years before the rise of the West. These range from peace treaties and interstate cooperation to freedom of the seas and environmental protection. Acharya argues that these contributions have often been overlooked in the mainstream history of international relations and world orders.

The book examines how the dominance of the European perspective over the last 500 years has contributed to two forms of historical misrepresentation: the sin of commission and the sin of omission. The sin of commission is largely the misinterpretation or distortion of the achievements of non-Western cultures and civilizations. The sin of omission occurs when fundamental facts about them are overlooked. A significant portion of the book is a chronicle of these sins. Acharya reveals what has been distorted, obscured, or omitted about non-Western civilizations. At the same time, the book considers the achievements and failures of both Western and non-Western civilizations. It also examines how the illusion of benevolence has repeatedly become a common denominator of imperial discourse. [ref: Review of the Once and Future World Order: Why Global Civilization Will Survive the Decline of the West, International Studies Review]

The civilizations explored in this book can be classified into four broad categories. Parallel civilizations coexist independently, with little interaction among them. Congruent civilizations exhibit accidental similarities despite the vast physical distance between them. Interactive civilizations can be known for their markedly asymmetrical relationships. Finally, a convergent civilization in theory entails the merging of civilizational values on the basis of parity of esteem.

In its discussion of the contemporary world order, the book identifies three schools of thought regarding the future of the United States as a preeminent power. The first, so-called “cry-wolf” school, postulates that the theory about the decline of the United States is nothing new. It has come and gone, but the United States remains the leading power, with no reason to assume that the future will be any different. The second is the “bionic-man” argument, which concedes that America is indeed on the decline, but it is likely to rebound. The third, the “Roman Empire” analogy, suggests that the US’s decline will be slow, like that of the Roman Empire, and may take up to two centuries.

The book also explores three fears in the West today about the end of the American-led Western order: the fear of the rise of the “civilization states,” the fear of the Chinese-built and Chinese-led order, and the fear of “chaos, violence, and conflict.” Although the future may not be “a garden of peace”, Acharya suggests, based on his examination of historical world orders, that the emerging order may be more humane and, almost certainly, no less so than the current world order.

== References ==

The European Academy of Childhood-onset Disability (EACD), formerly known as the European Academy of Childhood Disability, is an international multidisciplinary professional association focused on childhood onset disability. Established in 1989, it promotes research, education and cooperation among professionals working with people with childhood-onset disabilities in Europe and beyond. [ref: About us, European Academy of Childhood-onset Disability]Its members work in fields including medicine, health profession, social work, education and research. EACD has more than 500 members representing over 35 countries. [ref: Welcome to the European Academy of Childhood Disability, EACD Education]
__TOC__
== History ==
British child neurologist Brian Neville was EACD's founding chair and served from 1989 to 2000. He was succeeded by British developmental paediatrician Martin Bax, who chaired the academy from 2000 to 2008. [ref: Our organisation, European Academy of Childhood-onset Disability] Bax was also the editor of Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology. [ref: Martin Bax obituary, The Guardian]EACD was registered as a charitable organization in the United Kingdom in 1992 and as an international not-for-profit association in Belgium in 2021. In 2014, it joined the American Academy for Cerebral Palsy and Developmental Medicine and the Australasian Academy of Cerebral Palsy and Developmental Medicine in establishing the International Alliance of Academies of Childhood Disability. [ref: 'Better Together': achieving a global professional network for childhood disability, Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology] In 2016, EACD hosted its 28th annual meeting in Stockholm jointly with an international cerebral palsy conference and the alliance's first international meeting. [ref: Past meetings, EACD Education]

== Activities and education ==
EACD organizes an annual meeting hosted in a different European city every year. The meetings include presentations of research, educational courses and discussions involving clinicians and researchers. [ref: EACD Annual Meeting, European Academy of Childhood-onset Disability] The 38th annual meeting, held at the University of Galway in Ireland in June 2026, attracted approximately 1,300 delegates from 62 countries. A further 350 people participated in its public Experience Village, which was co-designed with people with lived experience and offered accessible activities, demonstrations and disability-related information. [ref: EACD Galway 2026 Wrap-Up, EACD Education]

Education is a central part of the academy's work. EACD maintains a digital educational platform that provides access to lectures, webinars, presentations from annual meetings, clinical resources and other material relating to childhood-onset disability. Its archives make educational content from previous meetings available beyond the annual congresses. [ref: EACD Education, EACD Education]In addition to its annual meetings, EACD organizes training for early-career researchers and clinicians. Summer schools were held in Pisa, Italy, in 2019 and 2022 and in Poznań, Poland, in 2023, [ref: Summer School for Early Career Researchers focusing on Childhood-onset Disabilities, European Academy of Childhood-onset Disability] and an autumn school at the University of Pisa 2025 on digital technologies and artificial intelligence in evidence-based medicine and rehabilitation. [ref: Autumn School 2025, EACD Education]

EACD has initiated clinical-practice recommendations relating to childhood-onset disabilities. These include recommendations on the definition, diagnosis, assessment and treatment of Developmental Coordination Disorder, first published in 2012 and subsequently updated as international recommendations in 2019. [ref: European Academy for Childhood Disability (EACD): recommendations on the definition, diagnosis and intervention of developmental coordination disorder, Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology] [ref: International clinical practice recommendations on the definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects of developmental coordination disorder, Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology]

Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology is an official journal of EACD and several other professional organizations concerned with paediatric neurology and childhood disability. [ref: Developmental Medicine & Child Neurology: Overview, Wiley Online Library]

== References ==

Draft text:
Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club is an English cricket club based in west London. It plays in the Premier Division of the Middlesex County Cricket League and is one of the closest clubs to the centre of London.

In 2026 Shepherd’s Bush CC won the ECB National Club Cricket Championship, [ref: Shepherd's Bush win National Cup] the most prestigious competition in English club cricket. They have also won the Middlesex Cup three times, in 1981, 1994 and 2024, [ref: Middlesex Cup Winners] as well as the Middlesex T20 Cup (2024). [ref: MCCL-T20-2024-Winners:Shepherds Bush]

The club was founded in 1882 [ref: History of Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club] by young men from the Shepherd's Bush parish church, St Stephen's, under the presidency of the vicar. Initially called St Stephen’s CC, they played first in a field just west of Old Oak Road in East Acton, then on a nearby tree-lined ground on East Acton Lane, remaining there for almost 120 years. In 1893, the club became known as Shepherd's Bush.

The first pavilion was erected in 1909, then replaced with a larger structure in 1935, after which the ground developed a reputation as one of the prettiest in London. [ref: History of Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club]

Among the earliest of more than 20 first class players to have played for the club were Manek Bajana of Somerset and Charles Burgess of Sussex, both in the early 1900s.

Shepherd’s Bush CC was one of the 16 founding members of the Middlesex County Cricket League in 1972. Having enjoyed a reputation as a sociable and hospitable club, during the 1980s and 1990s it became renowned for having a strong contingent of players from the Caribbean diaspora, [ref: We Were Pioneers] including Martin Jean-Jacques, who went on to play for Derbyshire and Hampshire, and Kervin Marc, who played for Middlesex. During that era, Jamaican-born Alf Langley, who is now the club’s president, had three spells as club captain. [ref: Interview with Alf Langley]

In the early 2000s the Goldsmiths company, which owned the East Acton Lane ground, declined to renew the club's lease and sold the land to developers, forcing the club to build a new facility just a few yards to the south in Bromyard Avenue, East Acton. It moved there in 2004. [ref: History of Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club]

Since then the club has been active in coaching initiatives in local primary schools. It has in excess of 250 boy and girl juniors, as well as three women's teams, five Saturday men’s teams and a Sunday team. It is one of the few clubs in the UK still maintaining the tradition of holding a Cricket Week each summer, with five midweek home matches against invited sides in July. [ref: Shepherd's Bush Cricket Club narrowly lose to Marylebone]

Shepherd's Bush's victory in the National Knockout Competition in 2026 came against the Bradford Premier League side New Farnley, [ref: New Farnley Cricket Club] of Leeds. They became the first Middlesex County Cricket League club to lift the national trophy since 1991.

SMiB describes its product approach as “DEVICOS”, a term referring to the combined use of cosmetic hair-care products and a scalp-care device. The plasma scalp massager is intended to be used alongside the company’s topical products as part of a home hair-care routine. In addition to its anti-hair-loss products, SMiB sells anti-ageing and anti-frizz hair-care products, including colour-change shampoo for grey hair and repair-focused products.

== Products ==
SMiB markets hair & scalp-care products through several product ranges. The brand’s products are primarily sold as shampoo, hair treatment, scalp essence, hair masks, scalp-cleansing products and home-use scalp-care devices. [ref: SMiB Products Review: This Iconic Brand Changed My Hair!] Its product line is aimed at consumers seeking products for general hair maintenance and scalp-related concerns, including oily scalp, dandruff, dryness, frizz, thinning hair and hair fall. [ref: About us - SMIB SINGAPORE PTE LTD, SMiB 스미브]

Coral Calcium Anti Hair Loss range

The Coral Calcium Anti Hair Loss range is SMiB’s principal product line. [ref: SMiB Anti Hair Loss Series - 500ML Coral Calcium Shampoo, SMiB 스미브] It includes Coral Calcium Shampoo, Coral Calcium Treatment, Hair Scalp Essence and a Plasma Scalp Massager. The products are sold individually and as bundled sets.

According to SMiB, the range uses coral calcium as a key ingredient, together with ingredients including biotin, niacinamide, dexpanthenol and zinc pyrithione. The company markets the products towards users with oily scalps, thinning hair, hair fall and postpartum hair fall. These uses are product-marketing claims made by the company and should not be presented as medical treatment claims.

The Plasma Scalp Massager is a handheld device intended for use alongside the shampoo, treatment and scalp essence. SMiB describes it as part of its “DEVICOS” approach, combining a device with cosmetic hair-care products. The company states that the device is intended to support scalp cleansing and product application as part of a home-use hair-care routine.

LactoBio Anti-Frizz & Repair range

SMiB also sells the LactoBio Anti-Frizz & Repair range. The range includes LactoBio shampoo, hair-mask treatment and scalp-scaler products. It is marketed for people with dry, damaged or frizzy hair, and is positioned by the company as a hair-maintenance range rather than a hair-loss line. [ref: SMiB Anti-Frizz & Repair Series - LactoBio Shampoo, SMiB 스미브]

The LactoBio range is sold in Singapore and Malaysia through SMiB’s regional online store. Product descriptions refer to probiotic-based hair-care ingredients, though specific performance claims should be attributed to the company unless supported by independent scientific sources.

Anti-Aging range

SMiB’s Anti-Aging range includes a Colour Change Shampoo and associated bundled products. The shampoo is marketed as a gradual colour-depositing product designed to blend or reduce the visibility of grey hair through repeated use. [ref: SMiB Anti-Aging Series - Colour Change Shampoo for Grey Hair, SMiB 스미브] Unlike conventional permanent hair dyes, the product is marketed as part of a regular shampoo routine.

According to SMiB, the Colour Change Shampoo was developed by its research and development team in South Korea. The product is available through the company’s Singapore and Malaysia distribution channels, while Korean SMiB online stores list additional hair-care products for the domestic South Korean market.

Sales and availability

SMiB products are sold through its official Singapore website and selected online retail platforms. The Singapore site lists delivery within Singapore and Malaysia, as well as shipping options to selected international destinations. Separate SMiB online stores in South Korea offer products for the Korean market. [ref: 스미브 온라인 스토어, 스미브]

== Availability ==
SMiB products are sold in South Korea through the brand’s Korean online stores. The company’s Korean product listings include hair-care products such as LactoBio shampoo, colour-change shampoo and other scalp-care products.

In Singapore, products are distributed through SMIB SINGAPORE PTE. LTD., a Singapore-incorporated company. The company was incorporated on 19 June 2019 and lists wholesale and retail of cosmetics and toiletries among its business activities.

José Aragüez is a Spanish-born architect, author, and educator. He has developed his intellectual production and teaching career mainly in the schools of architecture at Princeton University, Columbia University, and Yale University. His writings sit at the intersection of modern and contemporary architecture, the history of science and computation, and several modes of philosophical inquiry. He is the founding principal of Spatial Infrastructure Research Office (SIRO), an architecture, urbanism, and research practice.

== Early life and education ==

José Aragüez was born in Málaga. In 2006, he completed a B.Arch./M.Arch. at the University of Granada, where his interest in conceptual architecture was nurtured under the guidance of a group of teachers including Antonio Jiménez Torrecillas and Juan Domingo Santos. Upon graduation, he received a university-wide Graduation Extraordinary Award and was also awarded a 1st National End-of-Degree Prize in Architecture from the Spanish Ministry of Culture. [ref: Order ECI/3313/2007, of 24 October, awarding the National End-of-Degree Prizes for University Education for the 2005-2006 academic year. Retrieved October 09, 2026. https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=BOE-A-2007-19732] [ref: Roche, Antonio (6 November 2007). "Un Licenciado con Proyección." SUR. Retrieved February 23, 2026. https://www.diariosur.es/20071106/malaga/licenciado-proyeccion-20071106.html]

In 2008 Aragüez moved to New York City to pursue post-professional studies at Columbia University. At Columbia GSAPP he studied architectural design with François Roche and Juan Herreros as well as history and theory with Mark Wigley and Kenneth Frampton, who trained him in architectural theory and critical history, respectively.

== Architecture career ==

Prior to his move to New York City, José Aragüez received an Arquia Banca Foundation grant based on holding one of the top student records in architecture in Spain. [ref: "Becas Fundación Arquia. Ganadores convocatoria 2005." Fundación Arquia. Retrieved February 27, 2026. https://fundacion.arquia.com/convocatorias/becas/convocatoria-2005/ganadores/] After a stint at the Granada-based office of Antonio Jiménez Torrecillas, it was through that grant that he relocated to Rotterdam to work for Dutch architecture firm MVRDV, in 2007. [ref: "Motorcity Alcañiz." MVRDV. Retrieved February 23, 2026. https://www.mvrdv.com/projects/90/motorcity-alcaniz] In 2022 he started his own eponymous architecture practice, rebranded as Spatial Infrastructure Research Office (SIRO) in 2026. SIRO's work has focused on architectural competitions and experimental design research. The practice has entered public tenders and design competitions across Spain and in several other European countries, operating with a small team between Madrid and New York.

== Academia ==

During the 2010s Aragüez conducted doctoral studies at Princeton University under Prof. Sylvia Lavin. He also studied with Hal Foster—who introduced him to the role of 20th-century French theory in art—and wrote a dissertation on the concept of spatial organization in architecture. Aside from Lavin, his committee comprised Stan Allen, Sanford Kwinter, and Axel Kilian, then a tenure-track professor at Princeton. [ref: "Final Public Oral Exam of José Aragüez Escobar." Princeton University SoA. Retrieved February 23, 2026. https://soa.princeton.edu/content/final-public-oral-exam-jos%C3%A9-araguez-escobar]

In addition to his teaching engagements, he has lectured extensively at venues including Harvard University, Yale University, Columbia University, ETH Zurich, Brno University of Technology, The Berlage, the A+D Museum in Los Angeles, MIT, Cooper Union, Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, Kyoto University, Higher Technical School of Architecture of Madrid, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne, the Architectural Association School of Architecture, Rice University in Paris, Polytechnic University of Turin, and the Venice Biennale of Architecture. [ref: "The Building." Real Colegio Complutense at Harvard University. Retrieved February 23, 2026. https://rcc.harvard.edu/event/building] [ref: "José Aragüez: Dispositional Intelligence." The Cooper Union. Retrieved February 23, 2026. https://cooper.edu/events-and-exhibitions/events/book-talk-jose-araguez-dispositional-intelligence]

Draft: Die Gstettensaga: The Rise of Echsenfriedl

Draft text:
Die Gstettensaga: The Rise of Echsenfriedl is a 2014 Austrian post-apocalyptic science fiction comedy film directed by Johannes Grenzfurthner and written by Grenzfurthner and Roland Gratzer. Produced by the art group monochrom and the media collective Traum & Wahnsinn, it premiered on ORF III on 10 March 2014 as part of the broadcaster's Artists in Residence series. [ref: ORF III am Dokumontag: Der Arabische Frühling und seine Auswirkungen zwischen Traditionalismus und Freiheitswillen, APA-OTS]

Set in post-apocalyptic Austria, the film satirizes media monopolies, hacker culture and the politics of technological change. [ref: Österreichischer Mad Max II, Telepolis] [ref: Film Review: Die Gstettensaga: A Call to Class Consciousness for Hackers, 2600: The Hacker Quarterly]

== Plot ==
In the early 21st century, a conflict between China and Google escalates into the nuclear "Google Wars", destroying much of civilization. Decades later, a new society has formed among the ruins of Austria. In Mega City Schwechat, media proprietor Thurnher von Pjölk dominates public information through his newspaper and claims to have reinvented printing with movable type. His position is threatened by technologically minded "nerds" who have rediscovered television.

Pjölk sends journalist Fratt Aigner and technician Alalia Grundschober into the wasteland of Niederpröll to find the inventor Echsenfriedl and conduct a televised interview. Along the way they encounter armed postal workers, farmers who revere surviving European Union paperwork, undead miners and a community of traders. They also learn that several inventions credited to Pjölk may have originated with Echsenfriedl.

When they finally reach the inventor, they discover that he is a basilisk whose gaze turns people to stone. Pjölk intends to broadcast his image, killing the early adopters of television and protecting his newspaper monopoly. The scheme is exposed through the broadcast, and Pjölk is overthrown. Echsenfriedl subsequently takes over Pjölk's media empire, becoming the new media mogul and pushing for rapid technological innovation. Fratt and Alalia are hired to work for him.

== Production ==
The film was commissioned for ORF III's Artists in Residence series. In a September 2014 interview with Jungle World, Grenzfurthner said that ORF III had approved the proposal in late October 2013 for a March 2014 broadcast, and that the film had been shot in five days with €5,000 available for production. [ref: »Das Schockmoment ist nur noch Selbstmarketing«, Jungle World] [ref: Die Gstettensaga: The Rise of Echsenfriedl, pressplay]

Grenzfurthner and Gratzer developed the screenplay in November 2013, incorporating material from monochrom's earlier role-playing theatre project Campaign. Filming took place in December 2013 and January 2014, followed by approximately five weeks of post-production. Rather than commissioning an original score, the filmmakers used existing electronic, chiptune and synth-pop music. [ref: Die GstettenSaga: The Rise of Echsenfriedl. A post-apocalyptic aftermath of the 'Google Wars', Furtherfield]

The dialogue incorporates German, English, Austrian dialects and invented forms of speech. English subtitles sometimes deliberately depart from the spoken dialogue for comic effect.

An additional financing stunt was incorporated into the film itself: a notice resembling an anti-piracy warning invited viewers to report an allegedly unauthorized copy by calling a premium-rate telephone number. pressplay reported that the calls generated approximately €350. The filmmakers referred to the stunt as "crowdratting".

== Release ==
ORF III first broadcast the film on 10 March 2014. It was subsequently shown at the 2014 Slash Filmfestival in Vienna. The film was made available online in December 2015. [ref: Die Gstettensaga: a science fiction movie about the Google Wars, Boing Boing]

== Reception ==
Peter Mühlbauer, reviewing the film for Telepolis, discussed its post-apocalyptic media satire, performances and extensive cultural references. He singled out the deliberately inaccurate English subtitles as a further source of jokes and observed that much of the film's humor depended on the viewer recognizing its literary and cultural allusions.

Sebastian Vetter, writing for the Austrian cultural magazine skug, interpreted the film as a critique of failed revolutionary aspirations and of the political limits of technological subcultures. Comparing its post-apocalyptic landscape with the traditional Western, he argued that the film depicts progress as the recovery of a lost past rather than the creation of an alternative future. [ref: Pröll for ever – die Linke ist tot!, skug]

A May 2014 segment of Place de la Toile on France Culture described the film as an underground discovery for nerds, comparing it with Monty Python and the Frères Denis. [ref: Politique de l'algorithme, France Culture]

Bianca Hofbauer rated the film 8 out of 10 in pressplay. She praised the costumes, performances, dialogue and use of different languages, as well as the locations chosen to depict the post-apocalyptic landscape. She also found that the film's 72-minute running time felt overlong and prevented complete immersion in its fictional world.
[truncated]

Draft text:
WorkwithUSAID (launched as WorkwithUSAID.org and later WorkwithUSAID.gov) was a free online resource hub run by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) to help organizations learn how to partner with the agency and compete for its contracts, grants and cooperative agreements. Launched on 4 November 2021 by the Industry Liaison team in USAID's Office of Acquisition and Assistance and developed by the digital product studio Miew under USAID's Partnerships Incubator, [ref: USAID's Partnerships Incubator – Kaizen, A Tetra Tech Company, Anthem Awards] the platform offered a self-assessment tool, a searchable directory of prospective partners, aggregated funding opportunities, a private-sector portal, and a library of plain-language guidance, later translated into Arabic, French, Portuguese and Spanish. [ref: WorkwithUSAID, Partnership for Public Service] [ref: Case Study: Partner Engagement – WorkwithUSAID.gov, USAID Office of Acquisition and Assistance, Industry Liaison team] Nearly 20,000 organizations from more than 160 countries applied to join its Partner Directory, and the Partnerships Incubator program behind the site won a Gold Anthem Award for innovation in 2025. The site also received an honorable mention in Fast Companys 2023 World Changing Ideas Awards. [ref: World Changing Ideas Awards 2023: General Excellence finalists and honorable mentions, Fast Company] The site was shut down in 2025 during the Department of Government Efficiency's dismantling of USAID.

== Background ==
USAID worked with roughly 3,000 partner organizations a year in more than 100 countries. [ref: USAID wants to make it easier for partners to compete for its grant money, Federal News Network] Its funding was nonetheless concentrated among a small number of large implementers; in fiscal year 2021, 20 organizations received about 70 percent of the agency's funding. Prospective partners, particularly local organizations in partner countries and groups with no prior federal experience, reported that USAID's processes and language were complex and legalistic, that language barriers kept them from acting on opportunities in their own countries, and that entry points such as unsolicited proposals were difficult to use.

The platform supported the agency's New Partnerships Initiative and its broader effort to "localize" foreign assistance by directing more funding to local and first-time partners. [ref: 2023 USAID Customer Experience (CX), Performance.gov] USAID's designation as a federal High Impact Service Provider (HISP) in 2021 made the platform one of the agency's customer-experience commitments under the President's Management Agenda.

== History ==
=== Development and launch ===
The site was developed through USAID's Partnerships Incubator, a program for which Kaizen, A Tetra Tech Company, served as prime contractor. [ref: WorkwithUSAID.org Fact Sheet, USAID] Miew, a digital product studio with offices in Chicago and Porto, was the program's development lead and designed and built the platform. The site was initially hosted outside government systems.

WorkwithUSAID.org launched on 4 November 2021, as part of Administrator Samantha Power's "New Vision for Global Development" announcement. [ref: Advocacy Advisor: End of Year 2021, Humentum] USAID's chief acquisition officer, Mark Walther, described it as a site where "organizations can do self assessments and have other resource tools available to see how ready they are to partner directly with the agency". [ref: How procurement supports the mission at USAID, Federal News Network] The Industry Liaison team used a "hub and spoke" model: the website served as the central source of content, which was then distributed through social media, an email newsletter, webinars and industry events, with feedback from those channels and from user surveys used to shape new content. Power promoted the site in early 2022 as "a free, USAID-funded resource hub that empowers partners with the knowledge and networks to navigate how to work with USAID". [ref: Launch of WorkwithUSAID.org: Recent Initiative Announced by USAID Administrator Samantha Power, USAID Alumni Association]

In its first 13 months (to 15 December 2022) the site recorded about 1.7 million pageviews, approved 3,277 Partner Directory profiles and logged 2,464 completed pre-engagement assessments. Nearly 80 percent of directory members reported no previous USAID partnership experience, and about 60 percent were local organizations.

=== Expansion ===
In 2023 USAID expanded the platform, adding a funding feed that pulled solicitations from SAM.gov and Grants.gov by API, a page where prime partners could post subcontracting "sub-opportunities", an events calendar, and a portal for submitting and internally routing unsolicited proposals. [ref: USAID 2023 High Impact Service Provider Action Plan, Performance.gov] It also added a Corporate Partnering Portal to connect private-sector companies with USAID and its programs; the portal averaged about 175 unique users a month after launch. [ref: USAID 2024 High Impact Service Provider Action Plan, Performance.gov] Ruth Buckley, a USAID deputy assistant administrator, described the platform in 2024 as one of the agency's "big, big innovations". [ref: USAID Gathering CX Feedback Through Online Resource Hub, MeriTalk] In November 2024 the site was migrated from contractor hosting onto AidNet, USAID's internal network infrastructure.

Aleksandër Frangaj (born 4 October 1968) is an Albanian media entrepreneur and former journalist. He is the founder and majority shareholder of TV Klan, a television network established in 1997. [ref: TVSH, Klan dhe Top Channel dominojnë tregun televiziv në vend, Reporter.al]

== Early life and education ==

Frangaj was born in Lezhë, Albania, on 4 October 1968. He completed secondary education at Mujo Ulqinaku school in Durrës in 1987 and subsequently studied directing at the Academy of Fine Arts in Tirana, completing his studies in 1994. [ref: Aleksandër Frangaj: Hyj në politikë për t’u shërbyer njerëzve, Koha Jonë]

== Media career ==

In 1991, Frangaj became involved in the newspaper Koha Jonë, which was founded in Lezhë by Nikollë Lesi and became an independent publication that year. [ref: Koha Jonë, Media Ownership Monitor] Frangaj served as an editor at the newspaper during the early 1990s. [ref: Human Rights in Post-Communist Albania, Human Rights Watch]

In 1993, Frangaj and fellow journalist Martin Leka were arrested in connection with reporting about military affairs. The case was documented by human-rights organisations and press-freedom groups. [ref: Frangaj-Leka, Lesi: Si arrestoi Berisha dy gazetarët në '94, Shqiptarja.com]

In 1997, Frangaj established Media 6 with businessmen Julian Roche and Marsel Skëndo. The company published the weekly magazine Klan and launched the television station TV Klan.

TV Klan received a national terrestrial broadcasting licence in 2001. Its programming includes news, current affairs and entertainment. The programme Opinion (Albanian TV program))|Opinion]], hosted by journalist Blendi Fevziu, is among its current-affairs programmes.

In 2013, Media 6 changed its name to TV Klan. Frangaj holds 60% of the company's shares and his wife, Alba Gina, holds 40%.

Draft: Rhinoceros dolphin

Draft text:
The rhinoceros dolphin (Delphinus rhinoceros) is an alleged species of dolphin first discovered by French naval surgeons Jean René Constant Quoy and Joseph Paul Gaimard on the 19th of October, 1819, in the Pacific ocean while sailing between the Sandwich Islands (now the Hawaiian Islands) and New South Wales, Australia (5°28' N). [ref: Voyage Autour de Monde, Fait Par Ordere du Roi, Pillet Aîné, Printer-Bookseller, Rue Christine] It was formally described in Voyage Autour de Monde, Fait Par Ordere du Roi, a compendium of the scientific observations and accounts of the Uranie voyage around the world under the rule of Louis de Freycinet in 1824. The species is widely considered dubious. [ref: Delphinus rhinoceros, Quoy & Gaimard, 1824, World Cetacea Database]

== Morphology and discovery ==
The rhinoceros dolphin was described to have been dark in overall colour with sporadic white blotching along the dorsum which ceased around or soon after the dorsal fin closest to the fluke. The first dorsal fin was located close to or on the neck, and the species' head and face were not visible due to a hesitance to breach, a detail noted as being unlike the other dolphins encountered on the voyage. During interactions with the Uranie, the dolphins passed close to the prow of the vessel, though they did not surface frequently enough to be photographed. Consequently, the morphology of any potential beak or snout, was impossible to deduce. The cetaceans were encountered in a pod [ref: Mysterious Creatures: A Guide to Cryptozoology, ABC-CLIO] and individuals were said to have been double the length of a porpoise. Though the specific species of porpoise being referenced is not mentioned, if the size comparison was made in reference to the common porpoise (Phocoena phocoena), the rhinoceros dolphin would measure close to 3m (10ft) in length. Another two dorsal-finned cetacean resembling a dolphin was sighted breaching and playing amongst common dolphins (Delphinus delphinus) off Lantivet Bay, Cornwall, Wales, in April of 1856 by British naturalist Johnathan Couch who claimed them to have been a maximum of 2.4m (8ft) in length.

== Taxonomy and naming ==
The rhinoceros dolphin was named in reference to its frontal dorsal fin, a defining structure located close to or on the neck in superficial resemblence to the horn of a rhinoceros. [ref: The Natural History of the Ordinary Cetacea or Whales, Lizars] The species is not known from a type specimen or holotype, and is widely considered to be dubious altogether due to a lack of evidence supporting its existence beyond the description by Quoy and Gaimard. Upon description, Quoy and Gaimard suggested the taxonomic classification; (Delphinus rhinoceros), placing the species in the same genus as the common dolphin, though this conclusion was founded on little evidence. [ref: Cetaceans with two dorsal fins, Aquatic Mammals]

Later revisions of the taxonomy of the rhinoceros dolphin by French naturalist René Lesson in his 1828 book, Historie Naturelle Mammiferes place the species instead in the genus (Oxypterus). [ref: Historie Naturelle des Animaux Rares, Baudouin Brothers] This genus had been previously used by French naturalist and polymath Constantine Samuel Rafinesque in 1814 to refer to a large odotocete characterised by possessing two dorsal fins that had stranded itself 10km (6.2 miles) off Licata, Sicily in the September of 1741, which he had classified as O. mongitore. This specimen was said to have measured 13.2m (45ft) in length with a forked tail, a hole in its head that was leaking water, and a mouth equipped with strong teeth by Italian presbyter Antonio Mongitore, who illustrated the specimen along with two other whales, D. dalippus and Physeter urganantus. [ref: "Monstri Marini": Constantine S. Rafinesque's names for three of Antonio Montigore's Sicillian Whales, Archives of Natural History] Lesson refers to Oxypterus as a "subgenus" that he only gives serious attention to at all in light of the rhinoceros dolphin account. In Cetaceans with two dorsal fins, an article published as part of the seventeeth volume of the Aquatic Mammals journal in 1991, Michel Raynal dismissed this account as a misidentified basking shark (Cetorhinus maximus) rather than a newly undiscovered species of Mediterranean two dorsal-finned cetacean akin to the rhinoceros dolphin. Within the same article, Raynal proposed the hypothetical binomial name for the rhinoceros dolphin; (Cetodipterus rhinoceros), constituting a new genus within the family Delphinidae.

== Consensus in scientific literarure ==

=== In cryptozoology ===
Contemporary discussions of the rhinoceros dolphin occassionally refer to the species as a cryptid, an animal yet to be scientifically recognised due to a lack of substatiated evidence of its existence. It appeared in George M. Eberhart's 2002 book Mysterious Creatures: A Guide to Cryptozoology, where he described it as an "Unknown cetacean of the North Pacific Ocean" and discussed it alongside Couch's account of the two dorsal-finned dolphin spotted off Cornwall.
[truncated]

Knifetwister Records (stylized as knifetwister records) is an American independent record label and online music publication based in New York [ref: Pool Halls, Punk, and a Dog With a Grudge: Inside the World of Knifetwister Records with Raph Copeland, The MIC Magazine]. Founded by Raph Copeland in 2025, it focuses primarily on punk, hardcore, ska and metal, with an emphasis on independent and emerging artists. [ref: Single Use - Knifetwister Records, WRIR-LP 97.3 FM]

== History ==
Copeland established Knifetwister Records after previously working with musicians through music-video production and band management [ref: Punk Is Not Dead: How Knifetwister Records Is Keeping New York Loud, Mixed Alt Mag] [ref: Interview with Raph Copeland of knifetwister records, Racket Magazine]. The publication initially concentrated on the New York music scene before expanding its coverage beyond the region [ref: 2025 Recap, We Might Die]. Its interviews have included both established musicians and lesser-known independent acts [ref: Gallery 1, DOLL FEST], including interviews with War on Women, Dance Hall Crashers, 18fevers, Ryan Cassata and Angelo Moore of Fishbone. [ref: NY DIY Label Spotlight, In Effect Hardcore]

== Benefit compilations ==
The label's released the compilation Not in Our City in late 2025 [ref: Read a track-by-track breakdown for Knifetwister Records' new benefit comp, 'Not In Our City'!, www.punknews.org], which featured 21 bands with all proceeds toward The Bowery Mission, a New York City organization serving people experiencing homelessness. [ref: Knifetwister Records Compilation, coventrycarols.com] [ref: Current Reviews – In Effect Hardcore, ineffecthardcore.com] [ref: OfficialSoda - Releases, officialsoda.com]

A sequel, Not in Our City 2, followed in 2026 and benefited immigrant-rights organization Make the Road New York. [ref: Not in Our City 2 Charges for Compassion, In Spite Magazine] The compilation featured 22 bands from eight countries and included music spanning several punk subgenres. [ref: Music Review: Knifetwister Records' Not in Our City 2, A Punk Rock Compilation to Benefit Immigrant Rights, Rock DNA Magazine] [ref: Press - Saints of Lorain, saintsoflorain.com] [ref: Current Reviews – In Effect Hardcore, ineffecthardcore.com] [ref: Press, Skip The Needle]

A third compilation, Trans Riot!, to benefit the Transgender Law Center and Trans Closet Hudson Valley, is scheduled for release on November 20, 2026 [ref: ]

== Approach ==
Knifetwister's editorial coverage is centered largely on independent and underground music. [ref: Pool Halls, Punk, and a Dog With a Grudge: Inside the World of Knifetwister Records with Raph Copeland, THE MIC MG] [ref: knifetwister records’ Birthday Bash Show 7/26/2026!, Uncharted Music] Copeland has described providing exposure to smaller artists as one of the publication's primary goals and has stated that the magazine makes a particular effort to interview female-fronted and transgender bands.

Sigisfredo Garnica (born 30 December 1966, Chile) is a Chilean mycologist known for his work on the phylogeny and taxonomy of fungi, especially the ectomycorrhizal genus Cortinarius and the order Sebacinales. He studied biology and microbiology at the Universidad Austral de Chile and earned his doctorate at the University of Tübingen in 2003. After working in Tübingen for more than a decade, he joined the Universidad Austral de Chile in 2018. [ref: Dr. Sigisfredo Garnica Treufo, Facultad de Ciencias, Universidad Austral de Chile]

==Selected publications==

Yves Francesco Jeanne-Maria Gaspar is a physicist and researcher whose work focuses on mathematical cosmology [ref: Gaspar Yves (Catholic University, Milan) – “Time, between Mathematics and Physics” – Centre for Philosophy of Time], general relativity, gravitational physics, dynamical systems [ref: Late-time asymptotic dynamics of Bianchi VIII cosmologies, Classical and Quantum Gravity], and the conceptual foundations of physics. [ref: Randomness in Philosophy and Theology, Faraday Institute for Science and Religion] [ref: Gaspar, l'astrofisico belga che ha scelto Tregnago per amore, L'Arena] [ref: Realtà computabili: prospettive e limiti - Vatican News, Vatican News] He is a Visiting Scholar at St Edmund's College, University of Cambridge, and has been a professor with the Department of Mathematics and Physics of the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart in Brescia, Italy. [ref: "Un mondo improbabile", mistero di un universo sintonizzato, UCCR] His research has been published in Classical and Quantum Gravity, Foundations of Science and General Relativity and Gravitation.

== Education and career ==
Gaspar studied physics at the University of Liège in Belgium from 1990 to 1995, specializing in relativity and cosmology. He subsequently completed the Certificate of Advanced Studies in Mathematics, Part III of the Mathematical Tripos, at the University of Cambridge in1997. [ref: Dr Yves Gaspar, Faraday Institute for Science and Religion] He received his PhD from Cambridge in 2002 under the supervision of physicist John D. Barrow. His doctoral research examined the late-time behaviour of Bianchi type VIII cosmological models and resulted in the thesis Late-time behaviour of General Solutions to the Einstein Field Equations. [ref: Yves Gaspar - The Mathematics Genealogy Project, www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu] [ref: ]

Gaspar has taught cosmology and astrophysics at the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart in Brescia, including in its master's program in mathematics and physics. Since 2016, he has worked as a physics examiner and moderator for Cambridge Assessment International Education. [ref: Leonardo Da Vinci oltre le sue invenzioni, AllTopNetwork]

In 2020, Gaspar became a Visiting Research Scholar at St Edmund's College, Cambridge, where he is currently listed as a Visiting Scholar. [ref: Ci si può fidare della scienza?, Fondazione Toniolo Verona] His research has included cosmology and questions concerning randomness and uncomputability, including their implications for philosophy and theology.

== Research ==
Gaspar's early research concerned exact solutions of the Einstein field equations and the dynamics of homogeneous cosmological models. With John D. Barrow, he studied the late-time behaviour of Bianchi type VIII models, including whether chaotic behaviour occurring near an initial singularity persists during later cosmic evolution. Their findings were published in Classical and Quantum Gravity in 2001. [ref: Bianchi VIII empty futures, Classical and Quantum Gravity]

His subsequent work examined time asymmetry and chaotic behaviour in general relativity. In a 2004 paper in General Relativity and Gravitation, Gaspar investigated the late-time evolution of Bianchi VIII models and differences between approaches to their asymptotic behaviour. [ref: Time Asymmetry and Chaos in General Relativity, General Relativity and Gravitation]

Gaspar has also investigated complexity and unpredictability in gravitational systems. In Gravity and Complexity co-authored with Giovanni Acquaviva, he considered whether certain dynamical systems associated with the Einstein field equations could exhibit forms of unpredictability stronger than conventional chaos and whether some of their properties could be formally undecidable. [ref: Gravity and complexity, The European Physical Journal Plus]

His later research has increasingly incorporated philosophy of science and cosmology. With Paweł Tambor, he published The Laws of Nature and the Problems of Modern Cosmology in Foundations of Science, Springer Nature, examining the concept of natural laws in relation to modern cosmology, complex systems, time, causality, and the limits of mathematical descriptions. [ref: The Laws of Nature and the Problems of Modern Cosmology, Foundations of Science]  In 2025, Gaspar published the book (Cosmology Research – Addressing Current Problems with Astrophysics, Eds. Michael L. Smith and A. M. Mecit Ӧztas, IntechOpen, London, UK, 2025) chapter The Problems of Modern Cosmology, the Fine Tuning of Constants and Parameters, and the Notion of Time, which discusses unresolved problems in cosmology and questions concerning time, fundamental constants, initial conditions, and the limits of mathematical approaches to physical phenomena. He tried to show why mathematics has, in particular, difficulties with the concept of time, by reconsidering some simple foundational aspects of set theory. [ref: ]

Lauren Caster is a filmmaker and actress who wrote, directed, and starred in Rhythm Is a Dancer. Her work also includes the story concept for the Lifetime television film You're Not Supposed to Be Here. [ref: ] [ref: How an Isolated Camping Trip Inspired Lifetime Lesbian Thriller ‘You’re Not Supposed to Be Here’, TheWrap]

== Career ==
Caster's debut short film, Donor Baby, was acquired by Amazon. She subsequently made the short film Plan C.

In 2021, Caster won the inaugural PitchFest for Emerging Female Filmmakers, presented by WrapWomen and Lifetime, with You're Not Supposed to Be Here. The prize included a development deal with Lifetime. [ref: WrapWomen and Lifetime Name Winner of PitchFest for Emerging Female Filmmakers, TheWrap] The concept became a television film written by Erica Lane and directed by Nicole L. Thompson, which premiered on Lifetime on November 4, 2023.

In 2022, Caster earned a Grand Jury Honorable Mention for Bold and Honest Filmmaking for Plan C at the Utah Arts Festival's Fear No Film program. [ref: Focus on two independent short films with Utah significance: Arthur Veenema’s The Atomic Spawn and Lauren Caster’s Plan C, The Utah Review]

Caster made her feature directorial debut with Rhythm Is a Dancer, in which she plays Ro, a dancer who returns home to meet her biological father. The cast includes Amy Aquino and Tate Donovan. [ref: Austin Film Fest 2025 Interview: Lauren Caster, Amy Aquino, Tate Donovan and Marianne Mullerleile on Finding a Real Groove Together in “Rhythm is a Dancer”, The Moveable Fest] The film had its world premiere in competition at the Austin Film Festival in 2025. [ref: Austin Film Festival Debuts First Wave of Films and 2025 Writer’s Writer Award, Austin Film Festival] Its story was loosely inspired by Caster's experience of meeting her biological father.

In November 2025, the film was presented at the American Film Market to seek international sales representation and distribution. [ref: Austin Film Festival Hit ‘Rhythm Is a Dancer’ Heads to American Film Market for Worldwide Sales (EXCLUSIVE), Variety] It was subsequently released in the United States by Circle Collective, an imprint of Utopia, in July 2026. [ref: Exclusive Trailer for Rhythm Is a Dancer Finds Lauren Caster Making a Family Discovery, The Film Stage]

In September 2026, following the film’s limited theatrical release and availability on video on demand, Caster began a 30-day Instagram video diary campaign to find an audience for the film. Ivan M. Buzurović is a Serbian-American medical physicist and scientist who works in radiation oncology and medical physics. He is a professor in the Department of Radiation Oncology at Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston, Massachusetts. His research focuses on brachytherapy, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided radiation treatment, radiation dosimetry, and methods for improving the accuracy of radiation therapy.

== Academic career ==
Buzurović has conducted research in medical physics and radiation oncology at academic medical institutions in the United States, including Thomas Jefferson University and the Dana-Farber/Brigham and Women's Cancer Center, affiliated with Harvard Medical School. His work combines imaging, computational methods, radiation physics, and clinical treatment planning. [ref: ]Buzurović serves as a clinical mentor in the Harvard Medical Physics Residency Program [ref: Clinical Mentors at BWH: Harvard Medical Physics Residency Program].

== Research ==
Buzurović's research has addressed the development and evaluation of imaging-based methods for planning and verifying brachytherapy treatments. Brachytherapy is a form of radiation therapy in which a radioactive source is placed inside or near a tumor to deliver a prescribed radiation dose. [ref: Brachytherapy for Cancer - NCI, www.cancer.gov]

In 2011, while working as a medical physics resident and researcher in the Department of Radiation Oncology at Thomas Jefferson University, Buzurović co-authored research on a dynamic tumor-tracking technique for radiation therapy.The approach used computer algorithms to predict tumor motion and coordinate the movement of a treatment couch with a linear accelerator, with the aim of improving radiation delivery to moving tumors while reducing exposure to nearby healthy tissue. The research, evaluated through computer simulations, was reported in RSNA News in May 2011. [ref: ]

In 2021, Buzurović and colleagues investigated the feasibility of using MRI alone for high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy, a technique used to treat selected superficial tumors. Their study evaluated whether MRI-based treatment planning could replace conventional computed tomography (CT)-based planning in an appropriate clinical workflow.[2] [ref: Feasibility of magnetic resonance-only high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy for clinical application, Medical Physics]

In 2023, he co-authored research examining catheter reconstruction and dosimetric verification in MRI-only treatment planning for interstitial high-dose-rate brachytherapy. The study investigated the use of a pointwise encoding time reduction with radial acquisition (PETRA) MRI sequence in the treatment of gynecological cancers. [ref: Selection criteria for high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy and electron beam therapy in cutaneous oncology, Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy]

Buzurović has also contributed to research on treatment selection for cutaneous oncology. A 2021 study published in the Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy examined criteria for selecting high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy or electron beam therapy for skin cancer treatment. [ref: Selection criteria for high-dose-rate surface brachytherapy and electron beam therapy in cutaneous oncology, Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy]

In 2023, he co-authored an American Association of Physicists in Medicine (AAPM) medical physics practice guideline on high-dose-rate brachytherapy, addressing technical and clinical practice considerations in the field. [ref: AAPM medical physics practice guideline 13.a: HDR brachytherapy, part A, Journal of Applied Clinical Medical Physics]

His subsequent work has included research on the clinical implementation of MRI-guided surface brachytherapy, optimization of MRI sequences for patient-specific treatment planning, and the geometric accuracy of brachytherapy applicators and catheters. [ref: Feasibility and clinical implementation of MRI-guided surface brachytherapy, Journal of Contemporary Brachytherapy]

In 2026, Buzurović co-authored a study evaluating an adjustable tandem-and-ring applicator intended to improve radiation dose distribution in high-dose-rate brachytherapy for cervical cancer. [ref: A Novel Adjustable Tandem and Ring Applicator for Improved Dosimetry in Cervical Cancer HDR Brachytherapy, Technology in Cancer Research & Treatment]

is a Cambodian business executive and entrepreneur serving as Chief Executive Officer of AirAsia Cambodia [ref: VISSOTH NAM, AirAsia Newsroom] since its inception in 2022 [ref: Capital A to launch AirAsia Cambodia as it resumes growth, Reuters]. == Early life and education ==
Born in Phnom Penh and raised in France, Vissoth completed his higher education in Paris, studying law and economics at Université Paris-Panthéon-Assas from 2009 to 2012. He subsequently earned a Master’s degree in Management with a specialization in Global Financial Management from ESCEMBusiness School.

== Career ==

=== Economic research ===
Early in his career, Vissoth specialized in central banking and macroeconomic policy. He served as Deputy Section Chief in Economic Research at the National Bank of Cambodia (NBC), focusing on monetary policy, national financial stability, and macroeconomic indicators. He later joined the International Monetary Fund (IMF) as an economist, where he co-authored research analyzing domestic credit growth, banking sector leverage, and financial cycles in Cambodia. [ref: https://www.imf.org/-/media/Files/Countries/ResRep/BGD/2018/032018.ashx]

In 2017, Vissoth transitioned into the private sector, founding Sivilai Asia, a Cambodia-based investment and holding firm focused on hospitality and strategic local ventures [ref: Capital A Forms AirAsia Cambodia As Budget Carrier Seeks New Growth Markets, Forbes]. Through Sivilai Asia, he led development and management projects aimed at elevating Cambodia's regional hospitality and commercial ecosystem.

=== AirAsia Cambodia ===
In December 2022, Capital A (AirAsia Group) partnered with Sivilai Asia in a joint venture to establish AirAsia Cambodia, with Capital A holding a 51% stake and Sivilai Asia holding 49%. As Director of Sivilai Asia, Vissoth was appointed Chief Executive Officer of the new low cost airline.

Under his executive leadership, the airline navigated regulatory approvals with the State Secretariat of Civil Aviation (SSCA), securing its Air Operator Certificate (AOC) in April 2024 [ref: ]. AirAsia Cambodia launched domestic operations on 2 May 2024, connecting Phnom Penh, Siem Reap, and Sihanoukville [ref: AirAsia Cambodia Takes Off!, AirAsia Newsroom], before expanding to international regional routes [ref: AirAsia Cambodia launches first int’l flight to Kuala Lumpur] to boost tourism and economic integration within ASEAN.

Günther Fehlinger (born ) is an Austrian economist and political consultant. [ref: 20 Jahre AktionsGemeinschaft Festschrift] He was born in Linz, Austria. He is the secretary of the small and medium businesses association of the European People's Party, as well as being the Chairman of the Austrian Committee for NATO and EU Enlargement. He is also One of the Presidential Candidates for the next Austrian Presidential Election.

Günther Fehlinger is a supporter of EU enlargement as well as NATO enlargement. He gained popularity pro-atlantist position and activism on Twitter and Twitch, which are platforms on which he is very active. He is widely criticised for encouraging interferences in regional affairs, notably through calls to dismantle nations such as Russia in his ExRussia [ref: https://gunterfehlinger.substack.com/p/exrussia-now] and India, in his ExIndia Posts online, and his anti-Serb sentiment.

== Biography ==

=== Youth and studies ===
Günther Fehlinger was born on in the city of Linz, Austria. His father had been editor-in-chief of the Neues Volksblatt. [ref: Porträt: Der Don Quijote der flachen Steuer, Die Presse]. He went to the Khevenhüller Gymnasium Linz secondary school from 1979 to 1988 before serving in the Austrian Armed Forces as reserve lieutenant from 1988 to 1989. He studied at the Vienna University of Economics and Business from October 1989 to September 1998, wherein he obtained a Master in International Commerce, specialising in management and human resources [ref: Europeans For Tax Reform - Our People, www.flattax-europe.eu]

== Political positions ==
He is in favour of liberal internationalism, opposing socialism, but also Irish, Serbian and Arab nationalisms, as well as Shia Islamism.

He positions himself against Sinn Féin and the Irish reunification, accusing Sinn Féin of being a "pro-Russian propaganda organisation".

He is also a military interventionist, considering both the 2003 Iraq invasion and NATO's 2011 Libya intervention as successes, as they eliminated "Kadhafi the socialist" and "the genocidal terrorist nationalist socialist regime of Saddam Hussein".

He has severely criticised Serbia [ref: Wie ein Österreicher die Serben per Twitter auf die Palme bringt, kurier.at]. He has also said that "whoever refuses to recognise Kosovo should not consider themselves part of the free world".

== Controversies ==
His role as leader of a pro-NATO NGO led to misunderstandings wherein people believed he was speaking on behalf of NATO. Following a tweet in which he called on Nikol Pashinyan to join NATO and on Joe Biden to protect Armenia, Armenian vice-minister of Foreign Affairs Vahan Kostanyan stated that Fehlinger was only the head of an NGO bearing the word "NATO" in its name, not the actual intergovernmental alliance. Fehlinger's comments on the dismantlement of Russia led to the country's vice-minister of Foreign Affairs Aleksandr Grushko firm opposition to his "grand fantasy".

== Popularity in Video Games [ref: Russian diplomat calls EU's remarks about Armenia joining NATO 'grand fantasy', HyeTert] ==

Gunther Fehlinger is in the Hearts of Iron IV extension "The Fire Rises", since Gunther being in the mod his popularity has sky-rocketed in the Online Space. Some say that because of "The Fire Rises" he might be become the President of Austria. [ref: Gunther Fehlinger, The Fire Rises Wiki]
