Draft: TakeMe2Space

Draft text:
TakeMe2Space is a space company based in Hyderabad, India. It develops satellite payloads and subsystems and offers remote access to computing hardware on its spacecraft, so users can run software in orbit, including AI inference on imagery. The company plans to build an orbital data centre.

The company flew its first experiment, RSEM, aboard ISRO's PSLV-C58 on 1 January 2024. In November 2024, it announced MOI-TD, an AI payload, which was launched on PSLV-C60 on 30 December 2024. Its first satellite, MOI-1, was aboard PSLV-C62 on 12 January 2026; the rocket failed during ascent, and all 16 satellites on board, including MOI-1, were lost. A replacement, MOI-1a, was launched on 1 October 2026 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9.

== History ==

Ronak Kumar Samantray co-founded NowFloats, a software firm acquired by Reliance in 2019. When he turned to space technology, he found there was no satellite to rent, so he decided to build one. He conceived the idea in 2022, and in June 2023, he and three friends started TakeMe2Space in Hyderabad.

To extend the lifespan of satellite electronics, the company tested a tantalum coating as a low-cost radiation shield. The experiment, the Radiation Shielding Experimental Module (RSEM), flew on 1 January 2024 on PSLV-C58, mounted on POEM-3, the rocket's fourth stage used as an orbital platform.

The company announced its first mission, MOI-TD (My Orbital Infrastructure – Technology Demonstrator), in November 2024. It was launched on 30 December 2024 from Sriharikota. MOI-TD carried an onboard computer and an AI accelerator to test AI inference, sensor fusion, and high-speed data handling in low Earth orbit. This allowed users to upload AI models that could run on the payload through a web-based console called OrbitLab. Uses included environmental monitoring and tracking deforestation, among others. Samantray told ThePrint that his goal was to make space accessible to any researcher, student, educator, or start-up that wanted to be part of it. Its first research partners were a Malaysian university and a group of Class 9 and 10 students from an Indian school. The founder said a Class 9 student was among the company's first customers.

Chiratae Ventures led a seed round in which TakeMe2Space raised US$5 million in January 2026. The company said it would use the money to expand its constellation to six spacecraft and to scale real-time AI inferencing in orbit. It also said it planned to build an orbital data centre in Telangana.

=== PSLV-C62 and MOI-1 ===

MOI-1 was a 14 kg CubeSat developed by TakeMe2Space. It gave developers and organisations the opportunity to run AI workloads in space without needing to own or operate a satellite, and the company said the mission would demonstrate an AI-powered orbital image laboratory. Integrated with MOI-1 was MIRA, an electro-optical Earth-observation payload built by EON Space Labs, with an optical system carved from a single block of fused silica; it weighed 502 g and supported multispectral imaging across nine bands. The PSLV-C62, carrying Anvesha, a DRDO-designed Earth observation satellite, was to launch from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

A flight-ready CubeSat payload built by 17 students aged 12 to 15 at Blue Blocks Montessori School was also on the launch. The payload included real-time telemetry and commercial off-the-shelf sensors to study thermal behaviour in space, transmitting raw data on temperature, humidity and other weather parameters from an altitude of 450 km. Scientists from TakeMe2Space guided them, and the students executed the plan.

PSLV-C62 was launched on 12 January 2026 at 10:17 am IST and encountered a failure during ascent due to an anomaly in the rocket's third stage. MOI-1 was lost, along with all 16 satellites on the mission.

After the loss of MOI-1, the company booked the earliest available launch slot with SpaceX. The replacement, MOI-1a, was launched on 1 October 2026 aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 mission. The satellite allows customers to collect Earth observation data and process it in space. It weighs 14 kg, has 117 TOPS of onboard computing and 2 TB of storage, and has a nine-band multispectral imager. At launch, MOI-1a had 23 customers. ThePrint reported it as the first of five planned satellites, and the company described the mission as a step towards building an orbital data centre in space.

== Technology and products ==

OrbitLab, the company's web-based platform, was used by customers to rent satellite processing time. Initial reports put the price at $2 (₹180) per minute.

TakeMe2Space also produces PowerBank-50, a satellite battery pack designed to power a satellite while it passes through Earth's shadow. Weighing 380 g and storing around 50 Wh, it was onboard Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 first flight, Mission "Aagaman", launched on 18 July 2026, powering an experimental payload from Cosmoserve Space at approximately 450 km altitude. Samantray said the battery was "now space proven, made in India, and ready for every satellite builder in the world".

Jeremy Morris (born 26 November 1961) is a British jeweller and businessman who serves as chief executive officer and creative director of the London jewellery house David Morris. Under his leadership, the family-owned business has expanded internationally. Jeremy Morris is the son of jeweller David Morris, founder of the David Morris jewellery house. Morris left school at the age of 18 to become a jeweller. He subsequently studied fine art in London for five years, apprenticed with jewellers on Place Vendôme in Paris, and worked with a diamond supplier in Antwerp. [ref: [https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/uk-travel/england/london-travel/meet-the-morrises-the-middle-aged-ravers-tearing-up-primrose-hill-7cjprjnjcr9 The Times, October 2014.]] [ref: [https://rapaport.com/magazine-article/scion-of-bond-street/ Rapaport, "Scion of Bond Street".]]

Morris is responsible for gemstone sourcing and the creative direction of David Morris's fine jewellery and high jewellery collections. The World of David Morris describes him as overseeing collection design, client relationships and the acquisition of rare stones for the company's inventory. [ref: [https://davidmorris.com/product/the-world-of-david-morris The World of David Morris, David Morris.]]

He has worked extensively with rare stones, including Paraíba tourmalines and padparadscha sapphires, as well as conch pearls, in the company's high jewellery collections. [ref: [https://katerinaperez.com/articles/paraiba-tourmaline-blue-chip-gemstone Katerina Perez, "Paraiba Tourmaline: Blue-Chip Gemstone".]] [ref: [https://www.thejewelleryeditor.com/login/?next=/jewellery/know-how/conch-pearls/ The Jewellery Editor, "Conch Pearls".]] [ref: [https://spearswms.com/luxury/diamond-life-how-the-skilled-operators-at-david-morris-are-keeping-an-old-craft-alive/ Spears, "Diamond Life".]]

During his tenure, Jeremy Morris has expanded the retail presence of David Morris internationally, with boutiques and concessions in Europe, the Middle East and Asia. [ref: [https://davidmorris.com/boutiques/ David Morris, Boutiques.]]

== Publications ==

Jeremy Morris and the David Morris jewellery house were the subject of The World of David Morris, a book written by jewellery editor Annabel Davidson and published by Rizzoli International Publications in 2024.

== Personal life ==

Morris has five children, with three involved in the David Morris business as part of the third generation of the family-owned company: Cecily Morris, Brand and Retail Director; Phoebe Morris, Special Projects Coordinator; and Dillon Morris, who works in stone procurement.. [ref: [https://www.marieclaire.co.uk/fashion/watches-jewellery/cecily-morris-9-5-interview Marie Claire, January 2026.]] [ref: [https://davidmorris.com/the-world-of-david-morris-a-jewel-in-your-library/ David Morris, "The World of David Morris: A Jewel in Your Library", November 2024.]]

= Abiodun Ramon Oseni =
Abiodun Ramon Oseni is a Nigerian security analyst and former United States Army servicemember and police officer. He has spoken and written publicly on issues including security, policing, terrorism, international affairs, and economic issues both in Nigeria and internationally. His commentary has appeared in Nigerian newspapers and international publications, and he has participated in academic and professional forums. [ref: Decentralised policing, economic empowerment will curb banditry, says Oseni, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

== Early life and education ==
Abiodun Ramon Oseni was born on 6 February 1980 in Epe, Lagos State, Nigeria. He is reported to be from the Idisewe ruling compound of Idasho in Ibeju-Lekki and a first cousin of Oba Kamorudeen Ishola Animashaun, the Oloja of Epe. He completed his early education in Apapa and attended Sari-Iganmu Secondary School Lagos. [ref: From Frontlines to Classroom: How U.S. Army veteran, Oseni, is reshaping Nigerian, West African security, Vanguard News]

Oseni attended Adeniran Ogunsanya College of Education (AOCOED), where he earned a National Certificate of Education (NCE) in Economics and History in 2003. He later attended Lagos State University, where he obtained a bachelor's degree in international relations and history. He also completed expert training at the U.S. Army Quartermaster School in Virginia and the U.S. Army Leadership School in Mississippi. He obtained a master's certificate in international security from Harvard University and further got a master's degree in international relations and global security, with specialization in conflict resolution, from American Military University. [ref: LASU appoints U.S. Army veteran as entrepreneurship instructor, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

== Career ==
Oseni was active in the United States Army and later worked as a police officer in Tennessee. He described his professional interests as focusing on international security, counterterrorism, policing, and conflict resolution. Oseni also later served as a Diplomatic Security Officer with the U.S. Department of State's Special Operations Unit in Washington, D.C.

He has subsequently worked as a security analyst and public commentator. His analysis has focused on issues including terrorism, banditry, kidnapping, policing, food security, regional security, and international conflicts. [ref: Yoruba leaders, experts stress decentralised security model as threats close in, Businessday NG]In 2025, Oseni was appointed as an Entrepreneurship and Innovation (ENT 1000) instructor at Lagos State University. His public activities have included lectures on security and related subjects.

== Public commentary ==
Oseni has been featured and quoted by Nigerian and international media in connection with security and public policy issues. [ref: Deadly Cooperation Among Terror Groups in Nigeria, Africa Defense Forum]

In 2024, he participated in a National Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) public relations clinic addressing food security and related security concerns. He also participated in another NSCDC event concerning sustainable mining and environmental management. [ref: NSCDC seeks collaborative action to tackle food insecurity, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

In 2025, he participated in discussions on insecurity and security policy, including events addressing policing and the security situation in southwestern Nigeria.

BusinessDay gave reports on a presentation by Oseni concerning kidnapping and banditry in Nigeria, in which he lectured that these activities had developed into organised criminal enterprises and advocated for community policing, intelligence integration, and coordinated security strategies.

Oseni has also commented publicly on international security issues. In 2025, Vanguard quoted him in its coverage of the Israel–Iran conflict, where he talked about the difficulties involved in targeting Iran's underground nuclear facilities. [ref: The implications of Israeli/Iran war, Vanguard News]

The Guardian has published a number of Oseni's articles on international security and Nigerian public policy. These have included commentary on the United States' foreign policy, the Israel–Iran conflict, terrorism financing, drug trafficking and Nigeria's security challenges. [ref: Vote buying in Nigeria is national security threat, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

In March 2026, The Guardian reported on Oseni's call for the establishment of state police in Nigeria, made at an International Security Conference organized by the Institute of Security, Nigeria. The report covered his recommendations concerning community policing, intelligence gathering, and local security responses. [ref: Insecurity: State Police is an urgent need for Nigeria, says Oseni, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

In September 2026, Independent Newspaper Nigeria published an article discussing Oseni's views on West African security architecture, including decentralized policing and community-based intelligence. [ref: Navigating The Complexities Of West African Security Architecture, Independent Newspaper Nigeria]

Draft: Ryan Doherty

Draft text:
Ryan Doherty is an American hospitality entrepreneur, nightlife designer, and urban placemaker known for revitalizing downtown Las Vegas. He is the founder and president of Corner Bar Management, a company that operates a portfolio of bars, restaurants, and immersive nightlife concepts throughout the Fremont East and Arts District neighborhoods of Las Vegas. [ref: Nightlife Entrepreneur Ryan Doherty Brings Downtown Las Vegas to Life, Forbes]

== Early life and education ==
Doherty was born in Boston, Massachusetts. [ref: New Las Vegas nightclub has bite, but elegance, Las Vegas Review-Journal] His father once described a family friend's doberman as “sleek, elegant and dangerous … they look fast standing still,” a phrase that later inspired the name of one of Doherty’s venues. He moved west to attend the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, earning a degree from the William F. Harrah College of Hospitality. [ref: Corner Bar Management transforms downtown, Las Vegas Magazine]

== Career ==

=== Corner Bar Management and Fremont East ===
Doherty founded Corner Bar Management (CBM), beginning with the opening of Commonwealth in downtown Las Vegas. His company has since developed nearly a dozen distinctive concepts in the Fremont East area, including The Laundry Room, La Mona Rosa, Park on Fremont, DISCOPUSSY, Lucky Day, We All Scream, and Cheapshot.

In October 2025, *Las Vegas Weekly* described Doherty as the driving force behind Fremont East’s transformation in its feature “Fremont East evolves into a modern and diverse,” crediting him with building “a nightlife empire … without fully knowing what it would become.” [ref: Fremont East evolves into a modern and diverse, Las Vegas Weekly]

*Forbes* has characterized his body of work as “a master class in immersive nightlife design,” while *Las Vegas Magazine* noted that his projects have “transformed the social fabric” of downtown. [ref: Corner Bar Management transforms downtown, Las Vegas Magazine]

=== Doberman Drawing Room ===
In April 2025, Doherty opened Doberman Drawing Room in the Las Vegas Arts District, a moody cocktail parlor that blends vintage glamour and modern edge. The venue features a globally inspired cocktail program by award-winning mixologist Juyoung Kang. [ref: Doberman Drawing Room opens in Las Vegas, The Spirits Business]

*Eater Vegas* reported that the members-optional bar received over 4,000 applications prior to opening, with a 20-question membership form designed to attract dedicated cocktail enthusiasts. [ref: A new bar is opening in downtown Las Vegas — you'll just have to apply, Eater Vegas] The *Las Vegas Sun* described Doberman as a “reservations-only lounge focused on personal connection and craftsmanship.” [ref: New reservations-only bar focused on making custom cocktails, Las Vegas Sun]

In August 2025, *Forbes* featured Doberman in its “Where To Eat And Drink Off-Strip In Las Vegas Right Now” roundup, calling it one of the city’s most sophisticated new bars. [ref: Where To Eat And Drink Off-Strip In Las Vegas Right Now, Forbes]

=== Life Is Beautiful festival ===
From 2015 to 2019, Doherty served as co-owner and Chief Experience Officer of the Life Is Beautiful festival, where he helped establish its global reputation for art and immersive design. [ref: Behind the Successful Union Between Life Is Beautiful and Downtown Las Vegas, Forbes] He launched the festival’s mural program, commissioning more than 50 international artists—including Shepard Fairey and D*Face—to transform downtown’s landscape. The initiative earned the Las Vegas Mayor’s Urban Design Award in 2017.

During his tenure, the festival hosted headliners including The Killers, Kendrick Lamar, Billie Eilish, Mumford & Sons, and Chance the Rapper. [ref: Behind the Successful Union Between Life Is Beautiful and Downtown Las Vegas, Forbes]

=== Feed the Block and live music ===
Doherty co-created Feed the Block, a free concert series in partnership with Wynn Las Vegas, that brings major artists such as Major Lazer SoundSystem and Gryffin to perform downtown. The series has drawn thousands of attendees, further integrating music into the downtown experience.

=== Early media ventures ===
Before his hospitality career, Doherty co-founded Las Vegas Printing Press (later Environmental Ink) and WENDOH Media, publisher of *944 Magazine*, *Vegas SEVEN*, and *SpyOnVegas.com*.

== Design philosophy ==
Doherty’s venues are designed as immersive, art-driven environments, often blending surrealism, humor, and theatricality. *Forbes* described his approach as “a master class in immersive nightlife design.” *Eater Vegas* noted that he aims to keep guests “on the edge of disbelief.” [ref: Las Vegas's Newest Avant-Garde Cocktail Bar Opens With an Optional $3,000 Membership, Eater Vegas]

== Civic engagement ==
Doherty serves as chairman of the Citizens Advisory Committee for the Las Vegas Redevelopment Agency and is a member of the Downtown Vegas Alliance. He is also the founder of the @[user] movement and a board member of the RISE Festival.

== Personal life ==
Outside his professional career, Doherty enjoys camping in Zion and Sedona, playing tennis, and collecting art and artifacts. He has designed two custom homes in Costa Rica and regularly participates in art installations at Burning Man.

== References ==

Jeffry Burchard is an architect, urban designer, and educator. He is managing partner and design principal at Machado Silvetti and an Associate Professor in Practice of Architecture at the Harvard Graduate School of Design. [ref: Jeffry Burchard, Harvard Graduate School of Design] In 2020, he received the American Institute of Architects Young Architects Award, a national award recognizing early-career architects for leadership and contributions to the profession. [ref: Young Architect Award, American Institute of Architects] [ref: AIA Announces Winners of the 2020 Young Architects Award, Traditional Building]

== Education and academic career ==

Burchard studied architecture at the University of Idaho before completing the post-professional Master in Architecture II program at the Harvard Graduate School of Design, graduating with distinction in 2008.

He began teaching at Harvard GSD as a Design Critic in Architecture in 2012. He was appointed Assistant Professor in Practice of Architecture in 2017 and promoted to Associate Professor in Practice of Architecture in 2023. His teaching has included architecture core studios, thesis, and professional practice. [ref: Announcing GSD Faculty Appointments and Promotions for the 2023-2024 Academic Year, Harvard Graduate School of Design]

== Architectural career ==

After completing his graduate studies at Harvard, Burchard joined Machado Silvetti, initially working as senior project designer on New York University's Global Center for Academic and Spiritual Life. He later became a partner and principal of the practice and subsequently managing partner and design principal.

His work at Machado Silvetti has included architecture and urban-design projects in the United States and internationally. Harvard GSD identifies Burchard as project architect and urban designer for both the Tun Razak Exchange financial district in Kuala Lumpur and the Vietnamese-German University campus in Binh Duong Province, Vietnam.

In early 2025, Burchard and Stehanie Randazzo Dwyer succeeded founders Jorge Silvetti and Rodolfo Machado in the ownership and leadership of Machado Silvetti. According to The Architect's Newspaper, this succession followed a long-term process in which ownership and responsibility was gradually transferred to Burchard and Randazzo Dwyer. The two retained the companies name in order to continue the firm's identity. [ref: How are architecture firms using succession planning to build sustainable futures for their practice?, The Architect's Newspaper]

== Selected work ==

=== Denver Art Museum ===
Burchard was directly involved in the renovation and expansion of the Denver Art Museum campus. He focused on a new welcome center and working on the Gio Ponti-designed Martin Building. He was later interviews by public-radio station KUNC regarding the challenges of adapting the landmark museum without stripping it of its architectural character. [ref: Denver Art Museum Looks To Renovate A Work Of Art: Itself, KUNC]

The projects glass welcome center was later discussed on Engineering News-Record where Burchard was quoted on the decision to create a self-supporting glass enclosure and on the relationship between the new elliptical structure and the surrounding museum buildings. [ref: Glass Welcome Center Becomes Denver Art Museum's New 'Front Door', Engineering News-Record]

=== Downtown Cary Park ===

Burchard played a substantial role in the Machado Silvetti design team for Downtown Cary Park in Cary, North Carolina which was developed with OJB Landscape Architecture. [ref: Downtown Cary Park, American Institute of Architects]

In 2026, the seven-acre park was examined as a new civic center for Cary in Metropolis and the project's architecture and urban context was discussed with Burchard. [ref: In North Carolina, an Iconic Park Completes a Community, Metropolis] Subsequently, the project received national recognition from the AIA for regional and urban design.

=== Provincetown projects ===

Burchard has also worked on his fair share of redevelopment and preservation projects, specifically in Provincetown, Massachusetts. The Provincetown Independent reported on a waterfront redevelopment proposal designed by Burchard in 2023 and discussed how he intended to reconnect the site with Provincetown's historic maritime and industrial character. [ref: With More Space, Barker Unveils a Bigger Plan for the Waterfront, The Provincetown Independent]

The newspaper also covered Burchard's renovation design for the historic Lancy House at 230 commercial street. This article released in 2026 also included Burchard's plans to restore elements of its nineteenth-century Second Empire exterior while simultaneously adapting the building for its new public and commercial uses. [ref: Approvals Are in Hand, But Lancy House Renovations Hit Delays, The Provincetown Independent]

== Professional recognition ==

Burchard was one of few recipients of the AIA Young Architects Award back in 2020. The AIA describes the award as recognizing young architects who have demonstrated exceedingly impressive leadership skills and have made significant contributions to the profession early in their careers. This selection was also reported by independent architecture and building-industry publications. [ref: AIA gives Young Architects, Associates Awards, Metal Architecture]

== References ==

Heidrick & Struggles International Incorporated, commonly called Heidrick & Struggles, is an American executive search and management consulting company headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, United States, with offices in 56 offices across the Americas, Europe, Africa and Asia as of 2026. [ref: The Big 5 Executive Search Firms, Hunt Scanlon Media]

==History==

Heidrick & Struggles was founded in 1953 in Chicago by Gardner Heidrick and John E. Struggles, both of whom were former employees of American management consulting firm Booz Allen Hamilton. [ref: Heidrick & Struggles Company Overview & News, Forbes] [ref: Headhunting: A Brief History of a Profession, Eurogalenus]

From the late 1950s through the 1960s, Heidrick & Struggles opened offices in Los Angeles, San Francisco and New York City. In 1968, the firm established its first international office in London.

In 1999, the firm completed an initial public offering (IPO) and began trading on the NASDAQ under the ticker symbol HSII. [ref: Forbes: Headaches and Struggles, Forbes] [ref: Internet Cos., CONSOL Energy, Heidrick & Struggles Plan IPOs, Bloomberg] On April 30, 1999, the IPO closed with 4.2 million shares offered at $14/share. [ref: Internet deals shrug off technology scare, Deseret News] As of 2005, the company had more than 50 offices in six continents. [ref: Headhunters and How to Use Them: A Guide for Organisations and Individuals, John Wiley & Sons]

In January 2013, Heidrick & Struggles purchased Senn Delaney Leadership Consulting Group, a Huntington Beach organizational culture advisory firm, in an all cash deal for $53.5 million. [ref: Senn Delaney bought for $53.5 million, Orange County Register]

In September 2017, Heidrick & Struggles acquired 2GET, an executive search firm in Brazil. [ref: Heidrick acquires one of largest executive search firms in Brazil, Staffing Industry Analysts (SIA)] In December 2021, the company entered into an agreement to acquire two executive search and leadership consulting companies, RosExpert in Russia and WE Partners in Ukraine and Kazakhstan. [ref: Heidrick & Struggles Enters Agreement to Acquire RosExpert in Russia and WE Partners in Ukraine and Kazakhstan, Hunt Scanlon Media]

In March 2022, the company posted global revenues of $1 billion. [ref: Heidrick & Struggles Reports 61 Percent Revenue Rise; Names Diversity Leader, Hunt Scanlon Media]

In April 2021, the company acquired Business Talent Group, an online marketplace for on-demand independent consultants. [ref: Heidrick buys Business Talent Group, entering the on-demand talent platform space, Staffing Industry Analysts (SIA)] In January 2023 Heidrick & Struggles acquired Atreus, an executive interim management firm based in Germany. [ref: Heidrick & Struggles Plans to Acquire Atreus, Hunt Scanlon Media]

In 2024, the company appointed Tom Monahan as chief executive officer. [ref: Heidrick & Struggles’ new president shares what he learned about going for a CEO job, Fortune]

In December 2025, the company agreed to be acquired by an investor group led by Advent International and Corvex Private Equity, ending 26 years as a public company. [ref: Heidrick & Struggles soars after $1.3 billion go-private deal]

== Research studies ==
Heidrick & Struggles regularly conducts studies and research focused on industry trends.

In March 2026, Heidrick & Struggles found in their "Closing the CEO capability gap" study that, in 2025, one in five Fortune 500 companies appointed CEOs that had international work experience. [ref: Global experience enhanced CEO Ariane Gorin’s leadership skills, Fast Company]

In April 2026, Heidrick & Struggles released the findings of their 2025 "Private Equity–Backed Chief Financial Officer Compensation Survey". The survey found that, on average, CFOs working in PE-backed firms in the United States took home cash pay of $604,000 in 2025, an increase of 5% year over year. Mayhem began his involvement in professional wrestling in 2007 and made his in-ring debut in 2015. In May 2025, he returned from a six-month injury absence to win the RAW Heavyweight Championship. == Early life ==
Overton was raised in North Shields, North Tyneside, England. He attended John Spence Community High School, where he was a schoolmate of singer-songwriter Sam Fender. [ref: Matty Mayhem 'North Shields' Own Wrestling Star, I Love North Shields]

Overton began his involvement in professional wrestling in 2007 with the Independent Wrestling Federation (IWF) in Newcastle upon Tyne, where he worked as a referee while also undertaking wrestling training.

In 2012, he continued training with RAD:PRO in South Shields under professional wrestler Vulture. He made his in-ring debut in 2015 at a RAD:PRO event, competing in an eight-man tag team match under the ring name Matty Mayhem.

During his early career, Mayhem competed regularly for RAD:PRO and Maximum Pro Wrestling (MPW), primarily as a singles wrestler. He subsequently made appearances outside North East England, including for World Wide Wrestling League (W3L) in Scotland.

=== 5 Star Wrestling (2018) ===
In 2018, Mayhem appeared for 5 Star Wrestling, a British professional wrestling promotion that organised arena events across the United Kingdom.

On 15 February 2018, Mayhem defeated HT Drake and Alex Young in a three-way match at Sheffield Arena. [ref: 5 Star Wrestling Live Review – 15th February 2018, Across The Pond Wrestling]

The following week, Mayhem faced Flash Morgan Webster in a non-televised match in Plymouth.

On 1 March 2018, Mayhem faced HT Drake in a singles match at a 5 Star Wrestling event in Belfast, Northern Ireland. [ref: 5 Star Wrestling Review – 1st March 2018, Across The Pond Wrestling]

=== Anarchy Ink (2018–2026) ===
In 2018, Mayhem began teaming with Ryan Roode for Classic UK Pro Wrestling (CUKPW). Their partnership developed following an unexpected change to an event's scheduled matches, when Roode replaced another competitor in a triple-threat match.

The pair adopted the name Anarchy Ink, which Mayhem had previously used as part of a wrestling stable in RAD:PRO. They subsequently became regular competitors on the British independent wrestling circuit.

Following Mayhem's return to wrestling in October 2023, the pair resumed their partnership.

On 12 October 2024, Anarchy Ink defeated The Denizen (Bo Carter and Caleb Carter) at Firestar Championship Wrestling's A Cold Night in Hell event in Ripponden, West Yorkshire, to capture the FCW Tag Team Championship. [ref: FCW A Cold Night in Hell, Cagematch]

During their championship reign, Anarchy Ink became involved in an extended rivalry with Reform Wrestling, consisting of Ryan Ace and Kendoll.

On 26 September 2026, Anarchy Ink lost the FCW Tag Team Championship to Reform Wrestling in a ladder match at September Showdown in Greetland, Halifax. The result ended a championship reign lasting nearly two years. [ref: Firestar Championship Wrestling, BritWresEvents]

=== Hiatus and return (2020–2023) ===
Mayhem stepped away from professional wrestling in 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic and personal circumstances.

He remained absent from active competition for approximately three years before returning in October 2023 for Rapid Action Wrestling, facing Asylum in his comeback match.

Following his return, Mayhem continued to compete in singles competition while also resuming his tag team partnership with Ryan Roode.

=== Injury and comeback (2024–2025) ===
On 7 December 2024, Mayhem suffered a broken right collarbone during a match involving Anarchy Ink and Reform Wrestling in Ripponden, West Yorkshire. The injury occurred following an awkward landing during the match and required surgery, during which a metal plate and eight screws were fitted to stabilise the fracture.

The injury forced Mayhem out of in-ring competition for approximately six months. During his recovery, the ongoing rivalry between Anarchy Ink and Reform Wrestling continued.

On 24 May 2025, Mayhem returned to competition at a Rapid Action Wrestling event in Blyth, Northumberland, defeating X-Jack to win the RAW Heavyweight Championship. The victory ended X-Jack's 819-day championship reign.

The match had originally been scheduled before Mayhem's injury but had been postponed following an injury to X-Jack.

=== RAW Heavyweight Championship (2025–2026) ===
Following his return from injury, Mayhem competed as RAW Heavyweight Champion.

On 19 September 2025, he defeated Brandon Prince at a Rapid Action Wrestling event in Cramlington, Northumberland. [ref: Rapid Action Wrestling, BritWresEvents]

On 16 May 2026, Mayhem defeated veteran British professional wrestler Jonny Storm in a RAW Heavyweight Championship match in Cramlington.

Draft text:
A poker affiliate (also poker partner; in decentralized, club-based apps usually a poker agent) is a person or company that brings users to online poker and receives a commission for it from a poker room or club. The practice belongs to the wider affiliate marketing industry serving online gambling operators.

== Terminology ==
With centralized poker rooms, the intermediary is called an affiliate or partner. It works under an agreement with the operator: a player signs up through its link or promo code and is assigned to it.

In decentralized (club-based) poker apps the common term is agent. Such an intermediary represents one or more clubs, recruits members, sells and buys back chips, and in return receives a share of the rake. Trade press describes this environment as an ecosystem of clubs, agents, super agents and unions.

== History ==
Poker room partner programmes spread alongside the growth of online poker in the 2000s. Competition among partners popularised rakeback — a refund of part of the commission, paid out of the intermediary's own earnings.

During the 2010s several operators stopped paying rakeback through partners in favour of in-house loyalty schemes. In 2012 the relaunched Full Tilt Poker replaced partner deals with a VIP system paying players directly. The Merge Gaming network followed suit in January 2013.

From the late 2010s, decentralized poker apps, also known as club apps, became widespread; in them any user can open a club of their own. Games there are organised by club operators and their alliances, known as unions, while agents bring in new players. Alongside amateur communities, the scene includes companies that run clubs and unions as a professional business.

== Compensation models ==
In online gambling, poker included, partners are paid under one of three schemes:
* CPA (cost per acquisition) — a one-off fee for each new customer who meets the operator's condition, such as a first deposit;
* revenue share (revenue sharing) — a percentage of net revenue generated by the referred audience; in poker this comes mainly from rake;
* hybrid — a combination of the first two models.

For large firms both main models matter about equally: in 2019 revenue share brought Catena Media 43% of its revenue and CPA 40%.

An affiliate or agent may share part of its earnings with players as rakeback. Some operators have restricted this, substituting their own loyalty programmes.

== Agent model ==
In decentralized apps the developer supplies only the software platform; everything else is handled by users. A typical hierarchy:
* app — software and tables;
* union — a shared pool spanning several clubs;
* club — admits players and settles with them;
* agent — finds an audience, sells and buys back chips.

As a rule, each agent has its own ID, which players use to join a club and become assigned to that agent. From the rake those players pay, the club gives the agent a share, part of which the agent may return to them as rakeback. Deposits and withdrawals are handled by club administrators, sometimes through agents.

== Roles compared ==
{| class="wikitable"
! !! Affiliate !! Agent
|-
| Setting || Centralized poker rooms || Decentralized apps
|-
| Referral method || Partner link or promo code || Joining a club by ID
|-
| Flow of funds || Directly through the room's cashier || Within the club, including via the agent
|-
| Income || CPA, revenue share or hybrid || Share of rake from the club or union
|}
Sources:

== Regulation ==
Treatment of partners varies by jurisdiction. In 2014 the New Jersey Division of Gaming Enforcement ruled that flat-fee intermediaries register as vendors, while those paid by revenue share or on a hybrid basis need an ancillary licence.

The United Kingdom has no separate licence for partners; the government's 2023 white paper confirmed that licensed operators remain accountable for their marketing.

== See also ==
* Rake (poker)
* Online poker
* Affiliate marketing

Proxy Foods AI is an American food technology company that develops artificial intelligence software for food and beverage formulation. It was founded in 2022 by Panos Kostopoulos, a chemical engineer and food biotechnologist, and four co-founders, [ref: Proxy Foods: Τα σχέδια της startup που φέρνει την ΑΙ στην ανάπτυξη τροφίμων μετά τη χρηματοδότηση $2,5 εκατ., Capital.gr] and grew out of Georgetown University’s biotechnology program. [ref: Georgetown’s Bark Tank Competition: MS in Biotechnology Student Takes 1st Prize with Proxy Foods, Master of Science in Biotechnology] The company has raised $8.3 million across two funding rounds. [ref: Business Wire (5 August 2026). [https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260805888751/en/Proxy-Foods-AI-Raises-%246M-Seed-Round-to-Accelerate-AI-Native-Food-and-Beverage-Development-Platform "Proxy Foods AI Raises $6M Seed Round to Accelerate AI-Native Food and Beverage Development Platform"]. Business Wire. Retrieved 28 September 2026.] Its platform applies predictive machine learning models to recipe formulation, regulatory compliance, and sensory evaluation, with an initial focus on alternative proteins. [ref: ] Its clients include Barilla, CAVA, and MISTA, a food innovation center owned by Givaudan.

== History ==
Proxy Foods was conceived by Panagiotis (Panos) Kostopoulos while he was completing a master’s degree in biotechnology at Georgetown University in Washington, D.C. Kostopoulos, who also holds an integrated master’s degree in chemical engineering from the National Technical University of Athens, developed the initial concept around applying artificial intelligence to food formulation, with a focus on alternative proteins, including plant-based, fermentation-derived, and cultivated products. The company was co-founded in 2022 with Petros Mandalis, Dimitris Zisis, Sid Mitroo, and Ted Leonsis, with technical operations based in Athens and business operations in Washington, D.C. According to the company, its mission is to transform food and beverage product development by integrating artificial intelligence with food science and culinary knowledge.

In 2022, the concept was presented at Georgetown’s annual Bark Tank entrepreneurship competition, formally known as the Leonsis Family Entrepreneurship Prize, a joint initiative of the university’s biotechnology program and its McDonough School of Business. Kostopoulos and his team took first place and a $30,000 cash prize, which served as the company’s initial capital. [ref: Entrepreneurs Split $100,000 in Annual Bark Tank Competition, The Hoya] [ref: Georgetown Entrepreneurs Take Home $145,000 in Prizes During Annual ‘Bark Tank’ Pitch Competition, McDonough School of Business] The competition is named for and supported by Ted Leonsis, a Georgetown alumnus and founder and CEO of Monumental Sports & Entertainment, who later became a co-founder and lead investor in the company. [ref: Proxy Foods raises $2.3m to grow AI-based recipe formulation platform, FoodNavigator.com]

== Technology ==
Proxy Foods develops a cloud-based platform for food and beverage research and development. Kostopoulos, the company’s CEO, has described the platform’s role as analogous to design software in other creative industries: a tool that allows food scientists to model and iterate formulations digitally before any physical testing, much as a graphic designer works with visual elements on screen. [ref: Proxy Foods CEO on AI’s potential in alt-protein market, creating ‘Canva... for the food scientist', FoodNavigator.com]

The platform incorporates predictive formulation models that use machine learning to anticipate a recipe’s performance across dimensions such as taste, texture, nutrition, and production cost, before laboratory trials are conducted. It also addresses regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions and includes sensory evaluation simulation capabilities. One of its design goals is to integrate the institutional knowledge held by food companies — historical R&D data, supplier records, and process documentation — into a unified AI interface.

In June 2026, the company was named a collaborating partner in the launch of the Food Intelligence Lab, an initiative of Food System Innovations (FSI) supported by a $2 million grant from the Bezos Earth Fund. Working with FSI and Stanford University computer scientist Anna Thomas, Proxy Foods co-developed an expert-guided Bayesian optimization (EGBO) system that improved the sensory performance of a dairy-free Greek yogurt by 29 percent over ten formulation iterations across five days, matching the animal-derived benchmark on three of four key sensory attributes. [ref: This Bezos-Funded Lab Wants to Use AI to Make Better Vegan Burgers, Green Queen]

William David Neelands (born October 30, 1943) is a Canadian Anglican priest, theologian, and academic administrator. [ref: New degree helps Orthodox Church, The Toronto Anglican] He is dean emeritus of the Faculty of Divinity at Trinity College, University of Toronto. [ref: Moral standard: Anglican church's role in Parlee Beach campground, CBC News] His research focuses on English theologian Richard Hooker, the English Reformation, Augustinianism [ref: Richard Hooker: His Life, Work, and Legacy: Essays in Honour of W. David Neelands, Daniel F. Graves & Scott Kindred-Barnes (co-editors)], and Anglican theology. [ref: From cults to colonialism: Tri-History Conference explores church role in trauma, survival, Anglican Journal]

He was named an honorary canon of St. James Cathedral and was elected to Alpha Sigma Nu. [ref: Orthodox school finds ‘natural home’ at Trinity, Anglican Journal] He is also a honorary fellow of Trinity College. [ref: David Neelands: Sixty-five years of conversation, Trinity Magazine]

== Education and career ==
Neelands recieved a BA with honours in 1965 and an MA in philosophy in 1966 from Trinity College, University of Toronto. [ref: Faculty of Divinity Convocation 2026, Trinity College] His master's thesis examined metaphysical explanation in the philosophy of Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz. He later studied theology at Pembroke College, Oxford.

He received an MDiv from Trinity College in 1978 and a ThD from Trinity College and the University of Toronto in 1988 with a doctoral thesis, The Theology of Grace of Richard Hooker. [ref: The Theology of Grace of Richard Hooker, Trinity College] Neelands began teaching philosophy at the University of Toronto in the 1960s and later became a lecturer at Trinity College. [ref: David Neelands: A Man of the People] In 2002, Neelands became dean of Trinity College’s Faculty of Divinity and Margaret E. Fleck Chair in Anglican Studies. [ref: College's new degree a 'great benefit' to Orthodox Church, The Diocese of Toronto] He held both positions until his retirement in 2017 and was subsequently named dean emeritus. He continued teaching historical theology and Anglican studies at Trinity College.

Neelands was ordained deacon in the Anglican Diocese of Toronto in 1977 and priest in 1979. He served in Canadian parishes and held temporary clerical appointments in England and Ireland. [ref: Clergy in Motion - 17 October, The Diocese of Toronto] In 2004, he was named an honorary canon of St. James Cathedral in Toronto. [ref: The CATHEDRAL CHURCH of ST. JAMES THE 217th REPORT TO VESTRY, STJAMES]

== Research ==
Neelands's research has focused on the history of Christian theology, particularly the work of Richard Hooker and the development of Anglican thought during the Reformation. [ref: THE LAW ON OUR HEARTS: RICHARD HOOKER AND THOMAS AQUINAS, The North American Anglican] His publications examine Hooker's views on predestination [ref: Richard Hooker and the Debates about Predestination 1580-1600, Toronto Journal of Theology], grace, the church, Christology, and the sacraments. [ref: ENGLISH MOLINISM IN THE LATE 1590s: RICHARD HOOKER ON FREE WILL, PREDESTINATION, AND DIVINE FOREKNOWLEDGE, The Journal of Theological Studies] His other research interests include Augustine, F. D. Maurice, Christian apologetics, and the theological history of the Thirty-nine Articles. [ref: A Calvinist Confession? Interpreting the Thirty-Nine Articles and Writing the History of the Reformation in Eighteenth-Century Ireland, The Journal of Religion]He has written and spoken on Anglican doctrine, liturgy [ref: Review of Pleading for Diversity: The Church Caspar Coolhaes Wanted. Draft text:
== Introduction ==

Instructional design often begins with identifying content, objectives, and the steps needed to teach them. The Pebble in the Pond model, developed by M. David Merrill, approaches the process a little differently. Instead of beginning with individual pieces of content, the model starts with a real world problem or whole task that learns should eventually be able to complete (Merrill, 2002) [ref: A pebble-in-the-pond model for instructional design, Performance Improvement]. From that starting point, the remaining elements of the instruction are developed outward, much like the ripples created when a pebble is dropped in a pond.

The model is closely connected to Merrill's First Principles of Instruction, which proposes that learning is promoted when learners engage with real world problems, activate previous knowledge, observe demonstrations, apply new knowledge, and integrate that knowledge into their own world ([https://mdavidmerrill.wordpress.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/firstprinciplesbymerrill.pdf Merrill,2002]a [ref: First principles of instruction]). Pebble in the Pond is described as a whole task approach that begins with the complete task learners are expected to perform rather than first breaking the task into isolated components( Merrill, [https://files.eric.ed.gov/fulltext/EJ826059.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com 2007] [ref: A Task-Centered Instructional Strategy, Journal of Research on Technology in Education]).

=== Background and Development ===
Merrill introduced the Pebble in the Pond model in 2002 during a period in which traditional instructional systems design approaches were being criticized for being too procedural and for delaying detailed attention to the actual content learners needed to master. Merrill did not present the model as a complete replacement for instructional systems design. Instead, he described it as a content centered modification that could help designers incorporate effective instructional principles more directly into the final product (Merrill,2002). The central idea is fairly simple: begin with what learners should be able to do in the real world. Once that whole task is clear, the designer works outward from it. This differs from approaches that begin mainly with abstract objectives and only later determine the exact examples, problems, and content that learners will encounter. The model therefore places performance at the center of the design process and uses the task itself to guide later decisions about content and instruction. Merrill later described the approach as content first, task centered instructional design procedure ( Merrill, 2007)
[[File:M. David Merrill (3662310676) (2).jpg|thumb|Figure 1M. David Merrill

Note. M. David Merrill speaking at ED-MEDIA 2009 in Honolulu. Photograph by Kristina D. C. Hoeppner, 2009, via Wikimedia Commons. Licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0 [ref: File:M. David Merrill (3662310676) (2).jpg - Wikipedia, commons.wikimedia.org]]]

== The Man Behind the Theory: M. David Merrill ==
M. David Merrill is an instructional designer theorist and professor emeritus at Utah State University. He earned a bachelor's degree from Brigham Young University in 1961 and both a master's degree and PhD from the University of Illinois in 1964. Across a career extending for more than five decades, his work has focused in the design of effective instruction.

His contributions include work on the TICCIT computer based instructional system, Component Display Theory, Elaboration Theory, Instructional Transaction Theory, knowledge objects and First Principles of Instruction. These earlier ideas are important to understanding the Pebble in the Pond because the model did not appear in isolation. It developed from Merrill's continuing interest in how instructional designers can move from identifying what learners must know and do to designing instruction that helps them perform complete tasks. [ref: About, M David Merrill]

== Structure of the Model ==
[[File:Illustration of Pebble-in-the-Pond Model.png|thumb|Pebble-in-the-Pond Instructional Design Model [ref: ]]]
The Pebble in the Pond Instructional Design Model is represented as a set of expanding activities. The "pebble" is the first whole problem. Each additional design decision creates another ripple around it. Merrill's original model moves through problem specification, progression, component analysis, instructional strategy, interface design and production.

=== Problem ===
The first ripple is to identify and fully specify a real world problem or whole task that represents what learners should be able to accomplish after instruction. Merrill (2002b) argues that this different from beginning with abstract objectives because the task itself becomes the actual content around which instruction is designed.

=== Progression ===
The second ripple is to develop a progression of whole tasks that gradually increase in complexity, difficulty, or the amount of knowledge and skill required. Each task remains complete, but later tasks introduce additional details or components (Merrill, 2002b). Merrill (2007) explains that a good progression begins with a relatively simple version of the whole task and gradually adds complexity.
[truncated]

OHL (ONE HUNDRED LIMINAL) is a seven-member Japanese dance and vocal group, also known as Wanlimi (ワンリミ). Its official fan name is PIECE (ピース). The group is managed by 1NE Entertainment. [ref: MUSICIAN, 1NE Entertainment]

== Overview ==
In 2021, leader JUNYA brought together KTA, RYUSEI, SHURU and GEN to perform with him. They later decided that the performances they wanted to create called for a seven-member group, and formed the current line-up with NAO and KANNA.

When the COVID-19 pandemic caused their previous agency's plans to be cancelled, the youngest member, GEN, initiated the establishment of a company to keep the group together and preserve its freedom of expression, and the group resumed its activities.

The members operate as a DIY group, handling their own music, choreography, costumes and live-show production.

The group has three units: OHL-D, focused on dance; OHL-R, focused on rap; and OHL-V, focused on vocals.

The group's name expresses the idea of "unlocking a hundred forms of potential and creating a supernatural phenomenon in society".

The group aims to perform at the Nippon Budokan.

The fan name PIECE reflects the idea that "each person who supports us is an essential piece in the story of OHL. Together, we will build on the story we began from zero and complete one big puzzle".

Draft text:
Kyoto University Design School () is the name used for educational activities centered on the Collaborative Graduate Program in Design at Kyoto University. The interdisciplinary five-year doctoral program began in April 2013 under Japan's Program for Leading Graduate Schools.

== History ==

Kyoto University established the Unit of Design, a faculty organization supporting the new program, in November 2012. Plans for the program were reported by the Asahi Shimbun and Sankei Shimbun in early 2013. A Design Innovation Base opened at Kyoto Research Park (KRP) in April 2013, followed by the establishment of the Design Innovation Consortium in March 2014 to support collaboration with industry and public-sector organizations. MEXT's project period was fiscal 2012–2018, and the program received an overall rating of A in its 2019 post-project evaluation. The Unit of Design was subsequently reorganized within Kyoto University's cross-graduate education framework. The Collaborative Graduate Program in Design continues to be listed among Kyoto University's graduate education programs.

== Organization ==

The program involves four graduate schools: the Graduate School of Informatics (informatics), the Graduate School of Engineering (mechanical engineering and architecture), the Graduate School of Management (management), and the Graduate School of Education (psychology).

The Design Innovation Consortium supports collaboration outside the university. The Advanced Scientific Technology & Management Research Institute of Kyoto (ASTEM) is its managing organization, and KRP serves as its secretariat.

== Education ==

The program's curriculum combines design approaches from five disciplines with methods intended for use across disciplinary boundaries. Ishida et al. (2017) describe design as a "lingua franca" among specialists from different fields. Mountford et al. (2020) cited Ishida et al. (2017) in their discussion of interdisciplinary education in engineering. Their study of European doctoral research networks also identified the importance of developing a shared language across disciplines. The program uses the concept of "+-shaped people" to describe specialists who can work across disciplines while retaining expertise in their own fields.

Coursework is organized into three categories. Design methodology covers the concepts, philosophy, and history of design. Broad-area design introduces methods such as ethnography, data analysis, and simulation. Domain design covers methods specific to the participating disciplines.

During the first two years, students undertake field-based learning (FBL) and problem-based learning (PBL) using topics drawn from faculty projects. From the third year, they participate in open innovation projects with external organizations. The curriculum also includes multidisciplinary field internships in Japan and abroad. Doctoral research is conducted in each student's home graduate school, with guidance from researchers in other disciplines.

A Design Innovator Index was developed to assess students' competencies, drawing in part on the United Kingdom's Researcher Development Framework. It consists of 24 items in four areas: intelligence, personality, engagement, and governance.

The Summer Design School, a separate workshop first held in 2011, brings together participants from different disciplines to address social problems. The 2026 three-day event was scheduled for 16–18 September.

== Collaborations ==

From 2014, Kyoto University's Unit of Design and Hong Kong Baptist University's Department of Computer Science jointly held annual Design for Sustainability workshops. National Cheng Kung University joined in 2017. Kyoto University and the University of the Ryukyus also held joint design workshops beginning in 2013, addressing topics including employment and regional revitalization. Kyoto City University of Arts was a formal partner of the Unit of Design, contributing faculty to the Design School and later participating in its organizing committee.

== References ==

Lime Trading Corp. (operating as part of Lime Financial) is an American electronic brokerage firm and technology provider headquartered in New York City. The company provides direct market access (DMA), low-latency trade execution, and trading APIs to quantitative funds, proprietary trading firms, and independent algorithmic traders. [ref: About Us, Lime Trading] [ref: Lime Trading Corp. Profile, Bloomberg]
[ref: Lime Trading Corp. Announces Membership in SIFMA, Knox News] [ref: Terms and Conditions, Lime Trading] [ref: Lime Trading Crosses 18 Billion Shares in First Half of 2026 as Triple Witching Tests Execution Infrastructure, Barchart] [ref: Lime Trading Corp. Pairs Low-Latency Execution Technology with Sterling Trader® Pro to Advance Equities Trading, AP News]

== History ==
Lime originally traces back to Lime Brokerage LLC, that was founded in 2000 as an internal trading technology unit within a quantitative American hedge fund.

In 2011, brokerage firm Wedbush Securities acquired Lime Brokerage, integrating Lime's low-latency execution tools and routing technology into its suite of institutional services. [ref: Wedbush Acquires Lime Brokerage, Business Wire] In 2018, Lime Brokerage merged its retail operations with Lightspeed Trading, and formed Lightspeed Financial. [ref: Lime Brokerage Merges with Lightspeed Trading, Finextra]

In 2020, the financial technology firm Score Priority Corp. acquired the Lime technology stack and trade execution infrastructure from Wedbush, re-establishing the technology team under the trade name Lime Execution.

In 2022, Score Priority rebranded its collective brokerage operations under the banner Lime Financial, adopting Lime Trading Corp. for its broker-dealer arm. The same year Lime Financial was awarded the Best Quantitative Trading Broker at the Markets Choice Awards. [ref: Best Quantitative Trading Broker: Lime Financial, Markets Media] In 2023, the firm moved to doing business under its official name, Lime Trading Corp. [ref: Score Priority Rebrands to Lime Financial, Traders Magazine]

In 2024, Eva Sehic was promoted to CEO of the company. [ref: Eva Sehic Promoted to CEO of Lime Trading, Business Hub Middle East]

== Awards ==
* 2010 - Lime Brokerage was awarded the Most Cutting-Edge IT initiative by the American Financial Technology Awards. [ref: Lime - About Us, Lime Trading Corp.]
* 2016 - Lime Brokerage was awarded the Best Infrastructure/Technology Initiative by the Wall Street Letter Institutional Trading Awards. [ref: Lime Brokerage Recipient of "Best Infrastructure/Technology Initiative" By 2016 Wall Street Letter Institutional Trading Awards, EIN Press Wire]
* 2022 - Lime Trading was awarded the Best Quantitative Trading Broker at the 10th Annual Markets Choice Awards, hosted by Markets Media. [ref: 2022 Markets Choice Award Winners Announced, Traders Magazine]
* 2024 - CEO Eva Sehic received the Excellence in Innovation award at the 2024 US Women in Finance Awards. [ref: 2024 U.S. Women in Finance Award Winners Announced, Markets Media]

[ref: Cambodia courts US investors to boost digital, tech sectors, Khmer Times] [ref: Cambodia Courts US Investors for Digital and Technology Growth, Angkor Times]

Alberto Fassi (born 30 July 1975 in Bergamo) is an Italian entrepreneur and the founder and chief executive officer of Legami S.p.A. Società benefit, a company active in the stationery and lifestyle sectors.

== Biography and career ==

After graduating from Bocconi University with a degree in Business Economics, Fassi spent an exchange period at ESSEC Business School in Paris. Following an internship at the Italian embassy in Ankara and an experience as a financial consultant for KPMG, he embarked on a Master's degree in creativity and innovation at the Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore in Milan. [ref: "[https://kpmg.com/it/it/insights/2025/11/alumnus-kpmg-anno-2025-alberto-fassi.html 'Alumnus KPMG dell'Anno': a Alberto Fassi il riconoscimento per il 2025]", KPMG, November 2025.]

During the Master's programme, Fassi developed a book strap in a variety of colours, each associated with a feeling. The product became the basis for Legami, which he founded in Bergamo in 2003. The company was initially based in his parents' garage. [ref: Elisa Britzelmeier, "[https://www.sueddeutsche.de/wirtschaft/legami-hype-tierstifte-erfolg-bergamo-li.3351222 Legami: Der Stifte-Hype in deutschen Schulen und die Erfolgsgeschichte aus Italien]", Süddeutsche Zeitung, 29 December 2025.]

Between 2005 and 2014, Fassi oversaw Legami's expansion in the Italian market and its subsequent growth abroad, including the opening of new concept stores and the acquisition of key accounts in Italy and internationally. [ref: Rachele Anconetani, Federico Colantoni and Federico Pippo, "[https://iris.unibocconi.it/handle/11565/4045577 We are young, we are curious, we are dreamers: the Legami growth path]", Bocconi University, 2020.]

In 2023, Fassi opened Legami's share capital to the Flexible Capital Fund, managed by DeA Capital Alternative Funds, which acquired a 42% stake while he retained control of the company. [ref: Sara Bennewitz, "[https://www.repubblica.it/economia/2023/06/30/news/dea_capital_investe_sulla_cartoleria_e_le_penne_di_legami-406227496/ DeA Capital investe sulla cartoleria e le penne di Legami]", la Repubblica, 30 June 2023.] In 2025, De Agostini Group acquired the fund's entire stake, becoming the company's second-largest shareholder. [ref: Giovanna Mancini, "[https://en.ilsole24ore.com/art/de-agostini-takes-over-42percent-links-and-strengthens-growth-path-AHBEbSzD De Agostini takes over 42% of Legami and strengthens growth path]", Il Sole 24 Ore, 27 November 2025.]
Fassi remained at the helm of Legami as chief executive officer and continued to be directly involved in product development.

== Sustainability projects ==

Fassi promoted the development of Legami's sustainability strategy. In 2023, Legami became a Società Benefit, committing to allocate 5% of its annual profits to environmental and social sustainability projects. [ref: Giulia Cimpanelli, "[https://www.repubblica.it/dossier/economia/imprese-sostenibili/2026/01/30/news/legami_quando_la_sostenibilita_e_nel_dna_dell_impresa-425128036/ Legami, quando la sostenibilità è nel Dna dell'impresa]", la Repubblica, 30 January 2026.]

Fassi also oversaw the development of Dreamland, a protected natural area in Bergamo created to support biodiversity. [ref: "[https://www.compromisorse.com/rse/2026/06/04/dreamland-el-parque-natural-protegido-de-legami-cumple-tres-anos/ Dreamland, el parque natural protegido de Legami, cumple tres años]", Compromiso RSE, 4 June 2026.] Established in 2023 on approximately three hectares, the project subsequently expanded to more than 30 hectares. [ref: "[https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/economia/2026/05/27/legami-fa-crescere-dreamland-oltre-30-ettari-di-parco-natura-protetta-a-bergamo_1a471b99-9149-4d9a-bae0-5d59bdca90d9.html Legami fa crescere Dreamland, oltre 30 ettari di parco natura protetta a Bergamo]", ANSA, 27 May 2026.]

== Writing ==

In 2026, Fassi published his debut novel, We Are Dreamers - La battaglia delle fragole, an adventure novel for young readers released by Magazzini Salani. [ref: "[https://www.huffingtonpost.it/life/2026/05/23/news/un_mondo_senza_sbavature_quattro_ragazzi_pieni_di_difetti_il_romanzo_desordio_del_fondatore_di_legami-21978902/ Un mondo senza sbavature, quattro ragazzi pieni di difetti: il romanzo d'esordio del fondatore di Legami]", HuffPost Italia, 23 May 2026.] The novel debuted in the weekly top ten of children's books published by la Repubblica. [ref: Ilaria Zaffino, "[https://www.repubblica.it/robinson/2026/05/24/news/libri_per_ragazzi_un_romanzo_che_celebra_i_legami-425364157/ Libri per ragazzi, un romanzo che celebra i Legami]", la Repubblica, 24 May 2026.]

== Recognition ==

In 2025, Fassi received the Alumnus KPMG dell'Anno award from KPMG.

Jochi (Jocheved) Ritz-Olewski (15 March 1947 – 10 February 2024) was an Israeli activist involved in preserving the memory of the Holocaust and the heritage of Bergen-Belsen. She served as chair of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel from January 2022 until her death in February 2024. She was the first woman, and the first person born in the Bergen-Belsen displaced persons camp, to chair the organization. She was also editor-in-chief of the organization's international journal, Our Voice. [ref: History in the Belsen organization in Israel: Jochi Ritz-Olewski, born in Bergen-Belsen, elected chairperson of the organization, Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel]

== Early life ==
Ritz-Olewski was born Jocheved-Rivka Olewski on 15 March 1947 at the Glyn Hughes Hospital in the Bergen-Belsen displaced persons camp in Germany. [ref: שורדת השואה האהובה והפעילה החברתית יוכי ריץ-אולבסקי הלכה לעולמה, mynet Ra'anana] [ref: Babyboom in Bergen-Belsen, Jüdische Allgemeine]

Her parents, Rachela Zelmanowicz-Olewski and Rafael Gershon Olewski, were Holocaust survivors. Her mother had been imprisoned at Auschwitz, where she played the mandolin in the Women's Orchestra of Auschwitz. Her father survived Auschwitz III–Monowitz (Buna) and Bergen-Belsen and later became a journalist, writer and one of the founders and chairmen of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel.

Her parents met after liberation and married in Celle, Germany, in 1946. In April 1949 the family immigrated to Israel. They initially lived in Bnei Brak and later moved to Ramat Gan.

She served in an intelligence unit of the Israel Defense Forces, where she acquired the nickname "Jochi".

== Education and career ==
Ritz-Olewski studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, earning a bachelor's degree in English and French as well as a teaching certificate. She later earned a master's degree with distinction in public administration from Bar-Ilan University.

Early in her career, she worked at the Technion – Israel Institute of Technology, where she coordinated a pre-academic preparatory program.

In 1978 she joined the Open University of Israel. During her career there she held administrative positions in the Dean of Academic Studies' office and served for many years as deputy dean of academic studies. [ref: University authorities, Open University of Israel] [ref: סוגרת מעגל: תושבת רעננה שנולדה בברגן בבלזן חנכה השבוע במקום מרכז הנצחה, mynet Ra'anana]

She retired from the Open University in 2014.

== Holocaust remembrance and Bergen-Belsen activities ==
Alongside her professional career, Ritz-Olewski was active in the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel. She joined its leadership after people born in the displaced persons camp and members of subsequent generations became involved in the organization, and later served as deputy chair.

She represented the Israeli organization in the international advisory framework associated with the Lower Saxony Memorials Foundation in Germany.

In 2012 Ritz-Olewski signed a declaration calling for the preservation of the former Bergen-Belsen displaced persons camp area, historically significant buildings and the Jewish cemetery, and for their incorporation into the Bergen-Belsen memorial landscape. [ref: Jahresbericht 2012, Stiftung niedersächsische Gedenkstätten]

In 2019 she participated in efforts that led to the transfer of five historic buildings in the former displaced persons camp area to the Lower Saxony Memorials Foundation for preservation and educational use.

That year she was also involved in the organization's campaign against the auction of a historic Bergen-Belsen rabbinical court ledger, arguing that documents of Holocaust-era historical significance should remain accessible to the public. [ref: Bergen-Belsen survivors petition court to halt sale of camp ledger, The Jerusalem Post]

== Our Voice ==
Ritz-Olewski and her brother Arie Olewski revived Our Voice, the journal of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel. The publication continued the tradition of the Yiddish newspaper Unzer Sztyme, which had been published in the Bergen-Belsen displaced persons camp after the Second World War and with which their father Rafael Olewski had been involved.

Ritz-Olewski served as editor-in-chief of Our Voice, which covered Bergen-Belsen survivors, the displaced persons camp, later generations and the preservation of the community's historical memory.

== Chair of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel ==
Ritz-Olewski was elected chair of the Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel and began serving on 1 January 2022, succeeding Shraga Milstein.

She remained chair until her death in February 2024. In March 2024 her brother, Arie Olewski, was elected chair of the organization. [ref: Arie Olewski is the new Chairman, Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel]

== Personal life ==
Ritz-Olewski married Oded Ritz in 1969. They initially lived in Haifa and moved to Ra'anana in 1978. They had three children. Oded Ritz died in 2020.

Ritz-Olewski died on 10 February 2024 at the age of 76. [ref: Jochi Ritz-Olewski, chair, passed away, Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel]

* [https://bergenbelsen.org/ Bergen-Belsen Survivors Organization in Israel]

The 2027 Atlantic hurricane season is the future event for the annual Atlantic hurricane season in the Northern Hemisphere. The season officially begins on June 1, 2027, and ends on November 30, 2027. These dates, adopted by convention, historically describe the period in each year when most subtropical or tropical cyclogenesis occurs in the Atlantic Ocean (over 97%). The National Hurricane Center (NHC) will begin issuing regular Tropical Weather Outlooks on May 15, 2027, about two weeks prior to the start of the season.

In advance of, and during, each hurricane season, several forecasts of hurricane activity are issued by national meteorological services, scientific agencies, and noted hurricane experts. These include forecasters from the United States National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)'s Climate Prediction Center, Tropical Storm Risk (TSR), the United Kingdom's Met Office, and Colorado State University (CSU). The forecasts include weekly and monthly changes in significant factors that help determine the amount of tropical storms, hurricanes, and major hurricanes within a particular season.

According to NOAA and CSU, the average hurricane season between 1991 and 2020 contained about 14 named storms, 7 hurricanes and 3 major hurricanes (Category 3 and higher), as well as an accumulated cyclone energy (ACE) index of 72–111 units. Broadly speaking, ACE is the measure of the power of a tropical or subtropical cyclone multiplied by the length of time it existed. ACE is only calculated for full advisories on specific tropical or subtropical cyclones reaching wind speeds of 39 mph (63 km/h) or higher. NOAA typically describes a season as above-average, average, or below-average depending on the cumulative ACE index, but the number of tropical storms, hurricanes or major hurricanes can also be considered.

Charles Lynn Webb, is an American attorney who previously served as a Georgia judicial officer. His career has included work as a Fulton County prosecutor, DeKalb County Recorder's Court judge, and private-practice attorney. [ref: Georgia courts directory 2013-2014 - Digital Library of Georgia, dlg.usg.edu] [ref: Charles L. Webb, Law Office of Charles L. Webb]

== Early life and education ==
Webb was born and raised in White Springs, Florida, and attended Hamilton County High School.

Webb attended Edward Waters College (1991, summa cum laude) and then Florida State University, where he earned his MPA and J.D. in 1995. [ref: Find a Florida Bar Lawyer, The Florida Bar]

Webb was admitted to practice law on November 1, 1996.

Webb is currently listed as a member of good standing.

== Prosecutorial Career ==
Webb began his career as a prosecutor with the Fulton County Solicitor General's Office before joining the Fulton County District Attorney's Office in 1998. [ref: ]

During his time with the office, Webb served as a senior assistant district attorney in the Major Case Division, where his work included serious felony cases.

== Judicial Career ==
Webb served as a judge on the DeKalb County Recorder's Court in June 2010.

== Private practice and criminal defense ==
In 2010, Webb represented a defendant in an appellate court where the conviction was affirmed. [ref: Brown v. State (Ga. Ct. App. 2010), Justia Law]

In 2014, in a highly publicized fatal hit-and-run trial, Webb represented the defendant, who was acquitted. [ref: Man found not guilty in fatal hit-and-run, WSB-TV Channel 2 - Atlanta]

In 2016, Webb represented a defendant charged with misdemeanor disorderly conduct in the Mothers's Day brawl inside Kiku Japanese steakhouse. [ref: 4 facing charges in Mother's Day brawl, WSB-TV Channel 2 - Atlanta]

In 2019, Webb represented a defendant in DeKalb County on charges of aggravated assault, aggravated battery, and possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony, which resulted in a jury acquittal. [ref: State of Georgia v. Michael Lester Austin, Jr., DeKalb County Superior Court, Case No. 18CR-2097-10, Jury Verdict, June 12, 2019.]

== Professional recognition ==
In 2004, the Fulton County District Attorney's Office named Webb its Lawyer of the Year.

In 2022, Webb received the Pinnacle Leadership Award from the Fortitude Educational and Cultural Development Center, Inc. [ref: Past Honorees, FECDC]

Webb was recognized as a Top 100 member by the National Trial Lawyers. [ref: Charles Webb - Georgia (Atlanta) - The National Trial Lawyers Top 100, The National Trial Lawyers]

Mayookha is a 2026 Indian Telugu-language psychological crime thriller film written and directed by Shree Tej SK. [ref: Mayookha Movie Review: A Gripping Suspense Thriller, The Hans India] Produced by Sasidhar Nalla under the Prashvitha Entertainment banner, the film stars Payal Chengappa in the titular role alongside Dev D, Aman Masud, Muralidhar Goud, and Lavanya Rani. [ref: Mayookha Telugu Movie Review, 123telugu]

The film revolves around the concept of phrogging, following an independent working woman who experiences strange disturbances inside her flat while a serial killer targets women in the city. [ref: Mayookha Movie Review, Cinejosh] Mayookha was released theatrically on 9 October 2026. [ref: Cognier Cine Creations to Release Unique Thriller “Mayookha” Overseas, TELUGU TIMES]

== Plot ==
Mayookha is an independent banking professional living alone in an apartment in Hyderabad. Carrying trauma from a childhood incident, she struggles with anxiety and isolation. Her life takes an alarming turn when she begins to notice subtle, inexplicable changes in her flat at night, including moved objects and the feeling of a presence sharing her home. Unbeknownst to her, an intruder is secretly inhabiting her apartment without her knowledge—a phenomenon known as phrogging.

Simultaneously, the city is gripped by fear over a string of gruesome murders of young women living alone. The killer leaves distinct signatures, taking items from the victims and obsessively seeking fragrances. Sub-Inspector Dev leads the police investigation into the homicide spree. When Mayookha approaches the police reporting that someone is residing in her flat, her complaints are initially treated as paranoia due to lack of evidence.

The tension escalates when a visitor to Mayookha's apartment is killed, placing her under intense suspicion. As SI Dev digs deeper into the victims' backgrounds and Mayookha's surroundings, the investigation reveals the terrifying link between the intruder in her apartment and the serial murders terrorizing the city.

== Cast ==
* Payal Chengappa as Mayookha
* Dev D (Dev Shashank) as SI Dev
* Aman Masud as Kumar, a carpenter
* Muralidhar Goud as Veeru's father
* Lavanya Rani as the opposite flat neighbor / bank cashier
* Charishma Dabbara as Honey
* Janu Varma as Divya
* Nanaji Karri as Ravi, apartment security guard
* Raghu Vasireddy as Assistant Bank Manager
* Abhilash Adda as Bank Manager

== Production ==
The film was directed by Shree Tej SK and produced by Sasidhar Nalla under the banner Prashvitha Entertainment, with Manoj Pola serving as co-producer. The narrative was conceived around the premise of "phrogging", a thriller concept where an unauthorized individual resides secretly inside someone else's house.

Farhan Vadakkan handled the cinematography, with Sharat J editing the film. The dialogues and associate direction were handled by Chintakindi Kiran Kumar, alongside additional dialogues by Shiva Ram Charan. Sibi Mathew Alex composed the original background score and songs. Prior to its theatrical release, the film was screened at festival circuits and won the Best Mystery Film award at the New York International Film Awards (NYIFA).

== Release ==
Mayookha was censored with an 'A' (Adults Only) certificate by the Central Board of Film Certification and released in theatres on 9 October 2026. Overseas distribution was handled by Cognier Cine Creations.

== Reception ==
Mayookha received generally moderate to positive reviews from critics, who praised the novel premise of phrogging, the suspenseful second half, and Payal Chengappa's lead performance, while critiquing the slow pace of the initial portions.

The Hans India rated the film 3 out of 5 stars, describing it as a "gripping mystery thriller" and praising Chengappa's acting alongside the twists in the second half, though noting that tighter pacing in the early scenes would have helped.

Pinkvilla Telugu also awarded it 3 out of 5 stars, commending the film's atmospheric tension and the unique integration of phrogging within a serial-killer mystery. [ref: Mayookha Telugu Movie Review, Pinkvilla Telugu]

Writing for Sakshi, a reviewer gave the film 2.75 out of 5 stars, calling it a thrilling watch with commendable performances, particularly highlighting Chengappa's emotional range. [ref: మయూఖ మూవీ రివ్యూ, Sakshi]

NTV Telugu rated the film 2.75 out of 5 stars, stating that the climax twists and background music elevate the film, even if the investigation sequences occasionally feel familiar. [ref: మయూఖ మూవీ రివ్యూ, NTV]

Filmibeat Telugu gave it 2.5 out of 5 stars, noting that the concept is fresh and the murder mystery maintains curiosity despite minor pacing flaws. [ref: Mayookha Movie Review and Rating in Telugu, Filmibeat Telugu]

123telugu gave the film 2.5 out of 5 stars, praising the lead cast, technical values, and background score, while remarking that the narrative moves at a gradual pace before hitting its stride. [ref: సమీక్ష: మయూఖ – పర్వాలేదనిపించే క్రైమ్ థ్రిల్లర్, 123telugu]

Cinejosh noted that while the initial setup takes time, the second-half twists and Sibi Mathew Alex's score provide solid thrills for fans of the genre. [ref: Mayookha Movie Review, Cinejosh]
