Muriel Agatha Horrell (13 December 1910 – May 1994) was a South African pilot, military officer and race relations researcher. She served in the South African Women’s Auxiliary Air Force (WAAF) [ref: Flying High: The Story of the Women's Auxiliary Air Force 1939-1945, Military History Journal] during the Second World War, attaining the rank of major and serving in South Africa, Kenya, Egypt and Italy. She was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) in 1947 for her wartime service. After the war, Horrell worked for the South African Institute of Race Relations (IRR) for almost four decades, where she researched apartheid legislation and compiled the Institute's annual Survey of Race Relations, which became a widely used reference on South African social, political and economic conditions. She received honorary degrees from the University of Natal and the University of the Witwatersrand in recognition of her contributions to race relations research.

== Early life ==
Horrell was born on 13 December 1910 in Pretoria, South Africa, to Katherine (née Sutherns) and Lloyd Leslie Horrell, the eldest of five children. She attended Pretoria High School for Girls and then completed a Bachelor of Science at the University of the Witwatersrand, followed by a teacher’s diploma at the Johannesburg Teacher Training College. [ref: Muriel Horrell A tribute, Race Relations News]  She taught for just over eight years in Pretoria  and helped develop a geography syllabus as a member of a provincial committee. She was also an active Girl Guide leader serving as a District Captain, keen sports woman, and accomplished rider.

==WAAF and wartime service==
Horrell developed an early passion for aviation and is reputed to have been the first South African woman granted an airline pilot’s licence qualifying as a Flight Officer in 1938. She was active in the South African Women’s Aviation Association (SAWAA) and was a flight officer and lecturer. At the outbreak of World War ll on 1 September 1939, Egerton-Bird, a prominent member of the (SAWAA) had telegraphed General Jan Smuts offering the SAWAA’s services to the government. On 10 May 1940, the establishment of the South African Women’s Auxiliary Air Force (WAAF) was gazetted, [ref: Government Notices, The Union of South Africa Government Gazette] and Horrell was enlisted in 1940. [ref: Transnational Race Relations: Muriel Horrell’s Journey toward Understanding Reserves and Reservations in South Africa, Africa, and the United States, American Studies] The WAAF’s wartime activities included communications, intelligence, link-trainer instruction, armament training, and technical work on aircraft, in addition to clerical and logistical roles such as dispatch riding and administration.

In December 1940, Horrell led the first detachment of WAAFs to be sent north where they established a camp in Nairobi, Kenya. She was posted to Cairo in 1941 as deputy director of the WAAF in the Middle East. [ref: Muriel Horrell – chronicler of the banal evil of apartheid, queen of a million footnotes., Daily Maverick]

In April 1942, the WAAF and South African Air Force (SAAF) administrative functions were merged, with only a few officers remaining in the directorate. With the El Alamein offensive toward Alexandria and Cairo in June 1942, Horrell oversaw the evacuation of around 800 WAAF personnel from Cairo to Aswan.

In December 1943, Horrell was appointed as WAAF Staff Officer responsible to Air Headquarters Services back in Pretoria with the rank of Major. When mobilisation began, she visited WAAF contingents in Algeria and Italy in 1945 as part of a demobilization team.

==Demobilisation and postwar work==
After being demobilised on 15 May 1946, Horrell began working as a technical officer for the National War Memorial Health Foundation. The Foundation originated with a proposal to establish a living war memorial that provided health services to all South Africans, including non-European communities. Its guiding principles were that it be living, national, and support fundamental human rights. [ref: The National War Memorial Health Foundation., South African Medical Journal] In this role, she helped to plan health promotion projects and travelled widely throughout the country.

On 14 November 1947, Horrell was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE) for her wartime service [ref: Central Chancery of the Orders of Knighthood, The London Gazette] in recognition of her organisation and evacuation of WAAFs from Cairo during the El Alamein campaigns.

Following the election of the National Party (South Africa) in 1948 the government announced that the Foundation would receive no further grants other than those promised by the defeated Prime Minister, Jan Smuts. Due to dwindling funds, staff were advised to seek other employment, and Horrell accepted a post as Technical Assistant at the South African Institute of Race Relations (IRR). [ref: The South African Institute of Race Relations 1929–1979: A short history., South African Institute of Race Relations.]

The IRR, founded in 1929, is an organisation dedicated to researching socio-economic issues and improving race relations in South Africa. In a 1989 interview, Horrell stated: “I’ve always believed that one must be involved to effect change.” [ref: Muriel Horrell, Researcher extraordinary, Race Relations News]

Kevin J. Dunlap (born November 15, 1959) is an American software engineer and inventor. In 1985, while at Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC), he substantially revised the early BIND (Berkeley Internet Name Domain) DNS implementation, building on the first Unix name server written at UC Berkeley the year before. In 1986 he co-authored a paper on his experiences implementing [ref: Experiences Implementing BIND, A Distributed Name Server for the DARPA Internet] it and wrote the "Name Server Operations Guide for BIND" [ref: Name Server Operations Guide for BIND (SMM:11), University of California, Berkeley] distributed with 4.3BSD. He also co-authored "Development of the Domain Name System" (1988) [ref: Development of the Domain Name System, Association for Computing Machinery] with Paul Mockapetris, which received an ACM SIGCOMM Test of Time Paper Award in 2006 [ref: ACM SIGCOMM Test of Time Award, sigcomm], and he holds a on a reduced-broadcast variant of the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP).
In 1993, the USENIX Association gave a Lifetime Achievement Award (Flame) [ref: USENIX Flame Award, USENIX]
to the Computer Systems Research Group at University of California, Berkeley, honoring 180 individuals, including Dunlap, who listed as a major contributor to the CSRG's 4.3BSD release. He later worked on commercial DNS products and took part in IETF DNS standards work, and his career since
has spanned telecommunications, digital video and railroad communications software.

== Education and Training ==

While attending Eastport, New York High School, Dunlap learned how to program BASIC & MACRO-10 on a DEC PDP-10 at Long Island Regional Instructional Computer System (LIRICS).
Dunlap went on to earned a B.S. in Computer Science from Old Dominion University (1979–1983). He later completed two certificates at the University of Washington: Embedded and Real-Time Systems Programming (2011–2012) and Cybersecurity (2021).

== BIND & Domain Name System ==
=== Digital Equipment Corporation and UC Berkeley CSRG (1983–1990) ===

Dunlap joined DEC in 1983 and worked there as a software engineer, later senior software engineer. By 1986 he was in DEC's Ultrix Engineering Advanced Development Group, and from 1985 to 1987 he was on loan to the Computer Systems Research Group (CSRG) [ref: The Computer Systems Research Group 1979 - 1993, NetBSD] at the University of California, Berkeley, the group behind the Berkeley Software Distribution Unix distributions in which BIND was developed.

The first Unix implementation of a DNS name server, BIND, had been written in 1984 by four Berkeley graduate students: Douglas Terry, Mark Painter, David Riggle and Songnian Zhou. [ref: The History of BIND, ISC]
In 1985, Dunlap substantially revised that implementation. Mike Karels, Phil Almquist and Paul Vixie then took over its maintenance, and Vixie later co-founded the Internet Systems Consortium to maintain BIND. In October 1986 Dunlap presented on DNS at the 4th IETF meeting at SRI in Menlo Park [ref: 4th IETF Proceedings].

=== Check Point Software Technologies / MetaInfo (1996–2001) ===

As a staff software engineer, Dunlap was technical lead for the DNS component of Meta IP DNS [ref: IP Services on NT Made Easy -, Enterprise Systems], the first commercial product based on ISC BIND 8 to run on Windows NT/2000 [ref: The History of Microsoft DNS Server, O'Reilly] He led three major releases (3.0, 4.0 and NG) and three point releases. He represented Check Point at the IETF and at DNS interoperability testing for about five years, and wrote and presented Internet-Draft proposals to the DNSEXT working group.

Designed and implemented IXFR (Incremental Zone Transfer), which lets secondary name servers fetch only changed zone data, and states that his implementation was included in the Internet Software Consortium's reference implementation of BIND. Also contributed to ISC's effort in developing Dynamic DNS Implementation.

=== Nominum (2001–2003) ===

As a senior software engineer, Dunlap contributed to designed and implemented server-side GSS-TSIG support (used for secure dynamic DNS updates) for Unix and Windows.

== Patents ==

=== US 5,278,829: Reduced broadcast algorithm for address resolution protocol ===

Dunlap is the sole named inventor on
, filed 10 January 1991 and granted 11 January 1994, with DEC as original assignee. It addresses a weakness in ARP-style address resolution.
The approach reduces broadcast traffic without discarding addresses that are still valid. The patent's rights passed through successive corporate owners, including Cabletron Systems, Enterasys Networks and Compaq, and it has since expired. It has been cited by dozens of later patents, including filings from IBM, Cisco, Nortel and Microsoft.

== Publications ==

* Experiences Implementing BIND, A Distributed Name Server for the DARPA Internet

* Name Server Operations Guide for BIND (SMM:11), University of California, Berkeley

* Development of the Domain Name System, Association for Computing Machinery

* Status of the 4.3BSD Release of the Berkeley Software Distribution, European UNIX systems User Group

* Reduced broadcast algorithm for address resolution protocol

Clash of the Thundermans is a 2026 American superhero comedy film directed by Trevor Kirschner and written by Jed Spingarn, Sean W. Cunningham and Mark Dworkin. It is the second film in The Thundermans franchise, following The Thundermans Return (2024). The film stars Kira Kosarin, Jack Griffo, Maya Le Clark, Chris Tallman, Rosa Blasi, Addison Riecke and Diego Velazquez reprising their roles as the Thunderman family, with Ariel Winter joining the cast.

Clash of the Thundermans premiered simultaneously on Nickelodeon and Paramount+ on September 3, 2026.

== Plot ==
As the Thundermans are being rewarded at the Hall of Heroes by Super President Kickbutt, the Replicator, a villain Hank locked up years ago, crashes the ceremony. As the family fight off his various duplicates, Chloe has a sudden power surge which blows the family away. Not thinking too much of it yet, Max scans the duplicates to find the real Replicator and Phoebe freezes him.

Afterwards, Barb takes Chloe to the super doctor to determine what happened. When they return home, Chloe announces that she is developing a new power: enerkinesis, the power to manipulate energy; however, she can't control the power yet. On the Superhero Evening News, it is announced that Kickbutt may be stepping down and Phoebe may be taking her place. Kickbutt later calls the team and tells them to meet her in her office.

At her office, Kickbutt discusses Chloe's new power and its potential danger. Because of her inability to control her power, Kickbutt wants to send Chloe to Top Secret Hero League School for Gifted Supes (T.S.H.L.S.F.G.S.) so she can learn to control it. Kickbutt introduces the family to Cognita, the school's principal with hyper-intelligence, who shows them a presentation of the school's offerings.

After they return home, the family discuss the prospect of sending Chloe to the school. While Chloe goes upstairs, the family becomes split on the decision: Phoebe, Billy, and Barb want Chloe to stay while Max, Nora, and Hank feel she should go. An argument breaks out, and when Chloe breaks it up, her powers activate and destroy most the house. Kickbutt and Cognita show up for Chloe, the latter giving her a numbing agent to temporarily stop her powers. Phoebe refuses to give Chloe up, joined by Billy and Barb. Phoebe freezes Kickbutt, Cognita, Max, Nora, and Hank before making an escape with Billy, Barb, and Chloe.

Dr. Colosso unfreezes Max using a hair dryer, the latter unfreezing the rest of them. The escapees are declared fugitives of the Hero League, and Max is directed to lead what's left of the T-Force to retrieve Chloe. Meanwhile, Phoebe, Billy, Barb, and Chloe go to the Hall of Heroes Museum to retrieve Antidote Man's Lasso of Healing to undo the numbing of Chloe's powers. They are almost apprehended by Max, Nora, and Chloe, but Dr. Colosso crashes the Thunder Van into the wall, inadvertently giving them an escape route.

They go to the barn of Mee-Maw, Barb's mother whose power is sonic screaming, and she successfully uses the Lasso of Healing on Chloe, restoring her powers. Meanwhile, Max invents a quasiparticle thermo-energy detector to detect Chloe's power and track her location, which Chloe inadvertently reveals while Phoebe tries to teach her to control her power. After failing to control her power multiple times, cooking a chicken (that Dr. Colosso was flirting with) and destroying a tractor in the process, the other half of the family arrive for Chloe, but they are still denied her; this results in a fight between the two halves, with Phoebe facing Max, Barb facing Hank, and Billy facing Nora. Mee-Maw uses her sonic scream to halt the fighting, and Chloe announces she will go to the school.

She teleports into Kickbutt's office, resigning herself. One of Cognita's students, Granite Girl, enters and calcifies Kickbutt into a statue of stone. Afterwards, Cognita reveals her true intentions to utilize Chloe's power and Granite Girl takes her away. Back at home, the rest of the family are trying to clean up their destroyed home when two Hero League officials show up with news of an incident. Kickbutt, half-freed from the stone, and Captain Chisel appear. The family learns that Cognita is evil and took Chloe and six of her other students off the grid, but don't yet know her intentions.

Chloe is taken to Facility X, Cognita's lair, where she is introduced to Cognita's six students: Granite Girl, Magneteen, Toxic Todd, Sludgerella, and Desk Boy, all of whom are brainwashed. She reveals her full intentions to use Chloe's enerkinesis to obliterate all of Metroburg. Back in Hiddenville, the family realize they must come back together as a team to rescue Chloe; Max and Phoebe do so reluctantly. Meanwhile, Chloe is handcuffed and a headnamd is attached to her head. However, her legs aren't restricted, allowing her to kick Cognita into Magneteen, who gets stuck. As Cognita and the other students free her, Chloe uses the time to teleport to her wristwatch and send a distress signal to her family, allowing them to pinpoint her location.

Hamlet Ghazaryan (Armenian: Համլետ Ղազարյան; born 2 June 1994) is an Armenian actor, voice actor, radio presenter and poet.

== Early life and education ==

Ghazaryan was born on 2 June 1994 in Salut, Shirak Province, Armenia. In 2008, he moved with his family to Gyumri, where he attended Mesrop Mashtots School No. 29. In 2012, he entered the Gyumri branch of the Yerevan State Institute of Theatre and Cinematography, graduating in 2016. He subsequently moved to Yerevan and pursued work in theatre, film and television.

== Career ==

=== Theatre ===

Ghazaryan has performed in Armenian theatre. His stage roles include Mesrop in a production of Mesrop Mashtots, directed by Hovhannes Hovhannisyan, and Edmund in a production of William Shakespeare's King Lear, directed by Artur Sahakyan.

In September 2025, Ghazaryan portrayed Armenian poet Yeghishe Charents in Charents, a production directed by Davit Harutyunyan at the Hovhannes Abelian Vanadzor State Drama Theatre. The production was based on Valery Piloyan's play The Last Night of Charents. [ref: «Չարենցը»՝ վանաձորյան բեմում․ բացվել է քաղաքի թատրոնի 94-րդ թատերաշրջանը, Armenian Public Radio] [ref: «Ես լուծում չեմ տվել․ ուղղակի ասել եմ՝ այսպիսի բաներ կային ու հիմա էլ շորշոփները երևում են»․ «Չարենց»-ը՝ Վանաձորի թատրոնի բեմում, Aravot]

Tert.am published an interview with Ghazaryan in which he discussed the responsibility of portraying Charents and his preparation for the role. [ref: «Չարենցին մարմնավորելը մեծ պատիվ, բայց նաև լուրջ պատասխանատվություն է». Համլետ Ղազարյան, Tert.am]

==== Portrayal of Yeghishe Charents ====

A review published by Theatrical Points examined the production's interpretation of Charents and Ghazaryan's performance. The critic discussed the actor's restrained portrayal and the production's emphasis on the historical circumstances surrounding the poet, rather than relying primarily on familiar theatrical mannerisms. [ref: Չարենցից դուրս Չարենցի հետ, Theatrical Points]

Ghazaryan has performed in Armenian theatre. His stage roles include Mesrop in a production of Mesrop Mashtots, directed by Hovhannes Hovhannisyan, and Edmund in a production of William Shakespeare's King Lear, directed by Artur Sahakyan.

He portrayed Armenian poet Yeghishe Charents in the play Charents, directed by Davit Harutyunyan and staged at the Hovhannes Abelian Vanadzor State Drama Theatre. The production was based on Valery Piloyan's play The Last Night of Charents. [ref: «Չարենցին մարմնավորելը մեծ պատիվ, բայց նաև լուրջ պատասխանատվություն է». Համլետ Ղազարյան, Tert.am]

=== Film and television ===

Ghazaryan has appeared in Armenian films and television series. His television roles include Vahe in Open Your Eyes, Bakh in Burned Dreams, Vardan in More Than Honor, Mayis in Flowers Under the Snow, Narek in Special Class and Special Class 2, and Hamik in The Mountains Will Remember.

In an interview published by Showbiz.am in February 2021, Ghazaryan discussed his portrayal of the younger Mayis in Flowers Under the Snow and his work on More Than Honor. [ref: Շատերը մի քանի րոպե էկրաններին երևալուց հետո մտածում են այլևս քասթինգների չմասնակցել ու սպասել հրավերի․ Համլետ Ղազարյանը՝ «Ծաղիկներ ձյան տակ» սերիալում իր դերի մասին, Showbiz.am]

In 2018, Ghazaryan appeared in Hamlet Jan, an alternative drama inspired by William Shakespeare's tragedy Hamlet. The film explores the experience of an actor attempting to portray Hamlet on the stage of an abandoned theatre, interweaving theatrical scenes with reflections on contemporary life and social change. [ref: Համլետ [ ջան ], Hetq.am]

In 2020, Ghazaryan appeared in the short film Happy Bday 2U, as reported by Showbiz.am. [ref: Բռնություն, էրոտիկա․ «HAPPY BDAY 2U» 18+ ֆիլմի մանրամասներն ու զավեշտալի դեպքերը նկարահանման հրապարակից, Showbiz.am]

== Radio and voice acting ==

Ghazaryan began his broadcasting career at Shirak Public Radio and Television, where he worked from 2013 to 2016 as a programme creator, scriptwriter and presenter. His programmes included Fstatus, Shiraki Aravoty, Heqiat Papik and Bari Aravot Shirak.

From 2016 to 2025, he worked at Europe Plus as a programme creator, scriptwriter and presenter, contributing to the programme Euroformat.

Alongside his broadcasting career, Ghazaryan has established himself as a voice actor specialising in commercial voice-over and dubbing. His voice has been featured in numerous advertising campaigns in Armenia, and he has voiced dozens of television series for Shant TV.

== Poetry ==

Ghazaryan also writes poetry.

Draft: Dave Maris

Draft text:
David Maris is a Canadian artist whose painting "Truth and Reconciliation" represents Canada at the United Nations Office at Geneva.

Maris' painting is the only piece of permanent art that represents Canada at the Geneva offices of the United Nations. His painting was recommended for donation to the United Nations by Grand Chief Willie Littlechild, the Commissioner of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada. The painting was donated at an event organized by the Permanent Representative of Canada to the United Nations. [ref: Art Donation “TRUTH AND RECONCILIATION”, The United Nations Office at Geneva] His art was unveiled in September 2017, on the 150th anniversary of Canada, [ref: Blenheim artist has piece installed in the UN, Chatham Voice] and the tenth anniversary of the signing of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples. [ref: Bancroft artist featured by UN, Bancroft This Week] At the unveiling of his art in Geneva, Michael Møller's spokesperson said that Maris was "known to be outspoken for the rights of indigenous people in Canada." In 2023, the painting was displayed in a corridor linking and old and new buildings at the United Nation's offices in Geneva. [ref: Hannah Entwisle Chapuisat, [https://ualresearchonline.arts.ac.uk/id/eprint/22422/2/Entwisle%20Chapuisat%20Thesis%20%28FINAL%29%20%2811%20July%202024%29.pdf Policy-Oriented Art: Developing Disaster Displacement Norms in Diplomatic Venues], Chelsea College of Arts, 2023, page 170]

In November 2015, [ref: CAROL FEENEY: Art in Picton, The Intelligencer (Belleville)] Maris' art was featured in the "Consensual Discomfort" exhibit in the Art Gallery of Bancroft. In 2016, Maris' art was displayed at Blenheim United Church before being transported for exhibit in Switzerland. His exhibit "Flags" featured paintings that represented individual Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women. [ref: Artist, United Church team up to fight injustice, Chatham Voice] Maris' art was featured in a 2016 exhibit at the Palais des Nations in Geneva, documenting violence against Indigenous women and girls. The 2016 exhibit occurred during the 33rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council. In 2024, his art was featured at the Stories of Peace award ceremony. [ref: Stories of Peace Award 2024 handed out Sept. 24, The Hamilton Spectator]

Maris has lived in Blenheim, Ontario, in Bancroft, Ontario, and in Switzerland.

Humankind 2 is a turn-based strategy 4X video game currently in development by Amplitude Studios. A sequel to Humankind (2021), the game will be released for Windows in 2027.

== Gameplay ==
Humankind 2 is a 4X game similar to its predecessor. Like its predecessor, players are able to select whichever civilizations to play as across six eras of human history, from the nomadic age to the modern day, ultimately deciding how their civilizations evolve over time. The game introduces a new system called First Tales, which are founding myths that affect the development of civilizations in-game. [ref: Humankind 2 Rethinks One of Its Predecessor’s Most Divisive Ideas, Which May Solve The Great Culture-Switching Debate, IGN]

Players can also choose to keep playing as the civilization they chose at the start of the game, unlike its predecessor. Every civilization also has a new culture tree, which provides bonuses related to the chosen civilization's history and culture. A new system called Adaptations is introduced. Adaptations provide bonuses depending on which biomes your cities are located in on the world map. [ref: After Civ 7 stumbled, Humankind 2 looks like it's making smart choices to pick up the 4X torch, PC Gamer]For example, a city in the desert can adopt methods to gather water and protect against the heat, while a city in the forest can specialize in hunting animals and foraging fruit. Players can also adopt advancements from other civilizations they interact with in-game. [ref: 4X strategy sequel Humankind 2 gets its first extended in-game footage, rich in era-spanning, culture-shaping, history-rewriting action, Rock, Paper, Shotgun]

== Development ==
Humankind 2 is currently being developed by Amplitude Studios. [ref: Humankind 2 Forces You To Deal With The Consequences Of Climate Change, GameSpot] It was revealed at the 2026 Gamescom Opening Night Live with a live action trailer. [ref: Humankind 2 announced, coming 2027, and promises climate change and "a new take on historical strategy", Eurogamer] The trailer was produced by Nu Boyana Film Studios, which was based in Sofia. The game is set to be released for Windows in 2027. [ref: Humankind 2 trailer accused of being 'AI slop,' studio says nope: 'real actors, practical sets, and custom-made props', PC Gamer]

Draft text:
Jack Ridder (born 2004 or 2005) is a New Zealand software developer and entrepreneur from Southland. He is the founder of KiwiBudget, a personal budgeting app for New Zealand households that connects to users' bank accounts through open banking. Ridder left school at 15 and worked in supermarkets for several years before developing the app, which he has said was inspired by seeing customers struggle with the cost of living.

== Early life ==
Ridder is from Wyndham in Southland. He has been interested in technology and coding since childhood, and started building online servers for the video game Minecraft at the age of eight. He left school at 15. He has said that his school offered a business subject but nothing that taught students how to manage their own money, and that he would like to see a school subject on personal finance.

After leaving school, Ridder worked in supermarkets for about five years, including at New World and Pak'nSave. His work included pricing, which he said gave him an insight into the real cost of groceries. He has said that he noticed more shoppers using calculators to keep track of their spending, and that seeing people struggle with money there gave him the idea for a budgeting app.

== Career ==
Ridder's first app was a business-to-business tool for retailers. He held meetings with the supermarket cooperative Foodstuffs about it, but Foodstuffs was already developing a similar system, and he turned to building a budgeting app instead.

He began developing KiwiBudget in January 2026, working largely on his own through Bryder Holdings, a company he formed in Invercargill, with occasional help from freelancers. He said that being a solo developer in Southland was "a bit different" from working in larger cities, and could be lonely. By October 2026 he was working on the app full-time. He said he had averaged about 16 hours a day on it during development, falling to about eight as the coding work eased.

=== KiwiBudget ===
KiwiBudget is aimed at working-class households and at middle- and lower-income families. Its main target audience is university students, and solo parents are among its intended users. Ridder said that many of the budgeting apps he had tried were designed for businesses rather than households.

The app connects to users' bank accounts through the New Zealand open finance platform Akahu, and categorises transactions automatically using its own list of New Zealand merchants. Unlike budgeting tools that work by the calendar month, it is built around weekly and fortnightly pay cycles, and its home screen shows an amount that is safe to spend within the user's budget rather than their bank balance. It takes account of New Zealand IRD tax codes and KiwiSaver, and integrates with StudyLink and MyMSD, services of the Ministry of Social Development. It includes a grocery list tool and an AI "money coach", with its AI features turned off by default. Ridder also said he was developing features for comparing supermarket prices and for users to report grocery prices, which he compared to the fuel price app Gaspy.

The app was tested by 12 beta testers, and in October 2026 it was under review by Apple and Google for their app stores. It was scheduled to launch on iOS and Android on 16 November 2026, free to use with paid monthly subscription tiers. In October 2026 Ridder was interviewed about the app on Nine to Noon on RNZ National.

== Education ==
As of 2026, Ridder planned to begin a foundation certificate at the University of Otago the following year.

The Furuichi clan (, Furuichi-shi, also read Furuchi-shi) is a clan of Japan. Place names called Furuichi-gō existed in of Kawachi Province, in Higashinari () of Settsu Province, in Shiga District of Ōmi Province, and elsewhere, and the name derives from them. [ref: ]

== Furuichi clan of Yamato ==

The Furuichi of Yamato were a (provincial warrior) family based at Furuichi in Soekami District, Yamato Province, the present-day in Nara. They were (armed clerics) attached to the branch of Kōfuku-ji, and they built.

=== Origins and base ===
The site of Furuichi was once a market called. When its lord, the monzeki (abbot) of the Daijō-in, moved the market inside the Daijō-in's own district as the South Market (), the former site came to be called Furuichi ("old market"). [ref: 『戦乱と人物』、高柳光寿博士頌寿記念会 編、1968年、149頁]

As for the family's origin, the says that they were of the Kiyohara clan and descendants of Prince Toneri, and the (in the [ref: ]) says that they were descendants of, who had lived at Furuichi. Both, however, are sources of the early modern period, and there is no confirmation.

The home settlement of Furuichi-gō was surrounded by a moat and contained five machi (wards); village heads (shōya) and deputies (daikan) were placed there. They collected taxes but also represented the community, and the wards and villages ran annual observances such as festivals on their own., stressing this autonomy, argues that the Furuichi clan's control over the settlement has been overestimated, and that the moat around it should be seen as one of the moated villages (kangō) found widely in Yamato. He also holds that Furuichi Castle was not large enough to take in the town below it, and that it is reasonable to regard it as confined to the area of the aza (sub-district) named (old castle), the site of the present housing estate.

=== Successive heads ===
When the family began to use the name Furuichi is unknown, but the name appears in Shōchū 2 (1325). On the 4th day of the 12th month of the same year, the Daijō-in abbot left the (Zenjō-in) and moved to this Tajima-no-kimi (). Inaba Nobumichi sees this as a case in which the abbot relied on Tajima-no-kimi, a gobōnin (retainer of the abbot) who appears to have been the core of the abbot's armed force, and argues that the Daijō-in depended on the strength of the Furuichi. [ref: 中世寺院の権力構造, [[Iwanami Shoten] In Shitoku 3 (1386), took office as one of the (executive officers of the shuto assembly) together with and others, and the family had become the leading shuto of the Daijō-in side.

When the Daijō-in monzeki and the Tsutsui clan came into conflict from Kakitsu 2 (1442), Inken's grandson fought on Kyōkaku's side.

Insen died in Kyōtoku 2 (1453), and his son succeeded him. When the Ōnin War began in Ōnin 1 (1467), In'ei joined the Western Army. In'ei tightened his control over his retainers, for example by taking judicial authority within the house into his own hands, but, perhaps because this provoked opposition from kinsmen and vassals, he retired in Bunmei 7 (1475).

After In'ei's retirement his younger brother Chōin became head of the family. Since the Ōnin War the kokujin of Yamato had been divided into the Tsutsui faction and the Ochi faction, and Chōin acted as a leading figure of the Ochi faction second only to. At first the Ochi faction had the upper hand, and under Chōin the Furuichi reached their peak, but in Meiō 6 (1497) they were defeated in battle by the Tsutsui faction and went into decline. A peace was then concluded among the kokujin of Yamato, excluding the Furuichi, and Chōin sided with and, commanders of the Hosokawa clan who invaded Yamato, and fought against the Yamato kokujin.

After Chōin was killed in battle in Eishō 5 (1508), fighting between the Tsutsui side and the Ochi side broke out again in Yamato, and Chōin's successor joined the Ochi side. Furuichi Castle, the family seat, was taken several times during this period, and under Kōin it became difficult to hold. The Furuichi came to rely mainly on on the ridge (the of the sources) and on and Ōji () in the eastern hills (). Thereafter the Furuichi alternately fought and made peace with the Tsutsui side, and when Matsunaga Hisahide, a retainer of the Miyoshi clan, advanced into Yamato in Eiroku 2 (1559), they followed him.

=== Character of their power ===

==== Kinsmen and retainers ====
Asakura Hiroshi tentatively calls the league centred on the Furuichi the "Furuichi faction" (Furuichi-tō). Unlike the six leagues that served as sponsors () of the, no connection with the festival appears in the sources, but the entry for the 1st day of the 10th month of Meiō 6 (1497) in the names, as kokujin belonging to this league, the Furuichi, Yamamura, Nagai (), Tsubao (), Yamada (),,, Fukuzumi (), Uryū, Banjō () and Kushira (). Asakura cautions, however, that this is not the whole membership. Of these, the Kushira clan is described as distant relatives of the Furuichi through a brother in an entry of the Daijō-in Jisha Zōjiki for the 29th day of the 9th month of Bunmei 13 (1481) listing the relatives of shuto and kokumin.

Tanaka Keiji divides the Furuichi kin into "traditional kinsmen" and "fictive kinsmen". The former were the Yamamura,,, Yoshida,, Inoue, Nagata (Inagaki) and Nagai.

Smoking Groups for Art and Visual Composition is a Greek satire political party, founded in 2009. [ref: Ενώπιον κοσμογονίας το πολιτικό σύστημα;, Ημερησία On line] Its president is entrepreneur Nikos Louvros. The party's scope is to defends the rights of smokers. [ref: Οι Κ.Ο.Τ.Ε.Σ. και το... «Χαρίζω Οικόπεδα, Χαρίζω Χρέη», Καθημερινή]

== History ==
In 14 July 2009, it submitted a request to the Council of State to cancel the Avramopoulos Act, which, an action that gave it publicity. [ref: Η πρώτη προσφυγή στο ΣτΕ κατά της απαγόρευσης του καπνίσματος, Ελευθεροτυπία] [ref: Οι ΚΟΤΕΣ «τσιμπούν» το τσιγάρο, ΕΘΝΟΣ] [ref: Υποψήφιοι με χιούμορ, φαντασία, Έθνος]

The part made its first appearance in the 2009 Greek parliamentary election, running only in the parliamentary constituency of Athens A. The Greek press was surprised by the promotion of the part from a BBC show, in which a special mention to the party was made, as the first one globally to support the right of smokers. [ref: Συν & Πλην, Ποντίκι] [ref: Οι λοιποί των εκλογών, Νέα Εγνατία, Καθημερινή Εφημερίδα της Καβάλας] In the elections, is received 1 353 votes, [ref: National Elections October 2009] [ref: Ορισμένοι τα πήγαν καλά. Τι έκαναν οι «μικροί» - Η ΑΝΤΑΡΣΥΑ, οι Τροτσκιστές, το Μ-Λ ΚΚΕ, οι ΚΟΤΕΣ και οι άλλοι, ΤΟ ΒΗΜΑ] managing to keep itself on the focus of media post-election. [ref: Εκλογές και απρόοπτα…, Η Γνώμη]

A year after the elections, Nikos Louvros was called as the party's spokesperson in a radio poll regarding the smoking ban [ref: Απαγόρευση του Καπνίσματος, Flash 96]

In the 2019 parliamentary election, Nikos Louvros participated as a candidate under Syriza. [ref: Εκλογές 2019: Οι υποψήφιοι βουλευτές Α' Αθηνών - Αποτελέσματα εκλογών, ονόματα και κόμματα, NewsIT]

In the May 2023 parliamentary election, the party participated on itw own, gathering 11 522 votes, whereas in the June elections, party leader Louvros stated that he supported KKE. [ref: Οι ΚΟΤΕΣ το έσκασαν από τις εκλογές και στηρίζουν ΚΚΕ, ΤΟ ΒΗΜΑ]

== Other characteristics ==
The posters and emblems of the party made great use of the party's acronym ( ). The party's emblem was an image with three chickens and in its showcase, it used a chicken-related pun ("και στις βουλευτικές εκλογές ΚΟΤΕΣ τσιμπητό", a pun with the Greek words "τσιμπητό" and "δαγκωτό", with the later also meaning "to vote with complete confidence" [ref: ]). The party emblem with the chickens was used several times, in articles talking just about the party [ref: Κ.Ο.Τ.Ε.Σ. τσιμπητό, Νέο πολιτικό κόμμα, LIFO] in articles that mentioned other, smaller parties too, [ref: Διεκδικούν μια θέση στη Βουλή με «όπλο» τους το χιούμορ..., Εφημερίδα ΕΛΕΥΘΕΡΙΑ] even after the elections. The pun ("τσιμπητό") became pretty popular. Much attention was also given to the fact that the name and the party goals expressed originality, humor, [ref: ΕΙΚΟΣΙ ΤΡΙΑ ΚΟΜΜΑΤΑ ΜΕΤΕΧΟΥΝ ΣΤΙΣ ΕΚΛΟΓΕΣ ΟΚΤΩΒΡΙΟΥ, «Χαρίζω χρέη-χαρίζω οικόπεδα» και «Κ.Ο.Τ.Ε.Σ» διεκδικούν τον τίτλο ονομασίας, ΡΕΘΕΜΝΙΩΤΙΚΑ ΝΕΑ] rich fantasy, [ref: Κόμματα με χιούμορ, e-enimerosi.gr] and that the also gave (alongside other parties "more or less serious"), "a different color to the seriousness of the political system" (). [ref: ΚΟΤΕΣ, φως και οικόπεδα, Η Γνώμη]

Furuichi In'ei () was a Japanese Buddhist monk and warrior active from the middle of the Muromachi period into the Sengoku period. He was a (armed monk-retainer) of Kōfuku-ji in Yamato Province. His father was, and his younger brother was Chōin.

== Life ==
=== Meeting with Kyōkaku and the deaths of his parents ===
He was born the son of, head (tōryō) of the kanpu shuto of the of Kōfuku-ji in Yamato Province.

On 3 March 1447 (Bun'an 4, 2nd month, 17th day), he met for the first time, the abbot (monzeki) of Daijō-in, who had moved into the at Furuichi through his father Insen's arrangements.

On 14 August 1448 (Bun'an 5, 7th month, 15th day), his mother died. The hundredth-day memorial was held on the 26th day of the 10th month.

From 22 June to 7 July 1449 (Hōtoku 1, 6th month, 2nd–17th day), he suffered from a disorder of the stomach and became gravely ill. Kyōkaku wrote: " has a calm disposition, and when he grows up he will surely become a person above the ordinary. Lately he has become all the more attached to me, which makes this all the more pitiful. There is nothing to be done, and I am simply at a loss", and prayed for him again and again. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、135頁] Perhaps because the prayers were answered, showed signs of recovery that dawn, and by the 17th he had fully recovered.

From 25 to 31 May 1450 (Hōtoku 2, 4th month, 14th–20th day), he made a pilgrimage to Ise Grand Shrine together with his grandmother, the nun, and his younger sister. Before departing he received a woven-colour katabira (unlined robe) from Kyōkaku. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、135頁]

On 30 July 1453 (Kyōtoku 2, 6th month, 24th day), his father Insen died, and he became the head (sōryō) of the Furuichi house.

=== Appointment as head of the kanpu shuto ===

On 26 October 1455 (Kōshō 1, 9th month, 16th day), following the downfall of the Tsutsui clan, he was appointed head of the, and, a member of the Furuichi family, became his deputy (daikan). [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、355頁] Until his coming of age (genpuku), devoted himself to temple administration, and other matters were handled by the Furuichi deputies (Yamamura Inkei and ).,, and were also appointed heads of the kanpu shuto. [ref: ] [ref: 興福院所蔵 鷹山家文書調査報告書, 生駒市教育委員会]

On 27 June 1456 (Kōshō 2, 5th month, 25th day), the temple administration notified him that he would receive, as his first stipend, 13 koku of polished rice and 5 kanmon of gratuity money from the Furuichi and estates, shōen belonging to the Furuichi domain. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、44頁] By this time appears already to have been taking part in practical work as a shuto. The following month, on 14 July (6th month, 12th day), an order was issued to Furuichi, Ochi and Koizumi to collect the contributions levied on the temples and shrines of Yamato for the repair of Daijō-in's buildings. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、207頁] These included Shōryaku-ji,, Hase-dera, Chōgaku-ji, Shigisan-ji, and Tachibana-dera.

On 14 February 1457 (Kōshō 3, 1st month, 20th day), Toyoda Raiei entrusted him with supervising the work on the of the Zenjō-in. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第1巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、75-79頁] To prepare the groundwork, about thirty labourers a day were called up from the seven gō (villages) of the temple's domain, joined by two. On the 19th he went to Hannya-ji with Kyōkaku and.

On the 20th day of the 7th month of the same year, he married a daughter of the Kubojō clan.

In the 3rd month of 1459 (Chōroku 3), his grandmother the nun died, and in the 8th month of the following year his grandfather died.

On 16 March 1460 (Chōroku 4, 2nd month, 23rd day), he met with and other members of the opposing Tsutsui faction. On 22 November (Chōroku 4, 10th month, 10th day), in a battle at Tatsuta in Yamato,, a member of the Furuichi family, and his sons the brothers were killed. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第2巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、357頁] [ref: 『奈良県史第11巻 大和武士』、奈良県 編者／朝倉弘 著者、1993年、116頁] Yamato was divided by the succession dispute (o-ie sōdō) in the Hatakeyama clan, and the (local landholders) were fighting in support of either Hatakeyama Yoshinari or Hatakeyama Masanaga; In'ei supported Yoshinari together with. and his sons, on Yoshinari's side, attacked Masanaga's camp at Tatsuta (present-day Ikaruga, Ikoma District) but were defeated. Kyōkaku was told that this was because Tsutsui Jun'ei, in the rear of Masanaga's army, had attacked with about 500 men. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、194頁]

=== The dharma name "In'ei"; meeting the Shiba and Asakura ===
On 18 September 1465 (Kanshō 6, 8th month, 28th day), he took the tonsure and adopted the dharma name "In'ei". [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第3巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、518頁] The ordination followed due form: his two preceptors, and, supplied the robes and a full set of garments, and an offering of 300 hiki was made. Before the tonsure he offered a cup of sake in the room of, and afterwards he was granted a bundle of sugihara paper and a roll of white cloth.
[truncated]

Draft text:
Kyōkaku (, also read Gyōkaku; 1395 – 19 September 1473) was a Japanese Buddhist monk of the Hossō school in the Muromachi period. He was born in the 2nd year of the Ōei era and died on the 27th day of the 8th month of Bunmei 5. His father was the kampaku Kujō Tsunenori, [ref: コンサイス日本人名事典 第5版, 三省堂] and his mother came from the of Jōdo Shinshū (later the ). Through this maternal connection he took in Rennyo, who later became the 8th head of the Hongan-ji, as his disciple, and the two remained teacher and pupil for life despite belonging to different schools. He is also known for having served four times as bettō, the head of Kōfuku-ji (the great temple of Nara), with the rank of. His posthumous name was.

== Life ==
Records confirm that Kyōkaku's mother (Horikawa no Tsubone, Buddhist name ) came from the Hongan-ji, but her exact identity is unclear. Based on Kyōkaku's year of birth, however, she is generally considered to have been a daughter of the 5th head; if so, Rennyo's father was Kyōkaku's cousin. At the time the Hongan-ji was in a state of decline and, to obtain the protection of the Kujō family, one of the regent houses, it performed services for the family somewhat like those of a. Kyōkaku's mother is thought to have attracted Tsunenori's attention while she was in service with the Kujō family.

At the age of 13 he took Buddhist vows under at the of Kōfuku-ji. The abbacy (monzeki) of the Daijō-in was customarily held by members of the Kujō family, and at that time his elder brother occupied it. When died young, Kyōkaku succeeded him as abbot at the age of 16.

He was appointed bettō of Kōfuku-ji on the 7th day of the 2nd month of Ōei 33 (1426), and was later appointed three more times, in Eikyō 3 (1431), Kanshō 2 (1461) and Bunmei 1 (1469). He had close ties with the central government and was on friendly terms with leading figures of the Muromachi shogunate, including the 6th shōgun Ashikaga Yoshinori. In Eikyō 10 (1438), however, he incurred Yoshinori's displeasure by asking for a reduction of the contributions owed to the shogunate, and was expelled from the Daijō-in. There was no direct master–disciple relationship between him and, who was appointed abbot in his place, and after Kyōkaku's restoration following Yoshinori's death the two waged a long, covert struggle for control of the Daijō-in.

When Yoshinori was killed in the Kakitsu incident, Kyōkaku, with the support of the (local warrior families) of Yamato such as and, entered and resumed his activities. He contested the office of deputy administrator of the, toll barriers on the Yodo River system, with the brothers and. In Kakitsu 3 (1443), through the good offices of the kanrei (both men had been banished by Yoshinori), he was granted an audience with the 7th shōgun Ashikaga Yoshikatsu. [ref: 田中慶治「和泉国上守護代宇高氏と興福寺官符衆徒棟梁古市氏」（小山靖憲 編『戦国期畿内の政治社会構造』（和泉書院、2006年） ISBN 978-4-7576-0374-5 および田中慶治『中世後期畿内近国の権力構造』（清文堂、2013年） ISBN 978-4-7924-0978-4 所収] With Mochikuni's backing Kōsen was driven out, and under Kyōkaku, Furuichi Insen, and were entrusted with the control of Yamato.

In Kakitsu 4 (1444) he gathered the kokujin of Yamato and ordered them to attack Kōsen and his brother, but they were defeated, and he in turn came under attack from Jun'ei. He then built Kionzan Castle on the hill within the precincts of the Daijō-in and held out there, but the castle fell the following year and he fled to in.

In the 4th month of Bun'an 4 (1447), Furuichi Insen brought him by force to Furuichi, the base of his family. Kyōkaku tried several times afterwards to return to An'i-ji, but each time Insen stopped him, and he was compelled to stay in Furuichi. [ref: Kyōgaku Shiyōshō (), entries for Bun'an 4, 4th month 13th day; 5th month 23rd day; and 6th month 27th day.] Behind this lay Insen's wish, troubled as he was by his struggle with the Tsutsui clan and by defections within his own kin, to preserve the cohesion of the main line of the by keeping Kyōkaku under his protection; Kyōkaku, for his part, needed the military strength of the Furuichi to maintain his own authority and so could not refuse the demands of Insen and the Furuichi. As a result Kyōkaku remained in Furuichi until his death, a stay that lasted 27 years until he died in Bunmei 5. [ref: 田中慶治「中世後期畿内国人層の動向と家臣団編成 -大和国古市氏を中心に-」（初出:『日本史研究』406号（1996年）/所収:田中『中世後期畿内近国の権力構造』（清文堂、2013年） ISBN 978-4-7924-0978-4）] [ref: 田中慶治「国人古市氏の馬借・関支配について ―南山城を中心にして―」『高円史学』13号、高円史学会、1997年、62-79頁。]

In the 7th month of the same year, when an uprising of bashaku (packhorse drivers) broke out in Yamato, Ōmi, Kawachi, Yamashiro and elsewhere, a rumour spread that Kyōkaku and Insen had set the bashaku in motion in order to destroy Nara, and the (the assembly of Kōfuku-ji's monk-warriors) placed the two under the sanction known as. Kyōkaku condemned the uprising in his diary, and the charge against him was false; but the historian Tanaka Keiji holds that Insen, who was closely tied to the bashaku, can be regarded as having organized and supported the uprising.

Afterwards, however, Kyōkaku was again restored, reappointed bettō of Kōfuku-ji, and wielded great influence over the whole of Yamato.
[truncated]

Draft text:
Lilo & Stitch 2 is an upcoming American science fiction comedy film written and directed by Chris Sanders. Produced by Walt Disney Pictures, the film will be a sequel to the 2025 live-action adaptation of Lilo & Stitch and the sixth overall feature film in the Lilo & Stitch franchise.

The film will be released on May 26, 2028, by Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures via their Walt Disney Pictures banner.

==Cast==

* Chris Sanders as the voice of Stitch, a blue koala-like illegal alien genetic experiment known as Experiment 626, who is adopted by Lilo as a "dog".
* Maia Kealoha as Lilo Pelekai, an orphaned Hawaiian girl who adopted Stitch. After the events of the previous live-action film, she is being raised by her next-door neighbors David Kawena (previously played by Kaipo Dudoit) and his grandmother Tūtū while her older sister Nani attends college.
* Sydney Elizabeth Agudong as Nani Pelekai, Lilo's older sister, who is attending the University of California, San Diego after the events of the previous film.
* Amy Hill as Tūtū, David's grandmother and, after the events of the previous film, Lilo's foster mother.

Additionally, Angel (Experiment 624) is set to appear in the film. The D23 teaser reveals she now has glowing antennae tips similar to the esca of an anglerfish, an ability she did not have in traditional animation.

==Production==
On June 26, 2025, Disney announced that it had greenlit a live-action sequel to the 2025 live-action adaptation Lilo & Stitch. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Dancing Way Into Development, Deadline Hollywood] The announcement was accompanied with a video of a Stitch (voiced by Chris Sanders) animatronic driving a pink ride-on toy car (one of the animatronics used to promote the 2025 Lilo & Stitch film) through the Walt Disney Studios in Burbank, California, noticing a "2" on a sign. He then writes the words "Lilo and Stitch 2" by making skid marks and shouts "Stitch want!" as he drives off. The announcement on June 26 was done to coincide with "626 Day" or "Stitch Day", celebrating Stitch, whose codename is Experiment 626. No creatives were attached to the film at the time. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Live-Action Movie Set at Disney, [[Variety (magazine)] In July that same year, it was announced that Chris Sanders, who co-wrote and co-directed the original 2002 animated film in addition to providing the voice for Stitch, would write the screenplay for the film. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Brings Back Co-Creator Chris Sanders to Write Script (Exclusive), The Hollywood Reporter] In June 2026, it was announced that Sanders would also be directing the film. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' to be Directed by Co-Creator Chris Sanders (Exclusive), The Hollywood Reporter]

At the Disney Entertainment Showcase during D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event 2026, it was revealed that Angel (Experiment 624), a popular character introduced in Lilo & Stitch: The Series, will be appearing in the film. [ref: Disney Reveals 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Will Feature Stitch's Pink Counterpart Angel, The Hollywood Reporter] [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' Drops First Look of Pink Alien Angel in Live-Action Sequel, [[Variety (magazine)]

In September 2026, it was reported that the film would supposedly be introducing a new lead character named Nellie, who is "[d]escribed as a 9-year-old fast-talking girl who moves to Hawaii from a big city and quickly befriends Lilo and Stitch." Fan responses interpreted this character as a renamed and reimagined Victoria, a girl from the second season of Lilo & Stitch: The Series who becomes Lilo's best human friend. [ref: Live-Action Lilo & Stitch 2 Adding New Character In Major Change from the Animated Original, ComicBook.com]

=== Filming ===
In December 2025, it was revealed that filming was expected for Summer 2026. [ref: The DisInsider Mailbag – Rapunzel, Lilo & Stitch 2, 2026 Disney Offerings, Daily Disney News] Filming began on October 14 at the Bishop Museum in Honululu; a blessing ceremony was held at the museum to honor the first day of filming, with Governor of Hawaii Josh Green in attendance. [ref: Lilo & Stitch 2 kicks off production in Hawaiʻi with blessing at Bishop Museum, KHON-TV] [ref: Yesterday was a busy day, with events that reflected my vision for Hawaiʻi’s future: strengthening our economy, supporting our kūpuna and keiki and building stronger communities. I was proud to welcome Disney back for Lilo & Stitch 2, supporting our local film industry and creating more opportunities for Hawaiʻi’s talent.[...]] As with the previous film, most of the film's production crew consists of local talent. Filming took place at Hilton Hawaiian Village on October 19. [ref: Lilo & Stitch 2 Films In Waikiki, And Stitch Brought Angel Along, The Disney Scoop]

==Release==
Lilo & Stitch 2 is scheduled to be released in the United States on May 26, 2028. [ref: 'Lilo & Stitch 2' & 'Incredibles 3' Set 2028 Release Dates, Deadline Hollywood]

Justin Humphreys is an American drag racer who competed in the National Hot Rod Association (NHRA) Sport Compact and Pro Stock categories, as well as the NOPI Outlaw category. He won the 2005 NHRA Sport Compact Modified championship before entering NHRA Pro Stock competition in 2007. In Pro Stock, he won the 2008 NHRA Carolina Nationals at zMAX Dragway in Concord, North Carolina, and the 2010 Pro Stock Showdown at Las Vegas Motor Speedway. He was nominated for NHRA Rookie of the Year in 2007. [ref: Richard Maskin joins Justin Humphreys, Motorsport.com] [ref: Charlotte: GM Racing final report, Motorsport.com] [ref: Justin Humphreys defeats Johnny Gray to Win Pro Stock Showdown, Dragzine]

== Racing career ==

=== Sport Compact racing ===

Humphreys competed in the NHRA Xplod Sport Compact Drag Racing Series in the Modified category, driving a 2003 Lexus GS 300. In 2005, he won the NHRA Sport Compact Modified championship. He continued competing in Sport Compact racing before moving into NHRA Pro Stock competition in 2007.

=== NHRA Pro Stock ===

Humphreys entered NHRA Pro Stock competition in 2007, driving a Pontiac GTO for RaceRedi Motorsports. The car was sponsored by Knoll-Gas Energy. Engine builder Richard Maskin joined the team's program, while Eric Luzinski initially served as crew chief.

During his rookie season, Humphreys competed in multiple national events and was nominated for the NHRA Rookie of the Year award. [ref: Memphis: Justin Humphreys preview, Motorsport.com]

At the 2007 NHRA Finals in Pomona, California, Humphreys reached the Pro Stock final round and finished as runner-up to Jeg Coughlin Jr. [ref: Humphreys, Glidden Bradenton test wrap-up, Motorsport.com]

=== Bob Glidden and the Pontiac GXP ===

In 2008, Humphreys competed in a Pontiac GXP. Veteran Pro Stock racer Bob Glidden joined the RaceRedi Motorsports team during the final six races of the 2007 season and continued working with the team in 2008 as crew chief. [ref: Humphreys, Glidden Bradenton test wrap-up, Motorsport.com]

By April 2008, Humphreys was among the top ten drivers in the Pro Stock season standings after the first four events. [ref: Las Vegas: Justin Humphreys preview, Motorsport.com]

=== 2008 Carolina Nationals ===

On September 14, 2008, Humphreys won the Pro Stock category at the inaugural NHRA Carolina Nationals at zMAX Dragway in Concord, North Carolina. It was the first NHRA national event held at the newly constructed dragway.

Driving the RaceRedi Motorsports Pontiac GXP, Humphreys qualified 11th and defeated Rob Mansfield, Jim Yates and Jeg Coughlin Jr. to reach the final against Kurt Johnson. Johnson's car developed a starter-drive problem and could not stage for the final. Humphreys staged his car and completed the run to secure his first NHRA Pro Stock national-event victory. He became the 51st first-time winner in NHRA Pro Stock history, and the victory was Pontiac's 189th in the category.

=== Pro Stock Showdown ===

In February 2010, Humphreys won the Pro Stock Showdown at The Strip at Las Vegas Motor Speedway, driving a Pontiac GXP. In the final round, he defeated Johnny Gray after Gray's car lost traction. Humphreys recorded a 6.79-second run in the final.

=== 2015 K&N Horsepower Challenge standings ===

Humphreys was listed in the NHRA's 2015 K&N Horsepower Challenge standings in 36th place with 95 points. [ref: 2015 K&N Horsepower Challenge Standings, National Hot Rod Association]

=== Return to racing ===

After being away from professional racing for several years, Humphreys returned to NHRA Pro Stock competition in 2014. Larry Morgan contacted him and asked him to drive Morgan's Pro Stock car at the Charlotte event. Humphreys accepted the offer. His competition license had expired during his absence, so he worked with Morgan at Rockingham Dragway to renew it before returning to competition. [ref: Humphreys relapses: Returns to addictive Pro Stock racing, Competition Plus]

== Personal life ==

Humphreys is from Monrovia, Maryland. He competed in professional drag racing with RaceRedi Motorsports, his racing team. [ref: Seattle: Justin Humphreys preview, Motorsport.com] [ref: Humphreys relapses: Returns to addictive Pro Stock racing, Competition Plus]

== References ==

The Darling Causeway is a 10km (6.2 mi) major road connecting the Great Western Highway at Mount Victoria to the Bells Line of Road at Bell in the Blue Mountains of New South Wales, Australia.

The road is two lanes in each direction, with the occasional overtaking lane, but can get narrow in some sections, and many sections have no shoulders. The road gained unexpected importance as a result of the sudden closure of the Mitchell's Causeway on the Great Western Highway in March 2026 [ref: ] [ref: ] due to the discovery of deep cracks in the pavement as the result of the internal fill deteriorating. [ref: ]

As a result, Transport for NSW has been conducting roadworks along the route to strengthen and replace the pavement due to the increase in traffic volume along the route. [ref: ]

The road is classified as Main Road 184 for its entire length.

== Route ==
The Darling Causeway begins as Station Street at the intersection with the Great Western Highway at Mount Victoria, and heads north as the road changes name to the Darling Causeway as it passes the Mount Victoria railway station. The road follows a ridge in the Blue Mountains that it shares with the Blue Mountains Line, which the road parallels for its entire length. The road then terminates at an intersection with the Bells Line of Road and Chifley Road at Bell.

Parakode N. R. Kurup (died 3 July 2024) was an Indian poet, translator, editor, and literary worker associated with Janayugam, Malayalanadu, the Sarvavijnanakosham (Kerala Encyclopaedia), and the [https://ksicl.org/ State Institute of Children’s Literature(KSICL)]. Known for his romantic and lyrical style, Kurup authored several notable works and contributed significantly to Malayalam literary translation, including the Malayalam translation of Laila–Majnu.

== Biography ==

=== Early Life and Education ===
N. R. Kurup was born into a middle‑class farming family in Parakode, Pathanamthitta district, Kerala. He went to NSS College Pandalam and then to University College Thiruvananthapuram for his post-graduation. He wrote several poems while he was a student, as well as lyrics and articles in various periodicals. In his youth, he became acquainted and worked closely with prominent political workers and student activists like Adoor Ramachandran,Thirunalloor Karunakaran, C. Achuthamenon, Vayalar Ramavarma, Thoppil Bhasi which made him a staunch sympathiser of the Communist Party of India. and later joined Janayugam.

=== Career ===

==== Early Association with Janayugam ====
N R Kurup became involved with Janayugam, the Malayalam daily aligned with the Communist movement, during the 1950s. He contributed significantly to the Party’s efforts during the 1954 Adoor constituency election. In 1958, he formally joined Janayugam as a member of the editorial committee and served until 1964.

==== Editorial and Literary Roles ====
After leaving Janayugam in 1964, Kurup served as:

* Chief Editor, Malayalanadu [ref: Malayalanadu, Wikipedia] [ref: Sahitya Varaphalam – Column by Critic M. Krishnan Nair, Malayala Manorama] weekly
* Editor, Sarvavijnanakosham (1970–1983)
* Editor, [https://ksicl.org/ State Institute of Children’s Literature(KSICL)] (1983–1986)

Kurup was known for his disciplined editorial work and his contributions to major state‑sponsored literary projects. He played a significant role in the translation of Ambedkar’s works undertaken by the [https://keralabhashainstitute.org/ Kerala State Language Institute (Kerala Bhasha Institute)].

== Literary contributions ==

=== Poetry ===
Kurup was widely regarded as a poet of love and emotion. His major works include:

* Nee Entethanu
* Dheerasameere Yamuna Theere
* Balance Sheet [ref: Library Catalogue Record – 222929, University of Calicut Library Catalogue]
* Chuvanna Theeyilekku
* Sreeraman Enna Manushyan [ref: Library Catalogue Record – 205549, University of Calicut Library Catalogue]
* Delhi Muthal Helsingi Vare

His first work, Nee Ente Thaane, carried a foreword by noted poet Prof. Thirunalloor Karunakaran, who was an early mentor and influence on Kurup’s literary development.

=== Translations ===
Kurup’s Malayalam translation of the celebrated romantic epic Laila–Majnu is considered one of his most notable contributions. His translation work was recognized for its sensitivity and literary finesse.

* [http://[ip]/cgi-bin/koha/opac-detail.pl?biblionumber=25141 Doctor Ambedkar sampoorna krithikal] [ref: Library Catalogue Entry – Biblio Record 25141, Kerala State Central Library OPAC] [ref: Library Catalogue Record – SSU.11093, VuFind OPAC] [ref: Library Catalogue Entry – Biblio Record 25141, Kerala State Central Library OPAC] [ref: Library Catalogue Record – ch.10997, University of Calicut Library Catalogue]
* Lailayum Majnuvum

Additionally, during his time on the editorial board of Janayugam and the Malayalanadu weekly, he translated numerous contemporary socio-political essays and literary critiques from English into Malayalam to support the publications' weekly runs.

== Legacy ==
Although N. R. Kurup made notable contributions to Malayalam literature—as a poet, translator, and editor—he did not receive the level of recognition many felt he deserved. His works, especially his romantic poetry and translations, continue to be remembered by those familiar with his literary journey.

===== Yuvakala Sahithi   =====
Parakode N. R. Kurup was one of the early leaders of Yuva Kala Sahithi [ref: യുവകലാസാഹിതി, Malayalam Wikipedia],, a prominent cultural and literary youth movement in Kerala. He served as the organisation’s first president, helping shape its initial activities and literary outreach. His involvement in Yuvakala Sahithi reflects his broader engagement with progressive cultural platforms and his influence on Kerala’s literary activism..

Ahead of the first World Malayalam Conference held in Thiruvananthapuram, it was N. R. Kurup who led the Deepashikha Rally conducted from Kasaragod to Thiruvananthapuram. In 1965, he participated as the Indian representative at the World Peace Conference held in Helsinki. He had written multiple travelogues such as "Delhi Multhal Helsingi Vare" [ref: Library Catalogue Record – uok2.54781, University Library Catalogue (VuFind)] and "Hiroshima Diary" [ref: Library Catalogue Record – uok2.54871, University Library Catalogue (VuFind)] during his various travels during this period.

Parakode N. R. Kurup Foundation

The Parakode N. R. Kurup Foundation honors his memory, hosting annual memorial events (Parakode N. R. Kurup Anusmaranam) [ref: Parakode N. R. Kurup Anusmaranam, In My City Today] and literary award ceremonies (the inaugural award was presented to Prof. O. N. V. Kurup in 2014)

== Selected works ==

Draft text:
The Polish Parliament Youth Council is an official advisory body of the Polish Parliamentary Group for Youth Affairs, established in 2024 to address the underrepresentation of young people in the legislative process.

The Council has over 300 members from across Poland, making it the largest youth advisory body in Polish history.

== History ==
On 10 May 2024, the Polish Parliamentary Group for Youth Affairs appointed the leadership of its Youth Council and tasked it with developing the framework for a parliamentary youth advisory body, organising recruitment, drafting the Council’s rules of procedure, and establishing its organisational structure.

The Council officially began its work on 8 November 2024, during an inaugural session at the Senate of the Republic of Poland. Participants included Marshal of the Senate Małgorzata Kidawa-Błońska, Senators Jerzy Wcisła and Krzysztof Kwiatkowski, former Commissioner for Children’s Rights Marek Michalak, and Deputy Commissioner for Children’s Rights Adam Chmura. With 304 members, the Council became the largest youth advisory body in Polish history. [ref: Obrady Rady Młodzieżowej przy Parlamentarnym Zespole ds. Młodzieży, senat.gov.pl]

On 18 October 2024, the Council organised a conference on children’s rights, during which it called on Prime Minister Donald Tusk to ratify the Third Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of the Child. [ref: W Senacie konferencja poświęcona prawom dziecka, senat.gov.pl]

On 22 October 2024, the Council organised an event on additional educational programmes for schools funded through Poland’s National Recovery Plan, bringing together representatives of the Ministry of Education, local authorities, and NGOs. [ref: W Senacie o dodatkowych programach edukacyjnych, senat.gov.pl]

The Council held its second plenary session on 22 April 2025 at the Silesian Stadium in Chorzów. The session brought together regional government representatives and members of parliament, including Joanna Bojczuk, Member of the Board of the Silesian Voivodeship; Senators Joanna Sekuła, Halina Bieda, and Jerzy Wcisła; and Members of the Sejm Urszula Koszutska and Aleksandra Kot. The discussion focused on encouraging greater civic engagement among young people in Poland. [ref: Głos młodego pokolenia na Stadionie Śląskim, Aktualności i wiadomości * Zabrze, Chorzów, Bytom]

On 15 May 2025, at a press conference in the Senate of the Republic of Poland, the Council concluded its six-month “YouthVote” voter mobilisation campaign, which aimed to encourage young people to participate in the upcoming presidential election. [ref: Apel Rady Młodzieżowej o udział w wyborach prezydenckich, senat.gov.pl]

Together with the Commissioner for Children’s Rights, the Council contributed to drafting legislation aimed at lowering the age at which young people can independently access psychological support from 18 to 13. After being passed by the Sejm and the Senate in June and July 2025, the bill was submitted to President Andrzej Duda for signature. The President instead referred it to the Constitutional Tribunal, citing concerns relating to parental authority. [ref: Co w Zdrowiu, cowzdrowiu.pl]

On 21 November 2025, the Council co-organised a conference on necessary reforms to the Polish government’s housing policy. Young people presented their proposals to representatives of the Ministry of Economic Development and Technology, Ministry of Development Funds and Regional Policy, and Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development. [ref: Młodzi o polityce mieszkaniowej w Senacie RP, senat.gov.pl]

On 27 November 2025, the Council submitted to parliamentarians a comprehensive position paper on proposed changes to Poland’s 2026 state budget. [ref: W Senacie posiedzenie Parlamentarnego Zespołu ds. Młodzieży, senat.gov.pl]

On 26 March 2026, Commissioner for Children’s Rights Monika Horna-Cieślak, together with representatives of the Council and other youth organisations, presented at the Sejm a jointly developed proposal to amend the Social Assistance Act. The proposed amendment would exempt minors from the obligation to cover the costs of an adult’s stay in a social assistance home. [ref: Dzieciństwo bez długów. Konferencja Rzeczniczki Praw Dziecka, Rzecznik Praw Dziecka]

The Council held its fourth plenary session at the Senate of the Republic of Poland on 10 April 2026. Participants included Deputy Marshal of the Senate Rafał Grupiński; Senators Jerzy Wcisła, Jolanta Piotrowska, Agnieszka Gorgoń-Komor, and Krzysztof Kwiatkowski, as well as other parliamentarians; Commissioner for Children’s Rights Monika Horna-Cieślak; Deputy Minister of Education Paulina Piechna-Więckiewicz; and representatives of the Youth Council under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine and the Chancellery of the President of the Republic of Poland. [ref: 4. posiedzenie Rady Młodzieżowej przy Parlamentarnym Zespole ds. Młodzieży, senat.gov.pl]

Reptiles of Israel (Hebrew: שומרים על זוחלי הארץ, Shomrim al Zochalei Ha'Aretz) is an Israeli reptile education and conservation initiative founded in 2016 by snake catcher and educator Avi Zobel. The initiative focuses on making information about reptiles accessible to the public, reducing misconceptions and fear of snakes, and encouraging the protection of reptiles and amphibians. [ref: הנחש של ישראל: הצפע המצוי, Ynet]

The initiative uses and promotes citizen science by encouraging members of the public to document and report reptile observations. Photographs, observations and reports are used to collect and share information on species distribution, seasonality and encounters between reptiles and people. [ref: 173 Snake Captures in Haifa • The Most Prominent Species in the City, Haipo]

== National snake campaign ==

In 2018, Reptiles of Israel initiated a campaign to select a national snake of Israel. The campaign involved Israeli nature and wildlife organisations and included a public vote through Ynet.

The Palestine viper (Daboia palaestinae) received the largest number of votes and was selected as Israel's national snake. The campaign was also reported by the Jewish Telegraphic Agency, which credited Zobel with initiating it. [ref: Palestine Viper declared Israel's national snake, Jewish Telegraphic Agency]

The Israel Nature and Parks Authority identifies the Palestine viper as Israel's national snake and states that it has held the title since 2018. [ref: גאווה לאומית בטבע: הכירו את החיות הלאומיות של ישראל, Israel Nature and Parks Authority]

== International Toad Day ==

In 2026, Zobel founded International Toad Day, observed on May 15. The initiative aims to raise awareness of toads and amphibians, address negative perceptions of them, and promote education about their ecological importance. [ref: Building International Toad Day from Nothing, AmphiBios]

In Israel, May 15 was included as Toad Day in the Ministry of Education's environmental calendar, together with educational information and activities concerning toads and amphibians. [ref: מאי – תאריכים ירוקים, Israeli Ministry of Education]

The National Natural History Collections of the Hebrew University of Jerusalem also marked International Toad Day in 2026. Its publication describes May 15 as International Toad Day and explains the initiative's aim of raising awareness of amphibians and toad conservation. [ref: יום הקרפדה הבינלאומי (15 במאי), National Natural History Collections, Hebrew University of Jerusalem]

Draft text:
Dave Kerpen is a New York based author and entrepreneur [ref: From Sponsored Wedding to Sponsored Content: How One Man Uses Likability to Get What He Wants, Fast Company] [ref: Dave Kerpen runs for North Hempstead town supervisor, Long Island Press]. Kerpen authored several books including Likeable Social Media (2011), [ref: Likeable Social Media: How to Delight Your Customers, Create an Irresistible Brand, and Be Generally Amazing on Facebook (& Other Social Networks), McGraw Hill Professional] Likeable Business [ref: Likeable Business: Why Today's Consumers Demand More and How Leaders Can Deliver, McGraw Hill Professional] (2012) published by McGraw-Hill. The Art of People (Crown Business) [ref: ] came later in 2016 followed by Get Over Yourself (BenBella Books) in 2024. [ref: Get Over Yourself: How to Lead and Delegate Effectively for More Time, More Freedom, and More Success, BenBella Books] He cofounded a social media company Likeable Media with his wife Carrie that he later sold. Kerpen also appeared on Paradise Hotel on Fox in 2003. [ref: Good Company; When 'Reality' Ends And Reality Begins, The New York Times]

== Early life and education ==
After growing up in Brooklyn in a "typical dysfunctional Jewish" family, he went to Hunter College High School and then to Boston University. Kerpen began working as a vendor at Fenway Park in the summer of 1996, before his junior year at Boston University, and at the FleetCenter that fall, where he sold Crunch 'n Munch on commission. [ref: Vendor tries new song and dance: Concession king lands sales job, Boston Herald] His sales routine of shouting, singing and dancing in the aisles earned him the nickname "the Crunch 'n Munch Guy". [ref: Vendor tries new song and dance: Concession king lands sales job, Boston Herald] Clay Siegert of the Herald wrote in 1998 that the routine had made him "a local celebrity", [ref: Vendor tries new song and dance: Concession king lands sales job, Boston Herald] and Richard C. Whiteley, in his 2001 book Love the Work You're With, wrote that Kerpen had "turned a routine sales job into high-flying, first-class entertainment". [ref: Love the Work You're With, Henry Holt]

After graduating from Boston University, Kerpen worked as a financial counselor at Merrimack Estate and Business Planning Group in North Andover, Massachusetts, while continuing to work as a vendor at night. He had joined the firm as an intern after its managing director saw him vending at a Bruins game in 1996.

== Reality TV and other events ==
In 2003 Kerpen was a contestant on Paradise Hotel, a dating reality show on Fox filmed at a resort in Acapulco. [ref: This Wedding Is Brought to You by..., The New York Times] Andrew Goldman of The New York Times wrote that he "politicked and double-dealt for three months" to reach the last four contestants. Heather Havrilesky of Salon described him as the "smart, regular-looking guy" who became "the driving force" behind a group of contestants known as the Barbies. [ref: Lord of the 'hotel' flies, Salon] In the finale his game partner was given the option of splitting a $250,000 prize with him and kept the full amount, which left him the only finalist without prize money.

Kerpen married Caroline (Carrie) Fisher in July 2006 on the field at KeySpan Park in Brooklyn, after a Brooklyn Cyclones game. [ref: How to Score a Sponsored Wedding, CBS News] [ref: Hoping for extra innings: Couple ties the knot on field after Cyclones game, The Brooklyn Paper] The two had met while working at Radio Disney in Boston, and Kerpen was then an eighth-grade teacher in Queens. Unable to afford the wedding they wanted, they persuaded companies including 1-800-Flowers.com and Entenmann's to cover much of the cost in return for publicity. [ref: James Bernstein column, Newsday] [ref: Marriage Proposal, World News Tonight] The New York Times put the value of the wedding at $100,000, of which the couple paid $25,000, and CBS News reported that they donated $20,000 to the David Wright Foundation. Gersh Kuntzman of The Brooklyn Paper wrote that a sponsor video shown on the stadium screen "did elicit a groan from the sellout crowd".

== Likeable media ==
After their 2006 wedding, Dave and Carrie Kerpen started a company called Likeable Media that operated in the social media and word-of-mouth marketing space. Two of the wedding's sponsors, 1-800-Flowers.com and Entenmann's, became its clients. [ref: 10Pearls Acquires Creative Social Media Agency Likeable, Adweek] It was based in New York City and Kerpen was the chief executive. [ref: A Review of Likeable Social Media: How to Delight Your Customers, Create an Irresistible Brand, and Be Generally Amazing on Facebook (and Other Social Networks), Journal of Applied Communications] The technology company 10Pearls acquired Likeable in 2021.

== Publications and critical reception ==
Kerpen wrote two books under the Likeable name, both published by McGraw-Hill. Likeable Social Media set out 18 concepts for businesses using social media, with case studies of companies applying them. [ref: 2012 Book Review: 'Likeable Social Media' by Dave Kerpen, Oakland University News Archive] Likeable Business set out 11 goals for organizations, among them listening, storytelling, authenticity, transparency, responsiveness and gratefulness. [ref: Do they really like you?, CMA Magazine] He also wrote about eleven principles of what he called likeable leadership.
[truncated]
