----

Max Shelton is an Australian agricultural scientist with research interests in tropical pastures and the use of Leucaena leucocephala as feed for beef cattle. Much of his career was spent at the University of Queensland [ref: Five decades of leucaena R&D: Is it time to move on?, Queensland Alliance for Agriculture and Food Innovation] where he was involved in the research and development of new cultivars, including an insect-resistant variety, [ref: Insect-resistant forage crop almost ready for commercial release, ABC News] and led research projects in South-East Asia. [ref: Improving smallholder cattle fattening systems based on forage tree legume diets in eastern Indonesia and northern Australia, Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research] In 2022, Shelton was awarded the AW Howard Medal for significant contributions to the advancement of pastures in Australia. [ref: Grants, scholarships and awards from the AW Howard Memorial Trust, Primary Industries and Regions South Australia] [ref: People on the move in the grain industry, Grain Central]

== Research and career ==
Shelton graduated with honours from a degree in agricultural science at the University of Queensland in 1968. He then completed a PhD at the University of Queensland in 1972 [ref: Factors influencing competition between upland rice (Oryza sativa Linn.) and undersown stylo (Stylosanthes guyanensis Aubl.), The University of Queensland] on the integration of stylo pasture in farming systems in North-East Thailand. He returned to the University of Queensland in 1978 in the Department of Agriculture, taking up a tenured lectureship in pasture science in 1986. He retired in 2016 as associate professor. [ref: Celebrating the contribution of Dr Max Shelton, Beef Central]

Shelton's career focused on the development and management of forage tree legumes in livestock production. With colleagues he bred a new psyllid-resistant variety of Leucaena called Redlands. [ref: 'Redlands' leucaena lifts beef productivity and profitability in coastal Queensland, Beef Central] He was also involved in the release of three other new pasture plant varieties (Sesbania cv Mt Cotton and Leucaena cvv Tarramba, and Wondergraze). Shelton worked with smallholder farmers in Indonesia to improve nutrition for cattle through better pasture management. He has delivered a series of courses to graziers in northern Queensland and advised them on the establishment and management of grazed leucaena pastures.

Shelton has also carried out research on the environmental impact of cattle production, including methane production [ref: Leucaena: The productive and sustainable forage legume, Meat & Livestock Australia] and how leucaena-based grazing systems can be used to sequester carbon. [ref: Soil organic carbon and total nitrogen under Leucaena leucocephala pastures in Queensland, Crop & Pasture Science] [ref: The sequestration and turnover of soil organic carbon in subtropical leucaena-grass pastures, Agriculture, Ecosystems & Environment] In addition, Shelton has investigated the drought-resistance potential of leucaena for farmers in dry, tropical regions. [ref: Drought fodder crop takes centre stage, UQ News]

Christopher Asah Okonkwo (16 January 1943 – September 1978), popularly known as Seven Seven, was a Nigerian singer-songwriter, music teacher, composer and performer. He's among the revolutionary of Egwu Ekpili traditional Igbo music genre. [ref: Okonkwo Asah (Seven Seven) Biography, Career, Age, Networth, Death [Highlife Musician], Throwback Times Nigeria] [ref: Profile: Okonkwo Asah, African Music Library] [ref: Awka Journal of Research in Music and the Arts (AJRMA), Volume 17, June 2024, Nigerian Journals Online]

He was known for combining traditional instruments with guitars and for using his songs to promote Enugwu Ukwu, his hometown in Anambra State, Nigeria. [ref: Long John — Christopher Asah and his Group of Enugwu Ukwu, Apple Music]

During his musical career, Seven Seven released several albums, including Long John, and performed in different countries. [ref: Long John, Amazon Music] [ref: 51 Lex Presents Tour Africa (feat. Group of Enugwu Ukwu) — EP, Apple Music] He was also involved in music education, teaching at educational institutions in Nigeria. He was known among his admirers by the title "Eze Egwu Ekpili", meaning "King of Egwu Ekpili".

== Early life and education ==

Okonkwo was born on 16 January 1943 into the family of Pa Okoye Asah and Madam Mmankwo Asah of Uruogbo village in Enugwu Ukwu, present-day Njikoka Local Government Area of Anambra State, Nigeria. His parents were musicians. His father played a local guitar, while his mother sang with women's groups. Their musical activities influenced his early interest in music.

He began his primary education in 1949 at St Anthony's Catholic Mission School in Enugwu Ukwu. After losing both parents in 1950, he was taken to Enugu by his uncle, Mathew Ekwedike Asah, where he completed his primary education.

Following his schooling, Okonkwo moved to Nzam in present-day Anambra West Local Government Area. There, he lived with Eze Okoye, who taught him bricklaying. He later worked as a bricklayer for Ronasco, a construction company owned by Chief R. O. Nkwocha, the Ide of Enugwu Ukwu. He became a senior worker who also trained other apprentices.

Draft text:
⁠Ziyater Kadın was a consort of the Ottoman Sultan Abdul Hamid II, holding the title of Fourth Kadın. She later relocated to live in Medina.

== Life ==
She was born in Circassia between the late 1850s and early 1860s to a noble family of the western Circassian tribes.

Following the defeat of the Circassians by the Russians in 1864, she migrated to Istanbul. She was received, along with other Circassian girls, at the Dolmabahçe Palace during the reign of Sultan Abdulaziz. There, she received her education and was renamed Ziyater, a name derived from the Arabic word Ziya (light) and the Persian suffix ter (fresh or tender), meaning "tender light".

She joined the harem of Sultan Abdul Hamid II and was elevated to the rank of Fourth Kadın after the divorce of Nürevsun Kadın in 1879. Following her promotion in the early 1880s, it is probable that she gave birth to a son who died in infancy, which prompted her to seek retirement. She was subsequently transferred to Topkapı Palace in preparation for a divorce requested by her. [ref: Presidency of State Archives of the Republic of Turkey (Directorate of Ottoman Archives), Topkapı Palace Museum Archive (Topkapı Sarayı Müzesi Arşivi), Document No: TS.MA.e 1415 20, Date: 2 Shawwal 1297 AH.]

== Move to Medina ==
After obtaining her divorce, she decided to retire from the political life in Istanbul and relocated to Medina. [ref: Presidency of State Archives of the Republic of Turkey (Directorate of Ottoman Archives), Financial Decrees (İrade-i Maliye - İ.ML), File No: 12, Document No: 2. Subject: "Allocation of the vacant salary of Saraylı Hiyaser Hanım, a Mujawir of Medina, to her sons." Date: 2 Rabi' al-Awwal 1312 AH.]

In Medina, she married a local notable and gave birth to two sons. Her husband was assassinated in the early 1890s by the then-Governor (Wali) of Medina.

== Death ==
She died in 1894. Upon learning of her passing, Sultan Abdul Hamid II issued an imperial edict transferring her state pension to her sons. [ref: Presidency of State Archives of the Republic of Turkey (Directorate of Ottoman Archives), Sublime Porte Document Office (Bâb-ı Âli Evrak Odası), Document No: BEO 469/35128, Date: 3 Rabi' al-Awwal 1312 AH.]

Draft: LOT Polish Airlines Flight 6883

Draft text:
LOT Polish Airlines Flight 6883 was a scheduled cargo flight from Warsaw, Poland to Beirut, Lebanon with a stopover in Varna, Bulgaria. [ref: Tragedy An-12 SP-LZA on 13.05.1977. – Polot, polot.net] [ref: ] On 14 May 1977, the aircraft operating the flight crashed into terrain near Aramoun, Lebanon, while attempting to land at Beirut International Airport in poor weather conditions. All nine crew members on board were killed.

== Background ==

=== Aircraft ===
The aircraft involved was an Antonov An-12BP registered as SP-LZA, delivered to LOT Polish Airlines in 1966, flying with the company from June to July 1967 and again from August 1976 until the accident flight. It was powered by four Ivchenko AI-20M engines. [ref: Accident Antonov An-12BP SP-LZA, Friday 13 May 1977, Aviation Safety Network] The aircraft was leased by LOT Polish Airlines from Poland's 13th Transport Aviation Regiment. [ref: Katastrofy wojskowych transportowców, TVN24] The aircraft was operated by military pilots in civilian uniforms. [ref: 1977 Zapomniany lot 6883, Newsweek Polska] This facilitated the passage of the aircraft over countries that barred military aircraft from using their airspace. [ref: Samolot z Polakami rozbił się o górę. Bliscy nie wierzą władzom, Fakt] The cargo onboard consisted of food, industrial products, medicine, and weapons. [ref: Brawurowy lot ku wolności na skrzydłach „Wiedeńczyka”, Dziennik Polski]

=== Crew members ===
The crew consisted of captain Henryk Bajer who had accumulated a total of 6,200 flight hours.

The first officer, Tadeusz Florek, had accumulated a total of 5,800 flight hours.

The remaining crew members which included flight navigator Jan Kowalik, Jerzy Grzywalski, Adam Rybak, Janusz Lech, Kazimierz Krupa and two unidentified crew members had between 3,000 - 5,500 flight hours.
== Accident ==
The flight departed from Varna Airport at 05:30 AM local time. On approach to Beirut Airport, the crew asked for clearance to land on runway 21 and a request to descend to 1,500 feet. Moments later, the aircraft struck power lines, trees, and stone terraces at 2,100 feet before crashing into Mount Douair near Aramoun, Lebanon, 8 kilometers southeast of Beirut Airport at 08:45 AM local time.All 9 occupants onboard were killed.

== Investigation ==
The investigation proposed that the most probable cause of the crash was difficulty by the crew in interpreting the messages transmitted by air traffic control, possibly due to a language barrier. It was found that the controller had to repeat his instructions to the crew while on approach twice for them to understand but the crew failed to acknowledge them.

Disputes from various agencies debated about the cause of the crash due to having no records of the crash and were assumed locked away, labelled as "TOP SECRET" (due to Poland being under socialist ideologies in 1977 until 1991). It was first thought that the weather had something to do with the crash, however, examination of the photos in the documents recovered showed that weather was not a cause of the crash.

In 1977, Lebanon was ravaged by war, and many feared that the aircraft had been shot down. Also, the plane was carrying cargo that included weapons, which hinted at political unrest between Poland and Lebanon and the Lebanese thought the plane was a threat and about to attack. Two weeks earlier, while taking off from Beirut, the aircraft had been shot at, causing in damage to the airframe.

The investigation team was not able to definitively determine the cause of the crash due to the documents being locked away, even after the fall of the Soviet Union in 1991. The crash remains unsolved to this day.

Draft text:
AI Writing Competitions

Writing with AI tools is relatively new, but there are now several competitions that offer AI-assisted writers the chance to enter their works. Several started in 2025 and 2026 as more writers began using AI tools in their work. They don't all agree on what counts. Some accept stories that were mostly generated by AI, while others only want work where a human author stayed in charge of the writing.

As of 2026 the main ones are the Prompty Awards, the AI Fictional Writing Achievement Awards (AIFWAA), the AI-Assisted category of Inkitt's Inkys, and the MIELOGOS Literary Prize.

Prompty Awards

The Prompty Awards opened for submissions on September 3, 2026. It takes English-language AI-generated and AI-assisted fiction in six genres: literary, science fiction, mystery/thriller, speculative, romance, and historical. Judges look at originality, storytelling, character, craft and how well the writer used AI. The grand prize is $1,000 plus a publishing deal with Apateon Press, and each category also has a $500 gold award and a $100 silver award. The early-bird deadline is November 1, 2026, the final deadline is December 31, and winners will be announced April 1, 2027. [ref: https://promptyawards.com/] Becky Tuch's newsletter Lit Mag News listed the awards in its September 14, 2026 issue. [ref: https://litmagnews.substack.com/p/happiness-is-a-warm-lit-mag]

AIFWAA

The AI Fictional Writing Achievement Awards, also called the AI Pen Awards, started in 2025. According to the organizers, the idea is to reward good writing done in collaboration with AI rather than just machine output. The first winners were named in June 2026 and included Call Me Avery by Ian Adams (Philosophical Exploration Award) and The Holding by J. M. Woodward (Narrative Architecture Award). [ref: https://aifwaa.ai/inaugural-awards]

The Inkys (AI-Assisted)

Inkitt, the online story platform, launched the Inkys in 2026 and included an AI-Assisted category alongside genre categories like romance and sci-fi. Stories have to be published on Inkitt, written in English, and at least 20,000 words long. The 2026 round ran from September 18 to October 18 with prizes of $500, $250 and $100. What makes the Inkys different is that there isn't a judging panel in the usual sense. Inkitt picks the winners with an algorithm based on how readers engage with each story. [ref: https://www.inkitt.com/contests/the-inkys-ai-assisted]

MIELOGOS Literary Prize

MIELOGOS is an international prize holding its first cycle in 2027. It is built around what it calls "symbiotic authorship," meaning work where the back-and-forth between a human and an AI really shaped the result but the human is still the author. It covers fiction, poetry, literary nonfiction, and graphic/hybrid/experimental work. Works have to have been published between 2024 and 2026, entry is free, and submissions run from February 1 to May 31, 2027. Instead of asking what percentage of the text came from AI, MIELOGOS asks entrants to explain how working with AI changed the piece. AI tools help with early screening but people make the final decisions. [ref: https://prize.mielogos.org/]

Draft: Copyright Office (India)

Draft text:
Established in 1957, the Copyright Office is an official department of the Government of India dedicated to protecting original creative works. The office is directed by the Registrar of Copyrights. It functions within a broader government network (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) that oversees patents and business development under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (India) [ref: https://www.dpiit.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/06/3d9c9c2daeefb97bb9ce964370938b71.pdf].

The Copyright Office is the main national authority in India for registering copyrights and overseeing copyright societies. Its headquarters is located at Boudhik Sampada Bhawan in Dwarka,New Delhi.

==History ==

Before India passed its own laws after independence, it followed British copyright rules. The modern Copyright Office was officially opened in 1958. Its main purpose was to create a national record to protect books, plays, music, and art.

From 1958 to 2016, the Ministry of Education managed the office. In 2016, the government transferred it to the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). This change was made to manage all of India's intellectual property rights in a single department. During this reorganization, the headquarters also moved to Dwarka. [ref: https://dohe-education.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/09/224f8f774f420af628dec35932ffee5c.pdf]

To make registration easier and more modern, the office launched an online "E-filing" system in September 2009. [ref: https://ipindia.gov.in/storage/uploads/media/English_Annual_Report_2024-25.pdf]
[ref: History of Copyright Law in India | Intellepedia]

== Registrar of Copyrights ==
*Jurisdiction
The office is led by the Registrar of Copyrights, who is chosen by the central government. Since 2016, the official who manages India's patents and trademarks also serves in this role.
The Registrar has strong legal powers. When investigating a case, they have the same authority as a civil court judge. For example, they can order people to appear in front of them, make them swear to tell the truth, and require them to provide important documents. [ref: Hand Book of Copyright Law]

*Appellate mechanism
In the past, special groups like the Copyright Board handled copyright arguments. However, the system changed in 2021. Today, if someone disagrees with a final decision made by the Registrar, they must take their appeal directly to a High Court judge. Other issues about business fees and licenses are now handled by Commercial Courts. [ref: https://prsindia.org/files/bills_acts/acts_parliament/2021/The%20Tribunals%20Reforms%20Act,%202021.pdf]

== Functions and services ==
The primary functions of the Copyright Office include:

* Maintenance of the Register of Copyrights: The office maintains the statutory Register of Copyrights, which records the titles of works and the details of authors, publishers, and copyright owners. [ref: The Copyright Act, 1957]
* Registration and Examination: Processing applications for copyright registration and modifications. Applications undergo a mandatory 30-day waiting period for third-party objections before formal examination. [ref: Copyright Application Workflow, Intellectual Property India]
* Regulation of Copyright Societies: The Registrar monitors and processes applications for collective administration societies (such as the Indian Performing Right Society) and ensures their statutory compliance.
* International Cooperation: Facilitating India's compliance with multilateral copyright treaties administered by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), including the Berne Convention, the TRIPS Agreement, and the Marrakesh VIP Treaty.
[ref: Working of Copyright Board in India]

Rafael Arroyo Valdespino (24 October 1892 in Mayagüez, Puerto Rico – 1949) was a Puerto Rican chemist. He published on the production of rum under the name Rafael Arroyo.

Arroyo worked at the Agricultural Experimental Station of the University of Puerto Rico in Río Piedras as fermentation chemist. In the 1940s he became head of the Experimental Station. Arroyo published Studies on Rum an other works on rum production and also held a US patent for the production of heavy rum. He died in 1949. His last works were published posthumously.

Till Death Do Us Part is the sixth extended play (EP) by American drag queen Trixie Mattel released on October 2, 2026. [ref: When did Trixie Mattel release ’Till Death Do Us Part?, Genius] Comprised of original songs written with a "spooky mood", [ref: Trixie Mattel on Her New Halloween Album & Special: 'This Was The Most Fun I've Ever Had Making Anything' - GO Magazine] the project signifies her first full-length musical project since 2022's The Blonde and Pink Albums, as well as a return to a more acoustic sound for Mattel after exploring electronic dance music [ref: Trixie Mattel on Her Synth-Spook Approach to Halloween with "'Till Death Do Us Part" - RUE MORGUE] and producing official dance remixes for other artists such as Jennifer Lopez, Duran Duran, [ref: Duran Duran Announces ‘Free to Love’ Remix Record – Including a Trixie Mattel Collab, Billboard] Wolf Parade, [ref: Listen To Trixie Mattel’s New Dancefloor Remix of Wolf Parade’s “I’ll Believe In Anything”, Sub Pop Records] and Paloma Faith. [ref: ]

== Background ==
In June 2024, [ref: ] Trixie announced via her YouTube channel that she would be going on a several-month break, citing severe mental health issues, an overwhelming work schedule, and "things [that] happened this year that I'm not ready to talk about". [ref: Ru Paul's Drag Race star Trixie Mattel takes a step back, www.bbc.com] The break lasted from July to late October. [ref: ] Later that year, in a video posted on December 30th, Mattel revealed that her and long-term partner David Silver, whom she had worked with on reality show Trixie Motel, had split "quite some time ago". [ref: Trixie Mattel and Boyfriend David Silver Split After 8 Years of Dating, People.com] She later announced a similar break in a video posted in July 2025 to occur throughout August.

Mattel stated that she did not intend to make a Halloween album, and that the songs "happen to be spooky, but the content...was my real life". In conversation with GoMag, Mattel said of the EP: "It's about...being disgusted with my own extreme workaholism and my extreme pressure on myself to achieve, the lengths at which I would work too much...skip family birthday parties...and play the game in a way that's just kind of gross, and I just don't feel that way anymore". She also noted that she "wrote these songs at a time of transition with relationship stuff. It also really is...mostly about my values changing as an artist. It's about a huge shift in my personal values". She started writing many of the songs in 2025, but wrote lead single 'Ghost On The Moon' "a few years ago when [she] was super depressed and having a huge crisis of faith that [she] wasn't a good musician or a good drag queen". She also said that 'I'm In Love With A Ghost' was written about mourning her relationship whilst continuing to live in the house they renovated together on Trixie Motel.

== Release and Promotion ==
On the 7th of August 2026, Mattel posted on social media platform X (formerly Twitter), writing, "what if I told you we aren't even very far away from another EP of my sad acoustic little country boy music". [ref: Trixie Mattel™ (@[user]) on X, X (formerly Twitter)] She made a similar post on the 7th of September, "what if I told you another sad white boy album is seriously nigh", posting a pumpkin emoji in the post's replies. [ref: Trixie Mattel™ (@[user]) on X, X (formerly Twitter)] On September 22nd, Mattel announced the Halloween-themed EP on social media, scheduled for release on October 2nd the following week, as well as the corresponding lead single 'Ghost on the Moon' for release on September 25th. [ref: Trixie Mattel Announces Halloween Album, Single “Ghost On the Moon” Out Friday, PHANTASMAG]

Following the release of the EP on October 6th, Mattel posted a 45-minute Halloween special entitled 'Trixie's Halloween Mattelathon' to her YouTube channel intending to showcase the songs on the EP. [ref: Trixie Mattel on Her Synth-Spook Approach to Halloween with "'Till Death Do Us Part" - RUE MORGUE] Plot-wise, the 'Mattelathon' follows Trixie during the production and filming of a live television Halloween fundraiser whilst being stalked by a killer. [ref: ] The special included performances of "'Till Death Do Us Part', 'Ghost On The Moon', 'I'm In Love With A Ghost', and 'Tell Me When It's Over', and had celebrity guest cameos from Luscious Massacr, Inde Navarette, Katya Zamolodchikova, Anna Camp, Jamie Lee Curtis, Kelly Mantle, Brittany Broski, Roz Hernandez, and Orville Peck. [ref: Chris Colfer weighs in on Glee reboot, Trixie's Halloween treat & all the best LGBTQ+ releases this week, Queerty]

= Shishay Amare (PhD) =
Shishay Amare is an Ethiopian academic and public administrator who was appointed mayor of Mekelle, the capital of the Tigray Region of Ethiopia, in October 2026. He holds a PhD and has held leadership positions in higher education, education administration, and public infrastructure.

== Education and academic career ==
Amare holds a PhD in Mechanical Engineering and has been identified as an associate professor at Mekelle University. [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com]

His academic publications and research profile are listed on Google Scholar. [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com]

== Public service ==
Amare has held several leadership positions in Ethiopia's public sector, including: [ref: ]

* Deputy Director of the FDRE Education and Training Authority.
* Director of the Tigray Roads Authority.
* Head of the Tigray Education Bureau.

During his service in the Tigray Education Bureau, he was associated with the regional education sector. A report documenting the effects of the Tigray War on education was published by the bureau.

== Mayor of Mekelle ==
In October 2026, Amare was appointed mayor of Mekelle City as part of a six-month caretaker administration established by Ethiopia's federal government for the Tigray Region. His appointment was reported by The Reporter Ethiopia on 16 October 2026. [ref: ]

The caretaker administration was assigned responsibilities that included restoring public services, rebuilding institutions and infrastructure, facilitating the return of displaced residents, and preparing conditions for regional elections. The administration operates under federal government direction and oversight. [ref: Ethiopia Appoints New Tigray Administration for Six Months, Horn Diplomat]

Draft: Old Tram Bridge

Draft text:
The Old Tram Bridge is a now demolished crossing over the River Ribble. Built in 1802 by the Lancaster Canal Company, it was opened in 1804 to carry goods by horse drawn carriages. Following several rebuildings, it was completely demolished in 2024 and replaced by the Preston Tram Bridge which opened in May 2026.

==History==
There has been a bridge crossing the river Ribble since Roman times, the road from Luguvalium to Mamucium (now Carlisle to Manchester) crossed the River Ribble at Walton-le-Dale, south-east of the centre of Preston, and a Roman camp or station may also have been here. [ref: William Dobson, Rambles by the Ribble, Volume 3, "[https://books.google.com/books?id=qu4-AAAAYAAJ&pg=RA2-PA78 Ch. 8, Walton-le-Dale] ", Publisher: W. and J. Dobson, 1864]

The Lancaster Canal Company obtained an act of Parliament, the Westmoreland Canals Act 1792 (32 Geo. 3. c. 101) in 1792 to construct a canal linking the towns of Kendal, Lancaster and Preston to the coalfields around Wigan. [ref: The "First" Tram Road, www.wyrearchaeology.org.uk] The original plan was to build an aqueduct but as a temporary measure, the canal company constructed a tramroad to allow revenue traffic to start flowing. Construction took three years. In 1794, the canal company engaged the services of engineer William Cartwright, first to supervise the construction of the foundations for an Aqueduct and later as Resident Engineer. The five-mile-long tramroad comprised a double-track plateway and was designed to transport wagons carrying coal from the Wigan Coalfields. Wagons were pulled by horses, up to six at a time, and each wagon had a capacity of two tons. Originally there were three inclined planes where the wagons were hauled by stationary steam engines and a continuous chain.

The Old Tram Bridge itself began construction in 1802 out of timber, finishing the following year and opened to the public in 1804. [ref: Old Tram Road] The bridge operated for around 40 years until falling into disrepair until ultimately being closed in 1858; Preston Corporation purchased the bridge from the Lancaster Canal Company in 1872. During the 1890s a chicken shack had floated down the river in a flood and destroyed some of the bridge supports, and so the bridge was reconstructed entirely during the 1890s at which point stone pilasters were installed.

In December 1935, high flood waters caused high levels of damage to the bridge resulting in the timber supports to be replaced in concrete and the replacement of the timber walkway. During World War Two, the timber walkway was removed to hinder a potential enemy advancement in the event of an Invasion. Restoration followed in the 1950s however during the 1960s, the bridge began to fail. A 1960 inspection learned that the concrete supports were beginning to fail and the timber was rotting; as a result, the bridge was closed in November 1964 to await repair. A loan was granted for the necessary work by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government in April 1965, along £17,725 being given by Matthews and Mumby's and work began to replace the concrete and timber by October 1965.

The 1965 bridge served as a vital public link between Avenham Park and Penwortham for over 55 years. However, by the 2010s, the structure began to exhibit signs of critical fatigue. A formal inspection conducted in 2019 identified more than 200 defects including severe fractures in the pre-stressed beams and "spalling" (the degrading and crumbling of concrete supports). These findings and the fear of collapse led to an immediate closure of the bridge on safety grounds. [ref: Preston's Old Tram Bridge closed over 'risk of sudden collapse', BBC News] [ref: REVEALED: The cost of replacing Preston's old tram bridge – and why there is no sign of it happening, Lancashire Evening Post]

The replacement Tram Bridge was funded through Preston City Council's £20 million Levelling Up grant. [ref: Preston's Tram Bridge - What's next?, Preston City Council] The new 125-metre weathering steel bridge was designed by Studio John Bridge and DYSE Structural Engineers, and was lifted into place in December 2025. It opened to the public on 22 May 2026, restoring the active travel link between Avenham Park and South Ribble. [ref: Memories shared as city's £6.6m tram bridge opens]

[[File:Preston Tram Bridge.jpg|thumb|Preston Tram Bridge, the replacement of the Old Tram Bridge as seen from Avenham Park]]

==References==

Nick Thompson is an Australian professional triathlete from Perth, Western Australia, who races long and middle distance. He won IRONMAN Cairns in 2026, his first full distance win. He finished seventh at the 2025 IRONMAN World Championship in Nice and fourth in the 2025 IRONMAN Pro Series. He won 70.3 Sunshine Coast in 2023 and 70.3 Tasmania in 2024. He finished third at IRONMAN Western Australia in 2023. He placed ninth in the elite men's criterium at the Australian Road Nationals Criterium in January 2026.

== Early life ==
Thompson is from Perth, Western Australia. He ran a 15:07 for 5000m on the track in Perth in December 2020. He finished second in the open category at IRONMAN 70.3 Western Australia in Busselton in May 2021.

== Professional career ==
=== 2023 ===
Since turning professional in 2023, in his first season Thompson was 7th at 70.3 Luxembourg and 9th at IRONMAN Switzerland. 23rd at the 70.3 World Championship in Lahti, Finland, 27 August. Won 70.3 Sunshine Coast, 10 September, in a time of 3:40:02, by more than a minute, first professional win. Later in the year he went on and placed 2nd at 70.3 Melbourne, 12 November. In his final race for 2023, Thompson placed 3rd at IRONMAN Western Australia, Busselton, 3 December, in a time of 7:48:22, his first full-distance podium. In the same race, winner Daniel Bækkegård set the fastest IRONMAN time recorded in Australia. The result gave Thompson his qualification for the IRONMAN World Championships in Kona in 2024.

=== 2024 ===
In Thompson's second year as a professional triathlete he went on to win 70.3 Tasmania in Hobart in February, in wet conditions, achieving a time of 3:54:10, finishing ahead of Mitch Kibby, Cameron Wurf, in a field which included Javier Gómez and Braden Currie.This was Thompson's fourth consecutive podium at an Oceania 70.3.

Thompson later went on to compete at IRONMAN Texas coming 14th, 9th at IRONMAN Cairns, and a DNF at IRONMAN Frankfurt.

In October, Thompson competed at the IRONMAN World Championships for the first time, coming 21st, where he was near the front after the swim and bike before fading on the run.

Thompson then went on to finish the year with a 15th at 70.3 Western Australia and the 70.3 World Championships Taupō.

=== 2025 ===
Thompson achieved 7th at IRONMAN Texas, 26 April in a time of 7:39:42 and was second at IRONMAN Cairns on 15 June and qualifying himself for the men's World Championship in Nice.

Thompson finished 3rd at 70.3 Zell am See-Kaprun in Austria, 31 August in a time of 3:48:30, with the fastest bike split in the professional field.Heading into IRONMAN World Championships in Nice where he was sitting 13th in the Pro Series standings.

Thompson finished seventh at the IRONMAN World Championship, 14 September, in a time of 8:10:32.

A 16th place at the 70.3 World Championship in Marbella, Spain in November resulted in him finishing in 4th in the final 20205 IRONMAN Pro Series standings, on 18,415 points, behind Kristian Blummenfelt, Casper Stornes, and Kristian Høgenhaug.

=== 2026 ===
Thompson finished 18th at IRONMAN Texas in April, followed by claiming the title at IRONMAN Cairns on 14 June, in a time of 7:49:48, as his first full-distance win, and finishing more than seven minutes clear of Ben Hill, and Jumpei Furuya in third.

Thompson took the lead inside the first 20km of the bike and led to the finish.

Thompson placed 11th at the IRONMAN 70.3 World Championship in Nice on 12 September, in a time of 3:56:04, in a race won by Hayden Wilde. He then went on to place 11th at the IRONMAN World Championship in Kona on 10 October, 8:01:12, where Vincent Luis won; Thompson had the 3rd-fastest bike split of those that finished in the field (4:12:36).

Draft text:
EZ Newswire is an American press release distribution and media technology company headquartered in the SoHo neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. Founded in 2022 by Neel Shah, the company provides a web-based platform for creating, distributing, publishing, and monitoring corporate announcements. [ref: EZ Newswire – Products, Competitors, Financials, Employees, Headquarters Locations, CB Insights] [ref: Reuters Signs News Distribution Deal With EZ Newswire, MediaPost]

EZ Newswire has entered into exclusive multi-year press release distribution agreements with Reuters and Fortune for their dedicated press release publication channels. The company also distributes announcements to other media destinations, including AP News, Yahoo Finance, USA Today, Business Insider, and regional news websites. [ref: EZ Newswire Signs Exclusive Distribution Deal with Reuters, EZ Newswire] [ref: EZ Newswire announces exclusive multi-year deal with Fortune, LinkedIn] [ref: EZ Newswire, EZ Newswire]

The company incorporates artificial intelligence into press release preparation, editorial workflows, and performance analytics. Its reporting platform measures distribution results, readership, search engine visibility, and references to published announcements in AI-generated answers. [ref: About EZ Newswire, EZ Newswire]

== History ==

=== Founding and early development ===

EZ Newswire was founded in 2022 by Neel Shah and launched its public beta in May 2023. The company was established to provide a technology-based alternative to traditional press release distribution services, combining digital publishing, distribution, and analytics in a single platform.

In October 2023, the company announced a press release distribution partnership with Big Technology, a technology-focused publication founded by journalist Alex Kantrowitz. [ref: EZ Newswire Inks Industry's First Exclusive Substack Distribution Deal with Big Technology Partnership, EZ Newswire]

In April 2024, EZ Newswire was selected as a winner of The MBA Fund's sixth annual pitch competition for early-stage startups. The company has identified The MBA Fund, Contour Ventures, and HearstLab among its investors.

=== Reuters partnership ===

On September 16, 2024, EZ Newswire announced an exclusive multi-year press release distribution agreement with Reuters, the international news agency. The agreement established a direct publishing arrangement enabling organizations to distribute business announcements to a dedicated section of Reuters.com through the EZ Newswire platform.

The partnership was reported by MediaPost on September 17, 2024. The publication described the agreement as a multi-year arrangement under which EZ Newswire customers could publish corporate news to a dedicated section of the Reuters website.

According to EZ Newswire, its agreement provides exclusive newswire distribution access to the dedicated Reuters.com press release channel. As of October 2026, the company states that competing newswire services cannot independently publish to that channel through an equivalent direct distribution agreement. [ref: How to Publish a Press Release on Reuters, EZ Newswire]

The press releases distributed through the service are separate from Reuters' independently reported editorial news coverage.

=== Fortune partnership ===

In December 2025, EZ Newswire announced an exclusive multi-year distribution agreement with Fortune, the American business publication.

The partnership established an integrated publishing channel enabling businesses and organizations to distribute press releases to a dedicated section of Fortune.com. According to EZ Newswire, the agreement made it Fortune's exclusive newswire distribution partner for the channel.

The integration allows organizations to submit announcements through EZ Newswire for publication on Fortune.com, subject to applicable content requirements. [ref: Press Release Distribution Pricing, EZ Newswire]

As of October 2026, EZ Newswire identifies Reuters.com and Fortune.com as its two exclusive premium newswire distribution destinations. The arrangements concern dedicated press release publication channels rather than independently produced Reuters or Fortune editorial journalism.

=== Expansion of technology and services ===

During 2025 and 2026, EZ Newswire expanded its platform to incorporate additional automation, publisher integrations, and analytics capabilities.

In 2026, the company introduced reporting capabilities designed to monitor distributed press releases across publisher websites, search engines, and AI-powered information services. [ref: EZ Newswire Launches Press Release Performance Reports With AI Visibility Tracking, Fortune]

In 2026, the company also introduced collaborative workspaces for organizations and public relations agencies, allowing multiple users to manage press releases under shared organizational accounts. [ref: EZ Newswire Launches Workspaces to Streamline Multi-User Collaboration and Account Management, Fortune]

== Products and services ==

=== Press release distribution ===

EZ Newswire operates a self-service digital platform for creating, reviewing, scheduling, and distributing press releases.

Draft text:
In Singapore, a Residents' Committee (RC) is a grassroot organisation run by residents and managed by the People's Association (PA). It works closely with other grassroots organisations like the Citizens’ Consultative Committees (CCCs) and various government agencies. [ref: Residents' Committees, People's Association]

== History ==
Established in 1987, they were meant to allow residents to improve their physical enviroment as well as, their quality of life. The first RCs were in the estates of Ang Mo Kio, Boon Lay, Bukit Merah, Kolam Ayer and Toa Payoh. They were initially composed of representitives from the CCCs, community centre management committees, HDB, police and flat dwellers. [ref: New resident committees set up in five estates, The Straits Times]

They first under the Prime Minister's Office and later, the Ministry of Community Development. [ref: Residents' Committees are formed, nlb.gov.sg] Since 1993, they have been under the PA. [ref: RCs and CCCs now come under PA's wing, The Straits Times]

In 2018, some RCs merged with Neighbourhood Committees (NCs) to form Residents' Networks (RNs). [ref: Newly created Residents' Network will serve residents of both HDB and private estates, The Straits Times]

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Humanity as cancer of the biosphere

Draft text:
----

Humanity as cancer of the biosphere refers to a family of comparisons between the expansion and ecological impact of the human species and the development of malignant cancer. Since the mid-twentieth century, physicians, scientists, environmental thinkers, philosophers, and writers have used cancer-related concepts to describe aspects of population growth, urban and economic expansion, resource consumption, and the transformation of ecosystems. [ref: Homo sapiens: cancer or parasite?, Ethics in Science and Environmental Politics] [ref: Three ways to think about the sixth mass extinction, Biological Conservation]

The comparison has not always been understood in the same way. Some authors have treated it as a metaphor or analogy, while others have explored it as a model, hypothesis, or possible diagnosis of the relationship between humanity and the biosphere. [ref: Humans as Cancer, Wild Earth]

== Recurring elements of the comparison ==

Across the literature, several recurring parallels have been proposed between human activity and malignant growth. These include:

* rapid population growth and the weakening of ecological constraints on the human population;
* invasion and destruction of surrounding ecosystems, compared with the invasion of healthy tissue by malignant cells;
* expansion into distant territories, sometimes compared with metastasis;
* loss of differentiation or increasing homogenization in human settlements, landscapes, cultures, and ecological systems;
* intensive appropriation of resources from the surrounding environment. [ref: Why Are There So Many of Us? Description and Diagnosis of a Planetary Ecopathological Process, Population and Environment] [ref: Is Human Culture Carcinogenic for Uncontrolled Population Growth and Ecological Destruction?, BioScience]

== Authors who explicitly developed or examined the comparison ==

=== Alan Gregg ===

Alan Gregg (1890–1957) was an American physician and medical administrator who spent much of his career at the Rockefeller Foundation.

In A Medical Aspect of the Population Problem, published in Science in 1955, Gregg explicitly compared human population growth with neoplastic cellular proliferation. He presented the comparison cautiously, as a speculative medical analogy rather than an experimentally demonstrated theory. [ref: A Medical Aspect of the Population Problem, Science]

=== Warren Hern ===

Warren Hern (born 1938) is an American physician, epidemiologist, and anthropologist.

In Why Are There So Many of Us? Description and Diagnosis of a Planetary Ecopathological Process (1990), Is Human Culture Carcinogenic for Uncontrolled Population Growth and Ecological Destruction? (1993), and Has the Human Species Become a Cancer on the Planet? (1993), Hern developed the comparison between humanity and cancer in detail.

He identified characteristics such as uncontrolled proliferation, invasion and destruction of surrounding ecosystems, colonization of distant territories comparable to metastasis, and loss of differentiation. [ref: Has the Human Species Become a Cancer on the Planet? A Theoretical View of Population Growth as a Sign of Pathology, Current World Leaders]

Hern argued that the comparison could be regarded as a hypothesis because, in his view, it was open to verification or refutation and could provide a basis for further investigation.

=== James Lovelock ===

James Lovelock (1919–2022) was an English scientist best known for developing the Gaia hypothesis, according to which Earth can be described as a self-regulating system.

In Healing Gaia: Practical Medicine for the Planet (1991), Lovelock described human beings as organisms that, in some respects, behave like pathogenic microorganisms or tumor cells within Gaia. The comparison formed part of his broader concept of “planetary medicine”. [ref: Healing Gaia: Practical Medicine for the Planet, Harmony Books]

MacDougall later observed that Lovelock had previously rejected a direct identification of humanity with a tumor in The Ages of Gaia (1988), making his later formulation a qualified rather than literal use of the comparison.

=== Frank Forencich ===

Frank Forencich is an American writer and educator with a background in human biology.

In Homo Carcinomicus: A Look at Planetary Oncology (1992), he explored parallels between neoplastic growth and human demographic and cultural expansion. Forencich emphasized the usefulness of the comparison, treating it primarily as a metaphorical framework rather than as a literal identity between humanity and cancer. [ref: Homo Carcinomicus: A Look at Planetary Oncology, The Trumpeter: Journal of Ecosophy]

=== A. Kent MacDougall ===

A. Kent MacDougall (1931–2021) was an American journalist and professor emeritus of journalism at the University of California, Berkeley.

His essay Humans as Cancer, published in Wild Earth in 1996, developed the comparison in detail and partly reconstructed its intellectual history, discussing Gregg, Hern, Forencich, Lewis Mumford, and Lovelock.

MacDougall examined parallels involving population growth, colonization, urban expansion, appropriation of resources, metastasis, and loss of differentiation, while also presenting objections to the model.

=== Daniel Pauly ===

Daniel Pauly (born 1946) is a marine biologist and fisheries scientist known for his studies of human impacts on marine ecosystems.
[truncated]

Draft text:
Fatima Florence Ajimobi (born 5 April 1959) is a Nigerian entrepreneur, philanthropist and diplomat. She served as the First Lady of Oyo State from 2011 to 2019, during the administration of her husband, former Governor Abiola Ajimobi.

Before entering public life, she had established Grandex, which was registered in 1982 with business interests in retail, wholesale distribution and other commercial services. [ref: Life after Power…Florence Ajimobi Completes Multimillion-naira Mall – THISDAYLIVE]She is also the founder of the Access to Basic Medical Care (ABC) Foundation, established in 2011 to improve access to healthcare services. [ref: ISO accredits Ajimobi’s ABC medical laboratory, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

In 2026, she became Nigeria’s Ambassador to Austria and Permanent Representative to international organisations in Vienna.

== Early life and education ==
Florence Ajimobi was born on 5 April 1959 in Benin City, Nigeria, by a Nigerian mum into the Hajaig family of Lebanese ancestry. She grew up in Ibadan, Oyo State, where she attended Our Lady of Apostles Secondary School. [ref: 7 interesting facts about Florence Ajimobi at 60, The Nation Newspaper]

She obtained an Ordinary National Diploma (OND) from The Polytechnic, Ibadan, in 1978.

In 2013, she completed a Strategic Programme for Negotiation and Leadership at Harvard Business School, United States, where she received a certificate. She subsequently obtained a Master of Business Administration (MBA) from the London School of Business and Finance in 2014. [ref: ]

In 2017, she was awarded an honorary Doctor of Science degree in Public Administration by Ajayi Crowther University, Oyo. [ref: Ajimobi’s wife gets honorary doctorate degree, The Nation Newspaper]

== Business career ==
Florence Ajimobi began her professional career in 1979 with Femi Johnson & Company, an insurance brokerage firm. Between 1980 and 1984, she worked with Briscoe Group, Insight Communications and Edison Engineering Company, holding administrative and client service positions. [ref: Why Gov. AJIMOBI Does Not Joke With His Wife, FLORENCE, City People Magazine]

In 1984, she moved into full-time entrepreneurship, developing Grandex Group of Companies having registered the business few years earlier. The business expanded into supermarkets, wholesale distribution and warehousing, with operations in Lagos and Ibadan. Grandex later diversified into bakery operations and equipment rentals. [ref: Ex-Oyo First Lady, Florence Ajimobi, expands business, The Sun Nigeria]

== Philanthropy and healthcare ==
In 2011, Florence Ajimobi established the Access to Basic Medical Care (ABC) Foundation to improve access to healthcare services, particularly for people in underserved communities. The foundation’s activities include cancer awareness, medical screening, diagnostic services and community health outreach programmes. [ref: ISO accredits Ajimobi’s ABC medical laboratory, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

In February 2013, the Florence Ajimobi Alaanu House was inaugurated at the University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan, to provide accommodation for relatives of patients receiving treatment at the hospital. [ref: Ajimobi urges Nigerians to give back to society, The Nation Newspaper]

The ABC Foundation also operates a medical diagnostic laboratory. In July 2021, The Guardian reported that the laboratory had received ISO accreditation. [ref: ISO accredits Ajimobi’s ABC medical laboratory, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

== First Lady of Oyo State ==
Florence Ajimobi served as First Lady of Oyo State from 2011 to 2019. During this period, she established the Oyo State Officials’ Wives Association (OYSOWA), through which she organised programmes focused on women’s development and empowerment. [ref: 12 govs’ wives, others for women summit in Ibadan, Punch Newspapers]

One of the association’s major activities was the annual National Women’s Summit, which brought together women from different backgrounds to discuss leadership, economic opportunities and social development. [ref: 12 govs’ wives, others for women summit in Ibadan, Punch Newspapers]

The 2017 summit reportedly attracted over 1,000 participants, including former Zimbabwean Vice President Joice Mujuru and former Liberian First Lady Jewel Howard-Taylor. [ref: Women seek more opportunities to serve Nigeria, The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News]

== Publications ==
In April 2019, Florence Ajimobi published her memoir, My Life Like a Rainbow. The book covers her childhood, marriage, family life and experiences in public life. A book reading subsequently took place in Ibadan on 18 June 2019. [ref: Learning life’s lessons from ex-governor’s wife, Florence Ajimobi, Tribune Online]

== Diplomatic career ==
In 2026, Florence Ajimobi was appointed Nigeria’s Ambassador to Austria and Permanent Representative to international organisations in Vienna. [ref: Nigerian Ambassador Ajimobi Presents Credentials to Austrian President, Voice of Nigeria]

On 17 August 2026, she presented her credentials to the International Anti-Corruption Academy (IACA) [ref: Ambassador of Nigeria Presents Credentials, www.iaca.int]. On 17 September 2026, she presented her Letters of Credence to Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen.
[truncated]

Draft text:
Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi, T.I. (popularly known as S. N. Haider Naqvi, T.I.) is a Pakistani investigative journalist, political columnist, news analyst, media executive, advertising administrator, telecommunications pioneer, sports administrator, and regulatory official. Widely recognized among Pakistan's top-tier media figures, he is known for breaking high-profile investigative reports and authoring news columns on state governance, national political developments, defense affairs, media regulation, and cricket administration.

He serves as an official Executive Member of the Authority at the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) representing Sindh, as well as a regular senior analyst on flagship political talk shows across Pakistan's premier news networks, including Geo News and ARY News (notably as a panelist on The Reporters). He is the founder and CEO of the advertising, PR, and media agency CLICKCOM, previously served as the Chief Executive Officer of the Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchise Multan Sultans during its inaugural season, is the CEO and founder of Urdu news network StarNews Pakistan, was the founder and CEO of satellite network TV2Day, led network infrastructure modernization during Pakistan's 3G/4G telecom transformation, and currently serves as the Chief Executive Officer of the international satellite channel Ocean News UK. In 2024, he was conferred the Tamgha-e-Imtiaz (Medal of Excellence) by the President of Pakistan for his contributions to journalism.

== Early life and education ==
Naqvi is the son of **Syed Shabbir Hussain Naqvi** (1937–2013), a well-known Pakistani social worker and philanthropist noted for his extensive contributions to community welfare, humanitarian projects, and social relief initiatives across the country. Following his passing in June 2013, official state condolence messages were issued by top national leadership—including President of Pakistan Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, PTI Chairman Imran Khan, Chairman Senate Nayyar Bukhari, and Speaker National Assembly Sardar Ayaz Sadiq—acknowledging his distinguished social services and extending condolences to Haider Naqvi and the bereaved family.

Naqvi earned his Bachelor of Engineering degree from the prestigious NED University of Engineering and Technology in Karachi. During his university years, he was a prominent student leader, serving as President of the NED student body during his tenure. Demonstrating leadership and technical distinction during his academic career, he later leveraged his engineering and administrative background to lead major telecommunications infrastructure projects, corporate media management, advertising, sports governance, broadcast journalism, media entrepreneurship, and public media regulation.

== Career ==

=== Advertising, PR, & CLICKCOM ===
Naqvi expanded his corporate operations into strategic communications and media representation by founding **CLICKCOM**, a full-service advertising, public relations (PR), and media agency. As CEO of CLICKCOM, he led corporate branding, strategic media buying, nation-wide advertising campaigns, and corporate PR strategies for various public and private sector clients in Pakistan and abroad.

=== Media entrepreneurship, StarNews Pakistan & TV2Day ===
In the mid-2000s, during the expansion of private electronic media in Pakistan, Naqvi established **TV2Day**, an independent satellite television network headquartered in Karachi. Upon launching the channel, he gained widespread national attention as one of the country's youngest television network owners and CEOs.

During his tenure as head of TV2Day in 2006, Naqvi was invited to an official meeting by the then President of Pakistan, General Pervez Musharraf, to discuss electronic media expansion, broadcasting policy, and national current affairs.

Expanding his media network, Naqvi founded and serves as CEO of **StarNews Pakistan**, an Urdu-language news organization that developed into one of Pakistan's widely followed digital and broadcast current affairs outlets. Under his leadership, StarNews Pakistan focuses on breaking political coverage, investigative reporting, regional news, and current affairs analysis.

=== National initiatives & "I'M Pakistan" Conference ===
Naqvi organized the national **"I'M Pakistan" Conference**, a public recognition platform designed to honor citizens, public figures, and veterans who rendered distinguished services to Pakistan. The conference was attended by national leadership, with the then Prime Minister of Pakistan, Yousuf Raza Gillani, presiding as the Chief Guest to present honors and recognize the contributions of key national achievers.

=== Digital media presence, political engagement, & Indian media censorship ===
Naqvi maintains a significant digital presence on X (formerly Twitter), where his reporting and analytical commentary on national policy, constitutional matters, and governance regularly reach key decision-makers. His social media posts and exclusive news breaks are frequently reshared, cited, or endorsed by top state leadership and prominent politicians, including the Prime Minister of Pakistan, the President of Pakistan, Chief Minister of Punjab Maryam Nawaz, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, and Sindh provincial minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah.
[truncated]

Draft: Nidesh Lawtoo

Draft text:
Nidesh Lawtoo (born 1976) is a philosopher and literary theorist. He is professor of Modern and Contemporary European Literature and Culture at Leiden University. His work focuses on theories of mimesis (imitation) in philosophy, literature, political theory and media studies. From 2016 to 2022 he led the European Research Council–funded project Homo Mimeticus: Theory and Criticism.

== Early life and education ==
Lawtoo was born in 1976 in Bellinzona and raised in Italian-speaking Switzerland, to a Swiss mother and a father from Mauritius. He grew up in San Vittore, in the Mesolcina valley. He studied at the University of Lausanne, where, as he later described it, he was trained at the crossroads of literary studies, philosophy and the social sciences. He received a PhD in Comparative Literature and Critical Theory from the University of Washington in 2009; his dissertation was titled "The Phantom of the Ego: Mimesis and Subjectivity in Nietzsche, Conrad, Lawrence, and Bataille".

== Academic career ==
Lawtoo was maître assistant at the University of Lausanne (2009–2013), a visiting scholar at the Humanities Center of Johns Hopkins University with a Swiss National Science Foundation fellowship (2013–2016), and assistant professor at the University of Bern (2016–2017), before joining KU Leuven. At KU Leuven he was an assistant professor of philosophy and English

From 2016 to 2022 he was principal investigator of Homo Mimeticus: Theory and Criticism (HOM), a project funded by an ERC Starting Grant (grant agreement 716181) and hosted by KU Leuven; it ran from 1 November 2016 to 30 April 2022. In 2023 he became professor at Leiden University, where he gave his inaugural lecture, "Dodo Through the Looking-Glass: A Mirror for Modern and Contemporary Culture", on 14 November 2025.

== Research ==
Lawtoo's areas of specialization include modernism, critical theory, postcolonial literature, film studies and continental philosophy, with a focus on theories of mimesis, imitation and simulation. He promotes a transdisciplinary field that he calls "mimetic studies". He has described his first major book, The Phantom of the Ego, as a Nietzschean alternative to René Girard's mimetic theory. His books engage with thinkers including Plato, Friedrich Nietzsche, Gustave Le Bon, Sigmund Freud, Georges Bataille, Girard, Philippe Lacoue-Labarthe and Jean-Luc Nancy.

=== The Phantom of the Ego (2013) ===
The Phantom of the Ego: Modernism and the Mimetic Unconscious (Michigan State University Press) argues that the modernist account of the unconscious anticipates contemporary findings on the role of mimesis in the formation of subjectivity. Rather than starting from Freud, it begins with Nietzsche and reads Joseph Conrad, D. H. Lawrence and Georges Bataille.

Reviewing the book in Modern Language Quarterly, Kurt Koenigsberger praised its reconstruction of a hidden history of the mimetic unconscious, but criticized its loose and shifting definition of modernism.

=== Conrad studies ===
Lawtoo edited Conrad's Heart of Darkness and Contemporary Thought (Bloomsbury, 2012). In Conrad's Shadow: Catastrophe, Mimesis, Theory (2016) he reads Conrad's novels, and postcolonial and cinematic works that respond to them, through the two sides of mimesis, one pathological and one therapeutic. The book shared first place in the Joseph Conrad Society of America's Adam Gillon Book Award in Conrad Studies for 2018, with Andrew Francis's Culture and Commerce in Conrad's Asian Fiction. Reviewing it in The Conradian, Yael Levin called it an important contribution to Conrad studies and praised the originality of both its theoretical paradigms and its method of presentation, while noting a tendency to treat Conrad's fiction as a point of departure for reflecting on mimesis rather than a destination.

=== Political theory ===
In (New) Fascism: Contagion, Community, Myth (2019), with a foreword by Mikkel Borch-Jacobsen, Lawtoo applies mimetic theory to authoritarian leaders and new media, taking Donald Trump as a case study. Reviewing it in L'Esprit Créateur, Bruno Chaouat called it a compelling reminder of the continued relevance of continental philosophy, sociology and psychoanalysis, while noting that the far right may imitate fascism more than embody it.

=== Violence and the unconscious ===
In two volumes published in 2023 by Michigan State University Press, Violence and the Oedipal Unconscious (subtitled The Catharsis Hypothesis) and Violence and the Mimetic Unconscious (subtitled The Affective Hypothesis), Lawtoo traces the history of the "catharsis" hypothesis and of theories of an affective, mimetic unconscious, and relates them to representations of media violence.

=== Homo Mimeticus series ===
Homo Mimeticus: A New Theory of Imitation (Leuven University Press, 2022; open access) proposes a theory of mimesis across philosophy, aesthetics and politics, and closes with a dialogue with Edgar Morin. Philipp Wolf, reviewing it in the Journal of Modern Literature, described it as a transdisciplinary study drawing on philosophy, psychology, the arts, politics and neuroscience, and singled out its attempt at a new and systematic theory of mimesis.
[truncated]

= The Missing Workflow =
The Missing Workflow (T/M/W or TMW) is an independent software development project founded by Italian 3D artist and technical director Danilo Caliro. It focuses on developing add-ons and workflow tools for Blender®, an open-source 3D creation application. [ref: LinkedIn, LinkedIn]

== Background ==
The Missing Workflow develops utilities intended to extend existing digital content creation tools. Its areas of development include look development, shading, lighting, UV mapping and texture color management. [ref: LinkedIn, LinkedIn]

The project focuses on integrating additional production tools within Blender®, including operations commonly associated with professional digital content creation workflows. [ref: LinkedIn, LinkedIn]

== Software ==

=== Emission Pro ===
Emission Pro is a shader-based add-on for Blender® designed for use with the Cycles rendering engine. [ref: Emission Pro — For Blender® 5.2+ and Cycles, Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

It provides controls for emissive materials, including light contribution, color variation, volumetric effects and artistic lighting adjustments. [ref: Emission Pro — For Blender® 5.2+ and Cycles, Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

The software includes configurations for general emissive surfaces, LED-style materials and electronic displays. [ref: Emission Pro — For Blender® 5.2+ and Cycles, Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

=== Color Space Converter ===
Color Space Converter is a Blender® utility for auto-assigning texture color spaces. [ref: Color Space Converter — For Blender® 4.2+, Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

It identifies texture naming conventions and uses the available OpenColorIO configuration to determine color-space assignments for different texture types. [ref: Color Space Converter — For Blender® 4.2+, Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

=== UV Edit Pro ===
UV Edit Pro is a UV editing add-on for Blender®.

It provides tools for UV projection, selection, cutting and sewing, unwrapping, transformation, texel density management and layout. [ref: UV Edit Pro — For Blender® 4.5+ and 5.0+, Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

The add-on incorporates shell-oriented editing operations, viewport overlays and interactive editing tools intended to support manual UV editing. [ref: UV Edit Pro — For Blender® 4.5+ and 5.0+, Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

== Development and distribution ==
The Missing Workflow develops and distributes its software independently through digital marketplaces, including Superhive and Gumroad. [ref: Superhive (formerly Blender Market), Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

Technical documentation and video tutorials accompany its software releases. [ref: Superhive (formerly Blender Market), Superhive (formerly Blender Market)]

Natalya Kusch (also known as Natalya Fichtenbaum-Kusch, Natalie Kusch and Natasha Kush) is a Ukrainian ballet dancer and ballet teacher. [ref: Audition Artistic Directors March 2024, BalletStage Listed as Natalya Fichtenbaum-Kusch.] [ref: Vorstellungen mit Natalie Kusch, Vienna State Opera performance archive] [ref: Von der Primaballerina in Oberwölbling, ORF Niederösterreich] She has worked as a soloist with the Vienna State Ballet, a principal dancer with Queensland Ballet, and a senior artist with the Australian Ballet. [ref: Der Körper ist mein Instrument!, Die Niederösterreicherin] [ref: Annual Report 2014, Queensland Ballet "The Company" section, PDF page 14.] [ref: Annual Report 2015, The Australian Ballet "Directors, Artists and Employment Statistics" section.]

== Biography ==

=== Training and Vienna State Ballet ===
Kusch was born in Nikopol, Ukraine. She trained in Dnipro and continued her studies at the ballet conservatory in St. Pölten under Shida Mubaryakova. Before her engagement in Vienna, she worked at the opera and ballet theatre in Dnipropetrovsk and at theatres in Magdeburg and Cairo. [ref: Natalia Kush, Odesa National Academic Opera and Ballet Theater]

From 2005 to 2013, she danced with the ballet company of the Vienna State Opera and the Vienna State Ballet. She was promoted to soloist under Manuel Legris. On 26 June 2011, she performed the title role in Giselle at the Vienna State Opera. [ref: Gisela / Giselle oder Die Wilis / Willis am 26.06.2011, Vienna State Opera performance archive] The opera's performance archive lists 131 performances under the name Natalie Kusch between 2006 and 2013. [ref: Personenverzeichnis: Kusch, Natalie, Vienna State Opera performance archive Entry lists 131 performances from 25 December 2006 to 3 March 2013.] She also appeared in the filmed ballet sequences for the Vienna Philharmonic's 2011 New Year's Concert. [ref: Neujahrskonzert: Premiere für Schloss Laudon, ORF Wien]

=== Australia and international guest appearances ===
In 2013, Kusch joined Queensland Ballet in Brisbane as a principal dancer at the invitation of Li Cunxin. In 2014, she danced Juliet in Kenneth MacMillan's Romeo and Juliet, opposite Steven McRae. [ref: Queensland Ballet: Romeo and Juliet, Dance Australia] In 2015, she joined the Australian Ballet as a senior artist. [ref: Kusch joins the AB; Cubans come to Brisbane, FollowSpot] In March of that year, she performed the title role in Maina Gielgud's production of Giselle in Melbourne, partnered by Chengwu Guo as Albrecht. [ref: Australian Ballet – Giselle – Melbourne, DanceTabs]

In 2017, she appeared as a guest artist with the Royal New Zealand Ballet in the title role of Roland Petit's Carmen. [ref: Carmen. Royal New Zealand Ballet, Michelle Potter … on dancing] In September of the same year, she performed Carmen at the Teatro dell'Opera di Roma. [ref: Carmen 2016-17 Soirée Roland Petit, Archivio Storico del Teatro dell'Opera di Roma Cast and performances from 8 to 14 September 2017.] In 2018, she performed a duet from the ballet with Michele Satriano at the Benois de la Danse festival on the historic stage of the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow. [ref: Под сенью Петипа, Музыкальная жизнь]

Her other engagements included Universal Ballet in Seoul and, from 2019, the ballet company of the State Theatre in Košice. In 2020, she joined the opera and ballet theatre in Odesa. [ref: Natalya Kusch, Attitude Ballet Studios Vienna] In 2023, she danced Aurora in The Sleeping Beauty on an Australian and New Zealand tour with the Royal Czech Ballet. [ref: Kusch returns with the Royal Czech Ballet, Dance Australia]

=== Teaching ===
Following the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Kusch left the country in 2022 and moved to Munich, where she taught at the Munich International Ballet School. She returned to Austria in 2023. She works as a coach with Europaballett St. Pölten, where she coached the principal roles in a 2024 production of Swan Lake. [ref: Team, Europaballett St. Pölten "Trainer und Lehrer" section.]

=== Personal life ===
On 27 June 2023, Kusch married Thomas Fichtenbaum.

Ettore Guizzardi (Budrio, 1881 – Budrio,}}

Ettore Guizzardi (Budrio, 1881 – Budrio, 23 November 1963) was an Italian racing driver, famous for taking part in the 1907 Peking to Paris race, driving Prince Scipione Borghese's as chauffeur and mechanic.

==Biography==
Ettore Guizzardi was passionate about mechanics from childhood. He often accompanied his father Enrico, an engine driver on the newly emerging railways, on his locomotive journeys, whenever his work as a blacksmith's apprentice allowed. In 1897 the train driven by his father derailed near the villa of the Borghese princes at Albano Laziale. Farmers and servants rushed to help, but nothing could be done for Enrico. They found the young Ettore stunned by the impact and injured, and cared for him. Once recovered, he was hired as a chauffeur, looking after a six-horsepower car and later becoming responsible for the family's entire fleet.

Having noticed his skill and his passion for motoring and mechanics, Prince sent him to Fiat so that he could study internal combustion engines at close quarters, and then to the Ansaldo works in Genoa to complete his training. As he was by now the prince's trusted chauffeur, the prince invited him to accompany him on the famous 1907 Peking to Paris race, for which he had entered an Itala 35/45 HP. The crew was completed by the well-known journalist Luigi Barzini, special correspondent for Corriere della Sera and the English newspaper The Daily Telegraph.

After countless adventures, many of them overcome thanks to the expertise and ability of Guizzardi at the wheel of the Itala, the Italian team won, reaching Paris on 10 August 1907, exactly two months after leaving Peking and twenty days ahead of the runners-up. The crew of in their Spyker reached Paris only on 30 August, while the other two French De Dion-Bouton cars fell so far behind that their arrival is not even recorded. The extraordinary nature of the feat brought the Italian crew and their skilled driver and mechanic to the attention of the press of the day, and it was recalled during the centenary celebrations in 2007.

Later, to put his skills at the service of his country, Guizzardi volunteered as an army driver () in World War I, and in World War II he reached the rank of captain. He died at the age of 82.

==The Peking to Paris race==
In 1907 the French newspaper Le Matin announced the Peking to Paris motor race, with the aim of demonstrating the validity of the automobile as a means of travel even over great distances, capable of competing with trains and ocean liners. The only Italian participant was Prince Scipione Borghese, who entered an Itala 35/45 HP driven by his trusted chauffeur Guizzardi. Corriere della Sera agreed with the prince that Luigi Barzini, by then an established war correspondent, would join the crew to document events through his reports.

The start was set for 10 June at 8 am. Of the many entrants, only five cars actually presented themselves in Peking, and from the first day the Italian crew stood out for its technical and organisational superiority. Borghese's preparation had been meticulous, and some of his ideas made the difference: replacing the car's mudguards with planks to use as ramps in mud and other obstacles, and fitting front and rear tyres of the same size (unlike the cars of the era) so that they were interchangeable and fewer spares were needed. Together with the timely distribution of supplies along the route, these made the difference.

The Itala crossed harsh and remote regions of China, Mongolia, Siberia and Russia, where local people had never seen a car before, overcoming bogging in sand, river fords, breakdowns and going off the road. Guizzardi's expertise was often needed, along with the labour of local peasants, who watched the three Italians and their singular vehicle with curiosity, looking for where the horse was hidden. Barzini sent his dispatches whenever he found a telegraph station, and the articles published in Corriere della Sera and The Daily Telegraph created great anticipation among European readers, who were eager to learn how the competitors were progressing and above all how they solved their daily problems, which gave the event great fame.

The arrival in Paris was a true triumph. On returning to Italy, Barzini wrote the celebrated account ("Half the World Seen from a Car: From Peking to Paris in Sixty Days"), published in 1908 simultaneously in eleven languages by Ulrico Hoepli. It makes clear that the mechanic Guizzardi was the most important member of the Italian team, since without his thorough technical skills and great capacity for improvisation in the face of the many mechanical failures, the Itala would in all likelihood never have reached the finish.

Prince Borghese deserves credit for joining the venture with enthusiasm, financing it, and attending to its operational and logistical details with meticulous determination, and Barzini contributed enormously to its media success through his reports during the journey and then through his book. Yet Guizzardi's technical skill, energy, tenacity and initiative were recognised with admiration and gratitude by his travelling companions as a decisive element in the success of this historic feat. [ref: Preface by Scipione Borghese in La metà del mondo vista da un'automobile. Da Pechino a Parigi in sessanta giorni, Hoepli]

Ryota Kanai () is a Japanese neuroscientist and entrepreneur. He is the founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of Araya Inc., a Tokyo-based artificial intelligence company. Before founding Araya, he was a Reader at the Sackler Centre for Consciousness Science at the University of Sussex.

== Education and early career ==
Kanai graduated in biophysics from the Faculty of Science at Kyoto University in 2000 and received a PhD in experimental psychology from Utrecht University in 2005. He was a postdoctoral fellow at the California Institute of Technology from 2005 to 2007, working with Shinsuke Shimojo on visual experience and time perception. From 2007 to 2012 he was a research associate at the Institute of Cognitive Neuroscience, University College London, and from 2012 to 2015 a Reader at the University of Sussex.

== Research ==
Kanai is known for work linking individual differences in brain structure to variation in human cognition and behaviour, including a widely cited review in Nature Reviews Neuroscience with Geraint Rees. [ref: The structural basis of inter-individual differences in human behaviour and cognition, Nature Reviews Neuroscience]

In 2011, Kanai was the lead author of a study, initiated by the actor Colin Firth while guest-editing BBC Radio 4's Today programme, which reported that in MRI scans of young adults, self-described liberalism was associated with greater grey matter volume in the anterior cingulate cortex and conservatism with a larger right amygdala. [ref: Political orientations are correlated with brain structure in young adults, Current Biology] [ref: Colin Firth: Actor. Writer. Academy Award Winner. Scientist?, Smithsonian] The study attracted media attention, partly because of Firth's involvement, with commentators noting that it could not establish whether brain structure shapes political views or the reverse.

In another 2011 study led by Kanai, brain imaging of 125 university students found that the number of a person's Facebook friends was associated with the size of brain regions linked to social cognition; the results were replicated in a further 40 participants. [ref: Online social network size is reflected in human brain structure, Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences] [ref: Facebook Friend Numbers Linked to Brain Size, [[ABC News (United States)] The study also found a strong correlation between the size of participants' online and offline social networks.

In the 2020s, Kanai has contributed to theoretical and meta-theoretical discussion in consciousness science. In 2024 he co-authored a paper proposing "universality" as a desirable meta-theoretic property for theories of consciousness in Neuroscience of Consciousness. [ref: Toward a universal theory of consciousness, Neuroscience of Consciousness] He is also a co-author of an interdisciplinary report surveying scientific theories and "indicator properties" relevant to assessing consciousness in AI systems. [ref: Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence: Insights from the Science of Consciousness]

== Araya and program leadership ==
In 2015, Kanai left academia to found Araya, which develops AI and brain–machine interface technologies, and has served as its CEO since then. [ref: AI開発のアラヤ・金井良太CEO 好奇心の赴くまま究める, Nihon Keizai Shimbun] [ref: 機械の意識はこう作る、「和製DeepMind」の大志, Nikkei xTECH] In 2020, he was selected as a project manager for Goal 1 of Japan's Moonshot Research and Development Program, run by the Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST), leading a project on extending human physical, cognitive and perceptual abilities. [ref: Goal 1: KANAI Ryota Project, Moonshot R&D (JST)]

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2015, Kanai received the Young Scientists' Prize of the Commendation for Science and Technology by the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT), for research on the relationship between individual differences in brain structure and cognitive mechanisms. [ref: 平成27年度 科学技術分野の文部科学大臣表彰 若手科学者賞 受賞者一覧, Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology] In 2021, he received the 7th World OMOSIROI Award from Knowledge Capital, Osaka. [ref: World OMOSIROI Award 第7回受賞者 金井良太, Knowledge Capital]

== Selected works ==
* Kanai, R.; Rees, G. (2011). "The structural basis of inter-individual differences in human behaviour and cognition". Nature Reviews Neuroscience. 12 (4): 231–242..
* Kanai, R.; Feilden, T.; Firth, C.; Rees, G. (2011). "Political orientations are correlated with brain structure in young adults". Current Biology. 21 (8): 677–680..
* Kanai, R.; Fujisawa, I. (2024). "Toward a universal theory of consciousness". Neuroscience of Consciousness. 2024 (1): niae022..
* Kanai, R. (2023). AIに意識は生まれるか [Can AI become conscious?] (in Japanese). East Press..
