Jacomax is a Hong Kong-based Italian pizza brand founded in 2011 by Italian entrepreneur and content creator Jacopo Contiero and his partner Max. [ref: JACOMAX上環店月底結業 20萬租金僅肯減數千 店主：祝業主好運, HK01] The brand is known for its stone-baked thin-crust pizzas and localized recipes, most notably its signature Blue Cheese and Apple Pizza, which has received coverage from local food media. [ref: Jacomax Pizzeria驚喜重返銅鑼灣！必試全港獨家椰子號沙嗲醬Pizza 藍芝士蘋果薄餅, U Food]

== History ==
Jacomax opened its first restaurant on Wing Lok Street in Sheung Wan in 2011. Over the following decade, the business expanded to four dine-in branches across Hong Kong, including locations in Causeway Bay, Tsim Sha Tsui, and Tseung Kwan O. [ref: JACOMAX上環店開業14年宣佈結業！1理由或連執兩間 Youtuber老闆發文告急：呢個時勢真係無辦法, Sing Tao Headline]

In mid-2025, amid high commercial rents and economic pressures in the Hong Kong food and beverage sector, Jacomax downsized its brick-and-mortar footprint. The flagship Sheung Wan store closed on June 30, 2025, after 14 years of operation following unsuccessful lease negotiations over its $200,000 HKD monthly rent. Its Causeway Bay branch also closed in October 2025 after receiving an abrupt eviction notice from the landlord. [ref: Jacomax銅鑼灣店結業！業主通知要清場即走0交接期極錯愕, U Food] The brand subsequently secured a new location and returned to Causeway Bay in early 2026.

In April 2026, the company entered the retail packaged food market, distributing four varieties of frozen pizzas—including its signature blue cheese and apple flavor—through Yata supermarkets across Hong Kong. [ref: Jacomax推出4款急凍Pizza！全線一田百貨發售名物藍芝士蘋果薄餅, Weekend Weekly]

== Founder and media presence ==
In 2024, founder Jacopo Contiero launched a Cantonese-language YouTube channel, Jacopo Only Friends, documenting local culinary experiences and cultural topics in Hong Kong. The channel gained regional online viewership, helping sustain public interest in the Jacomax brand during the closure of its physical stores.

EZ Newswire is an American press release distribution and media technology company headquartered in the SoHo neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. Founded in 2022 by Neel Shah, the company provides a web-based platform for creating, distributing, publishing, and monitoring corporate announcements. [ref: EZ Newswire – Products, Competitors, Financials, Employees, Headquarters Locations, CB Insights] [ref: Reuters Signs News Distribution Deal With EZ Newswire, MediaPost]

EZ Newswire has entered into exclusive multi-year press release distribution agreements with Reuters and Fortune for their dedicated press release publication channels. The company also distributes announcements to other media destinations, including AP News, Yahoo Finance, USA Today, Business Insider, and regional news websites. [ref: EZ Newswire Signs Exclusive Distribution Deal with Reuters, EZ Newswire] [ref: EZ Newswire announces exclusive multi-year deal with Fortune, LinkedIn] [ref: EZ Newswire, EZ Newswire]

The company incorporates artificial intelligence into press release preparation, editorial workflows, and performance analytics. Its reporting platform measures distribution results, readership, search engine visibility, and references to published announcements in AI-generated answers. [ref: About EZ Newswire, EZ Newswire]

== History ==

=== Founding and early development ===

EZ Newswire was founded in 2022 by Neel Shah and launched its public beta in May 2023. The company was established to provide a technology-based alternative to traditional press release distribution services, combining digital publishing, distribution, and analytics in a single platform.

In October 2023, the company announced a press release distribution partnership with Big Technology, a technology-focused publication founded by journalist Alex Kantrowitz. [ref: EZ Newswire Inks Industry's First Exclusive Substack Distribution Deal with Big Technology Partnership, EZ Newswire]

In April 2024, EZ Newswire was selected as a winner of The MBA Fund's sixth annual pitch competition for early-stage startups. The company has identified The MBA Fund, Contour Ventures, and HearstLab among its investors.

=== Reuters partnership ===

On September 16, 2024, EZ Newswire announced an exclusive multi-year press release distribution agreement with Reuters, the international news agency. The agreement established a direct publishing arrangement enabling organizations to distribute business announcements to a dedicated section of Reuters.com through the EZ Newswire platform.

The partnership was reported by MediaPost on September 17, 2024. The publication described the agreement as a multi-year arrangement under which EZ Newswire customers could publish corporate news to a dedicated section of the Reuters website.

According to EZ Newswire, its agreement provides exclusive newswire distribution access to the dedicated Reuters.com press release channel. As of October 2026, the company states that competing newswire services cannot independently publish to that channel through an equivalent direct distribution agreement. [ref: How to Publish a Press Release on Reuters, EZ Newswire]

The press releases distributed through the service are separate from Reuters' independently reported editorial news coverage.

=== Fortune partnership ===

In December 2025, EZ Newswire announced an exclusive multi-year distribution agreement with Fortune, the American business publication.

The partnership established an integrated publishing channel enabling businesses and organizations to distribute press releases to a dedicated section of Fortune.com. According to EZ Newswire, the agreement made it Fortune's exclusive newswire distribution partner for the channel.

The integration allows organizations to submit announcements through EZ Newswire for publication on Fortune.com, subject to applicable content requirements. [ref: Press Release Distribution Pricing, EZ Newswire]

As of October 2026, EZ Newswire identifies Reuters.com and Fortune.com as its two exclusive premium newswire distribution destinations. The arrangements concern dedicated press release publication channels rather than independently produced Reuters or Fortune editorial journalism.

=== Expansion of technology and services ===

During 2025 and 2026, EZ Newswire expanded its platform to incorporate additional automation, publisher integrations, and analytics capabilities.

In 2026, the company introduced reporting capabilities designed to monitor distributed press releases across publisher websites, search engines, and AI-powered information services. [ref: EZ Newswire Launches Press Release Performance Reports With AI Visibility Tracking, Fortune]

In 2026, the company also introduced collaborative workspaces for organizations and public relations agencies, allowing multiple users to manage press releases under shared organizational accounts. [ref: EZ Newswire Launches Workspaces to Streamline Multi-User Collaboration and Account Management, Fortune]

== Products and services ==

=== Press release distribution ===

EZ Newswire operates a self-service digital platform for creating, reviewing, scheduling, and distributing press releases.

Haitham bin Shunayf bin Raddad Al-Jadaani (; 1979 – 22 April 2011) was a Saudi Quran reciter, imam, and khatib from Jeddah. He was known for his murattal recitation in the Hafs 'an Asim narration and for holding ijazahs in a number of Quranic readings. [ref: هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, midad.com] [ref: الترجمة الشخصية للشيخ هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, ar.islamway.net]

== Biography ==
Al-Jadaani was born in Jeddah on 8 Rajab 1399 AH (1979). He completed his primary, intermediate, and secondary education in the city, then studied at the Qassim branch of Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University, graduating from it. [ref: القارئ الشيخ هيثم الجدعاني رحمه الله, haithamaljadani.com] He married twice and had five children.

== Education and ijazahs ==
He began memorising the Quran in the Quranic study circles of Jeddah as a child under Sheikh Muhammad Bafil and a group of students of knowledge, until he was granted an ijazah in it. He then travelled to the Qassim region in pursuit of knowledge, where he attended the lessons of Sheikh Muhammad ibn Salih al-Uthaymeen, and after al-Uthaymeen's death he continued studying with his students.

He travelled outside Saudi Arabia to receive the Quran from those proficient in its narrations, obtaining ijazahs in several readings, including Hafs 'an Asim, Shu'bah 'an Asim, Al-Bazzi and Qunbul from Ibn Kathir, and Qalun from Nafi'.

== Career ==
He served as imam and khatib of Noor Al-Rahman Mosque in the Al-Salamah district of Jeddah until his death. He was already listed among the well-known reciters of Jeddah several years before his death. [ref: المساجد التي سيؤم بها قراء العالم الإسلامي هذا العام, mazameer.com]

== Recitations ==
Al-Jadaani recorded the complete murattal Quran in the Hafs 'an Asim narration, and also recorded recitations in the Al-Bazzi 'an Ibn Kathir narration as well as recordings of the tarawih and tahajjud prayers. [ref: مصاحف هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, midad.com] His recitations remain available on a number of Quran audio platforms and download archives. [ref: تلاوات القارئ هيثم الجدعاني, audio.islamweb.net] [ref: هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني: تلاوات القرآن الكريم بصوته, ar.assabile.com] [ref: القارئ هيثم الجدعاني, tahaquran.com]

== Death ==
On Friday 22 April 2011, Al-Jadaani drowned in the sea near the shore of Dhahban, north of Jeddah, during a family outing on a boat. When his nine-year-old nephew Abdulaziz fell from the boat, his father Abdulrahim and his uncle Haitham entered the water to rescue him; the boat's captain succeeded in saving the child, but the two brothers drowned. [ref: وفاة الشيخ هيثم الجدعاني إمام وخطيب جامع نور الرحمن بجدة, dd-sunnah.net]

The funeral prayer was offered for the two brothers after the Fajr prayer on Saturday 23 April 2011 at Al-Thunayan Mosque in Jeddah, and they were buried in the Dhahban cemetery.

== Legacy ==
After his death, Saudi Arabia's Quran Radio broadcast selections of his recitations, and his recordings continued to circulate among listeners. Several Quran audio platforms have kept his complete murattal recitation available for streaming and download.

His public statements have addressed online impersonation, account security, fraudulent links, and the misuse of artificial intelligence to create manipulated images and videos.

Marco Zappone, né en 1966 à Rome [ref: Marco Zappone, Les Rencontres d'Arles], en Italie, est un auteur [ref: Zappone] éditeur [ref: Champs de bataille, Éditions Photosynthèses] franco-italien installé à Arles, en Provence, depuis 1998.

=== Biographie ===
Après une enfance passée entre la France, l’Italie, l’Afrique et le Moyen-Orient, [ref: Marco Zappone, Les Rencontres d'Arles] il étudie l’anthropologie et le cinéma à l’université La Sapienza de Rome et à l’École des hautes études en sciences sociales (EHESS), à Paris. Après plusieurs années consacrées à la bibliophilie et au collectionnisme, il fonde la maison d’édition Photosynthèses, spécialisée dans la publication de beaux livres, ainsi que de textes et d’essais sur la photographie et les arts visuels [ref: ]. Rattachée au groupe Libella, la maison d’édition est située au 12, rue Vernon, à Arles [ref: ].

Bien qu’il ait envisagé dès son plus jeune âge de faire de la photographie son métier, cette passion devient finalement le fil conducteur du projet éditorial de la maison. Il participe notamment à la réalisation, avec Yan Morvan, de Champs de bataille, [ref: Yan Morvan: entretien avec Marco Zappone, L'Œil de la Photographie Magazine] un ouvrage consacré aux paysages de champs de bataille à travers le monde. L’ouvrage reçoit le Grand Prix du jury de la Nuit du livre en 2016 [ref: La Nuit du livre 2016 dévoile ses 13 lauréats, Livres Hebdo]. Après une tentative infructueuse de reconversion dans la tauromachie, passion qui l’anime toujours, Marco Zappone met fin à ses activités au sein des éditions Photosynthèses en 2023. Il est père de deux enfants, Niccolò et Giulietta.

Draft text:
Stanisław Jabłonowski of the Prus III coat of arms (born 10 March 1799, died 15 August 1878 in Kraków) – prince in the Congress Kingdom of Poland in 1820, participant in the November Uprising, pioneer of the oil industry, and knight of the Order of Virtuti Militari.

He was a direct descendant of the hetmans Stanisław Jan Jabłonowski and Paweł Jan Sapieha, and the son of Prince Stanisław Paweł Jabłonowski and Teodora née Walewska. He received his early education abroad, at an aristocratic boarding school in Paris and at Pastor Gerlach’s educational institution in Switzerland. When he finally returned to the country in 1815, he spoke Polish only with difficulty. In 1814, at a ball given by his mother, he was introduced to Emperor Alexander I; the young prince then declared his desire to enter military service. In 1816 he volunteered for an examination, after which he was accepted as a cadet into the positional battery of the mounted artillery of the Guard. Thanks to his background, he was promoted to the rank of second lieutenant after only two years. Having come into conflict with Grand Duke Konstantin Pavlovich, he resigned in 1821.

After the outbreak of the November Uprising he returned to the army. He served in the 4th Battery of Light Horse Artillery. He took part in the skirmish at Miłosna (18 February 1831), the First Battle of Wawer (19 February), and the Battle of Grochów (25 February), for which he received the Golden Cross of the Order of Virtuti Militari on 16 March 1831. He later fought in the Battle of Domanice and the Battle of Iganie (10 April). Immediately after the latter engagement he was promoted to the rank of captain. He took part in the expedition against the imperial guards. On 26 May 1831 he fought in the Battle of Ostrołęka. When the corps of Tomasz Łubieński crossed the Narew, the position of his battery became threatened. Warned of this, he reacted to the proposal of retreat with the words:

“Then I shall remain here alone. For the first time I am commanding a battery; I will not withdraw without an order.”

After Józef Bem assumed command of all Polish artillery, Jabłonowski became his chief of staff. He took part in the fortification of Warsaw and then took command of the 2nd Battery of Light Horse Artillery, which formed part of the Reserve Artillery Corps commanded by Colonel Chorzewski. He participated in the defence of Warsaw, fighting first near the Mokotów tollgates and later near the Jerusalem tollgates.

He is the author of memoirs of his participation in the November Uprising, entitled Recollections of the Positional Battery of the Mounted Artillery of the Royal Polish Guard.

He was a pioneer of the oil industry in Poland. In 1852, in the Empty Forest (Pusty Las) in Siary, he founded the first industrial-scale mine of so-called rock oil (crude oil seeping from the mountains) in the world [citation needed]. Near the palace in Kobylanka he owned an asphalt factory.

He was married twice. His first wife was Maria Gonzaga-Myszkowska-Wielopolska; his second, in 1875 (when he was already 76 years old), was her mother, Wanda née Ossolińska, secundo voto Potocka. He had no children. He is buried at the Rakowicki Cemetery.

Draft text:
The Interior Design Society of Kenya (IDSK) is a professional association representing interior designers, spatial planners, design studios, material suppliers, and allied manufacturers in Kenya. [ref: About Us – Interior Design Society of Kenya (IDSK), Interior Design Society of Kenya] Headquartered in Nairobi, the society advocates for formal industry regulation, professional accreditation, ethical practice, and sustainable interior architecture across residential, commercial, and public sectors in Kenya. [ref: IDSk Supports New Bill With Amendments and Demands Legal Recognition, Jicho News]

== History and Governance ==
The organization was established to serve as a unified voice for practitioners in Kenya's built-environment sector, where interior design had historically operated without a dedicated statutory framework.

IDSK is governed by an executive board led by President Cecilia Nakhungu Mbati. [ref: Architects' alliance opposes bill on regulation of built environment professions, Kenya News Agency] The society engages with national educational bodies, TVET institutions, and universities to ensure academic curricula align with evolving professional standards, spatial safety regulations, accessibility requirements, and building codes. [ref: IDSK Industry Integration Programme, Interior Design Society of Kenya]

== Key Objectives and Programs ==
The society's core mandate includes regulating professional practice, protecting consumers from unqualified operators, and facilitating professional development. Its main initiatives include:

* Industry Integration Programme (IIP): A structured transition and mentorship framework designed to connect interior design graduates and emerging professionals with practical studio experience, site mentorship, and industry network opportunities.
* Workforce Placement Programme: A professional pathway program matching qualified interior designers with employment opportunities across corporate fit-out firms, architectural practices, and design agencies.
* Circular Design and Sustainability: Advocacy initiatives promoting eco-friendly spatial planning, energy efficiency, acoustic design, indoor air quality, biophilic elements, and the sourcing of local timber, stone, and sustainable materials.
* Interior Design Summit: An annual flagship convention uniting design professionals, policy leaders, suppliers, and real estate developers. The 2026 summit took place at the Sarit Expo Centre in Nairobi under the theme "Building the Interior Design Economy." [ref: Interior Design Summit 2026: Building the Interior Design Economy, Interior Design Society of Kenya]

== Legislative Advocacy ==
In 2026, IDSK actively participated in legislative discussions before the National Assembly Committee on Housing, Urban Planning and Public Works regarding the Architectural and Quantity Surveying Practitioners Bill, 2026 (National Assembly Bill No. 47 of 2026), which sought to replace the colonial-era Architects and Quantity Surveyors Act (Cap. 525). [ref: Parliament Seeks Stakeholders’ Views on Bill to Regulate Architects and Quantity Surveyors, KTN News Kenya]

During parliamentary stakeholder submissions, IDSK President Cecilia Mbati expressed general support for statutory regulation while submitting clause-by-clause amendments aimed at safeguarding the independence of interior design practitioners:

1. Title and Scope Expansion: Requesting that the legislation be renamed the Built Environment Practitioners Act to explicitly encompass interior designers, landscape architects, and construction project managers.
2. Regulatory Council Representation: Advocating for dedicated statutory representation for interior designers on the proposed joint regulatory board under Clause 71D.
3. Transitional Grandfathering Provisions: Demanding clear grandfathering mechanisms under Part X (Clause 58) to register existing interior design professionals with over five years of verified experience who had operated legally prior to statutory enactment.
4. Stamping Authority for Fit-Out Documentation: Requesting statutory recognition under Clause 46(1) for technical documents, spatial planning layouts, material specifications, and interior fit-out drawings stamped by registered interior designers.

Rakesh Kumar Mishra, also known as R. K. Mishra, is an Indian politician and retired Indian Police Service (IPS) officer. A member of the 1986 batch of the Bihar cadre, he served in the Bihar Police and several central armed police forces, including the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF), Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP). He was also Director General-cum-Commandant General of Home Guards and Fire Services in Bihar.

Mishra joined the Jan Suraaj movement after retiring from the police service. He contested the 2025 Bihar Legislative Assembly election from Darbhanga as a Jan Suraaj Party candidate.

== Early life and education ==

Mishra is from Saharsa district in Bihar. He studied civil engineering at Banaras Hindu University, where he received a gold medal. According to his election affidavit, he graduated in 1983.

== Police career ==

Mishra joined the Indian Police Service in August 1986 and was assigned to the Bihar cadre.

Among his early postings was Bhagalpur, where he served as an Assistant Superintendent of Police during the communal riots of 1989.

He subsequently held district policing appointments in Bihar and the region that later became Jharkhand, before moving to central police organisations.

=== Central police organisations ===

Mishra served in the CISF in several capacities. In December 2016, his appointment as Additional Director General of the force was reported.

He also served in the CRPF, including as Inspector General of its Jharkhand sector. He was identified in that position in June 2015, when the force was involved in operations against Maoist insurgents in the state.

Mishra later became Additional Director General of the ITBP. The 2019 IPS civil list records his appointment to that position in July 2017.

=== Bihar Police and Home Guards ===

Mishra also held senior positions in the Bihar Police. In October 2012, he was promoted to Additional Director General and assigned responsibility for police modernisation.

After returning from central deputation, he took charge as Director General-cum-Commandant General of Bihar Home Guards and Fire Services on 27 August 2019.

During his tenure, the department announced measures concerning Home Guard personnel, including the processing of retirement benefits and the payment of allowances. In January 2020, Mishra described arrangements for more timely payments and settlement of retirement benefits.

In March 2020, Prabhat Khabar reported that the department had issued 18 standing orders governing service conditions, duty allocation, payments and grievance procedures.

The department was also involved in the deployment of trained Home Guards for the security of Reserve Bank of India currency chests in Bihar.

== Political career ==

Following his retirement, Mishra became associated with the Jan Suraaj movement led by Prashant Kishor.

In May 2023, he was among a group of retired IPS officers who joined the movement at an event in Patna. The Indian Express reported his participation alongside other former police and administrative officers.

Mishra remained associated with Jan Suraaj as it developed into a political party in October 2024.

In October 2025, the party selected him to contest the Darbhanga constituency in the Bihar Legislative Assembly election.

He finished third, receiving 11,758 votes. The seat was won by Sanjay Saraogi of the Bharatiya Janata Party, while Umesh Sahani of the Vikassheel Insaan Party finished second.

== Awards and honours ==

Mishra received the Police Medal for Meritorious Service in 2003, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs' IPS civil list.

He was awarded the President's Police Medal for Distinguished Service on Republic Day in 2010.

Draft: CMoMa

Draft text:
thumb|Schematic distribution of the three cell lines in a cMoMa individual. Cells with variant 1 are violet, cells with variant two are pink and wildtype cells are orange.

Clustered monoallelic mosaicism (abbreviated cMoMa) is a term in the field of human genetics describing a rare form of mosaicism. cMoMa individuals carry two distinct, closely spaced genetic variants (e.g. single nucleotide deletions). Both located on the same parental allele but mutually exclusive on the level of individual sequencing reads. Thus resulting in three distinct cell lines (the two variants and the remaining wildtype allele).

The term, as well as the postulated mechanism, originates from a 2026 publication by the group of Christian Schaaf at the Institute of Human Genetics at Heidelberg University Hospital, in Human Genetics and Genomics Advances (HGG Advances). The team first observed the specific genetic constellation in two monozygotic twins with HNRNPU-associated neurodevelopmental disorder.

== Background ==

=== Recurrent, surprising genotype constellations ===
In diagnostic human genetics, cases have repeatedly been described in which two distinct variants lie conspicuously close to each other on the same gene or allele, even though there was no indication that they shared a common origin (they behave like two independent mutational events). Such spatial proximity is statistically unlikely, although it is difficult to calculate exactly how unlikely.

Examples of such constellations that were retrospectively attributed to the cMoMa pattern can be found in several published case reports:

* WAS gene: two different mutations in a single male germ cell, resulting in a female carrier who was mosaic for two different variants.
* ACVRL1 gene: germline mosaicism with two distinct mutant alleles in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with pulmonary arterial hypertension.
* AHDC1 gene (Xia-Gibbs syndrome): two adjacent mosaic deletions that likewise never occurred together on the same sequencing read.

=== Genetic diagnostics in the Heidelberg twins ===
In the two twins in Heidelberg, two de novo 1-bp deletions (c.1463del, c.1466del; allele fractions ~20–39 %) were identified in the HNRNPU gene. The mosaicism was subsequently confirmed by Sanger sequencing in leukocytes and buccal mucosa. The two variants never occurred together on the same sequencing read, yet according to long-read sequencing both were located on the paternal allele; the maternal allele was wild-type throughout.

The diagnostic workup – whole-genome, long-read and Sanger sequencing as well as the molecular phasing analysis – was carried out largely by Julia Dennig.

== Definition ==

# Two closely adjacent genetic variants in the same gene.
# Located on the same parental allele.
# The variants are mutually exclusive at the read level.

== Proposed mechanism ==
Böhnlein and Maaß weighed two models against each other. Model 1 (two independent mutational events) would have required both deletions to arise independently within the same ±3-bp window before the twins separated – i.e. within roughly the first eight cell divisions; the calculated probability of this was 10⁻⁷ to 10⁻¹⁰, and the model was rejected as unlikely.

Model 2 (favoured) assumes a single mutational event, followed by divergent, error-prone repair on the two sister chromatids: one chromatid acquires deletion A, the other deletion B; after cell division, the two segregate into separate daughter cell lineages. This model explains both the mutual exclusivity and the shared paternal phase with only one mutational event.

== Relevance for genetic counseling ==
It is proposed, that the recurrence risc for parents with a cMoMa child is not elevated above baseline as the proposed mechanism is incompatible with a germline mosaicism.

== References ==

Draft text:
Magdalen College choir is the collegiate chapel choir of Magdalen College, Oxford, a constituent college of the University of Oxford. Established under the college statutes of 1480, it sings services in Magdalen College Chapel and also undertakes concerts and recordings. [ref: The Choir, Magdalen College, Oxford]

The choir is directed by the Informator Choristarum, the historical title of the college's director of music; since 2017 the post has been held by Mark Williams. [ref: People, Magdalen College Choir] Its membership consists of choristers, undergraduate singers known as Academical Clerks, and organ scholars. The choir has appeared at the BBC Proms [ref: Oxford's Magdalen College Choir Admits Girl Choristers for First Time, The Violin Channel] and toured Europe, Japan and the United States. [ref: Magdalen College Choir, Oxford – Biography, AllMusic] The choir is particularly associated with Oxford's annual May Morning celebrations, during which it sings from Magdalen Tower at 6 a.m. on 1 May.

== History ==

=== Foundation and early history ===

The choir was established under the college statutes of 1480, which provided for sixteen boy choristers, eight Academical Clerks and four chaplains. The foundation formed part of the religious and educational establishment of the college, founded by William Waynflete, Bishop of Winchester. Musical direction was entrusted to an Informator Choristarum, a title that remains in use.

The earliest recorded holders of the office included John Clavering, John Hardy, Alexander Bell and Richard Marbrooke, and the early succession also included the composer Richard Davy. In the sixteenth century the office was held by the Tudor composer John Sheppard. Research by Roger Bowers places Sheppard's tenure as one continuous appointment from September 1543 to early 1548, correcting an earlier chronology that divided it into two periods. [ref: John Sheppard (c.1514–1558/59) at Oxford and the Chapel Royal: exculpation and clarification, Early Music]

=== Seventeenth to nineteenth centuries ===

Several composers held the office in the seventeenth century, including Richard Nicolson, Arthur Phillips, Benjamin Rogers and Daniel Purcell. Rogers, appointed in 1665 according to the chapel's commemorative succession board, wrote the Hymnus Eucharisticus that is still sung at May Morning. [ref: Rogers, Benjamin, Dictionary of National Biography, 1885–1900]

In the eighteenth century the post passed from William Hayes to his son Philip Hayes. The nineteenth-century succession included Walter Vicary, Benjamin Blyth, John Stainer (1859), Walter Parratt (1872) and John Varley Roberts (1882).

=== Twentieth and twenty-first centuries ===

Twentieth-century holders of the office included Haldane Campbell Stewart (appointed 1919 and again in 1941, with William McKie in post in between), Philip Taylor, Bernard Rose (1957), John Harper (1981) and Grayston Ives (1991). The college's archives identify Rose's appointment as a change in the status of the post, since the Organist and Informator Choristarum had not previously been a Fellow of the college. [ref: Administration and Chapel Records, Magdalen College Archives] Daniel Hyde was appointed in 2009 and was succeeded by Mark Williams in 2017.

In 2010 the college established the Consort of Voices, a separate ensemble giving female students the opportunity to take part in chapel music. The choir welcomed its first female Academical Clerk in 2020. [ref: Music for May Morning, Opus Arte] In March 2026 the college announced that girls would be admitted as choristers from September 2027, following plans for Magdalen College School to become co-educational; the change was reported by national and student media as ending an all-male chorister tradition dating to the choir's foundation. [ref: Oxford's Magdalen College Choir will admit girl choristers for first time in over 500 years, [[Classic FM (UK)] [ref: Magdalen College Choir to admit girls for first time in 500-year history, [[Cherwell (newspaper)] The number of chorister places is to rise from sixteen to eighteen, with a fully mixed treble line expected by 2031. [ref: Magdalen College Choir to admit girls as choristers, Magdalen College, Oxford]

== Organisation and services ==

The trebles are choristers educated at Magdalen College School. The adult voices are the Academical Clerks, who are undergraduate members of the university, and the organ scholars play for services and accompany the choir.

During university terms the choir sings Evensong at 6 p.m. every day except Monday, together with the Sunday morning Eucharist. Its repertoire ranges from Renaissance polyphony and Anglican church music to contemporary commissions.

=== Recordings and reception ===
The choir has recorded for labels including Harmonia Mundi, Opus Arte and Coro. Gramophone named its 2024 album Voices of Thunder, which marked the installation of the chapel's new organ, an Editor's Choice in January 2025, [ref: Choir of Magdalen College Oxford, Presto Music] and reviewed the 2019 album The Pillar of the Cloud favourably.

Draft: Three-Phase Design Model

Draft text:
The Three-Phase Design Model is an instructional design model for online learning developed by Rob Sims and Deborah Jones in 2002. [ref: Continuous improvement through shared understanding: Reconceptualising instructional design for online learning, Winds of Change in the Sea of Learning: Proceedings of the 19th ASCILITE Conference] The model was developed in response to the limitations of traditional instructional design approaches when applied to online learning environments. Some traditional instructional designs, particularly, those based on a step-by-step process from print-based distance education, offered limited flexibility to change aspects of the course during the delivery. The model offers flexibility in evaluating and improving learning materials, instructional activities and teaching strategies continuously.

The three phases of the model are Functionality, Enhancement and Maintenance. The phases provide direction for the preparation of the course, improvement during delivery and continued maintenance of the online learning environment. At the functionality phase all essential components such as learning materials, instructional activities and technological devices are established to facilitate the beginning of teaching. The Enhancement phase focuses on making improvements during course delivery. This allows for changes to be made after an evaluation is done. The final phase, Maintenance, updates the necessary components for the course after it is taught, making improvements in preparation for future offerings.

The 3PD Model includes collaboration and feedback. Academic staff, instructional designers and technical personnel work together, bringing their different skills and knowledge to the development of the course. Feedback is important in helping to identify areas of the course that need improvement. Information gathered from learners, instructors and development teams can reveal problems with course components such as learning materials, activities and technological resources. [ref: Enhancing Quality in Online Learning: Scaffolding Planning and Design Through Proactive Evaluation, Distance Education]

==Background and Development==

Online learning in higher education was becoming increasingly popular around the time the 3PD Model was developed. The groups involved in creating and delivering course content faced challenges with existing approaches. These challenges included limited time for developing online courses and insufficient consultation between academic staff and development teams. Consequently, some of the resources developed were not completely suitable for the intended teaching and learning activities. Additionally, some of the instructional materials were prepared before they were delivered to students. This posed a problem because it was difficult to introduce changes when needs or problems emerged during the delivery of the course. These challenges highlighted the need for a different approach that would allow interaction, feedback and changes to take place during course delivery.

In 2002, Rod Sims, Graeme Dobbs and Tim Hand published a study examining the planning, design and evaluation of online learning resources. The focal point was the need to consider both educational and technological factors when developing online resources. The authors explained that technology alone was not adequate for the purpose of supporting teaching and learning. The suggestion was to use proactive evaluation, which would embed evaluation into the early stages of planning and designing online learning resources. The aim was not to depend on evaluation only after instructional materials had been developed but instead encourage designers to establish evaluation criteria during planning. The research reflected the wider concerns about instructional design around the same time the 3PD Model was introduced.
==The Three- Phase Model Phases==

===Functionality Phase===

Functionality is the first phase of the 3PD Model. The development team may conduct a preliminary needs analysis to identify what is necessary for the course. Appropriate instructional materials, technological resources, and teaching arrangements are then selected. [ref: E-Learning Development in Higher Education: Maximising Efficiency—Maintaining Quality, ERIC (Education Resources Information Center)] [ref: In search of an Instructional Material Design Model to Support the Implementation of IQF Oriented Curriculum at HEIs, Proceedings of the 1st International Conference on Education Innovation (ICEI 2017)] During this phase, the course is developed as a functional prototype. The essential components of the course must be prepared before teaching begins, leaving further improvements in the other phases. Learners must also be able to access the online course and its learning materials.

Draft: 681 (genre)

Draft text:
681 is the genre of music that consist of exactly vocals and percussion instruments. It combines a capella with minimalist dance music. An example is the song Crabapples by Bruce Peninsula. [ref: Bruce Peninsula climbing the musical ladder, Interrobang]

This is the artificial name of minimalist vocal dance music.

Many main genres have a given artificial name. For example, an artificial name trance is given to usually minimalist ambient rhythmic dance music with tempo between 120 and 150 BPM.

== Etymology ==

The name 681 originates from the list of natural numbers. We have a=1 and skip 2 to get b=3 as the next notable number. The formula of the square of a binomial is (a+b)^2=a^2+2\cdot a\cdot b+b^2. If we square the exponents of b in each addend, we get the addends a^2, 2\cdot a \cdot b and b^4, respectively. The addends are equal to 1, 6 and 81, respectively. The ratio when the second addend is divided by the first addend is 6/1=6, while the ratio when the third addend is divided by the first addend is 81/1=81. Its concatenation gives 681.

Draft text:
Richardson Robertson III, professionally known as Rick Robertson, is an American architect and principal of Robertson Partners Architects. His work encompasses private residences and proposals for large-scale urban development drawing on Neoclassical, Beaux-Arts, and other classical architectural traditions. His projects include the Fleur de Lys estate in Los Angeles and proposed developments in California and New York.

== Career and residential architecture ==
Robertson designed Fleur de Lys, a French-inspired estate in Los Angeles featured in Matt Tyrnauer's 2002 Vanity Fair article "Versailles on the Pacific". [ref: Tyrnauer, Matt. "Versailles on the Pacific." Vanity Fair, April 2002.] The Los Angeles Times also covered the estate and Robertson's work. [ref: "Now Anchored in Hollywood." Los Angeles Times, December 13, 1998.]

Jeff Hyland's The Legendary Estates of Beverly Hills includes a chapter on Fleur de Lys describing its site, architecture, construction, and landscape. [ref: Hyland, Jeff. The Legendary Estates of Beverly Hills. New York: Rizzoli, 2008. Chapter: "Carolwood Drive: Fleur de Lys."] The property was assembled from six adjacent parcels to create a site of approximately five acres.

In 2014, the Los Angeles Times reported that Fleur de Lys had sold for $102 million, identifying Robertson as its architect and quoting his description of the house as a Neoclassical design conceived as a decorative arts museum rather than a traditional French floor plan. [ref: "Westside mansion sells for $102 million, highest Southland price." Los Angeles Times, April 1, 2014.]

In 2013, the Los Angeles Times reported on Robertson's design for a proposed 25,000-square-foot penthouse at the W Hollywood, with four bedrooms, a ballroom, a screening room, a trophy room, a fitness center, and a beauty parlor. [ref: Lelyveld, Nita. "Above it all in Hollywood." Los Angeles Times, May 19, 2013.]

In April 2007, C Magazine published Degen Pener's profile "Classical Artist," examining Robertson's career, architectural philosophy, and use of classical precedents in residential and urban design. [ref: Pener, Degen. "Classical Artist." C Magazine, April 2007.]

Robertson designed a Mediterranean-style house in Tulsa, Oklahoma, for Bobby and Leslie Lorton. Southern Accents featured the residence in its May–June 2007 issue in "Together in Tulsa," discussing its limestone exterior, classical detailing, and the clients' interest in historical architectural accuracy. [ref: "Together in Tulsa." Southern Accents, May–June 2007.]

In January–February 2014, Veranda published "Glamorous Texas Home," featuring a Dallas residence designed by Robertson, with interiors by Beverly Field, text by Nancy Perot, and photography by Max Kim-Bee. [ref: Perot, Nancy. "Glamorous Texas Home." Veranda, January–February 2014.]

The Los Angeles Times featured a French Normandy-style residence designed by Robertson at Lake Arrowhead, California, in 2010. [ref: Marshutz, Scott. "Home of the Week: Chateau on Lake Arrowhead." Los Angeles Times, September 5, 2010.] In 2019, the newspaper identified him as the architect of a Mediterranean-style residence in Los Angeles's Bird Streets neighborhood offered for sale by former motorcycle racer John Kocinski. [ref: Flemming, Jack. "Retired motorcycle racer John Kocinski asks $30 million for Bird Streets abode." Los Angeles Times, January 16, 2019.]

== Urban design and planning ==
In May 2003, Urban Land published Brad Berton's "Northern Gateway" about Las Lomas, a proposed master-planned community in Los Angeles County, identifying Robertson as the project's architect. [ref: Berton, Brad. "Northern Gateway." Urban Land, May 2003, pp. 74–78.]

Robertson developed the Setauket Village Center proposal to redevelop the Route 25A retail district in Setauket, Long Island. [ref: Mastrosimone, Peter C. "A New Vision of Setauket Unveiled: Village center and park could remake Route 25A." The Village Times Herald, October 9, 2003, pp. A1, A13.] In October 2003, The Village Times Herald described his plan to unite three shopping plazas with apartments or condominiums above shops, a village green, gardens, a pond, and an amphitheater. The article characterized the design as a Beaux-Arts reinterpretation of early American architecture incorporating Tudor and shingle-style elements, and quoted Robertson on modern architecture and Long Island's changing development pattern.

In November 2003, Newsday published the editorial "A Model for Revitalizing LI Towns," presenting the proposal's combination of housing above retail space and a community park as a potential model for downtown revitalization. [ref: "A Model for Revitalizing LI Towns." Newsday, November 28, 2003, p. A42.]

In 2006, David Brussat discussed Robertson's proposed downtown Los Angeles residential towers, City House and the Olympic, in The Providence Journal, considering their designs in the context of classical architecture in contemporary American cities. [ref: Brussat, David. "Angeleno inspiration for Providence." The Providence Journal, May 18, 2006, p. B5.]

Draft text:
Alessandro Giannì (born 12 August 1989) is an Italian contemporary artist whose work encompasses painting, sculpture and multimedia art. [ref: Alessandro Giannì, Quadriennale di Roma] [ref: La Cina come ponte visivo tra pittura e AI. Intervista all'artista Alessandro Giannì, Artribune]

== Biography and work ==
As a painter, sculptor and multimedia artist, Giannì works across traditional media and digital forms, exploring the relationships between painting, sculpture, artificial intelligence and new technologies. A central concern of his practice is the image as an element in continual transformation, moving between physical and virtual states. His work also examines the relationship between contemporary images and historical iconography, reinterpreted through technological tools and digital processes. [ref: Le visioni in transizione di Alessandro Giannì sono in mostra a Modena, Artribune]

In 2014, he participated in Ñewpressionism, an exhibition introduced by Miltos Manetas at the Istituto Svizzero in Milan. Other participating artists included Sylvie Fleury, Olivier Mosset, Petra Cortright, Amalia Ulman, Luca Pozzi and Jon Rafman. [ref: Ñewpressionism in Milan, 1,11,111. From screen to nature and back again, Istituto Svizzero] During the 73rd Venice International Film Festival in 2016, he worked as art director on EGH, a project by Enrico Ghezzi and Emiliano Montanari. [ref: Alessandro Giannì, Tang Contemporary Art]

In 2019, Giannì began developing a custom artificial-intelligence system named VASARI, intended to emulate aspects of his creative and compositional process by generating digital sketches that he would subsequently develop into oil paintings. [ref: Lo squarcio: luci e ombre nella pittura di Alessandro Giannì, Balloon Project] [ref: Alessandro Giannì “Due to the Image”, Italian Cultural Institute of New York]

He was among the founders of Spaziomensa in 2020, an independent artist-run cultural space in Rome. [ref: Nuovi artist run space: nasce a Roma spaziomensa, Artribune] [ref: Vera: Roma, 8 spazi, 54 studi, Quodlibet]

In 2021, he presented the solo exhibition Due to the Image at Postmasters Gallery in New York City. It included paintings developed with the aid of VASARI and was accompanied by a publication featuring a critical text by Renato Miracco.

He held his first solo exhibition in Asia in 2023, Breaking Darkness, at Tang Contemporary Art in Bangkok. [ref: Alessandro Giannì: Breaking Darkness, Tang Contemporary Art] In 2024, he participated in The Power of Painting at the ENNOVA Art Museum in Langfang, China, exhibiting alongside artists including Marlene Dumas, Anish Kapoor, Bernard Frize, Christopher Le Brun and Jörg Immendorff. [ref: Alessandro Giannì, Tang Contemporary Art]

In 2025, Giannì held his second solo exhibition in Asia, Multiple Unrealities, at Tang Contemporary Art in Hong Kong. [ref: Alessandro Giannì Solo Exhibition: Multiple Unrealities, Tang Contemporary Art] Later that year, he opened a solo exhibition at Galleria Mazzoli in Modena, founded by gallerist Emilio Mazzoli.

During this period, his work increasingly explored painting as a means of seeing and as a kind of "screen" on which images are generated and reworked through processes combining pictorial language, visual memory and digital systems. The perceptual dimension of images and the use of algorithmic tools became particular areas of interest. [ref: Per Alessandro Giannì, la pittura accade quando l'immagine incontra lo sguardo, Exibart]

In 2026, Giannì presented the solo exhibition Eterno Antico at the Aurora Art Museum in Shanghai. [ref: Mostra “Eterno Antico” di Alessandro Giannì all'Aurora Art Museum di Shanghai, Italian Cultural Institute of Shanghai] In the same year, he exhibited Eco dal confine at the Complesso Monumentale del Purgatorio ad Arco in Naples. [ref: ECO DAL CONFINE di Alessandro Giannì, Complesso Monumentale Purgatorio ad Arco]

1) senior men,
2) senior women,
3) overall seniors (senior men and women combined),

The Arrowhead 120 (AH120) is a proposed frigate design developed by British defence company Babcock International in collaboration with Swedish defence company Saab AB. The design was offered for the Swedish Navy's Luleå-class frigate programme. [ref: Arrowhead 120, Babcock International] [ref: Saab in cooperation with Babcock for the Swedish Navy’s Future Surface Combatants, Saab]

In 2026 the Arrowhead 120 was one of the designs offered for Sweden's Luleå-class programme. The Swedish government subsequently selected the French Defence and Intervention Frigate (FDI) design offered by Naval Group. A contract for four FDI-based frigates was signed on 31 August 2026, and the Arrowhead 120 was not selected. [ref: Sweden inks deal with Naval Group for new frigates, Janes] [ref: Decision on negotiations with France on Luleå-class frigates for air defence role, Government Offices of Sweden]

== Design and development ==

The Arrowhead 120 was publicly presented by Babcock in 2017 as part of its Arrowhead family of naval designs. [ref: Babcock announces 'Arrowhead' – another option for the Type 31 frigate competition, Navy Lookout] The design was subsequently developed into a proposal for Sweden's future frigate requirement through cooperation between Babcock and Saab. [ref: Sweden prepares to put a foot back in blue water with frigate acquisition, Naval News]

Saab and Babcock signed a strategic cooperation agreement in September 2023 to explore joint development of advanced surface combatants. [ref: Saab signs strategic cooperation agreement with Babcock, Saab] In 2024 Saab was contracted by the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) to lead the basic design phase for the Luleå class, with Babcock providing engineering support.

The Swedish proposal combined Babcock's experience in naval architecture, ship construction and systems integration with Saab's experience in naval combat systems, sensors and weapons. Babcock's Arrowhead 140 design, which forms the basis of the Type 31 frigate programme in the United Kingdom, was cited as part of the larger design family's industrial background.

The proposed ship was intended for operations in the Baltic Sea and the High North. Babcock describes the design as incorporating features for cold-weather operation, including low-temperature steel, a strengthened ice belt and reinforcement of propulsion and steering systems.

== Design and characteristics ==

The proposed Arrowhead 120 measures 124 metres in length and has a stated displacement of 4,650 tonnes. Its construction combines a steel hull with a composite superstructure.

The Swedish configuration was based on Saab's 9LV combat management system and included an integrated mast housing radar and other electronic systems. The proposal incorporated Sea Giraffe 4A and Sea Giraffe 1X radar systems.

== Swedish frigate programme ==

The Arrowhead 120 was proposed for the Swedish Navy's Luleå-class programme, which sought to procure four new frigates to expand the navy's capabilities beyond its existing fleet of smaller surface combatants, including the Visby-class corvettes.

Saab and Babcock submitted their proposal as a joint industrial offering, with Babcock contributing ship design and construction expertise and Saab providing combat systems and Swedish equipment. [ref: More details emerge on Saab-Babcock frigate offer to Sweden, UK Defence Journal] [ref: Babcock pitches Arrowhead 120 variant for the Swedish Luleå-class frigate programme, Navy Lookout]

The principal competing proposals came from Babcock/Saab, France's Naval Group and Spain's Navantia. In May 2026 the Swedish government instructed the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration to begin negotiations with Naval Group for four frigates based on the FDI design. A contract for the four ships was signed on 31 August 2026, making the FDI the selected design for the programme.

The Arrowhead 120 therefore remained an unselected proposal rather than a class of ships ordered for the Swedish Navy.

== See also ==

* Arrowhead 140

Ada Kate Uchegbu (born September 30, 1982) is a Nigerian journalist, author, media entrepreneur, and political figure. She is the founder and publisher of Distinguished Africans Magazine and the CEO of ADA Consolidated Nigeria Limited. In 2025, she declared her intention to run for the presidency of Nigeria in the 2027 general elections under the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), advocating for structural reforms, gender inclusion, and generational shifts in governance.

== Early life and education ==
Ada Kate Uchegbu was born on September 30, 1982, in Nigeria. She completed her higher education at the National Open University of Nigeria. Seeking further specialization in communications and language, she attended the National Broadcast Academy in Lagos and studied at Alliance Française in Lagos. She holds the traditional title of Iyom Omelorah.

== Career ==
=== Journalism and media ===
Uchegbu began her career in writing and media, focusing on investigative reporting across West Africa. Her coverage frequently addresses governance, systemic inequality, economic issues, and national insecurity. Notable among her editorial works is "Roads of Blood – The Kidnap Highway," an investigative piece dealing with kidnapping incidents in Nigeria.

She established the media firm ADA Consolidated Nigeria Limited and subsequently founded Distinguished Africans Magazine, serving as its Editor-in-Chief. The publication acts as a pan-African platform focused on celebrating local achievements, cultural promotion, and documenting the profiles of African leaders and innovators.

=== Literary works ===
As an author, Uchegbu has written across both non-fiction political commentary and creative fiction:
* Wings of Destiny: My Journey Through Power, Politics and the Dream of Nigeria's First Female President (2026) – A political memoir evaluating her experiences within the Nigerian political space and advocating for female political participation.
* Ada the Future President – A children's book series focusing on civic responsibility and leadership.
* Kidnapped and The Dark Testament – Fiction books exploring contemporary socio-political anxieties.
* African Short Horror Stories (Volume 1 and 2) – Fiction collections utilizing traditional African folklore, superstitions, and supernatural motifs.

== Political activism and 2027 presidential campaign ==
Uchegbu's political career spans over a decade of continuous participation, during which she contested positions including the Anambra State House of Assembly, the PDP National Women Leadership, and an APC gubernatorial primary in Anambra State.

In June 2025, Uchegbu officially declared her intention to run for the President of Nigeria in the 2027 general election under the platform of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). Running under the campaign blueprint titled "The New Covenant," she argues that Nigeria's recurring socio-economic challenges stem from heavily recycled leadership and structural stagnation. She stands prominently as an advocate against the exclusion of women from major political party tickets, arguing that true democracy cannot be achieved without fair gender representation at the highest executive levels.

Her key campaign policy promises include:
* The establishment of a ₦150 billion Youth Enterprise Fund.
* Fully digitized public administration systems to counter institutional corruption.
* Standardized community health reforms and community-oriented policing.
* Increased representation of youth and women in the national cabinet.

Draft: Counterfactual measurement of marketing effectiveness

Draft text:
Counterfactual measurement of marketing effectiveness is the estimation of the causal effect of a marketing activity by comparing an observed outcome with a counterfactual, meaning the outcome that would have occurred without the activity. It is also called incrementality measurement, because the quantity estimated is the incremental outcome attributable to the marketing. The methods include randomised controlled experiments in which a treatment group is exposed to the marketing and a control group is withheld from it, holdout tests, and geographic experiments in which regions are assigned to treatment or control.

Counterfactual measurement is distinguished from methods that infer effect from observed associations between marketing exposure and outcomes, such as attribution models and marketing mix modeling, which typically use observational data.

== Concept ==
The central quantity in counterfactual measurement is incremental outcome: the sales, conversions or other results that occurred because of the marketing and would not have occurred otherwise. Outcomes that follow marketing exposure but would have happened anyway are not incremental. A customer who was already planning to purchase and later clicked an advertisement is an example.
Randomisation of exposure is intended to make the treatment and control groups comparable on all characteristics except exposure, so that a difference in outcomes can be attributed to the marketing.

== Methods ==
; Randomised controlled experiments
: Users, households or other units are randomly assigned to a group that can be shown the marketing and a group that cannot, and outcomes are compared between the groups.
; Geographic experiments
: Regions rather than individuals are assigned to treatment or control, for example by withholding advertising in selected regions.
; Calibration of other models
: Results from experiments can be used to check or adjust estimates from observational models.

== Empirical comparisons with observational methods ==
Several field studies have compared experimental estimates of advertising effect with estimates from observational methods applied to the same campaigns.

In a large-scale field experiment at eBay, Blake, Nosko and Tadelis found that returns from paid search advertising were a fraction of the returns suggested by conventional non-experimental estimates. For eBay, a large and well-known brand, advertising on brand keywords had no measurable short-term benefit.

Gordon, Zettelmeyer, Bhargava and Chapsky compared experimental results from 15 Facebook advertising campaigns with the results of observational methods. They reported that the observational methods often did not reproduce the experimental result, that they generally overstated advertising effectiveness, and that in some cases they understated it.

In a 2023 study of 663 Facebook experiments, Gordon, Moakler and Zettelmeyer reported median absolute differences between observational and experimental estimates of lift of 115 percent for upper-funnel outcomes, 107 percent for mid-funnel outcomes and 62 percent for lower-funnel outcomes. The authors concluded that the tested observational methods could not reliably recover the causal effect in their setting.

A 2026 working paper by the same group, covering 2,226 Meta advertising experiments, reported that a model calibrated on experimental results predicted incremental conversions per dollar with an out-of-sample R-squared of 0.88, compared with 0.19 for seven-day last-click attribution. The paper had not been peer reviewed at the time of retrieval.

The scope of these findings is specific to the studied platforms, methods and, in the eBay case, a single brand.

== Use in marketing decisions ==
Hanssens and colleagues state that return on marketing investment is interpreted and used in varied ways, which causes ambiguity and suboptimal marketing decisions. Incrementality estimates provide one way of defining the return attributable to marketing spend, because they compare spend with outcomes that would not have occurred without it.

* Marketing mix modeling
* Marketing effectiveness
* Return on marketing investment
* Randomized controlled trial
* A/B testing
* Causal inference
* Uplift modelling

Casey J. Hayes is an American music educator, choral conductor, and author. He is the A.J. Thurston Endowed Professor of Music at Franklin College in Franklin, Indiana, [ref: Casey J. Hayes, Ph.D., Franklin College] and the founding conductor and artistic director of the Vienna Gay Men's Chorus. [ref: It's gonna be …. LOUDER, Lambda Nachrichten] [ref: Künstlerische Leitung, Vienna Gay Men's Chorus] His research covers LGBTQ community choruses, inclusive music teaching, and the Jewish and LGBTQ cabaret performers of Weimar-era Germany and interwar Vienna. He was a Fulbright-Botstiber Visiting Professor of Austrian-American Studies at the University of Music and Performing Arts Vienna in 2021 [ref: Alum Chat: Katherine Baber and Casey Hayes in Discussion, Fulbright Austria] and wrote When the Music Stopped: Willy Rosen's Holocaust (2022), a historical novel about the German-Jewish cabaret artist Willy Rosen. [ref: Untold story: Franklin College professor pens book about famed musician during Holocaust, Daily Journal]

== Early life and education ==
Hayes began studying piano at age seven with teachers from the Juilliard School. [ref: Casey J. Hayes, Phi Delta Theta] He earned bachelor's and master's degrees in music education and choral conducting at Butler University in Indianapolis, where he studied with Henry Leck and James Mulholland. He received a PhD in music education from New York University's Steinhardt School in 2009. His dissertation, Building Bridges Through Song: A Qualitative Study of Educational Outreach by the New York City Ambassador Chorus, examined educational outreach by gay, lesbian, bisexual and transgender choruses. [ref: Building Bridges Through Song: A Qualitative Study of Educational Outreach by the New York City Ambassador Chorus, New York University]

== Career ==
=== Early choral work and New York ===
Hayes joined his first gay chorus, the Indianapolis Men's Chorus, in January 2000, serving as its accompanist and assistant conductor. In New York he chaired the creative arts department and directed the choral and band programs at The Hewitt School, a private girls' school in Manhattan. He was co-music director of the New York City Gay Men's Chorus and musical director of its outreach ensemble, the Ambassador Chorus. [ref: Community music and the GLBT chorus, International Journal of Community Music] The chorus performed at venues including Carnegie Hall, Avery Fisher Hall, Alice Tully Hall and Radio City Music Hall during his time with it.

In 2007 Hayes founded the Gay Men's Chorus of Manhattan and served as its artistic director. The chorus gave benefit concerts to raise money for other nonprofit organizations. [ref: A City That Sings, CityBeat] In June 2009 it performed a benefit concert with the Broadway actor Malcolm Gets at the Triad Theatre in Manhattan. The concert raised money to bring students from the Sidney Lanier School, a public school in Gainesville, Florida, for children with disabilities, to New York for a 2010 performance at Carnegie Hall's Weill Recital Hall. According to the project's organizers, the hall might not have been available without these funds. [ref: Harmony through DIScovering ABILITIES: An interdisciplinary music approach for students with disabilities with the Sidney Lanier Center, ISME CMA, and NACCM, International Society for Music Education] Hayes also hosted the first meeting of the North American Coalition for Community Music, held at the Hewitt School in January 2008. He also served as musical director for the actresses Joanna Gleason and Karen Ziemba, and as a music consultant for Joan Rivers.

=== Franklin College ===
Hayes joined the faculty of Franklin College in 2009. He has served as chair of the music department and director of choral activities, conducting the Franklin College Singers, Women's Chorus and Men's Chorus. He holds the A.J. Thurston endowed professorship in music and also works as an international admissions representative for the college.

=== Community choruses in the United States ===
Hayes was artistic director of the Cincinnati Men's Chorus. The chorus roughly doubled in size during his first seasons and grew from about 30 to 80 singers over his six years with it. He then became artistic director of the Quarryland Men's Chorus in Bloomington, Indiana. He served on the board of directors of GALA Choruses and on the board of the New York State chapter of the American Choral Directors Association.

=== Fulbright and Vienna ===
Hayes was named a Fulbright-Botstiber Visiting Professor of Austrian-American Studies for 2020–21 and was hosted by the University of Music and Performing Arts Vienna from February to July 2021. [ref: Casey Hayes, Fulbright Scholar Program] His research there examined Vienna's LGBTQ and Jewish cabaret communities from the end of World War I to the 1938 Anschluss, and how émigré performers recreated Viennese cabaret in New York. [ref: Rosa Wien: Gay Rights, Schlager and Self-Exile: 1918–1938, Botstiber Institute for Austrian-American Studies] In his essay "Rosa Wien: Gay Rights, Schlager and Self-Exile: 1918–1938", published by the Botstiber Institute for Austrian-American Studies, he traced Vienna's cabaret and Schlager scene between the wars. The essay discusses "Das lila Lied" as an early gay anthem, and the gay cabaret performer Paul O'Montis, who fled Germany for Vienna and died in Sachsenhausen concentration camp in 1940.

Sumit Kumar is an Indian advocate and tax lawyer based in Kolkata. He practises at the Calcutta High Court and is the founder of The Lord's Consultancy (TLC), a tax and corporate law practice, and a partner at Harvey Legal LLP. He has written practitioner books and articles on India's Goods and Services Tax and on corporate and regulatory law.

== Education ==
Kumar holds a Bachelor of Commerce (Honours) and a Bachelor of Laws, and a Master of Laws from O.P. Jindal Global University. He is a Fellow of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India and an Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India.

== Career ==
Kumar founded The Lord's Consultancy in Kolkata in 2011. The firm practises mainly in indirect taxation, including GST, customs and excise, and also handles direct tax, corporate, SEBI, FEMA and PMLA matters, with offices in Kolkata, Bengaluru and Chennai.

He practises as an advocate at the Calcutta High Court [ref: When Tax Appeal Backfires: How Far Can 'No Reformatio in Peius' Travel Under GST?, LiveLaw] and is a partner at Harvey Legal LLP. [ref: Death, Due Process and GST, The Bar Bulletin] He has appeared before the GST Appellate Tribunal, the Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal and the Supreme Court of India.

== Writing ==
With his firm, Kumar has written books on Indian tax law, including the GST-TLC series, the TLC–GST Ready Reckoner 2026, the TLC Income Tax Ready Reckoner on the Income-tax Act, 2025, and GST Appellate Tribunal: Procedure Rules, 2025 – Practitioner Commentary, Drafts, Case Law & Filing Guide.

He has written for legal publications on GST, corporate and regulatory law. These include an analysis in LiveLaw of appellate enhancement under Section 107(11) of the CGST Act following Saudi Arabian Airlines v. Union of India; a column in Bar and Bench on whether the Reserve Bank of India can require Tata Sons to list; [ref: Can RBI make a private holding company go public? The Tata Sons question, Bar and Bench] an article in The Bar Bulletin on GST liability after a sole proprietor's death under Section 93 of the CGST Act; and opinion pieces for Taxmann on angel funds under the SEBI (Alternative Investment Funds) Regulations and on the Income-tax (Fourth Amendment) Rules, 2026. [ref: Angel Funds vis-à-vis AI-only Funds under SEBI AIF Regulations, Taxmann] [ref: Income-tax (Fourth Amendment) Rules, 2026 – What Changed and What Practitioners Should Do Now, Taxmann]

Kumar is chairman and managing trustee of SEVA Foundation, a Kolkata-based charitable trust established in 2024 and registered under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, which works on child education, food distribution, women's empowerment and legal awareness. [ref: About Us, SEVA Foundation]

Draft: Ice River Complex

Draft text:
The Ice River Complex (also Ice River alkaline complex) is an alkaline ultramafic intrusion in the Canadian Rockies of southeastern British Columbia, Canada, located about south of Field. Most of its roughly of exposure lies within Yoho and Kootenay national parks. [ref: Alkaline ultrabasic rocks in British Columbia: carbonatites, nepheline syenites, kimberlites, ultramafic lamprophyres and related rocks, British Columbia Ministry of Energy, Mines and Petroleum Resources, Geological Survey Branch] It was the first alkaline intrusion recognized in British Columbia and is regarded as one of the world's major alkaline complexes, notable for its layered ijolite series, carbonatites and sodalite-bearing nepheline syenites.

==Geology==
The complex is an arcuate mass about long. It intrudes Cambrian and Ordovician shales and carbonates of the Chancellor, Ottertail and McKay formations; contact metamorphism of these host rocks produced hornfels and skarns, with some limited soda metasomatism. [ref: The geology and petrology of the Ice River alkaline complex, British Columbia, Geological Survey of Canada] The complex and its host rocks were later deformed and subjected to low-grade regional metamorphism during the Columbian orogeny.

Two distinct suites are present:
* An older, rhythmically layered, feldspar-free intrusion ranging from jacupirangite through melanite ijolite to melanite urtite. It consists of repeated graded layers 10 to 200 metres thick, with nepheline increasing toward the top of each layer. Jacupirangite, the most mafic rock, contains titanaugite, titaniferous magnetite, perovskite and phlogopite. This suite is cored by a carbonatite plug and cut by carbonatite dykes.
* A younger, zoned and crosscutting syenite complex forming an elliptical pipe-like mass, grading from a greenish sodalite syenite core through pale grey nepheline syenite to darker, mafic-rich rocks at the margin, rimmed by fine-grained leucosyenite. Nepheline makes up as much as 30 per cent of these rocks and sodalite up to 20 per cent.

Carbonatites occur at several localities and are lithologically varied. Those in the layered ultramafic series include black, buff and red-weathering types; the black variety carries siderite, calcite, green berthierine and the barium zeolite edingtonite, while pyrochlore and xenotime occur in the red variety. Carbonatite associated with the syenites contains only feldspars, zeolites and rare phlogopite as silicates, with ankerite, barytocalcite and strontianite reported at some localities. Late lamprophyre dykes cut the complex and its host rocks. Carbonatites and some melanocratic syenites are enriched in niobium, rare-earth elements and strontium.

===Age===
The age of emplacement has long been debated. J. A. Allan suggested a post-Cretaceous age in 1914, and in 1959 W. C. Gussow and C. W. Hunt argued the complex was a sample of Precambrian basement. Potassium–argon and rubidium–strontium dates from the early 1960s indicated a mid-Paleozoic (Devonian–Mississippian) age. Currie (1975) obtained Early Triassic dates and preferred an emplacement age of about 245 million years, but uranium–lead zircon work reported by R. Parrish in 1986 supported the mid-Paleozoic dates as closest to the true age of emplacement.

==History of study==
The complex was described around the turn of the 20th century by G. M. Dawson (1885), A. E. Barlow (1902) and T. G. Bonney (1902). Work by J. A. Allan in 1911 and 1914 established it as one of the world's major alkaline complexes. Renewed study followed in the 1950s and 1960s, and the Geological Survey of Canada mapped it in detail in the early 1970s, [ref: Ice River alkaline complex, British Columbia (82N), Geological Survey of Canada] [ref: A preliminary report on the Ice River alkaline complex, British Columbia, Geological Survey of Canada] culminating in K. L. Currie's 1975 monograph, the most comprehensive study of the complex.

Access is difficult because of steep mountainous terrain, a lack of roads and regulations imposed by Parks Canada.

==See also==
* Carbonatite
* Geology of British Columbia

Draft text:
The Kutcho deposit (also Kutcho Creek deposit) is a copper–zinc volcanogenic massive sulphide (VMS) deposit in the Cassiar Mountains of northern British Columbia, Canada, about from Dease Lake. [ref: MINFILE No. 104I 060: Kutcho, Main, Sumac, Kutcho Creek, Esso West, MINFILE Mineral Inventory] Discovered in the early 1970s, it has been the subject of exploration and mine proposals by a succession of companies, and of geological research because its host rocks record a primitive Permo-Triassic island arc unlike other VMS settings in the Canadian Cordillera.

==Geology==
The deposit lies within the Kutcho Assemblage (formerly Kutcho Formation), a latest Permian to Early Triassic volcano-sedimentary sequence within the fault-bounded King Salmon allochthon. [ref: Geological setting, U–Pb geochronology, and radiogenic isotopic characteristics of the Permo-Triassic Kutcho Assemblage, north-central British Columbia, Canadian Journal of Earth Sciences] The assemblage comprises basaltic to basaltic andesite flows and tuffs and rhyodacitic to rhyolitic flows, mass flows and pyroclastic flows, intruded by gabbro, diorite, trondhjemite and quartz–plagioclase porphyry. The ore is hosted by rhyolite mass flows near the top of the assemblage; rhyolites from the hanging wall and footwall have U–Pb ages of about 242 million years, and a nearby porphyry intrusion is dated at 244 ± 6 million years. Lead and neodymium isotope signatures indicate formation in an intra-oceanic island arc, probably on oceanic crust, and are inconsistent with the adjacent Stikine or Quesnel terranes. The stratigraphic, lithogeochemical and tectonic setting of the deposit was described by Barrett, Thompson and Sherlock in 1996. [ref: Stratigraphic, lithogeochemical and tectonic setting of the Kutcho Creek massive sulfide deposit, northern British Columbia, Exploration and Mining Geology]

Mineralization occurs in three stratabound, lenticular lenses — Main (Kutcho), Sumac and Esso (Esso West) — along about of a single stratigraphic horizon. The lenses strike about 280° and dip north at 40 to 45°. Sulphides include pyrite, sphalerite, chalcopyrite and bornite, with minor chalcocite and traces of tennantite and galena; the lenses have copper-rich cores and zinc-rich margins. They are surrounded by an alteration halo depleted in sodium and enriched in potassium that extends about 300 metres into the footwall.

Childe and colleagues (1998) interpreted Kutcho as a distinct type of Cordilleran VMS deposit formed in a primitive intra-oceanic arc, and noted similarities with the Sitlika assemblage and the Venables Valley–Red Hill area, which they considered prospective for similar deposits. [ref: Primitive Permo-Triassic volcanism in the Canadian Cordillera: tectonic and metallogenic implications, Economic Geology]

==History==
Sumac Mines Ltd. (controlled by Sumitomo Metal Mining) and Esso Minerals of Canada staked the deposit in 1972 and 1973 respectively, and carried out more than 50,000 metres of drilling and a bulk-sampling crosscut. Esso sold its interest to Homestake Mining (Canada) in 1989; Teck-Cominco held an option from 1992. Western Keltic Mines acquired the property from Barrick Gold and Sumitomo in 2004 and was purchased in 2008 by Sherwood Copper, which merged with Capstone Mining later that year. In June 2017 Desert Star Resources agreed to acquire the project from Capstone, and renamed itself Kutcho Copper Corp. in December 2017.

===Resource and reserve estimates===
All figures below are as reported by the companies and compiled by MINFILE:
* 1986 (published estimate, CIM Special Volume 37): Kutcho lens 17 million tonnes at 1.62% Cu and 2.32% Zn; Sumac about 10 million tonnes at 1.0% Cu and 1.2% Zn.
* 2017 (Desert Star Resources pre-feasibility study): probable reserves of 10.4 million tonnes at 2.01% Cu, 3.19% Zn, 0.37 g/t gold and 34.61 g/t silver.
* March 2019 (Kutcho Copper Corp.): measured and indicated resources (Main, Esso and Sumac combined) of 17.26 million tonnes at 1.85% Cu and 2.72% Zn, plus 10.7 million tonnes inferred.

===Environmental assessment===
A proposal for a 2,500-tonne-per-day underground mine in the Andrea Creek watershed, a tributary of Kutcho Creek, was assessed federally; in 2011 the assessment was downgraded from a comprehensive study to a screening after a redesign, and it was terminated on 20 June 2016. [ref: Kutcho Copper Zinc Silver Gold Mine Project, Dease Lake (Registry 36352), Canadian Impact Assessment Registry] A revised proposal for an underground copper–zinc mine of about 3,500 tonnes of ore per day with a mine life of up to 14 years entered British Columbia's environmental assessment process under the 2018 Environmental Assessment Act in December 2019. [ref: Kutcho, EAO Project Information Centre (EPIC)]

==References==
