Draft: Akido (healthcare company)

Draft text:
Akido (formerly Akido Labs) is an American healthcare technology company based in Los Angeles, California. The company develops artificial intelligence software for clinical care and operates a network of healthcare services. Its products include ScopeAI, a clinical support system designed to assist with patient interviews, medical assessments, and treatment recommendations.

== History ==

Akido was founded in 2015 and emerged from work associated with the University of Southern California's Digital Health Lab. Initially, the company developed data and software tools for healthcare providers and public-service organizations, including tools intended to identify people at risk of adverse health or social outcomes. [ref: The AI Doctor Will See New York Ride-Share Drivers Now, The Wall Street Journal]

In 2022, the company shifted toward directly delivering healthcare services after acquiring a multispecialty medical practice in Southern California. It developed a healthcare network combining clinical services with its technology.

In May 2025, Akido announced a $60 million Series B funding round led by healthcare investment firm Oak HC/FT. The company said the funding would support the expansion of ScopeAI and its clinical network. [ref: Akido Raises $60 Million Series B to Expand Reach of ScopeAI, Business Wire] [ref: Akido: $60 Million Series B Secured For Health AI Platform, Pulse2]

In July 2026, the company announced that it was dropping "Labs" from its name and expanding its AI-supported healthcare model under the Akido and Akido Medical brands. [ref: Akido Announces the First AI-Native Health System in the US, PR Newswire]

== Products and services ==

=== ScopeAI ===

ScopeAI is a clinical artificial intelligence system developed by Akido. It guides patient interviews, suggests follow-up questions, organizes clinical information, and generates proposed diagnoses, tests, and treatments for review by a licensed clinician. According to reporting by the Wall Street Journal, physicians retain authority to approve, modify, or reject its recommendations.

Akido has used ScopeAI in clinical settings that include conventional clinics, street medicine programs, and services for populations that may have difficulty accessing healthcare. In 2025, the company announced plans to use the system in a healthcare program for rideshare drivers in New York City.

=== Healthcare services ===

Akido operates healthcare services in conjunction with its technology. Its programs have included street medicine for people experiencing homelessness and partnerships with community organizations. In January 2026, CalMatters reported on the use of ScopeAI in street medicine programs in California, including its role in helping outreach workers gather patient information for subsequent physician review. [ref: Can AI help make homeless Californians healthier?, CalMatters]

In 2025, Akido partnered with community organizations to launch an AI-assisted street medicine program in the San Francisco Bay Area. [ref: Akido Labs launches AI-powered street medicine program in SF, Fierce Healthcare]

== Reception and concerns ==

Supporters of AI-assisted clinical care argue that these systems may help clinicians serve more patients and improve access to care in underserved communities. Akido’s partnerships have included organizations serving people experiencing homelessness and workers with limited time to seek medical attention.

The use of AI to support diagnosis and treatment has also raised questions about accuracy, privacy, bias, informed consent, and the quality of care for vulnerable patients. In its 2026 reporting, CalMatters described concerns from healthcare and AI researchers about the risks of using diagnostic AI with people experiencing homelessness, including the need for appropriate human oversight and safeguards.

Draft text:
Dionfest is an English-language website covering festivals, cultural traditions, religious observances, regional fairs and related subjects in India and other parts of the world. Founded by Abhay Ramola, the website was launched on 4 January 2026. Its articles explore festival dates, historical backgrounds, customs, rituals and cultural significance.

The website's coverage extends beyond festival descriptions to include environmental issues associated with celebrations, sustainable event practices, cultural heritage, festival travel, planning advice and educational articles about traditions and communities. Its regional coverage includes festivals and fairs in Uttarakhand, alongside articles about Indian and international celebrations.

== History ==

DionFest was founded by Abhay Ramola and launched on 4 January 2026. The website was established as a digital publication focused on festivals, cultural traditions and subjects connected with public celebrations.

Ramola has an undergraduate academic background in history, having completed a Bachelor of Arts degree in the subject. His interest in historical events and cultural traditions is reflected in the website's coverage of regional festivals and celebrations in different parts of the world.

The website covers local festivals and fairs in Uttarakhand, including events associated with Uttarkashi and the Rawain Valley. It also publishes articles about festivals in other parts of India and internationally.

== Content and coverage ==

DionFest publishes informational articles about festivals and related cultural, historical, environmental and practical subjects.

=== Festivals around the world ===

The website covers festivals and celebrations from different countries and regions. Articles explore festival dates, origins, historical context, rituals, customs and the ways celebrations are observed by local communities.

Its international coverage includes festivals in Asia and other parts of the world, with individual articles examining the distinctive traditions and cultural practices associated with particular events.

=== Indian festivals ===

DionFest covers religious celebrations, seasonal festivals, regional fairs and other cultural observances in India. Articles discuss the background of festivals, traditional practices, community participation and variations in how celebrations are observed across regions.

The coverage includes both widely observed celebrations and regional events associated with particular communities and traditions.

=== Local festivals and fairs in Uttarakhand ===

Regional festivals form part of the website's coverage of Indian cultural heritage. Its articles include local fairs and religious traditions associated with Uttarakhand, particularly the Uttarkashi district and the Rawain Valley.

One event covered by the website is the Danda Devrana Mela, a religious fair associated with Rudreshwar Maharaj. The website's article describes the event's rituals, traditional music, folk dances, procession and significance to surrounding communities.

Ramola has also written about his personal connection with the fair and his childhood in Naugaon. His account describes his experience of the event and aspects of the surrounding regional traditions.

=== Cultural traditions and heritage ===

DionFest publishes articles exploring the stories, beliefs and customs associated with festivals. Topics include the historical development of celebrations, traditional practices, community identity and the cultural meanings attached to rituals.

The website also covers cultural heritage and exploration, including information intended to help readers understand traditions and the historical context of places associated with celebrations.

=== Environmental impact of festivals ===

DionFest covers environmental issues associated with festivals and large public celebrations. Topics include air pollution, noise pollution, waste generation, water use and the environmental footprint of events.

Articles examine how travel, food, energy consumption and event operations can affect the environment. This coverage also considers the challenges of managing waste and protecting nearby communities and natural environments during celebrations.

=== Green festivals and sustainability ===

The website publishes material about sustainable festival practices and approaches to reducing the environmental impact of celebrations. Topics include waste reduction, reusable materials, responsible resource use and environmentally considerate event planning.

This subject area explores ways to consider sustainability while respecting cultural traditions and the significance of celebrations to local communities.

=== Festival waste management ===

Waste management is another subject covered by DionFest. Articles discuss festival waste, including plastic, food waste and discarded flowers associated with religious and cultural events.

The coverage considers waste reduction, responsible disposal and recycling as part of broader discussions about the environmental effects of public celebrations.

=== Climate and festivals ===

DionFest examines the relationship between festivals, climate and resource consumption. Relevant topics include emissions associated with travel and event operations, energy use, accommodation and other factors that contribute to the environmental footprint of celebrations.

Draft: Ouled Djellal ( sheep )

Draft text:
The Ouled Djellal (also known as the Algerian Arab or Western Thin-tailed) is a breed of domestic sheep native to the steppe and high plains of Algeria. It is the most dominant, widespread, and economically important sheep breed in the country, accounting for approximately 63% to 65% of the national flock with an estimated population of over 11 to 12 million head. It is primarily kept for meat production and wool, and is highly favored for its exceptional adaptability to arid and semi-arid pastoral systems.

== History ==
The breed takes its name from the town of Ouled Djellal, located southwest of Biskra, which represents its historical cradle. Historical hypotheses suggest that the thin-tailed, fine-wooled ancestors of the breed may have been originally introduced to North Africa from Italy by the Romans during the fifth century.

Due to its high commercial profitability and productivity, the breed expanded dramatically over the late 20th and early 21st centuries. Driven by the mechanization of the steppe and changing transportation infrastructures, its population increased from roughly 10 million in 1989 to over 11–12 million head, overrunning the geographical ranges of smaller native breeds. Today, it has spread far beyond its central-eastern Algerian origin into the western steppes and cross-border regions of western Tunisia.

== Characteristics ==
The Ouled Djellal is a large, long-legged, and slender thin-tailed breed explicitly built for high mobility and long-distance walking across sparse rangelands. It is entirely unicolored white, with white skin, a thin head, a convex or sub-convex facial profile, and long, drooping ears. The fleece is white and consists of a light, refined, carpet-grade wool. Rams generally display strong, spiral horns, whereas the ewes are typically polled (hornless).

At maturity, rams average 81 kg (with some selection strains reaching up to 140 kg) in weight and stand approximately 84 cm tall at the withers. Ewes average 49 kg (ranging up to 75 kg in optimized systems) and stand about 74 cm tall.

The breed is an exceptionally hardy and active forager, showing remarkable tolerance to extreme heat and prolonged nutritional stress in arid environments. Under standard management systems, ewes demonstrate high maternal capacity and produce an average litter size of 1.5 lambs. Lambs display excellent growth potential and rapid fattening profiles, typically starting at a birth weight of 3.5 kg and scaling efficiently to 30 kg by five months of age. Ewes also maintain a substantial dairy performance, lactating for approximately 180 days and yielding around 75 kg of milk.

== Economic Importance ==
The Ouled Djellal serves as the definitive cornerstone of Algerian agropastoralism and food security. It is the absolute reference breed for the national Eid al-Adha holiday market, commanding the highest buyer demand, commercial volume, and investment yields across local livestock corridors. Its meat is highly valued, and the breed produces a heavier, fat-retentive carcass profile compared to smaller regional types.

== Genetic Homogenization Impact ==
The commercial superiority of the Ouled Djellal has driven a widespread trend toward livestock homogenization across the North African steppes. To maximize economic returns, pastoralists throughout western Algeria have systematically introduced heavy Ouled Djellal rams into native western herds. This aggressive crossbreeding practice has resulted in severe genetic dilution and the absorption of smaller indigenous breeds—most notably pushing the native, high-meat-quality Hamra breed to the brink of extinction.

Draft text:
Kirenia Álvarez, known professionally as KIKI, is a Cuban visual artist based in Miami, Florida, who works in pigmented epoxy resin. She is the founder of KIKI by Kirenia Alvarez LLC, and her brand name, KIKI BY KIRENIA ALVAREZ, is a federally registered trademark for works of art of epoxy resin. Álvarez describes her resin wall pieces as "jewelry for walls".

== Background ==
Álvarez was born on November 16, 1983, in Guanabacoa, Havana, Cuba. Her family won the United States visa lottery and emigrated to the U.S. in March 1998; she was raised in Hialeah, Florida, where she attended Hialeah High School. She studied Web Page Design at Florida National College in 2001. Álvarez began working in the banking industry in 2008, starting as a receptionist, and worked in that field for about fifteen years. In a 2025 interview, she said she discovered epoxy resin as an artistic medium during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns, and that developing her first resin piece took more than six months.

== Career ==
Álvarez works from Miami, Florida, through her company KIKI by Kirenia Alvarez LLC, organized in Florida in 2021. In 2022, the mark KIKI BY KIRENIA ALVAREZ was registered with the United States Patent and Trademark Office (Reg. No. 6728425) for "works of art of epoxy resin".

In June 2021, her work went on sale at the Kendall branch of El Dorado Furniture in Miami; according to the artist's announcements at the time, her first two pieces there sold on July 4, 2021.

Her work has been presented at the Carnaval on the Mile juried art festival in Coral Gables.

Álvarez has discussed her work in Spanish-language media in South Florida, including a 2025 segment on Telemundo 51's Cuéntale a Marilys, a 2021 interview on MEGA TV with Jasmina Marazita, and an appearance on UniVista TV's El Show de Carlucho in 2022. In June 2025 she was the subject of a full episode of Emigrante Podcast, "Joyas de Pared, el Arte de Kirenia Alvarez" (Wall Jewelry: The Art of Kirenia Alvarez).

== Style and technique ==
Álvarez produces wall works in pigmented epoxy resin, building layered, high-gloss surfaces, frequently with gold-toned accents and onyx- or geode-like effects.

== Awards and recognition ==
* First Place, Mixed Media category, Carnaval on the Mile, Coral Gables (2023), for a resin depiction of La Catrina. The festival's awards program, run by the Kiwanis Club of Little Havana, grants first, second and third place awards in its Fine Arts Village categories. The festival's official winners board, published on Carnaval Miami's official event page, names her "1st Kiki Alvarez" in the Mixed Media category and shows her holding the first-place blue ribbon.
* In April 2021, she appeared on the cover of DMH Magazine.

== Exhibitions ==
* Carnaval on the Mile (juried art festival), Coral Gables, Florida, 2023.

Chinmay Pandya (born 9 April 1976) is an Indian psychiatrist, educationist, and academic administrator serving as the Pro Vice-Chancellor (Vice-President) of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya (DSVV) in Haridwar, Uttarakhand. He represents the All World Gayatri Pariwar (AWGP), an organization founded by his grandfather, Shriram Sharma Acharya. His work and public engagements span psychiatric medicine, yoga, Indian knowledge systems, interfaith dialogue, and the ethical governance of artificial intelligence.

== Early life and education ==
Pandya was born on 9 April 1976 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, India. He grew up at Shantikunj, the global headquarters of the All World Gayatri Pariwar in Haridwar.

He pursued medical studies at the Himalayan Institute of Medical Sciences in Dehradun, graduating with a Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) degree. He later moved to the United Kingdom for postgraduate psychiatric training, earning a postgraduate diploma in Public Health and obtaining Membership of the Royal College of Psychiatrists (MRCPsych).

== Medical career ==
Between 2002 and 2010, Pandya worked within the United Kingdom's National Health Service (NHS) across various psychiatric posts. His concluding clinical appointment was as an associate specialist in older adult psychiatric services at West London Mental Health Trust, focusing on the diagnosis and management of neurocognitive disorders, including Alzheimer's disease and other dementias.

In 2010, he relocated to India to join the leadership and voluntary initiatives of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya and All World Gayatri Pariwar in Haridwar.

== Academic leadership and institutional roles ==
Pandya serves as the Pro Vice-Chancellor / Vice-President of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya (DSVV), overseeing academic policy development, interdisciplinary curriculums, and global academic partnerships.

=== Academic and editorial work ===

* Editor of Dev Sanskriti: Interdisciplinary International Journal, an academic journal covering Indian philosophy, psychology, education, and Ayurveda.
* Chairperson and co-founder of the Centre for Baltic Culture and Studies at DSVV.
* Chairperson of the South Asian Institute of Peace and Reconciliation (SAIPR), established at DSVV in partnership with the University of Winchester.
* Founder Patron and Board of Founders member at Rishihood University.

=== Government and advisory committees ===
Pandya has served on several national statutory and advisory bodies in India, including:

* Governing Body of the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).
* Advisory Council of the Ministry of Ayush.
* Syllabus restructuring committee of the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE).
* Board of Trustees of the India Development Foundation of Overseas Indians.
* General Council of the National Culture Fund under the Ministry of Culture.

== Representation and public engagements ==
As a senior representative of the All World Gayatri Pariwar, Pandya represents the organisation at national and international forums on youth development, social reform, and cultural preservation. [ref: Three Jyoti Kalash Chariots depart from Shantikunj to spread message of centenary celebrations, ANI News] [ref: Gayatri Parivar's Jyoti Kalash chariots begin yatra for centenary, Asianet Newsable] [ref: Three Jyoti Kalash Chariots depart from Shantikunj to spread message of centenary celebrations, Lokmat Times]

=== International engagements and interfaith dialogue ===
Pandya has addressed global conferences on cultural dialogue, spirituality, and peacebuilding:

* Addressed discussions at the United Nations Office at Vienna and UNESCO forums concerning intangible cultural heritage.
* Attended the COP24 climate summit and delivered guest lectures at various global institutions including the University of Cambridge, as well as Indian institutes such as the Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs), and Bhabha Atomic Research Centre.
* Serves as a director of the Global Covenant of Religions and participated in the Parliamentary Conferences on Interfaith Dialogue in Marrakesh (Morocco) and Rome (Italy).

=== Artificial intelligence and ethics ===
Pandya has been active in international consultations focusing on the ethical governance of artificial intelligence (AI):

* In July 2024, participated in the interfaith summit "AI Ethics for Peace: World Religions Commit to the Rome Call" in Hiroshima, Japan.
* Appointed as an Associate member of the AI Faith and Civil Society Commission in Abu Dhabi.
* Speaker at the India AI Impact Summit in New Delhi (February 2026) and chaired discussions on AI and democratic governance.
* In July 2026, contributed to panels during UN-affiliated events in Geneva, including the Geneva Centre for Security Policy session on extreme AI risks and the ITU's AI for Good Global Summit.
* Member of the HumAIn Capital's Global South Leadership Council on responsible AI.

=== Yoga and wellness ===

* Served as Vice-President of the Indian Yoga Association.
* Chairperson of the International Festival of Yoga, Culture and Spirituality organized by DSVV.
* Speaker at the International Yoga Festival in Rishikesh, addressing psychological well-being and contemplative practices.

KinitoPET is a 2024 psychological horror video game developed by troy_en. It was released to steam on January 9th, 2024. The game is presented as an early-2000s virtual desktop assistant named Kinito, an axolotl who interacts directly with the player's computer. The game combines metafiction, simulated desktop interaction, and psychological horror.

==Gameplay==
The game takes place through a simulated desktop interface where the player interacts with Kinito, a virtual assistant. As you play the game Kinito starts to get a too nosy asking you about your personal life opening up different programs and giving you lots of little games and puzzles to solve. What you do in the game affects how it ends. There are many different endings, to Kinito depending on what you decide to do with Kinito.

==Plot==
The player downloads KinitoPET, a virtual assistant designed to become their best friend. At the start, he is friendly and helpful, but Kinito gradually reveals obsessive behavior as the story progresses, blurring the line between the game and the player's computer.

==Development==
KinitoPET was developed by the indie developer troy_en using the Godot Engine. An interview with the developer confirmed the game was made entirely using free software, such as the 3D models being made using Blender, and the artwork being made using Paint.NET. [ref: https://www.reddit.com/r/KinitoPET/comments/1b6p85n/interview_with_troy_en_developer_of_kinitopet/] One of the biggest issues he suffered when developing KinitoPET was procrastination. As he states, "Procrastination can kill dreams. It's never perfect and always needs changes - (To be honest I still don't like KinitoPET - I would have changed a lot if I were to redo it)". It was released for Microsoft Windows and macOS on January 9, 2024.

==Reception==
KinitoPET received generally positive reviews. On steam, the game has a total of 9,122 "Very Positive" reviews, and 138 "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews. [ref: https://store.steampowered.com/app/2075070/KinitoPET/#app_reviews_hash] According to the review aggregate website Metacritic, the game recieved many "generally favoriable reviews" by users, with praise directed toward its atmosphere, and very good experience. [ref: https://www.metacritic.com/game/kinitopet/user-reviews/?platform=pc]

Leaveland is a metropolitan outdoor leisure brand originating from Milan, Italy. In the early 1950s, Whitaman Hill, a Canadian-Italian, inherited his father's Emil shoe store in Milan, Italy. The brand was established in Milan, Italy, in 1952. [ref: 嘉隆商贸获意大利枫叶中国区独家运营权]

== History ==
In 1970, Leaveland established its base in Italy and gradually expanded into other European countries, as well as the Canadian and U.S. markets in North America. In 1982, Leaveland began entering the Asian market, first launching in Hong Kong, and over the next decade, expanded into markets across the Asia-Pacific region, including Malaysia, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, and Australia. In 1990, Leaveland officially entered China and became the sponsor of the Chinese delegation for the 1990 Beijing Asian Games. In 1992, Leaveland provided sponsorship to the Chinese Football Association, with its products designated as the official products of the association. Through market expansion, it has now secured a certain market share in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and the East China region. In 2017, Leaveland was appointed by Maple Leaf International Investment Co., Ltd. as the sole authorized Maple Leaf International Commercial Co., Ltd. for global brand management and operations, specializing in footwear, apparel, leather goods, socks, and underwear.

= Pocket FM =

Pocket FM is an Indian audio entertainment platform that distributes serialized fiction and other audio content. It was founded in 2018 by Rohan Nayak, Prateek Dixit and Nishanth Srinivas. [ref: Pocket FM raises $22.4 million in Series B funding led by Lightspeed, The Economic Times] [ref: Rohan Nayak, Prateek Dixit, Nishant KS, Fortune India]

The platform uses a freemium model in which some episodes are available without charge while subsequent episodes can be unlocked using virtual currency purchased through in-app transactions. The company is actively incorporating artificial intelligence for audio production as well as translation into other languages. [ref: Pocket FM partners with ElevenLabs to convert scripts into audio content quickly, TechCrunch] [ref: Pocket FM wants to be the Netflix of long-form audio, www.forbesindia.com]

As of 2026, The Pocket FM website claims the company is serving 20+ countries in 15 international languages. [ref: Pocket FM: The home of the world's best audio dramas, pocketfm.com]

== History ==
Pocket FM began offering content across multiple formats like audiobooks, podcasts and other spoken-word content before shifting its focus toward serialized fiction. [ref: Pocket FM: The Startup that Pioneered Audio Series and Made the Entertainment Industry Follow in Its Footsteps, OK Magazine] By 2021, the platform was describing itself primarily as a community of content creators, and an audio entertainment service serving fictional content in an episodic story format. [ref: Audio OTT app Pocket FM raises $22.4mn funding in round led by Lightspeed, Business Standard]

In December 2021, Pocket FM raised $22.4 million in a Series B funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from Tanglin Venture Partners and existing investor Times Group. The company said the funding would be used to expand its operations, creator community and geographical presence.

In September 2023, the company announced that its Android application had surpassed 100 million downloads on Google Play. The company attributed the growth to its serialized-fiction format and expansion across languages and genres. [ref: Pocket FM crosses over 100 million downloads on Google Play Store, The Times of India]

In March 2024, Pocket FM raised $103 million in a Series D funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from StepStone Group. TechCrunch reported that the round brought the company's total funding to approximately $196 million and valued it at $750 million. The company said the funding would support expansion into Europe and Latin America following growth in the United States. [ref: Audio platform Pocket FM bags $103M in funding as it eyes global expansion, TechCrunch]

== Content and business model ==
Pocket FM's principal offering is serialized audio fiction. The platform hosts stories released in episodes, with content spanning genres including romance, fantasy, science fiction, thriller and drama. Pocket FM uses a freemium, pay-as-you-go model in which users can listen to some episodes for free and unlock additional episodes by purchasing virtual coins. [ref: Out of Pocket, The Verge]

The company expanded into the United States in 2022. By March 2024, the company said it had generated more than $150 million in annual recurring revenue, including $100 million from the United States, and was expanding into Europe and Latin America.

Pocket FM's revenue stood at ₹1,768 crore for the financial year 2024–25, an increase of 68 percent from the previous year. More than half of the company's revenue came from user payments through microtransactions, with the remainder coming from advertising. In April 2026, Pocket FM said it had reached approximately $450 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). The company said it had reached approximately $200 million ARR in the fourth quarter of financial year 2025 and approximately $400 million in the fourth quarter of financial year 2026. [ref: Pocket FM hits $450 million ARR in April after accelerating AI-led content creation, The Economic Times]

== Notable series ==
According to play counts displayed by Pocket FM, Insta Millionaire and Super Yoddha have each accumulated approximately 1.4 billion plays, Ek Ladki Ko Dekha To approximately 1.3 billion, Secret Ameerzaada approximately 885 million, and Insta Empire approximately 556.4 million. [ref: Pocket FM: The home of the world's best audio dramas, pocketfm.com]

== Creator ecosystem ==
Pocket FM relies upon its community of writers and voice artists to produce content for the platform. In 2021, the company reported working with more than 17,000 writers and voice artists for content production. In February 2026, The Economic Times reported that Pocket FM said more than 20 percent of its monetized creators earned more than ₹1 lakh per month and that total creator payouts had exceeded ₹300 crore.

== Artificial intelligence ==
Pocket FM has increasingly incorporated artificial intelligence into the production of its audio content. In June 2024, the company announced a partnership with ElevenLabs to convert written scripts into audio using AI-generated voices. Pocket FM reported produceding 30,000 hours of audio series using ElevenLabs' technology during a testing phase, and planned to make the technology available to its creators in the future.

Draft text:
Rally Takes the Train is a 2022 American children's picture book written by Kelsey Cecil and illustrated by Leslie Dunn. Told in rhyming verse, it follows Rally, a corgi, on his first train journey to visit his grandparents, whom the book calls his "grand-paw-rents." The story is set aboard a passenger train traveling along the Southern California coast, and the title character is based on the author's own dog. [ref: Rally Takes the Train, Rally Takes the Train]

== Plot ==
Rally wakes early on the morning of a big journey. Seeing a suitcase, he assumes his family is going away and packs his favorite things: a turtle toy, a green bone, and a yellow ball. At a Spanish-style train station lined with palm trees, Rally runs ahead in excitement, but his short legs cannot climb the train's tall steps, and his father lifts him aboard.

On the train, the family finds their seats and Rally greets the other passengers. Children reach down to pet him, and he leaves a trail of shed fur, described as "corgi glitter," as he walks the aisle. When the train departs, Rally watches the ocean through the window, greets a seabird, shares a pretzel with his mother, and meets the conductor.

The train then enters a dark tunnel. Rally is frightened at first, but soon sees light ahead, hears cheering, and emerges onto a stretch of track running beside coastal cliffs and the sea. Near the end of the trip, Rally sees his grandparents, Grandmommy and Papa, waving from the platform of another station. He runs to the door to greet them.

== Background ==
The idea for the book, including its title, plot, and the "grand-paw-rents" wordplay, originated with the author's mother, who discussed it for years but died in 2021 before writing it. Cecil subsequently wrote the book to realize her mother's idea and as a memorial to her. [ref: Our Story, Rally Takes the Train]

The character of Rally is based on the Cecil family's corgi. The tunnel scene was inspired by a photograph of the dog sitting frightened in a car during a rainstorm.

== Setting ==
The journey depicted in the book corresponds to a trip on Amtrak's Pacific Surfliner from San Diego to Orange County. The departure station illustrated in the book is modeled on San Diego's Santa Fe Depot, and the ocean views depict the coastline near San Clemente, where the rail line runs directly along the beach.

== Illustrations ==
The book was illustrated by Leslie Dunn of 9+C Designs. Each page was hand-painted in watercolor. [ref: The Art, Rally Takes the Train]

In her review for Reedsy Discovery, Kathryn Bettendorf highlighted the illustrations' use of a corgi-eye-level perspective and their depiction of the train journey. [ref: Rally Takes the Train, Reedsy Discovery]

== Publication ==
Rally Takes the Train was independently published in paperback through Kindle Direct Publishing on November 5, 2022. The original edition contains 25 pages and has the ISBN 9798846419773. [ref: Rally Takes The Train, Open Library]

The book is also available in paperback and digital formats through Barnes & Noble, including an edition for its NOOK e-reading platform. [ref: Rally Takes The Train, Barnes & Noble]

A Kindle edition is also available through Amazon. [ref: Rally Takes the Train, Amazon]

== Critical reception ==
In a review published by Reedsy Discovery, Kathryn Bettendorf praised the book's rhyming narrative, read-aloud qualities, and watercolor illustrations by Leslie Dunn. Bettendorf highlighted the illustrations' use of a corgi-eye-level perspective and described the book as a heartwarming account of family and adventure.

Bettendorf also discussed the book's appeal to children interested in trains and dogs, noting its suitability as a read-aloud picture book.

Draft: Narrative intelligence

Draft text:
Narrative intelligence refers to the ability to create, tell, and understand stories and to respond to them emotionally. Research on computational narrative intelligence examines these abilities in artificial intelligence systems. [ref: Computational Narrative Intelligence: A Human-Centered Goal for Artificial Intelligence, arXiv]

In information warfare, the term narrative intelligence, or NARINT, is used to analyze narratives, their circulation, and their influence on perceptions and behavior. [ref: Inteligencia narrativa en la era de la IA: análisis de la desinformación antiucraniana de Rusia, Ministerio de Defensa]

This analysis examines how people interpret events through stories, how ideas gain attention, who promotes them, and how they change over time. Analysts connect individual posts to recurring themes and the networks that spread them to help identify emerging narratives and potential influence campaigns.

== Background ==
Michael Mateas and Phoebe Sengers co-chaired the 1999 AAAI Fall Symposium on Narrative Intelligence. The symposium's call for participation covered story generation and understanding, interactive storytelling, and autonomous agents, alongside contributions from psychology, cultural studies, and art. [ref: Call for Participation: Narrative Intelligence, Carnegie Mellon University]

Mateas and Sengers later edited the 2003 collection Narrative Intelligence. It examined how people use stories to make sense of the world and how this could inform computer design, with chapters on narrative generation, agents participating in stories, and tools for storytellers. [ref: Narrative Intelligence, John Benjamins]

== Computational narrative research ==
Stories often leave characters' motives and connections between events unstated. In a 2016 position paper, Mark O. Riedl identified the background knowledge and causal inferences needed to understand such stories as obstacles for computational systems.

Story generation also requires attention to characters' motives. In their 2010 paper Narrative Planning: Balancing Plot and Character, Mark O. Riedl and R. Michael Young developed a planning method that incorporated character goals into plot generation. They evaluated it by testing readers' understanding of the characters' intentions. [ref: Narrative Planning: Balancing Plot and Character, Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research]

In his 2016 paper, Riedl proposed applications in entertainment and training, as well as using stories to explain AI decisions and teach machines social norms. His paper also discussed difficulties with figurative language and causal connections across long passages.

In a 2023 study of visual storytelling, Brett A. Halperin and Stephanie M. Lukin analyzed 100 stories composed from image sequences, examining characterization, visual grounding, and narrative bias. [ref: Envisioning Narrative Intelligence: A Creative Visual Storytelling Anthology, Association for Computing Machinery]

== Information operations and disinformation ==
In information operations, narratives connect events and actors to explain what is happening. They are not necessarily deceptive or hostile. Strategic narratives can support democratic communication or be used to manipulate audiences.

In a study published by Spain's Ministry of Defence, Viktoriia Romaniuk and Yevhen Fedchenko examined recurring narratives in Russian disinformation about Ukraine and how they are adapted to events and audiences. For example, the portrayal of Ukraine as a failed state recurs across different messages, giving otherwise separate claims a common interpretation. They also discussed identifying influential sources and mapping the connections between them.

Analysts can draw on open-source intelligence to trace narratives across news outlets and social media. In a 2024 Foreign Policy Research Institute article, EdgeTheory chief executive Joe Stradinger illustrated theme tracing, source mapping, and changes in amplification using coverage of NATO and the war in Ukraine. [ref: Narrative Intelligence: Detecting Chinese and Russian Information Operations to Disrupt NATO Unity, Foreign Policy Research Institute]

DARPA's completed Narrative Networks program investigated how narratives influence cognition and behavior through quantitative analysis, neurobiological research, and modeling. [ref: Narrative Networks, DARPA] A Joint Special Operations University study by Troy Troublefield examined narrative intelligence in internet-based military information support operations, with attention to emotional connection, contextualization, and counternarratives. [ref: Narrative Intelligence in Internet-Based Military Information Support Operations: A Cyberpsychology Perspective Under the Irregular Warfare Construct, Joint Special Operations University]

=== AI methods ===
One approach to disinformation narrative mining combines large language models with clustering methods: models extract claims from text, and clustering groups them by similarity in meaning to identify shared narratives.

DiNaM, presented by Witold Sosnowski and colleagues at EMNLP in 2025, applies this approach to false claims extracted from fact-checking articles. It generates descriptions of the resulting groups, which the authors evaluated against narratives compiled by experts. [ref: DiNaM: Disinformation Narrative Mining with Large Language Models, Association for Computational Linguistics]
[truncated]

Draft text:

William Gill (1795 – 14 September 1863) was a British-born surgeon and naturalist who practiced in the Cape Colony. He is best known for the large bequest in his will that established Gill College in Somerset East (today KwaNojoli), one of the older educational institutions in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. [ref: Gill College – Sursum Prorsusque – Upwards and Onwards]

== Early life and training ==
Gill was born in Market Harborough, Leicestershire, in 1795 to the Reverend George Gill and his wife (name unknown). [ref: Cape Province. Probate Records 1861–1862, 1863] He started work in Wellingborough, Northamptonshire in 1810 as a medical apprentice to Thomas Peck, under whom he was indentured for five years, subsequently studying medicine at the University of Glasgow. He became a member of the Royal College of Surgeons of England in 1817 and a licentiate of the Society of Apothecaries in 1818. He spent a year travelling in continental Europe, during which he developed a lasting interest in botany. [ref: S2A3 Biographical Database of Southern African Science, www.s2a3.org.za]

== Career in the Cape Colony ==
Gill arrived at the Cape Colony in June 1818 and was licensed to practise as a surgeon, obstetrician and pharmacist later that year. [ref: Cape of Good Hope Government Gazette, 16 September 1862, "List of the medical practitioners in the Cape Colony"] He initially served as the district surgeon at Caledon and later settled in the Zwartland district (near present-day Malmesbury) in 1822, where he was noted for his work during a typhoid outbreak.

In 1826 he undertook an expedition northward for hunting and natural-history collecting, reaching as far as Kuruman, where he met the explorer and geologist Andrew Geddes Bain. He suffered heavy losses when his wagons were destroyed and returned to Cape Town in 1827, before trekking inland again. Around 1830 he collected plant and shell fossils along the Sundays River near Uitenhage. [ref: Botanical Exploration of Southern Africa, SANBI] [ref: Notes on South African geology, South African Quarterly Journal, 1830, No. 4]

On the recommendation of Dr James Barry and the Reverend George Thom, Gill was appointed district surgeon of the newly established settlement of Somerset (later Somerset East) in 1829 at £100 per annum. [ref: South Africa: its medical history 1652-1898; a medical and social study, Struik] He maintained a private practice there for many years and was a respected member of the local community, with a wide circle of friends and known for his generosity. When the district surgeoncy was abolished in 1845, Gill declined an alternative appointment as resident surgeon on Robben Island, instead opting for an annual pension of £50 and continued to practice medicine in the town. He acquired a number of farms in the district and became a wealthy merino sheep farmer.

He co-founded the Somerset Reading Society in 1832 and was a member of the Literary, Scientific and Medical Society of Grahamstown [ref: Grahamstown Journal, 15 March 1856, p. 2, "Literary, Scientific and Medical Society"]. He continued to collect botanical specimens, particularly orchids, and sold approximately 400 specimens to Thom that eventually reached the Herbarium at Kew Gardens. Several plant species, including Myrsine gilliana [ref: [https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn%3Alsid%3Aipni.org%3Anames%3A589125-1 Myrsine gilliana Sond. | Plants of the World Online | Kew Science]], Aspalathus gillii (renamed Aspalathus setacea) [ref: ] and Erica gillii [ref: ], were named after him.
== Death and legacy ==
Gill, unmarried, died of oedema on 14 September 1863 in Somerset East, aged 68. [ref: Obituary, Eastern Province Herald] [ref: Dictionary of South African biography, Nasional Boekhandel Bpk. for National Council for Social Research, Dept. of Higher Education] In his will dated 19 January 1863 he left the bulk of his estate, approximately £23 000, for the formation and future maintenance of a higher educational institution in the Eastern Province. Local residents raised funds for the buildings. The Gill College Corporation was formed, land was granted in 1867, and the college opened on 18 March 1869. Its architecture was modelled on that of the University of Glasgow. [ref: Dr William Gill of Somerset East] Originally intended as a university college, it later became a high school (from 1903) and continues today as a co-educational dual-medium school.

Gill was originally laid to rest in the town's cemetery at the foot of the Boschberg. In 1916 his remains were reinterred in front of the college, and a monument to him was erected in 1923 alongside his grave.

==Further reading==
* A History of Medicine in South Africa Up to the End of the Nineteenth Century, A.A. Balkema
* Journals of Andrew Geddes Bain: trader, explorer, soldier, road engineer and geologist, Van Riebeeck Society

Axel Hutter (born 1961 in Berlin) is a German philosopher and university lecturer.

==Life==
===Academic career===

Hutter studied philosophy, German studies, musicology and medicine at the Free University of Berlin (FU Berlin) from 1982 to 1988. In Berlin, his philosophy tutors were Michael Theunissen and Ernst Tugendhat. He completed his medical studies with the state examination and was granted a licence to practise medicine. His Master’s thesis, ‘Plato’s Modernity in the Light of Platonic Modernity’, marked the completion of his philosophy studies. He was awarded his doctorate in 1993 at the Free University of Berlin with his doctoral thesis ‘Historical Reason: The Continuation of Kant’s Critique of Reason in Schelling’s Late Philosophy’. Both his Master’s thesis and doctoral thesis were supervised by Michael Theunissen.

From 1994 to 1998, Hutter was a lecturer at the Institute of Philosophy at the Free University of Berlin; from 1998 to 2006, he was a research fellow at the Institute of Philosophy at the Ruhr University Bochum and at the Hegel Archive there. In Bochum, he obtained his habilitation in philosophy with the book ‘The Interest of Reason. Kant’s Original Insight and Its Development in the Major Works of Transcendental Philosophy’. The habilitation thesis was supervised by Walter Jaeschke.

Since March 2006, Axel Hutter has held the Chair of Theoretical Philosophy at the Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich. Since 2025, he has also been a visiting professor at the Institute of Philosophy in Leipzig.

===Scholarships and awards===
* University scholarship (1982–1988) and doctoral scholarship (1990–1992) from the German National Academic Foundation (Studienstiftung)
* Habilitation scholarship (1995–1998) from the German Research Foundation (DFG)
* Awarded the ‘[https://cas.au.dk/filosofi-og-idehistorie/forskningsprogram/annual-justus-hartnack-lecture Justus Hartnack Lecture]’ in Aarhus, Denmark (2008)

==Works==

Axel Hutter conducts research and teaches in the field of contemporary theoretical philosophy. From a systematic perspective, his main areas of focus are the philosophy of language, epistemology, the theory of rationality and metaphysics; his historical focus lies on classical German philosophy and classical analytic philosophy. His research is devoted to the development of a narrative ontology that rethinks the relationship between meaning (language) and being (the world) by granting meaning systematic priority over being.

===I. Historical Reason===

In Historical Reason [ref: ], Axel Hutter examines the systematic structure and epistemological claims of Schelling’s late philosophy. His central aim is to reconstruct positive philosophy as a continuation of Kant’s critical philosophy under historical conditions. Hutter thus refutes interpretations that see Schelling’s late work as a departure from the rationality of the Enlightenment.

Central to the argument is the thesis that Schelling does not abandon the idea of reason, but rather gives it a historical turn. Drawing on key texts – in particular from the Philosophy of Mythology and the Philosophy of Revelation – Hutter demonstrates that Schelling no longer understands reason primarily as a transcendental structure, but as a force that unfolds historically. The distinction between myth and revelation thus appears as an expression of the historical articulation of the Absolute.

Schelling’s philosophy is thus conceived as an attempt at a rationality that does not ignore the factual and the contingent, but integrates them into reason’s self-understanding. This form of ‘historical reason’ differs from Hegel’s speculative idealism without sacrificing systematic coherence.

===II. The Interest of Reason===

In The Interest of Reason [ref: ], Hutter analyses a central yet frequently overlooked concept in Kantian philosophy: the notion of the ‘interest of reason’. The starting point is the observation that Kant himself speaks on several occasions of the ‘true interest of pure reason’ without systematically elaborating this concept. Hutter takes up this hint and develops from it a guiding category that brings the three Critiques – Critique of Pure Reason, Critique of Practical Reason and Critique of Judgement – into a coherent whole.

The aim of the study is to reconstruct the internal connection between theoretical, practical and aesthetic-teleological reason from the perspective of a common interest. This ‘interest’ is not to be understood in psychological or subjective terms, but rather structurally: it denotes reason’s intrinsic claim to assert its own unity, freedom and final purpose. Hutter demonstrates that the pursuit of knowledge, moral action and aesthetic judgement are based on a common rational orientation, which finds expression in this interest.

Particular focus is placed on the transition from theoretical to practical reason. Hutter argues that reason is not merely a cognitive faculty, but necessarily also an active one. Moral legislation appears not as a mere postulate, but as an expression of a rational interest that finds its form in the idea of freedom. The third critique, on the power of judgement, is also situated within this structure: according to Hutter, it represents a mediating level in which reason’s interest in the unity of nature and freedom, of what is and what ought to be, comes to light.

Syed Naqi Haider Naqvi, T.I. (popularly known as S. N. Haider Naqvi, T.I.) is a Pakistani investigative journalist, political columnist, news analyst, media executive, advertising administrator, telecommunications pioneer, sports administrator, and regulatory official. Widely recognized among Pakistan's top-tier media figures, he is known for breaking high-profile investigative reports and authoring news columns on state governance, national political developments, defense affairs, media regulation, and cricket administration.

He serves as an official Executive Member of the Authority at the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) representing Sindh, as well as a regular senior analyst on flagship political talk shows across Pakistan's premier news networks, including Geo News and ARY News (notably as a panelist on The Reporters). He is the founder and CEO of the advertising, PR, and media agency CLICKCOM, previously served as the Chief Executive Officer of the Pakistan Super League (PSL) franchise Multan Sultans during its inaugural season, is the CEO and founder of Urdu news network StarNews Pakistan, was the founder and CEO of satellite network TV2Day, led network infrastructure modernization during Pakistan's 3G/4G telecom transformation, and currently serves as the Chief Executive Officer of the international satellite channel Ocean News UK. In 2024, he was conferred the Tamgha-e-Imtiaz (Medal of Excellence) by the President of Pakistan for his contributions to journalism.

== Early life and education ==
Naqvi is the son of **Syed Shabbir Hussain Naqvi** (1937–2013), a well-known Pakistani social worker and philanthropist noted for his extensive contributions to community welfare, humanitarian projects, and social relief initiatives across the country. Following his passing in June 2013, official state condolence messages were issued by top national leadership—including President of Pakistan Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, PTI Chairman Imran Khan, Chairman Senate Nayyar Bukhari, and Speaker National Assembly Sardar Ayaz Sadiq—acknowledging his distinguished social services and extending condolences to Haider Naqvi and the bereaved family.

Naqvi earned his Bachelor of Engineering degree from the prestigious NED University of Engineering and Technology in Karachi. During his university years, he was a prominent student leader, serving as President of the NED student body during his tenure. Demonstrating leadership and technical distinction during his academic career, he later leveraged his engineering and administrative background to lead major telecommunications infrastructure projects, corporate media management, advertising, sports governance, broadcast journalism, media entrepreneurship, and public media regulation.

== Career ==

=== Advertising, PR, & CLICKCOM ===
Naqvi expanded his corporate operations into strategic communications and media representation by founding **CLICKCOM**, a full-service advertising, public relations (PR), and media agency. As CEO of CLICKCOM, he led corporate branding, strategic media buying, nation-wide advertising campaigns, and corporate PR strategies for various public and private sector clients in Pakistan and abroad.

=== Media entrepreneurship, StarNews Pakistan & TV2Day ===
In the mid-2000s, during the expansion of private electronic media in Pakistan, Naqvi established **TV2Day**, an independent satellite television network headquartered in Karachi. Upon launching the channel, he gained widespread national attention as one of the country's youngest television network owners and CEOs.

During his tenure as head of TV2Day in 2006, Naqvi was invited to an official meeting by the then President of Pakistan, General Pervez Musharraf, to discuss electronic media expansion, broadcasting policy, and national current affairs.

Expanding his media network, Naqvi founded and serves as CEO of **StarNews Pakistan**, an Urdu-language news organization that developed into one of Pakistan's widely followed digital and broadcast current affairs outlets. Under his leadership, StarNews Pakistan focuses on breaking political coverage, investigative reporting, regional news, and current affairs analysis.

=== National initiatives & "I'M Pakistan" Conference ===
Naqvi organized the national **"I'M Pakistan" Conference**, a public recognition platform designed to honor citizens, public figures, and veterans who rendered distinguished services to Pakistan. The conference was attended by national leadership, with the then Prime Minister of Pakistan, Yousuf Raza Gillani, presiding as the Chief Guest to present honors and recognize the contributions of key national achievers.

=== Digital media presence, political engagement, & Indian media censorship ===
Naqvi maintains a significant digital presence on X (formerly Twitter), where his reporting and analytical commentary on national policy, constitutional matters, and governance regularly reach key decision-makers. His social media posts and exclusive news breaks are frequently reshared, cited, or endorsed by top state leadership and prominent politicians, including the Prime Minister of Pakistan, the President of Pakistan, Chief Minister of Punjab Maryam Nawaz, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari, and Sindh provincial minister Syed Nasir Hussain Shah.

Chinmay Pandya (born 9 April 1976) is an Indian psychiatrist and academic administrator. He serves as the Pro Vice-Chancellor of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya (DSVV) in Haridwar, Uttarakhand, and is a senior representative of the All World Gayatri Pariwar (AWGP), founded by his grandfather Shriram Sharma. His public work focuses on education, youth development, and interfaith dialogue.

== Early life and medical training ==
Pandya was born on 9 April 1976 in Indore, Madhya Pradesh, and was raised at Shantikunj in Haridwar. He completed his Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) from the Himalayan Institute of Medical Sciences in Dehradun. He subsequently pursued postgraduate medical training in the United Kingdom, obtaining a postgraduate diploma in Public Health and becoming a member of the Royal College of Psychiatrists (MRCPsych).

Between 2002 and 2010, Pandya practiced within the United Kingdom's National Health Service (NHS). His clinical appointments included work as an associate specialist in older adult psychiatric services with the West London Mental Health Trust, focusing on neurocognitive disorders and dementia management. In 2010, he returned to India to take up institutional responsibilities at Shantikunj and DSVV.

== Academic and public roles ==
As Pro Vice-Chancellor of Dev Sanskriti Vishwavidyalaya, Pandya oversees institutional administration, international partnerships, and academic development. In his capacity as a representative of All World Gayatri Pariwar, he coordinates various national and global outreach programs, including cultural awareness and centenary campaigns. [ref: Three Jyoti Kalash Chariots depart from Shantikunj to spread message of centenary celebrations, Asian News International] [ref: Gayatri Parivar’s Jyoti Kalash Chariots begin Yatra for centenary, Asianet News]

He has participated in interfaith and international dialogues, speaking on ethics, mental health, and Indian philosophy at academic and intergovernmental forums. He has also served in advisory capacities for statutory bodies, including the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR).

== Personal life ==
Pandya is married to Shefali Pandya, and they have two children. He is the son of Pranav Pandya and Sailbala Pandya.

== References ==

Rohit Shanmukhappa is an Indian actor and film producer who works primarily in Kannada cinema. A model and theatre artist, Rohit made his lead acting debut in the 2024 Kannada feature film Raktaksha, directed by Vasudeva S. N. and produced by Rohit under the Sai Production banner. [ref: Model-turned-actor Rohit turns lead with Raktaksha, Cinema Express] [ref: Rohit's debut 'Raktaksha' locks release date, The New Indian Express] [ref: Kannada Movie Review-Rakthaksha: Drugs, suspense and violence, Bangalore Mirror] [ref: ರಕ್ತಸಿಕ್ತ ಕಥೆ ಹೊತ್ತ ರಕ್ತಾಕ್ಷ, Chittara] [ref: ರೋಹಿತ್ ಕಣ್ಣಲ್ಲಿ ರಕ್ತಾಕ್ಷ ಕನಸು, Roopatara] He was previously cast in a negative role in the unreleased film AB Positive.
== Early life and career ==
Rohit is from Mudgal in Raichur district, Karnataka. He began his career in modelling and gained experience in theatre before entering feature films. Public TV reported in May 2023 that Rohit had six years of modelling experience and two years of theatre experience before entering films. Media coverage described him as a model and theatre artist during his transition to cinema. Rohit has said that becoming an artiste was a childhood ambition. In connection with Raktaksha, he said he underwent multiple physical transformations for the role and sought to establish himself through his work in cinema. [ref: 'ರಕ್ತಾಕ್ಷ' ಸಿನಿಮಾ ಮೂಲಕ ಬೆಳ್ಳಿತೆರೆಗೆ ಮಾಡೆಲ್, Kannada Prabha] [ref: 'ರಕ್ತಾಕ್ಷ’ ಸಿನಿಮಾ ಮೂಲಕ ಸ್ಯಾಂಡಲ್ ವುಡ್ ಗೆ ಕಾಲಿಟ್ಟ ಮಾಡೆಲ್, Public TV]
[ref: Raktaksha film review: ಪ್ರತೀಕಾರದ ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಘಾತಕಾರಿ ಮಾಫಿಯಾ, ಪ್ರೇಕ್ಷಕ ಕೂಡ ಅಚ್ಚರಿ, Asianet Suvarna News]
== Film career ==
Raktaksha marked Rohit Shanmukhappa's lead acting debut in Kannada cinema. Directed by Vasudeva S. N., the film was produced by Rohit under the Sai Production banner and was released in July 2024. Actor Pramod Shetty played the antagonist. The film's title track was sung by actor and playback singer Vasishta N. Simha. Actors Vijay Raghavendra and Suman Nagarkar attended the film's trailer launch, where the release date was announced. [ref: Rohit's debut 'Raktaksha' locks release date, The New Indian Express] At a title-track launch event in May 2023, Rohit said that Raktaksha was inspired by true incidents and would incorporate a reverse-screenplay concept. In a July 2024 feature in *Chittara*, Rohit discussed the challenges of acting in and producing *Raktaksha* simultaneously. He said his responsibilities extended beyond acting to overseeing different production departments and addressing problems that arose during filming. He also discussed the financial risks of filmmaking and the need to work within the available budget.
Following its release in July 2024, Raktaksha was reviewed by Kannada entertainment publications. Bangalore Mirror discussed the film's crime-thriller storyline, suspense and action sequences, and commented on Rohit's performance. In its review, Asianet Suvarna News rated the film three out of five stars and described Rohit as a promising talent in Kannada cinema.[8] CiniMirror's review described Rohit's performance as conveying vulnerability, anger and charm. [ref: Raktaksha Kannada Movie Review: An Gripping Revenge Thriller, CiniMirror] In an August 2024 interview with CiniMirror, Rohit discussed his experience of acting in and producing Raktaksha. He described the experience of producing the film and spoke about his plans to continue acting and develop further film projects. [ref: North Karnataka Witnesses a New Star, CiniMirror]
== Reception ==

Reviews of Raktaksha discussed its action sequences, suspense and revenge storyline. In its review published on 28 July 2024, Bangalore Mirrorpraised the handling of the action sequences and the film's thriller and dramatic elements [ref: Kannada Movie Review-Rakthaksha: Drugs, suspense and violence, Bangalore Mirror]. A review published by Kannada Prabha on 27 July 2024 described Rohit as a promising talent in Kannada cinema for his portrayal of a man seeking revenge for his younger brother's death. [ref: ಕ್ರೈಮ್, ಸಸ್ಪೆನ್ಸ್, ಥ್ರಿಲ್ಲರ್‌ ನೆರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾಗುವ ಪ್ರತೀಕಾರದ ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಘಾತಕಾರಿ ಮಾಫಿಯಾ, Kannada Prabha]
== Awards and nominations ==
Rohit Shanmukhappa was nominated for Best Debut Actor for his performance in Raktaksha at the sixth Chandanavana Film Critics Awards, according to a report published by The Hans India on 5 May 2025. [ref: VI Chandanavana Film Critics Awards 2025 nominations announced, The Hans India]

Marilou "Malou" Flores-Morillo is a Filipino businesswoman, philanthropist, and politician from Oriental Mindoro. She made history as the first female city mayor of Calapan, serving from 2022 to 2025.

==Early Life and Business Career==
Before entering public service, Morillo established herself in the private sector as a prominent corporate executive and entrepreneur. In 1994, she founded Sixteen Enterprises, a heavy equipment operations and commercial trading firm based in Calapan City. Deeply involved in social and civic work, she launched the Morillo Foundation in 2019 to spearhead local philanthropic, educational, and livelihood development initiatives across the province.

==Political Career==
===2022 Calapan City Mayoralty Campaign===
Morillo entered local politics by running for the mayoral seat of Calapan City during the May 2022 local elections under the Aksyon Demokratiko banner. She won her first public office by securing 36,452 votes, defeating incumbent vice mayor Gil Ramirez of Mindoro Bago Sarili (39,824 votes) and lawyer Gilbert Repizo of PDP–Laban (12,040 votes). She officially took her oath of office on June 30, 2022.

===Mayor of Calapan (2022–2025)===
Upon assuming office, Morillo introduced her flagship "Green Calapan" administrative platform, which focused on balancing city-wide economic advancement and infrastructural upgrades with environmental protection and public safety.

Her term was characterized by high administrative marks:
* Government Performance: Under her leadership, Calapan City ranked first nationwide in the Government Efficiency and Resiliency Pillars during the 10th Cities and Municipalities Competitiveness Index (CMCI) Summit.
* National Recognition: In November 2024, the Civil Service Commission and Gawad Pilipino named her one of the "Most Outstanding Mayor" awardees in the Philippines for her excellence in executive governance and community program delivery.
* Regional Hub Development: She successfully collaborated with regional departments to establish major administrative infrastructure, including securing the groundbreaking of the DENR MIMAROPA Regional Office in Barangay Sapul, alongside initiating the construction of the Calapan City Heritage, Culture, and Arts Building.

===2025 Re-election Bid===
In the May 2025 local elections, Morillo sought a consecutive second term under the local Galing sa Puso Movement (GSM) coalition. However, she was unseated by returning mayor and former congressman Paulino Salvador "Doy" Leachon. Following the transition of power, Morillo officially stepped down from office upon the expiration of her term on June 30, 2025.

Beta Systems Software AG is a German software provider that develops intelligent automation and orchestration solutions for IT operations. [ref: Key Takeaways: 2024 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Service Orchestration and Automation Platforms, Solutions Review] [ref: Beta Systems erweitert SSO-System, Computerwoche] The company develops products that can be accessed through the cloud, on-premises, and through a software as a service (SaaS) model. [ref: Beta Systems: Comprehensive IT Products & Solutions, Beta Systems]

The company is headquartered in Berlin, in the Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf borough, and has subsidiaries in other countries. [ref: Beta Systems zieht an den Berliner Ernst-Reuter-Platz, IZ]

== History ==

Beta Systems was founded in 1983 by Alfred Tauchnitz, Bill Schmidt, and James Henderson. [ref: Die Lage der Firma war dramatisch, Berliner Morgenpost] [ref: Beta Systems geht in den Neuen Markt, Der Tagesspiegel] In the same year, the company introduced its first product, the Beta 91 Quality Management System, for quality assurance of input data. [ref: Beta Systems hat das Angebot für Rechenzentren aufpoliert, Computerwoche] This was followed by Beta 92 Process History Manager, a product for controlling and archiving job logs. [ref: Moderne Verknüpfung von Mainframe mit offener Serverwelt, eGovernment] In 1987, Beta Systems released Beta 93, its report distribution and print management system. [ref: Beta Systems, Computerwoche]

In 1991, Beta Systems was converted into a stock corporation. [ref: Beta Systems jetzt eine AG, Computerwoche] The company became one of the first companies in its industry to have an initial public offering on the Neuer Markt in 1997. [ref: Beta Systems geht in den Neuen Markt, Der Tagesspiegel] [ref: Beta Systems: Teilrückzug des Firmengründers, Computerwoche] A year later, Beta Systems acquired Harbor Systems Management. [ref: One-time charges drive Beta Systems further into the red, Tech Monitor] [ref: Neuer Firmenchef will Beta Systems aus der Krise führen, Computerwoche]

In April 2000, Harbor's storage division was transferred to Beta Systems' Boulder, Colorado-based subsidiary, Tantia Technologies.

Beta Systems acquired Systor Security Solutions in 2003. [ref: Systor sells security business to Beta Systems, Tech Monitor] The following year, it acquired a majority stake in Kleindienst Datentechnik AG. [ref: Beta Systems greift nach Kleindienst Datentechnik, Computerwoche]

Beta Systems acquired SI Software Innovation in 2008. [ref: Beta Systems übernimmt SI Software Innovation, Finance Magazin] In 2009, the company acquired Detec Decision Technology Software and Detec Software Products. [ref: Beta Systems übernimmt Detec, IT-Times] In the same year, Beta Systems chief executive officer Kamyar Niroumand was dismissed from his position. No reason was given for his dismissal. [ref: Neuer Firmenchef will Beta Systems aus der Krise führen, Computerwoche]

In 2012, Beta Systems sold Detec Software to Unicorn Systems. [ref: Beta Systems Software AG verkauft Tochtergesellschaft DETEC Software GmbH an UNICOM Systems, Inc., PresseBox] Beta Systems also acquired the Munich-based software developer Horizont Software. [ref: Beta Systems acquires Horizont Software GmbH, Conectronica]

At the end of 2017, Beta Systems acquired Lynet Kommunikation AG. [ref: Beta Systems Software AG: Acquisition of LYNET Kommunikation AG, EQS Group AG] In February 2018, the company also acquired Auconet / Asdis GmbH. [ref: Beta Systems acquires Auconet / Asdis GmbH, PresseBox]

MUGnet is a Japanese fan-based circle that creates visual novels.

== Overview ==
Under the slogan "Questioning the World," the circle creates works that explore philosophical themes such as perspectives on life and happiness. Its works are characterized by a fusion of story-driven scenarios and graphic expressions that enhance immersion. Through the visual novels it produces, the circle offers players a different perspective on the world.

The circle's name, "MUGnet," is a portmanteau combining English slang, the nature of the circle's activities, and the homonym "magnet." Zakinu, one of the founders, revealed in an official note post that the name was derived from the following two elements. [ref: MUGnetについて語る, note]

* MUG： English slang meaning a "fool" or "gullible person."
* net：Derived from the internet-based nature of their activities.

Although the spelling differs from the actual English word "magnet," this is intentional rather than a typo.

It conveys the meaning that "fools (MUG) active on the internet (net) attract or involve people like a magnet."

== History ==

* July 17, 2024 – Established for creative activities. [ref: MUGnet 1周年記念特設サイト, mugnet.jp]
* December 30, 2024 – Released their debut work, Journey to die, at Comic Market 105 (C105).
* May 2025 – Featured in an interview by the indie game event DREAMSCAPE, discussing the circle's origins and production structure.
* July 17 – 31, 2025 – Offered Journey to die at a 50% discount on the official BOOTH store to commemorate the circle's 1st anniversary.
* August 17, 2025 – Participated in Comic Market 106 (C106).

* April 2026 – Bonten Sekai no Kowashikata was featured in the serial column "Mirai no Game ni Tsuite Ohanashi Shimasu" by Kosaku Akano in the April 2026 issue of S-F Magazine.
* July 17, 2026 – Opened a special website to commemorate the circle's 2nd anniversary, featuring statements from MUGnet members.
* August 16, 2026 – Participated in Comic Market 108 (C108).

In May 2025, an interview with MUGnet's representative members, Zakinu and Usagi Moto, was published as part of a serialized feature in the indie game media outlet DREAMSCAPE. The interview covered topics such as the circle being composed primarily of junior and senior high school students, the background behind the production of Journey to die, and the division of roles in scenario writing and system development.

According to the interview, the circle is mainly composed of junior and senior high school students, and the members discussed the production background of Journey to die along with their division of roles in scenario and system development. [ref: DREAMSCAPE JOURNAL#20 【MUGnet】｜DREAMSCAPE, note（ノート）]

In 2026, Bonten Sekai no Kowashikata was featured in Kosaku Akano's serialized column "Mirai no Game ni Tsuite Ohanashi Shimasu" in the April 2026 issue of S-F Magazine. Carlos "Caloy" B. Brucal (October 4, 1946 – December 24, 2011) was a veteran Filipino politician and lawyer who played an instrumental role in the foundational growth and early governance of Calapan City, Oriental Mindoro. Alongside Arnan Panaligan and Doy Leachon, he is recognized as one of the co-founding city mayors who steered Calapan during its developmental years following its transition from a municipality.

==Early Political Career and Vice Mayoralty (1995–2004)==
Brucal served as the Vice Mayor of Calapan under then-Municipal Mayor Arnan Panaligan. When Republic Act No. 8475 was ratified on March 21, 1998, converting Calapan into a component city, Brucal made local history by becoming the first City Vice Mayor of Calapan. As the presiding officer of the last Sangguniang Bayan and the inaugural Sangguniang Panlungsod, he led the first generation of city councilors through the legislative transitions required for early cityhood.

==Mayor of Calapan (2004–2007)==
Following his vice mayoral tenure, Brucal successfully ran for the local chief executive position and served as the Mayor of Calapan from June 30, 2004, to June 30, 2007.
His mayoral administration was marked by several local milestones:
* The City College of Calapan (CCC): While the original vision for a local government-managed tertiary institution was conceived under the Panaligan administration, Mayor Brucal drove the actual groundwork. In 2005, Brucal formed the technical working group that conducted structural feasibility studies, directly laying the foundations for the official establishment of the institution.
* Crisis Management: In December 2005, his administration led emergency relief and infrastructure response efforts when severe flash floods submerged 48 out of Calapan's 62 barangays, prompting the local government to place the city under a state of calamity.
* Administrative Strategy: His term introduced localized corporate management practices to the local government unit through his "8-Point Agenda" structural program.
Upon the expiration of his term in 2007, he was succeeded in office by Paulino Salvador Leachon.

==Personal and Family Life==
Brucal was married to Luzviminda S. Brucal. His family remains active in public service in the province; his son, C. Voltaire "Bong" S. Brucal, entered local politics and served as a multi-term city councilor, Vice Mayor of Calapan (2013–2016), and currently serves as a Member of the Provincial Board representing the 1st District of Oriental Mindoro.

He pursued a PhD in educational and organizational leadership at National University￼ and enrolled in a Doctor of Philosophy program in Educational Leadership at Liberty University in 2026. His theological writings concern Christian faith, salvation, redemption, charismatic manifestations and the history of Christianity in Rwanda.

== Early life and background ==
Kanyabigega was born in Rwanda and later relocated to the United States, where he continued his involvement in Christian ministry, theological education and religious publishing.

His religious activities have involved Christian communities in Rwanda, the United States and the African Great Lakes region.

== Education ==

=== Doctor of Ministry — Unification Theological Seminary ===
Kanyabigega earned a Doctor of Ministry (D.Min.) from Unification Theological Seminary in Barrytown, New York, on 26 May 2018.

His doctoral education included spiritual formation, theological and ethical perspectives on ministerial leadership, transformational leadership, religious education, family ministry, social justice and research methodology.

His academic program included doctoral research and dissertation work in family and educational ministry. His academic transcript records 34 completed credits and a cumulative grade point average of 3.56.

Between 2022 and 2026, Kanyabigega successively completed all coursework for a Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Educational and Organizational Leadership at National University in California.

His studies included educational leadership theories, diversity and social justice, educational policy, educational administration, finance and budgeting, research methodology, statistical analysis, qualitative research and dissertation preparation.

His academic record includes a doctoral comprehensive assessment and dissertation proposal coursework.

A transcript issued on 28 September 2026 records 54 earned doctoral credits and a cumulative grade point average of 3.51.

=== Ph.D. studies — Liberty University ===
In 2026, Kanyabigega enrolled in the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) in Educational Leadership program at Liberty University in Lynchburg, Virginia.

His continuing studies concern educational leadership, educational research, organizational development and the relationship between leadership practices and educational outcomes.

== Christian ministry and organizational leadership ==

=== Movement for Christ in Rwanda ===
Kanyabigega has been involved in Christian evangelism and religious education in Rwanda.

A ministerial order published in Rwanda's Official Gazette on 5 April 2010 identified Kanyabigega as the authorized legal representative of Mouvement pour Christ au Rwanda (MPCR), with Eraste Ndayisenga as deputy legal representative. The organization has been associated with Christian evangelism, biblical teaching and community-oriented ministry.

=== International Movement for Christ ===
Kanyabigega has been associated with International Movement for Christ (IMC), a Christian ministry organization involved in evangelism, theological education and religious outreach.

The organization's activities have included Christian teaching, leadership development, religious communication and proposed community development initiatives in Rwanda and other parts of the African Great Lakes region.

=== International Movement for Christ Theological Seminary ===
Kanyabigega has been associated with International Movement for Christ Theological Seminary (IMCTS), an organization providing theological instruction and Christian ministerial training.

Its educational activities have focused on biblical studies, theology, pastoral ministry, Christian leadership and the preparation of religious workers.

=== Ministry in the United States ===
Kanyabigega has been associated with the Free Methodist Church tradition in the United States.

A January 2025 profile published by Ukweli Times discussed his Christian ministry and evangelistic activities, including work connected with presentations of the Jesus Film in Rwanda.

His ministry activities have included preaching, biblical instruction, pastoral leadership and Christian education.

Kanyabigega has participated in Christian media initiatives intended to provide religious teaching to audiences in Rwanda and internationally.

These initiatives include Kwizera Yesu TV, a Christian video broadcasting project, and Radio Kwizera, an online Christian radio service.

Their programming has included biblical teaching, Christian preaching, worship, evangelism and religious education.
