URINE is an American band from Albany, New York, formed in 2018. The band was founded by members Nick Hauprich and Jacob Roberts. initially as a joke project intended to release a single song. URINE's music incorporates elements of slam metal, grindcore, beatdown hardcore, industrial metal, death metal and electronic music. The band has released several recordings, including "NIGHT OF THE PISSING DEAD" (2021), "EXCRETA LOTIUM MIASMA" (2023) and "PEEMOCRACY" (2025).
[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]

== History ==

=== Formation And Early Years ===

URINE officially debuted with the release of their first song "F*** Mike Pence" on December 26th, 2018. After a couple of attempts to start a death metal band. Vocalist Nick Hauprich (Also known as Postal Malone) and drummer and producer Jacob Roberts (Also known as The Artist Formally Known As Sir Kix Alot, Casually Known As Jean Claude Van Damnation) made the first song with a laptop, and a USB microphone. Originally starting as a two-piece, in the upcoming months they would have more members join within the next couple of months. Very shortly after releasing their first song, they began working on their first EP, "URINE FOURSOME SHIT"
[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]
[ref: Metal Horror Pi*score!!!! Come take a bathroom break with us! We’re got urine!]

=== "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" & "URINE FOURSOME SHIT II: THE TRICKLING" ===
After the release of "F*** Mike Pence" in late 2018, the two founding members decided to go for a much more raw and sloppy sound with their next release. Very consistently stating that they originally did not take the project seriously, their first EP, named "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" opted out of using guitars, and instead had cello VST's ran through distortion effects to create the sound of the project. Everything was done for as cheap as possible, with most of the vocal recordings taking place in closets, and inside cars. "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" while very much non-serious in musical production, was political in message. It also featured future members, Stephen Harrington and Brandon Collins (Also known as his nickname Breo) on vocals for a song. The project was released in mid March of 2019.
Shortly after the release of "URINE FOURSOME SHIT" Breo (Known as PISS BARNES) joined as a full time vocalist alongside Nick. The three of them began work on what was supposed to be the first full length. A 53 song long concept album named "PISS INFUSED GUTTURAL TRASH. They switched from cellos, over to a multitude of guitar plugins and VST's and began writing the album, about a creature who comes to life after people starting urinating radioactive material on a garbage heap after a nuclear apocalypse. It was around this time that BJ Patrignani IV joined the band as his first character: 'Lord Diabeticus'.
However, after about 43 songs were completely instrumentally, and only a handful with recorded vocals, the laptop that Jacob was using became unusable, thus making the album completely lost media. Although a couple years later, a handful of them would be found in an email, and released on their first compilation album "GREATEST PISSES VOL. 1".
After a new laptop was obtained, a very immediate production came on the next release which would be called "URINE FOURSOME SHIT II: THE TRICKLING'. This EP would be much more serious in sound, but was much less politically driven. The EP would feature future URINE vocalist Frank Cogliando (Also known as DANK SINATRA). The EP was released in early October of 2019, just 7 months after the first. During this time URINE played its first shows, calling themselves 'death metal karaoke' and performing with Nick and Breo using microphones, and Jacob playing instrumentals over his laptop. They would perform twice with this set up.

[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]

=== "NIGHT OF THE PISSING DEAD" ===

After the loss of "PISS INFUSED GUTTURAL TRASH" and the subsequent release of "URINE FOURSOME SHIT II:THE TRICKLING", the now four manned URINE started their work on another full length album. Taking the name from classic horror movie "Night Of The Living Dead" they named this new project "NIGHT OF THE PISSING DEAD".
At this point, Frank Cogliando had joined, marking 4 vocalists (Nick, Breo, Frank and BJ) and Jacob continued to do production with DAWs. BJ's character 'Lord Diabeticus' was killed off, and his new character 'Gint Eastwood' took over.
Shortly after production began, COVID-19 swept through the world. This gave the members more time to work on the album. Going for a more sludgy and heavy sound, they started using more down-tuned tunings on the plugins, and taking inspiration from Vinnie Paul, Jacob and Nick used a lot of reverb on the drums.
During production, another issue came about with the computer being used to make the album. Unlike "PISS INFUSED GUTTURAL TRASH", they had taken precaution by emailing an almost finished version to themselves. They would not end up releasing "NIGHT OFTHE PISSING DEAD" until July, 21st, 2021. This would be the last album to include non-real guitars and bass. It would also be the last album to feature BJ Patrignani as a full time vocalist, as his character was killed off and he left the band in late 2021.
[ref: Urine - An Interview with Liam Sweeny]

Draft text:
Deaf President Now (DPN) was an eight day student protest at Gallaudet University in Washington, D.C. It started on March 6 and ended on March 13, 1988 (Gallaudet University). The reasoning for this is the Board of Trustees chose Elisabeth Zinser, a hearing woman, over two qualified deaf candidates, Dr. I. King Jordan and Dr. Harvey Corson, to be the seventh president of Gallaudet University (Gallaudet University). Since Gallaudet had been in existence for 124 years and had never had a deaf president leading the university, students and the deaf community were extremely angry about this decision. They felt that no one was allowing them to make decisions about their own education (Gallaudet University)

As a result, students, faculty, staff, and alumni came together and shut down the entire campus. They did this by barricading all of the gates, burning effigies, and holding press conferences to demand changes (Gallaudet University, n.d.). Some of the student leaders involved in organizing the protest were Greg Hlibok, Bridgetta Bourne-Firl, Tim Rarus, and Jerry Covell. These students worked behind the scenes to bring together various groups of deaf people to work toward a common goal.

For example, they were able to unite oral deaf students with culturally deaf students who use American Sign Language (Gallaudet University, n.d.; Rarus, n.d.). Protesters made four non-negotiable demands to the Board of Trustees before anyone would stop protesting: Elisabeth Zinser must resign immediately and a deaf president must be selected; Board Chair Jane Bassett Spilman must resign from her position; the Board of Trustees must be restructured so that at least 51% of its members are deaf; and no one will be punished or disciplined for participating in the protest (Gallaudet University, n.d.). By the end of the week, the protest was successful and the students achieved all four of their demands. Zinser resigned from her position, Spilman stepped down from her role as Board Chair, Phil Bravin became the first deaf individual to serve as chairperson of the Board of Trustees, and Dr. I. King Jordan was selected as Gallaudet's first deaf president in history (Bravin, n.d.; Gallaudet University, n.d.)

However, DPN did not only affect Gallaudet University. It served as a major turning point for disability rights throughout the United States. The momentum generated by DPN led directly to several significant pieces of legislation being enacted such as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) in 1990, the Closed Captioning Bill, and the Telecommunications Act of 1996 (Gallaudet University, n.d.; Rarus, n.d.). Most importantly, DPN fundamentally changed how hearing individuals perceive deaf individuals. It demonstrated to the entire world that what deaf individuals can accomplish far exceeds what they cannot hear (Gallaudet University, n.d.). This entire civil rights movement increased interest in American Sign Language courses offered at both high schools and colleges, provided more opportunities for deaf actors to appear on mainstream television programs and in movies, and provided deaf adults and children worldwide with a strong "Yes, I can" attitude that continues to inspire people today (Gallaudet University, n.d.; Rarus, n.d.).

"The impact of the Deaf President Now protest - The Deaf President Now (DPN) Protest". Gallaudet University. [ref: The impact of the Deaf President Now protest - The Deaf President Now (DPN) Protest, Gallaudet University]

"The Issues" Gallaudet University. [ref: The Issues - The Deaf President Now (DPN) Protest, Gallaudet University]

"The Deaf President Now: Profiles and viewpoints" Gallaudet University. [ref: Deaf President Now: Profiles and viewpoints - The Deaf President Now (DPN) Protest, Gallaudet University]

Yaser Natour (Al-Natour) is a Jordanian Speech and Language Pathologist and academic. Whose work has focused on voice disorders, swallowing disorders (dysphagia), resonance and neurogenic disorders. Golden Drum () is an international festival of creativity and advertising held annually in Slovenia since 1994. It is organised by the Slovenian Advertising Chamber (SOZ) and is usually held in the coastal resort of Portorož. [ref: 22nd Golden Drum announced its Multi Channel Jury, AdHugger] [ref: International Festival of Creativity Golden Drum, Culture.si (Ministry of Culture of Slovenia)] Founded as the Golden Drum Advertising Festival of New Europe, it became one of the principal regional advertising competitions for Central and Eastern Europe; it is now styled the Golden Drum International Festival of Creativity. [ref: Golden Drum is coming home to Portorož, Media Marketing] Its honorary president is the Slovenian advertising executive Jure Apih. [ref: About — Golden Drum Festival, Golden Drum]

== History ==
The first festival was held in Portorož in 1994; the 22nd edition took place in 2015, the 25th in 2018 and the 30th in 2024. [ref: Golden Drum Program Announced, Little Black Book] [ref: Golden Drum Festival Celebrates 30th Anniversary, Little Black Book] The tenth, jubilee festival in 2003 received 2,108 entries across its categories; the Golden Rose (Zlata vrtnica) award for the most successful agency went to Leo Burnett Prague. [ref: Končan festival Zlati boben, MMC RTV SLO] From 2007 until 2014 the festival took part in the Intercontinental Advertising CUP, a global competition rewarding local ideas that it ran together with ADFEST, FIAP and ADC*E.

At the 2016 festival 72 Silver Drums, 42 Golden Drums and 15 Grands Prix were awarded; McCann Worldgroup received the Golden Net award for the most successful network and Publicis Romania the Golden Rose award for the most successful agency. [ref: Who Came Out on Top at the 2016 Golden Drum Awards?, Little Black Book] In 2018 the 25th festival returned to Portorož and adopted a new visual identity designed by Luna\TBWA Ljubljana. The 2022 edition was held in Rovinj, Croatia.

The 30th anniversary festival took place on 9–10 October 2024 at the Grand Hotel Bernardin in Portorož. The 31st festival's awards show was held in Portorož on 14 October 2025, with winners from 40 European countries. [ref: Golden Drum 2025 Winners Announced at 31st Festival of Creativity, Little Black Book] The 2026 festival, held in Portorož on 12–13 October, awarded 43 Bronze, 46 Silver and 34 Golden Drums and 14 Grands Prix out of 187 shortlisted entries from 30 countries. LePub (Milan) was named both Network and Agency of the Year, hasan & partners (Helsinki) Independent Agency of the Year and McCann Skopje Adriatic Agency of the Year; the Brand Grand Prix went to Heineken. [ref: Golden Drum Announces the Winners of 2026, Golden Drum]

== Competition and awards ==
The festival presents a Golden Drum award to the winning entry in each category; the category groups are revised from edition to edition to reflect changes in advertising practice and media. Awards are given at Bronze, Silver and Golden Drum level as well as Grand Prix. The festival also runs the Young Drummers Competition for creatives under 30. Alongside the competition, the programme features lectures and workshops by international advertising professionals.

University of Limerick Aeronautical Society High Powered Rocketry (ULAS HiPR, colloquially HiPR) is a student-led high-power rocketry team at the University of Limerick in Ireland. [ref: About, ULAS HiPR] [ref: University of Limerick students pioneer a 3D-printed rocket engine, Limerick Leader] The team was reported to be the first group to represent the Republic of Ireland at the European Rocketry Challenge (EuRoC). == History ==
The team is reported to have been established in 2022 and to comprise more than 100 students from aeronautical, mechanical, software and design engineering. Another report states that it was set up by aeronautical engineering graduate Daire O'Sullivan in November 2023.

In July 2024 the team's rocket Morrígu was presented at the Mach-24 conference at Spaceport Machrihanish in Scotland, supported by sponsorship from Analog Devices, the team's first sponsor. [ref: UL rocketry team and Analog Devices announce stellar partnership, I Love Limerick] [ref: Lift-off for UL's Aeronautical Society high-powered rocketry as Analog Devices acts as support booster, Engineers Ireland] The team has also competed internationally at EuRoC in Portugal.

== Liquid rocket engine ==
The engine, named Lúin of Celtchar, is a 2 kN, water-cooled bipropellant design using isopropyl alcohol and nitrous oxide, designed by the student team. It is being produced using metal additive manufacturing at IMR's Advanced Manufacturing Lab in Mullingar, and is to be returned to the University of Limerick for machining and final assembly. The team was accepted into the UK-based Race2Space 2026 International Propulsion competition, its first year in that event and received "Best Newcomer" award

= Electronic Business One-Stop Shop in the Philippines =

== Overview ==
The Electronic Business One-Stop Shop (eBOSS) is an online system used by local government units (LGUs) in the Philippines to process business permit applications and related transactions. It allows business owners to submit documents, pay fees, and receive permits through an online platform. The system aims to simplify business registration and reduce the need for applicants to visit government offices in person. [ref: ARTA sets Nov. 1 deadline for LGUs to shift to online business permit processing – Philippine Information Agency]

== Legal basis ==
Republic Act No. 11032, also known as the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018, requires cities and municipalities to automate their business permitting and licensing systems or establish an electronic Business One-Stop Shop. Its implementing rules provide guidelines for setting up electronic business permitting systems and issuing electronic permits. [ref: Republic Act No. 11032, lawphil.net]

Republic Act No. 12254, or the E-Governance Act, was signed in 2025. It provides a broader legal framework for digital government services and is relevant to the implementation of eBOSS in local government units. [ref: REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11032 - AN ACT PROMOTING EASE OF DOING BUSINESS AND EFFICIENT DELI VERY OF GOVERNMENT SERVICES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9485, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE ANTI-RED TAPE ACT OF 2007, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES - Supreme Court E-Library, elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph]

== Implementation ==
The Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA) works with other government agencies to promote the implementation of eBOSS. The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) also provides support for the digitalization of local government services. [ref: ARTA sets Nov. 1 deadline for LGUs to shift to online business permit processing – Philippine Information Agency]

According to the Philippine Information Agency, only 127 out of 1,642 local government units were fully compliant with eBOSS requirements as of December 31, 2025. In June 2026, ARTA announced efforts to require all LGUs to process business permits online by November 1, 2026. [ref: ARTA sets Nov. 1 deadline for LGUs to shift to online business permit processing – Philippine Information Agency]

== Challenges ==
The implementation of eBOSS faces challenges related to resources, technical capacity, and coordination among government systems. A 2026 study by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies examined the relationship between automated business permitting and local government revenue. The study identified limitations involving resources, willingness to adopt the systems, and system functionality. It also discussed the need for better integration between local and national government systems. [ref: PIDS study finds fully automated business permitting boosts local tax revenues, pids.gov.ph]

The study recommended improving information and communications technology infrastructure, strengthening the technical capacity of local governments, and integrating local systems with the DICT's eLGU platform. These measures may help local governments improve their digital services and make online business transactions more accessible. [ref: PIDS study finds fully automated business permitting boosts local tax revenues, pids.gov.ph]

== References ==

Irr republic act no. 11032 (CSC, Arta, DTI joint memorandum circular no. 2019-001) - the implementing rules and regulations of republic act no. 11032 otherwise known as the “ease of doing business and efficient government service delivery act of 2018” - supreme court e-library. (2019). Judiciary.Gov.Ph. https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/96391

More LGUs urged to fully automate biz registration, licensing processes. (2026). Pids.Gov.Ph. https://serp-p.pids.gov.ph/publication/public/view?slug=more-lgus-urged-to-fully-automate-biz-registration-licensing-processes

Afterwards, Anne married John Knight of Gosfield Hall, Essex and Robert Nugent, 1st Earl Nugent.

Monex Global is part of Monex S.A.P.I. de C.V. ("Monex"). [ref: Monex 40+ Years of FX Expertise, Monex Global]

Monex Global specializes in foreign exchange (FX) risk management and international payments for corporate and institutional clients.

Monex reports combined annual foreign-exchange volume of more than $198 billion and approximately $16.1 billion in total assets. The company reports serving more than 73,000 individuals and corporate clients worldwide.

Monex operates in Mexico, the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Spain, the Netherlands and Singapore. [ref: ]

=== History ===
Monex was founded in 1985 and is headquartered in Mexico City. [ref: ] According to the company, Monex was established to address the payment and currency exchange needs of companies conducting business internationally.

Monex expanded its international foreign-exchange operations through acquisitions in North America and Europe. Monex's corporate history states that the group acquired Tempus Consulting in 2010. [ref: ] [ref: Monex Acquisition of Tempus Consulting, BGL] The US business was later rebranded as Monex USA in January 2022.

In July 2012, Monex group acquired London-based Schneider Foreign Exchange. [ref: Monex Group acquires Schneider Foreign Exchange, Euromoney] The company subsequently became Monex Europe. Monex later developed additional operations in European markets, including Spain and the Netherlands.

=== Operations ===
Monex Global comprises the international operations of the Monex group through entities established in several jurisdictions.

==== North America ====
The group's North America operations include Monex Inc. in the United States and Monex Canada Inc. in Canada.

==== Europe ====
In Europe, Monex operates through entities including Monex Europe Limited and Monex Europe Markets Limited in the United Kingdom and Monex Europa S.L.U. and Monex Europe Markets, S.V., S.A.U. in Spain.

==== Asia ====
Monex's international operations in Asia include MonFX Pte. Ltd. in Singapore.

=== Products and Services ===
Monex Global's principal activities relate to foreign exchange and cross-border financial transactions.

The business provides services including:

* Foreign exchange
* International payments
* FX risk management/hedging

William Augustus Townshend (10 March 1776 – 3 July 1816) was a British politician and soldier. He sat as MP for Whitchurch from 15 July 1800 till his death on 3 July 1816. [ref: TOWNSHEND, Hon. William Augustus (1776-1816)., History of Parliament Online]

Makai Jackson is an American college football wide receiver for the Liberty Flames. He has previously played for the Indiana Hoosiers, Appalachian State Mountaineers, and Saint Francis Red Wolves.

== Career ==

=== Saint Francis ===
Jackson was a zero-star recruit out of Harry S. Truman High School in Levittown, Pennsylvania. [ref: Former Appalachian State wide receiver Makai Jackson signs with Indiana football, Former Appalachian State wide receiver Makai Jackson signs with Indiana football - Indiana Daily Student] He committed to play for the Saint Francis Red Wolves. In his freshman season with the Red Wolves, Jackson had 85 receptions for 991 yards and 9 touchdowns, finishing 3rd place in voting for the Jerry Rice Award. [ref: Makai Jackson - Football, Saint Francis University Athletics] [ref: McCoy Named 2022 Jerry Rice Award Winner, University of Idaho Athletics] On December 2nd, 2022, Jackson announced he was entering the transfer portal. [ref: St. Francis WR announces he intends to enter the NCAA Transfer Portal, Transfer Portal Home]

=== Appalachian State ===
On December 11, 2022, Jackson announce his commitment to play for the Appalachian State Mountaineers. [ref: Makai Jackson, Appalachian State Mountaineers, Wide Receiver, 247Sports] In his first year with the Mountaineers, Jackson had 27 receptions and 418 yards with 2 touchdowns for the Mountaineers. [ref: Makai Jackson - Football, App State Athletics] In 2024, Makai Jackson was second on the Mountaineers in receiving yards with 752 yards on 46 receptions with 5 touchdowns and earning third-team All-Sun Belt team as a receiver. [ref: Sun Belt Announces 2024 Football Postseason Awards & All-Conference Teams, sunbeltsports.org] [ref: IU football adds Appalachian State transfer WR Makai Jackson from the portal, The Daily Hoosier] On December 9th, 2024, Jackson announce he would be entering the transfer portal for the second time in his career. [ref: App State football players entering the transfer portal, Watauga Democrat]

=== Indiana ===
On December 24th, 2024 Jackson committed to play for the Indiana Hoosiers [ref: Indiana Adds Transfer Wide Receiver Makai Jackson, Indiana Hoosiers On SI], reuniting with former Saint Francis teammate Elijah Sarratt. [ref: Sarratt, Hoosiers Using Spring Practice to ‘Keep Building’, Indiana University Athletics] After appearing in the first three games for the Hoosiers, playing a total of 51 snaps and recording three catches for 15 yards, Jackson decided to [https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Redshirt_%28college_sports%29&wvprov=sticky-header#Rationale conserve his eligibility and redshirt for the rest of the season], and entered the transfer portal. [ref: Wide receiver Makai Jackson no longer with the IU football program, The Daily Hoosier]

=== Liberty ===
After entering the transfer portal, on January 5th, 2026, Jackson announced his commitment to play for the Liberty Flames. [ref: Makai Jackson - Liberty Flames - Wide Receiver, Rivals]

Cloud Chamber are a modern classical musical duo consisting of pianist Gavin Greenaway and cellist Caroline Dale. The ensemble was formed to present original compositions and arrangements for piano and cello, stepping into the spotlight after decades of collaborative work on film scores [ref: Gavin Greenaway imdb, IMDb] [ref: Caroline Dale IMDB, IMDb]and theatrical productions including the Emmy award wining illuminations:Reflections of Earth [ref: Disney official fan club]

== Overview ==
Emmy award winning composer, Gavin Greenaway has conducted over 200 film scores (Gladiator [ref: imdb], How to Train Your Dragon, [ref: imdb]Wicked, [ref: imdb] Interstellar [ref: imdb]), composed music for the theatre, TV and film, the Vancouver Winter Olympics, songs with Bryan Adams and two solo albums of his own piano music.

Caroline Dale has performed with the Nigel Kennedy Quartet, the English Chamber Orchestra, David Gilmour, David Gray and Sinead O’Connor; as concerto soloist with the LPO, RPO etc; and as featured soloist on film such as 1917, Atonement, Hilary and Jackie and Truly Madly Deeply. Her solo album Such Sweet Thunder combines classical repertoire with her own compositions..

== Members ==

=== Gavin Greenaway (Piano) ===
Gavin Greenaway (born 1964) is an Emmy award-winning composer and conductor known for his extensive work in film and orchestral music. He has conducted scores for over 200 films across multiple genres, including blockbuster franchises (How to Train Your Dragon, Wicked, Interstellar) and acclaimed dramas (Gladiator). His conducting work has spanned collaborations with composers Hans Zimmer, John Powell, and other leading orchestral artists. Beyond conducting, Greenaway has composed original music for theatre, television, and film, including scores for the 2010 Vancouver Winter Olympics and songs with singer Bryan Adams. He has released two solo albums of his own piano music: Il Falco Bianco (2016) and contributions to collaborative projects.

=== Caroline Dale (Cello) ===
Caroline Dale (born 1965) is a British cellist with a distinguished career spanning classical, orchestral, and popular music. She is principal cellist for the English Chamber Orchestra and London Metropolitan Orchestra. As a performer, she has worked with the Nigel Kennedy Quartet, David Gilmour, David Gray, and Sinéad O'Connor, among others. Dale has performed as concerto soloist with major orchestras including the London Philharmonic Orchestra and Royal Philharmonic Orchestra. Her film work includes featured solo roles on soundtracks for Atonement, Hilary and Jackie, and Truly, Madly, Deeply. She released the solo album Such Sweet Thunder in 2002, combining classical repertoire with her own compositions.

Mateo Tompkins is a curler. As of 2026, he plays lead for the Mexican men's team. [ref: Mateo Tompkins - Historical Results & Statistics, World Curling]

== Early life ==
Tompkins was raised in Toronto, Canada, along with his brother Diego. Both learned curling at a young age. [ref: The Tompkins Brothers: Pioneering Curling Growth in Mexico] Their father, Douglas Tompkins, is a former curler, and has served as Coach for the Mexican team since 2020. [ref: Douglas Tompkins - Historical Results & Statistics, World Curling]

== Career ==

=== Men's ===
Tompkins was recruited by the [https://www.curlingmexico.com/ Mexican Curling Federation] for the Men and Mixed teams at various World Curling Competitions. [ref: Mateo Tompkins - Historical Results & Statistics, World Curling]
Tompkins, his brother Diego, and teammates Ramy Cohen, and Ismael Abreu won silver at the America's World Curling Championship Challenge in November 2019 in Minnesota, United States. Earning the one Americas Zone slot to advance to the World Qualification Event, in January 2020 in Lohja, Finland, where they finished 8th overall. [ref: World Qualification Event 2020 - Historical Results & Statistics, results.worldcurling.org]

The America's World Curling Championship Challenge competitions were replaced by the Pan Continental Curling Championships. Tompkins and his teammates finished 4th at the Pan Continental Curling Championships in November 2023 in Kelowna, Canada. [ref: Pan Continental Curling Championships 2023 B-Division - Historical Results & Statistics, results.worldcurling.org]

For the 2025-26 curling season, Tompkins formed a new team with his brother Diego, along with Ramy Cohen and Joaquin Villanueva to compete at the last Pan Continental Curling Championships [ref: Mexico's Diego Tompkins6-4 at 2026 U.S. Steel Pan-Continental Championships -- B-Division, www.curlingzone.com] in October 2025 in Minnesota, USA where they finished 6th place. [ref: Pan Continental Curling Championships 2023 B-Division - Historical Results & Statistics, results.worldcurling.org]The Pan Continental Curling Championships were replaced by the introduction of World Curling Championships B and C Divisions for the 2026-2027 curling season. [ref: Major changes to World Curling competition structure for 2026–2030 Olympic cycle confirmed, World Curling] As a result, Mexico had another opportunity to earn a promotion to the World Championship Qualifier by participating in the World Championship Pre-Qualifier (Pan Continental) in Dumfries, Scotland, in April 2026.

Tompkins was the lead for the team at the World Championship Pre-Qualifier (Pan Continental) 2026 in Dumfries, Scotland, where they went undefeated in the round robin with a 5-0 record, ultimately winning the first gold medal for Mexico, and securing promotion to the World Championship Qualifier in November 2026. [ref: Mexico and India promoted to World Championship Qualifier, World Curling]

=== Mixed ===

After the COVID-19 pandemic, Tompkins was the second for the first-ever Mixed Team for Mexico with teammates that included his brother Diego, Estefana Quintero, and Monica Díez at the 2022 World Mixed Curling Championships in Aberdeen, Scotland, in October. The team gave Mexico its first victory at a world event against Luxembourg, and later versus England, placing 7th in the round robin and finishing 26th overall. [ref: ]

Clobuthedrone, is an atypical like psychotometic & psychostimulant that is investigated in the treatment of major depressive disorder and It is a norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitor (NDRI) alongside possessing Serotonin-norepinephrine-dopamine releasing capacity and VMAT-2 re-uptake inhibition and up-regulation. Promoting its investigation into Parkinson’s disease treatments like its sister compounds 4-MMC.

Common adverse effects of clobuthedrone with the greatest difference from placebo are euphoria, stimulation, dry mouth, nausea, constipation, insomnia, anxiety, tremor, and excessive sweating. Raised blood pressure is notable.Rare but serious side effects include seizures, liver toxicity,psychosis, and risk of overdose. clobuthedrone use during pregnancy may be associated with increased likelihood of congenital heart defects.

Clobuthedrone acts as a norepinephrine–dopamine reuptake inhibitor (NDRI) and serotonin-norepinephrine-dopamine releasing agent and a nicotinic receptor modulator. Chemically, clobuthedrone is an aminoketone that belongs to the class of substituted cathinones and more generally that of substituted amphetamines and substituted phenethylamines.

York Supplies Community Society is a community benefit society based in Kings Heath, Birmingham, England. The society operates the business as a community co-operative, with local members able to hold shares and participate in its governance. It aims to maintain York Supplies as an independent local retail and community resource. Draft: Irvings of Bonshaw

Draft text:
The Irvings of Bonshaw were a landed family of Annandale whose principal seat was Bonshaw Tower, near Kirtlebridge in present-day Dumfries and Galloway, Scotland. [ref: The Castles of Scotland, Goblinshead]

The family is documented in records relating to the western Anglo-Scottish border during the late medieval and early modern periods, and formed part of the society of landowners, military retainers, officials and surname groups that operated within the Scottish West March. [ref: England's Northern Frontier: Conflict and Local Society in the Fifteenth-Century Scottish Marches, Cambridge University Press] [ref: Violence, Custom and Law: The Anglo-Scottish Border Lands in the Later Middle Ages, Edinburgh University Press]

Modern historians interpret the family within the broader context of Border society rather than through later clan traditions, emphasising kinship, lordship, frontier administration and cross-border relations. [ref: The Scottish Middle March, 1573–1625, Boydell Press] [ref: A British Frontier? Lairds and Gentlemen in the Eastern Borders, 1540–1603, Tuckwell Press]

== Bonshaw Tower and estate ==
Bonshaw Tower served as the principal seat of the Irving family and survives as one of the fortified tower houses of the western Borders. [ref: The Border Towers of Scotland: The West March, Alba Publications]

The Bonshaw estate lay within Annandale, a region occupying an important position in the western sector of the Anglo-Scottish frontier. [ref: Medieval Scotland: Crown, Lordship and Community, Edinburgh University Press] During the later Middle Ages and the sixteenth century the region was shaped by warfare between Scotland and England, the authority of regional magnates, and the distinctive administrative structures of the Border Marches. [ref: ]

Documentary evidence places the Irvings among the established landed interests of Annandale. [ref: The Irvings, Irwins, Irvines, or Erinveines; or Any Other Spelling of the Name, an Old Scots Border Clan, Rosemount Press] Their estate formed part of the political and social landscape shared with other prominent Border surnames, including the Johnstones, Maxwells, Grahams, Bells and Armstrongs. [ref: The Steel Bonnets, HarperCollins]

== The Irvings in Border records ==
Members of the Irving family appear in numerous governmental and administrative records relating to the Anglo-Scottish frontier. [ref: The Border Papers: Calendar of Letters and Papers Relating to the Affairs of the Borders of England and Scotland] References occur throughout the collections of Border Papers, which preserve official correspondence and reports concerning frontier affairs between 1560 and 1603.

The family also appears in the Calendar of State Papers Relating to Scotland and the Register of the Privy Council of Scotland, which document land disputes, military service, feuds, local administration and law enforcement in the Borders. [ref: Calendar of State Papers Relating to Scotland] [ref: Register of the Privy Council of Scotland]

Because many references survive only in relation to specific incidents, historians generally interpret the Irvings through broader patterns visible in Border society rather than through a continuous family narrative.

== Role within Annandale and the West March ==
The Irvings formed part of the society of the Scottish West March, one of the three administrative divisions established to govern Scotland's frontier with England. [ref: Leges Marchiarum, or Border Laws] The March system relied on wardens, commissioners and special legal procedures intended to manage violence and disputes across the frontier.

Studies by Cynthia Neville, Anna Groundwater and Maureen Meikle have emphasised that Border landowners were active participants in royal government while also maintaining local kinship networks and obligations. The Irvings occupied this frontier environment as members of the landed elite of Annandale.

== Notable members ==
=== Edward Irving of Bonshaw ===
Edward Irving of Bonshaw is mentioned repeatedly in sixteenth-century governmental correspondence relating to the Borders, and appears among the principal lairds of Annandale during the period of the Johnstone–Maxwell feud. His appearances in official records illustrate the family's active participation in the affairs of the Scottish West March.

=== Colonel John Beaufin Irving of Bonshaw ===
Colonel John Beaufin Irving of Bonshaw was a British Army officer, genealogist and historian of the family. [ref: The London Gazette] In 1907 he published The Irvings, Irwins, Irvines, or Erinveines; or Any Other Spelling of the Name, an Old Scots Border Clan, one of the most extensive genealogical works relating to the Irving family. Although parts of the work reflect the genealogical methods of its period, it remains a major source for the study of Irving family history.

=== Captain Sir Robert Beaufin Irving of Bonshaw ===

Captain Sir Robert Beaufin Irving, son of Colonel John Beaufin Irving, had a distinguished career in the Royal Naval Reserve, the Merchant Navy and latterly the Cunard Line.

== Chiefship ==
The Bonshaw line is the historic chiefly line of the Irving family. Under Scots heraldic law, recognition as Chief of the Name and Arms of Irving of Bonshaw falls within the jurisdiction of the Court of the Lord Lyon and depends upon proven genealogical descent and heraldic succession. [ref: Scots Heraldry] [ref: Heraldry in Scotland]
[truncated]

Draft text:
Team, Inc. (stylized in all caps) is a global industrial services company with its headquarters located in Sugar Land, Texas. Founded in 1973, the company provides specialty maintenance, inspection, and mechanical integrity services to facilities in the refining, petrochemical, power generation, and manufacturing sectors. The company's common stock is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol TISI.

== History ==
The company was established in 1973 as an industrial maintenance services contractor primarily serving petrochemical facilities along the Texas Gulf Coast.

In 1995, the company completed an initial public offering on the Nasdaq exchange and later moved its listing to the New York Stock Exchange in 2001 under the ticker symbol TISI.

Throughout the 2000s and 2010s, Team, Inc. expanded its geographic footprint and technical scope through acquisitions of regional inspection and specialty service providers. In February 2016, the company acquired Furmanite Corporation, a major competitor in specialized on-site industrial services and leak sealing, in an all-stock transaction.

In the early 2020s, the company began operational reorganization programs to consolidate service lines and address debt from major transactions, and it completed a 1-for-10 reverse stock split in December 2022 to remain compliant with exchange listing requirements.

== Operations and services ==
Team, Inc. provides asset-integrity, inspection, maintenance, and repair and rope access services for industrial facilities and equipment. Its service offerings cover six main areas: inspection, detection, repair, heat treating, digital services through OneInsight, and advanced asset and project solutions. [ref: Industrial Asset Integrity Services, TEAM, Inc.]

=== Inspection ===
Team provides conventional and advanced non-destructive testing, tank inspections, and valve testing. Its inspection capabilities also include robotics and drones, computed and digital radiography, laser inspection, infrared thermography, three-dimensional imaging, and data collection to assess the condition of industrial equipment and structures.Inspection and Testing (NDT/NDE), TEAM, Inc.

=== Detection ===
Detection services focus on identifying and measuring leaks and emissions. They include leak detection and repair (LDAR) programs, greenhouse gas measurement and control, methane emissions reduction, and optical gas imaging. These services support emissions monitoring, repair coordination, and environmental compliance reporting. [ref: Detection and Emissions Reduction, TEAM, Inc.]

=== Repair ===
Team provides specialty mechanical repair services, including leak sealing on operating equipment, hot tapping and line intervention, field machining, controlled bolting, valve repair and insertion, welding services, and engineered composite repairs. It also offers vapor barrier and hydrostatic weld testing.On-Stream Mechanical Repair & Online Leak Sealing Services, TEAM, Inc.

=== Heat treating ===
Heat treatment services include preheating and post-weld heat treatment, dehydrogenation, solution annealing, normalizing, and curing of coatings and refractory materials. Team also provides equipment thawing, expansion heating, temperature monitoring, and mobile heat treatment equipment.Heat Treating, TEAM, Inc.

=== OneInsight ===
OneInsight is Team’s digital platform for collecting, managing, and reporting information associated with inspection, maintenance, and repair activities. Its tools support field service management, remote monitoring, asset-integrity records, repair documentation, and turnaround coordination. The platform also provides dashboards, audit logs, and mobile reporting.Heat Treating, TEAM, Inc.

=== Advanced asset and project solutions ===
Team provides industrial project support for maintenance, fabrication, shutdowns, and asset-integrity management. Services include IRATA-certified rope access for inspection and repair in difficult-to-reach locations, custom component manufacturing, turnaround planning and execution, and engineered line lifts to provide access to pipes and supports. Asset-integrity management services support risk assessment and maintenance planning. [ref: Industrial Project Support Services, TEAM, Inc.]

Team, Inc. operates service locations across the United States, Canada, Europe, and Latin America. The company is governed by a board of directors and executive management led by Chief Executive Officer Gary L. Hill. Draft: Sunrise (novel)

Draft text:
Sunrise is a 2026 novel by Téa Obreht, published by Random House on August 11, 2026. Obreht’s fourth novel, it interweaves three storylines set in the same Wyoming ghost town across 1902, 2003, and 2024. The book was a national bestseller and received positive reviews for its genre-blending structure and its treatment of myth-making in the American West. [ref: ] [ref: This Ghost Town Hides Century-Spanning Secrets, The New York Times]

== Plot ==
The novel opens in 2024 with Nina Terzić, a young nanny, surviving the crash of a small plane into a Wyoming lake. Her boyfriend Ben, the pilot, is missing. Nina swims ashore and eventually finds Sunrise, a seemingly abandoned but well-preserved ghost town. Inside one of the buildings, she discovers the body of a woman and a manuscript titled Sunrise. [ref: Sunrise by Téa Obreht review – secrets and myths in the American west, The Guardian] [ref: ]

The manuscript forms the novel’s second strand, set in 1902. Anton Vargas, a gunslinger whose exploits were embellished in dime novels, returns to Sunrise after a long absence. He is drawn into the search for a missing boy, and the narrative gradually reveals a gap between Vargas’s heroic reputation and the man himself. [ref: This Ghost Town Hides Century-Spanning Secrets, The New York Times] [ref: ]

The third timeline, set in 2003, follows Coll Yard, an amateur historian who stages annual re-enactments of Vargas’s legendary shootout. Coll’s authority over the town’s history is challenged when a writer named Louise Hawley arrives with research that complicates the accepted story of Vargas. The three narratives converge as Nina’s survival story, Vargas’s reckoning, and Coll’s crisis of ownership over the past illuminate one another.

== Background ==
Obreht has said the novel grew from an early obsession with Western dime novels. About a decade before Sunrise was published, she began drafting a book about an aging gunslinger, but struggled to finish it. [ref: Téa Obreht on Writing a Layered, Intertextual Tale of the American West, Literary Hub] The project stalled until she found a way to frame the Western material through other timelines and voices. The novel’s structure three distinct periods connected by a single place allowed her to examine how stories about the West are made, revised, and defended across generations.

The town of Sunrise in the novel is fictional, though Obreht has acknowledged a real ghost town of the same name in Wyoming. She has said the name was chosen to honor the moment of discovery that drives Nina’s storyline.

== Themes ==
Reviewers identified myth-making and the ownership of history as central concerns. The New York Times wrote that Obreht’s “larger project” is “to challenge our romanticism of the West by questioning how legends are made, burnished and mythologized”. The Guardian noted that the 2003 section, in which Coll resists Louise’s revisionist research, dramatizes the conflict between inherited legend and historical scrutiny. Kirkus Reviews observed that all three protagonists are “driven by secrets,” and that the narratives “illuminate each other in ways that are both elegant and emotionally deep”.

The novel also examines survival, gender, and the violence buried beneath frontier mythology. Booklist described it as “exult[ing] in emulating and subverting tales of the Old West while exposing the poisonous complexities of gender, taboo love, myth, history, and our desecration of the wild”. The Irish Times called the book “a propulsive metafiction” whose central inquiry is “who has the authority to write history, and what is at stake for those authoring and/or perpetuating certain versions of events”. [ref: Sunrise by Téa Obreht: Timelines converge successfully in absorbing novel, The Irish Times]

== Reception ==
Sunrise received starred reviews from Kirkus Reviews and Publishers Weekly, and was named a national bestseller by Penguin Random House. [ref: Sunrise by Téa Obreht, www.publishersweekly.com]

The New York Times praised the novel as “masterful,” saying Obreht “delightfully mashes up several genres, including Western gothic, murder mystery and survival saga”. The Guardian called it “an engrossing, original and thought-provoking novel, effortlessly readable and beautifully told”. Publishers Weekly wrote that Obreht “employs impressive restraint, providing just enough clues to create intrigue” and concluded that “readers will have a blast”. The Irish Times highlighted the “richly drawn” characters and said the novel “delivers a rewarding denouement”. [ref: Sunrise by Téa Obreht: Timelines converge successfully in absorbing novel, The Irish Times]

Peter N. Cheimets is an American mechanical engineer and telescope developer. He is a senior engineer at the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory and the Harvard–Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics. [ref: A Security Camera for the Planet, The New Yorker] His work has focused on the design, development, testing, and deployment of astronomical instruments [ref: “The Dynamic Sun” Combines Solar Physics and Visualization, www.lib.ncsu.edu], particularly space-based solar and X-ray telescopes. [ref: Boulder researchers at center of eclipse-focused studies, Boulder Daily Camera] He led the development of the X-Ray Telescope aboard the Hinode mission [ref: The X-Ray Telescope (XRT) for the Hinode Mission, Solar Physics], the telescope for the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), and the telescopes comprising the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) aboard the NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO). [ref: The Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) on the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), Solar Physics]

== Biography ==
Cheimets is the son of Sheila Cheimets, a newspaper editor and Massachusetts municipal official who was elected as Canton, Massachusetts' first female selectman in 1972. [ref: Sheila Cheimets, Canton’s first female selectman, dies at 75, Wicked Local]

Cheimets received a Bachelor of Science degree in mechanical engineering from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1978, with a concentration in mechanical design. [ref: Mission2007 mentors: alumni, web.mit.edu] He subsequently earned a Master of Science in mechanical engineering from Stanford University in 1981, concentrating on mechanical dynamics and control-systems design. [ref: Peter Cheimets, Mass Innovation Nights] He later received a master's degree in engineering management from Tufts University in 2007, focusing on negotiation. [ref: Launching into Space Peter Cheimets, MSEM ’07, turned his MS in Engineering Management, Gordon Institute]

== Career and research ==
Cheimets joined the Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory as a mechanical engineer in 1983, initially working on projects involving aerospace engineering, energy systems, and medical equipment. [ref: Cheimets, Peter, profiles.si.edu] He later specialized in astronomical instrumentation, serving as project engineer for the Transition Region and Coronal Explorer (TRACE) [ref: Mr Cheimets was also responsible for the four telescopes in this instrument know as AIA., Mass Innovation Nights] and contributing to the X-Ray Telescope aboard Japan's Hinode mission. He also designed and oversaw construction of the four telescopes used in the Atmospheric Imaging Assembly aboard NASA's Solar Dynamics Observatory. [ref: The Atmospheric Imaging Assembly (AIA) on the Solar Dynamics Observatory (SDO), Solar Physics]

Cheimets contributed to the early development of MethaneSAT and oversaw the development of MethaneAir, an airborne instrument for methane-emissions research. [ref: Quantifying Methane – To the Sky and Beyond, The Salata Institute] His subsequent work has included the Marshall Grazing Incidence X-ray Spectrometer (MaGIXS) [ref: The Marshall Grazing Incidence X-Ray Spectrometer, NASA], the proposed AXIS and Lynx X-ray missions [ref: ], the Black Hole Explorer, and NASA's MUSE mission. [ref: Metal-coated carbon nanotube ultrathin pellicles: a high-performance solution for the optical blocking filters of the NASA MIDEX solar mission MUSE, International Conference on Space Optics]

Matthias G. R. Faes (born 15 October 1991) is a Belgian engineer and academic who works on uncertainty quantification and reliability engineering. Since February 2022 he has been a full professor at TU Dortmund University, where he heads the Chair for Reliability Engineering (CRE) in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.

== Early life and education ==
Faes was born in Lier, Belgium. He studied engineering technology at the De Nayer campus in Sint-Katelijne-Waver, obtaining a bachelor's degree in 2012 and a master's degree in engineering technology with a specialization in manufacturing engineering in 2013, which he completed summa cum laude.

He then carried out his doctoral research in the Department of Mechanical Engineering of KU Leuven under the supervision of David Moens. He obtained his PhD in engineering technology in 2017 with a dissertation on interval methods for the identification and quantification of inhomogeneous uncertainty in finite element models.

== Career ==
From 2013 to 2017 Faes worked as a scientific and teaching assistant at KU Leuven. After completing his doctorate he remained there as a postdoctoral researcher, from 2019 to 2022 as a postdoctoral fellow of the Research Foundation – Flanders (FWO). In 2020 he received a postdoctoral research fellowship from the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, which he held at the Institute for Risk and Reliability of Leibniz University Hannover.

In February 2022 he was appointed full professor (W3) of Reliability Engineering at TU Dortmund University.

== Research ==
Faes's research concerns computational methods for uncertainty quantification and reliability analysis of engineering structures and systems. The main areas of his work are positioned in the reliability analysis of complex structures, uncertainty quantification under scarce data and the extension of numerical models with scientific machine learning and artificial intelligence tools. [ref: Matthias Faes, ORCID]

His doctoral and early postdoctoral work developed interval field methods, which represent spatially varying non-probabilistic uncertainty in finite element models, together with inverse methods to identify such uncertainty from measurement data. His later work addresses the efficient estimation of small failure probabilities, including first-passage problems in stochastic structural dynamics, Bayesian active learning with Gaussian process surrogate models, the propagation of imprecise probabilities such as probability boxes, and reliability-based design optimization of complex systems.

== Awards and honours ==

* 2018: ECCOMAS Award for the best PhD theses of 2017 on computational methods in applied sciences and engineering, one of two winners selected from 17 nominated theses.
* 2018: Second laureate of the award of the Belgian National Committee on Theoretical and Applied Mechanics for the best PhD thesis of 2017.
* 2019: IJAR Young Researcher Award of the International Symposium on Imprecise Probabilities: Theories and Applications (ISIPTA), shared with Arthur Van Camp.
* 2023: Junior Research Prize in the area of Development of Methodologies for Structural Dynamics of the European Association for Structural Dynamics (EASD).
* 2026: Olgierd Cecil Zienkiewicz Young Investigator Award of the European Community on Computational Methods in Applied Sciences (ECCOMAS), presented at the WCCM-ECCOMAS 2026 Congress in Munich.

== Professional service ==
Faes is an associate editor of the journals Reliability Engineering & System Safety and Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing, and associate managing editor of the ASCE-ASME Journal of Risk and Uncertainty in Engineering Systems.

Draft: The Conveyor System

Draft text:
The Conveyor System is a theory of ancient stone transport proposed by Paul Sullivan, an independent researcher from Cambridge, Ontario, Canada. It proposes that the builders of Stonehenge in England and the Egyptian pyramids moved massive stones using a self-advancing track made of stones, with each megalith riding on log rollers.

Sullivan first shared the theory publicly in 2011 and refined it through 2025. It is documented in his ebook, The Conveyor System: Solving the Mystery of How the Stones Were Moved at Stonehenge and the Pyramids. The theory is derived from Lean thinking and makes six testable predictions.

== Background ==

How ancient builders moved stones weighing 30 to 40 tonnes, without modern machinery, remains one of archaeology's best-known unanswered questions. Proposed explanations have included ramps, sledges, and ropes. Sullivan argues that rope technology was in its infancy when Stonehenge was built, and that the accepted methods do not account for the precision and scale of the work.

== The system ==

In the Conveyor System, one long line of stones forms a track, a roadway that runs directly under the stone being moved, inside its footprint. The megalith rides on log rollers on top of that stone track and is pushed forward. As it advances, the crew takes the back track stone and moves it to the front, so the roadway leapfrogs ahead of the load continuously. The conveyor is the roadway itself.

Propulsion comes from the crew: three to four workers push along each side of the stone, and three to four more push at the back, against one long log, 12 to 14 feet long, laid across the back of the stone and centred on its middle. All workers walk on the ground beside the track, never on the track stones. The stones moved to Stonehenge under this system are the bluestones, 10 to 12 feet long and 3 feet wide.

== Lean thinking ==

Sullivan developed the theory by applying lean thinking, the discipline of identifying a problem and then running root cause analysis to find the real problem, to the question of ancient construction. The Conveyor System is presented as a waste-free flow: a small crew, simple materials, and a roadway that rebuilds itself ahead of the load.

== Testable predictions ==

The theory makes six testable predictions. The principal prediction is that wood particles from the log rollers became embedded in the stone surfaces during transport, and that those particles can be detected today through tribochemical wear analysis.

== Mathematical confirmation ==

The calculations, timelines, and efficiencies behind the Conveyor System have been mathematically confirmed by five separate AI tools. Physical confirmation depends on testing the testable predictions, beginning with tribochemical wear analysis of stone surfaces.

Draft text:
Artizan Joyería is an American jewelry company headquartered in Aventura, Florida, in the Miami metropolitan area. It was founded in 2008 by Venezuelan-born designer Keren Yoshua and is a family-owned business run by Yoshua and her husband. The company is known for pre-styled layered necklace sets and stackable bracelets made mainly of gold-plated stainless steel.

== History ==
Yoshua studied advertising at Andrés Bello Catholic University in Venezuela and graduated in 2004. She then moved to Madrid, where in 2008 she began buying artisanal jewelry and selling it wholesale to retail stores. That business became the basis of Artizan Joyería, and Yoshua later began designing her own pieces. According to Yoshua, the name was chosen to combine the traditional feel of artisan jewelry with a modern fashion sensibility.

Yoshua and her husband, Sasha, grew the company through wholesale jewelry trade shows in Spain, Paris and New York City. In 2015 the couple relocated to Miami, a move Yoshua has described as a source of design inspiration.

By 2019 the company had launched a direct-to-consumer online store. According to Yoshua, its pre-styled layered necklace and bracelet sets performed well with customers after the launch. The company continues to offer wholesale accounts alongside its online retail business.

== Products ==
The company's catalog includes necklaces, bracelets, rings, earrings and anklets, as well as individual charms and a men's line. Its product line centers on pre-styled sets of layered necklaces and stacked bracelets, which often combine gold-tone and silver-tone metals in the same set.

Most pieces are made of hypoallergenic stainless steel plated in 18k gold, and many are priced under US$100. The company states that its steel jewelry is made with recycled stainless steel. Its named collections include Herradura, built around a horseshoe-shaped clasp, and The One, a collection of statement bangles and earrings designed to be worn on their own, which was its newest line in early 2026.

== Media coverage ==
Artizan Joyería was included in lists of recommended affordable jewelry brands by Business Insider in 2024 and InStyle in 2025. The brand has also appeared in roundups of jewelry from woman-owned and Latina-founded businesses by BuzzFeed and HipLatina.

Sripur is a rural area in the Malda district of West Bengal, India. It falls under the Ratua II community development block and the Chanchal subdivision. The wider Sripur area is large and includes two gram panchayats, Sripur I and Sripur II. This article focuses on a specific locality also known as Sripur, located near Sripur Halt railway station (SRPU).

== Geography and location ==

The locality extends along the road connecting Sripur bus stand to Gangadevi via GSA Road. Sripur is located approximately 42 km from Malda Town. The nearby town of Samsi provides access to educational institutions and healthcare facilities.

== Education ==

=== G.S.A. High Madrasah ===

G.S.A. High Madrasah is an educational institution located in Sripur. It is affiliated with the West Bengal Board of Madrasah Education (WBBME) and the West Bengal Council of Higher Secondary Education (WBCHSE). Students can study from Class V to Class XII. After Class X, the institution offers Arts subjects, with no Science department at the higher secondary level.

=== KGBV Girls' Hostel ===

A girls' hostel named KGBV Girls' Hostel is located under G.S.A. High Madrasah. It provides residential facilities for girls from disadvantaged backgrounds and families below the poverty line who study in Classes V to VIII. The hostel has a capacity of 100 students and approximately 20 staff members involved in cooking, management, cleaning and other duties.

=== Sripur Primary School ===

Sripur Primary School is another educational institution in the locality. Students can study from Class I to Class IV.

== Transport ==

Sripur is connected to nearby towns and areas by road and railway. National Highway 12 (NH 12) and state highways provide road connectivity between the locality and Malda Town. Railway services also connect the area with Malda Town and Malda Court. Sripur Halt railway station, with the station code SRPU, serves the locality.

== Healthcare ==

Samsi Rural Hospital is the nearby hospital serving the locality and surrounding rural areas.

== Economy ==

Agriculture is one of the main occupations of the people living in Sripur. Farming provides a livelihood for a significant part of the local population.

== Nearby educational institutions ==

Samsi College is located in the nearby town of Samsi and serves students from the surrounding areas.

Moyo Ogunseinde is a Nigerian architect, real estate developer, designer, and hospitality entrepreneur. She is the founder and Group Chief Executive Officer of Club Concierge Africa, a travel and hospitality group whose brands include Club Concierge International, GoTravelCC, GoPartnerCC and MyTravelCC. Trained at University College London, Moyo Ogunseinde designed the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel in Lagos and sits on the board of its owner, Anchorage Leisures. Earlier in her career she was an executive director of Uraga Real Estate, a member of the Honeywell Group, where she led the development of the Upbeat Recreation Centre, described in the Nigerian press as West Africa's first trampoline park. She has chaired the Lagos State Gymnastics Association since 2018.

== Early life and education ==
Moyo Ogunseinde is from Ibadan, Nigeria. She has cited the city's markets, colours and cultural life as an influence on her later design work. She trained as an architect at University College London and later undertook executive education at Harvard Business School. She is a chartered architect.

== Career ==

=== Architecture and real estate ===
Moyo Ogunseinde began her career in architecture before moving into real estate development in Nigeria. She designed the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel on Victoria Island, Lagos, which opened in 2011, and later oversaw the renovation of its rooms and business lounge. She became an executive director of Uraga Real Estate Limited, a subsidiary of the Honeywell Group, contributing to design, land acquisition and planning.

=== Upbeat Recreation Centre ===
As an executive director of Uraga Real Estate, Moyo Ogunseinde led the development of the Upbeat Recreation Centre, a multi-purpose leisure facility on Admiralty Road, Lekki, which opened in December 2017 and was reported in the Nigerian media as West Africa's first trampoline park. The project was conceived during Nigeria's 2016 recession as a diversification into recreational real estate, aimed at the country's young population. The centre set up a gymnastics club in February 2018 and held its first trampoline gymnastics competition in October 2018. In 2024 it hosted a fun day for underprivileged children in Lekki.

=== Aga Culture ===
In 2017 Moyo Ogunseinde founded Aga Culture (originally Àga Concept), an African lifestyle and design brand based in Lagos, and serves as its creative director. The name derives from the Yoruba word àga, meaning a chair or functional object. The brand produces clothing, furniture and homeware that combine Yoruba and wider African traditions with a contemporary, minimalist aesthetic, and emphasises slow fashion and ethically sourced materials such as Adire cotton and linen. Its furniture includes the Oko chair, drawn from traditional farming tools, and the Egungun accessories collection, inspired by Egungun masquerades; in 2020 the American trade magazine Hospitality Design named Moyo Ogunseinde one of six rising product designers. The brand's Mmanwu chair featured in Cultured magazine's 2021 survey of the Lagos design scene. Its work has also included the AADA clothing collection and participation in design exhibitions.

=== Hospitality ===
Moyo Ogunseinde has served as executive director of Anchorage Leisures Limited, owner of the Radisson Blu Anchorage Hotel, and sits on its board. She is also a board member of the Honeywell Group and an advisory board member of Wavecrest College of Hospitality, Lagos. In a 2022 interview she argued that Nigeria could develop world-class tourism by investing in local infrastructure and emphasised local content in the hotel's operations, art and food sourcing. In November 2025 she accepted the Best Corporate Hotel award at the World Luxury Awards in Barcelona on behalf of the Radisson Blu Anchorage, where she was described as a board member and key owner of the property. In 2025 she was included in a Nigerian trade listing of "Top 100 Women in Hospitality".

=== Club Concierge Africa ===

Moyo Ogunseinde founded Club Concierge Africa (CCA) during the COVID-19 pandemic, building a travel, hospitality and lifestyle group intended to serve African travellers. The group offers travel membership, travel management, hospitality partnerships and concierge services. Its brands are:
* Club Concierge International (CCI), a travel club offering vacation-ownership membership for leisure travellers and, through Club Concierge for Business, corporate travel membership;
* GoTravelCC, a travel-management company offering flights, hotels and related services;
* MyTravelCC, a flights-first travel booking brand;
* GoPartnerCC, the group's partnership brand;
* Concierge Resort, which manages resort destinations; and
* CSolute, a business-to-business travel affiliate arm.

As Group CEO, Moyo Ogunseinde oversees operations across several African and international markets. In September 2026 she spoke on a panel on cross-border payments at the 22nd Akwaaba African Travel Market in Lagos, calling for closer cooperation between regulators, payment providers and tourism operators to reduce the cost of travel within Africa.

== History ==

WeFixMoney.com was officially launched in 2008 as a web-based financial portal to assist consumers in obtaining short-term liquidity. [ref: ]

* 2013: The platform expanded its network to include its 100th direct lending partner
* 2014: WeFixMoney.com reached a milestone of over 1 million total customers served.
* 2015: The company was recognized by the Online Lenders Alliance (OLA), recieving the Extraordinary Contribution Award for its work within the online lending marketplace ecosystem
* 2025: The company reported serving over [https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7417513467890319360 8 million customers] since inception.

== Services & Business Model ==
WeFixMoney.com operates as a non-bank financial connection platform rather than a direct lender. The service is free to use and operates entirely online: [ref: ]

# Application: Applicats fill out a single online form specifying desired funding amount (typically between $100 and $5000), monthly income, and basic personal details.
# Matching: The platform evaluates applicat data against criteria provided by its network of independent third-party lenders.
# Redirection & Disbursement: If a match is found, appliants are redirected to the respective lender's portal to review and finalize loan terms, with funding discbuersed as soon as the same business day.

The company states its primary mission is providing accessible liquidity options for consumers, including individuals with bad or limited credit histories who may not qualify for standard bank products. [ref: ]

== Industry Accrediations & Memberships ==

* Online Lenders Alliance (OLA): Member of the [https://onlinelendersalliance.org/ OLA], adhering to industry standards for best practices and fair online lending principles.
* Better Business Bureau (BBB): Holds an [https://www.bbb.org/us/va/lorton/profile/payday-loans/fix-media-llc-0241-5717809 "A" rating] from the Better Business Bureau.

== User Feedback ==

=== Posetive Feedback ===
Users often cite the platform's rapid approval process, ease of application, and availability to borrowers with subprime credit profiles as primary advantages. The matching service is completely free to applicants. who remain under no onlihation to accept any loan offer or terms presented by direct lenders. Operating 24/7, the platform allows users to complete applications from mobile devices in the comfort of home, backed by responsive customer support. [ref: ]

=== Market Considerations ===
As an intermediary, WeFixMoney.com does not set interest rates, loan terms, or fees. Industry analysts and consumer reviews note that third-party lenders within online loan networks can charge High Annual Percentage Rate (APRs), often associated with short-term installment and payday loans. Additiional criticisms focus on variable transparency dependent on individual matched lenders. [ref: ]

Draft: Sullivan multiplication solution

Draft text:
The Sullivan multiplication solution is a visual method for teaching Basic Multiplication developed by Paul Sullivan of Cambridge, Ontario, Canada. Sullivan describes it as a Universal Solution for Basic Multiplication, used Universally and applicable universally in classrooms and homes. The method uses a coded multiplication grid to make the steps of multi-digit multiplication visible to the Student. It is designed so that the largest single calculation a Student must perform is 9 x 9.

Sullivan presents the method as one written standard for Basic Multiplication. In his account, the Student begins with instructional codes in the grid, then works with the codes removed, then drops the grid and the times table, and finally performs the standard algorithm without support.

== Background ==

Sullivan argues that children leaving Grade 4 are too often unable to do Basic Multiplication because elementary instruction exposes Students to several written procedures for the same calculation without giving them one reliable method. In his published comparison, the five written methods are the standard algorithm, partial products, the area model or box method, the lattice method, and the grid method. He argues that four of the five are not used in later algebra, the trades, or digital work, while the standard algorithm is difficult for many Students because it is commonly taught through spoken steps that the Student cannot see or check.

He developed this argument in two essays, The Virus Within and One Equation, Six Methods. The latter compares the methods on the equation 34 x 27 = 918 and includes The Sullivan Multiplication Solution as a visual alternative.

== Method ==

The Sullivan Multiplication Solution uses a worksheet range for the multiplication forms Students are expected to master: 1 x 1 (one digit by one digit), 2 x 1 (two digits by one digit), 2 x 2 (two digits by two digits), and 3 x 2 (three digits by two digits). The grid contains instructional codes that show where each partial result belongs. The Teacher introduces the worksheet with a times table available, and the Student calculates in their head where possible or uses the times table where needed.

The intended progression has three stages. First, the Student practises with the codes visible. Second, the codes are removed while the grid remains. Third, the grid and the times table are dropped, and the Student performs the standard algorithm alone. Sullivan describes accuracy, rather than speed, as the measure of success.

== Assistive technology ==

The online service includes an Assistive Technology section. Sullivan has described that section as usable in the manner of a basic app, so a Student can practise with a Parent away from a desk or classroom.

== Evidence status ==

As of October 2026, The Sullivan Multiplication Solution has not been independently evaluated in a completed formal trial. Sullivan has proposed school pilot studies in which baseline scores from the first part of the school year would be compared with results at the end of the pilot, with Friday test worksheets recorded by worksheet type and by whether the times table was used. Data handling in the proposed pilot removes Student names at the school level before results are returned.

== References ==

Sullivan, Paul. One Equation, Six Methods. Substack, 14 October 2026. https://rackrunner1963.substack.com/p/one-equation-six-methods

Sullivan, Paul. The Virus Within. Substack, 16 September 2026. https://rackrunner1963.substack.com/p/the-virus-within

Statistics Canada. Elementary-Secondary Education Survey, Table 37-10-0007, regular programs for youth, public schools, Canada, 2023/24.

OECD. PISA mathematics results for Canada, score 485.

[https://www.instagram.com/ihsanudinprorakyat/ Ihsanudin] saat ini menjabat sebagai Direktur Perencanaan Strategis dan Teknologi Informasi BPJS Ketenagakerjaan Periode 2026-2031. Ia adalah aktivis muda Nahdlatul Ulama (NU) berlatar belakang santri sekaligus profesional.

Sebelum menjadi Direksi, pria kelahiran 15 November 1979 ini merupakan [https://dprd.jabarprov.go.id/profil/ihsanudin-m-si Anggota DPRD Provinsi Jawa Barat] (2019-2024) dari daerah pemilihan Kab. Karawang dan Purwakarta, Tenaga Ahli Anggota DPR RI (2014-2019), Wakil Sekretaris Lembaga Pendidikan Ma'arif PBNU (2015-2019), Wakil Ketua DPD Gerakan Indonesia Raya Provinsi Jawa Barat (2014-2025), Wakil Sekretaris Jenderal DPP Konfederasi SARBUMUSI (Sarikat Buruh Muslimin Indonesia) Masa Khidmat 2010-2015, Pengurus Besar - Pergerakan Mahasiswa Islam Indonesia (PB PMII)  Masa Khidmat 2009-2011, Sekretaris Umum PC PMII Daerah Istimewa Yogyakarta (2004-2006).

Saat ini ia juga aktif sebagai Wakil Ketua Komite Pemberdayaan dan Pembinaan SDI PP MES ([https://www.ekonomisyariah.org/tentang-kami/ Pengurus Pusat Masyarakat Ekonomi Syariah]) Periode 2026-2031, Ketua Bidang Koperasi Perikanan dan Kelautan DPN HKTI (Dewan Pengurus Nasional - Himpunan Kerukunan Tani Indonesia) Periode 2025-2030, Ketua DNIKS ([https://www.instagram.com/dewannasionalkessos/ Dewan Nasional Indonesia untuk Kesejahteraan Sosial]) Periode 2024-2029, Wakil Ketua PW Gerakan Pemuda Ansor (2024-2028), Ketua Harian DPD Komite Nasional Pemuda Indonesia Provinsi Jawa Barat (2021-2025), CEO dan Pendiri PT Airlangga Bintang Kreasi (2020).

Setelah tamat dari SD (1992) di Karawang, kemudian ia nyantri di Pesantren Nihayatul Amal Karawang (1992-1993), lalu ke Pesantren Al-Jawami Bandung (1993-1995) sambil merampungkan studi SLTP. Kemudian dilanjutkan di Pesantren Modern [https://albasyariyah.com/ Al-Basyariyah Bandung] (1995-1999), sambil menyelesaikan studi SLTA.

Seusai nyantri di Jawa Barat, kemudian ia hijrah ke Yogyakarta untuk mengikuti kuliah Strata Satu (S1) di [https://syariah.uin-suka.ac.id/ Fakultas Syariah] UIN Sunan Kalijaga (2000). Namun karena gelora aktivisme yang menyala, membuat waktunya lebih banyak dihabiskan di “ruang-ruang” gerakan dan demonstrasi. Hal inilah yang menyebabkan program kuliah formalnya sempat terbengkalai. Tapi segera ia tunaikan dengan menyelesaikan kuliah dari Jurusan [https://afi.uin-suka.ac.id/ Aqidah dan Filsafat], Fakultas Ushuluddin UIN Sunan Kalijaga (2004-2007). Tidak hanya itu, pada upacara wisuda ia dianugerahi Pin Emas dan Piagam Penghargaan oleh Rektor UIN Sunan Kalijaga sebagai Wisudawan Terbaik dan Tercepat pada Wisuda Periode III Tahun Akademik 2007/2008. Kemudian ia melanjutkan pendidikan akademik Strata Dua (S2) pada [https://fisip.unas.ac.id/program-studi-ilmu-politik/ Program Studi Ilmu Politik] Sekolah Pascasarjana Universitas Nasional (UNAS) Jakarta (2010-2014). Sekarang ia sedang menempuh Strata Tiga (S3) pada Program Studi [https://mdkik.pasca.ugm.ac.id/doktor-kepemimpinan-dan-inovasi-kebijakan-dkik/ Doktor Kepemimpinan dan Inovasi Kebijakan] (DKIK) Sekolah Pascasarjana Universitas Gajah Mada (UGM) Yogyakarta.

Berkah keterlibatan dan aktivisme yang dijalani, ia pun dianugerahi penghargaan oleh DPD KNPI Provinsi Jawa Barat atas dedikasi dan kontribusinya terhadap Pembangunan Pemuda Jawa Barat (2019), dan tidak lama kemudian dianugerahi penghargaan oleh DPD KNPI Kab. Karawang sebagai Tokoh Peduli Pemuda (2020).
