Jeremie H. Lefevre (born 1977; French: Jérémie Lefevre) is a French colorectal surgeon and professor of digestive surgery at Sorbonne University and Hôpital Saint-Antoine in Paris. He is known for research on hereditary colorectal cancer syndromes, for coordinating the GRECCAR-6 randomised trial on the interval between chemoradiotherapy and surgery in rectal cancer, and for work on the management of anastomotic leaks after colorectal surgery. He is secretary general of the French Society of Digestive Surgery (Société française de chirurgie digestive, SFCD).

== Education and career ==
Lefevre studied medicine at the Pitié-Salpêtrière faculty of Pierre and Marie Curie University. He was a surgical resident of the Paris hospitals from 2002, obtained his medical doctorate in 2008 and was awarded the AP-HP gold medal in surgery the same year. [ref: Les médailles d'or de l'AP-HP, aaihp.fr] After a research fellowship in Walter Bodmer's laboratory at the Weatherall Institute of Molecular Medicine, University of Oxford (2008–2009), he completed a PhD on familial colorectal cancer at Pierre and Marie Curie University in 2012. [ref: Role of rare variants in undetermined multiple adenomatous polyposis and early-onset colorectal cancer, Journal of Human Genetics]

He was appointed associate professor (maître de conférences des universités – praticien hospitalier) in 2012 [ref: Arrêté portant admission au concours de recrutement de maîtres de conférences des universités – praticiens hospitaliers au titre de l'année 2012, legifrance.gouv.fr] and full professor (professeur des universités – praticien hospitalier) of general surgery by presidential decree of 13 October 2015, with assignment to the department of general and digestive surgery of Hôpital Saint-Antoine. [ref: Décret du 13 octobre 2015 portant nomination, titularisation et affectation (enseignements supérieurs), legifrance.gouv.fr] [ref: Pr Jérémie Lefevre, aphp.fr] Since November 2025 he has headed the department of visceral and digestive surgery of the Sorbonne University faculty of health and coordinated the Île-de-France residency programme (DES) in visceral and digestive surgery. [ref: Arrêté n° SU/DAJI/2026/303 portant nomination, Sorbonne Université]

== Research ==
Lefevre's early work, with Yann Parc at Saint-Antoine, concerned the genetics of colorectal polyposis, including the role of MUTYH in colorectal polyposis, [ref: Implication of MYH in colorectal polyposis, Annals of Surgery] risk factors for desmoid tumours in familial adenomatous polyposis [ref: Risk factors for development of desmoid tumours in familial adenomatous polyposis, British Journal of Surgery] and screening for Lynch syndrome. [ref: Screening for Lynch Syndrome in Colorectal Cancer: Are We Doing Enough?, Annals of Surgical Oncology] As a member of Alex Duval's Inserm team on microsatellite instability and cancer, he contributed to the identification of HSP110 mutations as a prognostic factor in MSI colorectal cancer. [ref: Expression of a mutant HSP110 sensitizes colorectal cancer cells to chemotherapy and improves disease prognosis, Nature Medicine]

He was the coordinating investigator of GRECCAR-6, a French multicentre randomised trial comparing a 7-week and an 11-week interval between the end of neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and surgery for rectal cancer. The trial, published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology in 2016, found no increase in pathological complete response with the longer interval but higher morbidity; [ref: Effect of Interval (7 or 11 weeks) Between Neoadjuvant Radiochemotherapy and Surgery on Complete Pathologic Response in Rectal Cancer: A Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled Trial (GRECCAR-6), Journal of Clinical Oncology] three-year [ref: Does A Longer Waiting Period After Neoadjuvant Radio-chemotherapy Improve the Oncological Prognosis of Rectal Cancer?: Three Years' Follow-up Results of the Greccar-6 Randomized Multicenter Trial, Annals of Surgery] and five-year [ref: Final Results of the GRECCAR-6 Trial on Waiting Period Following Neoadjuvant Radiochemotherapy for Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer: 5 Years of Follow-up, Diseases of the Colon & Rectum] follow-up confirmed the absence of oncological benefit. Within the GRECCAR group he also led a multicentre cohort of 564 patients on delayed coloanal anastomosis [ref: Is Delaying a Coloanal Anastomosis the Ideal Solution for Rectal Surgery: Analysis of a Multicentric Cohort of 564 Patients from the GRECCAR, Annals of Surgery] and a study of outpatient stoma closure. [ref: Outpatient Stoma Closure in 130 Patients. Insights From the GRECCAR Multicentric Study, Annals of Surgery]

Schiavello Group is a privately owned Australian company engaged in commercial furniture design and manufacturing, interior construction and fit-out, property development and workplace technology. It was founded in Melbourne in 1966 by Italian-born furniture maker Tony Schiavello with his younger brother Joe, initially as a partitioning and joinery business. The group is headquartered in Tullamarine, employs around 1,100 people and reported revenue of approximately A$700 million in 2025. It has been described as one of Australia's oldest manufacturers of high-end furniture and is ranked among the country's top 100 private companies.

== History ==

=== Founding and early years (1966–1979) ===
Tony Schiavello, a furniture maker by trade, migrated to Australia from Calabria, southern Italy, in the 1950s. In 1966 he secured a labour-only subcontract to install toilet partitions at 15 William Street, Melbourne, and registered the partnership TT&G with his brother Joe Schiavello and friend Tony Cipollone. Schiavello Bros Pty Ltd was established two years later.

The company's early product was MK1, a series of demountable partitions, and its first large-scale partition project was completed for Victoria Insurance in 1968. Growth led to new factory premises in Airport West from 1970. In 1971 the company produced more than 8,000 voting booths for the Australian Electoral Office ahead of the 1972 Australian federal election. The office furniture operation was established in 1978 with the Series 35 and Series 45 foldable desk collections.

=== Office furniture and expansion (1980s–1990s) ===
In 1982 Schiavello designed its first ergonomic, height-adjustable desks to meet Federal Government requirements for computer desks; the resulting Primatic desk, launched in 1983, was among the first ergonomic desks with a fully user-adjustable main worktop. The company's first workstation system, Interstat, was exhibited at the Orgatec furniture fair in Cologne in 1986, its first international trade show. Interstate offices opened in New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory in the late 1980s, with Queensland, Western Australia and South Australia following by 1993.

In 1990 Tony Schiavello won the National Australia Bank Ethnic Business Award, broadcast live on SBS. In 1992 the company won a contract to supply more than 20,000 workstations to the World Bank headquarters in Washington, D.C., which the company describes as the start of its significant international presence. The following year it completed one of its largest interior construction projects as head contractor for Clayton Utz in Sydney, and launched the Sesto desking system with a worktop height-adjustment design.

In 1995 the Newtech height-adjustable workstation received an award for excellence in design and manufacture of systems furniture at the Australian Furniture Fair, and Schiavello developed the "Hot Desk" concept, described as Australia's first mobile workplace, in collaboration with RMIT's federally funded EcoReDesign programme. Schiavello carried out interior construction and joinery for the opening of Crown Melbourne in 1997, beginning a long-term relationship that included hotel refurbishments in 2007. The company also obtained ISO 14001 environmental management accreditation in the late 1990s.

=== Diversification (2000s) ===
Schiavello established bathroomware company Omvivo and, in 2003, Italian architect Mario Bellini commissioned the company to manufacture the NGV bench for the reopening of the National Gallery of Victoria. In 2005 Victorian Premier Steve Bracks opened the group's purpose-built 70,000 square metre headquarters and factory in Tullamarine, which consolidated the group's divisions on one site. The project was recognised with the 2005 Victorian Master Builder of the Year award. Tony Schiavello was inducted into the Victorian Manufacturing Hall of Fame in 2008.

The group entered property development in 2007 with The Artist, a multi-residential building in Fitzroy developed in joint venture with PDG and completed in 2011. In the same year it took a shareholding in Melbourne hospitality operator Atlantic Group, founded by Hatem Saleh, in which Schiavello (Vic) Pty Ltd became a joint shareholder and Tony Schiavello a director. The group's venues and contracts expanded from Central Pier in Docklands to The Atlantic restaurant at Crown Melbourne, opened in 2011, catering at the Melbourne Cup Carnival from 2011 and the Australian Grand Prix from 2013, Gardens House in the Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria and the Port Melbourne Yacht Club. By 2019 Atlantic Group was Central Pier's anchor tenant; the pier was closed by Development Victoria that year on safety grounds, and Atlantic Group led tenants in a A$100 million Federal Court claim against the agency. Peter Schiavello, Tony's eldest son, who had run the furniture operation since 1982 and served as Deputy Managing Director from 1992, was appointed Managing Director of the group in 2009.

=== Recent history (2010–present) ===
In 2010 the company released Climate, a workstation system designed around the concept of "malleability", in which electronics, shelving and panels are housed in a channel independent of the work table so that layouts can be reconfigured without rebuilding. Schiavello was appointed head contractor for the Sydney Commonwealth Parliament Offices in the early 2010s.

== Introduction ==
The Four Component Instructional Design (4C/ID) Model is an instructional design framework created to help students learn difficult cognitive skills and professional competencies. Jeroen J. G. van Merriënboer, Otto Jelsma, and Fred Paas established the concept in 1992 and it offers a systematic to constructing or building educational programs that integrate information and skills, inside authentic learning experiences.

Neek et al. (2025) states that "The four-component instructional design (4C/ID) model is designed to support complex learning by the facilitation of the transfer of theoretical knowledge into practice [ref: Implementing the four-component instructional design model in professional development programs: a systematic review with a focus on teachers, Frontiers in Education]." The 4C/ID paradigm provides a theoretical foundation for developing learning environments and training programs. The model's four components closely match the qualitative characteristics of good and effective training programs. As such, it is believed that 4C/ID can be extremely imperative in the development of high quality teacher training programs, especially for in-service training, when professionals already have both an educational background and personal experience with their specialized real-world activities.

Unlike instructional approaches that focus on isolated objectives or specific abilities, the 4C/ID Model prioritizes whole task learning and the continual development of competence. It is made up of four interconnected components:

# learning tasks
# supportive information
# procedural knowledge
# part task practice. [ref: Blueprints for complex learning: The 4C/ID-model, Educational Technology Research and Development](van Merriënboer et al. (2002)

It is noteworthy, that this model has been applied in educational and professional training contexts where learners must integrate multiple skills, solve problems, and transfer their learning to uncommon or unfamiliar situations. Its principals are backed by research on cognitive load, acquisition of skills and the development of expertise with special emphasis on promoting effective learning and the transfer of complex cognitive skills [ref: Training for reflective expertise: A four-component instructional design model for complex cognitive skills, Educational Technology Research and Development] (van Merriënboer et al., 1992, 2002).

A meta analysis by Costa et al. (2022) reported positive effects on learning performance [ref: Four-component instructional design (4C/ID) model: a meta-analysis on use and effect, Learning Environments Research], while a systematic review by Qi et al. (2026) identified promising outcomes relating to skill development and knowledge transfer [ref: The Four-Component Instructional Design (4C/ID) Model in Higher Education: A Systematic Literature Review, Journal of University Teaching and Learning Practice], although limitations in the available research remain. Together, these findings articulate the model's relevance to instructional environments requiring learners to integrate and apply complex skills.

== Origins and Development of the 4C/ID Model ==
The Four Component Instructional Design Model emerged in the late 1980s as a response to the constraints of instructional approaches that focused on teaching skills separately. Jeroen J. G. van Merriënboer, Otto Jelsma, and Fred Paas created a framework to help learners build complex cognitive skills that integrate knowledge, procedures and decision making abilities. van Merriënboer et al. published "Training for Reflective Expertise: A Four Component Instructional Design Paradigm for Complex Cognitive Skills [ref: Training Complex Cognitive Skills: A Four-Component Instructional Design Model for Technical Training, Educational Technology] in 1992, which formally established the paradigm.

== Theoretical Foundations of the 4C/ID Model ==

* Cognitive Load Theory

The 4C/ID Model is closely related to cognitive load theory, which investigates how limitations in working memory affect learning. Complex tasks frequently need learners to comprehend many interacting elements at the same time, which might strain their cognitive resources. The model addresses this difficulty by carefully structing learning activities, providing appropriate instructional guidance, and gradually reducing support as learners gain experience (Sweller et al., 2019) [ref: Cognitive Architecture and Instructional Design: 20 Years Later, Educational Psychology Review]

* Whole Task Learning

Whole task learning is a key component of the 4C/ID Model, emphasizing the development of integrated competencies rather than teaching individual skills separately. Learners participate in authentic tasks that simulate real world professional scenarios, allowing them to synchronize their knowledge, abilities and attitudes. Instruction proceeds from simple activities to more complicated scenarios, with help gradually reduced as students gain independence (Frerejean et al., 2019) [ref: Ten steps to 4C/ID: training differentiation skills in a professional development program for teachers, Instructional Science]

* Routine and Non-Routine Skills

Doctor Marrax (born 21 May 1953 as Gerhard "Max" Matheis) is a German magician, street performer, and author. Matheis became known for his stage character Doctor Marrax, a quack doctor and miracle healer inspired by historical travelling medicine men. For several decades, he performed as Doctor Marrax at street festivals, variety and small-theatre venues, fairs, and magic events in Germany and abroad. [ref: Doctor Marrax, Zauber-Pedia]

== Life and career ==

Matheis completed an apprenticeship as a typesetter in 1971 and subsequently worked as an offset lithography assembler, graphic artist, and phototypesetter in the graphic arts industry until 1993.

He began performing traditional magic in 1981. From 1989 to 2002, he was a member of the magic theatre ensemble Ein Magisches Spektakulum, together with Signora Tre Face, Frascatelli, and Shri Magada. During this period, Matheis developed the character of the quack doctor Doctor Marrax, which became his trademark and remained central to his performances for more than three decades.

Matheis became a professional magician in 1992. [ref: Performance 2018, City of Paderborn] He participated in national and international magic competitions. His competition results include:

* 1993: German champion in the category General Magic with Presentation
* 1994: 3rd place in Comedy Magic at the Fédération Internationale des Sociétés Magiques (FISM) World Championships of Magic in Yokohama, Japan
* 1999: 1st place at the International Street Magicians Competition in Sankt Wendel, Germany
* 2000: 2nd place at the French Magie Comique championship in Paris, France
* 2003: 3rd place in Stage Illusions at the FISM World Championships of Magic in The Hague, Netherlands
* 2007: 2nd place with Doctor Marrax & Söhne at the International Street Magicians Competition in Sankt Wendel
* 2012: 2nd place with Doctor Marrax & Söhne at the 13th International Kleinkunstfestival on the island of Usedom

His German championship title and his two third-place finishes at the FISM World Championships in 1994 and 2003 are documented in literature on the history of magic.

From 2002, Matheis performed as a solo artist. Between 2007 and 2015, he performed together with his son Paul Scharkowski under the name Doctor Marrax & Söhne ("Doctor Marrax & Sons").

In 2018, Matheis announced his retirement from performing. He ended his active stage career in 2019.

In addition to his work as a performer, Matheis has been involved in preserving and documenting the history of magic. He collects historical souvenir postcards, magic props, and documents, and has given lectures on the history of magic. [ref: Wissenswertes von Agoston und Bosco bis Sparovitz und Werry, ZZZAUBER Blog]

== Doctor Marrax ==

The character Doctor Marrax portrays a travelling miracle healer, charlatan, and quack doctor from around 1900. With a rolled "R", a Bohemian-style accent, long beard, black top hat, and a mobile "medicinal cart" or "quack doctor's stage", Matheis presented a medicine show combining street theatre, magic, and comedy.

Central to the performances was the supposed universal remedy Marrax-o-fax, a fictional miracle cure with which Doctor Marrax claimed to be able to perform seemingly impossible healings and other magical feats. Among other things, the character claimed that Marrax-o-fax could replace lost eyes, heal deep wounds, and even cause severed heads to grow back. Marrax-o-fax became one of the characteristic elements of the Doctor Marrax persona.

One of the character's recurring introductory phrases was:

:"Birrrger, mecht ich mich vorstellen, bin ich Doctor Marrax!"

The character was conceived as a historical stage persona inspired by the world of travelling medicine men, miracle healers, charlatans, and itinerant entertainers of the late 19th century.

== Publications ==

Together with street performer Radalou, Matheis published the specialist book Anlocken – Fesseln – Abkassieren! Handbuch der Straßenzauberei ("Attract – Captivate – Cash In! A Handbook of Street Magic") in 2008. The book discusses both the artistic and practical aspects of street magic and draws on the authors' experience as street performers.

Matheis has also published articles on magic, including the 2002 article Akustische Täuschungen in der Zauberkunst ("Acoustic Deceptions in Magic") in the German magic journal Magie.

== Film ==

Following his retirement from active stage performance, Matheis increasingly devoted himself to documentary projects. In 2021, he produced the documentary film GILBERT le Saltimbanque – Ein Gespräch unter Gauklern ("Gilbert le Saltimbanque – A Conversation Among Street Performers"). Matheis and Rainer Schwarz co-directed the film. [ref: Neuer Dokufilm von Gerhard Max Matheis: „GILBERT le Saltimbanque – Ein Gespräch unter Gauklern“, Magischer Zirkel von Deutschland]

The film portrays Belgian-French street performer Gilbert Jakubczyk-Liberman, a longtime friend and fellow performer of Matheis. In the documentary, Matheis and Schwarz visit locations associated with Gilbert's life and document his work as a street performer and itinerant entertainer. [ref: Gilbert le Saltimbanque – Ein Gespräch unter Gauklern, Filmhaus Köln]

The documentary has a running time of 105 minutes.

== Work on the history of magic ==

Nura Space is an Australian software as a service company that develops a workplace management platform for hybrid work. Founded in Melbourne in 2017, the company is a subsidiary of the Schiavello Group, a privately owned Australian furniture manufacturing, construction and property business. The platform combines booking of desks, meeting rooms, lockers and car spaces with occupancy analytics, visitor management and space planning tools, and is supported by proprietary IoT hardware.

== History ==
Nura Space was established in 2017 within the Schiavello Group, led by Anton Schiavello, a member of the founding family. The platform was developed from insights gathered during Schiavello's workplace change-management programmes and was initially trialled in a small number of enterprise environments.

The product was publicly launched as a standalone offering in late 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, with the Schiavello Group planning to deploy it across its own seven Australian offices. At launch the company said it would target medium and large enterprises in Australia before expanding to the United States, United Kingdom and Asia, and that the software was hosted on Microsoft Azure with an integration to Microsoft Teams scheduled for early 2021.

In 2023, Schiavello Furniture released NEXUS, a range of technology-integrated furniture including height-adjustable workstations, locker storage and meeting room booking panels that operate through the Nura Space platform.

== Products ==
The Nura Space platform is delivered through a web dashboard and mobile applications for iOS and Android. Its functions include desk, room, locker and car park booking, team and neighbourhood zoning, mobile check-in, visitor management, real-time occupancy analytics and block-and-stack scenario planning for office portfolios. The platform integrates with Microsoft 365, Azure Active Directory and Microsoft Teams, as well as third-party systems such as Vecos smart lockers and occupancy sensors.

The company also designs its own hardware, including the Nura Vision above-desk device, which combines a touchscreen with NFC and presence sensing to provide check-in, desk status indication and ambient availability signalling, and a power control module and remote sit-stand controller for height-adjustable desks.

== Awards ==
In June 2025 Nura Vision, developed by Nura Space and exhibited by its parent company Schiavello, won the Gold award in the Technology – Integrated Solutions category at the Best of NeoCon awards, judged by a 42-member jury at the NeoCon commercial interiors show at The Merchandise Mart, Chicago.

== Ownership ==
Nura Space operates through Nura Space Technology Services Pty Ltd and is backed by the Schiavello Group, whose managing director Peter Schiavello is a co-founder of the company. Schiavello Group has stated it continues to provide support and funding for the platform's development.

= Grass Patch =
Grass Patch was an American rock band from Fort Lauderdale, Florida, active during the 1990s. The band was associated with South Florida’s independent music scene and released a track on the 1995 split 7-inch A Field Guide to Crop Circle Activity, shared with Milk-Shed and released by Space Cadette Records.[1][2]

== History ==
Grass Patch was part of the South Florida underground music scene during the 1990s. In a September 1996 article, Miami New Times described the band as working in a heavier musical style than local punk band Milk-Shed and noted the two groups’ split single on Space Cadette Records.[1]

The band’s documented release, A Field Guide to Crop Circle Activity, was issued in 1995. The record paired Grass Patch with fellow Florida band Milk-Shed and featured elaborate artwork and packaging.[1][2] Grass Patch’s credited track on the split was “Xenogamy.” The tracks “Whoa” and “Live” were credited to Milk-Shed, not Grass Patch.[2]

In an April 2002 article about the Fort Lauderdale band the Remedy Session, Miami New Times described Grass Patch as a noisecore band and reported that it had split up before drummer Alex Osuna and guitarist Chris Polito began working on a new musical project.[3]

== Members ==
The band’s lineup was:

* Ray Sousa – guitar, vocals
* Josh Gibbs – guitar
* Scott Hanzlik – bass
* Alex Osuna – drums[2]

== Discography ==

=== Split releases ===

* A Field Guide to Crop Circle Activity (1995, split 7-inch with Milk-Shed; Space Cadette Records)[1][2]

The other tracks on the split, “Whoa” and “Live,” were credited to Milk-Shed.[2]

Monireh Baradaran Khosroshahi (born 1954–1955 in Tabriz) is an Iranian women's rights activist, political activist, and former political prisoner. [ref: Biography, Forough Book]

== Life and activities ==

Baradaran attended school in Tehran and graduated from the University of Tehran with a degree in sociology. She later continued her studies at the University of Hanover in Germany. She was imprisoned in Evin Prison during the mass executions of Iranian political prisoners in the summer of 1988.

== Arrests and imprisonment ==

Baradaran was first arrested in June 1978 and released in December that year. Following the Iranian Revolution of 1979, she was arrested again in October 1981, alongside her brother and sister-in-law. Her brother was executed 40 days later. Baradaran remained imprisoned for nine years and was released in October 1990. [ref: Monireh Baradaran, Abdorrahman Boroumand Foundation] She witnessed the events surrounding the 1988 prison executions and subsequently published an account of her imprisonment.

Shubha V. Iyengar also known as Shubha Venkatesha Iyengar is an Indian scientist. She is best known for her contributions to civil aviation, defence and indigenous technology sectors in India. She served at the CSIR-National Aerospace Laboratories for a period of approximately five decades (46 years). [ref: A Bengaluru Aerospace Scientist Built the Made-in-India System That Reads Fog for Pilots, thebetterindia.com] [ref: Who is Dr. Shubha V Iyengar? Meet the unsung Indian hero who guides thousands of flights through fog every day by giving runways 'Drishti', The Times of India]

== Biography ==
She was born in Bengaluru as the youngest in a family of nine children. She faced barriers to continue her higher studies in science, at a time when girls in India had severe societal restrictions to pursue their education and career choices. [ref: This Indian woman scientist’s research was published by NASA and her technology now guides flights across India, The Times of India] However, she was encouraged by her father to pursue her studies in science.

== Career ==

Iyengar was a batch topper in academics during her higher studies by achieving distinction in both her graduation and post-graduation studies at the Bangalore University. She also received gold medals in the field of Physics and obtained first rank in MSc physics examination in 1974. Following her distinction pass, she subsequently received a Government of India merit scholarship. [ref: https://www.news18.com/amp/india/one-has-to-persevere-scientist-behind-indias-indigenous-aircraft-landing-system-shares-her-journey-at-news18-amrit-ratna-ws-l-10156554.html] She joined as a research scientist at the National Aerospace Laboratories in 1974, where she was assigned at Material Science Division and Airport Instrument Division. [ref: Meet Padma Shri Shubha V Iyengar, the scientist behind India’s aviation safety tech, India Today] During her stint with, National Aerospace Laboratories, her job role was emphasised heavily on designing and improving devices that support safer aircraft operations. She also focused mainly in developing gadgets to combat challenging weather and low-visibility conditions, which were central to the aviation industry. She also engaged in creating devices incorporating portable, FPGA-based humidity and temperature sensors.

In 2011, Shubha collaborated with the Indian Meteorological Department and conceptualised a unique model to monitor aviation weather and runway visibility measurement, which was later named as "Drishti". Her innovative model "Drishti" transmissometer has since been approved by the Government of India and has been predominantly used in across various international airports in India as well as by the Indian Air Force. [ref: Meet Dr. Shubha Venkatesh Iyengar, Agni missile scientist, whose tech is now being used by every international airport in India, The Economic Times] Prior to her innovation, the aviation industry had faced the longstanding issue with regards to making arrangements to fly the aircraft safely onto fog-covered runways. [ref: 'She helps planes land through fog': Anand Mahindra calls Indian scientist his motivation. Who is Dr Shubha V Iyengar? - The Economic Times, m.economictimes.com] Shubha pioneered to build a cost-effective, indigeneous homegrown system which could measure runway visibility and weather conditions, as well as to detect possibilities for aeroplanes to land safely even when issues pertaining to poor visibility exist. Prior to the introduction of "Drishti", Indian airports had long practiced the approach of purchasing expensive runway visibility measuring instruments from Finland and Australia. Over the years, Drishti also gained widespread international attention, where prominent organizations such as World Meteorological Organization and the International Civil Aviation Organization had recommended the usage of Drishti. She also actively involved in India's defense system and during an occasion, she served as a chief architect to solve complex technical issue that had prevented the Agni missile from reaching its intended target.

She devised a blueprint to develop indigenous components which could withstand temperatures of 3000K, while operating at optimum speed levels of Mach 5. Eventually the indigenous components developed by Iyengar had been mandatorily used for missile systems and ramjet-scramjet engines. Those components have also been vital in India's satellite launch initiatives which have been carried out over the years. Some of her research papers were also published as official reports by NASA, taking insights from Iyengar's technical knowledge on aviation and space.

In 2015, she was conferred with the "Make in India" award, in recognition of her contributions in indigenous technological development and self-reliance. She retired from National Aerospace Laboratories in 2020 after having served for 46 years. [ref: Eight from Karnataka to be honoured with 2026 Padma awards, The Hindu] Shubha was also conferred with the Padma Shri award, India’s fourth-highest civilian honour, in the category of Science and Engineering in 2026, in recognition of her contributions to aerospace technology. [ref: They started small, but left lasting impact: from Anke Gowda to Shubha Iyengar, meet Karnataka’s Padma Shri winners, The Indian Express] [ref: Eight luminaries from Karnataka win Padma awards, The New Indian Express]

Dabloons is a collaborative online role-playing game and Internet meme that became popular on TikTok in November 2022. [ref: Hello traveler…have ye heard about TikTok Dabloons?, The Verge] Within the game, participants collect and spend an imaginary currency called "dabloons" via "encounters" with videos featuring cats as merchants or other characters. [ref: What are dabloons? A guide to TikTok’s new favourite meme currency, Dazed] Its name comes from doubloon, a Spanish gold coin. [ref: What are dabloons?: Tiktok's new imaginary economy explained, The Guardian]

The Internet trend started from an image of a cat with an outstretched paw, which was posted to Instagram in April 2021 with the caption "4 dabloons". Players kept track of their own dabloons balances, and TikTok's recommendation algorithm also supplied personalized encounters to players. Users also collaboratively added thieves, lotteries, government agencies, and rival factions to the game.

Large dabloons giveaways led to fictional hyperinflation, rising prices, and debt. The fictional economy of dabloons was analyzed in a 2026 study in the journal Convergence. [ref: Dabloons, autopsy of a TikTok meme: Self-excitation and self-destruction in social media cultures, Convergence]

Julius Grafton (born 1957) is an Australian entertainment technology publisher, journalist and trade show organiser. He founded the trade magazine CX and the ENTECH exhibition for the professional audio, lighting and audiovisual industry, and is the subject of a chapter in Stuart Coupe's 2018 history Roadies.

== Early career ==
Grafton was born in Melbourne in 1957. He began in the Australian live production industry in the early 1970s, running psychedelic light shows for bands before moving into stage and theatre lighting. Based in Sydney, he started his own lighting company in 1974 and in 1980 opened a production company, Grafton's Sound and Lighting, touring as a sound engineer with Australian rock bands; the first band he worked with regularly was the ska revival group The Allniters. He also founded the loudspeaker manufacturer Australian Monitor. His years on the road, and his views on the working conditions and welfare of road crews, are the subject of a chapter in Stuart Coupe's Roadies: The Secret History of Australian Rock'n'Roll (Hachette, 2018).

== Publishing ==
Grafton moved into publishing in 1990 and edited and published CX Magazine, a trade journal for the entertainment, sound and lighting industry, for almost thirty years. He sold the magazine in January 2020 to VCS Creative Publishing, owned by its then editor Jason Allen, and has continued to contribute articles.

He has written opinion pieces for the general press, including a 2019 Sydney Morning Herald column opposing the New South Wales government's interim music festival guidelines, which he argued would restrict live performance beyond dance festivals.

== ENTECH and other events ==
Grafton founded the ENTECH entertainment technology trade show in Sydney in 1993. It grew into a multi-day exhibition occupying more than 10,000 square metres at the Sydney and Melbourne exhibition centres. In 2003 he sold the event to Exhibitions and Trade Fairs Pty Ltd, a trade show organiser backed by Publishing and Broadcasting Limited, with CX remaining the official show publication. He returned to run the educational program for the 2010 edition under its new owners.

Grafton later reacquired the ENTECH name and relaunched it as the ENTECH Roadshow, a one-day touring format staged annually in Australian capital cities and every second year in New Zealand. A planned United States edition was abandoned before launch ahead of the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2014 he founded SECTECH, a companion roadshow for the security technology industry, which he operated in partnership with a publishing house until 2022, when the partnership broke down and the company was placed in voluntary liquidation.

In 2025 Grafton stepped aside from ENTECH, with Kate McKenzie appointed chief executive, and acquired Sydney PA Hire, a corporate audiovisual rental company. In 2026 Mumbrella reported on his public rejection of an influencer agency's request for about $16,000 of audiovisual services in exchange for exposure.

== Training and industry involvement ==
From about 2001 to 2010 Grafton ran Julius Events College, a privately funded registered training organisation in Sydney offering full-time technical production courses, with scholarships funded by industry suppliers. He has served on the board of CrewCare, a charity for Australian live production workers.

== Book ==
Grafton self-published a memoir, This Could Be Serious, in 2020, with proceeds directed to CrewCare.

== References ==

Hayder Al Hamdany

Hayder Kareem Al Hamdany is an Iraqi-Australian academic, researcher and higher-education leader. Born in Iraq, he developed his academic career across Iraq and Australia, where he has lived, studied and worked in higher education.

His career spans more than two decades in higher education, combining academic scholarship with senior university leadership, academic governance, quality assurance, postgraduate education, internationalisation and international higher-education projects.

His research has developed from applied linguistics and English for Academic Purposes into broader work on education, identity, belonging, intercultural relations and higher education.

Early life and education

Al Hamdany was born in Iraq, where he completed his early education before undertaking university study in the field of education, English language and literature.

He subsequently moved into postgraduate study and developed an academic career connecting Iraqi and Australian higher education.

He completed a Bachelor’s degree in Education, English and Literature at the University of Thi Qar in Iraq.

He later undertook postgraduate study in Australia, completing an MA in Education/TESOL at the University of South Australia and an MPhil at the University of Adelaide.

He subsequently completed a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in Education, specialising in Applied Linguistics, at the University of Adelaide.

His doctoral thesis, An Exploration of Perceptions and Applications of Spoken Register: Iraqi Students at a South Australian University, examined the experiences of Iraqi students using spoken academic English in Australian higher education.

Career in Iraq

University of Kufa

Al Hamdany established a substantial part of his academic and leadership career at the University of Kufa in Iraq.

His work at the university has encompassed teaching, research, postgraduate education, university governance, international scholarships, academic development and international cooperation.

During his career at the University of Kufa, he held a number of leadership and institutional responsibilities, including:

* Secretary of the University Council;
* Director of Missions and Scholarships;
* UNESCO Chair;
* Founding Director of Graduate Studies; and
* academic and research leadership responsibilities within the university.

These positions placed his work at the intersection of academic governance, postgraduate education, international mobility, research development and institutional strategy.

University governance

As Secretary of the University Council, Al Hamdany was involved in university-level governance and institutional decision-making.

His responsibilities included supporting the operation of university governance processes and contributing to the coordination of academic and administrative matters at institutional level.

The position formed an important part of his transition from an academic and researcher into broader higher-education leadership.

Scholarships and international mobility

As Director of Missions and Scholarships, Al Hamdany worked in an area central to the internationalisation of Iraqi higher education.

His responsibilities included matters relating to international scholarships, academic mobility and the development of overseas study opportunities for Iraqi academics and students.

This experience subsequently contributed to his involvement in international university partnerships and European higher-education projects.

Postgraduate education

Al Hamdany also served as Founding Director of Graduate Studies, contributing to the development and coordination of postgraduate education and research at the University of Kufa.

His postgraduate leadership has included academic-program development, research coordination, supervision structures and institutional processes associated with graduate education.

Career in Australia

Al Hamdany subsequently developed a significant academic career in Australia, particularly in South Australia.

His Australian academic experience includes work with the University of Adelaide and the University of South Australia.

His Australian career has combined teaching, research and academic development with an ongoing focus on international students, English language education, higher education and academic quality.

His experience working across Iraqi and Australian universities has provided a comparative perspective on higher-education systems, academic standards, internationalisation and institutional development.

2000s–2010s: Applied linguistics and English language education

During the earlier stage of his research career, Al Hamdany focused primarily on applied linguistics, English language education and English for Academic Purposes.

His research examined how Iraqi students and other English-as-an-additional-language learners develop the language practices required for successful participation in higher education.

His work particularly examined spoken academic register, a relatively underexplored dimension of academic English compared with written academic language.

2013: Research on Iraqi students and academic register

In 2013, Al Hamdany, Michelle Picard, Nina Maadad and Indrawati Darmawan published research examining the perceptions and use of spoken academic register among Iraqi students participating in an English for Academic Purposes program at an Australian university.

[[File:Solid beige.svg|thumb|300x300px|The color beige]]
A beige flag is an Internet slang term for an unusual habit or characteristic considered neither clearly positive nor negative, especially in a romantic relationship. [ref: Why Beige Flags Are TikTok's Latest Obsession, [[Time (magazine)] The term is derived from the terms "red flag" for negative or worrying behavior and "green flag" for positive or desirable qualities in a romantic partner. [ref: beige flag, Dictionary.com] In 2023, users shared videos describing their partners' beige flags as part of a TikTok trend, often with jazz music in the background.

In May 2022, TikTok user @[user] coined the term to indicate signs that someone might be "very boring". Her examples included cliché discussions of food, and references to mainstream television programs on dating profiles. [ref: Beige Flags Are the Latest Dating Phenomenon Dividing the Internet, [[Glamour (magazine)] In early 2023, the meaning of the term underwent a semantic shift to refer to generally harmless habits.

In 2023, Oxford University Press included beige flag on its shortlist for the Oxford Word of the Year. [ref: Eight words go head-to-head for Oxford Word of the Year 2023, Oxford University Press] A 2024 analysis published in Contexts found that according to Google Trends, search interest in the term peaked in June 2023 and fell sharply by the end of that year. [ref: It's Still Complicated, Contexts]

Draft text:
The USC Signal and Image Processing Institute (SIPI) is a research institute within the Ming Hsieh Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering in the USC Viterbi School of Engineering, focused on signal and image processing.

==History and research==

SIPI was established in 1972 (initially as the USC Image Processing Institute, or IPI) by Professors William K. Pratt and Harry C. Andrews with support from ARPA. [ref: Image Processing Research Semiannual Technical Report: 3 August 1971 through 29 February 1972, Defense Technical Information Center] Image processing was in the early stages of development in the 1960s and 1970s, and SIPI/IPI was one of the first university groups in the world dedicated to image processing research [ref: 40 Years at SIPI: The Past, Present and Beyond] [ref: USC Living History Project - Dr. Alexander A. Sawchuk (2022)]. In addition to performing fundamental early research that helped lay the foundation for the JPEG and MPEG image and video compression standards [ref: Machine vision: The past, the present and the future See also [https://www.vision-systems.com/knowledge-zone/article/14069209/the-history-of-machine-vision adapted online version, “The history of machine vision” (2019)].] [ref: Culture, Communication, and an Information Age Madonna, IEEE Professional Communication Society Newsletter] [ref: Nearly Every JPEG on Earth Runs on Math a Reviewer Called Too Simple to Fund in 1972, Fstoppers], SIPI/IPI was also a key member of the ARPANET (the precursor to the Internet) where it provided image processing hardware and software services for other members of the network [ref: IMAGE PROCESSING OVER THE ARPA COMPUTER NETWORK, University of Arizona Libraries Campus Repository].

In the early 1970s, SIPI/IPI research focused on the basic theory of image processing with applications to image compression and image transmission/communication (including pioneering work on transform coding [ref: Origins of the zigzag scan in transform-based picture coding, SPIE] [ref: How I came up with the discrete cosine transform, Digital Signal Processing]), image restoration and enhancement (including topics such as denoising, super-resolution, and color enhancement), image analysis, and display.

In 1977, SIPI released the first version of the USC-SIPI image database [ref: The USC - Image Processing Institute Data Base, Defense Technical Information Center] [ref: The USC-SIPI Image Database]. The database provides a large collection of standard test images that were scanned and digitized using SIPI's image acquisition hardware. Many of these images have been influential in image processing research [ref: Data Compression: The Complete Reference, Springer] [ref: Image Restoration: Fundamentals and Advances, CRC Press] [ref: Forty years of color quantization: a modern, algorithmic survey, Artificial Intelligence Review], including the widely-used, Peppers, and Lenna test images.

Over the years, SIPI's scope expanded beyond just image processing to involve a broader range of signal processing applications, including audio signal processing, speech processing, video processing, and the processing of data from a variety of sensors, imaging systems, and other information sources. [ref: USC Signal and Image Processing Institute]

== References ==

Bloxd.io is a free online video game, released in January of 2021 by an independent developer, Arthur Benedict Baker. It is a sandbox game inspired by the games Minecraft, and Roblox. The game features blocky 3D graphics all ran on a web browser, needing no download. As of 2026 Bloxd.io has 461 million plays on Crazy Games and an average player count of 21,000 people.

== Gamemodes ==
Bloxd.io has many gamemodes to choose from. The gamemodes range from being Open world, games such as survival, creative, and Bloxdsmp where you can gather resources, farm, and build houses. Another genre of gamemodes is PvP. PvP gamemodes include bedwars, Skyblock, and cube warfare. In these gamemodes, it is fast paced, and player will need to utilize their material to the max. Skill games are another type of gamemode mostly including parkour, where you would have to jump over obstacles to make it to the end. Bloxd.io also has a feature where you can create a new world where you have the power of using commands and code blocks to make your own mini games. None of the gamemodes contain a pay-wall [ref: Bloxd.io Wiki, bloxd-io.fandom.com]

== Ranks ==
Bloxd.io has only 1 rank, Super Rank. Super Rank Is a 30 days paid rank added on December 18, 2024. The rank is not pay-to-win because it doesn't give the user any gameplay advantage. The rank's perks are cosmetics. Spending $10 on Super Rank would give you the following, visual badges, name colors (would allow you to change the color of your username), capes, and remove all advertisements. The only free way of getting Super Rank is through winning it through a YouTube giveaway, or reporting a bug. [ref: Bloxd.io Wiki, bloxd-io.fandom.com]

Fox On Ice is the joint artistic project of writer and performer Anna Luca Poloni and composer and musician Christian Mair. The shows are Performing Arts Concerts which combine original music, lyrics and film with performance.

Recent works are Orlando Trip (after Ludovico Ariosto and Virginia Woolf) and Polyxena – Female Voices of Troy (based on narratives surrounding the Trojan War). [ref: Mit Orlando auf Reisen, Die Presse] [ref: Macherin der Wortwiege mit Projekt in der Türkei, Kurier]

Fox On Ice is Vienna-based and touring internationally.

== Background and artistic work ==

Fox On Ice is the artistic project of Anna Luca Poloni and Christian Mair, which combines literary and mythological sources with original music, text, film and performance.

Currently, Fox On Ice is working on the trilogy “FE.MALE MYTH”, which consists of Orlando Trip (touring since 2022) [ref: Thomas Maurer ++ Fox On Ice, Ö1 Kulturjournal], Polyxena – Female Voices of Troy (premiered in 2026) and Joanna’s Love (planned for 2028).

== Orlando Trip ==

The Performing Arts Concert Orlando Trip is the first part of FE.MALE MYTH and deals with themes of transformation, identity, gender, travel and freedom.

It is based on Ludovico Ariosto’s epic poem Orlando furioso and Virginia Woolf’s novel Orlando: A Biography. Original songs and intermezzi are telling the story of the key moments in Orlando’s life. Film is an integral part of the show.

The music is characterised by Die Presse as incorporating indie, punk, chanson and spoken poetry.

Orlando Trip has been presented internationally since 2022, including the United States, Canada, Europe, Turkey and Sri Lanka. [ref: ORLANDO TRIP - Performing Arts Concert by Fox On Ice, Austrian Embassy Ottawa] [ref: Orlando Trip, Austrian Cultural Forum Washington DC]

In 2024, a studio concept album Orlando Trip was released. [ref: Musikalischer Tribut an Orlando auf Virginia Wolfs Spuren, Kronen Zeitung]

== Polyxena – Female Voices of Troy ==

Polyxena – Female Voices of Troy is the second part of FE.MALE MYTH and premiered on 13 August 2026 at the Troy Museum in Çanakkale, Turkey. [ref: POLYXENA – Female Voices of Troy, Austrian Cultural Forum Istanbul]

Drawing on literary and mythological traditions surrounding the Trojan War, including Homer, Euripides and Ovid, Polyxena approaches the material from female perspectives.

The work combines music, literature, film and live performance.

On October 7, 2026 Austrian Radio Ö1 broadcasted a radiosession of Polyxena. [ref: Neue Lesarten überlieferter Mythen: Fox On Ice, Ö1]

Hazrat Khawaja Pir Ghulam Ahmed Chishti Sabri is a Sufi saint of the Chishtiya Sabriya order based in Matli, District Badin, Sindh, Pakistan.

== Biography ==
Pir Ghulam Ahmed Chishti Sabri was associated with the Chishti Sabri spiritual lineage. His teachings focused on love, peace, and service to humanity in accordance with Sufi traditions.

== Shrine ==
His shrine (Dargah) is located in Matli, Sindh. Devotees from across Sindh visit the shrine to pay respects.

== Urs ==
The annual Urs (death anniversary) of Hazrat Pir Ghulam Ahmed Chishti Sabri is observed every year on 6th March at his shrine in Matli. The Urs is observed with religious devotion. The gathering includes recitation of the Holy Quran, Naat Khwani, and Mehfil-e-Sama. A large number of devotees, scholars and spiritual leaders attend the Urs. Langar is also distributed among attendees.

== Legacy ==
He is remembered for his contributions to promoting Sufi teachings, interfaith harmony, and spiritual guidance in the region of Matli and lower Sindh.

Vino Volta is an Australian Wine producer based in the Swan Valley (Western Australia) Wine Region. It was founded by winemaker Garth Cliff and Kristen McGann, and it released its first wines in 2019 [ref: WA Wine Review 2026, Ray Jordan Wine] [ref: Vino Volta, Wine Companion]. Vino Volta is known mainly for producing Chenin Blanc and Grenache from Swan Valley fruit and has been associated with renewed interest in the region's wines. [ref: The Best Swan Valley Wineries Featured in the 2020 YGOW Top 50, Young Gun of Wine] [ref: What to Know About Swan Valley, the Birthplace of Western Australian Wine?, Vino Joy News]

== History ==
Cliff began working in the wine industry around 2000. He held winemaking roles in the Hunter Valley wine region and at the South Australian wineries Stonehaven and Tintara, and worked vintages in Napa Valley and on California's Central Coast before joining Houghton Wines in the Swan Valley. He was a winemaker at Houghton for about ten years.

Cliff began developing the Vino Volta label in 2018, and its first wines were released in 2019. Cliff and McGann also established a wine import business, Wine Terroirists.

In 2020, Vino Volta was named in the Young Gun of Wine Top 50.

== Vineyards and Winemaking ==
Vino Volta sources fruit from leased vineyards and independent growers, mainly in the Swan Valley, with some fruit from the Geographe wine region and the Perth Hills. The producer focuses on varieties suited to warm climates, particularly Chenin Blanc and Grenache, alongside other varieties including Dolcetto, Vermentino and Fiano, and a fortified Verdelho.

The Vino Volta winemaking process uses wild yeast fermentation and no added enzymes, with techniques such as skin contact, whole-bunch fermentation and maturation in older oak. Production is around 2,800 dozen per year, and the wines are sold locally and exported to the United States, Japan, Singapore and Sweden.

== Reception ==
Wine writer Ray Jordan profiled Vino Volta in his WA Wine Review 2026, describing Cliff as an advocate for the Swan Valley as a warm-climate wine region. He rated the producer's Intimations of Immortality Liqueur Verdelho 98 out of 100. The producer has also been reviewed in Business News, [ref: Review: Elements in balance at Vino Volta, www.businessnews.com.au] The West Australian, [ref: Looking back to the future with chenin blanc, The West Australian] and Gourmet Traveller. [ref: Wine country: Swan Valley wineries to know about, Gourmet Traveller]

The company develops digital products intended to address needs across the private and public sectors. Its broader ambition is to support the adoption of digital tools that can improve record-keeping, transaction transparency, and operational efficiency.

== Products and services ==

Blockmec Verify is a product authentication and verification initiative within Blockmec Technology's product portfolio. It is designed to help users verify product information and address risks associated with counterfeit goods.

The product focuses on digital verification and its potential applications in product identification, consumer protection, and counterfeit-risk detection.

=== BinPay ===

BinPay is a digital payment initiative focused on waste-management billing and collection processes. It aims to support the digitization of waste bills and provide a more organized approach to recording payments.

Draft text:
Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta: Travelling Islam is an edited academic book edited by Abbas Panakkal and published by Palgrave Macmillan in 2026. It examines the travels of the fourteenth-century Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta and the historical relationships between Islam, commerce and cultural exchange across Africa, Asia and Europe. [ref: Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta: Travelling Islam, Palgrave Macmillan]

== Contents ==

The volume consists of fifteen (15) chapters arranged in three sections: "Historical Accounts of Travel and Tradition", "Textual Tradition, Jurisprudence and Cultural Exchange", and "Pilgrimage, Faith, and Identity Across Borders". The chapters examine Ibn Battuta's accounts of African societies, religious and commercial networks in South and Southeast Asia, Islamic finance in the Maldives, the history of Calicut, and Muslim communities in precolonial Malabar. Other subjects include the transmission of cultural traditions between India and Southeast Asia, women and religion in Ibn Battuta's accounts of India, and pilgrimage and religious revivalism in West Africa. [ref: Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta: Travelling Islam, Palgrave Macmillan]

The contributions approach Ibn Battuta's travel narrative, commonly known as the Rihla, from historical, archaeological, religious, legal and cultural perspectives. The final chapter examines encounters between travelling musicians and Indian performers in nineteenth-century Australia.

== Publication ==

The book was published by Palgrave Macmillan, an imprint of Springer Nature, as part of the Palgrave Series in Indian Ocean World Studies.

The pront edition has ISBN 978-3-031-97882-1, and the electronic edition has ISBN 978-3-031-97883-8. [ref: Faith, Commerce, and Cultural Exchange in the World of Ibn Battuta: Travelling Islam, Palgrave Macmillan]

Draft: Parsamian 21

Draft text:
Parsamian 21 (also spelled Parsamyan 21) is a cometary reflection nebula approximately 400 pc (1,304 ly) away in the constellation Aquila. The was discovered by Armenian astronomer Elma Parsamian in 1965 and is one out of 23 cometary nebulae discovered by her. [ref: Catalogue of Cometary Nebulae Discovered on Palomar Maps, Izvestiya Akademiya Nauk Armyanskoi SSR]

Parsamian 21 is highly polarized and illuminated by its central star designated as HBC 687. The nebula exhibits a fan-like structure with two highly illuminated bands on both sides. Two parallel bands also extend across the head of the nebula and the central star, these bands formed by aligned grains in the circumstellar disc surrounding the central star. The polarization structure of Parsamian 21 is very similar to well-studied cometary nebulae like NGC 2261 and NGC 6729. [ref: A polarization study of the cometary nebula Parsamyan 21, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society] A study utilizing an F814W filter revealed a faint southern structure. The northern structure that makes up most of Parsamian 21 features a compact northern knot and a bowed shaped southern knot. [ref: The FU Orionis--Type Spectrum and Bipolar Outflow of Parsamyan 21, Astrophysical Journal] A study reported 2-3 mag brightness fluctuations in the B band between 1966 and 1990, most of the time, Parsamian 21 barely or does not fluctuate and has remained constant at roughly 15 per cent, this leads to no significant flux have been detected in longer wavelengths. [ref: Spectroscopic observations of parsamian 21, Astronomy and Astrophysics]

Cental star HBC 687 is a low-mass, pre-main sequence FU Orionis star with an edge-on circumstellar disc. The disc appears to be flat, extending between 48 and 360 au from the central star. [ref: High-resolution polarimetry of Parsamian 21: revealing the structure of an edge-on FU Ori disc, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society] [ref: Massive Compact Disks around FU Orionis–type Young Eruptive Stars Revealed by ALMA, The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series] An of gas with a solar mass of approximately surrounds HBC 687. This envelope is expanding at about 120 km/sec away from the central star. [ref: Investigation of the cometary nebula Parsamyan 21, Astrofizika]

He was knighted on 18 May 1542.

== Political career ==
He also served as clerk of the counting house by 1520; treasurer of the chamber from 1 May 1522 till 1 January 1524; cofferer of the Household from January 1524 till 31 March 1547; justice of the peace for Buckinghamshire from 1525 till 1543, for Middlesex from 1537 till 1543, quorum Buckinghamshire, and Middlesex from 1554 till 1558/59; constable of Scarborough Castle in Yorkshire from 1529 till 1537; high treasurer of all the mints from 25 March 1544 till his death; member of the Privy Council from 6 till 30 October 1549, and 29 July 1553 till November 1558; commissioner of relief in Buckinghamshire, and Middlesex in 1550, commissioner of goods of churches and fraternities in 1553, commissioner of subsidy in Buckinghamshire in 1558; and receiver-general of the Exchequer on 1 December 1553.

== Family ==
He was the second son of Peter Peckham of London and Denham by his second wife Elizabeth, the daughter of Henry Eburton of London. By 1516, he was married to Anne, the daughter of John Cheyne of Chesham Bois, Buckinghamshire and they had four sons (including Henry and Sir Robert Peckham) and two daughters.

[ref: GIST Kenya - Green Interventions for Sustainable Towns, www.gist-ke.org] [ref: Seeding Climate-Smart Food Systems in Kenya, The Pollination Project] [ref: Day of the African Child: B-Ball for Life introduced in Kenya, sportanddev]

[ref: The Ground-Level Changemaker: How Emmanuel Is Rebuilding Communities From the Inside Out - Peace First] In its early work in Kisumu County, GIST Kenya has focused on sustainable waste management and environmental health, including research on healthcare sharps waste and the safety of informal waste workers. Mübeccel Akdis, is a Turkish physician and immunologist based in Switzerland. She is a professor at the University of Zurich and leads the Immune Regulation research group at the Swiss Institute of Allergy and Asthma Research (SIAF) in Davos. Her research focuses on mechanisms of immune tolerance in allergic diseases, allergen-specific immunotherapy, and regulatory immune-cell populations. [ref: Editorial: Women in primary immunodeficiencies, Frontiers in Immunology]

== Education and career ==
Akdis graduated from the Faculty of Medicine at Uludağ University in Bursa, Turkey, in 1985. She joined the Swiss Institute of Allergy and Asthma Research in 1995, where she received a PhD in immunology, worked as a postdoctoral scientist and became a group leader in 2003. [ref: Board Member Biographies – Mübeccel Akdis, European Journal of Immunology]

She completed her habilitation (Venia Legendi) in experimental immunology at the Faculty of Medicine of the University of Zurich in 2005 and later became a professor at the university.

== Research ==
Akdis's research has addressed the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying immune tolerance and allergic inflammation. A 2023 editorial in Frontiers in Immunology described her as having contributed to understanding skin allergy and atopic dermatitis and as having played a leading role in research on immune-tolerance mechanisms.

Her research has included studies of allergen tolerance, high-dose allergen exposure in humans, mechanisms of allergen-specific immunotherapy, regulatory T cells, regulatory natural killer cells and IL-10-producing regulatory B cells.

More recently, her research has examined allergen-specific B-cell responses and their roles in food allergy and the development of immune tolerance. [ref: FEBS Datta Lecture – Mechanisms of food allergy and the role of allergen-specific B cells, 49th FEBS Congress]

== Awards and recognition ==
In 2006, Akdis received the Sedat Simavi Medicine Award.

In 2018, the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology (ACAAI) presented Akdis with its International Distinguished Fellow Award. [ref: 2018 Award Winners, ACAAI Annual Scientific Meeting] The award is given to an individual living outside the United States and Canada who has demonstrated scholarly achievement, leadership or an outstanding professional reputation, or has participated in ACAAI's international activities. [ref: Awards and Lectureships, American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology]

In 2020, she received the Paul Ehrlich Award for Experimental Research from the European Academy of Allergy and Clinical Immunology. The University of Zurich reported that the award recognized her long-term research on allergy, immune regulation and skin immunology. [ref: Research Awards 2020, University of Zurich]

In the same year, the Government of the Canton of Graubünden presented Mübeccel Akdis and Cezmi Akdis with a Recognition Award for their research on human immune regulation. [ref: Anerkennungspreis an Mübeccel und Cezmi Akdis, Faculty of Medicine, University of Zurich]

Akdis received the Medical Science Award of the Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı Medical Awards in 2021. The Turkish Academy of Sciences reported that the award was given for her research in human immunology and noted that the Medical Science Award recognizes scientists whose body of research has made contributions to science at an international level. [ref: TÜBA-GEBİP Ödülü Sahibi Prof. Çadırcı'ya "Dr. Nejat F. Eczacıbaşı Tıp Ödülü", Turkish Academy of Sciences]

In 2025, Akdis received the FEBS Datta Medal from the Federation of European Biochemical Societies. She delivered the Datta Lecture, titled "Mechanisms of food allergy and the role of allergen-specific B cells", at the 49th FEBS Congress. [ref: Plenary Lectures, 49th FEBS Congress]

In 2026, the Austrian Society for Allergology and Immunology (ÖGAI) awarded Akdis the Karl Landsteiner Medal. The society describes the medal as recognizing scientists who have made important contributions to immunology. [ref: ÖGAI Medals – awardees 2026, Austrian Society for Allergology and Immunology]

Apoorva Gokhale (born 5 December 1973) is an Indian Hindustani classical vocalist associated with the Gwalior gharana. She was born into a family of traditional musicians and is the granddaughter of vocalist Gajananrao Joshi and the great granddaughter of musician Antubua Joshi, who served as a court musician in the erstwhile state of Aundh. [ref: ]

== Early life and training ==
Gokhale began learning Hindustani classical music at the age of five under the guidance of her grandfather, Gajananrao Joshi. She later received training from her uncle, Madhukar Joshi. She also received guidance from her father, Manohar Joshi, her aunt Sucheta Bidkar, and vocalist Ulhas Kashalkar. [ref: A Khayal Recital by Apoorva Gokhale, NCPA]

She later received guidance from Pt. Shankar Abhyankar, Manik Bhide, Ashwini Bhide-Deshpande, Pt. Yashwant Mahale and Pt. Arun Kashalkar. [ref: Apoorva Gokhale & Pallavi Joshi Official Website, www.apoorvapallavi.com]

== Musical style ==
Gokhale's approach to khayal singing incorporates lyrical and evocative expression while maintaining the traditional structure of the form. Her performances emphasise the development of the raga through alaap and improvisation, along with attention to swara and laya (rhythm). [ref: Ghan Garaje: Monsoon Melodies, NCPA]

She has been described as presenting khayal through a systematic development of the raga, combining melodic expression with rhythmic structure. [ref: Ghan Garaje: Monsoon Melodies, NCPA]

Isima is a hair care brand founded by Colombian singer-songwriter Shakira. Launched in July 2025, the brand was developed to cater primarily to wavy, curly, coily, and highly porous hair types.

The brand's name is derived from the Spanish feminine suffix -ísima, which translates to "extra" or "maximum". Isima's initial product line includes shampoos, conditioners, curl creams, and scalp treatments formulated with Latin American-sourced botanicals, such as Peruvian maca root extract, Brazilian sugarcane, and Mexican aloe. Upon its launch, the brand debuted exclusively through its direct-to-consumer website and the United States cosmetics retailer Ulta Beauty.

== History ==
Before launching, the Isima brand was in development for three to four years, a process inspired by Shakira's personal struggles managing her naturally curly, thick hair, which had become highly porous and damaged from frequent styling, coloring, and heat treatments throughout her career. [ref: Isima, Isima: Shakira is Serving Hair Care con Amor, American Salon] [ref: Exclusiva: Shakira pone a ritmo tu melena con Ísima su nueva línea de productos para el cabello. ¡Enamórate de sus productos!, People en Español] [ref: ¡Ahora empresaria! Shakira lanza Ísima, su nueva línea para el cabello, así puedes adquirirla - Telemax] To address the lack of products catering to the complex hair textures of the Latin community and the industry's reliance on oversimplification, she partnered with Sid Katari, who serves as the brand's CEO and founding member. [ref: I Tried Shakira’s Curly Hair Care Line Isima On My Type 4 Hair—Here’s What Happened, Forbes] The brand's identity and packaging were designed by the agency Established, utilizing a "joyful maximalism" aesthetic based on the brand's "más es más" (more is more) philosophy. [ref: How Shakira's Hair Care Brand Isima Breaks the Celebrity Brand Mold, Dieline]

Isima announced its launch in June 2025. [ref: Shakira launches haircare brand isima, Fashion and Beauty Monitor] The brand officially debuted its initial eight-product lineup through its direct-to-consumer website on June 16, 2025, followed by an exclusive physical retail launch at Ulta Beauty on July 6, 2025. The initial collection included items designed to target the health of the scalp, cortex, and cuticle, utilizing Latin American-sourced botanicals such as Peruvian maca root extract, Brazilian sugarcane, and Mexican aloe. Following its United States retail rollout, the brand expanded to flagship locations in Mexico in August 2025. The brand expanded to the UK in October 2025. [ref: Shakira conquista Europa, pero ahora como empresaria: su marca de cuidado capilar debuta en el Reino Unido, infobae] [ref: Shakira desembarca en Europa con isima, su línea de cosmética capilar, La Razón]

== Products ==
Upon its launch in June 2025, Isima introduced an initial lineup of eight products intended to create a comprehensive wash day routine for diverse hair textures and porosities. [ref: Latin-Rooted, Clinically-Proven Haircare Brand isima, Ignited by Shakira Mebarak, Promises To Give Hair What It Deserves: More, PR Newswire] The brand utilizes culturally inspired Spanish names for several of its formulas, reflecting the Shakira's heritage. [ref: I Tried Shakira's New Haircare Line—Here's How My Curls Held Up, Who What Wear] Isima's products are all vegan, cruelty-free and use susainable packaging. [ref: Colombian singer Shakira enters the beauty space with new hair care line, isima, Premium Beauty News] [ref: Meet Isima, Shakira’s Most Personal Project Yet, WWD]

The inaugural collection includes:

* Reset Clarifying Shampoo – A deeply cleansing shampoo designed to strip away product buildup and detoxify the hair and scalp. [ref: Here Are the Five Best Products to Shop from Shakira's Haircare Brand Isima, Billboard]
* Riquísima Hydrating Shampoo – A daily moisturizing cleanser.
* Suavísima Hydrating Conditioner – A hydrating and detangling daily conditioner.
* Súperbomba Triple Repair Peptide Mask – A protein-rich, restorative deep conditioning treatment designed to repair damaged hair.
* All In Restorative Leave-In Conditioner – A softening cream that doubles as a thermal heat protectant (up to 450°F).
* Curls Don't Lie Curl Perfector – A curl-defining styling cream named in reference to Shakira's hit song "Hips Don't Lie".
* Iconic Densifying Scalp Serum – A targeted treatment intended to promote a healthy scalp and encourage thicker, fuller hair density.
* Delicia Reparative Hair Oil – A nourishing hair oil designed for moisture retention and shine.

== Reception ==
Within its first few months of availability, Isima became the top-selling hair care line at Ulta Beauty in the United States, as well as the retailer's third best-selling brand overall. [ref: Isima, la marca capilar de Shakira, logra su cuarto premio internacional de belleza en solo tres meses, Infobae] Following its initial launch, the brand expanded its retail presence in Mexico, opening physical retail spaces in shopping centers such as Antara in Polanco and Galerías Metepec in Toluca.

Steffen Klamt (born February 4, 1972 in Magdeburg) is a German researcher in computational and systems biology. Since 2009 he is a research group leader at the Max Planck Institute for Dynamics of Complex Technical Systems in Magdeburg.

=Education and professional career=

Steffen Klamt studied Applied Systems Science at the University of Osnabrück and received his Diploma degree in 1998. From 1998-2005 he was a PhD student at the Max Planck Institute for Dynamics of Complex Technical Systems in Magdeburg and received his doctoral degree (Dr.-Ing.) with a thesis on Metabolic Network Modeling at the University of Stuttgart. Since 2009 he heads the research group Analysis and Redesign of Biological Networks [ref: ARB Group, Max-Planck-Institut Für Dynamik Komplexer Technischer Systeme Magdeburg] at the Max Planck Institute in Magdeburg.

=Research=

Steffen Klamt’s research focuses on systems and computational biology, with a particular emphasis on metabolic networks and metabolic engineering. His research group develops algorithms and mathematical modeling approaches to analyze cellular metabolism at the systems level and to enable the rational engineering of microbial cell factories for biotechnological applications. Theoretical investigations are frequently combined with experimental studies, particularly using Escherichia coli and other bacterial model organisms.

===Major research contributions===

* Metabolic network analysis: Klamt and coworkers have developed computational methods for the analysis of metabolic networks based on stoichiometric and constraint-based modeling approaches. This work includes the theory and application of elementary modes for metabolic pathway analysis, [ref: Von der Information zur Funktion, Deutschlandfunk] [ref: Metabolic network structure determines key aspects of functionality and regulation, Nature] [ref: Computation of elementary modes: a unifying framework and the new binary approach, BMC Bioinformatics] [ref: From elementary flux modes to elementary flux vectors: Metabolic pathway analysis with arbitrary linear flux constraints, PLoS Computational Biology] concepts for analyzing the effects of thermodynamic constraints on metabolism, [ref: OptMDFpathway: Identification of metabolic pathways with maximal thermodynamic driving force and its application for analyzing the endogenous CO2 fixation potential of Escherichia coli, PLoS Computational Biology] [ref: Network-wide thermodynamic constraints shape NAD(P)H cofactor specificity of biochemical reactions, Nature Communications] and methods for efficiently constructing metabolic models with enzyme-capacity constraints. [ref: Automatic construction of metabolic models with enzyme constraints, BMC Bioinformatics]

* Integration of constraint-based and kinetic modeling (COBRA-k): Klamt’s group introduced the COBRA-k framework, which integrates constraint-based and kinetic metabolic modeling to predict enzyme abundances, metabolite concentrations, and metabolic fluxes in cellular metabolism. [ref: COBRA-k: A powerful framework bridging constraint-based and kinetic metabolic modeling, Science Advances]

* Minimal cut sets and metabolic engineering: Klamt developed the computational framework of minimal cut sets for metabolic networks. [ref: Minimal cut sets in biochemical reaction networks, Bioinformatics] [ref: Enumeration of smallest intervention strategies in genome-scale metabolic networks, PLoS Computational Biology] [ref: ) An extended and generalized framework for the calculation of metabolic intervention strategies based on minimal cut sets, PLOS Computational Biology] [ref: Minimal cut sets in metabolic networks: from conceptual foundations to applications in metabolic engineering and biomedicine, Briefings in Bioinformatics] The approach can be used to identify combinations of metabolic interventions for redirecting cellular metabolism towards the production of desired compounds. [ref: Growth-coupled overproduction is feasible for almost all metabolites in five major production organisms, Nature Communications] The methodology was applied to guide the metabolic engineering of an E. coli strain for high-yield production of itaconic acid. [ref: Model-Based metabolic engineering enables high yield itaconic acid production by Escherichia coli, Metabolic Engineering]

* Bioprocess design: His research also includes concepts and strategies for the design and optimization of biotechnological production processes. [ref: When do two-stage processes outperform one-stage processes?, Biotechnology Journal] [ref: Design of microbial catalysts for two-stage processes, Nature Reviews Bioengineering] [ref: Model-based optimization of cell-free enzyme cascades exemplified for the production of GDP-fucose, Metabolic Engineering]

== Gildas Loaëc ==
Gildas Loaëc (born 1973) is a French entrepreneur and music producer. He is best known as co-founder of the lifestyle brand Maison Kitsuné. In the mid-1990s he became closely involved with the electronic duo Daft Punk. He later turned Kitsuné into a record label, fashion brand, and café chain that mixes Japanese and French influences. [ref: Gildas Loaëc, le roman du renard, Libération] [ref: In Bali, a House That Taught a Fashion Executive How to Relax, The New York Times]

== Early life ==
Loaëc was born in 1973 in Lesneven, in the Finistère department of Brittany. At lycée he became friends with Loïc Prigent, who went on to become a fashion journalist. The two made fanzines, ran a radio show, and went to some of the early raves in France and the UK.

== Career ==
=== Street Sounds ===
In 1995 Loaëc opened a vinyl record shop called Street Sounds near the rue de Rivoli in Paris. It specialized in house and techno and quickly turned into a hangout spot for DJs and musicians in the French electronic scene. Regular customers included Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo (who later formed Daft Punk) as well as the Japanese designer Masaya Kuroki, who later became Loaëc's business partner.

=== Association with Daft Punk ===
From the mid-1990s onward Loaëc was part of Daft Punk's inner circle and stayed involved with the duo for about fifteen years. He has called himself an “homme à tout faire," describing his role as someone who did a bit of everything. He is credited as artistic director on several of the group’s album covers and also ran their individual labels: Roulé (founded by Bangalter) and Crydamoure (founded by de Homem-Christo). Both labels put out a number of French house records during the late 1990s and early 2000s.

=== Maison Kitsuné ===
In 2002 Loaëc and Kuroki started Kitsuné (later Maison Kitsuné) as a record label. The name means “fox” in Japanese and points to the brand’s Franco-Japanese identity. What began as a label later added fashion and cafés and eventually opened stores and locations in several countries. [ref: How Kitsuné Cultivated a Loyal Fashion Fanbase Through Music, The Business of Fashion]

Fashion accounts for the large majority of the brand’s revenue. By the mid-2020s the company operated more than 75 fashion boutiques worldwide, with particularly strong sales in Asia.

=== Café Kitsuné and later expansion ===
The first Café Kitsuné opened in Tokyo in 2013. Later it expanded to Paris and other cities, becoming an integral part of the brand’s lifestyle offering. By the mid-2020s there were approximately 35 cafés worldwide.

== Personal life ==
Loaëc is based in Tokyo.
