Memorygram is an American company that produces printed memoir books from personal stories collected through written, recorded, and telephone responses to guided questions. It also sells memorial products that link to online memorial pages.

== History ==
According to a 2022 interview published by The Ancestor Hunt, Memorygram began operating in August 2021 and launched its service in November 2021. The founder interviewed, Sara Damiano, described herself as a clinical social worker and gerontologist and said the company was created as a legacy-building tool for individuals and families. Later coverage credits childhood friends Paul Damiano and Larry Scharra with creating the company.

== Products ==
=== Legacy Book ===
The Legacy Book is a service in which a storyteller answers questions about their life, family, and experiences. Responses can be typed, recorded in a web browser, sent by text message, or given during an automated, AI-based telephone interview. Spoken answers are transcribed and edited into written prose, and users can attach photographs to each story. The finished stories are printed as an 8.5 by 11 inch hardcover book that includes a QR code linking to the original audio recordings. More than one storyteller can contribute to a single book, and a Spanish-language version is offered.

=== Memorial Medallion ===
The Memorial Medallion is a custom-engraved medallion bearing a person's name, birth year, and year of death, designed to be placed on a headstone, urn, or indoor memorial. Scanning its QR code opens an online memorial page where visitors can view photos and videos, leave memories, and listen to recordings from the Legacy Book. The medallion also includes a feature that uses a voice sample and information about the deceased to generate a conversational recreation of the person's voice.

=== Other products ===
Memorygram also offers Tribute Books for occasions such as graduations, retirements, weddings, and memorials.

Draft: Is mathematics invented or discovered?

Draft text:
Is mathematics invented or discovered? is a question in the philosophy of mathematics concerning whether mathematical objects, concepts, and truths exist independently of human thought, and are therefore discoveries to be found, or are products of human intellectual activity, and are therefore inventions to be made. The question invokes related debates about mathematical realism and broader questions on the nature of mathematical knowledge and the relationship between mathematics and the physical world. [ref: Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University] [ref: Why Math Works, Scientific American] [ref: Mathematics: Art and Science, The Mathematical Intelligencer]

==Overview==
The epistemological question of whether mathematical knowledge is a priori, capable of being justified independently of experience, or a posteriori, dependent upon empirical experience, is distinct from the question of whether mathematical objects exist independently of human thought. The former concerns the justification of mathematical knowledge, while the latter concerns the nature and existence of the objects of that knowledge. [ref: A Priori Justification and Knowledge, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

The distinction between invention and discovery can also be applied separately to the foundations of mathematics, including the concept of natural numbers, the formulation of axioms, the development of logical systems, and the nature of mathematical proof. Whether the birth of mathematics was by chance or induced by necessity during the development of similar subjects, such as physics, remains an area of contention. [ref: Is Mathematics Discovered or Invented?, Philosophy of Mathematics Education] [ref: Math: Discovered, Invented, or Both?, pbs.org] Different philosophical approaches do not necessarily regard each of these components of mathematics in the same way. For example, mathematical Platonism holds that abstract mathematical objects exist independently of human thought, while other approaches emphasize mathematical objects or systems as constructions dependent upon human intellectual activity. [ref: Platonism in the Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

At least as early as 1969, the question was being explicitly formulated in terms of invention versus discovery. In Extending Understandings of Mathematics, [ref: Extending Understandings of Mathematics] published that year, Roger Osborn wrote:

Osborn thereby described the debate as a centuries-old controversy, asking whether mathematics was invented or discovered and contrasting mathematics as a creation of the human mind with mathematics as an independently existing structure awaiting discovery.

==Philosophical approaches==

The question of whether mathematics is invented or discovered depends in part on what is understood to constitute a mathematical object. A mathematical object is an abstract entity arising in mathematics. Commonly encountered mathematical objects include numbers, expressions, shapes, functions, and sets. Mathematical objects can be very complex; for example, theorems, proofs, and even formal theories are considered as mathematical objects in proof theory. Philosophers debate whether such objects have an independent existence outside of human thought or whether their existence is dependent on mental constructs or language. [ref: Abstract Objects, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

Mathematical Platonism is a form of realism that holds that mathematical objects exist independently of human thought, language, and practices. Such objects are understood to be abstract, lacking spatiotemporal or causal properties. Under this view, mathematical truths are discovered rather than invented, just as scientific investigation discovers properties of independently existing physical objects. The position is associated with Plato's theory of forms, although contemporary mathematical Platonism is distinguished from Plato's own philosophical doctrines. Prominent proponents have included Kurt Gödel, who argued for a form of mathematical intuition through which mathematical objects could be apprehended.

One objection to mathematical Platonism concerns how human beings could acquire knowledge of mathematical objects if those objects exist independently of human minds and cannot be encountered through sensory experience. This difficulty, associated particularly with philosopher Paul Benacerraf, raises questions about the relationship between accounts of mathematical truth and explanations of mathematical knowledge. [ref: Mathematical Truth, The Journal of Philosophy]

By contrast, mathematical nominalism denies the existence of abstract mathematical objects. Nominalist approaches include mathematical fictionalism, which regards mathematical discourse as useful without requiring that the abstract objects to which it apparently refers actually exist. [ref: Nominalism in the Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University] Other approaches, including formalism, emphasize the manipulation of symbols according to the rules of formal systems rather than the investigation of independently existing mathematical entities. [ref: Formalism in the Philosophy of Mathematics, Metaphysics Research Lab, Stanford University]

Draft text:
WD J1011+2845 also known as SDSS J1011+2845 is a cool White dwarf star located approximately 48 Light-years(approx. 15 parsecs) from Earth in the constellation Leo Minor. In a study published in October 2026, a research team led by the University of Warwick identified it as potentially the reddest-colored star ever recorded, exhibiting a distinct deep salmon-pink hue to human vision.

While the majority of nearby white dwarfs appear white or pale blue, [ref: Astronomers reveal surprising true colours of white dwarfs, warwick.ac.uk] WD J1011+2845 is a rare exception due to its unique atmospheric composition consisting largely of carbon, giving it a spectral type of DQ, indicating that it is a white dwarf that is carbon rich. The star features a deep Convection zone that has dredged up carbon from its core to the surface. Under intense atmospheric density and pressure, these carbon molecules heavily distort the star's light, absorbing shorter wavelengths of light and squeezing nearly all of its emitted visible light beyond 600 nanometers. This creates its characteristic salmon-pink hue.

=== Designation ===
The designation WD J1011+2845 follows the standard naming system established by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) for white dwarfs. The WD prefix identifies the object as a White dwarf, while the J indicates the positioning using the modern J2000 coordinates epoch. The numbers 1011+2845 represent the star's precise celestial coordinates in the sky: a Right ascension of 10 hours 11 minutes, and a Declination of +28° 45 minutes.

=== Discovery and Characteristics ===
WD J1011+2845 was analyzed as part of a spectroscopic survey of 151 white dwarfs within 20 Parsecs of Earth. The research group, led by astrophysicist Dr. Mark Hollands, utilized light-spectrum data from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey alongside color vision models to determine how the star's atmospheric elements would filter light to the human eye. [ref: Green, Pink And Purple: Astronomers Reveal Surprising True Colors Of White Dwarf Stars - Eurasia Review, www.eurasiareview.com]

Unlike other color-shifted white dwarfs whose unusual hues are caused by temporarily accreted planetary debris (such as WD J1330+6435, a chartreuse-green white dwarf identified in the same study [ref: First Green Star Adds to Milky Way's Rainbow, Newser]), the salmon-pink coloring of WD J1011+2845 is driven by internal stellar forces. Because the carbon is continually supplied from within the star's interior, astronomers project that WD J1011+2845 will retain its distinctive salmon-pink color for billions of years.

Hitmarker is a British online recruitment platform for the video game industry, esports and related
creator and entertainment businesses. Founded in Newcastle upon Tyne in 2017, it lists jobs from game
studios, publishers, esports organisations and content creators, and describes itself as the largest jobs
platform for gaming and esports.

== History ==
Hitmarker was founded by Philip Huggan and launched in mid-2017 as a jobs platform for the esports industry;
his brother Richard Huggan joined later that year and became managing director.
It later broadened from esports to the wider games industry.

In 2019 the company ran an equity crowdfunding campaign on Crowdcube, seeking a minimum of £80,000 for
4% of its equity, and reached 207% of that target within seven days.
A second Crowdcube round in December 2020 raised approximately €568,000 to fund expansion into new markets.
The company states that both rounds were led by Ironmonger360, the investment vehicle of Duncan Ironmonger,
co-founder and former chief executive of the controller maker Scuf Gaming, and that Ironmonger Properties made a
further strategic investment in 2025.

In April 2026 Hitmarker launched Hitmarker Pro, a subscription hiring product for games companies with
applicant tracking, AI-assisted candidate matching and automation.

== Platform ==
Employers post vacancies, and candidates create profiles and apply. Roles span game development (engineering,
art, design, audio, production), esports, community and content, marketing and business functions.
According to the company, more than 200,000 jobs have been posted on the platform, and by 2024 it had over
300,000 registered members and around one million annual users.

Draft text:
Andrew Jordan Wright, who publishes as A. Jordan Wright, is an American clinical psychologist known for his work on psychological assessment, including assessment training, tele-assessment, and the role of culture in assessment. He is a clinical associate professor at NYU Steinhardt [ref: Jordan Wright, New York University Steinhardt] and served as president of the Society of Clinical Psychology (American Psychological Association Division 12) in 2025. [ref: The Clinical Psychologist, The Clinical Psychologist]

== Education ==
Wright received a master's degree in psychology in education from Teachers College, Columbia University in 2001 and a PhD in clinical psychology from Columbia University in 2005. [ref: Andrew Jordan Wright, Society for Personality Assessment]

== Career ==
From 2006 to 2011, Wright was on the faculty of Teachers College, Columbia University, where he coordinated training in psychological assessment. From 2007 to 2011 he also directed the mental health department of The HOPE Program, a workforce development organization in Brooklyn. From 2011 to 2017 he was on the faculty of SUNY Empire State College, where he served as statewide chair of psychology.

Wright joined NYU Steinhardt in 2017. He is a clinical associate professor in the Department of Applied Psychology, directs the combined clinical and counseling psychology PhD program, and is the founding director of the program's training clinic, the Center for Counseling and Community Wellbeing.

Wright joined Parallel Learning, a company that provides virtual special education and related services to schools, as an advisor in 2021 and became its chief clinical officer in 2022. [ref: Dr. Jordan Wright, Parallel Learning]

== Professional service ==
Wright was president of the Society of Clinical Psychology's assessment section in 2017, president-elect of the Society of Clinical Psychology in 2024, and its president in 2025. In 2021 he chaired the APA Board of Educational Affairs. [ref: Board of Educational Affairs 2021 Annual Report, American Psychological Association] He chaired the APA task force that developed guidelines for education and training in psychological assessment in health service psychology, published in American Psychologist in 2020.

He is president of the American Board of Psychological Assessment (formerly the American Board of Assessment Psychology) and serves on the executive board of the Society for Personality Assessment (2025–2027 term). Since 2024 he has been an associate editor of the journal Professional Psychology: Research and Practice. [ref: Editorial Board for Professional Psychology: Research and Practice, American Psychological Association]

== Recognition ==
Wright is a fellow of the American Psychological Association through Division 12 (Society of Clinical Psychology, 2022) and Division 17 (Society of Counseling Psychology, 2025), and a fellow of the Society for Personality Assessment (2015). He is board certified by the American Board of Psychological Assessment (2012) and by the American Board of Professional Psychology in clinical psychology (2022).

He received the Association of Psychology Training Clinics' Spruill Award in 2024 [ref: APTC Bulletin: Practicum Education & Training Announcements, Association of Psychology Training Clinics] and the Society for Personality Assessment's Distinguished Service and Contribution to Personality Assessment Award in 2025. [ref: Distinguished Service and Contribution to Personality Assessment Award, Society for Personality Assessment]

== Research ==
Wright's research covers training and supervision in psychological assessment, the equivalence of remote and in-person cognitive testing, cultural factors in assessment, and the measurement of microaggressions experienced by LGBTQ people. With K. Constantine, he developed the Wright–Constantine Structured Cultural Interview (WCSCI), a free structured interview for evaluating the cultural context of an individual. [ref: Wright-Constantine Structured Cultural Interview (WCSCI), NYU Steinhardt]

Dionys Jobst (5 September 1927 – 25 March 2017) was a German lawyer, railway official and politician of the Christian Social Union (CSU). He was a member of the Bundestag from 20 October 1969 to 26 October 1998, representing the Burglengenfeld constituency, later renamed Schwandorf, by direct mandate. He chaired the Bundestag's Committee on Transport from 1988 to 1998.

== Early life and education ==

Jobst was born in Teublitz in the Upper Palatinate and attended an Oberrealschule. From 1943 to 1945 he served as a Flakhelfer, in the Reich Labour Service and in the Wehrmacht. He was wounded and taken prisoner. On 20 March 1944 he applied for membership of the Nazi Party (NSDAP) and was admitted on 20 April 1944, with membership number 10,116,768.

He completed his Abitur in 1947 and studied law at the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München until 1950. He passed the first state law examination in 1951, received a doctorate in law in 1954 and passed the second state examination in 1955.

== Civil service career ==

Jobst worked as a Regierungsassessor for the government of the Upper Palatinate in Regensburg and then as a legal officer at a district office. In January 1956 he joined the Deutsche Bundesbahn, where his last post was as a department head (Dezernent) at the Regensburg railway directorate.

He was a member of the supervisory board of Erste Bayerische Basaltstein AG Steinmühle, a member of the administrative board of the Deutsche Siedlungs- und Landesrentenbank and a board member of the German friends' association of Tel Aviv University.

== Political career ==

Jobst joined the CSU in 1959. He was a member of the Teublitz town council from 1960 to 1991, the Burglengenfeld district council from 1960 to 1972 and the Schwandorf district council from 1972 to 1996. From 1965 to 1972 he chaired the CSU district association in Burglengenfeld.

=== Member of the Bundestag ===

Jobst won the Burglengenfeld constituency in the 1969 federal election and sat in the CDU/CSU parliamentary group. He was re-elected at each election until 1994. He did not stand in the 1998 election and left the Bundestag on 26 October 1998.

He was president of the cross-party parliamentary group on railways and chairman of the German–Japanese parliamentary friendship group. In 1990 the Japanese government awarded him the Order of the Rising Sun, Grand Cordon.

On 9 July 1993 Bild published a front-page story stating that members of the Bundestag were considering leasing or buying Majorca from Spain for 50 billion marks and make it the country's seventeenth state. [ref: Kein Anschluss unter dieser Nummer, BILDblog] Jobst said, the idea was meant as a joke during a conversation about transport matters and that some readers took it literally. [ref: Ich habe verstanden: Das Sommerloch fällt aus, Der Tagesspiegel]

=== Chair of the Committee on Transport ===

Jobst was a member of the Bundestag's Committee on Transport from 1980 and its chairman from 1988 until he left parliament in 1998. As chairman he presented the committee's reports and recommendations to the plenary.

== Personal life and death ==

Jobst was Roman Catholic, married, and had three children. He lived in Teublitz and died on 25 March 2017 at the age of 89.

== Honours ==

* Cross of Merit on ribbon (1978)
* Bavarian Order of Merit (1980)
* Cross of Merit, 1st Class (1983)
* Order of the Rising Sun, Grand Cordon (Japan, 1990)

Draft text:
== Deafness In Sweden ==

Sweden is home to around 8,000 deaf sign language users and 600 Swedish Sign Language interpreters. [ref: Sweden, European Union of the Deaf] Sweden was one of the first countries to recognize their official sign language, Swedish Sign Language (also known as SSL or STS). The country did so in 1981 and implemented bilingual education soon after in 1983. Sweden signed onto the UN Committee on Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) in 2007 and it was ratified it a year later. Their own law is sufficient in following the rules outlined in the UN CRPD but is continuing to implement more policies outlined in the CRPD as time goes on. Sweden has good infrastructure to facilitate early intervention for deaf or hard of hearing children as around 95% of children are screened for hearing loss at birth and those children are referred to rehabilitation centers that facilitate access to hearing technology and other necessary therapies. Sweden has a bilingual education system as outlined in their national curriculum which is applied in both deaf schools and mainstream schools. Today, around 90% of Swedish deaf or hard of hearing children receive cochlear implants which impacts where they are sent to school, however placement in deaf schools is still recommended by the Swedish government.

=== Human/Civil Rights ===
The World Federation for the Deaf is an organization that focuses on ensuring the human and civil rights for all Deaf people are protected by their individual legislatures. [ref: Human Rights - World Federation of the Deaf, https://wfdeaf.org/] They do this by referring to the UN Committee on Rights for Persons with Disabilities (UN CRPD) which addresses some key areas of concern for disabled persons across the world. [ref: Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, OHCHR] They specifically focus on the following sections:

* Article 2 – Definition
* Article 9 – Accessibility
* Article 21 – Freedom of expression, opinion, and access to information
* Article 24 – Education
* Article 30 – Participation in cultural life, recreation leisure and sport

These are all detailed in the UN CRPD which is why the following section refers to that document to assess the state of human and civil rights for the deaf in Sweden.

The UN CRPD was signed in Sweden in 2007 and ratified in 2008. Sweden's law was found to be in good accordance with the UN CRPD so not much changed as far as the state legislation or the available resources [ref: Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities - Combined second and third periodic reports submitted by Sweden under article 35 of the Convention pursuant to the optional reporting procedure, due in 2019]. However, parts of the UNCRPD have been adopted into Swedish law, for example, as of 2013, the European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (ECHR) and as of 1 January 2020 the Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). These have both been signed into law in Sweden. These are considered preemptive efforts and the Swedish government plans to continue to evaluate the effects of incorporating these conventions before continuing to incorporate the UNCRPD in its entirety into law.

Despite the amount of legal protections, Swedish citizens have voiced that there is still room for improvement in the disability rights of deaf and hard of hearing people in Sweden [ref: Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities - List of issues in relation to the initial report of Sweden, adopted by the Committee at its tenth session (2–13 September 2013)]. The most recent report from 2023 replies to complaints that the implementation of disability policy has been a particular shortcoming saying that the Swedish government has many systems in place to observe implementation on state, local and regional levels. Swedish citizens have also asked for the Swedish government disclose the specific parts of the Swedish disability legislation to see if it falls in line with the things outlined in the UN CRPD as they feel as though it is not being appropriately implemented and that the UN CRPD does in fact need to be adopted in it's entirety. The point being made in these reports is that despite the fact the Swedish government has most of their bases covered legally, they are not actually implementing policy in the ways they should be.

=== Sign Languages ===
Swedish Sign language is the recognized sign language in the state of Sweden and has about 8,000 scattered speakers making up about.1% of the population [ref: ]. It is a deaf community sign language used since 1800 with the first deaf school established in 1809. Swedish sign language is sometimes referred to as SSL and sometimes referred to as STS. Sweden recognized sign language first in 1981 giving Swedish signers access to interpretation in public places as well as access to Swedish Sign Language use in school [ref: ]. The Language Law of 2009 recognizes SSL in a way similar to the other 5 minority languages (Sámi, Finnish, Meänkieli, Romani Chib, and Yiddish) making it a more official recognition that requires its promotion and encouragement and makes acquisition of deaf education easier.

Mitti de Putt (Punjabi: ਮਿੱਟੀ ਦੇ ਪੁੱਤ) is a 2026 Indian Punjabi-language action drama film directed by R. Malkana and written by Amar Hundal, Ryan Khan and Raj S. Jhinjar. Produced by Iqbal Cheema and Amar Hundal, it stars Dev Kharoud, Sharan Kaur and Vikramjeet Virk, alongside Yograj Singh, Anita Meet and Mahabir Bhullar.

The film was released in Indian cinemas on 18 September 2026. It received mixed review from critics, with praise for its action sequences, performances and production quality, while criticism was directed at its screenplay.

== Plot ==
The story follows two villages whose rivalry has persisted across generations over land and pride. Left with his family destroyed, Bikkar Singh vows to bring his mother home and confront the man responsible.

== Cast ==

* Dev Kharoud as the protagonist, Bikkar Singh
* Vikramjeet Virk as the antagonist, Jang Singh, Bikkar's uncle
* Pardeep Cheema as Sarwan, Jang's second son
* Aman Sutdhar as Shera, Jang's first son
* Deepak Kamboj as Kartar, Bikkar's cousin
* Sharan Kaur as Basant Kaur, Bikkar's wife
* Anita Meet as Bikkar's mother, Jang's sister
* Yograj Singh as Bikkar's paternal grandfather
* Mahabir Bhullar as Jang's father
* Ashish Duggal
* Aman Dhaliwal
* Dilawar Sidhu as Gindar
* Manjit Singh
* Vikramjit Khehra
* Ravinder Mand
* Rang Dev
* Sukh Dandiwal
* Ravneet Kaur
* Harinder Bhullar
* Gurinder Makna
* Jasbir Gill

== Production ==
Mitti de Putt was produced by Iqbal Cheema and Amar Hundal under the banners of Liv Lyf Films and Zora Studios. R. Malkana directed the film, with Amar Hundal responsible for the story and screenplay. Ryan Khan and Raj S. Jhinjar contributed additional screenplay and dialogue work.

The film's technical crew included cinematographer Sukh Kamboj, editor Gurjeet Hundal and composer Avvy Sra. Siraj Sayed served as action director. The production was promoted through official teasers released by Zora Studios and Dharma Productions in August 2026.

== Release ==
The film was released in Indian cinemas on 18 September 2026. Dharma Productions handled distribution across India, while The Next Film Studios handled overseas distribution. The film was also released in the United States on a limited theatrical basis.

== Reception ==
Critical response

Viewer reviews praised the film's action choreography, particularly its hospital fight sequence. Some audience reviews also commended its soundtrack and the presentation of the central family feud, while negative reviews criticised the characterisation, dialogue and motivations behind the conflict.

The Times of India covered the film before its release, describing it as a revenge saga centred on family, culture and loyalty. Actor Vikramjeet Virk characterised the film as a tribute to the strength, pride and spirit of Punjabi people.

Audience rating

As of October 2026, Mitti de Putt had received positive audience ratings across several online platforms. On IMDb, the film was rated 9.5 out of 10 from approximately 882 votes. On BookMyShow, it received a rating of 9.5 out of 10 from more than 1,200 votes.

== Theory of Industrialization ==

The theory of industrialization of education (also called the industrialization theory of distance education [ref: Exploring Otto Peters' Theory: Industrialisation in Distance Education - Distance Learning Institute]) is a theory of distance education proposed by the German educator Otto Peters. It holds that distance education is the most industrialized form of education, because it shares the organizational principles of industrial production.

The theory is premised on the principles of industrialization as they stood in the 1960s, and proposes that distance education is an industrialized form of teaching and learning. [ref: Exploring Otto Peters' Theory: Industrialisation in Distance Education - Distance Learning Institute] Peters compared the industrial production process with the structure of distance education, and described industrialized education as resting on elements such as planning, rationalization, and mechanization [ref: ]. Peters was arguably the first scholar to advance a theory of distance education [ref: ].

== The Core Claims and Industrial Principles ==
The central claim is that distance education has structural features in common with industrial production, and that these are more developed there than in any other form of education. One overview lists the principles he identified as rationalization, division of labor, mechanization, assembly-line processes, mass production, standardization, and scientific control methods [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].

=== 1. Organizing and planning the work ===

* Rationalization - Redesigning the teaching process so that it uses time, staff and money efficiently. One study lists rationalization among the resource factors affected by Industry 4.0, alongside specialization, preparatory work, and capital intensive techniques. In practice, [https://zenodo.org/records/4293232 one course is built once and used for many learners].
* Planning - Decisions about content, sequence and delivery are made in advance, and production is scheduled. Peters used business management terms [ref: ], including planning, to show the industrial character of distance education.
* Preparatory work - A great deal of effort goes into designing and testing materials before any learner sees them, in contrast to a lecturer who prepares shortly before class. This is the front loading that justifies the cost.
* Organization - Producing and delivering courses requires an administrative structure that coordinates authors, printers, mailing, tutors and assessment, much as a factory coordinates departments.

=== 2. Dividing and mechanizing the work ===

* Division of labor - A French chapter on Peters says that teaching no longer depends on one person, because division of labor now prevails. One overview describes subject experts developing content, instructional designers optimizing learning, technical specialists managing platforms and tutors handling student contact, each playing a distinct role. This is the principle most closely tied to the instructional design profession [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].
* Mechanization - Technical media, such as print, broadcast, audio, video and digital platforms, carry out functions the teacher once performed.
* Assembly line - Course production moves through ordered stages (writing, review, editing, production, distribution), each handled by a different group. Assembly line is one of the terms Peters borrowed from business management [ref: ].
* Mass production - Mass production is another of those terms. One overview says the aim was to reach thousands of students efficiently, which no single classroom teacher could do [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].

=== 3. Controlling quality and consistency ===

* Scientific control methods - Industrial quality control has an equivalent in course evaluation, testing materials with sample learners and monitoring results. One overview lists scientific control methods among the principles [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].
* Formalization - Procedures, roles and responsibilities are written down and made explicit rather than left to individual judgement.
* Standardization - Learners receive the same materials, tasks and assessment criteria, which makes quality predictable. It is also the principle that Industry 4.0 puts under most strain. That [https://zenodo.org/records/4293232 study] found personalization and individual production conflicting with the standardized mass production described by the theory.

=== 4. Changing the nature of teaching ===

* Change in the teacher’s role - The teacher shifts from deliverer of lessons to designer, tutor or assessor. The same overview contrasts classroom teaching, which it compares to craft production, with distance education [ref: Philosophical Underpinnings of Open and Distance Learning (ODL) • Sociology.Institute].
* [https://zenodo.org/records/4293232 Objectification] - The teaching is built into the course materials and technical means. The Anadolu study notes that most teaching functions in distance education are objectified in this way. A learner works with a fixed, pre-made course, not a person responding in real time.

=== 5. Structure of the institution ===

Draft text:
Friedrich Vogel (2 June 1929 – 9 December 2005) was a German judge and politician of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU). He was a member of the Bundestag from 1965 to 1966 and from 1969 to 1994. He was Minister of Justice of North Rhine-Westphalia in 1966 and Minister of State to the Federal Chancellor from 1982 to 1987.

== Early life and education ==

Vogel was born in Hahnenknoop, then in the district of Wesermünde and now part of Loxstedt in Lower Saxony. His father was an estate manager and later the farm manager at Handorf airfield near Münster. At the end of the Second World War, aged 15, Vogel served with a Luftwaffe unit in Denmark.

He attended the Ratsgymnasium in Münster and, from 1945, the Gymnasium Laurentianum in Warendorf, where he completed his Abitur in 1949. From 1949 to 1952 he studied law and political science at the University of Münster. He passed the first state law examination in 1952 and the second in 1956.

== Legal career ==

Vogel became a judge in July 1956. In April 1960 he was appointed Landgerichtsrat at the regional court (Landgericht) in Münster. He was a member of the Deutscher Richterbund, the German association of judges. From 1977 he practised as a lawyer in Warendorf, and from 1980 also as a notary.

== Political career ==

Vogel joined the Junge Union in 1952 and the CDU in 1953. He was deputy federal chairman of the Junge Union from 1963 to 1967. He was a co-opted member of the federal board of the CDU/CSU association for local politics and deputy regional chairman of the party's Protestant Working Group (Evangelischer Arbeitskreis) in Westphalia-Lippe. He was deputy federal chairman of the Protestant Working Group from 1978 to 1993. From 1956 to 1972 he was a member of the Warendorf town council.

From 1970 to 1986 he chaired the Federal Working Group of Christian Democratic Lawyers (Bundesarbeitskreis Christlich-Demokratischer Juristen, BACDJ). During this period the group held legal policy congresses in Karlsruhe under the title Recht sichert die Freiheit ("Law secures freedom") in 1975, 1978, 1983 and 1986.

=== Minister of Justice of North Rhine-Westphalia ===

On 5 October 1966 Minister-President Franz Meyers appointed Vogel Minister of Justice of North Rhine-Westphalia. After the coalition between the CDU and the FDP ended, the FDP and the SPD elected Heinz Kühn Minister-President. Vogel left office on 8 December 1966.

=== Member of the Bundestag ===

Vogel was elected to the Bundestag in the 1965 federal election. He left parliament on 6 October 1966 on joining the state government of North Rhine-Westphalia. He was elected again in 1969 and remained a member until 1994. He entered the Bundestag each time through the CDU state list in North Rhine-Westphalia and stood as the party's candidate in the Ennepe-Ruhr-Kreis. Bundestag records list him as "Vogel (Ennepetal)".

From 1968 to 1969 he was a member of the commission under the Article 10 Act, which oversees restrictions on the privacy of correspondence and telecommunications. From 1971 to 1977 he chaired the CDU/CSU parliamentary group's working group on home affairs and legal policy.

From 1977 to 1982 he chaired the Mediation Committee of the Bundestag and Bundesrat. As chairman he signed the committee's notices to the President of the Bundestag, including those on an amendment to the law on public assemblies in September 1978 and on the Tax Amendment Act 1979 in November 1978. He presented the committee's recommendations to the plenary.

=== Minister of State to the Federal Chancellor ===

Following the election of Helmut Kohl as Chancellor, Vogel was appointed Minister of State to the Federal Chancellor on 4 October 1982. He was responsible for the government's relations with the Bundesrat. He left office on 12 March 1987, after the 1987 federal election.

=== Human rights subcommittee ===

From 1987 to 1994 Vogel chaired the Subcommittee on Human Rights and Humanitarian Aid of the Bundestag's Foreign Affairs Committee. On 22 February 1988 the subcommittee held a public hearing on whether German citizens were held against their will and under conditions violating human rights in Colonia Dignidad in Chile. Former members of the colony, their relatives and the colony's doctor Hartmut Hopp took part. The hearing was not a committee of inquiry, and those invited did not appear as witnesses. The public prosecutor's office in Bonn investigated Hopp from at least the time of the hearing.

=== Committee of inquiry on Kommerzielle Koordinierung ===

In the 12th Bundestag (1990–1994) Vogel chaired the first committee of inquiry, which examined the Kommerzielle Koordinierung (KoKo), the East German foreign-currency organisation headed by Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski. The committee issued interim reports in 1992, a final report in May 1994 and a supplementary report in November 1994. He did not stand in the 1994 federal election.

== Personal life ==

Vogel was a Protestant. He was married and had five children. He died in Warendorf on 9 December 2005. His papers are held by the Archive for Christian Democratic Policy in Sankt Augustin.

= Louis Brown: King of Clubs =
Louis Brown (c. 1934–1986) was a British nightclub proprietor associated with London's West End nightlife during the 1960s, 1970s and early 1980s. He was known for his association with La Valbonne, a nightclub in Soho, and his venues which attracted entertainers, musicians and other prominent figures. He was known for his distinctive ideas and designs within his clubs making a name for himself as the King of Clubs.

== Career ==
Louis Brown was a British nightclub entrepreneur who became a prominent figure in London's West End nightlife during the 1960s and 1970s. Working alongside business partner Leonard Bloom, he established and operated a number of nightclubs, including La Poubelle, Le Kilt and the Scotch of St James, before opening La Valbonne in Soho in 1967.

Known for his distinctive approach to nightclub design and entertainment, Brown developed venues that attracted musicians, celebrities and fashionable clientele. His business interests later extended beyond London to Skindles Hotel in Taplow, Berkshire, where he established Studio Valbonne as a nightclub and entertainment venue. Brown continued to operate his nightclub businesses into the 1980s and died in 1986.

=== Skindles ===
Brown was also involved in the ownership and management of Skindles Hotel, a historic riverside hotel in Taplow, Berkshire, during the 1970s. Under his involvement, the establishment formed part of his wider interests in the hospitality and nightclub industries. In 1978, plans were proposed for an extension comprising 81 additional bedrooms, reflecting efforts to redevelop the property as a hotel and leisure destination. Skindles subsequently closed in 1995.

=== La Valbonne ===
La Valbonne was a nightclub at 62 Kingly Street in Soho, London, which opened in 1967 and became Louis Brown's best-known establishment. The venue was noted for its elaborate interior, featuring multiple bars, tropical plants, large fish tanks and a heart-shaped swimming pool incorporated into the dance floor. It attracted musicians, entertainers and other prominent figures, and appeared in Pete Walker's 1970 film Cool It Carol.

=== Other clubs ===
Le Kilt was a Soho nightclub associated with Louis Brown and his business partner Leonard Bloom. Situated on Greek Street, it formed part of Brown's expanding portfolio of West End entertainment venues during the 1960s and 1970s. The club operated within London's emerging discothèque culture, which increasingly centred on recorded music, dancing and fashionable nightlife.

La Poubelle was an early London discothèque associated with Louis Brown. It opened in 1959 and is described in historical accounts as one of London's earliest venues devoted to recorded-music dancing. Located initially on Great Marlborough Street, near Oxford Circus, the club attracted socialites and helped establish the discothèque format that subsequently spread throughout the capital.

The Scotch of St James opened in Mason's Yard, Mayfair, in July 1965 and became a prominent nightclub and live-music venue during London's Swinging Sixties. Associated with Louis Brown's nightclub interests, it attracted musicians and other figures from the British and American music scenes. American guitarist Jimi Hendrix famously joined musicians for an impromptu performance there on his arrival in England in September 1966.

=== Relationship with Peter Stringfellow ===
Brown's La Valbonne nightclub reportedly attracted the interest of fellow nightclub entrepreneur Peter Stringfellow. A retrospective account states that Stringfellow regarded the venue as influential and that Brown offered to sell it to him however the deal never fulfilled.

== Personal life ==
Brown was known for his enthusiasm for music, nightlife and entertainment. His professional interests extended beyond running venues to the atmosphere and technology of the nightclub experience, including the development of elaborate lighting effects and distinctive interior designs. This was shown through his desire for cars when being seen driving his Jaguar E-Type and his Rolls-Royce Silver Cloud.

== Legacy ==
Louis Brown was an ambitious and influential figure in London's nightclub scene, whose establishments helped shape the atmosphere of fashionable nightlife during the Swinging Sixties and the decades that followed.

With a distinctive vision for entertainment, music and interior design, he created venues that offered more than a traditional nightclub experience, transforming them into destinations for celebrities, musicians and London's social elite. La Valbonne became the defining example of his approach, while his involvement with the Scotch of St James and Skindles extended his influence across London's West End and beyond.

His ability to combine striking surroundings with an atmosphere of exclusivity and excitement reflected the changing character of British nightlife during a period of significant cultural transformation. Although many of the venues associated with Brown have since closed or disappeared, their place in the history of the era remains a testament to his entrepreneurial ambitions and his contribution to the development of the modern nightclub experience.

This allowed him to be known within the entertainment industry as the King of Clubs.

The Republican Movement (RM) is a Venezuelan political party with republican and liberal leanings. Its ideological and institutional platform is based on the defense of fundamental individual rights [ref: Movimiento Republicano - English, www.movimientorepublicano.org]—private property, liberty, and life—the restoration of republican institutions, the market economy, and the strict separation of powers.

== Political Principles and Ideology ==
The Republican Movement bases its doctrine on five fundamental pillars set forth in its statements of organizational principles:
# Defense of Individual Rights: It considers the safeguarding and protection of private property, individual liberty, and the right to life to be essential and non-negotiable conditions—the pillars for the full exercise of citizens’ rights.
# Institutional Framework and the Republic: Promotes the revival of the republican model based on the premise that all citizens are free and equal before the law, thereby laying the foundation for a robust rule of law.
# Libertades económicas y civiles: It explicitly advocates for the free market, freedom of action and enterprise, freedom of thought, religious freedom, and the fundamental right to freedom of movement within the country, in addition to guaranteeing unrestricted access to justice.
# Separation of Powers and Alternation in Office: It upholds the strict necessity of a division and independence of public powers that allows for mutual and effective checks and balances. It also supports the democratic election of state officials for fixed terms of office.
# Transparency and Public Administration: Calls for rigorous oversight of public spending and absolute transparency in state administrative expenditures. Promotes active citizen participation aimed at fostering respect for institutions and legitimizing a responsible political class in the country. [ref: Movimiento Republicano reafirma su compromiso con la participación electoral en Anzoátegui - El Tiempo, eltiempove.com]

Ben Mora (b. 1994) is an American game show host, podcaster, and former political organizer. He created and hosts Interior Motives, a YouTube game show with the tagline, "You show us your bed and we guess who's been in it," and co-hosts the comedy podcast Seeking Derangements. [ref: ] [ref: The YouTube Game Show That Judges You by Your Bedroom, Dwell] He is known for his large bright blue eyes, causing him to suffer frequent comparisons to a memefied photograph of the pop singer Miley Cyrus. [ref: Please Stop This Miley Cyrus Meme, W Magazine]

== Early Life and Education ==
Mora grew up in Des Moines, Iowa, in a house built partly by his father, a contractor from Costa Rica. His mother was an occupational therapist for Des Moines Public Schools. He said that he was a difficult teenager, a heavy marijuana smoker who often fought with his parents. [ref: Interior Motives Host Ben Mora Knows You by Your Stuff, Curbed] At seventeen, he moved to Denver, where he worked in restaurants as a maid. He has said that when he first moved out, he slept for a year and a half on a pile of clothes that he molded into a makeshift mattress with a fitted sheet. [ref: Ben Mora, TANKtv] According to Mora's longtime friend Chloe Truong-Jones, he left Colorado after falling out with a group of Buffalo Exchange employees who accused him of being "the [[Osama bin Laden|[O]sama bin Laden]] of the Denver Arts Community." [ref: chlobuchar (@[user]_im_chloe) on X, X (formerly Twitter)]

== Career ==

===== Politcal Organizing =====
In 2019, Mora, now living in Iowa again, began volunteering for Bernie Sanders's presidential campaign. He was hired full time on the basis of his door knocking prowess, and went on to organize events for service workers in Des Moines. After the Iowa caucuses, the campaign sent him to Michigan, where by February 2020 he had been promoted to regional field director. [ref: ] Mora has said that during the campaign he slept in the campaign office, a former Office Max store in Dearborn. He was fired that first month (see Controversies). [ref: Bernie Sanders Staffer Fired for Mocking Warren, Buttigieg on Private Twitter Account, The Daily Beast]

===== Seeking Derangements =====
After his dismissal, Mora received hate mail from some strangers and donations from others, the latter of which he called his "Venmo severance package." He felt to New York City in March 2020 and by his own account, arrived as "an instant microcelebrity," with invitations to appear on "dirtbag left" podcasts; he was a guest on Red Scare that month. [ref: Red Scare Podcast: Corona Crush w/ Ben Mora, redscarepodcast.libsyn.com] He also started his own comedy podcast, Seeking Derangements, with friends, among them Hesse Deni and Jacques Gonsoulin. In December 2020, he and journalist Glenn Greenwald started a weekly podcast on Substack, Ben and Glenn's After Hours. [ref: ] The podcast later ended over creative differences. [ref: New: Ben And Glenn's After Hours, Podcast Business Journal]

===== Interior Motives =====
In 2025, while scrolling through TikTok, Mora came across a video of a messy room and wondered who lived there. He said that he then looked around his own room, where he was lying on a mattress with no bed frame, and thought, "This room looks really gay." He tested the idea as a game on Seeking Derangements. Listeners responded at once; in the summer of 2025, Mora relaunched the game as a separate YouTube show, recording from his childhood bedroom in Des Moines. He has named the online games GeoGuessr, in which players guess a location from street-level photographs, and the television series Queer Eye as influences: "What if you did GeuGuessr for gender? For sexuality?" He has also said that the show draws on his own experience of poor housing and that "the show is in some ways about the housing crisis." [ref: The YouTube Game Show That Judges You by Your Bedroom, Dwell]

In each episode, which runs about an hour, Mora and guest contestants join a remote call and examine photographs of three bedrooms submitted by viewers, along with a photograph of another space, such as the inside of a refrigerator or a medicine cabinet, a car, a workplace, or an Instagram Explore page. The contestants guess the age, gender, sexuality, and location of the person who lives in room and receive a point for each correct guess. Mora opens each episode by asking the contestants which object in their own rooms might give away where they are calling from. Mora releases two episodes a week, some of which are devoted to submissions from outside the United States. Mora edits each episode himself, with emoji captions, satirical sponsorships, canned applause, and an opening sequence in retro graphics. Subscribers on Patreon pay $7 a month for extra episodes, some of them R-rated, and the change to play the game live against one another. [ref: Interior Motives Host Ben Mora Knows You by Your Stuff, Curbed]

Contestants have included Courtney Love, Margaret Cho, Kim Petras, John Early, Kate Berlant, Julio Torres, Hari Nef, Juliana Huxtable, Gregg Araki, Jeremy O. Harris, and Hasan Piker. Mora said in 2026 that he received more than 5,000 room submissions. In September 2026, the Youtube channel had 140,000 subscribers and more than 6.9 million views. By October 2026, Mora had hosted nearly 75 episodes. [ref: Ben Mora wants to see your bedroom, Dazed]

Draft text:
Andrew Jordan Wright, professionally known as A. Jordan Wright, is an American clinical psychologist most noted for his award-winning work in the field of psychological testing and assessment. He has won awards from the Association of Psychology Training Clinics (APTC), the American Psychological Association's Society of Clinical Psychology (SCP), and the Society for Personality Assessment (SPA) for his contributions to the field of psychology, training, and assessment, and he is a fellow of the American Psychological Association and the Society for Personality Assessment, as well as a Diplomate of the American Board of Psychological Assessment (ABPA) and the American Board of Professional Psychology. He is currently a clinical associate professor and program director of the combined clinical/counseling psychology PhD program at New York University and the founding director of NYU's training clinic, the NYU Center for Counseling and Community Wellbeing. He also serves as the chief clinical officer at Parallel Learning, a technology and service company in the special education space.

== Education ==
Wright received his master of arts in psychology in education in 2001 from Teachers College, Columbia University, followed by his PhD in clinical psychology in 2006 from Columbia University.

== Career ==
After receiving his PhD and license as a New York State psychologist, Wright joined the faculty of Teachers College, Columbia University, where he coordinated the psychological testing and assessment curriculum for the PhD program in clinical psychology (2006–2011). During this time, he also served as the director of mental health for The HOPE Program, a workforce development program in downtown Brooklyn that helps chronically under- and unemployed adults reintegrate into the workforce (2007–2011). He then joined the faculty of SUNY Empire State College, where he served as the statewide department chair of psychology and coordinated the online psychology program (2011–2017). He joined the faculty of New York University in 2017, where he founded and runs the Center for Counseling and Community Wellbeing, directs the PhD program in combined clinical/counseling psychology, and coordinates the psychological testing and assessment curriculum.

In 2011, Wright published his first book, Conducting Psychological Assessment: A Guide for Practitioners (Wiley Publishers), which came out in its second edition in 2020. Following the success of his first book, he collaborated with Gary Groth-Marnat on the sixth edition of the Handbook of Psychological Assessment (Wiley Publishers), the most widely used textbook in graduate psychological assessment coursework.

== Scholarship ==
Wright's scholarship focuses on two primary areas (and their intersection): psychological testing and assessment (including evidence-based assessment, tele-assessment validity, and cultural factors in the assessment process) and social justice (including LGBTQIA+ issues in psychology). He has authored many peer-reviewed journal articles, including "Evidence-based clinical psychological assessment (EBCPA): Review of current state of the literature and best practices" (2022) in Professional Psychology: Research and Practice, "Queering psychological assessment" (2024) in Professional Psychology: Research and Practice, and "Equivalence of remote, digital administration and traditional, in-person administration of the WISC-V" (2020) in Psychological Assessment. He is the co-author of the Wright-Constantine Structured Cultural Interview (WCSCI), a qualitative, structured interview to collect information about clients' culturally lived experience as part of a psychological assessment process.

== Professional service ==
Wright has served as president of the Society of Clinical Psychology (2025), chair of the American Psychological Association's Board of Educational Affairs (2022), and president of the American Board of Psychological Assessment (2025–present). He has also served on the executive board of the Society for Personality Assessment (2025–2027). He chaired a task force at the American Psychological Association that developed educational and training guidelines for psychological assessment in health service psychology, published in American Psychologist (2020), led guidance development for psychological tele-assessment during COVID for APA (2020), and was the lead author of the process-oriented competency framework (POCF), a new set of competencies for education and training in health service psychology, published in 2025 in Training and Education in Professional Psychology.

== Recognition ==
Wright is a fellow of the American Psychological Association and the Society for Personality Assessment. He holds board certification from the American Board of Psychological Assessment and the American Board of Professional Psychology in Clinical Psychology. He is also a diplomate of the American Board of Psychological Assessment (ABPA; 2012) and the American Board of Professional Psychology (ABPP; 2022). In 2024, he won the Association of Psychology Training Clinic's Jean Spruill Achievement Award, their highest honor, as well as the American Psychological Association Society of Clinical Psychology's Award for Distinguished Contribution to Assessment Psychology. In 2025, he won the Society for Personality Assessment's Distinguished Service and Contribution to Personality Assessment Award.

Chiharu Kihara (, Kihara Chiharu, born 1979) is a Japanese painter from Misumi (now Nagato), Yamaguchi Prefecture. A self-taught artist, she is known for her dynamic brushwork and vivid colors depicting animals, insects, and plants, expressing what she calls "vitalism" — the raw energy of living things. [ref: 作家 木原千春 編 / 連載「作家のアイデンティティ」Vol.4, ARToVILLA]

== Early life and career ==
Kihara was born in 1979 in Misumi, Ōtsu District, Yamaguchi Prefecture (now part of Nagato). From an early age, she aspired to become a painter. She was deeply inspired by Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa and the head studies of Francis Bacon, which she encountered in art textbooks, as well as the landscape paintings of Sesshū Tōyō. [ref: 木原千春インタビュー, PEELER]

During high school, while drawing a bamboo shoot in pencil, she experienced what she described as "the sensation of lines coming alive, moving as if they were living creatures themselves," a moment that defined her artistic direction. She dropped out of high school and continued to develop her painting entirely through self-study.

In 1999, she held her first solo exhibition at Gallery Den in Tokyo, marking the formal beginning of her career as an artist.

In 2006, she was selected for the VOCA exhibition (The Vision of Contemporary Art) at the Ueno Royal Museum, Tokyo, which showcases emerging talents in contemporary Japanese art. [ref: 木原千春, Bijutsu Techō]

In 2012, she began her ongoing solo exhibition series Vitalism at roidworksgallery in Tokyo, which has been held almost annually since (except 2014). [ref: ]

In 2015, she participated in the Peko-chan Exhibition at the Hiratsuka Museum of Art, Kanagawa Prefecture.

In 2020, she created the artwork for the main lobby of Hoshino Resorts KAI Nagato in Nagato, Yamaguchi Prefecture. The same year, she held the solo exhibition CREATURES at 3331 Arts Chiyoda, Tokyo, featuring 30 drawings and 5 canvas works. [ref: CREATURES / 木原千春, 3331 Arts Chiyoda]

In December 2024, her first monograph Vitalism was published by Geijutsu Shinbunsha. The book features approximately 120 works spanning from her first solo exhibition in 1999 through to the Vitalism series, with essays by art historian Shimao Arata and contemporary art critic Tsuda Naomi, and a dialogue with comedian Shizuyo Yamasaki of Nankai Candies. [ref: 木原千春作品集 Vitalism, Geijutsu Shinbunsha] [ref: 木原千春 個展「Vitalism Ⅻ」, Ginza Tsutaya Books]

In 2026 (Reiwa 8), Chiharu Kihara received the Yamaguchi Prefecture Art and Culture Promotion Encouragement Award (山口県芸術文化振興奨励賞) from Yamaguchi Prefecture in the painting category of the fine arts division. [ref: 令和8年度文化芸術関係表彰・芸術文化振興奨励賞受賞者, Yamaguchi Prefecture] She is listed among the official recipients for that year, and the award was also covered by KRY Yamaguchi Broadcasting and the Yamaguchi Shimbun. [ref: 陶芸家の田原崇雄さんと画家の木原千春さんが受賞 県芸術文化振興奨励賞表彰式, Livedoor News] [ref: 山口県芸術文化振興奨励賞 萩焼・田原さん、画家・木原さんに/山口県庁で表彰式, Yamaguchi Shimbun]

== Artistic style ==
Kihara's subjects are drawn from the natural world she grew up with in Yamaguchi — animals, insects, plants — as well as portraits of artists she admires. She describes her process as involving hundreds of sketches of each subject until the image and her own sensibility become one, at which point the final work is completed in a single, intense session.

In addition to oil painting, she also produces drawing works she calls "5-minute drawings," which she sells through the online marketplace Mercari.

Sir Thomas Barrington (1530 – 1581) was an English politician. He sat as MP for Essex in 1572. [ref: BARRINGTON, Sir Thomas (1530-81), of Hatfield Broad Oak, Essex., History of Parliament Online]

He was knighted in 1571.

== Family and education ==
He was the only son of John Barrington (died 1537) of Hatfield Broad Oak by Elizabeth, the daughter of Thomas Bonham. He was admitted into Gray's Inn in 1554. He married Alice, the daughter of Sir Henry Parker (probably 10th) Lord Morley and they had one son (who predeceased him) and one daughter. he married Winifred, the daughter of Sir Henry Pole, 1st Baron Montagu and widow of Sir Thomas Hastings and they had two sons (Francis and Henry Barrington) and one daughter.

== Offices held ==
He served as chief forester of Hatfield forest; captain of levies in Hertfordshire in 1562; Sheriff of Hertfordshire, and Essex in 1562; commissioner of musters in Essex in 1563; commissioner to raise a benevolence in Essex in 1564; commissioner of restraint of victuals in Essex in 1573; commissioner of grain in Essex in 1579; justice of the peace for Essex from 1564; and sheriff of Essex from 1580 till 1581.

The post was made on r/maryland and quickly blew up and gained 100k views and many replys. The post goes as follows:

I reported this on encounter atlas but wanted to share this here to see if anyone else has seen this thing.

This was summer of 2024. Me and my best friend Joe were in the North Beach/Chesapeake Beach area for the few days leading up to and including the 4th of July. The night of the 2nd, we decided to take a walk and smoke a blunt we had been saving. We were both 21 years old at the time and going into our Junior Year of college. I say that so you understand that we were dumb and at that age were you feel invincible.

As we were approaching the Wetlands Overlook Park, walking along the side of the road, we both caught sight of an odd silhouette. At first we both were freaked out because we thought it must be a kid who was lost and scared in the dark. We both started jogging towards the figure and as we got closer (we had been walking for a while and our eyes were adjusted to the dark) we both stopped. We were probably 8 feet from the figure and now could make out details. It was probably 3-3.5 ft tall and was dark green. The face resembled a toad but it almost appeared like it had a small elephant trunk in place of the nose. the arms were lanky, with the knuckles almost dragging on the floor, and the hands each had 3 fingers that ended in claws. The legs were short and stumpy. The thing had ears like a bat, coned and pointed, but they were much larger than a bats ears. Its eyes were large and they glowed a super bright white. We stood staring at the thing for a good 10 seconds before it put its hands on the ground and sprung off, and with two big jumps it disappeared into the marsh.

I remember that much because it was so odd and otherworldly that I took in every detail. I know how so crazy this sounds and so i have only ever told close family and friends. The reason I am writing this now, is that my fiancée and I are moving to North Beach in a few months and I had to know if anyone has seen thing. I know what I saw.

After the post went viral, the OP put an update along with a rough sketch:

Edit: I feel like I should add a few things.

I was smoking weed, not anything that would have given me visions of hallucinations. We also were not even high at the time of the event.

I swear this is truthful.

I would never lie about something like this, and really debated coming forward with this account.

I work as a naturalists in Anne Arundle County and I know what normal animals look like.

I am not offended by the jokes or people not believing me. I know how crazy it sounds so the jokes are inevitable. I appreciate those who do believe me and have offered kind words and theories.

North Beach has its own cryptid now ig. The North Beach Terror Toad sounds nice

I also did a quick drawing of what the thing looked like. I am a terrible artist

== Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE)==
Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE) is an instructional design model developed by educational researcher Atsusi Hirumi. Developed in the 1990s and formally described in a 2002 publication, the model uses eight instructional events to support student-centred learning based on constructivist principles. It focuses on active participation, knowledge construction and learner independence, and uses technology to support the learning process. [ref: Student-Centered, Technology-Rich Learning Environments (SCenTRLE): Operationalizing Constructivist Approaches to Teaching and Learning, Journal of Technology and Teacher Education]

== Theoretical background ==

The SCenTRLE model is grounded in constructivist learning theory, which positions learners as active participants in the development of knowledge. Hirumi identified four foundations for the model: societal, psychological, epistemological and pedagogical. These principles are also discussed in wider research on technology-enhanced student-centred learning environments. [ref: The Foundations and Assumptions of Technology-Enhanced Student-Centered Learning Environments, Instructional Science]

Hirumi posits that the societal foundation is based on the growing role of information and technology in education. He argued that greater access to information requires learners to develop competences beyond subject knowledge, including problem-solving, communication and independent learning.

Secondly, the psychological foundation draws on constructivist perspectives, particularly those of Jean Piaget, Jerome Bruner and Lev Vygotsky. It explains how learners acquire knowledge through experience, cognitive development and social interaction.

Thirdly, the epistemological foundation is rooted in pragmatism. While recognising an external reality, this perspective claims that individuals construct knowledge through experience, prior understanding and interaction with others.

Finally, the pedagogical foundation integrates student-centred learning, generative learning, situated cognition, problem-based learning and performance assessment. Together, they foster active participation, authentic learning and the practical application of knowledge. In SCenTRLE, learners contribute to decisions about their learning, while instructors provide ongoing guidance and feedback.

== The eight instructional events ==

The SCenTRLE model comprises eight instructional events that guide student-centred learning. These events provide a framework in which learners help establish objectives, select learning strategies and assess their progress. Although the events are presented sequentially, learners may revisit earlier activities as their understanding develops. [ref: Vicarious Interactions and Self-Directed Learning of Students by Course Delivery Strategy, Texas A&M University]

# Set Learning Challenge: The instructor establishes a learning challenge that defines what students should be able to accomplish and provides the overall direction.
# Negotiate Learning Goals and Objectives: Learners collaborate with the instructor to determine the knowledge and skills required to meet the challenge. This includes assessing prior knowledge, identifying areas for improvement and developing individual learning objectives.
# Negotiate Learning Strategies: Students identify the activities and resources they will use to achieve their learning objectives. The instructor provides guidance while encouraging learners to determine which approaches best address their needs.
# Construct Knowledge: Learners apply their selected strategies, individually or collaboratively, to develop knowledge and skills. The instructor monitors progress and provides support when needed.
# Negotiate Performance Criteria: Learners and instructors establish criteria for determining whether the learning objectives have been achieved. Assessment rubrics may be developed to help learners evaluate the quality of their work.
# Conduct Self, Peer and Expert Assessments: Students evaluate their work against the agreed performance criteria and receive feedback from peers and individuals with relevant expertise.
# Monitor Performance and Provide Feedback: Monitoring and feedback occur throughout the learning process rather than at a single stage. Instructors review students' work, respond to questions and provide feedback on their progress and students monitor their own progress.
# Communicate Results: The final event involves formally presenting the outcomes of learning. Students may use portfolios, presentations or other work samples to demonstrate their achievements.

The eight events promote learner independence while preserving the instructor's role as a facilitator.

== Applications and case studies ==

=== Initial implementation in higher education ===

Hirumi reported an initial field test of SCenTRLE in a 15-week undergraduate course on the educational applications of computer technology. The course included 30 students with varying levels of computer experience: seven novice users, 17 apprentices and six more proficient users. The model was introduced to address these differences and enable students to pursue learning objectives aligned with their existing knowledge and interests.

What is Social Health?

Social health is a person’s overall well-being, including relationships, social support systems, and community. It studies how people establish links with family, friends and their place of work. Physical health relates to physical health, mental health and psychological well-being. Social health relates to the quality and importance of human interaction that affects overall health.

The concept of social health is not new and has been researched for a long time before the establishment of modern educational programs. The term has been used frequently by public health experts and researchers to explain how a person’s well-being is affected by involvement in the community and relationships. Over the years, a variety of frameworks have been developed.

The concept of social health is not new, and has been studied long before modern educational programs were created. Researchers and public health experts have often used the term to explain how relationships and community participation shape an individual's well-being. Over time, different frameworks have placed social health alongside physical and mental health as an integral part of overall wellness. Social health is a crucial component of overall health, alongside physical and mental health, and has been so throughout history, albeit in different frameworks.

There is a lot of research that shows that stronger relationships and social connections are related to better overall health. Feeling lonely and isolated is linked to poor physical and mental health, while feeling connected and supported is linked to lower risk of depression and anxiety. This can be a two-way thing, experts say, with mental health problems also making it more difficult to sustain relationships.

Because social connections have health effects, educators and therapists wonder if the skills that make them possible can be taught directly. Relationships are a natural thing. Communication can be taught using a skill based approach.A skill-based approach can teach communication, listening, and working through difficult conversations/conflict, rather than taking relationships as something that happens naturally.

Therapist David Koslowski, who spent years working with teens in his private practice and running free community support groups, created a social health class. In Utah, at Herriman High School, he created a program called Level Up to teach students practical communication and relationship skills. Koslowski has said he did not create the idea of social health, but formed the class as a practical use of it to be taught in schools.

== Background and Development ==
L. Dee Fink, an American scholar and consultant  whose work focuses on higher education and instructional  design,  which  mainly concentrates on the significant learning experience. He served as director of the Instructional Development Program at the University of Oklahoma and has written about faculty development and approaches to improving teaching in higher education. [ref: Becoming a Professional Engineering Educator: A New Role for a New Era, Journal of Engineering Education] [ref: Toward learning‐centered education in colleges and universities, New Directions for Teaching and Learning]

Fink is particularly interested in the types of learning that have significant and lasting effects on students. He moved beyond the belief which places emphasis on planning courses around the content and skills that students are required to obtain at the end of the unit. Fink argued that  learning outcome should not only include learning goals but also apply know knowledge, make connection across subjects, understand others, develop different interest and continue to learn independently [ref: 7: Higher–Level Learning: The First Step toward More Significant Learning, To Improve the Academy] [ref: Creating Significant Learning Experiences: An Integrated Approach to Designing College Courses, Canadian Journal of University Continuing Education]

"Higher-Level Learning: The First Step toward More Significant Learning," was a taxonomy presented in 2001 to help educators develop more rigorous learning goals. He expanded this methodology in his 2003 Creating Significant Learning Experiences connecting the taxonomy to an integrated process for designing and developing courses in higher education. This approach requires higher education educator to not only present the content of the course but facilitate how students apply it in academic, professional and personal contexts, therefore integrating course design, teaching strategies and assessment within a single process.

Draft text:
The Mountaineer Mall and Professional Plaza is a shopping mall and business park located in Morgantown, West Virginia. It is the first of two malls built in Morgantown; the other being the Morgantown Mall. Major tenants are Senior Monongalians, Spark! Imagination and Science Center, and Osher Lifelong Learning Institutes. [ref: Mountaineer Mall, more than just stores, [[The Dominion Post (Morgantown)]
== History ==

=== 1975–1999: Early history, expansion, and decline ===
Mountaineer Mall was developed by First Union Management [ref: Shopping center takes new direction, Morgantown Dominion Post] on the south side of Morgantown, off of U.S. Route 119 and on a raised bluff near the Monongahela River. The mall started construction in 1973 [ref: Shop center name: 'Mountaineer Mall', Sunday Dominion-Post] and it partially-opened with 19 stores on August 5, 1975. [ref: 30,000 attend first day at mall, Morgantown Dominion Post] 32 stores were open by January the next year. [ref: Progress, [[The Dominion Post (Morgantown)] Anchors were Murphy's Mart (later Ames), JCPenney, and Montgomery Ward. [ref: Mountaineer Mall; Morgantown, West Virginia, labelscar.com] [ref: Adventures in West Virginia: day trips & longer travels, Huntington, W. Va.: Aegina Press] It was the first mall to open in the Morgantown metropolitan area and despite its compact size, was a big success. In 1987, the mall was expanded, which would include the construction of a freestanding Giant Eagle and a new anchor store, Stone & Thomas, [ref: Realty Stock Review Vol. XVIII, No. 5, Audit Investment Research, Inc. (New York)] which opened in November. [ref: Mrs. Hoffman Promotes Upcoming State Pageant, [[Cumberland Times-News]

In the 1990s, many tenants began leave the after the early 1990s recession and the opening of the newer Morgantown Mall. JCPenney followed suit, as they needed more space. [ref: Discount stores anchor Mountaineer Mall's comeback, The State Journal] The mall then transitioned to attract discount businesses. [ref: Mountaineer Mall finds identity with eclectic tenants, WV News] JCPenney was replaced by U.S. Factory Outlets in 1993, which became Gabriel Brothers in 1996. A Walmart opened in the former Ames space in January 1994. [ref: Mall bounced back from troubled times, Morgantown Dominion Post] Stone & Thomas became Elder-Beerman in 1998. Montgomery Ward closed in 1999.

=== 2000–present: Further decline and transition into business ===
TeleTech opened in 2000, in part of the former Montgomery Ward space. The rest was taken up by General Glass, which opened in February 2005. In 2002, Spark! opened as the Children's Discovery Museum of West Virginia. In April 2005, the International Council of Shopping Centers and the Environmental Protection Agency awarded the Mountaineer Mall with "Best Community Partnership (Large Shopping Center)" for its recycling program. [ref: ICSC and EPA Announce Winners of America’s Marketplace Recycles! Awards Program, icsc.org] Walmart closed in October 2006, when two new Supercenters opened near Morgantown. [ref: Wal-Mart selling all but walls, Morgantown Dominion Post] In 2007, Gabriel Brothers opened their flagship store in Morgantown Commons near Morgantown Mall, keeping the Mountaineer Mall location open but with a "smaller selection". [ref: Gabriel Brothers opens flagship store in Morgantown Commons, Morgantown Dominion Post] [ref: Mountaineer mall: Life after wal-mart, The State Journal] This would, however, close the next year. Elder-Beerman closed in January 2008 after its lease expiry, having become redundant as the chain had a store at Morgantown Mall. [ref: Elder-Beerman to close its doors in January, Morgantown Dominion Post] Rex Appliances, one of the last remaining large stores, closed in 2009 when the entire chain shut down.

In February 2010, Mylan Pharmaceuticals announced that it would renovate the former Walmart space into offices for its IT and legal departments. [ref: Mylan moving IT, legal staff to former Walmart, Morgantown Dominion Post] The next year, Mylan started renovating the former Gabriel Brothers to expand its offices. [ref: Mylan to lease at mall, Morgantown Dominion Post]

On February 15, 2020, Eloquence Antiques & Artisans moved and reopened in Mountaineer Mall. [ref: Eloquence Antiques & Artisans reopens in the Mountaineer Mall, The Dominion Post] The store expanded in 2026. [ref: Vintage, antique lovers take over Mountaineer Mall, [[WBOY-TV] In early August 2024, the United States Army Reserve held decontamination training drills at the mall. [ref: Mass casualty exercise held at Mountaineer Mall, WBOY] As of 2026, Mylan and TeleTech have vacated the site. [ref: ]

== Description ==
The Mountaineer Mall (as of 1975) is primary made up of rusted-brick wall with tiled flooring and carpets, facing its 65 stores; benches, trees, and planters laid throughout the walkways. The singular corridor had Montgomery Ward to the east, JCPenney in the center, and Murphy’s Mart to the west. The 80s addition extruded from the central area and had fake skylights and brass fixtures. The addition was built on a slight incline, so a ramp and accompanied stairs were needed to connect the two.

== Incidents ==
* On November 29, 2011, a woman sued GP-Mountaineer LLC after claiming that she was injured on the property due to "dangerous conditions". [ref: Morgantown woman sues for injuries at Mountaineer Mall, Legal Newsline]
