John Rock Grosett ( – September 1866) was an British soldier and politician. He sat as MP for Chippenham from 1820 till 1826. [ref: GROSETT, John Rock (?1784-1866), of Lacock Abbey, nr. Chippenham, Wilts.; Spring Garden and Petersfield, Jamaica, History of Parliament Online]

== Political career ==
He served as cornet of the 13th Dragoon in 1804 and was promoted to lieutenant in 1805, he retired in 1807; he served as member of assembly in Jamaica from 1831 till 1844; and member of council.

== Family ==
He was the second but only surviving son of the merchant Schaw Grosett (died 1820) and Mary, the daughter of Thomas Rock, a Bristol merchant. On 19 February 1810, he married his first cousin Mary Spencer (died 31 October 1820), the daughter of Edward Shirley and they had at least four sons (three predeceased him) and at least two daughters (whom predeceased him). On 20 July 1825, he married Christina Maria de Kantzow and they had at least one son whom predeceased him.

Draft text:
Radio Swammerdam is een Amsterdams wetenschapsradioprogramma en podcast. Het programma wordt sinds 2 mei 2010 gemaakt door een redactie van Amsterdamse studenten en recent afgestudeerden met interesse in wetenschap, journalistiek en radio. In de uitzendingen worden wetenschappers geïnterviewd over hun onderzoek, met als doel wetenschappelijke onderwerpen toegankelijk te maken voor een breder publiek.

Geschiedenis

Radio Swammerdam werd opgericht in 2010 en is vernoemd naar de zeventiende-eeuwse Amsterdamse natuuronderzoeker Jan Swammerdam. Swammerdam deed onderzoek naar onder meer insecten en menselijke fysiologie en hield in Amsterdam een rariteitenkabinet bij.

Het programma ontstond als studenteninitiatief en wordt sindsdien grotendeels vrijwillig gemaakt. De redactie bestaat uit Amsterdamse studenten en net afgestudeerden, vaak met een achtergrond in wetenschap, journalistiek of academisch onderzoek.

Format

Elke aflevering staat in het teken van een wetenschappelijk onderwerp. In de uitzending schuiven een of meerdere onderzoekers aan om hun onderzoek toe te lichten. De gesprekken duren doorgaans ongeveer een uur en richten zich op het toegankelijk maken van academische kennis voor luisteraars buiten het specifieke vakgebied.

Naast interviews bevat het programma regelmatig columns of vaste rubrieken. De onderwerpen lopen uiteen van natuurwetenschappen en geneeskunde tot geesteswetenschappen, sociale wetenschappen en maatschappelijke vraagstukken.

Uitzending en distributie

Radio Swammerdam wordt uitgezonden op Radio SALTO, op zondag van 11:00 tot 12:00 uur. De opnames vinden plaats in Pakhuis de Zwijger in Amsterdam. Afleveringen zijn daarnaast terug te luisteren als podcast via onder meer Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Pocket Casts en andere podcastplatforms.

Redactie

De redactie wisselt per seizoen en bestaat uit studenten en pas afgestudeerden uit Amsterdam. Volgens de eigen omschrijving wordt het programma vrijwillig gemaakt door mensen met een passie voor onderzoek, journalistiek en radio.

Activiteiten

Hoewel de meeste afleveringen studio-interviews zijn, verzorgt de redactie ook veel specials: afleveringen opgenomen op locatie. In 2026 organiseerde de redactie onder meer een evenement in de Universiteitsbibliotheek van de Universiteit van Amsterdam onder de titel Radio Swammerdam Slaat Alarm: Pas Op Voor De Negentiende Eeuw!.

Naam

De naam verwijst naar Jan Swammerdam (1637–1680), een Amsterdamse natuuronderzoeker die bekendstaat om zijn werk op het gebied van anatomie, insectenonderzoek en microscopie. De verwijzing sluit aan bij het wetenschappelijke karakter van het programma.

xFarm Technologies is a Swiss company with headquarters in Manno, operating in the agricultural technology sector. [ref: Una pioggia di milioni per una startup insediata in Ticino, Corriere del Ticino] It develops digital farm management tools used by farmers and agri-food supply chain operators, including farm management software (xFarm), Internet of Things (IoT) field sensors, decision support systems (DSS) and supply chain analytics software. [ref: xFarm Technologies, la startup agritech chiude il round Serie C da 36 milioni di euro - StartupItalia, StartupItalia]

Founded in 2017 as xFarm by Matteo Vanotti, xFarm Technologies took its current form in 2021, following the merger with the Italian company Farm Technologies. [ref: Digital ag platforms xFarm & Farm Technologies merge to become 'Spotify of agtech', AgFunderNews] [ref: xFarm merges with Farm Technologies to create leading agri-tech company, Startupticker] Between 2019 and 2024, the company raised funding in three rounds of €3 million, [ref: Agritech, xfarm chiude round da 3 mln con United Ventures, Fortune Italia] €17 million, [ref: xFarm, scommessa svizzera da 17 milioni sulla fattoria «smart», Il Sole 24 Ore] €36 million, [ref: La startup agritech xFarm Technologies raccoglie 36 milioni di euro per l'espansione globale, Forbes Italia] [ref: xFarm raises €36m to build superapp for farmers, Sifted] and it expanded internationally, acquiring Greenfield Technologies (Spain) [ref: xFarm integra a la extremeña Greenfield Technologies para consolidarse como líder europeo en el agrotech, elEconomista.es] and SpaceSense (France) in 2024, [ref: Agritech xFarm Technologies merges with Greenfield and Spacesense to hone its Geospatial AI, Tech.eu] [ref: XFarm Technologies cresce all'estero con SpaceSense in Francia e Greenfield in Spagna, Il Sole 24 Ore] and Checkplant (Brazil) in 2025. [ref: Suíça Xfarm Technologies Entra no Brasil para Investir em Agricultura Digital, Forbes Brasil]

At the time of the Checkplant transaction, the company reported supporting more than 500,000 farms across 8.3 million hectares. Since July 2025, xFarm Technologies has been a certified B Corporation. [ref: xFarm Technologies SA - Certified B Corporation - B Lab, www.bcorporation.net]

== History and international expansion ==

Matteo Vanotti, who serves as the company's chief executive officer, founded xFarm in 2017 to support the management of his family's farm in Monferrato, Piedmont. [ref: ] In 2019, the company closed a €3 million funding round led by United Ventures.

In 2021, xFarm merged with Farm Technologies, an Italian company developing agronomic algorithms, thus becoming xFarm Technologies. At the time, the company reportedly supported around 80,000 farms across one million hectares.

In 2022, xFarm Technologies closed a €17 million Series B round led by Swisscom Ventures. At the time, the company was active in Switzerland, Italy and Spain, where it had local branches. [ref: Swiss-Italian startup xFarm Technologies secures €17 million, Startupticker]

In April 2024, the company acquired both SpaceSense, a French company specializing in geospatial artificial intelligence and satellite-based climate intelligence, and Greenfield Technologies, a Spanish company active in soil characterization.

In October 2024, xFarm Technologies closed a €36 million Series C round led by Partech with existing and new investors, [ref: XFarm Technologies punta sull'intelligenza artificiale. 450 mila aziende sulla piattaforma, la Repubblica] [ref: XFarm lève 36 millions d'euros pour son application de gestion agricole, L'Usine Digitale] including Mouro Capital, the venture arm of Banco Santander, linked to the creation of a fintech and insurtech division dedicated to risk and credit management services for farmers. [ref: Mouro Capital (Santander) aterriza en la 'agrotech' suiza xFarm en una ronda de 36 millones, La información]

In March 2025, xFarm Technologies officially entered the Latin America market through the acquisition of Checkplant, a Brazilian company operating the Farmbox platform in Brazil, Colombia and Paraguay. [ref: Europeia xFarm e brasileira CheckPlant fecham "M&A da agricultura digital", AgFeed] [ref: xFarm si espande in America Latina, accordo con Checkplant, L'Informatore Agrario]

== Products and services ==
xFarm Technologies develops xFarm, a farm management platform available as both a mobile and a web application, supporting agronomic, administrative, economic and environmental management of farms. [ref: Farm-Management mit KI: Satelliten, Sensoren, Modelle, top agrar] [ref: Catalyzing Digital Innovation in AgTech: The Case of XFARM as a Digital Innovation Ecosystem, Research and Innovation Forum 2025 Vol2] The company also provides a line of IoT devices, including weather stations, soil moisture sensors and leaf wetness sensors, [ref: Enablers to Digitalization in Agriculture: A Case Study from Italian Field Crop Farms in the Po River Valley, with Insights for Policy Targeting, Agriculture] [ref: Dai sensori all'intelligenza artificiale: "Controlliamo 700 ettari di frutteti", Il Resto del Carlino] complementing the software and feeding data into forecasting models and DSS. In addition, xFarm Technologies provides satellite imagery for remote field monitoring.

Joseph Spiess Company, colloquially as Joseph Spiess, or just Spiess, was an American department store chain that was founded in 1921 in Elgin, Illinois, that went defunct in 1996.

== History ==

=== Founding and early history ===
Joseph C. Spiess founded the company in 1921 in Elgin, Illinois. The store in downtown Elgin would serve as the company's only store for decades.

=== Expansion ===
Spiess would open its first branch location at the Crystal Point Mall in Crystal Lake in 1976. [ref: MALL ISN’T GOING TO PIECES OVER SPIESS, Chicago Tribune] It would open another one at St. Charles Mall in St. Charles in 1979. [ref: ST. CHARLES’ PUZZLING FLOP, Chicago Tribune] In 1984, Spiess permanently shuttered its flagship store in Elgin to relocate it at the Spring Hill Mall in West Dundee and Carpentersville that same year. [ref: Old Spiess store falls so new Elgin can rise, Chicago Tribune] Spiess then opened its final branch store in 1988 at the Randhurst Mall in Mount Prospect. [ref: SPIESS, MAINSTREET TO CONSTRUCT STORES AT RANDHURST CENTER, Chicago Tribune]

=== Demise ===
Due to excessive debt from overexpansion, Spiess filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 1991 [ref: RETAILER SPIESS FILES FOR CHAPTER 11, Chicago Tribune]. The Chapter 11 bankruptcy then converted to Chapter 7, but the company was shortly then acquired by Maurice L. Rothschild. Spiess gradually closed their stores at Randhurst in 1992, Spring Hill Mall in 1994, and St. Charles in 1995. Spiess permanently closed their final store at Crystal Lake in 1996, ending the chain.

The former Spiess flagship store in downtown Elgin was demolished in 2005. The empty land was cleared for a $44 million residential and retail revitalization project named Fountain Square on the River, which built 190 condominiums across two eight-story buildings alongside 20 luxury townhouses overlooking the Fox River. [ref: Old Spiess store falls so new Elgin can rise, Chicago Tribune]

== Locations ==

* Elgin (flagship store): Opened in 1921, closed in 1984
* Crystal Point Mall, Crystal Lake: Opened in 1976, closed in 1996
* St. Charles Mall, St. Charles: Opened in 1979, closed in 1995
* Spring Hill Mall, West Dundee and Carpentersville: Opened in 1984, closed in 1994
* Randhurst Mall, Mount Prospect: Opened in 1988, closed in 1992

Salah Mansour (born November 14, 1942) is a Lebanese-Canadian otolaryngologist, academic, and medical author. [ref: Environmental noise in Beirut, smoking and age are combined risk factors for hearing impairment, Eastern Mediterranean Health Journal] He was a Professor of Otolaryngology at the Lebanese University Faculty of Medical Sciences, served as Vice Dean of the faculty, and was President of the Scientific Council for Otolaryngology Head and Neck Surgery under the Arab Board of Health Specializations. [ref: Comprehensive and Clinical Anatomy of the Middle Ear, Springer Berlin, Heidelberg] [ref: Middle Ear Diseases: Advances in Diagnosis and Management, Springer International Publishing]

== Medical education and career ==
Mansour earned his Doctor of Medicine (MD) degree from Saint Joseph University in Beirut in 1970. He completed surgical and otolaryngological post-graduate training in Canada at Université Laval, McGill University, and the Université de Montréal hospital network. He earned the License of the Medical Council of Canada (LMCC) in 1972, and became a Fellow of the Royal College of Physicians and Surgeons of Canada (FRCSC) in 1975. He was made a Fellow of the American College of Surgeons (FACS) in 1976.

Mansour practiced clinical otolaryngology in Quebec at Honoré-Mercier Hospital in Saint-Hyacinthe, Quebec and Charles-Le Moyne Hospital in Longueuil. In Lebanon, he served as:
* 1998–2012: Vice Dean of the Faculty of Medical Sciences at the Lebanese University.
* 1998–2016: Full Professor of Otolaryngology at the Lebanese University Faculty of Medical Sciences.
* 1989–2003: President of the examination commission and Scientific Committee of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery of the Arab Board of Health Specializations.
* 2003–2013: President of the Scientific Council of the Arab Board of Otolaryngology – Head and Neck Surgery.

In 2016, he relocated to Montreal, Quebec, practicing as an ORL consultant at Westmount Square Medical Center until his retirement in 2022.

== Publications ==
Mansour led an international team of otologists, embryologists, and neuroradiologists to produce a series of medical reference textbooks on middle ear anatomy and pathology published by Springer Nature:

=== Textbooks ===
* Mansour, Salah; Magnan, Jacques; Haidar, Hassan; Louryan, Stéphane (2013). Comprehensive and Clinical Anatomy of the Middle Ear. Springer Berlin, Heidelberg...
* Mansour, Salah; Magnan, Jacques; Haidar, Hassan; Nicolas, Karen (2015). Tympanic Membrane Retraction Pocket: Overview and Advances in Diagnosis and Management. Springer International Publishing... [ref: Tympanic Membrane Retraction Pocket: Overview and Advances in Diagnosis and Management, Springer International Publishing]
* Mansour, Salah; Magnan, Jacques; Nicolas, Karen; Haidar, Hassan (2018). Middle Ear Diseases: Advances in Diagnosis and Management. Springer International Publishing...
* Mansour, Salah; Magnan, Jacques; Haidar Ahmad, Hassan; Nicolas, Karen; Louryan, Stéphane (2019). Comprehensive and Clinical Anatomy of the Middle Ear (2nd ed.). Springer Nature Switzerland... [ref: Comprehensive and Clinical Anatomy of the Middle Ear, Springer Nature Switzerland]

Hojat Amani (Persian: حجت امانی; born 30 July 1978) is an Iranian contemporary artist, researcher, and educator. His artistic practice encompasses painting, photography, digital imagery, installation, and Persian calligraphy. His work draws on Persian miniature painting, Qajar-era visual culture, Persian poetry, and Islamic artistic traditions, reinterpreting historical imagery through contemporary visual forms. [ref: Hojat Amani, Fallen angels, from the series Angels in Paradise, 2012, Los Angeles County Museum of Art] [ref: Between Tradition and Modernity, Haleh Gallery] In February 2017, the Iranian newspaper Shargh reported his appointment as acting head of the Saba Cultural and Artistic Institute, affiliated with the Iranian Academy of Arts. [ref: حجت امانی سرپرست مؤسسه صبا شد, Shargh]

== Life and education ==

Amani was born in Lorestan, Iran, in 1978, according to the Los Angeles County Museum of Art. He studied painting at the University of Art in Isfahan and later pursued graduate studies in art. Haleh Gallery's biographical account lists a bachelor's degree completed in 2004 and a master's degree in fine arts completed in 2008.

According to his professional curriculum vitae, Amani holds a PhD in comparative and analytical art history, with a focus on the Middle East, a master's degree in art research, and a bachelor's degree in painting. His studies also included fine art and Persian calligraphy.

Amani's research and artistic practice focus on Persian calligraphy, Islamic aesthetics, traditional Iranian painting, and the relationship between historical visual traditions and contemporary art.

== Career ==

Amani has worked as an artist, researcher, and educator. His professional curriculum vitae lists academic appointments at Tarbiat Modares University in Tehran and Isfahan University of Arts, as well as teaching activities in Pakistan and Germany. It also records research and administrative roles associated with the Iranian Academy of Arts.

In February 2017, Shargh reported that Amani had been appointed acting head of the Saba Cultural and Artistic Institute, an institution affiliated with the Iranian Academy of Arts. The newspaper described him as an artist from Lorestan with a background in art research and Persian calligraphy. It also discussed his work across painting, photography, calligraphy, installation, and other media.

Amani's listed professional activities include research on Persian calligraphy and Iranian visual culture, participation in art conferences, teaching traditional calligraphy, and contributing to exhibitions and cultural programmes.

== Artistic practice ==

Amani works across painting, photography, digital imagery, installation, and calligraphy. His art draws on Persian poetry, miniature painting, historical portraiture, and Islamic cultural traditions, bringing these references into dialogue with contemporary visual culture.

=== Persian miniature painting and Qajar imagery ===

Amani has developed works that reinterpret Safavid and Qajar portraiture through contemporary visual strategies. In its presentation of his exhibition Between Tradition and Modernity, Haleh Gallery described his portraits as a transformation of historical Persian miniature painting into a modern visual language, drawing a comparison with the use of existing popular images in Andy Warhol's pop art.

His work also engages with representations of women in Iranian visual history. The Museum of Islamic Art in Doha included discussion of Amani's work in its exhibition Qajar Women: Images of Women in 19th-century Iran, which ran from 8 April 2015 to 11 June 2016. The exhibition explored historical Qajar representations of women and their continuing influence on contemporary artists. The museum identified Amani, alongside Shadi Ghadirian and Mahmood Sabzi, as an artist who adapts Qajar visual aesthetics to comment on modernity, femininity, and the relationship between past and present. [ref: Qajar Women: Images of Women in 19th century Iran, Museum of Islamic Art]

=== Angels and photography ===

One of Amani's recurring subjects is the angel, interpreted through Iranian cultural and religious traditions. His series Angels in Paradise includes Fallen Angels (2012), a digital image in the collection of the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA).

LACMA's curatorial notes describe Amani's angels as figures that reflect human shortcomings and explain that his imagery draws on traditional Iranian Muslim beliefs about angels accompanying human beings throughout their lives. In Fallen Angels, a contemporary woman is depicted with wings formed from golden leaves, combining symbolic imagery with references to the natural world.

In February 2014, Amani participated in the Colombo Art Biennale in Sri Lanka. In a report published by The Sunday Times, journalist Adilah Ismail discussed his work under the heading “Angelic touch to human worldliness”. The article described photographs featuring people posed against angel wings incorporating intricate Persian calligraphic details, linking spiritual imagery with everyday human experience. [ref: 'Making history' around Colombo, The Sunday Times]

In 2024, the institution officially launched its Patient Blood Management program, following approximately two years of multidisciplinary preparation. Fernandez was among the physicians involved in its development and implementation. [ref: Hospital de Clínicas Gaspar Vianna lança programa inovador de Manejo do Sangue do Paciente, Agência Pará]

In September 2026, Agência Pará identified Fernandez as the hospital's hemotherapy coordinator and as responsible for the implementation of PBM. She also presided over the International Conference on Hemotherapy and Patient Blood Management, held in Belém on 9–10 September 2026.

Fernandez has also worked in hemotherapy at Hospital Regional Dr. Abelardo Santos. In February 2022, she was identified by Agência Pará as a hematologist at the hospital in a report about initiatives to increase blood donation. [ref: Hospital Abelardo Santos usa telecaptação para ampliar doação de sangue, Agência Pará]

At Hospital Oncológico Infantil Octávio Lobo (HOIOL), she participated in hemotherapy activities involving pediatric oncology patients. In 2025, she was part of a team that presented research on the rational use of blood components in pediatric oncology at the Brazilian Congress of Hematology, Hemotherapy and Cell Therapy (HEMO 2025). [ref: Equipe do HOIOL aborda sobre segurança transfusional durante congresso em São Paulo, Agência Pará]

Her professional activities also include technical and administrative responsibilities at PROHEMO Serviços Médicos, a company providing hematology and hemotherapy services in Pará.

== Patient Blood Management ==

Fernandez has been involved in the institutional implementation of Patient Blood Management, a multidisciplinary approach to improving patient blood health, diagnosing and treating anemia, reducing blood loss, and supporting appropriate transfusion decisions.

At Fundação Hospital de Clínicas Gaspar Vianna, she coordinated the PBM program officially launched in October 2024. [ref: Programa de Gerenciamento do Uso do Sangue completa um ano de implantação no Hospital de Clínicas, Agência Pará]

According to an institutional report published in October 2025, the hospital recorded an approximate 25% reduction in the use of red blood cell concentrates and a 60% reduction in the use of fresh frozen plasma during surgical procedures in the program's first year. Artistic practice
Mund's work focuses on functional pottery intended for domestic use. His approach combines simple forms with attention to weight, ergonomics, surface decoration and the relationship between form and finish. His work draws on historical pottery traditions while incorporating contemporary design ideas. [ref: Richard Mund, Owen Sound Artists' Co-op]
His work includes wheel-thrown stoneware, decorated ceramics using maiolica glazing techniques, and practical objects for the home and garden. His product designs have included flower holders made to fit standard Mason jars. [ref: Gallery of Images, Richard Mund Pottery]
=Exhibitions and events
In 2025, Mund was named the featured artist at the Hamilton Potters Guild's fall sale in Dundas, Ontario. The event brought together more than 100 potters and included the guild's annual Empty Bowl fundraiser for Hamilton Food Share. [ref: Hamilton Potters Guild Fall Sale returns, DundasToday]

Larivaar () is the traditional style of writing the Gurmukhi script in which words are written continuously, without spaces between them. It is a form of scriptio continua. Larivaar was the standard form of Sikh scriptural manuscripts, including handwritten copies of the Guru Granth Sahib, and of the scripture's early printed editions. The contrasting style, in which words are separated by spaces, is called pad chhed (). Printed editions of the Guru Granth Sahib switched to word-separated text in the early 1970s, a change that met strong opposition before it was accepted. Some Sikhs continue to learn to read scripture in larivaar.

== Characteristics ==
In larivaar text, letters run on continuously, and whitespace is used only to separate a heading from the text beneath it. Verses are divided by the double danda (॥), and it is left to the reader to work out where one word ends and the next begins. Word boundaries are therefore not marked on the page and are realised only when the text is read aloud.

In historical larivaar manuscripts, the double danda was not written as a free-standing pair of strokes. Its first stroke was joined to the last letter of the preceding verse, and, if another verse followed in the same block of text, its second stroke was joined to the first letter of that verse. According to a 2020 proposal to the Unicode Consortium, this way of writing the double danda disappeared with the introduction of lithography and the printing press in India.

The opening verse of the Guru Granth Sahib, the Mul Mantar, illustrates the difference between the two styles:

{| class="wikitable"
! Style !! Text
|-
| Larivaar ||
|-
| Pad chhed ||
|}

== History ==

=== Printed editions ===
The first printed edition of the Adi Granth appeared in 1865. Single-volume printed editions continued the manuscript tradition of writing words without breaks between them. In the early twentieth century, the printed text was collated against the Kartarpur Pothi, a process that lasted several decades and culminated in the standard 1,430-page edition published by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) in 1951.

=== Transition to pad chhed ===
According to the historian Gurinder Singh Mann, the connected style of writing was given up in printed editions of the Guru Granth Sahib in the early 1970s. The change was strongly opposed, and some critics saw it as "tearing apart the body of the Guru". Supporters of the change argued that separating the words would make the text easier to read for those not trained in reading continuous script, and would help readers make the correct breaks between words. After a period of controversy, the word-separated text was accepted, and it is now the version in use in Sikh homes and gurdwaras around the world, retaining the standard pagination of 1,430 pages.

== Reading and study ==
Because word divisions are not indicated, reading larivaar requires the reader to determine where each word begins and ends. Instruction in the correct reading and pronunciation of Gurbani is known as santhiya. Writing in 2020, the authors of a Unicode proposal stated that many Sikhs studying the scriptures were learning to read them in larivaar.

== Digital encoding ==
Larivaar text can be represented in Unicode by omitting spaces between words, or by using the zero-width space. In a 2020 proposal to the Unicode Consortium, Manvir Singh and Irvanjit Singh argued that standard fonts rendered the double danda incorrectly in larivaar text, because they display it as two detached strokes rather than joining it to the adjacent letters as in historical manuscripts. They described the detached form as a departure from the written tradition and as an example of Western or British influence on the script. They proposed either encoding new Gurmukhi double danda characters at reserved code points (U+0A64 and U+0A65) or adding guidance on contextual rendering to the Unicode Standard.

== See also ==
* Scriptio continua
* Gurmukhi
* Santhiya
* Word divider

Cayosoft is a privately held software company based in the Columbus, Ohio, area. The company develops software for administering, monitoring, and recovering Microsoft identity environments, including Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft 365, Exchange, Microsoft Teams, and Intune. [ref: Cayosoft Inc. transaction profile, KPMG Corporate Finance] [ref: Cayosoft company profile, CB Insights]

== History ==
Cayosoft was founded in 2013 by Robert Bobel and Andrey Polevoy, who had previously worked in identity and systems-management software. The company was established to develop administration and automation software for organizations operating Microsoft directory services across on-premises and cloud environments. [ref: Cayosoft company profile, PitchBook] [ref: An Interview With Robert Bobel, CEO & Founder Of Cayosoft, Tech Company News]

The company’s initial products focused on automating user, group, and Microsoft 365 administration in hybrid Active Directory environments. It later added change auditing, rollback, threat detection, and recovery capabilities, broadening its focus from routine administration to identity security and operational resilience. [ref: Cayosoft company profile, CB Insights]

In November 2021, Cayosoft launched Guardian Forest Recovery, extending its Guardian product with automated recovery for Active Directory objects, domain controllers, and forests. The product used continuous change monitoring and a standby recovery environment to reduce the time required to restore directory services after corruption, operational errors, or cyberattacks. [ref: Cayosoft Launches Innovative, All-In-One Active Directory Recovery Software, Cayosoft Guardian Forest Recovery, PR Newswire]

In March 2024, Cayosoft received a $22.5 million minority investment from Centana Growth Partners. The company said the financing would support product development, sales and marketing, and international expansion. [ref: Cayosoft Raises $22.5M in Funding, FinSMEs] [ref: Cayosoft attracts $22.5m from Centana Growth Partners, FinTech Global] In September 2024, the company announced that it had received a United States patent covering its directory-service backup and recovery technology. [ref: Cayosoft Wins Patent for Revolutionary Instant Active Directory Recovery Solution, AI-TechPark]

In February 2025, Cayosoft acquired the Petri IT Knowledgebase, a technology publication founded in 1999 that covers Microsoft enterprise products and related IT topics. Petri Media LLC was established as an independent subsidiary, and Petri stated that it would retain editorial independence. [ref: Cayosoft acquires the Petri IT Knowledgebase, Cayosoft] [ref: About Petri.com, Petri IT Knowledgebase]

== Products ==

=== Cayosoft Administrator ===
Cayosoft Administrator automates identity lifecycle tasks and delegated administration across hybrid Microsoft environments. Its functions include user and group administration, provisioning and deprovisioning, Microsoft 365 license management, policy enforcement, reporting, and auditing. [ref: Cayosoft Administrator, Microsoft Marketplace]

=== Cayosoft Guardian ===
Cayosoft Guardian provides identity-change monitoring, audit history, threat detection, rollback, and recovery. The product includes tools for restoring objects and attributes and recovering an Active Directory forest through a preconfigured standby environment. The standby recovery is called Cayosoft Guardian Instant Forest Recovery and it is the first and only patent for standby active directory recovery [ref: Cayosoft Guardian, Microsoft Marketplace] [ref: Forest Recovery Overview, Cayosoft Support] [ref: Intellectual Property, Cayosoft]

== Patents ==
Cayosoft is the assignee of United States patents covering directory-service recovery and administrative-unit management. U.S. Patent Nos. 12,093,141, 12,399,791, and 12,743,349, granted between September 2024 and September 2026, are related patents in a continuation family titled “Systems and methods for directory service backup and recovery.” They describe maintaining a standby directory service that can be implemented when a host directory service is interrupted. U.S. Patent No. 12,254,107, granted in March 2025, is titled “Orchestration of administrative unit management” and covers methods for evaluating and implementing directory-object membership changes across administrative units. [ref: Patents Assigned to Cayosoft, Inc., Justia Patents]

== Gartner research mentions ==
Since 2024, Cayosoft has appeared in Gartner research concerning Microsoft identity administration, governance, backup, rollback, and recovery. Inclusion in Gartner research does not constitute an endorsement, ranking, or product recommendation.

=== 2024 ===

= Pocket FM =

Pocket FM is an Indian audio entertainment platform that distributes serialized fiction and other audio content. It was founded in 2018 by Rohan Nayak, Prateek Dixit and Nishanth Srinivas. [ref: Pocket FM raises $22.4 million in Series B funding led by Lightspeed, The Economic Times] [ref: Rohan Nayak, Prateek Dixit, Nishant KS, Fortune India]

The platform uses a freemium model in which some episodes are available without charge while subsequent episodes can be unlocked using virtual currency purchased through in-app transactions. The company is actively incorporating artificial intelligence for audio production as well as translation into other languages. [ref: Pocket FM partners with ElevenLabs to convert scripts into audio content quickly, TechCrunch] [ref: Pocket FM wants to be the Netflix of long-form audio, www.forbesindia.com]

As of 2026, The Pocket FM website claims the company is serving 20+ countries in 15 international languages. [ref: Pocket FM: The home of the world's best audio dramas, pocketfm.com]

== History ==
Pocket FM began offering content across multiple formats like audiobooks, podcasts and other spoken-word content before shifting its focus toward serialized fiction. [ref: Pocket FM: The Startup that Pioneered Audio Series and Made the Entertainment Industry Follow in Its Footsteps, OK Magazine] By 2021, the platform was describing itself primarily as a community of content creators, and an audio entertainment service serving fictional content in an episodic story format. [ref: Audio OTT app Pocket FM raises $22.4mn funding in round led by Lightspeed, Business Standard]

In December 2021, Pocket FM raised $22.4 million in a Series B funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from Tanglin Venture Partners and existing investor Times Group. The company said the funding would be used to expand its operations, creator community and geographical presence.

In September 2023, the company announced that its Android application had surpassed 100 million downloads on Google Play. The company attributed the growth to its serialized-fiction format and expansion across languages and genres. [ref: Pocket FM crosses over 100 million downloads on Google Play Store, The Times of India]

In March 2024, Pocket FM raised $103 million in a Series D funding round led by Lightspeed, with participation from StepStone Group. A TechCrunch report states the round brought the company's total funding to approximately $196 million, and new valuation at $750 million. The company said that the fresh infusion of funds would support expansion into Europe and Latin America, and growth in the United States. [ref: Audio platform Pocket FM bags $103M in funding as it eyes global expansion, TechCrunch]

== Content and business model ==
Pocket FM's main product is serialized audio fiction dramas in episodic format across genres including romance, fantasy, science fiction, thriller and drama. The website uses a freemium, pay as you go model in which users can listen to initial episodes for free and unlock future episodes by purchasing virtual coins. [ref: Out of Pocket, The Verge]

Pocket FM expanded into the United States in 2022. By March 2024, the company said it had generated more than $150 million in annual recurring revenue, including $100 million from the United States, and was expanding into Europe and Latin America.

Pocket FM's revenue stood at ₹1,768 crore for the financial year 2024–25, an increase of 68 percent from the previous year. More than half of the company's revenue came from user payments through microtransactions, with the remainder coming from advertising. In April 2026, Pocket FM said it had reached approximately $450 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR). The company said it had reached approximately $200 million ARR in the fourth quarter of financial year 2025 and approximately $400 million in the fourth quarter of financial year 2026. [ref: Pocket FM hits $450 million ARR in April after accelerating AI-led content creation, The Economic Times]

== Notable series ==
According to play counts displayed by Pocket FM, Insta Millionaire and Super Yoddha have each accumulated approximately 1.4 billion plays, Ek Ladki Ko Dekha To approximately 1.3 billion, Secret Ameerzaada approximately 885 million, and Insta Empire approximately 556.4 million. [ref: Pocket FM: The home of the world's best audio dramas, pocketfm.com]

== Creator ecosystem ==
Pocket FM relies upon its community of writers and voice artists to produce content for the platform. In 2021, the company reported working with more than 17,000 writers and voice artists for content production. In February 2026, The Economic Times reported that Pocket FM said more than 20 percent of its monetized creators earned more than ₹1 lakh per month and that total creator payouts had exceeded ₹300 crore.

== Artificial intelligence ==
Pocket FM has increasingly incorporated artificial intelligence into the production of its audio content. In June 2024, the company announced a partnership with ElevenLabs to convert written scripts into audio using AI-generated voices. Pocket FM reported produceding 30,000 hours of audio series using ElevenLabs' technology during a testing phase, and planned to make the technology available to its creators in the future.

Brian P. Hall was a values researcher, author, and professor emeritus of pastoral counseling at Santa Clara University. He was an ordained Episcopal priest and served as chairman of Values Technology. [ref: Values Shift: A Guide to Personal and Organizational Transformation, Wipf and Stock Publishers] With Benjamin Tonna, he developed the Hall–Tonna Inventory of Values, an assessment intended to identify values priorities and describe aspects of personal development. [ref: Review of Transition-Related Assessment Instruments, Transition Research Institute, University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]

== Career and publications ==
Hall's work concerned pastoral counseling, values, and personal and organizational development. His publisher describes his work with Values Technology as applying values theory to religious and corporate leadership.

Hall authored The Genesis Effect: Personal and Organizational Transformations and Values Shift: A Guide to Personal and Organizational Transformation. Resource Publications published editions of both books in 2006. The Genesis Effect discusses relationships between values and personal and institutional growth, while Values Shift addresses values, leadership, and organizational change. [ref: The Genesis Effect: Personal and Organizational Transformations, Wipf and Stock Publishers]

== Hall-Tonna Inventory of Values ==
The Hall–Tonna Inventory of Values was developed to identify individuals' values priorities. A 1995 review described the version then available as a computer-scored assessment containing 77 forced-choice items addressing 125 values, eight developmental stages, and seven developmental cycles. It could be administered individually or in groups.

=== Applications in research ===
In a 1991 article in the Journal of School Leadership, Robert P. Craig and Cynthia J. Norris described using the inventory in a university preparation program for prospective school administrators. They examined participants' values clusters in relation to leadership classifications and argued that the process could help participants clarify the philosophical foundations of their educational practice and career decisions. [ref: Values Perception and Future Educational Leaders, Journal of School Leadership]

In 2014, Corne Thomas, Sanetta Henrietta Johanna du Toit, and Susanna Maria van Heerden discussed the Hall–Tonna Values Map in research on leadership and person-centred residential care. The authors used the framework to interpret relationships between organizational values and leadership styles, associating its self-initiating phase with interpersonal relationships, shared responsibility, and recognition of individuality. [ref: Leadership: The key to person-centred care, South African Journal of Occupational Therapy]

=== Evaluation ===
Eleanor E. Sanford reviewed the inventory in the 1992 Eleventh Mental Measurements Yearbook. A summary of her assessment appeared in Teresa A. Dais and Paula D. Kohler's 1995 Review of Transition-Related Assessment Instruments. The summary recorded a recommendation for the instrument while also reporting that further technical information and evidence of validity were needed. It noted Sanford's caution that additional empirical support was necessary before using the inventory to predict or judge individuals' values development and change.

== Selected publications ==

* Values Shift: A Guide to Personal and Organizational Transformation, Resource Publications

Nick Paley is an American screenwriter, director, and editor. He co-wrote the screenplay for the Oscar-nominated feature Marcel the Shell with Shoes On [ref: ] (2021) with Marcel's creators Dean Fleischer Camp and Jenny Slate. [ref: Jenny Slate Can’t Wait for You to See ‘Marcel the Shell with Shoes On’, Vanity Fair] [ref: How 'Marcel the Shell' went from viral sensation to 2022's most adorable movie star, Los Angeles Times] [ref: A Beautiful Collage of Obstacles and Heartbreaks: An Interview with ‘Marcel the Shell with Shoes On’ creators Dean Fleischer-Camp and Nick Paley, Script Magazine] Nick is the creator, showrunner, director, executive producer, and writer of the Hulu television series Phony (2026– present). == Early Life and Education ==
Paley was born and raised in Northern Vermont and graduated from New York University with a film degree.

== Career ==
Paley worked as an editor and director on television projects before collaborating with filmmaker Dean Fleischer Camp on Marcel the Shell with Shoes On. Camp and Paley met while working in television editing.

Paley co-wrote Marcel the Shell with Shoes On with Camp and Jenny Slate. The screenplay was developed through an iterative process in which Paley and Camp wrote sections, recorded Slate improvising dialogue as Marcel, and revised the script using material from those sessions. The process continued over several years. [ref: How 'Marcel the Shell' went from viral sensation to 2022's most adorable movie star, Los Angeles Times] [ref: ‘Marcel the Shell’ made it to the big screen by staying small, The Washington Post] The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Animated Feature, A New York Film Critics Association Award [ref: 'Marcel The Shell With Shoes On' Wins Best Animated Feature From New York Film Critics Circle], and Paley won an Annie Award for Outstanding Achievement in Writing for an Animated Feature. Paley’s television work includes editing and directing on Broad City, Hack Into Broad City [ref: Nick Paley List of Movies and TV Shows - TV Guide, www.tvguide.com], Inside Amy Schumer [ref: TV Review: ‘Inside Amy Schumer’, Variety], and Brody Stevens: Enjoy It!. [ref: Brody Stevens: Enjoy It! credits - Metacritic, www.metacritic.com] He has been nominated for two Emmys for editing and producing, [ref: Telvision Academy Bios - Nick Paley, Telvision Academy] and won an American Cinema Editors award. [ref: ACE Eddie Awards: ‘Mad Max’ & ‘The Big Short’ Take Top Prizes; TV Trophies To ‘Mad Men’, ‘Amy Schumer’ – Winners List, Deadline]

Paley created the Hulu mystery-comedy series Phony, which premiered on October 20, 2026. The series stars Connie Britton and Sam Nivola. It follows a teenager who, after a car accident, suspects that his mother has been replaced by an impostor. [ref: ‘Phony’ Trailer: Sam Nivola Suspects Connie Britton Is An Imposter In Hulu’s Coming-Of-Age Mystery, The Playlist] Paley wrote the first two episodes, directed half of the first season, and executive-produced the series; Anthony King served as co-showrunner. Agata Zając (also written Agata Zajac; born 1995) is a Polish orchestral and operatic conductor based in the United Kingdom. She won second prize in conducting at the Princess Astrid International Music Competition in Trondheim in 2026 and second prize and the audience prize at the Siemens Hallé International Conductors Competition in Manchester in 2023. She has held fellowships and assistantships with the NDR Elbphilharmonie Orchester, the Barcelona Symphony Orchestra, the Royal Northern College of Music and the Tanglewood Music Center.

== Early life and education ==
Zając was born in Poznań. She began her musical education as a violinist at music schools in Poznań, and in 2015 began studying orchestral conducting at the Ignacy Jan Paderewski Academy of Music in Poznań in the class of Marcin Sompoliński, graduating with a master's degree in July 2020. She has also studied in masterclasses and conducting academies with Paavo Järvi (Tonhalle Conductors' Academy, Zürich, 2022), Marin Alsop (NOSPR conducting workshops, 2021), Peter Eötvös, Jorma Panula, Johannes Schlaefli and Mark Heron. In 2018 she received scholarships from the Polish Minister of Culture and National Heritage and the Marshal of the Greater Poland Voivodeship.

== Career ==
=== Early career in Poland ===
From April 2018 Zając worked as an assistant conductor at the Warsaw Chamber Opera on three premieres, including a historically informed reconstruction of Stanisław Moniuszko's Halka (Vilnius version) on period instruments, which was broadcast by TVP Kultura in 2019. In 2018 she received a special prize at the Malta International Conducting Masterclass and Competition, after which she assisted the Greek conductor Michalis Economou with the Malta Philharmonic Orchestra and the Greek Radio Symphony Orchestra; in 2019–20 she assisted him on a New Year concert tour of China with the Athens Philharmonia Orchestra, conducting one of its eleven concerts.

She was resident conductor of the Toruń Symphony Orchestra in the 2020/21 season and of the Sudeten Philharmonic (Filharmonia Sudecka) in Wałbrzych in 2021/22, under a residency programme of the National Institute of Music and Dance.

=== Fellowships and assistantships ===
In 2022 Zając was appointed Mills Williams Junior Fellow in Conducting at the Royal Northern College of Music in Manchester for the 2022/23 season, selected from more than 120 applicants. In the summer of 2023 she was a Conducting Fellow at the Tanglewood Music Center, where she conducted the Tanglewood Music Center Orchestra in works including Rachmaninoff's Isle of the Dead.

She was assistant conductor to Ludovic Morlot at the Barcelona Symphony Orchestra in the 2023/24 and 2024/25 seasons, and one of three Conductor Fellows of the NDR Elbphilharmonie Orchester in Hamburg under Alan Gilbert in 2024/25. She is represented by TACT Artists Management.

=== Guest conducting ===
Zając has conducted orchestras including The Hallé, the Britten Sinfonia, the National Symphony Orchestra of Ireland, the orchestra of the Teatro Regio di Torino, the Grazer Philharmoniker, the Orchestre national de Metz Grand Est, the Pfalzphilharmonie Kaiserslautern, the Real Filharmonía de Galicia, the Siemens Türkiye Symphony Orchestra (at its first concert, in Istanbul in November 2023), the Polish National Radio Symphony Orchestra, the Szczecin Philharmonic and the Poznań Philharmonic.

Her scheduled appearances in the 2026/27 season include the Orquestra Gulbenkian in Lisbon and the NDR Radiophilharmonie, with which she conducts the opening concert of the Harzburger Musiktage in Wolfenbüttel in May 2027.

== Competitions and awards ==
* 2018 – Special prize, Malta International Conducting Masterclass and Competition
* 2021 – Special distinction, International Conducting Competition "Città di Brescia – Giancarlo Facchinetti"
* 2023 – Second prize and audience prize, Siemens Hallé International Conductors Competition, Manchester
* 2026 – Second prize, Princess Astrid International Music Competition (conducting), Trondheim

== Repertoire ==
Zając's repertoire includes symphonic and operatic works, with an emphasis on Central and Eastern European music and Polish composers, including Grażyna Bacewicz.

HiringCafe is a United States-based job search engine that crawls the open web to discover jobs that are not widely promoted. [ref: HiringCafe lands $6.8M to fix the broken job hunt with AI talent agent, TheNextWeb] The service launched in December 2022 as a viral spreadsheet of mostly unpublicized jobs at tech startups, and was later upgraded to an actual search engine, and profiled by Business Insider for its use of ChatGPT to structure job data, and for positioning itself as an alternative to larger, recruiter-driven job boards. [ref: An ex-Meta engineer and Stanford Ph.D. student built a bot in a bid to take on big job sites and put the power in the hands of job seekers, Business Insider]

== History ==

=== 2022–2023: Origins ===
HiringCafe was created by former Meta engineer Ali Mir and Stanford Ph.D. student Hamed Nilforoshan. [ref: https://knight-hennessy.stanford.edu/people/hamed-nilforoshan-dardashti] Mir first maintained a public list of tech employers hiring during the late-2022 technology layoffs and, on 22 December 2022, released an initial directory of links to company career pages. [ref: A brief history and future roadmap of HiringCafe, LinkedIn] The site subsequently added an automated crawler that scanned corporate sites and used OpenAI models to generate short, structured summaries of job descriptions.

=== 2023–2025: Transition from side-project to working app ===
Coverage by Business Insider highlighted the platform’s use of ChatGPT to normalize unstructured postings. The product did not gain widespread popularity, but developed a niche following and a very active [https://www.reddit.com/r/hiringcafe/ user community on Reddit].

Later reporting stated that the creators used OpenAI’s API to process large volumes of listings taken directly from company websites, with claims of several million jobs analyzed. [ref: ChatGPT helps man scrape millions of jobs, leads to new hiring platform, India Today] [ref: Man scrapes 4.1 million jobs with ChatGPT, turns data into new hiring platform, India Today] According to these reports, HiringCafe's AI system was able to extract a lot of data from job descriptions that is usually presented as un-structured text (e.g., specific licensure or security clearance required, working hours and shifts, benefits and perks offered, etc., which are commonly mentioned in job description text, but not usually provided as standardized filterable data fields).

=== 2026: Funding and AI Agent ===
In 2026, HiringCafe raised a round of funding from investors, including Spark Capital and angel investors affiliated with ZipRecruiter and Indeed. [ref: HiringCafe Raises $6.8 Million Pre-Seed And Launches Free AI Talent Agent For Job Seekers, Pulse 2.0] At the same time, HiringCafe announced the launch of an AI agent, called "Talent Agent" that partially automates the process of finding relevant jobs.

== Positioning and Reception ==
While the platform is often lauded for its power and flexibility, reported limitations include a unintuitive user interface with an overwhelming amount of filtering functionality and a steep learning curve, as well as occasional duplicate or overlapping listings and the absence of some résumé-writing, career-advice, and application-automation features offered by other employment platforms. [ref: Best FlexJobs Alternatives To Find Relevant Tech Jobs]

Business Insider characterized HiringCafe as “a bot built to take on big job sites and put the power in the hands of job seekers,” focusing on its use of ChatGPT and its positioning relative to larger boards. The University of Southern California includes HiringCafe among job aggregators in guidance for graduating students, [ref: Job Search Guide for Graduating Students, USC Career Center] and Cornell University notes that some job-search sites (including HiringCafe) publish salary ranges as a filter and allow filtering by degree or major. [ref: Careers Beyond Academia: Creating Lists of Potential Employers, Cornell University Library Guides] Other notable Universities recommending HiringCafe to student job seekers include [https://students.tippie.uiowa.edu/tippie-resources/career-services/undergraduate-career-services/undergraduate-career-resources-0 University of Iowa], describing it as an “ultra-flexible job search engine”. Other institutions listing the service include the [https://customcareer.miami.edu/resources/hiring-cafe/ University of Miami], [https://careerservices.smumn.edu/resources/hiringcafe-job-search-board/ St. Mary's University], [https://www.umass.edu/humanities-arts/careers/resources/finding-jobs-and-internships University of Massachusetts Amherst], [https://careerhub.ufl.edu/blog/2025/01/07/19-job-boards-of-paid-global-early-career-opportunities-for-international-students-recent-grads/ University of Florida], and [https://cdi.ku.edu/technology University of Kansas]. Mashable likewise includes HiringCafe in its roundup of AI-enabled job-search tools, describing its extensive filter set and AI-based extraction of fields from postings. [ref: 11 AI tools to help with your job search, Mashable]

Draft: Giovanni Kasermann

Draft text:
Giovanni Kasermann was a luthier in Naples, Italy during the first half of the 20th century specializing in mandolins [ref: Imposta sui redditi di ricchezza mobile elenco dei contribuenti privati possessori di redditi incerti e variabili delle categorie B e C (esclusa la rivalsa), Italia: Direzione generale imposte dirette]. His workshop was located at Via Carbonara 112 in Naples, Italy, and he was an active luthier until at least 1951 [ref: Dictionnaire universel des luthiers, Bruxelles: Les Amis de la Musique].

His instruments from the early 1900s bear various labels marked "Fratelli Häsermann," while later instruments in the 1910s to 1940s are labeled "Giovanni Kasermann." His craftsmanship featured classic Neapolitan mandolin styles apparent on his decorative bowlback mandolins, but he is also credited with employing a novel double-top design [ref: Mandolin patents in Italy between 1870 and 1930: between real innovations and commercial strategy., "Il periodo d'oro del mandolino" curated by Ugo Orlandi].

An advertisement for Kasermann's workshop published in the 1922 Musique-Adresses Universel states, "A distinguished workshop for Neapolitan mandolins. Unsurpassed concert mandolins for soloists, featuring a marvelous tone and absolutely perfect intonation in every position—a level of quality never before attained in such instruments. We also offer mandolas, mandoloncellos, lutes, mandolones, and guitars, as well as tortoiseshell picks and high-quality musical strings for all types of instruments." [ref: Musique-Adresses Universel, Paris: Office Général de la Musique]

Aside from plucked instruments, Kasermann also made at least one violin that was exhibited at the 1937 Exhibition of Modern and Contemporary Violin Making in Cremona, Italy [ref: Italian Violin Makers, London: Paul Hamlyn] [ref: Le Celebrazioni stradivarianne a Cremona, Turris].

Draft text:
The Memory of the Nations is a historical research project examining Indigenous identity, territorial sovereignty, racial classification, slavery, emancipation, colonial administration, and cultural continuity. It brings together historical maps, treaties, census instructions, land records, legal decisions, photographs, books, and cultural symbols to investigate how governments and institutions have influenced the recognition of peoples and the interpretation of history.

The project connects case studies from North America and other regions, including Indigenous communities in the United States, colonial racial classifications, and historical debates concerning Moorish identity. Its central theme is the relationship between the authority to define identity, control territory, and establish official historical narratives.

1. Indigenous geography and historical names

Indigenous nations across the Americas developed distinct languages, political systems, traditions, territories, and relationships to the land before the formation of modern national borders. These nations included the Muscogee, Cherokee, Chickasaw, Choctaw, Seminole, Lenape, Nanticoke, Catawba, Caddo, Quapaw, Haudenosaunee, and Shawnee, among many others.

Maps associated with the Native Niiji videos identify Indigenous nation names across the Southeast, Great Lakes, Plains, Southwest, Mexico, and Gulf Coast. Examples include Mvskoke, Chickasha, Chahta, Ani’yunwi’ya, Lenni-Lenape, Nanticoke, Shawano, Quapaw, and Caddo.

These maps provide starting points for examining Indigenous geography, migration, settlement, and political relationships. However, historical names may vary between Indigenous languages, colonial records, missionary accounts, treaties, and later publications. Maps must therefore be evaluated alongside archaeological findings, community histories, treaties, and other primary sources.

Lenape and Nanticoke histories are associated with the Mid-Atlantic region, including present-day Delaware. Chickasaw and Choctaw histories connect to the southeastern United States and later settlement in Indian Territory. Seminole history includes Florida, connections with Muscogee communities, forced removal, and continuing questions of sovereignty.

2. Texas, Galveston, land ownership, and slavery

The Akokisa and Karankawa have documented histories along the Texas coast before the establishment of the Republic of Texas.

In February 1836, Sam Houston negotiated a treaty with Cherokee and other East Texas communities. The Convention of 1836 did not ratify the agreement. Texas authorities subsequently relied on the absence of recognized land titles in decisions affecting Indigenous territorial claims and removal.

On June 13, 1837, the Telegraph and Texas Register published legislation concerning the relinquishment of one league and one labor of land at the eastern end of Galveston Island to Michael B. Menard and associates, subject to specified conditions. Texas General Land Office records preserve documents concerning land transactions, certificates, purchasers, and patents.

Galveston also participated in the domestic slave trade. Rosenberg Library preserves manifests associated with enslaved people transported aboard the steamships Galveston and Texas. The records include one manifest listing eight enslaved people and another listing 63. A bill of sale dated May 13, 1865, documents the sale of Louise, an eight-year-old child, and a six-month-old infant.

Together, these sources provide evidence of systems through which land and human beings were transferred under legal and commercial arrangements. They also offer opportunities for research into individual property transactions, enslaved families, and the consequences of slavery.

Sources: "Texas State Library and Archives Commission" (https://www.tsl.texas.gov/arc/local/galveston.html); "Texas State Historical Association" (https://www.tshaonline.org/); "Rosenberg Library African American history resources" (https://www.galvestonhistorycenter.org/research/african-american-history-resources-from-slavery-to-juneteenth).

3. The American Civil War and emancipation

The American Civil War lasted from 1861 to 1865. The Confederacy seceded to preserve slavery, which Confederate leaders identified as central to their social and economic order. The conflict involved enslaved people seeking freedom, free Black communities, Union soldiers, Indigenous nations, abolitionists, and political leaders.

The Emancipation Proclamation, effective January 1, 1863, declared enslaved people in designated areas still in rebellion against the United States to be free. It did not immediately abolish slavery throughout the entire country. As Union forces advanced, enslaved people escaped bondage, sought refuge, resisted plantation labor, and joined the military struggle. Black military service became an important component of Union victory.

On June 19, 1865, Union Major General Gordon Granger issued General Order No. 3 in Galveston, Texas, announcing freedom for enslaved people in Texas under the authority of the Emancipation Proclamation. The event became known as Juneteenth.

The Thirteenth Amendment, ratified on December 6, 1865, abolished slavery throughout the United States, except as punishment for a crime following conviction. Emancipation did not end racial discrimination, violence, or disputes over labor, land, and citizenship.

Draft text:
Samuel Bird was a 14-year-old member of Paul First Nation who disappeared in Edmonton, Alberta, on June 1, 2025, after leaving his home to visit a friend. His remains were discovered in a rural area outside Edmonton on October 16, 2025. [ref: Mother of Samuel Bird calls for more awareness of all missing, murdered Indigenous children, CBC News]

On October 15, 2025, Edmonton police arrested Bryan Farrell, 38, and charged him with second-degree murder and interfering with a body in connection with Bird's death.

== Disappearance ==
On June 1, 2025, Samuel Bird left his home in west Edmonton to visit a friend. According to police, surveillance footage recorded him at approximately 8:30 p.m. walking through the grounds of Holy Cross School, near 151 Street and 104 Avenue. He subsequently went to a friend's residence near 150 Street and 106 Avenue in the Canora neighbourhood, where investigators said he was last seen. [ref: Man charged with murder as remains of Samuel Bird located outside Edmonton, Yahoo News Malaysia] [ref: Search for Samuel Bird: New information leads police to wooded area 160km west of Edmonton, CityNews Toronto]

In the months following his disappearance, Bird's family and volunteers searched Edmonton and surrounding areas. Missing-person posters were distributed throughout the city, and his mother, Alanna Bird, helped organize community searches. In August, searchers from Manitoba joined efforts to examine the shores and waters of the North Saskatchewan River. [ref: Missing Edmonton teen Samuel Bird presumed dead; police deem death criminal in nature, CityNews Toronto]

Police searched the residence where Bird was last seen on September 18. On September 29, emergency crews responded to a fire at the same property, which investigators described as suspicious. [ref: Family of missing Edmonton teen Samuel Bird pushes to expand search before winter, CityNews Toronto]

On October 1, Edmonton police announced that Bird was presumed dead and that they believed his death was criminal in nature. Investigators said his body might have been concealed in a rural area west of Edmonton and appealed to landowners, hunters and other members of the public for information. His family subsequently redirected its volunteer search efforts toward the area identified by police.

== Search efforts ==
The Evelyn Memorial Search Team from Manitoba assisted with searches of the North Saskatchewan River, using an AquaEye handheld sonar device to scan underwater. [ref: Manitoba group helping search for missing Edmonton teen Samuel Bird, Raven Radio Network] Volunteers with diving experience and underwater cameras also participated, while a community crisis team supplied food and water to searchers. [ref: ]

A Facebook group named Bring Samuel Bird Home supported the search by sharing notices about upcoming searches and gatherings. A fundraiser organized by Samantha Dornbusch on behalf of Alanna Bird directed supporters to the group and sought donations for search supplies, boat rentals, licensed drone operators and specialist water-search teams.

The Confederacy of Treaty No. 6 First Nations supported the family and sought additional assistance from regional and external partners. In an August statement, it acknowledged responders, volunteers and community members searching within Edmonton and neighbouring First Nations, noting that many were using personal resources. [ref: Confederacy of Treaty No. 6 First Nations asks EPS to designate Samuel Bird case as Search and Recovery, Treatysix]

Police-led searches also covered wooded and agricultural land near Carrot Creek, approximately 160 kilometres west of Edmonton. These efforts involved professional ground searchers, cadaver dogs, civilian search dogs and drones.

== Discovery of Remains ==
On the morning of October 16, 2025, Edmonton police located Samuel Bird's remains in a rural area outside the city, more than four months after his disappearance. Police Chief Warren Driechel said developments in the investigation the previous day had led to searches continuing overnight and the recovery the following morning. Police notified Bird's family before publicly announcing the discovery. [ref: Edmonton teen Samuel Bird's body found, arrest made, CityNews Toronto]

The following day, investigators disclosed that the remains had been found in a treed area near a farmer's field south of Stony Plain, west of Edmonton. The location was separate from the area near Carrot Creek where police had concentrated search efforts the previous week. [ref: False tips, narratives complicate difficult investigation death of Samuel Bird: EPS, CityNews Edmonton]

Bird's mother, Alanna Bird, acknowledged the discovery in a social media post and thanked police, volunteer searchers and those who had donated to support the search. [ref: ]

== Perpetrator ==
On October 15, 2025, Edmonton police arrested Bryan Farrell, who was 38 at the time, and charged him with second-degree murder and interfering with a body in connection with Samuel Bird's death. Police stated that Farrell was the only person charged in the homicide and that they were not seeking additional suspects at that time. == User Needs for News ==
User needs for news is a strategic and planning framework used by newsrooms and journalists to maximise audience engagement. As the name suggests, this approach is used to ensure that news articles, videos and other content is commissioned, created and published from angles which address the specific needs of the audience.

It draws from principles of human-centred design and User-centered design, in which the needs of the audience, or end user influence how the product or design is developed and created.

Proponents argue that if done correctly, newsrooms can create content that is more relevant for audiences [ref: [https://www.journalism.co.uk/why-user-needs-model-has-the-power-to-transform-your-newsrooms-beyond-traditional-reporting/] "Why user needs have the power to stop audiences feeling overwhelmed by the news". Journalism UK. 2025-03-19. Retrieved 2026-09-02] - and audiences will engage for longer, and with more regularity.

== Origins and background in news media ==
While news is most often associated with the relaying of facts, consumers have long read, watched or listened to news for a wide variety of reasons.

"Back in the 1940s, Bernard Berelson (1949) described how people living in New York felt a sense of companionship and connectedness from reading the newspaper, and from the 1970s onwards, researchers have detailed a wide range of ‘uses and gratifications’ – such as entertainment and escapism – that people can find through news or other forms of media use." [ref: [https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/more-just-facts-how-news-audiences-think-about-user-needs] "More than 'just the facts': How news audiences think about 'user needs' | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism". reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk. Retrieved 2026-09-02.]

News outlets had - and have - different ways of communicating information to publishing simple updates. Opinion pieces bring a personal perspective to any issue or subject; interviews allow readers to feel inspired or moved by a direct experience. Concise explainers provide context and background to unfolding events.

In short, before user needs was named thus, they mostly certainly existed.

The BBC was among the first to formalise a user needs approach, and in 2016 it developed the first user needs model [ref: [https://theaudiencers.com/9-the-model-that-transformed-the-bbc/] White, Madeleine (2023-03-15). "#9. The model that transformed the BBC". Audiencers. Retrieved 2026-09-02.], from which many subsequent frameworks have evolved. In this, the BBC identified six core reasons (needs) readers sought out news:

# Update me
# Keep me on Trend
# Educate me
# Give me Perspective
# Inspire me
# Divert me

These were not selected from inside the newsroom: it followed a thorough analysis of audience engagement and came from cues from the audience themselves. They discovered, for example, that while 70% of their published content on one of their news sites (BBC Russia) could be classed as updates, but in fact Update Me content accounted for only 7% of page views.

Data analysis is a key part of the user needs process: those applying this framework to their own newsrooms must combine audience-centric planning with post-publication data analysis in order to ascertain what works, what doesn't - and why.

== Development and versions ==
Since 2016, many other news organisations have adopted, adapted or created their own user needs framework. These organisations include (but are not limited to) The Conversation [ref: [https://smartocto.com/client-case/identifying-brand-specific-user-needs-the-conversation/]"Identifying brand-specific user needs with The Conversation". smartocto. Retrieved 2026-09-02.], The Atlantic [ref: [https://www.editorandpublisher.com/stories/the-atlantic-spent-two-years-studying-what-readers-and-listeners-need-heres-what-they-found,216143] Lab, Emily Goligoski "The Atlantic spent two years studying what readers and listeners need. Here's what they found". Editor and Publisher. Retrieved 2026-09-02], Berlingske Media [ref: [https://wan-ifra.org/2026/01/from-user-needs-to-digital-innovation-5-lessons-from-leading-danish-publishers/] Radcliffe, WAN-IFRA External (2026-01-27). "From user needs to digital innovation: 5 lessons from leading Danish publishers". WAN-IFRA. Retrieved 2026-09-02.], and Vogue [ref: [https://medium.com/hacks-hackers-london/how-vogue-is-growing-audiences-by-focusing-on-readers-needs-39c48cbc3cf5] Zaffarano, Francesco (2021-03-23). "How Vogue is growing audiences by focusing on readers' needs" Medium: Hacks/Hackers London. Retrieved 2026-09-02.].

Dmitry Shishkin, the editor who had developed and championed the original BBC model, started working with editorial analytics company, smartocto, to finesse the user needs framework, and in 2022 together they announced User Needs 2.0 [ref: [https://theaudiencers.com/user-needs-2-0-a-plug-and-play-model-to-be-more-valuable-to-audiences/] Khalil A. Cassimally "User needs 2.0: a plug-and-play model to be more valuable to audiences" The Audiencers. 6 March, 2023]. This expanded the original six user needs to eight 'universal needs'.

[[File:Eurasian Curlew Numenius arquata by Vedant Raju Kasambe DSC 4507 (11).jpg|thumb|The Eurasian curlew, which the Whistlers are often identified with.]]

The Seven Whistlers are ill omens from English folklore, composed of seven birds that foretell or cause misfortune. [ref: Rustic Speech and Folk-lore, H. Milford] [ref: Washington University Studies, Washington University.] Variably said to be the spirits of the dead, a transformed group of seven coal miners, or the souls of wondering Jewish people, they were a common belief among coal miners and seamen in the 19th century. [ref: A Dictionary of English Folklore, Oxford University Press] [ref: Notes and Queries, Oxford University Press] In some variations, it’s a group of six searching for the seventh, and if they reunite the world will end. [ref: History of British Folklore, Routledge]

== Identification ==
The Seven Whistlers are identified with several birds; such as the eurasian curlew [ref: On World Curlew Day, a Song of Hope for Whimbrel, whsrn.org], the corn crake, the swift, and the wigeon. One particular example, the whimbrel, notably has a 5-7 note call.

== Belief ==
Beliefs about the nature of the Seven Whistlers vary. Beliefs include that they are the souls of Jews who assisted in the crucifixion, condemned with eternal restlessness; that they are the souls of the dead, returned to warn people of danger; and that they are seven coal miners, who after either getting drunk and engaging in whistling at night for a bet were carried up into the sky and transformed.

Coal miners were known to refuse to work in the mines the day after the sound of the Whistlers was heard.

== In Culture ==
The Seven Whistlers are referenced in Edmund Spenser’s 1590 epic poem The Fairy Queene, with the line “The Whistler shrill, that who so heares, doth dy”. [ref: The Faerie Queene, Book II., The University Press]

William Wordsworth’s poem Though narrow be that old man’s cares directly references the Seven Whistlers. [ref: The Earlier Poems of William Wordsworth: Corrected as in the Latest Editions. With Preface, and Notes Showing the Text as it Stood in 1815, E. Moxon]

O. Henry’s short story The Door of Unrest features the Seven Whistlers, going by the story of them being the Jews who assisted with the crucifixion. [ref: Sixes and Sevens]

== References ==

Cayosoft is a privately held American software company that develops administration, monitoring, and recovery tools for Microsoft identity environments, including Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, and Microsoft 365. Independent product analyses have described the company’s approach as combining day-to-day hybrid identity administration with change monitoring, rollback, and directory recovery. [ref: Cayosoft Review, Start with Identity] [ref: Cayosoft Administrator: In-Depth Review & Analysis, Expert Insights]

== History ==
Cayosoft was founded in 2013 by Robert Bobel and Andrey Polevoy. In a 2024 profile, Pulse 2.0 discussed the founders’ backgrounds in enterprise identity software, the company’s focus on hybrid Microsoft environments, and its development from administration software into monitoring and recovery products. [ref: Cayosoft: Helping Organizations Manage And Protect Their Microsoft Infrastructures, Pulse 2.0]

The company initially concentrated on automating user, group, licensing, and delegated-administration tasks across on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft cloud services. It later expanded into change auditing, threat monitoring, rollback, and disaster recovery. Start with Identity characterized the resulting platform as strongest for Microsoft-centric organizations seeking administration and resilience in one product, while noting that its narrower Microsoft focus and limited cross-cloud behavioral analytics may make it less suitable for organizations seeking a detection-only or broad software-as-a-service identity-security platform. [ref: Cayosoft Review, Start with Identity]

In 2021, Cayosoft added automated Active Directory forest recovery to its Guardian product line. Independent reviews subsequently examined Guardian as a combined monitoring and recovery product rather than solely as a backup utility. PeerSpot describes it as software for automated protection, anomaly detection, permissions oversight, and recovery, while Start with Identity places it in the identity threat detection and response market but emphasizes its operational-resilience focus. [ref: Cayosoft Guardian reviews 2026, PeerSpot] [ref: Cayosoft Review, Start with Identity]

In March 2024, Cayosoft raised $22.5 million from Centana Growth Partners. Coverage of the financing described the company as a provider of hybrid directory-management and recovery software and reported that the investment was intended to support product development and international expansion. [ref: Cayosoft attracts $22.5m from Centana Growth Partners, FinTech Global]

== Products ==
=== Cayosoft Administrator ===
Cayosoft Administrator automates identity-lifecycle and delegated-administration tasks across hybrid Microsoft environments. In its detailed review, Expert Insights examined onboarding and offboarding, group lifecycle management, license optimization, delegated help-desk access, workflow controls, and audit history. The review identified broad hybrid-Microsoft coverage and policy-based delegation as strengths, while observing that the product is primarily suited to organizations already centered on Microsoft identity services. [ref: Cayosoft Administrator: In-Depth Review & Analysis, Expert Insights]

=== Cayosoft Guardian ===
Cayosoft Guardian provides identity-change monitoring, threat detection, rollback, and recovery. Independent reviews describe its principal distinction as combining administration and monitoring with recovery of individual directory objects and entire Active Directory environments. Reviews also note limits associated with its Microsoft-specific scope and its emphasis on resilience rather than broader cross-cloud identity analytics. [ref: Cayosoft Review, Start with Identity] [ref: Cayosoft Guardian reviews 2026, PeerSpot]

== Patents ==
Cayosoft is the assignee of United States patents covering directory-service recovery and administrative-unit management. U.S. Patent Nos. 12,093,141, 12,399,791, and 12,743,349, granted between September 2024 and September 2026, are related patents in a continuation family titled Systems and methods for directory service backup and recovery. They describe maintaining a standby directory service that can be implemented when a host directory service is interrupted. U.S. Patent No. 12,254,107, granted in March 2025, is titled Orchestration of administrative unit management and covers methods for evaluating and implementing directory-object membership changes across administrative units. [ref: Patents Assigned to CAYOSOFT, INC., Justia Patents Search] [ref: U.S. Patent No. 12,093,141, Google Patents]

Since 2024, Cayosoft has appeared in Gartner research concerning Microsoft identity administration, governance, backup, rollback, and recovery. Inclusion in Gartner research does not constitute an endorsement, ranking, or product recommendation.
