RigER (RigER Inc.) is a software company that makes operations management software for oilfield service and equipment rental companies. It was started in Calgary, Alberta, in 2012 by Michael Maltsev, who had worked as chief financial officer of an oilfield rentals company. The company later moved to Texas, and since February 2026 its headquarters has been in Bee Cave, a suburb of Austin. The name stands for "Rig Equipment Rental".
== History ==
Before starting RigER, Michael Maltsev spent three years as chief financial officer of an oilfield rentals company. In a 2014 interview with the Calgary Herald, he said the software available to such companies was expensive and complicated, and that spreadsheets did not work well when many people needed to share data and reports. He said the first prototype took about two months to build, and the first full version was ready about six months later. The Calgary Herald featured the company that year in its "Startup of the Week" column, describing it as software for small and medium-sized energy services companies.

In April 2016, Alberta Oil magazine profiled RigER and Maltsev, whom it described as a former oilfield financial officer with a background in technology. It described RigER's software as cloud-based, usable through mobile apps and designed for small and medium-sized oilfield rental and energy service companies. The magazine reported that RigER had decided to make its software available to other equipment rental firms rather than keep it only for the in-house rental fleet it was first built for. The firm said it had 10 client companies at the end of February 2016. It noted that while other invoice-management software firms operated in Canada, none appeared to focus as closely on oilfield rentals.

In October 2018 the Odessa American put Maltsev on its front page in its coverage of the Permian Basin International Oil Show, where RigER was exhibiting. The paper described RigER as a company operating out of western Canada that makes software for equipment rentals, field tickets and invoicing. Maltsev told the paper that the company had three or four competitors in North America.

In December 2020, Permian Basin Oil & Gas Magazine described RigER as an Alberta-based company in an article about oilfield firms adopting software after the economic crash of spring 2020. Maltsev told the magazine that the COVID-19 pandemic had pushed more oilfield companies to go digital, and that RigER had added new modules.

By 2022 the company was based in Fort Worth, Texas. In June of that year it announced a partnership with CashLine Solutions, a company that provides order-to-cash services to the oil and gas industry. In July, the Midland television station KMID reported that RigER was marking its tenth anniversary and planned to set up a presence in the Midland area.

According to the company, RigER has exhibited at oil and gas trade shows in Canada, the United States and the Middle East since 2017. At ADIPEC in Abu Dhabi in November 2024, the event's official daily newspaper carried a profile of the company. Maltsev spoke at Offshore Europe in September 2025.

In February 2026 RigER moved its headquarters to Bee Cave, Texas. Maltsev said the Austin area's mix of energy and technology companies made it a good fit for the business.
== Products ==
RigER's main product is a cloud-based system with mobile apps. It covers sales, dispatching, field operations, equipment maintenance, asset tracking, safety records, field tickets, invoicing and billing. The company says its software is used in the Americas, Europe and the Middle East.

In 2019 the company presented version 6.5, "Houston", at the Offshore Technology Conference and version 7.0, "Oklahoma", at the Oklahoma Oil & Gas Expo. Version 8.0, called "Odessa", came out in December 2020. It added mobile apps that work offline, customer relationship management tools, a built-in email client and barcode scanning for checking equipment in and out. Version 9.0, "Greeley", was announced in October 2021. It added a web portal for customers, QR-code check-in and check-out of equipment, and a direct link to the OpenInvoice billing platform.

In April 2026 the company released RigER PRO, a separate mobile-first app for field ticketing aimed at small and mid-sized oilfield service companies. Version 2.0, shown at Oil Sands Canada in Calgary in June 2026, added syncing with QuickBooks Online.
== Recognition ==
In 2022 RigER was one of three winners in the digitalization category of E&P magazine's Meritorious Awards for Engineering Innovation, run by Hart Energy. Entries were judged by a panel of engineers and scientists from operating and consulting companies.

Anime Impulse is an American multi-city fan convention focused on Japanese anime, manga, video games, cosplay, and popular culture. FEST] and [https://www.impulseuniverse.com/collectors-expo Collectors Expo]. [ref: IMPULSE UNIVERSE, IMPULSE UNIVERSE]

Originally launched alongside the [https://aaexpo.com/ Asian American Expo] in Pomona, California, Anime Impulse has expanded into a series of conventions held across the United States, including events in California, Arizona, Texas, and Washington. [ref: ]

Anime Impulse features appearances by voice actors, content creators, cosplayers, and other entertainment personalities, alongside artist exhibitions, merchandise vendors, live performances, panel discussions, and interactive fan programming. [ref: Program Rundown, ANIME Impulse] [ref: ] At co-located events, admission also provides access to other Impulse Universe conventions, connecting anime fandom with Korean pop culture, gaming, and collectibles.

== History ==

=== Founding and Early Development (2016–2020) ===
Anime Impulse debuted on January 16–17, 2016, at the Fairplex in Pomona, California, as part of the 35th annual Asian American Expo. [ref: Asian-American Expo returns to Pomona with some new additions, Daily Bulletin]

The convention was established to introduce anime, manga, video games, and cosplay programming to a broader audience within the existing Asian American Expo. Its inaugural event featured appearances by internationally recognized cosplayers Alodia Gosiengfiao, Ashley Gosiengfiao, and VampyBitMe. [ref: Anime Impulse 2016 Information, AnimeCons.com.]

Convention producer Kaila Yu described the co-location arrangement as a distinguishing feature, allowing attendees to experience anime-related programming alongside the food vendors and cultural attractions offered through the larger exposition.

The convention's organizers also emphasized accessibility to casual anime fans, describing an environment designed for visitors who enjoyed Japanese popular culture without necessarily identifying as dedicated convention attendees.

=== Expansion and Diversification (2022–present) ===
Following its early years in Pomona, Anime Impulse expanded its event programming and geographic presence.

Impulse Universe introduced K-Play! Fest in 2022, expanding its convention portfolio into Korean popular music and entertainment. [ref: K-PLAY! Fest 2022 to Host Flagship Event at The Pomona Fairplex, K-Pop Concerts] Collectors Expo subsequently contributed a focus on trading cards, collectibles, and related hobbies.

In 2024, Impulse Universe expanded its convention operations beyond California, holding events in the Seattle [ref: Anime Impulse Seattle 2024 Information, AnimeCons.com] and Phoenix [ref: Anime Impulse Phoenix 2024 Information, AnimeCons.com] markets.

The expansion continued into Texas, with Anime Impulse Dallas held at the Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center on November 15–16, 2025. [ref: Anime Impulse Dallas 2025 Information, AnimeCons.com]

== Convention Programming ==
Anime Impulse organizes a range of activities centered on anime, gaming, cosplay, and fan communities.

Programming includes voice actor autograph sessions and meet-and-greets, celebrity panels, cosplay gatherings and competitions, live performances, artist exhibitions, and vendor marketplaces.

The convention has also incorporated virtual entertainers, including VTubers, into its guest programming. Gaming-related activities and appearances connect the event with audiences of Japanese role-playing games, online games, and other interactive entertainment. [ref: ]

=== Programming and Entertainment ===
Anime Impulse features programming related to Japanese animation, video games, cosplay, music, and online entertainment. Events typically include voice actor autograph sessions, guest panels, live performances, artist exhibitions, merchandise vendors, cosplay competitions, and organized fan gatherings.

Additional attractions have included gaming tournaments, free-play arcade areas, customized Japanese automobiles known as itasha, [ref: ] and interactive exhibitions organized in collaboration with entertainment companies.

=== Musical Performances ===
Anime Impulse has hosted musical performers associated with Japanese animation and video game soundtracks, including the Japanese rock band BURNOUT SYNDROMES, known for songs featured in Haikyu!! and other anime series. [ref: Anime Impulse Dallas 2025 Information, AnimeCons.com]

Music programming also takes place through the co-located K-PLAY! FEST, which focuses on Korean popular music and culture. Its featured performers have included South Korean artists Lee Young-ji, Sik-K, and pH-1, [ref: Previous Events, K-PLAY! FEST] as well as Japanese rapper and music producer Lotus Juice. [ref: Lotus Juice Information, AnimeCons.com]

=== VTuber and Digital Creator Appearances ===
Virtual YouTubers, commonly known as VTubers, have become a recurring component of ANIME Impulse programming. The convention has collaborated with VTuber agencies including NIJISANJI EN and hololive, featuring virtual entertainers through meet-and-greet sessions, panels, and live performances. Draft text:
The 2023 Shell oil platform protest was a Greenpeace action in which activists boarded and occupied a Shell oil platform being transported across the Atlantic Ocean.

== Historical background ==

In 2018, Shell began investing in the redevelopment of the Penguin oil and gas field, northeast of the Shetland Islands. It authorized the construction of the Penguins FPSO, the company's first manned installation in the UK North Sea in 30 years. [ref: Shell approves development of Penguins oil, gas field in North Sea, Reuters] [ref: Shell hits Greenpeace protestors on Penguins FPSO with injunction, Energy Voice]

Construction of the platform was completed by China's Offshore Oil Engineering Company in November 2022. The 34,000-tonne FPSO was then transported from China by Dutch shipping company Boskalis with its vessel the White Marlin. [ref: Greenpeace activists end 13-day occupation of Shell's oil platform, Offshore Energy] [ref: Greenpeace Activists Board Heavy-lift Vessel Carrying Shell's Penguins FPSO, Offshore Engineer] The platform was said to allow Shell to develop eight new wells at the Penguins field, with expected output reaching up to 45,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. [ref: Shell Gives North Sea Shot in Arm With Field Redevelopment, Bloomberg]

== Boarding and protest ==

On January 31, 2023, six Greenpeace activists approached the White Marlin in three boats launched from the Greenpeace ship Arctic Sunrise. The platform was still in route to the North Sea and in the Atlantic Ocean north of Gran Canaria at the time. Four of them used ropes to climb onto the deck. [ref: Footage shows the moment Greenpeace activists scaled a Shell oil platform that was being transported in 'rough conditions' in the Atlantic, Business Insider] The four activists occupied the vessel's cargo and displayed a banner reading "Stop Drilling. Start Paying."

Shell sought an injunction against Greenpeace while the four activists occupied the platform. The injunction required two of Greenpeace's ships to stay clear of the White Marlin. After the injunction, two more activists boarded using a chartered trimaran and small boats which were not listed in the injunction. [ref: More Greenpeace Protestors Board Heavy-Lift Vessel Carrying Shell FPSO, The Maritime Executive] The following day, a court issued an order barring further boardings and requiring the six activists to leave the platform upon its arrival in Norway.

The activists set up a wind turbine on the platform to power their communications equipment. [ref: Activists disembark Shell Penguins FPSO after 13-days, Energy Voice] Other activists who did not board sailed out to confront the White Marlin without boarding it. The occupation ended on February 12, 2026 when the vessel docked at Haugesund, Norway. No arrests were made after the activists left the platform.

== Litigation and settlement ==

In February 2023 Shell sent a claim to Greenpeace $120,000 over damage it claimed was caused during the occupation. In November 2023 Shell filed a lawsuit against Greenpeace, seeking $2.1 million for legal, safety and security costs it incurred because of the protest. [ref: Shell sues Greenpeace for $2.1 million after boarding oil vessel, Reuters] Shell also asked the court to bar Greenpeace from protesting at its offshore infrastructure.

Shell offered to settle for $1.4 million if Greenpeace agreed to never protest against against future Shell infrastructure at sea or port, but Greenpeace refused the settlement, calling it a strategic lawsuit against public participation. [ref: Shell sues Greenpeace after FPSO boarding, Splash247] In a December 2023 filing Shell reduced the claim to about $1 million. [ref: Greenpeace to donate £300,000 to RNLI as part of lawsuit settlement with Shell, Civil Society]

The lawsuit was settled out of court in December 2024 with Greenpeace donating £300,000 to the Royal National Lifeboat Institution and accepting no liability or paying anything directly to Shell. The activists involved agreed not to travel within 500 metres of three Shell North Sea sites for five years. [ref: Greenpeace settles lawsuit with Shell over North Sea protest, Riviera Maritime Media]

His roleplaying content on the "GTA RP" servers acted as his first major breakout, pushing his average viewership into the thousands [ref: FaZe Silky on Beef with Adin Ross, Almost Losing His Life, Joining Faze Clan].

In 2021, Silky experienced a breakthrough year, transitioning from a growing gaming streamer into a major personality-driven, "Just Chatting" powerhouse.

== Early life and Studies ==
János Farkas's family history is rooted in political tragedy and noble secrecy. Following the war of independence in 1848, his maternal

great grandparents. [ref: Love story a szobor talpán, VAOL] participated in a conspiracy against the Viennese court. When the plot was uncovered, they were convicted and executed. Their orphaned daughter, Mária Szigeti was raised in the house of count Batthyány and his wife with the count's son in Zalacsány. When they grew up, they fell in love, but the Countess did not approve. They had a son József (adopted name Farkas). János Farkas, the sculpture, was the son of József, the grandson of the count. He was born in a small village in [https://savoly.hu/ Sávoly] (Somogysávoly) in western Hungary. He had a sister, Aranka and a brother Lajos.

[Name change: Although Farkas had a noble lineage, due to the situation, the child could not carry on the Batthyány name as Lajos Batthyány, in the extended family, was Hungary's first prime minister in 1848. A wealthy agricultural property owner, István Farkas married his biological mother Magda Szigeti, and adopted [ref: Love story a szobor talpán, Love story a szobor talpán] the boy, hence the name Farkas instead of Batthyány.]

Janos Farkas was born shortly after Worlds War I. He entered the world during a period of national despair, when the country lost 80% its territories. Political uncertainty peeked with a brief rise of communist flair of Hungarian Soviet Republic (Tanácsköztársaság) in 1919. [ref: Visit Szombathely]

Despite these turbulent times, his abilities were recognized early. He began school at age four at Keszthely, later moved to Balatonlelle, where he attended upper school (polgári). He completed the curriculum in two years, instead of four.

His artistic abilities caught the attention of the local priest who encouraged the youngster who started to sculpt at age 8. By age 11, he created a portrait of Christ [ref: Tizennégyéves szobrász zseni, Tolnai világlapja] and at fourteen, an industrialist [https://www.vaol.hu/kultura/2009/07/love-story-a-szobor-talpan? Nándor Rott] [ref: Titokzatos szobrok, rejtélyes üzenetek Farkas Jánostól, VAOL Vas vármegyei Hírportál], took the youngster to study at the Budapest School of Applied Arts (Országos Magyar Királyi Képzőművészeti Iskola), where he studied under Imre Simai. Farkas received recognition from János Pásztor, an established sculptor at the time. In his teen years, Farkas worked on private commissions to support his stay in Vienna where he was a frequent at the Art Gallery and enjoyed guiding visitors (unofficially). He passed his matura exams at 16 (customarily 18) [https://www.kozterkep.hu/adattar/lexikon_szocikk/1216? 1935-37]. His education was further sponsored by Baron Paul Szunyogh [ref: László Gyula: Farkas János (1920-1994), Hungaricana - Életünk 1997 (35. évfolyam 8. szám)]. Media coverage of Farkas's work began as early as age twelve and continued to gain attention including the supplementary section of Pesti Napló in 1936 [ref: Egy 14 éves szobrásztehetség útja a világhír felé, Uj Somogy].

The young sculptor continued his studies at the Academy of Fine Arts (Képzőművészeti Főiskola) a six-year institution, where he was formed by master artists Ferenc Medgyessy and Ferenc Sidló. Sidló remarked about Farkas: "We have embraced a talent such as the Hungarian land gives birth to just one or two every century" [ref: Látogatás Farkas Jancsinál az Epreskertben, Balatoni kurir] and Medgyessy similarly considered Farkas a "natural talent of his generation". The respect was mutual, Medgyessy was an important artistic influence. Farkas's nude sculpture Combing Hair, [ref: Fésülködő leány, Farkas János, Nemzeti Galéria] was submitted to the Szinyei competition and was accepted to the collection of the Museum of Fine Arts. Farkas won most competitions held for young artists. He started to read about art and sculptors at a very early age, finding the Museum of Fine Arts in Budapest to be perfect setting, where he could offer visitors his contextual interpretations.

Farkas spent his post-college scholarship years to study further in Vienna in 1941 and in Rome 1942-43. Rome was transformative, this was where he solidified his artistic style, devotion to renaissance. He worked in multiple mediums, but he had a preference to marble.

In 1947, he finally got his diploma.

== Family Life and Final Illness ==
Farkas met his first wife, Ilona Görgey ([https://www.myheritage.hu/family-trees/farkas/OYYV7RFEJWOJUIHMH7OOHJ37BE3DYBY?familyTreeID=0 1919-]2009) in college at the Budapest School of Fine Arts from where she graduated as a goldsmith. She had quite a historic prominent family background.

linscp (Linux Secure Copy) is a cross-platform file manager and SSH File Transfer Protocol (SFTP), File Transfer Protocol (FTP), WebDAV, Amazon S3, and Secure copy protocol (SCP) client for Linux and Microsoft Windows. Its source code is publicly available on [https://github.com/99ecarvalho/linscp GitHub]. The software is distributed under the GNU General Public License, version 3. [ref: linscp, linscp.org]

==Program==
linscp transfers files between a local computer and remote servers. It also provides tools to browse and manage remote files, compare directories, and synchronize their contents. SFTP and SCP connections use the Secure Shell (SSH) protocol.

The application provides two graphical layouts. Its Commander layout displays local and remote files in side-by-side panels, while the Explorer layout displays the remote files with a folder tree. The client can queue transfers and edit remote files using an internal or external editor.

The separate linscp-cli console client supports scripting and automation. The graphical and console clients share sites, settings and scripts across Linux and Windows. The project distributes packages for 64-bit Linux and for 64-bit Windows 10 and 11. [ref: linscp, GitHub]

linscp uses WinSCP's core for sessions, transfers, scripting and messages, with an interface built using Qt. Its SSH, SFTP and SCP support uses components from PuTTY; FTP and FTPS use FileZilla's FTP engine; WebDAV uses neon; and Amazon S3 support uses libs3. OpenSSL provides TLS and cryptographic functions. linscp is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by WinSCP. [ref: Licence and credits, linscp]

==Features==
* Support for SFTP and SCP over SSH, FTP and FTPS, WebDAV, and Amazon S3-compatible storage.
* Commander and Explorer graphical layouts.
* A site manager for saved connections, session URLs, and imports from PuTTY and KiTTY sessions, OpenSSH configuration, FileZilla, and WinSCP INI files. [ref: Site Manager, linscp]
* Queued and resumable transfers, transfer presets, and speed limits.
* Preservation of file modification timestamps during transfers. [ref: Transfer settings, linscp]
* Directory comparison and synchronization, including keeping a remote directory up to date.
* Remote file editing with automatic upload after saving.
* Command-line automation through linscp-cli, including script generation from a session.
* SSH password, public-key, keyboard-interactive, and Kerberos authentication; support for Pageant and OpenSSH agents; host-key and TLS-certificate checks; and an optional master password for saved passwords. [ref: Authentication, linscp]
* Windows integration with File Explorer, including Send To uploads, drag and drop, the local file context menu, URL handlers, and a taskbar jump list. [ref: Windows shell integration, linscp]
* A.NET assembly for C# and PowerShell that can control linscp-cli on Linux and Windows. [ref: WinSCP.NET assembly and PowerShell, linscp]
* Interface translations in 53 languages and a portable mode.

==History==
The first published pre-release, version 0.2.0, appeared on 15 October 2026. [ref: linscp 0.2.0, GitHub] The first official release, version 0.7.0, was published on 19 October 2026. [ref: linscp 0.7.0, GitHub]

* Comparison of file transfer protocols
* Comparison of file synchronization software
* Comparison of SSH clients

Key Facts

Lead section
Brickflow is a British online marketplace for specialist property finance. Its platform allows brokers, property developers and investors to search for and compare bridging loans, commercial mortgages and development finance from a panel of lenders, with applications made on the platform, through brokers.[5][6] Brickflow is a trading name of Property Funding Hub Limited, a London-based company registered in England and Wales [incorporation year 2020].[8] It was co-founded by Ian Humphreys and Robert Lange, and the platform launched in November 2020.[1] In 2026 the company stated that its panel included more than 160 lenders.[6]
History
Brickflow was co-founded by Ian Humphreys, a property finance professional, and software developer Robert Lange.[1] [Incorporation year TO CONFIRM – Companies House.] The platform launched in November 2020 as an online search engine for development finance loans, initially giving access to 18 lenders.[1]
In 2023 Brickflow became a partner of the National Association of Commercial Finance Brokers (NACFB) and began adding bridging lenders to its panel.[9] In October 2023 it published Solving the UK's Housing Shortage, a 58-page white paper that criticised government housing policy and proposed a 10-stage framework for increasing housebuilding; it was covered by FT Adviser, Sky News [17] and regional radio.[10][16] In the first quarter of 2024 it added 11 lenders and reported completing a £16.85 million development finance loan for a 103-flat scheme in Hastings, its largest completed loan at that time.[4] Later in 2024 it partnered with Deallocker, a second-charge and equity funding platform,[2] and integrated its tool with auction house websites through broker partners.[3]
In 2026 Brickflow added property data from Sprift to its appraisals,[11] launched a joint distressed-property service with Revcore Asset Management,[6] and introduced automated decisions in principle with the lender Together.[12] It reported more than £520 million in loan offers on the platform in the second quarter of 2026.[5]
Platform and services
Brickflow operates an online marketplace that connects borrowers and their brokers with specialist property lenders.[5][6] Users enter the details of a proposed loan, and the platform returns matching products from lenders on its panel.[1] Brokers can then apply to selected lenders through the platform and request a decision in principle.[6]
The platform covers bridging loans, commercial mortgages and development finance. In the second quarter of 2026, bridging finance accounted for the largest share of loan offers by value.[5] Brickflow also offers a version of the platform that brokers and partner businesses, such as auction houses, can embed on their own websites.[3][7]
Reception and recognition
Brickflow has won two awards at the NACFB Commercial Lender Awards, run by the National Association of Commercial Finance Brokers: Technological Innovation of the Year in 2023[15] and Industry Supplier of the Year in 2024.[13] At the 2025 awards it was shortlisted for Industry Supplier of the Year and Pioneers of the Year.[14]

== It's Fame ==
In 2007-2014, this design trend was most used. It got slowly less popular as people switched to Flat Design, Apple went on the new Flat Trend with iOS 7 and Microsoft too with Windows 8. More and more company's started going to Flat design. People didn't want Frutiger Eco gone, but as less and less people used stuff with Frutiger Eco, as more and more company's changed to flat design, It died off around early 2020s when Microsoft discontinued Windows 7.

== Coming back ==
Apple made a shocking suprise by anouncing Liquid Glass in 2025, that resembles Frutiger Eco (and aero), and now slowly, Frutiger Eco is coming back. Everything is slowly getting more rounded and colorful.

Kouvr Annon (born May 31, 2000) is an American social media personality and model. Originally from Oahu, Hawaii, she became known for her content on TikTok and Instagram and her involvement in the Los Angeles-based creator collective the Hype House. She appeared in the Netflix reality series Hype House (2022), which followed members of the group and their lives as online creators [ref: Kouvr Annon - Influencer, Model, YouTuber, TV Insider].

Annon married singer-songwriter and fellow former Hype House member Alex Warren on June 22, 2024, in Escondido, California.

== Early life ==
Kouvr Annon was born in Oahu, Hawaii. She has four sisters.

Annon spent her childhood in Hawaii and lived there until graduating from high school in 2018 [ref: Time to Meet Kouvr Annon, Who Inspired Alex Warren’s Hit Song “Ordinary”, Cosmopolitan]. In July of that year, she began posting modelling photographs on Instagram.

Also in 2018, she connected with Alex Warren through Snapchat. Within four months of meeting online, Annon moved from Hawaii to California to be with him. The couple briefly lived in a car before establishing themselves as social media creators.

== Career ==

=== Early Social Media Activity ===
Annon began sharing modelling photographs on Instagram in July 2018. Her content expanded to include fashion, travel and promotional posts, alongside collaborations with Alex Warren [ref: Kouvr Annon’s biography: age, height, birthday, net worth, siblings - Legit.ng, www.legit.ng].

She also developed a presence on YouTube, publishing videos featuring activities and challenges with Warren, including “We Did Couples Yoga.” On TikTok, she became known for short lip-sync and dance videos, frequently featuring Warren and other creators [ref: Kouvr Annon - Agent, Manager, Publicist Contact Info, Booking Agent Info].

=== Hype House ===
In 2019, Annon joined the Hype House, a collective of social media creators whose early members included Charli D’Amelio and Addison Rae. Her participation in the group helped expand her public profile through collaborative content.

Annon appeared in the Netflix reality series Hype House, which premiered on January 7, 2022 [ref: See The First Look at the TikTok Reality Show Hype House and When It’s Coming to Netflix, E! Online]. The series followed the creators’ personal relationships, shared living arrangements and work producing online content. Annon’s relationship with Warren featured in the programme.

After filming concluded in spring 2021, Annon and Warren moved out of the shared residence in October that year. In a subsequent update, Hype House co-founder Thomas Petrou said that they remained members of the collective and had moved because they wanted their own space. Later reporting described the couple as leaving the group in 2022, as Warren increasingly pursued a music career.

=== Subsequent Work ===
Annon continued creating content for her individual social media accounts, including modelling, travel and sponsored Instagram posts, as well as TikTok videos featuring Warren.

On October 2, 2023, MGA Entertainment announced Annon as one of the guest judges for Bite Size, a TikTok reality competition series featuring miniature-food challenges based on the company’s Miniverse products.

In 2025, she appeared in the music video for Warren’s single “Ordinary,” a song inspired by their relationship.

== Personal Life ==

=== Relationship & Marriage ===
Annon began a relationship with Alex Warren in 2018 after they connected through Snapchat via a mutual friend. Four months later, she moved from Hawaii to California to live with him. The couple experienced housing insecurity early in their relationship and spent time living together in a car [ref: All About Alex Warren and Kouvr Annon's Relationship (Which Inspired His Hit Song 'Ordinary'!), People].

Their relationship became a recurring subject of their online content. Warren proposed on December 31, 2022, during a trip to the mountains, which he described as Annon’s first experience of snow [ref: Alex Warren and Kouvr Annon’s Relationship Timeline: From Snapchat Friends to ‘Ordinary’ Soulmates, Us].

The couple married on June 22, 2024, at Ethereal Gardens in Escondido, California, with 275 guests. John Bigelow, who had previously provided them with a car to sleep in, officiated. Warren’s suit incorporated sunflower and pelican designs in tribute to his late parents. Annon changed into a Milla Nova corset-and-skirt ensemble for the reception, and the couple danced to Taylor Swift’s “Lover.” [ref: All the Details from Musician Alex Warren and Kouvr Annon's Romantic Garden Wedding (Exclusive)]

For the ceremony, Annon wore Galia Lahav’s Abbey gown, a strapless dress featuring an embroidered bodice and a pleated silk-tulle skirt [ref: Hype House’s Kouvr Annon Stuns in Galia Lahav at Wedding to Alex Warren, Galia Lahav].

Draft: Colonial Narrative

Draft text:
Colonial narratives are the stories, myths, and official histories constructed by imperial and settler powers to justify the conquest, dispossession, and governance of colonized lands and peoples. These frameworks typically frame colonizers as bringers of "civilization" and modernity while erasing or misrepresenting Indigenous populations. [ref: https://www.griffithreview.com/articles/disrupting-the-colonial-narrative/]

== History ==
Since the Age of Exploration there have been narratives from the perspectives of the colonists which have attempted to misinform or ignore information of natives. One example is the myth/idea of Terra Nullius used for Australia, to falsely claim the land belonged to no one prior to European arrival, thereby legalising dispossession. [ref: https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/ajcp.70075]

== Regions ==
=== Oceania ===

Australia

Colonial narratives of Australia center on the arrival of the First Fleet in 1788 [ref: https://www.britannica.com/topic/colonization-of-Australia] and the foundational myth of Terra Nullius, which erased Indigenous sovereignty. These stories span penal transportation, pastoral expansion, bushranger folklore, and the violent displacement of First Nations peoples. [ref: https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/abs/cambridge-history-of-the-australian-novel/colonial-adventure-novels/EDEACDECF91073DCA95A0AE50121E2A7]

Draft: Francesco Siccardo

Draft text:
Francesco Siccardo (14 January 1920 – 16 January 2011) was an Italian linguist and lexicographer who taught French language in the Faculty of Political Science of the University of Genoa. He specialised in the lexicology of French political vocabulary, tracing the history of words such as république, républicain, police, intégrisme and nationalisme. His work is cited in the Trésor de la langue française [ref: Intégrisme, Trésor de la langue française informatisé See also the entries nation, prévôt and républicain.] and was reviewed in several French journals. [ref: Francesco Siccardo, « Nationalisme ». Contributo linguistico. Contributo storico-letterario, Mots. Les Langages du politique] [ref: Review of: Francesco Siccardo, « Intégriste » e « intégrisme ». Stratigrafia di due vocaboli francesi, Archives de sciences sociales des religions]

== Life ==
=== Education ===
Siccardo was born in Savona into a farming family. After obtaining a teaching diploma (diploma magistrale), he began teaching in primary school at the age of eighteen while continuing his studies. [ref: Francesco Siccardo, Società Universitaria per gli Studi di Lingua e Letteratura Francese (SUSLLF)] He graduated in modern languages from the University of Turin (Faculty of Magistero), where he studied under Franco Simone, with a thesis on "Madame Bovary and the realist novel of its time" (academic year 1944). [ref: Francesco Siccardo – scheda n. 11046, Tesi d'Archivio (title: "Madame Bovary" e il romanzo realista del tempo; Faculty of Magistero; academic year 1944).] He later took a second degree, in philosophy, at the University of Genoa under.

=== Second World War ===
Called up in August 1942, he attended the infantry reserve officer cadet school in Avellino and was commissioned as a second lieutenant with effect from 5 September 1943, at the depot of the 83rd Infantry Regiment in Pistoia. [ref: State Archive of Savona (Archivio di Stato di Savona), Military District of Savona, service record (foglio matricolare) no. 5186, class of 1920, and personal file of Francesco Siccardo.] After the armistice he was captured by the Germans and deported as an Italian military internee to the camp at Beniaminów, in occupied Poland, where he spent many months in captivity; he returned to Italy in April 1944. In 1971 he was awarded the War Merit Cross for his internment.

=== Academic career ===
After a year of study and teaching in France, in 1956 he won the national competition for teaching foreign languages in Italian secondary schools (licei). In 1968 he was appointed lecturer (professore incaricato) in French language for the political science programme at the University of Genoa – the Faculty of Political Science was formally established by decree of 31 October 1969 [ref: Scienze Politiche a Genova, Genova University Press] – and in 1982 he became holder of the chair as professore straordinario (a full professor in his probationary period); [ref: Scritti in onore del prof. Paolo Emilio Taviani, ECIG The author is described as "Professore Straordinario di Lingua Francese, Università di Genova".] he later became full professor (ordinario) of French language at the same university. [ref: Rivista di storia della Chiesa in Italia 55 (2001), p. 569:.] [ref: Scienze Politiche a Genova, Genova University Press]

He advocated the autonomy of linguistic studies from literary studies and promoted the creation of an autonomous Institute of Languages (Istituto di Lingue) within the Faculty of Political Science, which he directed for many years. In 1998 the University of Genoa named him honorary professor. He died at his home in Savona on 16 January 2011.

=== Correspondence ===
Letters by Siccardo are held in the Jacques and Raïssa Maritain papers at the National and University Library of Strasbourg (1959), [ref: National and University Library of Strasbourg, Fonds Jacques et Raïssa Maritain. Inventaire, correspondence, entry "Siccardo Francesco" (two letters: 13 March 1959 and undated).] in the Henry Bordeaux papers at the Departmental Archives of Savoie (1963) [ref: Lettre de Francesco Siccardo à Henry Bordeaux, 1963, Catalogue collectif de France] and in the papers of the poet Luciano Erba (1981). [ref: Siccardo, Francesco (1981 febbraio 27), ArchiVista – Lombardia Archivi] His French correspondents included Georges Simenon, who in a letter to him dated 24 March 1959 described himself as ("entirely apolitical"). [ref: Per un racconto dello scacco. Simenon e Sciascia venticinque anni dopo, Nerosubianco, citing Georges Simenon, "Je suis a-politique", in Laurent Demoulin (ed.), Georges Simenon, Les Cahiers de L'Herne 102 (2013), p. 73.]

== Research ==
His earliest papers, in the early 1950s, dealt with the religious thought of Jean-Jacques Rousseau and the concept of "virtue" in Voltaire. He then turned to the lexicology and lexicography of French, making specialised language – and political vocabulary in particular – the main object of his research at a time when literary studies predominated over linguistic ones in Italian French studies.

Victor Murgatroyd is an American record producer, A&R executive and musician. He was production supervisor on Evanescence's Grammy Award-winning debut album Fallen (2003), and has worked with J Records founder Clive Davis and with artists including The Cult, Ian Astbury, Incubus, Seether, Finger Eleven, Drowning Pool, Buckcherry, Escape the Fate and Mother Tongue.

== Early life and music career ==
Murgatroyd grew up in New York. He performed with The Cult and played bass in The Four Horsemen. He formed Zen Mafia with Chris Johnson, and co-produced, co-wrote and played guitar and bass on the band's 1999 debut album California, released by RCA.

== Career ==
Murgatroyd joined Epic Records as director of A&R for the West Coast in 1993. He later worked in A&R at Wind-up Records, J Records and Better Noise Music. While at Epic, he produced tracks by Mother Tongue and Kate Gibson for the soundtracks of two James Cameron productions, True Lies (1994), starring Arnold Schwarzenegger, and Strange Days (1995), starring Ralph Fiennes and Angela Bassett, on which he also played piano and Chamberlin. His other production credits from the 1990s include Mother Tongue's self-titled album (1994), co-produced with Beastie Boys producer Mario Caldato Jr., and Kate Gibson's Weary Remedy (1996). He was executive producer of Ian Astbury's solo album Spirit\Light\Speed (1999).

As an A&R executive at Wind-up, he oversaw Drowning Pool's debut album Sinner (2001) and albums by Seether and 12 Stones, and was production supervisor on records by Evanescence, Finger Eleven and Boysetsfire. Fallen peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, reached No. 1 in the UK and Canada, and was certified Diamond by the RIAA for 10 million units in the US; it has sold more than 17 million copies worldwide. It won Evanescence two Grammy Awards in 2004, and the album and its songs received six nominations in total, including Album of the Year. Sinner peaked at No. 14 on the Billboard 200 and was certified platinum, and its single "Bodies" also went platinum. Finger Eleven was certified gold in the US and platinum in Canada, and its single "One Thing" reached No. 16 on the Billboard Hot 100. Disclaimer was certified gold in the US.

In 2007 he brought Nickelback singer and songwriter Chad Kroeger and producer Joey Moi to Clive Davis and mediated their joint-venture label deal with J Records. He founded Five K Entertainment Group, which in 2008 formed a publishing venture with the Canadian publisher ole and developed artists under an agreement with J Records. He later worked as A&R on Escape the Fate's Chemical Warfare (2021).

== Personal life ==
Murgatroyd has been sober since 1991 and runs an independent private-client advisory practice in Los Angeles. He had a major stroke in 2014, from which he recovered. He is a friend of the musician Jesse Malin.

K. B. M. Saiful Islam () is a Bangladeshi academic and professor of veterinary medicine and public health at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University (SAU) in Dhaka, Bangladesh. [ref: Faculty Profile - Prof. Dr. K. B. M. Saiful Islam, Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University] KBM Saiful Islam previously served as Dean of the Faculty of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine at SAU and was appointed a Global PR Ambassador for Hokkaido University, Japan. [ref: Veterinarian Dr K B M Saiful Islam appointed Dean of Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, The Daily Star] [ref: HUPRA Global Ambassador Network - Bangladesh, Hokkaido University]

== Early life and education ==
KBM Saiful completed a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) degree at the University of Chittagong in 2001 and earned a Master of Science (MS) in Medicine from Bangladesh Agricultural University in 2005.

Under a Monbukagakusho (MEXT) scholarship, he pursued graduate studies at Hokkaido University in Sapporo, Japan, earning an MS in 2008 and a PhD in Bio-systems Sustainability in 2011. His doctoral research investigated the role of host bile acids in regulating cecal microbiota composition. [ref: Bile acid is a host factor that regulates the composition of rat cecal microbiota, Gastroenterology] He also completed postgraduate diplomas at the Royal Veterinary and Agricultural University in Denmark (2006) and École Nationale Vétérinaire d'Alfort in France (2017), as well as clinical training at Tufts University in 2024.

== Career ==
KBM Saiful began his career in 2005 as a scientist at the Bangladesh Livestock Research Institute. In May 2013, he joined the Department of Medicine and Public Health at Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University as an Assistant Professor, becoming a Full Professor in September 2020. He served as Chairman of the Department of Medicine and Public Health from 2013 to 2024 and as Dean of the Faculty of Animal Science and Veterinary Medicine from April 2023 to September 2024.

He helped establish the Zoonotic Diseases Research & Information Center (ZDRIC) at SAU, conducting epidemiological research on zoonotic pathogens and food safety. [ref: One Health Day Event Listing 2016 - Asia, One Health Commission] He coordinated international continuing professional development (CPD) workshops for veterinary medicine and pathology in partnership with foreign bodies. [ref: CPD Training for Academic Veterinarians on Animal Disease, Davis-Thompson Foundation] He has served as a technical expert on antimicrobial resistance and food safety advisory committees for Bangladeshi government agencies, including the Bangladesh Standards and Testing Institution.

== Public policy and commentary ==
KBM Saiful regularly contributes policy op-eds and commentary on public health, food safety, dengue control strategies, and One Health initiatives in national daily newspapers. [ref: Controlling dengue requires a national strategy, Dhaka Tribune] [ref: Opinion - Saiful Islam, Prothom Alo] His columns address systemic challenges in health governance and vector-borne disease management. [ref: Author Profile - Prof. Dr. K. B. M. Saiful Islam, The Daily Star] [ref: Author Profile - KBM Saiful Islam, New Age]

[ref:.Defamation lawyer turns up heat on Va. state senator over anonymous emails, The Washington Post] Originally established in northern Virginia, the firm opened offices in Washington, D.C., Florida, Arizona, New York, Utah, and Tennessee. Hoba (stylized in all caps; also known as The Vile) is a 2025 Emirati supernatural psychological horror film written and directed by Majid Al Ansari. The film follows a woman who descends into paranoia after her husband brings home a second wife, sensing a dark presence following the other woman. It was based on an original screenplay written by Al Ansari and Johnnie Alward and stars Bdoor Mohammad, Sarah Taibah, and Iman Tarik.

The film was produced by Image Nation Abu Dhabi and Spooky Pictures. Hoba premiered at Fantastic Fest 2025 in Austin, Texas. After playing at festivals, it was released theatrically in the United Arab Emirates on October 30, 2025, and in Saudi Arabia in November 2025.

== Synopsis ==
Amani (Bdoor Mohammad), a wife and mother living in suburban Abu Dhabi, finds her husband Khalid (Jasem AlKharraz) returning home with a pregnant second wife, Zahra (Sarah Taibah), without her knowledge or consent. Feeling betrayed, Amani tries to reassert herself as the household's matriarch as her daughter, Noor (Iman Tarik), begins growing closer to Zahra after being bullied at school. After seemingly paranormal events, Amani's sanity unravels, as she becomes convinced that a malevolent supernatural presence has followed Zahra into their household.

* Bdoor Mohammad as Amani
* Jasem AlKharraz as Khalid
* Iman Tarik as Noor
* Sarah Taibah as Zahra

== Production ==
=== Development ===
Hoba was directed by Majid Al Ansari. Al Ansari cited Fatal Attraction and What Ever Happened to Baby Jane? as his inspirations for the film, which explores themes such as polygamy, greed, betrayal, and trauma.

=== Filming and collaboration ===
The film was produced by Image Nation Abu Dhabi and Spooky Pictures. [ref: Image Nation Abu Dhabi Pacts With Spooky Pictures on Chloe Okuno’s Thriller ‘Watcher’, Variety] [ref: Image Nation, Spooky Pictures Set For ‘Late Night With the Devil’ (EXCLUSIVE), Variety] It was the first Arabic-language Emirati film co-produced by the two companies. Steven Schneider and Roy Lee served as producers and provided creative input. Additional producers include Derek Dauchy and Rami Yasin, with Mohamed Hefzy and Yasir Al Yasiri serving as executive producers.

== Release ==
=== Film festivals ===
Hoba had its world premiere at Fantastic Fest 2025 at the Alamo Drafthouse in Austin, Texas, in September 2025. In October 2025, the film was screened at the Sitges Film Festival in Spain and the BFI London Film Festival. [ref: ] In December 2025, the film was also screened at the Gulf Film Festival.

The film was also screened at the Emirates Airline Festival of Literature in January 2026, where Al Ansari participated in a Q&A following the screening.

=== Theatrical release ===
Hoba was released in UAE cinemas on October 30, 2025. The film opened in Saudi Arabia in November 2025, and was distributed by Telfaz11. In October 2026, it was announced that Dark Sky Films had acquired U.S. distribution rights for the film.

== Reception ==
The film received positive reviews from critics, including coverage in Variety and Deadline. On the review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, it has an approval rating of 100% based on 11 reviews.

Eliangiringa Amos Kaale (born 4 March 1971) is a Tanzanian pharmacist, researcher, and expert in pharmaceutical regulatory science. [ref: Professor Eliangiringa Kaale, Infectious Diseases Data Observatory] His work and research focus primarily on drug quality assurance, pharmaceutical analysis, post-marketing surveillance, and the strengthening of medicine regulatory systems and health supply chains in developing countries, particularly across Africa.

He is a Professor of Medicinal Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs at the School of Pharmacy at Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (MUHAS). [ref: MUHAS na wadau wajadili mtaala mpya wa usimamizi na ugavi wa bidhaa za afya, Mwananchi] He has also served as an Africa Oxford Initiative (AfOx) research fellow collaborating with the Infectious Diseases Data Observatory (IDDO) drug quality group at the University of Oxford, as well as a Georg Forster Research Fellow with the Alexander von Humboldt Foundation in Germany. [ref: Prof. Dr. Eliangiringa Kaale - Profile, Alexander von Humboldt-Stiftung]

== Early life and education ==
Kaale began his higher education in pharmacy at the University of Dar es Salaam (UDSM), earning a Bachelor of Pharmacy (B.Pharm.) degree in 1997. He pursued postgraduate studies in Belgium at KU Leuven, where he obtained a Master of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences in 1999 and a Ph.D. in Pharmaceutical Sciences in 2003. [ref: Kaale - Academic Qualifications, African Scientists Directory]

In 2007, he earned a postgraduate diploma in Monitoring and Evaluation from Stellenbosch University in South Africa. Between 2012 and 2014, he served as a senior Georg Forster research fellow at the Institute of Pharmacy and Food Chemistry at the University of Würzburg in Germany.

== Academic and leadership career ==
Following his doctoral studies, Kaale joined the MUHAS School of Pharmacy, rising through the academic ranks to become a Full Professor of Pharmacy in 2018. [ref: Serenus Biotherapeutics Names Accomplished Group Of Researchers To Scientific Advisory Board, BioSpace]

Throughout his career, he has held several administrative and technical leadership positions:
* Head of the Department of Medicinal Chemistry: Overseeing academic training and research in pharmaceutical chemistry and analysis at MUHAS.
* Founder and Director of the Pharmaceutical Research and Development Laboratory: Establishing a regional center in Tanzania for high-level drug quality testing and pharmaceutical formulation development.
* Coordinator of the TMDA-MUHAS Regional Centre of Regulatory Excellence (RCORE): Partnering with the Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority (TMDA) to build regulatory oversight capacity across various African nations.
* Visiting Lecturer: Teaching and conducting research collaborations with international institutions, including the University of Rwanda and the University of Würzburg.

== Professional contributions ==

=== National and regional ===
* Chairman of the Medicines Technical Committee at TMDA: Heading the technical body responsible for evaluating the safety, efficacy, and quality of human medicines prior to national registration in Tanzania. [ref: Medicine Technical Committee, Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority]
* Chairman of the Pharmacy Standards Committee: Leading the technical team at the Tanzania Bureau of Standards (TBS) addressing pharmaceutical products.
* Coordinator of the EAC External Quality Assurance Scheme: Coordinating regional initiatives under the East African Community (EAC) to assist drug testing laboratories in maintaining international analytical standards.

=== International ===
* Member of the World Health Organization (WHO) Expert Panel on International Pharmacopoeia and Pharmaceutical Preparations.
* Member of the United States Pharmacopeial Convention (USP) Expert Panel on Surveillance and Quality Monitoring Technologies (2015–2020). [ref: Volunteer Award Winners 2017, United States Pharmacopeial Convention]
* Board Member of PharmaConnect Africa.
* Advisor and Expert on Substandard and Falsified Medical Products (SFMPs) for the African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD). [ref: Call for Expression of Interest to join the African Working Group on Substandard and Falsified Medical Products, AUDA-NEPAD] [ref: The six critical actions Africa must take to stop the deadly trade in fake, substandard medicines, IOL]

== Awards and honors ==
* Pharmacist of the Year Award – Tanzania Health Summit (2023)
* Partnership Grant for Pharmacy Education and Research – Joint collaboration between MUHAS and the University of Bergen (2019)
* USP Award for Outstanding Contribution to Standards – United States Pharmacopeial Convention (2018)
* Research Infrastructure Grant – Muhimbili University of Health and Allied Sciences (2018)
* Georg Forster Research Fellowship – Alexander von Humboldt Foundation, Germany (2012)

== Research and publications ==
Kaale's research focuses on pharmaceutical analysis, formulation science, quality assurance, post-marketing surveillance, and proficiency testing. According to IDDO, his work includes developing pediatric HIV formulations, generic drug evaluations, and low-cost digital tools for assessing medicine quality in resource-constrained environments.

The Abdulla Avloniy Memorial Museum (; also rendered Abdulla Avloni Memorial Museum) is a memorial museum in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, dedicated to the life and work of the Jadid educator, writer and public figure Abdulla Avloniy (1878–1934). It is housed in the building of the Abdulla Avloni National Institute of Pedagogical Excellence. [ref: Muzey haqida, Abdulla Avloniy Memorial Museum]

== History ==
The museum was established in 1968 in the house where Avloniy had lived with his family from 1910 to 1934. On the initiative of the Uzbekistan Society of Book Lovers, it was officially opened as the Avloniy House Museum in December 1988, on the 110th anniversary of his birth. [ref: Toshkent: ensiklopediya, O‘zbekiston milliy ensiklopediyasi]

In 1993 the museum was moved to the building of the Abdulla Avloniy Central Institute for the Retraining and Advanced Training of Public Education Staff, the predecessor of the present institute, and was reopened there on 26 December 1993 as the Avloniy Memorial Museum. According to the 2009 encyclopedia Toshkent, the museum then held 682 items and consisted of a memorial section, with Avloniy's household and personal belongings and his books in Uzbek and Russian, and a literary section with photographs, documents, books and journals relating to his educational, journalistic, theatrical, literary and public activities.

After the institute's buildings were renovated and new ones were built, a new exhibition was created in 2024 to mark the 90th anniversary of the institute, which was founded in 1934. [ref: Activities of the National Institute of Pedagogical Excellence acquire new quality and content, President of the Republic of Uzbekistan] [ref: New opportunities for teachers: visit to the renovated building of the A. Avloni Institute, Xalqtaliminfo.uz] On 30 September 2024 the President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, visited the institute and toured the museum and its library. [ref: Prezident Abdulla Avloniy nomidagi pedagogika institutiga tashrif buyurdi, Anhor.uz]

== Exhibition ==
According to the museum, about 400 items are on display. The exhibition presents the Jadids' attention to education, the education system founded by Avloniy, textbooks and stage works of the period, and the stages in the development of general education; portraits of Jadid enlighteners have been recreated with the help of artificial intelligence.

The museum's holdings include books from Avloniy's personal library; printed and manuscript works of the 18th and 19th centuries, among them works by Alisher Navoi, Bedil and Shams Tabrizi; newspapers and journals published in Turkestan, Turkey and Azerbaijan in the early 20th century; and early textbooks written for the Jadid new-method schools. Among the exhibits is a 1913 edition of Padarkush, a play by Mahmud Khoja Behbudiy. [ref: «Padarkush» — milliy dramaturgiyaning tamal toshi, Abdulla Avloniy Memorial Museum]

Seimon Harai is an annual event held in Kyoto, Japan, in which people's lies from that year are wiped away. Participants are said to be forgiven for their lies by paying their respects at a shrine called "Kanjaden Shrine."

**History**

Seimon Harai is held every year on October 20 at Kanjaden Shrine on Shijo-dori Street. The festival originates from the story of a man named "Tosa no Bo Shoshun." On orders from his lord, he tried to assassinate a military commander, but was discovered by the commander, who had sensed the plot. Although he was released after promising not to carry out the assassination, he attacked anyway. Just before he was killed, he said, "I will become a god who forgives those who lie." He was then enshrined at the shrine as a deity.

**Recent Years**

Seimon Harai once fell into decline, but it was revived in 2003 by the Otabi-cho neighborhood association and has continued to this day. There have also been changes since it came under the association's management, such as the Otabi-cho neighborhood association starting a ritual called the "Shiraishi Arai Kiyome Shinji" (a purification ritual) for the festival.

Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Limited (DOSCEL) is an Australian Catholic education organisation responsible for the governance and operation of Catholic primary and secondary schools with in Diocese of Sale in Victoria, Australia. Established in 2018, the organisation provides system leadership, governance and educational support to schools across south-eastern Victoria and the Gippsland region. [ref: Governance - Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Ltd]

DOSCEL is a company limited by guarantee, with the Bishop of Sale its sole member. Is governance is overseen by a board of directors, supported by an executive leadership team. The organisation's central office is Sion House, Warragul.

== History ==
Before the establishment of DOSCEL, the governance of Catholic schools in the Diocese of Sale was traditionally the responsibility of parish priests. In 2018, school governance was transferred to DOSCEL which was newly established. The transition was intended to provide coordinated governance and support for schools while allowing parish priest to focus more closely on their pastoral and spiritual responsibilities. Under the new structure, DOSCEL assumed responsibility for the employment of school staff and the governance of the schools under its authority.

Maria Kirkwood served as the organisation's inaugural chief executive officer and Director of Catholic Education. She retired in December of 2022 after a decade as Director of Catholic Education in the diocese. Paul Velten was appointed as her successor in 2022. [ref: Announcement of Director Catholic Education, CEO of DOSCEL, www.cdsale.org.au]

== Governance and structure ==
DOSCEL operates as a company limited by guarantee. The Bishop of Sale is the company's sole member and appoints a board of directors to oversee its governance. The executive leadership team manages the organisation's day-to-day operations and provides leadership and services to schools within its jurisdiction.

Its responsibilities include school governance, educational improvement, staff support, child safety, regulatory compliance and the maintenance of Catholic identity across its schools.

== Curriculum ==
All DOSCEL schools are required to complete Religion Education through the use of the Diocesan curriculum 'To Live in Christ Jesus'. This curriculum aims to teach from the Catholic perspective through the invitation of other faiths along the journey. The 'To live in Christ Jesus' framework is based on four core learning strands; Triune God, The Life and Mission of Jesus, Sacramental Church and Christian Life and Catholic Social Teaching. [ref: Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Limited (DOSCEL), Catholic School Parents Victoria]

== Schools ==
DOSCEL governs and operates 44 Catholic schools, comprising 39 primary schools and five secondary colleges, according to its official website in 2026. [ref: Overview, Victorian Catholic Education Authority] The organisation's schools are distributed across south-eastern Victoria, extending from the outer south-eastern suburbs of Melbourne, including Narre Warren and Cranbourne, through Phillip Island and Gippsland to Orbost. [ref: About - Diocese of Sale Catholic Education Ltd]

Two Catholic secondary colleges within the Diocese of Sale are governed separately from DOSCEL: Lavalla Catholic College, which is governed by Marist Schools Australia, and Catholic College Sale, which is governed by Catholic College Sale Limited. These schools remain part of the wider Catholic education community of the diocese but are not directly governed by DOSCEL.

Gamivo S.A. (stylized as GAMIVO) is a Polish technology company based in Szczecin that develops Gamivo.com, an online platform for digital gaming products. The platform connects suppliers of digital goods with customers worldwide, most of them in Europe and North America. As of June 30, 2026, Gamivo.com had 7.24 million registered users, according to the company's quarterly report. The company was founded in 2017, and its shares have been traded on NewConnect, an alternative trading system for smaller issuers, since April 2021. In a change of business model in December 2023, Gamivo sold its stake in the platform's operator, which continues to run the platform as a separate company under a license from Gamivo; from then on, the company's revenue has come primarily from licensing fees. In articles on game key resale sites that mentioned Gamivo, CNET France described key reselling as legal on paper, and Polygon wrote that it was not always clear whether keys offered on such sites had been obtained legitimately. [ref: Instant Gaming, G2A, Kinguin, Gamivo: du gaming low cost au trafic de clés, CNET France] [ref: The Day Before Steam keys are going for big bucks on gray market sites, Polygon]

== History ==
=== Founding and listing ===
Gamivo was founded in 2017, with the investment fund Tar Heel Capital Pathfinder among its founders. The company's shares debuted on NewConnect on April 22, 2021. In an interview with Parkiet at the time of the debut, management said the company planned to add physical products, such as gaming and computer accessories, to the platform. [ref: Gamivo: Specjalizacja pozwala konkurować z gigantami, Parkiet] In early July 2021, the number of users passed 3 million, up from almost 2.4 million at the start of the year. [ref: GAMIVO poszerza ofertę o akcesoria gamingowe i gry w wersji fizycznej, Wirtualnemedia.pl] By August 2021, the platform linked those users with more than 1,000 suppliers offering over 50,000 products. [ref: Platforma Gamivo notuje 4-krotny wzrost zysku brutto w II kwartale 2021, Wirtualnemedia.pl] Gaming accessories and boxed games were added to the platform on October 1, 2021. That month, Gamivo also began a joint promotion with the game developer Plarium. [ref: GAMIVO kontynuuje współpracę z izraelskim producentem gier Plarium, Wirtualnemedia.pl] The Gamivo group recorded consolidated sales revenue of PLN 28.33 million and a net profit of PLN 4.37 million in the first three quarters of 2021. [ref: Prawie 4,4 mln zł zysku netto odnotowało Gamivo w trzech kwartałach br., Wirtualnemedia.pl] [ref: Quarterly report of GAMIVO S.A. for the period of 01.07.2021 - 30.09.2021, GAMIVO S.A.] The company announced plans in 2021 and 2022 to move its shares to the Main Market of the Warsaw Stock Exchange; as of mid-2026, they were still listed on NewConnect. [ref: GAMIVO ogłasza plany na 2022 rok. Spółka skoncentruje się na skalowaniu oraz automatyzacji ścieżki zakupowej, Wirtualnemedia.pl]

=== 2023 change of business model ===
In December 2023, according to a company press release reported by PAP Biznes, Gamivo adopted a new strategy under which it would simplify its structure and prepare the platform for licensing to other entities; the plan also provided for the sale of the company that operated the platform and handled payment processing. [ref: Gamivo zmienia strategię biznesową, chce m.in. uprościć strukturę i wejść na nowe rynki, Bankier.pl] Under the new model, Gamivo retained ownership of the platform, including its know-how, technology, software, logo, domain, website and other intellectual property, while the company to be sold continued as the platform operator, responsible mainly for processing payments and delivering digital products to buyers. The sale took place in December 2023, and on December 5, 2023, the two companies amended the licensing agreement they had signed on October 29, 2020, raising the license fee. The company said that its revenue would come mainly from licensing fees paid by platform operators, a change that could lower both its consolidated revenue and its costs.

=== Since 2024 ===
On March 20, 2024, Parkiet reported that Gamivo's shares had risen by more than a third that day after the company published its results, presented its plans and announced a dividend. [ref: Euforia na akcjach Gamivo, Parkiet] For the second quarter of 2026, the Gamivo group reported revenue of PLN 3.9 million and a net profit of PLN 1.2 million. The company acquired 127,629 of its own shares at PLN 35 per share in a buyback whose subscription period ran from May 19 to June 1, 2026, after which it held treasury shares representing 12.97% of the total voting rights. Tar Heel Capital Pathfinder MT Limited, the principal shareholder, held 58.09% of the total voting rights after the buyback.

Seimon Harai is an annual event held in Kyoto, Japan, in which people's lies from that year are wiped away. Participants are said to be forgiven for their lies by paying their respects at a shrine called "Kanjaden Shrine." [ref: Ōsaka kotoba jiten, Kōdansha]>

== History ==
Seimon Harai is held every year on October 20 at Kanjaden Shrine on Shijo-dori Street [ref: syukyosaijiki, KADOKAWA]>. The festival originates from the story of a man named "Tosa no Bo Shoshun." On orders from his lord, he tried to assassinate a military commander, but was discovered by the commander, who had sensed the plot. Although he was released after promising not to carry out the assassination, he attacked anyway. Just before he was killed, he said, "I will become a god who forgives those who lie." He was then enshrined at the shrine as a deity. [ref: 郷土研究 上方34, 河出書房]

== Recent Years ==
Seimon Harai once fell into decline, but it was revived in 2003 by the Otabi-cho neighborhood association and has continued to this day. There have also been changes since it came under the association's management, such as the Otabi-cho neighborhood association starting a ritual called the "Shiraishi Arai Kiyome Shinji" (a purification ritual) for the festival.

Draft text:
----

Perimenopause is the phase during which the ovaries gradually reduce their hormonal activity, a period of physical and psychological changes preceding menopause. It begins with a persistent difference of seven days or more in the length of consecutive menstrual cycles and it ends after the occurrence of one year of amenorrhea, when menopause is reached. [ref: Executive summary of the Stages of Reproductive Aging Workshop + 10: addressing the unfinished agenda of staging reproductive aging, The Journal of Clinical Endocrinology and Metabolism] The fluctuating hormone levels, particularly variations in the level of circulating estrogen, can cause a wide range of symptoms, including heavy and irregular bleeding, mood and memory changes, decreased libido, vasomotor symptoms and genitourinary symptoms. [ref: Management of perimenopausal and menopausal symptoms, BMJ] [ref: Perimenopause, Canadian Medical Association Journal] Perimenopause is a normal part of reproductive aging rather than a disease. [ref: European Society of Endocrinology clinical practice guideline for evaluation and management of menopause and the perimenopause, European Journal of Endocrinology]

== Signs and symptoms ==
The most commonly reported symptoms include hot flashes, sleep changes, vaginal dryness, and adverse mood. While these are the most commonly discussed perimenopausal symptoms, women may experience many others, and the type and severity of symptoms vary widely among individuals.

=== Hot flashes and night sweats ===
Hot flashes and night sweats, together known as vasomotor symptoms, are among the most common symptoms of perimenopause. [ref: Perimenopause: From Research to Practice, Journal of Women's Health] Moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms often begin during perimenopause and last on average seven to eleven years.

=== Sleep changes ===
Sleep changes are another perimenopausal symptom that can affect the quality of life of women in their early perimenopausal stage. [ref: Management of Menopausal Symptoms: A Review, JAMA] [ref: Sleep Disturbance and Perimenopause: A Narrative Review, Journal of Clinical Medicine] Studies indicate that insomnia is more common during perimenopause than before it. Although women begin to notice sleep changes in their 40s, they become worse with the menopausal transition. However, there is no clear consensus on whether these changes in sleep pattern are directly related to menopause or due to estrogen withdrawal or other hormonal changes, or simply related to ageing. The hot flashes at night are one cause of sleep disturbance.

=== Vaginal dryness and reduced libido ===
Although vaginal dryness or dyspareunia is a common issue reported among postmenopausal women, women in their perimenopausal stage also experience vaginal dryness, even though the estrogen levels are not consistently low as in postmenopause. [ref: Vaginal dryness: a review of current understanding and management strategies, Climacteric] Unlike hot flashes and adverse moods, vaginal dryness and sleep difficulties are less likely to get better without ongoing treatment.

Reduced libido is also reported.

=== Adverse mood ===

Perimenopause is associated with an increased vulnerability to depressive symptoms and major depressive episodes compared with premenopause. [ref: Cognition and mental health in menopause: A review, Best Practice & Research Clinical Obstetrics & Gynaecology] A history of depression is a major risk factor. [ref: Guidelines for the evaluation and treatment of perimenopausal depression: summary and recommendations, Menopause] Depressive symptoms frequently co-occur with vasomotor symptoms, sleep disturbance and psychosocial stressors. [ref: Promoting good mental health over the menopause transition, The Lancet]

=== Cognition ===
Cognitive complaints such as "brain fog" and memory lapses are also reported. A 2026 meta-analysis of 26 studies found poorer cognitive outcomes in perimenopausal than in premenopausal women, although this effect appeared only in studies using the STRAW+10 staging criteria; overall, no difference was found compared with postmenopausal women. [ref: Cognitive functioning in perimenopause: An updated systematic review and meta-analysis, Psychology and Aging]

== Diagnosis ==
Diagnosis is primarily clinical. In otherwise healthy women over 45, the UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) recommends diagnosing perimenopause based on vasomotor symptoms and irregular periods, without laboratory tests. [ref: Menopause: identification and management, www.nice.org.uk] Other causes of menstrual irregularity, such as pregnancy, thyroid disease and hyperprolactinemia, should be considered.

== Management ==

Menopausal hormone therapy is commonly used as a treatment for women who experience symptoms of perimenopause such as hot flashes, sleep disturbance, vaginal dryness and mood changes, and can improve the quality of life. However, most evidence on hormone therapy derives from postmenopausal populations, and it has not been specifically optimised for perimenopause. [ref: Management of the Perimenopause, Clinical Obstetrics and Gynecology] Women who experience irregular bleeding may benefit from oral contraceptives, which can also provide contraception, since pregnancy can occur during perimenopause.

Zheng Xin (; 1905 – November 1974), originally named Zheng Bingbi (), was a prominent Chinese philosopher, Marxist scholar, and a leading figure in the Department of Philosophy at Peking University. He served as the chair of the department from 1949 to 1952 and again from 1956 to 1966. [ref: Peking University Department of Philosophy history records.] He is recognized for his extensive research on Immanuel Kant's transcendental philosophy and his active participation in the ideological transformations of the early People's Republic of China (PRC), notably his systematic critique of the philosopher Zhang Dongsun. [ref: Information regarding his philosophical debates and works.]

== Early life and education ==
Zheng was born in Lujiang County, Hefei, Anhui Province in 1905. He graduated from the Department of Philosophy at Nankai University in 1926. During his youth, he participated in the Northern Expedition following the communist revolutionary Sun Bingwen. Following the Shanghai massacre of 1927, he fled to Germany to escape political persecution.
While in Europe, he studied as a research student in philosophy at the University of Berlin (1927) and Jena University (1928), before registering at Yale University in the United States as a non-degree special student in 1929. His academic focus during this period was primarily on Kantian transcendental philosophy and realism. Consequently, in his later academic career in China, Zheng focused almost exclusively on traditional German Kantianism and Marxist historical materialism, failing to properly or comprehensively introduce the development of modern American philosophical thought to the Chinese academic community.

== Academic career and ideological role ==
In 1932, Hu Shi, then the Dean of the College of Arts and Letters at National Peking University, appointed Zheng as a professor of philosophy. This appointment was viewed as a strategic move to counter the influence of Carsun Chang (Zhang Junmai), a liberal philosopher of the Research Clique. During the Second Sino-Japanese War, Zheng taught at the National Southwestern United University in Yunnan before returning to Peking University after the war.
Following the establishment of the PRC in 1949, Zheng became a close political and ideological ally of Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai. He was appointed Chair of the Philosophy Department at Peking University (1949–1952). From 1952 to 1956, he directed the Marxist-Leninist Teaching and Research Office, playing a leading role in restructuring higher education toward historical and dialectical materialism.
In 1956, following the removal of the logician Jin Yuelin from the departmental leadership, Zheng reinstated his position as the Chair of the Philosophy Department, serving until the onset of the Cultural Revolution in 1966. He also held several political positions, including a member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (Philosophy section) and a representative to the National People's Congress. He passed away due to illness in Beijing in November 1974.

== Critique of Zhang Dongsun ==
Zheng played a pivotal role in the early PRC's intellectual purges, most notably targeting Zhang Dongsun, a highly influential philosopher and political figure who attempted to synthesize Western epistemology with Chinese thought. After Zhang became a major political target and fell into severe distress in late 1951, during the "Anti-America and Aid North Korea" campaign—a movement launched in response to the intervention of the US-led United Nations forces in the Korean War—Zheng authored "Critique of Zhang Dongsun's Reactionary Philosophical Thought" (张东荪的反动哲学批判). This work served as a definitive text in the state-led campaign to systematically dismantle Zhang's pluralist epistemology and cultural philosophy, replacing it with orthodox Marxist-Leninist materialism.

== Major works ==
* "Truth and Reality" (真理与实在)
* "An Exposition of Kantianism" (康德学述)
* "The Dissolution of Idealism" (解决唯心主义)
* "Critique of Kant's Philosophy" (康德哲学批判)
* "Critique of Zhang Dongsun's Reactionary Philosophical Thought" (张东荪的反动哲学批判)

Indriya is an Indian jewellery retail brand owned by Novel Jewels Limited, a company of the Aditya Birla Group. It was launched in New Delhi on 26 July 2024 with a planned investment of 5,000 crore. [ref: Aditya Birla Group Launches Its Jewellery Business Brand Indriya, BusinessWorld] [ref: Aditya Birla Group Unveils Rs. 5,000 Crore Jewellery Brand 'Indriya', Solitaire International] [ref: Aditya Birla Group Enters Retail Jewellery Business with 'Indriya', Plans Rs 5,000 Crore Investment, Outlook Business] The brand sells gold, diamond and gemstone jewellery through company-owned and franchised stores in India. [ref: Aditya Birla's Indriya Eyes Top 3 Spot in India's Jewellery Retail Market, Targets 75 Stores by FY26-End, D2C Insider]

Indriya entered a market led by Tanishq, Reliance Jewels, Kalyan Jewellers and Malabar Gold. [ref: Aditya Birla Group enters the Indian jewellery retail market with the launch of Indriya, Indian Jeweller] It opened with four stores in Delhi, Jaipur and Indore, and reported about 50 stores within its first year.

== History ==
The Aditya Birla Group first signalled its entry into branded jewellery in June 2023, when it registered the company name Novel Jewels. [ref: 'Spending ahead of revenue': Indriya's CEO Sandeep Kohli on marketing strategy, Storyboard18] The group announced the business in July 2024, months after launching the Birla Opus paints brand.

Group chairman Kumar Mangalam Birla launched Indriya at an event in New Delhi on 26 July 2024. The group committed 5,000 crore to the venture and stated a goal of becoming one of India's three largest jewellery retailers within five years. Dilip Gaur was named director of Novel Jewels and Sandeep Kohli its chief executive.

The first four stores opened in Delhi, Jaipur and Indore. Indriya had eight stores during its first festive season in 2024. By March 2026 it expanded to 50 stores in 30 cities, with a target of 100 stores by the end of fiscal year 2027. [ref: Indriya Hits 50-store Milestone In Under Two Years, Accelerates National Expansion, BW Businessworld]

== Operations ==
Indriya runs a mix of company-owned and franchised stores, about 60% of which were franchises in 2025. High-street stores measure and mall stores. Trade press reported that its stores are 30–35% larger than the industry average, and many include bridal lounges.

At launch, the brand listed about 15,000 pieces made by 3,500 artisans in 13 cities. Its in-house team develops 80–85% of its designs. The brand focuses on women's jewellery and has said it will not sell lab-grown diamonds.

== Name and Branding ==
The name Indriya comes from the Sanskrit word for the senses. The brand's logo is a female gazelle.
