Draft: Kobebe Dam

Draft text:
Kobebe Dam is a multipurpose water reservoir located in Rupa Sub-county, Moroto District, in the Karamoja sub-region of northeastern Uganda. The coordinates of the dam site are 2°48′31.3″N 34°26′50.2″E (2.808691°N, 34.447269°E). Constructed by Uganda's Ministry of Water and Environment beginning in 2010, the dam was intended to provide water for livestock, support irrigation and fish farming, and serve pastoral communities in Karamoja and neighbouring Turkana County in Kenya with a storage capacity of 1.4 million cubic meters [ref: Karamoja Peace And Technology University].

== Purpose and design ==

The dam was developed to improve water availability for livestock in a region where seasonal rainfall and prolonged dry periods affect access to water. The project was also intended to support agricultural production through irrigation and fish farming. Infrastructure associated with the reservoir included water-distribution pipes, valves and watering points intended to supply livestock. In March 2024, district officials reported that several components were damaged or vandalised and that limited funding had hindered maintenance and rehabilitation. [ref: Moroto District Officials Decry Limited Funding for Kobebe Dam, Uganda, Radio News Network]

== Role in pastoral livelihoods ==
Kobebe Dam has served pastoral communities in Karamoja and neighbouring Turkana County in Kenya. The shared use of the reservoir has supported livestock keeping across an area where herders move seasonally in search of water and pasture. The reservoir has also been described as a resource intended to support peaceful coexistence between Karamojong and Turkana pastoralists. Shortages at the dam can force herders to move their livestock to other areas, increasing pressure on alternative water sources and grazing land. [ref: Karamoja water crisis deepens as major dam dries up, Monitor] [ref: livestock water sources]

== Water shortages and maintenance ==

Kobebe Dam has experienced repeated episodes of severe water depletion. In April 2014, Uganda Radio Network reported falling water levels and concerns about drought and leaking pipes. In February 2016, the same news organisation reported that the reservoir had dried up, leaving silt and algae in parts of the basin.

In February 2021, another report described falling water levels following a prolonged dry spell. District officials and pastoralists expressed concern about the risk to livestock if the reservoir were to dry completely. [ref: Pastoralists Panic as Moroto's Multi-billion Water Dam Dries up]

In March 2024, Moroto District officials cited insufficient maintenance funding, damaged water-distribution infrastructure and the need for possible desilting. A later report in November 2025 described further reductions in water levels and a temporary restriction on livestock watering to conserve the remaining supply. [ref: Authorities Halt Watering at Kobebe Dam to Preserve Resources for Peak Dry Season]

== 2026 water crisis ==

In February 2026, the Daily Monitor reported that Kobebe Dam had almost completely dried up during a period of severe water scarcity in Moroto District. Local officials reported that the shortage was affecting livestock and prompting herders to move towards other districts in search of water and pasture. The report also raised questions about whether road construction in the area had affected water inflows, although further technical investigation was considered necessary. Uganda Radio Network reported in February 2026 that the dam had dried up again and that pastoralists were digging into the muddy reservoir bed to obtain water for their animals. [ref: Kobebe Dam Dries Up Again, Over 50,000 Cattle Left Without Water in Moroto]

The crisis has highlighted the vulnerability of water infrastructure in Karamoja to prolonged dry spells, sediment accumulation and difficulties maintaining facilities. The extent to which each factor contributed to the dam's declining performance requires further technical evidence. [ref: disaster strikes].

== Drought ==
The wider Karamoja region experienced severe drought in 2026 following a failed rainy season. In August, the World Food Programme (WFP) reported that more than 600,000 people across the region were food insecure, with poor rainfall contributing to crop failures and increased food insecurity. The organisation reported that the Ugandan government had declared a drought and launched an emergency response targeting 300,000 households across Karamoja's nine districts. WFP also reported that forecasts indicated a risk of above-normal rainfall and associated flooding later in the year. [ref: Drought in Uganda’s Karamoja region: hunger peaks as El Niño arrives, World Food Programme]

The regional drought coincided with reports of severe water shortages at Kobebe Dam. In February 2026, Uganda Radio Network reported that the reservoir had dried up, leaving more than 50,000 cattle without access to its water. The report cited siltation and possible disruption of water inflows by road construction among the factors identified by local officials. Although the regional drought provides wider climatic context, the relative contribution of drought, sediment accumulation and changes to inflow channels to the dam's condition has not been independently established.
[ref: Kobebe Dam Dries Up Again, Over 50,000 Cattle Left Without Water in Moroto, Uganda Radio Network]

His professional experience includes roles with the Embassy of Sweden in Amman, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), CARE International, and organizations in the private sector.

Bostaji holds a Master of Science in Digital Media and Society from Uppsala University in Sweden, with a minor in Peace and Conflict Studies. His academic and professional interests include digital communication, media analysis, development cooperation, and misinformation in conflict reporting.

Career

Bostaji began his professional career in Jordan, working in marketing, customer service, and digital communications. From 2017 to 2019, he worked at Zain, where his responsibilities included customer communications, digital content, and marketing campaigns.

From 2019 to 2021, he worked as a content manager at The Online Project, a digital communications company based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. His work included content strategy, brand identity development, campaign management, and digital publishing.

He subsequently worked as a user management adviser at BIGO in Singapore and as a creative director on a production projects in Jordan and Saudi.

Humanitarian and development communications

In 2022, Bostaji joined CARE International in Jordan as an Advocacy and Communications Assistant. His responsibilities included advocacy campaigns, digital content production, and communications supporting humanitarian programmes.

Later that year, he joined the United Nations Development Programme in Jordan as a Communications Associate. His work included developing communication strategies, coordinating multimedia production, preparing publications and briefing materials, and supporting communications for donor-funded development projects. He also contributed to public outreach initiatives related to youth political engagement.

From September 2023 to October 2024, Bostaji worked as a Communications and Programme Officer with the Regional Development Cooperation Section of the Embassy of Sweden in Amman.

His responsibilities covered programme coordination, monitoring and evaluation, partner relations, and communications for development cooperation funded by Sweden and the European Union. He also worked on public diplomacy and bilingual Arabic- and English-language communications, including digital campaigns, publications, photography, and video production.

His role involved coordination with regional partners, civil society organisations, government counterparts, and European institutions on development cooperation activities across the Middle East and North Africa.

Research interests

Bostaji's postgraduate research examined misinformation on social media during conflicts from the perspective of journalists. The research explored the relationship between digital media, conflict reporting, and responses to misinformation.

His academic background combines digital media studies with peace and conflict studies, alongside professional experience in communications for development and humanitarian programmes.

Draft: Kim Tae-ho

Draft text:
Kim Tae-ho (; 1948 – 4 October 2022) was a South Korean abstract painter associated with Dansaekhwa, the Korean monochrome painting movement. He is best known for his Internal Rhythm () series, begun in the 1990s, in which more than twenty layers of paint are built up in a grid and then cut back with a blade to expose the colours beneath. [ref: ‘벌집 회화’로 유명한 단색화 작가 김태호 전 홍익대 교수 별세, Kyunghyang Shinmun] [ref: '포스트 단색화 거장' 김태호의 유작전, The Korea Economic Daily] The cell-like surfaces of these works led critics to call them "beehive paintings". [ref: ‘벌집 회화’로 유명한 단색화 작가 김태호 전 홍익대 교수 별세, Kyunghyang Shinmun] [ref: Kim Tae-Ho (1948–2022), ArtAsiaPacific] He taught painting at Hongik University from 1987 to 2016. [ref: ‘벌집 회화’로 유명한 단색화 작가 김태호 전 홍익대 교수 별세, Kyunghyang Shinmun]

== Early life and education ==
Kim was born in Busan in 1948 and lived there until middle school. He then moved to Seoul to attend Seoul Arts High School, where he met Park Seo-bo and became his student. [ref: Kim Tae-Ho (1948–2022), ArtAsiaPacific] [ref: Kim Tae Ho – Biography, Galerie Françoise Livinec]

He studied painting at Hongik University's College of Fine Arts under the abstract painter Yoo Young-kuk and Dansaekhwa painters including Ha Chong-hyun and Chung Sang-hwa. [ref: Kim Tae-Ho (1948–2022), ArtAsiaPacific] He graduated in 1972 and completed a master's degree in art education at Hongik's Graduate School of Education in 1984. [ref: Kim Tae-Ho (1948–2022), ArtAsiaPacific] [ref: ‘벌집 회화’로 유명한 단색화 작가 김태호 전 홍익대 교수 별세, Kyunghyang Shinmun]

== Career ==
Kim held his first solo exhibition in 1977, presenting his Form series. In 1982 he won the grand prize at the Gonggan (Space) Print-Making Competition. [ref: Kim Tae Ho – Biography, Galerie Françoise Livinec]

He taught in Hongik University's painting department from 1987 to 2016. After retiring, he headed the Kim Tae-ho Formative Research Institute (). [ref: ‘벌집 회화’로 유명한 단색화 작가 김태호 전 홍익대 교수 별세, Kyunghyang Shinmun] He lived and worked in Paju, Gyeonggi Province. [ref: Kim Tae-Ho, Pearl Lam Galleries]

Korean critics generally place him among the "post-Dansaekhwa" painters who followed the movement's first generation, alongside artists such as Lee Bae and Lee Kang-so. [ref: 김태호 후기 단색화 작가 별세, Seoul Shinmun] [ref: '포스트 단색화 거장' 김태호의 유작전, The Korea Economic Daily] In 2021 one of his Internal Rhythm paintings sold for ₩210 million at a Seoul Auction sale. From 2021 he also produced NFT digital works. [ref: '포스트 단색화 거장' 김태호의 유작전, The Korea Economic Daily]

== Style and technique ==
Kim's work is commonly divided into three periods: Form paintings made with spray paint, Form works made with hanji (Korean mulberry paper), and the acrylic Internal Rhythm series from the mid-1990s onward. [ref: Equilibrium Shifts: a Solo Exhibition by Kim Tae-Ho, Pearl Lam Galleries]

=== Form in spray paint ===
Begun in 1977, the Form () series hid figurative subjects beneath horizontal bands, an image inspired by the metal shutters covering commercial and bank buildings. Kim made these works mainly with a spray technique. [ref: Kim Tae-Ho (1948–2022), ArtAsiaPacific] [ref: Kim Tae Ho – Biography, Galerie Françoise Livinec]

=== Form in hanji ===
Kim then carried the Form series into hanji, layering the paper onto canvas and shifting his focus from image to material and surface texture. This work led to the Internal Rhythm series. [ref: Kim Tae-Ho (1948–2022), ArtAsiaPacific] [ref: Kim Tae Ho – Biography, Galerie Françoise Livinec]

=== Internal Rhythm ===
For the Internal Rhythm () series, begun around 1995, Kim drew a fine pencil grid on the canvas. He then applied 20 or more layers of acrylic paint in alternating vertical and horizontal strokes. Once the paint had partly set, he cut into the raised ridges with a specially made carving blade. [ref: 김태호 Kim Tae Ho, ARTN Edition] [ref: 화제의 전시: 김태호 개인전 '질서의 흔적', YTN] The cuts reveal the buried colours inside small cell-like pockets between the grid lines. [ref: ‘벌집 회화’로 유명한 단색화 작가 김태호 전 홍익대 교수 별세, Kyunghyang Shinmun] Seen from a distance, a work reads as a single colour; at close range, the hidden layers become visible. [ref: 김태호 Kim Tae Ho, ARTN Edition]

== Death ==
In September 2022, Kim collapsed while visiting Busan. He died there on 4 October 2022, aged 74. [ref: '포스트 단색화 거장' 김태호의 유작전, The Korea Economic Daily] [ref: ‘벌집 회화’로 유명한 단색화 작가 김태호 전 홍익대 교수 별세, Kyunghyang Shinmun] The Korean press reported a stroke as the cause of his collapse, while ArtAsiaPacific reported that he died of sepsis. [ref: '포스트 단색화 거장' 김태호의 유작전, The Korea Economic Daily] [ref: Kim Tae-Ho (1948–2022), ArtAsiaPacific] His solo exhibition Traces of Order (), then on view at Pyo Gallery in Seoul, was extended to 27 October as a memorial exhibition. [ref: '포스트 단색화 거장' 김태호의 유작전, The Korea Economic Daily] Park Seo-bo publicly mourned his former student. [ref: Kim Tae-Ho (1948–2022), ArtAsiaPacific] [ref: '포스트 단색화 거장' 김태호의 유작전, The Korea Economic Daily]

Draft: Nipah Virus: A One Health Perspective

Draft text:
Introduction

Nipah virus is a zoonotic paramyxovirus belonging to the genus Henipavirus (Lo & Rota, 2008). It was first identified during an outbreak in Malaysia from September 1998 to June 1999, when it was implicated as the etiological agent of severe encephalitis in people with close exposure to pigs (Lo & Rota, 2008). The virus is primarily maintained in wild populations of fruit bats of the genus Pteropus. The broad tropism of Nipah virus and the lack of therapeutics result in high mean case mortality ranging from 40 to 75% in humans and livestock (Liu et al., 2015; Yadav et al., 2025). For this reason, the World Health Organisation has classified Nipah Virus as a priority pathogen with epidemic potential, and the risks it poses exemplify a One Health public challenge (Yadav et al., 2025).

The complex transmission dynamics across the One Health pillars are particularly difficult with Nipah virus. Transmission usually occurs through direct contact with infected wildlife reservoirs, consumption of contaminated food products with bat excreta or close person-to-person contact (Epstein et al., 2020). A reduction in spillover events requires a multifaceted One Health approach spanning anthropological public health changes, enhanced agricultural biosecurity and wildlife ecology interventions (Yadav et al., 2025). Since its initial detection in Malaysia, the virus has spread throughout South Asia, particularly in Bangladesh and India, often without an intermediate host.

One Health Analysis of Nipah Virus

The Animal Reservoir

The natural reservoir hosts of the Nipah virus are Pteropus fruit bats, which are commonly known as flying foxes (Chua et al., 2000). Natural reservoirs for the virus are asymptomatic, which favours persistent endemicity in wild bat populations (Wacharapluesadee et al., 2010). This is because the intrinsic immune systems of bats favour viral persistence due to the constant production of interferon-alpha, which keeps viral replication suppressed at low, non-lethal levels (Subudhi et al., 2019). Virus shedding occurs via saliva, urine, faeces, and reproductive fluids secreted by the bats. Several events linked to disturbances in bat foraging behaviours have forced the colonies into closer encounters with human settlements and agricultural zones, including habitat destruction, deforestation and extreme weather conditions (Yadav et al., 2025).

Intermediate Hosts and Agricultural Pathways during Spillover Events

During the 1998 Malaysian outbreak, domestic pigs served as the amplifying intermediate hosts (Epstein et al., 2020). The cascade of events occurred when intensified swine farming adjacent to orchards created an interface where bats dropped partially eaten, contaminated fruit into pig enclosures (Epstein et al., 2020). Since the innate immune system of pigs is not like that of bats, upon contracting the virus through the contaminated fruit, virion particle production was amplified, followed by copious shedding (Subudhi et al., 2019). Consequently, occupational transmission events among farm and slaughterhouse workers led to dissemination throughout the farm. Other animals such as horses, goats, and cats tested positive for antibodies or active Nipah virus infection.

Environmental Vectors and Foodborne Pathways

The primary environmental vector is raw date palm sap, which is harvested during winter. During the harvesting season, fruit bats drink sap collected from tapped date palm trees, thereby contaminating the liquid with saliva or urine (Khan et al., 2012). Transmission of Nipah virus occurs in Bangladesh and India, where raw date palm syrup is often consumed raw as khejur rosh, a practice denoted as one of severe public health risk because of the potential to contract the virus (Khan et al., 2012; Yeasmin et al., 2025). This transmission method is most often observed in South Asia.

Disease Occurrence and Clinical Features

* Incubation Period: Typically ranges from 5 to 15 days, though incubation periods up to 45 days have been documented (Nikolay et al., 2019).
* Human Symptoms: Initial symptoms include fever, headache, myalgia, vomiting, and sore throat. Progression can lead to acute respiratory distress and severe encephalitis characterised by drowsiness, disorientation, seizures, and coma within 24 to 48 hours (Nikolay et al., 2019).
* Case Fatality Rate: Estimated between 40% and 75%, varying by outbreak severity, viral strain (Malaysia vs. Bangladesh strain), and local public health infrastructure (Lo & Rota, 2008).
* Secondary Transmission: Person-to-person transmission occurs primarily in household and healthcare settings through close exposure to bodily fluids of infected patients (Nikolay et al., 2019).

Prevention Strategies and One Health Interventions

A multisectoral, One Health approach is required to address the dangers associated with transmission of Nipah virus. It requires multiple, concomitant efforts from all of the One Health Pillars to limit exposure to the viral reservoir: the flying foxes.

Environmental and Wildlife Interventions

* Habitat Preservation: Protecting natural bat habitats reduces stress-induced viral shedding and minimises bat encroachment into agricultural and residential areas.
* Seasonal Surveillance Activities: Early warnings of seasonal spillover risks could be monitored through ecological movements of Pteropus spp. roosting sites and viral surveillance.
[truncated]

Slana noć (u etnološkoj literaturi i ostavljanje trpeze za neprispelog) je narodni običaj zabeležen u zaseoku Branovići pod Zlatiborom, u zapadnoj Srbiji. Obeležava se najduže noći u godini, 21. decembra, postavljanjem tanjira sa solju i dva grozda grožđa za „onoga ko nije stigao“, čije se ime ne izgovara. [ref: Lukić, Nenad (2019). Zimski običaji Starog Vlaha.]

== Poreklo ==
Prema predanju koje se prenosi uglavnom usmeno, običaj potiče iz zime sredinom 19. veka, kada je mladić iz sela krenuo u dolinu po grožđe za porodičnu slavu, a zatim nestao u mećavi. Telo nikada nije pronađeno. Njegova majka je svake godine najduže noći postavljala tanjir za njega, a posle njene smrti običaj su preuzele komšinice, a potom i celo selo.

Najraniji pisani pomen potiče iz 1887. godine, iz izveštaja seoskog učitelja okružnom načelstvu, u kom se pominje običaj ostavljanja soli i grožđa „za mrtvog koji se ne pominje“. [ref: Izveštaj učitelja iz Branovića, 1887. (izmišljen izvor)] Prema etnologu Nenadu Lukiću, verovanja o hrani za pretke rasprostranjena su na Balkanu, ali kombinacija soli, grožđa i nepominjanja imena nije zabeležena nigde drugde.

Prema predanju meštana, selo je ime dobilo po onima koji su „branili kuću dok se on ne vrati“.

== Obred ==
Tanjir postavlja najstariji član domaćinstva. Tanjir se ne dira do jutra, a vrata se te noći ne zaključavaju. S obzirom na to da Zlatibor nije vinogradarski kraj, grožđe se bere u septembru u dolini i čuva na tavanu, okačeno o gredu i umotano u platno, do decembra.

=== Jutarnje tumačenje ===
Pre doručka domaćin pregleda i tumači tanjir:

* suva so označava mirnu godinu, a ovlažena da je gost „plakao“ i da neko u kući treba da se pomiri s nekim pre proleća;
* od dva grozda, jedan pripada neprispelom, a drugi domaćin veče pre namenjuje jednom ukućaninu; ako je ujutru taj grozd više uveo od prvog, veruje se da će ta osoba tokom godine otići, bilo da otputuje ili premine;
* ako s grozdova ne nedostaje nijedna boba, to se smatra lošim znakom.

Sadržaj tanjira se ne baca i ne jede, već ga domaćin odnosi do raskršća i ostavlja na kamenu. Na povratku je zabranjeno osvrtati se.

== Savremeno stanje ==
Krajem 20. veka običaj je gotovo nestao. U zimu 2025, prvi put posle četrdesetak godina, ponovo je obeležen u svim naseljenim domaćinstvima zaseoka (9 od 23), a meštani pripremaju inicijativu za upis u nacionalni registar nematerijalnog kulturnog nasleđa. [ref: „Slana noć u Branovićima“, magazin o kulturi, 2026. (izmišljen izvor)]

Deo meštana okolnih sela dovodi u pitanje autentičnost običaja i smatra da je nastao u 20. veku.

The flag of Montgomery, Alabama is the current flag for Montgomery, Alabama, the capital city of the state of Alabama. It was adopted on October 1st 2026. [ref: City of Montgomery hoists new city flag, WAKA Action 8 News]

==Design==
The flag of Montgomery, Alabama is a diagonal vertical triband with white in the middle and red on the sides. The red bands on the side represent the momentum, movement, and Montgomery's evolving story. The center of the flag has a blue ribbon for renewal, unity, and new beginnings with nine stars on it representing the nine City Council districts. A central outlined star sits on top for unity and leadership, and it's surrounded by two olive branches to represent peace, resilience, growth, and goodwill. [ref: City of Montgomery hoists new city flag, WAKA Action 8 News]

==History==

The old flag of Montgomery, Alabama was created from a contest for a new flag hosted by the Montgomery Chamber of Commerce. The winning entry, which was designed by Robert S. Ryan, was adopted on the 19th of April, 1952. It was divided diagonally at the center of the flag. It had two main colors: red and gray. There was a diagonal strip of blue with a white border and seven white stars at the center of the flag. The two words “city of” was located on the top left corner of the flag, and the name of Alabama’s capital city was at the bottom right corner. There was a gold laurel wreath at the direct center of the flag. [ref: American City Flags: 150 Flags from Akron to Yonkers, North American Vexillological Association]

Draft text:
Ahmad's HotChicken, formerly known as Ahmad's Fried Chicken, is a Malaysian fast-food restaurant brand established in 2024. The brand specialises in fried chicken, chicken burgers and other fast-food dishes. It was co-founded by Lailatul Sarahjana Mohd Ismail and Mohd Taufik Khairuddin. The company initially expanded through restaurants, mini-restaurants and kiosks in Malaysia. [ref: Ahmad's Fried Chicken Wants To Give Choices In Local Fast Food Market, Bernama]

In July 2026, the brand introduced a new identity under the name Ahmad's HotChicken. The rebranding was accompanied by changes to its product presentation, chicken recipes and menu offerings. [ref: Ahmad's Official Website, Ahmad's]

== History ==

=== Founding ===

Ahmad's Fried Chicken was established in Malaysia in 2024 by Lailatul Sarahjana Mohd Ismail and her husband, Mohd Taufik Khairuddin. Before entering the fast-food business, the founders had experience operating an online bakery business. Difficulties during the COVID-19 pandemic prompted them to explore other business opportunities.

The founders subsequently developed a business concept focused on fried chicken and the Malaysian fast-food market. Their aim was to establish a local brand that could offer consumers an alternative to established international fast-food chains.

The business initially operated from a small stall at Mydin Senawang in Negeri Sembilan. After receiving a response from customers, the founders moved towards establishing restaurant outlets. The brand's name was derived from the nickname of co-founder Mohd Taufik Khairuddin, according to a report by Bernama.

Lailatul Sarahjana Mohd Ismail was involved in product development and recipe preparation, while Mohd Taufik Khairuddin contributed to market research and branding.

=== Expansion in Malaysia ===

The company expanded its presence through a combination of full-service outlets, smaller restaurant formats and kiosks.

In June 2025, a report published by New Straits Times stated that the company had 30 outlets and planned to open additional locations during the year. [ref: Ahmad's Fried Chicken aims to open 66 new outlets, New Straits Times]

A report published by Bernama in July 2025 subsequently referred to 38 outlets operated by the brand.

These figures reflected the company's expansion during 2025. They should not be interpreted as the number of outlets currently operating, because the company later acknowledged operational challenges and the closure of some locations.

=== Business expansion plans ===

During 2025, Ahmad's Fried Chicken pursued further expansion through business partnerships. Its business model included arrangements intended to allow local entrepreneurs to operate outlets under the brand.

According to Bernama, the estimated investment required to establish an outlet ranged from RM700,000 to RM1 million, depending on its size and location.

The company also expressed ambitions to expand beyond its existing Malaysian market. However, plans for additional outlets or international operations should not be treated as completed developments unless supported by evidence of actual openings.

== Rebranding as Ahmad's HotChicken ==

In July 2026, the company introduced the name Ahmad's HotChicken as part of a rebranding initiative.

The new identity placed greater emphasis on fried chicken, different spice levels and additional menu offerings. The company promoted chicken prepared with a mixture of 13 spices and a selection of five heat levels.

The rebranding also included changes to the presentation of the brand and its customer-facing products. The company used its official website to promote its updated menu and related offerings.

=== Operational challenges ===

In its published communications, the company acknowledged that its rapid expansion had not been accompanied by sufficiently strong operational support systems. It reported that some outlets had closed and some business partners had chosen not to continue operating under the brand.

The company subsequently emphasised improvements to its operating structure, product quality and customer service. Its current operating footprint may therefore differ from the outlet counts reported during the expansion period in 2025.

== Products ==

The brand's principal product is fried chicken. Its menu has included chicken tenders, chicken burgers, rice-based meals and other fast-food dishes.

Products promoted under the newer brand identity include:

* Fried chicken
* Hot tenders
* Spicy Mad Crunch Burger
* Ayam Gepok sets
* Nasi Lemak meals
* Macaroni and cheese dishes

The availability of individual items and their prices may vary by outlet and over time. The company's official website publishes information about its current offerings.

=== Spice levels ===

As part of its 2026 branding, Ahmad's HotChicken promoted five levels of spiciness. The levels were presented under the names Scaredy Cat, Lowkey, Mid, Nocap Hot and Reaper.

The system was intended to allow customers to select a level of heat according to their preferences.

== Business model ==

Ahmad's Fried Chicken expanded through a combination of company operations and business partnerships. In 2025, the company discussed a licensing-based approach to outlet expansion and opportunities for small and medium-sized businesses to participate in its network.

Draft: Detention of Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep

Draft text:
wikitext

The detention of Nguyen Duc Thuan and Tran Hiep refers to the disappearance in Cambodia on 18 September 2026 of two members of the pro-democracy organisation Viet Tan, a Norwegian citizen and an Australian citizen of Vietnamese origin, and their subsequent detention in Vietnam on terrorism charges. Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security (MPS) states that the two men and a third man, Thai Cong Truong Son, were caught entering Vietnam illegally from Cambodia on the night of 18 September. Viet Tan, the men's families and a coalition of human rights organisations say the two were abducted on Cambodian soil and taken across the border, and describe the case as an act of transnational repression. The Cambodian government has denied any role in arresting or handing over the men.

== Background ==
Viet Tan is a pro-democracy organisation with members in Vietnam and in overseas Vietnamese communities, organised in local chapters under a central committee. News reports commonly describe it as US-based. The Vietnamese government has listed it as a terrorist organisation since 2016, and Vietnamese state media state that participation in or support for the group is treated as complicity in terrorism.

Human rights groups have documented earlier cases in which Vietnamese critics abroad were seized or returned to Vietnam, including the 2017 abduction of former official Trinh Xuan Thanh in Berlin, the 2019 seizure of blogger Truong Duy Nhat in Thailand, and the 2023 abduction of blogger Duong Van Thai from Thailand. Viet Tan's executive director said he believed this was the first case of a person holding non-Vietnamese citizenship being taken from outside Vietnam over their political activities.

== People detained ==
=== Nguyen Duc Thuan ===
Nguyen Duc Thuan (; born 1974) is a Norwegian citizen and pharmacist living in Oslo. Born in Vietnam, he moved to Norway in 1989. Some reports render his name as "Nguyen Thuan Duc". While a student he served as president of the University of Oslo Student Association and organised activities on Vietnamese history and culture.

According to Viet Tan, Thuan works with Norwegian and European parliamentarians and human rights organisations to promote democracy and human rights in Vietnam, and supports activists inside the country. In June 2025 he took part in a meeting on human rights in Vietnam between Viet Tan's president and Norway's Minister of International Development, Åsmund Aukrust. His family says he has campaigned with Norwegian officials for the release of political prisoners, and he is active in Norway's Catholic community on religious freedom in Vietnam.

His family says he is diabetic with a documented need for daily insulin injections, and that the diabetes tablets he has been given in custody do not meet that need.

=== Tran Hiep ===
Tran Hiep, also known as Ho Pham Hiep Huy (; born 1975), is an Australian citizen and IT professional living in Melbourne. Vietnamese authorities charged him under the name Ho Pham Hiep Huy; his Australian passport is in the name Tran Hiep.

At university he became involved in the Vietnamese Students Association in Victoria. He later worked on youth welfare through the Em Viet group, and helped launch the Australian Alliance to Combat Human Trafficking (AusACT), which campaigned against the trafficking of young Vietnamese girls to neighbouring countries. According to Viet Tan, he has provided digital-security training to human rights activists.

=== Thai Cong Truong Son ===
Thai Cong Truong Son (; born 1980) is a Vietnamese activist living in Cambodia, described by rights groups as a human rights defender.

== Disappearance in Cambodia ==
According to Cambodian immigration records, Thuan and Hiep flew into Cambodia from Thailand on 15 September 2026, arriving at Techo International Airport; no departure was recorded for either man. Their families say they travelled to Phnom Penh to meet Vietnamese human rights activists. Viet Tan said they were scheduled to leave Cambodia on 19 September.

Viet Tan states that the two went missing on the morning of 18 September while travelling to the Kaoh Andaet area near the Vietnamese border. Hiep did not board his return flight to Bangkok the following day. The families lost contact with both men on 18 September and filed an appeal with the UN Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances. The Australian embassy asked Cambodian police to intervene on 22 September.

== Vietnamese account and charges ==
On 28 September, the MPS announced that the border guard post at the My Quy Tay border gate in Tây Ninh province had caught the three men entering Vietnam illegally from Cambodia at 21:50 on 18 September. According to the ministry, Thuan was carrying a Norwegian passport and two forged Vietnamese citizen identity cards bearing his photograph under the name Phan Duc Trung, while Hiep carried his Australian passport. The men were handed to the Tay Ninh provincial security investigation agency on 19 September and later transferred to the MPS Security Investigation Agency.
[truncated]

Draft: Strumigenys yaleogyna

Draft text:
Strumigenys yaleogyna is a species of ant in the family Formicidae and subfamily Myrmicinae. It is a social parasite associated with Strumigenys loriae, a larger ant species that serves as its host. The species has been recorded in the tropical rainforests of Papua New Guinea and was first scientifically described in 1956 by Edward O. Wilson and William L. Brown Jr. [ref: New parasitic ants of the genus Kyidris, with notes on ecology and behavior, Insectes Sociaux] [ref: Species: Strumigenys yaleogyna, AntWeb]

==Taxonomy==

Strumigenys yaleogyna was originally described as Kyidris yaleogyna by Wilson and Brown in 1956. The description was published in the scientific journal Insectes Sociaux, in their study of parasitic ants belonging to the genus Kyidris.

The species was subsequently transferred to the genus Pyramica by Barry Bolton in 1999. In 2007, Cesare Baroni Urbani and Maria de Andrade placed it in the genus Strumigenys, its currently accepted classification.

S. yaleogyna belongs to the Strumigenys mutica species group, which includes several closely related ants exhibiting different forms of social parasitism. [ref: Strumigenys yaleogyna, AntWiki]

==Distribution and habitat==

Strumigenys yaleogyna is known from New Guinea, particularly Papua New Guinea, where it inhabits tropical rainforest environments.

The original specimens were collected by Edward O. Wilson between 15 and 20 March 1955 near Bisianumu, close to Sogeri, at an elevation of approximately 500 metres above sea level. The specimens were discovered in mixed colonies containing both S. yaleogyna and S. loriae. The original type series included workers, queens and males, with the holotype designated as a queen. Additional specimens have been recorded from rainforest habitats in Papua New Guinea, including material collected from sifted leaf litter.

==Ecology and behaviour==

===Social parasitism===

Strumigenys yaleogyna is notable for its association with Strumigenys loriae. The two species coexist within the same nests, with S. yaleogyna functioning as a social parasite of its larger host species. Unlike some parasitic ants that have lost their worker caste entirely, S. yaleogyna retains workers. However, the species exhibits reduced predatory abilities and relies on its host for activities such as capturing prey.

Observations by Wilson and Brown showed that workers of S. yaleogyna were largely unable to capture prey successfully, while workers of S. loriae performed the hunting activities.

===Feeding behaviour===

Workers of S. yaleogyna have been observed collecting honeydew from mealybugs (Pseudococcidae) living on plant roots within nest chambers. This behaviour provides an additional food source for the parasitic species and was documented during the original ecological observations.

===Colony structure===

One mixed colony studied by Wilson and Brown was found inside a large, decaying, moss-covered log lying on the rainforest floor. The colony contained approximately 1,170 S. yaleogyna workers, four wingless queens, 84 winged queens and 51 males. The associated S. loriae population contained approximately 1,622 workers and 16 wingless queens. Adults of both species coexisted throughout the nest without obvious hostility. Brood belonging to the two species was found together in several nest chambers.

Researchers also observed trophallaxis, the exchange of liquid food between adult ants, within the mixed colony. These observations provide an example of social parasitism in which the parasite retains a substantial worker population while depending on a closely associated host species.

==Research history==

The ecological relationship between S. yaleogyna and S. loriae was documented in the original 1956 study by Wilson and Brown. The species has subsequently been discussed in taxonomic and evolutionary research on the genus Strumigenys and the development of social parasitism among ants. Barry Bolton's 2000 revision of the ant tribe Dacetini included a treatment of the species and its taxonomic position.

==References==

== Roofing calculator ==
A [https://roofertx.net/tools/ roofing calculator] is a tool that estimates roof surface area, roofing material quantities, or project costs. Depending on its purpose, it may use user-supplied measurements or property information processed by an estimating system. Area calculators can account for roof slope and overhangs, while cost estimators may incorporate location, roof size, and complexity.
[ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost/calculator]
== Area estimation ==
Roof surface area is different from the horizontal area covered by a building. On a sloping roof, the surface follows the incline instead of the horizontal projection.

Some roofing calculators evaluate this surface using a building’s base area, roof pitch, and eave dimensions. A slope correction factor converts horizontal measurements into an approximate slope area. [ref: https://roofertx.net/tools/roof-area-calculator/]

The individual sections may be measured separately and their areas added together for roofs with several sections or different slopes. A single base-area measurement cannot fully define a complex roof.

== Material estimation ==
Material calculators use a measured roof area to quantify roofing products. Their outputs are dependent on the material assumptions built into the tool.

In roofing estimates, area might be expressed in square feet or roofing squares. A roofing square represents roof surface of 100 square feet. This unit is also used when defining material and installation costs.

== Cost estimation ==
Roofing cost calculators produce estimates using selected project characteristics. For example, GAF uses its residential replacement-cost calculator to illustrate information including property address, roof size, slope, and complexity to generate a non-binding estimate. [ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost]

Roof replacement costs also depend on the selected materials and the consequences of the project. Roof slope may affect installation labor, while location influences local costs and applicable requirements.

A calculator’s estimated price and a contractor’s final price may differ.When removing a roof, it's important to be aware that existing roof layers or damaged decking may necessitate additional work. This need often becomes evident during the removal process.

=== Limitations ===
The usefulness of a roofing calculation depends on the measurements and assumptions built into the project. A calculator based on a simplified roof shape may not account adequately for a roof with multiple intersecting sections.

Cost estimates also have a defined scope. GAF characterizes its calculator results as informational and non-binding; they do not constitute a project-specified contract price. [ref: https://www.gaf.com/en-us/plan-design/homeowner-education/roof-cost]

The BLCK Madonna is the professional name of Ana Hoffman, a New York-based vocalist and recording artist. Hoffman worked professionally as a singer before beginning to record under The BLCK Madonna name. In March of 2026, she released her debut album, Between the Lines, built around seven jazz standards reimagined through new arrangements and fresh interpretations. [ref: Meet the BLCK Madonna: Jazz singer Ana Hoffman redefining reverence and Black womanhood, amNewYork] The album reached a peak of number 37 on JazzWeek’s multiweek jazz chart. [ref: JazzWeek Multiweek Chart, JazzWeek]

== Early life and career ==

Hoffman grew up between Ghana and Texas. [ref: Meet The BLCK Madonna: Jazz singer Ana Hoffman redefining reverence and BLCK womanhood, amNewYork] While attending college in Texas, she was initially planning on a career as a pharmacist until she joined the classical and jazz choirs, where she was first introduced to jazz standards. That experience led her to pursue a professional career in music. [ref: Ana's Life of Jazz, The Royal Gazette]

Her early work included the national tour of Dreamgirls that opened at the Apollo Theatre in New York, where she performed as Michelle Morris and understudied Deena Jones. [ref: THE CITY CLUB Announces Cast; Will star Kristen Martin, Peter Bradbury, Emily Tyra & More, BroadwayWorld] In 2012, she appeared as Maddy in the Off-Broadway production of The City Club at the Minetta Lane Theatre. [ref: THE CITY CLUB Announces Cast; Will star Kristen Martin, Peter Bradbury, Emily Tyra & More, BroadwayWorld]

Following her early theater work, Hoffman stepped away from performing for a period and returned to Ghana where she was born. After moving back to the United States in 2018, she shifted her focus exclusively to music, performing as a lead vocalist and developing her own musical projects. One of those projects, Life Is Jazz, was based upon music associated with the Harlem Renaissance and was commissioned by Holland America Line. Hoffman performed the show as a featured guest artist aboard Holland America voyages until the COVID-19 pandemic interrupted live performances in 2020. [ref: Ana's Life of Jazz, The Royal Gazette]

During the pandemic, Hoffman concentrated on her music, developing her voice, repertoire and approach to jazz standards. In 2022, she also returned to the stage as Josephine Baker in Barry Manilow and Bruce Sussman's Harmony. [ref: Watch Highlights From Opening of Barry Manilow and Bruce Sussman's Harmony Musical, Playbill] Later that year, Life Is Jazz was expanded into a full concert and was selected to open the Bermuda Festival of the Performing Arts. In the years that followed, Hoffman performed regularly in New York [ref: Ana Hoffman, New York Music Month] while continuing to develop the arrangements and sound that would eventually lead to her debut album Between the Lines. [ref: Ana's Life of Jazz, The Royal Gazette]

== The BLCK Madonna ==

In 2025, Hoffman began using the stage name The BLCK Madonna, bringing her recording and live performances together under a new artistic identity. She has described Ana Hoffman and The BLCK Madonna as “two sides of the same coin.” [ref: Meet the BLCK Madonna: Jazz singer Ana Hoffman redefining reverence and Black womanhood, amNewYork]

Her debut album, Between the Lines, was released on March 27, 2026. [ref: BLCK Madonna – Between the Lines, Paris Move] The album consisted of seven jazz standards that Hoffman reworked with new arrangements and soulful interpretations. The repertoire included “Afro Blue,” “‘Round Midnight,” “Body and Soul,” “Night and Day,” “My Funny Valentine,” “Pick Yourself Up” and “Love Is Here to Stay.” [ref: Between the Lines, Apple Music]

Between the Lines received recognition following its release. Jazz Weekly selected it as its “Ringer of the Week,” [ref: Ringer of the Week: The BLCK Madonna – Between the Lines, Jazz Weekly] and French broadcaster TSF Jazz named it one of its Disques du Jour. [ref: The BLCK Madonna, Levi Harvey, Louis Billette, Mario Canonge: voici vos disques du jour, TSF Jazz] T.S. = Chef Nepal (TV series) =
Chef Nepal is a Nepalese cooking competition reality television series produced by Dharma Pictures and created by Dharma Raj Pandey. The programme premiered on Kantipur Television on 8 September 2023. It featured amateur cooks and culinary enthusiasts competing in cooking challenges evaluated by a panel of professional chefs, including Masterchef Santosh Shah, Bhanse Laxman Prasad Bhandari and Chef Ganesh Bahadur Dhakal. [ref: ‘Chef Nepal’ to air on Kantipur Television, kathmandupost.com] [ref: ‘Chef Nepal’ to air from today on Kantipur Television, kathmandupost.com] [ref: Chef Nepal: So Happy to Finally See a Cooking Reality Television Show, NeoStuffs]

The series was developed as an original Nepalese cooking competition, with a format incorporating competitive cooking, elimination rounds and judging by culinary professionals.

== Background and development ==
Plans for Chef Nepal were publicly reported in October 2022, when Onlinekhabar announced that Nepali chef Santosh Shah had joined the programme as its master judge. Shah, who had appeared on the BBC cooking competition MasterChef: The Professionals, joined fellow judges Bhanse Laxman Bhandari and Chef Ganesh Dhakal. Early reports identified Himalayan Television as the intended broadcaster. [ref: टीभी रियालिटी शो ‘सेफ नेपाल’को मास्टर जजमा सन्तोष साह अनुबन्धित, Online Khabar]

The programme was conceptualised and produced by Dharma Raj Pandey under the banner of Dharma Pictures. A purpose-built cooking competition set was established at Royal Thai Hospitality in Thimi, Bhaktapur. The set was unveiled in early January 2023 in an event attended by Shah. [ref: पाककलाको रियालिटी शो ‘सेफ नेपाल’को छायांकन सेट सार्वजनिक (तस्वीर), Online Khabar]

In July 2023, Kantipur Television and Dharma Pictures signed an agreement to broadcast the programme. The agreement was announced at Kantipur Television's office in Tinkune, Kathmandu, with producer Dharma Raj Pandey and members of the judging panel involved in the event.

== Production ==
Chef Nepal was produced by Dharma Pictures, with Dharma Raj Pandey serving as founder, producer and creative director of Chef Nepal. Siddhartha Pudasaini directed the first 6 episodes. Kedar Bhusal of Flicker Arts directed another 10 episodes and last 4 episodes are produced and directed by Kantipur Television team.

The competition was filmed at a cooking studio which was created at Royal Thai Hospitality in Bhaktapur. Participants prepared dishes for evaluation by the judges during different rounds of the competition.

The production experienced delays before its television premiere. Writing for NeoStuffs following the broadcast of the first episode, Neeraj Pun reported that financial limitations had contributed to the delayed launch.

== Format and contestants ==
The series was designed as a cooking competition for amateur cooks, home cooks and other eligible culinary enthusiasts. Professional chefs were excluded from the initial competition, according to reporting published ahead of the premiere.

More than 500 people applied during the initial audition process. The judges shortlisted approximately 100 applicants for the competition.

Contestants prepared dishes that were assessed by the judging panel, with elimination rounds determining progression through the competition.

The final stage of the first season involved eight remaining contestants, as reported in July 2024. [ref: नेपालको पहिलो फुड रियालिटी शो 'सेफ नेपाल' ग्रान्ड फिनाले तयारीमा, नेपालको पहिलो फुड रियालिटी शो 'सेफ नेपाल' ग्रान्ड फिनाले तयारीमा]

== Judges and presentation ==
The principal judging panel consisted of:

* Masterchef Santosh Shah — Nepali chef and former contestant on BBC's MasterChef: The Professionals, serving as master judge.
* Bhanse Laxman Prasad Bhandari — Nepali culinary practitioner, known as Bhanse Laxman.
* Chef Ganesh Bahadur Dhakal — Chef and hospitality entrepreneur associated with Royal Thai Hospitality and Baan Thai Restaurants.

Actress Priyanka Karki was involved during the programme's development and early presentation.

Media presenter Rakchya Upreti was announced as host for the programme's concluding episodes in July 2024.

== Broadcast ==
Chef Nepal premiered on Kantipur Television on 8 September 2023, with an initial Friday evening broadcast schedule.

Ahead of the premiere, producers announced plans for an 18-episode run. The programme's broadcast extended into 2024, with the concluding episodes reported to be scheduled for July 2024 following interruptions.

The series was also made available through Chef Nepal's online video platforms. [ref: ]

== Season 1 results ==
The first season concluded in 2024, with Ajuehang Rai of Udayapur winning the competition. Bikesh Manandhar finished as first runner-up, while Ingwa Subba was second runner-up. [ref: Australian ambassador congratulates winners of Chef Nepal, www.myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com]

In August 2024, Australian Ambassador to Nepal Felicity Volk congratulated the competition's participants and production team. Volk had previously appeared as a guest on the programme's fourteenth episode.

----

Bedrock Robotics is an American company, based in San Francisco, that develops sensor, computing and machine learning systems to automate heavy construction equipment, beginning with excavators. [ref: The AI Boom Has a Dirt Problem. This $1.75 Billion Startup Says Robots Can Fix It, Inc.] It was founded in 2024 by former Waymo engineers.

In August 2026 excavators equipped with the company system were working without an operator in the cab on three commercial sites in Texas and Nevada. [ref: First came self-driving cars. Now, Waymo veterans are building autonomous construction equipment., Business Insider] [ref: Bedrock Robotics deploys fully autonomous excavators on jobsites, Construction Dive] Independent observers described the deployments as an early-stage and limited test, noting that their productivity and need for human intervention had yet to be tested across more projects and over longer periods. [ref: Autonomous excavators are digging with empty cabs, Fox News]

== History ==
Bedrock Robotics was founded in 2024 by Boris Sofman, Ajay Gummalla, Kevin Peterson and Tom Eliaz. Three of the four had previously worked at Waymo, where Sofman led the autonomous trucking program and Peterson led perception for that division. Sofman had earlier co-founded the consumer robotics company Anki, which shut down in 2019. [ref: Ex-Waymo engineers launch Bedrock Robotics with $80M to automate construction, TechCrunch] Kevin Peterson also previously co-founded Marble, a robotics company acquired by Caterpillar Inc. in 2020. [ref: Caterpillar Acquires Robotic Specialist Marble Robot Inc, RER Magazine]

In July 2025, Bedrock announced $80 million in combined seed and Series A funding led by Eclipse and 8VC; at the time it was testing its system in Arkansas, Arizona, Texas and California with four contractors. In 2026, the company raised $270 million in a Series B round, giving it a valuation of $1.75 billion. [ref: Bedrock, an A.I. Start-Up for Construction, Raises $270 Million, The New York Times]

Bedrock began field-testing its system on contractors' projects with human operators driving equipped excavators to collect training data and later with the machines digging autonomously while a safety operator remained in the cab. The company also used a test site at Proto-Town, an industrial campus in Lockhart, Texas. [ref: 'Startup Cowboys' Are Making This Texas Town the New Tech Hotspot, The Wall Street Journal] As of December 2025, the system had been installed on excavator models from 20 to 80 tons. [ref: Bedrock Robotics Moves Earth With Autonomous Excavators, Engineering News-Record]

By mid-2026, Bedrock had approximately 50 equipped machines working on projects in six states. In July 2026, a Bedrock-equipped Caterpillar 352 excavator dug to a preset grade and loaded a dump truck for several hours with no one in the cab and no remote intervention; its productivity varied from lower to higher than that of a human operator. In August 2026, excavators using the company system were operating without onboard operators on three commercial sites in Texas and Nevada.

== Technology ==
Bedrock's system, which the company calls the Bedrock Operator, consists of cameras, lidar, GPS receivers and onboard computers added to an excavator, together with machine-learning software. The kit interfaces with the drive-by-wire hydraulic controls used on modern excavators. [ref: These Driverless Construction Vehicles Could Speed the Data Center Boom, [[The Information (website)]

When no operator is in the cab, a remote worker monitors several machines and can take control of one that has stalled; the machines stop automatically if a person or unauthorized object comes too close.

== Reception and analysis ==
Independent observers describe Bedrock's technology as being in its early stages, limited to no-operator excavators on three sites, and wrote that it was unclear whether autonomous machines could adapt to unpredictable construction sites reliably and cheaply enough for contractors to adopt them.

Vineet Kamat, a professor of construction management at the University of Michigan, called the deployments "a limited test" and said that contractors working on thin margins would need to be sure of a return on investment before spending a few hundred thousand dollars on robotic equipment. Fernanda Leite, a civil engineering professor at the University of Texas at Austin, said she expected sites in the near term to combine highly automated systems with highly skilled workers.

Fox News columnist Kurt Knutsson wrote that it remained to be seen whether the near-human productivity reported by the company would hold across more job sites, how intervention rates would change as one person monitored a larger fleet, and whether the machines could work safely around people over long periods.

=== Regulatory considerations ===
Because the machines operate on private construction sites rather than public roads, Bedrock does not face the same regulatory issues as robotaxis and autonomous trucks. Bryant Walker Smith, an associate professor of law at the University of South Carolina who studies automation, noted that it was unclear how Occupational Safety and Health Administration rules referring to an equipment "operator" would apply when one person remotely monitors several machines and intervenes only when something goes wrong.

* Construction robots
* Automation in construction
* Built Robotics

Lala Khadija Azaroual, known as Chef Maman Hanane, is a Moroccan-born chef, pastry chef and cookbook author based in Belgium. She shares recipes from Moroccan cuisine on social media. Her first cookbook was published in Dutch and French in 2026. [ref: Chef Maman Hanane, Lannoo] [ref: Proef de echte Marokkaanse keuken, Lannoo] [ref: Goûtez la vraie cuisine marocaine, Lannoo]

== Background and career ==

Born in Morocco, Azaroual moved to Flanders to pursue further studies in international law, having already earned a master's degree in the field. [ref: Deze populaire chef leert je Marokkaans koken met handig stappenplan, Gazet van Antwerpen]

To finance her studies, she took a student job at Désiré de Lille in Antwerp, working with Marc Stoffels. She began by clearing tables before moving into the kitchen a few months later.

She later trained as a chef and pastry chef at PIVA in Antwerp. At Désiré de Lille, she became responsible for the kitchen and eventually took over the management of the establishment.

== Cooking and family influences ==

In a profile published by Gazet van Antwerpen, Azaroual describes learning to cook from three women in her family: her Amazigh grandmother from the High Atlas, her grandmother from Fez, and her mother, who taught her French cooking techniques.

Her cookbook draws on what she learned from her mother and grandmothers. It brings together traditional Moroccan recipes and her own adaptations of dishes from the Maghreb.

== Social media ==

Under the name Chef Maman Hanane, she shares recipes on YouTube and Instagram. In June 2026, Gazet van Antwerpen reported that her YouTube channel had more than 350,000 subscribers and her Instagram account nearly 80,000 followers.

== Cookbook ==

Her first cookbook, Proef de echte Marokkaanse keuken, was published by Lannoo in June 2026. It contains 70 recipes, including preparations of couscous, chermoula and zaalouk, alongside family stories and memories.

According to the profile in Gazet van Antwerpen, selecting, testing and refining the recipes took more than two years.

A French edition was also published in 2026 under the title Goûtez la vraie cuisine marocaine: Plats authentiques et délicieux, du couscous au zaalouk.

==Plot==
The Chicken and the Egg arrive at the same time in a line, only to find themselves in a tense standoff. Each was insisting the other should go first. Just as the argument reaches its peak, a giant hand descends from above, telling them to not whine because they're others in line waiting. The book later shows that the animals are actually stuffed animals that are trapped inside a claw machine aptly named “The Hand.” The other animals watched as the others were taken by a group of kids from within; the ending shows the Chicken and the Egg inside a boy's backpack.

==Publication==
Buena Batiste-Webber and Kenniece Webber began the idea of The Chicken and The Egg after Buena made daily prank calls while Kenniece was working at a children's library in Baton Rouge, Louisiana. [ref: http://thechickenandtheegg.com/beatrice-s-story.html] After several calls, Kenniece responded: “You should write that book.” Together, they formed Beatrice Ann, LLC, which was named after their grandmother whose middle name was Beatrice. [ref: https://beatriceann-769636.square.site/] Beatrice Ann published the book on June 8, 2012. It is currently available for purchase in online stores or in a booth at the French Market. [ref: https://beatriceann-769636.square.site/]

==Reception==
The book holds a 5.0-star rating across reader and platform reviews (such as BooksRun and general retail feedback). [ref: https://booksrun.com/9780615636856-the-chicken-and-the-egg]

==Sequel and short film adaptation==
On October 26, 2014, Beatrice Ann published a sequel to the book called "The Chicken and The Egg: Hit the Road". [ref: https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Chicken_and_The_Egg.html?id=BdsArgEACAAJ] The book is a slice of life story about exercising, patience, and uncertainty. This is Buena Batiste-Webber's favorite book in the series because, to her, it's about someone having a hard time. [ref: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9E_zXFbLd68] A short film adaptation of both books by Zeke Benoit under his vanity card Puppet Enterprises, Inc., is currently in the works. [ref: https://www.instagram.com/p/DemNhTHx1S9/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&srtk=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==]

The detention of Reza Valizadeh is the Iranian government's ongoing incarceration of Reza Valizadeh (also known as Abdolreza Valizadeh), an Iranian-American journalist. The Iranian government has detained Valizadeh in Iran since September 2024, where he was sentenced in December 2024 to ten years in prison on charges of “collaborating with a hostile government.” [ref: Iranian court jails Iranian-American journalist for 10 years, lawyer says, Reuters] [ref: Reza Valizadeh, Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty] In May 2025, the U.S. Department of State designated Valizadeh as wrongfully detained. [ref: From inside Iran's Evin Prison, journalist Reza Valizadeh pleads for medical help for him and other American captives - CBS News, www.cbsnews.com] [ref: Concerns mount over Iranian-American journalist Reza Valizadeh, wrongfully detained in Iran - CBS News, www.cbsnews.com] Valizadeh's detention has received sustained coverage from international media outlets and press freedom organizations.

== Valizadeh's journalism career ==
Valizadeh began his journalism career in Iran. He was arrested in 2007 in connection with a blog post critical of then-President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad’s security team. [ref: Imprisoned for telling the truth: A Q&A with Iranian-American journalist Reza Valizadeh’s brother, Committee to Protect Journalists]  Following the 2009 Iranian presidential election and the protests known as the Iranian Green Movement, he left Iran and later received asylum in France.

After leaving Iran, Valizadeh worked for international Persian-language media outlets, including Radio France Internationale, Voice of America Persian, and Radio Farda. [ref: Reza Valizadeh, UANI] His Iran-focused reporting for Radio Farda included stories on corruption, protests, and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

== Arrest, trial, and sentencing ==
On March 6, 2024, Valizadeh returned to Iran for the first time since 2009 to visit his aging parents.  He was arrested by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps in Tehran on September 22, 2024.  Following his arrest, Valizadeh was held in Evin prison without access to his lawyer. [ref: U.S. Confirms Reports That Iran Arrested an Iranian-American Citizen, The New York Times]  Iranian intelligence interrogated Valizadeh while he was detained and pressured him to cooperate against his former employer, Radio Farda.  Valizadeh reportedly refused to cooperate.

On December 14, 2024, an Iranian court found Valizadeh guilty of “collaborating with a hostile government,” charges that stemmed from his work at a U.S.-funded radio outlet. [ref: Iran sentences an Iranian-American journalist to 10 years in prison, AP News]  The court sentenced Valizadeh to ten years in prison.  Valizadeh’s sentence also included restrictions on his residence, travel, and political-party membership following his imprisonment.  Valizadeh's attorneys have noted concerns about the fairness of his trial, including that the judge acted as both prosecutor and adjudicator for a trial lasting less than an hour.  Valizadeh’s appeal of his conviction was denied in January 2025.

== Detention conditions and health ==
Valizadeh has been held primarily in Evin Prison in Tehran since his arrest, a facility commonly used to hold political prisoners and foreign detainees.  During his imprisonment, Valizadeh has endured solitary confinement and repeated interrogation. [ref: Advocacy groups push for jailed Americans to be included in U.S.-Iran negotiations, The Washington Times]  He has suffered from deteriorating health conditions while imprisoned, including coughing, asthma-related breathing issues, persistent back pain, and dental problems. Conditions at Evin Prison, including unsanitary housing, polluted water, contaminated food, and inadequate medical treatment, have reportedly exacerbated Valizadeh’s health conditions. [ref: CPJ alarmed by new prison recording from Reza Valizadeh in Iran’s Evin Prison, Committee to Protect Journalists]

Valizadeh was briefly transferred to Fashafouyeh Prison following Israeli airstrikes on Evin Prison in June 2025, before being returned to Evin Prison. Valizadeh’s family believes that the strike and Valizadeh’s subsequent transfer contributed to his worsening asthma.

== Public attention and advocacy on behalf of Valizadeh ==
Valizadeh’s detention has received coverage from Reuters, the Associated Press, CBS News, Fox News, the Washington Post, Al Jazeera, and Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. [ref: US detainees in Iran risk becoming collateral damage in war, families and supporters fear, AP News] [ref: American journalist detained in Iran as Supreme Leader Khamenei threatens US, Israel, State Department says, Fox News] [ref: Iran jails journalist Reza Valizadeh for ‘hostile’ US collaboration, Al Jazeera] Press freedom organizations have also called attention to his case. [ref: Reza Valizadeh, Foley Foundation]  The United States Department of State formally designated Valizadeh as “wrongfully detained” in May 2025, which authorizes the Special Presidential Envoy for Hostage Affairs to coordinate activities across the Executive Branch to seek Valizadeh’s release. [ref: Office of the Special Presidential Envoy for Hostage Affairs, United States Department of State]  On January 20, 2026, attorneys for Valizadeh filed a petition with the United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention on his behalf.
[truncated]

The Pioneertown International Film Festival, also known as the Pioneertown Film Festival, was a one-off film festival devoted to the Western genre, held in Pioneertown, California, a former film-set town in the high desert of San Bernardino County near Joshua Tree National Park. The festival was co-founded by filmmaker Julian T. Pinder and artist Keely King, who also served as its creative director.

Its first edition took place over Memorial Day weekend, May 27–29, 2022, after a planned August 2021 debut was postponed because of the COVID-19 pandemic. The inaugural program, curated by head programmer Todd Luoto, a former Sundance programmer, combined premieres of new Westerns with restored classics from the Paramount Pictures archive, anniversary screenings, short-film programs, panels and live music. It opened with the world premiere of the Jason Momoa–produced The Last Manhunt.

The festival was presented by Fistful of Bourbon and organized in partnership with the Autry Museum of the American West in Los Angeles, the archive and restoration division of Paramount Pictures, and the Palm Springs Art Museum.

== History ==

=== Background ===
Pioneertown was established in 1946 by a group that included actor Dick Curtis and Roy Rogers, as a working town that doubled as a Western film set. Productions shot there included The Cisco Kid, The Gene Autry Show and Annie Oakley.

Pinder, a documentary and film director who grew up in rural Canada, had lived on a ranch outside Pioneertown for about a decade. His credits include the Netflix series Fire Chasers, executive produced by Leonardo DiCaprio, and the films Jesus Town, USA, Trouble In The Peace, and Population Zero, among others. He said he conceived the festival to mark the town's role in the history of Western film, and to celebrate it through film and music.

=== Development ===
Todd Luoto, a former programmer for the Sundance, CineVegas, Newport Beach and Silver Lake film festivals, came on during the development of the film festival as head of programming. The organizers were initially unsure whether enough new Westerns were being made to sustain a genre-specific festival. Luoto and Pinder spent nearly two years canvassing other festivals and distributors for titles, and the team adopted a broad definition of the genre that included films following Western story archetypes. Artist Keely King, the festival's creative director, developed the unique branding, artwork, and posters, including a limited screen-print run.

Organizers launched the festival in late February 2020, shortly before the COVID-19 pandemic. The first edition was scheduled for August 27–29, 2021, but was postponed after a rise in COVID-19 cases and moved to May 27–29, 2022. During the delay, members of the community non-profit group Friends of Pioneertown helped maintain a drive-in theater that had been built as one of the festival's venues.

== Venues and format ==
Pioneertown has no movie theater, so organizers converted the town's historic soundstage, where interiors for Roy Rogers and Gene Autry productions were filmed, and a nearby ranch barn into temporary cinemas with 4K digital projection and Dolby sound. Other historic sites, including Desert Willow Ranch, the Pioneertown Motel, the Red Dog Saloon and Super X Ranch, served as screening venues, lounges and bars.

The 2022 edition had capacity for about 1200 attendees. It ran 20 to 25 screenings in two screening rooms over three days, including two blocks of short films. Pinder said the festival intended to stay small and improve the quality of its program rather than grow its audience.

== 2022 festival ==
The festival opened on May 27, 2022, with a performance by The Dandy Warhols and the world premiere of The Last Manhunt. The feature film, directed by Christian Camargo and produced by Jason Momoa, dramatizes the 1909 pursuit of Willie Boy, a Chemehuevi man, based on the Chemehuevi oral account of the events. The Autry Museum presented the screening. Two days earlier, on May 25, the Palm Springs Art Museum hosted a screening of the film in association with the festival, attended by members of the Twenty-Nine Palms Band of Mission Indians and descendants of the Mike family. The band The Dandy Warhols played the Opening Night show.

New films in the program came from the United States, Ukraine, Australia, Italy and Spain. They included Roman Perfilyev's Ukrainian action Western The Inglorious Serfs, whose director attended after relocating to the United States because of the war in Ukraine, and Tim Kirk's documentary The Mystery of Durango!.

Retrospective programming included:

* a series of recently restored Westerns presented by Paramount Pictures' archive and restoration department, which also gave a masterclass on film restoration;
* an anniversary screening of An American Tail: Fievel Goes West, attended by director Phil Nibbelink;
* an anniversary screening of From Dusk till Dawn, presented by co-producer Robert Kurtzman;
* a tribute to Monte Hellman, with The Shooting and Ride in the Whirlwind presented by Melissa Hellman and Jennifer Nicholson, daughters of Hellman and Jack Nicholson;
* Heartworn Highways and Heartworn Highways Revisited, presented by producer Graham Leader.
[truncated]

Draft text:
Shakira Stadium () was a temporary, purpose-built music venue located within the Iberdrola Music complex in the Villaverde district of Madrid, Spain. The 50,000-capacity pop-up stadium was constructed specifically to host the European residency of Colombian singer Shakira's Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour in September and October 2026. The venue served as the centerpiece of Parque Macondo, an immersive cultural festival and event space inspired by the work of Gabriel García Márquez that celebrated Latin American identity, art, literature, and gastronomy. Hosting 13 sold-out concerts for over half a million attendees, the stadium introduced an unprecedented international artistic residency format to Spain and stands as a notable example of multi-use, temporary entertainment architecture.

== Background and conception ==
Eight years after her last concert in Spain during the El Dorado World Tour (2018), Colombian singer Shakira announced her return to Europe as part of her Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour. [ref: Shakira, Tourism Madrid] Rather than adopting a traditional multi-city European routing, Shakira and tour promoter Live Nation established a single-site, multi-date concert residency in Madrid, marking the first international artistic residency of this scale in Spain. [ref: Shakira construirá un estadio para 50.000 espectadores por concierto: recinto "de quita y pon" abierto 12 horas al día, Somos Madrid - elDiario.es] [ref: Shakira llena Madrid y pone el foco en el consumo eléctrico de sus conciertos] [ref: Lo que se sabe del misterioso 'Estadio Shakira', donde la cantante actuará en España: del diseño a su capacidad por concierto, Telecinco]

To host the event, organizers selected the 185,000-square-meter Iberdrola Music complex in Madrid's Villaverde district to construct a pop-up cultural hub named "Macondo Park". [ref: BIG designed an ephemeral city for Shakira inspired by One Hundred Years of Solitude, [[Domus (magazine)] Named after the fictional town from Gabriel García Márquez's novel One Hundred Years of Solitude, the park was conceived as an event space focused on Latin American culture. It was designed to encompass a central plaza connected to eight themed pavilions offering music, literature, fashion, visual arts, and gastronomy, organized under the banner "Es Latina". [ref: BIG's Macondo Park Opens as a Temporary Cultural Landscape for Shakira's Madrid Residency, ArchDaily]

At the center of Macondo Park stood Estadio Shakira (Shakira Stadium). Designed by the Danish architecture studio Bjarke Ingels Group (BIG), the temporary venue held a capacity of 50,000 spectators per night, divided between 30,000 tiered seats and a 20,000-person standing area. [ref: Todo lo que se sabe sobre el Estadio Shakira de Madrid, el recinto de los conciertos de 'Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour', EuropaFM] [ref: El 'Estadio Shakira' de Madrid estará terminado en diez días y tendrá capacidad para 50.000 personas, www.20minutos.es - Últimas Noticia] [ref: Macondo Park for Shakira's Residency in Madrid - BIG Bjarke Ingels Group, Arquitectura Viva] [ref: https://es.euronews.com/2026/09/18/shakira-inicia-madrid-serie-12-conciertos-para-cerrar-gira-mundial-tras-8-anos-ausencia] Rather than relying on permanent construction, BIG assembled the stadium and the surrounding temporary structures in ten days. Built with reversibility in mind, the project utilized modular scaffolding systems and lightweight reusable fabrics, alongside over 500 trees that were temporarily planted with the intention of returning them to local nurseries upon the residency's conclusion. The cost of constructing and deconstructing the stadium is estimated to be over €37 million. [ref: Un experto confirma cuánto le ha costado a Shakira las 13 noches en Madrid: “Hablamos de un recinto para más de 50.000 personas levantado en menos de dos meses”, infobae]

The decision to host the residency in Madrid's Villaverde district initially sparked local debate. Residents and local officials from the neighboring municipality of Getafe, including Mayor Sara Hernández, voiced concerns regarding the potential public nuisance of transforming the site into a 12-hour-a-day festival. [ref: A once-in-a-lifetime experience or a public nuisance? The big debate over Shakira's stadium in Madrid, El País] Critics cited past logistical, noise, and traffic issues caused by events at the Iberdrola Music venue, such as the Mad Cool music festival, and questioned the area's infrastructure and its ability to handle the anticipated influx of attendees.

== Design ==
The design of Macondo Park and Estadio Shakira was led by the Danish architectural firm Bjarke Ingels Group. Conceived as a 185,000-square-meter ephemeral city at the Iberdrola Music site, the complex was designed to expand the conventional concert arena into an urban landscape. Macondo Park was described by chief architect Bjarke Ingels as an "architectural manifestation of magical realism" and a temporary town meant to represent a fusion of Europe, the Americas, and Africa. [ref: Macondo Park: BIG builds an ephemeral 'Gig-City' for Shakira, ArchiPanic]
[truncated]

[[File:CLIMAVORE_On_Tidal_Zones.jpg|thumb|CLIMAVORE: On Tidal Zones. Cooking Sections, 2017-ongoing. Isle of Skye]]

Cooking Sections investigates the systems that shape the world through food, tracing the spatial, ecological, and political legacies of extractivism. Using site-responsive installations, performances, and video, their practice confronts the overlapping boundaries of art, architecture, ecology, and geopolitics. [ref: about - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com]

Founded in London in 2013 by Daniel Fernández Pascual and Alon Schwabe, Cooking Sections uses food as both a lens and a tool to trace the metabolic relations behind industrialised food systems. Since 2015, they have run CLIMAVORE, a long-term, site-responsive project, exploring how to eat as humans change climates and how to metabolise climate breakdown. [ref: About CLIMAVORE, CLIMAVORE] [ref: about - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com]

Alon and Daniel are Readers in Architecture and Spatial Practice at the Royal College of Art, London, and Fellows at the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research. [ref: Dr Daniel Fernández Pascual, RCA Website] [ref: Alon Schwabe, RCA Website]

== [https://www.climavore.org/ CLIMAVORE] ==
CLIMAVORE [ref: CLIMAVORE, www.climavore.org] uses cultural platforms to amplify civic resistance: removing farmed salmon from the menus of over 20 major museums; regranting art funds to farmers trailing agrochemical-free methods in Lake Erie; launching a nationwide baking challenge for breads against soil depletion in Finland; turning museums' living collections into protocols for peasant seed exchange in Southern Italy; or creating a water buffalo festival to protect Istanbul’s urban wetlands from extinction. [ref: The Turner Prize-Nominated Art Collective Cooking Sections Wants to Change the Way You Think About Food, Artnet News] [ref: Rights to Seeds, Rights of Seeds - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com] [ref: Maaleipä - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com] [ref: To Those Who Nourish - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com] [ref: Istanbul Wetlands - CLIMAVORE, CLIMAVORE]

== Exhibitions ==
Their work has been exhibited internationally, including at Tate Britain, Serpentine Galleries, SALT, Centro Botín, Bonniers Konsthall, Carnegie Museum of Art, Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh, Museo delle Civiltà, among others. They have created site-specific performances and installations for the Taipei Biennial, 58th Venice Biennale, Istanbul Biennial, Performa17, Manifesta12, Los Angeles Public Art Triennial, Sharjah Architecture Triennial, Folkestone Triennial, and New Orleans Triennial among others. Residencies include the Headlands Center for the Arts, Prospect Cottage, Fogo Island Arts and Delfina Foundation. [ref: about - Cooking Sections, cooking-sections.com]

== Awards ==
Cooking Sections was nominated for the Turner Prize in 2021, received the Special Prize at the 2019 Future Generation Art Prize and were nominated for the Visible Award for socially-engaged practices. Daniel was awarded the 2020 Harvard GSD Wheelwright Prize for Being Shellfish. [ref: Cooking Sections, www.somersethouse.org.uk] [ref: Daniel Fernández Pascual Wins Harvard Graduate School of Design’s 2020 Wheelwright Prize, Harvard Graduate School of Design] [ref: ] [ref: Cooking Sections, PinchukArtCentre]

== Books ==

They have authored four books:

* The Empire Remains Shop (2018) [ref: The empire remains shop, Columbia University Press]
* Salmon: A Red Herring (2020)
* Offsetted (2022) [ref: Cooking Sections: Offsetted, Hatje Cantz Verlag]
* Waves Lost at Sea (2026) [ref: Cooking Sections: Waves Lost at Sea, Spector Books]

== External Links ==

* [https://www.cooking-sections.com/ Official Website]
* [https://www.climavore.org/ CLIMAVORE]
