= Adv Nivedida Subramanian =
Nivedida Subramanian is an Indian lawyer and politician associated with the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), India. She served as Kerala state president of the BJP’s women’s wing, Mahila Morcha, and later as president of the party’s Thrissur North district unit in Kerala. In September 2026, the Government of India appointed her as a member of the National Commission for Women (NCW). [ref: Baptised in Emergency Fire, Nivedita Braces for Battle in Guruvayur, The New Indian Express] [ref: Notification S.O. 5257(E): Appointment of Members, National Commission for Women, The Gazette of India] [ref: ] [ref: NCW (@[user]) on X, X (formerly Twitter)]
== Early life and family ==
Subramanian is from Guruvayur in Thrissur district, Kerala. Her mother, Radha Balakrishnan, was active in the Bharatiya Jana Sangh and later held a leadership position in the BJP’s women’s organisation. Her father, Balakrishnan, was also reported to have been associated with the Jana Sangh. The family’s political involvement meant that Subramanian was exposed to party workers and political activity from childhood. [ref: ]

In 1975, during the Emergency declared by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi, Radha Balakrishnan was arrested after taking part in protests against the Emergency. Subramanian, then approximately three years old, accompanied her mother to Palakkad Fort prison. In an interview published in 2016, Subramanian recalled that she remained with her mother in prison and that the experience had stayed with her. [ref: Nivedida Subramanian, BJP's Experimental Candidate For Ponnani, TimelineDaily]

Subramanian has described the experience as an early encounter with political adversity. The episode has subsequently been highlighted in profiles of her political career.

== Education and legal career ==
Subramanian holds a bachelor’s degree and a law degree. A 2016 profile reported that she was then pursuing a master’s degree in law at Annamalai University. A 2026 report by Madhyamam states that she obtained an LL.M. in labour law from Annamalai University, an LL.B. from Mangalore University, and an MBA in human resources from ICFAI University.

She has worked as an advocate in the civil and criminal courts at Chavakkad. Madhyamam reported that she had practised there for more than 12 years and had been a Supreme Court-accredited mediator since 2014. She also served as vice-president of the Chavakkad Bar Association. A company disclosure by Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited (MRPL) described her as a lawyer, mediator and social-service participant, and recorded her tenure as a non-executive independent director. She was reappointed to the board with effect from 28 March 2025, and her tenure ended on 27 March 2026. [ref: Statutory disclosure: Board of Directors, Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited] [ref: Integrated Filing (Governance): Mangalore Refinery and Petrochemicals Limited, National Stock Exchange of India] [ref: MRPL reappoints four independent directors to its board, FilingReader]

== Political career ==

=== BJP Mahila Morcha ===
Subramanian became a prominent figure in the BJP’s Kerala women’s organisation, Mahila Morcha, and served as its state president. Her mother, Radha Balakrishnan, had also held a leadership role in the organisation as a former state president.

As Mahila Morcha state president, Subramanian publicly advocated greater participation by women in BJP activities. In a 2021 Times of India report on the party’s efforts to expand its women’s cadre in Kerala, she said that social media was being used to interact with women volunteers and involve them in party activities. The report also discussed the role of the Sabarimala protests and local political mobilisation in the party’s outreach to women. [ref: Kerala: BJP claims its women cadre is blooming, The Times of India]

Her profile within the state BJP became more visible around the Mahila Sangamam, a large women’s gathering organised by Mahila Morcha in Thrissur on 3 January 2024. The New Indian Express reported that Subramanian was a principal organiser of the event, which the BJP had promoted as a gathering of two lakh women. The newspaper described the programme as a significant organisational moment for her within the party. India Today subsequently reported that the BJP’s women-focused event in Thrissur was seen by party sources as Subramanian’s initiative and quoted her discussing the party’s campaign approach towards women voters. [ref: Kerala Mahila Morcha president Nivedida steals the show at women’s conference, The New Indian Express] [ref: Modi in Thrissur, BJP on cloud nine: What next?, India Today]

The event brought her into greater public view alongside senior BJP leaders during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Thrissur. Contemporary reporting connected her role in organising the gathering with her standing in the state unit.

=== Thrissur North district president ===
On 27 January 2025, the BJP’s Kerala unit appointed Subramanian president of its Thrissur North organisational district. She was one of four women among the 27 district presidents named that day. [ref: BJP ‘doubles’ Kerala districts to 30, Christian push evident as it appoints 27 unit heads, @[user]]

Demid Odonchimeg is a Mongolian dentist, academic, and researcher in the fields of dentistry, orthodontics, and maxillofacial prosthetics. She holds a Doctor of Medical Sciences degree and the academic title of associate professor.

== Early life and education ==
Demid Odonchimeg was born in 1961 in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. [ref: Employment profile of Demid Odonchimeg, 2002.10.01.]

She graduated from Secondary School No. 23 in Ulaanbaatar in 1979 and completed her dental education at the Irkutsk State Medical Institute in 1984. [ref: Employment profile of Demid Odonchimeg, 2002.10.01.]

== Career ==
From 1984 to 1986, Odonchimeg worked as a dentist in the maxillofacial prosthetics department of the State Central Clinical Hospital. From 1986 to 1989, she worked at the Specialized Center for Dental Care as a dentist and department head. [ref: Employment profile of Demid Odonchimeg, 2016.09.09.]

From 1989 onward, she worked as a lecturer and later senior lecturer at medical university institutions in Mongolia, including AUDS, AUIS, EMSU, and MNUMS. [ref: Employment profile of Demid Odonchimeg, 2016.09.09.]

== Degrees and academic title ==
In 1996, she earned a master's degree in medical sciences with a thesis titled A Comparative Study of the Size of Permanent Human Teeth. [ref: List of publications of D. Odonchimeg.]

In 2004, she earned a Doctor of Medical Sciences degree with a dissertation titled Diagnostic and Treatment Approaches for Ectopic Eruption of the Maxillary Permanent Canine. [ref: Supplement to Doctor of Medical Sciences Diploma, No. F 20041951.]

In 2011, she received the academic title of associate professor. [ref: Associate Professor Certificate, No. 072, Registration No. DP 20110072.]

== Research and publications ==
Her research and publications cover topics such as permanent tooth size, eruption patterns of maxillary canines, dentofacial development, mixed dentition space analysis, cleft lip and palate care, and maxillofacial prosthetic rehabilitation. [ref: List of publications of D. Odonchimeg.]

Selected works include:

* Maxillofacial Prosthetic Rehabilitation of Oral and Facial Defects in Mongolia (2000)
* Measurement of Condylar Position in Permanent Dentition of Mongolian Females (2006)
* Mixed Dentition Space Analysis for Mongolians (2009)
* Tweed-Merrifield Directional Force Technology (translated and edited, 2010)
* Removable Appliances in Orthodontics (translated and edited, 2016) [ref: List of publications of D. Odonchimeg.]

== Supervision of master's theses ==
According to her professional record, Odonchimeg supervised master's theses on dental occlusion in young children, prediction of eruption space for permanent canines and premolars, dental crowding, craniofacial growth patterns, and the prevalence of malocclusion among schoolchildren in Ulaanbaatar. [ref: List of publications of D. Odonchimeg.]

* Leading Youth Gold Medal (1987)
* Commendation of the Ministry of Health (1996)
* Distinguished Health Worker of the Capital City (2007)

Draft: Three-Phase Design Model

Draft text:
----

The Three-Phase Design Model (3PD) is an iterative and collaborative model used to support the delivery of online education. [ref: Survey of Instructional Design Models, Association for Educational Communications and Technology] [ref: Continuous Improvement Through Shared Understanding: Reconceptualising Instructional Design for Online Learning, ASCILITE] The model was developed in 2002 by Rod Sims and Deborah Jones. Around the time the 3PD Model was developed, traditional instructional designs were used to facilitate the development and design of online learning resources. There were concerns regarding the use of these traditional approaches due to inconsistencies in catering to the needs of learners and supporting instructors and course developers. The concerns stemmed frrom the need to have flexibility when designing and delivering a course, limited resources available to the academic staff and technological personnel and the need for collaboration among all three.
==The Three- Phase Model Phases==
There are three phases of the 3PD Model. They are Functionality, Enhancement and Maintenance. In each of the phases, scaffolding gives support to learners and academic staff and there is also continuous evaluation throughout the course. The information provided as feedback from both learners and staff is valuable in making decisions to either improve or change any course component if necessary. It is important to note that the hierarchy of roles in the team changes in different phases. [ref: The Design of a Computer-Supported Collaborative Learning Environment that Promotes Interaction, 2014 International Conference on Teaching and Learning in Computing and Engineering (LaTiCE)]

Functionality

The first stage of the model, the Functionality phase, sets the online learning space to one that is operational and can support the teaching and learning regardless of the course not fully complete. [ref: Developing a Challenging Online Doctoral Course Using Backward and Three-Phase Design Models, The Journal of Aviation/Aerospace Education and Research]A functional prototoype is first created. [ref: E-Learning Development in Higher Education: Maximising Efficiency—Maintaining Quality, ERIC (Education Resources Information Center)]This covers the necessary materials and activities needed for the course to begin. The prototypes may include learning objectives, teaching resources such as study guides, unit guides and required reading materials related to topics in the course and instructions given to access these resources.

The model supports collaborative efforts and even though there are different roles and responsibilities of the experts designing and developing the course, there is a partnership to get the inital stages going. To differentiate roles, the team is placed into two groups: the Support Team and the Faculty Team. The Support Team consists of educational designers, interactive architects, and information analysts who contribute to the instructional and technical development of the course. The educational designer plays the major role at this phase and is responsible for curriculum and instructional design guidance and assisting in coordinating teams involved in the development of the course. On the other hand, the Faculty Team is described as content specialists. This is due largely to their expertise in the course content. The members of this team, which include academic staff, develop the objectives of the course, the appraoches and strategies to teach the content and also the types of assessments to be used.

The Model is used through an online space to deliver course content. An hindrance may be the limited experience some instructors may have in using the new technologies. The Support Team gives guidance on how to use the technologies so that the instructors can carry out their roles more efficiently.

Enhancement

The Enhancement Phase takes place while the course is being delivered. The course is monitored and evaluated to see what changes should be made that would be beneficial to the learners and make the course run smoothly. An activity done in this phase called shadowing, assesses the effectiveness of course components. The task is undertaken by members of the development team. Scaffolding is another activity in the phase. Even though technological assistance is offered at the Functionality Phase, it is still offered at the Enhancement Phase to support those instructors who are still experiencing difficulties. There is also support for learners to help to effectively participate in the online learning environment. [ref: In search of an Instructional Material Design Model to Support the Implementation of IQF Oriented Curriculum at HEIs, Advances in Social Science, Education and Humanities Research] Feedback is provided by the instructors and learners. The Enhancement Phase not only make adjustments or fix the problems, but there can be a further expansion of course materials that were developed in the functionality stage.

Purohit is named as the inventor of Adaptive Intelligent Pipeline Integrity System (AIPIS) with Contextual Self-Learning Distributed Artificial Intelligence and Hybrid Sensor Arrays for Real-Time Predictive Pipeline Management. In July 2026, Analytics India Magazine reported that an AIPIS software prototype incorporated XGBoost for prediction and anomaly detection and included a monitoring dashboard. The publication described controlled testing and plans to seek operational pilot collaborations.

Draft: 681 (genre)

Draft text:
----

681 is the genre of music that consist of exactly vocals and percussion instruments. It combines a capella with minimalist dance music. An example is the song Crabapples [ref: Bruce Peninsula: "Crabapples", Pitchfork] by Bruce Peninsula. [ref: Bruce Peninsula climbing the musical ladder, Interrobang]

It follows that this is the alternative name of the genre of minimalist vocal dance music.

Many genres have a given alternative name. For example, an alternative name trance is given to usually minimalist ambient rhythmic dance music with tempo between 120 and 150 BPM.

== Name origin ==

The name origin of this genre is mathematical. The name 681 originates from the list of natural numbers. The main values are taken as the rank of the dominance of elements of vocal music in general. Call them a, b, c, etc. We have a=1 because of the existence of vocals as the primary element of most vocal songs. [ref: Musical Texture, Fundamentals: Music in World Cultures] Then we skip 2 because there are no instruments other than percussion in this genre to function as the secondary element of most vocal songs. Hence we take b=3 as the next notable number because there is percussion in this genre and is the tertiary element of most vocal songs. The formula of the square of a binomial is (a+b)^2=a^2+2\cdot a\cdot b+b^2. If we square the exponents of b in each addend, i.e., raise them to the 2nd power, because 2 is the skipped natural number, we get the addends a^2, 2\cdot a \cdot b and b^4, respectively. The addends are equal to 1, 6 and 81, respectively. The ratio when the second addend is divided by the first addend is 6/1=6, while the ratio when the third addend is divided by the first addend is 81/1=81. Its concatenation gives 681.

== References ==

WohSend is a European file transfer service launched in October 2026. Files are stored and delivered without compression or re-encoding. [ref: WohSend – WeTransfer alternative, AlternativeTo] Data is stored on Cloudflare infrastructure under Portuguese law with optional end-to-end encryption. [ref: Read Customer Service Reviews of wohsend.com, Trustpilot] [ref: WohSend reviews and trust score, ScamAdviser]

The service includes an "Upload Method" feature that modifies MP4 container metadata before upload to social media platforms. [ref: WohSend – European file transfer with zero compression, Reddit] Processing occurs client-side in the browser. [ref: WohSend side project, Reddit]

== History ==
The service was created by Guilherme Anjos, a developer based in Portugal. Development of the Upload Method feature involved testing MP4 container structures against TikTok's CDN behaviour. The platform launched publicly in October 2026 with support for 16 languages.

== Features ==

=== File storage ===
Uploaded files are stored without modification. EXIF metadata in photos is preserved. Videos retain their original resolution, codec and bitrate.

=== Upload Method ===
The feature modifies MP4 container structure before upload to social media platforms:
moov atom positioned before mdat (fast-start flag)
Colour space tags (colr/nclx) preserved
GPS location data removed from metadata
Original codec and bitrate maintained

Supported codecs include H.264 and HEVC/H.265 at resolutions up to 8K with frame rates including 60fps and 120fps.

=== Encryption ===
Optional end-to-end encryption uses a user-provided password. Encrypted files are decrypted after download.

=== Expiration ===
Files expire between 1 hour and 90 days based on user selection.

== Pricing ==
The free tier allows transfers up to 1.5 GB without an account and up to 30 GB with a registered account. Paid tiers (Plus, Pro, Studio) provide additional Upload Method credits. Payment is processed via Stripe with support for regional methods including MB Way, iDEAL and Pix.

== Technology ==
Backend services run on Cloudflare Workers with D1 (SQLite) for database storage and R2 for object storage. The frontend uses vanilla JavaScript and CSS without frameworks.

Draft: Fujishima

Draft text:
Fujishima was the third son of Fujishima Masakata. His family had quite a long connection to the Satsuma domain. He also became head of the household while still in his early teens after his two older brothers died from injuries sustained during the Satsuma Rebellion of 1877. [ref: FUJISHIMA Takeji, Dictionary of Artists in Japan]

Before he moved to Tokyo, Fujishima studied Japanese-style painting under Hirayama Tōgaku in Kagoshima. He participated in the Second National Painting Competition in Tokyo in 1884. The following year he became a pupil of Kawabata Gyokushō and adopted the artistic name Gyokudō.

Cruelty (Muzan) reportedly depicted two girls striking butterflies with branches. The painting was exhibited under the name of Fujishima's friend Shirataki Ikunosuke. Mori Ōgai praised the work in a newspaper review, however, the original painting has not survived.

Additionally, in 1892, Fujishima produced Cherry Blossom Hunt or (Sakuragari). The painting depicted women of the Genroku period partaking in a cherry-blossom viewing. Although the original is unable to be found, a preparatory study is held by the Kagoshima City Museum of Art. These earlier paintings introduced subjects that continued to appear throughout Fujishima's career.

In July 1895, Fujishima became an assistant teacher at Mie Prefectural Ordinary Middle School in Tsu. He continued exhibiting his paintings during his time there.

Kuroda introduced Fujishima to plein-air painting, which involved working outdoors and observing natural light. Fujishima later became interested in Art Nouveau and other European styles from the end of the nineteenth century. His earlier training in Japanese-style painting also helped influence the decorative characteristics of his later creations. [ref: Fujishima, Takeji, Oxford University Press]

Around 1900, Fujishima began moving away from Kuroda's (Fujishima's mentor and colleague) approach to natural light. His paintings became more closely reminiscent of the Meiji Romanticism period. This change was interconnected to the literary culture of the period. The poet Yosano Akiko and the magazine Myōjō were also important figures in that cultural movement.

Beginning in 1900, Fujishima made cover illustrations for the literary magazine Myōjō. His work during this period showed his budding interest in decorative design. His paintings In Praise of the Tenpyō Era (1902) and Butterflies (1904) helped establish his reputation as an artist.

His painting titled Reminiscence of the Tempyo Era (1902) expressed an interest in Japan's Nara period. Fujishima researched about historical art while he was developing the painting. He also drew from ancient Greek art and French painting styles. The work was exhibited at the Seventh Hakubakai Exhibition. It is now held by the Artizon Museum in Tokyo. [ref: FUJISHIMA Takeji: Reminiscence of the Tempyo Era, Artizon Museum]

Fujishima's studies in Europe were funded by Japan's Ministry of Education. He left Japan in 1905 and spent approximately four years abroad. He studied in Paris before moving to Rome.

While in Europe, Fujishima encountered modern artistic movements with his academic training. He attended an exhibition of works by Paul Gauguin in 1906. The following year he attended an exhibition honouring Paul Cézanne. In Rome, he associated with Italian painters including Giacomo Balla.

During his studies in Europe. Fujishima spent around two years in Italy. There, he studied portraiture under the wing of Carolus Duran. His painting Woman of Italy (c. 1908–1909) depicts his academic oil-painting techniques. The period when he painted that work showed his focus on academic technique before he later took to Romantic qualities; showcased in his later works of female portraits. [ref: Woman of Italy, Google Arts & Culture]

At his later role, as a professor at the Tokyo School of Fine Arts, Fujishima taught younger artists and helped organize official art exhibitions. His responsibilities therefore extended beyond teaching to developing public art exhibitions in Japan.During the 1930s, Fujishima produced several landscape paintings that focused on Japanese scenery. These included Surging Waves at Daio Point (1932) and Terraced Fields (1938). His paintings from this time period used clear and bold brushwork to portray the landscape.

Draft text:
The Nazareth German war cemetery () is a First World War military cemetery in Nazareth, Israel, near the Holy Family Hospital. It holds the graves of German soldiers who died in what became British Mandate Palestine and Transjordan during the Sinai and Palestine campaign of the war. This includes many airmen and members of the Royal Bavarian Flying Corps.

It was built by the German War Graves Commission (Volksbund Deutsche Kriegsgräberfürsorge) with a design by and dedicated on 30 June 1935.

It is the only German war cemetery in Israel.

== History ==
=== Wartime burials ===
During the First World War the Holy Family Hospital of the Austrian Brothers of Mercy in Nazareth served as Imperial German Field Hospital No. 213. Nazareth was also the headquarters of the Yildirim Army Group, the Ottoman army group under German command.

Fifty-one German soldiers who were killed in action or died in the hospital were buried next to it. Those not buried at Nazareth lay in small cemeteries and single graves across the country, most of them in poor condition by the late 1920s.

=== Construction and dedication ===
The Treaty of Versailles required of the British to care for the graves of enemy soldiers in Palestine. In December, 1928, British authorities in Palestine agreed with the German consul-general to establish a central German cemetery. It would be located at Nazareth for the burial of German dead of Palestine and Transjordan. Some German soldiers remained buried at smaller cemeteries in Jerusalem or in British war cemeteries.

The German War Graves Commission agreed in May 1931 to meet the cost. The High Commissioner for Palestine acquired a plot beside the hospital, and it was leased to the German Reich for 999 years without charge. The municipality of Nazareth issued the building permit on 11 August 1934.

The commission's architect, Robert Tischler, designed the cemetery, and construction began in 1934. Builders from Nazareth carried out the work. The dead were brought in from temporary graves across Palestine and Transjordan, including Anabta, Beersheba, Jenin, Ma'an, Mafraq, Salt, Samakh and Tulkarm, with the help of the British war graves authorities.

The cemetery was dedicated on 30 June 1935. Representatives of Germany's wartime allies, the Evangelical and Catholic churches, the Templers and the local Nazi Party attended and a swastika flag flew from the tower. Adolf Hitler sent a telegram regarding the dedication.

=== Later history ===
During the Arab revolt of 1936 Austrian brothers continued to tend the graves, keeping in touch with the German Foreign Office through the Spanish consul in Jerusalem until the end of the Second World War. The hospital and the care of the cemetery later passed to Italian brothers that were from the same Christian order.

The German War Graves Commission has paid for the upkeep since the end of Second World War. Major repairs were carried out in 1967 and 1982. In 1982 Cardinal Joseph Höffner donated a new bell frame and a motor for the bell.

The land is now owned by the State of Israel, from which it is leased. There is no war-graves agreement between Germany and Israel, but the Israeli government guarantees the permanent right of rest of the dead and the protection of the site.

== Description ==
The cemetery is reached through a locked gate to the right of the hospital, across the brothers' cemetery and up a narrow stair. As built, it consisted of a court of honor, a bell tower, a covered hall of honor and two rows of open tomb chambers.

The tower holds a bell cast in Munich, about across and weighing nearly two tonnes, one of the largest in Israel.

Wooden crosses made from the propellers of crashed aircraft hang on the tower walls. Red Weser sandstone slabs were shipped from Germany for its construction.

== Burials ==
The cemetery holds primarily German, but also some Austro-Hungarian, soldiers and airmen of the First World War. The number buried is somewhere between 217 and 261. Tablets give each man's name, dates and place of death and are arranged by place of death. A second row of tablets commemorates about 250 German and Austrian dead whose graves were never found.

Among those buried is Alfred Gerechter, a German Jewish soldier killed at Salt on 30 April 1918.

== Commemoration ==
Since the early 1980s the German embassy in Israel has held an annual ceremony at the cemetery on Volkstrauertag, the German day of national mourning. It is attended by foreign military attachés and Israeli soldiers.

The service is interfaith, and an Israel Defense Forces rabbi recites the Kaddish for the dead.

== Further reading ==
* Deutsche Soldatengräber in Israel: Der Einsatz deutscher Soldaten an der Palästinafront im Ersten Weltkrieg und das Schicksal ihrer Grabstätten, Aschendorff

Paige Plaisance is an American singer, songwriter and pianist based in Austin, Texas. She describes her music as "swampytonkin'", a blend of Texas two-step and classic country with blues and soul influences. Her second album, Swampwater (2026), produced by Jonathan Tyler, reached number 16 on the Americana Music Association's Americana Radio Airplay albums chart.

== Early life ==
Plaisance was raised in rural northeast Louisiana, on a farm near the Mississippi River where her father farmed. She writes her songs at the piano. She moved to Austin in 2014.

== Career ==
Plaisance performs regularly at the Austin venues Sagebrush, the White Horse and the Continental Club. She has shared stages with Nikki Lane, Reckless Kelly, Noeline Hofmann and The Band of Heathens. She also runs Ramblin' Rose Co., a vintage clothing trailer behind Sagebrush, and organizes and hosts the Honkytonk Catwalk, a recurring fashion show at the venue.

Her 2022 EP, Different Now, introduced her "swampy-tonk" sound. In 2023 she released the single "Good Time Girl", produced by Jonathan Tyler at Clyde's VIP Room in Austin, with a music video directed by Dan Brown. Her first full-length album, Louisiana Lonely, followed in August 2024. Saving Country Music rated it 8 out of 10, and the album reached the top 20 on Americana radio.

In August 2026, Austin public radio station KUTX named Plaisance its Artist of the Month. Her second album, Swampwater, was recorded at the Finishing School in Austin with her band, the Yeah You Right Boys, and produced by Tyler. It was released in September 2026, with a release show at Antone's. Saving Country Music rated it 8.1 out of 10, and North Carolina public radio station WNCW placed it in heavy rotation. In October 2026 the album reached number 16 on the Americana Radio Airplay albums chart, and its opening track, "Make Mine Country", reached number 34 on the corresponding singles chart.

== Band ==
Plaisance performs and records with her band, the Yeah You Right Boys.
Members of the Yeah You Right Boys credited on Swampwater include: [ref: Swampwater, Timeless Echo Recordings]

[[File:Argentine-passport-ecover-front.jpg|thumb|Accepted investors are eligible to apply for an Argentine passport|alt=Picture of the Argentinian passport front cover]]
Argentina has been running a citizenship by investment programme since July 2025, to encourage foreign direct investment, job creation, and attract global talent and innovation within the country. [ref: Argentina – Investing in Argentina: New Pathway to Citizenship, KPMG] [ref: Citizenship by Investment Program Details Announced; Applications Expected to Open Before Year-End, Fragomen - Immigration attorneys, solicitors, and consultants worldwide - Citizenship by Investment Program Details Announced; Applications Expected to Open Before Year-End]

On the 31st July 2025, the Government of Argentina published Decree no.524/2025, in the nation's gazette to establish a formal framework for foreign investors who make a 'relevant investment' to apply for Argentinian citizenship. [ref: Argentina establishes a citizenship-by-investment framework, United Nations Trade and Development]

== Cost ==
Foreign nationals are charged either a $350,000 non-refundable contribution, or must purchase a government bond subscription worth $800,000. [ref: Citizenship by Investment Program Details Announced; Applications Expected to Open Before Year-End, Fragomen - Immigration attorneys, solicitors, and consultants worldwide - Citizenship by Investment Program Details Announced; Applications Expected to Open Before Year-End] Spouses and children (aged 18-25) of applicants are charged an additional $100,000 each, with minors contributing $25,000 each. [ref: Argentina launches cash-for-citizenship scheme, dw.com]

== Due diligence process ==
Applicants must undergo identity verification, financial analysis, a juristictional risk assessment, and a review of criminal records and previous immigration history. These due dilligence processes are aligned with OECD and FATF recommendations, to ensure a rigorous evaluation process, to maintain national security. [ref: Luis Caputo anunció la puesta en marcha del Programa de Ciudadanía por Inversión de Argentina, Argentina.gob.ar]

==Background==

In April 2025, Argentina recieved emergency loans from the IMF and World Bank, with it's national economy being considered one of the world's most fragile in the world. The country has defaulted on or restructured parts of it's national debt multiple times in the 2020s. President Javier Milei intends the programme to attract wealthy investors, to 'strengthen the Argentine Republic's fiscal and financial position'. In 2025, the country lost 33 companies a day under his government.

Draft: Archaeolingusitics

Draft text:
Archeolinguistics is an interdisciplinary field that brings archaeology and linguistics together in an attempt to find out more about human past via the means of linguistic analysis.

Main branches of the field concern themselves with studies of evolution of language and symbolic thought via archaeological analysis of lithics and paleolithic art as well as methods coming from cognitive linguistics and theories of hominin evolution. This branch also uses historical linguistic and archaeology to study prehistoric migration patterns, diffusions of technology as well as reconstruction of proto-language. [ref: What is archaeolinguistics?, Glossographia]

Archeolinguistics also concerns itself with historic periods, like in case of archaeological decipherment of recovered, ancient texts. An example of that would be the decipherment of the Maya script by an English archaeologist, J. Eric S. Thompson and a Soviet linguist born in Ukraine, Yuri Walentinowicz Knorozow.

In case of historic periods, archaeolinguistics also focuses on studies of literacy, dialectal variations, language contact etc. and analysis of written texts in order to date objects and sites.

== History ==
Huxley and Darwin were among the first thinkers to integrate linguistics and archaeology. In “The Descent of man” (1865) the need of inclusion of linguistic diversity is highlighted. [ref: Archaeology, Genetics and Linguistic Diversity, Man]

“The Aryans” by Gordon Childe was published. There he argued for the homeland of Indo-Europeans in steppe areas of the northern Black Sea around the time of the late Neolithic. In his work, Childe used both archaeological and linguistic reasonings, second of which being mostly about the “core” vocabulary used for mostly plant and animals, especially for horses, in order to properly date the dispersal. All that was accompanied by his interpretations of findings from the Corded Ware culture. Childe’s work in “The Aryans” went on to inspire more archaeologists and linguists alike and became the base of the Kurgan Invasion Hypothesis. At the time it was a revolutionary work, which, despite numerous edits and criticisms, became widely accepted. However, archaeologists of the twenty first century have moved away from the hypothesis and continue the search. [ref: The Origins of Indo-European Languages, Scientific American]

Many German scholar joined the conversation of the origins of Indo-Europeans in the 30’ and 40’, generally placing the homeland in northern Europe. That work was then used by the Nazis to prove that the “original” language of Indo-Europeans was spoken by the master race of Aryans in Germany. Most of that research was weaponised by the Third Reich in their propaganda in order to push inferiority of other languages, most notably the Semitic ones.

Post-war most of that research was abandoned and other scholars became very careful about their findings in the filed.

In the following decades, linguists and archaeologists worked further. Many languages were grouped into families, such as the Indo-European one or Afro-Asiatic one, previously known as Hamito-Semitic, which are still widely accepted today. Some hypothesis about language connections however cause much controversies. Like in 1963, when an American linguist Joseph Greenberg proposed four language families of Africa: the Afro-Asiatic, the Nilo-Saharan, the Niger-Kordofanian and the Khoisan. Such taxonomy, modernly accepted, polarised the academic community, splitting linguist and enthusiasts into so-called “lumpers”; of similar views as Greenberg; and “splitters”, who believed the American linguist to be to generalising.

Greenberg’s classification of the Americas from 1987 brought even more antagonism, due to the division into just three families: the Amerind, the Na-Dene and the Inuit-Yupik-Unangan, originally called the Eskimo-Aleut family.

During 1980’, biological anthropology and archaeology’s combined efforts resulted in two vital conclusions. 1) that modern humankind, our own (sub)species Homo sapiens sapiens, evolved from its hominid predecessors in only one area and period, namely in southern Africa rather more than 100,000 years ago;
2) that full linguistic ability, the capacity for speech enjoyed by all living human groups, and the associated capacity for symbolic thought, seem to be characteristic of our species and ours alone.1990’ and early 2000’ saw a rise in the molecular approach and the new approach; focusing on DNA analysis.

== Approaches ==

=== Traditional approach – osteometry ===
This approach focuses on cranial, dental and other skeletal measurements. It was popular before 1970’, but even during it’s time of relevance it had rather low scientific value due to the similarities to racial typology and poor statistical methods.

In it’s later years, osteometry became characteristic of Russian archaeologists and linguists, who believed to had proven a gene flow western Iran to the Central Asia in the east. [ref: ]

=== Classical approach – biochemical methods ===
Osteometry was abandoned with the shifting towards biochemical methods and markers, such as blood groups, blood serum, proteins, antigens etc. The approach became more popular with the discovery that those biochemical systems fell under genetic determination. Another factor considered in this approach was phenotypic differences, such as Rhesus positive and Rhesus negative markers.

Tsismis Central (formerly Pinoy Circle Showbiz) is a Philippine entertainment news website and social media brand that covers local showbiz news, celebrity stories and Philippine television. Its name comes from tsismis, the Filipino word for gossip. The site publishes in Taglish, a mix of Tagalog and English, and runs on the Blogger platform. [ref: Tsismis Central]

== History ==
=== Pinoy Circle (2015) ===
The brand began in June 2015 as Pinoy Circle, a Filipino website and video page that posted short videos about news and stories from the Philippines.

=== Pinoy Circle Showbiz (2016) ===
In 2016, Pinoy Circle started Pinoy Circle Showbiz, a separate page for entertainment content. It covered showbiz news about Filipino celebrities and recaps of Philippine teleseryes.

=== YouTube channel hack (2024) ===
In December 2024, the Pinoy Circle YouTube channel was hacked. The hackers renamed the channel and used it to stream fake videos of Elon Musk promoting a cryptocurrency giveaway, a scam that hit many YouTube channels at the time. The owners were not able to get the channel back because of limited support from YouTube, and the brand moved its work to its other pages.

=== Rebrand to Tsismis Central (2026) ===
In September 2026, Pinoy Circle Showbiz was rebranded as Tsismis Central and moved to its own domain, tsismiscentral.com. Under the new name it posts short-form videos, called reels, which are shared on Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram and X.

== Content ==
Tsismis Central publishes:
* Showbiz news about Filipino actors, singers and public figures, based on reports from Philippine news outlets such as GMA Network and ABS-CBN.
* TV recaps of Philippine teleseryes, with a summary of each episode and its air date.
* Reels, short videos about the day's top showbiz stories, which are also placed inside the matching articles on the website.

Each variant is designed to perform specific roles. [ref: Ukraine unleashes 'Katran Venom' deadly new drone boat armed with torpedoes, missiles, and Miniguns]

However, the Katran drones are primarily noted for their versatility and their ability to complement one another during complex, multi-layered operations. In such scenarios, they are intended to operate not as individual naval drones, but as an integrated system. [ref: ]

== History ==
According to publicly available sources, the development of the Ukrainian unmanned surface vessels involved the same naval designer who had previously participated in the design of the russian cruiser Moskva. [ref: KATRAN – морський дрон, який може сам визначити та уразити ціль]

Representatives of the Ukrainian authorities have stated that detailed information regarding operations involving these drones remains limited in publicly available sources. [ref: Ukraine Unveils "Katran" Secret Naval Drone With 1,000 km Range, Armed With Torpedoes and Minigun, UNITED24 Media]

== Combat use ==
On the night of 21 September 2025, Katran naval drones were reportedly involved in an attack on the so-called “Boyko Towers.” According to published accounts, the unmanned surface vessels were equipped with FPV drones and fixed-wing aerial drones. In 2026, Ukrainian Defense Forces reportedly began using Katran naval drones not only to strike enemy targets but also to defend Ukrainian cities against Shahed-type UAVs. A Katran X1.2 can deploy 27 MAC Dead Fly interceptor drones. [ref: Ukraine-Krieg: „Die Russen sind weit hintendran“ – Die Strategie, mit der Kiew den Krieg entscheiden will - WELT, DIE WELT]

MAC HUB is also preparing the Katran family for a new type of mission: intercepting and seizing commercial vessels of the “shadow fleet” carrying sanctioned goods through the Black Sea. The vessels would be warned of their seizure and, following the arrest, escorted to port by Katran naval drones. Necropolis is a 1987 American horror film written and directed by Bruce Dickey and starring LeeAnne Baker, Jacquie Fitz, and Michael Conte. It was produced by Cynthia De Paula and Tim Kincaid. The original music score was composed by Don Great. The film was a Tycin Entertainment production and was distributed in the United States by Empire International Pictures.

The film's storyline concerns a reincarnated evil witch who absorbs the life force of her victims in order to achieve eternal youth.

== Plot ==
In New Amsterdam in 1686, Henry follows a beautiful and mysterious white-haired woman (Eva) through a desolate woodland to her lair, a ruined stone structure. A group of robed figures join Eva as she prepares a Satanic rite that will give them eternal life. Elsewhere, a preacher performs the wedding ceremony of William and Dawn. Eva uses witchcraft to make Dawn’s hand bleed, causing her to flee the wedding. Eva captures Dawn, eventually slitting her throat. William and Henry enter, stabbing Eva who vows to rise again and get her revenge.

In the modern era, Eva rides a motorcycle through New York City. She arrives at a store where she attempts to purchase a magic ring known as ‘the Devil’s Ring’ from a sleazy proprietor (Rudy) who admits he already sold it. Eva uses mind control to force Rudy to give her the buyer’s name (Reverend Henry James) before killing him. Eva travels to the Neighbourhood Center, an organization that serves marginalized youths and which is run by the Reverend. Eva asks the Reverend for help, claiming to be in danger. The Reverend tries to give her a crucifix, but she recoils.

Later that night, Eva travels back to the Neighbourhood Centre. Dawn Phillips, an NPR journalist, is interviewing the Reverend and one of his program participants, Philly, a former junkie and sex worker. Eva uses witchcraft to make Philly appear to be crashing from drug withdrawal, forcing Dawn and the Reverend take him to the hospital. Eva enters the Center, where she uses magic to convince the remaining staff member, Tony, to kill himself. Eva takes the key to the Reverend’s safe and leaves on her motorcycle. Now wearing the magical Devil’s Ring, Eva breaks into an abandoned factory, the site of her former lair. She summons her former followers, who now have a grotesque, zombie-like appearance.

Back at the Neighborhood Center, Tony’s body is surrounded by Benny (a medical examiner), Dawn, the Reverend, and NYPD Lieutenant Billy Cervetti. Benny declares Tony’s death a suicide. The Reverend attempts to convince Cervetti otherwise, insisting that something unusual is happening, but the officer is not swayed. Cervetti offers to drive Dawn home, but she suggests a drink instead. She takes Cervetti back to her place, where both agree that they feel like they’ve met before. Dawn suggests that they met in a previous life. They are in fact reincarnations of the Dawn and William- the couple whose marriage was stopped by Eva in the 1600s. Dawn flashes back to her earlier self’s throat being cut. Later, when Cervetti attempts to kiss her on the neck, she reveals an aversion to having her neck touched.

Eva sees a couple (Cat and Snake) making out. She charms Snake away, killing him and then branding with the pentagram inscribed on the Devil’s Ring. The act produces ectoplasm on the body. Eva then entrances Cat, arousing her latent homosexuality. Back at the factory, Eva grows four additional breasts which produces ectoplasm that she uses to feed her followers. Benny examines Cat’s body, which also has a pentagram brand. He writes it up as a cardiac arrest. Dawn and Cervetti argue over the actual cause of death.

A group of female prostitutes talk on a street corner. One of them, Candy, complains of a lack of customers, and gets a pep talk on the power of visualization from her pimp, Steady Eddie. Eddie leaves and Eva arrives, stealing a customer from them which she later kills. Cervetti, with Dawn riding along, is called to see the body. Once again Benny calls it a cardiac arrest but the Reverend disagrees. Back at the Neighbourhood Center, the Reverend explains to Dawn and Cervettti the nature of ectoplasm. Eva follows Dawn back to her apartment, then returns to Candy and the other prostitutes. Steady Eddie takes Eva to his car, where she kills him. Once again, Benny, Cervetti, the Reverend and Dawn attend the body. Candy tells them that a “witch” did it. Cervetti visits Rudy’s shop where he finds Eva’s Satanic altar and discovers Rudy’s dead body.

David S. Lawrence is the Fred Eshelman Distinguished Professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. He is known for his work in chemical biology, developing strategies for the design of self-assembling molecular systems, methods for detecting and manipulating protein kinase activity, and the construction of light-responsive proteins and drug delivery systems. [ref: Lawrence, David – APS2025] [ref: David S. Lawrence: Biology and Biochemistry Researcher – H-Index, Publications & Awards, Research.com]

== Education ==
Lawrence received his Bachelor of Science degree in the biological sciences from the University of California at Irvine. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy in chemistry from the University of California at Los Angeles in 1982, where he pursued the total synthesis of steroids and Vitamin D analogs. [ref: Vitamin B12: A Tunable, Long Wavelength, Light-Responsive Platform for Launching Therapeutic Agents, Accounts of Chemical Research]

== Career ==
Lawrence was a National Institutes of Health postdoctoral fellow at the Rockefeller University in New York City. He subsequently served as a professor in the Department of Chemistry at the State University of New York at Buffalo for 10 years. He joined the Department of Biochemistry at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine in 1996, and then moved to the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2007 as the Fred Eshelman Distinguished Professor. He was elected a fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 2005. [ref: Faculty in the American Association for the Advancement of Science, UNC Research] He holds affiliated appointments across multiple schools at the University of North Carolina and chaired the Division of Chemical Biology and Medicinal Chemistry in the UNC Eshelman School of Pharmacy from 2011 to 2025.

== Research ==
Lawrence's research in chemical biology explores the design of molecules that emulate or control biological processes. His work intersects the areas of supramolecular chemistry, cellular signaling, and targeted drug delivery. In the area of supramolecular chemistry, he created "self-assembling molecules by selecting component molecules whose parts carry different electric charges or are either attracted to or repelled by water...the molecules snap together automatically, like a self-assembling jigsaw puzzle." [ref: Chemists Make Molecule With Hint of Life, The New York Times] The assembled multicomponent entities mimic the oxygen carrying protein hemoglobin and the cytochrome P-450 family of proteins. [ref: Self-Assembly of Porphyrin Complex, Chemical & Engineering News Archive]

Lawrence also developed molecules programmed to target protein kinases, [ref: Purely Peptidic Enzyme Inhibitor Made, Chemical & Engineering News Archive] [ref: Cell Signaling Pathway Controlled By Light, Chemical & Engineering News Archive] signaling enzymes that, if mutated, can promote various cancers, as well as neurological, autoimmune, and cardiovascular diseases. Light-activated analogs of these protein kinase targeting molecules were designed as well, in order to "turn [signaling] pathways on and off non-invasively”. A collaborative research program with Zhong-Yin Zhang at Purdue University generated bidentate inhibitors for another family of signaling enzymes, protein tyrosine phosphatases, thereby furnishing "opportunities for drug discovery against diseases such as diabetes, cancer, autoimmune diseases, and tuberculosis". [ref: Bidentate Inhibitors of Protein Tyrosine Phosphatases, Antioxidants & Redox Signaling] Lawrence's lab also created a technology for delivering drugs to diseased sites using laser light. [ref: This Revolutionary New Tech Uses Light to Activate Medicine, Fortune] [ref: UNC-Chapel Hill researchers use light to launch drugs from red blood cells, Drug Discovery News] [ref: Using light, red blood cells and a honey bee peptide to deliver therapeutic proteins, ScienceDaily] [ref: Targeted Drug Delivery through Optical Control of Cell Lysis, ACS Central Science] This therapeutic platform has been licensed by Covalt Bio, a biotechnology company. [ref: Covalt Bio, Covalt Bio]

Christian G. Rodriguez (Born in 1984) is an American federal civil servant and veteran of the United States Air Force whose academic research focuses on leadership styles, job satisfaction, and person-organization fit within public sector institutions.

== Early Life and Education ==
Rodriguez graduated from Alta Loma High School [ref: Alta Loma High School, Chaffey Joint Union High School District] in Rancho Cucamonga, California, in 2002. [ref: Christian G. Rodriguez Research Profile, ResearchGate] In February 2016, he was inducted into the Grand Canyon University chapter of the Psi Chi International Honor Society in Psychology.

== Military Service ==
Rodriguez served 16 years in the United States Air Force, completing 10 years of active-duty service followed by six years in the Air Force Reserve.

== Career and Research ==
Rodriguez has served over two decades in public sector operations across state and federal levels. As a federal civil servant based in the Washington, D.C. area, he applies organizational behavior and behavioral science frameworks to public sector operations, administrative processes, and governance.

His scholarly work examines organizational dynamics within civil service and public administration. In 2020, he authored doctoral research titled An Examination of the Correlation Between Leadership Style and Job Satisfaction for Predicting Person-Organization Fit in Public Sector Organizations, investigating how supervisory leadership behaviors influence employee retention and organizational alignment among public sector personnel.

= Michael E. Smith (U.S. Navy admiral) =
Michael E. Smith is a retired United States Navy rear admiral and national security advocate. He served in the United States Navy for more than three decades, including as commander of Carrier Strike Group Three and president of the Navy's Board of Inspection and Survey. After retiring from active military service, he became involved in national security advocacy and founded National Security Leaders for America.

== Military career ==
Smith graduated from the United States Naval Academy in 1983 and subsequently completed nuclear power training. His early assignments included service aboard the guided-missile cruiser USS Texas and the destroyer USS Leftwich. He participated in Operation Desert Storm and later served in assignments connected with U.S. naval operations in the Mediterranean and the Persian Gulf.

Smith commanded the destroyer USS Porter and Destroyer Squadron 23. He also served as sea combat commander for the Nimitz Strike Group and as deputy task force commander for coalition maritime operations in the northern Persian Gulf.

His senior staff assignments included work in the offices of the Chief of Naval Operations, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the U.S. Pacific Fleet, and U.S. Pacific Command. He served as director of the Navy's Strategy and Policy Division and later commanded Carrier Strike Group Three.

His final active-duty assignment was president of the Board of Inspection and Survey, which evaluates the material condition and operational readiness of Navy ships and submarines. Smith retired from active duty in 2015. His military awards include the Bronze Star Medal for combat service.

== Post-military career ==
Following his retirement from the Navy, Smith worked in national security advocacy and writing. He has contributed commentary on national security and East Asian affairs to publications including 38 North and The National Interest. He has also served as president of the American College of National Security Leaders.

Smith founded and leads National Security Leaders for America, an organization of former senior national security officials that advocates for democratic institutions and constitutional principles.

== Political advocacy ==
Smith became publicly involved in presidential politics during the 2024 United States presidential election. Through National Security Leaders for America, he participated in efforts opposing Donald Trump's return to the presidency. The organization endorsed Democratic presidential nominee Kamala Harris.

Smith has also publicly criticized actions by the Trump administration that he argues threaten democratic norms, the nonpartisan character of the armed forces, and national security. His public commentary has addressed military leadership, civil-military relations, and the consequences of political decisions for the U.S. military.

Draft: Dar Erengà

Draft text:
Dar Erenga is a historical and geographical region located in the northern part of West Darfur State, Sudan. Situated along the modern Sudan–Chad border, the region historically functioned as a transitional corridor linking various sultanates in western Sudan. Its administrative and territorial boundaries were formally documented in early 20th-century treaties. Geographically and historically, Dar Erenga forms part of Dar Masalit and is situated between the Masalit country proper and Dar Qimr. [ref: Darfur Linguistics, Sudan Notes and Records]

==== Geography and Administrative Boundaries ====
The region is centered in northern West Darfur, where its lands (hawakir) border several historical territories:North: It shares borders with Dar Tama (extending toward Tumtuma) and Dar Jebel near the town of Sileia.
• South: It opens directly into Dar Masalit, situated immediately north of the city of El Geneina and the town of Adré. West: The frontier runs parallel to the international border along the strategic cross-border axis leading to Dar Sila.In his 1924 study on the Masalit Sultanate, British administrator Reginald Davies documented this administrative layout, noting that Dar Erenga formed a crucial geographical and political link between Dar Masalit to the south and Dar Jebel and Dar Qimr to the northeast. [ref: The Masalit Sultanate, Sudan Notes and Records] [ref: Darfur – Livelihoods Under Siege, Feinstein International Famine Center, Tufts University]

==== Ethnic Composition and History ====
The history of Dar Erenga is linked to a confederation of closely related ethnic groups, including the Awra, Asungor, Mararit, Girga, Dula, and Shali.
Historical records indicate that "Dar Erenga" began to emerge as a unified administrative entity in the late 1880s. Prior to this consolidation, each ethnic group maintained its own local leadership within the western Darfur administrative framework.
The explorer Gustav Nachtigal described these groups as distinct yet interconnected entities sharing a common lineage with the Qimr (Guimir). Nachtigal historically referred to the area on the eastern bank of Wadi Kaja as "Dar Shali," which later integrated into the core geography of contemporary Dar Erenga. [ref: Mahdisme et tradition au Dar For: Histoire des Massalit 1870–1930, E.J. Brill]

==== Settlements and Hydrology ====
Human settlement and economic activity in Dar Erenga are highly dependent on seasonal watercourses (wadis). The town of Sirba serves as the historical capital and primary administrative hub of the region. Further north, the settlement of Abu Qurayn acts as a transitional point bordering Dar Jebel.
The region's agricultural and pastoral life is sustained by two main seasonal valleys: Wadi Kaja, which flows through the eastern sector, and Wadi Asunga, which delineates the western border with the Republic of Chad. [ref: Mahdisme et tradition au Dar For: Histoire des Massalit 1870–1930, E.J. Brill]

==== International Legal Status ====
The boundaries of Dar Erenga were recognized under international law through the 1919 British-French boundary agreements, which were annexed to the Milner-Berthelot convention. On the official maps attached to the treaty, "Dar Erenga" was explicitly marked by name as a recognized territorial entity within the basins of Wadi Kaja and Wadi Asunga along the boundary. [ref: Treaty Series No. 6 (1921): Convention between the United Kingdom and France respecting Boundary Delimitation in West Africa (1919), Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (UK Treaties Online)]

Under the 1953 Anglo-Egyptian Agreement concerning self-government for the Sudan, Dar Erenga was formally incorporated into the "Dar Masalit North" electoral constituency (Constituency No. 59) alongside Geneina Town, Dar Jebel, Dar Gimr, Zaghawa Kubja, and adjacent Arab Omodias. [ref: "Agreement between the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland and the Egyptian Government concerning Self-Government and Self-Determination for the Sudan", Cairo, February 12, 1953, Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (UK)]

== References ==

==Early life and education==
Ananta Mandal spent his childhood in Chakdaha, West Bengal. He has a degree in Fine Arts from the Government College of Art & Craft, Kolkata, Calcutta University in 2007. Mandal stayed in Kolkata from 2002 to 2007, during this period he began painting scenes of everyday life in Kolkata. In 2008 he moved to Mumbai. Draft text:
Valentine Eckert (1733 – December 1821) was a German-born Pennsylvania politician, militia officer, and judge active during and after the American Revolution. He represented Berks County in the Pennsylvania Provincial Conference and the Pennsylvania Constitutional Convention of 1776, served in the Pennsylvania Assembly, commanded militia during the Revolutionary War, and later served for seven years as a judge of the Berks County Court of Common Pleas. [ref: History of Berks County, Pennsylvania, in the Revolution, from 1774 to 1783] [ref: J. W. Vandervort, "The Supreme Court of West Virginia", Part I, The Green Bag, vol. 12 (1900), pp. 188–189.]

==Early life==
Born in Langenselbold, in present-day Hesse, Germany, [ref: Historical and Biographical Annals of Berks County, Pennsylvania] he emigrated to Pennsylvania with his parents in 1741, with the family settling in the Tulpehocken Valley, east of present-day Womelsdorf. He was naturalized in September 1761, and worked as a blacksmith in Cumru Township. [ref: Biographical Publishing Company, Biographical Sketched of Leading Citizens of Berks County, Pennsylvania (1898), p. 99.] Eckert was a slaveholder, in 1773 placing an advertisement in The Pennsylvania Gazette offering a reward for the return of an enslaved man named Joe who had escaped Eckert's property in Cumru Township. [ref: Berks County, Pennsylvania Slaveholders A–Z, Afrolumens]

==Political and military career==
In June 1776, Eckert was one of ten Berks County delegates to the Provincial Conference held at Carpenters' Hall in Philadelphia. The conference called for the election of a constitutional convention to establish a new government based on the authority of the people. The following month, Eckert was elected as one of eight Berks County delegates to the Provincial Convention that drafted the Pennsylvania Constitution of 1776.

Eckert was elected to represent Berks County in Pennsylvania's Provincial Assembly in 1776, 1777, and 1779. During the American Revolutionary War, he offered his services to the revolutionary government, which were accepted. He commanded a company of cavalry Associators and participated in the Battle of Germantown, in October, 1777, where he was wounded. Having been appointed Sub-Lieutenant of the county on March 21, 1777, he also served in this office until his promotion to Lieutenant of the County in January, 1781. He continued to act as Lieutenant until the close of the war. While serving as Sub-Lieutenant, he also acted as a commissioner for the purchase of army supplies.

On March 1, 1780, he was among the legislators who voted against the Act for the Gradual Abolition of Slavery, and he joined the formal protest entered by legislators opposed to the measure. [ref: An Historical Memoir of the Pennsylvania Society for Promoting the Abolition of Slavery] He returned to the Assembly again on January 16, 1784, replacing John Bishop, who had declined his seat. [ref: Pennsylvania General Assembly – 1783–4, Wilkes University] As county lieutenant, Eckert was also involved in the supervision of prisoners of war being held at Reading. In June 1781, he reported that approximately 1,100 prisoners had arrived in the area and corresponded with Pennsylvania president Joseph Reed concerning their guarding and accommodation. Eckert, Major Bayly, and Colonel Wood were charged with selecting a site outside Reading where the prisoners could be housed in huts. [ref: Prisoners of War in the American Revolution: A Community Perspective, Military Affairs]

==Judicial service and later life==
In 1784, he was appointed judge of the Court of Common Pleas of the county and occupied this office for a term of seven years, when, by the Pennsylvania Constitution of 1790, a president judge of all the courts was appointed to take the place of the several judges. In the Pennsylvania Militia, he was brigade inspector for the county from April 11, 1793, for a period of 20 years.

Around 1816 he moved to Winchester, Virginia, where he died in December 1821 at the age of 88. His son, Peter Eckert, was engaged in farming and merchandising all his life in Berks County, near Womelsdorf, the family home.

==References==

==External links==
* "[https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-pennsylvania-gazette/99458684/ A petition from Valentine Eckert, of the county of Berks]", The Pennsylvania Gazette (January 25, 1786), p. 2.

Markpain (born Mark Wilson; also credited as Mark Andrew Wilson) is an American hip-hop and R&B record producer and songwriter from New York. He is best known as a co-writer of Bell Biv DeVoe's 1993 single "Above the Rim", and was a featured performer on "1-4-All-4-1" from the 1992 compilation East Coast Family Volume One. Both parent albums were certified Gold by the RIAA. He is the founder of the independent label 50 Producers.

== Career ==
=== BIV10 era ===
In the early 1990s Wilson was part of Michael Bivins' Biv 10 Records/Motown circle, performing as one half of the duo Mark Finesse. In 1992 he appeared as a featured performer on "1-4-All-4-1", a track from East Coast Family Volume One that also featured Boyz II Men; the album was certified Gold. In 1993 he co-wrote "Above the Rim", the lead single from Bell Biv DeVoe's second album Hootie Mack, including Michael Bivins' rap verse; [ref: Shazam – "Above the Rim": "Mike's Rap (Co Written By Mark Wilson AKA Markpain)". https://www.shazam.com/song/1440770407/above-the-rim] He is also credited as a co-writer of "Lovely", another track from the album. [ref: "Hootie Mack" album credits, Qobuz: "Lovely" lists Mark Wilson among the composers/lyricists. https://www.qobuz.com/gb-en/album/hootie-mack-bell-biv-devoe/0060252740442] Hootie Mack was certified Gold by the RIAA on August 25, 1993, and the single charted on Billboard's Hot R&B Singles chart. [ref: "Above the Rim (song)", Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Above_the_Rim_(song); "Hootie Mack", Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hootie_Mack] "Above the Rim" was later featured in HBO's 2025 docuseries Celtics City.

=== Production work and 50 Producers ===
Wilson has worked as a producer and engineer for other artists, including Positive K (the 2022 singles "I Get It Done" and "Nobody") and Kool Kim of The UMCs ("Don't Talk No More", 2023), and wrote and produced "Make It Hot" for DJ Epps. In the 2020s he founded 50 Producers, an independent imprint distributed by EMPIRE, through which he releases his own instrumental albums, including the Instruments of Pain series. His compositions are original works created without samples, which he licenses for film, television, and advertising.

Draft text:
Expo Agrofuturo is an annual trade fair for the agriculture and agribusiness sector held in Colombia. It brings together producers, traders, suppliers of machinery, inputs and technology, investors and financial institutions, and combines exhibition halls with business matchmaking and a conference programme. [ref: Informe de feria: Expo Agrofuturo 2022, Economic and Commercial Office of the Embassy of Spain in Bogotá; ICEX] Since 2018 it has been organised in partnership with Corferias, alternating between Medellín, at the Plaza Mayor convention centre, and Bogotá, at the Corferias fairgrounds. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo se extiende y llegará a Bogotá en 2018, Agronegocios]

== History ==
The fair began in Medellín, where its early editions took place at Plaza Mayor. Its fifth edition, directed by Ricardo Jaramillo Gaviria, was held in June 2011 and included the third International Agricultural Congress and the second International Livestock Forum. [ref: Inicia en Medellín Quinta Feria Expo Agrofuturo 2011, ABC Economía] The ninth edition took place at the same venue in 2015, [ref: Aprenda y conozca las innovaciones del campo en Expo Agrofuturo 2015, CONtexto Ganadero] and the tenth from 7 to 9 September 2016. [ref: Este 7 de septiembre empieza el VIII Congreso Internacional Agropecuario, Semana]

The eleventh edition, in 2017, drew around 25,000 visitors from some 30 countries and 420 participating companies. That year a strategic partnership with Corferias was announced, under which the fair would be held in Bogotá in even-numbered years and in Medellín in odd-numbered years. Accordingly, the 2018 edition took place at Corferias from 22 to 24 August. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo 2018: Regulamento de participação, Apex-Brasil] In 2019 the fair returned to Plaza Mayor from 18 to 20 September, with Italy as guest country of honour. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo: el campo colombiano se reúne en Medellín, Portafolio] [ref: Lanzamiento de la feria Expo Agrofuturo 2019 se llevó a cabo en la ciudad de Medellín, La República]

The fifteenth edition was held at Corferias from 26 to 28 October 2022, with the European Union as guest of honour. According to a report by the Economic and Commercial Office of the Spanish Embassy, it featured more than 350 exhibitors, about 120 talks and over 11,000 professional visitors. The sixteenth edition returned to Medellín from 6 to 8 September 2023. [ref: Expoagrofuturo regresa a Medellín para el desarrollo de un agro más inteligente y sostenible, CONtexto Ganadero]

The seventeenth edition (Bogotá, 2024) had more than 320 exhibitors from 15 countries and 13,500 attendees, with the department of Casanare as guest region. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo cerró con expectativas de negocio por US$6,16 millones, Portafolio] The eighteenth edition was held at Plaza Mayor from 10 to 12 September 2025, with 388 exhibitors from Colombia and eleven other countries and 14,154 visitors. [ref: Expo Agrofuturo Concludes with Over 14,000 Attendees and Nearly $6 Million USD in Projected Business Deals, Finance Colombia]

The 2026 edition took place at Corferias from 21 to 23 October. [ref: El conocimiento del agro se transforma: así será la gran novedad de Expo Agrofuturo 2026, Publimetro Colombia] It hosted the first International Meeting of Market Squares (Encuentro Internacional de Plazas de Mercado). [ref: Bogotá será sede del Primer Encuentro Internacional de Plazas de Mercado en Expo Agrofuturo 2026, Noticias RCN]

== Organisation ==
The fair is organised by the company Agrilink together with Corferias. In 2018 the organisers were listed as Grupo NovoAgro and Corferias. Its spokespeople have included co-founder Ricardo Jaramillo [ref: Medellín se consolida como una plataforma para promover el campo inteligente en Latinoamérica, Publimetro Colombia] and Doris Chingaté, Expo Agrofuturo project manager at Corferias.

== Programme ==
Alongside the commercial halls, organised by production sector such as fruit and vegetables, livestock and machinery, or grains, oils and forestry, the fair includes several parallel spaces:

* FIXA (Agrofuturo Innovation Forum): the fair's academic component, traditionally split into one day devoted to livestock and another to agriculture. In 2026 it was reorganised as a "knowledge ecosystem" with six themed spaces across the venue, covering technology, productivity, agribusiness, livestock, entrepreneurship and finance.
* AgStar: a space for startups in the AgTech, FoodTech and AnimalTech categories.
* Business matchmaking: meetings between exhibitors and domestic and international buyers. In 2025, under the name AgroMatch, it connected 160 exhibitors with 33 buyers in 459 meetings.
* Agrotalks and Agrosolutions: exhibitor presentations and free advisory sessions for attendees.

Draft text:
Erwin Horn (2 May 1929 – 13 May 2006) was a German teacher and politician of the Social Democratic Party (SPD). He was a member of the Bundestag from 1969 to 1998, representing the Gießen constituency in Hesse by direct mandate for most of that period. He was deputy chairman of the Bundestag's Defence Committee from 1980 to 1983.

== Early life and education ==

Horn was born in Annerod, a village near Gießen that is now part of Fernwald. He was a Protestant. After attending a Volksschule and an Aufbauschule, he passed his Abitur in 1948. From 1949 to 1955 he studied history, German, English, philosophy and politics, and took the state examination for teachers in 1955.

== Teaching career ==

Horn worked as a Studienrat from 1955 to 1962. From 1962 to 1966 he was Fachleiter (subject supervisor) for social studies at the teacher training seminar (Studienseminar) in Gießen. From 1966 to 1969 he was headmaster (Oberstudiendirektor) of the Gymnasium in Nidda.

== Political career ==

=== Local politics ===

Horn chaired the SPD sub-district (Unterbezirk) of Gießen from 1962 to 1988. He was a member of the district council (Kreistag) from 1960 to 1976.

=== Member of the Bundestag ===

Horn was elected to the Bundestag in the 1969 federal election. He won the Gießen constituency in each election from 1969 to 1994 except 1983, when he entered parliament through the SPD's Hesse state list. He did not stand in the 1998 election and left the Bundestag at the end of the 13th legislative term.

He was deputy chairman of the Defence Committee from 1980 to 1983 and the SPD's Obmann (lead member) on the committee from 1983 to 1990. From 1977 to 1988 he was a member of the executive board of the SPD parliamentary group. During the 13th legislative term he was a deputy member of the Foreign Affairs Committee and, from 1997, a deputy member of the Defence Committee.

In the Bundestag debate of 21–22 November 1983 on the deployment of American intermediate-range missiles under the NATO Double-Track Decision, Horn spoke for the SPD. He said the decision had become a source of dispute within the alliance and a burden on domestic politics in the countries where the missiles were to be stationed. He said the SPD had originally regarded the decision as a means of bringing the superpowers to negotiations on disarmament, and that the deployment would not change the global strategic balance. The Bundestag approved the deployment with the votes of the CDU/CSU and FDP.

In 1990, during the debate on the equipment of the former East German National People's Army, Horn proposed that the Bundeswehr take over all of its MiG-29 fighter aircraft and that Germany withdraw from the Jäger 90 project. He said that scrapping usable weapons while placing new arms contracts could not be justified given the level of public debt.

=== International assemblies ===

Horn was a member of the North Atlantic Assembly. He chaired its Military Committee from 1981 to 1985 and its socialist group from 1985 to 1988. He was part of the German delegation to the assembly's spring session in Paris in May 1990. He was a substitute member of the German delegation to the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe from 1981 to 1984 and from 1995 to 1999, and a deputy member of the Assembly of the Western European Union.

== Conviction ==

In 1990 a Schöffengericht (lay-judge court) in Cologne fined Horn 24,000 DM for false unsworn testimony and attempted obstruction of prosecution. The court found that he had made false statements in a traffic case against a master mason from Bornheim. Horn had been a passenger in the man's car in April 1988 when it damaged another vehicle while leaving a parking space in central Cologne and drove away. The driver was convicted of leaving the scene of an accident.

== Death ==

Horn died on 13 May 2006.

== Honours ==

* 1983: Cross of Merit, 1st Class (Verdienstkreuz 1. Klasse) of the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany
* 1988: Grand Cross of Merit (Großes Verdienstkreuz) of the Order of Merit of the Federal Republic of Germany

Originating from the indie web series [https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/battle-for-dream-island/1060525925 Battle for Dream Island], the microgenre of object shows was conceptualized sometime during 2008 with Total Firey Island, and officially became a noted trope during 2011-2013. The most major parts of the style are anthropomorphic objects with black stick-line limbs and "doodle" faces. They were animated on Adobe Flash the majority of the time, however as of now they are made on a variety of platforms such as the animation app Flipaclip, sometimes even using unconventional applications such as Google Slides, another early software used in the 2011-2013 era. The first and most well-known object show, BFDI, was created by Cary and Michael Huang. [ref: BFDI 2: Barriers and Pitfalls]

The official community, or often referred to as a fanbase of the microgenre, is the Object Show Community, commonly shortened to OSC. The TikTok branch of the fandom is referred to as OSCTT (Standing for Object Show Community Tiktok). Other object shows, such as Inanimate Insanity (the unofficial 'sister show' to BFDI) or One (called hfjone to avoid confusion and to clarify its creator, Cheesy Hfj) are common examples of it.

As of 2020 and onwards, the Object Show Community has experienced a massive growth in interest, with Gen Alpha taking root in it. There are also many major controversies tied to the fandom, though are not listed.
