Draft: Faith Tabernacle Congregation

Draft text:
Faith Tabernacle Congregation is a Christian Fundamentalist non-denominational church based in Philadelphia. The church was started in 1897 as an off-shoot of John Alexander Dowie's faith-healing ministry. Faith Tabernacle Congregation has been the subject of controversy due to its belief in faith healing and rejection of modern medicine. Faith Tabernacle Congregation was prominently involved in the 1990-91 Philadelphia measles outbreak.

== Origin ==
In 1896, Jacob Wilhide established a divine healing ministry in Philadelphia. [ref: Out of Zion Into Philadelphia and West Africa: Faith Tabernacle Congregation, 1897-1925, Pneuma] He aimed to spread John Alexander Dowie's faith healing ministry and establish a divine healing church. This church was not officially associated with the Dowie's Christian Catholic Church, but Dowie later integrated Wilhide's Philadelphia Ministry into his own church.

John Wesley Ankins was a member of Wilhide's faith healing mission, and was one of the first people baptized into it. Ankins quickly rose into a leadership role alongside Wilhide. In 1897, he established his own separate meeting in 1897. He called this Gospel Mission, and associated himself with Wilhide's mission in 1898. However, by 1899, Ankins had separated his own mission from Wilhide and Dowie's.

In 1904, Ankins's Gospel Mission purchased a church building that it had been using for the past seven years and renamed itself to Faith Tabernacle Congregation. In 1907, Faith Tabernacle opened a healing home, modeled after those of the Christian Catholic Church.

Faith Tabernacle Congregation gathered new members through distributing free literature. The primary publications were entitled Sword of the Spirit and Leaves of Healing. Correspondence was also published internationally, which led to the formation of branches of Faith Tabernacle Congregation in Nigeria and Ghana.

== Beliefs ==
Faith Tabernacle follows a fundamentalist interpretation of the bible. Most notably, the church preaches a literal belief in praying to heal the sick, as well as rejection of modern medicine. [ref: Bad Faith: When Religious Belief Undermines Modern Medicine, Basic Books] This includes prohibition of vaccination, glasses, hearing aids, and over-the-counter painkillers. [ref: God's will vs. medicine: Does Faith Tabernacle beliefs put children at risk?, pennlive] Faith Tabernacle Congregation also prohibits drinking alcohol, smoking cigarettes, and premarital sex. Women are forbidden to wear pants and are expected to be subservient to their husbands. [ref: When Prayer Fails: Faith Healing, Children, and the Law, Oxford Academic] Faith Tabernacle Congregation preaches against associating with members not in the church, which leads to members who leave the church being shunned. Some former members have called Faith Tabernacle Congregation a cult. [ref: From fear to freedom: Family urges others to leave faith-healing church they call a cult, WHP] [ref: Former 'cult' members call for Pennsylvania church to be shut down, investigated, WHP]

== 1990–1991 Philadelphia measles outbreak ==

Faith Tabernacle Congregation gained national attention during the 1990-91 measles outbreak in Philadelphia. The outbreak was declared in October 1990. On January 16, 1991, the Philadelphia Health Commission received an anonymous call detailing the caller's granddaughter who was sick with measles. [ref: A 1990 Measles Outbreak Shows How the Disease Can Roar Back, The New York Times] The caller believed that measles was spreading at Faith Tabernacle School, a private school for children of church members. On February 7, a 9-year-old Faith Tabernacle School Student died of measles. The Philadelphia Health Commissioner, Dr. Robert Ross, then asked Pastor Charles Reinert to vaccinate Faith Tabernacle School Students. He refused, citing a belief in prayer to heal the sick, but did agree to give Ross addresses and phone numbers of members of the church. The commissioner started calling members of the church and asked them to report sick children. However, a child from one of the families Ross had called died a few days after he had called them. Due to the refusal of members of the church to report sick children, Commissioner Ross obtained a court order allowing him to compel medical treatment for sick children against their parents' will and to compel vaccinations for children.

Out of the 9 children that died in the outbreak, 6 of them were members of Faith Tabernacle Congregation and First Century Gospel Church, an off-shoot with similar faith-healing beliefs. [ref: 1991: The Philly measles outbreak that killed 9 children, 6abc Philadelphia] 438 of the 1,424 measles cases reported were among members of Faith Tabernacle Congregation and First Century Gospel Church. [ref: High attack rates and case fatality during a...: Pediatric Infectious Disease Journal, Ovid] Members of the two churches were roughly 1,000 times more likely to catch the disease than non-members, and roughly 4 times more likely to die from the disease than non-members.

Bilal Dayani (; born 22 July 1964) is a media executive based in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. He is the chief operating officer of Eagle Films Middle East, a film distribution and production company. [ref: Abu Dhabi Film Commission announces multifaceted enhancements to the 35% rebate programme, Abu Dhabi Media Office] He previously spent fourteen years as executive general manager of the Saudi music label and distributor Megastar, [ref: «شعبية الكرتون» إلى الإنجليزية, Emarat Al Youm] and in 2004 was president of the Arab Music Academy in Dubai, which organised the first Arab Music Awards. [ref: المستمعون يصوّتون للفنانين والفنانون يصوّتون لبعضهم: المهرجان الأول لجوائز الموسيقى العربية, As-Safir] In 2005 Ahlan! magazine included him in its list of the 100 most prominent faces of UAE society. [ref: بلال دياني, Ahlan! (Arabic edition)]

== Early life ==
Dayani was born on 22 July 1964. He is of Syrian nationality and worked in Saudi Arabia before moving to Dubai in the late 1990s.

== Career ==

=== Saudi Arabia and the music industry (1985–2009) ===
Dayani worked in the Saudi media sector from the mid-1980s. In 1995 he joined Al Faisaliah Group as executive general manager of Megastar Home Entertainment, a music label and distributor, a post he held until 2009. At Megastar he was responsible for the production and regional distribution of Arabic albums and music videos by artists including Samira Said, Amal Arafa, Fairuz and Nancy Ajram, and for the distribution of international record labels in the MENA region.

In February 2004 he became president of the Arab Music Academy, a Dubai-based body formed to promote Arabic music and to address piracy and intellectual-property issues facing producers and distributors. The academy organised the first Arab Music Awards, in which winners in 24 categories were chosen by public vote and the ceremony, in Dubai, was to be broadcast by Future TV. Dayani hosted the awards ceremony.

=== Eagle Films Middle East ===
Dayani joined Eagle Films Middle East in the mid-2010s [ref: «لف ودوران».. كوميديا السهل الممتنع, [[Al Bayan (newspaper)] and is the company's chief operating officer. The company distributes international films in the Middle East and produces Arabic television series and films. [ref: تعرف على تفاصيل "قصتي" الذي يجسد حياة محمد بن راشد وموعد العرض والقنوات الناقلة, UAE Barq]

In 2020 he was operations manager of My Story (Qesaty), a docudrama series executive-produced by Eagle Films for the Executive Office of Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum and broadcast on Dubai TV by Dubai Media Incorporated, based on the memoir My Story: 50 Memories from Fifty Years of Service. [ref: «قصتي» سيرة محمد بن راشد في برنامج وثائقي درامي, [[Al Bayan (newspaper)] [ref: إطلالة تلفزيونية جديدة بأسلوب درامي مبتكر, Emarat Al Youm] [ref: العمل الدرامي التوثيقي الأول من نوعه "قصتي" يعرض مراحل حياة محمد بن راشد على مدار 50 حلقة, Government of Dubai Media Office]

In December 2022 Eagle Films received the Excellence in Arabic-Language Productions award at the ASBU BroadcastPro ME Awards in Dubai; Dayani accepted the award on the company's behalf. [ref: Raising the curtain: applauding the best of the best in MENA media and entertainment at the 2022 BroadcastPro Awards, BroadcastPro ME] According to the Abu Dhabi Film Commission, Eagle Films produced the series From Al Haram Street To... and Milh Wa Samrah in Abu Dhabi under his supervision, using the emirate's production rebate programme, [ref: Eagle Films ME, COO, Bilal Dayani, has produced numerous successful projects in Abu Dhabi, Abu Dhabi Film Commission] and in December 2024 he was quoted in the Commission's announcement of enhancements to that programme.

In April 2019, Eagle Films was among the film distributors and cinema operators that signed memoranda of understanding with the UAE National Media Council under its National Program to Support Emirati Films, an initiative to extend the theatrical run and promotion of Emirati films. [ref: 16 جهة متخصصة تدعم تسويق السينما المحلية, Emarat Al Youm] [ref: «الوطني للإعلام».. برنامج لدعم صنّاع السينما الإماراتية, [[Al-Ittihad (newspaper)] [ref: "الوطني للإعلام" يطلق البرنامج الوطني لدعم الأفلام الإماراتية, Emirates News Agency]

=== Media appearances ===
Dayani has appeared as a commentator on CNBC Arabia, discussing the commercial state of Arab cinema [ref: السينما العربية.. هل هي في المقاعد الخلفية؟, CNBC Arabia] and whether streaming platforms will displace traditional television. [ref: هل تنجح المنصات الرقمية في إنهاء عصر التلفزيون التقليدي؟, CNBC Arabia] He spoke on the panel "Ramadan and Beyond: The Year-Round Content Formula" at the Dubai International Content Market in 2025. [ref: Speakers, Dubai International Content Market]

Jules Désiré Bourdais (born April 6, 1835 in Brest, France; died June 2, 1915 in Paris) was a French architect.

Bourdais is best known for designing the Trocadéro Palace with Gabriel Davioud and for creating a design for a stone column for the 1889 World's Fair, the Colonne Soleil (Sun Column), which would have rivaled the Eiffel Tower.

==Biography==
Jules Désiré Bourdais was born on April 6, 1835, in Brest, France, to Jean Julien Bourdais, a ship's captain and officer of the Legion of Honour, [ref: Recherche - Base de données Léonore, www.leonore.archives-nationales.culture.gouv.fr] and Fanny Marie Louise Valéri. Bourdais graduated from the École Centrale Paris in 1857. He married Blanche Marie Juliette Fauvelet de Charbonnière in 1867.

Between 1868 and 1870, Bourdais designed the Saint-Pierre-ès-Liens church and the Protestant church in Nègrepelisse. During the Franco-Prussian War in 1870, Bourdais served as a lieutenant in the engineering corps. Between 1876 and 1878, Bourdais and Gabriel Davioud designed the town hall for the 19th arrondissement of Paris and in May 1876, Bourdais and Davioud won a competition to design the Trocadéro Palace.

In 1881, Bourdais created a design for a "sun column" – a granite tower topped with a beacon that would be capable of illuminating all of Paris as far as Neuilly-sur-Seine, Levallois-Perret, and the Bois de Boulogne. In 1886, with the support of engineer Amédée Sébillot, [ref: Musée d'Orsay: Jules Bourdais, Phare monumental] Bourdais submitted his design proposal to a competition for the 1889 World's Fair, but lost to Gustave Eiffel's proposal for the Eiffel Tower.

Bourdais died at his residence in the 16th arrondissement of Paris on June 2, 1915, [ref: Visionneuse - Archives de Paris, archives.paris.fr.] and was buried in the Montmartre Cemetery. [ref: Cimetière de Montmartre-Répertoire annuel d'inhumation: Aaron-Bourgeois (1912-1920)]

Karlis Beinerts (born April 1952, Latvia) is a Latvian choir conductor and music pedagogue, best known as the long-serving director of the Riga 3rd Music School (Rīgas 3. mūzikas skola) [https://katalogs-iksd.riga.lv/lv/Iestade/R3MS [16]] — a post he has held since December 1982 — and as the founder and conductor of the school’s children’s choir “Varavīksne” (“Rainbow”). He has also conducted the youth chamber choir “Daugaviņa” and the National mixed choir “Rīga”, and has appeared as a chief conductor (virsdiriģents) at Latvian Song Festivals.
----Early life and education

Beinerts studied music for about twenty years: first at the Emīls Dārziņš Special Music School (Riga), and then at the Jāzeps Vītols Latvian State Conservatory, where he earned a bachelor’s degree in conducting; after the conservatory was renamed the Latvian Academy of Music (Jāzeps Vītols Latvian Academy of Music), he also completed a master’s degree in music.

His conducting teachers included Krišs Deķis, Jānis Dūmiņš, Gido Kokars, Eriks Eriksons and Mariss Jansons. As a boy, he sang in the Riga boys’ choir circles led by Krišs Deķis, together with his older brother Zigurds Beinerts (later an engineer-mechanic). In his youth he also took part in amateur youth choirs.[[:lv:Jānis_Dūmiņš|[15]]]

In 1985, at the young conductors’ competition dedicated to the centenary of Emīls Dārziņš, Beinerts was awarded first place. [https://www.rsu.lv/aktualitates/dziesmu-svetku-virsdirigentam-un-rsu-goda-doktoram-janim-duminam-100 [1]]

Career

Riga 3rd Music School

In December 1982, Beinerts was appointed director of the Riga 3rd Music School — at the time the youngest school director in Latvia; by 2020 he was described as the longest-serving music school director in the country. In his 2020 essay in Latvijas Avīze he wrote critically about the state of Latvian music education: falling enrolment, the replacement of graded assessment with descriptive feedback, and what he saw as a growing bureaucratic burden on schools. The essay is titled “Par kļūdām izglītībā nākas maksāt dārgu cenu” (“For mistakes in education one pays a high price”). [https://www.la.lv/darga-cena [2]]

Choirs

* “Varavīksne” (“Rainbow”), Riga 3rd Music School children’s choir. When Beinerts became the school’s director in 1982 he opened the school’s choir class; the choir grew from 8 singers in its first year to a collective of up to 40 singers aged 8–18. In 1995 the choir won 1st place and Grand Prix at the competition of Latvian music school choirs organised by Latvian Radio. Its repertoire ranges from Bach, Mozart, Pergolesi, Cherubini, Mendelssohn, Schubert, Fauré, Grieg and Rachmaninoff to Latvian choral music. The choir has premiered large-scale works by composer Ingmars Zemzaris (Magnificat, Stabat Mater, Ofertorium de venerabili, Missa Brevis, Nisi Dominus, an Advent oratorio, and the cycle Ar māti pie baznīcas), recorded a Christmas-album CD with tenor Žoržs Siksna, appeared in Latvian National Opera productions (Turandot, Tosca, Uguns un Nakts, Noah’s Ark), and took part in the Latvian premiere of Mauricio Kagel’s Sankt-Bach-Passion with the Latvian National Symphony Orchestra and the choir “Latvija” on 1 April 2000. It has toured Denmark, Germany, England and Wales, Sweden, Finland and Estonia, and its recordings have been broadcast on Latvian, Danish and Swedish radio and on Latvian, Welsh and German television. [https://www.r3ms.lv/gallery/skolas-kolektivi/koris-varaviksne/ [3]]
* “Daugaviņa.” A youth chamber choir led by Beinerts; under him it won first place in the “choir war” (kora kari) at the 1985 Latvian Song Festival. The choir performed in the landmark 1988 Riga staging of the rock opera “Lāčplēsis” (director Valdis Lūriņš, conductor Zigmars Liepiņš). [https://enciklopedija.lv/skirklis/111395 [4]][https://labsalv.blogspot.com/2009/07/rokopera-lacplesis.html [5]] In 2013 he led the group of mixed choirs (Daugaviņa, Dzīne, Gaismaspils, Motus, Muklājs, Mūza, Saules Mājas, Senrīga, Skaņupe, Vecrīga, Vidus, Vox Animae) in the Riga amateur choir network. [https://avesol.riga.lv/lv/rigas-kori/rigas-koru-grupas-2013-gada/ [6]]
* Mixed choir “Rīga.” Beinerts is listed among the conductors of the National mixed choir “Rīga”, which was awarded National Choir status in 1968 and repeatedly won first places at the Song Festival choir competitions. [https://www.rsu.lv/en/mixed-choir-riga [7]]
* Riga Dom School / Riga Cathedral choirs. After a transition period under Aldis Andersons, Beinerts — “director of the Riga 3rd Music School and conductor of the choir Daugaviņa” — for a time took over the duties of chief conductor at the Riga Dom (Cathedral) school’s choral tradition. [https://doms.lv/lapas/42 [8]]

Song Festivals

Beinerts has served as a Song Festival chief conductor (virsdiriģents); in a 2023 interview on amateur choirs in Riga he is named among the conductors “almost all of whom have been chief conductors of past Song Festivals”. [https://www.la.lv/mernieku-laiki-rigas-amatier-maksla [9]] Recordings of his choirs and orchestral-choir programmes are held in the Latvian Song Festival digital archive of the National Library of Latvia. [https://dom.lndb.lv/data/obj/880450.html [10]]

Draft: Vatthe Conservation Park

Draft text:
The Vatthe Conservation Park, also called the Vatthe Conservation Area, is a community-managed protected area on the north coast of Espiritu Santo, the largest island of Vanuatu. It lies at Big Bay in Sanma Province and covers about of lowland forest on alluvial soils and raised limestone. The area was established in 1994 and in June 2004 became the first conservation area registered under Vanuatu's Environmental Management and Conservation Act 2002. It has been on Vanuatu's tentative list for World Heritage status since 1 October 2004. [ref: Vatthe Conservation Area, UNESCO World Heritage Centre] [ref: Protected Area Management in Vanuatu, Macquarie Journal of International and Comparative Environmental Law]

== History ==
The name Vatthe means "eye of the sea" in the local language. The idea of protecting the area followed biodiversity surveys carried out in 1993 by the Vanuatu Environment Unit and the Royal Forest and Bird Protection Society of New Zealand, which recorded the birds of the area. In the same year Anthony H. Whitaker surveyed the reptiles of Vanuatu, and a decade later Philippe Keith surveyed the fish of the Matantas River.

In 1994 the Vatthe Conservation Area Project was launched with funding from the South Pacific Biodiversity Conservation Programme, administered by the South Pacific Regional Environment Programme. A land dispute between the traditional owners meant that the project initially had little community support; in 1995 the two families settled the dispute and abandoned plans to log the area. In 1996 the communities formed a joint Conservation Area Community Committee.

The project provided training so that the villages could manage the area themselves, and it funded infrastructure including solar lighting, a water well, improved sanitation and radio-telephone links. Local guides were trained and a handicrafts centre and tourist bungalows were completed in 1997.

Vatthe was registered in June 2004 under the Environmental Management and Conservation Act 2002, the first conservation area to be registered under that act, and registration required the communities to prepare a conservation management plan. Vanuatu submitted the area to the World Heritage tentative list on 1 October 2004, under criteria (vii), (ix) and (x).

Several other Vanuatu sites appear on the tentative list: Yalo, Apialo and the sacred geography of north-west Malakula; the wreck of the liner, sunk in 1942; Lake Letas; and the Nowon and Votwos site on Ureparapara. [ref: Vanuatu, UNESCO World Heritage Centre] Chief Roi Mata's Domain was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2008.

== Geography and geology ==

The park lies on the north coast of Espiritu Santo at Big Bay. It extends west to the Jordan River, one of the largest rivers in Vanuatu, and south across the bay's black sand beach and the Matantas River, reaching four kilometres inland to the top of a raised limestone cliff above sea level.

Espiritu Santo covers and is volcanic in origin, with a mountain range along its west coast rising to Mount Tabwemasana at, the highest point in the country. [ref: Espiritu Santo] The island lies close to the boundary of the Australian and Pacific plates, and uplifted coral terraces occur along many parts of its coastline; uplift rates of between 2 and 6 mm a year have been measured, the highest on the west coast. [ref: Human–climate–environment interactions in Espiritu Santo, Vanuatu during the past millennium, Frontiers in Earth Science]

UNESCO gives the area as; a study of protected-area management in Vanuatu gives of lowland alluvial rainforest. A later project description gives of lowland forest. The World Heritage nomination states that the area contains the only extensive alluvial and limestone forest left in Vanuatu, and the National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan describes it in similar terms.

Vanuatu has a tropical climate with a warm, wet season from November to April and a cooler, dry season from May to October. Annual average temperatures are between. Tropical cyclones occur between November and April. [ref: Current and future climate of Vanuatu, Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-Hazards Department / Pacific Climate Change Science Program]

The park lies in the Vanuatu rain forests ecoregion, which covers more than eighty islands of volcanic or uplifted limestone origin. [ref: Vanuatu Rainforests, One Earth] The mountainous interior of the island forms the Santo Mountain Chain Key Biodiversity Area, one of 27 in the country, designated for species including the endangered Santa Cruz ground dove and mountain starling; the park itself lies on the coastal lowlands below it. [ref: Key Biodiversity Areas factsheet: Santo Mountain Chain, Key Biodiversity Areas Partnership]

== Flora and fauna ==
UNESCO describes the vegetation as falling into seven broad plant communities: alluvial plain forest, species-rich forest, species-poor Namatal forest with Kleinhovia hospita, nakatambol forest with Dracontomelon vitiense, bin-tri forest of Antiaris toxicaria, swamp forest, coral limestone forest, savanna and the riparian vegetation of the Jordan River. Some 265 species of trees, shrubs, palms and vines with traditional uses have been identified in the area. The species-rich forest is dominated by melektri (Antiaris toxicaria).

Draft: Memorial Park (Providence, RI)

Draft text:
Memorial Park is a public park in Providence, Rhode Island, located along the Providence River. The park features monuments dedicated to Rhode Island residents who fought in World War I, World War II, and the Korean War. [ref: Memorial Park, www.goprovidence.com] The park is managed by the City of Providence Parks Department. [ref: ]

== History ==
The park was opened in 1996 in front of the Providence County Courthouse after significant redevelopment resulting from the Providence River Relocation Project. [ref: Providence River Relocation, CNU] [ref: Cret’s wandering WWI shaft, Architecture Here and There] Following the destruction of Memorial Square, the park became the new home for a 150-foot tall memorial honoring more than 700 Rhode Island residents who died in World War I. [ref: World War I Monument, Memorial Square, Providence, Providence County, RI, Library of Congress, Washington, D.C. 20540 USA] The monument was designed by the French-American architect Paul Cret and built in 1929. The monument was disassembled starting in 1987 before being rebuilt in 1986. [ref: War Memorials Will Shine Bright for WaterFire Salute to Veterans - WaterFire Providence, waterfire.org] [ref: RI monuments on the move, The Providence Journal]

Two years after the park opened, the Rhode Island legislature allocated money to the Korean War Memorial Commission of Rhode Island. The memorial was built on the park's northern side by a Massachusetts-based sculptor and dedicated on October 8, 1998. [ref: Rhode Island Korean War Memorial, Photograph by Sylvie Watts] The memorial is flanked by the flags of Providence, the State of Rhode Island, the United States, and South Korea. [ref: Rhode Island Korean War Memorial, Photograph by Sylvie Watts]

In 2007, following contributions from Brown University, the City of Providence, the CVS Corporation, and other entities, a World War II memorial was dedicated on Veterans Day. [ref: Rhode Island World War II Memorial, Photographs by Edan Larkin] [ref: WWII Monument, www.bensavelkoul.nl] [ref: Brown University Contributes $50,000 to R.I. WWII Memorial, archive2.news.brown.edu] The memorial is surrounded by a stone wall featuring the seals of all of Rhode Island's cities and towns and the number of people who served from that town. Construction of the memorial was led by Joseph Corrente, a World War II and Korean War veteran who had earlier been co-chairman for the construction of the Korean War monument. [ref: JOSEPH CORRENTE Obituary (2009) - CRANSTON, RI - The Providence Journal, Legacy.com] [ref: When the Written Word Fails: Human Histories of WWII · The World War II Memorial in Providence: Untold Stories and Desperate Remembrance · Commemorative Works of Providence, commemorativeworksprovidenceri.digitalscholarship.brown.edu]

The Rhode Island Holocaust Memorial opened next to the World War II memorial in August 2015. [ref: Rhode Island Holocaust Memorial, Photographs by Sophia Siegel] The memorial incorporates prominent elements of Holocaust remembrance, including railroad tracks and entrance gates. [ref: The Rhode Island Holocaust Memorial in Providence, RI, Public Art Archive] [ref: Rhode Island Dedicates Holocaust Memorial In Providence, TPR: The Public's Radio]

=== Proposed Vietnam War memorial ===
After years of stalled efforts in the Rhode Island General Assembly to establish a memorial for Vietnam War veterans from Rhode Island, the state government announced on August 19, 2026, that a memorial would be constructed across the Providence River from Memorial Park. [ref: Last Honors with Providence's War Memorials, Rhode Island Monthly] [ref: Rhode Island’s Vietnam veterans have waited decades for a memorial. Now they know where it will be. • Rhode Island Current, Rhode Island Current] [ref: State of Rhode Island General Assembly, www.rilegislature.gov]

== References ==

Mahatma Gandhi (1869–1948) was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist who played a leading role in India's independence movement. His philosophy emphasized nonviolence (ahimsa), truth (satya), self-discipline, and peaceful resistance. His speeches, writings, and public statements have influenced political and social movements around the world.

=== Mahatma Gandhi Quotes ===

==== Truth and Nonviolence ====
Gandhi's writings frequently explored the relationship between truth and nonviolence. He regarded nonviolent resistance as a means of confronting injustice without resorting to physical violence.

==== Peace and Social Justice ====
Gandhi advocated peaceful political action, religious tolerance, and social reform. His views influenced later civil rights and independence movements.

==== Self-Discipline and Personal Responsibility ====
His writings also addressed personal conduct, simplicity, ethical living, and the responsibility of individuals to contribute to social change.

== References ==

* Gandhi, Mohandas K. The Story of My Experiments with Truth.
* Gandhi, Mohandas K. The Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi.

Draft text:
Patrice Mousseau is a Canadian Anishinaabe entrepreneur and a former broadcast journalist. She is the founder and CEO of [https://satya.ca/?srsltid=AYCX9vJ4H1oT0izks46EzFEK5z2N-Ss5rImC1Q8tOHWfK4KJDa_WHnWH Satya Organics], a BC-based company producing plant-based skincare products. [ref: Patrice Mousseau is building an Indigenous business ecosystem, one entrepreneur at a time, The Globe and Mail]

== Personal life ==
Mousseau was raised in Sioux Lookout, Ontario. She is a member of the Fort William First Nation. Patrice Mousseau is a single mother. Her daughter, Esme, was born in 2011. [ref: How Patrice Mousseau Went from Model to Journalist to Organic-Skincare Entrepreneur, Canadian Business]

== Career ==

In the mid-1990s, Patrice Mousseau worked as a model before entering Canadian news broadcasting, including roles at the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC), Aboriginal Voices Radio Network, and the Aboriginal Peoples Television Network.

In 2012, she formulated a steroid-free skincare balm sourced from natural ingredients to treat her daughter's eczema. [ref: Ojibway entrepreneur creates product for daughter, now it's in 400 stores] She began selling it at local farmer's markets. She then founded Satya Organics in 2015. [ref: SATYA ORGANICS INC. - WEST VANCOUVER BC CANADA] The company became the first indigenous-owned brand carried by Shoppers Drug Mart. By 2025, its products were sold in more than 1,000 Shoppers Drug Marts, as well as being available with other Canadian, American, and Hong Kong retailers.

== Other activities ==
Mousseau serves as Entrepreneur in Residence at [https://www.flinthub.ca/ Flint Hub], an Indigenous-focused business incubator at the University of Waterloo's United College. [ref: Flint Hub, Empowering Indigenous Entrepreneurs]

= Karl Vandenhole =
Karl Vandenhole ist ein Film- und Fernsehschaffender, der vor allem an deutschen Dokumentarfilm- und Fernsehproduktionen beteiligt ist. Seine Tätigkeiten umfassen unter anderem Produktion, Recherche, Drehbucharbeit, Regie, Kamera und Ton. Er arbeitete hauptsächlich an Dokumentationen für die ZDF-Reihe Terra-X und weitere deutschsprachige Fernsehsender sowie an späteren Fernseh- und Streamingproduktionen.

== Beruflicher Werdegang ==
Karl Vandenholes berufliche Tätigkeiten sind in Film- und Fernsehbranchenverzeichnissen sowie in Sendungs- und Programmangaben dokumentiert. Zu seinen frühen Arbeiten zählen Produktionen der Dokumentationsreihe Tauchfahrt in die Vergangenheit, die zwischen 2000 und 2011 im ZDF ausgestrahlt wurde. Als festangestellter Redakteur bei Spiegel TV war er maßgeblich für den Aufbau der Abteilung Co-und Auftragsproduktionen verantwortlich sowie für die erste große Cross-mediale Publikation von Der Spiegel, Spiegel TV und ZDF mit der Terra-X Filmveröffentlichung "Kolumbus' letzte Reise", zusammen mit Titelstory im Spiegel und einer Buchveröffentlichung "Die letzte Reise" von den Autoren Klaus Brinkbäumer und Clemens Höges.

Für die Folge Operation Caesar – Jagd auf U-864 wird Vandenhole als Drehbuchautor genannt. In Programmangaben von PHOENIX wird er zudem neben Marc Brasse und Christopher Rowley als einer der Filmschaffenden aufgeführt. Crew United führt ihn bei der Produktion Tauchfahrt in die Vergangenheit – Operation Caesar – Jagd auf U-864 als Co-Regisseur sowie für Recherche, Autorentätigkeit und Produktion.

In den folgenden Jahren arbeitete Vandenhole an verschiedenen Dokumentationen, darunter Produktionen aus dem Umfeld der ZDF-Reihe Terra X. Zu seinen verzeichneten Tätigkeiten gehören die Produktion beziehungsweise Recherchekoordination für Terra X – Schatzjagd in der Tiefe (2009) und Terra X – Kampf um die Ostsee (2010). Weitere Produktionsarbeiten sind für Die Geisterflotte vom Yukon (2010) und Terra X – Sibirien und die Deutschen (2012) dokumentiert.

Neben seiner Tätigkeit im Dokumentarfilm war Vandenhole an Fernsehfilmen, Reportagen und Dokuserien beteiligt. Zu den verzeichneten Arbeiten gehören Geheimnisse Asiens – Die schönsten Nationalparks, Länder Menschen Abenteuer Spezial – Thailand & Island sowie die Dokuserie Diese Ochsenknechts. Bei verschiedenen Produktionen übernahm er Kamera- und Tonaufgaben.

Seit 2012 ist Karl Vandenhole in Thailand und Südostasien als freischaffender Multimedia Journalist tätig für Zeitungsreportagen, Magazinbeiträge und Dokumentarfilme. Er produziert aber weiterhin Dokumentarfilme in Zusammenarbeit mit deutschen Produktionsfirmen

Draft: Elimu Academy

Draft text:
----

Elimu Academy[i] was set up in Liverpool L8 (latterly called Toxteth)[ii]  Toxteth England in 1999 and was co-founded and led by the city’s first Black Head Teacher Gloria Hyatt  MBE[iii]. It housed the UK’s first Independent School[iv] that was black led, a charity[v] and limited company[vi] for black secondary school pupils in Merseyside and white pupils residing in Liverpool 8 who were permanently excluded or at risk of exclusion from school. [viii]

It's educational approach included an African-centred curriculum and predominantly support for pupils from Black and mixed-race backgrounds [viii] Within Elimu Academy there was an after-school, for pupils attending mainstream secondary schools and an adult learner’s service [viiii]

=== History ===

=== Elimu Wa Nane ===
The origins of Elimu Academy can be traced to Elimu Wa Nane, a library and educational resource established in 1979 at Princes Park Methodist Church and Centre in Liverpool 8. The library held literature relating to Africa and the Caribbean and provided a resource for the local community that was set up by Wally Brown  CBE, DL.pg.1.[x]

The library’s activities included educational resources and opportunities for reading, writing and cultural learning. Its development reflected concerns about the availability and representation of Black history, literature and culture within mainstream educational provision.

=== Elimu Study School: After School Service ===
In the 1990s, the project transformed into an after school called [https://register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk/en/charity-search/-/charity-details/1039434/full-print Elimu Study School] under the leadership of Gloria Hyatt, a teacher with QTS. The service expanded beyond its original library function to provide educational support for young people in Liverpool 8. Historical accounts place the Study School at Princes Park Methodist Church and Centre before its relocation to Streatlam Tower in 1994 and later in 1996 to Dove Street during which time it became Elimu Academy, where it operated till 2009.[xi] [xii]

The provision included after-school classes in subjects such as English and mathematics, and most parts of the national curriculum and Black Studies as an additional curriculum alongside teaching relating to African and Caribbean history and culture. Its educational approach incorporated an African-centred perspective into learning materials and classroom activities. The programme was intended to support pupils’ educational attainment and provide additional educational resources for children attending mainstream schools. [xiii]

=== Black Learners Project ===
The organisation subsequently expanded its work to include daytime educational provision for young people who experienced difficulties in mainstream education. The Black Learners Project formed part of this development and focused on pupils who had been excluded or were considered at risk of exclusion.[xv]

As Elimu’s success grew, schools in Liverpool and Liverpool Education Authority collaborated, as noted in the December 2000, Ofsted Inspection report, “That provision, the Elimu centre, is now to be brought into a more formal relationship with the LEA”. (para148, pg. 33). [xvi]

The educational model combined anti racist teaching with support intended to address barriers to learning. Hyatt argued that schools needed to address differences in educational outcomes and the treatment of Black pupils. In contemporary reporting, she discussed the effects of racial stereotyping, the representation of Black people in the curriculum and the need for teachers to understand the experiences of their pupils.[xvii]

=== Elimu Academy ===
Elimu Academy was established as an independent school in Dove Street, Toxteth, where it continued with its afterschool and BLP project. The Department for Education records its opening date as 1 March 2000 and lists Gloria Hyatt as headteacher. The school was registered as an independent school for pupils aged 13 to 15. [xviii]

The Academy provided education for pupils who had been excluded from mainstream schools or were at risk of exclusion. Its approach included an African-centred curriculum alongside the national curriculum. Contemporary reporting described its work with Black and mixed-race pupils and its use of teaching strategies intended to address educational underachievement and exclusion. [xix]

=== Adult Learning ===
In 1999, NCFE accredited adult learning classes were created to create a stepping stone into teaching this included overseas qualified teacher training, classroom assistant training (now called Teaching Assistants) and mentor training. [xx] [xxi]

Ray Costello said of Hyatt: “In developing the Elimu Wa Nane Project into a successful independent school for disaffected black pupils, Gloria Hyatt pioneered the case for future black teachers to rise to management positions in Liverpool” (Costello, 2007, pg.85).[xxii]

The Africa International Housing Show (AIHS) is an annual housing and construction exhibition and conference held in Abuja, Nigeria. It was founded by Festus Adebayo.

== History ==
Adebayo said the event began as the Abuja Housing Show and was renamed after participants from other countries attended. The 2026 edition was presented as the show's 20th anniversary. At its opening, Adebayo said the event had started with 10 participants and had grown into an exhibition featuring 350 companies.

== Editions ==
The 2022 edition, described as the 16th, focused on capital market financing for housing and the effects of climate change on affordable housing. Adebayo said it would include 31 international speakers and more than 400 exhibitors.

The 2023 edition was themed "Beyond Rhetoric To Homes; Making Housing Happen". Adebayo said the organisers were partnering with the International Finance Corporation on green housing finance.

The 19th edition was scheduled for 27 July to 1 August 2025 at the Transcorp Hilton Hotel under the theme "Reimagining Housing Through Innovation, Collaboration, and Policy". The organisers expected about 40,000 participants and 200 exhibitors from 21 countries.

The 20th edition opened in Abuja on 15 July 2026.

== Housing TV Africa ==
The Africa International Housing Show launched Housing TV Africa, a television channel focused on housing. At the 2026 opening, Adebayo described it as the continent's first dedicated housing television channel.

Kawanthissa (also spelled Kavanthissa or Kavantissa) was a Sri Lankan wild tusker that lived around the Galgamuwa area of Sri Lanka's North Western Province. Kawanthissa was known for his magnificent tusks and his friendly behaviors with the people. He was a calm elephant and attracted most of the Sri Lankans and tourists whi travel Sri Lanka.

== Background ==

Kawanthissa lived in the Galgamuwa area and the recidents in the area and the wildlife enthusiasts were concerned about his welfare and treatments following an injury in 2026 September. [ref: Outrage and calls for investigation following tragic death of iconic Kawanthissa, The Sunday Times]

== Injury and death ==

Kawanthissa was found with an injury to his right foreleg in the Galgamuwa area In September 2026 and the Wildlife officials and veterinarians treated the injury and monitored his condition. [ref: Ailing tusker Kavanthissa in critical condition, public urged to stay away, Daily Mirror]

The elephant's condition deteriorated overtime and reduced food intake and eventually a diarrhea condition occurred.

Kawanthissa tusker died in October 2026 while receiving veterinary care and his death raised public concerns and many parties requested investigation about the treatments he received.

== Investigation ==

The Environment Ministry of Sri Lanka announced an independent investigation about the treatment procedures to find out if any mistakes or deliberate misconduct had been occurred. [ref: Independent probe into tusker Kawanthissa's death, Daily Mirror]

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake appointed an expert committee on 19 October 2026 to investigate the elephant's death. The duties of the committee was to examine the possible causes of the death and findout the mistakes and negligence had occurred during treatment. [ref: President appoints committee to probe Kavanthissa's death, Daily Mirror]

The New Hampshire Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force (NH ICAC) is a law enforcement task force headquartered at and managed by the Portsmouth Police Department in New Hampshire. Established in 1998, it participates in the national Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force Program. Its activities include investigating technology-facilitated crimes against children, conducting forensic examinations, supporting criminal prosecutions, and providing community education.

In 2017, New Hampshire Public Radio reported that funding shortages were limiting the task force’s investigative capacity. The report examined a proposal to provide state funding to supplement federal support.

An investigation involving NH ICAC resulted in the federal prosecution of John Allen Wright of Milton, New Hampshire. On February 22, 2013, Wright was sentenced to 160 years in federal prison after pleading guilty to five counts of sexual exploitation of children and one count of possessing child pornography.

=== Logo history ===
The task force’s logo has changed over time. The current longstanding design featuring binary digits, the old man on the mountain and photographs of children was created by Detective Kenneth Tapscott during his service with the New Hampshire Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force. IThat design has been used for more than 15 years.

Draft text:
----

Tia Adan is an Australian youth advocate, community leader and social entrepreneur based in Queensland. She is the founder and president of Rise as One Association Inc., a youth-led organisation focused on leadership development, education, community engagement and the empowerment of young people.

Adan has participated in youth representation, public policy discussions, child protection advocacy and initiatives supporting women and girls. Her affiliations include the Bravehearts Youth Advisory Council, the Queensland Curriculum and Assessment Authority's myQCE Student Reference Group, the Morayfield Youth Advisory Council and the YMCA Queensland Youth Parliament.

In 2025, Adan was featured in The Courier-Mail as one of 22 young people contributing to the future of the City of Moreton Bay. In 2026, she received second place in the Zonta District 22 Young Women in Leadership Award, according to information provided by Adan.

== Early life and education ==
Adan was born in Pakistan and spent part of her childhood in Thailand before migrating to Australia in 2019.

She grew up in a culturally traditional household where, according to Adan, her parents held conservative views about gender roles and women's participation in public life. She has described an upbringing in which women were discouraged from expressing independent opinions and participating in political discussions.

Adan has stated her parents opposed her involvement in politics, viewing political leadership and public decision-making as traditionally male responsibilities. She developed different views about gender equality and believed women should have equal opportunities to participate in political, social and community leadership.

These differences contributed to tensions within her family as she became increasingly involved in youth advocacy and political activities.

In May 2026, at the age of 17, Adan moved out of her family home while completing her final year of secondary education. She began living independently, managing her accommodation, finances and household responsibilities while attending school full-time and working three jobs.

Despite these circumstances, Adan continued participating in community organisations, youth representation and the development of Rise as One Association Inc.

=== Secondary education and student leadership ===
Adan attended Caboolture State High School in Queensland, where she became involved in student leadership, community service and youth advocacy.

During Year 11 in 2025, she served as Vice President of the school's Student Council and held the position of Senior School Ambassador. Her responsibilities included representing students, supporting school initiatives and participating in activities promoting student wellbeing and leadership.

In Year 12 in 2026, Adan stepped away from her formal school leadership positions to focus on her personal circumstances, education and responsibilities associated with independent living.

She continued her involvement in youth advocacy and community initiatives outside school, including the development of Rise as One and participation in statewide advisory groups.

== Youth advocacy and public affairs ==

=== YMCA Queensland Youth Parliament ===
In 2025, Adan represented the electorate of Morayfield in the YMCA Queensland Youth Parliament, a youth civic education program in which participants debate policy and develop proposed legislation.

During her term, she participated in the Health and Emergency Services and Family, Seniors and Disability Services Committee.

She contributed to the development of the Hospital and Health Boards (Ryan's Rule) Amendment Youth Bill 2025, which addressed patient rights, communication and accountability within Queensland's healthcare system.

Her involvement in the program formed part of her broader interest in government, public policy, human rights and political representation.

=== Morayfield Youth Advisory Council ===
Adan has participated in the Morayfield Youth Advisory Council, an initiative associated with Queensland Member of Parliament Mark Ryan.

Through the council, she has contributed to community consultation, youth leadership activities and initiatives encouraging young people to participate in local decision-making.

The council was also involved in the organisation of the 2026 Youth Leadership Forum in collaboration with Rise as One.

=== Bravehearts Youth Advisory Council ===
Adan serves as a youth advisor with Bravehearts, an Australian child protection organisation focused on the prevention of child sexual abuse and support for affected children and young people.

Through the Bravehearts Youth Advisory Council, she contributes youth perspectives to discussions concerning child safety, prevention strategies, education and the protection of children's rights.

Her involvement reflects her interest in improving systems intended to protect vulnerable young people and increasing youth participation in decisions affecting their wellbeing.

=== myQCE Student Reference Group ===
In 2026, Adan was selected as one of 15 Queensland students to join the myQCE Student Reference Group, administered by the Queensland Curriculum and Assessment Authority (QCAA).

The group provides student perspectives on senior secondary education, assessment and resources supporting the Queensland Certificate of Education.

Adan represented Caboolture State High School as part of the statewide group.

Draft: Ahlam Gharbaoui

Draft text:
Ahlam Gharbaoui is a Dutch-Moroccan international business consultant, entrepreneur, author and English-language poet, with experience in international affairs, public diplomacy and strategic partnerships.

== Early life and education ==
Born in Brabant, the Netherlands, Gharbaoui built a career spanning commercial business, government, diplomatic affairs, media and international strategic partnerships. [ref: De zin van Ahlam Gharbaoui: 'Waar een wil is, is een weg', Trouw] She began her career as a government official at the Dutch Ministry of Justice. An Arabic-language women's magazine profile described her as the first Moroccan and Arab woman to work at a refugee reception centre in the Netherlands. [ref: سيدة الأعمال المغربية الهولندية أحلام الغرباوي, Estesmarat] [ref: Two-page feature on Ahlam Gharbaoui, Arabic-language women's magazine (print)] After working in the insurance division of Rabobank, she obtained a postgraduate diploma in legal interpreting and translation from the SIGV Institute for Legal Interpreters and Translators in Utrecht in 2002 and became a sworn court interpreter and translator. She also holds a Master's degree in Intercultural Communication from the University of California, Los Angeles (2012). [ref: Personal Portfolio 2024 (self-published)] Throughout her career, she has provided interpreting services for members of the Dutch Royal House, presidents and senior government officials from across the European Union and the MENA region. [ref: Dutch-Moroccan Businesswoman / Ahlam Gharbaoui: An Arab Woman with Inspiring Global Steps and Achievements, Estesmarat]

== Business career ==
At the age of 24, she founded Averto Tolken & Vertalers Adviezen, building a network of more than 800 interpreters and translators serving government institutions, commercial organizations and the media sector throughout the Netherlands. [ref: De banden versterken, De Groene Amsterdammer] [ref: AIM Congress is delighted to announce Ahlam Gharbaoui as our Master of the Ceremony for the SMEs Track at AIM Congress 2024!] She also worked as an editor and interviewer for NOVA, a Dutch current affairs television programme renowned for setting the political agenda in The Hague.

In 2009, Gharbaoui relocated to the United Arab Emirates to serve as a commercial and cultural adviser at the Embassy of the Kingdom of the Netherlands in Abu Dhabi. [ref: Promotional reel for AIM Congress 2025 featuring Ahlam Gharbaoui] In this role, she represented the Netherlands across multiple policy portfolios and facilitated bilateral cooperation and international partnerships. Building on her experience in the UAE, she subsequently served as general manager for the Gulf region at Farouk Systems USA, an American multinational. Her international work includes facilitating partnerships across the MENA region, including, as she described in an interview with Estesmarat, a government-to-government memorandum of understanding between Morocco and the Netherlands on social affairs.

AIM Congress announced her as Master of the Ceremony for the SMEs Track and keynote speaker at AIM Congress 2024 (7-9 May, ADNEC, Abu Dhabi), an annual international investment forum. [ref: Thank-you post to the Masters of Ceremony of AIM Congress 2024] [ref: Report on AIM Congress 2024 quoting Ahlam Gharbaoui, Al Ittihad (print, economy page)] She returned as Master of the Ceremony, this time for the Global Manufacturing and Industrialization track, at AIM Congress 2025 (7-9 April, Abu Dhabi). [ref: Post on AIM Congress 2025 (self-published)] [ref: Post on AIM Congress 2025 (self-published)]

Gharbaoui is the founder of Ahlam Consultancy, which specializes in international business development, strategic partnerships and investments. The firm supports companies entering new markets, developing market-entry strategies, pursuing strategic investments and engaging with governmental and institutional stakeholders across the Netherlands, the UAE, the MENA region and Africa. [ref: Exclusive Strategic Advisory With Ahlam Consultancy: Ahlam Gharbaoui, Emirates Times]

Among her projects was her role in initiating and executing an oil and gas higher education and vocational training centre for the Abu Dhabi Government, delivered through Dutch innovation and expertise, with estimated costs of around USD 28 million (AED 100 million).

In a 2023 interview with Estesmarat, Gharbaoui said that in 2022 she had been nominated by H.E. Sheikh Nahyan bin Mubarak Al Nahyan, Minister of Tolerance and Coexistence, for the UAE Golden Visa in recognition of her contributions to public diplomacy, large-scale investment projects and knowledge transfer.

In March 2024, she was honored at the 7th Estesmarat Awards for 2023, in a ceremony at Atlantis The Palm, Dubai, held under the patronage and in the presence of Sheikh Salem bin Sultan Al Qasimi, before more than 150 guests from media, business and diplomacy. [ref: Video of the 7th Estesmarat Awards for 2023 ceremony at Atlantis The Palm, Dubai] [ref: Reel on the 7th Estesmarat Awards]

In 2026, she received the Morocco With Purpose Award from H.E. Mehdi Bensaid, Minister of Youth, Culture and Communication, in the presence of H.E. André Azoulay, Senior Advisor to His Majesty King Mohammed VI, during the awards ceremony at the historic Chellah in Rabat. [ref: Morocco With Purpose Award ceremony video, Chellah, Rabat; winner confirmed by organizer Hiba El Aidi]

Draft text:
Proda (stylized PRODA) is an American beverage brand that produces carbonated, sugar-free soft drinks containing whey protein. The company was founded in 2026 by actor and entrepreneur Matthew Postlethwaite and beverage entrepreneur Jeff Church, a co-founder of Suja Juice, who serve as co-chief executive officers. [ref: Justin Timberlake, Jessica Biel enter protein soda market, Food Dive] [ref: Justin Timberlake and Jessica Biel Joined a Protein Soda Startup. Now Comes the Hard Part, [[Inc. (magazine)] In October 2026, Justin Timberlake, Jessica Biel and Barry's executive chairman Joey Gonzalez joined the company as co-founders. [ref: Justin Timberlake and Jessica Biel Jump in on Protein Craze in First Joint Business Venture, The Hollywood Reporter]

== History ==
Proda was founded by Postlethwaite and Church and launched its drinks in 2026. [ref: Justin Timberlake co-founds PRODA brand taking on Coca-Cola and Pepsi, TheStreet] Postlethwaite has said the idea originated with his grandmother, who struggled to consume enough protein through shakes and supplements but enjoyed soda, and that the product took more than two years to develop. Church has said that advances in clarified whey protein made it possible to produce a protein drink that was clear and soluble enough to carbonate. [ref: Justin Timberlake And Jessica Biel Join Protein Soda Startup As Co-Founders, Forbes] The company is based in Los Angeles. [ref: PRODA, Better Soda, Inc.]

On October 13, 2026, the company announced that Timberlake, Biel and Gonzalez had joined as co-founders, in what The Hollywood Reporter described as Timberlake and Biel's first joint business venture. Both had prior involvement in beverages: Timberlake had invested in Bai Brands in 2016 and served as its chief flavor officer, and Biel had co-founded the children's drink company Kinderfarms in 2021. According to the announcement, the couple would work on the brand's creative strategy, flavor innovation, product development and cultural partnerships, and said that "the opportunity to work with Matthew and Jeff in shaping the brand, its products and where it goes next" had drawn them to the company. Gonzalez, the executive chairman and former chief executive of Barry's, said Timberlake had been working with Postlethwaite on the brand's visual identity in what he described as a creative-director capacity before the announcement. Gonzalez himself was described as bringing operational scale and fitness-industry experience to the company. Inc. described the challenge facing the company as converting celebrity attention into repeat purchases in a category that larger competitors were entering.

== Products ==
Proda's drinks are sold in 12-ounce cans, each containing 10 grams of whey protein and no sugar. As of October 2026 the range comprised seven flavors: Lemon Lime, Classic Orange, Cherry Lime, Strawberry Lemonade, Golden Apple, Shirley Temple and Root Beer. The drinks were sold through Sprouts Farmers Market, Amazon and the company's website, with the company stating that it aimed to expand into grocery and club channels.

Draft: Air Transportable Mobile Medical Facility

Draft text:
The Air Transportable Mobile Medical Facility (ATMMF) was a prototype deployable medical shelter system developed by Hawker de Havilland (HdH) in Melbourne, Australia, between 1988 and 1990. The concept originated with Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) Wing Commander Dave Robson, who sought improved field medical infrastructure after observing limitations in existing shelters.

== History ==

In 1988, the RAAF commissioned Hawker de Havilland to design and construct two demonstration units. The project was led by Chief Designer Andrzej Grocholski, who oversaw structural integrity, airworthiness compliance, and final design approval. Designer Greg Thomas contributed to design solutions and specification compliance. Production was completed in 1990 under Production Manager Denis Baker.

Despite successful field trials and positive feedback from personnel involved, the RAAF did not proceed with further procurement. The current status of the two prototype units is unknown.

== Design ==

The ATMMF was intended as an innovative alternative to contemporary deployable shelters. Each unit was towable on- and off-road, expandable, and interconnectable. The shelters were designed to be air-transportable by both helicopter and fixed-wing aircraft, and required minimal site preparation. Deployment could be performed by two personnel.

Air locks sealed the interior from the external environment, providing a sterile, quiet, air-conditioned space suitable for medical treatment or nursing wards. Air-lock areas could be converted into washbasin, shower, or toilet modules. Depending on configuration, shelters could serve as mobile hospitals, health centres, communication centres, workshops, or emergency accommodation.

Each unit incorporated electrical wiring, plumbing, and interchangeable internal stores modules. A built-in battery system provided power for deployment and 24-hour emergency lighting, while external field generators supplied power for air conditioning, lighting, and battery charging.

== Expandable configuration ==
A minimum expanded configuration consisted of two interconnected shelters, joined by integral roof, floor, and wall panels to create an enclosed floor area of 26.2 m². Multiple units could be connected side-by-side or via concertina walk-through ends to form larger complexes. In closed configuration, a single shelter could support surgical operations.

== Construction ==
The primary structure used welded aluminium tubular framing. Walls, roof, and floor panels were of sandwich construction, providing thermal and acoustic insulation. Removable service modules were made of fibreglass. Hinged interconnecting panels allowed limited self-alignment to compensate for accidental misalignment during deployment.

Draft text:
The translation of the Bible into Sea Dyak or Iban (ISO-639: iba) commenced in the year 1864 in close association with missionary priests from the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel from the Anglican church. The first complete New Testament translation was published by the British and Foreign Bible Society in 1933. Subsequently, the Old Testament was translated by a committee of native Iban Christians in Sarawak. The first full Bible in Iban (Bup Kudus: Berita Manah Ka Rebak Diatu), translated with the translation principles of dynamic equivalence, was then published by the Bible Society of Malaysia in 1988. An ecumenical revision of the full Bible with the Deuterocanonical books was done in consultation with the Anglican Diocese of Kuching, Methodist Sarawak Iban Annual Conference, and the Roman Catholic church. The revision published by the Bible Society of Malaysia in 2011, named Bup Kudus Baru (+ Deuterokanonikal), revised earlier renderings to adhere to the formal equivalence principle. In 2026, the Iban Study Bible was published by the Bible Society of Malaysia. [ref: Iban Study Bible launched in Kuching after eight-year effort, Borneo Post Online]

Draft: Dane Lam

Draft text:
Dane Lam is an Australian conductor. He is Music and Artistic Director of the Hawaiʻi Symphony Orchestra, Artistic Director of State Opera South Australia and Principal Conductor of the Xi'an Symphony Orchestra, and has been described as the only conductor holding simultaneous leadership positions at major institutions in the United States, Australia and Asia. [ref: Interview: Conductor Dane Lam on New Album, Globe-trotting, and Why 'Classical Music Is Better', Blogcritics] [ref: 'Orchestra of the Pacific': HSO extends inaugural music director's contract, Hawaiʻi Public Radio] [ref: New State Opera artistic director's international ambitions, InDaily]

Appointed in 2023 as the first music director in the Hawaiʻi Symphony Orchestra's history, Lam had his contract extended to 2031 in 2025. [ref: Hawai'i Symphony Orchestra appoints music director, BBC Music Magazine] At Xi'an, where he has led the orchestra since 2014, he was the first non-Chinese national to hold its chief conducting post. [ref: New State Opera South Australia Artistic Director announced, Government of South Australia] He was previously the first conductor to hold an official position with Opera Queensland.

In opera he has conducted for Opera Holland Park, Scottish Opera, Opera Australia and West Australian Opera. In 2025–26 he conducted The Magic Flute, the first co-production between Australian and Chinese opera companies, in Hong Kong, Adelaide and Beijing, where he made his debut with the London Philharmonic Orchestra at the Beijing Music Festival. [ref: Opera review: The Magic Flute, InDaily] [ref: Central Opera House, Beijing, London Philharmonic Orchestra] Reviewing his Scottish Opera Carmen, Opera Now described his conducting as "the best thing about this production". [ref: Bizet: Carmen at Scottish Opera – Live Review, Opera Now]

== Career ==

=== Hawaiʻi Symphony Orchestra ===
On 18 January 2023 the Hawaiʻi Symphony Orchestra announced Lam's appointment as its first music director, on a five-year contract beginning with the 2023–24 season; he had guest-conducted the orchestra in 2022. [ref: Hawai'i Symphony Orchestra Names First-Ever Music Director, The Violin Channel] In August 2023, in his first weeks in the post, he conducted the orchestra in Maui Ola, a benefit concert for victims of the Maui wildfires that raised more than one million dollars. [ref: Hawaii Symphony Orchestra joins benefit performance for Maui, Limelight]

In November 2025 the orchestra extended his contract through 2031 and gave him the title Music and Artistic Director. Under Lam the orchestra has broadened its programming to include collaborations with Hawaiian artists and premieres of music from across the Pacific, and he has campaigned for the orchestra to be recognised as the state orchestra of Hawaiʻi; Lam has described the ensemble as "the orchestra of the Pacific". In September 2026 the orchestra gave a free concert, Mele for Maui, in West Maui. [ref: Free 'Mele for Maui' concert in West Maui celebrates resilience, healing, Hawaii News Now]

=== State Opera South Australia ===
In September 2023 Lam was appointed Artistic Director of State Opera South Australia in Adelaide, succeeding Stuart Maunder. [ref: State Opera South Australia announces new AD, Limelight] On his appointment he said he intended to conduct at least one production each season, to commission works telling Australian and South Australian stories, and to develop locally made productions capable of touring internationally.

In 2025 Lam conducted a new production of Mozart's The Magic Flute, co-produced by State Opera South Australia, Opera Hong Kong, the Beijing Music Festival and the China National Opera House, described by Limelight as "the first major co-production between Australian and Chinese opera institutions". [ref: SOSA unveils "Opera without Borders" premieres, Limelight] It was staged in Hong Kong and then in Adelaide in August 2025, where Graham Strahle in InDaily wrote that Lam "imparts real energy and dynamism both as conductor and guiding light" and had the Adelaide Symphony Orchestra "playing with flowing tempos, neat articulation and great spirit", before its Chinese mainland premiere at the Beijing Music Festival in October 2026. [ref: The 29th Beijing Music Festival Celebrates Mozart and the Unifying Power of Music, Musical America] The Beijing performances, on 10 and 11 October 2026 at the Central Opera House, were given by the London Philharmonic Orchestra, the festival's orchestra-in-residence, and marked Lam's debut with the orchestra.

=== Xi'an Symphony Orchestra ===
Lam became Principal Conductor of the Xi'an Symphony Orchestra in 2014, [ref: Bach to Xi'an – UQ alumnus takes up post in Xi'an Symphony Orchestra, University of Queensland] the first non-Chinese national to hold the orchestra's chief conducting post. With the orchestra he conducted the 2016 CCTV-1 Mid-Autumn Festival Gala and, in 2017, a joint project with students of the University of Queensland Symphony Orchestra in China. At Xi'an he brought in international soloists including Sumi Jo and programmed works by living and neglected composers.

=== Opera in the United Kingdom ===
Lam made his London debut conducting Rossini's La Cenerentola at Opera Holland Park, where he later conducted Don Giovanni, Norma and a new production of Così fan tutte in 2018. [ref: New artist: conductor Dane Lam, Rayfield Allied] He was nominated for Best Newcomer at the 2018 International Opera Awards.

== Hanish Gupta ==

Hanish Gupta is an Indian entrepreneur and corporate executive. He is the founder, promoter, and managing director of Sunkind India Limited, an Indian renewable energy company active in solar energy project development, engineering, procurement, and construction (solar EPC), solar component manufacturing, and battery energy storage. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India]
== Early life and education ==
Gupta completed the fifth semester of a Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) course at Amity University, Uttar Pradesh in December 2008. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India]

== Career ==
Gupta has over 16 years of professional experience across industrial engineering, steel manufacturing, and renewable energy sectors. Prior to establishing Sunkind, he served on the boards of directors for several industrial and manufacturing firms, including J.D. Industries India Limited and J.D. Metalloys Limited. [ref: Director Profile: Hanish Gupta (DIN 02194659), ZaubaCorp]

In September 2019, Gupta co-founded Sunkind Energy (now Sunkind India Limited). He was appointed as a director on the company's board in April 2021 and was designated as managing director on August 12, 2024. [ref: Draft Red Herring Prospectus: Sunkind India Limited, Sunkind India Limited / National Stock Exchange of India] As managing director, he oversees corporate strategy, business planning, project execution, corporate governance, and the company's backward integration into solar mounting structure manufacturing (under the Strucmax brand) and photovoltaic module production. [ref: By 2030, We Aim to Contribute 10–12 GW Cumulatively: Hanish Gupta, Sunkind Energy, Energetica India]

== Industry commentary and public affairs ==
Gupta regularly publishes industry commentary and participates in media discussions regarding India's renewable energy policies, power transmission infrastructure, solar manufacturing, and grid-scale storage:

* Grid Infrastructure & Energy Storage: In September 2026, The Financial Express featured commentary from Gupta on India's power transmission infrastructure upgrades, grid integration of renewable energy, and the commercial viability of battery energy storage systems (BESS). In June 2026, he discussed financing capital-intensive renewable storage projects in an interview with BusinessWorld. [ref: "Solar And Storage Must Go Together", Says Hanish Gupta, Founder & MD, Sunkind India Ltd, BW Hotelier / BusinessWorld]
* Solar Supply Chain & Geopolitics: In July 2026, Gupta authored an analysis in PV Magazine India on global solar manufacturing geopolitics, addressing China's supply chain dominance and outlining strategies for India to build domestic wafer and cell manufacturing capabilities. [ref: The geopolitics of solar manufacturing and how India can build a China-alternative supply chain, pv magazine India]
* Domestic Manufacturing & Policy: In December 2025, Gupta contributed an opinion piece to ET EnergyWorld examining policy measures under the PLI scheme and India's push to localize clean energy manufacturing. [ref: Inside India's push to localize its solar future, ETEnergyworld (The Economic Times)]
* Business Leadership & Manufacturing Expansion: In July 2026, Gupta discussed Sunkind's vertical integration, energy security, and manufacturing expansion in an exclusive interview with APAC News Network. [ref: 'Domestic manufacturing strengthens energy security by reducing import dependence': Hanish Gupta, Founder & Managing Director, Sunkind India Limited, APAC News Network]

Dellove Ondongo (full name Adrard Guez-Dellove Ondongo Aucibi) is a Congolese technology entrepreneur and cybersecurity specialist. He is the founder and chief executive officer of BEGU Corporation OÜ, a technology company registered in Tallinn, Estonia. [ref: Newsroom, BEGU Corporation] [ref: Begu Corporation OÜ (17290858), e-Business Register] He is also involved in diplomatic networking, connecting individuals and organisations across international and professional networks.

== Early life and education ==
Ondongo was born in the Republic of the Congo (Congo-Brazzaville) and moved to India as a student about ten years ago; he has lived mostly in Bangalore since.

He completed a Master of Computer Applications (MCA) in cybersecurity and is a PhD scholar in Computer Science and Information Technology (CSIT) at Jain (Deemed-to-be University) in Bangalore. According to BEGU Corporation, he is the first Congolese student to pursue a PhD at Jain University, and one of only a few Congolese PhD scholars in Bangalore.

== Career ==
Ondongo began his career in Bangalore in technical information technology recruitment and client relationship management, working at Awnics from 2019 to 2020 and at Lancesoft in 2023.

From August 2023 to February 2025 he was a program manager at the American company Engage2Excel, working remotely with a team based in Montreal on projects for the Government of Canada, mainly for National Defence and Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada.

== Entrepreneurship ==
Ondongo is an e-resident of Estonia and the founder of BEGU Corporation OÜ, based in Tallinn; the commercial register lists him as its sole shareholder and management board member. Under his leadership the company is building a group of businesses in commerce, technology and services, starting with the online marketplace BEGU Deals.

== Research ==
Ondongo's research focuses on cybersecurity, mobile application security and natural language processing. He is a co-author of a paper on natural language processing in recommender systems. [ref: Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Recommendation Systems, ResearchGate]

== Recognition ==
In 2023 Ondongo was named Outstanding International Student in Bangalore for 2022–2023 by the Federation of All International Students in Bangalore.

= Lêna Bùi =
Lêna Bùi (born 1985) is a Vietnamese visual artist based in Saigon [ref: about, lêna bùi]. Her practice includes painting, drawing, video, installation, and performance. Her work examines relationships between people and the natural environment, including the effects of urban development and the role of spiritual beliefs in everyday life. [ref: ]

== Early life and education ==
Bùi was born in Đà Nẵng, Vietnam. She received a Bachelor of Arts in East Asian Studies from Wesleyan University in the United States.

== Work ==
Bùi’s work moves back and forth between various cultures and values, sometimes comparing and contrasting to better understand the socio-political make-up of the society.

During a 2023 residency at Delfina Foundation in London, Bùi developed Root People and the Circle Line. Presented that November as part of [https://www.delfinafoundation.com/whats-on/cyphering-vibrating-emanating/ Cyphering, Vibrating, Emanating], the performance combined video, spoken reflections, and diagrams to explore movement, belonging, and rootedness. [ref: Cyphering, Vibrating, Emanating, Delfina Foundation]

== Selected exhibitions ==
Bùi’s work has appeared in Foreign Bodies at Wellcome Collection in London in 2013 and Residual: Disrupted Choreographies at Carré d’Art in Nîmes, France, in 2014. She also participated in the 2022 Jeju Biennale, the 2024 Bangkok Art Biennale, and the 15th Shanghai Biennale in 2025.

== Residencies ==
Bùi was an artist in residence at Delfina Foundation in autumn 2023 [ref: Lêna Bùi, Delfina Foundation] and at NTU CCA in 2020. [ref: Lêna, archive.ntu.ccasingapore.org]

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Liujia mizhu

Draft text:
Liujia mizhu (, literally "Secret Prayer of the Six Jia") is a nine-character Daoist prayer for entering famous mountains, first attested in Ge Hong's Baopuzi, Inner Chapter 17, Dengshe ("Climbing [Mountains] and Crossing [Rivers]"), in the Eastern Jin dynasty. It is also known in later Chinese usage as the Nine-Character Prayer ().

== Name ==
"Liujia mizhu" is the name used in the Baopuzi itself. "Nine-Character Prayer" is a later general name for the same nine characters. The related Japanese practice, known as kuji-goshin-hō (九字護身法), uses a different ending and a different ritual system, and is treated separately below; it should not be conflated with the Chinese prayer.

== Text and context in the Baopuzi ==
The Baopuzi states:

The context is entering mountains. The same passage also mentions hanging five-colour silk on a large rock on a jiazi opening day. The key instruction is secret, constant recitation (). The claim that "nothing will not be warded off" is the text's own statement, not a modern verified efficacy claim.

=== Recitation ===
Point by point, the original text prescribes only the following; nothing further may be added to the original method:
* Secret recitation (): recited secretly, not chanted aloud in public;
* Constant recitation (): recited often; the text prescribes no fixed number of repetitions;
* One whole prayer: the nine characters are recited as a single sentence; the text prescribes no pause between characters, no paired hand seals, and no visualisation;
* Occasion: entering mountains.
The neighbouring jiazi opening-day silk-hanging rite in the same passage is a separate mountain-entering rite; its calendrical requirement must not be transferred into the secret prayer's recitation method.

=== Explanation ===
Character-by-character pinyin and literal glosses ( is read xíng, not háng; is the archaic graph in the quotation):
* lín: to approach, to face;
* bīng: soldiers, weapons;
* dòu: to fight, combat;
* zhě: one who …;
* jiē: all;
* zhèn: battle array;
* liè: to array, to line up;
* qián: forward;
* xíng: to march, to advance.
Syntax: ("those who face battle") is the subject, ("array in formation and march forward") is the predicate; the literal sense of the whole sentence is "the warriors facing battle all array in formation and march forward." Ge Hong's own gloss, "the essential way is not troublesome" (), marks the limit of the original explanation: it stops at the literal sense and does not develop per-character powers, symbolism, or meditation. Later per-character symbolic meanings are modern additions and are kept in the modern reception section, not in the original explanation.

The Baopuzi passage prescribes no hand seals (mudra), breathing technique, or per-character meditation paired with the nine characters. Those belong to later Japanese developments, below.

== The Six Jia ==
The Six Jia () are the six sexagesimal combinations beginning with the stem jia: jiazi, jiaxu, jiashen, jiawu, jiachen, and jiayin. In Daoist usage they are personified as protective generals, later commonly paired as the Six Ding and Six Jia.

== Character forms and variants ==
* 陣列前行 (zhen lie qian xing): the ending in the Baopuzi, meaning to array in formation and then march forward.
* 陳列前行: chen is an older graph for the same word as zhen ("battle array").
* 陣列在前 (zhen lie zai qian): the Japanese transmission form, meaning to be arrayed in front, rather than to march forward. It appears in Japanese Shugendo and Onmyodo sources and is a Japanese development, not the Baopuzi text.
* 數組: not a historical variant. No historical or liturgical form containing this reading has been located; do not list it as a variant.

== Japanese development ==
In Japan, the nine characters were developed in Shugendo and Onmyodo into a system pairing the characters with nine hand seals and a cutting grid of four vertical and five horizontal strokes, known as kuji-goshin-hō or kuji-kiri. Its nine characters end in zai qian ("in front"), not qian xing. Japanese sources themselves describe this system as a distinctively Japanese practice, not as orthodox esoteric Buddhist transmission. See Kuji-in.

== Modern reception ==
In contemporary Chinese source-citing contexts, the Baopuzi original ending qian xing is taken as the standard form.

In popular culture and in the existing Chinese Wikipedia article on jiuzi hushanfa, the Japanese zai qian form still circulates. Both facts should be stated side by side, rather than presenting either form as the whole of contemporary usage.

== References ==
* Ge Hong, Baopuzi neipian jiaoshi, collated by Wang Ming, Beijing: Zhonghua Shuju, 1985, juan 17, Dengshe.
* Stephen R. Bokenkamp, "Lingbao", in Fabrizio Pregadio (ed.), The Encyclopedia of Taoism, Routledge, 2008, vol. 1, pp. 663–669. (For Lingbao background only, not for a DZ 388 quotation of the nine characters.)
* Lingbao wufu xu (DZ 388), in the Daozang.
* A Chinese scholarly dictionary entry for "六甲".

== See also ==
* Kuji-in
* Baopuzi
* Ge Hong

Motu strikes a deal with the local tea stall owner, promising him a lifetime supply of free samosas if they win. However, the duo faces a major problem—they do not own a scooter. As the vehicle flies through the air, crashes through obstacles, and creates absolute chaos, it disrupts all the other racers trying to compete. Desperate to fix the speed, Motu starts pressing random buttons on the dashboard, making the vehicle even more dangerous by activating booster-like speed and extreme horsepower.

After a wild, gravity-defying ride, Motu and Patlu manage to cross the finish line first. However, their celebration is cut short. The judges disqualify them from winning the ₹100,000 prize because the hyper-modified vehicle was completely destroyed during the race—leaving behind no seat and nothing but a bare handle, which the judges refuse to classify as a legal scooter.
