Draft: Howard Lamar (Artist)

Draft text:
Howard Lamar (September 7, 1947 – November 15, 2018) was an American painter and sculptor associated with Ojai, Carmel-by-the-Sea, and Santa Barbara, California. Working across painting, sculpture, glass, and ceramics, Lamar developed a colorful figurative style characterized by personal narrative and recurring symbolic imagery. [ref: Off the Wall: Art in Unusual Places, Santa Barbara Independent] [ref: Howard Lamar, Focus on the Masters Arts Archive & Library] Critics and arts organizations identified influences in his work from European Modernists including Marc Chagall, Henri Matisse, Pablo Picasso, and Wassily Kandinsky.

== Early life and career ==
Lamar was born in Greenville, South Carolina, on September 7, 1947. A 1983 profile in the Sedona Red Rock News reported that he had drawn and painted since childhood and described him as a self-taught artist whose success in competitions encouraged him to pursue art full-time. [ref: Sedona Red Rock News, 1983-06-15, Sedona Red Rock News]

Lamar's early work included small, largely Impressionistic landscape watercolors. Focus on the Masters Arts Archive & Library later described his earliest exhibitions as watercolors displayed on a blanket and noted the substantial changes in his work over the course of his career.

By 1983, Lamar was exhibiting paintings, drawings, and sculpture at the Forms Gallery at Hozho in Sedona, Arizona. The Sedona Red Rock News described his work at the time as symbolic and narrative and reported that, after feeling constrained by the two-dimensional limitations of pictorial media, he had expanded into sculpture. The same profile noted earlier exhibitions in Beverly Hills and at the Santa Barbara Museum of Art.

== Carmel and Ojai ==
During the 1990s, Lamar operated the Howard Lamar Studio in Carmel-by-the-Sea, California. A 1995 interview in LEADERS identified him with the Carmel studio and discussed his preference for maintaining artistic control over his work rather than adapting it to the prescriptions of dealers or the commercial art market. [ref: The 'Maverick' Artist, LEADERS]

Around 2000, the Dallas Observer reported that a body of Lamar's work known as The Dallas Collection had been donated for an auction benefiting the Shakespeare Festival of Dallas and a matching grant from the McDermott Foundation. The works were also placed on public display at Samuell-Grand Park during the festival's summer performances. The newspaper identified Lamar at the time as a Carmel, California, artist. [ref: Blink, Dallas Observer]

Lamar subsequently returned to Ojai, where he operated Galerie Lamar. In 2004, he was selected for documentation by Focus on the Masters, a nonprofit arts education and archival organization that documents the lives and work of contemporary artists. Lamar's documentation took place in 2004, and the organization's archive holds extensive material concerning his career and work.

== Artistic practice and influences ==
Lamar worked in a range of media during his career, including painting, sculpture, glass, and ceramics. [ref: The Business of Art, LEADERS]

Writing about an exhibition of Lamar's work in Santa Barbara in 2008, Heather Jeno of the Santa Barbara Independent described his style as combining playful imagery and lighthearted colors with a distinctive symbolic language. She noted affinities with Chagall and Kandinsky and described Lamar's use of whimsical figures, animals, abstracted dots and lines, narrative compositions, and flattened or tilted pictorial planes.

Focus on the Masters similarly identified elements of Chagall, Matisse, and Picasso in Lamar's work while noting the development of his own recognizable expression and symbolism.

In 2024, art critic Abigail Leali examined Lamar's work in two essays for MutualArt Magazine. In “Returning, Reflecting, Rebuilding: The Art of Howard Lamar,” Leali considered Lamar's use of symbolism and the relationship between representation, abstraction, and the viewer's encounter with the work. [ref: Returning, Reflecting, Rebuilding: The Art of Howard Lamar, MutualArt] In a subsequent essay, “Howard Lamar and the Lineage of French Modernism,” she examined his work in relation to the French Modernist tradition, particularly the influence of Picasso and Matisse, and discussed his use of iconography as a means of visual communication. [ref: Howard Lamar and the Lineage of French Modernism, MutualArt]

== Iconography ==
Recurring symbols became a prominent feature of Lamar's work. In a 2015 interview with LEADERS, Lamar said that his icons had begun appearing when he was in his late twenties and had continued to develop as his exploration of different themes evolved. [ref: The Universal and The Esoteric, LEADERS]

Lamar divided the icons into what he called “universal” and “esoteric” groups. The first included familiar forms such as the sun, moon, hearts, stars, flowers, and cats. The second included symbols particular to his own work, including the Bird of Discernment, Energy, No-Time, and Infinity. Lamar described the meanings of the icons in relation to the themes he explored within individual works.

Leali subsequently discussed Lamar's iconography as part of his broader approach to visual communication, emphasizing the relationship between symbolic meaning and the viewer's experience of the work.
[truncated]

Draft text:
IEEE 1621 ("Standard for User Interface Elements in Power Control of Electronic Devices Employed in Office/Consumer Environments") is a standard published by the IEEE and appoved by ANSI that describes human interface guidelines regarding power controls in consumer electronics. [ref: IEEE Std 1621-2004 - IEEE Standard for User Interface Elements in Power Control of Electronic Devices Employed in Office/Consumer Environments, webstore.ansi.org] [ref: IEEE Standards Association, IEEE Standards Association] It includes terminology, icons, and lighting. [ref: ] IEEE 1621 references the following standards: ANSI/VITA 40, CIE 107, IEC 60073, IEC 60417, IEC 60447, IEC 62301, IEC 80416-1, IEC 80416-3, ISO 7000, ISO 9186, ISO 9241-1, ISO 9241-10, and ISO/IEC 13251.

== History and Motivation ==
Standardization of power controls in consumer electronics was spearheaded by Bruce Nordman at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory with funding provided by the California Energy Commission Public Interest Energy Research Program. [ref: Power Management Controls - Contact Us, ea-controls.lbl.gov] Nordman's reseach showed that many computers had power saving features disabled, mainly due to consumer confusion due to the lack of standardization of terminology and symbols in both hardware and software. [ref: Power Control Made Easy, EE Product News] Confusion was further componded due the symbol IEC 60417-5009 (⏻) meaning that the device was only disconnected from its power supply. Per IEC 60417-5009 this is defined as "stand-by." [ref: products.iec.ch] [ref: IEC 60417 – 5009, Stand-by, IEC] This allows for ambiguity. For example it could mean that the device is entirely off aside from an illuminated "off" indicator or in a sleep mode.

In April, 1998 the project was submitted to the California Energy Commission with the project starting in June of 2000. [ref: Power Management Controls - News, ea-controls.lbl.gov]

The IEEE New Standards Committee approved working group 1621 to develop a power controls standard in September of 2002. Three months later a draft of IEEE 1621 was published. [ref: Power Management Controls - User Interface Standard - IEEE 1621, ea-controls.lbl.gov]

The final standard was approved by the American National Standards Institute on 2005-03-24 and the standard was published on 2005-06-08.

Draft text:
The National Employment Law Project (NELP) is an American nonprofit organization focused on employment law, labor policy, and workers' rights. Founded in 1969, it conducts research and advocates for policies concerning wages, unemployment insurance, workplace safety, employment discrimination, and enforcement of labor laws. [ref: About Us, National Employment Law Project]

== History ==

NELP was founded in 1969 by students at Columbia Law School in New York City as a legal clinic serving workers. During the 1970s and 1980s, it provided litigation assistance, legal research, training, and expert testimony to legal-aid attorneys throughout the United States. The organization subsequently expanded its work in labor-policy research and advocacy. [ref: NELP's History of Fighting for Racial & Economic Justice, National Employment Law Project]

== Policy and advocacy ==

=== Minimum wage and employment standards ===

The NELP has advocated for increases to federal and state minimum wages. In 2014, The Washington Post reported that the organization's federal advocacy coordinator, Judith Conti, had criticized the Obama administration's initial proposal to raise the federal minimum wage to $9 per hour as insufficient. [ref: The inside story of how the White House learned to love the minimum wage, The Washington Post]

=== Wage-theft enforcement ===

The NELP has participated in California's Strategic Enforcement Partnership, a collaboration between the state's labor commissioner, worker centers, and legal-aid organizations to investigate wage theft and other labor-law violations.

A 2022 CalMatters investigation described NELP's role in coordinating participating organizations and their wage-theft investigations. The report identified Amaya Jennifer Lin, a NELP campaign manager, as a coordinator of the partnership. [ref: To fight wage theft California gets strong assist from worker centers, CalMatters]

=== Workplace safety ===

The NELP has also researched enforcement of workplace health and safety regulations. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the organization published research examining staffing levels at the Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA). In October 2020, The New Yorker cited NELP's research on the decline in federal workplace-safety inspectors and interviewed its worker-health-and-safety program director, Deborah Berkowitz. [ref: Trump's Labor Secretary Is a Wrecking Ball Aimed at Workers, The New Yorker]

Bou (legal name Bou Oy) is a brand agency headquartered in Helsinki, Finland, with a second studio in London, United Kingdom. Founded in 2018, the company provides branding, marketing, communications and public relations, and web development services, and describes itself as a "brand company" working across those four disciplines from a single point of contact. [ref: About, Bou] Its clients have included Klarna, Rovio Entertainment, Polestar, and the mobile game developer Metacore. In addition to its in-house team, Bou operates a freelance network with over 10,000 creative freelancers.

== History ==
Bou Oy was incorporated on 21 February 2018 in Helsinki. [ref: Bou — yritystiedot, päättäjät, taloustiedot, Finder.fi] According to the company, its founding team previously worked together on the brand of Slush, the Helsinki-based technology and startup conference, which the company cites as the origin of its focus on fast-growing technology companies. [ref: ”Slush oli meille yrityskiihdyttämö” –Teknologiatapahtuman johtajisto perusti bränditoimiston viemään Suomea maailmalle, Kauppalehti]

The company operates a second office in London and describes an extended freelance network marketed under the name "Bou & Co." through which it engages outside creative freelancers for specialized briefs.

In 2023, Bou was named as one of Adweek’s Fastest Growing Agencies. [ref: Fastest Growing Agencies 2023:, Adweek] In 2024, was featured in the Financial Times FT1000 ranking of Europe's fastest-growing companies. [ref: FT 1000: the eighth annual ranking of Europe’s fastest-growing companies, Financial Times]

== Services ==
Bou organizes its work into four service areas:
* Marketing — brand and go-to-market strategy, campaign planning, and paid/organic growth marketing.
* Communications & PR — media relations and public relations campaigns, including product launches.
* Design — brand identity, visual and verbal identity systems, and creative production.
* Web development — websites and digital products for client brands.

The company also offers brand "launch" services for new products and companies, and connects clients with independent creative freelancers through Bou & Co.

== Notable work ==
Bou states it has worked with more than 200 brands across Europe and the United States. Publicly documented client work includes:

=== Klarna ===
Bou served as an extension of Klarna's public relations team between 2021–2023, covering media relations, spokesperson training, and content across lifestyle, technology, and business media. [ref: Case: Klarna, Bou]

=== Rovio Entertainment ===
Bou worked as Rovio's lead PR and communications agency between 2023–2025, working on ongoing media relations alongside major launches for the Angry Birds franchise. The agency's work has also covered Rovio's sustainability and diversity initiatives within the games industry, including an inclusive game-design guide that received trade press coverage. [ref: Case: Rovio, Bou]

=== Polestar ===
Bou has provided public relations and brand awareness support to Polestar, the Swedish electric-vehicle manufacturer. Work has spanned earned media, media training, and brand activations addressing sustainability, design, and technology themes, including pop-up brand experiences such as a snow-built showroom that received international press coverage. [ref: Case: Polestar, Bou]

=== Merge Mansion ===
Bou has worked with Helsinki and Berlin based game studio Metacore since its inception, beginning with brand positioning and global launch work for its mobile game Merge Mansion. Since the game's 2020 launch, Bou has contributed to creative advertising and user acquisition campaigns, as well as website design and development for the game's companion site. [ref: Case: Merge Mansion, Bou]

=== PolyAI ===
In 2025, Bou led a brand renewal for the London-based voice-AI company PolyAI, encompassing brand strategy, visual and verbal identity, and a new website. The engagement also included a launch campaign for the company's platform featuring chef Gordon Ramsay, which ran across digital, out-of-home, and television placements in the United States. [ref: Gordon Ramsay and PolyAI Call Out Customer Service That Doesn't Listen, LBB Online]

=== Slush ===
Bou's founding team led marketing, communications, PR, and design for the startup event Slush in 2016 and 2017. The work included Slush 2016's entrance banner, which gained wide social media attention, and a redesigned event website that the agency states sold out the event and received design awards. [ref: This Is How Finland Greets Visitors Who Dare to Brave Its Bitter Winter, [[Fortune (magazine)]

=== City of Helsinki ===
Bou has worked on multiple creative campaigns with the City of Helsinki’s marketing department, with the goal of increasing Helsinki’s appeal in the eyes of global tech talent. For example, during the Covid19 pandemic, the agency’s “Helsinki, home-delivered” campaign packaged physical items representing the various benefits that Helsinki offers – from a sports watch to communicate proximity to nature to an old Nokia phone to communicate work-life balance – into physical boxes that were shipped overseas to potential talent. [ref: How design is bringing new places to life, Creative Review]

Peña Madridista Bangladesh (PMBD) is an official supporters' club (peña) of the Spanish football club Real Madrid, based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. It began in 2011 as an online group of Real Madrid fans and was recognised by Real Madrid as an official peña on 26 December 2019. The Spanish outlet La Galerna described it as the first Real Madrid peña in Bangladesh.

== History ==
=== Origins ===
According to Prothom Alo, the group started on 11 June 2011 with 60 members. La Galerna reported that it began in 2011 as an online community called "Madridista Bangladesh" with about 50 members, and that it grew to about 4,000 members within just over two years. Its early activity took place in a Facebook group and on other online platforms; members later began meeting in person for gatherings and match screenings. One of the group's administrators told The Daily Star that its first in-person meetup was held in Dhaka in 2012.

For the 2014 UEFA Champions League final between Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid, nearly 500 members gathered at the same time in Dhaka and Chittagong to watch the match. The same year, members attended an event of the Real Madrid Foundation in Chittagong, where a foundation official gave them the contacts needed to apply for official peña status. A first application, with 60 initial members, did not progress; Sifat Jasim and Tanbir Hossain later restarted the process with 54 founding members.

=== Official recognition ===
Real Madrid recognised the group as an official peña on 26 December 2019. It appears in the club's directory of supporters' clubs. The peña had 76 official members in March 2021 and 450 registered members in January 2025. Bangladesh has a second official Real Madrid supporters' group, All Whites Bangladesh.

=== Jeddah, 2025 and 2026 ===
In January 2025, four members of the peña, including president Md. Tanbir Hossain and secretary Sifat Jasim, travelled to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, to watch Real Madrid at the 2025 Supercopa de España, using four tickets allocated to the peña by Real Madrid. During the trip they met the club's president, Florentino Pérez. Hossain gave Pérez a Bangladesh jersey bearing his name and received a Real Madrid jersey in return, and the members also presented Pérez with a nakshi kantha. [ref: Florentino Pérez presides the meeting of peñas madridistas in Jeddah, Real Madrid TV]

In January 2026 representatives of the peña again attended Real Madrid's gathering of supporters' clubs at the Hilton hotel in Jeddah, held before the 2026 Supercopa de España final and attended by around 500 fans from 26 supporters' clubs. [ref: Florentino Pérez leads Real Madrid supporters' club gathering in Jeddah, Real Madrid CF] [ref: Bangladeshi fans present Nakshi Kantha to Real Madrid president, Daily Times of Bangladesh] They presented Pérez with a framed, hand-stitched nakshi kantha.

== Activities ==
The peña organises group screenings of Real Madrid matches and celebrations of the club's titles. In March 2021 it held an event in Banani, Dhaka, marking Real Madrid's 119th anniversary, which included a quiz about the club. During the COVID-19 pandemic its activity moved largely to social media, including a podcast broadcast on Facebook before each Real Madrid match. Its stated aims include uniting Real Madrid supporters across the country and helping disadvantaged children in Bangladesh to play football. Bangladesh national football team captain Jamal Bhuyan recorded a video message in support of the peña.

Draft text:
Network Tasman Limited is a New Zealand electricity distribution company based in Hope, near Richmond, in the Tasman District. It owns and operates electricity distribution infrastructure supplying homes and businesses across the Nelson and Tasman regions in the northern South Island.

The company is wholly owned by Network Tasman Trust [ref: About the Trust - Network Tasman], a consumer trust established in 1993 [ref: Energy Companies (Tasman Energy Limited) Vesting Order 1993, New Zealand Legislation] following restructuring of the New Zealand electricity industry. The trust holds the company's shares on behalf of eligible electricity consumers in the historic Tasman network area.

Network Tasman adopted its present name in 1998, following the separation of the electricity distribution and retailing operations of Tasman Energy Limited. The company's history can be traced to the establishment of electricity supply in the region in 1908 [ref: History of Network Tasman - Network Tasman].

On 31 March 2026, Network Tasman amalgamated with Nelson Electricity Limited, combining two previously separate electricity distribution businesses. The amalgamated company reported 53,809 electricity connections as at 31 March 2026 [ref: Amalgamation of NTL and NEL - Network Tasman] [ref: Network Tasman Announces 2026 Annual Results - Network Tasman].

== History ==

=== Early electricity supply, 1908–1958 ===
The origins of electricity distribution in the Tasman region date to 1908, when Kōhatu farmer Robert Ellis introduced electric power to his home. In 1911, Ellis obtained a licence to supply electricity commercially through the Waimea Electric Supply and Manufacturing Company, using a waterwheel at a flourmill. The company continued operating independently until 1933.

Other electricity undertakings developed during the early twentieth century, principally under local authority ownership. Motueka Borough Council began generating electricity in 1921, followed by Murchison County Council, which commissioned the Six-Mile hydroelectric scheme in 1922.

Nelson City Council established a coal-fired electricity generating station at Wakefield Quay in 1923, beginning the development of a separate municipal electricity supply system for central Nelson.

The Golden Bay Electric Power Board was established in 1925, with the Pupu hydroelectric scheme commissioned in 1929. The Waimea Electric Power Board was established in the same year, absorbing existing electricity supply undertakings in Brightwater and Motueka.

Development of electricity generation continued during the following decades. Construction of the Cobb hydroelectric scheme began in 1935, with the project completed by the government in 1944. A hydroelectric plant was commissioned at Maruia Falls in 1951.

A major development occurred in 1958 when the Nelson and Tasman electricity supply system was connected to New Zealand's national electricity grid, reducing the region's dependence on local generating schemes [ref: History of Network Tasman - Network Tasman] [ref: Nelson Electricity buyout welcomed - Network Tasman].

=== Consolidation of electricity authorities, 1963–1988 ===
During the second half of the twentieth century, electricity supply authorities in the region were progressively consolidated.

In 1963, the Waimea Electric Power Board merged with the Murchison electricity undertaking. In 1976, the Waimea and Golden Bay electric power boards amalgamated to form the Tasman Electric Power Board.

The combined authority was responsible for electricity distribution across a geographically extensive area, incorporating rural communities, coastal settlements and growing urban centres.

In 1988, the Tasman Electric Power Board became Tasman Energy [ref: History of Network Tasman - Network Tasman].

=== Electricity industry reform, 1990–1998 ===
Reform of New Zealand's electricity industry during the early 1990s led to the commercialisation of regional electricity authorities.

Under the Energy Companies Act 1992, electricity authorities were required to adopt corporate structures. Tasman Energy considered alternative ownership arrangements, including private ownership, local authority ownership and a consumer trust.

In 1992, the company's directors recommended that the business be owned through a trust representing electricity consumers. Following public consultation, the Tasman Electric Power Trust was established on 30 April 1993 to hold the shares in the company on behalf of consumers.

Sir Wallace Rowling, a former Prime Minister of New Zealand and former Member of Parliament for Tasman, became the trust's founding chair.

Further electricity industry reforms [ref: www.beehive.govt.nz] in 1998 - the Bradford reforms - required electricity distribution businesses to be separated from electricity retailing activities. Tasman Energy retained the electricity distribution network and sold its retailing business to Contact Energy.

The distribution company was renamed Network Tasman Limited, while the Tasman Electric Power Trust became Network Tasman Trust [ref: ].

=== Network Tasman from 1998 ===
Following the 1998 restructuring, Network Tasman continued developing and maintaining the region's electricity distribution infrastructure under consumer trust ownership.

The company retained responsibility for the electricity network, while electricity retailers supplied electricity to consumers and issued electricity bills.

Karen Schepers (1959–1983) was an American woman from Elgin, Illinois, who disappeared in April 1983 after spending an evening at a bar in nearby Carpentersville. [ref: Coroner confirms human remains found Tuesday belong to Karen Schepers, www.dailyherald.com] She was last seen in the early hours of April 16, and her yellow 1980 Toyota Celica was also missing. [ref: 'Where is Karen?': Police who started cold case podcast find woman's remains after 42 years, USA TODAY]

On March 25, 2025, searchers located a vehicle in the Fox River and found a license plate matching Schepers' missing car. [ref: Skeletal remains found in car pulled from Fox River that belonged to Karen Schepers, missing since 1983 - CBS Chicago, www.cbsnews.com] The vehicle, a 1980 Toyota Celica, was recovered the following day, with skeletal remains inside. The Kane County Coroner's Office identified the remains as Schepers through dental records and a forensic dentist.

Schepers worked as a computer programmer at a bank and had previously participated in music and cheerleading during high school. She lived alone in Elgin at the time of her disappearance. Investigators later found that her bank accounts and credit cards had shown no activity after she went missing. BR Fares is a British website that lists fares for journeys on the National Rail network in Great Britain. It was founded in 2012 by Paul Kelly and is operated by BR Fares Ltd. [ref: About BR Fares, BR Fares Ltd.]

== Content ==
For any pair of stations, the site lists the available fares with their price, route, time restrictions and validity. Railcard discounts can be applied. [ref: Are new Scottish operators less generous than before?, [[Rail (magazine)] [ref: Many staff appear to lack knowledge – across all lines, [[Rail (magazine)] Mark Smith, author of the rail travel website The Man in Seat Sixty-One, has described it as an online version of the rail industry's fares manuals, noting that it takes some getting used to. [ref: Train travel in Britain, The Man in Seat 61] Since June 2026 the site has also sold tickets for walk-up fares, as a sub-agent of the rail ticket retailer Raileasy. [ref: About ticket purchase, BR Fares Ltd.]

== Reception ==
Barry Doe, who wrote a fares column for Rail, recommended the site in several columns. In 2015 he highlighted the detail it gives on ticket restrictions and validity, information he argued operators should be required to show before sale. In 2021 he noted that some through fares missing from the National Rail journey planner were listed on BR Fares. At a time when some industry systems were applying railcard discounts with incorrect rounding, he recommended the site for checking the correct fare, describing it as accurate where many internal industry systems were not. [ref: Unreliability a barrier towards transport integration, [[Rail (magazine)] In 2022 he advised readers to check fares on the site before buying any walk-up ticket, contrasting it with journey planners, which show only the fares for the trains they list.

Smith recommends the site for "London International (CIV)" fares, which connect domestic journeys with Eurostar. [ref: Starting your journey from the UK regions, The Man in Seat 61] The Financial Times used BR Fares data in a 2025 analysis of season-ticket value and quoted Kelly on the loss of flexible fares. [ref: In charts: Death of the season ticket, Financial Times] In 2016 the campaign group Railfuture, testing how quickly websites and ticket machines added newly opened stations, found that BR Fares did not yet list two stations several days after they opened. International Northern Ssireum Federation (INSF) is a United States-approved non-profit organization established to preserve and internationalize "Northern Ssireum" (including Tti-ssireum and Sokswae), a traditional style of Korean wrestling rooted in the northern regions of the Korean Peninsula and Manchuria.

== Overview and Status ==
The federation operates a global governance framework with participation from 19 countries to systematize and standardize Northern Ssireum.

INSF is registered as a non-governmental organization (NGO) with the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA). It is also officially listed in the database of the Union of International Associations (UIA) under Organization ID: AA7728. The UIA profile defines the organization's primary aim as the preservation and globalization of Northern Ssireum, recognizing its identity within the context of UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.

== Core Activities ==
=== UN High-Level Political Forum (HLPF) Side Event ===
On July 9, 2026, INSF hosted an official side event at the United Nations High-level Political Forum (HLPF). The event focused on the sustainable transmission of traditional wrestling heritage along the Silk Road and highlighted the role of physical culture in achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

=== International Competitions ===
The federation organized the International Northern Ssireum Championship to commemorate UN International Youth Day. Additionally, to celebrate the joint inscription of Ssireum on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, the federation hosted the 2nd International Northern Ssireum World Championships to mark the "2026 UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage Day."

=== Academic Research and Publications ===
INSF conducts research focusing on the technical and historical connections between Korean Ssireum and other Eurasian traditional wrestling styles, such as Central Asian Kurash, Pakistani Kushti, and Mongolian Bokh.
* The research findings have been published as a book series titled The Warrior's Path: Silk Road Traditional Wrestling and Physical Culture on Amazon.
* Academic papers and archived materials from the "Silk Road Warrior Arts Research Project" are indexed and preserved with Digital Object Identifiers (DOIs) in the Zenodo repository operated by CERN.

an on-chain Merkle claim contract.

== NOVAP token ==

NOVAP is a TEP-74 standard token (jetton) on TON mainnet with a
fixed supply of 100,000,000. [ref: NOVAP jetton, Tonviewer]
The project states that 79 million NOVAP — covering the airdrop pool and
liquidity reserve — are held in a 2-of-3 multisignature treasury
contract. Project documentation describes a Season 1
distribution of a 25,000,000 NOVAP pool capped at 50,000 NOVAP per user,
with allocations vesting 25% at the token generation event and 25% per
month for three months thereafter.

Cuffem (born April 30, 2002) is an American online streamer and internet personality. Originally from Alabama, he is known for his gaming, reaction, online dating and in-real-life (IRL) livestreams. He first gained recognition on Twitch before becoming active on Kick, where he frequently collaborated with fellow streamer Adin Ross. [ref: The 25 Up-And-Coming Streamers You Need To Know, Ranked, Complex]

In February 2025, Complex ranked Cuffem 12th on its list of up-and-coming livestreamers. His Kick channel recorded a peak of 236,746 concurrent viewers in November 2025, according to streaming analytics provider Streams Charts. [ref: cuffem – Kick Stats, Analytics and Channel Overview, Streams Charts]

== Early life ==
Cuffem grew up in Alabama, United States. Biographical listings report his date of birth as April 30, 2002.

== Career ==

=== 2019–2022: Streaming beginnings ===
Cuffem began streaming in 2019, initially broadcasting gameplay from NBA 2K and Fortnite. He subsequently expanded into Grand Theft Auto V roleplay, conversational broadcasts and other variety content. He became associated with Adin Ross's SSB streaming group, which included several other gaming personalities.

=== 2023–2024: Kick and collaborations ===
Cuffem developed an audience on Kick through a combination of gaming, commentary, online dating and IRL streams. His broadcasts frequently featured interactions with viewers and collaborations with other online personalities.

=== 2025–present: Audience growth ===
In February 2025, Complex ranked Cuffem 12th on its list of 25 up-and-coming streamers, highlighting his online dating and Grand Theft Auto broadcasts.

In September 2025, he appeared during Kai Cenat's Mafiathon 3 livestream event. [ref: Kick streamer Cuffem finally gets chance to join Kai Cenat's Mafiathon 3, Sportskeeda] On November 30, 2025, his Kick channel reached a peak of 236,746 concurrent viewers, according to Streams Charts.

In January 2026, Cuffem, Adin Ross and rapper 6ix9ine recorded a diss track during a livestream, attracting coverage from Complex. [ref: 6ix9ine, Adin Ross, and Cuffem Record Diss Track, Complex]

In October 2026, he appeared on Bradley Martyn's Rawtalk podcast to discuss his streaming career and online content. [ref: Cuffem Exposes The Truth About Streaming, Money & Beef With Jshock, Apple Podcasts] That month, reports also described his proposal for a streaming collective called Sinister Six. [ref: Cuffem Announces New Content Group Called Sinister Six, NDTV Sports]

Cuffem is primarily known for variety livestreams, including gaming, reactions, video-chat interactions, online dating and IRL broadcasts. Complex highlighted his energetic presentation and transition from gaming content into a broader range of livestream formats.

In May 2025, Dexerto reported that Cuffem had been arrested in Georgia on alleged speeding and reckless-driving offenses. He was subsequently released and returned to livestreaming. [ref: Twitch streamer Cuffem goes live right after getting out of jail for alleged reckless driving, Dexerto]

In July 2025, Cuffem was temporarily banned from Kick following a livestream described as a "lean mukbang". Cuffem disputed that the broadcast involved actual lean, and Adin Ross publicly defended him. [ref: Adin Ross Defends Kick Streamer Cuffem After Alleged Lean Mukbang Ban, Complex]

Lee Su-yeon (born 1982) is a South Korean picture book author, illustrator, and graphic novelist. Her work focuses on emotions and memories, growth and healing, employing watercolor and anthropomorphic animal characters to portray the inner lives of her characters. Her notable works include Breakfast On the Moon, Two Friends on My Shoulders, I Sell Furniture Somehow, and It Rains and the Grass Grows.

== Life and Career ==
Lee was born in Seoul and studied for an MA at the Camberwell College of Arts in the United Kingdom. She teaches picture book making and graphic novel courses at Hankyoreh Education and Chungkang College of Cultural Industries.

In addition to writing and illustrating her own works, Lee illustrates books by other authors. Her works include 《우리 마을에 온 손님》 (Visitors in Our Village) and 《커다란 집》 (The Big House), both written by Park Hye-sun and 《많은 사람들이 바다로 가》 (Many People Go to the Sea), written by Kim Gaemi.

《내 어깨 위 두 친구》 (Two Friends on My Shoulders) was mentioned in the 2023 White Ravens catalogue selected by the International Youth Library in Munich. Her graphic novel 《어쩌다 보니 가구를 팝니다》 (I Sell Furniture Somehow), based on her experience working as a furniture salesperson in her twenties, was featured in the 2025 Book Illustrators Gallery at the Asian Festival of Children's Content (AFCC).

In 2026, Lee participated in a discussion program featuring children's literature creators from South Korea and Australia in Sydney.

== Awards and Recognition ==

== Artistic Style ==
Lee explores deep emotions, relationships, growth, and healing through her writing and image making. She observes everyday events and shifts in characters' feelings, portraying people's inner lives through anthropomorphic characters. Lee seeks to express a range of emotions through her characters and share stories of empathy and comfort with readers.

Paul Hallam is a British DJ, film maker, publisher and former Mod Impresario.

Born in Staines, Middlesex, England in 1965, Hallam began his career as a professional Mod in 1983 aged 17 by dj'ing and promoting his RnB nights at Feltham Football Club and a Mod club called Sneakers, in Shepherds Bush. The Dj's were Hallam and Richard "Shirley" Early and is now fondly remembered as "the mod club" of the 1980s period. [ref: PAUL HALLAM - SNEAKERS, suityourself]

Later that year he launched his own fanzine Sense of Style - which was arguably the first professionally typeset and printed fanzine due to Hallam's day job in print and design.

In the latter part of the decade Hallam along with many others left the mod scene preferring the Jazz Revival scene which saw Hallam work as the resident dj at the world famous 100 for nearly 10 years. He was honoured with a photograph on the clubs wall of fame between Noel Gallagher and the Sex Pistols.

In the early 90s Hallam partly abandoned music for a career in politics. Running twice for Labour councilor in very Tory Cobham. He also made a speech at the Labour Party Conference of 1992 introduced by the then shadow home secretary Tony Blair. [ref: Paul Hallam speaking at The Labour Party Conference, 1992]

In 1997 at the height of Brit Pop Hallam dj'd and promoted 'Club Popcorn' along with fellow former mods Danny Decourtelle and Dave Edwards at the Oxford Street club. Other 100 Club events he was responsible for included the reformation gig of the Mod Revival band The Chords and the sold-out 20th anniversary Punk festival (which was ironically 21 years on after the original event) which saw The Buzzcocks, Subway and Perry return to the club for the first since the original festival.

Club Popcorn went on tour in the summer of 1998 playing seaside towns including Exmouth Pavilion where local band Muse were 3rd on the bill.

In 1999 Hallam became associate producer for the Save GLR campaign promoting the 2 night fund raising concerts at the 100 club which included Bez and Joe Strummer, Inspiral Carpets Hingley and Spizz Energi who would go on to work with Paul in the next decade.

Just before the turn of the millennium Hallam bought a 50% stake in the Northern Bohemian Velvet Rock Club in Teplice (Czech Republic).

In 2000 he fulfilled a lifetime ambition of owning his own London bar by opening the S.M.E.R.S.H. bar in the then, not quite so fashionable Shoreditch. Ran with fellow former mod Piller the bar sold eastern European drinks in a cold war style bunker.

BBC'S Big Read top 100 books of all time used SMERSH to film its James Bond piece in 2003 with Hallam providing the cold war narration for the TV show. Bizarre in the fact that Hallam had never read an Ian Flemming book.

Smersh is generally remembered as one of the first cool bars of Shoreditch.

Throughout the early 2000s Hallam worked on radio with the former Punk legend Spizz Energi including a residency on one of the pioneers of internet radio Soul 24-7 for almost two years before being sacked for "talking too much on air".

In 2003 he founded the company Filthy Lucre Limited with Decourtelle which purchased Filthy Macnastys pub in Islington - spiritual home of TheLibertines and former residence of Pete Doherty who worked as a barman there with Carl Barat. Filthys claimed to sell the second best Guinness In London.

In 2006 Filthy Lucre purchased the Gladstone in Borough.

Hallam guested on the Craig Charles show on BBC Radio 6 in 2005. The same year he guest DJ'd at the Isle of Wight festival - on the same bill as the Rolling Stones.

2013 saw Hallam launch Street sounds, music paper along with Bushell. It ran for 5 years and 17 issues. At one point being the biggest selling music paper in the UK.

Hallam retired from dj'ing in 2016 but nobody noticed so he returned in 2019 and retired for good to a sold-out venue in Brighton in the August bank holiday of that year.

In 2015 Hallam appeared on a TV show Street Sounds and Style, talking about 80s youth culture. Acclaimed photographer EwenSpencer was so impressed by Hallam's 80s photos his company SeeW published a book of Hallams 80s photos called Odds & Sods. [ref: Odds & Sods - Record Collector Magazine]

Numerous exhibitions followed in London, Italy, Spain and LA. Along with radio and TV appearances to promote it. [ref: Diving into the 1980s Mod Scene with Photographer Paul Hallam, VICE] [ref: Paul Hallam on Robert Elms, BBC London. Odds & Sods Book. 17 02 2016] [ref: Paul J Hallam, YouTube]

In 2015 Hallam was made a listed Londoner on the Robert Elms show on BBCRadioLondon. [ref: Paul Hallam as Robert Elms' Listed Londoner. BBC Radio London.] In the same year he launched Old Dog Books - a publishing house producing 21st century-pop-pulp-fiction in an attempt to recreate the excitement of the Pulp Fiction novels that so many grew up with like Richard Allens’ Skinhead books. Between 2015 and 2025 they published over 20 titles.

2022 Paul conceived Produced and appeared in the Documentary KICK OUT THE JAMS - The XFM Story. Featuring Ricky Gervais and Steve Merchant amongst others which premièred at Vue Cinema Shaftsbury Avenue and is currently available to watch on Amazon Prime.

Paul Lives in Cobham Surrey and supports MillwallFootballClub.

== [user] ==
Muayad "Mo" Abbas is a real estate development executive and university lecturer known for his involvement in residential, hospitality, and mixed-use developments in the United States and international markets. He is Managing Director of Development at OKO Group and a lecturer at the University of Miami School of Architecture. [ref: Bisnow's Hurricane Irma Miami State of the Market, Bisnow] [ref: Former Ritz president leads new North Miami project, The Real Deal] [ref: Rafael Moneo Reveals Design of His First Condo Tower in Miami, ArchDaily]

== Career ==

=== Related International ===
Abbas previously served as Vice President of Related International, the international development arm of the Related Group, overseeing real estate operations in Panama, Colombia, and Argentina. [ref: Bisnow's Hurricane Irma Miami State of the Market, Bisnow]

=== Urbanis Advisors and Apeiron Living ===
Abbas founded Urbanis Advisors, a real estate development and advisory firm. He subsequently co-founded Apeiron Living, a luxury residential and hospitality venture conceived in collaboration with Horst Schulze, co-founder and former president of the Ritz-Carlton Hotel Company, and Michael Bedner, co-founder of Hirsch Bedner Associates (HBA). [ref: Former Ritz president leads new North Miami project, The Real Deal] [ref: Rafael Moneo Reveals Design of His First Condo Tower in Miami, ArchDaily] [ref: Apeiron at the Jockey Club wins approval, plans to launch sales, The Real Deal]

The founders developed Apeiron as a hospitality and residential brand combining luxury living with personalized service, health and wellness, preventive medical care, and arts and cultural programming. The concept was designed primarily for affluent, active older adults seeking a residential environment that supported independent living and aging in place.

The brand's development included a positioning and identity exercise undertaken with international design consultancy Pentagram in 2014. [ref: Developers of luxe North Miami project get $21M in financing, The Real Deal] The concept emphasized architecture, hospitality, wellness, and curated experiences as elements of an integrated residential lifestyle. Apeiron's proposed wellness program included medical services coordinated with the Cleveland Clinic. [ref: Apeiron at the Jockey Club wins approval, plans to launch sales, The Real Deal]

Apeiron at the Jockey Club in Miami, Florida, was conceived as the venture's flagship development and a model for potential expansion into other U.S. markets. The proposed redevelopment of the historic waterfront property included serviced residences, hospitality amenities, wellness facilities, dining, cultural programming, and a marina. [ref: Apeiron at the Jockey Club wins approval, plans to launch sales, The Real Deal]

The architectural design was led by Spanish architect Rafael Moneo, recipient of the Pritzker Architecture Prize, with Stantec serving as local architect of record. [ref: Rafael Moneo Reveals Design of His First Condo Tower in Miami, ArchDaily] The project attracted media attention for its architecture, financing, development approvals, and legal disputes.

The development faced legal challenges from existing condominium associations seeking to block construction. In June 2020, Florida's Third District Court of Appeal upheld the trial court's rulings, affirming Apeiron Miami LLC's development and property rights at the Jockey Club. [ref: Jockey Club residents reignite lawsuit against next-door landowner, The Real Deal] [ref: Apeiron at the Jockey Club Developer Wins Key Ruling from Appeals Court, Carlton Fields] [ref: Developer Wins Key Ruling from Appeals Court in Miami-Dade, Council on Vertical Urbanism]

=== Mast Capital ===
Abbas subsequently served as Senior Vice President of Development at Mast Capital, a Miami-based real estate investment and development firm.

During his tenure, he was involved in the development of Cipriani Residences Miami, an 80-story, 397-residence luxury condominium tower in Miami's Brickell neighborhood, designed by Arquitectonica. [ref: Mast Capital, www.mastcapital.com] [ref: ] [ref: Mast Capital, www.mastcapital.com]

The project was developed through a collaboration between Mast Capital and the Cipriani family, whose international hospitality business traces its origins to Harry's Bar in Venice, founded in 1931. Led by Giuseppe Cipriani, the family's hospitality organization partnered with Mast Capital to establish its first ground-up residential development in the United States.

=== OKO Group ===
In 2025, Abbas joined OKO Group as Managing Director of Development, overseeing a portfolio of luxury residential, hospitality, and mixed-use developments. His responsibilities encompass development strategy, design, entitlements, construction, and project execution. [ref: About us, OKO Group]

== Academic career ==
Abbas is a lecturer at the University of Miami School of Architecture, where he teaches real estate entrepreneurship in the Master of Real Estate Development + Urbanism (MRED+U) program.

Mass Effect: Universe is the name associated with a cancelled Mass Effect video game developed by BioWare, Published by Electronic Arts (EA). The project, commonly referred to as Mass Effect 5, was announced in 2020 and cancelled on 21 October 2026 as EA announced the closure of BioWare. The name Mass Effect: Universe appeared in an internal trailer leaked after the cancellation, but had not been formally announced by EA as the game's final title. [ref: BioWare Update, BioWare Blog] [ref: A Convincing Trailer For What May Have Been Mass Effect 5 Has Leaked [UPDATE: It's Real], Kotaku]

The cancelled project was intended to continue the science-fiction role-playing series following 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda. An internal cinematic trailer that surfaced online on 22 October 2026 included an appearance by Liara T'Soni, a character from the original trilogy. Its authenticity was corroborated by journalists at IGN and Bloomberg News. [ref: Leaked Mass Effect: Universe trailer gives a taste of what we're all missing, Ars Technica]

== Development ==
BioWare publicly revealed that a new Mass Effect game was in pre-production at The Game Awards 2020 in December 2020. The accompanying teaser included an N7 insignia, and gaming publications identified the figure at its conclusion as apparently being Liara T'Soni. The trailer ended with the statement that Mass Effect would continue; no release date or official title was announced. [ref: New Mass Effect Debuts At Game Awards, GameSpot] [ref: BioWare Double Feature at The Game Awards, BioWare Blog]

BioWare released further teasers during its annual N7 Day celebrations, including three short clips in November 2023. The studio said at the time that the game remained in pre-production. [ref: BioWare Is Teasing The Next Mass Effect With Cryptic Videos For N7 Day, GameSpot]

Following the release of Dragon Age: The Veilguard, BioWare announced in January 2025 that a smaller core team was working on the new Mass Effect game. The team included developers from the original trilogy, among them executive producer Mike Gamble, Preston Watamaniuk, Derek Watts and Parrish Ley. [ref: BioWare Studio Update, BioWare Blog] On 7 November 2025, Gamble reaffirmed that the game was in development and that BioWare and EA remained committed to the series. [ref: N7 Day 2025, Electronic Arts]

== Cancellation and closure of BioWare ==
On 21 October 2026, EA announced it would close BioWare and cancel development of the next Mass Effect game as part of a wider restructuring. Bloomberg News reported that the company planned to cut approximately 400 jobs, including around 50 positions at BioWare. According to an internal EA communication reported by the press, the company had decided not to proceed with the project, which it characterised as being in early development. [ref: Electronic Arts to Shed 400 Jobs, Shut Down BioWare to Cut Costs, Bloomberg News] [ref: RIP BioWare: EA shuts down storied RPG studio after over three decades, Ars Technica]

BioWare confirmed the decision in a statement on its website, saying that the studio was closing after more than three decades and that early development of the next Mass Effect project was ending.

== Leaked trailer ==
On 22 October 2026, a previously unreleased trailer for the cancelled game appeared on Reddit. It was labelled as in-engine material produced with pre-production assets by a small development team. Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier confirmed that the footage was from the game BioWare had been developing before its closure. [ref: Mass Effect Universe trailer leaks online, showcases what BioWare was working on before being shut down, Video Games Chronicle]

The trailer depicts a former military officer meeting an asari in a bar and alludes to the character undertaking covert operations. It features a confrontation involving Liara T'Soni and ends with the title Mass Effect: Universe. Commentators described its apparent direction as resembling a spy thriller, although the footage did not establish the final scope, gameplay or story of the cancelled project.

== Public response ==
The cancellation and leaked trailer prompted criticism from fans and discussion about the future of the franchise. A petition using the hashtag #SaveMassEffect was launched following the studio's closure, asking EA to resume the franchise under another developer or license the intellectual property to another company. IGN reported on 23 October 2026 that the petition had surpassed 50,000 signatures; it later reported calls from some fans for a boycott of EA products. [ref: Save Mass Effect Petition Hits 50,000 Signatures, Just Days After BioWare Closure, IGN] [ref: Mass Effect Fans Call for EA Boycott as Petition to Save BioWare's Canceled Game Garners More than 75,000 Signatures, IGN]

Lindsey James Alvarez Lee (born 1979), known professionally as Lindslee, is a Filipino contemporary artist based in Metro Manila, Philippines. He began his career as an abstract painter in the early 2000s before expanding into sculpture, installation, taxidermy and conceptual art. His work incorporates everyday objects, food and familiar cultural forms to explore consumption, Filipino culture, social behavior and the relationship between art and society.

== Early life and education ==
Lindslee was born in 1979 in Bacolod and is of Chinese-Filipino descent. He grew up in Hinigaran, Negros Occidental. He attended St. John's Institute in Bacolod, where he took part in painting competitions. He was a national finalist in the 1998 Shell National Students Art Competition and a semi-finalist in the Metrobank Young Painters competition in 1999 and 2000. He earned a Bachelor of Fine Arts in painting from the University of Santo Tomas College of Fine Arts and Design in 2000.

After graduating he went to New York City, where he took courses in mixed media, drawing, painting, and color and composition at the Art Students League of New York. While there he showed in juried exhibitions, was associated with the Greenwich Art Society and won first prize in the mixed-media category of the 2001 Annual Fine Art Show in Long Beach, New York. After winning a local art competition, he held his first solo exhibition at the Harrison Public Library in New York in 2002. He also worked as a house painter during this period, an experience he later connected to his interest in surfaces and repetition.

== Career ==
=== Abstraction (2002–2006) ===
After returning to the Philippines, Lindslee held the solo exhibitions Perception at Avellana Art Gallery (2002) and Cause and Effect at The Drawing Room in Makati (2003). His early work was abstract, mostly in grays and earth tones. In April 2004 he exhibited with former University of Santo Tomas classmates Julio Jose "Jo" Austria, Jeffrey "Jeps" Belen and Artemio "Art" Bermido in Fibonacci, a group show based on the numerical sequence. His 2004 show SR at The Big & Small Art Co. in SM Megamall consisted of square mixed-media works built from layered resin, wax, acrylic, mesh and plastic. The Philippine Star read the surfaces as a reference to grime on Manila's city walls. Reviewing the same show in the Philippine Daily Inquirer, Constantino C. Tejero called him "one of the more accomplished abstractionists of his generation". That year he was shortlisted for the Ateneo Art Awards for his Cause and Effect series.

In 2005 he exhibited Face:Phase, a series of two-sided mixed-media works, at the Cultural Center of the Philippines. His 2006 exhibition Finding Normal at the Goethe-Institut Manila was his eighth solo show. It marked a return to acrylic and oil and introduced a wider color range than his usual grays. In June 2007 he and Austria held Black and White Conversation, a two-person exhibition at West Gallery in Quezon City that dealt with the commercialization of abstract painting.

=== Taxidermy and conceptual work (2007–2012) ===
In 2007 Lindslee began combining taxidermied animals with paintings. His exhibition Animan at The Drawing Room included Sleep for Sale, a taxidermied duck on a pillow, and Pork Chop Explosion, a pig standing on a painting. The Inquirer compared these works to Robert Rauschenberg's combines and saw them as a move away from abstract expressionism. The Manila Bulletin read the show as a comment on commercial gimmickry and copying in Philippine abstract art. He continued the approach in Figuring Abstraction (2008), which included a taxidermied rooster on a lightbox and a duck beside an oversized egg. In 2008 he was a Joan Mitchell Foundation scholar at the Ox-Bow fall artist residency in Saugatuck, Michigan.

In May 2009 he exhibited Metamorphosis, a series of abstract works that drew on familiar images such as a television station's sign-off screen, at Galleria Duemila in Pasay. Later that year he was one of ten artists selected for the "10 Most Exciting Young Artists" exhibition organized by Nokia and the Inquirers Lifestyle section at the Gallery of Greenbelt 5 in Makati. In September 2009 Tropical Storm Ondoy flooded his studio in Cainta, Rizal, leaving works in progress caked in mud. He was a finalist in the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas Tanaw national art competition in 2011 and 2013.

=== Paintings as objects (2013–2019) ===
He later reworked the flood-damaged canvases by cutting, rolling and stacking them, and the Inquirer identified the storm as a turning point toward conceptual art. The resulting exhibition, It's All in the Mind, opened at Galleria Duemila in Pasay in August 2013. It included Ignorant Critic, a taxidermied goat that appears to have bitten off part of a painted landscape. Reviewers compared it to Rauschenberg's Monogram.

In December 2014 he took part in the S-AIR artist-in-residence program in Sapporo, supported by the Japan Foundation. His 2016 exhibition Untitled Cliché at Artery Art Space in Cubao satirized the art market. One work, Pain Thing, connected canvases to intravenous bottles of paint labeled with roles such as "collector" and "financier". Your Personality Is Your Worst Enemy at Galleria Duemila (2017) dealt with the tension between freedom and pragmatism. In 2019 he held a solo exhibition, You Are What You Cheat, at the Pinto Art Museum in Antipolo.

Guru Organic Energy Corp. (), commonly known as Guru (stylized GURU), is a Canadian beverage company based in Montreal, Quebec, that produces organic energy drinks. The company launched its first energy drink in 1999 and markets its products as plant-based alternatives to conventional energy drinks, with caffeine derived from green tea and guarana. Guru has been listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange since November 2020 and sells its products in Canada and the United States.

== History ==
=== Origins and early years ===
According to the company, Guru's origins trace to the mid-1990s at SONA, an electronic dance music venue in Montreal, where plant-based "smart drinks" were served to patrons as an alternative to synthetic energy products. The drink was canned and brought to market in Montreal in 1999. Accounts of the founding differ: a 2009 company announcement described Guru as having been founded by four college friends and quoted Ray Jolicoeur as a co-founder, while later coverage and regulatory announcements identify Joe Zakher as the company's founder.

By 2008, Guru's lineup in Canada included its original energy drink and a low-calorie Lite version alongside juice, lemonade and iced tea varieties, sold through retailers such as Petro-Canada, Loblaws, Sobeys and Walmart. In 2009, the company announced that rapper Kanye West had become an equity partner and would help develop a new product; the product never materialized, and the juice, lemonade and iced tea lines were later discontinued.

=== Organic positioning and growth ===
Guru later obtained USDA organic certification for its energy drinks and, over the 2010s, made its natural and organic claims the centre of its marketing. In 2016, it introduced a zero-sugar line of organic "energy waters". In 2017, the company began targeting U.S. convenience stores, mainly in the San Francisco Bay Area.

In December 2018, Guru stated that it held close to 10 percent of the energy drink market in Quebec and about 4 percent in Canada, citing Mintel data, which it said placed it fourth among energy drink brands in Canada behind Red Bull, Monster and Rockstar.

=== Public listing ===
In August 2020, Guru announced that it would go public through a transaction with Mira X Acquisition Corp., a capital pool company listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. At the time, its drinks were sold at about 15,000 points of sale and the company generated annual revenue of roughly CA$30 million, about 70 percent of it in Canada, mainly in Quebec. Ahead of the listing, Guru raised CA$34.5 million in a brokered private placement led by Stifel Nicolaus Canada, at a pro forma valuation of about CA$160 million. Its share of the Quebec energy drink market was then estimated at 13 percent. Its shares began trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange in November 2020.

=== Financial results ===
In September 2025, Guru reported net income of CA$1.3 million for its third fiscal quarter, compared with a net loss of CA$2.2 million a year earlier, on record quarterly revenue of CA$10.4 million; it was the company's first profitable quarter since its public listing. For fiscal 2025, Guru reported revenue of CA$34.7 million and a net loss of CA$1.4 million.

== Products ==
Guru's products are sold in cans and include its original energy drink, the stevia-sweetened Guru Lite, the fruit-flavoured Guru Punch line launched in 2021, and the zero-sugar Guru Zero line, which the company began rolling out in the United States in 2024. The drinks are made without sucralose or aspartame, and their caffeine comes from organic guarana seed and green tea extracts.

Tito Bautista is a Filipino-American technology executive, information technology consultant and entrepreneur based in Las Vegas, Nevada. Over a career of more than three decades he worked on enterprise systems for companies in the media, automotive, insurance, finance and telecommunications industries, led the consulting firm TechSite America, and served as chief operating officer of Web Deposition, a developer of software for remote participation in legal depositions. He is a named co-inventor on a United States patent application for the secure real-time broadcast of deposition testimony. [ref: System and method for secured peer-to-peer broadcast of instantaneous testimony in text format (US 2011/0258442 A1), Justia Patents]

== Early life and education ==
Bautista was born in Manila, Philippines. He attended San Beda in Manila for his secondary education, graduating in 1971, and went on to earn a bachelor's degree in business administration from De La Salle University in 1976.

In 1977 his family emigrated to the United States, one of many Filipino families who left the country during the period of martial law under Ferdinand Marcos, which had been declared in 1972 and was accompanied by political repression and economic instability.

== Career ==

=== Move into information technology ===
In his first years in the United States, Bautista worked as an accountant. He later enrolled at the Chubb Institute in Short Hills, New Jersey, a technical school known for training career-changers in computer programming, where he studied computer systems analysis and programming between 1980 and 1982. After earning his certificate he left accounting for the information technology industry, a shift that allowed him to combine his background in finance with systems design.

=== Enterprise consulting ===
Through the 1980s and 1990s Bautista worked as an information technology consultant and project leader for several large corporations in the New York metropolitan area, including companies in the telecommunications, media, insurance, finance and automotive industries.

=== TechSite America and work in the Philippines ===
From 1992 to 2014 Bautista was president of TechSite America, a Los Angeles–based IT consulting firm that placed business and systems consultants with corporate clients and coordinated offshore programming and call-center teams.

Through TechSite, Bautista was involved in early efforts to computerize the Philippine Bureau of Customs, a project undertaken with the United Nations Development Programme, the Science and Technology Advisory Council of the Philippines in New York, Stevens Institute of Technology, Hewlett-Packard and the Swiss inspection firm SGS. He also promoted the introduction of electronic data interchange (EDI) in the Philippines, under which import, export, brokerage and financial documents were exchanged electronically between trading partners. EDI later became one of the standard channels for lodging electronic entries with the Bureau of Customs. [ref: Customs Reforms and Modernization: The Philippine Experience, CAREC Program]

=== Web Deposition ===
From 2009 to 2013 Bautista served as chief operating officer of Web Deposition, a Los Angeles company that developed a cloud-based platform allowing attorneys and other participants to join live depositions remotely. The software captured, encrypted and transmitted audio, video and transcript data from remote proceedings, and the company stated it could cut the cost of attending depositions by as much as 70 percent compared with in-person attendance.

With colleagues Allan Casilao and Monday U. Abengowe, Bautista is listed as a co-inventor on a patent application filed in April 2010 and published in October 2011 for a "system and method for secured peer-to-peer broadcast of instantaneous testimony in text format," which describes capturing and authenticating a witness's testimony and transmitting it in real time to authorized remote participants. [ref: US20110258442A1, Google Patents] The approach anticipated remote and virtual depositions, which became widespread in the U.S. legal profession during the COVID-19 pandemic.

=== Jets Inc. ===
In October 2020, during the COVID-19 pandemic, Bautista founded Jets Inc., doing business as Jets Air Pro, an environmental technology company in Las Vegas. The company supplied air purification and sanitizing systems using UV-C light and ionizers, many connected through Internet of Things sensors, and consulted on indoor-air-quality measures for businesses, schools and public venues. It operated until December 2022.

=== Later work ===
In recent years Bautista has focused on artificial intelligence strategy, advising organizations as a fractional chief AI officer and developing AI-driven products. He also produces and presents Consciousness + AI, a YouTube documentary series examining questions in the philosophy of mind, including the hard problem of consciousness, integrated information theory, panpsychism and whether artificial intelligence systems could be conscious. [ref: Consciousness + AI, YouTube]

Cryptocurrency Operations in Texas

Cryptocurrency operations in Texas include areas such as cryptocurrency mining, trading, and business services. The development of cryptocurrency related services is largely attributed to Texas’s energy system, business environment, and state regulations. Originally starting with the Bitmain mining center in Rockdale in 2018, and boosted by China's refusal to continue operations in 2021, The state of Texas has seen an increase in operations, mostly in cryptomining. Because of this growth, an increase in jobs has occurred, alongside a rise in environmental concerns and scams.

== History ==
In December of 2017, it was announced that the town of Rockdale would lose the Alcoa smelting factory. The facility, founded in 1952, was the lifeline of the city, and brought in jobs which, in turn, doubled the population. This crippled the town's economy, and left many without a reliable source of income. This would soon change, as on October 21, 2019, things would change for Rockdale, as Bitmain (Now Bitdeer), a notable cryptocurrency equipment manufacturer and cryptomining company, announced plans to purchase the rusting Alcoa factory and convert it into a cryptomining facility. This marked the start of cryptocurrency's rise in Texas, as the Bitmain facility, despite taking three years to build alongside multiple delays, proved that large scale operations could be made. [ref: Mayor of Rockdale says Bitcoin mining saved the town’s economy, Cryptopolitan]

On May 31, 2021, China, then the world's leading cryptomining nation, would pass a law stating that cryptocurrency trading, mining, and related services would be permanently banned amid energy consumption, financial regulation, and illegal activity. [ref: The China Bitcoin Ban: A History of Shifting Regulations, OKX]
Upon hearing this news, Greg Abbott, Governor of Texas, would state that “Texas is open for Crypto business.” on X, signaling the start of many cryptomining operations in Texas and the United States. [ref: A North Texas community will vote to form a city in an effort to quiet down a crypto mine, The Texas Tribune]

On October 7, 2021, Core Scientific Holding Co. announced that the company, alongside the city of Denton, agreed to make a cryptomining facility. [ref: Crypto mine to be turned into $6B data center in Denton, Dallas Buisness Journal]Although the Core Scientific cryptocurrency mine was the largest mine announced in 2021, multiple cryptocurrency mining companies such as Riot, Cipher Mining, US Bitcoin, Rhodium, and Bitdeer announced and began to construct cryptomines. Notable examples include the creation of the Alborz, Bear, Chief and Odessa sites. [ref: Bitcoin Mining Companies in 2026: MARA, Riot, CleanSpark and the Public Crypto Miners Explained, Miner Compare]

On April 16, 2022 The Fort Worth City Council voted in favor of buying crypto equipment and actively mining cryptocurrency. With the council accepting a donation of three Bitcoin mining machines from the Texas Blockchain Council. “The goal wasn’t to make money, that wasn’t the primary objective. It was for people to know about the city, know that Fort Worth is a dynamic, forward-thinking city and doing innovative things that no other cities have done. So in that sense, it’s been very successful.” Stated Carlo Capua, chief of strategy and innovation. [ref: Fort Worth was the first city to adopt bitcoin mining to attract attention. Was it worth it?, Fort Worth Report]

Throughout 2022, multiple cryptocurrency plants were made, most notably with Cipher Mining. Cipher Mining would create the Alborz and Chief cryptomines in early 2022, with the Alborz mine starting mining operations on August 9, and the Chief mine becoming operational in mid October. Cipher Mining would also create the Bear mine, which would start construction in mid 2022. Alongside opening their most notable operation, the Odessa cryptomining facility. The facility started mining cryptocurrency on November 29, and has been expanded multiple times, most recently in 2024. [ref: Cipher Mining, A Bitcoin Miner Installs 40-MW Wind Powered Site In Texas, DC Forecasts] Compute North would create the Upton County cryptomine in February, and would eventually file for Chapter 11 Bankruptcy on September 22, leading to their assets being seized and given to rivals. [ref: Compute North Post-Mortem: When Hosting Customers Went Broke First, Idea Proof]A joint effort by MARA and US Bitcoin would lead to the construction of the Granbury mine in mid April, [ref: MARA-Granbury, MARA] And Riot would begin construction of the Corsicana mine, with groundbreaking beginning in October. [ref: Construction of Navarro County Bitcoin Mining Site Met by Protesters, NBC DFW] By the end of 2022, there were at least twenty seven mining operations within Texas as reported by the Texas Comptroller. [ref: Cryptocurrency in Texas: Opportunities and Challenges in Mining Digital Coins, Texas Comptroller]

On January 1, 2023, Bitcoin hit an all time low with a price of $16,625.08. This sparked many debates over the ethics and profitability of cryptomining within the state. The drop in price, combined with rising electricity costs, increased the break even price and profit margin, allowing for major operations to be delayed or run on a shorter platform than usual. [ref: A Visual Look Back on Bitcoin in 2023, Coin Market Cap]
[truncated]

Draft text:
Crisis Connect is a free, open-source, offline-first disaster communication application developed by Emirhan Duman for Android and iOS. [ref: İnternetsiz Afet İletişimi: Türk Liseli Geliştiriciden Bluetooth Tabanlı Uygulama Crisis Connect!, ShiftDelete.Net] It supports internet-based communication when connectivity is available and direct Bluetooth messaging between nearby devices when internet access or cellular networks are unavailable. [ref: Dank Emirhans (17) Erfindung bleiben Katastrophen-Opfer verbunden, 20 Minuten]

== Development ==
The project was inspired by communication outages during the 2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes. Duman, a high school student in Istanbul, began developing it in April 2025. [ref: Teen's Disaster Messaging App Can 'Hop' Across Bluetooth When Cellular Networks Collapse, Good News Network] By September 2026, the application was available for Android and iOS. Its source code is published on GitHub under the GNU Affero General Public License version 3. [ref: Crisis Connect, GitHub]

== Features ==

=== Messaging and calls ===
Crisis Connect supports direct Bluetooth communication between nearby devices. The project's documentation lists text messaging, voice notes, image and file transfers, and real-time voice calls between Android and iOS devices. When internet access is available, the application supports end-to-end encrypted messaging and one-to-one voice and video calls over an internet connection.

=== Contacts and message relay ===
Contacts can be added by scanning a QR code or using a short-code pairing process with a nearby device. A relay mode allows messages to pass through intermediate phones running the application when the recipient is outside direct Bluetooth range. The relay feature is disabled by default to conserve battery. Users need to install and configure the application before an outage.

=== SOS and response coordination ===
The application includes SOS broadcasts and location sharing for emergency communication. [ref: News Bulletin of 19 October 2026, 3pm, 919 FM] Its documentation also describes a separate response-team module with role-based access, agency channels and live location sharing during operations.

=== Offline tools ===
Additional tools listed by the project include maps that can be downloaded before an outage, a compass, an emergency whistle and a survival guide with checklists. [ref: About Crisis Connect, Crisis Connect]

Bluetooth range varies with hardware, obstacles and interference. The application is intended to supplement established emergency communication systems.

= Chef Nepal (TV Series) =
Chef Nepal is a competitive cooking reality TV show produced by Dharma Pictures. Created and produced by Dharma Raj Pandey, the program began broadcasting on Kantipur TV on 8 September 2023. It featured amateur cooks and culinary enthusiasts competing in a series of cooking challenges, with their dishes evaluated by judging paned led by Nepali celebrity masterchef Santosh Shah as master judge. [ref: ‘Chef Nepal’ to air on Kantipur Television, kathmandupost.com] [ref: ‘Chef Nepal’ to air from today on Kantipur Television, kathmandupost.com] [ref: Chef Nepal: So Happy to Finally See a Cooking Reality Television Show, NeoStuffs]

The competition also featured Bhanse Laxman Prasad Bhandari and Chef Ganesh Bahadur Dhakal as judges. Its first season concluded in July 2024, with Ajuihang Rai winning the competition. [ref: राईलाई सेफ नेपालको उपाधि, Naya Patrika News]

== Background and Development ==
The development of Chef Nepal preceded its television premier by several years. In an interview published by Kantipur daily newspaper in September 2023, producer Dharma Raj Pandey described an earlier attempt to develop a cooking competition for Nepali television. He said the concept had initially been researched several years before production began but had been set aside because of the market conditions at that time. [ref: ‘सेफ नेपाल’ आजदेखि, Ekantipur]

The project was subsequently revived under Dharma Pictures. Public announcements about the program appeared in 2022, with early reports naming Himalayan Television as the prospective broadcaster. [ref: टीभी रियालिटी शो ‘सेफ नेपाल’को मास्टर जजमा सन्तोष साह अनुबन्धित, Online Khabar]

In October 2022, Onlinekhabar reported that masterchef Santosh Shah had joined the production as master judge. Chef Santosh Shah had received international attention through the BBC television competition MasterChef: The Professionals. The Program also announced the involvement of Chef Ganesh Dhakal, Bhanse Laxman Bhandari and actress Priyanka Karki, who was described in contemporary reporting as an executive producer and celebrity judge.

In July 2023, Kantipur Television and Dharma Pictures entered into an agreement to broadcast the programme. The agreement was signed at Kantipur Television's office in Tinkune, Kathmandu, by the broadcaster's chief executive, Shishir Pachhai, and Shah, representing the program as masterjudge.

== Production ==
Chef Nepal was developed and produced by Dharma Raj Pandey through Dharma Pictures. Siddhartha Pudasaini was identified as the program's director at the time of its television debut.

A competition kitchen and filming set were established at Royal Thai Hospitality in Bhaktapur. The facility was used for contestant cooking challenges and the judges' assessments.

The program experienced delays between its initial announcement and television broadcast. In a review published shortly after the first episode, entertainemnt writer Neeraj Pun reported that financial constraints had affected the production's original schedule.

The series eventually premiered on Kantipur Television in September 2023.

== Competition Format ==
The first season was designed primarily for home cooks, students and amateur cooking enthusiasts rather than established professional chefs.

According to reporting published before the premier, the organiser received more than 500 applications through an online audition process. Approximately 100 applicants were shortlisted for subsequent selection round

Participants were required to prepare dishes for a panel of judges, who assessed their culinary performance and determined which contestants would advance. The competition progressed through auditions, elimination rounds and later cooking challenges.

The announced format included 18 episodes; two audition episodes, four elimination episodes, then competition episodes and two finale episodes. This represented the production plan reported before broadcast rather than a confirmed final episode total.

Contestants advanced from the initial selection pool to a Top 16 stage, followed by a Top 8 stage and the final competition. The program included dishes from different Nepali communities and culinary traditions.

== Judges and Presenters ==
The competition's principal judges were:

* Masterchef Santosh Shah: Nepalese chef known internationally for his participation in BBC's Masterchef: The Professionals. He served as master judge.
* Chef Ganesh Bahadur Dhakal: Chef and Hospitality entrepreneur associated with Royal Thai Hospitality and Baan Thai Restaurants.
* Bhanse Laxman Prasad Bhandari: Nepalese chef popularly known as Bhanse Laxman

Actress Priyanka Karki was associated with the program in executive production and celebrity judgin capacity during its development and initial presentation. But she did not appear in any episode of the series broadcasted in Kantipur Television. There is no any report available for her absence in the show.

In july 2024, Onlinekhabar reported that Rakchya Upreti would present the program's remaining episodes following an interruption to the broadcast schedule. [ref: फुड रियालिटी शो ‘सेफ नेपाल’को बाँकी एपिसोड बिहीबारदेखि, Online Khabar]

== Broadcast History ==
Chef Nepal began airing on Kantipur Television on 8 September 2023. The original schedule provided for a weekly Friday evening broadcast at 9 PM.
