Draft: Sicariid and bacterial phospholipase D toxins

Draft text:
----

Sicariid and bacterial phospholipase D (PLD) toxins are proteins found in recluse spider venom, most infamously the brown recluse (Loxosceles reclusa), as well as certain types of bacteria. The term PLD broadly refers to a family of enzymes that are the primary active toxins in the venoms of recluse spiders (genus Loxosceles). PLD toxins function molecularly by chemically modifying certain types of lipids in cell membranes, forming lipids containing ring-structures called cyclic phospholipid products, which are thought to disrupt cell surfaces. Physiological symptoms of envenomation can result in the formation of dermonecrotic lesions, hemolysis, and a systemic syndrome called loxoscelism. [ref: Forty Years of the Description of Brown Spider Venom Phospholipases-D, Toxins] [ref: Loxoscelism: Old obstacles, new directions, Annals of Emergency Medicine] Closely-related enzymes are also expressed in tick saliva, [ref: Biochemical characterization of a novel sphingomyelinase-like protein from the Rhipicephalus microplus tick, Experimental Parasitology] and are pathogenicity factors in certain pathogenic bacteria [ref: Toxic phospholipases D of Corynebacterium pseudotuberculosis, C. ulcerans and Arcanobacterium haemolyticum: cloning and sequence homology, Gene] and fungi. [ref: Identification of New Sphingomyelinases D in Pathogenic Fungi and Other Pathogenic Organisms, PLOS ONE] [ref: The Toxicogenomic Multiverse: Convergent Recruitment of Proteins Into Animal Venoms, Annual Review of Genomics and Human Genetics]

== Structure ==

PLD toxins are around 31 kDa in size and consist of alternating beta sheets and alpha helices in a circle that overall form a hollow cylindrical structure called a beta barrel. One side of the opening to the beta barrel forms the active site that engages with lipids in cell membranes. Disordered loops around the active site have been shown in computer simulations to dip into the membrane, to hold on, as the enzyme binds to the surface. [ref: Specificity of Loxosceles α Clade Phospholipase D Enzymes for Choline-Containing Lipids: Role of a Conserved Aromatic Cage, Biophysical Journal] The structures of four members of the PLD toxin family have been solved via protein X-ray crystallography, including PLDs from Loxosceles intermedia, [ref: Structure of a novel class II phospholipase D: Catalytic cleft is modified by a disulphide bridge, Biochemical and Biophysical Research Communications] Loxosceles laeta, Sicarius terrosus, [ref: Variable Substrate Preference among Phospholipase D Toxins from Sicariid Spiders, Journal of Biological Chemistry] and the bacterium Arcanobacterium haemolyticum. [ref: Crystal Structure of PLD From Arcanobacterium haemolyticum Identifies a Novel Class IIa-α Variant With Unusual Thermostability, Journal of Molecular Biology] Structures of the PLD toxin from Sicarius terrosus were solved in 2026 at high resolution with lipid substrate and cyclic lipid product bound. [ref: Spider venom phospholipase D toxin structure: Interfacial binding site, mechanism, activation, and head group preference, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences]

== Substrates and molecular mechanism ==
PLD toxins catalyse a chemical reaction called transphosphatidylation, which involves the formation of a bond between part of the lipid carbon chain and the phosphorus in the lipid head group; this reaction forms lipids with either hexagonal or pentagonal ring structures, called cyclic phosphate products. PLD toxins were originally called sphingomyelinase D (SMaseD) toxins because the original characterization showed activity against sphingomyelin. However, after the discovery that PLD toxins could also catalyze the cyclization of other types of lipids, including certain lysophospholipids including lysophosphatidylcholine, the enzyme was renamed phospholipase D (PLD) to more accurately reflect its target profile. [ref: Brown recluse spider (Loxosceles reclusa) venom phospholipase D (PLD) generates lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), Biochemical Journal] Targets include both sphingolipids and lysophospholipids containing a hydroxyl (OH) group on the lipid backbone, which is what forms the chemical bond to the phosphate, and that have a positive or neutral head group recognized by the PLD, including sphingomyelin (SM), lysophosphatidylcholine (LysoPC), ceramide phosphoethanolamine (CPE), and lysophosphatidylethanolamine (LPE). Enzyme activity is magnesium dependent, with the target lipid coordinated in the active site by a covalently bound Mg2+ ion. [ref: Structural Basis for Metal Ion Coordination and the Catalytic Mechanism of Sphingomyelinases D, Journal of Biological Chemistry]

----

The CanJoe is a one-stringed, fretted folk instrument associated with the musical traditions of the Appalachian region of the United States. Constructed from a wooden neck and a metal beverage can used as a resonator, the instrument shares characteristics with homemade stringed instruments such as the diddley bow and cigar box guitar. [ref: Music for All: The Can Joe Man, Our State]

The instrument was developed during the late 1980s by North Carolina craftsman Herschel R. Brown, who also coined the name "CanJoe." [ref: “A Can-did Legend of CanJoe John.” Can Joe Country News!, vol. 1, circa 1997 (company newsletter; primary source).] Brown's design was later further developed and commercially promoted by Tennessee musician and instrument maker John VanArsdall, who became known as "CanJoe John." The Can Joe Company was established in Blountville, Tennessee, in 1994 and sold finished instruments, kits, and custom-built models. [ref: Tennessee Department of Revenue, Certificate of Registration for The Can Joe Company, effective December 1, 1994 (primary record).] [ref: The Can Joe Company, CanJoe Order Form and Product Flyer, circa 1990s (primary promotional material).]

The instrument gained national recognition through public performances, festivals, recordings, and media coverage. [ref: “To ‘Can-Joe’ John VanArsdall and Fred Hall, an old can is no piece of trash.” Empire Magazine (Bristol Herald Courier), November 13, 1997.] [ref: Reunion Time, Empire Magazine (Bristol Herald Courier)]

== Etymology ==

The name "CanJoe" was coined by Herschel R. Brown, the instrument's creator, during the late 1980s. The name combines the words "can" and "banjo."

== History ==

=== Origins ===

The CanJoe originated during the late 1980s, when Brown developed a one-stringed instrument derived from an earlier instrument known as the "uni-can." Brown recognized that the earlier instrument's fret arrangement resembled that of the mountain dulcimer and redesigned it using a wooden neck and a metal beverage can as a resonator. [ref: Onslow loses relentless advocate, Jacksonville Daily News]

VanArsdall became acquainted with Brown and his instruments during the late 1980s. Brown and VanArsdall became friends and worked together on the CanJoe's design and construction.

=== Relationship to earlier instruments ===

The CanJoe shares the use of simple, readily available materials with earlier homemade instruments such as the diddley bow and cigar box guitar.

An earlier homemade instrument identified as a “Canjo,” dating to around 1930, is held by The Charleston Museum in South Carolina. The museum describes it as a banjo-guitar hybrid made from an old coffee pot, with a carved neck, bridge, and walnut tuning pegs. [ref: The Charleston Museum, “Canjo,” ca. 1930, museum exhibit label (photographed artifact; primary source).]

The term “canjo,” without the final “e,” has also been used to describe other homemade stringed instruments created by different makers. These instruments vary in design and are not necessarily related to Brown's CanJoe. The Louisiana Folklife Program, for example, has documented instrument maker Gladys Miller making and selling one-stringed instruments called canjos using food cans as resonators. [ref: Innovation, Tradition, and Change in Louisiana Musical Instrument Making and Repair, Louisiana Folklife Program]

One of the CanJoe's distinguishing features is its fretted, dulcimer-style fingerboard paired with a metal beverage can resonator.

According to Our State, Brown first encountered the uni-can while traveling in the mountains of North Carolina. The earlier instrument used a plastic fingerboard, a plywood stick, and a metal can. Brown recognized that its fret arrangement was similar to a mountain dulcimer and developed a sturdier version of the instrument.

=== Development by John VanArsdall ===

VanArsdall later became a prominent builder, performer, and promoter of the CanJoe.

VanArsdall's late wife gave him the nickname "CanJoe John," which he used as his performing name. [ref: Wherever the Sound Takes You: Heroics and Heartbreak in Music Making, University of Chicago Press]

In 1994, the Can Joe Company was formally established in Blountville, Tennessee. [ref: Sullivan County, Tennessee, business license for The Can Joe Company, 1994 (primary record).] The company produced completed instruments, custom instruments, and assembly kits.

VanArsdall continued developing the instrument while keeping the basic one-string, fretted-neck, and can-resonator design created by Brown. His CanJoes were featured in regional newspapers and magazines during the 1990s and 2000s.

VanArsdall created the first website about the CanJoe in 1998.

=== SmithHaven and public recognition ===

Events devoted to the instrument included the First Annual CanJoe Festival at SmithHaven Farm in Blountville, Tennessee, in 1999. [ref: First Annual CanJoe Festival, promotional poster, SmithHaven Farm, 1999 (primary promotional material).] CanJoe performances were also promoted at the Appalachian Fair in Gray, Tennessee, in 2003. [ref: 77th Annual Appalachian Fair, promotional poster, Gray, Tennessee, 2003 (primary promotional material).]

A 2001 Empire Magazine article documented VanArsdall performing the CanJoe during a celebration of Bristol's musical heritage.

Draft: Helene Verin

Draft text:
----

Helene Verin is an American designer, author, and curator. Across a career documented in The New York Times from 1988 onward she has designed shoes, wallpaper, furniture, rugs, tiles and interiors; the paper has described her variously as "a designer of shoes and home furnishings", "a designer of furniture, wallpaper, rugs and shoes", and "a product and interior designer". [ref: Like a Fly On the Wall, The New York Times] [ref: CURRENTS; Making Furniture 'Seem Like Clouds', The New York Times] [ref: CURRENTS: INNOVATIONS; Skateboards That Step, The New York Times] She later taught at the Fashion Institute of Technology and wrote Beth Levine Shoes (2009), a monograph on the American shoe designer Beth Levine, whose work she presented in three museum exhibitions. [ref: Beth Levine: The First Lady of Shoes, Face to Face]

== Early life and education ==
Verin grew up in Highland Park, Illinois, the daughter of Bernard D. Verin, a former president of Chicago Aligraphy Inc. She graduated from the University of Wisconsin–Madison. Before entering design she worked as assistant director of special projects at KTCA-TV in Minneapolis and, by 1979, as a management consultant for arts organizations. [ref: Helene Verin Wed in Illinois To Rodney Ripps, an Artist, The New York Times]

== Design career ==

=== Shoes ===
The New York Times reported in 1992 that Verin had designed shoes for Bernardo and Keds. [ref: Sometimes the Art on the Wall Happens to Be the Wallpaper, The New York Times] In later coverage the paper described her as a shoe and accessories designer, a housewares and shoe designer, and a designer of "shoes, purses, pillows, floor tiles, rugs and wallpaper". [ref: CURRENTS; Where the Accessories Are for Deaccessioning, The New York Times] [ref: Bringing the Party to Sotheby's, The New York Times] [ref: Habitats/East 22nd Street; They're Living Together, But Four Floors Apart, The New York Times]

=== Massachusetts Museum of Culture and Accessories ===
In May 1988 Verin opened the Massachusetts Museum of Culture and Accessories, a 200-square-foot shop in Lenox, Massachusetts, selling avant-garde housewares and fashion accessories by twenty artists. She said the name was partly a joke at the expense of the much larger Massachusetts Museum of Contemporary Art, then being developed in North Adams. Verin displayed the stock as art, with lamps and glass on pedestals and jewelry hung in gilded frames: she "wanted to showcase the designs in a museum setting where they wouldn't get lost, as they do when they are sold in a department store." The shop also carried her own work, including a rug designed to resemble a wood floor.

=== Wallpaper ===
Verin designed and hand-printed wallpaper in Lenox under the company name Fern I. Tchur. Her pattern Flypaper, introduced at the International Contemporary Furniture Fair in Manhattan in 1991, scattered gold-rendered flies, butterflies, ladybugs and beetles at wide intervals against plain grounds; she consulted entomology books for the renderings. A companion pattern, Tape Measure, staggered six measuring tapes so the repeat appeared random. "Very few wallpapers are hip," she told the Times. "Most are those all-over rose patterns with vines, and they don't appeal to me."

A 1992 Times survey of artist-designed wallpaper discussed her work alongside that of Roy Lichtenstein, Gerhard Richter and Donald Judd, and described a second Verin design, Truth, printed with the words serenity, liberty, justice, sublime, honesty, artistry and strength. "Covering the walls is such an ancient art," she said. "Since the caves of Lascaux, people have been decorating their walls." The papers were sold through the John Boone showroom in Manhattan. Her hand-printed wallpaper was covered again in The New York Times Magazine in 1996. [ref: Back in Prints, The New York Times Magazine]

In 1991 Verin and the decorative painter Benjamin Pasteur created a sitting room called "Rome at Dusk" for a designer show house at Edith Wharton's home The Mount, covering the ceiling in her hand-painted royal blue paper with gilt stars. [ref: Producing Illusions in an Edith Wharton Show House, The New York Times]

=== Furniture and interiors ===
After buying a small studio apartment in Greenwich Village in 1993, Verin designed a line of lightweight solid maple furniture — two desks, two consoles, a coffee table and chairs — that could be recombined for different uses, with tapered ends and edges carved to follow the grain. She cited Charles Eames's bentwood chairs and "his feeling of lightness" as the inspiration: "This room is not an architectural wonder. Anything heavy or bold would overwhelm it. I wanted to make the furniture seem like clouds and disappear."

In 1999 she and the artist Mike Stoughton built a staircase to her son's loft bed from painted skateboards: "Aliens, thunderbolts and bull's-eyes are on backgrounds of brilliant oranges, apple greens and electric blues," she said. "They're the canvases of young artists." In 2000 the Times commissioned her as one of three Manhattan designers asked to produce a budget concept kitchen, for which she combined inexpensive IKEA frosted-glass cabinets lit from within with custom-cut solid walnut counters, and cut the pass-through to the dining room in the shape of an egg — the thick walnut sill beneath it, she said, being "the shadow of the egg." [ref: TRADE SECRETS; 4-Star Kitchens Delivered on a Takeout Budget, The New York Times]

Draft text:
Sooppy Narikkatteri (also spelled Soopy Narikkattery) is an Indian politician and local governance administrator from Kerala. His public career centers on state-level corporate administration and statutory advisory planning within the Panchayati Raj framework of Kerala. He is the former executive Chairman of the state-level public undertaking, the Kerala Rural Employment and Welfare Society (KREWS), and serves as a working group member under the Chief Minister-chaired Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC). Additionally, he holds office as the General Secretary of the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) Kozhikode District Committee.
== Sub-National Public Enterprise and Policy Roles ==
=== KREWS Corporate Oversight ===
Narikkatteri was appointed by the state government as the executive Chairman of the Kerala Rural Employment and Welfare Society (KREWS), serving a five-year tenure from 2011 to 2016. In this role, he directed public sector operations managing asset-creation funds, capital investments for infrastructure development, and state-subsidized labor welfare safety architectures across rural local self-government institutions statewide.
=== K-DISC Strategic Planning ===
In 2021, Narikkatteri was nominated to the Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC), a premier strategic think-tank advisory council guided directly by the Chief Minister of Kerala. Operating as part of its decentralized governance working groups, his responsibilities focus on formulating public policy blueprints targeting the growth of grassroots employment ecosystems, rural social innovations, and the structural integration of technology systems into local self-government institutions.
=== Inter-Governmental Negotiations and Legal History ===
• Kerala Grama Panchayat Association: Served as the State General Secretary, managing inter-governmental policy negotiations with the state executive cabinet concerning municipal functional autonomy and fiscal devolution.
• Constitutional Electoral Roll Litigation (2020): Narikkatteri acted as a chief petitioner in a notable legal challenge regarding municipal voter registration roll updates before the High Court of Kerala, resulting in subsequent administrative actions from the State Election Commission and the Supreme Court of India.
== Municipal Governance and Conflict Resolution ==
=== Local Administration Metrics ===
Narikkatteri served three consecutive terms as the President of the Nadapuram Grama Panchayat between 2000 and 2015. His office directed structural workflow adjustments that transitioned the municipal office into the first ISO-certified Grama Panchayat in Kerala. In 2015, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India, awarded his administration the national [[Panchayat Raj Sashaktikaran Puraskar], ranking it as the top-performing rural local body out of over 265,000 grama panchayats nationwide based on auditing compliance, document transparency, and scheme execution metrics. The council also won the state-level [[Swaraj Trophy] during his tenure.
=== The Cross-Party Consultative Model ===
Operating inside a regional jurisdiction historically subject to recurrent inter-party political conflicts, his municipal tenure introduced balanced cross-party consultative committees. This mechanism decoupled local capital expenditures and public utility development from ongoing partisan rivalries, ensuring the completion of rural road networks, water lines, and primary health installations without project delays stemming from localized friction.
== Electoral and Party Positions ==
• 2011 Assembly Election: Nominated as the official UDF candidate to contest the newly drawn Kuttiady Assembly constituency during the 2011 Kerala Legislative Assembly election, finishing as runner-up with a base of 63,286 votes.
• District Executive: Following a multi-year tenure heading the Nadapuram constituency organization as president, a regional reorganization in October 2026 placed him into the office of General Secretary for the IUML Kozhikode District Committee alongside District President T.T. Ismail.
• LGML Presidency: Serves as the active State President of the Local Governance Members League (LGML).

== Jasmin Parkin! ==
“ You shine, you know that you're the most inspiring person, when you stop crying ” -Jasmin parkin.
Music has the power to express emotion, identity and personal growth. One musician who demonstrates this through her voice, songwriting, and performance is Jasmin Parkin! She is the keyboardist and vocalist for the indie rock band Mother Mother. Jasmin has played an important role in the band providing friendship to the other band members and bringing lively and spiritual energy to Mother Mother. Jasmin has brought a distinctive voice ever since Deabra Jean-Creelman left the band in 2008. Jasmin was born and raised in Vancouver, Canada.

In a 2021 interview,‌ Jasmin states that when she was younger, she was surrounded by music, her father played guitar and had an amazing voice, her mother loved music as well, however her mother got into singing later in life. When Jasmin was Six or Seven years old, she got into piano lessons even though she resented playing piano “the correct way.” Jasmin hated sitting up straight, she states that she became irritated when her teachers corrected her posture describing herself as a rebel. Jasmin later mentions that she wanted to take up Jazz since her name was JASmin, to which a family friend who was also her teacher agrees to teach her jazz only if she learns the blues first which is an important blueprint for jazz. Jasmin’s teacher later realized that she had a good voice and her teacher taught her how to sing and play which later shaped and influenced her early career as a jazz musician (Parkin 2021).

The struggles that Jasmin faced growing up were eating disorders and body positivity. Jasmin states that she struggled with an eating disorder that was not specified, most likely anorexia, from 12 to 16. Later when she discovered social media she realized with the help of other people online, that it was okay to be who she was and that she didn't have to shape herself to the likeness of other people. Jasmin states that she still feels as if she still has habits from her eating disorder today, she describes it as if there is a tiny voice that discourages her every day but she has the strength to ignore it. (Parkin 2021)

During her early career as a solo artist, she performed under the name “The Jasmin Parkin Trio.” Even though the name suggests a group.. with more than one real person, the trio actually consisted of Jasmin and the instruments she performed with, which is why the “group name” was simply just her own name. The Jasmin Parkin Trio is considered a musical group despite having only one real member. The group released only one album titled “No Reason Why”. The album was released on September 3rd, 2003, and contains fourteen tracks. Some songs to note are “My Funny Valentine” “No Reason Why” “Willow Weep for Me” and “Sara.” (Discogs 2003)

A notable song that was written by Jasmin Parkin off of No Reason Why that shows Jasmin Parkin's excellent songwriting is “Sara.” The song focuses on a woman named Sara who is struggling emotionally and feels overwhelmed by her thoughts and experiences. In the first verse, Sara comes home late at night and cries while dwelling on her problems, that tells us that Sara is dealing with  inner conflict. Later the chorus shifts the tone towards encouragement, telling Sara that she is the most inspiring person when she stops crying. This balance between sadness and reassurance suggests the song is not only about pain but also about recognizing Sara's strength. The song is written as if Jasmin is directly confronting her; we can see this by the repeating of Sara's name all throughout the song with the last word being, Sara. The lyrics also describe Sara as a star that glows so near, and so far. This may symbolize the idea that even when Sara feels terrible or emotionally distant, she still has value and brightness to the people around them. When listening to  these lyrics Jasmin Parkin shows her ability to combine emotional vulnerability with encouragement. Later in mother mother you can see this style of writing as well.

Although Jasmin is known today for performing with Mother Mother, a five person band that plays alternative rock and pop rock, and other rock genres, she actually began her musical career as a jazz musician. (you could call her JAZZmin Parkin!!)  Her solo album previously mentioned “No Reason Why” is considered a contemporary jazz album. Due to the fact that she was involved in many choir groups growing up, Jasmin developed somewhat of a vocal range. She is generally a soprano, her voice is often described as heavenly or wordless. She can sing in higher treble ranges but has more difficulty singing lower tenor notes due to her voice being naturally higher. Jasmin may have also influenced Mother Mother to branch out into other rock genres. For example, the band's first album “Touch Up” was released before she joined the band. The music on that album generally follows a similar style throughout and mostly features acoustic guitar and the drumset leading the songs. However when looking at "O My Heart", which was Jasmin's first album with the band, the sound becomes more varied. For example track three “Body of Years” has stronger jazz tendencies, with the bass being much much more prominent compared to “Touch Up.” Songs such as “Try to Change,” “Body of Years,” “Burning Pile,” “Hayloft,” “Sleep Awake” and “O My Heart” show a noticeable difference in instrumentation

The Orthodox Jewish Chamber of Commerce (OJC or OJCC) is an American business membership organization serving Orthodox Jewish business owners and professionals. It was founded by Duvi Honig, who serves as its chief executive officer, and is headquartered on Wall Street in Manhattan. [ref: "MBDA and Orthodox Jewish Chamber of Commerce Unite to Boost Economic Opportunities for MBEs." Minority Business Development Agency, January 2025. https://www.mbda.gov/news/press-releases/2025/01/mbda-and-orthodox-jewish-chamber-commerce-unite-boost-economic] [ref: "Democrats Are Left Off the Guest List at White House Hanukkah Party." The New York Times, December 7, 2017. https://www.nytimes.com/2017/12/07/us/politics/democrats-white-house-hanukkah-party.html] [ref: "Orthodox Jewish Chamber of Commerce (OJC)." InfluenceWatch, Capital Research Center. https://www.influencewatch.org/organization/orthodox-jewish-chamber-of-commerce-ojc/] The chamber describes itself as a global umbrella of businesses of all sizes together with professionals, elected officials and communal activists, and says it exists to help members network with one another and to use that network to stimulate economic opportunity and shape public policy internationally. [ref: "About." Orthodox Jewish Chamber of Commerce. https://www.ojchamber.com/about] Its activities combine business networking and expositions with public policy advocacy at municipal, state and federal level.

== History ==

The chamber grew out of Parnassah Network, an employment and business-networking organization Honig founded in Lakewood, New Jersey in response to the 2008 financial crisis. Beginning with a program pairing Torah study with job training and networking, the effort expanded into the Parnassah Expo, first held in Lakewood in 2012 and subsequently at the Meadowlands Exposition Center and in Edison. [ref: "Parnassah Expo To Be Held In Lakewood." The Yeshiva World, 2012. https://www.theyeshivaworld.com/news/human-interest/117861/parnassah-expo-this-sunday-in-lakewood.html] [ref: "Learn & Network Announces Nationwide Parnassah Expo At Meadowlands Expositions Center." The Lakewood Scoop, 2012. https://thelakewoodscoop.com/news/learn-network-announces-nationwide-parnassah-expo-at-meadowlands-expositions-center/] [ref: "PHOTOS & VIDEO: Parnassah Expo Draws Unprecedented Crowd." The Lakewood Scoop, 2013. https://thelakewoodscoop.com/news/photos-video-parnassah-expo-draws-unprecedented-crowd/] [ref: "Edison, NJ – Business Expo Hopes To Provide Parnassah Opportunities For Thousands." VINnews, January 22, 2014. https://vinnews.com/2014/01/22/edison-nj-business-expo-hopes-to-provide-parnassah-opportunities-for-thousands/] Honig has said the success of that network prompted the creation of a year-round chamber of commerce. [ref: "Orthodox Community's First Ever Chamber of Commerce Launched to Service the Jewish Business World." Matzav. http://matzav.com/orthodox-communitys-first-ever-chamber-of-commerce-launched-to-service-the-jewish-business-world/] Honig organized the first Parnassah Expo in February 2012 at Bais Yaakov High School in Lakewood, which organizers said drew more than 7,000 attendees. The following year the event moved to the Meadowlands Exposition Center in Secaucus as the Nationwide Parnassah Expo and Networking Event, occupying more than 60,000 square feet; attendees included New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Kim Guadagno, Lakewood Mayor Isaac Akerman and Assemblyman Gary Schaer. By its third year the expo had moved to Edison and was described by organizers as the largest business-to-business expo of its kind in the United States.

The chamber opened a New York City office in 2017 and launched an Israel division in Jerusalem in 2018, later opening an office in Tel Aviv and Bnei Brak. Its annual exposition was subsequently renamed the JBiz Expo.

== Activities ==
=== Expositions and conferences ===

The chamber's principal public event is the JBiz Expo and Business Conference, an annual business-to-business exposition. During the COVID-19 pandemic it held an outdoor exposition in Lakewood aimed at businesses affected by the pandemic. [ref: "In hard-hit New Jersey, Jewish group seeks to boost small businesses." JNS, November 24, 2020. https://www.jns.org/news/in-hard-hit-new-jersey-jewish-group-seeks-to-boost-small-businesses] In December 2025 it held the JBiz Economic Summit in Atlantic City, at which New Jersey Lieutenant Governor-elect Dale G. Caldwell made his first public appearance since the election and delivered a keynote; Governor Phil Murphy sent a recorded message and Senator Andy Kim sent a letter of commendation. [ref: "Lt. Governor–Elect Dr. Dale G. Caldwell Makes First Post-Election Public Appearance at JBiz Economic Forum." The Lakewood Scoop, December 14, 2025. https://thelakewoodscoop.com/news/lt-governor-elect-dr-dale-g-caldwell-makes-first-post-election-public-appearance-at-jbiz-economic-forum-as-governor-phil-murphy-acknowledges-chambers-eight-year-economic-partnershi/] The summit included panels on banking, artificial intelligence and New Jersey economic development, the last featuring the chief executive of the New Jersey Economic Development Authority.

=== Publishing ===

The chamber operates JBizNews, an online business news publication launched to cover business, economic development and public policy affecting the New York, New Jersey and Connecticut region. [ref: JBizNews. https://www.jbiznews.com/]

Sooppy Narikkatteri (also spelled Soopy Narikkattery) is an Indian politician from Kerala. He belongs to the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML). He is the General Secretary of the IUML Kozhikode District Committee. He works in local governance administration, public corporate boards, and state planning committees in Kerala. He was the head of the Kerala Rural Employment and Welfare Society (KREWS) and is a working group member of the Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC).
== Public and Administrative Roles ==
=== KREWS and K-DISC ===
The state government appointed Narikkatteri as the Chairman of the Kerala Rural Employment and Welfare Society (KREWS). He held this position from 2011 to 2016. In this role, he managed rural development funds and asset creation programs across various panchayats in the state.
In 2021, he was appointed to the working groups of the Kerala Development and Innovation Strategic Council (K-DISC). This is a strategic planning and advisory body headed by the Chief Minister of Kerala. His work here involves local planning, rural employment schemes, and introducing innovation tools to local self-government institutions.
=== Panchayat Work and Legal Cases ===
Narikkatteri was the General Secretary of the Kerala Grama Panchayat Association. In this role, he discussed administrative issues and fund allocations with the state cabinet.Staff Reporter. (2013, June 7). Panchayat librarian is anything but one. The New Indian Express. https://www.newindianexpress.com/states/kerala/2013/Jun/07/panchayat-librarian-is-anything-but-one-484429.html
In 2020, he filed a legal challenge in the High Court of Kerala regarding local voter registration lists. This petition led to actions by the State Election Commission and went up to the Supreme Court of India.Special Correspondent. (2020, February 15). Voters' list: SEC to approach Supreme court. The Hindu. thehindu.com
== Local Governance at Nadapuram ==
Narikkatteri was the President of the Nadapuram Grama Panchayat for 15 years, serving three consecutive terms from 2000 to 2015. He changed the administrative workflow of the office, making Nadapuram the first ISO-certified Grama Panchayat in Kerala.
In 2015, the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Government of India, gave the Nadapuram panchayat the national Panchayat Raj Sashaktikaran Puraskar. It was selected as the best performing rural local body out of 265,000 panchayats in India based on file tracking, transparency, and project execution metrics.Joseph, M. (2015, November 3). Nadapuram turns a new leaf. The Hindu. thehindu.com The panchayat also won the state-level Swaraj Trophy during his term.
Nadapuram was historically known for frequent political clashes between rival parties. Narikkatteri used cross-party consultative committees during his tenure. This split local development work away from political rivalries, allowing the completion of rural roads, water supply projects, and health centers without party violence stopping the work.Staff Reporter. (2013, April 21). Progress hides behind a facade of violence. The Hindu. thehindu.com
== Party Positions and Elections ==
Narikkatteri contested the 2011 Kerala Legislative Assembly election as the UDF candidate from the Kuttiady Assembly constituency. He finished as the runner-up, getting 63,286 votes in a close election.Kerala Assembly Election Results 2011: Kuttiadi. keralaassembly.org

----Johann "Hans" Coetzee is a veterinarian, veterinary pharmacologist, and university administrator. He is a university distinguished professor and vice president for research at Kansas State University. His research focuses on assessing and managing pain in food-producing animals. [ref: Vice president for research profile, Kansas State University] In 2025, he received the National Academy of Sciences Prize in Food and Agriculture Science for his work on livestock pain management. [ref: Dr. Hans Coetzee Awarded the 2025 NAS Prize in Food & Agriculture Sciences, Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research]

== Education and early career ==
Coetzee earned a Bachelor of Veterinary Science from the University of Pretoria in 1996. After graduating, he worked in mixed-animal veterinary practice in Northern Ireland for four years, followed by two years in pharmaceutical research and development at Norbrook Laboratories. He received a Certificate in Cattle Health and Production from the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons in 2000 and a doctorate in veterinary microbiology from Iowa State University in 2005.

== Academic career ==
Coetzee held assistant and associate professor positions in clinical sciences at Kansas State University before serving on the veterinary faculty at Iowa State University. He returned to Kansas State in 2016 as head of the Department of Anatomy and Physiology in the College of Veterinary Medicine. He was named a university distinguished professor in 2022 and also served as associate dean for research and graduate programs. [ref: Coetzee honored for pain management research in livestock, American Veterinary Medical Association] [ref: Hans Coetzee appointed vice president for research, Kansas State University]

He became interim vice president for research in 2024. Following a national search, Kansas State announced his appointment as vice president for research in May 2025. As the university's chief research officer, his responsibilities include research development, sponsored programs, research infrastructure, commercialization, and research integrity and compliance.

== Research ==
Coetzee's research examines methods for measuring pain and evaluating pain-relief treatments in livestock, including beef and dairy cattle, sheep, and pigs. His work combines behavioral observations with physiological and neuroendocrine measures to assess responses to painful conditions and routine animal-management procedures.

He has developed and validated experimental models for evaluating analgesic drugs in food-producing animals. In its coverage of his 2025 National Academy of Sciences award, the American Veterinary Medical Association reported that this research contributed to the first regulatory approval of an analgesic drug for livestock.

== Professional service and recognition ==
Coetzee is a diplomate of the American College of Veterinary Clinical Pharmacology, the American College of Animal Welfare, and the European College of Animal Welfare and Behavioural Medicine. He is a fellow of the Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons and has chaired the American Veterinary Medical Association's Animal Welfare Committee.

His awards include:

* American Association of Bovine Practitioners (AABP) Award of Excellence (2014)
* American Veterinary Medical Association Animal Welfare Award (2017). [ref: AVMA recognizes excellence in veterinary medicine, American Veterinary Medical Association]
* World Veterinary Association Global Animal Welfare Award (2017).
* World Buiatrics Congress Ruminant Well-being Achievement Award (2018). [ref: Boehringer Ingelheim recognizes Hans Coetzee for ruminant welfare, www.k-state.edu]
* The Irvin Youngberg Higuchi-KU Endowment Research Achievement Award (2025). [ref: KU, Kansas State faculty receive Higuchi-KU Endowment research achievement awards, university-research-awards.ku.edu]
* National Academy of Sciences Prize in Food and Agriculture Science (2025).

AP (Thailand) Public Company Limited (often abbreviated as AP) is a Thai real estate development company. The company primarily develops residential properties, including single-detached homes, twin homes, townhomes, and condominiums, with a focus on the Bangkok Metropolitan Region.

History

AP (Thailand) Public Company Limited was founded in 1991 as a limited company under the name Asian Property Co., Ltd., with the objective of operating a real estate development business. Later, in 2000, the company was listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) through a backdoor listing by merging with PCM Precast Floors Public Company Limited, a manufacturer of precast concrete floors that had been listed on the SET since September 22, 1992. [ref: AP - Factsheet - ตลาดหลักทรัพย์แห่งประเทศไทย, www.set.or.th]

Following the merger, the company changed its name to Asian Property Development Public Company Limited and established a new subsidiary, PCM Construction Material Co., Ltd., to continue the precast floor business. At that time, the company held a 99.99% stake in this new subsidiary.

In 2002, the company transitioned its SET trading classification from the Building and Furnishing Materials sector to the Property Development sector. During the same year, the corporate headquarters was relocated from Lam Luk Ka District, Pathum Thani Province, to Ocean Tower 1 in Khlong Toei District, Bangkok, which remains its current headquarters.

Business Operations

AP Thailand's operations are structured into four main divisions:

# Real Estate Development: The core business focuses on developing residential properties, including single-detached homes, twin homes, townhomes, and condominiums, with projects located across Bangkok, the Bangkok Metropolitan Region, and all regions of Thailand.
# Real Estate Investment Consulting: Managed by the subsidiary Bangkok Citismart, this division provides property brokerage, consignment for sale, and leasing services.
# Property Management: Smart Service and Management (SMART) operates as the juristic person manager for various condominiums and housing estates.
# Secondary Market Startup: Homerun, an affiliated startup, operates in the second-hand real estate market by acquiring, renovating, and reselling existing residential properties.
Residential Projects

AP has developed more than 400 residential projects.  [ref: AP Thailand Expands APITOWN Brand Nationwide, Bangkok Post] The company's diverse portfolio  covers various market segments, ranging from entry-level to ultra-luxury. It develops properties under several brand names, categorized by housing type

* Single-Detached Homes: THE PALAZZO, BEON, BAAN KLANG KRUNG, THE CITY, CENTRO and MODEN.

* Twin Homes:  BAAN KLANG MUANG THE EDITION and GRANDE PLENO.

* Townhomes: BAAN KLANG MUANG CLASSE, BAAN KLANG MUANG, PLENO and PLENO TOWN.

* Home Offices: DISTRICT.

* Condominium Brands: THE ADDRESS, RHYTHM, LIFE, ASPIRE and GOOD DAY.

* Provincial Projects: APITOWN.

== References ==

Draft: Forsythe conjecture

Draft text:
The Forsythe conjecture is a question in dynamical systems about the behaviour of an algorithm in numerical linear algebra. It concerns the limiting directions of residual vectors generated by the conjugate gradient method with fixed-length restarts. The conjecture was first formulated by George Forsythe for the equivalent s-dimensional optimum gradient method in a 1967 technical report and subsequent 1968 article.

For restart length s, each cycle of the method consists of s conjugate-gradient steps followed by a restart from the resulting residual. The conjecture asserts that, in exact arithmetic, the iteration for any real symmetric positive-definite linear system either terminates or becomes asymptotically two-periodic in direction. In other words, the even and odd subsequences of normalized residuals at each restart converge to two respective unit vectors.

The case s=1, corresponding to steepest descent with exact line search, was first proved by Hirotugu Akaike in 1959. In 2026, separate proofs for s=2 were given by Colbrook, Stepaniants, and Townsend, by Liesen, and by Richard Peng. A later 2026 paper by Colbrook, Stepaniants, and Townsend gave a proof for s=3 and counterexamples for every s\geq4, with these results formally verified in Lean.

== Statement ==

Consider the linear system Ax=b, where A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n} is symmetric positive-definite and hence the system has a unique exact solution x_*. For v\in\mathbb R^n, define the Euclidean norm \|v\|_2=(v^{\mathsf T}v)^{1/2} and the A-norm \|v\|_A=(v^{\mathsf T}Av)^{1/2}.

This section describes the restarted conjugate gradient method with integer restart length s>0. All computations are assumed to take place in exact arithmetic. Initialized at any x_0\in\mathbb R^n, the method takes s conjugate-gradient steps per iteration unless the exact solution is reached earlier.

Denote by x_k the iterate at the start of restart cycle k and its residual by r_k=b-Ax_k. At each restart cycle, the method discards the accumulated search directions and begins a new conjugate-gradient run from this iterate and its residual.

One cycle of s conjugate gradient steps can be described by a minimization problem. The residual r_k generates the Krylov subspace\mathcal K_s(A,r_k)=\operatorname{span}\{r_k,Ar_k,\ldots,A^{s-1}r_k\}.The next approximation x_{k+1} is obtained by adding to x_k a correction from this space that minimizes the error measured in the A-norm. This can be written asx_{k+1}\in x_k+\mathcal K_s(A,r_k),\qquad \|x_*-x_{k+1}\|_A=\min_{z\in x_k+\mathcal K_s(A,r_k)}\|x_*-z\|_A.The approximations converge to x_*, so the residuals tend to zero. To study their directions as they shrink, define the normalized residualy_k=\frac{r_k}{\|r_k\|_2}where y_k is a unit vector pointing in the direction of r_k and is well-defined whenever r_k\ne0.

The Forsythe conjecture asserts that these iterations either terminate after finitely many cycles, or there are two unit vectors y_{\mathrm e} and y_{\mathrm o} such thaty_{2k}\longrightarrow y_{\mathrm e},\qquad y_{2k+1}\longrightarrow y_{\mathrm o}\qquad\text{as }k\to\infty.Normalized residuals from the even restart cycles converge to one fixed direction, while those from the odd restart cycles converge to another. These limiting directions may depend on the matrix, the restart length, and the initial residual.

The restarted conjugate gradient method converges in a finite number of restart cycles whenever the starting residual has nonzero projections onto at most s distinct eigenspaces of A. In particular, if s is at least the number of distinct eigenvalues of A, the first cycle reaches the exact solution.

== History ==

The phenomenon of two-direction asymptotics was first conjectured by [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Forsythe Forsythe] and Motzkin in their 1951 abstract on the optimum gradient method. This method is equivalent to the conjugate gradient method with restart length s=1 and the steepest descent method with exact line search. The conjugate gradient method was formally introduced by Hestenes and Stiefel in 1952. In 1959, Akaike proved the conjecture for the s=1 case by viewing the squared spectral components of the normalized residual as an evolving probability distribution. Motivated by numerical experiments for s=2, Forsythe later proposed analogous two-direction behavior for larger fixed restart lengths in his 1967 report and 1968 article.

In 1982, Zhuk extended Forsythe’s construction of alternating residual directions to more general eigenvalue configurations and established sufficient conditions for convergence from nearby initial residuals.

Zhuk and Bondarenko published a claimed proof of the conjecture for s=2 in 1983. The approach proved convergence of residual polynomial coefficients, citing Zabolotskaya’s 1979 paper to conclude that even and odd subsequences of normalized residuals converge. In their 2023 review, Faber, Liesen, and Tichý distinguished coefficient convergence from convergence of residual directions, leaving the case s=2 unresolved. Their review restated the conjecture in modern Krylov subspace notation and formulated a related cross iteration for symmetric and nonsymmetric matrices.
[truncated]

Short description|Railway station in Germany}}

Selters (Westerw) station, German Bahnhof Selters (Westerw) is a train station located in the Westerwald district in Rhineland-Palatinate.

== Location ==
The Selters (Westerw) station is located in the landscape Westerwald, along the Engers-Au railway as well as the former Selters - Hachenburg narrow gauge railway, which leaded from Selters via Hattert to Hachenburg, where it endet as an interchange to the Limburg-Altenkirchen railway.

== History ==

During the 19th century, plans established to open railway lines inside the Westerwald, especially for the purposes the transportation of regional raw materials.

The Engers–Au railway (between Siershahn and Altenkirchen (Westerwald) also known as Holzbachtalbahn (Holzbach valley railway), on which Selters station also is located, was opened in the year1884.

After that, the construction works for the Selters - Hachenburg narrow gauge railway began in the year 1900, and the line opened just a short time later, on August 1, 1901.

Selters station featured a station building with administrative and waiting rooms, along with other operational facilities. The transshipment of freight from the narrow-gauge line took place at Selters station.

Although in 1951, further investment have been done on the lines infrastructure, that were two pits for transporter wagons were installed, that caused an elimination of the need for the labor-intensive manual transshipment process previously required at Selters station.

But not even ten years later, the Selters - Hachenburg narrow-gauge line was closed in 1960, and the tracks were primarely dismantled.

Also the passenger service on the Engers - Au railway ended in 1989.

Today, the former station building in Selters is under private use, the platforms are deconsteucted, while the site itself largely serves as an industrial area for the locally based factories of the company Schütz.

Nowadays Selters station is served in fright train service through the in the year of 2025 new foundet Holzbachtalbahn GmbH and trains running on order of the Schuetz company.

The local bus line 420 of Westerwaldbus GmbH serves a bus stop near Selters station and nowadays runs mostly along the former Selters - Hachenburg railway from Montabaur via Siershahn, Selters and Hattert to Hachenburg.

Concluding that his future depended solely on himself, he prayed and wept until he died. Thereupon, a bat kol announced that Eleazar was assured of happiness in the hereafter. When Rabbi (Judah ha-Nasi) heard this story, he exclaimed, "Verily, some procure eternal happiness only after toiling many years, while others obtain the same result in a short time". Draft: Injection waterproofing of concrete structures

Draft text:
Injection waterproofing of concrete structures is a repair technique in which liquid resins or cementitious grouts are introduced into cracks, joints and voids in concrete to restrict or prevent water penetration. Injection systems are used in the repair of concrete structures where leakage occurs through localized defects. Depending on the repair objective, the injected material may provide water sealing, flexible filling or structural bonding. [ref: Injection products and systems, Deutsches Institut für Bautechnik]

Injection waterproofing forms part of the broader field of waterproofing and pressure grouting. The selection of injection material depends on the condition of the structure, the characteristics of the defect, the presence of flowing water and the required performance of the repair. [ref: Guide for the Selection of Grouts to Control Water Leakage Through Cracks in Concrete Structures, International Concrete Repair Institute]

== Operating principle ==
Injection waterproofing involves introducing a sealing material into a crack, joint or void through purpose-installed injection ports or packers. The material is delivered under controlled pressure and is intended to occupy the accessible leakage path. [ref: Injection Waterproofing: How It Works and When to Use It, knowledge.semeonidis.com]

Depending on its chemical composition, the injected material may react with water, expand, cure into a flexible seal or form a rigid bond between adjacent concrete surfaces. Different material systems are used for sealing and structural repair, and these functions are not necessarily interchangeable.

The method can be used to address leakage through defects in concrete structures. Injection may also be considered where an existing waterproofing layer is inaccessible and a suitable injection system has been designed for its repair. [ref: Technical Evaluation Method for Physical Property Changes due to Environmental Degradation of Grout-Injection Repair Materials for Water-Leakage Cracks, Applied Sciences]

== Injection materials ==

=== Polyurethane resins ===
Polyurethane injection materials are used in certain water-sealing applications, including the treatment of leaking cracks in concrete. Some formulations react with water and expand to fill accessible cavities. Other formulations produce flexible seals that can accommodate limited movement. [ref: Evaluation of polyurethane resin injection for concrete leak repair, Case Studies in Construction Materials]

Fast-foaming polyurethane materials may be used to control flowing water before additional sealing treatment, depending on the selected repair system.

An experimental study published in Case Studies in Construction Materials in 2019 investigated polyurethane resin injection for concrete leakage repair. The research reported a reduction in water penetration in the tested concrete specimens following injection treatment. [ref: Evaluation of polyurethane resin injection for concrete leak repair, Case Studies in Construction Materials]

=== Epoxy resins ===
Epoxy resins are used for repairing cracks in concrete where a rigid, force-transmitting bond is required. [ref: Construction products detail, DIBt]

Unlike flexible sealing materials, conventional structural epoxy systems are intended to bond crack surfaces and restore continuity between concrete elements. Their suitability depends on the moisture condition, crack stability and other characteristics of the substrate. [ref: Construction products detail, DIBt]

Epoxy injection is therefore associated primarily with structural crack repair, although certain epoxy systems may also contribute to sealing applications.

=== Acrylic gels ===
Acrylic-based injection gels are used in selected sealing applications where swelling properties and compatibility with permanently damp conditions are required.

Certain acrylic gel systems can absorb and release water, making environmental moisture conditions important to their intended performance.

These materials are classified separately from rigid structural injection products.

=== Cementitious grouts ===
Cement-based injection materials include cement suspensions and other hydraulic-binder formulations.

They are used for particular crack- and void-filling objectives, depending on the required material properties and repair design.

The suitability of cementitious injection depends on the dimensions of the defect, the intended repair function and the properties of the selected grout.

== Applications ==
Injection waterproofing is associated with repairs to concrete structures affected by water penetration through cracks, construction joints or connected voids. [ref: Injection Waterproofing: How It Works and When to Use It, knowledge.semeonidis.com]

Applications described in technical literature include underground structures, tunnels, retaining walls, tanks and other concrete elements exposed to water. [ref: Properties and Application of Chemical Grouting Materials for Construction Joint Leakage, Advances in Materials Science and Engineering]

The method may provide an alternative to external access where the leakage path can be reached from the accessible face of the concrete structure.

Its applicability depends on the identified defect and whether the injection material can adequately penetrate and seal the relevant pathway.
[truncated]

Zoltán Mészáros (born 2 May 1964) is a Hungarian-German actor, theatre and film director, musician and writer based in Munich, Germany. He gained nationwide recognition in Hungary through his leading role as András Urbán in the television series Angyalbőrben. His artistic career encompasses stage and screen acting, theatre and film direction, music, and audiobook production. [ref: Mészáros Zoltán, József Attila Library, Dunaújváros]

== Early life and education ==

Mészáros was born in Dunaújváros, Hungary, and grew up in Miskolc-Diósgyör. He studied acting at GNM in Budapest, graduating with a diploma in acting.

== Acting career ==

=== Television and film ===

Mészáros first appeared on Hungarian television in Linda. He achieved nationwide popularity through his leading role as András Urbán in Angyalbőrben (1988–1990). His portrayal of Urbán brought him considerable public recognition and established him as a familiar face to Hungarian television audiences. [ref: Interjú Mészáros Zoltán színésszel, József Attila Library – Local History Archive]

In 2020, he played the leading role of Zoltán Farkas in Don Juan Is Balding (Don Juan kopaszodik), a Hungarian television film directed by Linda Dombrovszky, based on works by Ferenc Herczeg. The film was selected for the Tiburon International Film Festival and the White Nights Film Festival in Saint Petersburg in 2020. It received a nomination for Best Television Film at the 2021 Hungarian Motion Picture Awards. [ref: Don Juan Is Balding, Linda Dombrovszky – Official Filmography]

Mészáros also appeared in the Hungarian television series S.E.R.E.G. (2024).

=== Theatre ===

From 1990 to 1996, Mészáros was a member of the Hungarian-language ensemble of the National Theatre in Târgu Mureș, Romania. He subsequently worked at the Szigligeti Theatre in Szolnok and the Figura Studio Theatre in Gheorgheni.

One of his significant stage performances was the role of Teodul in Lucian Blaga's Cruciada copiilor (The Children's Crusade), directed by Victor Ioan Frunză at the National Theatre in Târgu Mureș. The production, in which Mészáros performed, was nominated for Best Performance at the 1993 UNITER Awards. [ref: Cruciada copiilor de Lucian Blaga, UNITER – Romanian Theatre Union]

In 1998, he founded an independent theatre company in Gheorgheni, Romania.

=== Selected leading and major stage roles ===

* Euripides – Iphigenia in Aulis: Achilles
* Nikolai Gogol – Diary of a Madman: Poprishchin
* William Gibson – Two for the Seesaw: Jerry Ryan
* Sławomir Mrożek – The Emigrants: AA
* Lucian Blaga – The Children's Crusade: Teodul
* Ödön von Horváth – Tales from the Vienna Woods: Havlicsek
* Ray Cooney – Run for Your Wife: Inspector Troughton
* Gábor Görgey – Komámasszony, hol a stukker?: Cuki
* András Sütő – Álomkommandó: Interior Ministry official
* Ephraim Kishon – The Marriage Certificate: Robert Knoll
* William Shakespeare – The Merchant of Venice: Lucentio

== Directing career ==

Mészáros has directed stage productions as well as documentary, independent and experimental films.

=== Selected theatre productions ===

* Frigyes Karinthy – Kis Rómeó, kis Júlia
* Sławomir Mrożek – The Emigrants
* William Gibson – Two for the Seesaw

=== Selected film directing credits ===

* 2003: Kerlerspaan – experimental film
* 2004: Die Mission – educational film
* 2004: Go West! – documentary
* 2007: Wenn der Papst kommt – independent film
* 2007: Lepradorf in Europa – documentary
* 2010: Kerlerspaan – ten-minute festival version
* 2011: Mandy – short film

== Music ==

In 1991, Mészáros appeared alongside Hungarian actor Mátyás Usztics on the musical release Jelentsen, Olajbogyó!. The project involved collaboration with Hungarian musician Róbert Szikora.

During 1992 and 1993, Mészáros participated in more than sixty live concerts.

In Munich, he continued his musical activities. His projects include the rock band Minga Brezn, founded in 2026, and work under the artistic name Ólafur Andersson.

His musical work also includes You Take Us Down with You, a peace oratorio exploring war, violence, human responsibility and the pursuit of peace. The project incorporates literary and mythological themes, including ancient Mesopotamian texts and European literary traditions. The work is in development.

== Audiobook production ==

Mészáros has worked in Hungarian-language audiobook production in Munich, including recordings of works by Hungarian literary authors. His work has been associated with AVL Media.

Selected recordings include:

* Jenő Rejtő – Pipacs, a fenegyerek
* Sándor Szathmári – Kazohinia
* Kálmán Mikszáth – A jó palócok
* Kálmán Mikszáth – Tót atyafiak
* Mór Jókai – A nagyenyedi két fűzfa
* Gyula Krúdy – Rózsa Sándor
* Ferenc Móra – Rab ember fiai
* Ferenc Móra – Kincskereső kisködmön

== Work in Germany ==

Mészáros moved to Munich in 1999, where he continued his work as an actor, director, writer and musician.

In 2026, he founded Kunstbühne München, an independent multidisciplinary theatre and cultural initiative intended to bring together dramatic theatre, film, music and literature.

His literary and musical works are also published or developed under the name Ólafur Andersson.

Draft: Russification of Georgia

Draft text:
The Russification of Georgia includes a system of measures, actions and legislations undertaken by the Russian Empire, later Soviet Union and currently Russian-occupied Abkhazia, aimed at linguistical and cultural assimilation of Georgians to eredicate their identity, terminate Georgia's cultural uniqueness and fully integrate it into Russia.
==Imperial Russification policy in Georgia==
Russian conquest of the South Caucasus began in the late 18th century and included various territorial acquisitions from Qajar Iran and the Ottoman Empire. Various Georgian kingdoms and principalities, threatened by Iran and the Ottoman Empire, voluntarily placed themselves under the protection of the Russian Empire. Georgian and Armenian attitudes towards the Russian Empire contrasted with the Muslim struggle against Russian expansion, as broad sections of the Georgian and Armenian populations sought ties with Russia to liberate themselves from Islamic rule. However, they also expected Russia to grant them political and cultural autonomy, which was not respected. Russia instead proceeded to outright annex Georgia while abolishing its local dynasties, suppressing its dynastic autonomy and violating the bilateral treaties. The eastern Georgian king Erekle II placed his kingdom under Russian protection through the Treaty of Georgievsk in 1783. However, in September 1801, the eastern Georgian kingdom was unilaterally and directly annexed by Russian Empire, which was rationalized by the need to defend Russia's new subjects against domestic discord and external enemies, but actually ran contrary to previous agreements between Kartli-Kakheti (Eastern Georgia) and Russia. The western Georgian principalities, which were part of the Ottoman Empire, placed themselves under Russian protection from 1803 to 1811 and were able to preserve their autonomy under the native princely families for several decades, with the exception of the Kingdom of Imereti.

In 1811, the centuries-old autocephaly of the Georgian Orthodox Church was abolished, and it was forcibly integrated into the Russian Orthodox Church. In 1817, it was placed under an ethnic Russian exarch. The liturgy of the Georgian Church was gradually brought into line with the Church Slavonic Russian rite. The Georgian language was excluded from schooling and replaced by the Russian-language school system. This contrasted with the policy towards the Muslims of Transcaucasia and the Armenian Church, whose autonomy was recognized in 1836 and which was initially viewed as an ally in the campaigns of expansion against the Ottoman Empire. The policy towards Georgia resembled that towards the Romanians in Bessarabia, who were subjected to early assimilatory measures because they were Orthodox Christians and were therefore considered closer to Russians in religious and sociocultural terms.

Under Nicholas I, the Transcaucasus was regarded as a colony, while the peoples of Transcaucasia were viewed as "uncivilized Asiatics", which was followed by repressive policies aimed at fully integrating Transcaucasia into Russia. In 1833, the Russian State Council identified its goal as linking Transcaucasia to Russia "as one body, and its population be brought to speak, think, and feel Russian". The repressive policies led to numerous Georgian uprisings,, 1832, and 1841, as well as Muslim uprisings in the 1830s. By the middle of the 19th century, the system of far-reaching local autonomies under native vassals was eventually replaced by the Russian gubernia (province) system. The provinces of Tiflis and Kutais were created and headed by non-native civil servants appointed by St. Petersburg, although local anomalies persisted in the judicial and local administration.

The ongoing resistance in both the South and North Caucasus, as well as the failure of forced integration and the absence of economic profit from the colony, led to a shift towards a more pragmatic and flexible policy under Mikhail Vorontsov, the viceroy of the Caucasus from 1845 to 1855, who sought cooperation with the non-Russian elites. Vorontsov implemented reforms aimed at fully integrating the Georgian nobility into the regional administration, army, and bureaucracy, and introduced an estate-based organization of the nobility. The reforms aimed to transform the rebellious noble layer of society into a loyal and uniform official service nobility, while the peasants lost their traditional rights.

In the 1860s and 1870s, there was again an increase in Russification efforts in Transcaucasia due to the more systematic Russification and standardization program adopted by the Russian Empire across the country. Judicial and municipal reforms were introduced, and the office of the viceroy was abolished in 1883. While there was a certain revival of the Georgian language in the middle of the century, in the 1870s and especially the 1880s, Georgian was systematically excluded from schools. In 1872, the theological seminary in Tiflis replaced Georgian with Russian as the language of instruction. In 1882, the use of the term "Georgia" in the print press was forbidden. In 1886, the director of the Tiflis Theological Seminary, Reverend Chudetsky, who opposed the introduction of Georgian and called it a "language for dogs", was murdered by Ilia Laghiashvili, one of his expelled students.

The Koipuram Palliyodam is a prominent snake boat (palliyodam) from Koipuram village, situated on the northern bank of the Pamba River in Pathanamthitta, Kerala. The boat is famously known by its popular moniker, "Madachadi Chundan" (meaning "the chundan that jumped over bunds"). It is strictly owned, maintained, and operated by the 569th Number NSS Karayogam Koipuram.The vessel is believed to carry the blessings of the local deity of [https://www.justdial.com/Pathanamthitta/Nellickal-Koipuram-Devi-Temple-Koipuram/9999PX468-X468-251014154949-I6A1_BZDET Koipuram-Nellickal Devi Temple] [ref: Aranmula Vallamkali - Official Website of Aranmula Palliyoda Seva Sangam, Aranmula Vallamkali]

The boat regularly participates in the prestigious annual Aranmula Uthrattathi Vallamkali (snake boat regatta) and the ritualistic Vallasadya feast offerings dedicated to the Aranmula Parthasarathy Temple. Throughout its racing history, the Koipuram Palliyodam has established a reputation as one of the most highly competitive and formidable boats in the waters of the Pamba River.

Koipuram has a rich maritime heritage, with the village owning and operating a snake boat for the last several centuries. It belongs to the lineage of the very first boats built in the Aranmula region of Kerala. The current version of the boat was last reconstructed in 2014 by the renowned craftsman "Ayroor Chellappan Achari".

Draft text:
Datu Batuling Bantayao Gumander (November 15, 1937 – April 16, 1976) was a political leader, a community figure, and one of the most prominent symbols of revolution and resistance among the Moro people in the Philippines. He was known for his prominent political role in leading the community of the Sultan Kudarat municipality in Maguindanao province, and was famous for his leadership of the political wing in the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF). [ref: The Life and Martyrdom of Datu Batuling Bantayao Gumander, Medium]

He is considered in local accounts and memory as the "First Martyr" of the Sultan Kudarat municipality after his summary execution by the Philippine Armed Forces during the martial law era under Ferdinand Marcos in 1972. [ref: The Life And Martyrdom Of Datu Batuling Bantayao Gumander] [ref: ] [ref: Infographic: The day Marcos declared Martial Law]

== Personal life ==
Batuling was born in the village of Bungabong in the municipality of Sultan Kudarat in Maguindanao province. He descends from the Gumander family; his father was Datu Salusub Gumander (known as "Ama i Angkog"), and his grandfather was the Muslim scholar and judge Datu Kali Gumander. [ref: Historical Biography: The Life and Martyrdom of Datu Batuling Bantayao Gumander, Zenodo]

He married Undang Ara Butuan, who belongs to the "Bilawatao" family [ref: 1st GRAND REUNION ""BILAWATAO CLAN"" MANOCOB DESCENDANTS] from the village of Mulawug in Sultan Kudarat, and had four children with her: Abdulhadie, Yaqub, Nusaibah, and Mujahid. [ref: "BRIEF HISTORY OF MAGUINDANAO" (PDF).]

== Political career ==

Batuling Gumander began his career in public service as an elected and appointed official in leadership positions, rising through the political ranks in the municipality of Sultan Kudarat, where he held several notable positions:
* Municipal Councilor (Kagawad): He was first elected as First Municipal Councilor for the term (1962–1965), and was re-elected for a second term (1965–1968).
* Vice Mayor: During his third term, he was appointed Vice Mayor of Sultan Kudarat (1968–1970).
* He continued to perform his duties as Vice Mayor until 1971, following the death of former Vice Mayor Datu Mamur Matabalao, working alongside then-Mayor Hajj Datu Sangacala Baraguir (who governed the municipality between 1956 and 1971).

When Mayor Sangacala Baraguir was appointed Governor of Maguindanao province, [ref: List of Municipal Officials and Employees in the Municipality of Sultan Kudarat (1970-1971), Internet Archive] an official offer was made to Datu Batuling to assume the position of Mayor of Sultan Kudarat municipality. However, he refused the position, preferring to abandon formal government work and join the ranks of the armed struggle to defend the rights of the Bangsamoro people.

== Role in the Bangsamoro struggle ==
Datu Batuling joined the ranks of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) early in its formative years, working as a co-founder of the protest and revolutionary movement. He adopted a nom de guerre in the Iranun language, "Langkom Pangulima" (LANGKOM PNGULIMA), which translates to "Commander-in-Chief". [ref: The Life and Martyrdom of Datu Batuling Bantayao Gumander] [ref: ]

He assumed a pivotal leadership role by taking the position of General Chairman of the Political Committee (POLCOM) of the Front. He was also a founding member of the "Ansarul Islam" movement in the Sultan Kudarat area, a movement formed to protect Islamic identity and communities against marginalization policies.

== Personality and social standing ==
Datu Batuling was known for his good character and altruistic leadership among the members of his community. He was distinguished by his extreme humility and dedication, often spending his own money to help young people unable to afford marriage costs, and to provide direct support to needy and poor families in his area. This generosity and community-oriented behavior made him a beloved leader whose services transcended the boundaries of politics and became woven into the social welfare fabric of his town.

== Death (Execution) ==
On April 16, 1976, during the strict implementation of martial law under President Ferdinand Marcos, Datu Batuling was attacked by members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) while he was with some of his men at his farm in the "Tinedteban" area (which is currently located within the municipality of Sultan Mastura).

According to local accounts and testimonies, Datu Batuling fought fiercely, refusing to surrender or let go of his two personal handguns even after his ammunition ran out. Following his death, military forces decapitated him and hung his head on a military tank, parading it through the villages to terrorize the residents; the tank was seen crossing the Simuay River. The burial site of his body and head remains unknown to this day, and his family has been unable to retrieve them. [ref: Historical Biography: The Life and Martyrdom of Datu Batuling Bantayao Gumander, Zenodo] [ref: Martial Law, the dark chapter in Philippine history, RAPPLER]

As a result of this incident, the community bestowed upon him the title of "The First Martyr of Sultan Kudarat".

Draft: Injection waterproofing of concrete structures

Draft text:
Injection waterproofing of concrete structures is a repair technique in which liquid resins or cementitious grouts are introduced into cracks, joints and voids in concrete to restrict or prevent water penetration. Injection systems are used in the repair of concrete structures where leakage occurs through localized defects. Depending on the repair objective, the injected material may provide water sealing, flexible filling or structural bonding. [ref: Injection products and systems, Deutsches Institut für Bautechnik]

Injection waterproofing forms part of the broader field of waterproofing and pressure grouting. The selection of injection material depends on the condition of the structure, the characteristics of the defect, the presence of flowing water and the required performance of the repair. [ref: Guide for the Selection of Grouts to Control Water Leakage Through Cracks in Concrete Structures, International Concrete Repair Institute]

== Operating principle ==
Injection waterproofing involves introducing a sealing material into a crack, joint or void through purpose-installed injection ports or packers. The material is delivered under controlled pressure and is intended to occupy the accessible leakage path.

Depending on its chemical composition, the injected material may react with water, expand, cure into a flexible seal or form a rigid bond between adjacent concrete surfaces. Different material systems are used for sealing and structural repair, and these functions are not necessarily interchangeable.

The method can be used to address leakage through defects in concrete structures. Injection may also be considered where an existing waterproofing layer is inaccessible and a suitable injection system has been designed for its repair. [ref: Technical Evaluation Method for Physical Property Changes due to Environmental Degradation of Grout-Injection Repair Materials for Water-Leakage Cracks, Applied Sciences]

== Injection materials ==

=== Polyurethane resins ===
Polyurethane injection materials are used in certain water-sealing applications, including the treatment of leaking cracks in concrete. Some formulations react with water and expand to fill accessible cavities. Other formulations produce flexible seals that can accommodate limited movement. [ref: Evaluation of polyurethane resin injection for concrete leak repair, Case Studies in Construction Materials]

Fast-foaming polyurethane materials may be used to control flowing water before additional sealing treatment, depending on the selected repair system.

An experimental study published in Case Studies in Construction Materials in 2019 investigated polyurethane resin injection for concrete leakage repair. The research reported a reduction in water penetration in the tested concrete specimens following injection treatment. [ref: Evaluation of polyurethane resin injection for concrete leak repair, Case Studies in Construction Materials]

=== Epoxy resins ===
Epoxy resins are used for repairing cracks in concrete where a rigid, force-transmitting bond is required. [ref: Construction products detail, DIBt]

Unlike flexible sealing materials, conventional structural epoxy systems are intended to bond crack surfaces and restore continuity between concrete elements. Their suitability depends on the moisture condition, crack stability and other characteristics of the substrate. [ref: Construction products detail, DIBt]

Epoxy injection is therefore associated primarily with structural crack repair, although certain epoxy systems may also contribute to sealing applications.

=== Acrylic gels ===
Acrylic-based injection gels are used in selected sealing applications where swelling properties and compatibility with permanently damp conditions are required.

Certain acrylic gel systems can absorb and release water, making environmental moisture conditions important to their intended performance.

These materials are classified separately from rigid structural injection products.

=== Cementitious grouts ===
Cement-based injection materials include cement suspensions and other hydraulic-binder formulations.

They are used for particular crack- and void-filling objectives, depending on the required material properties and repair design.

The suitability of cementitious injection depends on the dimensions of the defect, the intended repair function and the properties of the selected grout.

== Applications ==
Injection waterproofing is associated with repairs to concrete structures affected by water penetration through cracks, construction joints or connected voids. [ref: Injection Waterproofing: How It Works and When to Use It, knowledge.semeonidis.com]

Applications described in technical literature include underground structures, tunnels, retaining walls, tanks and other concrete elements exposed to water. [ref: Properties and Application of Chemical Grouting Materials for Construction Joint Leakage, Advances in Materials Science and Engineering]

The method may provide an alternative to external access where the leakage path can be reached from the accessible face of the concrete structure.

Its applicability depends on the identified defect and whether the injection material can adequately penetrate and seal the relevant pathway.
[truncated]
