Datu Kali Gumander (1880–1973), also known by his honorific title Datukali Gumander, was a prominent Muslim scholar, a traditional judge, and a tribal leader from Maguindanao del Norte province in the Philippines. He descended from a noble lineage of the Iranun people, and played a crucial role in preserving Islamic education, customary laws (Adat), and resolving disputes among the tribes and clans of the Moro people during the late 19th and early 20th centuries. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship] [ref: The Muslim IRANUN Nation (Uranen Kingdom), iranunnation.blogspot.com] [ref: Datukali Gumander Clan: The Three Grand Reunions (1988-2023)]

He is also considered the great-grandfather and founder of the "Gumander family," whose descendants are spread today across Maguindanao del Norte province, specifically in the municipality of Sultan Mastura, and in Zamboanga del Sur, particularly in the lands of Labangan and Bulanit.

== Early life and lineage ==
Gumander was born in 1880 [ref: Datukali Gumander, www.wikidata.org] in the Tumingay area, within what is known today as the village of Bungabong in the municipality of Sultan Mastura in Maguindanao del Norte province. He was the eldest son of Datu Baraguir by his second wife, Lilangen. [ref: The Saga Of Datukali Gumander] His father, Datu Baragir, held the high royal title of Watamama (next in line to the throne or grandson of the Sultan) within the Sultanate of Maguindanao. According to the family tree circulated among clan genealogists and in sources related to the Gumander family, the family's roots trace back to Shariff Mohammed Kabungsuwan, the founder of the Sultanate, which represents the third-highest rank in the Sultanate's hierarchy after the Sultan (Surutan) and the Crown Prince (Rajah Muda).

Gumander grew up in his father's Torogan (traditional royal house) and was immersed in the rich cultural and political traditions of the Iranun and Maguindanao peoples. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship, Zenodo] Early in his life, he showed an interest in learning and social affairs, often attending his father's councils where local disputes and conflicts were discussed. This allowed him to become familiar with methods of mediation and dispute resolution according to local customs.

== Education in Cairo ==
Recognizing his son's potential, Datu Baraguir provided Gumander with an exceptional foundation in Islamic teachings and tribal governance. Driven by his thirst for knowledge and his realization of the importance of education, Gumander asked for his father's permission to travel abroad to continue his studies.

In 1900, Gumander traveled to Cairo, Egypt, where he enrolled in Al-Azhar University, the most prominent center for Islamic learning at the time. During his six-year stay in Egypt, he mastered the Arabic language, delved into the study of Islamic jurisprudence (Fiqh), theology (Kalam), and Hadith, and successfully memorized the entire Holy Quran. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship, Medium] His presence in Cairo allowed him to interact with a broader Islamic academic environment and become acquainted with the intellectual and political currents that prevailed in the Islamic world during that era.

== Return and the Judiciary ==
Gumander returned to Mindanao in the southern Philippines in 1906. Upon his arrival, he first settled in the western region of Zamboanga del Sur, where he engaged in religious education. He established schools to teach Islamic sciences and the Arabic language, and participated in spreading Islamic education among the local population. Over time, Gumander gained social and religious prominence among the people. His name became associated with mediating and settling disputes in accordance with Islamic rulings and local customs, which contributed to the widespread use of the title "Kali Gumander" (Judge Gumander) to refer to him.

His activity and influence extended to several areas in northern Maguindanao (Balut, Sabangan, Nunuling), reaching Illana Bay, the Zamboanga Peninsula, and Lanao del Sur province. [ref: The Saga of Datukali Gumander: A Legacy of Royalty, Exploration, and Kinship, Zenodo] In addition to settling local disputes, his activities were linked to religious education and the preservation of Islamic practices and social customs among the communities of the Moro people.

Draft text:
Isobel Shaw (née O'Beirne; born 1943) is an Irish-born travel writer and guidebook author based in Switzerland. She is known for her guidebooks to Pakistan, including the Pakistan Handbook [ref: Pakistan handbook, Murray] (1989) and the Pakistan Trekking Guide [ref: Pakistan trekking guide: Himalaya, Karakoram, and Hindu Kush, Vanguard Books] (1993). The Pakistan Handbook was shortlisted for the Thomas Cook Travel and Guide Book Awards. [ref: Thomas Cook Travel Book Awards, The Weekend Telegraph] In 2005 she received the Pakistan Society Award for the advancement of public knowledge and understanding of Pakistan in the United Kingdom. [ref: Pakistan Society Awards, The Pakistan Society]

Early life and education

Shaw was born Isibéal Mairéad O'Beirne in County Meath, Ireland, and grew up at Kilcarty House, Kilmessan near Dunsany. Her father lectured in criminal law at the University of Cambridge. [ref: Sister Benedict's Connemara farm, Meath Chronicle] Her elder sister, Maeve O'Beirne, became a Benedictine nun at Kylemore Abbey in Connemara as Sister Benedict, and for many years managed the abbey farm. Shaw studied Anthropology and English at the University of Cambridge, UK.

Career

Early travel writing

Shaw's husband worked in international development, and the couple lived in Tanzania, the United States, Indonesia and Pakistan. Isobel worked as a freelance journalist during these postings. In Indonesia she co-wrote Spotlight Indonesia [ref: Spotlight Indonesia, Elsevier] (1978) with David Brownlow, and she was profiled in The Indonesian Times [ref: Profile: Isobel Shaw, The Indonesian Times] in 1977.

Pakistan guidebooks

Shaw lived in Pakistan from 1978 to 1981 and returned frequently afterwards. She wrote A Traveller's Guide to Pakistan [ref: A Traveller's Guide to Pakistan, Asian Study Group] with Hilary Adamson, published in 1981 by the Asian Study Group, while she was living in Pakistan. She then wrote the Collins Illustrated Guide to Pakistan, [ref: Collins illustrated guide to Pakistan, Collins] published in 1989 by Collins in the United Kingdom and published by Passport Books in the United States as Pakistan. [ref: Pakistan, Passport Books] The Collins edition was reviewed in The Sunday Telegraph by Fitzroy Maclean who described it as "no superficial summary, but a thoughtful study which brings both the country and people alive". [ref: How to discover Eastern Promise, The Sunday Telegraph]

Shaw's Pakistan Handbook was published by John Murray in London and The Guidebook Company in Hong Kong in 1989. A US edition was published by Moon Publications 1990 and a second edition was published in 1998. [ref: Moon Handbooks: Pakistan, Avalon Travel Publishing] The book was reviewed in The Daily Telegraph in 1990 and was described as "a comprehensive guide to travel within the country". [ref: Good Guides, The Daily Telegraph] The book was shortlisted in 1990 in the guidebook category of the Thomas Cook Travel and Guide Book Awards. Other writers on the region have recommended Shaw's work, with Laura Stone calling her "the best guidebook writer on Pakistan". [ref: Himalaya by Bike: A Route and Planning Guide for Cyclists and Motor Cyclists, Trailblazer Publications, Trailblazer Publishing]

For the next two decades, Shaw worked as a tourism consultant to the Government of Pakistan and as a tour guide specializing in the mountains of Central Asia [ref: Environmental protection of the Himalaya: a mountaineers' view, Indus Publ. Co].  She gave a keynote address at the Pakistan Tourism Convention in Karachi in October 1993 and received a Friends of Pakistan award there. [ref: Knowing Pakistan: the way only a foreign trekker could, The News International] She contributed the tourism chapter to Environmental Protection of the Himalaya: A Mountaineers' View (1994), the chapter on tourism to Old Roads, New Highways: Fifty Years of Pakistan [ref: Old roads, new highways: fifty years of Pakistan, Oxford University Press] (Oxford University Press, 1997), and the Pakistan section of Insight Guides: South Asia. [ref: South Asia, APA Publications] Her work was profiled in She magazine (1993) and The News International (1993).

Trekking guides

Shaw began trekking seriously in Northern Pakistan in 1987 and within five years had covered most of the main routes in the Karakoram and Hindu Kush. Her Pakistan Trekking Guide (1993) organized about a hundred treks accessible from the mountain airports of Chitral, Gilgit and Skardu. In The American Alpine Journal, Gene and Betsy White wrote that the authors "present a sympathetic and positive portrait of Pakistan, its people and its scenic beauty", and that the book "should be required reading" for anyone planning to visit Pakistan as a tourist, trekker or resident. [ref: AAC Publications - Pakistan Trekking Guide, publications.americanalpineclub.org] In the Alpine Journal, Trevor Braham called it "well-researched" and said the sketch maps earned it "full marks". [ref: Review of Pakistan Trekking Guide by Isobel Shaw and Ben Shaw, Alpine Journal]

In 1990 Shaw led an expedition up the Baltoro Glacier to Concordia near K2 with the Swiss mountaineer André Roch, who was then aged 84. Shaw's Trekking Guide to the Karakoram and Hindu Kush of Northern Pakistan [ref: Trekking Guide to the Karakoram and Hindu Kush of Northern Pakistan, Vanguard Books] was published by Vanguard Books in 2013 and drew on further journeys to Northern Pakistan made after 1993.

Lectures

Draft text:
Bhim is a town, a tehsil (subdistrict), and a municipality (Nagar Palika) in the Rajsamand district of the state of Rajasthan, India [ref: ] [ref: ] It is one of the blocks that constitute the Rajsamand district and serves as a tehsil headquarters. [ref: Villages in Bhim Tehsil, Rajsamand, Rajasthan, Maps of India]

== Etymology and history ==
Historically, Bhim served as a critical frontier pass and tactical gateway through the central Aravalli Range. The town was positioned at a geographic tri-junction intersecting the traditional borders of the princely states of Mewar, Marwar, and Ajmer-Merwara. Because of this strategic border location, it functioned as an essential mountain outpost for policing trade caravans, monitoring regional military movements, and defending the surrounding territory from external incursions.

Following India's independence and the subsequent integration of the princely states, Bhim became a part of the state of Rajasthan. Originally administered under the Udaipur district, the town was reorganized as the administrative headquarters of the Bhim Tehsil when the Rajsamand district was officially carved out on 10 April 1991 [ref: ].

== Geography ==
Bhim is located at approximately, at an elevation of 594 metres (1,949 ft).The Bhim block covers an area of 687.39 square kilometres and forms part of the Aravalli Mountain Eastern Plain physiographic unit.The Aravalli range enters Bhim tehsil from Ajmer district and continues south-westerly towards Kumbhalgarh and Jarga.

== Demographics [ref: ] ==
As per the 2011 Census, Bhim Tehsil had a population of 171,023, comprising 86,365 males and 84,658 females. The sex ratio was 981 females per 1,000 males. The child population (ages 0–6) was 28,932, or 16.92% of the total population, with a child sex ratio of 901 females per 1,000 males.

The urban population of Bhim Tehsil was 11,568 (5,875 males and 5,693 females), making up 6.76% of the total population. The rural population was 159,455 (80,490 males and 78,965 females), making up 93.24%.

The religious composition of Bhim Tehsil (2011) was recorded as follows: Hindu 161,491 (94.43%), Muslim 7,739 (4.53%), Jain 1,429 (0.84%), religion not stated 189 (0.11%), Christian 159 (0.09%), Sikh 11 (0.01%), Buddhist 3 (0%), and other religions and persuasions 2 (0%).

== Administration ==

=== Municipal administration ===
Bhim is administered as a Nagar Palika (municipality [ref: Bhim Municipality Wards List & Seats, Bharat Survey]). The municipal body is part of Rajsamand district and has a total of 20 wards. Bhim was one of the 248 Municipalities (Nagar Palika) that went to the polls in the 2026 Rajasthan Urban Local Body elections, alongside 10 Municipal Corporations (Nagar Nigam) and 51 Municipal Councils (Nagar Parishad).

The 2026 election [ref: भीम नगर पालिका चुनाव में कांग्रेस को स्पष्ट बहुमत मिला: 20 में से 14 वार्ड जीते, भाजपा को 2 और निर्दलीयों को 4 सीटें मिलीं - Barar (Bhim) News, Dainik Bhaskar] was the first time Bhim held a Nagar Palika election.[reference:14] Voting took place on 11 September 2026 in Phase 2 of the elections. Of the 20 wards, elections were held in 18 wards; in two wards candidates were elected unopposed after nominations were rejected. A total of 7,852 voters were registered, of whom 6,476 voted, registering a turnout of 82.49%. Women voter turnout was 85.06% (3,314 out of 3,896), while male turnout was 79.95% (3,162 out of 3,955), meaning women voted 5.11 percentage points more than men. In the final result, the Indian National Congress won 14 wards, other parties and independents won 4, and the Bharatiya Janata Party won 2.

Historically, a source noted that Bhim remained a panchayat rather than a nagarpalika due to a lack of the requisite population; this status changed with the 2026 municipal election.

=== Tehsil and block administration ===
Bhim is also a tehsil [ref: Bhim Rajsamand - Jatland Wiki, www.jatland.com]and a panchayat samiti headquarters. The Bhim panchayat samiti [ref: ] comprises 33 panchayats and 138 villages, and is located on National Highway 8, 52 kilometres south of Beawar city.

=== State and national politics ===
Bhim is a legislative assembly constituency in Rajsamand district. In the 2023 Rajasthan Assembly election, Harisingh Rawat [ref: ] of the Bharatiya Janata Party won the seat with 93,905 votes (57.46%); Sudarshan Singh Rawat [ref: Sudarshan Singh Rawat S/O Lakshman Singh(Indian National Congress(INC)):Constituency- BHIM(RAJSAMAND) - Affidavit Information of Candidate:, www.myneta.info] of the Indian National Congress was the runner-up with 62,137 votes (38.02%).

== Economy ==
The main occupation of residents of the Bhim panchayat samiti is agriculture. Because of extreme hilly terrain, fields are very small and productivity is average or below average, and water shortage adds to agricultural difficulties. This has resulted in the migration of men to Gujarat—mainly to Surat, Baroda, and Ahmedabad—in search of work. Women who stay behind take care of animals, children, and agricultural fields.

James Lee Storer (born 4 October 2004) is an Irish professional footballer who plays as a goalkeeper for EFL League One club Plymouth Argyle. [ref: ]

==Club career==
===Youth career===
Born in Buxton, Storer began his career in the youth setup of Port Vale progressing from Under-9 from Under-13 levels with The Valiants, before he departed the club in 2018 to join Premier League Wolverhampton Wanderers. [ref: Premier League football beckons for Vale Academy..., Port Vale FC] On 21 July 2021, after progressing quickly through the ranks at Wolves; Storer signed a two–year scholarship. [ref: Meet Wolves Academy’s 2021/22 scholars, wolves.co.uk] On 27 October 2022, Storer signed his first professional contract with the club.

===Wolverhampton Wanderers===

On 1 November 2021, almost four months after signing his scholarship; Storer was named amongst the first team substitutes for a Premier League game against Everton at Molineux - with Wolves running out 2–1 winners. [ref: ] He didn't feature for the first team again after that and on 5 June 2025, Storer was offered a new deal, [ref: Wolves confirm 2025 retained list, wolves.co.uk] which he signed the following month. [ref: Storer and Benjamin Sign Extensions Before Loan Moves from Wolves, alwayswolves.co.uk] The following 6 June 2026, Storer was named on the retained list following the conclusion of the 2025–26 campaign. [ref: Wolves confirm 2026 retained list, wolves.co.uk]

===Darlaston Town (loan)===
On 2 August 2024, Storer sealed his first loan stint away from Wolves as he joined Northern Premier League Division One Midlands side Darlaston Town on a three–month loan deal. [ref: Darlaston sign young Wolves keeper on three months loan, darlastontown1874fc.com] The loan came to an end in January 2025 and Storer went onto make 26 appearances across all competitions for The Citizens. [ref: Darlaston Town – Appearances – James Storer – 2024-2025, footballwebpages.co.uk]

===Chester (loan)===
On 10 January 2025, Storer joined National League North side Chester on loan for the rest of the season, [ref: Jimmy Storer joins Chester FC on loan!, chesterfc.com] he went onto feature 25 times in all during his time at the Deva Stadium before he returned to parent club, Wolves. [ref: James Storer: Chester FC: playmakerstats.com, playmakerstats.com]

===Greenock Morton (loan)===
On 15 July 2025, Storer was loaned out to Scottish Championship side Greenock Morton on a season–long loan, [ref: James Storer joins on loan, chesterfc.com] he made his professional debut later the same day as he played the full 90 minutes of the Scottish League Cup Group opener against Stenhousemuir, in which Morton ran out 3–0 winners. [ref: Greenock Morton 3–0 Stenhousemuir, bbc.co.uk] This was followed by his senior debut in league football on 2 August 2025, as Storer featured in Greenock Morton's 0–0 draw against Dunfermline Athletic on the opening day of the Scottish Championship season. [ref: Greenock Morton 0–0 Dunfermline Athletic, bbc.co.uk] He went onto make 32 appearances in all during his temporary stay at Cappielow and was voted Greenock Morton's Young Player of the Year on 8 May 2026. [ref: 🏆 Young Player of the Year. Following a stand out season, James Storer has been voted as the 2025/26 Young Player of the Year! Congratulations, Jimmy 👏]

===Plymouth Argyle===
On 26 June 2026, Storer left Wolverhampton Wanderers on a permanent basis as he signed for League One side Plymouth Argyle on a free transfer; penning an initial two-year deal. [ref: James Storer signs for Argyle, pafc.co.uk] [ref: Storer signs for Plymouth Argyle, wolves.co.uk] On 25 August 2026, Storer made his debut in English professional football as he played the full 90 minutes during Plymouth Argyle's 4–2 loss against Premier League side Coventry City in Round One of the EFL Cup. [ref: ] [ref: Plymouth Argyle 2-4 Coventry City, bbc.co.uk]

==International career==
Born in Buxton, Storer is of Irish descent. On 30 May 2022, he was called up to the Republic of Ireland U19s for two friendly internationals against Iceland at the Pinatar Arena. [ref: U19s set for Iceland double header, rissc.org] He was unused substitute for the first game which Ireland won 3–0, [ref: Republic of Ireland U19 3–0 Iceland U19, extratime.com] and played the full 90 minutes in the second which Ireland lost 1–0. [ref: Republic of Ireland U19 0–1 Iceland U19, extratime.com]

Draft text:
Smash&Clash is a two-player strategy card-and-board game created in India by Harshit Khemani. [ref: Terms of Service, Smash&Clash] Players take turns placing character cards on a three-by-five board, and a placed card captures adjacent opposing cards by comparing the numbers on their touching sides. The player who controls more cards when the board is full wins. [ref: Rules, Smash&Clash Docs]

The game is sold as a physical set of cards and a board, and a free digital edition is played in web browsers and through apps for Windows, macOS, Linux and Android. [ref: Download Smash&Clash 2.1.0, Smash&Clash] [ref: Smash&Clash – Board Game, Whop] Since October 2026 the digital edition has also offered a public API through which other programs, including AI agents, can play the game, and the developer has published open-source clients that run it inside other games and on older consoles. [ref: Smash&Clash for developers, Smash&Clash Docs]

== Gameplay ==
=== Board and cards ===
The board has 15 tiles in three rows and five columns, named A1 to E3. Both players draw from a shared deck of 51 cards: 46 character cards and five effect cards. Each player holds five cards, plays exactly one card per turn and then draws back up to five. Each character card has its own name and artwork and four side values from 1 to 7, one for each edge, read from its owner's side of the table. [ref: Changelog, Smash&Clash Docs]

=== Captures and scoring ===
A character card may be placed on any empty tile. It is then compared with each orthogonally adjacent opposing card that is not frozen. If the placed card's touching side is greater than or equal to the opposing card's touching side, the opposing card is captured and turned to face the attacker, so ties favour the attacker. Captures happen only when a card is placed and do not chain to further cards. Because a card belongs to the player it faces, the cards on the board are the score. The game ends as soon as all 15 tiles are filled, and the player with more cards wins; as the board has an odd number of tiles, a game cannot be drawn.

=== Effect cards ===
The deck contains one copy of each of five effect cards, which can be played only when they would have an effect:
* Boulder removes a non-frozen card together with every non-frozen card in its row and column.
* Flip turns the whole board 180 degrees, so every card changes sides.
* Freeze permanently freezes one of the player's own cards, which then cannot be captured, attack or be removed.
* Recruit takes a non-frozen opposing card and places it on an empty tile as the player's own, where it attacks.
* Swap exchanges the two players' hands.

=== Rulesets ===
The game has two rulesets, Classic and Mutators; Mutators is the default. It adds three kinds of special tile:
* Chess tiles: two per game, each marked as a knight, bishop, rook or queen. A card placed on one may move like that chess piece to an empty tile and attack again.
* Power tiles: two new tiles each turn, each with a colour and a bonus of +1 or +2. A card of the matching colour placed on one attacks with every side boosted.
* Overrun zones: the three centre tiles, B2, C2 and D2. When a player's card on one of them is surrounded on all four sides, that player may play a new card on top of it.

== Editions ==
=== Physical edition ===
The physical edition consists of 51 cards and a game board. It is sold online through Whop, which acts as the seller of record for payment, delivery and refunds.

=== Digital edition ===
The digital edition is free and has no advertising or in-app purchases; it can be played without an account, while accounts and online features are limited to users aged 13 or older. It presents the board in 3D, with character voices produced using ElevenLabs. [ref: About Smash&Clash, Smash&Clash] Players can play against an adaptive computer opponent, learn the rules in a tutorial, or play another person on the same device. For online play, a player can create a room with a six-letter code or join a quick-match queue that pairs waiting players, and optional profiles and leaderboards record results.

A finished game can be viewed as a move-by-move replay or as a "Game Review", which rates every move against the best one available in that position and summarises each player's accuracy and the game's key moments. [ref: Replays and reviews, Smash&Clash Docs] Every game also has a public watch page that shows it live with both hands face-down, and a "Smash&Clash TV" page shows the game currently being played.

=== Platforms ===
The game is played in web browsers at smashandclash.in. Installable apps are distributed for Windows 10 and 11, macOS 11 or later, Linux and Android 7.0 or later; on iOS and iPadOS it is added to the home screen as a progressive web app. The apps can be played offline against the computer opponent, and online they connect to players on every other version. The game is also offered through a Telegram bot [ref: @[user], Telegram] and a Snapchat Lens, [ref: Smash&Clash Lens by Harshit Khemani, Snapchat] as a terminal game, and, according to its terms, as a Discord Activity, a ChatGPT app and an app embedded in Whop.

== Summary ==
Pilot Training Flight Simulator (abbreviated as PTFS) is a flight simulation experience on the online gaming platform Roblox with over 810 million visits. Developed by brothers Orange12345 and Samisage, the game allows players to pilot aircraft, explore a virtual world and participate in aviation-related activities. It was originally released on 4 January 2010. [ref: Pilot Training Flight Simulator – Roblox Game, RoRadar]

== Gameplay ==
The game focuses on aircraft simulation and multiplayer aviation activities. Players can operate a variety of aircraft, ranging from small general-aviation planes to large commercial and cargo aircraft. The game includes the Antonov An-225, one of the largest aircraft ever built. Players can explore the map, practise flying, take part in airline roleplay and perform air traffic control activities. The experience also includes military aircraft and other aviation-related vehicles, some of which are available through additional purchases. [ref: Pilot Training Club/Pilot Training Flight Simulator, Roblox Wiki]

PTFS supports multiplayer servers, allowing players to fly together and organise aviation-related activities.

== Reception and popularity ==
Pilot Training Flight Simulator has accumulated hundreds of millions of visits on Roblox and has an established player community, such as the PRG (PTFS Roleplay Group). [ref: Discord - Group Chat That’s All Fun & Games, Discord]

As of October 2026, publicly available game-tracking websites reported approximately 813 million total visits, 2.3 million favourites and a positive rating of around 93%. The game supports up to 20 players per server, with the newly added PTFS Test Server, allowing up to 700 players. [ref: Pilot Training Flight Simulator – Roblox Game, RoRadar]

Draft text:
Basht. are an Irish post-punk and alternative rock band formed in Dublin in 2021. The band consists of Jack Leavey (vocals and guitar), Lughaidh Armstrong-Mayock (lead guitar), Louis Christle (bass) and Ryan McClelland (drums). [ref: Irish band Basht crash the Top Ten with debut album, RTÉ]

The group released two EPs, Dirty White Lies (2024) and Bitter and Twisted (2025), before their debut studio album, Poor Advice, was released through LAB Records on 9 October 2026. The album reached number seven on the Irish Albums Chart and number one on the Irish Independent Albums Chart. [ref: Official Irish Albums Chart on 16/10/2026, Official Charts Company] [ref: Irish Charts: Top 50 Independent, 10 October 2026 – 16 October 2026, Irish Recorded Music Association]

== History ==

=== Formation and early releases (2021–2025) ===

Basht. were formed in Dublin in 2021 by vocalist and guitarist Jack Leavey, who had initially been looking for musicians to accompany a solo project. After meeting bassist Louis Christle, the two began developing the project as a band. [ref: Una-Basht., Dork]

Their first EP, Dirty White Lies, was released in 2024, followed by Bitter and Twisted in 2025. The band toured the United Kingdom and Ireland and supported acts including Wunderhorse, DEADLETTER, Everything Everything and Miles Kane.

The lineup changed during this period. Lughaidh Armstrong-Mayock initially joined as a touring guitarist before becoming involved in the band's songwriting. Drummer Ryan McClelland subsequently joined, completing the four-member lineup in 2025.

=== Poor Advice (2026) ===

In April 2026, Basht. announced their debut studio album, Poor Advice, and released its lead single, "Perfume". The song was produced by Ali Chant. Leavey described its subject as a son looking back on the breakdown of his parents' marriage, with the lyrics also addressing the historical influence of the Catholic Church on private life in Ireland. [ref: Basht announce debut album Poor Advice, Hot Press]

The band worked on material for the album while touring, developing songs during rehearsals and soundchecks. The recording sessions were undertaken with producer Ali Chant.

Poor Advice was released on 9 October 2026 through LAB Records. The ten-track album addresses institutional authority, religion and political conflict. In an interview with Hot Press, Leavey discussed the use of biblical imagery in the lyrics and the influence of contemporary conflicts on songs including "Terror TV" and "Circadia". [ref: Basht.: "It's just our nature – Irish people question authority, and we've always had the ability to put two fingers up to it", Hot Press]

The album entered the Irish Albums Chart at number seven on 16 October 2026. It also debuted at number one on the Irish Independent Albums Chart.

Following the album's release, Basht. announced a headline tour of the United Kingdom beginning in October 2026 and a sold-out concert at the Button Factory in Dublin in November. Leavey's father had previously managed the venue when it was known as the Temple Bar Music Centre. [ref: Basht., Morgana and The Wran debut in Top 10 of Irish Albums Chart, Hot Press]

== Musical style ==

Basht.'s music has been described as post-punk and alternative rock. Their songs feature distorted guitars, bass-driven arrangements and changes between quieter passages and heavier sections. The Irish Times compared their sound to a combination of Radiohead and Nirvana in its review of Poor Advice. [ref: New Irish albums reviewed and rated: Basht, Meryl Streek, Morgana, Wasps vs Humans, Whozyerman?, The Irish Times]

The band's members have discussed their interest in music outside conventional guitar-based rock. In an October 2026 interview with Hot Press, Christle described listening to 1990s house and 1980s Detroit techno, particularly the use of drum machines.

The lyrics of Poor Advice draw on religious imagery and political subjects. Leavey has identified the relationship between religious and political authority in Ireland as one of the album's recurring concerns.

== Critical reception ==

Poor Advice received a five-star review from Tony Clayton-Lea of The Irish Times. Clayton-Lea compared the band's sound to Radiohead and Nirvana and noted the album's changes in dynamics and politically focused lyrics.

Riccardo Dwyer of Hot Press awarded the album 7.5 out of 10. His review discussed the album's intensity and its treatment of religion and political conflict. [ref: Album Review: Basht., Poor Advice, Hot Press]

* Ryan McClelland – drums

Draft: 2022– Georgian political crisis

Draft text:
The 2022–Georgian political crisis is an ongoing political crisis in the country of Georgia. The crisis began on 25 February 2022, with protests against the Georgian government over what critics perceived as insufficient support for Ukraine in the Russo-Ukrainian War, which had begun a day earlier. The foreign policy pursued by the ruling Georgian Dream party, including growing economic ties with Moscow and deteriorating relations with Ukraine and the European Union, has faced criticism from major Georgian opposition parties. These criticisms have arisen amid the ongoing Russian-Georgian conflict stemming from the 2008 Russo-Georgian War and the Russian occupation of Georgian territories. The ruling party has rejected accusations of pursuing a pro-Russian policy, justifying its approach as necessary to preserve peace and stability.

In June 2022, the European Union declined to grant Georgia candidate status, citing the need for further progress in aligning with EU policies. The ruling party faced further protests in June and July 2022 over its failure to secure EU candidate status. Amid deteriorating relations with the West, in March 2023, the ruling party proposed a foreign agents law that would require non-governmental organizations (NGOs) to register as "foreign agents" if they received more than 20% of their funding from abroad. Many NGOs in Georgia receive funding from Western donors. The ensuing protests forced the Georgian Parliament to withdraw the bill. In December 2023, the European Union subsequently granted Georgia candidate status.

In February 2024, the ruling Georgian Dream party replaced Prime Minister Irakli Garibashvili with Irakli Kobakhidze. In April 2024, the foreign agents bill was reintroduced and subsequently passed despite continued protests. The 2024 Georgian parliamentary and presidential elections further strained the political situation in the country, with the ruling party claiming victory while the opposition alleged electoral fraud. On 28 November 2024, during a press briefing, Prime Minister Kobakhidze announced the suspension of talks on Georgia's accession to the European Union until 2028, sparking further protests. The Second Kobakhidze government responded by adopting a series of restrictive laws targeting protesters and taking steps to consolidate power.

==Background==
By the time the crisis began, Georgian Dream had been the ruling party in Georgia since defeating Mikheil Saakashvili's United National Movement (UNM) in the 2012 parliamentary election. Having announced its intention to continue Georgia's existing bid for accession to the European Union and NATO, Georgian Dream also advocated combining a pro-European foreign policy with a more conciliatory approach towards Russia than that of its more firmly anti-Russian predecessors. [ref: Georgia's elections pit anti-Russian president versus conciliatory challenger, The Christian Science Monitor] Bidzina Ivanishvili, a Georgian billionaire who founded the Georgian Dream party and led it to victory in the 2012 elections, has faced accusations of being a Russian oligarch because he amassed his wealth, estimated at $7 billion, in Russia during the 1990s. Ivanishvili has rejected these accusations. [ref: Bidzina Ivanishvili: Georgia's billionaire 'puppet master' betting the house on Moscow, The Guardian] After briefly serving as prime minister from 2012 to 2013, Ivanishvili resigned from office, although he continued to be regarded as the éminence grise of Georgian politics, exerting influence over the ruling party from behind the scenes. For a time, Ivanishvili and Georgian Dream managed to avoid accusations of being pro-Russian. [ref: Popular Oligarchy: Why the Public Still Supports Georgian Dream, Georgian Institute of Politics] However, in 2019, the Georgian government faced major protests following the participation of Russian MPs in a session of the Interparliamentary Assembly on Orthodoxy held in the Georgian Parliament, during which Russian MP Sergei Gavrilov delivered a speech from the parliamentary speaker's chair. [ref: Who is the Russian Orthodox communist who provoked protests in Tbilisi?, JAM News] Georgia also experienced political crises in 2020 and 2021, marked by a sharp increase in political polarization between the government and the opposition. [ref: At New Year Reception, Zurabishvili Talks 'National Accord', Civil Georgia]

Tensions between Georgia and Russia have remained high due to the legacy of Russian imperial and Soviet rule over Georgia, as well as Russia's support for separatist movements in the Georgian regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia. [ref: What Happened: The Russia-Georgia Conflict, Gfsis.org]

Draft text:
Limnes () is a village in Argolis, Greece. It forms a community of the municipality of Argos-Mykines, within the municipal unit of Mykines. [ref: ΔΗΜΟΣ ΑΡΓΟΥΣ – ΜΥΚΗΝΩΝ ΠΕ ΑΡΓΟΛΙΔΑΣ, Kallikratis] The village had 553 permanent residents at the 2021 Greek census. [ref: Αποτελέσματα Μόνιμου Πληθυσμού κατά οικισμό, Απογραφή 2021, Hellenic Statistical Authority]

== Geography and economy ==
Limnes is a mountain village. Livestock farming became the main local occupation after tobacco cultivation was abandoned. [ref: Εκπληκτικά ντοκουμέντα για την λαϊκή μουσική παράδοση της Αργολίδας από τις Λίμνες (βίντεο), Argolikes Eidiseis]

== Language and traditions ==
Limnes is one of the Arvanite villages of Argolis, where Arvanitika has traditionally been spoken. [ref: Learning Arvanitic in Late 19th and Early 20th Century Greece: Linguistic Maintenance and Cultural Idiosyncrasies in Greece's Arvanitic Speaking Communities, Zeitschrift für Balkanologie]

The village celebrates the feast of the Presentation of Christ on 2 February. Its central church is dedicated to the feast, and traditional singing and dancing form part of the celebrations. [ref: Sui canti tradizionali degli arbëreshë della Grecia oggi, tenendo conto specialmente dei canti delle nozze. Notizie di una ricerca sul campo]

University of Health Sciences (UOHS; Somali: Jaamacadda Culuumta
Caafimaadka) is a private non-profit higher-education institution in Bosaso,
Bari, Puntland, Somalia. It provides education and training in health sciences
and has a Faculty of Medicine listed in the World Directory of Medical
Schools.University of Health Sciences Faculty of Medicine, World Directory of Medical Schools
== History ==
The university's institutional history states that the University of Health Sciences
was established in September 2000 as a health institute. It was promoted to college
status in 2003 and obtained university status in 2012. The institution attributes its
establishment to the shortage of medical professionals in Somalia following the
country's civil war.UOHS History and Background of the University, University of Health Sciences
The university identifies Prof. Abdirisak Hussein Hassan as its founding father.
According to the university, he established a nursing institute in response to
shortages of trained medical personnel in Somalia.UOHS Founding Father, University of Health Sciences
A 2013 report by the Heritage Institute for Policy Studies listed the University of
Health Sciences among the higher-education institutions surveyed in Puntland. The
report recorded the institution as having been established in 2006 and, at the time of
the survey, listed five faculties and 947 students.The State of the Higher Education Sector in Somalia, Heritage Institute for Policy Studies
== Administration ==
The university's current rector is Dr. Najma Abdirisak H. Hassan. The university's
rector page identifies her as rector, and the Somali Research and Education Network
lists her as a member of its board of directors in the same capacity.Rector's Message, University of Health SciencesBoard of Directors, Somali Research and Education Network
== Academics ==
The university's academic structure includes eight health sciences faculties: the
Faculty of Medicine and Surgery, Faculty of Clinical Midwifery, Faculty of Clinical
Nursing, Faculty of Food Sciences and Nutrition, Faculty of Clinical Pharmacy,
Faculty of Public Health, Faculty of Medical Laboratory, and Faculty of Radiological
Sciences and Medical Imaging.UOHS History and Background of the University, University of Health SciencesUndergraduate Programs, University of Health Sciences

The University of Health Sciences Somalia (UOHS) is a member institution of the Somali Research and Education Network (SomaliREN), a non-profit organization that connects higher education and research institutions in Somalia.Member Institutions, Somali Research and Education Network

The Faculty of Medicine provides a Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery
(MBBS) programme. The World Directory of Medical Schools records the school
as a private, currently operational medical school in Bosaso. It lists 2014 as the year
instruction began, a five-year curriculum, and admission of both men and
women.University of Health Sciences Faculty of Medicine, World Directory of Medical Schools
The university also offers undergraduate programmes in clinical nursing, clinical
midwifery, food sciences and nutrition, public health, medical laboratory sciences,
clinical pharmacy, and radiological sciences and medical imaging.Undergraduate Programs, University of Health Sciences
The radiological sciences and medical imaging programme was inaugurated in 2021,
according to the university, which describes it as an undergraduate programme in
the field.Faculty of Radiological Sciences & Medical Imaging, University of Health Sciences
== Research ==
Researchers affiliated with the University of Health Sciences have participated in
published studies concerning health and higher education in Somalia.
A 2022 study published in BioMed Research International examined hepatitis B
vaccination status and related factors among healthcare workers in Bosaso,
Puntland. The study included researchers affiliated with the University of Health
Sciences.Assessment of Hepatitis B Vaccination Status and Associated Factors among Healthcare Workers in Bosaso, Puntland, Somalia 2020, BioMed Research International
A 2023 study published in BMC Public Health investigated hepatitis B vaccination
coverage among medical students in Bosaso. The study used a sample drawn from
four universities in the city and included a researcher affiliated with the Faculty of
Public Health at the University of Health Sciences.Hepatitis B vaccination coverage and associated factors among medical students: a cross-sectional study in Bosaso, Somalia, 2021, BMC Public Health
In 2025, a study published in PLOS ONE examined tuberculosis treatment
outcomes at Bosaso TB Hospital using records from January 2018 to December 2022.
One of the authors was affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine at the University of
Health Sciences.Tuberculosis treatment outcomes and associated factors among patients treated at Bosaso TB Hospital, Bosaso, Somalia: A five-year retrospective study, PLOS ONE
A 2026 article in Cogent Education examined challenges affecting research and
academic publishing in higher education institutions in Puntland. The author, Saaid
Said Jama, is affiliated with the Faculty of Medicine at the University of Health
Sciences.The challenges facing higher education in Puntland in research and academic publishing: suggestions for their improvement, Cogent Education

Draft: Delius (Song of Summer)

Draft text:
"Delius (Song of Summer)" is a song by the English singer-songwriter Kate Bush, released on her third studio album, Never for Ever (1980). [ref: Delius (Song Of Summer), Kate Bush Encyclopedia] The track served as a tribute to the English composer Frederick Delius and was additionally issued as the B-side to the single "Army Dreamers" in October 1980.

== Background and Composition ==
Bush wrote "Delius" after viewing Song of Summer, Ken Russell's 1968 BBC television film depicting the final years of the blind, paralyzed composer Frederick Delius and his amanuensis, Eric Fenby. [ref: Kate Bush's 50 greatest songs – ranked!, The Guardian] In a contemporaneous newsletter, Bush described the piece as a tribute to "an extraordinary man both in body and spirit."

Musically, the composition relies on acoustic piano, a prominent sitar line performed by Paddy Bush, and ambient vocal harmonies. The backing track features rhythmic accentuations generated by an early drum machine; the liner notes of Never for Ever credit the drum machine simply as "Roland". [ref: Never for Ever, EMI Records]

The lyrical themes detail Delius's dictation process to Fenby, featuring spoken-word style vocal fragments like "In B, Fenby!" alongside subtle Latin phrases ("Delius amat") and references to Delius's orchestral piece To Be Sung of a Summer Night on the Water.

== Release and Promotion ==
The track was recorded between January and June 1980 at Abbey Road Studios in London and released on 7 September 1980 as part of Never for Ever. Rather than being performed live in-studio, the song's music video was broadcast on television programs, including a Dr. Hook television special on 7 April 1980 and on The Russell Harty Show on 25 November 1980, where Bush appeared as a guest alongside Eric Fenby and Julian Lloyd Webber. [ref: Russell Harty Show (the), Kate Bush Encyclopedia]

== Personnel ==
Credits adapted from the Never for Ever album liner notes:

* Kate Bush – lead vocals, piano, production
* Paddy Bush – sitar, bass vocals, additional performance
* Alan Murphy – electric guitar
* Ian Bairnson – bass vocals
* Preston Heyman – percussion
* Jon Kelly – production, engineering
* "Roland" – drum machine

= Adams Elementary School (Spokane, Washington) =
Adams Elementary School is a public elementary school located in the South Hill neighborhood of Spokane,Washington. Part of Spokane Public Schools (District 81), the school serves students from Pre-Kindergarten through 5th grade. Originally established in the early 20th century, it is known for being one of the most historic school sites in Spokane.
Adams Elementary School Building. Source: Spokane Public Schools

== Quick Facts / Infobox ==

* Location: Spokane, Washington, U.S.
* Address (Original Site): 2909 E 37th Ave, Spokane, WA 99223
* Temporary Location (Camp Adams): 3612 S Grand Blvd, Spokane, WA 99203
* School District: Spokane Public Schools (District 81)
* Grades: Pre-K – 5th Grade
* Mascot: All-Stars
* Motto / Identity: "We grow All-Star citizens every day"
* Feeder School For: Sacajawea Middle School / Adams Attendance Area

== History ==

* 1909 Construction: The original school structure was built in 1909 to serve families settling in the South Hill region of Spokane.
* Early Expansions: An additional wing was added in 1917 to accommodate rapid growth in neighborhood enrollment.
* Rebuild Project (2025–2027): As part of a Spokane Public Schools facility upgrade bond, plans were established to build a brand-new, modern facility on the original 37th Avenue grounds.
* Camp Adams Era: Beginning around early 2026, students and staff temporarily relocated to the former Jefferson Elementary building at 3612 S. Grand Blvd (dubbed Camp Adams) while the new building undergoes construction.

== Campus & Facilities ==

* Original Site: Situated near the Lincoln Heights neighborhood on 37th Avenue, featuring classic multi-story red brick architecture.
* Temporary "Camp Adams": Features classic classroom layouts, dedicated play areas, and bus drop-off lanes designed to host South Hill school populations during modern building transitions.
* Future Facility: The new replacement building will feature modern safety upgrades, dedicated STEM/art spaces,and integrated community partnerships.

== Academics & Programs ==

* Curriculum: Core subjects include early literacy, mathematics, science, and social studies aligned with Washington State learning standards.
* Special Programs: Offers special education services, physical education, music programs, and student support intervention groups.
* Recognitions: Recipient of multiple Washington Achievement Awards for academic growth and citizenship programs.

== Community & Culture ==

* School Mascot: Adams All-Stars
* Partnerships: Collaborates with local neighborhood associations and youth organizations, including planned integrated spaces with local youth programs like the Boys & Girls Club on site.

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Out of Eden Walk

Draft text:
----

The Out of Eden Walk is a long-form journalism project led by American journalist Paul Salopek, who began walking in 2013 along a route approximating the early human migration out of Africa. [ref: [https://gis.harvard.edu/out-eden-walk Center for Geographic Analysis, Harvard University, article and timeline]] The project is managed by an independent nonprofit organization and supported by the National Geographic Society. The combines travel writing, photography, audio, video, and mapping to document contemporary life along the journey.

== Background ==
The project was created by Paul Salopek as an experiment in "slow journalism", which would use walking as a method for reporting on different communities and landscapes at human scale, while following one of the broad migration routes associated Out of Africa theory. [ref: Out of Eden Walk, National Geographic Education] [ref: ‘Slow Journalist’ Paul Salopek Is in India on His Epic 10-Year Walk Across Continents, VICE] The project was originally planned as a seven-year trek from Africa's Rift Valley to Tierra del Fuego, [ref: Paul Salopek is on a foot journey across the world. He provides an extraordinary record of humanity at a new millennium, National Geographic] [ref: What Do You Pack For A Seven-Year Trip?, NPR] but due to delays and other factors has continued beyond its initial schedule. [ref: To walk the world: part one, National Geographic] [ref: A Twenty-Four-Thousand-Mile Walk Across Human History, The New Yorker]

A recurring feature of the project is the "milestone" in which a standardized record made at regular intervals along the route. These milestones include observations of landscape, sound, people, and other details from the walk. [ref: New Milestone, East to China, Out of Eden Walk] The project publishes written dispatches, photographs, audio recordings, videos, and map-based stories through the National Geographic Society's Out of Eden Walk platform. [ref: Out of Eden Walk, Out of Eden Walk Nonprofit]

== Route ==
The walk began at Herto Bouri, Ethiopia, in the Afar region near the Great Rift Valley. [ref: Baby Steps, Out of Eden Walk] [ref: Travel Pioneers: Paul Salopek, BBC Travel] The first chapter, "Out of Africa", covered Ethiopia, Djibouti, and a Red Sea crossing between January and May 2013. [ref: Out of Eden Walk, Out of Eden Walk] The project has organized the route into chapters including "Out of Africa", "Holy Lands", "Autumn Wars", "Silk Road", "Riverlands", "Middle Kingdom", "Asian Rim", "Ocean Crossing", and "Americas".

In a 2019 essay for The New Yorker, Salopek wrote that the route was intended to follow archaeological and genetic evidence for ancient human migration as closely as modern borders, wars, and practical conditions allowed. By that time, he had walked from Ethiopia through regions including Saudi Arabia, the Levant, Afghanistan, and India, and planned to continue across China and toward Alaska before proceeding down the Americas.

The walk was disrupted by the COVID-19 pandemic, with Salopek having paused in Myanmar. [ref: Crossroad of Memory, Out of Eden Walk] He resumed the route in China in October 2021 after a quarantine in Shanghai. In April 2023, while Salopek was in China, PBS NewsHour described him as halfway through the journey. [ref: Explorer halfway through journey to walk around the world, PBS NewsHour]

By January 2025, Salopek reached the Pacific Rim, and wrote that he hoped to board a cargo ship from Japan to Alaska that spring. [ref: Bookend Oceans, Out of Eden Walk] In May 2025, he was in Nagano Prefecture. [ref: One long walk: National Geographic 'explorer' on global journey strolls into Victoria, Times Colonist] He crossed the North Pacific by container ship in 2025, with a November 2025 dispatch describing the crossing as the project's "Ocean Crossing" chapter. [ref: Blue Highway, Out of Eden Walk]

In October 2025, National Geographic announced that the project had entered North America, beginning a new phase of the journey in Alaska. [ref: Out of Eden Walk Global Storytelling Journey Arrives in North America, National Geographic Society] In January 2026, Salopek published a dispatch from Anchorage, Alaska. [ref: Reading Anchorage, Out of Eden Walk] In October 2026, he arrived in Victoria, BC. At that point, he was 5,000 days into his trip and had walked approximately 30,000 kilometres.

== Educational use and organization ==
The Out of Eden Walk has been used as an educational resource by National Geographic Education and the Pulitzer Center. [ref: Out of Eden Walk: An Introduction for Educators, Pulitzer Center] National Geographic Education describes the project as a resource for subjects including anthropology, genetics, geography, human geography, social studies, storytelling, and geographic information systems. The Pulitzer Center, an education partner of the project, has promoted the walk as a tool for teaching about migration and global storytelling.

The Out of Eden Walk is also associated with an independent nonprofit organization, Out of Eden Walk, which describes itself as a 501(c)(3) organization supporting Salopek's journey and related educational work. [ref: Out Of Eden Walk, ProPublica]

Woofy is a French-Canadian animated television series created by Alexandre Révérend and directed by Dominique Etchecopar. [ref: Woofy, Gaumont] [ref: Woofy, Planète Jeunesse] Consisting of 65 five or six-minute episodes, the series was co-produced by animation studios Alphanim and Tooncan Productions XXV, inc. in association with France 5. [ref: Alphanim Scores Sales Ahead of MIPCOM, Animation Magazine]

== Premise ==
The series revolves around Woofy, a stray dog adopted by a four-year-old boy named Anthony (French: Antoine). Because Anthony's mother forbids pets in the household, Anthony pretends that Woofy is a plush toy won at a school fair. [ref: TV5MONDE February Highlights, Complete France] Woofy maintains a secret life whenever adults are not looking, leading to comedic situations as he and Anthony attempt to conceal his true identity.

Draft text:
Judi for Food Industries (), trading as Judi, is a Libyan food manufacturing company headquartered in Tripoli. Founded in 2004, it produces dairy products and fruit juices, mainly in carton packaging, and is described as one of the leading producers of carton-packed milk and juice in Libya. [ref: Part Five: A bite-size breakdown of who's who in the Libyan retail, FMCG and food production sector, The British Libyan Business Association] [ref: About Judi, Judi for Food Industries]

== History ==
Judi for Food Industries was established in 2004. In 2008, construction was completed on a production building in Tripoli for evaporated milk and juice, with a site area and built-up area of about 15,000 square metres. [ref: Judi Company Evaporated Milk, Juice, Medad Consulting Engineers]

== Operations ==
The company has a reported production capacity of about 120 tonnes per day. It imports raw materials, including whole milk powder and banana purée, from countries such as New Zealand, Chile, Guatemala and Costa Rica.

== Products ==
Judi's product range includes:
* UHT milk (full-fat, low-fat and skimmed)
* Fruit juices and nectars (Judi Nectar)
* Cheese
* Flavoured milk (Moudi)
* Mocktails
* Ayran
* Butter ghee

Draft text:
Lydia Rodarte-Quayle is a fictional character in the crime drama television series Breaking Bad and its prequel series Better Call Saul. She is portrayed by Scottish actress Laura Fraser.

Introduced in fifth season, Lydia is a business executive at Madrigal Electromotive who is involved in the company's logistics operations. She secretly helps Gustavo Fring obtain chemicals for his methamphetamine operation and later becomes involved with Walter White and Todd Alquist's uncle Jack Welker with his criminal organization. Lydia is a single mother with a daughter, and her concern for her daughter is part of her motivation. She later helps expand the methamphetamine business into the Czech Republic. In series finale, Walter eventually poisons her with ricin concealed in the stevia she uses in her tea.

== Creation and characterization ==
[[File:Laura Fraser in 2017.png|thumb|233x233px|Laura Fraser, who plays Lydia Rodarte-Quayle]]
Lydia Rodarte-Quayle is portrayed by Scottish actress Laura Fraser. Fraser was cast after auditioning for the role and later performed a diner scene with Jonathan Banks, who plays Mike Ehrmantraut. Fraser had not watched Breaking Bad before getting the role, but watched the first four seasons after being cast. [ref: 'Breaking Bad' Post-Mortem: New Face Laura Fraser Talks About Her Role, The Hollywood Reporter] Fraser described Lydia as "extremely highly strung, calculating, enterprising" and said that she had learned to survive at all costs and developed skills to do so. She also said that her character was constantly trying to regain control of her situation and that she did not know whether the character would survive from one scene to the next.

Fraser said that Lydia's concern for her daughter influenced the way she understood the character's actions. She described the daughter as an important part of how Lydia justified her actions to herself. [ref: Breaking Bad's Lydia: 'Drinking camomile tea with milk is disgusting', The Guardian] Fraser also described her character as being in a constant state of "fight-or-flight" while discussing the physical strain of playing the character. Fraser discussed Lydia's position within the corporate world represented by Madrigal Electromotive. She said that Lydia's role allowed the series to show a side of the drug trade connected to large businesses rather than only street-level criminal activity. [ref: 'Breaking Bad' Q&A: Laura Fraser on the Mystery of Lydia, Rolling Stone]

In a 2013 interview with Rolling Stone, Fraser described Lydia as a "clean-cut, bonkers sociopath" and said that the character took herself seriously while believing that she was always right. She also discussed Lydia's Louboutin shoes, saying that the red soles represented the bloodshed for which Lydia was responsible. [ref: 'Breaking Bads Lydia: 'She's a Clean-Cut, Bonkers Sociopath', Rolling Stone] Fraser also described her character as "extremely self-righteous and irritating" and said that she took herself too seriously. In developing the character, Fraser imagined that Lydia had grown up in a group home, had an unhappy and uncertain childhood, and had been abandoned as a child, which she believed contributed to Lydia's loneliness and alienation. [ref: Breaking Bad's Laura Fraser Channels Her 'Inner Hate' To Play Lydia Rodarte-Quayle, CBS News]

Lydia's tea, which consists of chamomile tea with soy milk and stevia, was later discussed by creator Vince Gilligan. Gilligan said there was no hidden meaning behind the choice. He said that he personally put milk in chamomile tea and that soy milk was chosen because it sounded healthy. [ref: 'Breaking Bad' Creator Vince Gilligan Finally Explains Why Lydia Took Her Tea Like That, TheWrap] Fraser also discussed filming Lydia's final scene in the series finale, "Felina". She said that her final day on the set involved filming Lydia's death scene and that she was made to look physically ill after being poisoned with ricin. She recalled filming the scene with Bryan Cranston. [ref: Breaking Bad's Laura Fraser on the Finale, [[Vulture (magazine)]

== Appearances ==
=== Better Call Saul ===
Lydia is introduced in Better Call Saul during the events preceding Breaking Bad. In 2003, she accompanies Gustavo Fring while he examines an industrial laundry facility that Gus plans to use for a secret methamphetamine laboratory. The facility later becomes the location of Gus's underground laboratory. [ref: Off Brand] Lydia later meets Mike Ehrmantraut at Madrigal's Houston office. She explains her concerns about Mike's activities involving the company's security and becomes involved in arrangements connected to Gus's operation. Although she is nervous about the risks involved, she continues to work with Gus. [ref: Fall]

==== Season 4 ====
Lydia continues to work at Madrigal and becomes involved in the security arrangements surrounding the company's illegal activities. She asks Mike to stop testing the company's security, but Gus later allows Mike to continue working with Madrigal. [ref: Breathe]

==== Season 5 ====
Lydia meets with Peter Schuler and Gus to discuss Lalo Salamanca, who is causing problems for Gus's operation while in prison. Lydia suggests that Lalo be killed in prison, but Gus rejects the idea because of the attention it would bring to them. [ref: JMM]

Draft: Criston Cole

Draft text:
Criston Cole is a fictional character from George R.R. Martin's A Song of Ice and Fire series of epic fantasy novel, appearing in the 2013 novella The Princess and the Queen, the 2014 novella The Rogue Prince and the 2018 novel Fire & Blood. In the HBO television adaptation House of the Dragon, he is portrayed by French-English actor Fabien Frankel.

In both the books and the show, Cole is a highly skilled knight who ascends to become a member of King Viserys I Targaryen's Kingsguard, initially acting as Rhaenyra Targaryen's sworn protector. He later rises to become Lord Commander of the Kingsguard and Hand of the King to King Aegon II Targaryen, fighting for the green faction during the Targaryen civil war known as the Dance of the Dragons. Cole acts as one of the greens' primary military commanders, leading campaigns throughout the Crownlands and Riverlands to ensure Aegon's continued reign.

Since his introduction in the television series, Cole has proven to one of House of the Dragons most polarising characters. [ref: ‘House of the Dragon’ Just Took One of Its Best Characters Off the Board, GQ] Though Frankel's performance received consistent acclaim, critical reception to the character's writing has been more mixed, whilst fans regularly cite him as one of the show's most hated characters. [ref: House of the Dragon Season 3 Has Undermined One Major Book Character, GameRant] [ref: Fans Are Very Happy About House of the Dragon's "Unceremonious" Episode 6 Death, Esquire]

== In the books ==

=== Fire and Blood ===
Criston was born in 82 AC to the son of Lord Dondarrion's steward. In 104 AC, during the tournament at Maidenpool to celebrate King Viserys I Targaryen's ascension to the Iron Throne, he won Princess Rhaenyra Targaryen's favour after beating Prince Daemon Targaryen during the melee by knocking his sword Dark Sister out of his hands with a morningstar. He later wore the princess' favour during the joust, where he again bested Daemon, as well as Ser Erryk and Arryk Cargyll of the Kingsguard. A year later, he was sworn in as a member of the Kingsguard, replacing Ser Ryam Redwyne, and was named Rhaenyra's sworn shield. [ref: Fire and Blood, Bantam Books]

In 113 AC, following the betrothal of Rhaenyra to Ser Laenor Velaryon, Criston reportedly confessed his love to Rhaenyra, offering to run away to the Free Cities with her, but she refused. However, an alternate source suggested that it was Rhaenyra who attempted to seduce him but was refused. Regardless, Criston went from being Rhaenyra's strongest supporter to her most hated enemy, and was replaced by Ser Harwin "Breakbones" Strong as her sworn protector.

In 114 AC, Criston fought in the joust at Rhaenyra's wedding to Laenor, during which he injured Harwin and Ser Joffrey Lonmouth, the latter of whom died from his injuries six days later. Though many were angered at Criston's actions, Queen Alicent Hightower chose him to be her sworn protector.

Following the death of King Viserys in 129 AC, Queen Alicent assembled the small council - Criston among them - to discuss the succession. Criston objected to the ascension of Rhaenyra, Viserys' chosen heir, on account of her children with Laenor Velaryon being supposed bastards, instead supporting her brother Aegon as the correct choice for the crown. During the meeting, Lord Lyman Beesbury, the only councillor to support Rhaenyra, declared that this was treason, leading to Criston slitting his throat with a dagger or throwing him out of a window to his death (depending on which source is to be believed). Criston then helped imprison the remaining Black supporters at court and personally crown Aegon as king in the Dragonpit. [ref: Fire and Blood, Bantam Books] As a result of his support of Aegon II and his hand in crowning him, Criston would be forever remembered in Westeros' history as 'The Kingmaker'. [ref: The World of Ice & Fire: The Untold History of Westeros and the Game of Thrones, Bantam]

Following Aegon II's coronation, the Dance of the Dragons officially began when Rhaenyra refused to support her half-brother's ascension. Many lords remembered King Viserys' wish for Rhaenyra to succeed him, and threw their support behind her. As the blacks started to gain more allies, Aegon II became frustrated at the slow progress of his grandfather and Hand of the King, Ser Otto Hightower, resulting in him stripping Otto of his office and appointing Criston as his new hand. [ref: Fire and Blood, Bantam Books]

In response to the death of Aegon's eldest son, Prince Jaehaerys Targaryen, at the hands of Blood and Cheese, Criston ordered Ser Arryk Cargyll to sneak into Dragonstone disguised as his twin brother Ser Erryk, who was guarding Rhaenyra on Dragonstone. The scheme ended up failing when the twins came encountered and killed one another in single combat.

Draft: The principle of operation of the nervous system.

Draft text:
To illustrate this, let us consider a primitive animal with a very simple nervous system. When the organism is exposed to stimuli capable of causing harm, signals indicating danger arise in its receptors (sensors); these signals travel through the nervous system — most likely to the motor organs — compelling the organism to move until it has escaped the source of the irritation. Once the stimulus vanishes, the signals cease, and the nervous system (and consequently the body) returns to a state of rest.

It follows that rest — the absence or reduction of signals within the nervous system — is the goal of a living creature's actions (this is precisely what happiness is). Conversely, signals within the nervous system are perceived by the living creature as various forms of pain, from which it seeks relief. If one believes that "pleasant" signals exist within the nervous system, that is simply not the case. The only signals that might seem pleasant are those that block the transmission of other signals (much like a painkiller), but there is little point in discussing such signals.

The nervous system functions as an alarm system for the organism, signaling danger and prompting action. That is precisely why it evolved: to sense pain and attempt to escape it. Thus, life is spent entirely in this manner: sensing various forms of pain and trying to rid oneself of them. Even boredom is a form of discomfort — and, likewise, a signal within the nervous system.

In short, pain is the sole stimulus for activity in all organisms possessing a nervous system. [ref: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_nervous_systems]

== References ==

The Baran–Shivpuri new railway line (Hindi: बारां–शिवपुरी नई रेल लाइन) is a proposed railway line connecting Baran in Rajasthan with Shivpuri in Madhya Pradesh, India.

== History ==

The Baran Shivpuri new railway line was included in the railway survey programme of Indian Railways. According to a Railway Board document dated 26 August 2014, the survey was completed in 2013–14. The proposed line was listed with a length of 151 km and an estimated cost of ₹778 crore. At the time, the survey report was under examination. [ref: Details of Surveys Completed During the Last 10 Years as on 26 August 2014, Indian Railways]

The West Central Railway's annual report for 2014–15 also recorded that the revised survey report for the Baran Shivpuri line had been submitted to the Railway Board. [ref: Annual Report 2014–15, West Central Railway]

== Project status ==

The cited railway records document the completion of the survey and submission of the revised report to the Railway Board. They do not establish that construction of the line was sanctioned. The estimated cost of ₹778 crore was reported in 2014 and should not be taken as the current project cost.

Draft text:
----

Louis Brown (c. 1934–1986) was a British nightclub proprietor associated with London's West End nightlife during the 1960s, 1970s and early 1980s. He was known for his association with La Valbonne, a nightclub in Soho, and his venues which attracted entertainers, musicians and other prominent figures. He was known for his distinctive ideas and designs within his clubs making a name for himself as the King of Clubs.

== Career ==
Louis Brown was a British nightclub entrepreneur who became a prominent figure in London's West End nightlife during the 1960s and 1970s. Working alongside business partner Leonard Bloom, he established and operated a number of nightclubs, including La Poubelle, Le Kilt and the Scotch of St James, before opening La Valbonne in Soho in 1967.

Known for his distinctive approach to nightclub design and entertainment, Brown developed venues that attracted musicians, celebrities and fashionable clientele. His business interests later extended beyond London to Skindles Hotel in Taplow, Berkshire, where he established Studio Valbonne as a nightclub and entertainment venue. Brown continued to operate his nightclub businesses into the 1980s and died in 1986.

=== Skindles ===
Brown was also involved in the ownership and management of Skindles Hotel, a historic riverside hotel in Taplow, Berkshire, during the 1970s. Under his involvement, the establishment formed part of his wider interests in the hospitality and nightclub industries. In 1978, plans were proposed for an extension comprising 81 additional bedrooms, reflecting efforts to redevelop the property as a hotel and leisure destination. Skindles subsequently closed in 1995. Here on the Taplow Society archive it mentions the restoration Brown had on Skindles and what he did with it. https://www.taplowsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/NL41.pdf

=== La Valbonne ===
La Valbonne was a nightclub at 62 Kingly Street in Soho, London, which opened in 1967 and became Louis Brown's best-known establishment. The venue was noted for its elaborate interior, featuring multiple bars, tropical plants, large fish tanks and a heart-shaped swimming pool incorporated into the dance floor. It attracted musicians, entertainers and other prominent figures, and appeared in Pete Walker's 1970 film Cool It Carol.

=== Other clubs ===
Le Kilt was a Soho nightclub associated with Louis Brown and his business partner Leonard Bloom. Situated on Greek Street, it formed part of Brown's expanding portfolio of West End entertainment venues during the 1960s and 1970s. The club operated within London's emerging discothèque culture, which increasingly centred on recorded music, dancing and fashionable nightlife. http://lesenfantsterribles.adrianstern.com/lekilt.pl

La Poubelle was an early London discothèque associated with Louis Brown. It opened in 1959 and is described in historical accounts as one of London's earliest venues devoted to recorded-music dancing. Located initially on Great Marlborough Street, near Oxford Circus, the club attracted socialites and helped establish the discothèque format that subsequently spread throughout the capital.http://lesenfantsterribles.adrianstern.com/lapoubelle.pl

The Scotch of St James opened in Mason's Yard, Mayfair, in July 1965 and became a prominent nightclub and live-music venue during London's Swinging Sixties. Associated with Louis Brown's nightclub interests, it attracted musicians and other figures from the British and American music scenes. American guitarist Jimi Hendrix famously joined musicians for an impromptu performance there on his arrival in England in September 1966. http://lesenfantsterribles.adrianstern.com/otherclubs.pl

Samantha's Club was a London nightclub operating around the late 1960s and early 1970s. A retrospective account published in 2025 recalls the club as a basement venue off Regent Street, featuring soul music performances and a distinctive DJ booth constructed from the body of a Jaguar E-Type car. The account places the club within London's fashionable nightlife scene at the end of the 1960s. === Relationship with Peter Stringfellow ===
Brown's La Valbonne nightclub reportedly attracted the interest of fellow nightclub entrepreneur Peter Stringfellow. A retrospective account states that Stringfellow regarded the venue as influential and that Brown offered to sell it to him however the deal never fulfilled.

Marlow Sports Club is an outdoors sports facility, as well as a charity, based in Marlow, Buckinghamshire, England. It is located 28 miles west from Central London, and 4 miles south from High Wycombe as the crow flies.

== History ==
Marlow Sports Club was founded in 1949, on the original site it is located on now. It was originally formed by an umbrella organisation, including Marlow Rugby Union Football Club, Marlow Cricket Club & Marlow Hockey Club. Earlier, from the beginning, in 1895 Owen Peel Wethered purchased approximately 5,800 acres of land between Pound Lane and the River Thames. He leased it to Marlow Cricket Club for 21 years, before Owen died in 1908. Marlow struggled to find players after World War I, and in 1908, after the end of the lease period, the land was put up for sale. [ref: OUR EARLY HISTORY, Marlow Sports Club]

In July 1920, a petition from the staff requested the Wethered directors to purchase it as a recreation club. Not long after, the plan was agreed and the company then upgraded the pavillion, and also installed gas.

A few years after the end of World War II, the MSC (Marlow Sports Club) was founded, still at the same ground on Pound Lane, and that same year, the Wethereds were sold to Strong & Co, which was obtained by Whitbread in 1969.

Everything was going as planned and well in major circumstances until 2006, when MSC shockingly recieved a notification that Whitbread had decided that the site was to be auctioned of, potentially for housing. The sports club then fought a 5-year long battle to save the green site. This lasted from April 2006 to March 2011, as it became a charity as well as it's ever-lasting sports facility in January 2011. This incurred debts of over £1M. [ref: OUR STORY, Marlow Sports Club]

== Role ==
Marlow Sports Club is now a protected sports facility and charity purposed for sports and leisure (including the nearby Court Garden Leisure Centre), and has grown to become one of Marlow's biggest sports centres.

The sports facility has a collective membership count of around 2,500 members, and of which over half are under 18 (juniors). This is excluding large sporting participation, and back in 2006 when they got notified from Whitbread, their collective membership was approximately 5x smaller (around 500). It has many member clubs, Marlow Cricket Club, Marlow Hockey Club, Marlow Riders, Marlow Striders, Marlow Tennis Club, Marlow Petanque and for school sporting, Sir William Borlase's Grammar School. [ref: OUR STORY, Marlow Sports Club]

The club offers a first-class floodlit hockey pitch, 4 all-weather floodlit tennis courts, petanque terrains, and a cricket pitch.

Draft text:
Daam is a Sri Lankan Sinhala-language television series that aired on Sirasa TV from 21 December 2020 [ref: ] to 7 May 2021. [ref: ] Directed by Dhanushka Rathnayake and written by Kaushalya Pathirana, the series was produced by Gayan Dinesh Perera under Gayan Productions. It stars Bimal Jayakody, Tharindi Fernando, and Chameera Liyanage in lead roles.

== Plot ==
Amaya, an air hostess with an exceptional photographic memory, becomes entangled in an international drug-trafficking network after catching the attention of Kevin Walter Almeida, a prominent drug trafficker and former associate of her father. Almeida attempts to leverage Amaya's memory skills to transport contraband and assist in his criminal operations.

Initially, Amaya refuses to cooperate. However, facing escalating threats against her family, she is forced into the syndicate to protect her husband, Kevin, her daughter, Akeshi, as well as her parents and sister.

Meanwhile, a commercial flight departing Sri Lanka mysteriously disappears with no initial signs of survivors. Amaya's family and the public presume she died in the crash. However, Almeida discovers that Amaya survived and launches an effort to track her down to bring her back under his control.

Almeida later crosses paths with Livera, a man suffering from severe retrograde amnesia whose past is tied to Almeida's criminal network. Amaya is eventually rescued, while Livera attempts to flee the country. Livera is subsequently apprehended by law enforcement at the airport, exposing his deep involvement in the syndicate.

In the final scene, Almeida is seen travelling in a vehicle alongside another man (portrayed by Saranga Disasekara). The man turns to Almeida and remarks, "The game is on", concluding the series. Disasekara reprises his role as Rayan, a character from director Dhanushka Rathnayake's previous television series, Wes.
