Draft text:
Webtronaut Innovations LLC is an American internet holding company based in Albuquerque, New Mexico. It was founded by Sahil Kazi, an Indian/Pakistani serial entrepreneur and SAP Certified Systems Analyst. The group's first venture, the legal-tech marketplace SueEasy, began in 2007 and was a semi-finalist in the inaugural TechCrunch startup competition, TechCrunch40. [ref: Ambulance Chasers Have A New Home, SueEasy, TechCrunch] The company's current ventures include Richlisted, GuiltyAF, SwaxAwards and LabCauldron.

== History ==

=== SueEasy and Filmmortal (2007–2009) ===
Webtronaut's first ventures were developed under the Webtronaut Innovations name (including an Indian entity, Webtronaut Innovations Pvt. Ltd.) and operated from Mountain View, California. [ref: Filmmortal.com, Film Is Immortal. So Is Your Brand, PRLog]

SueEasy, launched in 2007 by Kazi and Faraz Matin, was a marketplace that inverted the traditional lawyer directory: would-be plaintiffs posted grievances and documents, individually or as potential class actions, and licensed attorneys bid for the right to contact the client. Crunchbase lists SueEasy as a sub-organisation of Webtronaut Innovations. [ref: SueEasy — Company Profile, Crunchbase] SueEasy launched publicly in April 2008 with a searchable class-action repository covering nine filing categories. [ref: SueEasy Goes Live — Your Class Action Lawsuit Lottery Ticket, TechCrunch] The ABA Journal described the service as a "reverse Martindale-Hubbell" that matched would-be plaintiffs with lawyers. [ref: New Website Plays Matchmaker For Would-Be Plaintiffs, ABA Journal] United Press International also reported on the service in April 2008. [ref: Web Site Makes Suing Easy] The Los Angeles Daily Journal later profiled SueEasy among attorney-client matchmaking services, quoting Kazi and reporting that more than 1,200 California lawyers were paying customers. [ref: Attorney-Client Matchmakers, Los Angeles Daily Journal] The model also drew criticism from legal commentators over case quality and legal ethics. In September 2009 the business was put up for sale by online auction, [ref: Running SueEasy Turned Out To Be Not So Easy, Overlawyered] According to the company, SueEasy was subsequently acquired by a mass-torts law firm. Company databases list the original company as closed.

In 2008 the group launched Filmmortal, an auction marketplace for product placement, described as "the eBay for product placement," in which independent filmmakers listed projects and advertisers bid to have products placed in them. [ref: Filmmortal — Company Profile, Crunchbase] The launch was covered by BusinessWeek and by GigaOM's NewTeeVee, which described Filmmortal and rival PlaceVine as new matchmakers for product-placement deals, reporting that Kazi had bootstrapped Filmmortal with $130,000 and that placement deals started at around $3,000. [ref: Startups Take on Product Placement Dealmaking, BusinessWeek] [ref: The New Matchmakers: Startups Tackle Product Placement Deals, NewTeeVee] Media in Canada profiled the service in April 2009, calling it an "eBay for product placement" with around 80 projects listed. [ref: Filmmortal breathes life into indie scripts, Media in Canada] IndieWire also covered the service in October 2009. [ref: Product Placement Ought to Know Where It's Being Placed, IndieWire] Product Placement News announced the marketplace in February 2009. [ref: Introducing Filmmortal, Product Placement News] Kazi served as Filmmortal's chief executive. According to the company, Filmmortal was subsequently acquired. Company databases list it as closed.

=== Holding company and current ventures (2023–present) ===
In April 2023 the group launched Richlisted, a service that records members' names on a public blockchain as a permanent record of achievement; a launch announcement quoted Kazi as managing director of Richlisted. [ref: RichListed Launches Exclusive Blockchain-Listed Network for Self-Made Individuals to Showcase Status, PRLog]

In October 2026, Webtronaut Innovations LLC was formed in New Mexico as the holding company for the group's web businesses, which it describes as an "internet holding company operating multiple web-based businesses." [ref: Webtronaut Innovations]

== Ventures ==
=== SueEasy ===
SueEasy (2007–2009) was a legal marketplace and class-action repository. Plaintiffs posted cases across categories including class actions; only licensed attorneys could browse the listings, and attorneys bid for the right to contact a client, with the client free to reject a bidder.

=== Filmmortal ===
Filmmortal (2008) was an online auction marketplace for product-placement deals between independent filmmakers and advertisers, including barter arrangements such as transport, hotels, catering, props and equipment.

=== Richlisted ===
Richlisted (2023–present) offers a one-time paid listing recorded on a public blockchain as a permanent, uneditable record.

=== GuiltyAF ===
GuiltyAF (2025–present) is an interactive live-streamed show in which two parties present a dispute and the audience votes on the outcome in real time.

=== SwaxAwards ===
SwaxAwards is a monthly awards programme recognising creators on TikTok across categories including comedy, dance and wholesome content.

Hanoi Archers () are a Vietnamese amateur baseball team based in Hanoi. One of the pioneering clubs in Vietnam, they regularly compete in the Vietnam Baseball Championship, winning a title in 2025.

== History ==
Arguably the first baseball club in Hanoi, the Archers were founded in 2006 as the FisHANU Baseball Club () by a group of college students. The founding group consisted of students of the Faculty of International Studies (Fis) of the Hanoi University (HANU) in southwestern Hanoi, thus the name. [ref: ] The club called the HANU campus sports field home up until circa 2019, as the club failed to recruit HANU students and the school's new sports field planning scheme made it impossible for baseball, effectively forcing it out.

Under the new name Hanoi Archers, the newly independent club juggled between weekend operation in multiple locations and weekday practice downtown, before sharing a baseball-specified field, the first of its kind in the city, with expat clubs in western Hanoi. The club, however, remained highly competitive under the management of former LG Twins prospect Yoo Jae-ho, winning local Hanoi league titles in 2023 and 2024. [ref: Hall of Fame (Champion of 2023 2nd Season), Hanoi Baseball League] [ref: Hall of Fame (Champion of 2024 Season), Hanoi Baseball League] Come the advent of the annual national championship, the Archers made the championship game back-to-back in 2022 and 2023, only to lose both to HCMC powerhouse Saigon Storm. [ref: Đội HCM II – CLB Sài Gòn Storm lên ngôi vô địch Giải cúp Các câu lạc bộ Bóng chày Toàn quốc 2022 (HCM II - Saigon Storm wins the 2022 National Baseball Club Cup), Facebook] [ref: Á QUÂN GIẢI CÚP CÁC CÂU LẠC BỘ BÓNG CHÀY TOÀN QUỐC 2023- HANOI ARCHERS (Runners-up of the 2023 National Baseball Club Cup - the Hanoi Archers), Facebook]

After losing to the Storm in the 2024 semifinals, their woes would finally come to an end in the 2025 Vietnam Baseball Club Championship. The Archers came swinging early on, beating Saigon by mercy rule in pool play, before beating them again in the championship game to win the club's first national title. [ref: Hanoi Archers vô địch Giải các Câu lạc bộ Bóng chày toàn quốc 2025, Chính sách và Cuộc sống - Thông tấn xã Việt Nam]

= CycloGen AI =
CycloGen AI, Inc. is a Canadian biotechnology software company developing artificial intelligence tools for structure-guided molecular discovery. The company was incorporated in British Columbia on January 8, 2026. [ref: BC Registry, CycloGen AI]

CycloGen AI develops a no-code computational platform that integrates protein structure prediction, molecular docking, structural biology, protein binder engineering, ligand design, and virtual screening. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

The company's software is intended for biotechnology companies, pharmaceutical research organizations, contract research organizations, and academic institutions. [ref: whiteford research database, CycloGen AI]

== History ==
CycloGen AI was established in British Columbia, Canada, in 2026. [ref: BC Registry, CycloGen AI]

The company develops computational tools intended to integrate structural biology, machine learning, and molecular modelling within a unified software environment. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

== Technology ==
CycloGen AI develops software for structure-guided molecular discovery. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

Its platform includes tools for protein structure prediction, molecular docking, nanobody and mini-binder design, mutation analysis, ligand discovery, and target identification. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

The company offers on-premises software deployment intended to support organizations working with proprietary biological and molecular research data. [ref: CycloGen AI - Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

== Business and Research Applications ==
CycloGen AI operates primarily as a computational discovery software provider rather than a clinical-stage therapeutics developer. [ref: CycloGen AI Enterprise AI Drug Discovery Platform, CycloGen AI]

Its technology is intended to support early-stage drug discovery, protein engineering, structural analysis, and computational evaluation of molecular candidates.

Draft text:
The Kanaya Maru is a Japanese roll-on/roll-off passenger and vehicle carrier operated by Tokyo-Wan Ferry.

== Construction ==
The ship was laid down in August 1991 and completed in February 1992 by the Niihama Shipbuilding yard in Tamano, Japan. Built as a steel-hulled roll-on/roll-off passenger and vehicle carrier, the vessel was specifically designed to handle the choppy, heavily trafficked waters of the Uraga Channel at the mouth of Tokyo Bay. [ref: Kanaya Maru (3rd Generation) Vessel Specifications, Wakanatsu Marine Database]

== Career ==
The ship entered service in April 1992 [ref: ], operating on the route between Kurihama Port in Yokosuka, Kanagawa Prefecture, and Kanaya Port in Futtsu, Chiba. For over three decades, the vessel has served alongside its sister ship, the Shirahama Maru [ref: ], as a vital marine bypass. [ref: 料金案内と船内設備のご案内, Tokyo-Wan Ferry Official]

== Maintenance==
To comply with domestic Japanese maritime safety regulations and regular ship inspection codes, the ship undergoes mandatory drydocking procedures once per year. [ref: 空飛ぶ船ジェットフォイルの「翼」その意外すぎる形 ドックでの検査, Traffic News] The annual overhaul typically takes place in December at the Kanazashi Heavy Industries shipyard (Kanasashi Shipbuilding yard) located in Shimizu Port, Shizuoka Prefecture. [ref: 東京湾フェリー公式アカウント: かなや丸ドック報告, Tokyo-Wan Ferry Official Instagram] During this offline period, which spans approximately two to three weeks, the ferry is removed from the Uraga Channel route entirely, triggering temporary timetable adjustments for the fleet. Drydock maintenance protocols include complete hull sandblasting and anti-fouling repainting, detailed safety inspections of the lower bow thruster units, dual-propeller adjustments, steering rudder overhauls, and deep-engine compartment load tests. [ref: かなや丸ドライドック入渠の様子, Tokyo-Wan Ferry Official Facebook]

Aditya Praristama Santoso, juga dikenal sebagai Keo Santoso, adalah seorang pengusaha Indonesia yang diketahui terlibat dalam sektor energi panas bumi. Aditya Praristama Santoso, yang dikenal sebagai Aditya Keo Santoso atau Keo Santoso, merupakan anak dari Supramu Santoso dan Yenni Rista Santoso. Pada Oktober 2025, ia disebut sebagai Komisaris Supreme Energy dalam pemberitaan mengenai pengembangan proyek Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Panas Bumi (PLTP) Muara Laboh di Kabupaten Solok Selatan, Sumatera Barat.

== Karier ==

=== Stellar Kapital ===
Aditya Keo Santoso membangun Stellar Kapital pada 2014. Perusahaan tersebut berfokus pada investasi dan pengembangan perusahaan rintisan di Indonesia, termasuk perusahaan yang bergerak dalam bidang teknologi finansial, perdagangan elektronik, dan layanan lainnya.

Dalam pemberitaan pada Mei 2018, ia disebut sebagai salah satu pendiri dan ketua Stellar Kapital. Perusahaan tersebut dilaporkan memiliki portofolio investasi yang mencakup UangTeman, Sepulsa, Dananikah, Rajamobil, Tado, Travelio, dan Freeware.

Pada Oktober 2025, Aditya Praristama Santoso diberitakan menjabat sebagai komisaris Supreme Energy. Ia menghadiri kegiatan dimulainya pengeboran sumur pertama untuk pengembangan tahap kedua PLTP Muara Laboh di Kabupaten Solok Selatan, Sumatera Barat.

== Pendidikan ==
Profil profesional Aditya mencantumkan De Anza College dan Santa Clara University Leavey School of Business sebagai institusi pendidikannya. Rincian program studi dan status kelulusan memerlukan verifikasi lebih lanjut.

Draft text:
== New Government Procurement Act ==
The New Government Procurement Act (NGPA), officially known as [https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_12009_2024.html Republic Act No. 12009], is a Philippine law that establishes the legal framework for government procurement of goods, infrastructure projects, and consulting services. It was signed into law on July 20, 2024, and took effect on August 13, 2024. The law replaced Republic Act No. 9184, also known as the Government Procurement Reform Act, and aims to promote transparency, competition, efficiency, accountability, sustainability, and value for money in government spending. [ref: Philippines: New Government Procurement Act Enters into Force, Library of Congress] [ref: Republic Act No. 12009, The LawPhil Project]

=== Overview ===
The New Government Procurement Act sets rules for how government agencies acquire goods and services, contract infrastructure projects, and use public funds for procurement. It applies to national government offices and agencies, state universities and colleges, government-owned or controlled corporations, government financial institutions, and local government units, subject to the law's provisions and applicable agreements.

The law seeks to improve government procurement by establishing principles that support open information, fair competition, efficient procedures, accountability, public monitoring, and sustainable purchasing. It also emphasizes value for money in the use of public resources.

=== Background ===
Before the passage of Republic Act No. 12009, government procurement in the Philippines was mainly governed by Republic Act No. 9184, or the Government Procurement Reform Act. Research by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies examined procurement reforms under the earlier framework and discussed implementation challenges, including delays and difficulties in procurement processes. [ref: The Promises and Pains in Procurement Reforms in the Philippines, Philippine Institute for Development Studies]

In July 2024, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. signed Republic Act No. 12009 into law. It took effect on August 13, 2024, and revised the previous legal framework for government procurement. The law's implementing rules and regulations were published on February 10, 2025, to guide its implementation. [ref: Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 12009, Supreme Court E-Library]

=== Legal framework and scope ===
Republic Act No. 12009 provides the legal basis for procurement activities involving goods, infrastructure projects, and consulting services by covered government entities. The law applies regardless of whether the funds come from local or foreign sources, subject to applicable treaties and international or executive agreements.

The law also provides for implementing rules and regulations to guide procurement planning, procedures, and contract implementation. These rules support the application of the law's policies and principles in government procurement activities.

=== Governing principles ===
Republic Act No. 12009 identifies several principles for government procurement:

* Transparency: Providing access to procurement information and supporting the disclosure of information throughout the procurement process.
* Competitiveness: Giving eligible and qualified suppliers, contractors, consultants, and service providers fair opportunities.
* Efficiency: Promoting organized and straightforward procedures, including the use of technology and innovative solutions.
* Proportionality: Ensuring that procurement requirements are appropriate to the needs of the government entity and the nature of the project.
* Accountability: Holding responsible public officials and personnel accountable for their actions when necessary.
* Public monitoring: Allowing public oversight of procurement processes and contract implementation.
* Sustainability: Considering the life cycle of property and the environmental and social effects of procurement.
* Professionalism: Supporting qualification standards, competency development, and ethical conduct among procurement personnel.

=== Procurement procedures ===
The law establishes a framework for government procurement that covers planning through contract implementation. Its implementing rules and regulations provide guidance for government entities in carrying out procurement activities and selecting appropriate procedures for their needs.

The law also provides for the development and use of standard procurement forms. These measures are intended to support consistent procedures and the implementation of procurement requirements across covered government entities. [ref: Important Update: Effectivity and Transitory Periods under RA 12009, Government Procurement Policy Board]

=== Transparency and public monitoring ===
Transparency and public monitoring are among the central principles of the New Government Procurement Act. The law supports open contracting practices that make procurement information accessible and facilitate information sharing at different stages of procurement.

The Library of Congress reported that the law includes measures related to open contracting standards and public monitoring, including the participation of observers and civil society organizations in procurement oversight.
[truncated]

----

== Relume ==
Relume is a private company whose primary product is a Saas tool. It was founded in 2020 by Dan Anisse and Adam Mura in Sydney, who first ran a website design agency before turning to software [ref: Relume: The Aussie website creator powering Trump's meme coin, Forbes Australia]. Relume offers a suite of tools based on AI to improve website building workflows with planning, designing and building tools for marketing websites [ref: Meet Relume, the bootstrapped AI web builder that wants to supercharge Figma and Webflow, TechCrunch]. They have 5 core products, Relume Publish, Relume Component Library, Relume MCP, Relume Export and Relume Style Guide Builder.

Relume's first product, the Relume Library, was a collection of 1000+ website components for both Webflow and Figma, launched in November 2021. In August 2023 it added an AI site builder that could generate sitemaps and wireframes from a text prompt, then export to Webflow, Figma and later, React, called Relume Export [ref: What's New — Relume AI Website Builder Updates, www.relume.ai]. In August 2026 it launched Relume Publish, a website builder with hosting, moving beyond exporting to publish sites itself.

Relume has grown without venture capital. It reportedly turned down a US$35 million acquisition offer in 2024 [ref: #2: Dan Anisse - Going global from day one, building a brand synonymous with design, supercharging growth with their home run AI product & turning down $35m to stay the course by Remarkable By Design, Spotify for Creators].

== History ==

=== Relume Component Library ===
Before Relume, Dan had founded several businesses, including Foenix and Lumio. Lumio was later acquired for an unknown amount.Dan & Adam started a Webflow design agency in August 2020 [ref: Productising Agency Insights — Dan (Relume) · UntilNow, www.untilnow.com.au]. To speed up repetitive wire framing work, they built an internal tool to which now represents the Relume Component Library, which became their first product. Founding engineer Daniel Slater later joined as a third co-founder and CTO, and the agency was phased out once the Relume Component Library covered costs [ref: Relume — AI Website Builder for Marketing Websites, www.relume.ai]. Early staff included people that worked at Canva, Antler and [https://mitti.com/ Mitti].

The Relume Component Library launched in November 2021 as a library of copy-and-paste components for Webflow. In December 2021 the components adopted a fluid responsive method built with [https://finsweet.com/ Finsweet], and were later made compatible with Finsweet;s Client-First class naming system. A free Figma kit followed on in February 2022, along with a community website and voting board for requesting components. From April 2022 the company released new components on the first Monday of every month aptly named "Component Day" by Relume and their customer base known as "Lumers". A Chrome extension and a class-syncing tool for Webflow entered beta in November 2022.

=== Relume Export ===
Relume added an AI sitemap generator in June 2023 and launched the full AI Site Builder using its Webflow compatible component system in August 2023. According to TechCrunch, about 10,000 people signed up in the two weeks after launch, bringing Relume's total user base to around 54,000. The company had 7 staff at the time. Webflow CEO Vlad Magdalin public praised the AI feature set.

In 2024 Relume released a React component library, which then left beta in December 2024. By 2024, the Relume team had grown to 11 people. Dan said in interviews that he turned down a US$35 million acquisition offer in 2024.

In January 2025 Forbes Australia reported that the website for the Official Trump meme coin had been build with Relume and hosted on Webflow. The same article reported more that 500,000 sign ups and a 12,000 member slack community. During 2025, Relume added React and HTML export, an AI Style Guide Builder and compatibility with Figma Sites.

=== Relume Publish ===
In May 2026 it added export of design systems to Anthropic's Claude Design and in July it released an MCP server that made it's component library available to AI agents and coding tools.

In August 2026, Relume launched Relume Publish into Beta, a website builder that hosts sites directly instead of relying on export to third party tools and providers. It added a Publish MCP server shortly after for building sites from Claude or ChatGPT on the 14th October 2026 and a content management system (CMS) later in the same month.

== Business Model ==
Relume sells subscriptions on a freemium model aimed at freelance designers, web design agencies and marketing teams. Pricing started at US$32 a month in 2023. As of 2026, building a site is free, paid plans can add more AI usage, and hosting on a custom domain is charged per site.

The company has not raised outside capital. It is bootstrapped and funded early development from agency revenue and according to Dan, was profitable by September 2024 [ref: Building a Profitable AI-Driven Design Platform Without VC Funding, Day One]. Dan said about 80% of new users arrive through organic channels rather than paid marketing.
[truncated]

Draft text:
Sanjeev Jaiswal is an Indian Administrative Service (IAS) officer of the Maharashtra cadre. He has served in various administrative positions in the Government of Maharashtra, including as Municipal Commissioner of Thane and Nagpur, Additional Municipal Commissioner of the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, and Vice President and Chief Executive Officer of the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA).

== Early life and education ==
Mr. Sanjeev Jaiswal was born in Kolkata. His early education completed at St. Paul’s Boarding School. Then he pursued higher secondary and graduation in Political Science (Honors) from St. Xavier’s College, Kolkata. After college he enrolled in postgraduate studies in Political Science and International Relations at the University of Calcutta before leaving to prepare for the Civil Services Examination.

== Early administrative career ==
Sanjeev Jaiswal is a 1996 batch IAS officer of the Maharashtra cadre. He has held several administrative positions, including;

* CEO, Nashik Zilla Parishad - 2000 to 2002
* District Collector, Chandrapur, Aurangabad, Nashik - 2004 to 2010
* Municipal Commissioner, Nagpur - 2010 to 2012
* Divisional Commissioner, Aurangabad - 2012 to 2015
* Municipal Commissioner, Thane - 2015 to 2020
* Additional Commissioner, BMC - 2020 to 2021
* Principal Secretary, Water Supply - 2021 to 2023
* Vice President & CEO, MHADA - 2023 to Present Date

== Tenure at MHADA ==
Jaiswal assumed office as the Vice President and Chief Executive Officer of the Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA) in June 2023. [ref: ]

During his tenure, MHADA has undertaken several housing, redevelopment and administrative initiatives across Maharashtra.

=== Cluster redevelopment ===
MHADA announced plans to redevelop approximately 923 acres of MHADA layouts across Mumbai. According to the authority, the project is expected to rehabilitate more than 75,000 residents through phased redevelopment projects over the coming years. [ref: 923 acres of MHADA layouts will be redeveloped across Mumbai, The Times of India]

=== Motilal Nagar redevelopment ===
In 2026, MHADA presented the master plan for the redevelopment of Motilal Nagar in Goregaon, one of the authority's largest redevelopment projects. The project covers approximately 143 acres and is planned under a Construction and Development Agency (C&DA) model, with MHADA acting as the Special Planning Authority. [ref: Motilal Nagar redevelopment master plan unveiled, Hindustan Times] [ref: Motilal Nagar Redevelopment Master Plan, MHADA]

=== Affordable housing projects ===
MHADA continued the implementation of housing lotteries under Jaiswal's tenure, including the Konkan Board Lottery and other regional housing schemes intended to increase the supply of affordable housing in Maharashtra. [ref: MHADA Lottery attracts strong response, Economic Times]

=== Digital governance ===
MHADA introduced digital governance measures aimed at improving service delivery, project monitoring and citizen access to housing-related services. These initiatives included expansion of online services and digitization of administrative processes. [ref: MHADA's Digital Transformation in Public Housing]

=== Housing policy ===
In interviews, [https://realty.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/sanjeev+jaiswal Sanjeev Jaiswal] stated that MHADA intends to expand affordable housing through large-scale redevelopment, rental housing initiatives and public-private partnerships to increase housing supply in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region. [ref: Exclusive Interview with Sanjeev Jaiswal, NDTV]

Jobstore (also known as Jobstore.com) is a global online job search platform headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia. Jobstore provides international talent acquisition, job aggregation, and automated job syndication services for employers and job seekers across Asia-Pacific and international markets.

== History ==
Jobstore was founded in 2015 by entrepreneur Anson Wang, who previously founded regional internet ventures including Recruitmap in 2006 and Joukuu in 2010. [ref: Going Global: Jobstore.com, BFM 89.9 - The Business Station]

During its initial growth phase, Jobstore was structured to provide job distribution services, syndicating employment listings across multiple recruitment sites and social networks to help employers manage cross-border hiring. [ref: SEA tech startups cannot simply copy Chinese models, TechNode Global (TNGlobal)]

But today Jobstore has transferred into a global job search platform servicing in 50+ countries. Jobstore aggregates job listings from thousands of websites, including job sites, staffing firms, associations, and company career pages. [ref: Worldwide Countries, Jobstore]

Jobstore received institutional early-stage investment and venture backing from Cradle Fund, a tech co-investment agency under the Ministry of Finance (Malaysia). [ref: Cradle Fund Portfolio Companies, Cradle Fund Sdn Bhd]

The company's employment metrics and regional labor market research have been cited by regional business publications and economic agencies, such as the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation (MDEC), to evaluate digital workforce trends and talent demand across Southeast Asia.

In 2018, Jobstore Group initiated preparation for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) to finance international market expansion, lodging a public prospectus before deciding to withdraw the application in 2019 to focus on regional organic growth. [ref: Jobstore Group Limited Prospectus, Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC)]

MoveInSync Technology Solutions Private Limited, commonly known as MoveInSync, is an Indian enterprise software company headquartered in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Founded in 2009, the company develops employee commute software used by organizations to schedule, track, and manage the daily commuting of their staff. It also offers a workplace-management product, WorkInSync, used to manage office space including desk booking, meeting-room booking, parking, visitor management, and cafeteria operations.

== History ==

=== Founding and early pivot (2009–2015) ===
MoveInSync was founded in 2009 in Bengaluru by three graduates of the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi: Deepesh Agarwal, Akash Maheshwari, and Anuvrata Arora. It was initially launched as a consumer carpooling service called RideInSync before shifting to a business-to-business model. Google was an early client; the company has also named Amazon, Oracle, Infosys, HCL, and Tech Mahindra among its customers.

In August 2014, the company raised $2 million in Series A funding led by Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, and Qualcomm Ventures.

=== Series B and expansion (2018) ===
In April 2018, MoveInSync raised $8 million in Series B funding led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, and Qualcomm Ventures.

=== Workplace-management line (WorkInSync) ===
MoveInSync launched its workplace-management product, WorkInSync, in 2020. According to the company, it introduced the product to help organizations manage office space as hybrid and distributed work expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic.

=== Series C funding (2024) ===
In January 2024, the company raised $15 million in Series C funding led by Bessemer Venture Partners, with participation from Saama Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Athera Venture Partners, and Nexus Venture Partners. The company said the funds would go toward expanding its managed-fleet product, MoveInSync ONE, and into international markets including the Philippines, South Africa, and the Middle East.

=== Acquisition of eFmFm (2025) ===
In May 2025, MoveInSync acquired eFmFm, an enterprise transport technology company founded in 2012 by Satish Goel. The company stated the acquisition would support further development in the employee commute space.

== Products and services ==
MoveInSync offers its software as a service under the name MoveInSync Ion, covering both employee commute management and, through WorkInSync, workplace management. The commute-management software supports home-to-office cabs, shuttles, corporate car rental, carpooling, and inter-office shuttle routes, while the workplace-management software covers desk booking, meeting-room booking, parking, visitor management, and cafeteria management.

The company also offers MoveInSync ONE, a managed-fleet service that combines the software platform with a vehicle fleet and transport operations run by the company.

== Operations ==
MoveInSync is privately held. Reported figures for its client count, Fortune 500 clients, and country footprint have varied by source and date; company and press materials between 2018 and 2025 have cited enterprise client counts ranging from around 50 to more than 400.

Total disclosed venture funding across the Series A (2014), Series B (2018), and Series C (2024) rounds has been reported at approximately $25 million to $32 million, with investors including Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, Qualcomm Ventures, Nexus Venture Partners, Athera Venture Partners, and Bessemer Venture Partners.

== Mobility Symposium ==
Since 2024, MoveInSync has organized an annual event in Bengaluru called the Mobility Symposium. The company has said the first edition produced a set of policy recommendations that were submitted to the Government of Karnataka. The 2025 edition, held on 10 October, was addressed by Priyank Kharge, Karnataka's Minister for Information Technology and Biotechnology; Member of Parliament Tejasvi Surya; and Maheshwar Rao, Chief Commissioner of the Greater Bengaluru Authority. The third edition was held on 8 October 2026 under the theme "Resilient Mobility".

== Recognition ==
In 2026, MoveInSync was ranked third on the India's Fastest-Growing Companies list published by TIME in partnership with Statista, a ranking based on companies' revenue growth between the 2022 and 2025 fiscal years.

== References ==

== History ==
=== Founding and early pivot (2009–2015) ===
MoveInSync was founded in 2009 in Bengaluru by Deepesh Agarwal, Akash Maheshwari, and Anuvrata Arora, graduates of the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU) Varanasi. It initially launched a consumer carpooling service under the name RideInSync. According to a 2015 account in Business Today, the founders shifted to a business-to-business model after a conversation with a Google India employee about the difficulty of coordinating transport for the company's Hyderabad staff, which they concluded pointed to a wider market among corporate employers.

In August 2014, the company raised $2 million in Series A funding from Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, and Qualcomm Ventures.

=== Series B and expansion (2018) ===
In April 2018, MoveInSync raised $8 million in Series B funding led by Nexus Venture Partners, with participation from Inventus Capital Partners, Saama Capital, and Qualcomm Ventures. At the time, the company said its clients included Google, Facebook, Amazon, and Microsoft.

Sid Yiddish is the stage name of Charles Bernstein (born c. 1962), an American performance artist, avant-garde vocalist, actor, poet, and writer based in Evanston, Illinois. He is known for his distinctive throat singing, experimental and improvisational music with the ensemble Sid Yiddish & His Candy Store Henchmen, absurdist humor, and supporting roles in television and film. His multidisciplinary work combines sound, philosophy, humor, and composition, frequently incorporating unconventional instruments such as the shofar and systems of physical gesture-based conduction.Jumpin’ with Sid, Chicago TribuneSid Yiddish CV, SidYiddish.com
== Early life and education ==
Charles Bernstein was raised in the Evanston/Skokie area of Illinois and attended Niles West High School in Skokie. He has described himself as an “international industrial poet actor throat-singing tap-dancing spy.” He is the brother of writer and teacher Arnie Bernstein. As a child, he attended his first Major League Baseball game in 1969 (Cubs vs. Mets at Wrigley Field) and later contributed baseball-related writing to Bardball.com.He began writing poetry in grade school and by 1979, while still a student at Niles West, was calling himself a poet. From 1986 to 1991 he published the poetry fanzine Cops Hate Poetry, which included his own poems, record reviews, and interviews with figures such as Carl Perkins, the Circle Jerks, and Allen Ginsberg.Potty Poet, Chicago ReaderBernstein earned a Bachelor of Arts in Print Journalism from Columbia College Chicago in 1990 and a Master of Arts in Interdisciplinary Arts and Media from the same institution in 2016. Additional training includes jazz vocals, piano instruction, tap dance, and throat singing at the Old Town School of Folk Music in Chicago (approximately 2001–2006); a playwright workshop at Infinite Theater (2019); and stand-up comedy, improvisational sketch comedy, and laughing yoga at Gilda’s Club Chicago (2019–2020).He adopted the stage name Sid Yiddish publicly around June 4, 2004 (the day Ronald Reagan died), during a poetry reading. “Sid” is his middle name; “Yiddish” refers to his Jewish background. He has described the persona as bridging gaps in performance art involving instruments, music, and ideas that others might avoid.Sid Yiddish Interview, Art InterviewsAnswers: Toilet talk, The Daily NorthwesternMedia Student Sid Yiddish Interviewed for Performance in Kansas, Columbia College Chicago Art and Art History News
== Career ==
=== Acting, television, and film ===
Yiddish has appeared in a range of television, film, commercial, and music-video projects, often in distinctive or character roles. Notable credits include:
Shameless (Showtime): Chasidic Rabbi (Season 6, Episode 1) and Homeless Man (Season 7, Episode 5).
America’s Got Talent (NBC): reality-show contestant (Seasons 6 in 2011 and 8 in 2013).
Empire (Fox): Café Patron, Businessman, Hospital Pedestrian, and other roles.
Chicago PD and Chicago Fire (NBC): homeless or drunken characters.
Philip K. Dick’s Electric Dreams (Amazon): Jewish Alien Father.
Patriot (Amazon): International Traveler.
Feature and short films including Death Wish (2018, Businessman), the documentary Sid Yiddish (2014, directed by Ryan Buckley, in which he appears as himself), and the Ludacris music video “Jingalin’” (Chasidic Rabbi).
Commercials (including Exxon-Mobil and Burt’s Bees) and other projects such as DOCTA films and The Life of Jimmy Bracken.
The 2014 documentary Sid Yiddish, directed by Ryan Buckley (with cinematography by Zach Mehrbach), followed him in Evanston, Chicago, and New York. It received its world premiere in Aarhus, Denmark, and an American debut in Portland, Oregon.Sid Yiddish’s Unstoppable Summer, Columbia College Chicago Art and Art History NewsSid Yiddish: a star is born, WGN RadioHe has also performed in theatrical and site-specific works, including as understudy Rabbi in a production of Fiddler on the Roof, The Great Fire: A Traveling Truck Show, solo pieces at the Rhinoceros Fest (Prop Theater), and events at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago.
=== Music and performance art ===
Yiddish is known as a performance artist and conductor of the improvisational collective Sid Yiddish & His Candy Store Henchmen (founded on or around December 10, 2010). The group operates as a collective using “The Henchmen Method,” a system of physical gestures (reportedly 75–100 or more) that he developed over several years and has taught in locations including Mexico and Denmark. Instrumentation has included guitars, violin, piano, electronics, shofar, slide whistles, cigar-box guitar, animal horns, double-belled trumpets, and found objects. The sound is often described as experimental, blending atonal improvisation, harmonic elements, absurdist humor, theater, comedy, and performance art.Sid Yiddish And His Candy Store Henchmen, Reggies LiveSid Yiddish And His Candy Store Henchmen, SpotifyHe developed throat singing around 2004 while studying voice and piano at the Old Town School of Folk Music and has incorporated it into solo performances, television appearances (including America’s Got Talent), radio, and collaborations. Notable collaborations include work with the Danish punk band Clean Boys (including the album Safari Freakshow Adventure and tours) and the Chicago jazz fusion group Marbin. He has performed at the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago, as a regular participant in Make Music Chicago, on college radio

Arango is a software company based in San Francisco, California, and Cologne, Germany. [ref: Arango Invites AI Leaders and Builders to Explore the Contextual Data Layer Powering Production AI Agents at NVIDIA GTC 2026, Business Wire] The company develops ArangoDB, a multimodel database management system, and the Arango Contextual Data Platform, a software platform for enterprise artificial intelligence applications.

ArangoDB supports graph, document, and key-value data models within a single database engine and uses the ArangoDB Query Language (AQL). The database also supports full-text and vector search.

In October 2025, Arango introduced a preview of the Arango AI Data Platform. The platform was subsequently renamed the Arango Contextual Data Platform, with version 4.0 announced in March 2026 and made generally available in April 2026.

== History ==

=== Origins and founding ===
Development of ArangoDB began in October 2011, when the first code was committed to the project, originally known as AvocadoDB. [ref: Evolving ArangoDB's Licensing Model for a Sustainable Future, Arango] The project was renamed ArangoDB in May 2012. [ref: "AvocadoDB" becomes "ArangoDB", Another Word For It]

The company was founded by Claudius Weinberger and Frank Celler and subsequently developed the database as a commercial product. [ref: Open source database ArangoDB raises €2.2 million in fresh funding, Tech.eu]

=== Funding and growth ===
In 2017, ArangoDB completed a €4.2 million funding round led by Target Partners. The total included an initial €2.2 million investment made in November 2016 and an additional €2 million invested in 2017. [ref: German database startup ArangoDB closes funding round at €4.2 million, Tech.eu] [ref: Target Partners leads €4.2m round for ArangoDB, Unquote] [ref: Osborne Clarke berät ArangoDB bei Investment durch Target Partners, Osborne Clarke]

In March 2019, the company raised $10 million in Series A funding led by Bow Capital. [ref: ArangoDB raises $10 million for NoSQL database management, VentureBeat] In October 2021, it announced a $27.8 million Series B funding round led by Iris Capital. The company had previously raised approximately $19.2 million. [ref: Open source graph database company ArangoDB raises $27.8M, VentureBeat] [ref: ArangoDB brings yet more money into graph database market with $27.8M round, SiliconANGLE]

In 2025, ORIX USA's Growth Capital business made a strategic investment in ArangoDB. [ref: ArangoDB Secures Strategic Investment from ORIX USA to Power the Future of AI-Native Data Infrastructure, ORIX USA]

=== Licensing changes ===
In October 2023, ArangoDB announced changes to its software licensing model. Beginning with version 3.12, the database's source code moved from the Apache License 2.0 to the Business Source License 1.1. [ref: Incompatible changes in ArangoDB 3.12, Arango Documentation]

The company also introduced a Community License for precompiled binaries, permitting internal business use while restricting commercial use and limiting production deployments to 100 GiB of data. [ref: ArangoDB Editions and Licensing, Arango Documentation]

Under the Business Source License, covered source-code versions transition to the Apache License 2.0 four years after their initial public distribution.

=== Expansion into AI platforms ===
In October 2025, Arango announced a preview of the Arango AI Data Platform at NVIDIA GTC Washington, D.C. The platform extended ArangoDB with capabilities for graph-based retrieval and applications using large language models. [ref: Arango Launches AI Data Platform at NVIDIA GTC Introducing Contextual AI: Enterprise AI Powered by Business Context, Business Wire]

In March 2026, the company announced version 4.0 of the platform, renamed the Arango Contextual Data Platform, at NVIDIA GTC. The release included a Contextual Data Layer architecture and an Agentic AI Suite with services including AutoGraph, AutoRAG, and Arango Ada. [ref: Arango Launches Contextual Data Platform 4.0 for AI-Agent-Ready Enterprise Data, Business Wire] [ref: What NVIDIA GTC Made Clear: The Future of AI Is Context-Driven, And It Requires More Than a Single-Model Database, Arango] Version 4.0 became generally available in April 2026. [ref: What's new in the data platform, Arango Documentation]

In August 2026, version 4.1.0 introduced AutoGraph Studio, combining the AutoGraph and GraphRAG interfaces into a single interface for constructing and querying knowledge graphs.

In July 2026, Arango was named a Strong Performer in The Forrester Wave: Multimodel Data Platforms, Q2 2026. [ref: Arango Recognized as a Strong Performer in Multimodel Data Platforms, Q2 2026 Evaluation, Business Wire]

== Products ==

=== ArangoDB ===
ArangoDB is a multimodel database management system supporting graph, document, and key-value data within a single database engine. [ref: Feature list of the ArangoDB core database system, Arango Documentation]

The database uses the ArangoDB Query Language (AQL) for data retrieval, filtering, aggregation, and graph traversal. It also supports full-text search through ArangoSearch and vector similarity search. [ref: Information Retrieval with ArangoSearch, Arango Documentation] [ref: Vector indexes, Arango Documentation]

Raviinder Bhinder released music professionaly from 2016. His early releases included "Balle Balle" "Grarri," and "Nakhre." He later released song such as "Yaaran di Yaari,"Bachelors Life," "Kitte Miliye," "Laung Te Laachi," "DJ Waleya," and "Koka."

His music draws on Punjabi folk, bhangra, punjabi pop, and Hindi songs and his songs explore themes including friendship, relationships, celebration, and everyday life.

=== Film Music ===
In 2018, Bhinder contributed to the song "Ho Jaye Balle Balle," Featured in the hindi film Preshan Parinda - EK Bechara. The song was credited to Ravinder Bhinder and Sher Azad and relesed through T-Series.

=== Live Performance ===
Ravinder Bhinder has performed at cultural programmes, music events, bhangra shows, and Bollywood-related events. His performance have included appearances in India and Southest Asian locations, including Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand. He has also been featured in a special international talent episode of television music programme Rising star.

=== Theatre and Acting ===
Alongside music, Ravinder Bhinder has participated in theatre and film projects. He appeared in the theatre production Online Shopping, presented at Dastak - A Festival of Hindi Theatre in Singapore. He also played a supporting role in Lizard on the Wall (2017), a film by Singapore-based filmmaker K. Rajgopal.

Bryan Sperry is a visual artist based in Chicago, Illinois, known for his commissioned artwork and participation in the Chicago Art District. Sperry was the original founder and main force behind Pilsen Art Nation, which originated the [http://chicagoartsdistrict.org/secondfridays_main.asp 2nd Friday Art Walk] in the Chicago Pilsen neighborhood. [ref: Chicago Art District, chicagoartsdistrict.org] [ref: In Chicago, the Pilsen neighborhood reflects Mexican flavors, Washington Post] [ref: In Chicago, colorful Pilsen broadens its palate, Chicago Tribune] His works have been featured in various exhibitions, such as the "Warriors of the Apocalypse" series. [ref: Warriors of The Apocalypse Series By Brian Sperry, The Worley Gig] [ref: Warriors of the Apocalypse - The Visualist, The Visualist - Chicago Visual Arts Calendar] [ref: ]

== Education ==
Bryan Sperry attended the School of the Art Institute of Chicago.

== Notable Works ==
The Warriors of the Apocalypse: This sculptural series is a standout in Sperry's body of work, featuring life-size cyborg figures made from recycled elements of the urban landscape. Set in a post-apocalyptic world of the year 3095, these sculptures represent hybrid super soldiers fighting against tyranny and oppression. The series serves as an awareness campaign, illustrating the control exerted by media, propaganda, and government.

== Exhibitions ==
House of the Apocalypse: Sperry's Pilsen gallery, located at 1908 S. Halsted Street, Chicago, is a significant venue where his work, including "The Warriors of the Apocalypse," is displayed.

Sensible Decisions: This exhibition featured works by Bryan Sperry among other artists and was presented as an interwoven installation. It showcased Sperry's ability to blend strong lines and industrial elements with whimsical expressions, highlighting themes of alienation and the contemporary quest for truth and beauty. [ref: Sensible Decisions - The Visualist, The Visualist - Chicago Visual Arts Calendar]

IMPACTinterview: This exhibition featured works by Bryan Sperry alongside other artists and was also presented as an interwoven installation. The collaborative nature of this show allowed for a diverse exploration of contemporary issues through visual art. [ref: IMPACTinterview — lithium.gallery, lithium.gallery]

Other known exhibitions:
* Design Cloud – 2012 [ref: Chicago Art District, chicagoartsdistrict.org]
* Carlos Humenez Gallery – 2012
* Flexspace – 2010
* MK Gallery – 2009
* Zhou B. Space – 2009
* Blake Palmer Gallery – 2006
* Corrosive Gallery – 2005
* Open Door Gallery – 2004
* Mars Gallery – 2003
* Humility Gallery – 1998
* Eastwick Gallery – 1995
* Randolph Street Gallery – 1995
* Around The Coyote – 1993–1997
* Art Attack – 1993

== Installations ==
* Field Museum Campus – 2009
* "Cool Globes" Sculpture Tour – 2009

== Style ==
Expressionistic Edginess: Sperry's art often features strong lines that evoke a sense of order, while also incorporating whimsical lines, facial expressions, or gestures for human emphasis. This juxtaposition creates an expressionistic edge that offers a contemporary slant on themes of truth and beauty. [ref: Listenbee, www.listenbee.com]

Industrial and Robotic Themes: His works, particularly in sculpture, are formulated with robotic and industrial elements, which dominate the senses and contribute to the overarching theme of alienation present throughout his art.

== Mediums ==
Figurative Paintings: Sperry's paintings utilize line, texture, form, and color, with a strong use of light and shadow. His methodical approach to line work results in dynamic, multi-dimensional images that have a sculptural impact.

Abstracts: In his abstract works, Sperry combines free-flowing color with gravity and slope, creating a balance between randomness and controlled illusion. This technique creates spatial contrast and evokes the sense of imagined objects within an infinite space.

Sculptures: Sperry is particularly noted for his found-object warrior sculptures, which are made from recycled elements from the urban landscape. These sculptures bring life to materials from urban decay and are characterized by their bold, dramatic presence, often with a tragic-comic or opposing force aspect.

The European Biotechnology Thematic Network Association (EBTNA) is an international association concerned with biotechnology education and cooperation between academic institutions and industry [ref: Biotechnology worldwide and the 'European Biotechnology Thematic Network' Association (EBTNA), Current Opinion in Biotechnology]. It was formally established in Perugia, Italy, in 2007 by Mariapia Viola-Magni, following an earlier biotechnology network [ref: ].

The 2016 congress took place in Riga, Latvia, where the association also held its general assembly and elected its governing board [ref: European Biotechnology Congress 2016 – Water Research laboratory]. In September 2025, EBTNA organised the congress in Tirana, Albania, with support from the Academy of Sciences of Albania [ref: European Biotechnology Congress 2025, which will take place from 11–13 September 2025 in Tirana, Albania., fshmn.uni-pr.edu]. Alam Nyo Na, also known as RJ Sabuero, is the public persona of Filipino trivia content creator Robin James A. Sabuero, a graduate of Bachelor of Arts in Mass Communication, major in Broadcasting, from Palawan State University in Puerto Princesa City, Philippines.

He is known for producing educational content about biodiversity, wildlife, environmental conservation, local history, geography, and lesser-known facts, particularly those related to Palawan and other parts of the Philippines.

Before establishing his identity as a trivia content creator, Sabuero worked as a broadcaster for Radyo Bandera Philippines, Radyo Mo Nationwide (RMN), and the Philippine Broadcasting Service–Bureau of Broadcast Services (PBS-BBS).

Through Alam Nyo Na, Sabuero aims to make knowledge more accessible to the general public. Recognizing that not everyone enjoys reading books or has the opportunity to visit libraries, he takes the initiative to read, research, and translate information from books, scientific studies, and other credible sources into engaging video content using language and storytelling that ordinary Filipinos can easily understand and enjoy. His goal is to bring the knowledge contained in books to audiences through videos, allowing them to discover and appreciate valuable information in a more accessible and entertaining format.

A particular focus of his work is giving greater visibility to scientific research on biodiversity. He believes that important studies conducted by researchers deserve opportunities to reach wider audiences beyond academic institutions and scientific publications. Through Alam Nyo Na, he seeks to bridge the gap between scientific research and public understanding by transforming complex findings into engaging educational stories without losing their essential meaning.

Sabuero has also collaborated with government agencies, other organizations, and fellow biodiversity content creators to develop and share educational content about biodiversity and environmental conservation.

Alam Nyo Na maintains an online presence on Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok, where it shares trivia, educational stories, and informative videos designed to spark curiosity and encourage appreciation of the Philippines' natural and cultural heritage.

Pei-Kun Xi (; October 24, 1948 – December 30, 2005) was a Chinese-American conductor, composer, and music educator. He was a prominent figure in the post-1970 classical, film, and operatic scenes in Shanghai—most notably serving as the music director and conductor of the Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra (上海乐团)—before immigrating to the United States in 1985. [ref: Table of Contents: Cover Photo Credits, Yinyue Aihaozhe (音乐爱好者 / Music Lover)] Following his relocation to the United States, his career expanded into guest conducting across major American symphonies. He specialized in arranging and performing works that seamlessly fused traditional Chinese instruments with a full Western classical orchestra, while fostering community arts development in the San Francisco Bay Area. He dedicated his life to orchestral leadership across both China and the United States spanning decades until he died in 2005. [ref: Him Mark Lai Research Files, Organizational Records: Box 9, Folder 8 (Xi, Peikun), East Asian Library, University of California, Berkeley] [ref: Pei-Kun Xi Obituary, Obituary Notice]

== Early life and education ==

Pei-Kun was born on October 24, 1948, in Shanghai, China. He began his early musical training on the flute, piano, violin, and other traditional Chinese instruments from 1956 to 1968. In 1969, he graduated from the Middle School affiliated with the Shanghai Conservatory of Music (上海音乐学院附中), where he majored in bassoon and flute. Between 1980 and 1982, he pursued private studies in orchestral conducting under the French conductor Jean Périsson and Chinese conductor Yi-Jun Hung in Shanghai.

In 1985, Pei-Kun immigrated to the United States to advance his academic and practical training on a full scholarship:
* 1985–1987: Studied conducting under Peter Black at the San Francisco Institute of Music and Arts.
* 1987–1989: Earned a Master of Arts in Music (Conducting) under Carl St. Clair at the New England Conservatory of Music.
* 1990: Selected as a Special Conducting Fellow at the Tanglewood Music Center by invitation of Seiji Ozawa, where he studied under Ozawa, Leonard Bernstein, and André Previn.
* 1990: Appointed as an Artist Diploma Candidate in Conducting at Boston University under David Hoose.

== Career ==
=== China Era (1969–1985) ===
Upon graduating from the Music Middle School Affiliated to Shanghai Conservatory of Music (上海音乐学院附中) in 1969, Pei-Kun joined the orchestra of the Shanghai Peking Opera Theatre（上海京剧团）for its production of the opera Taking Tiger Mountain by Strategy (智取威虎山), serving as its orchestra conductor for ten years. Throughout the 1970s, he served as a principal conductor for both the Shanghai and Peking Opera companies, conducting over 600 performances across six distinct Chinese operas.

From 1978 to 1985, Pei-Kun served as the music director and conductor of the Shanghai Philharmonic Orchestra (上海乐团), leading more than 40 concert programs per season. Concurrently, from 1981 to 1985, he served as the principal conductor for the Shanghai Youth Orchestra.

During this era, Pei-Kun was active in the Chinese film industry, working as the music director and conductor for three feature films and several television screen productions between 1971 and 1984. He recorded a catalogue of commercial albums, LPs, and cassettes, establishing a reputation as one of China's prominent young conductors of the period.

=== United States and guest conducting ===

After completing his graduate studies at Boston's New England Conservatory of Music, Pei-Kun relocated to San Francisco in 1992, frequently guest-conducting major symphonies, cultural and holiday concert programs across the United States. While a comprehensive catalog of his performances during this time period is not undocumented in public archives, his notable conducting engagements—many of which spotlighted traditional Chinese music alongside Western classical repertoire—included the following highlights:

* 1991: Led performances with the New England Symphony Orchestra and the Boston Civic Symphony Orchestra.
* 1992: Guest-conducted the Longwood Symphony Orchestra in Boston.
* 1993: Conducted the South Bay Chamber Orchestra Concert (南湾室内乐团音乐会) in California.
* 1994: Directed the *Summer Melody* (夏日旋律) concert program.
* 1994: Conducted the inaugural kickoff celebration of the Eastern Philharmonic Orchestra（东方爱乐乐团）in the San Francisco Bay Area.
* 1995: Appointed guest conductor for the *Silk Road Music Concert* (丝绸之路音乐会) composition and conducting program hosted at San Francisco State University during the regional Chinese Arts Festival (旧金山地区海华文艺季活动).
* 1995: Led the Boston University Symphony Orchestra.
* Other Engagements:** Served as a guest conductor for the Brooklyn Symphony Orchestra (New York), the Oakland Symphony (California), the Philadelphia Orchestra, the Evans Symphony, and the Los Angeles United Symphony Orchestra.

From 1995 to 1996, Pei-Kun returned to China by invitation to conduct a series of high-profile concerts, leading both the Shanghai Symphony Orchestra and the Shanghai Traditional Chinese Orchestra.

Tamami Honma is a Japanese-American concert pianist, chamber musician, educator and recording artist. In 2024, she became the first female pianist to record the complete cycle of 35 Beethoven piano sonatas, released as a 10-CD set by Divine Art Recordings. [ref: Tamami Honma plays Beethoven's Complete 35 Piano Sonatas, Pianist Magazine] She is an advocate for 20th and 21st-century repertoire, having premiered and recorded works by several British and Lithuanian composers. She serves on the music faculties at Stanford University and Santa Clara University. [ref: Tamami Honma, Stanford Department of Music] [ref: Tamami Honma Faculty Profile, Santa Clara University] [ref: ]

== Education and early history ==
Honma studied with Byron Janis, one of the few students of Vladimir Horowitz, at the Manhattan School of Music where she earned a bachelor's degree in piano performance. She subsequently studied with Christopher Elton at the Royal Academy of Music in London, earning a master's degree, and joined the academy's academic faculty; she was later awarded an honorary ARAM degree.

Early in her career, she won first prize at several national and international piano competitions, including the Yamaha Competition at the MTNA (Music Teachers National Association) in Little Rock, Arkansas, [ref: Logan Pianists Get 2 Top Music Contest Awards, Deseret News] the Stravinsky Awards International Piano Competition, [ref: Nine Young Utahns Picked to Solo on 30th Annual 'Salute to Youth', Deseret News] the Gina Bachauer International Young Artists Piano Competition (1990), [ref: Return recital part of circle of learning and sharing, Deseret News] and the Kingsville (Isabel Scionti) International Young Performers Competition (1991). [ref: Utah People in the Arts, Deseret News] [ref: Isabel Scionti Piano Solo First Place Winners, Kingsville Young Performers Competition] She has also appeared as a soloist at Bolshoi Hall in Moscow with the Moscow Radio Symphony Orchestra.

== Contemporary music advocacy ==
Honma maintained a long-standing collaboration with composer John McCabe. In 2001, she released Star Preludes (Metier), featuring her performance of McCabe's title work alongside violinist Peter Sheppard Skærved. [ref: Star Preludes, Divine Art Recordings] In 2002, she gave the world premiere of McCabe's solo piano study Scrunch at Weill Recital Hall in New York; Allan Kozinn of The New York Times wrote that she "negotiated the work's thickets easily and produced an eloquent, powerful performance". [ref: Works, John McCabe official website] [ref: Music Review; Capturing Eclectic Energy and South Asia's Melodies, The New York Times] On November 28, 2003, she premiered McCabe's "Snowfall in Winter" — like Scrunch, a study dedicated to her — at St John's Smith Square in London; reviewing the concert for The Independent, Robert Maycock wrote that she "played with both flair and immediate understanding". [ref: Operest, St John's, Smith Square, London, The Independent] That same year, she released a recording of McCabe's Piano Concerto No. 2 (Sinfonia Concertante) with the St. Christopher Chamber Orchestra (Dutton Digital). [ref: Composition Discography, John McCabe official website] This partnership culminated in the 2005 recording Two Pianos (Dutton Digital), on which she performed alongside the composer. [ref: Two Pianos: Stravinsky, McPhee, McCabe, Copland, Britten, Presto Music] She contributed the chapter "The Piano Music" to Landscapes of the Mind: The Music of John McCabe (2008), a collection of essays on the composer edited by George Odam. [ref: Landscapes of the Mind: The Music of John McCabe, Ashgate] In 2006, she performed piano duets by Alan Rawsthorne and Constant Lambert with McCabe on his recording of Rawsthorne's complete solo piano music (Dutton Digital), which received a Gold Star rating from Gramophone. [ref: 'Gramophone' Gold Star for Rawsthorne CD, John McCabe official website] Beyond McCabe's music, she has also premiered and recorded music by British composer Nigel Clarke on the album Premonitions (2002). [ref: Nigel Clarke: Premonitions, Divine Art Recordings]

Honma has also been a prominent advocate of Lithuanian music. On October 2, 2003, she made her Wigmore Hall solo recital début, in a program including the world premiere of Cascades-3 by Lithuanian composer Osvaldas Balakauskas; [ref: Tamami Honma's Wigmore Hall solo recital début, Music & Vision] her recording of the work appeared the following year on the compilation Zoom In 3: New Music from Lithuania. [ref: Zoom In 3: New Music from Lithuania, Music Information Centre Lithuania] At the St John's Smith Square concert that November, she also premiered an arrangement made for her by Lithuanian composer of his percussion work No moon, no flowers, no friend – and he drinks sake. By decree of President Valdas Adamkus of January 10, 2006, Honma was awarded the Medal of the Order of the Lithuanian Grand Duke Gediminas. [ref: Apdovanotų asmenų duomenų bazė: Tamami Honma, Office of the President of the Republic of Lithuania] [ref: Dėl Lietuvos Respublikos ir užsienio valstybių piliečių apdovanojimo Lietuvos valstybės ordinais ir medaliais Vasario 16-osios – Lietuvos valstybės atkūrimo dienos proga, President of the Republic of Lithuania]
[truncated]

Draft: Golden jackals in Italy

Draft text:
Golden jackals of the subspecies C. a. moreoticus have been present in Italy since the mid-1980s. They expanded into Italy from neighbouring Slovenia and established several isolated populations in the northeast, particularly in Friuli-Venezia Giulia and Veneto. This expansion accelerated throughout the 2010s and 2020s, with the species reaching as far west as Piedmont and as far south as Lazio.

Data on the diet of jackals in Italy indicate they are primarily scavengers that feed on animal remains discarded by humans. Parasitological examinations of jackal carcasses show that the species is host to over a dozen endoparasite species. They dominate red foxes, but are outcompeted and sometimes killed by wolves.

The Italian golden jackal population is fully protected and classed as least-concern, though because its range is still fragmentary, poaching and vehicular collision still pose a serious threat, with the potential of causing localised extinctions. Public perception of jackals in Italy is largely negative among hunters and urban citizens living in regions where jackals are present.

==Species overview==
The golden jackal is a medium-sized canid whose basic fur colour is golden, though seasonal variations occur, from pale creamy yellow to dark tawny. [ref: Canids: Foxes, Wolves, Jackals, and Dogs:Status Survey and Conservation Action Plan, IUCN, The World Conservation Union] It can be distinguished from the red fox by its slightly larger size, shorter tail and light-coloured ruff around the neck. The jackal also lacks the fox's white tail tip and the backs of its ears are the same colour as the rest of its body rather than black. In winter, when its fur is longer and gives the impression of larger size, the golden jackal can be mistaken for a wolf, but is distinguished by its more slender build, shorter tail, more pointed muzzle and its more fulvous colour. It is an opportunistic, omnivorous forager that can live in a variety of different habitats, from deserts to evergreen forests.

The golden jackal populations in Italy have been classed, together with all other populations in Europe, as belonging to the subspecies C. a. moreoticus, which was first described by French naturalist Isidore Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire during the Morea expedition. It is the largest subspecies, measuring in length and cm in height, with males weighing and females kg.

==Range and population==
The jackal is present in most of Northern Italy, both in alpine/prealpine regions and the Po Valley, where it ranges westwards from Friuli-Venezia Giulia to Piedmont and southwards from Trentino-Alto Adige/Südtirol to Ravenna in Emilia-Romagna. As of 2024, the jackal has been reported in ten regions of Italy: Friuli-Venezia Giulia, Veneto, Trentino-Alto Adige, Lombardy, Piedmont, the Aosta Valley, Emilia-Romagna, Tuscany, Marche and Lazio.

In 2021, it was estimated that 196-250 jackals, divided into 37-47 family groups, inhabited Italy based on bio-acoustic monitoring. The largest population, consisting of 2-5 packs, is found in Friuli-Venezia Giulia, in large part due to the low number of wolves there. As of 2024, the population of jackals in Friuli-Venezia Giulia has been calculated at 400. This region is considered the core area of the Italian jackal population, as it contains the largest number of reproducing individuals and provides a genetic link to neighbouring populations from the Balkans. Packs present in the karsts of Isonzo, Gorizia and Trieste near the Slovenian border seem to be the only self-sustaining populations in Italy.

==History==
===Background===
Several pre-Holocene fossil canids found in Italy and neighbouring countries initially attributed to the golden jackal were later found to have belonged to wolves, dogs or unrelated extinct canids. The species is therefore a relatively recent arrival to southeastern Europe, colonising the area during the Late Pleistocene from Anatolia via a land bridge on the Bosporus. Its expansion into the Balkan peninsula was however limited by climate, extensive woodland and the presence of wolves, thus limiting its range to the coastline, some islands, and steppe zones.

The species' eventual arrival in Italy coincided with its expansion throughout neighbouring Yugoslavia from the 1950s onwards, which had been facilitated by the elimination of government-sponsored bounties, an increase in pastoral activity in Slovenia, and a reduction in wolf populations. Jackals were already reported in the Slovenian village of Smast, a few kilometres from the Italian border, as early as 1953, and an increase in jackal populations on the Dalmatian and Montenegrin coasts resulted in the species colonising northwestern Istria during the early 1980s.

===Expansion===
Comparative studies undertaken in 2014 on the mtDNA control region and autosomal microsatellite loci of golden jackals in Italy and eastern Europe showed that the Italian populations descend from admixed Dalmatian and Slavonian jackals, thus conferring high genetic diversity.

Draft text:
Absolutarget is a Portuguese company specialising in the coordination of clothing, home textile and footwear development and production. Based in Vila do Conde, in northern Portugal, the business operates as a business-to-business (B2B) intermediary between fashion brands and Portuguese manufacturers. Its activities are organised under the Portugal Textile and Portugal Shoes brands. [ref: Prémios Exportação & Internacionalização: Os vencedores da edição de 2023, Jornal de Negócios]

According to Jornal de Negócios, the company recorded revenue of €17 million in 2022, with exports accounting for approximately 99% of its business. It received an honourable mention in the Services SME category at the 2023 Export and Internationalisation Awards. In February 2024, Exame named Absolutarget the sector winner for textiles, clothing and leather in its ranking of Portuguese small and medium-sized enterprises. [ref: Conheça as empresas distinguidas nas 1000 PME, Exame]

== History ==

The business traces its origins to 1999, when Paulo Silva established Portugal Shoes to coordinate footwear production in Portugal. In 2007, the operation expanded into clothing and textiles with the creation of Portugal Textile. The company Absolutarget was formally incorporated on 10 July 2008. [ref: Absolutarget, Lda, Racius] [ref: About Portugal Textile, Portugal Textile]

The company's project titled Internacionalização da Absolutarget e da sua marca (Internationalisation of Absolutarget and its brand) was listed among approved projects in the Norte 2020 regional programme, supported by the European Regional Development Fund. The published record lists an eligible investment of €355,650 and approved support of €160,042.50, under project reference NORTE-02-0752-FEDER-021758. [ref: Projetos Aprovados – Área Metropolitana do Porto, Norte 2020]

By 2022, Absolutarget had eight direct employees and reported annual revenue of €17 million, of which approximately 99% came from exports.

== Business operations ==

Absolutarget operates as a production coordination and sourcing business rather than as a single manufacturing facility. It provides collection-development and production-management services and works with Portuguese manufacturers on behalf of fashion brands. A 2022 academic study described the company as serving mainly European and North American brands and providing support with collection planning, factory liaison, production oversight and quality control. [ref: Compreender perfil do consumidor de moda têxtil sustentável, em Portugal: Estudo de caso do marketplace Sustainable Makers, Instituto Português de Administração de Marketing (IPAM Porto)]

The company operates through two brands:

* Portugal Textile – Established in 2007, it coordinates the development and manufacturing of clothing, fashion accessories and home textiles through Portuguese production partners.
* Portugal Shoes – Established in 1999, it specialises in footwear development, material sourcing and manufacturing coordination in Portugal. [ref: About Portugal Shoes, Portugal Shoes]

== Academic research and digital projects ==

Absolutarget developed the Sustainable Makers online marketplace, a business-to-consumer project focused on fashion products associated with environmental and social sustainability. The initiative was examined in a 2022 master's internship report completed at IPAM Porto. Research concerning the Sustainable Makers marketplace was subsequently published by Springer Nature in the proceedings of the ICMarkTech conference. [ref: Marketing and Smart Technologies, Springer Nature]

The company also participated in Plug-In, a business and student networking event organised by the Polytechnic Institute of Porto's School of Media Arts and Design (ESMAD). It was listed among the participating organisations in 2019 and 2021. [ref: 3.ª edição do Plug-IN, Escola Superior de Media Artes e Design] [ref: Plug-In, Escola Superior de Media Artes e Design]

== Awards and recognition ==

* 2023 – Honourable mention in the SME Services category at the Export and Internationalisation Awards, organised by Jornal de Negócios and Novo Banco.
* 2024 – Sector winner for textiles, clothing and leather in Exame magazine's annual Portuguese SME awards, held in association with Informa D&B and EY.

The Shirahama Maru is a Japanese roll-on/roll-off passenger car ferry operated by Tokyo-Wan Ferry Co., Ltd [ref: 東京湾フェリー／TOKYO WAN FERRY, www.tokyowanferry.com]. The vessel connects Kurihama Port in Yokosuka, Kanagawa Prefecture, to Kanaya Port in Futtsu, Chiba Prefecture. [ref: ]

== Construction ==
The vessel was constructed in Japan by Sumitomo Heavy Industries at its Uraga Shipyard under yard number 1164. Construction commenced with her keel being laid down in June 1989, and she was launched and completed later that same year in December 1989. [ref: ]

== Career ==
Since the ship entered service in December 1989, She has reliably sustained the vital maritime corridor between the Miura and Boso peninsulas alongside her sister ship, the Kanaya Maru.

Designed with a maximum passenger capacity of 680 people, her garage decks can simultaneously accommodate up to 110 standard passenger cars, or a mixed commercial load of 36 trucks and 16 buses. Over her decades of service, the Shirahama Maru has remained a highly popular option for leisure travelers targeting the Mount Nokogiri Ropeway. In recent years, she has frequently operated under a distinct "Black Ship" (Kurofune) commemorative livery, referencing the historic arrival of Commodore Perry's fleet in nearby Kurihama.
