Draft: Ruhr miner's strike (1889)

Draft text:
----

The Ruhr miner's strike of 1889 was one of the largest labor strikes in German history, and the largest at the time. [ref: Bismarck Urpreuße und Reichsgründer]. It took place in the highly industrial Ruhr area of the German Empire as a consequence of the 1873 Stock Market Crash, poor working conditions and the anti-socialist laws imposed by Chancellor Otto Von Bismarck [ref: Deutsche Gesellschaftsgeschichte, München: C.H. Beck]. It saw over 100.000 people participating in the strike and it was active during the months of April and May [ref: This Day in Labor History: May 14, 1889, Lawyers, Guns & Money] and it led to the creation of the Union of Miners of Germany (which would later be called the "Old Union" and is the modern day IG Bergbau, Chemie, Energie)

== Background ==
The strike originated as a result of the poor working and living conditions of working class families in this era. Most of them, like in many other industrialized regions of Europe, lived with their families in closed, cramped, and poorly maintained apartments with costly rent. Conditions in the mines as well were rather miserable, with barely any safety regulations in place and over 10 hour work shifts, alongside minimal pay.

Because of this, many workers in different areas of the empire started supporting workers movements, such as the Free Trade Unions or the SDAP (Sozialdemokratische Arbeiterpartei Deutschlands, which later turned into the modern-day SPD). However, with the "Bismarckian" anti-socialist laws passed by the Reichstag in 1878, many social democrat politicians and supporters were repressed or prosecuted.

Workers in the Ruhr organized a strike of about 21,000 miners in 1872. Although this was largely unsuccessful and it led to the workers subsequently organizing better, albeit initially without an official union or clear leadership.

Mining workers wanted wage increases like that of the mining entrepreneurs. The aim was a 15-20% wage increase, no more extra shifts, a reduction to 8 hours of working time, including entrances and exits, and, overall, better working conditions. [ref: Chronologie der deutschen Gewerkschaftsbewegung von 1794 bis 1918 / von Dieter Schuster. - Teil: Chronologie 1888-1889, library.fes.de]

== Strike ==

The strike began on the 25th of April in Bochum. At first, the strikers managed to get an 8.2% increase in pay and a short period of calm went onwards. However, the strikes quickly resumed on the 4th of May after police repression had started and about 80 union miners were fired from their positions and a full-on General Strike had begun, with numerous other workforces in Herne, Dortmund, Hörde, Witten, Oberhausen, Essen, and Recklinghausen deciding to join the strike. [ref: ]

As the strike continued, the two sides became increasingly aggressive. In order to “protect” their facilities and the miners that were willing to work, many mines requested police or even military protection, and the tense atmosphere of the strikes erupted into violence and the use of weapons against the miners, which, on May 12th, resulted in several workers being shot and a substantial increase in police brutality.

After the incident, on May 14, the strike committee decided to send a delegation to Kaiser Wilhelm II. The delegates (Friedrich Bunte, August Siegel and Ludwig Schröder) were received in Berlin by the emperor, whom they intended to appeal to as the supreme mining authority. [ref: Colorado Historic Newspaper Collection] Although the emperor criticized the strike, he did agree to have the grievances officially investigated. The talks with the emperor brought the strikers a great deal of attention, particularly among the middle classes of the empire, who tended to be skeptical on socialist ideas.

Through the mediation of Friedrich Hammacher, a member of the Reichstag, a protocol was finalized the following day, establishing an 8 hour workday for the miners, including a half-hour each for entering and exiting the mine. In addition, overtime shifts were to be worked on after prior agreement between the mine administration and the workers’ unions. When the association signaled a willingness to accommodate the miners’ interests, the strike initially subsided. However, they started once again on May 21st as the mining companies failed to comply with, and ignored, the agreements made in Berlin, and even introduced blacklists containing the names of many of striking miners in to make it impossible for them to find employment in the mining industry. In early June 1889, the strikes lost force and came to an end without any immediate lasting gains for the workers. [ref: Sozialpolitik—Description and Documentation: The Quest for Clarity, German History]
[[File:German soldiers coal strikers.png|thumb|Drawing of German mounted troops attacking strikers.]]
The strike triggered the founding of the Union of Miners of Germany in the Rhineland and Westphalia, [ref: Historisches Bochumer Ehrenfeld - Geschichte des alten Verbandes, www.historisches-ehrenfeld.de] the starting point for the breakthrough of the trade union movement in the Ruhr mining industry.
[truncated]

Kurunegala Main Sri Vishnu Maha Devalaya (Sinhala: කුරුණෑගල ප්‍රධාන ශ්‍රී විෂ්ණු මහා දේවාලය) is the principal Vishnu Devalaya in the Kurunegala District of Sri Lanka. The shrine is located within the premises of the historic Angangala Purana Rajamaha Viharaya.

== Location ==
The Devalaya is situated approximately 1.5 km from the Kurunegala clock tower along the Kurunegala–Puttalam main road, inside the Angangala temple grounds. The site lies on land that belongs to the Department of Archaeology, Sri Lanka.

== History ==
The shrine is traditionally regarded as the main Vishnu Devalaya of the Kurunegala District. It functions within the Angangala Purana Rajamaha Viharaya, which is an ancient royal temple.

== Rituals ==
Devotees gather for poojas every Saturday, except on full moon Poya days. Special Thevava rites are conducted for devotees seeking blessings and relief from difficulties. The annual Maha Pooja is held on December 31st.

Compass Group India is the Indian subsidiary of Compass Group plc, a British multinational contract foodservice and facilities management company. Headquartered in Gurugram, it provides catering and workplace management services to corporate offices, manufacturing facilities, healthcare institutions, and educational campuses in India. [ref: Compass Group India serves the right menu, Business India]

== History ==
Compass Group initially entered the Indian market in 1996 through a joint venture with Radhakrishna Hospitality Services. The joint venture dissolved in 2008, and Compass Group subsequently acquired local food and support services businesses to re-establish independent operations.

In September 2020, the company acquired a majority stake in SmartQ, an Indian food technology company focusing on digital cafeteria systems. [ref: Indian Foodtech Startup SmartQ Acquired By UK-Based Compass Group, Inc42]

In March 2022, the company launched Saarthi-FX, a digital workplace platform designed to manage asset compliance, facility maintenance, and workplace ticketing. [ref: Compass Group India Revolutionizes Workplace Management with AI-Powered Saarthi-FX, Xcan.it]

In August 2024, Compass Group India acquired a 70 percent stake in ICS Foods Private Limited, a Delhi-based catering company specializing in the manufacturing sector. [ref: Compass Group India acquires 70% stake in ICS Foods, Verdict Food Service]

Rahul Shinde was appointed Managing Director in June 2026. [ref: Compass India appoints Rahul Shinde as Managing Director, People Matters]

== Operations ==
Compass Group India operates across two primary segments: contract catering and facilities management. Its foodservice activities cover workplace dining, while facilities management involves the operation and maintenance of corporate and industrial sites.

As of early 2026, industry reports indicated the company operated across 1,100 to 1,200 sites in India, employing approximately 45,000 frontline staff. This included managing cafeterias for over 120 Global Capability Centres (GCCs). [ref: From cleaning robots to smart kitchens: How Compass Group India embeds AI across operations, TechCircle] The company also operates a healthcare division under the Medirest brand and manages retail micro-markets in cities such as Bengaluru and Hyderabad. [ref: Food services provider Compass India looks to tap into travel retail, Business Standard] [ref: Compass Group India addresses nutrition for patients and staff in hospitals through Medirest Platform, ETHealthWorld]

== Technology ==
The company utilises automated systems for facilities operations, energy monitoring, and food ordering. In 2026, Compass Group India integrated autonomous cleaning robots, camera-based workplace safety systems, and digital kiosks across its managed sites. [ref: From BPO to robo-BPO: Why robotics labs may need Indian homes, factories, Business Standard]

Draft text:
The 2039 FIFA Women's World Cup is scheduled to be the 13th edition of the FIFA Women's World Cup, the quadrennial international women's football championship contested by the national teams that represent the member associations of FIFA. The tournament has a potential bid to be hosted by Portugal, Spain, and Morocco. It is possible that this will be the third tournament to feature 48 national teams.

The tournament will be the first time Portugal, Spain and Morocco host the FIFA Women's World Cup if the bid is accepted. This will also be the fourth FIFA Women's World Cup in Europe after Sweden in 1995, Germany in 2011, France in 2019, and England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in 2035, as well as the first in Africa, and Portugal, Spain and Morocco will also become the ninth countries to host both the men's and women's World Cup, with all three having hosted in 2030.

== The Bids ==
The host nation for the 2039 Women's world cup is Expected to be officially decided around 2029-2031 in a FIFA Congress. There is also another bid to host the tournament. Japan want to host the tournament solo. Japan originally wanted to host the 2031 Women's World Cup, but FIFA's bidding restrictions prevented Asian countries from bidding for the 2031 and 2035 editions. Japan subsequently turned its attention to 2039.

== Format ==
It is possible that the 2039 FIFA Women's World Cup will be contested by 48 teams. If so, it will be the third tournament to do so. Starting in 2031, and also happening in 2035. Otherwise, it will have 64 teams, the first to do so.

== Venues ==
There are currently no venues announced for this tournament. Please update when venues are announced.

== Teams ==

=== Qualification ===
FIFA's confederations organise their own qualifying competitions, with the exception of CAF and CONCACAF which qualify teams through continental championships. The hosts Spain, Portugal, Morocco and Japan would receive automatic qualification for the tournament, leaving most of the remaining FIFA member associations eligible to enter qualification if they chose to do so. Portugal and Morocco could participate for the first time ever, but may still qualify for 2027, 2031 or 2035. FIFA is yet to announce the allocation of slots.

Draft text:
----

The Government Optimization Act, officially known as [https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2025/ra_12231_2025.html Republic Act No. 12231], is a Philippine law enacted on August 4, 2025, that establishes a framework for optimizing the organization and operations of the national government to improve public service delivery. The law aims to promote government efficiency, strengthen institutional capacity, minimize overlapping functions, simplify administrative processes, and protect the welfare of civil servants and other government workers. [ref: [https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2025/ra_12231_2025.html Republic Act No. 12231: An Act Optimizing the National Government for Efficient Public Service Delivery]. LawPhil Project, August 4, 2025.]

== Overview ==

The Government Optimization Act establishes the Government Optimization Program (GOP), which provides for the review of government agencies' mandates, functions, organizational structures, staffing patterns, systems, and processes. The program seeks to ensure that government institutions perform their essential functions and use public resources efficiently in delivering services.

Under the Act, government optimization includes reviewing agency responsibilities, identifying redundant or overlapping functions, simplifying procedures, modernizing systems, and determining the appropriate organizational structure and staffing requirements of government institutions. The law also recognizes digitization and electronic governance as means of improving public service delivery. [ref: [https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/99481 Republic Act No. 12231]. Supreme Court E-Library.]

== Provisions ==

=== Government Optimization Program ===

The Government Optimization Program is designed to improve the effectiveness, efficiency, economy, equity, and ethical accountability of government operations. It provides a framework for assessing the functions and structures of agencies and determining whether changes are necessary to improve institutional performance.

The program follows principles that include simplifying government operations, clearly defining the responsibilities of national and local governments, encouraging public-sector employee participation in matters affecting their rights, and improving systems for delivering public services.

=== Reorganization of government agencies ===

Section 6 of the Act grants the President authority to optimize the operations of executive branch agencies, subject to the requirements of the law. Organizational actions may include creating, reorganizing, merging, streamlining, abolishing, or deactivating agencies, offices, or units when determined to be in the best interest of the State through the prescribed process.

The Act also allows changes in agency functions, including transferring or integrating functions between agencies and discontinuing activities that can be better performed by other institutions or by the private sector, subject to the law's governing principles and conditions.

=== Committee on Optimizing the Executive Branch ===

The Act establishes the Committee on Optimizing the Executive Branch (COEB) to oversee and coordinate the Government Optimization Program. The committee is chaired by the Executive Secretary, with the Secretary of the Department of Budget and Management serving as co-chairperson. Other members are identified in the Act.

The committee's responsibilities include developing the program's policies and implementation framework, conducting studies on government agencies, preparing optimized organizational structures and proposed executive issuances, and monitoring the implementation of approved optimization plans. It is also responsible for developing change-management measures to support the transition and safeguard the welfare of affected employees. [ref: [https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/101010 Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 12231, Otherwise Known as the Government Optimization Act]. Supreme Court E-Library, January 23, 2026.]

=== Agency reviews and optimization plans ===

Section 10 of the Act requires covered agencies to conduct an organizational review and study of their mandates, objectives, functions, systems, procedures, programs, activities, projects, organizational structures, staffing patterns, and personnel requirements.

Based on this review, each agency must formulate an optimization plan consistent with the governing principles of the Act. The plan identifies areas requiring improvement and areas where resources may need to be redirected to strengthen institutional capacity. It may also address staffing requirements for qualified personnel, subject to the conditions and limitations established by the law.

The implementing rules and regulations provide additional procedures for strategic reviews, the preparation of optimization plans, consultations with affected personnel, and the development of optimized organizational structures.

=== Protection of government personnel ===

The Act includes provisions for government employees affected by organizational changes. It addresses personnel evaluation, staffing requirements, and measures for managing the transition from existing organizational structures to optimized structures.

Nagarajan Ramakrishnan is an Indian physician who works in critical care and sleep medicine in Chennai. He works at Apollo Hospitals and founded the Nithra Institute of Sleep Sciences, a sleep medicine centre established in 2004.

==Early life and education==
According to a biography submitted by his institute to World Sleep Day, Ramakrishnan graduated from Stanley Medical College in Madras. He then worked in the United Kingdom and the United States for more than 13 years before returning to India in 2003. The same biography states that he holds American Board certification in internal medicine, critical care medicine, sleep medicine and obesity medicine, and a master's degree in medical management from the University of Southern California. [ref: Delegate: Dr N. Ramakrishnan, World Sleep Day]

==Career==
Apollo Hospitals lists Ramakrishnan as a senior consultant in critical care and sleep medicine and director of critical care services, a post it dates from 2003. [ref: Dr N Ramakrishnan – Critical Care Specialist, Apollo Hospitals]

In 2004 he established the Nithra Institute of Sleep Sciences in Chennai, which now operates as Nithra Sleep and Health Care and describes itself as a multispecialty centre. [ref: About Us, Nithra Health] He is also the founder of the TACT Academy for Clinical Training, a simulation-based healthcare training centre in Chennai. [ref: 10th anniversary celebration 2024, Dr. Jeyasekharan Medical Trust]

Ramakrishnan has been quoted in the Deccan Chronicle on sleep apnoea and diabetes [ref: Obstructive sleep apnea can cause diabetes, Deccan Chronicle] and on disrupted sleep-wake cycles and mental health. [ref: Daily routine is key for mental wellness, says study, Deccan Chronicle]

==Professional societies==
According to the Nithra website, Ramakrishnan has held roles on the executive committees of the Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine and the Indian Sleep Disorders Association, and is a past president of the latter. [ref: About Dr. Nagarajan Ramakrishnan, Nithra] He was organizing chairperson of SLEEPCON 2025, the association's annual international conference. [ref: Apollo Consultants Honour list June 2025, Apollo Hospitals]

==Publications==
Ramakrishnan has published in the Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine. He was first author of the Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine's 2024 position statement on care after intensive care. [ref: Post-ICU Care: Why, What, When and How? ISCCM Position Statement, Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine] He is among the co-authors of a 2016 study of case mix and practice patterns in Indian intensive care units [ref: Intensive care in India: The Indian intensive care case mix and practice patterns study, Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine] and of the Indian Society of Critical Care Medicine's 2009 quality indicators for Indian intensive care units. [ref: Quality indicators for ICU: ISCCM guidelines for ICUs in India, Indian Journal of Critical Care Medicine]

Hakan Kousetta is a British television producer and media executive. He is the co-founder of 60 Forty Films, an independent television production company, and previously served as chief operating officer of the television division at See-Saw Films.

Kousetta has received three Primetime Emmy Award nominations, including a win for State of the Union and nominations for Slow Horses. [ref: ]

== Career ==
In 2008, Kousetta co-founded the specialist media law firm Aslan Charles Kousetta in London alongside Susan Aslan and Sue Charles. As a partner, he specialized in legal matters relating to film and television production and financing. [ref: New law firm Aslan Charles Kousetta launches in London, Screen]

In October 2014, Kousetta joined See-Saw Films as chief operating officer of its television division, overseeing the company's commercial and operational activities alongside television head Jamie Laurenson. [ref: Top of the Lake to return for second series, Screen]

During his tenure at See-Saw, Kousetta co-led the company's television operations and executive produced a number of television productions from its United Kingdom and Australian offices, including Top of the Lake: China Girl, The End, The New Legends of Monkey, State of the Union, The North Water, Slow Horses, The Essex Serpent, and Heartstopper. [ref: See-Saw Executives Jamie Laurenson, Hakan Kousetta Depart to Start 60Forty Films, Variety] [ref: Jamie Laurenson, Hakan Kousetta depart See-Saw to launch TV outfit 60Forty, Screen]

In 2020, Kousetta was appointed chair of the Producers Alliance for Cinema and Television (PACT), succeeding Sara Geater. Prior to his appointment, he had served on the PACT Council and co-chaired the organisation's Film Policy Group. [ref: U.K. Producers Org Pact Taps See-Saw Films Executive Hakan Kousetta as Chair, Variety] In 2021, he received a special innovation award from the Producers Guild of Great Britain for his work with the UK Government on the design and implementation of the COVID Film and Television Production Restart Scheme. [ref: BFI Adds Six Members To Board Of Governors, Deadline]

In February 2021, Kousetta, alongside Jamie Laurenson, departed See-Saw Films to establish the independent television production company 60 Forty Films. Although leaving See-Saw, the pair continued as executive producers on several ongoing productions, including Slow Horses, The Essex Serpent, The North Water, State of the Union, and Heartstopper.

In 2022, 60 Forty Films entered into an overall production agreement with Apple TV+. Among the company's first productions was the thriller series Hijack, starring Idris Elba, which Kousetta executive produced alongside Laurenson. [ref: Apple TV+ Inks Overall Deal With ‘Slow Horses’ Producers’ 60Forty Films (EXCLUSIVE), Variety] [ref: Hijack EP Hakan Kousetta On Working With Idris Elba & Chances Of A Season 2, ScreenRant]

In June 2026, Kousetta was appointed to the Board of Governors of the British Film Institute for a four-year term.

Karel Havlíček (born 31 July 1974), also known by the pseudonym Karzi, is a Czech composer, pianist and music producer whose work includes film and television scores, advertising music and solo instrumental compositions. [ref: Karel Havlíček, Filmový přehled] He was a member of the Czech indie rock band Southpaw before concentrating on screen composition. [ref: Hudební skladatel Karel Havlíček: Největší hvězdy mají největší pokoru, Novinky.cz] His screen credits include the films Ghoul, Němá tajemství and Bratři, as well as the television series Terapie, Mamon (TV series), Vzteklina and Profesor T. His score for Bratři was nominated for Best Music at the 2024 Czech Lion Awards. [ref: Bratři, Český lev]

== Biography ==
Havlíček was born in Prague in 1974 and has also worked under the name Karzi. In 1996, Havlíček co-founded the Prague indie rock band Southpaw with Jiří Burian. He worked as a keyboardist, composer, programmer and sound engineer. [ref: SOUTHPAW MAJÍ PLNÝ HEART DISK, iREPORT] The group released several albums during the 2000s, including Pop Secret, Pleasure You Can Measure, Boys Make Noise and Heart Disk.

Southpaw ended its original run in 2011. The group returned in 2021 with the album I'm Really Gonna Miss These Songs When I'm Dead, on which Havlíček and Burian collaborated again. [ref: Na desce je náš pohled na vztahy, duševní svobodu i smrt, říká kapela Southpaw, iDNES.cz]

After his work with Southpaw, Havlíček concentrated on composing and producing music for film and television. The National Film Archive records his work in several capacities, including composer, musician, producer and sound engineer. His film credits include the American documentary Lion Ark (2013), the horror film Ghoul (2015), Carpe Noctem (2022), Němá tajemství (2023) and Bratři (2023). [ref: Lion Ark – Full Cast & Crew, TV Guide] His television work includes the Czech adaptation of the Israeli drama series Terapie and the series Mamon, Vzteklina, Profesor T and Polda.

Havlíček composed the music for Czech Television's news programming, including the news channel ČT24 and the main news programme Události. Czech Television reported on the news themes and identified him as their composer. [ref: Znělky zpravodajství ČT se začaly používat před deseti lety. Složil je hudební skladatel Karel Havlíček, ČT24]

In 2023, Havlíček composed the scores for Němá tajemství and Bratři, both directed by Tomáš Mašín. [ref: Karel Havlíček, Czech Film Center] Bratři, a historical drama concerning the Mašín brothers, received several nominations at the 2024 Czech Lion Awards. Havlíček's score was nominated in the Best Music category.

In addition to film and television scores, Havlíček has worked on advertising music and trailer soundtracks. His work includes music for the Penny Market Christmas 2018 advertising campaign, which became a finalist in the Film Craft – Direction category at the 2019 New York Festivals Advertising Awards. [ref: Penny Market Christmas 2018, New York Festivals Advertising Awards]

In 2024, Havlíček composed music for the official trailer of the HBO series The Penguin. [ref: HBO Releases Official Trailer For The Penguin, Starring Colin Farrell, Debuting September 19, Warner Bros. Discovery Pressroom] In 2026, he also worked on trailer music for ELLE, a television series associated with the Legally Blonde franchise. [ref: Karel Havlíček — Czech Film & Television Composer, Karel Havlíček]

Havlíček released the solo album Spoken in 2020. The instrumental recording combines piano, orchestral textures and electronic elements. [ref: RECENZE: Album Spoken je luxusně zařízený byt, v němž nikdo nežije, iDNES.cz] In his review, music critic Jindřich Göth discussed the album's atmospheric arrangements and its relationship to the idea of a soundtrack for an imaginary film.

In October 2022, KlasikaPlus published a review of a concert based on Spoken. The review discussed the work's extended melodic lines, recurring musical patterns and dramatic development, as well as the integration of music with lighting and visual effects. [ref: Karel Havlíček v bazénu, KlasikaPlus]

In 2023, Havlíček presented Electric Universe, an audiovisual concert project combining orchestral and electronic music. Czech Radio covered the project and interviewed him about the eight-hour musical event. [ref: Propojím svět klasické a elektronické hudby, zve na osmihodinovou show skladatel Karel Havlíček, Rádio Praha]

On 11 June 2025, Havlíček appeared with composer Vadim Petrov in a programme of their compositions at Czech Radio's Studio S1 in Prague, presented in association with the Prague Philharmonia. [ref: Special concert: Between classical and electronic music — Vadim Petrov & Karel Havlíček, Prague Philharmonia] The concert was reviewed by OperaPlus, which discussed five of Havlíček's compositions and their combination of ambient, minimalist, melodic and electronic elements. [ref: Dva skladatelé, dvě cesty. Havlíček a Petrov na jednom pódiu, OperaPlus] KlasikaPlus also reviewed the concert in the context of contemporary music and its accessibility to audiences. [ref: Že je soudobá hudba přístupná, může překvapit, KlasikaPlus]

Ustad Mubarak Ali Khan (1940 – 23 October 2024), also known as Ustad Mubarak Ali Khan Bahawalpuri or by his childhood name Jind Badda, was an eminent Pakistani classical vocalist, master musicologist, and ancestral chief of the **Walyani tribe**. He represented the orthodox Gwalior Gharana tradition and was historically recognized as the last direct custodian of the ancestral Shahi Singers (royal court musicians) of the princely state of Bahawalpur Riyasat. Khan spent over five decades broadcasting classical art music across South Punjab and the Siraiki belt, maintaining a legendary reputation for his strict adherence to Hindustani classical ragas, his leadership of the Walyani clan, and his highly specialized renditions of spiritual Siraiki Kafi structures. [ref: A short brief on Ustad Mubarak Ali Khan by Radio Pakistan Multan, Radio Pakistan Multan] [ref: استاد مبارک علی خان کی برسی عقیدت واحترا م سے منائی گئی, Daily Raigzar Bahawalpur]

== Ancestral History, Tribal Leadership, and Royal Migration ==
Ustad Mubarak Ali Khan belonged to an ancient, multi-generational dynasty of classical vocalists who simultaneously held hereditary leadership within the **Walyani tribe**. For centuries, his family line had been deeply intertwined with the royal court music traditions of the subcontinent. His ancestors were originally residents of the Bikaner State in Rajasthan, India, where they served as the celebrated state musicians under the patronage of Maharaja Ganga Singh.

Prior to the partition of India, a historic transition of patronage occurred when the grandfather of the final ruler of Bahawalpur, Nawab Sir Sadiq Muhammad Khan V, visited Bikaner. Deeply captivated by the family's melodic prowess, the Nawab formally requested Maharaja Ganga Singh to allow the family to relocate to the Bahawalpur royal court. The family migrated to the Bahawalpur Riyasat, where they were officially designated as Shahi Singers (Royal Court Musicians). At the time of this transition, the family collective was led by Mubarak Ali Khan's father, Ustad Kayam Ali Khan, alongside his paternal uncle, Ustad Jivan Khan. Khan eventually inherited the traditional mantle of leadership, serving as the official **Chief (Head) of the Walyani tribe** throughout his later life in Bahawalpur.

== Early Life, Training, and Discipleship ==
Born in Bahawalpur in 1940, Mubarak Ali Khan initiated his musical training and initial accompaniment (Sangat) under the guidance of Ustad Ali Bux Khan, a resident of Bahawalpur and father of the notable musician Ustad Nazar Hussain Khan.

Following this foundational phase, he moved during his youth to Hyderabad, Sindh, to seek advanced mentorship from the legendary maestro Ustad Umeed Ali Khan (son of Ustad Pyare Khan), one of the grandest proponents of the Gwalior and Kotwali Gharana systems in United India. Khan spent approximately seven years in Hyderabad undergoing rigorous training in Khayal gayaki under Umeed Ali Khan's direct supervision, and subsequently earned the distinction of performing alongside his master on stage, as well as with Ustad Asad Ali Khan. [ref: Official Request and Statement to the Executive Director, Punjab Arts Council]

== Performance Artistry and Raga Repertoire ==
Ustad Mubarak Ali Khan possessed a comprehensive master-level repertoire over a vast catalog of Hindustani classical frameworks. While he possessed mastery over folk idioms, his core musical focus remained strictly classical, characterized by flawless note execution (Swar Shuddhi) and deep microtonal development. He was particularly famous for his exceptional live renditions of the following classical modes:
* Abhogi and Bageshree
* Bhairavi, Bhoopali, and Yaman
* Darbari Kanada and Jaunpuri
* Desh, Kedar, and Hansadhwani (Huns Dhuni)
* Malkauns: Celebrated for his classical interpretation of the spiritual Sufi bandish "Peer E Nizam Ud Din" dedicated to Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya. [ref: محفلِ موسیقی ’خیال‘ میں استاد مبارک علی خان کی شاندار کارکردگی, Daily Vintage Archive]
* Pratap Varali (Partab Varali): An exceptionally rare raga in the Hindustani system that very few classical practitioners attempt, which Khan famously performed and preserved during a private assembly recording using mobile-media documentation.

Khan seamlessly brought the classical structural weight of Gwalior vocalization into regional Urdu poetry—notably rendering Abdul Hamid Adam's ghazals—as well as the mystical Siraiki Kafis of Khwaja Ghulam Farid, such as "Chola Mera Rut Nal Ratiya" and "Dukhan Lagi Tey Yar Bhoven".

GIOYA Higher Education Institution is a higher education institution based in San Ġwann, Malta. It operates within Malta's higher education accreditation and quality assurance framework overseen by the Malta Further and Higher Education Authority (MFHEA). [ref: External Quality Assurance, Malta Further and Higher Education Authority]

== History ==
The institution was founded in March 2019 as GIOYA Academy by a group of professionals with backgrounds including business management, higher education administration and international organisations. [ref: GIOYA Higher Education Institution – External Quality Assurance Audit Report, Malta Further and Higher Education Authority]

It subsequently adopted the name GIOYA Higher Education Institution.

== Academic activities ==
GIOYA offers higher education programmes in areas including business administration and entrepreneurship, commercial diplomacy and management. [ref: Academic Programmes, GIOYA Higher Education Institution]

Its programmes include the Bachelor in International Business Administration and Entrepreneurship, which is part of a double-degree arrangement with the University of Turin. [ref: Double degree programs/Joint degree programs, University of Turin]

In the field of commercial diplomacy, GIOYA has collaborated with the University for Peace (UPEACE). In 2023, the two institutions entered into an agreement concerning the Executive Doctorate in Commercial Diplomacy. [ref: First executive doctorate in commercial diplomacy, Times of Malta]

== Quality assurance ==
In 2024, GIOYA underwent an external quality assurance audit by the Malta Further and Higher Education Authority. The audit report was published on 21 October 2024.

The assessment found the institution compliant with the majority of the standards examined while identifying areas where improvements were required. The MFHEA subsequently published a follow-up report in November 2025. [ref: External Quality Assurance, Malta Further and Higher Education Authority]

== Institutional collaborations ==

=== University of Turin ===
GIOYA has a double-degree agreement with the University of Turin involving the university's degree programme in Information and Business Communication Management.

In July 2025, the University of Turin's Board of Directors approved the renewal of the agreement concerning the structured mobility programme leading to the award of the two degrees. [ref: Resoconto del Consiglio di Amministrazione del 18 luglio 2025, University of Turin]

=== UNITAR and NAVIGO ===
In 2025, GIOYA, NAVIGO and the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) announced a collaboration to develop an executive programme on sustainability and management in the maritime sector. [ref: NAVIGO, GIOYA and UNITAR Join Forces for an Executive Programme on Sustainability and Management in the Maritime Sector, United Nations Institute for Training and Research]

=== Sport-related education ===
In 2025, GIOYA and The Embassy Sport Premium launched an initiative focused on the professional transition of athletes following their competitive careers. [ref: NBA star Jose Calderón helping athletes' transition beyond sport, Times of Malta]

In March 2026, GIOYA signed a memorandum of understanding with the Authority for Integrity in Maltese Sport (AIMS) concerning education and professional development for athletes and sports professionals in Malta. [ref: AIMS signs Memorandum of Understanding with GIOYA Higher Education Institution, Times of Malta]

Draft text:
----

KubeVirt is an open-source virtualization project that extends Kubernetes to manage traditional Virtual machine (VM) workloads. It allows organizations to deploy, run, and manage VMs side-by-side with containerized applications within the same Kubernetes cluster, utilizing the same underlying orchestration, networking, and tooling. [ref: What is KubeVirt?, Red Hat] The project is heavily adopted by organizations seeking to unify their infrastructure platforms and is an incubating project under the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF). [ref: KubeVirt - Cloud Native Computing Foundation, CNCF]

== History and timeline ==
KubeVirt was developed as Kubernetes emerged as a standard platform for application deployment. The project was designed to directly complement Kubernetes by extending its control plane to natively host and manage legacy VM workloads alongside containers. This design allowed organizations adopting Kubernetes to use a single foundational layer for both modern containerized applications and traditional virtual machines. KubeVirt entered the CNCF Sandbox and later graduated to an Incubating project as its adoption across the cloud-native ecosystem grew.

KubeVirt aligns its release cycle closely with Kubernetes, typically trailing standard Kubernetes minor releases by roughly two months to allow for proper stabilization.

Key milestones:
* June 2016: Initial commit.
* September 2019: KubeVirt was accepted into the CNCF Sandbox.
* April 2022: The project was promoted to the CNCF Incubating maturity level.
* July 2023: KubeVirt v1.0 was officially released, marking a major maturity milestone for the project.
* August 2025: A formal [https://github.com/cncf/toc/issues/1822 pull request] for CNCF Graduation was opened, signaling the project's push toward the foundation's highest maturity tier.

== Architecture and dependencies ==
KubeVirt extends the Kubernetes API using custom resource definitions (CRDs) to represent virtual machine objects. It relies on the Linux virtualization stack rather than inventing a new hypervisor stack. From the perspective of Kubernetes, a KubeVirt VM is simply treated as a pod with specific resource requests. From the Kubernetes perspective KubeVirt is a cloud-native application and implemented using the Kubernetes controller (VM life-cycle management) and operator (KubeVirt lfie-cycle management) patterns.

=== Core dependencies ===
* Kubernetes: The foundational orchestration engine.
* KVM: The underlying Linux hypervisor used to execute the virtual machines.
* QEMU & libvirt: Used to configure, execute, and manage the VM processes.

* KVM

National Squash League (NSL) is a professional, city-based team squash league in the United States. It was created by Timmy Brownell, Spencer Lovejoy and Fernando Valdizan. The league uses a team-based format featuring franchises representing cities, an annual player draft, a running clock, substitutions, power plays and playoffs. [ref: About the NSL, National Squash League]

The NSL played its inaugural season in 2024 with six men's teams. A women's division was introduced in 2025. For the 2026–27 season, the league consists of ten men's teams and six women's teams. [ref: Teams, National Squash League]

The league has a strategic partnership with US Squash, the national governing body for squash in the United States. [ref: US Squash and National Squash League form strategic partnership, SportsTravel] Matches are carried by HomeTeam Network. [ref: HTN Squash: Your Home for the National Squash League, HomeTeam Network]

== History ==

=== 2024: inaugural season ===

The NSL held its first player draft in Nashville in early 2024 to fill six franchises: the Derby City Colts, now the Louisville Colts; the Atlanta Tornados; Chicago Grizzlies; Newport Dragons; the New York City Knights, now the New York Knights; and the Nashville Crushers.

Twenty-four players were drafted. The teams were split into North and South divisions of three, and the two division winners advanced to a championship match.

In June 2024, the New York Knights, who were undefeated during the season, defeated the Nashville Crushers in the inaugural NSL final at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia. [ref: New York Knights Defeat Nashville Crushers to Lift Inaugural NSL Title, US Squash]

At the trophy ceremony, commissioner Fernando Valdizan announced plans to expand the league with additional men's and women's teams.

=== 2025: expansion and women's division ===

The league's second season expanded to nine men's teams and four women's teams.

The Philadelphia Lightning, Greenwich Panthers and men's Lake Erie Beacons joined the men's competition.

The women's division was also introduced in 2025.

The finals were held June 27–29, 2025, at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia. Four men's teams and four women's teams advanced to the semifinals.

The Philadelphia Lightning won the men's championship in their first season, recording a 4–0 shutout in the final.

The Philadelphia Freedom won the first NSL women's championship after the DC Inferno forced the final into a shootout. [ref: Philadelphia Freedom and Lightning Conquer NSL Finals, US Squash]

=== 2026 season ===

Two women's expansion teams, the New York Queens and Seattle Freeze, expanded the women's division to six teams.

The Queens made their debut on January 31, 2026, against the DC Inferno.

The 2026 finals were played at MSquash in South Norwalk, Connecticut.

In the men's semifinals, the Greenwich Panthers defeated defending champion Philadelphia Lightning 3–1, while the Chicago Grizzlies defeated the Newport Dragons 4–0.

In the women's semifinals, the New York Queens defeated the Seattle Freeze 3–1.

The DC Inferno won the women's championship by defeating the Queens 3–2 in an overtime shootout following a 2–2 draw.

=== 2026–27 season ===

Beginning with the 2026–27 campaign, the league labels its seasons across calendar years.

The regular season began in October 2026 with ten men's teams and six women's teams. [ref: Schedule, National Squash League]

The Carolina Pirates and a men's Seattle Freeze team joined the men's competition.

The Newport Dragons no longer appear on the league's official 2026–27 team list.

The top four teams in each division advance to the playoffs, scheduled for March 5–7, 2027, at the Arlen Specter US Squash Center in Philadelphia.

metals4U is a United Kingdom–based metal supplier that sells cut-to-size metal products through an e-commerce platform. The company supplies metals including aluminium, steel, stainless steel and brass to trade, industrial and individual customers.

metals4U was established in 2002 and was initially based in Pontefract, West Yorkshire, with around six staff. The company was founded to supply metal products to both commercial businesses and individual consumers, particularly smaller-scale buyers who do not typically use traditional trade suppliers.

In 2015, the company relocated to Wetherby, West Yorkshire, to increase its warehouse capacity. As of May 2026, the company employed approximately 53 staff, comprising 37 warehouse operatives and 16 customer service and administration staff.

=== Transition to e-commerce ===
In 2008, metals4U began selling online. The move enabled nationwide ordering and delivery, and made the company's custom cutting service available through a digital ordering platform. Customers can also collect orders from the company's head office in Wetherby.

== Industry involvement ==
Material specifications supplied by metals4U have been cited in university engineering research, including studies of synthetic inflow turbulence generation at the University of Southampton and of the ductility of lap joints in reinforced concrete beams published by the University of West London. The company has also provided material sponsorship for student engineering projects, including the University of Huddersfield's Formula Student team, Team HARE.

== Leadership ==
The company's co-founder, chairman and majority shareholder is Paul McFadyen. McFadyen has written and been quoted in business and trade media on topics including skills in construction and engineering, global metal markets, circular economy models and international trade policy.

"The Subliminal Man" is a dystopian science fiction short story by J.G. Ballard. It was first published in the January 1963 issue of New Worlds (Volume 42, Number 126) and later reprinted in The Disaster Area and The Terminal Beach. [ref: JG Ballard Cover Scans 1962-1963, www.rickmcgrath.com]The story is, like many other of his short stories, very political at its core. [ref: ] It thematizes the power of technology and media, [ref: ] as well as subliminal messaging and consumerism.

== Plot ==
The story opens with Hathaway calling out to Dr. Robert Franklin "The signs, Doctor! Have you seen the signs?" Franklin tries to ignore Hathaway and get away, but fails. He vexedly asks him what the matter is, to which Hathaway replies that the government has "started to build the first big signs! Over a hundred feet high, on the traffic islands outside town. They‘ll soon have all the approach roads covered. When they do we might as well stop thinking." Franklin doesn’t believe Hathaway, a former patient, and instead believes that he is mentally ill and needs professional help. He urges Hathaway to think of his wife and child. Hathaway insists that he is and that the signs are dangerous for his family, claming that the government is trying to "transistorize our brains!" Franklin dismisses him, telling him that if he had any evidence of the emittance of subliminal messages and commands, he would help him, but he doesn't. He reminds him that subliminal advertising was banned 30 years ago and calls his conspiracy preposterous. Hathaway drops the issue and instead points out that all the cars in the parking lot are identical in design and color. He argues that the standardization removed variety without making the cars any cheaper. He asks Franklin about his new car, since he only had his old one for 3 months. Franklin answers that he traded it in and defends himself by stating that "If you ever had any money you‘d realize that it‘s the most economical way of owning a car. You don‘t keep driving the same one until it falls apart. It‘s the same with everything else—television sets, washing machines, refrigerators. But you aren‘t faced with the problem." Hathaway replies „Not a bad idea, either, Doctor. It gives me time to think. I‘m not working a twelve-hour day to pay for a lot of things I‘m too busy to use before they‘re obsolete.“ After driving off, Franklin reflects on his own life and realizes that he envies Hathaway's freedom, since he is not restricted by mortgages, social obligations or private work like Franklin is. [ref: ]

As Franklin drives home, he observes the enormous motorway network that covers much of the country. Although the roads are impressive, they have created serious congestion, and his journey is much longer than it used to be. The roads are designed to force drivers to maintain specific speeds through rubber studs that produce unpleasant vibrations when cars travel too slowly or too quickly. These systems are supposedly intended to improve safety, but they also force motorists to replace their tyres regularly. Cars are deliberately designed to wear out quickly, encouraging people to buy new models more frequently and increasing profits for manufacturers. Franklin then sees workers constructing one of the giant signs beside the motorway. He initially assumes that it is connected to the airport, but after seeing another similar structure, he begins to suspect that the signs have a different purpose.

When Franklin arrives home, he finds his wife, Judith, watching television and writing down numbers from a shopping programme called Spot Bargains. The programme offers discounts on household products, encouraging viewers to trade in their possessions for new ones. Judith wants to replace their barbecue spit even though they have only owned it for two months. Franklin refuses because he believes the purchase is unnecessary, but Judith insists that buying a replacement will save them money. Franklin then notices the giant sign outside their home and asks Judith about it. She believes it is part of the airport system, but Franklin is becoming increasingly suspicious that the signs are connected to the strange behaviour of consumers.

When Franklin meets Hathaway again, he is less doubtfull of Hathaway's 'conspiracy' but isn't fully ready to admit it yet. Hathaway asks him what he's gonna do about the signs to which Franklin replies

"Nothing, of course. Damn it, it may be just auto-suggestion, you‘ve probably got me imagining—“

"Don‘t be absurd, Doctor! If you can‘t believe your own senses what chance have you left? They‘re invading your brain, if you don‘t defend yourself they‘ll take it over completely! We‘ve got to act now, before we‘re all paralysed.“

Franklin questions why the signs would command people to consume more, since the spending power isn't increasing. Hathaway retorts that an increase in working hours is imminent, Franklin doesn't think that society would let that happen. Hathaway argues that it did already happen in the past, and people won't do anything about it this time, either. Franklin asks Hathaway what he is going to do, but he won't tell him unless he joins. Franklin refuses.
[truncated]

Choirs Aotearoa New Zealand appointed him to the prestigious national role, succeeding David Squire as the leader of the world's longest-running national youth choir.

==Current Roles & Leadership==

• New Zealand Youth Choir: Appointed as the fifth Music Director, leading the premier 50-member ensemble for singers aged 18–25. [ref: [https://www.thepost.co.nz/culture/360986057/new-maestro-town-rowan-johnston-leading-nzs-top-youth-choir ThePost Rowan Johnston leading NZ's top youth choir]] [ref: [https://www.choirs.nz/our-choirs/our-people/ NZYC Our people]]

• Voices New Zealand Chamber Choir [ref: [https://www.voicesnz.com/people/rowan-johnston/ VoicesNZ Rowan Johnston]]: Maintains a long-standing position as an active bass chorister (since 1999) and serves as an Associate Conductor.

==Early life and education==
Johnston grew up in a highly musical family environment. He learnt a number of instruments growing up, sang in church choirs, and played in pipe bands. In high school, Johnston successfully auditioned into the New Zealand Secondary Students' Choir (NZSSC). During this time, he discovered his passion for choral music, wanting to pursue singing at the highest level. Later, he advanced into the New Zealand Youth Choir (NZYC) as a bass vocalist. While in the choir, Dr. Karen Grylls, the music director at the time, actively encouraged choir members to try their hand at leading and conducting sections. This experience inspired Johnston to pursue choral direction alongside his passion for singing. [ref: [https://www.rnz.co.nz/concert/programmes/three-to-seven/audio/2019029848/back-where-it-all-began/ RNZ Concert 'Back where it all began']] [ref: [https://www.rnz.co.nz/concert/programmes/upbeat/audio/2018775537/rowan-johnston-passionate-about-choral-music/ RNZ Concert Rowan Johnston passionate about choral music]]

Johnston earned a Bachelor of Music (BMus), specializing in classical singing and composition from Victoria University of Wellington, and later completed a Diploma of Teaching, formally training as a high school music educator from Wellington College of Education. He later went on to complete a Postgraduate Diploma of Music in Conducting (awarded with Distinction), followed by earning a Master of Music in Choral Conducting with First-Class Honours, studying directly under his former youth choir mentor, Dr. Karen Grylls, at the University of Auckland.

==Career==
Rowan Johnston is very well-known in choral circles in New Zealand both as a choir member and as one of New Zealand's top choral conductors.

Johnston is regularly invited to conduct the Gondwana National Choral School in Australia, the premier national choral program, where he conducts intensive performance seasons for young singers from across the country. He is currently a member of Voices NZ, and directs a multitude of high-level choirs, including the New Zealand Youth Choir and the Wellington Youth Choir. Johnston also has an impressive record at the New Zealand Choral Federation's Big Sing competition, having guided multiple ensembles to the National Finale across his tenures at different schools.

Johnston has served as Director of Music at Auckland’s Holy Trinity Cathedral, Musical Director of the Auckland Youth Choir, and conducted Choralation (the combined choir of Westlake Boys and Westlake Girls High Schools), achieving international recognition at the Summa Cum Laude International Music Festival held in Vienna.

Alongside Elise Bradley, Johnston founded and co-directed the Aotearoa Academy Choir, a national training choir for students in preparation for the New Zealand Youth Choir and New Zealand Secondary Students' Choir. Competing at the 13th World Choir Games held in Tāmaki Makaurau, Auckland, in July 2024, the choir achieved exceptional success, earning a Gold Diploma V, 2nd Place Overall in Category 4, "Youth Choirs" of the Open Competition, and Top 5 Score across the entire competition. [ref: [https://www.interkultur.com/newsroom/choir-games/details/news/world-choir-games-2024-results-of-the-champions-competition/ World Choir Games 2024 Results]]

== Introduction ==

Orbilia xanthostigma.

== History ==
O. xanthostigma was described by a Swedish mycologist, Elias Magnus Fries, in 1815, and was later renamed by Fries in 1849. [ref: Index Fungorum, Index Fungorum] [ref: Cryptic speciation in Orbilia xanthostigma and O. leucostigma (Orbiliomycetes): an aggregate with worldwide distribution, Mycological Progress] It was first described in Scandinavia and published in his work “Summa vegitabilum Scandinaviae”, a botanical work written in Latin. [ref: https://search.library.ucla.edu/discovery/fulldisplay/alma9946789483606533/01UCS_LAL:UCLA, search.library.ucla.edu] The common English name of this fungus is the Glasscup.

== Morphology ==

O. xanthostigma are tiny disk/saucer shaped fungi, ranging in size from 0.3mm to 1mm (roughly 1/8 inch across). The fruiting body does not possess a pileus, stipe, ring, or vulva. The hymenium is cup shaped, smooth, and waxy. [ref: Orbilia xanthostigma - Fungipedia Mushroom Guide, Fungipedia] They sit flat on the surface and do not have a stalk. The apothecial coloration is described as golden yellow to orange yellow. When dry, the fruiting bodies may appear wavy or lobed, and irregularly shaped. [ref: ] They typically grow in high numbers, in close proximity to one another. [ref: Glasscup (Orbilia xanthostigma), Mushrooms of Nebraska]

They typically appear in largely dense groups called gregarious clusters and are commonly found on fallen hardwood in moist or shaded woodlands. The disc fungi is a wood decomposer saprotroph. Most of the species are located in temporal regions and are present on rotting wood or tree stumps; found on Various kinds of wood, including broadleaf and coniferous trees [ref: Orbilia xanthostigma - Fungipedia Mushroom Guide, Fungipedia], particularly oak and pine, from the spring to the fall seasons.

The members of this group can also be classified through their spores: cashew shaped and warted [ref: New species and records of orbiliaceous fungi from Georgia, USA, Mycological Progress] ascospores that range from about 2.5-3 micrometers in length with a curvature of about 120-180 degrees. They appear in ascus sacks, typically 8 at a time. The species also has Dicranidion like conidia, a form of asexual spore. These are distinctive spores, developed primarily for the purpose of easier dispersal and spore transport by vectors where anchoring or aquatic adaptations are necessary. Asci are characteristically trunicate at the apex, the base is prolonged in an L shape. The paraphyses are inflated at the apex.

Members of the family Orbiliaceae are typically characterized through the production of light colored and partially translucent apothecia. They also contain small asci and ascospores with KOH soluble spore bodies.

== Carnivorous Nematode Trapping: ==
The class Orbiliomycetes is a large class of fungi within the phylum of Ascomycota; it contains free living, nematophagous, soil fungi that are known for their ability to trap and consume nematodes (as well as other small organisms). They do so through the usage of several trapping mechanisms. Within the members of Orbiliacaea, these mechanisms include adhesive sticky knobs, adhesive networks, constrictor rings, nonconstrictor rings, and sticky adhesive branches. [ref: Nematode-Trapping Fungi, Microbiology Spectrum] [ref: Nematode-Trapping Fungi Eavesdrop on Nematode Pheromones, Current Biology]

Fungi can live saprophytically on wood, and as predators, capturing nematodes. The presence of nematode traps indicates a switch from a saprophytic to predacious feeding system.

The fungi within the genus Orbilia are carnivorous; however, most only supplement their diet through the consumption of nematodes. However, a standing hypothesis claims the species within this genus use nematodes as the primary supply of nitrogen, and in fact are weak wood decomposers. During periods of nutritional starvation or in the presence of nematodes, nematode trapping fungi switch towards predation and produce nematode trapping mechanisms. [ref: Key processes required for the different stages of fungal carnivory by a nematode-trapping fungus, PLOS Biology]

In the asexual state, the telemorph, O. xanthostigma acts as a carnivore.

These organisms play a crucial role in soil dynamics, regulating nematode populations in the ecosystems. Nematode trapping fungi serve as a wonderful model system, and stand indicative of fungal evolution, as well as the evolution of organismal interactions between fungi and nematodes. Similarly, this relationship is also indicative of nematode evolution, representing a marker that promoted nematode fitness against predation and other factors alongside it.

== Phylogeny: ==
O. xanthostigma is a species within the family Orbiliacea, which belongs to the order Orbiliales and the class Orbiliomycetes. It is in the subphylum Pezizomycotina, which resides within the Ascomycota. Orbiliaceae contains more than 200 species in 12 genera. The species Orbilia xanthostigma represents the most commonly recorded species of the Obiliomycetes.

Molecular and genetic analysis of nematode trapping fungi indicates that the monophyletic classes of Orbiliomycetes and Pezizomycetes are two of the earliest branches to diverge from Pezizomycotina. Certain genera are well known nematode trapping fungi. Evidence suggests this ability evolved only once in Orbiliales.
[truncated]

Niko Health is a Swedish health tech company that offers technology-driven preventative health scans. [ref: Full-body scans: are Neko Health and the like more panic than panacea?, The Week US] [ref: I tried a £300 scan that promises to help you avoid illness – and I was impressed, The Independent] It was co-founded in 2018 by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. [ref: Is Daniel Ek’s Neko Health worth $1.7bn?, Sifted] Neko Health is headquartered in Stockholm, Sweden, with clinics in Stockholm, London, Manchester, Birmingham, and New York City. [ref: Nowhere to hide, www.healthcare-management.uk]

== History ==
Neko Health was founded in 2018 by Hjalmar Nilsonne and Daniel Ek, the founder and Executive Chairman of Spotify. [ref: Verifying Device, www.thetimes.com] [ref: Verifying Device, www.thetimes.com] [ref: Daniel Ek’s Next Act: Full-Body Scans for the People, The New York Times] The company develops technology intended to support preventive healthcare and early disease detection. Between 2018 and 2023, it developed its own hardware, software, and medical technology. [ref: Neko’s full-body scan costs £300 and has a 100K waiting list. Is it worth it?] [ref: Age against the machine: what I learned after stripping down for a full body scan, The Guardian] [ref: I Tried the Viral Health Scan With a 100,000-Person Waitlist—These are My Honest Thoughts, Marie Claire UK]

In February 2023, Neko Health launched its first clinic in Stockholm, Sweden. [ref: The Hottest Startups in Stockholm in 2024, Wired] After immediate customer demand and a waitlist of up to 100,000 customers, Neko Health began expanding. [ref: I Tried The New £299 Health Scan With A 40,000-Strong Waitlist… Was It Worth It?, British Vogue] In 2024, Neko Health expanded to clinics in London and further across the UK, including Manchester and Birmingham. [ref: We took a Neko Health scan – the future of preventative healthcare?, Wallpaper*] [ref: Swedish start-up Neko Health brings its sci-fi scanning suite to central London, Wallpaper*] [ref: Daniel Ek’s body scanning startup Neko unveils massive new London clinic, Sifted]

In January 2025, following its Series B funding, Neko Health announced the funding would be used for expansion across Europe, entering the U.S. market, and continuing to develop new diagnostic technologies. [ref: Neko Health Accelerates UK Expansion, Fitt Insider] [ref: The Swedish Start-Up Aiming to Conquer America’s Full-Body-Scan Craze, The New York Times]

In June 2026, Neko launched the Neko Health App on iOS.

== Technology ==
The Neko Health Scan is a health assessment that combines imaging, physiological testing, laboratory analysis, and a clinician consultation during a single appointment. [ref: Neko Health: A Unique Twist on Whole-body Scans, Healthcare Huddle] The assessment does not use ionizing radiation and includes:

* 2D and 3D imaging, thermal imaging, and depth-sensing technology
* Measurements including blood pressure, body composition, and electrocardiography (ECG), cardiac and arterial assessments, and blood analysis
* Other measurements including grip strength and intraocular pressure

The assessment is used to identify health markers associated with conditions including cardiovascular disease, metabolic disorders, and some skin cancers.

== Funding ==
Neko Health was initially financed by Daniel Ek through his investment firm, Prima Materia, before raising outside capital.

In July 2023, Neko Health raised €60 million in a Series A funding found led by Lakestar, Atomico, and General Catalyst. [ref: Daniel Ek's Neko Health raises $65M for preventative healthcare through full-body scans, TechCrunch] [ref: Atomico raises $1.24bn to back European startups from Series A and beyond, Sifted] [ref: Neko Health – What People Are Missing, Healthy Debate by Max Marchione] Following that round, Klaus Hommels and Niklas Zennström joined the company's board.

In January 2025, Neko Health raised $260 million in a Series B funding round at a reported valuation of approximately $1.8 billion. [ref: Daniel Ek’s Neko raises $260mn in push to be Apple of healthcare, www.ft.com] [ref: ] [ref: Full-body scan startup Neko Health raises $260 million, Axios] [ref: Neko, the body-scanning startup co-founded by Spotify's Daniel Ek, snaps up $260M at a $1.8B valuation, TechCrunch] [ref: Neko Health Raises $260M Ahead of U.S. Launch, Athletech News] Investors included Lightspeed Venture Partners, General Catalyst, Atomico, Lakestar, O.G. Venture Partners, and Rossello. [ref: Preventing illness, not treating it: Neko Health raises €250 million to expand globally, EU-Startups]

In July 2026, Neko Health raised $700 million in a Series C funding round co-led by O.G. Venture Partners and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Investors in the round included Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan, model Claudia Schiffer, former tennis player Maria Sharapova, and musician will.i.am. [ref: Neko Health, a Body-Scan Startup, Raises $700 Million in Latest Fundraising, Wall Street Journal] [ref: Daniel Ek’s body-scanning start-up raises $700mn for US push, www.ft.com] [ref: Tech Investors and Longevity Influencers Back Neko Health’s Expansion, The New York Times]

He serves as the Vice President of Exploration Tooling and Global Supply Chain at Boart Longyear, a multinational corporation specializing in the manufacturing of drilling services and tooling equipment for the global mining and resource extraction sectors. He attended the Instituto Tecnológico y de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey (ITESM) to study manufacturing systems before pursuing advanced management and business administration training in the United States.

In 2021, he completed his doctoral research at the University of Phoenix, earning a Doctor of Business Administration (DBA) degree. His peer-reviewed doctoral dissertation deployed a quantitative correlational research design utilizing multiple regression analyses and independent-samples t-tests across a dataset of 465 randomly sampled Mexican enterprises. His operational implementations during this period focused on the execution of cellular manufacturing, the elimination of cross-border supply frictions, and the deployment of Lean Six Sigma continuous-improvement models.

In January 2025, Rodríguez joined the global executive leadership team at Boart Longyear as the Vice President of Exploration Tooling and Global Supply Chain, operating out of the corporation's headquarters in Salt Lake City, Utah. Operating under the motto "emprendiendo con valor" (entrepreneurship with courage), the organization designs community programs that foster social equity, support continuous learning, and eliminate systemic developmental disparities across regional populations.

As a business author and optimization practitioner, Rodríguez's research centers on the reduction of systemic organizational complexities through strategic simplicity.

In his 2021 doctoral treatise, Servant Leadership and Business Models as Predictors of Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises Financial Success, Rodríguez mapped the intersection of human-centric management and financial risk metrics. Utilizing multiple regression techniques, the study isolated how specific dimensions of Servant Leadership (SL) and structured Business Model (BM) parameters correlate with an enterprise's debt ratio and long-term financial insolvency risks. The work has been referenced as an empirical validation connecting organizational behavioral economics with macroeconomic enterprise survival rates.

Jeroen de Valk (born June 19, 1958) is a Dutch journalist, author and jazz historian. Internationally, he is primarily known as the author of the first biographies of the jazz musicians Chet Baker and Ben Webster. Both books have been translated into English; the Baker-bio as well in several other languages.

Education and career

De Valk was born in Rotterdam, grew up in Amsterdam, where he started writing professionally for the daily newspaper Het Parool in 1979, and has been living in the town of Amersfoort since 1987, where he still works as a general reporter. He studied double bass at the jazz section of the Royal Conservatory in The Hague (1982-1985). Since 2021, he is editor-in-chief of Jazz Bulletin, a quarterly magazine devoted to Dutch jazz history, published by the Nederlands Jazz Archief (Dutch Jazz Archive).

Writings

Since 1979, De Valk published countless articles in newspapers and magazines. His first book was Chet Baker / Herinneringen Aan Een Lyrisch Trompettist (1989), a biography for which he started his research in the early 80s. De Valk published a drastically updated edition in English in 2017 and hopes to release another update in 2027. This book was available in several languages, see the bibliography below.

His biography Het Levensverhaal Van Ben Webster (1992) was translated into in English in 2001. De Valk traces Webster’s life from family members who were forced to live in slavery to the donation – after Webster’s passing - of his favorite tenor saxophone ‘Ol’ Betsy’ to the Institute of Jazz Studies.

De Valk compiled series of his jazz portraits and interviews in Go Man, Go! (2009), So Near So Far (2016) and Jazz In De Schaduw (2025). He devoted a biography as well to Dutch veteran drummer John Engels, at the occasion of Engels’ 80th birthday: Hé Vogel, Wanneer Spelen We Weer? (2015).

Chet Baker research

De Valk examined at length what he considers ‘assumptions and misconceptions’, among others those surrounding Baker’s death in 1988 after falling from his hotel window. De Valk inspected the hotel room, talked extensively with the police officer who researched the circumstances of his passing, the police man who actually found him and people who were close to him in his last days.

In the same detailed manner, De Valk followed Baker’s musical career. The Valk concludes that Baker was a great trumpeter, almost to the very end. This contrasts with the image of Baker as a washed-up musician, created in the popular ‘documentary’ Let’s Get Lost. The book closes with an annotated discography with more than 250 albums.

Amersfoort history

De Valk writes regularly about the history of Amersfoort, his hometown, in local media. Among publications in book form are De Wagenwerkplaats / Het Spoor, De Strijd, De Toekomst (with Arjan Klaver).

Poetry

De Valk debuted as a poet with his collection Dagen Zonder Licht / Sonnetten Over Depressie, Dood En Rouw (2026). He wrote these sonnets after the passing of his son, journalist Arnold de Valk. His primary goal was to provide ‘a sense of recognition and comfort for people with depression and their caregivers, as well as understanding from those around them.’ Nevertheless, he received explicit support from Jean Pierre Rawie, the best-selling poet in the Netherlands. (1) In interviews, De Valk revealed that he himself had suffered from periods of depression and anxiety, but was always able to recover. (2)

Music

De Valk can be heard as a jazz bassist on the album Traces Of Chesney / A Tribute To Chet Baker, with a band lead by trumpeter Edu Ninck Blok (2015, Silence! Records) and several albums with Dutch Treat, the band of singer and lyricist Nynke Geertsma. The latter’s band had noted tenor saxophonist Leo Janssen (Metropole Orkest) as a guest soloist on Dit Is Pas Het Begin (2025, Dutch Treat Music).

= PolarX =
PolarX AS is a Norwegian logistics and production services company headquartered in Longyearbyen, Svalbard. [ref: POLARX AS (992143568), Longyearbyen – regnskap, roller og eiere, Byggsikt] Founded by Australian filmmaker and polar expert Jason Roberts, the company specialises in providing film production support, scientific mission logistics, and marine transport in the Arctic and Antarctic regions. [ref: Svalbard and PolarX: Filming at the Edge of the Earth, NORWEGIAN FILM COMMISSION] [ref: Explorer Yachts Summit 2025: Q&A with polar expert Jason Roberts of PolarX, www.boatinternational.com]

== History ==
The company traces its origins back to the early 1990s, when Jason Roberts established "Jason Roberts Productions" in Svalbard. [ref: Home, PolarX] Roberts had moved from Australia to the High Arctic, initially working as a field technician and research diver before transitioning into polar filmmaking and production facilitation. [ref: “I have to send 97 emails just to set up a tent.” - Jason Roberts, Artica Svalbard]

As the demand for highly specialized logistical support in cold climates grew beyond media production, operations were expanded in January 2008 into the formal incorporation of PolarX AS as an aksjeselskap (Norwegian: joint-stock company). [ref: ] [ref: ] Over more than three decades of operation under its original and current brandings, the company has grown into a primary logistics interface for bespoke operations in both polar zones. [ref: Home, PolarX]

== Operations and Services ==
PolarX operates from their expansive office and warehouse location the township of Longyearbyen, utilizing Svalbard's infrastructure - including it's international airport and year-round marine access - as a primary hub for High Arctic deployments. The company provides a wide range of services tailored to extreme environments:

* Media and Film Production: PolarX provides comprehensive field fixer and location services for natural history documentaries, commercial photography, and feature films. Its services include permitting, risk assessments, specialized equipment rentals, and cold-weather safety management, as well as pre-production consulting and location management on site.

* Marine and Vessel Support: The company operates its own vessel, the R/V PolarXplorer, to support marine biology, photography, and film crews. [ref: Polarxplorer AS - Org.nr. 928 138 895 - Longyearbyen - Se Regnskap, Roller og mer, www.proff.no] It also acts as an agency for polar superyachts, providing ice pilots, navigation assistance, high-resolution ice charts, dedicated field techinicians and polar bear guards, and local regulatory dispensations across Svalbard and Northern Norway, Greenland, the Canadian North, and sub-Antarctic islands.

* Scientific and Institutional Support: Through the teams' field experience, PolarX assists international researchers with data collection and local permissions for field studies in glaciology, marine biology, and ornithology. Together with Rydd i Tide (Norway's largest national marine litter cleanup program) [ref: Rydd i Tide — vi rydder kysten, tonn for tonn, Handelens Miljøfond], PolarX acts as the operational arm on Svalbard, having cleaned 36 tons in 2025. [ref: (+) Finner fremdeles døde dyr viklet inn i plast, svalbardposten]
* Safety and Expedition Support: PolarX consults on and organises private, bespoke experiental travel itineraries and guided expeditions across remote polar terrains using assets like custom snowmobile fleets, the PolarXplorer or chartered vessels.

== Notable Productions ==
PolarX has facilitated numerous high-profile media projects. The company is noted for securing historic polar bear footage and supporting prominent documentary series, including the BBC's Blue Planet and Frozen Planet franchises. [ref: BBC One - Frozen Planet, Series 1 - Jason Roberts, BBC] [ref: ] In 2024, the compay provided the primary logistics and location management for the Svalbard-based filming of James Gunn's blockbuster feature film Superman (released 2025), where Adventdalen served as the backdrop for the iconic Fortress of Solitude. Other norable film production management and location credits include Marvel Studios' Black Widow (2021), Disney's Aladdin (2019) and Paramount Pictures' Mission Impossible - The Final Reckoning (2025). [ref: Showcase, PolarX]

[ref: CHRYSALIS FINANCE LIMITED, company number 06541664, Companies House] [ref: About us, Chrysalis Finance] Its finance is offered through dental practices, private hospitals and clinics, covering dental, cosmetic, eye, hearing, diagnostic and fertility treatment. [ref: Financial Services Register: firm reference numbers 631193 and 720098, Financial Conduct Authority]

== History ==
The company was incorporated on 20 March 2008 as Hewlett Mortimer Limited and changed its name to Chrysalis Finance Limited on 4 February 2013.

In August 2015, the dental trade publication Dentistry reported a partnership between Chrysalis and the dental plan provider Patient Plan Direct. [ref: Patient Plan Direct and Chrysalis Finance announce new partnership, Dentistry] The report described a model under which dental practices could become appointed representatives of Chrysalis, offering patient finance without holding their own consumer credit authorisation.

According to the company, it acquired the dental finance brokers Financing First and Dental Finance in 2020, and later launched Treatment Pay, a card payment service for healthcare providers.

== Operations ==
Chrysalis arranges loans that patients repay over periods of between three months and five years, including interest-free options. [ref: Medical finance, Chrysalis Finance] Patients apply either in the clinic or from home.

Private hospital groups that list Chrysalis as their patient finance provider include Nuffield Health, [ref: Personal medical loans, Nuffield Health] Ramsay Health Care UK, [ref: Finance options, Ramsay Health Care UK] Practice Plus Group [ref: Finance options, Practice Plus Group] and Benenden Hospital. [ref: Finance, Benenden Hospital]

== Regulation ==
Chrysalis Finance Limited is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority for lending and credit broking under firm reference number 631193. Its sister company Financing First Limited, incorporated in 2000, is authorised for credit broking under firm reference number 720098. [ref: FINANCING FIRST LIMITED, company number 04114714, Companies House] Both companies, together with Treatmentpay Limited, are registered at the same address in Worsley. [ref: Gecko Robotics raises $125 million in deal valuing critical infrastructure startup over $1 billion, CNBC] [ref: Software start-up Airtable hits $11 billion valuation in latest funding, adds Salesforce, Michael Dell as investors, CNBC]

[ref: Team & Board, Georgetown]

In 2026, Kapadia founded Totei, an online arts and culture magazine focused on craftsmanship. [ref: Exclusive / New arts magazine Totei to focus on the ‘creative process’, Semafor]

Draft text:
CoursePro Africa Ltd is a Nigerian educational technology (EdTech) firm based in Oron, Akwa Ibom State. Conceived in October 2018 and incorporated on November 28, 2024, the company creates curriculum-aligned animated video books and digital learning aids for higher education students across Africa. [ref: From Student's Search For Understanding To Birth Of CoursePro Africa, Independent Newspaper Nigeria]

== History ==
The venture began on October 18, 2018, when co-founder Elijah Effiong Amah, then a mathematics undergraduate at Abia State University, sought visual aids for complex real analysis theories and started a YouTube channel with his mother, Kate Micheal Edet. After Amah graduated in 2021, the project broadened to cover subjects such as medicine, law, and engineering. Computer scientist Imoh Davis Udofa joined in December 2023 to structure the content around institutional learning goals and manage formal registration.

== Business model and operations ==
CoursePro partners directly with universities, converting approved textbooks and materials into "animated video books" for internal learning portals without upfront production fees for the institutions. Costs are offset through student access fees, with revenue shared with academic contributors. These animated assets serve strictly as supplementary learning tools rather than replacements for standard lectures or labs.
