Draft text:
The Golden Mile is the second studio album by the English pop group My Life Story. It was released on 10 March 1997 by Parlophone, peaking at number 36 on the UK Albums Chart. [ref: TOP 75 ALBUMS, Music Week] It spawned the five singles that all entered the lower half of the UK Top 40, [ref: British Hit Singles & Albums, Guinness World Records] "12 Reasons Why I Love Her", "Sparkle", "The King of Kissingdom", "Strumpet" and "Duchess".

"Sparkle" is a re-recorded version of one of the band's previous singles, "You Don't Sparkle (In My Eyes)". The song "You Can't Uneat the Apple" had produced promotional CDs planned for single release although was replaced by "Duchess". [ref:...now the pawn takes queen..., twelvereasonswhy.co.uk] The album was originally due for release on 3 March 1997, although was moved by a week. [ref: The Golden Mile, twelvereasonswhy.co.uk]

== Production ==
Following praise from NME and Melody Maker, who both gave their 1993 single "Girl A, Girl B, Boy C" from their debut album Mornington Crescent (1995), the band signed to Parlophone in 1996 and started working on a new album. [ref: ]

The Golden Mile was recorded at RAK Studios in London from 1996-1997. The only two tracks that were not recorded in 1997 were "12 Reasons Why I Love Her" and "Sparkle". [ref: The Golden Mile, EMI Records] The album was produced by Gary Langan and George Shilling. "Duchess" was produced by Steve Lovell and Pete Jones. It was mixed by Pete Smith and later mastered by Tim and Jacko. An enhanced version of the album was reissued soon after its release.

== Reception ==
AllMusic gave The Golden Mile a rating of 3 out of 5. [ref: ] It was ranked at 168 on NMEs best albums of 1997 list. [ref: NME's Best Albums of 1997, albumoftheyear.org] Dom Gourlay of Drowned in Sound wrote that it "should have been the record that cascaded them onto superstardom." [ref: Britpop's forgotten gems — Jake Shillingford and My Life Story, Drowned in Sound] South China Morning Post's Clarence Tsui referred to the album as their "first mainstream release" and recommended it to people "stifled by the domination of guitar-driven pop-rock over the past year". [ref: The Golden Mile, South China Morning Post]

At the time of its release, the music press had mixed reviews of the album. Q magazine wrote its songs, excluding "12 Reasons Why I Love Her" and "Sparkle", had no "real bite" to them, concluding that "all the orchestral pomp in the world can't make The Golden Mile much more than a fitfully entertaining parade of largely empty gestures." Select strongly criticised it, calling it "the worst album ever made", as well as accusing their lead singer, Jake Shillingford of stealing ideas from Scott Walker, Lionel Bart, and the Divine Comedy. Smash Hits, however, praised it, stating "Jake is a great pop star and though he is still to capture the live sizzle completely, this album may get him the audience he deserves." Vox said the record is "packed with hooks and epic choruses," and found it as an improvement from their 1995 debut album, Mornington Crescent.

George Morland (13 February 1643 – 1712) was an English politician. He sat as MP for the City of Durham (constituency) from 1689 till 1695. [ref: MORLAND, George (1643-1712), of Elvet, Durham and Greystones, co. Dur., History of Parliament Online]

He also served as commissioner for recusants for County Durham in 1675; freeman of Hartlepool in 1680; alderman of Durham by 1684 till 1687, and 1688 till his death; and Mayor from 1690 till 1691.

He was the first son of John Morland (died 1689), attorney of Durham by Thomasina, the daughter of George Martyn of Durham. He was educated in Durham School, Magdalene College, Cambridge in 1659, he earned a BA in 1662. On 7 November 1671, he married Mary (died 1721), the daughter of Cuthber Carr of Auckland St. Helen and the widow of Alexander Davidson of Blakiston. They had two sons (one predeceased) and two daughters.

Kanaris C. Tsinganos (Greek: Κανάρης Τσίγκανος) is a theoretical astrophysicist, professor emeritus at the Department of Physics of the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, [ref: Emeritus Professors, siteA-EN] elected director of the National Observatory of Athens. [ref: Prof. Tsinganos Kanaris – Former Director of the National Observatory of Athens (2011–2016), National Observatory of Athens] As the first national representative of Greece to ESA (Science Programm Committee, ESA/SPC), led his scientific team to become the first Greek group to participate to an ESA science space misssion (Proba 3). Tsinganos's contributions in refereed journals [ref: Google Scholar, scholar.google.com] are on MHD phenomena at the solar atmosphere, solar wind, stellar winds and astrophysical jets. He is known for the Sauty-Tsinganos criterion [ref: Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows. IV The transition from jets to winds, Astronomy and Astrophysics] for the transition of a stellar wind to a selfsimilar jet and the Vlahakis-Tsinganos systematic construction of exact selfsimilar MHD solutions for astrophysical winds and jets [ref: Systematic construction of exact magnetohydrodynamic models for astrophysical winds and jets, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society].

== Education and Academic Career ==
Tsinganos was born and completed his early education in Filiatra, Messinia, Greece (1951). After a BSc in physics from the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki (Department of Physics, 1974), moved to the USA to further his studies, obtaining a MSc (1976) and a PhD (1980) in physics from the University of Chicago, wherein his doctoral thesis was supervised by the renowned astrophysicist Eugene N. Parker. Research associate at Chicago's Enrico Fermi Institute (1980–1981) and the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (1981–1984), Lecturer at Harvard University (Department of Physics,1983–1984), Professor of Physics at the University of Crete and researcher at the Foundation for Research & Technology – Hellas (1984). In 2001 he was appointed professor of astrophysics at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens by the honorary appointment of invitation. His visiting professor appointments include world-renowned institutions such as the University of Turin (1991), the Paris Observatory and the University of Paris VII (1992), the University of St Andrews (1992), the University of Porto (1994) and the KU Leuven (1996).

== Scientific Contributions ==
Tsinganos's research has focused on plasma astrophysics and magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). Indicative multi-part series of scientific papers are (i) “Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes", by E.N. Parker and K. Tsinganos [ref: Bernoulli forces on an elliptical cylinder by a nonuniform flow, Physics of Fluids] [ref: Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes. IV. Aerodynamic lift on a thin cylinder in convective flows., Astrophysical Journal] [ref: Sunspots and the physics of magnetic flux tubes. X - On the hydrodynamic instability of buoyant fields, Astrophysical Journa] (ii) "MHD equilibrium" by K. Tsinganos, for obtaining exact solutions of the full set of the MHD equations under the assumption of one-ignorable coordinate in a system of general curvilinear coordinates [ref: Magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium. I. Exact solutions of the equations, Astrophysical Journal] [ref: Magnetohydrodynamic equilibrium. II. General integrals of the equations with one ignorable coordinate, Astrophysical Journal], (iii) "Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows", 10 papers focused on obtaining exact solutions of the MHD equations appropriate for cosmic winds and jets under the assumptions of radial or meridional selfsimilarity, developed by K. Tsinganos and collaborators, including C. Sauty, E. Trussoni, N. Vlahakis, and others [ref: Analytical studies of collimated winds. I. Topologies of 2-D helicoidal hydrodynamic solutions, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: An analytical MHD wind model with latitudinal dependences obtained using separation of the variables, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: Nonradial and nonpolytropic astrophysical outflows. IV. Magnetic or thermal collimation of winds into jets?, Astronomy and Astrophysics]. This study includes, as special cases, known polytropic models, such as the Parker description of a solar/stellar wind and the Blandford & Payne description of a magnetorotational disk wind. Among the results is an energy integral and criterion distinguishing the formation of collimated jets from uncollimated winds (TS94) and how protostellar jets play the role of the ex machina Deus by intervening in collapsing protostellar disks to give birth to stars, inside dark nebulae. (iv) MHD simulations for the magnetic collimation of the solar and stellar winds by S. Bogovalov, K.Tsinganos, T. Matsakos, A. Mignone and others. [ref: Magnetic collimation of the solar and stellar winds, Astronomy and Astrophysics] [ref: Magnetic collimation of relativistic outflows in jets with a high mass flux, Monthly Notice of the Royal Astronomical Society] [ref: Shock formation at the magnetic collimation of relativistic jets, Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society] [ref: Two-component jet simulations. Kinedyne is an American manufacturer of cargo securement, cargo capacity, and cargo access products for the transportation industry. Founded in 1968, the company manufactures and distributes products used in commercial trucking, logistics, military, aerospace, and government applications. The company operates facilities in the United States and maintains operations in Canada, Mexico, and China. [ref: Kinedyne Continues to Revolutionize Cargo Control After 55 Years, Work Truck Online] [ref: Kinedyne: Company Profile & Ownership, Mergr]

== History ==
Kinedyne was founded in 1968 as a manufacturer of cargo control products for the transportation industry. The company initially focused on cargo securement equipment used in freight transportation and trucking applications. [ref: Kinedyne Continues to Revolutionize Cargo Control After 55 Years, Work Truck Online]

In 1990, Kinedyne began operations at a facility in Lawrence, Kansas after acquiring assets associated with the Cargo Control Division of Aeroquip Corporation. Originally established as a warehousing operation, the facility later expanded to include manufacturing activities such as the fabrication of cargo nets and strap assemblies. [ref: Kinedyne Celebrates 20 Years of Manufacturing Excellence at Kansas Facility, Work Truck Online] [ref: Kinedyne facility celebrates two decades in business, Truck News]

By the 2000s, the Lawrence operation had evolved into a hub supporting logistics, global purchasing, customer service, quality assurance, and testing functions, including for military load securement equipment. [ref: Kinedyne Celebrates 20 Years of Manufacturing Excellence at Kansas Facility, Work Truck Online]

The company expanded its cargo management offerings during the late twentieth century beyond traditional tie down and securement products to include decking systems and engineered cargo capacity solutions intended to increase freight efficiency. [ref: Kinedyne Continues to Revolutionize Cargo Control After 55 Years, Work Truck Online]

In 2013, Kinedyne was acquired by The Heico Companies, a privately held industrial holding company based in Illinois. The acquisition included Kinedyne's Lawrence, Kansas manufacturing facility while allowing the company to continue operating under the Kinedyne name. [ref: The Heico Companies Acquires Kinedyne, Mergr] [ref: Large conglomerate purchases Kinedyne and its Lawrence plant in East Hills, Lawrence Journal-World]

In 2019, Kinedyne opened an additional distribution facility in Prattville, Alabama. The expansion followed the consolidation of engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, quality control, customer service, and government contract functions within the company's Alabama operations. [ref: Kinedyne opens new distribution facility, Refrigerated & Frozen Foods]

== Products and operations ==
Kinedyne manufactures and distributes cargo control products including winches, cargo straps, chains, logistics track systems, cargo beams, decking systems, curtain side trailer systems, and engineered cargo management solutions. Its products are used across commercial transportation, logistics, agriculture, moving and storage, automotive transport, and recreational vehicle markets. [ref: Kinedyne: Company Profile & Ownership, Mergr]

Kinedyne serves military and government customers through its Kinedyne Defend division. Introduced in 2022, the division focuses on military grade cargo securement products meeting National Stock Number (NSN), National Aerospace Standards (NAS), and MIL-SPEC requirements. The product line includes nearly 350 active NSN products used in aerospace, aviation, maritime, rail, and defense applications. [ref: Kinedyne introduces 'Kinedyne Defend' military product line, Fleet Equipment Magazine]

== Patents ==
Kinedyne and its subsidiaries have been assigned patents relating to cargo securement systems, adjustable decking assemblies, logistics track systems, vehicle restraint mechanisms, and wheelchair securement technology. [ref: Patents Assigned to KINEDYNE LLC, Justia Patents] [ref: Patents Assigned to Kinedyne Corporation, Justia Patents]

In 2025, a United States design patent for a cargo securement logistics track assigned to Kinedyne LLC was published by the United States Patent and Trademark Office. [ref: US D1,082,494 S Cargo-securement logistics track, United States Patent and Trademark Office]

== Ownership ==
Kinedyne is owned by The Heico Companies, which acquired the company in 2013. The acquisition added Kinedyne to Heico's portfolio of transportation and cargo related businesses. [ref: The Heico Companies Acquires Kinedyne, Mergr]

== [user] ==
[user] (IBC) is a British website providing reviews of children’s books with a focus on diversity and inclusion. It also organises the annual [user] Book Awards, and provides funding to other not-for-profit organisations that work to improve inclusion in children’s books and access to these. The charity is registered in the United Kingdom under charity number 1201129. [ref: [user] - Charity 1201129, prd-ds-register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk]

== History ==
The charity was founded in 2022 by Marcus and Sarah Satha following the couple’s experience of finding children’s books that reflected the multiracial composition of their family. [ref: Inclusive books: founder of Inclusive books Sarah Satha talks to Jake Hope, Pen & Inc]

Before establishing the charity, Marcus and Sarah Satha consulted a range of organisations and individuals involved in children’s literature, education and libraries. These included BookTrust, CILIP and the Centre for Literacy in Primary Education (CLPE).

The website's aim was to be a resource where families could locate reviews of children’s books and search for books that included different forms of representation and inclusion. The website was launched in September 2023 at the Centre for Literacy in Primary Education headquarters in London. [ref: Charity launches award and database to encourage diversity in children’s books, The Guardian]

The charity has subsequently undertaken advocacy and training with schools, libraries and literacy organisations to promote awareness and use of the website.

== Services ==

=== Review Website ===
The charity’s review process focuses on children’s books featuring human characters.  Books considered for review are primarily aimed at children aged between birth and nine years.  Fabia Turner, Head of Content for the organisation, described the review process in an interview with Pen & Inc Magazine in 2023 [ref: Pen&Inc10 Autumn/Winter 2023, content.yudu.com].

The charity states that it intends to expand the age range of books covered by its reviews when sufficient review capacity is available.

=== Book Awards ===
The [user] Book Awards were inaugurated in 2024 [ref: The Catchpoles, Sumana Seeboruth and Zanib Mian win inaugural £30k [user] Prize, The Bookseller]. The awards have three categories: books for babies and toddlers; picture books; and highly illustrated fiction.

Books are nominated by publishers annually and considered by the organisation before a longlist is produced.  A judging panel then selects a shortlist and an overall winner in each category. Category winners receive a shared of a £10,000 prize fund [ref: Winners of the inaugural [user] Book Awards – Books For Keeps, booksforkeeps.co.uk] [ref: New charity [user] launches inaugural awards worth £30,000, The Bookseller], divided between the author and illustrator of the winning book.

In 2026, the organisation piloted a shadowing scheme through which children and families could vote for their preferred winners [ref: ReadingZone, ReadingZone].

=== Book Box Scheme ===
[user] operates a book box scheme through which schools and community groups can apply for collections for 100 children’s books. The scheme is intended to support communities identified by the organisation as having a particular need for access to contemporary diverse and inclusive children’s books. [ref: IBC Book Box: free books for schools, [user]]

=== Small Grants ===
The charity provides annual grants to other not-for-profit organisations undertaking projects intended to improve inclusion in children’s books or access to such titles.

=== Research ===
The charity publishes an annual report examining representation in children’s literature focusing on the work of writers and illustrators from under-represented groups. Findings have been reported via the media outlets such as children's news programme Newsround. [ref: ReadingZone, ReadingZone] [ref: Book and diversity: New report calls for more representation in children's books, BBC Newsround] [ref: Excluded Voices report, [user]].

IBC are critical of the ‘own voices’ phrase with concerns about the use of the term as a broad category for literature by under-represented creators and about assumptions concerning the subjects that such creators should write about.

IBC reports also examine particular areas of representation and barriers experienced by writers and illustrators.

Higher Up Texas (HUT) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization based in Dickinson, Texas, that provides life skills education, professional development, financial literacy, critical thinking, and career exploration and guidance to young adults transitioning from high school into adulthood. [ref: Higher Up Texas Inc, ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer] [ref: Dickinson program helping students 'bloom' in high school and beyond, ABC13 Houston]

Founded in 2019, the organization serves students attending Dickinson High School, La Marque High School, and Texas City High School in Galveston County, Texas. [ref: Higher Up Texas, Cause IQ] [ref: FAQs, Higher Up Texas]

Higher Up Texas operates a three-phase program beginning with classroom instruction during students' senior year of high school. Following graduation, the organization provides individualized guidance, career development support, and connections to professional opportunities. The program also engages alumni as mentors and speakers. [ref: FAQs, Higher Up Texas] [ref: Dickinson program helping students 'bloom' in high school and beyond, ABC13 Houston]

== History ==

Higher Up Texas originated in 2018, when Rick Gornto and Tony Annunziato began discussing gaps in resources, opportunities, and professional networks available to young adults transitioning from high school into adulthood. Later that year, the founders met with leadership at Dickinson High School to propose a program addressing these challenges. [ref: HUT Happenings – April 2022, Higher Up Texas]

In June 2019, Hillary Gramm joined the organization and developed its initial life skills curriculum. The program launched in August 2019 with a founding class of 27 seniors at Dickinson High School. [ref: Learning for Life, The Daily News]

In spring 2020, the organization adapted its programming in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The disruption contributed to the development of its second program phase, which provides continued guidance and support following high school graduation. [ref: Learning for Life, The Daily News]

In 2023, Higher Up Texas expanded into Texas City Independent School District, adding programs at Texas City High School and La Marque High School. [ref: Higher Up Texas, Higher Up Texas] The organization operates a three-phase model encompassing high school preparation, post-graduation guidance, and alumni engagement. [ref: FAQs, Higher Up Texas]

Aristide Saggino is an Italian psychologist and psychotherapist, and former full professor of psychometrics at the University of Chieti–Pescara. [ref: Curriculum vitae – Aristide Saggino, Open Science Framework] He is co-author of the Teate Depression Inventory and served two terms as national president of the Italian Association for Behaviour Analysis and Modification and Behavioural and Cognitive Therapy (AIAMC). He is known for his advocacy of scientifically grounded, evidence-based psychotherapy.

== Education and career ==
Saggino graduated in psychology from Sapienza University of Rome in 1979 and completed a specialization in clinical psychology there in 1992. He received a PhD in psychology from the Pontifical Salesian University in 2000, with a dissertation on the Myers–Briggs Type Indicator.

From 1979 to 2001 he worked as a psychologist in the Italian national health service in Campania, while conducting research on psychological testing at Sapienza University from 1985 to 1999. In 1994, supported by a CNR–NATO Senior Fellowship, he was a research fellow at the University of Exeter with psychometrician Paul Kline, with whom he co-authored studies of the Italian Myers–Briggs Type Indicator. [ref: Item factor analysis of the Italian version of the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator, Personality and Individual Differences] Between 1998 and 2007 he was repeatedly a visiting professor at the Institute of Psychiatry, King's College London, working on personality theory and assessment.

He joined the University of Chieti–Pescara as associate professor in 2001 and was full professor from 2006 until his retirement in 2026. Since October 2026 he has been scientific director of the postgraduate schools of cognitive behavioural psychotherapy of the Centro per lo Studio della Personalità (CSP), which are recognised by the AIAMC. He chaired the undergraduate programme in psychological sciences from 2005 to 2012 and headed the university's Psychometrics Laboratory and its laboratory for research on cognitive behavioural and evidence-based psychotherapy (LARIPSI).

He was national president of the AIAMC from 2014 to 2017 and again from 2020 to 2024. [ref: Psicoterapia e Salute Mentale: incontro con il Prof. Saggino a EXPO, State of Mind] [ref: Gli organi sociali – Past Presidents, AIAMC] [ref: 12a Conferenza Internazionale di Applied Behavior Analysis – programma ECM, University of Chieti–Pescara] [ref: La Psicoterapia Cognitiva e Comportamentale in Italia oggi – Intervista al Prof. Aristide Saggino, State of Mind] During his first term, in March 2016, the AIAMC became the first Italian association to have its training programmes accredited by the European Association for Behavioural and Cognitive Therapies (EABCT). [ref: Accredited associations, European Association for Behavioural and Cognitive Therapies] From 2017 to 2023 he was the AIAMC's representative to the EABCT. Since 2019 he has been vice-president of IACABAI, the Italy Associate Chapter of the Association for Behavior Analysis International formed by AIAMC and AARBA. [ref: About us, IACABAI] From 2012 to 2020 he chaired the Abruzzo–Molise section of CICAP, the Italian skeptics' organization.

== Research ==
Saggino's research covers the construction and validation of psychological tests, individual differences with a focus on psychometric theories of intelligence, and cognitive behavioural therapy.

With Michela Balsamo he developed the Teate Depression Inventory (TDI), a self-report measure of depression built using the Rasch model. [ref: TDI – Teate Depression Inventory. Manuale, Hogrefe] [ref: Building a new Rasch-based self-report inventory of depression, Neuropsychiatric Disease and Treatment] In the United States, the construct validity of the TDI has been the subject of graduate theses at Eastern Illinois University, including studies with Black/African American and Middle Eastern/Arab American samples. [ref: Construct Validity of the Teate Depression Inventory with a Black African American Sample, Eastern Illinois University] [ref: Construct Validity of the Teate Depression Inventory (TDI) with a Middle Eastern/Arab American Sample, Eastern Illinois University] [ref: Construct Validity of the Teate Depression Inventory: Convergent and Discriminant Validity and Equivalence for Black/African American and White/Caucasian Samples, Eastern Illinois University]

He has also led Italian adaptations of several instruments, including the Myers–Briggs Type Indicator, the Eysenck Personality Profiler and the WPPSI-IV.

Since 2022 he has served on the scientific advisory board of the Treatments That Work series of Oxford University Press, edited by David H. Barlow. [ref: Treatments That Work – Editorial Board, Oxford University Press]

He has also been active in public outreach on evidence-based psychotherapy; in 2015, for example, he spoke at Expo 2015 in Milan in a round table titled "Towards an evidence-based psychotherapy". On 26 October 2023 he testified as an expert before the 10th Standing Committee of the Italian Senate during its examination of bills on the employment of people with autism spectrum disorders. [ref: 10ª Commissione Affari sociali, sanità, lavoro pubblico e privato, previdenza sociale del Senato della Repubblica, Radio Radicale]

=== 1. Early life and background ===
Emeka Okonkwo, popularly known as E-Money, is a Nigerian businessman and entertainment executive. Born February 18th 1981 in the tough highly populated Ajegunle. It is clear money was a scarce resource in his upbringing. His roots trace back to Uli village in Ihiala Local Government Area of Anambra State, in the South-East of Nigeria.He has never hidden this identity and represents it through his many acts of giving through his career. On the 30th of June 2022, alongside Nigerian billionaire Kennedy Okonkwo, a donation of N100M was donated to the government of Anambra state to tackle insecurity. [ref: Anambra: Obi Cubana, E-Money, others donate N100m to tackle insecurity, Punch Newspapers]

Okonkwo grew up in Ajegunle, Lagos State, Nigeria. His family had connections to music through his father, who worked as a disc jockey and sold musical records. While their mother, Martha Okonkwo, provided emotional and domestic support. Okonkwo and his brother Kcee also developed an early interest in music and worked as disc jockeys before establishing their careers in business and entertainment. The family was not raised in wealth. Okonkwo worked as a manager for his elder brother Kcee showing a strong relationship between the two from the beginning. [ref: E-Money used to be my manager, I made money before him – KCee, The Sun Nigeria]

Although he became widely known for his wealth and lifestyle, Okonkwo has also discussed his early business experiences and his interest in working behind the scenes to develop musical talent. He is known for his association with the Nigerian music industry and his role in the development of Five Star Music, a record label associated with many influential nigerian musicians. Such as Kcee, Skiibii, SoSo Soberekon and Harrysong. [ref: Five Star Music]

=== 2. Education ===
E-Money completed his primary education at Ajegunle Primary School, the same as his elder brother Kcee.

To fund his education and to support his family, he reportedly took on menial jobs during his school years, showing his hustling mentality at a young age.

For tertiary education, E-Money pursued a Bachelor of Arts in Political Science, with a concentration in the American Government and Political Systems from Elizabeth City State University. His academic journey did not stop there. Recognising his extraordinary accomplishments in business, he was awarded an Honorary Doctorate Decree in Business Management, Hence the honorary title “Dr” that is often used. [ref: E-Money Reveals The Institution He Got His Doctorate Degree From, 102.3 Max FM]

=== 3. Career ===

==== Early business activities ====
Before becoming widely recognised as an entertainment executive, Okonkwo was involved in commercial activities, including importing goods and automobiles. In a 2015 interview reported by Pulse Nigeria, he and his wife discussed his involvement in business and his work as a licensed Nigeria Customs Service agent. [ref: 5 Star Music boss, wife talk about their rags to riches love story, Pulse Nigeria]

Okonkwo has also been associated with shipping and cargo-related businesses. [ref: EMY CARGO AND SHIPPING SERVICES UK LIMITED people - Find and update company information - GOV.UK, find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk]

Entry into the entertainment industry

Okonkwo developed an interest in music from an early age. In an interview published in 2015, he explained that he preferred working behind the scenes rather than pursuing a career as a performing artist.

His work in entertainment included songwriting and composing before he became more closely associated with music management and record-label operations. His partnership with his brother Kcee became an important part of his public profile.

=== 4. Five Star Music ===
Okonkwo is widely associated with Five Star Music, a Nigerian record label linked to the career of his brother Kcee.

The label became known for its involvement in Nigerian popular music and for working with recording artists, including Kcee. Other artists associated with the label during its development included Harrysong and Skiibii, according to Nigerian entertainment reporting.

The label’s activities contributed to Okonkwo’s recognition as an entertainment executive rather than solely as a businessman.

==== Relationship with Kcee ====
Kcee, whose full name is Kingsley Chinweike Okonkwo, is E-Money’s brother and a Nigerian singer.

Their professional relationship combines family ties with business and entertainment activities. In a 2024 interview, Kcee discussed their shared background in disc jockeying and their father’s influence on their early exposure to music. Reporting on the interview also identified E-Money as a co-founder of Five Star Music.

=== 5. Business interests ===
Beyond entertainment, Okonkwo has been associated with commercial activities in shipping, importing and real estate.

Draft text:
Kimaya Diggs (born 1992 or 1993) is an American singer-songwriter based in Northampton, Massachusetts. Her music combines acoustic and indie-folk foundations with elements of soul, R&B and jazz. She has released three studio albums as an independent artist: Breastfed (2018), Quincy (2023) and Green (2026).

== Early life ==
Diggs grew up in western Massachusetts, the daughter of a Black father and an Indian mother. As a child she played music with her two sisters, learning instruments including cello, violin and viola. She attended college in Pennsylvania before returning to western Massachusetts.

== Career ==
=== Breastfed (2018) ===
Diggs released her debut album, Breastfed, in 2018. It was made with bassist Jacob Rosazza. Most of the songs feature Diggs accompanying herself on acoustic guitar, with occasional cello. WBUR later described the record as contemplative and self-produced in character.

=== Quincy (2023) ===
Diggs began work on her second album before the COVID-19 pandemic and continued it through 2020. In 2021 her mother died of cancer, a close friend and musical mentor was killed in a bicycle accident, and her dog, a retired racing greyhound named Quincy, died. The album was named after the dog. Diggs aimed for a fuller sound than on her debut, and her father contributed flute to three tracks.

Quincy was released on March 9, 2023, preceded by the singles "If You Love Me" and "Rainbow". Under the Radar characterized the album's style as indie pop with R&B and soul elements. In a 2023 profile, WBUR highlighted the album's retro-influenced R&B arrangements and noted that Diggs did not regard it as an album about grief. Later that year she released an EP of live versions of songs from the album.

=== "Everything Is Not Lost" (2024) ===
In 2024 Diggs released the single "Everything Is Not Lost", which she described as more dance-oriented than her earlier work. She photographed the single's cover art herself.

=== Green (2026) ===
Diggs released three singles ahead of her third album: "I Know That I'm Perfect", a rock-influenced track, followed by "Dance with Me" and "Plants (Still Grow)". Green was released on October 2, 2026. It is the first of her albums on which she is credited in a production role: she co-produced the record and engineered roughly a quarter of it. She and her partner, also a musician, converted the basement of their Northampton home into a studio and rehearsal space. Eighty-two artists from western Massachusetts contributed to the album.

The album explores the question of what makes a place feel like home and Diggs's relationship with the region where she grew up. The song "A Sense of Place" addresses the racial isolation she experienced in New England. The title refers to the point each spring when trees leaf out almost all at once.

== Live performance ==
Diggs has performed as a supporting act for artists including Mavis Staples, Trombone Shorty, Emily King and Tank and the Bangas.

== Discography ==

* "Everything Is Not Lost" (2024)
* "I Know That I'm Perfect" (2026)

Seth Josel (born 1961) is an American guitarist, electric guitarist, banjoist, educator, and writer specializing in contemporary classical and experimental music. He is known for his performances of contemporary repertoire and for collaborations with composers including Helmut Lachenmann, Mauricio Kagel, Tristan Murail, Louis Andriessen, Gavin Bryars, and James Tenney. He has participated in the premieres of more than one hundred works and has appeared as a soloist and ensemble musician throughout Europe, North America, and Japan. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website]

== Early life and education ==
Josel was born in New York City in 1961. [ref: Seth Josel, Cybele Records] He studied at the Manhattan School of Music, earning a Bachelor of Music degree, and subsequently attended Yale University, where he received Master of Music, Master of Musical Arts, and Doctor of Musical Arts degrees. His principal teachers included Manuel Barrueco and Eliot Fisk. [ref: Seth Josel, Orpheus Institute]

== Career ==
Beginning in the 1980s, Josel established an international career as a performer of contemporary music. From 1991 until 2000, he was a permanent member of Ensemble Musikfabrik (then musikFabrik NRW). [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website]

As a soloist and ensemble musician, Josel has performed with the New York Philharmonic, BBC Symphony Orchestra, Berliner Philharmoniker, Rundfunk- Sinfonieorchester Berlin, American Composers Orchestra, and numerous contemporary music ensembles. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website] [ref: Seth Josel, Orpheus Institute]

His festival appearances have included the Salzburg Festival, Donaueschinger Musiktage, Holland Festival, Munich Biennale, Huddersfield Contemporary Music Festival, MaerzMusik, and musikprotokoll Graz. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website] [ref: Seth Josel, Orpheus Institute]

Josel has collaborated closely with composers including Peter Ablinger, Richard Barrett, Gavin Bryars, Mauricio Kagel, Helmut Lachenmann, Olga Neuwirth, Sarah Nemtsov, Tristan Murail, Ming Tsao, and James Tenney. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website]

In addition to his performing activities, Josel has given lectures and masterclasses at institutions including Yale University, Northwestern University, California Institute of the Arts, the Universität der Künste Berlin, and the Musik-Akademie Basel. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website] In 2022, he joined the Hochschule für Musik Carl Maria von Weber Dresden as a lecturer in guitar. [ref: Biography, Seth Josel Obicial Website] He is also a co-founder of Sheer Pluck, an online database and research resource devoted to contemporary guitar repertoire. Draft: Neostoic Foolism

Draft text:
Neostoic Foolism sees philosophy and its whole point is to find a way to live. What's your way to live? How do you see life? Your vision on it. Philosophy is to question life / knowledge / morality, etc., and so far I have been exploring different philosophies, from popular ones to lesser-known ones; I have seen many, but for a way of life that genuinely checks all the marks, I have yet to find. And so I question for my reasoning to find that it simply does not exist and will not. It combines Christian theology with Stoicism, as well as Tabula Rasa (life as a blank canvas; present-moment action of Existentialism), finished with the radical, unburdened freedom of the Fool. And so you see, when you take these elements and combine them, you get, in what I see, the best way of life. ( Yes, this philosophy inscribes itself in the ethics/moral branch of philosophy ) (it has been very recently developed)

Christian theology is the anchor of the philosophy. Each ideology has a base, something it can rely on, and the core of Neostoic Foolism lies here with Søren Kierkegaard. The "Knight of Faith" of Kierkegaard described the true man of faith as someone who looks entirely ordinary, even foolish to society, yet inwardly walks hand-in-hand with God, completely unbothered by worldly opinions. He argued that life isn't an abstract system to be solved, but a reality to be lived through individual, passionate choices, and understood that trying to gain status, approval, and ego-fulfillment from a broken society is absurd. True freedom comes when you stop playing the world's games and live authentically before God. With Christian theology, morality is not subjective anymore but absolute exist; you are made in the image of God and have dignity that you must preserve and live in accordance to Lord’s will.

This alone brings a way of life that few philosophies do, because living as a true Christian is defined not by hollow ritual or performative righteousness, but by a radical, active love that pours out into everyday life. It means embodying genuine kindness in a harsh world, rolling up your sleeves to help the vulnerable and the neighbor in need, and choosing to forgive others deeply and repeatedly even when it is difficult. True Christian living is marked by mercy, humility, and an uncalculated willingness to serve, reflecting the very heart of God through concrete actions rather than mere words. It’s walking the extra mile, and letting go of the desperate need for public applause or self-preservation. But it is also to be a truth-seeker; to abandon the exhausting rat-race of worldly anxiety and status-seeking. It means refusing to let the crowd dictate your worth, releasing the need to hoard prestige, and trusting so completely in your divine security that you can walk through life light, unbothered, and entirely free. Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied. Don't judge a human being because you do not know the suffering and the pain that God allowed to be buried in their person. Don't judge anyone who struggles with an addiction, who struggles with a passion, who struggles with a sin, because you do not know what lies hidden in the ground. Look at the context and try to have compassion. Look at the context and try to be humbled. How can we judge when we ourselves walk as imperfect men?

Nevertheless, it's about living in the present as well. Anxiety (Angst) about the future, worrying about status, security, failure, and what the crowd thinks happens when we try to be our own gods, desperately calculating every outcome to protect our fragile egos. Jesus cuts straight through this by commanding us not to worry about tomorrow, pointing to the birds of the field and telling us that each day has enough trouble of its own. He calls us out of the future-tripping trap and into a radical, unburdened presence in the now (Carpe Diem if you want). It is a leap of faith. Before you can leap, you have to stand at the edge of a cliff. For Kierkegaard, that cliff is human reason and logic. When trying to prove everything objectively, claiming that if you just think hard enough, the universe will make total, logical sense, Kierkegaard argued that this is an illusion. When it comes to the deepest questions of existence: suffering, death, love, and ultimate meaning, pure logic hits a wall. You cannot mathematically prove or rationally deduce how you ought to live or why your life matters. Objective proof runs out. Once you realize that objective reason cannot give you a definitive safety net for your existence, you are left standing over an abyss. If you demand absolute, 100% objective proof before you make any meaningful choice or commitment in life, you will be paralyzed forever. The "Leap" is the moment you realize that action must precede certainty. It’s a passionate, conscious decision to step out into the unknown and commit yourself to a path, a truth, or a purpose.

Draft text:
San Pedro Daijingū () was a Shinto shrine serving the Japanese American fishing community on Terminal Island in Los Angeles, California. Its Japanese name appears in the 1937 community history San Pidoro Dōhō Hattenroku. [ref: 第32回 「サンピドロ同胞発展録」― 日本の海岸線の旅の途中で①, Discover Nikkei]

== History ==
Shinkichi Miyoshi proposed establishing the shrine in 1930. A lease for its site at 226 Terminal Way was approved in March 1931, and a ceremony marking construction of its foundation took place on 6 December that year. In 1933, the organization incorporated in California under the name San Pedro Daijin-Gu. [ref: Terminal Island: Lost Communities on America's Edge, Angel City Press]

Following the forced removal of Terminal Island's Japanese American residents in 1942, the United States Navy demolished the shrine along with most of the settlement's buildings. [ref: Japanese American History at Terminal Island, Los Angeles Conservancy]

== Architecture ==
The shrine consisted of a small, single-room building in Japanese architectural design. A torii and two fox statues marked the entrance to the property. [ref: Fishermen Far from the Sea: Excavation of the Block 9 Mess Hall Japanese Garden, National Park Service]

== Legacy ==
The Terminal Island Japanese Memorial, dedicated in 2002, includes a torii recalling the community's former Shinto shrine. [ref: Terminal Island, Preserving California's Japantowns]

Draft: Swindon Railway Village

Draft text:
The Works transformed Swindon from a small 2,500-population market town into a bustling railway town. Built to the north of the town centre, the works had need for locally accessible housing and services for the workers. The development of the railway village was on the lines of similar Victorian era socially-encompassing lifestyle concepts, such as that at Bournville but architect/builder Rigby's signed an agreement in February 1841 to build 300 cottages at their own expense. [ref: Swindon The Legacy of a Railway Town, HMSO] The completed village provided to the town medical and educational facilities that had been sorely lacking, The large St Mark's Church was built in 1843-45. The Bakers Arms public house was built as a shop with accommodation above in 1846. [ref: Former Bakers Arms Public House, 16 Emlyn Square, Historic England] The Cricketers' public house was built in 1846. [ref: 14 Emlyn Square, formerly The Cricketers Public House, Historic England]

Construction of the Railway Village began in 1841. In 1891 it had around 287 houses, a large mechanics' institute, a market with capacity for 32 shops and standings for thirty stalls, a cottage hospital, a park, an Anglican church, a Methodist chapel, swimming baths and a medical dispensary. The financial difficulties of the contractors J.D. & C. Rigby, who undertook to build 300 cottages but only completed 130, delayed the completion of the village until the 1850s. The cottages to the west of Emlyn Square were built first (1842–43), followed by those on the east side (1845–1847). The end blocks towards Emlyn Square, having corner shops on the ground floor, were built in 1845–1847, and the remainder, mostly end blocks on the outer ends of the streets, in 1853–1855. In 1966, the local authority acquired the cottages from British Rail and restored them. The village is one of Britain’s best-preserved and architecturally most ambitious railway settlements. [ref: 30-50, Exeter Street, Swindon, SN1 5EF, Historic England] [ref: Made in Swindon a social history 1840s-1940s; The Architectural Legacy of Swindon Railway Village, The Hobnob Press]

The terraced two-storey cottages were built on two blocks of four parallel streets, not dissimilar in appearance to passing trains. Each road was named after the destinations of trains that passed nearby: Bristol, Bath, Taunton, London, Oxford and Reading among them. Built in the nearby open area, named Emlyn Square after GWR director Viscount Emlyn (later known as John Campbell, 1st Earl Cawdor), was the Mechanics Institute (MI). Designed and constructed by Edward Roberts, the MI was completed in 1855. It contained one the UK's earliest public lending libraries and provided health services to workers. The GWR Medical Fund Baths and Dispensary (which housed Victorian Turkish baths from 1906) were built in 1891–92, becoming the NHS Health Centre and Milton Road Baths in 1947 and the Health Hydro in 1986. The Mechanics' Institute (founded in 1843) moved into a purpose-built building in 1854. [ref: Made in Swindon a social history 1840s to 19140s, The Hobnob Press] The Mechanics' Institute building was closed in February 1986 [ref: We're Left in the Cold, Swindon Advertiser] and remains unoccupied. The Barracks were built in 1853–55 as a lodging house but became a Wesleyan chapel in 1867, the GWR Museum in 1962 and then The Platform (Swindon Music Service) in 2000. The Armoury, built in 1862, became the GWR Hospital in 1871, a Workers' Club in 1960 and the Central Community Centre in 1979. [ref: Swindon in 50 Buildings, Amberley Publishing] The GWR Park, adjacent to St Mark's Church, was acquired in 1844. The Octagonal Market started in 1892 and was demolished in 1977. A house and shop built in the 1840s became a public house in the 1850s and is now the Glue Pot public house. [ref: Swindon An Illustrated History, The Breedon Books Publishing Company Limited]

In 1846-1847 a terrace of 16 cottages was built on the north side of Faringdon Road (Nos 4-34). One of the last houses to be built, 34 Faringdon Road, originally 1 Faringdon Street is now the 'Railway Village Museum' and is maintained as a typical railwayman's house of about 1900. It retains original features such as glazing, window sashes, margin lights and plank door. [ref: 4-34, Faringdon Road, Swindon, SN1 5BJ, Historic England] [ref: Railway Village Museum, Swindon Heritage Preservation]
link=File:20261022_Park_House.jpg|thumb|Park House
1876 saw the GWR directors agree to build a house and surgery combined. The house, Park House, was for the company’s chief medical officer and his family and was built in 1876-77. Built in yellow brick with stone dressings and a slate roof. Three stories and basement. [ref: Park House, Church Place, Swindon, SN1 5ED, Historic England] [ref: A Century of Medical Service, Great Western Railway Medical Fund Society] Park House today provides serviced offices. [ref: Park House, total Guide to Wiltshire]

In the 1960s, the Borough of Swindon municipal council applied to demolish much of the village, but poet and railway enthusiast John Betjeman [ref: No 3: GWR Railway Village, Born Again Swindonian] led a successful campaign to preserve it. Today the Railway Village is part of the Swindon Railway Conservation Area, and many structures within it are listed buildings. [ref: Railway Village, Swindon.co] [ref: Swindon railway conservation area appraisal and management plan, Swindon Borough Council]

Andion CH4 Renewables SAS, also known as Andion CH4, is a Luxembourg-based renewable energy company with its operational headquarters in Milan. The company develops, finances and operates facilities that produce biogas and biomethane from organic waste. [ref: Goldman Sachs Alternatives backs European biogas developer Andion with €67m credit facility, Bioenergy News] Founded in 2017, it has operations and projects in countries including Italy and Sweden. [ref: Andion CH4 Renewables, LinkedIn] [ref: Andion CH4 gets EUR-24m loan for its 1st biomethane plant in Italy, Renewables Now] [ref: Groundbreaking held for Eskilstuna Biogas bioLNG, Bioenergy International] Jonas Martin-Löf is the company's chief executive officer and chairman, while Mattias Pihlgren is deputy chief executive officer and CIO. [ref: About, Andion CH4 Renewables]

== History and financing ==
The company was founded in 2017. For a period, it was legally domiciled in Canada before returning to Luxembourg. The move was completed before a capital raise announced in January 2025. Investors included Equitix New Generation Fund, which was funded by an investment company associated with Ikea. [ref: GSK Stockmann advises Andion CH4 Renewables on the first capital raise after its migration from Canada to Luxembourg, GSK Stockmann]

In February 2026, Andion secured a €67 million credit facility from Goldman Sachs Alternatives. The financing, together with new equity from existing shareholders, was intended to support the company's project portfolio in Italy and the Nordic region. In March that year, the company was reported to have secured €24 million in project financing for a facility in Mirandola in northern Italy.

== Operations and projects ==
Andion's activities include the development, construction, financing and operation of facilities that convert organic residues into biogas or biomethane.

The company and its technology operations have delivered more than 50 anaerobic digestion facilities, as well as numerous advanced wastewater treatment facilities in Europe and North America. Andion owns or holds stakes in several biogas and biomethane facilities in Italy and Sweden. [ref: Andion Global, BDC Capital]

=== Sweden ===
Andion is involved in the development of Eskilstuna Biogas, a liquefied biogas facility outside Eskilstuna. The project has been carried out with partners including Gotlandsbolaget and Equitix New Generation Fund. In 2025, Wärtsilä announced that Andion Scandinavia AB had commissioned it to supply biogas upgrading and liquefaction technology for the facility. Its planned production capacity was stated as up to 17 tonnes of bio-LNG per day. [ref: Wärtsilä to supply Andion Scandinavia AB with bioLNG solution for new biogas plant in Sweden, Wärtsilä]

The Swedish company Andion Scandinavia AB was registered in 2021. According to its company registration, its activities include the development, construction, management and maintenance of waste and energy facilities. [ref: Andion Scandinavia AB, Allabolag.se]

=== Italy ===
In Mirandola, in the Emilia-Romagna region, Andion is developing a facility to produce biomethane from organic residues. In 2025, industrial gas company SOL Group acquired a 20 per cent minority stake in Biomethan Green 1, the project company controlled by Andion Italy. Investment in the facility was reported to exceed €20 million. [ref: SOL Group joins Andion in €20m+ bioLNG plant project with offtake deal, Gasworld]

During 2026, Andion expanded its portfolio of facilities in Italy. In January, it became the majority owner of the Enerland facility in Baricella, in the province of Bologna. The facility had a capacity of approximately 11 GWh and was intended to be converted from biogas-based electricity generation to biomethane production. [ref: Acquisition of the Enerland plant in Northern Italy, Andion CH4 Renewables] [ref: Explore our assets, Andion CH4 Renewables]

In February 2026, the company announced that it had signed a binding agreement to acquire the Cella Dati facility in the province of Cremona. Its existing capacity was stated as approximately 44–45 GWh, with a planned expansion to 56 GWh. [ref: Acquisition of the Cella Dati plant, Andion CH4 Renewables] In May, Andion signed a binding agreement to acquire the Q Energia facility in Quargnento, in the province of Alessandria. The facility had a capacity of approximately 22 GWh and was to be converted from biogas-based electricity generation to biomethane production. [ref: Acquisition of the Q Energia plant, Andion CH4 Renewables]

In June 2026, Andion signed a binding agreement to acquire a majority stake in the Agromet facility in Barbianello, in the province of Pavia. The press release stated an installed capacity of approximately 42 GWh, while the company's subsequent overview of its assets listed 44 GWh. [ref: Acquisition of the Agromet plant, Andion CH4 Renewables]

== Management ==
Jonas Martin-Löf is the company's chief executive officer and chairman. Mattias Pihlgren is deputy chief executive officer and CIO. He has worked at Andion since 2017, including in business development and fundraising. [ref: Mattias Pihlgren, Andion CH4 Renewables]

Vibin Baskar is an Indian music composer, music producer, and independent artist who works primarily in the Tamil and Kannada film industries. He is known for composing music for the Tamil ZEE5 original web series Sattamum Neethiyum (2025), Veduvan(2025), Thadayam(2026), Kaakee Circus(2026) and Sattamum Neethiyum 2 (2026) for which he created both the songs and the background score. He has also composed music for Tamil and Kannada feature films. He has released several independent Tamil songs.

== Early life and Education ==
Vibin Baskar is based in Chennai, Tamil Nadu. He completed a Bachelor of Business Administration from Alagappa University before earning a Master of Business Administration from the same institution in 2014. His interest in music began during childhood after being enrolled in piano classes by his mother. He later pursued formal training in western music from Trinity College London in Piano and Music Theory. He completed his Bachelor's degree in Audio Engineering and Recording Arts from the School of Audio Engineering. During this period, he also performed as a keyboardist in live shows across Chennai.

== Career ==
Vibin Baskar began his professional career in 2012 as an Audio Engineer, Chennai. In 2013, he became Assistant Music Director and worked with composer James Vasanthan, contributing to music production and programming. From 2017 onward, he started composing music independently for South Indian films, television productions and OTT platforms.

=== Film and Television ===
Sattamum Neethiyum 2 (2026)

Kaakee Circus (2026)

Thadayam (2026)

Veduvan (2025)

Sattamum Neethiyum (2025)

Vibin Baskar composed the songs and original background score for the Tamil court room drama web series Sattamum Neethiyum 1& 2, released on ZEE5 in 2025 and 2026. The series received positive reviews, with several critics highlighting vibin's music as one of its major strengths.

== Samharini ==
Vibin Baskar composed the music for the Kannada-language feature film Samharini, where he was credited as Vibin Baskar (V2).

== Independent Music ==
Alongside his work in films, Vibin is active in the Tamil independent music scene. He maintains the YouTube channel VibinBaskar, where he publishes original compositions, music videos, behind-the-scenes content and promotional material for his projects.

His independent works include:

* Chellame

== Reception ==
Vibin Baskar's work on Sattamum Neethiyum received positive critical attention. Reviews published by Cinema Murasam, Angusam, and Hindu Tamil Thisai praised his background score for enhancing the emotional depth of the narrative and supporting the performances. Critics particularly highlighted the courtroom sequences and climax episode for their effective musical treatment. Although one review considered the series' title song stylistically inconsistent with the realistic tone of the drama, the overall reception to the soundtrack and score was positive.

Draft text:
Brondell is a manufacturing company based in the United States that produces bathroom and home utility products. The company has received investment from entrepreneur Mark Cuban and has acquired shower technology company Nebia.

== Overview ==
Brondell manufactures products for residential and light commercial use across several categories related to bathroom e, and indoor air quality. Its product range includes bifixtures, water usdet toilet seats and bidet attachments, integrated smart bidet toilets, standard and filtered toilet seats, kitchen and bathroom faucets, showerheads and shower filtration systems, drinking water filtration systems, and air purifiers. [ref: Bottom line means more to this firm, SFGATE]

The company’s products are sold through direct-to-consumer channels, third-party e-commerce platforms, and brick-and-mortar retail partners in the United States, with distribution extending to selected international markets.

== History ==
Brondell was founded in 2003 in the United States by Dave Samuel. The company was named after J.F. Brondel, an English architect who developed the first valve flush toilet in 1738. In its early years, the company focused on the development and sale of bidet-related products for the North American market.

In 2005, Brondell received a $1.3 million investment from entrepreneur and Dallas Mavericks owner Mark Cuban. [ref: High-Tech Investor Cuban Gives Toilet-Seat Maker $1.3 Million - WSJ, Wall Street Journal] As the company expanded, it introduced additional product categories related to household water use and sanitation, followed by products addressing indoor environmental conditions. Over time, its product offerings grew to include bidet toilet seats, bidet attachments, integrated smart bidet toilets, kitchen and bathroom faucets, shower filtration systems, and air purification devices.

The company subsequently expanded its distribution model to include direct-to-consumer sales through its website, partnerships with national retail chains, and listings on major e-commerce platforms. During the 2010s, Brondell products were exhibited at industry trade events, including the Kitchen & Bath Industry Show (KBIS). In the same period, the company received recognition through third-party design and product awards. In 2023, Brondell acquired Nebia, a company specializing in shower and water technology.

== Philanthropy ==
Brondell participates in philanthropic initiatives through its membership in the 1% for the Planet network. As part of this program, the company allocates a portion of sales from select bidet attachment products to nonprofit organizations focused on environmental and community-related causes. The company has partnered with nonprofit organizations on time-limited campaigns addressing issues such as water conservation, environmental restoration, food insecurity, and public health awareness. In addition to financial contributions, Brondell employees have taken part in volunteer activities, including habitat restoration projects and food distribution programs conducted in collaboration with regional nonprofit organizations. [ref: Best Filtered Shower Heads 2026 - Forbes Vetted, Forbes]

== Awards and Recognition ==

* Good Housekeeping VIP Product Award
* Design Journal ADEX Platinum Award Home Magazine American Building Products Award
* Design Bites People’s Pick Award (2022, 2023)
* KBB Award for Best Kitchen Accessory (2022)
* Silver CLIO Award for Product Design (2017)
* Fast Company Innovation by Design Awards recognition
* Best of KBIS awards in multiple categories

The San Diego County Bar Association (SDCBA) is a professional association for lawyers and other members of the legal community in San Diego County, California. Founded in 1899, the organization supports the legal profession through professional education, public service, lawyer referral, judicial candidate evaluations, pro bono initiatives, and community programs. Over its history, the SDCBA has also helped establish and support organizations serving people who need legal assistance. [ref: 100 years and counting for San Diego's lawyers, archive.calbar.ca.gov]

== History ==

The SDCBA was founded on April 22, 1899 as the Bar Association of San Diego. During a meeting at the newly established San Diego Superior Court, San Diego lawyer Eugene Daney Sr. was elected as the organization's first president. [ref: Footprints of Justice in San Diego: Profiles of senior members of the bench and bar, San Diego County Law Library] A graduate of Hastings College of the Law, Daney would later become the president of the San Diego Lawyers Institute, established in 1919 by a group of lawyers interested in discussing law review articles, ethics and fee cutting. The Institute, which later merged with the SDCBA, became one of the nation's first regulatory law organizations, screening applicants, disciplining attorneys, and working to simplify legal proceedings.

Over time, the SDCBA participated in the launch of several organizations and programs that provide legal assistance or conflict resolution services in San Diego. For instance, In 1919, the SDCBA created the first Office of the Public Attorney. Local attorney DeWitt C. Mitchell died in 1918 while serving in the Army Air Corps during World War I. DeWitt's dream of creating a public attorney to represent the rights of all citizens, as well as a bequest of $20,000 to the SDCBA from DeWitt's estate, spurred the formation of the Office of the Public Attorney, providing people living in poverty with access to a free civil lawyer. In 1953, the Office incorporated and changed its name to the Legal Aid Society of San Diego (LASSD). LASSD continues to operate as a nonprofit law firm, providing free legal services to lower income San Diego residents. [ref: About, Legal Aid Society of San Diego]

The SDCBA played a major role in the creation of Appellate Defenders, Inc. (ADI) in 1972. Originally known as Defenders, Inc., ADI was formed to improve the quality of representation in appointed criminal appeals. With SDCBA sponsorship and federal grant funding, ADI used experienced staff attorneys to handle appeals and supervise a panel of private attorneys. In 1980, all ADI employees were hired by the State Public Defender, and the organization became inactive. In 1983, the budget cuts led to the closure of the State Public Defender's office in San Diego. To help it reorganize, ADI sought a $30,000 start-up loan from the SDCBA, which was approved. ADI then resumed operations in 1983, and the loan helped kickstart the organization back into service. [ref: Public defenders for poor restored, The San Diego Union] ADI eventually expanded its work across California's Fourth Appellate District. [ref: ADI's History, Appellate Defenders, Inc.]

In 1983, the SDCBA teamed with the University of San Diego School of Law to create the San Diego Volunteer Lawyer Program (SDVLP). The program was designed to be a clearinghouse for pro bono legal services, connecting volunteer legal professionals with people who could otherwise not afford legal representation. SDVLP continues to provide free legal assistance to disadvantaged individuals and families across San Diego County. [ref: ]

SDCBA and University of San Diego School of Law also teamed up in 1983 to launch the San Diego Mediation Center, which provided community-based alternative dispute resolution services. The center later became known as the National Conflict Resolution Center (NCRC). Through mediation, conflict resolution, and other related services, NCRC strives to reduce conflict, intolerance, and incivility in our modern society. [ref: About NCRC – Conflict Resolution & Mediation Experts, National Conflict Resolution Center]

The SDCBA and its members are often on the frontlines of disaster relief and pro bono service. Following the Southern California wildfires of 2003, the SDCBA led the San Diego County Disaster Relief Coalition, bringing together more than 20 bar-related organizations and law firms to help those affected by the fires. The Coalition setup a toll-free information hotline, recruited and trained volunteer lawyers, and helped arrange legal assistance for homeowners and others displaced. For its efforts, the Coalition was recognized by the State Bar of California with the Distinguished Pro Bono Service Award in 2004. [ref: California Bar Journal, archive.calbar.ca.gov]

== Lawyer Referral and Information Service ==
In 1952, the SDCBA launched the Lawyers Reference Plan, which intended to help members of the public connect with attorneys who handle particular legal matters. Lawyer referral services help members of the public identify appropriate legal assistance and, depending on the service, obtain an initial consultation at a reduced or no cost. [ref: ] The service, one of the first of its kind, is known today as the Lawyer Referral and Information Service and is certified by the State Bar of California. [ref: ]

Draft: Rajali Birds Park

Draft text:
Rajali Birds Park is a privately owned interactive aviary, zoological exhibition, and eco-tourism attraction located in Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu, India. Situated approximately 100 meters from the peripheral parking grounds and visitor facilities of the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Brihadeeswara Temple, the park functions as a major urban wildlife tourism hub within the Thanjavur district. It is characterized primarily by its immersive, cage-free walk-in aviary design, which distinguishes it from conventional regional zoological parks.

History and Development

The establishment of Rajali Birds Park was conceived to diversify the tourism profile of the Cauvery Delta region, which historically relies predominantly on cultural, religious, and architectural heritage tourism. Developers sought to introduce a modern, interactive wildlife exhibit modeled after contemporary international aviaries. By selecting a site adjacent to the city’s primary historic monument, the park was integrated into the high-density tourist corridor of Thanjavur, capitalizing on the heavy foot traffic generated by the temple complex.

Architecture and Enclosure Design

The park's architectural centerpiece is a large-scale, high-clearance steel and mesh dome enclosure. This structural design is engineered to optimize airflow and mimic localized microclimates while preventing the escape of non-native species.

The interior environment integrates elements of both natural landscape architecture and synthetic containment infrastructure:

* Arboreal Canopies: The enclosure incorporates pre-existing mature trees alongside curated tropical flora, providing natural nesting, perching, and foraging spaces for the avian population.
* Aquascaping: Simulated streams, waterfalls, and shallow wading pools are distributed throughout the enclosure to facilitate natural bathing behaviors and maintain ambient humidity levels necessary for tropical species.
* Visitor Walkways: Elevated and ground-level paved pathways isolate human foot traffic to designated zones, ensuring minimum disruption to ground-dwelling avian behaviors while maximizing visitor sightlines.

Avian Collection and Taxonomy

Rajali Birds Park houses a diverse inventory of over 1,000 birds, comprising dozens of species across several taxonomic orders. The collection focuses heavily on exotic, visually distinct, and socially gregarious species capable of thriving in a dense, multi-species communal habitat.

Psittaciformes (Parrots and Allies)

The park features a significant concentration of psittacines, known for their bright plumage and high cognitive capabilities. Notable exhibits include:

* South American Macaws: Including large-bodied blue-and-gold macaws (Ara ararauna) and green-winged macaws (Ara chloropterus).
* Australian Cockatoos: Including sulphur-crested cockatoos (Cacatua galerita) and various smaller corellas.
* Neotropical Conures: Diverse flocks of sun conures (Aratinga solstitialis) which fly freely in synchronized groups throughout the dome.
* Australasian Parrots: Extensive populations of budgerigars (Melopsittacus undulatus) and cockatiels.

Passeriformes and Columbiformes

A wide variety of smaller soft-billed birds inhabit the lower and mid-canopy layers. This includes various mutations of domestic lovebirds (Agapornis), exotic finches, and ground-dwelling ornamental doves, which occupy specialized niches within the ecosystem.

Ratites and Large Enclosures

Dedicated, barricaded ground paddocks house large, flightless ratites. These include African ostriches (Struthio camelus) and Australian emus (Dromaius novaehollandiae), which are separated from the main walk-in dome due to their size and distinct management requirements.

Other Fauna

To broaden its appeal to younger demographics and school tour groups, the park maintains a secondary petting zoo sector. This area is occupied by domesticated small mammals, primarily European rabbits (Oryctolagus cuniculus) and guinea pigs, housed in low-walled contact pens.

Visitor Interaction and Educational Programs

The operational philosophy of Rajali Birds Park emphasizes direct human-animal interaction as a tool for public engagement. Under the strict supervision of trained park handlers, visitors are permitted to purchase or receive approved grain and seed mixtures. This facilitates hand-feeding, during which various psittacines and passerines land directly on visitors' hands, arms, and shoulders.

The educational framework of the park includes:

* Species Identification Boards: Informational plaques detailing the common names, binomial nomenclature, native geographical distribution, natural diet, and IUCN Red List conservation status of each prominent species.
* Guided Interpretive Walks: Staff members conduct informal educational sessions for visitors, highlighting the ecological importance of bird conservation and the threats of habitat destruction in tropical rainforests.

Veterinary Care and Husbandry

To sustain a high-density, multi-species population within a confined airspace, the park implements strict veterinary and husbandry protocols. The birds are provided with specialized diets tailored to their taxonomic requirements, consisting of fresh fruits, sprouted seeds, nuts, and mineral supplements. Regular sanitation of the enclosures, water filtration systems, and quarantine procedures for newly acquired or symptomatic birds are maintained to prevent the introduction or spread of avian pathogens.

Over time, he acquired the nickname “The Farmfoods Lord”, alongside the title “The Best Buyer”, which became central to his reputation among his friends.

His unofficial title of “Farmfoods Lord” further distinguishes him from other trainspotters, although the precise origins of the title remain a matter of local legend.

Rivalry with Rhys Wright

Legacy

Leland Fitzpatrick remains known by the titles “The Farmfoods Lord” and “The Best Buyer” within the circle in which these nicknames originated. His rivalry with Rhys Wright forms a central part of his unofficial legend.

Central Maine Healthcare (CMH) is a non-profit integrated healthcare delivery system based in Lewiston, Maine. It serves approximately 400,000 residents in central, western, and mid-coast Maine. Since February 2026, it has been a member of the Prime Healthcare Foundation.

== History ==
Central Maine Healthcare was established as an integrated system in 1982. It originally operated as an independent regional health system centered around Central Maine Medical Center in Lewiston.

In January 2025, CMH announced an agreement to affiliate with the California-based Prime Healthcare Foundation. The transaction closed on February 16, 2026, making Prime Healthcare Foundation the sole corporate member and parent organization of Central Maine Healthcare. As part of the agreement, Prime Healthcare Foundation committed to investing $150 million over five years in facilities, services, and infrastructure across the CMH system. CMH hospitals and facilities retained their names. Local leadership structures were retained in the initial period after closing, though subsequent leadership changes have occurred, including the appointment of a new chief executive officer in March 2026.

== Facilities ==
Central Maine Healthcare includes the following main facilities:
* Central Maine Medical Center (Lewiston) — flagship hospital (formerly a Level III Trauma Center; ACS verification lapsed in December 2025, with state conditions requiring re-establishment by 2028)
* Bridgton Hospital (Bridgton)
* Rumford Hospital (Rumford)
* Central Maine Comprehensive Cancer Center
* Central Maine Heart and Vascular Institute
* Maine College of Health Professions
* Rumford Community Home
* Bolster Heights (assisted living)
* More than 40 outpatient physician practices

== Affiliation with Prime Healthcare Foundation ==
On February 16, 2026, Prime Healthcare Foundation completed its affiliation with Central Maine Healthcare, becoming the sole corporate member and parent organization. The transaction expanded Prime Healthcare Foundation’s portfolio to 21 not-for-profit hospitals across eight states. Under the structure, Central Maine Healthcare continues to operate its facilities under their existing names while becoming part of the larger Prime Healthcare network. The affiliation was subject to regulatory conditions imposed by the Maine Department of Health and Human Services, including commitments regarding essential services and trauma-center status.

== Services ==
CMH provides a full range of healthcare services, including:
* Primary and specialty care
* Emergency and trauma services
* Cancer care
* Cardiovascular services
* Surgical services
* Medical education through the Maine College of Health Professions

Draft: Michael Needham

Draft text:
Michael "Mike" Needham is a retired British police officer who served with Lancashire Constabulary in England and later as a superintendent in the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service (RCIPS). [ref: Gunning for you!, Lancashire Telegraph] [ref: Another top cop leaves, Cayman Compass] During his career in the Cayman Islands, Needham headed the RCIPS Financial Crime Unit and Marine Unit and was involved in the development of the service's financial-crime, intelligence and marine capabilities. [ref: Needham retires from RCIPS, Cayman News Service] He received the Colonial Police Medal in the 2009 Birthday Honours.

==Police career==

===Lancashire Constabulary===

Needham served with Lancashire Constabulary before moving to the Cayman Islands. A contemporary report in the Lancashire Telegraph in March 1997 identified him as Acting Chief Inspector Mike Needham in the Lancaster and Morecambe area.

The report concerned a Lancashire police road-safety initiative introduced following a series of fatal and serious road accidents. Needham said that police analysis had identified speeding as a significant factor in accidents on rural roads and described the deployment of mobile speed-camera enforcement as part of the police response.

An account of his career published at the time of his retirement from the RCIPS stated that Needham had served with Lancashire Constabulary for more than three decades before moving to the Cayman Islands.

===Royal Cayman Islands Police Service===

Needham joined the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service in January 1999 as a detective chief inspector with responsibility for the Commercial Crime Branch. He was promoted to detective superintendent in May 2003.

In 2001, Needham was involved in establishing the Joint Intelligence Unit, which brought together personnel from the police, customs and immigration authorities. He subsequently established the Financial Crime Unit and became its head.

As head of the Financial Crime Unit, Needham was the senior police officer publicly associated with a number of financial investigations in the Cayman Islands. In August 2008, the Cayman Compass reported on several investigations being conducted by the unit and quoted Needham on the time and resources required to investigate complex financial cases. The matters included investigations relating to the Affordable Housing Initiative, financing arrangements for the Boatswain's Beach development and failed Cayman-domiciled investment funds. [ref: Police ask for patience, Cayman Compass]

In March 2009, the Cayman Compass described Needham as a high-ranking member of the RCIPS command staff and identified him as the superintendent responsible for the Financial Crime Unit.

===Marine Unit===

Needham also headed the RCIPS Marine Unit and oversaw a programme to expand and modernise the Cayman Islands' marine law-enforcement capability.

In February 2007, the Cayman Compass reported that Needham was overseeing plans for a new joint marine base for the police, customs and immigration authorities. The Cayman Islands government had committed approximately CI$5 million to the proposed facility. Plans associated with the expansion included a 65-foot patrol vessel, fast interceptor vessels and increased staffing. [ref: $5M marine base planned, Cayman Compass]

The programme also involved the acquisition of the Cayman Defender, one of a number of new law-enforcement vessels. Reporting in September 2008 identified Needham as project leader for the programme, which formed part of a CI$7.7 million investment in border protection. [ref: Marine cops get new boat, Cayman News Service]

==Retirement==

Needham retired from the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service in March 2009 after approximately ten years with the service. Contemporary reports stated that his retirement brought to an end a policing career of approximately 41 years in the United Kingdom and the Cayman Islands.

At the time of Needham's retirement, acting commissioner of police James Smith said that Needham had "clearly achieved a great deal" during his policing career and referred to his contribution to the RCIPS.

==Honours==

Needham received the Colonial Police Medal in the 2009 Birthday Honours for his service with the Royal Cayman Islands Police Service.

==References==
