Draft text:
Yangjiaping (杨家坪) most commonly refers to a major, bustling commercial and residential subdistrict located in the Jiulongpo District of Chongqing, China. Known historically as one of the city's oldest industrial hubs, it has evolved into a vibrant urban destination famous for its massive pedestrian shopping street, modern high-rises, and unique multi-layered transit infrastructure. A major hub on Line 2 and Line 18 of the Chongqing Rail Transit network. Line 2 is famous for its monorail trains that weave dramatically through and around the city's mountainous high-rises. Historically, Yangjiaping is also famous in religious history as the location of the Our Lady of Consolation Abbey. Established in 1883 by French Catholic Trappist monks in the rugged mountains of Hebei province (just outside the Great Wall), it grew into a prominent monastery. However, it was tragically destroyed in August 1947 during the Chinese Civil War when Communist forces burned it down during what is known as the Yangjiaping Massacre. Thus, the name historically means "The Yang Family's Flat Land," indicating that these locations originally began as settlements established by families sharing the Yang surname on level terrain.

Leslie James Milton, Sr is an American drummer, singer and bandleader born in 1938 [ref: Leslie Milton, Discogs].  His career includes music played in and around New Orleans, LO [ref: Modern Jazz Concert, L.L.A Auditorium, 2700 S. Claiborne Ave, New Orleans LO, The Louisiana Weekly] [ref: Talented Musicians have new 'Jazz" Idea, The Louisiana Weekly], San Francisco, CA [ref: Jazz, The Beat of the City, San Francisco Examiner], Los Angeles, CA [ref: Sonny, Cher Impressive, Los Angeles Citizens News], Long Beach, CA [ref: In Person: Judy, Les, John and Steve are 'Something New' and they are Truly Something Special, The Independent], and the Pacific Northwest (WA [ref: Put me on the Guest List: Strypes, Isaac Scott, Blue Lights, The Rocket] [ref: Blues Calendar, The Rocket] [ref: Leslie Milton's Stardoms Big Band Laser Blues, The Rocket] [ref: Jolly Roger 8721 Lake City Way, The Rocket] [ref: Thursday 3: Leslie Milton's Star Drums, The Rocket] [ref: Special: Leslie Milton's "Star Drums", The News Tribune] [ref: Meadow Park Golf Course, The News Tribune] [ref: Big-mama blues, The Spokesman-Review Spokane Chronicle] [ref: Leslie Milton's Star Drums, The Rocket] [ref: Bluestars know their business, The Spokane Review Spokane Chronicle] [ref: Owl Cafe, The News Tribune] [ref: Ticket Alert, The News Tribune] [ref: Hot Summer Jazz, The Rocket] [ref: New Orleans Restaurant, The Rocket] [ref: Melody Ballroom, The Oregonian]).

Early Life and Education

Leslie James Milton, Sr., better known by his current stage name Leslie “Star Drums” Milton [ref: The Chat: Talkin' blues, space and loose garbage with Leslie 'Star Drums' Milton, Heraldnet.com] [ref: Leslie "Star Drums" Milton & the Star Drums Light Show, https://wablues.org/bluesletter/], is an American drummer and bandleader.   His motto is: ”Listen, Concentrate, and have Fun!”

Milton was born in New Orleans, Louisiana. He began his drumming career "at about 5 years old, playing little toy drums. It was a passion. I saw my uncle play drums and he took me under his wing. That was it, I was a drummer." His uncle was Ernest ‘The Kid’ Milton, a well-known show drummer in New Orleans, [ref: ] who taught him the art of drumming and showmanship.   While attending Joseph S. Clark Sr. High School, [ref: ] Milton joined the marching band led by Yvonne V. Bush [ref: Yvonne Busch Obituary (2014) - New Orleans, LA - The Times-Picayune, Legacy.com] [ref: ].   Milton met his wife Janice Carol Thornton while in 9th grade and they married when he was 19 years old.

Early Career

As a teenager and through his early 20s, Milton played drums professionally in and around New Orleans and traveled with Roy "Good Rockin" Brown [ref: ] to New York to play in Brown's orchestra at the Apollo Theater. Milton also played in a variety of burlesque halls and night clubs in New Orleans including one led by Bill Senegal [ref: Bill Sinegal, wikilink].

In 1961, Milton moved to Los Angeles, CA where he had an active career as a session and touring musician.  Milton worked with "Robert Bumps Blackwell"   [ref: Robert Blackwell, wikilinks] for Mercury Records. Blackwell at the time was managing Sam Cooke and Little Richard with whom Milton participated in session recordings.  "Bumps" hired Milton to back "Bessie Griffin and the Gospel Pearls" for the "Ed Sullivan Show". [ref: Bessie Griffin, wikipedia]  Milton was an active session musician working on studio tracks with a variety of musicians including Johnny Otis, Etta James, Little Richard, Jackie DeShannon, Roy Brown, Ike & Tina Turner and Connie Stevens. He performed regularly with "Sonny and Cher". [ref: Leslie "Star Drums" Milton Still Having Fun Doing What He Loves, The Seattle Times]. Milton played with the Watts' 103rd Street Rhythm Band on American Bandstand performing their hit called "Spreading Honey" [ref: American Bandstand Episode #11.4, YouTube]. In 1962, Milton recorded "Papa-Oom-Mow-Mow" with The Rivingtons. [ref: Papa-Oom-Mow-Mow, Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia]. Milton also appeared, uncredited, in the movie, The Hotel [ref: The Hotel, Hotel (1967 film)], playing drums in the scenes showing the cabaret go-go dancers, visible at about 90 minutes in the film.

Milton also performed in bands supporting musical scenes in several "Alfred Hitchcock" thrillers. For instance, in the TV episode of Alfred Hitchcock Presents (1961), "You Can't Trust a Man", [ref: Alfred Hitchcock Presents season 6, Wikipedia, The Free Encyclopedia] he can be heard playing drums for a nightclub vocalist who walks into her room and says "I asked for drums in the last number, not an active uprising. Musicians!"

In 1976, inspired by America's Bicentennial Celebration, Milton created his persona as Leslie 'Star Drums' Milton.  He used his 'extra-terrestrial' imagination to take the audience on an imaginary journey into space using special effects and show drumming. At that time, Milton was the drummer for the Something New group. He performed drum solos including the 'Space Odyssey' show that included special lighting effects, creating a feeling of a rocket flight deep into outer space. These 'show drumming' performances evolved into his persona as Leslie 'Star Drums' Milton. The band also played several original songs by Milton including Gator Joe and Somebody Make it Right.

Jahsean Corbett (born July 1, 2002) is an American professional basketball player who plays for the CD Español Osorno team in Liga Nacional de Básquetbol (LNB). [ref: Jahsean Corbett – CD Español Osorno, LatinBasket] He played college basketball for Chicago State and Duquesne. [ref: Jahsean Corbett Player Profile, ESPN]

== Early life ==
Corbett was born in Orlando, Florida, and attended West Oaks Academy, where he played high school basketball. [ref: 2022-23 Men's Basketball Roster, Chicago State Cougars]

== Career ==

=== Chicago State ===
Corbett played three seasons for Chicago State from 2021 to 2024. [ref: Jahsean Corbett College Stats, Sports-Reference] In 2022, he represented the U.S. Virgin Islands in the 2022 FIBA AmeriCup.

=== Duquesne University ===
For the 2024–25 season, Corbett transferred to Duquesne University [ref: West Oaks basketball gains 3 transfers and scrutiny, Orlando Sentinel] and joined the Duquesne Dukes men's basketball program. [ref: Duquesne to receive official visit from productive Chicago State transfer guard Jahsean Corbett, Yardbarker]

Before committing to Duquesne, Corbett received interest from programs including Miami, Mississippi State, UAB, Virginia Tech, Utah State, Bowling Green, Loyola Chicago, Illinois State, UMBC, and UTEP.
Corbett recorded a double-double with 13 points and 10 rebounds in a 67–55 victory over Rhode Island. [ref: Jahsean Corbett propels Duquesne to 67-55 victory over Rhode Island, CBS Sports]

In another game, Corbett scored a career-high 29 points and grabbed six rebounds, but ultimately Duquesne lost 77–71 to Davidson. [ref: Jahsean Corbett's 29 points not enough as Duquesne falls to Davidson, TribLIVE]

== Professional career ==
In 2026, Corbett started playing professionally for CD Español Osorno in the Liga Nacional de Básquetbol. In August 2026, he scored 35 points in a game and was named the league's Player of the Week. At the time, he was averaging 25.3 points per game, making him the league's leading scorer.

On March 22, 2026, Corbett, along with the entire CD Español Osorno team, won the Chery Super Cup, qualifying for the South Conference of the 2026 Ligo UNO. [ref: Español de Osorno was crowned champion of the 2026 Chery Super Cup, Radio Sago]

Also, in August 2026, Diario de Osorno described Corbett as Español de Osorno's best player for that month. [ref: Español de Osorno closed the Zonal Phase with a loss on the road, Diario de Osorno]

James Baca (born April 21, 1983) is an American journalist, author, podcaster, and consumer advocate based in Las Cruces, New Mexico. He is the founder and publisher of AGGREGATOR, an independent publication covering New Mexico State University athletics, and has produced consumer advocacy commentary under the name The Notorious Banker.

Baca's reporting on New Mexico State athletics has been credited by the Albuquerque Journal, the Las Cruces Sun-News, and Sports Illustrated. [ref: NMSU fires running backs coach, general manager, Albuquerque Journal] [ref: NMSU GM, RBs coach David Cobb fired, Las Cruces Sun-News] [ref: Former New Mexico State Softball Coaches Speak Out After Sexual Misconduct Allegations, Sports Illustrated]

== Early life and education ==

Baca grew up in Socorro, New Mexico, and graduated from Socorro High School in 2001.

He attended Eastern New Mexico University–Roswell, where he earned an associate degree in 2008. He subsequently attended Eastern New Mexico University in Portales, earning a bachelor's degree.

== Career ==

=== Banking and consumer advocacy ===

Baca worked for Bank of America from 2005 to 2018. Following his banking career, he began producing consumer-oriented commentary concerning banking practices, customer service, financial institutions, and consumer rights.

He developed the podcast The Notorious Banker, originally known as Why Your Bank Sucks. The program discussed retail banking, consumer experiences, financial products, and corporate accountability. [ref: The Notorious Banker, Apple Podcasts] [ref: The Notorious Banker, Spotify]

His consumer commentary has also appeared through independent publications, including Consumer Beast and Terms & Conditions.

=== Journalism and AGGREGATOR ===

In November 2023, Baca founded AGGREGATOR, an independent, subscription-supported publication based in Las Cruces, primarily covering New Mexico State University athletics.

According to Baca, the publication was established in response to what he considered insufficient local media coverage of New Mexico State's football program during its successful 2023 season. The Aggies finished that season with a 10–5 record and appeared in the Conference USA Football Championship Game. Baca argued that the program's accomplishments were not receiving sustained coverage from traditional local news organizations. [ref: About AGGREGATOR, AGGREGATOR]

Baca has also identified his dissatisfaction with coverage of controversies surrounding the university's men's basketball program as a factor in establishing the publication. These included the November 2022 shooting involving New Mexico State basketball player Mike Peake and the hazing scandal that led to the cancellation of the remainder of the 2022–23 men's basketball season.

Baca has criticized what he perceived as sensationalized coverage of those controversies, arguing that some local reporting emphasized negative developments while providing comparatively limited attention to other university athletic programs. These views formed part of his stated motivation to develop an alternative source of coverage focused on New Mexico State athletics.

AGGREGATOR publishes game reports, statistical analysis, interviews, commentary, and coverage of athletic administration. Its reporting includes football, men's and women's basketball, volleyball, soccer, and other university sports.

The publication also addresses conference realignment, collegiate athletics finances, media rights, and issues affecting Southern New Mexico.

In July 2026, the Albuquerque Journal and Las Cruces Sun-News credited Baca and AGGREGATOR with first reporting the dismissal of New Mexico State running backs coach and general manager David Cobb.

In September 2026, Sports Illustrated referenced Baca's reporting concerning statements obtained from former New Mexico State softball coaches Kathy Rodolph and Cat Heifner during coverage of allegations involving the university's softball program.

=== Athlon Sports ===

Baca has stated that he contributed freelance material to Athlon Sports, including its annual college football preview publication.

His work included material concerning New Mexico State's football program, including team analysis and depth-chart information. [ref: Jody Adams Resurfaces as Head Coach, AGGREGATOR]

== Recognition ==

Baca was listed among the finalists for Best Local Newspaper Columnist in the Las Cruces Bulletin annual Bulletin's Best recognition for 2024–25. [ref: Bulletin's Best 2024–25, Las Cruces Bulletin]

== Writing and public commentary ==

=== Local journalism and media ownership ===

Baca has written critically about the consolidation of local newspapers and television stations under national media companies, including Gannett, Nexstar Media Group, and Sinclair Broadcast Group.

His commentary has addressed newsroom staffing reductions, centralized editorial decision-making, and the effects of corporate ownership on reporting about local institutions.

He has argued that reduced newsroom resources can diminish coverage of community affairs and collegiate athletics, particularly in smaller media markets such as Southern New Mexico.

=== Mental health awareness ===

Baca has expressed support for mental health awareness and has criticized what he considers inadequate institutional responses to mental health crises.

Gábor Ágoston is a historian of the Ottoman Empire and a professor of history at Georgetown University. His research concerns Ottoman warfare and relations with other early modern empires, including diplomacy and intelligence gathering. [ref: Gabor Agoston, Georgetown University School of Continuing Studies]

== Education and career ==

Ágoston received his master’s degree from Eötvös Loránd University and his PhD from the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. He taught at the universities of Budapest and Pécs before joining Georgetown in 1998. In 2003, he was a visiting professor at the University of Vienna. He is also affiliated with Georgetown’s Center for Eurasian, Russian and East European Studies. [ref: Georgetown University Faculty Directory, gufaculty360.georgetown.edu]

== Scholarhip ==

Ágoston’s scholarship examines Ottoman military institutions, weapons production, and relations with European powers. In Guns for the Sultan: Military Power and the Weapons Industry in the Ottoman Empire (2005), he used archival records to investigate firearms manufacture, gunpowder production, and military supply. He challenged explanations of Ottoman military technology based on religious conservatism, arguing that adaptation and pragmatism shaped the adoption and production of weapons. [ref: Project MUSE -- Verification required!, muse.jhu.edu]

In The Last Muslim Conquest: The Ottoman Empire and Its Wars in Europe (2021), Ágoston placed Ottoman warfare and expansion within the broader history of European power politics. He argued that Ottoman expansion depended on military capabilities alongside flexible policies of incorporation and governance. [ref: Gábor Ágoston. The Last Muslim Conquest: The Ottoman Empire and Its Wars in Europe., The American Historical Review] Drawing on Ottoman and Western sources, the book examines the relationship between Ottoman institutions, diplomacy, and warfare and the empire’s interactions with its European rivals. [ref: Michigan War Studies Review - book reviews, literature surveys, original essays, and commentary in the field of military studies, www.miwsr.com]

Ágoston co-edited the Encyclopedia of the Ottoman Empire (2009) with Bruce Masters. The first English-language encyclopedia devoted to the Ottoman Empire, it brought together contributions from 90 scholars. [ref: Encyclopedia of the Ottoman Empire, Reference Reviews] He also co-edited, with David Parrott, War and the Early Modern World (2025), the third volume of The Cambridge History of War. [ref: The Cambridge History of War: Volume 3: War and the Early Modern World, Cambridge University Press]

== Selected publications ==

* Guns for the Sultan: Military Power and the Weapons Industry in the Ottoman Empire. Cambridge University Press, 2005. [ref: Guns for the sultan: military power and the weapons industry in the Ottoman Empire, Cambridge University Press]
* Encyclopedia of the Ottoman Empire. Co-edited with Bruce Masters. Facts On File, 2009. [ref: Encyclopedia of the Ottoman Empire, Facts On File]
* The Last Muslim Conquest: The Ottoman Empire and Its Wars in Europe. Princeton University Press, 2021. [ref: The last Muslim conquest: the Ottoman Empire and its wars in Europe, Princeton University Press]
* The Cambridge History of War, vol. 3: War and the Early Modern World. Co-edited with David Parrott. Cambridge University Press, 2025. [ref: The Cambridge history of war, Cambridge University Press]

Andrew Whitaker (born January 16, 1999) is an American former professional football cornerback and former collegiate track and field athlete. He played football and track and field at Washington University in St. Louis, where he earned NCAA Division III All-American honors, won the NCAA Division III 60-meter hurdles championship in 2022, won the 4×400-meter relay championship in 2019, and was a member of Washington University's men's track and field team that won the 2022 NCAA Division III indoor national championship. [ref: Andrew Whitaker - 2021-22 - Track and Field, Washington University in St. Louis Athletics] [ref: Men's track and field team shares national title at indoor championship, The Source, Washington University in St. Louis]

Whitaker played 39 games for Washington University's football team from 2017 through 2021, starting 30, and recorded 145 tackles, 23 passes defensed and seven interceptions. He later played for the Houston Roughnecks of the XFL before signing with the Seattle Seahawks as an undrafted free agent in 2023. [ref: Andrew Whitaker - 2021 - Football, Washington University in St. Louis Athletics] [ref: Seahawks Sign CB Andrew Whitaker, CB Chris Steele and OLB Levi Bell, Seattle Seahawks]

== College career ==

=== Track and field ===
Whitaker competed in track and field at Washington University in St. Louis while also playing football. He competed primarily in the hurdles and relay events and earned NCAA Division III All-American honors in multiple events.

In 2019, Whitaker was a member of Washington University's 4×400-meter relay team that won the NCAA Division III Outdoor Track and Field Championship. The team recorded a school-record time of 3:09.77.

At the 2021 NCAA Division III Outdoor Track and Field Championships, Whitaker ran the opening leg of Washington University's 4×400-meter relay in the qualifying round and recorded a 45.789-second split. [ref: 2021 NCAA Division III Outdoor Track & Field Championships Results, NCAA Division III]

In 2022, Whitaker competed as a graduate student and won the NCAA Division III indoor 60-meter hurdles championship in 7.943 seconds. [ref: NCAA Division III Indoor Track & Field Championships - Men's 60 Hurdles, TFRRS] He also ran on Washington University's 4×400-meter relay team, which finished second at the championships and earned All-American honors.

Washington University's men's track and field team won the 2022 NCAA Division III indoor team championship. Whitaker scored 10 points for Washington University by winning the 60-meter hurdles and also competed on the 4×400-meter relay team.

=== Football ===
Whitaker played defensive back for Washington University's football team from 2017 through 2021. He appeared in 39 games and started 30, recording 145 tackles, 23 passes defensed and seven interceptions.

In 2021, Whitaker started all 11 games at defensive back, recorded 46 tackles and led Washington University with four interceptions, including a pick-six. He was named First Team All-CCIW and was selected as an Academic All-American and Academic All-District honoree.

Whitaker received the Fritz Pollard Trophy in 2021. The award recognizes college football players for achievements on and off the field and for leadership and commitment to diversity and inclusion. [ref: Highlights - Fritz Pollard Alliance Foundation, Fritz Pollard Alliance Foundation]

He was a semifinalist for the William V. Campbell Trophy in 2020 and 2021. He was also a two-time Academic All-American, a two-time Academic All-District selection and a three-time Academic All-CCIW honoree.

== Professional career ==
After completing his collegiate football career, Whitaker pursued professional football. He attended the University of Missouri's Pro Day in 2022 and later played for the Houston Roughnecks of the XFL. [ref: Athlete Profile: Andrew Whitaker Preps for Draft Day, Washington University in St. Louis Athletics]

=== Seattle Seahawks ===
Whitaker signed with the Seattle Seahawks as an undrafted free agent on July 26, 2023.

According to a report by NFL reporter Aaron Wilson, Whitaker measured 6 feet 1 inch (1.85 m), weighed 192 pounds (87 kg), recorded a 4.37-second 40-yard dash, had a 78-inch wingspan and 10-inch hands, and recorded a 10-foot-6-inch broad jump and 18 repetitions of 225 pounds on the bench press. [ref: Seahawks invited these players to 2023 rookie minicamp, Yahoo Sports]

Whitaker competed for playing time at cornerback and on special teams during the Seahawks' 2023 training camp. He suffered a patellar tendon injury during a team mock game in August 2023 and was waived with an injury designation. After clearing waivers, he reverted to the Seahawks' injured reserve list. [ref: Seahawks Sign DE Jordan Ferguson; CB Andrew Whitaker Waived/Injured, Seattle Seahawks]

The Seahawks released Whitaker on July 25, 2024. [ref: Seattle Seahawks 2024 Transactions, Seattle Seahawks]

== Academics and community service ==
Whitaker studied biomedical engineering at Washington University in St. Louis and graduated with an undergraduate degree in the field in 2021. He subsequently competed as a graduate student at Washington University. [ref: Washington Magazine, August 2022, Washington University in St. Louis]

Cyclone Arnab is a currently active cyclone in the Bay of Bengal threatening southern India. The eighth depression and first cyclone of the 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season, Arnab originated from a low-pressure area in the eastern Bay of Bengal that had been meandering for several days.

==Meteorological history==

At 12:00 UTC on 24 October, a well marked low pressure that had been monitored for days by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) intensified into a depression over the central Bay of Bengal. [ref: REGIONAL SPECIALISED METEOROLOGICAL CENTRE -TROPICAL CYCLONES, NEW DELHI SPECIAL TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK, India Meteorological Department] [ref: REGIONAL SPECIALISED METEOROLOGICAL CENTRE -TROPICAL CYCLONES, NEW DELHI SPECIAL TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK, India Meteorological Department] The system, marked Invest 98B by the United States Navy's Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), consisted of a partially exposed but consolidating low-level circulation and developing banding features to the south and east of the depression’s vicinity as a TCFA was issued at 11:00 UTC. On 25 October at 09:30 UTC, the IMD reported that the system intensified to a deep depression. [ref: REGIONAL SPECIALISED METEOROLOGICAL CENTRE -TROPICAL CYCLONES, NEW DELHI SPECIAL TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK, India Meteorological Department] The next day, the system strengthened into a cyclonic storm and was assigned the name Arnab. [ref: NATIONAL BULLETIN NO. 8 (BOB/08/2026), rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in]

==Preparations==
Andra Pradesh called on boats to return from sea and identified 570,000 people as vulnerable in preparation for evacuations. Odisha announced the closure of schools and colleges in five districts for 28–29 October. [ref: India to evacuate thousands as Cyclone Arnab nears eastern coast, Reuters] By 26 October, Andra Pradesh officials stated that over 30,000 fishing boats had returned to harbour. [ref: ] The Chintoor Integrated Tribal Development Officer directed the suspension of tourism boat operations to the Papikonda hills in Godavari Valley. [ref: Cyclone Arnab: Over 4,800 fishing vessels return safely to Kakinada coast, The Hindu]

The IMD declared red alerts in seven districts in Andra Pradesh on 26 October. The government of Odisha declared that over 1,700 shelters were prepared in the state's southern districts. Eight teams of the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and 40 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force teams were mobilised. [ref: A.P., Odisha on alert as cyclone ‘Arnab’ nears land, The Hindu]

Schools are shut and people in Andhra and Odisha were evacuated. [ref: Cyclone Arnab Live: Schools shut, evacuations begin in Andhra, Odisha ahead of landfall, India Today]

==Impacts==
Persistent rainfall in the Nilgiris district in Tamil Nadu caused as many as 62 landslips on 25 Octoberdamaging power lines, revetments, and 16 hutsand a further seven on 26 October. [ref: Nilgiris district hit by 62 minor landslips in a day till October 25 morning, The Hindu]

Draft: Gaytha Langlois

Draft text:
Gaytha Langlois is an American biologist, academic, university professor and Wikipedia editor. She is officially recognised as the first woman to edit Wikipedia. [ref: Wikipedia often gets taken for granted – but its history is fascinating, and its future is fragile, The Guardian] Her job portfolio ranks her as the past Professor of environmental policy at Bryant University in Smithfield, Rhode Island. [ref: Wikipedia still No 1 after 15 years, The National] [ref: ]

== Career ==
She completed her Bachelor of Science at the Eastern Nazarene College. She pursued her Master of Science at the University of Rhode Island. She obtained Doctorate of Philosophy in the field of Marine Ecology at the University of Rhode Island. [ref: Gaytha Lanlois, Ph.D.]

Prior to the initiative "Women in Red" which had been launched by group of volunteer Wikipedia editors in order to address the gender gap between male and female biographies in Wikipedia, Gaytha had already established herself as the first female Wikipedia editor to edit Wikipedia articles. She began editing Wikipedia in January 2001.

On January 17, 2001, two days after the launch of Wikipedia, Langlois submitted one of the earliest entries in the history of Wikipedia. She published article on “standard poodle”, by her account (during the time of having published the article), had been termed as “a dog by which all others are measured”. [ref: Opinion: How Wikipedia became one of the greatest inventions of the modern age, The Globe and Mail] She also served as Nupedia’s biology and zoology editor for a brief tenure from 2000 to 2001. Her contributions in Wikipedia have gained little attention and largely remains unnoticed according to Richard Cooke, the author of The Last Best Place on the Internet: A Human History of Wikipedia.

She joined as a Professor at Bryant University and lectured in the Science & Technology Department from 1970 until her retirement in 2022. She became the first woman to be employed at Bryant College while simultaneously holding a Ph.D. She has engaged in environmental policy related studies and research activities specifically focusing on protists on the Great Barrier Reef, redwoods in China, grasslands in Inner Mongolia, the after-effects of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster in Russia, Arctic ecosystems, coral reef ecosystems and oil pollution in coastal waters of New England. She was also associated with the International Society of Protistologists and served as its President for a period of two-years from 2019 to 2021. [ref: Women Protistologists Who Set the Stage for Today’s Successes, Part II, International Society of Protistologists]

Jobstore is a global online job search platform headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia with office in Sydney, Australia; Perth, Australia and Singapore.

Jobstore aggregates job listings from thousands of websites, including job sites, staffing firms, associations, application tracking system and company career pages across 50 Asia-Pacific and International markets. [ref: Worldwide Countries, Jobstore]

Jobstore was founded by Anson Wang, who previously founded regional internet ventures including Joukuu in 2010. [ref: Joukuu Lets You Manage Files Across Google Docs, Dropbox And Box.net, TechCrunch]

Jobstore was founded in 2014 in New York City with the aim of helping employers to source and hire the right candidates through their internal employee networks. In 2015, the company moved back to Malaysia and re-launched as an online job distribution platform to serve the South-East Asian employers. [ref: SEA tech startups cannot simply copy Chinese models, TechNode Global (TNGlobal)]

In 2018, Jobstore initiated preparation for an initial public offering (IPO) on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) to finance international market expansion, lodging a public prospectus before deciding to withdraw the application in 2019 to focus on regional organic growth. [ref: ASX aspirant Jobstore pivoted to offer AI to recruiters, Financial Review]

In 2022, Jobstore sold its HR software subsidiary, [https://www.talentcloud.ai talentcloud.ai], to SEA Capital to focus on its core online job search business. [ref: Jobstore sells HR software unit to SEA Capital for $2.6m, www.techinasia.com]

== Funding ==
In October 2018, Jobstore raised an undisclosed amount of equity investment from Malaysia's Cradle Fund Sdn Bhd, a tech co-investment agency under the Ministry of Finance (Malaysia). [ref: Cradle Fund Portfolio Companies, Cradle Fund Sdn Bhd]

The Windana Maryknoll Therapeutic Community is a residential alcohol and other drug (AOD) rehabilitation facility located in Maryknoll, Victoria, Australia. Situated on a 40-acre rural property southeast of Melbourne, it is the largest of three therapeutic communities (TCs) operated by Windana Drug and Alcohol Recovery Inc. The facility provides long-term residential treatment programs using a peer-driven, holistic recovery model.

== History and Expansion ==
The Maryknoll Therapeutic Community was established by Windana Drug and Alcohol Recovery Inc., a Victorian non-profit organization founded in 1984 to address substance use and addiction harms. Originally operating smaller-scale localized services, Windana expanded its operations into rural and regional settings to provide comprehensive, nature-integrated treatment environments. [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

In 2019, the facility announced the planned development of a $3.5 million, 12-bed "Welcome House" on-site. Designed in collaboration with addiction specialists, the Welcome House functions as a purpose-built entry point to assist new residents with stabilization, assessment, and early-stage addiction education before transitioning into the main therapeutic environment. In late 2023, Windana combined its organizational services with TaskForce, maintaining the operations of the Maryknoll facility under the consolidated entity. [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

== Facility and Environment ==
The Maryknoll facility spans a 40-acre property containing native bushland, shared living areas, and active agricultural zones. Designed around a campus-style farm layout, the property features: [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

* An assortment of farm animals including cows, alpacas, chickens, goats, and peacocks.
* A vegetable production garden, a dedicated herb garden, and a native plant garden.
* A reflection labyrinth located within the property's natural bushland.

The agricultural elements are integrated directly into the treatment regimen via a "garden-to-plate" culinary program, which focuses on nutritional education and nutritional rehabilitation. [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

== Treatment Model ==
The Maryknoll program is based on the "community as method" therapeutic model, which utilizes a structured, peer-led environment where residents act as primary agents of change for one another. The program accommodates up to 77–78 adult residents concurrently. While Windana's secondary facilities in Ballarat and Corio offer condensed three-to-six-month terms, the core Maryknoll residential framework is structured as an immersive program lasting between 9 and 12 months. [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

The rehabilitation structure is divided into three primary phases: [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

# Phase One: Induction and Education – Focuses on stabilization, adjustment to community routines, and introductory addiction education.
# Phase Two: Core Therapy – Involves extensive group and individual therapy targeting underlying behavioral and emotional drivers of substance dependence.
# Phase Three: Integration and Consolidation – Focuses on transition-planning, post-program responsibility, and preparation for life after residential care.

=== Daily Operations and Services ===
Residents adhere to a structured daily schedule starting at 6:15 AM. Program members participate in specialized work groups responsible for the facility's daily operational survival, including administration, commercial kitchen duties, grounds maintenance, cleaning, and animal care. [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

In addition to traditional behavioral therapies and case management, the community incorporates complementary healthcare services, including naturopathy, art therapy, and general physical fitness. [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

== Admissions and Integration ==
Admission requires individuals to be aged 18 or older and to have successfully completed a recognized acute withdrawal or detoxification program prior to entry. Financial structures involve a standardized fortnightly contribution deducted from eligible social security or personal allowances. [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

Upon completion of the primary program, residents are eligible for Windana's transitional services, which include localized aftercare support networks and integration housing, allowing former residents to live independently while returning to the Maryknoll farm on a part-time basis to maintain peer accountability. [ref: Enable JavaScript to use search, www.google.com]

Kristoffer "Kris" B. Berse is Dean, Professor, and Scientist II at the University of the Philippines National College of Public Administration and Governance (UP NCPAG) in Diliman, Quezon City. He earned his Ph.D. and master's degrees in Urban Engineering and Environmental Studies, respectively, from the University of Tokyo, and his bachelor's degree in Public Administration from UP. He works broadly in the intersecting areas of public policy, sustainable development, inter-local cooperation, crisis management, climate adaptation, and disaster governance. [ref: Kristoffer B. Berse, PhD, NCPAG - UP National College of Public Administration and Governance]

== Educational background ==
Kris earned his Ph.D. in Urban Engineering from the University of Tokyo in Tokyo, Japan. He is a recipient of the Monbukagakushō Scholarship, an academic scholarship offered by the Japanese Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology and selected on the recommendation of the Japanese Embassy or Consulate General. At the same university, he also completed his Master's degree in Environmental Studies through the ADB-Japan Scholarship Program at the Graduate School of Frontier Sciences. He completed his Bachelor of Arts in Public Administration from the National College of Public Administration and Governance at the University of the Philippines.

== Career ==
Dean Berse began his career as a University Research Associate in UP NCPAG after his graduation, from July 1999 to March 2002. His first experience outside of the college was serving as a Legislative Staff Officer for the Senate of the Philippines from March 2002 to September 2002.

He then pursued higher education at the University of Tokyo through the [https://www.adb.org/what-we-do/funds/japan-scholarship-program-jsp ADB-JSP Scholarship] in 2002. He worked as a Research Assistant for the Global Environment Information Center of United Nations University in Tokyo, Japan from August 2002 to September 2004. In the same year, he was a Programme Fellow for Communications and Development for the Asia-Pacific Network for Global Change Research in Kobe, Japan until June 2006.

Going back to the Philippines in July 2006, he served as the Head of the Knowledge Management Team for the [https://emi-megacities.org Earthquakes and Megacities Initiative] in Quezon City until September 2009. He began his Doctoral studies in Urban Engineering at the University of Tokyo shortly after. He worked as Technical Staff for the Urban Planning Group of the Project on Sustainable Urban Renewal for the Elderly in the Japan Science and Technology Agency from November 2010 to March 2013.

Upon completion of his doctorate, he went back to UP NCPAG as an Assistant Professor in November 2014. He became an Associate Professor in 2019 and was promoted to Professor in 2025. Kris was appointed as the Dean of NCPAG in February 2023 and reappointed for another three-year term in February 2026. [ref: UPD has 3 new deans, 1 reappointed]

He teaches fundamental courses in undergraduate and graduate programs of NCPAG, such as PA 101 Introduction to Public Administration, PA 141 Public Policy and Program Administration, and even new courses such as PA 152 Urban and Metropolitan Governance. Dean Berse also serves as a mentor, adviser, critic, and panel member to graduate students of UP NCPAG.

== Awards and achievements ==

* 2019 [https://pssc.org.ph/vamera/ Virginia A. Miralao Excellence in Research Award], Philippine Social Science Council [ref: UP NCPAG prof bags VAM Award - University of the Philippines]
* Rafael M. Salas Professorial Chair in Public Administration, University of the Philippines Diliman (2018–2019)
* UP Diliman Centennial Professorial Chair
* UP Diliman Centennial Faculty Grant
* UP International Publication Award
* One UP Faculty Grant Award in Public Administration (Public Policy), Teaching and Research, Research and Public Service
* Senior Research Fellow, Development Academy of the Philippines (2020–2022)
* Senior Fellow, Council of Fellows, Philippine Public Safety College (2020)

* Young Scientist, Integrated Research on Disaster Risk (2018)

* Best Paper Awardee, [https://tiara-tu.ac.th/tiara-international-conference-on-asia-pacific-futures-opportunities-for-connectivity/ TIARA (Thammasat Institute of Area Studies) International Conference] (2024)
* Best Paper Awardee, 4th International Conference on Magsaysay Awardees: Good Governance and Transformative Leadership in Asia in Mahasarakham, Thailand (2016)
* International Network for Government Science Advice-Asia Essay Writing Contest (2020)

* Cum Laude and Class Valedictorian, Batch 1999 of UP NCPAG
* Class Valedictorian, Batch 1995 of San Juan National High School
* Most Outstanding Public School Student of San Juan, Jaycees International 1995

== Public service ==
Kris' public service and extension work involves his expertise in public policy, crisis management, climate adaptation, and disaster governance. He was Director of the Research and Creative Work Division at the University of the Philippines Research Institute from 2019 to 2023. Prior to that, he was a Residential Program Coordinator for the Center of Public Administration and Governance Education (CPAGE) in UP NCPAG from 2016 to 2019.

= Uthumalai, Tamil Nadu =
Uthumalai, also spelled Uttumalai, is a village in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu. It is situated in Veerakeralampudur taluk of Tenkasi district, in the southern part of the state. The settlement is associated with the agricultural landscape and historical political structures of the former Tirunelveli region. Uthumalai is also notable for its historical connection with the poligar and zamindari systems that shaped local administration during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries.[1][2]

== Geography and location ==
Uthumalai is located in southern Tamil Nadu, in the region historically administered as part of Tirunelveli district. Following the reorganisation of district boundaries in 2019, the village falls within Tenkasi district.[1][3] The surrounding region includes rural settlements and agricultural land, and the area forms part of the wider cultural and economic landscape of southern Tamil Nadu.

The village is situated within Veerakeralampudur taluk, an administrative subdivision of Tenkasi district. Surandai is identified as a nearby town in village-directory records.[1] Its geographical position connects it to a region characterised by rural communities, agriculture and longstanding local administrative institutions.

== History ==
Uthumalai has a historical association with the poligar system of southern India. Poligars, also known as palaiyakkarars, were local political and military authorities who exercised varying degrees of control over territories and settlements. Their responsibilities could include revenue collection, the maintenance of armed forces and the administration of local affairs. The relationship between these rulers and larger political powers changed considerably during the expansion of British colonial rule.[2]

Historian Nicholas B. Dirks examined Uthumalai in his research on the transformation of local rulers into landlords under British administration. His 1986 study, “From Little King to Landlord: Property, Law, and the Gift under the Madras Permanent Settlement”, discusses how colonial revenue arrangements altered the political and economic status of traditional ruling families.[2]

During the early nineteenth century, Uthumalai became associated with the zamindari system under the Madras Presidency. Under this arrangement, recognised estate holders were responsible for revenue obligations to the colonial administration, while retaining certain rights over their estates. The establishment of zamindari arrangements in southern Tamil Nadu formed part of a broader transformation of land ownership, taxation and political authority following conflicts involving the poligars.[2]

The history of Uthumalai therefore provides an example of the wider changes experienced by rural estates in southern India during the colonial period. The transition from local political authority to a more formalised landlord system affected relationships between ruling families, agricultural communities and the colonial state.[2]

== Administration ==
Uthumalai is administered within the present-day framework of local government in Tamil Nadu. The village is listed in village-directory records under Veerakeralampudur taluk in Tenkasi district.[1] Local administration operates within the state's wider system of district, taluk and village-level governance.

Tenkasi district was established in November 2019 after being separated from the former Tirunelveli district. The district administration oversees public services and development activities across its rural and urban areas.[3] This administrative change placed Uthumalai within the newly constituted district while maintaining its connection to the historical Tirunelveli region.

== Demographics ==
According to figures reported from the 2011 Census of India, Uthumalai had a population of 7,737 people living in 2,168 households. The recorded population consisted of 3,788 males and 3,949 females.[1] These figures provide a historical demographic reference for the village rather than a current population estimate.

The 2011 population data also indicate that the village was a substantial rural settlement within the surrounding area. Census records are useful for examining population distribution, household numbers and other characteristics of rural communities in Tamil Nadu.[4]

More recent population figures should be established through an updated official census or other authoritative government publication before being added to this article.

== Economy ==
Agriculture has historically played an important role in the economy of the wider Tenkasi region. The district administration describes agriculture and related activities as major sources of livelihood and identifies rivers, reservoirs and irrigation tanks as important water resources supporting cultivation in the district.[3]

Uthumalai's rural setting places it within this broader agricultural environment. However, the principal crops, employment distribution and present-day occupational structure of the village require confirmation from village-level government statistics or reliable published studies.
[truncated]

Draft text:
Vaccine law, also known as vaccination law or immunization law, is a field of law concerning the development, testing, approval, manufacture, distribution, financing, administration, and use of vaccines, as well as legal responsibility for vaccine-related injuries and governmental policies concerning vaccination. [ref: Vaccine Law and Policy, Springer] [ref: Vaccine, Vaccination, and Immunization Law, Third Edition, Bloomberg Law] [ref: Vaccine Law 101, Journal of Law, Medicine & Ethics] It draws on multiple areas of law, including administrative law, public health law, intellectual property law, tort law, constitutional law, and health law. Vaccine law encompasses legal questions arising throughout the life cycle of a vaccine, from initial research and clinical trials through approval, production, distribution, administration, safety monitoring, and potential injury compensation, [ref: A Proper Introduction to Vaccine Law, and a Very Necessary National Vaccine Law Conference, American Bar Association] often with special rules to be implemented in response to public health emergencies. [ref: Legal Issues in COVID-19 Vaccine Development and Deployment, Congressional Research Service]

Vaccination policy is a related field concerned particularly with decisions about recommending, promoting, providing, or requiring vaccination. Vaccine law also encompasses legal frameworks governing the vaccines themselves, independently of policies concerning their use.

==Scope==

The scope of vaccine law extends beyond vaccination mandates and other measures intended to increase vaccination rates. It includes the legal conditions under which vaccines are developed and marketed, the rights and responsibilities of manufacturers and healthcare providers, and the mechanisms through which governments and other institutions make vaccines available to the public. Hargan and colleagues have described the field in terms of the regulatory framework governing the production, procurement, distribution, and administration of vaccines, as well as liability arising from their use. Yang and Reiss examine these subjects alongside the legal treatment of vaccination requirements, vaccine safety, intellectual property, and public health policy.

Areas within the field include:

* Regulation of vaccine clinical trials
* Vaccine licensure, as an aspect of regulation of therapeutic goods
* Vaccine intellectual property, primarily patents
* Vaccine equity; Vaccine access, funding and distribution
* Vaccination mandates and exemptions
* Vaccine injury compensation
* Legal responses to vaccine misinformation

The COVID-19 pandemic brought renewed attention to these issues, including emergency authorization of vaccines, the allocation of initially limited supplies, government vaccination requirements, and the legal treatment of injuries attributed to emergency countermeasures.

===Development and regulation===
The development and approval of vaccines are governed by laws regulating clinical research, pharmaceutical products, and biological products. These laws establish requirements for testing vaccine safety and efficacy, obtaining authorization to market vaccines, maintaining manufacturing standards, and monitoring safety after authorization. Legal requirements governing vaccine research include informed consent, the protection of human research participants, oversight of clinical trials, and the collection and reporting of research results. Research involving vaccine candidates may raise additional questions concerning the use of control groups, the participation of minors and other vulnerable populations, the recruitment of sufficiently representative trial participants, and liability for injuries or misconduct during clinical research.

Regulatory agencies also oversee vaccine manufacturing, labeling, advertising, and postmarketing surveillance. In the United States, the Food and Drug Administration regulates human vaccines under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act and the Public Health Service Act. The agency may inspect manufacturing facilities, impose product requirements, and take enforcement action for violations of applicable law. Special regulatory pathways may permit access to vaccines that have not received ordinary marketing approval. In the United States, an emergency use authorization may permit the use of certain medical products during a qualifying public health emergency, subject to statutory conditions. Legal systems often provide mechanisms to accelerate the development or regulatory review of vaccines intended to prevent serious diseases, including expedited development and review procedures, such as fast-track designation and priority review, as well as accelerated approval based on qualifying evidence.

===Intellectual property===
Intellectual property protections for vaccines, and the technologies used in their development and production, include patents for vaccine compositions, components, manufacturing processes, and methods of use, as well as trade secrets and, to a lesser extent, trademarks.

Shadow Slave is an English language dark fantasy web novel written by Russian author Barisbi Alborov, also known as Guiltythree. It was first published on WebNovel in 2022. [ref: Shadow Slave] A webcomic adaptation by Laurel Pursuit was released on August 19, 2026 through Aethon Webcomics. [ref: The Shadow Slave Webcomic Is Coming!, aethonbooks.com]

== Plot ==
In a distant, post-apocalyptic future, the Nightmare Spell is a mysterious phenomenon that infects humans from the waking world (Earth), pulling them into the Dream Realm and putting them through trials known as Nightmares. Conquering a Nightmare grants a person unique, supernatural powers, while failure results in death.

Sunny, a 16-year-old orphan residing in the outskirts of a city in the Northern Quadrant of the waking world falls victim to the Nightmare Spell, and is transported to his First Nightmare. After completing the Nightmare, Sunny unlocks his aspect and flaw: Shadow Slave and Clear Conscience, respectively. His aspect grants Sunny an affinity to shadows, while his flaw prevents him from lying.

To survive in the Dream Realm, Sunny must make allies, find better equipment, develop new abilities, and conquer increasingly difficult Nightmares. Throughout his journey, Sunny navigates through a complex system of clans overseen by the most powerful carriers of the Nightmare Spell, and gradually uncovers the history of the lost civilizations of the Dream Realm on a mission to save his own.

== Media ==

=== Web novel ===
The original web novel has been serialized daily on WebNovel since 2022. Alborov typically published two chapters daily for volumes 1-12, taking a few days of break between each volume, but has been publishing around one chapter daily since the start of volume 13. Over 3,500 chapters have been released as of October 2026.

Aden Joel Valencia is an American wrestler who competes for the Stanford Cardinal. In 2026, he won the 149-pound title at the NCAA Division I Wrestling Championships, defeating previously undefeated top seed Shayne Van Ness of Penn State in sudden-victory overtime. [ref: NCAA Wrestling Championships 2026 Results, Champions, Team Scores, FloWrestling] The championship made Valencia the third individual NCAA wrestling champion in Stanford history and the first Stanford freshman to win an NCAA wrestling title. [ref: Valencia Wins National Title, Stanford Cardinal]

Before competing collegiately, Valencia competed in freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling at national and international events. His results included a title at the 2024 Henri Deglane Grand Prix in France and top-eight finishes at senior-level United States freestyle competitions while still in high school. [ref: Aden Valencia Named USA Wrestling Athlete Of The Week, USA Wrestling]

== Early life and high school career ==

Valencia was born in Redwood City, California, and grew up in Morgan Hill, California. [ref: Aden Valencia - Wrestling, Stanford Cardinal] He began wrestling at three and a half years old and also trained in judo during his childhood. [ref: Aden Valencia's will: How a freshman became a national wrestling champion, The Stanford Daily]

His older sister, Nyla Valencia, is also a competitive wrestler. The two trained together while growing up, and in 2021 served as warm-up partners for competitors at the United States Olympic Team Trials.

Valencia attended Ann Sobrato High School in Morgan Hill, graduating in 2024. His high school and age-group career included runner-up finishes at the 2021 Super 32 and Fargo tournaments and a victory in the college division of the 2022 Reno Tournament of Champions, where he was named the tournament's most outstanding wrestler.

Valencia competed in freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling in addition to folkstyle. He was a member of a United States age-group Greco-Roman world team and placed sixth in freestyle at both the 2023 U.S. Senior Open and the 2023 Senior World Team Trials. Wrestling Insider Newsmagazine later described Valencia as having established a national reputation through age-group and senior-level international-style competition despite not winning a California state high school championship. [ref: Spoken into Existence: WIN's NCAA champion feature on Stanford's Aden Valencia, Wrestling Insider Newsmagazine]

In 2024, Valencia won the 65-kilogram freestyle division at the Henri Deglane Grand Prix in France.

Valencia later enrolled at Stanford University and joined its wrestling program.

== College career ==

=== 2024–25 season ===

Valencia redshirted during his first season at Stanford. Wrestling primarily at 141 pounds, he finished 3–3 overall and 3–1 in dual competition.

He recorded a pin in his collegiate debut against Zach Redding of Iowa State.

=== 2025–26 season ===

Valencia competed at 149 pounds during his redshirt freshman season. He entered the 2026 NCAA Division I Wrestling Championships as the No. 10 seed after recording seven losses during the season.

At the NCAA championships in Cleveland, Valencia defeated No. 23 seed Max Petersen of North Dakota State in the opening round before defeating No. 7 Ethan Stiles of Ohio State.

In the quarterfinals, Valencia faced No. 2 seed Jaxson Joy of Cornell. Valencia trailed 8–1 entering the third period before scoring three takedowns and winning 12–9. He then defeated No. 11 seed Lachlan McNeil of Michigan 9–5 in the semifinals.

Valencia faced No. 1 seed Shayne Van Ness of Penn State in the championship match. The match was tied 5–5 after regulation before Valencia scored a takedown in sudden victory to win 8–5.

The victory gave Valencia the NCAA championship at 149 pounds. He became the first Stanford freshman to win an NCAA wrestling title and the program's third individual champion, following Matt Gentry in 2004 and Shane Griffith in 2021. Valencia was also the first wrestler seeded outside the top nine to win an NCAA individual title since 2016.

Stanford finished sixth at the championships with 67.5 team points, the highest NCAA team finish in program history at the time.

Following the NCAA tournament, USA Wrestling named Valencia its Athlete of the Week.

He was later named the Atlantic Coast Conference Co-Wrestler of the Year and ACC Freshman of the Year, sharing the conference's Wrestler of the Year award with NC State heavyweight and NCAA champion Isaac Trumble. [ref: National Champions Trumble, Valencia Headline 2025-26 ACC Wrestling Honors, Atlantic Coast Conference]

== Personal life ==

Valencia's parents are Joel and Sandra Valencia. His older sister, Nyla Valencia, competes in collegiate wrestling for the Iowa Hawkeyes.

Valencia has described his sister as an important influence on his wrestling career. During his comeback against Jaxson Joy in the 2026 NCAA quarterfinals, Valencia said he thought about wrestling for his sister while attempting to overcome the seven-point deficit.

After winning the NCAA championship, Valencia said that he intended to pursue another collegiate title and hoped to compete at the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.

== Championships and awards ==

* NCAA Division I champion, 149 lb (2026)
* NCAA Division I All-American (2026)
* ACC Co-Wrestler of the Year (2026)
* ACC Freshman of the Year (2026)
* Henri Deglane Grand Prix champion, 65 kg freestyle (2024)

Cas-Andy Maisonneuve, known professionally as Cas-Andy, is a Haitian rapper, songwriter, record producer and recording artist from Ouest, Haiti. His music is primarily associated with hip-hop and incorporates influences from Afrobeat, gospel and other contemporary styles. [ref: Cas-Andy, Apple Music] [ref: Cas-Andy, Spotify]

==Biography==

Cas-Andy Maisonneuve was born in Haiti. According to a professional biography published by Haiti Restoration, he graduated from high school in 2016 and obtained certificates in audiovisual communications and entrepreneurship from Haiti Tech in 2017. [ref: Program Manager, Maisonneuve C., Haiti Restoration]

In 2018, Maisonneuve served as president of the Cultural Commission of the Youth Association at Canaan III God's Church. In 2019, he enrolled in economics at the Université d'État d'Haïti. The Haiti Restoration biography also states that he co-founded Economy's Style, a training platform developed with professional colleagues, and taught English at the primary level.

Maisonneuve developed an interest in music at an early age. In his Apple Music artist profile, Cas-Andy described one of his earliest musical memories as composing a song titled "S-U-N-S-H-I-N-E" while participating in a musical group.

==Career==

Cas-Andy began releasing music commercially in the 2020s. His documented discography includes the single Etidyan Nou Ye, released on March 15, 2024. Apple Music classifies the release as Hip-Hop/Rap. [ref: Etidyan Nou Ye - Single, Apple Music]

A remastered version, Etidyan Nou Ye (Remastered 2025), was subsequently released and is listed by Apple Music as a single. [ref: Etidyan Nou Ye (Remastered 2025) - Single, Apple Music]

On January 12, 2025, Cas-Andy released Yon Madi. The recording is listed by Apple Music and Amazon Music as a Cas-Andy single. [ref: Yon Madi, Apple Music] [ref: Yon Madi, Amazon Music]

The song addresses loss, frustration and social conditions following a destructive earthquake in Haiti. Published lyrics for the recording reference the January 12, 2010 earthquake and include a social message concerning construction standards and unsafe construction practices. [ref: Cas-Andy — Yon Madi, Lirik.web.id]

Cas-Andy released Te Quiero on April 30, 2025. Apple Music classifies the recording as Latin. [ref: Te Quiero - Single, Apple Music]

His 2025 releases also included Dekole W (Remix), released on November 7, 2025 and classified by Apple Music as Afro-Beat. [ref: Dekole W (Remix) - Single, Apple Music]

In 2026, Cas-Andy released Yon Madi (Remix) on February 10, 2026. Apple Music classifies the release as Hip-Hop/Rap. [ref: Yon Madi (Remix) - Single, Apple Music]

On February 22, 2026, he released Dekole W Full Afro, which Apple Music classifies as Afro-Beat. [ref: Dekole W Full Afro - Single, Apple Music]

MusicBrainz lists Dekole W Full Afro as a digital single in Haitian Creole and credits Cas-Andy Maisonneuve as composer and lyricist. The database also credits him as lead vocalist, solo performer and executive producer. [ref: DEKOLE W FULL AFRO, MusicBrainz]

On April 11, 2026, Cas-Andy released Fanm Se Lavi, classified by Apple Music as Afro-Pop. [ref: Fanm Se Lavi - Single, Apple Music]

His subsequent release Moleno was released on October 6, 2026 and is classified by Apple Music as Dance. [ref: Moleno - Single, Apple Music]

==Musical style and themes==

Cas-Andy is primarily associated with hip-hop and rap. His Spotify artist profile describes his music as combining Afrobeat with gospel and hip-hop and emphasizes themes including hope, resilience and positive storytelling.

His recorded work includes Haitian Creole-language material such as Etidyan Nou Ye, Yon Madi and Dekole W Full Afro, as well as the Spanish-language single Te Quiero. [ref: Te Quiero - Single, Apple Music]

Cas-Andy has described Yon Madi as a song created during a difficult period in his life. In his Apple Music artist profile, he explained that the song's chorus addresses the tendency to redirect frustration, anger or pain from its original source toward another person or object.

Draft: Oil pollution and health in Akwa Ibom State

Draft text:
=== Gas flaring in Ibeno ===

In August 2025, Punch published an investigation into the effects of oil exploration and gas flaring in Inua Eyet Ikot, a community in Ibeno Local Government Area. Residents interviewed by the newspaper reported problems including poor eyesight, breathing difficulties and changes in menstrual health. Some residents linked these problems to gas flaring and oil pollution in their surroundings. [ref: How gas flaring silently steals sights of Akwa Ibom residents, Punch]

The report also described oil contamination on farmland and residents' concerns about the quality of rainwater and well water. Health professionals interviewed for the report discussed possible health risks associated with prolonged exposure to pollutants from gas flaring and oil spills.

=== Hydrocarbon discharge ===

In September 2024, Punch reported a hydrocarbon discharge and fire at an oil facility in Ibeno Local Government Area. The newspaper reported that smoke spread into nearby communities, including areas in Eket, Esit Eket and Onna, and that some residents sought medical treatment following the incident. [ref: Toxic discharge sparks health fears in A’Ibom communities, Punch]

The Akwa Ibom Oil Producing Community Development Network called for environmental remediation and measures to reduce exposure to harmful emissions. Mobil Producing Nigeria Unlimited, now (Seplat) in its response to the newspaper, described the incident as a process upset that caused a temporarily elevated flare at the Qua Iboe Terminal. The company said production was stopped as a precaution while the situation was managed.

=== Polluted water and health concerns ===

In June 2023, Daily Post reported complaints from residents of Ibeno about the condition of local water sources following oil spills. Residents described oily or discoloured water and said that access to affordable drinking water was a problem in some communities. The report also recorded residents' concerns about respiratory problems and pregnancy loss, which they associated with pollution and gas flaring. [ref: Oil Spills: Akwa Ibom oil community battles deadly polluted water, Daily Post]
=== Abandoned oil wells and environmental risks ===

In September 2026, Premium Times reported concerns raised by residents of oil-producing communities in Ikono and Ibiono Ibom local government areas about abandoned oil wells and ageing petroleum infrastructure. At a community dialogue organised by the Health of Mother Earth Foundation, residents reported oil pollution, declining agricultural yields and damage to the surrounding environment. Some called for environmental assessment, clean-up and government action. [ref: Akwa Ibom communities demand action on abandoned oil wells, Premium Times]

The report described concerns about oil sheen on streams and the possible risks posed by old oil wells and pipelines. These reports highlight the need to assess the condition of abandoned petroleum infrastructure, although the presence and level of contamination at individual sites require specific investigation.

== Environmental degradation and livelihoods ==

Oil pollution in Akwa Ibom has also been associated with concerns about farming, fishing and access to water. A study published in 2020 examined oil-producing communities in the state and discussed environmental degradation linked to oil exploration. It reported that damage to agricultural land and aquatic resources had affected activities such as farming, fishing and hunting. [ref: The Impact of Oil Exploration and Environmental Degradation in the Niger Delta Region of Nigeria: A Study of Oil Producing Communities in Akwa Ibom State, ResearchGate]

Damage to farmland, fishing grounds and water sources can affect food production and household income. The extent of these effects varies between communities and depends on the nature of pollution.

Draft text:
Neraidovrysi (; until 1927 Koutsoumadi, ) is a small settlement in southwestern Messenia, in the Peloponnese region of Greece. It lies on the southern side of Mount Lykodimos at an elevation of. Administratively it is part of the Adriani community in the Aipeia municipal unit of the municipality of Messini. The name means roughly "fairy spring" (see Etymology). At the 2021 census the settlement had no permanent residents.

==Etymology==
The name Neraidovrysi is a compound of two Greek words: neráida (), which in Greek folk tradition denotes an imagined being in the form of a very beautiful young woman who lives far from inhabited places, [ref: νεράιδα, Dictionary of Standard Modern Greek (Triantafyllidis)] and vrýsi (), a built fountain or similar structure from which (usually drinking) water runs. [ref: βρύση, Dictionary of Standard Modern Greek (Triantafyllidis)] The name can therefore be translated as "fairy spring" or "fairy fountain".

The Municipality of Messini's description of the Aipeia municipal unit says that the present name is presumed () to come from a spring in the settlement where, according to the inhabitants, fairies appeared very often. This is a local tradition: no detailed story, such as a named tale about the spring or its fairies, has been found in the published sources consulted.

Before 1927 the settlement was called Koutsoumadi. According to the same municipal source, this name derived from the Turkish personal name Koutsou Meti (), said to be that of a Turkish landowner who lived there. The settlement was renamed Neraidovrysi in 1927. [ref: Koutsoumadi – Neraidovrysi, Pandektis: Name Changes of Settlements in Greece]

==Geography==
Neraidovrysi is a semi-mountainous settlement built on the southern slope of Mount Lykodimos, in the south-west of Messenia. Its elevation is given as. The village of Adriani, after which the community is named, lies about south-west of Kalamata and about from the sea; the community also includes Kleisoura and Nea Adriani.

==History==
The settlement appears in the Venetian census of 1700, when the Kingdom of the Morea was under Venetian rule, as Koutsoumadi with eight families and 34 inhabitants.

Under the administrative reorganisations of the 19th century and later, Koutsoumadi was successively attached to different municipalities. It was first assigned to the municipality of Aipeia (seat: Longa) when that municipality was created in 1835; in 1840 it was moved to the municipality of Koroni (seat: Petalidi); in 1890 it was returned to Aipeia; and in 1912 it was attached to the community of Remoustafa. [ref: Δ. Αιπείας (Μεσσηνίας) – Διοικητικές Μεταβολές, Εθνικό Μητρώο Διοικητικών Μεταβολών των ΟΤΑ] The community of Remoustafa was renamed Adriani in 1927, the same year Koutsoumadi became Neraidovrysi. [ref: Διοικητικές μεταβολές οικισμού: Νεραϊδόβρυση (Κουτσουμάδι), Εθνικό Μητρώο Διοικητικών Μεταβολών των ΟΤΑ]

Under the 1997 Kapodistrias Plan the settlement was assigned to the municipality of Aipeia, and under the 2010 Kallikratis Plan Aipeia was merged into the new municipality of Messini, becoming a municipal unit.

==Demographics==
The settlement recorded 27 inhabitants in the 2001 census, one resident in 2011 and none in 2021. Greek census publications give both a "de facto" population and a "permanent resident" population; the table states which basis each figure uses. The 2001 figure is the de facto population and the 2021 figure is the permanent resident population, so the series is not strictly like-for-like.

Hickmanolobus nimorakiotakisi is a species of spider in the family Orsolobidae. It is endemic to Queensland, Australia, and was described in 2011 from male specimens collected in rainforest at Lamington National Park.

==Taxonomy==
The species was described in 2011 by Barbara Baehr, Robert Raven and Wendy Hebron in a paper on the Orsolobidae collected during the IBISCA-Queensland Project, a survey of invertebrates along an altitudinal gradient in Lamington National Park. It is placed in the genus Hickmanolobus, which was established by Forster and Platnick in 1985, and is listed as an accepted species in the World Spider Catalog.

The holotype is a male collected at IBISCA site 1100C in Lamington National Park (about above sea level) on 26 October 2006 by C. Burwell using a pyrethrum knockdown; it is held in the Queensland Museum (registration number QM S86313). A second male, collected at Mount Asplenium in January 1993 by G. Monteith, was also examined.

===Etymology===
The specific epithet is a patronym in honour of Dr Bill Nimorakiotakis, then Deputy Director of the Australian Venom Research Unit at the University of Melbourne, whom the authors credit with supporting spider taxonomy "with great passion".

==Description==
Only the male is known. Photomicrographs of the male in dorsal, frontal, lateral and ventral views are published in the original description. [ref: Orsolobidae (Araneae) of the IBISCA-Queensland Project at Lamington National Park, Australia, Memoirs of the Queensland Museum – Nature] The holotype has a total length of, with the carapace long and wide, and the abdomen long and wide. The carapace is yellow-brown and the legs are yellow-brown. There are six well-developed eyes. The abdomen is purple, with five pale, inverted V-shaped chevrons along the midline. The male pedipalp has a pyriform (pear-shaped) bulb with a long, thin embolus.

The authors distinguished the species from Hickmanolobus mollipes of Tasmania, which it resembles, by its abdominal pattern of five inverted V-shaped chevrons (rather than five transverse bars) and by a more slender male palpal bulb.

==Distribution and habitat==
Hickmanolobus nimorakiotakisi is known only from Queensland. The holotype was collected in rainforest at Lamington National Park at about, and the second known specimen at Mount Asplenium at about. In the IBISCA-Queensland survey, all five orsolobid species recorded were collected only above about; the authors suggested that orsolobids could be useful for monitoring the effects of climate change on the park's fauna.

Webtronaut Innovations LLC is an American internet holding company located in Albuquerque, New Mexico. Sahil Kazi, an Indian/Pakistani serial entrepreneur and SAP Certified Systems Analyst, founded the company. Webtronaut's first venture was the legal-tech marketplace SueEasy, which launched in 2007 and was a semi-finalist in the first-ever TechCrunch startup competition, TechCrunch40. [ref: Ambulance Chasers Have A New Home, SueEasy, TechCrunch] Currently, Webtronaut's ventures include Richlisted, GuiltyAF, SwaxAwards, and LabCauldron.

== History ==

=== SueEasy and Filmmortal (2007–2009) ===
Webtronaut's first ventures were created under the name Webtronaut Innovations (including an Indian entity, Webtronaut Innovations Pvt. Ltd.) and operated out of Mountain View, California. [ref: Filmmortal.com, Film Is Immortal. So Is Your Brand, PRLog]

SueEasy, launched in 2007 by Kazi and Faraz Matin, was a marketplace that turned the traditional lawyer directory upside down: would-be plaintiffs posted grievances and documents, either individually or as potential class actions, and licensed attorneys bid on the opportunity to contact the client. Crunchbase identifies SueEasy as a sub-organisation of Webtronaut Innovations. [ref: SueEasy — Company Profile, Crunchbase] SueEasy launched publicly in April 2008 with a searchable class action database containing nine filing categories. [ref: SueEasy Goes Live — Your Class Action Lawsuit Lottery Ticket, TechCrunch] The ABA Journal called the service a "reverse Martindale-Hubbell" that connected would-be plaintiffs with attorneys. [ref: New Website Plays Matchmaker For Would-Be Plaintiffs, ABA Journal] United Press International also wrote about the service in April 2008. [ref: Web Site Makes Suing Easy] The Los Angeles Daily Journal later wrote about SueEasy among attorney-client matchmaking services, quoting Kazi and stating that more than 1,200 California attorneys were paying customers. [ref: Attorney-Client Matchmakers, Los Angeles Daily Journal] The model also received criticism from legal commentators regarding case quality and legal ethics. In September 2009, the business was put up for sale via online auction. [ref: Running SueEasy Turned Out To Be Not So Easy, Overlawyered] According to the company, SueEasy was subsequently purchased by a mass torts law firm. Company databases indicate that the original company has been closed.

In 2008, the group launched Filmmortal, an auction marketplace for product placement, described as "the eBay for product placement," where independent filmmakers listed projects and advertisers bid to have their products placed in those projects. [ref: Filmmortal — Company Profile, Crunchbase] BusinessWeek and GigaOM's NewTeeVee both wrote about Filmmortal and competitor PlaceVine as new matchmakers for product placement deals, reporting that Kazi had bootstrapped Filmmortal with $130,000 and that placement deals started at approximately $3,000. [ref: Startups Take on Product Placement Dealmaking, BusinessWeek] [ref: The New Matchmakers: Startups Tackle Product Placement Deals, NewTeeVee] Media in Canada wrote about the service in April 2009, calling it an "eBay for product placement" with approximately 80 projects listed. [ref: Filmmortal breathes life into indie scripts, Media in Canada] IndieWire also wrote about the service in October 2009. [ref: Product Placement Ought to Know Where It's Being Placed, IndieWire] Product Placement News announced the marketplace in February 2009. [ref: Introducing Filmmortal, Product Placement News] Kazi was Filmmortal's chief executive. According to the company, Filmmortal was subsequently acquired. Company databases list it as closed.

=== Holding company and current ventures (2023–present) ===
In April 2023, the group launched Richlisted, a service that records members' names on a public blockchain as a permanent record of achievement; a launch announcement quoted Kazi as managing director of Richlisted. [ref: RichListed Launches Exclusive Blockchain-Listed Network for Self-Made Individuals to Showcase Status, PRLog]

In October 2026, Webtronaut Innovations LLC was established in New Mexico as the holding company for the group's web-based businesses, which it refers to as an "internet holding company operating multiple web-based businesses." [ref: Webtronaut Innovations]

== Ventures ==
=== SueEasy ===
SueEasy (2007–2009) was a legal marketplace and class action repository. Plaintiffs posted cases across various categories including class actions; only licensed attorneys could view the listings, and attorneys bid on the opportunity to contact a client, with the client having the right to reject any bidder.

=== Filmmortal ===
Filmmortal (2008) was an online auction marketplace for product placement deals between independent filmmakers and advertisers, including barter arrangements such as transportation, lodging, catering, props, and equipment.

=== Richlisted ===
Richlisted (2023–present) provides a one-time paid listing recorded on a public blockchain as a permanent, unalterable record.

=== GuiltyAF ===
GuiltyAF (2025–present) is an interactive live-streamed show where two parties present a dispute and the audience votes on the resolution in real-time.

=== SwaxAwards ===
SwaxAwards is a monthly awards program recognizing creators on TikTok across various categories including comedy, dance, and wholesome content.
[truncated]
