Draft: Cycling at the 1900 Summer Olympics – Men's team sprint

Draft text:
The men's professional team sprint also named Course des Nations was a track cycling event contested at the 1900 Summer Olympics in Paris. It was classified as an Olympic non-medal event. The competition was held on 14 September 1900 at the Vélodrome de Vincennes. A total of 24 cyclists from nine countries participated in the event, with eight three-man teams competing, including one mixed team. [ref: Team Sprint (Professionals [Course des Nations]), Men, Olympedia]

Unlike the modern Olympic team sprint, in which riders race in succession, the 1900 competition was conducted as a series of match races in which all six riders from two opposing teams competed simultaneously. Point-for-place scoring was used to determine the winning team.

The competition began with four first-round heats. France, Italy, the United States, and the mixed British-New Zealand team advanced to the semi-finals. In the semi-finals, the United States defeated Italy, while France defeated the mixed team, setting up a final between the United States and France.

The final was closely contested, with the United States defeating France by one point. The American team of Tom Cooper, Floyd McFarland, and George Banker scored 10 points, compared with France's 11. The individual finishing order was Edmond Jacquelin, Cooper, McFarland, Paul Bourillon, Banker, and Jean-Baptiste Louvet. Italy defeated the mixed British-New Zealand team to finish third.

Nowadays, the professional events are not recognized by the International Olympic Committee as official Olympic medal competitions, as only amateur events are classified as medal events. Before July 2021 the IOC has never officially decided which events were "Olympic" and which were not. [ref: Olympische Spiele 1900 in Paris, Agon-Sportverlag]

==Competition format==

Eight teams of three cyclists competed in the tournament. The teams represented seven national delegations, together with a mixed team comprising two British cyclists and one New Zealand cyclist. Each match involved two teams, with all six riders racing on the track simultaneously.

The competition consisted of four first-round heats, two semi-finals, and two final-round races. The winners of the first-round heats advanced to the semi-finals. The semi-final winners contested the championship final, while the other two semi-finalists competed for third place. Point-for-place scoring determined the winning team in each match. The team whose riders accumulated the lower total score won the race.

Draft: Fakir Garibullah

Draft text:
Fakir Garibullah (1680-1770) was a revolutionary 18th-century medieval Bengali poet and mystic who fundamentally reshaped vernacular literature in Bengal. He is celebrated as the absolute pioneer of the Puthi literature movement and the first prominent architect of Dobhashi (literally "two languages")—a syncretic literary style that blended Bengali with Arabic, Persian, and Hindustani vocabulary. [ref: ফকির গরীবুল্লাহ, Teachers Portal] [ref: ]

== Life ==
Because of a lack of formal historical documentation, exact biographical details regarding Garibullah's life are scarce.He was born in the village of Hafizpur, situated in the Baliya Pargana of the Hooghly district (which was a part of the greater Bardhaman region at the time) in 1680. [ref: ]His father was a local devout figure named Shah Dhundi (or Saha Dundi). The honorific title "Fakir" suggests that Garibullah either followed a family tradition of Islamic mysticism (Sufism) or adopted a lifestyle of ascetic, spiritual devotion.

== The Birth of the "Dobhashi" Style ==
Before Garibullah, medieval Bengali literature heavily relied on traditional Sanskritised vocabulary. Living during a time when the Mughal influence was deeply entrenched yet transitioning into colonial rule, Garibullah broke traditional conventions to cater to the masses.He blended everyday regional Bengali grammar with Arabic, Persian, and Hindi terms that ordinary Bengali Muslims used in their daily speech.This hybrid linguistic style came to be known as Dobhashi Bengali or Musalmani Bangla.

== Major Literary Contributions ==
Garibullah did not just write poems; he created narrative epics (puthis) meant to be rhythmically recited aloud to large rural audiences as a form of cultural memory and entertainment.His most celebrated works include Amir Hamza,Yusuf-Zulekha,Sonabhan & Sonabhaner Puthi and Satyapir Puthi. [ref: Lost-and-found: an epic tale, www.business-standard.com]

== Historical Legacy ==
Fakir Garibullah’s life marks the transition of Bengali literature out of the strict medieval courtly traditions and into the hands of the common folk. By normalising Arabic and Persian loanwords, his work paved the way for cheap, mass-printed Battala publications in 19th-century Calcutta, cementing his status as one of the most culturally influential Muslim voices in pre-modern Bengal.

== References ==

Draft text:
----
The OGC SWE Common Data Model Encoding Standard (OGC document identifier 24-014) is an open geospatial standard published by the Open Geospatial Consortium (OGC) as part of its Sensor Web Enablement (SWE) suite. It defines low-level, self-describing data models and encodings for describing, structuring, and exchanging sensor observations, system parameters, and scientific datasets.

Version 3.0 supersedes version 2.0 (OGC 08-094r2) and introduces major updates, notably transitioning from XML to JSON encodings and aligning with modern OGC API standards.

== Overview ==
The SWE Common Data Model provides a conceptual and technical framework for describing heterogeneous sensor datasets and streams. It enables client applications and servers to interpret raw data values without prior out-of-band knowledge by bundling structural definitions, unit definitions, quality metrics, and external semantic links alongside the data payloads.

The standard addresses five primary aspects of data representation:

# Data Structure: Defining scalar values, records, arrays, and matrices.
# Semantics: Linking properties to external dictionaries, ontologies, or URIs.
# Representation: Explicitly defining data types such as numeric quantities, booleans, categories, or geometry components.
# Data Quality: Attaching accuracy, precision, and error metadata to components.
# Encoding: Specifying how values are formatted for transmission (e.g., JSON, ASCII, or binary).

== Key Changes in Version 3.0 ==
Version 3.0.0 represents a modernization of the standard, shifting toward JSON-centric web architectures and OGC API standards [ref: OGC SWE Common Data Model Encoding Standard, docs.ogc.org].

* JSON Encodings & Schemas: Added native JSON implementation schemas to streamline Web API integration and developer adoption.
* Removal of XML Encodings: Deprecated and removed legacy GML/XML encodings from the core specification to simplify the standard.
* Geometry Data Component: Introduced explicit geometry components modeled on OGC Simple Feature Geometries to allow vector spatial geometries to be embedded directly into sensor data components.
* Integration with Modern Standards: Serves as a foundational building block for contemporary specifications, including SensorML 3.0 and OGC API — Connected Systems.

== Core Data Components ==
The standard defines basic data components that can be composed into complex data structures:
{| class="wikitable"
!Data Component
!Description
!Example
|-
|Boolean
|Binary state representation (true/false).
|Motion detector status.
|-
|Category
|Discrete categorical value referencing a controlled vocabulary or code space.
|Camera mode (AUTO_FOCUS, MANUAL).
|-
|Quantity
|Continuous numeric value bound to a unit of measure or scale factor.
|Temperature reading (23.51 °C).
|-
|Count
|Discrete integer value for counting events or items.
|Particle count per volume.
|-
|Text
|Free-text string value or identifier.
|Sensor serial number or error code.
|-
|Time
|Temporal instant or interval tied to a time frame or epoch.
|ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.
|-
|Geometry
|Vector geometry object modeled on simple features.
|Point, LineString, or Polygon coordinates.
|}

=== Aggregate Components ===
These primitive components are combined into higher-level constructs:

* DataRecord: A collection of fields of varying types (similar to a struct or dictionary).
* DataArray: An array of homogeneous data components, allowing efficient streaming of time-series or multi-dimensional blocks.
* Vector / Matrix: Mathematical constructs built from ordered numerical quantities.

== Relationship to Other OGC Standards ==
SWE Common Data Model 3.0 is a shared specification within the OGC ecosystem:

* OGC SensorML 3.0: Uses SWE Common components to define inputs, outputs, parameters, and settings for sensor systems and processing chains.
* OGC API — Connected Systems Standard: Uses SWE Common 3.0 structures to encode observation data, stream payloads, and control commands in modern RESTful/JSON web interfaces.

= Sähköverkon inertia =
Sähköverkon inertialla tarkoitetaan sähköjärjestelmään sitoutunutta liike-energiaa, joka vastustaa verkon taajuuden muutoksia. Tämä liike-energia muodostuu sähköverkkoon kytkettyjen suurien pyörivien koneiden massasta. Nämä koneet voivat sijaita voimalaitoksissa tai tehtaissa ja ne pyörivät sähköverkon kanssa samalla taajuudella. Sähköverkossa tuotannon ja kulutuksen täytyy olla koko ajan tasapainossa, tämän tasapainon heiluessa pyrkii myös verkon taajuus muuttumaan. Jos kulutus ylittää tuotannon, ottaa kuormitus tehonsa tahtigeneraattoreiden pyörivästä liike-energiasta, mikä hidastaa generaattoreita. Jos tuotantoa on enemmän kuin kulutusta, käy päinvastoin: tahtigeneraattoreiden liike-energia kasvaa, ne alkavat pyöriä nopeammin ja verkon taajuus kasvaa. Kulutuksen ja tuotannon välinen hetkellinen tasapaino siis ilmenee sähköverkon taajuudesta. [ref: Elovaara, J., & Haarla, L. (2011). Sähköverkot 1: järjestelmätekniikka. Gaudeamus.] Suomessa sähköverkon taajuuden sallittu vaihteluväli on 49,9 ja 50,1 Hz välillä [ref: Kulutuksen ja tuotannon tasapainon ylläpito, Fingrid].

Jesse van den Boogaard is een Nederlandse student uit Gelderland. Hij volgde middelbaar beroepsonderwijs aan het Candea College te Duiven en vervolgde in 2026 zijn opleiding in de richting van het spoorvervoer. Hij richt zich op een toekomstige loopbaan als treinmachinist.

== Biografie ==

=== Jeugd en Opleiding ===
Van den Boogaard volgde zijn middelbare schoolopleiding aan het Candea College in Duiven. Hij volgde daar de mavo/vmbo-gl-leerweg en rondde deze opleiding in 2026 af. [ref: ]

Tijdens zijn middelbare schooltijd volgde hij verschillende algemene en praktijkgerichte vakken. Voor zijn profielwerkstuk werkte hij samen met medeleerlingen aan een onderzoek naar landbouw. Het project werd beoordeeld met de kwalificatie goed. Ook verzorgde hij samen met zijn groepsgenoten een presentatie over het onderzoek.

Na het afronden van zijn middelbare school koos Van den Boogaard voor een vervolgopleiding die aansluit bij zijn belangstelling voor techniek en spoorvervoer.

=== Opleiding tot machinist ===
In 2026 begon Van den Boogaard aan de mbo-opleiding Machinist Railvervoer aan het ROC van Amsterdam. De opleiding is gericht op het beroep van treinmachinist en omvat kennis en vaardigheden die nodig zijn om veilig en verantwoordelijk in het spoorvervoer te werken.

Met deze opleiding richt hij zich op een loopbaan binnen de Nederlandse spoorwegsector. [ref: Home (Jongeren) - ROC van Amsterdam, www.rocva.nl]

=== Belangstelling voor het spoorvervoer ===
Van den Boogaard heeft bijzondere belangstelling voor het spoorvervoer en de techniek achter treinen. Zijn keuze voor de opleiding Machinist Railvervoer sluit aan bij zijn ambitie om beroepsmatig in deze sector te werken.

Floribert Hengwa Mubalama is a Congolese-American nonprofit leader and author. He is the founder and chief executive officer of the Congolese Integration Network (CIN), a refugee-led nonprofit organization based in SeaTac, Washington, that serves Congolese and other refugee and immigrant families in King County, Washington. [ref: Announcing Our Parent-Child Home Awards, Best Starts for Kids Blog] [ref: How one refugee's story of organizing holds lessons for all of us, Communities of Opportunity] A former refugee from the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mubalama spent more than eight years in a refugee camp in Malawi before resettling in the United States in December 2014. [ref: For Refugees In Seattle, Rising Rents Mean The Search For Home Isn't Over, KNKX Public Radio]

== Early life and resettlement ==
Mubalama fled the Democratic Republic of Congo in 2006 amid violence and lived in a refugee camp in Malawi. According to a King County profile, he arrived in King County in December 2014 with his family and was among the first Congolese refugees to settle in the area. The Communities of Opportunity profile describes his experience of isolation and housing and employment instability after arrival, and his door-to-door organizing among Congolese families in King County, including a community gathering attended by more than 120 Congolese community members and 20 county service providers.

== Congolese Integration Network ==
Mubalama organized the Congolese Integration Network in response to the isolation he observed among Congolese refugees navigating new systems and communities in King County. With support from Global to Local, he founded CIN in SeaTac; its first program, Congolese Housing First, combined language classes, employment workshops, and support groups. CIN was fiscally sponsored by Global to Local from July 2016 to July 2018. [ref: RVC Partner Spotlight: Congolese Integration Network Takes Steps Away From Tragic History, Looks Forward to Future Growth, Rainier Valley Corps] A 2017 public radio report described Mubalama as the person many Congolese refugees in Seattle called for help with appointments, rides, first jobs and documents such as eviction notices, and identified affordable housing as one of the biggest barriers facing newly arrived refugees. In 2017, CIN was among the recipients of Parent-Child Home Program funding announced by King County's Best Starts for Kids initiative, in partnership with United Way of King County and the City of Seattle.

A 2022 Washington State Senate resolution recorded that an estimated 8,000 Congolese refugees live in Washington and are served by the Congolese Integration Network, and noted the organization's advocacy for a healing center for refugees recovering from trauma. [ref: Senate Resolution 8627 — Honoring the Congolese Integration Network, Washington State Senate] In June 2019, CIN convened what organizers described as the first Washington State Congolese Summit, in Seattle, combining cultural celebration with discussion of integration. [ref: First of its kind in Seattle, Washington State Congolese Summit celebrates culture and discusses integration, Rainier Valley Corps] For CIN's planned Washington Refugee Healing Center, U.S. Representative Adam Smith submitted a Community Project Funding request, and $500,000 was included in the House Appropriations Committee's fiscal year 2023 appropriations bill; Smith cited CIN's language services, housing assistance and employment support. [ref: Rep. Smith Submits Community Project Funding Request for Congolese Integration Network, adamsmith.house.gov]

== Hengwa Star Foundation ==
In 2021, Mubalama founded the Hengwa Star Foundation in Bukavu, South Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, a nonprofit working with vulnerable people in eastern Congo, including a program that pays the hospital bills of mothers detained in health facilities after childbirth so that they can return home. [ref: From Refugee to Community Builder: Dr. Floribert Mubalama's Vision for Global Impact, YouTube]

== Author ==
Mubalama is the author of Echoes of the Ancients: Breaking Colonial Silence and Restoring Afrikan Dignity Within the Universal Story of Salvation, published in July 2026 (ISBN 979-8188740320). [ref: Echoes of the Ancients, Amazon]

== Recognition ==
In February 2022, the Washington State Senate adopted two resolutions connected with Mubalama's organization: Senate Resolution 8627, "Honoring the Congolese Integration Network" (adopted February 14, 2022), and Senate Resolution 8651, "Honoring the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Congolese Integration Network" (adopted February 21, 2022). [ref: SR 8627 — 2021-22: Honoring the Congolese Integration Network, Washington State Legislature] In 2026, the Congolese Integration Network received the WAVE Global Impact Organization Certification.

== References ==

Dulat Tursynuly Tastekey (; born 22 June 1982; [ref: Ұлттық спорт жанашыры Дулат Тастекей 44 жасқа толды, Adyrna.kz] also spelled Tastekeev) is a Kazakhstani entrepreneur and philanthropist. [ref: Более 1 млрд тенге на благотворительные проекты направил TAS GROUP за 5 лет, Kapital.kz] [ref: Танымал кәсіпкер Дулат Тастекеев әлеуметтік осал топқа жататын отбасыға үй әперетін болды, gov.kz] He is the founder and chief executive of TAS Group. [ref: В Казахстане может появиться еще один коммерческий банк, но придется подождать, Digital Business] [ref: Дулат Тастекеев намерен создать в Казахстане банк, Kapital.kz]

Dulat Tastekey is the founder of the Assyltas Public Foundation, vice-president of the International Kazakh Language Society (Qazaq Tili), and a deputy of the Almaty City Maslikhat since 2023, a trustee of the IQanat Foundation in Abai Region, chairman of the Board of Trustees of the Republican Abai National School, a member of the Board of Trustees of the Nazarbayev Intellectual School of Physics and Mathematics in Almaty, a member of the Board of Trustees of the Almaty City Toghyzkumalak Federation since 2023, and vice-president of the Kazakhstan Audaryspak Federation.

== Education ==
Dulat Tastekey graduated in 1999 from the Abai Republican Specialized Boarding School for gifted children in Almaty, with advanced study of the Kazakh language and literature.

In 2003, he graduated from the Kazakh Institute of Economics and Law in Almaty (now Caspian University).

In 2007, he graduated from the Kazakh Humanities and Law University (now Maqsut Narikbayev University).

In 2009, he graduated from the French business school HEC Paris.

In 2015, he completed the Practicum for Directors: Company Management at the Moscow School of Management SKOLKOVO.

In 2019, he received a PhD degree in Business Administration from Narxoz University. He also completed the Digital Transformation Management programme at the Moscow School of Management SKOLKOVO in 2019.

In 2024, he graduated from Harvard Business School. [ref: Дулат Тастекей: Приличные деньги нужно делать прилично, Forbes Kazakhstan] [ref: Стратегия вверх, Forbes Kazakhstan] In 2025, he completed a programme at the Stanford Graduate School of Business. [ref: Калифорния төріндегі кездесу: Дулат Тастекей Марат Омаровқа шапан жапты, Kursiv.media]

== Business career ==
Since 2003, Tastekey has held various positions in banking and financial institutions in Kazakhstan. In 2010, he became director of TAS Group. [ref: Дулат Тастекеев: Дерзкие мечты и кумиры финансиста, BIB.kz]

In 2018, he founded the Assyltas Public Foundation. [ref: Public Foundation "ASSYLTAS", Kompra]

== Public activities ==

=== Philanthropy and culture ===
From 2016 to 2019, an international aitys competition entitled Tugan zherge tuyngdy tik was held in Aksuat village, Tarbagatai District, with financial support from Tastekey. Six volumes of the almanac Tarikhka Toly Tarbagatai were published, as well as a collection of aitys performances from Aksuat entitled Tugan zherge tuyngdy tik. Since 2021, Tastekey has provided financial support for the organization and holding of the Asyl Dombra aitys competition.

Tastekey has supported the Abai Republican Specialized Boarding School for gifted children with advanced study of the Kazakh language and literature. With his sponsorship, an English-language specialist from abroad conducted courses at the school, and aitys competitions were organized among its students. [ref: АСЫЛ ӨНЕР САЙЫСЫ, Aikyn] Since 2018, he has awarded the Tarbagatai Tarlany medal to people originating from the Tarbagatai region who have made contributions to the region. In 2019, he established the Assyltas medal. [ref: Рухани жаңғыру: «Туған жер» мецената Дулата Тастекеева, Pushkin Library]

In 2018, Tastekey undertook to complete an unfinished central mosque in Semey, construction of which had begun in 2008; Kazinform reported in June 2018 that 500 million tenge had been allocated for the work. [ref: Кәсіпкер Семейдің 10 жылдан бері «сақалды» құрылысқа айналған мешітін салып бермек, Kazinform] The Abai Mosque, a four-minaret building with a capacity of 2,500 worshippers, was officially opened on 22 March 2021. Local media reported that the construction was financed with Tastekey's own funds. [ref: В Семее состоялось открытие новой мечети, AltaiNews]

In 2021, Tastekey published a book entitled Öte mañyzdy (Very Important). [ref: Өте маңызды. Кәсіпкер алдыңғы 10 жылда не нәрсеге дайын болуы керек, AmalBooks]

In 2025, to mark the 180th anniversary of the poet Abai Kunanbaiuly, the Assyltas Public Foundation announced that it would pay 180,000 tenge to families whose sons were born on 10 August 2025 and named Abai. The foundation later reported 33 such newborns in 13 regions of Kazakhstan. [ref: В Казахстане заплатят по 180 тысяч тенге каждому, кто выполнил это условие, Digital Business] [ref: По 180 тысяч тенге за сына с именем Абай: кто получит выплаты в Казахстане, Lada.kz]

Emilio Antonio Peroni (born 1977) is an Argentine pianist and teacher. He studied at the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén and at the Hochschule für Musik und Theater Rostock in Germany, where he lived and taught. In 2007, in a duo with violinist Pauline Reguig, he won the Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy Competition in the violin and piano duo category. [ref: Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy Wettbewerb 2007 entschieden – morgen Preisträgerkonzert, Stiftung Preußischer Kulturbesitz] He teaches piano and chamber music at the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén. [ref: Peroni: El piano en la música de cámara, Radio Nacional]

== Early life and education ==
Peroni was born in Neuquén in 1977 and grew up in Cipolletti, Río Negro Province. [ref: Emilio Peroni, una vida marcada por el tango, [[Río Negro (newspaper)] He entered the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén at the age of seven, graduated as a piano teacher, and taught there from 1995 to 2002. [ref: Famoso pianista regional en concierto, Río Negro] He studied with Miguel Martín Morales, Aldo Antognazzi and Bruno Leonardo Gelber in Argentina, with Carlo Bruno in Italy, with Ángel Soler in Barcelona and with Bernd Zack in Germany. [ref: Gala argentina en el Centro Sinfónico Nacional, Metro Blog La Paz] In the 1990s he and his brother, violist Eduardo Félix Peroni, played piano four hands on television. [ref: De las tandas de Canal 7 en la década del 90, a brindar conciertos en el CCK, LM Neuquén]

He received scholarships to study in Rome (1999) and Barcelona. In 2002 he moved to Rostock to study with Bernd Zack, [ref: Peroni viaja a Alemania y se despide con conciertos, Río Negro] and completed three postgraduate degrees at the Hochschule für Musik und Theater, two in piano and one in chamber music. [ref: Emilio Peroni, Editorial Municipal de Rosario]

== Career ==
In September 2005 he performed Mendelssohn's Concerto for Piano and Strings with the Neuquén Symphony Orchestra under Marcelo Álvarez; critic Horacio San Miguel called his performance "truly memorable". [ref: Peroni y Cazeneuve en un concierto para recordar, Río Negro] While living in Germany he formed a tango quintet. [ref: El pianista Emilio Peroni, clásico y popular, en Cipolletti, Río Negro] He has appeared as a soloist with orchestras in Germany, including the Rostock Philharmonic, and in Argentina, including the National Symphony Orchestra and orchestras in Rosario, San Juan and Neuquén. He has toured in Asia, with performances in the Philippines and Kuwait. In 2020 The Manila Times published an interview with him. [ref: A chat with Argentinian pianist Emilio Peroni, The Manila Times]

After returning to Argentina he settled in the Alto Valle region and joined the faculty of the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén. In March 2014 he opened the concert series of the Legislature of Neuquén Province with the recital Romanticismo puro. [ref: Emilio Peroni abre el ciclo de conciertos en la Legislatura, Neuquén Informa] In April 2016 he took part in the Uruguay for Export festival at the SODRE Auditorium in Montevideo. [ref: Espectáculos musicales para esta semana, [[El Observador (Uruguay)] In September 2017 he performed Rachmaninoff's Piano Concerto No. 2 with the National Symphony Orchestra of Bolivia under Weimar Arancibia in La Paz.

On 2 February 2018 he played Schubert's Trout Quintet at the Elbphilharmonie in Hamburg with Annette Schäfer, Naomi Seiler, Thomas Tyllack and Stefan Schäfer. [ref: Boletín Cultural e Informativo, febrero de 2018, Consulate General of Argentina in Hamburg] On 17 April 2019 he was the soloist in Dvořák's Piano Concerto with the National Symphony Orchestra under Rodolfo Saglimbeni at the Centro Cultural Kirchner in Buenos Aires. [ref: La Orquesta Sinfónica Nacional en el CCK los días 5, 17 y 26 de abril, Barriada] That year he and violinist Marco Fattorello gave a cycle of Mozart's violin sonatas at the Escuela Superior de Música de Neuquén. In May 2022 he gave a piano masterclass at the Faculty of Arts and Design of the National University of Cuyo and performed a Gershwin concerto with the university's orchestra. [ref: Emilio Peroni dictará una clase magistral de piano, Facultad de Artes y Diseño, Universidad Nacional de Cuyo] In July 2023 he returned to the Centro Cultural Kirchner as soloist with the National Symphony Orchestra in Schumann's Piano Concerto. Since 2019 he has hosted small recitals at his home in Neuquén, followed by conversations with the audience. [ref: Como en el teatro, pero en casa: los recitales íntimos de un músico neuquino, LM Neuquén]

== Awards ==
* First prize, Oscar Lorenzo Fernández Competition.
* Prize, 5th Pablo Casals Competition of the Centro Catalán de Rosario.

Draft text:
Wheel Well is a South African non-profit organisation working on child road safety and paediatric injury prevention. Founded in 2012 by road safety advocate Peggie Mars, the organisation operates from Bedfordview, Gauteng, and focuses on child restraint accessibility, pedestrian visibility, road safety education, and legislative advocacy.

Wheel Well's main programmes are the "Car Seats for Kids" campaign, which inspects, refurbishes, and redistributes pre-owned child safety seats to lower-income families, and the "Halo Beanie Project", a pedestrian safety campaign that provides reflective knitted beanies to primary school children who walk in low-light conditions. In 2016, the organisation received a Prince Michael International Road Safety Award in the Safer Road Users category.

== History ==
The legal entity behind Wheel Well was incorporated in 2008 as a shelf company under registration number 2008/004093/08. Following a transfer of the entity and a change of name and purpose, the organisation began operating in 2012 under founder Peggie Mars to address child road crash injuries and deaths in South Africa.

The organisation was established to counter the cost barrier to certified child restraints. Wheel Well is registered with the Department of Social Development as a Non-Profit Organisation (NPO 283-349) and recognised by the South African Revenue Service as a Public Benefit Organisation (PBO 930041005) with Section 18A tax-exempt status. Its showroom and testing facility are in Bedfordview, Gauteng.

== Road safety context in South Africa ==
According to the Road Traffic Management Corporation (RTMC), road traffic crashes in South Africa caused 11,485 deaths in 2025. Pedestrians were the largest group, accounting for 45.49% of road deaths (5,224 fatalities). Children aged 14 and younger accounted for 8.9% of road deaths (1,034 children in 2025). National records show that 39% of pedestrian fatalities and 35% of fatal crashes occur between 17:00 and 22:00, when visibility is reduced.

Economic modelling by the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and the RTMC estimates that for every road death, South African health services treat about 4.8 to 4.9 serious injuries and 14.9 slight injuries. Research at Red Cross War Memorial Children's Hospital has found that road traffic crashes are a leading cause of severe paediatric trauma and intensive care admissions, with pedestrian injuries the most common among primary school-aged children.

== Programmes ==
=== Car Seats for Kids ===
Launched in 2012, "Car Seats for Kids" collects donated pre-owned infant, toddler, and booster seats from the public. Each seat is inspected, cleaned, and refurbished before being passed on to families unable to afford new certified restraints.

Seats that fail safety checks, have been in a collision, or are past the manufacturer's expiry date are taken out of circulation and dismantled for recycling. By 2026, the campaign had provided seats to more than 12,000 children. The organisation also offers fitment demonstrations and gives installation and sizing advice to parents through messaging platforms.

=== Halo Beanie Project ===
The "Halo Beanie Project" is a pedestrian visibility campaign aimed at children who walk to school along unlit roads in informal settlements and peri-urban areas, under the slogan "Children should be seen and not hurt".

Wheel Well supplies community knitting groups and older crafters with packs of acrylic yarn blended with retroreflective thread. The resulting beanies reflect vehicle headlights, making child pedestrians visible to drivers from further away. The beanies are distributed to learners at primary schools along busy roads.

== Advocacy ==
Wheel Well campaigns for changes to road safety regulation under the National Road Traffic Act, including:
* extending mandatory child restraint requirements to all child passengers up to 1.5 metres in height;
* a 30 km/h speed limit around school zones, supported by traffic calming infrastructure;
* amending scholar transport and public passenger vehicle loading rules to count every child as a full occupant ("Every Child as a Person") rather than applying fractional passenger allowances;
* expanding national crash records to show whether child victims were travelling in private cars, scholar transport, or open light delivery vehicles.

== Recognition ==
* 2016: Prince Michael International Road Safety Award (Safer Road Users category) for the Car Seats for Kids campaign.
* 2018: Gumtree Women in Autos Award, presented to founder Peggie Mars.
* 2024: Rotary International Paul Harris Fellow, awarded to Peggie Mars.
* 2025: Old Mutual Award for Excellence in Child Road Safety.

Draft text:
The mayor of Santa Monica is the presiding officer and ceremonial head of the municipal government of Santa Monica, California. Santa Monica has a council–manager government in which legislative authority is vested in the seven-member Santa Monica City Council, while the administration of city services is supervised by a professional city manager. [ref: Charter of the City of Santa Monica, Article V: Form of Government, City of Santa Monica]

The mayor is not elected separately by the public. Instead, the City Council selects one of its own members to serve as mayor. The mayor remains a voting councilmember and has the same voice and vote in council proceedings as every other member. [ref: Charter of the City of Santa Monica, Article VI: The City Council, City of Santa Monica] The incumbent mayor is Caroline Torosis, who was sworn in on December 9, 2025, succeeding Lana Negrete.

==Mayor pro tempore==

The council also designates a mayor pro tempore. The mayor pro tempore presides over council meetings and performs the mayor's duties when the mayor is absent or unable to serve. Unlike the mayoral rotation, the mayor pro tempore may be selected by a simple majority without regard to length of council service. [ref: Rules of Order and Procedure for the Conduct of City Council Meetings, City of Santa Monica]

If both officers are absent from a meeting, the city clerk calls the meeting to order and the councilmembers present elect a temporary presiding officer. The incumbent mayor pro tempore is Jesse Zwick, who was sworn in on December 9, 2025.

==History==

Santa Monica was incorporated in 1886. Juan José Carrillo is identified by the Santa Monica History Museum as the city's first judge, mayor and city trustee. [ref: Santa Monica History, Santa Monica History Museum]

In 1975, Nat Trives became Santa Monica's first African-American mayor. [ref: On the Ground Q&A: Nat Trives, Stanford Law School] In 2015, Antonio Vazquez became the city's first Latino mayor. [ref: Santa Monica's First Latino Mayor Prepares to Take Office During Development Wars, Santa Monica Lookout]

== ZAŠTO U KESICAMA OMILJENIH GRICKALICA DOBIJAMO SVE MANJE SADRŽAJA: NAUČNICI OTKRILI TAJNU FORMULU “TIHOG SAMANJIVANJA” ==
Jeste li primijetili da kada otvorite vašu omiljenu grickalicu da obicno na dnu kesice ostane mnogo više praznog prostora nego ranije? Svi smo mislili da nam se pričinjava ili da fabrike samo štede na pakovanju, ali najnovija nezavisna istraživanja tržišta pokazuju da je riječ o sistematskom planu čiji je jedini cilj da nam daju manje, a da platimo [ref: DOI desativado, doi.org]više.

=== Šta kaže analiza “nestajuce gramaže”? ===
U nedavnoj studiji koju su sprovele evropske institucije za zaštitu potrošača naučnici su uporedili staru fabričku specifikaciju grickalica sa ovim što se danas nalazi na rafovima. Ispostavilo se da proizvođači već godinama ne mijenjaju cijenu, niti da drastično smanjuju samu kesicu spolja, već primjenjuju metodu poznatu kao „mikro-skaliranje mase“.

Istraživači tvrde da fabrike svake dvije godine tiho smanje količinu proizvoda u pakovanju tačno 5 do 8 gr. Pošto je ta razlika premala da bi je čovjek primijetio golim okom kada uzme kesicu u ruku, kupac nastavlja da plaća istu cijenu, nesvjestan da zapravo kupuje sve vazdušastiji I prazniji proizvod.
[[File:SnackfoodRackDF.JPG|thumb|Rafovi sa grickalicama]]

Dr Marko Vasic, stručnjak za ekonomiju maloprodaje, objasnio je za stručne časopise kako fabrike uspijevaju da sakriju ovu prevaru: [ref: referenca se odnosi na izjavu stručnjaka]

„Proizvođači su shvatili da bi naglo podizanje cijena odmah izazvalo revolt kod kupaca. Zbog toga se odlučuju za mnogo efikasniji metod – tiho smanjivanje gramaže unutar iste ambalaže. Kupac misli da kupuje isto pakovanje kao i prije pet godina, ali zapravo u prosjeku dobija i do 20% manje proizvoda po istoj cijeni. To je čist profit za fabrike, dok potrošač plaća 'prazan hod',“ navodi se u izvještaju.

Moya Chou () is a Taiwanese film colorist who has worked in post-production color grading for nearly thirty years, spanning both the photochemical and digital eras. [ref: 周佳聖獲金馬傑出電影工作者 調光周處除三害等片, [[Central News Agency (Taiwan)] [ref: 〈金馬63 年度台灣傑出電影工作者〉橫跨底片數位30年 光影魔術師周佳聖獲獎, Liberty Times] [ref: 第63屆金馬獎入圍名單公布, Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee] In 2026 he was named Outstanding Taiwanese Filmmaker of the Year by the Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee at the 63rd Golden Horse Awards, [ref: Nominees of the 63rd Golden Horse Awards Announced, Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee] [ref: Sabu's 'Arrested Memory' Leads Golden Horse Awards Nominations, Shu Qi's 'Girl' Close Behind, [[Variety (magazine)] and accepted the drama Innovation Award at the 61st Golden Bell Awards on behalf of the Netflix series Agent from Above (Jishen), on which he served as colorist. [ref: 金鐘61／《乩身》奪創新獎！調光師周佳聖緊張喊「想退休」 盼台劇登國際, Videoland News]

== Career ==
Moya Chou has worked in post-production color grading for close to thirty years, a career that spans the transition from photochemical film to digital cinema. He originally aspired to be an animator and had been accepted by an animation company, but on the advice of his elder brother, who worked at a film equipment company, he entered color grading instead, while the industry was still working on film. [ref: 調光師／周佳聖 《誰先愛上他的》驚艷許多觀眾的色彩，就是他的傑作！, Facebook (official page of Dear Ex)] In the early 2010s he graded films whose post-production was handled by 利達數位影音科技, including Taipei Exchanges and 金城小子; from 2011 he was credited as digital colorist under Pixelfly (傳翼數位影像) on films such as 10+10 and Machi Action, and on The Soul (2021) he was credited under Tetsujin Post-Production (大鐵人影製所). While at Pixelfly he took on his first television series, An Innocent Mistake (罪美麗), at the request of writer-producer Mag Hsu, and went on to grade her series Apple in Your Eye (妹妹) and her film Dear Ex. In December 2017 he spoke on digital grading practice, representing Pixelfly, at a forum of the Formosa Festival of International Filmmaker Awards in Taichung. [ref: 【國際論壇｜認識影像後期流程：數位調光實務分享】主講人：傳翼數位影像周佳聖, Facebook (Formosa Festival of International Filmmaker Awards)] He has graded feature films including Dear Ex, The Soul, I WeirDO, The Pig, the Snake and the Pigeon and A Foggy Tale, and in 2026 graded Sayang, 告別的年代 and The Photo from 1977. In television he has graded series such as Three Tears in Borneo and Imperfect Us, and Taiwan Cinema describes him as a renowned colorist who also runs filmmaking and color grading workshops to train industry talent. [ref: Moya CHOU, Taiwan Cinema]

On the public television series Three Tears in Borneo, Moya Chou set a warm, yellow-brown base grade with Kodak 400T-style film grain to convey the weight of a Second World War prison-camp story, contrasting it with brighter, more saturated colors for flashback scenes. [ref: 《聽海湧》主創分享系列 調光師_周佳聖, Facebook (official page of Three Tears in Borneo)] In 2020 he discussed his grading of I WeirDO in an interview on the podcast 後期刊. [ref: EP.09｜用顏色說故事的「怪胎」專訪 Ft. 調光師周佳聖, 後期刊 (podcast)] He has also taught color grading workshops, including at Unseen Film Studio's training program, covering shot balancing, color continuity and look development. [ref: 【調光工作坊｜課程紀錄】, Facebook (Unseen Film Studio)] [ref: 獨家｜走自己的路 金鐘導演孫介珩在高雄打造影視培力基地, Next Apple News]

On 1 October 2026, Wen Tien-hsiang, CEO of the Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee, announced Moya Chou as the Outstanding Taiwanese Filmmaker of the Year at the nominations press conference of the 63rd Golden Horse Awards. The committee cited his close collaboration with directors and cinematographers on stories set in different eras and cultural backgrounds. On 26 October 2026 he accepted the drama Innovation Award at the 61st Golden Bell Awards on behalf of Agent from Above, on which he served as colorist; in his speech he described innovation as "using new methods to explore more beautiful possibilities". [ref: 金鐘61／周佳聖憑《乩身》奪創新獎！自曝曾考慮退休 謝團隊開拓未知, Wow!NEWS (via yam.com)]

== Awards ==
* 2026: Outstanding Taiwanese Filmmaker of the Year, 63rd Golden Horse Awards [ref: 第63屆金馬獎 入圍及得獎名單, Taipei Golden Horse Film Festival Executive Committee] [ref: 金馬63／完整入圍名單揭曉！影后竟無台灣女演員 《狂忘警探》11項大贏家《女孩》緊追在後, Mirror Daily (via Yahoo News Taiwan)]
* 2026: Innovation Award (drama), 61st Golden Bell Awards – accepted on behalf of Agent from Above

= Vident Group =
Vident Group is a Latvia-based financial research and consulting institution specialising in equity research, investment analysis, and financial market research. Based in Riga, the firm focuses on publicly traded companies across European and international equity markets. [ref: Vident Group, SIA, www.firmas.lv]

Its research combines fundamental and technical analysis to assess corporate financial performance, business valuations, competitive positioning, and investment risks. [ref: Vident Group SIA - LEI: 894500RKYWIBW8KM7S55, Bloomberg LEI]

== History and Background ==
Vident Group was established in Riga, Latvia, in May 2026, operating within the financial research and consulting sector. The firm was founded with a focus on equity research, corporate financial analysis, and the evaluation of publicly traded companies across international capital markets. Its research activities encompass both buy-side and sell-side equity analysis, incorporating fundamental financial assessments and market-based analytical methodologies. [ref: Sabiedrība ar ierobežotu atbildību "Vident Group", 40203744523 - about - Kombo.lv, www.kombo.lv]

The company is registered in the Latvian Commercial Register and is also mentioned on Bloomberg business, which maintains corporate identification and registration information for entities operating across international financial markets. [ref: Vident Group SIA - LEI: 894500RKYWIBW8KM7S55, Bloomberg LEI]

== Operations ==
Vident Group conducts financial research on publicly traded companies across different industries and geographic markets. [ref: Vident Group,SIA - VERTA.LV]

Its activities include evaluating corporate financial performance, estimating intrinsic valuations, examining competitive environments, and assessing economic developments that may influence business performance. [ref: Vident Group,SIA - VERTA.LV]

The firm's research combines quantitative and qualitative methods, incorporating financial statement analysis, valuation modelling, financial forecasting, scenario analysis, and technical market analysis. [ref: Vident Group, SIA, www.firmas.lv]

== Research Methodology ==

Cyclone Arnab is a currently active cyclone in the Bay of Bengal threatening South India. The eighth depression and first cyclone of the 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season, Arnab originated from a low-pressure area in the eastern Bay of Bengal that had been meandering for several days.

==Meteorological history==

On 20 October, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) began to monitor the Bay of Bengal for a low-pressure area that was likely to develop within 24 hours. [ref: REGIONAL SPECIALISED METEOROLOGICAL CENTRE -TROPICAL CYCLONES, NEW DELHI TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK, India Meteorological Department] Three days later, a low-pressure area formed over the eastcentral–southcentral Bay of Bengal under the influence of an upper-level cyclonic circulation. Favourable conditions prevailed over the central Bay of Bengal, with the Madden–Julian oscillation enhancing thunderstorm activity. Sea surface temperatures were, while wind shear was moderate. [ref: REGIONAL SPECIALISED METEOROLOGICAL CENTRE -TROPICAL CYCLONES, NEW DELHI TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK, India Meteorological Department] By 12:00 UTC on 24 October, the well-marked low pressure area concentrated into a depression over the central Bay of Bengal. [ref: REGIONAL SPECIALISED METEOROLOGICAL CENTRE -TROPICAL CYCLONES, NEW DELHI SPECIAL TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK, India Meteorological Department] [ref: REGIONAL SPECIALISED METEOROLOGICAL CENTRE -TROPICAL CYCLONES, NEW DELHI SPECIAL TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK, India Meteorological Department] The system, marked Invest 98B by the United States Navy's Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC), consisted of a partially exposed but consolidating low-level circulation and developing banding features to the south and east of the depression’s vicinity as a TCFA was issued at 11:00 UTC. On 25 October at 09:30 UTC, the IMD reported that the system intensified to a deep depression. [ref: REGIONAL SPECIALISED METEOROLOGICAL CENTRE -TROPICAL CYCLONES, NEW DELHI SPECIAL TROPICAL WEATHER OUTLOOK, India Meteorological Department] The next day, the system strengthened into a cyclonic storm and was assigned the name Arnab. [ref: NATIONAL BULLETIN NO. 8 (BOB/08/2026), rsmcnewdelhi.imd.gov.in] 12 hours later, Arnab intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. [ref: NATIONAL BULLETIN NO. 12 (BOB/08/2026), mausam.imd.gov.in] Six hours later, Arnab intensified into a very severe cyclonic storm. [ref: NATIONAL BULLETIN NO. 14 (BOB/08/2026), mausam.imd.gov.in]

==Preparations==
===India===
====Andhra Pradesh====
The IMD declared red alerts in seven districts in Andhra Pradesh on 26 October. 15 teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) were mobilised in Andhra Pradesh while ₹27 crore in relief was released by the state. Schools in 10 districts were closed. [ref: Schools closed tomorrow in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha amid Cyclone Arnab, India Today] By 27 October, at least 89,000 people were evacuated in Andhra Pradesh. [ref: India evacuates tens of thousands as Cyclone Arnab nears eastern coast in Andhra Pradesh state, Associated Press]

Andhra Pradesh called on boats to return from sea and identified 570,000 people as vulnerable in preparation for evacuations. [ref: India to evacuate thousands as Cyclone Arnab nears eastern coast, Reuters] By 26 October, Andhra Pradesh officials stated that over 30,000 fishing boats had returned to harbour. [ref: ] The Chintoor Integrated Tribal Development Officer directed the suspension of tourism boat operations to the Papikonda hills in Godavari Valley. [ref: Cyclone Arnab: Over 4,800 fishing vessels return safely to Kakinada coast, The Hindu] Rail service on 53 routes in southern India were suspended on 27–28 October, [ref: Thousands evacuate India's eastern coast ahead of Cyclone Arnab, Reuters] including the Godavari Express, Gowthami Express, Visakha Express, Falaknuma Express, Narasapur Express, and the Garib Rath Express. 21 flights were cancelled at Vijayawada Airport and Visakhapatnam Airport, with cancellations also occurring at Gannavaram Airport. [ref: Cyclone Arnab Live: Schools shut, evacuations begin in Andhra, Odisha ahead of landfall, India Today]

====Odisha====
The government of Odisha declared that over 1,700 shelters were prepared in the state's southern districts. Eight NDRF teams and 40 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force teams were mobilised. [ref: A.P., Odisha on alert as cyclone ‘Arnab’ nears land, The Hindu] The closure of schools and colleges in five districts was announced for 28–29 October.

==Impacts==
===India===
====Andhra Pradesh====
As Arnab approached landfall, trees were uprooted in Visakhapatnam. A man died after touching a fallen live wire in Visakhapatnam. [ref: ]

====Elsewhere====
Persistent rainfall in the Nilgiris district in Tamil Nadu caused as many as 69 landslips on 25 and 26 October, damaging power lines, revetments, and 16 huts. [ref: Nilgiris district hit by 62 minor landslips in a day till October 25 morning, The Hindu]

Robert Perks (Dec 1919 – July 2005) was a New Zealand music educator, conductor, composer and multi-instrumentalist. He founded the Christchurch School of Instrumental Music in 1955 and served as its musical director until 1975. [ref: Let the Children Play: A 25-Year History of the Christchurch School of Instrumental Music, University of Canterbury]. Perks was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire for services to music education in 1985. [ref: Award to Musician, The Press]

== Biography ==

=== Early life ===
Robert Perks was born in St Clair Dunedin, New Zealand, in December 1919 to John Alfred Perks (a newsagent or delivery agent for the "Evening Star") [ref: Many high notes in a lifetime of music, The Christchurch Star] and Mabel May Perks. He attended St Clair Primary School from 1925 to 1931. He entered Dunedin Technical High School (also known as King Edward Technical College) in 1932.

While at the Dunedin Technical College, he came under the influence of T Vernon Griffiths, and credits his musical career to Professor Griffiths: "He started me on my musical career. What a great man he is. I owe him more than any other man." Griffiths paid for his advanced piano tuition out of his "own meagre pay". According to Perks, it was the intervention of Griffiths and Perks' headmaster, that meant the young Perks did not become a butcher and was able to pursue a music education career.

He married Myrtle Wood of Roxburgh in 1942.

=== Education ===
In 1938, Perks began studying at Dunedin Teachers' Training College, specialising in music and received a University of Otago music bursary. He completed a Bachelor of Music degree in 1941. [ref: NZ Composers' Festival - Centennial Composition of Robert Perks, The Press]

Perks enlisted in the Army in 1941 and later transferred to the Navy and was able to continue his studies while a Petty Officer radio mechanic in the Navy. While at the Devonport Base he became the official organist and took lessons from the Auckland Cathedral organist, Edgar Randal. He gained the Licentiate of the Royal Schools of Music diploma in organ in 1944. [ref: Music Appointment, The Press]

=== Career ===
In 1945, Perks became music master at Christchurch Technical College, where he worked for eight years before joining Christchurch Teachers’ College in 1955. [ref: Pupils 9 Orchestras To Give Concert, The Press] He had broad experience teaching young people and wrote two school music publications that were widely used in New Zealand schools. In 1955, Perks began an experimental instrumental scheme for 50 primary-school pupils under a subcommittee of the Primary Schools’ Music Festival Association. The scheme aimed to provide affordable group tuition and practical experience of orchestral playing. This grew quickly and became the Christchurch School of Instrumental Music (later the Christchurch School of Music | Te Kura Puoro), which regularly celebrates its founding by Robert Perks in 1955. This work provided music education to over a thousand students each year while he was the Music Director of that organisation from 1955 to 1975.

Perks was also an award-winning composer, winning the composition competition run by the Canterbury Centennial Association in 1950 [ref: Awards in NZ Composers' Contest, Greymouth Evening Star], among other awards. An Allegro was performed by the Christchurch Chamber Music Players in 1952 [ref: Works by NZ Composers - Concert in the Civic Theatre, The Press]. He regularly composed music for young musicians to play.

== Published works ==
Robert perks wrote a series of books for music teachers, learners and families. They were published by local publishers AH and AW Reed. The series was called Music in School, A modern approach in the classroom. Book 1 was the Teacher's Manual, book 2 was Short Score, and book 3 was The Main Progression (for beginners) Supplementary Parts. The series included scores for playing in groups for different instruments including recorder (descant), cello, bass, B Flat clarinet, percussion, melodica and autoharp, chime bar, and guitar. He also wrote Music Making in School and Home, also published by Reeds in 1965. [ref: Music Making in School and Home, A H Reed & A W Reed]

As an academic, Perks published a few accounts of his musical education endeavours, or as he termed them, "experiments". In the London journal, "Music in Education" he described his work in mass music education as, "an interesting New Zealand experiment." [ref: An interesting New Zealand experiment, Music in Education] Similarly, a year earlier he published "Christchurch music experiment: schools instrumental scheme" in the New Zealand journal "National Education". [ref: Christchurch music experiment: schools instrumental scheme, National Education]

== Honours and legacy ==
Perks was awarded life membership of the Christchurch School of Instrumental Music in 1978. At the time the newspaper, The Press, commented, "The success attending Mr Perks' efforts has aroused interest abroad, and the numbers of players in orchestras from the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra downwards, who began their training in the C.S.I.M. orchestras, is sufficient tribute to the worth of the training. They and the many hundreds of others who owe their present love of music and attendant broadening of their experiences to Mr Perks and his work must be a constant satisfaction to him in his retirement." [ref: Fine Progress shows in young orchestras, The Press]
[truncated]

For other people named William Clark, see William Clark (disambiguation).

William Clark (1953 - 2017) was a Historian and author. Though trained in the History of science, much of his work was on the broader History of European universities, about which he wrote many articles. This was also the topic of his award-winning book, Academic Charisma and the Origins of the Research University. In addition, he also published several edited books on the history of science and of modern Bureaucracy.

== Early life and education ==
William Clark was born in southern California and grew up there, studying at the University of California, Los Angeles. He received his Ph.D. degree in European history from there in 1986, with a dissertation titled "From the Medieval Universitas Scholarium to the German Research University - A Sociogenesis of the German Academic"; the dissertation was advised by Robert S. Westman and M. Norton Wise. [ref: https://www.proquest.com/docview/303398279/abstract/E2B1833B558C40B1PQ/1?sourcetype=Dissertations%20&%20Theses]

== Career ==
Clark was an expert on the history of the University. In his numerous articles, he traced the origins of such features of academic life as the Doctor of Philosophy and the Seminar. [ref: Bill Clark or the Ironic Analyst of homo academicus, History of Science Society Newsletter] [ref: Bill Clark or the Ironic Analyst of homo academicus, CAKtus: Le carnet du Centre Alexandre-Koyre] His book Academic Charisma and the Origins of the Research University traced a series of shifts from the Oral culture of the Medieval university to the modern Research university. In an essay review of the book in The New Yorker, Anthony Grafton described it as a study of "the mixed inheritance of the modern university", and said that Clark "[made] his case with analytic shrewdness, an exuberant love of archival anecdote, and a wry sense of humor." [ref: The Nutty Professors, The New Yorker] The book won the Morris D. Forkosch Prize awarded by the Journal of the History of Ideas for the best book in Intellectual history published in 2006. [ref: Notices, Journal of the History of Ideas]

Clark was also active in assembling Edited volumes on the history of science. One such volume he edited (with co-editors Jan Golinski and Simon Schaffer), titled The Sciences in Enlightened Europe, assembled scholarly contributions on a wide range of Branches of science during the 18th century Age of Enlightenment. [ref: The Sciences in Enlightened Europe, University of Chicago Press] Another work he edited, along with Peter Becker, was Little Tools of Knowledge: Historical Essays on Academic and Bureaucratic Practices. [ref: Little Tools of Knowledge: Historical Essays on Academic and Bureaucratic Practices., University of Michigan Press]

Clark held teaching positions at a number of institutions including Columbia University and Bryn Mawr College in the US, the University of Göttingen in Germany, and the University of Cambridge in the UK. He also held a research fellowship at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science in Germany. Despite these accomplishments, however, he never held a Tenure-track position. [ref: In Memoriam - William Clark, 1953-217, History of Science Society Newsletter] [ref: Erinnerung an Bill Clark, Nach Feierabend: Materialgeschichten]

== Bibliography ==

=== Books ===

* Clark, William (2006). Academic Charisma and the Origins of the Research University. Chicago, Illinois, U.S.: University of Chicago Press.  ISBN 9780226109213
* Becker, Pete; Clark, William, eds. (2001). Little Tools of Knowledge: Historical Essays on Academic and Bureaucratic Practices. Ann Arbor, Michigan, U.S.: University of Michigan Press.  ISBN 9780472111084
* Clark, William; Golinski, Jan; Schaffer, Simon (1999). The Sciences in Enlightened Europe.  Chicago, Illinois, U.S.: University of Chicago Press.  ISBN 9780226109398

=== Scholarly articles ===

* Clark, William (2007). “Les trois épreuves de la quête du diplôme en Europe." Trans. Aurélien Berra. In Christian Jacob, ed.  Lieux de savoir. Espaces et communautés, pp. 77-98. Paris, France: Albin Michel.  ISBN 9782226179043
* Clark, William (2007). “Die Politik der Ontologie." Trans. Martin Dehli. In Michael Hagner & Manfred Laubichler, eds. Der Hochsitz des Wissens: das Allgemeine als wissenschaftlicher Wert, pp. 97-127. Zürich, Switzerland: Diaphanes.  ISBN 9783935300797
* Clark, William (2005). “Einsteins Haar." Trans. Michael Adrian. In Michael Hagner, ed. Einstein on the Beach. Der Physiker als Phänomen, pp. 15-39. Frankfurt am Main, Germany: Fischer.  ISBN 9783596165155. Republished in Michael Hagner & Christoph Hoffmann (2018), Nach Feierabend: Materialgeschichten, pp. 203-228. Zürich, Switzerland: Diaphanes.  ISBN 9783035801309
* Clark, William (2003). “On the Professorial Voice." Science in Context 16, 1/2: 43-57.  doi: https://doi.org/10.1017/S0269889703000693
* Clark, William (2003). “The Pursuit of the Prosopography of Science." In Roy Porter, ed. The Cambridge History of Science, vol. 4: Eighteenth-Century Science, pp. 211-237. Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press.  doi: https://doi.org/10.1017/CHOL9780521572439.010

Yan Margulis is a renovation contractor and owner of Capable Group, an Ontario business whose work includes basement, kitchen, bathroom and full-home renovations in Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area. [ref: Cap-Able Group Consulting Inc., Better Business Bureau] [ref: Home Renovation in Toronto, Capable Group]

== Career ==
Before establishing Capable Group, Margulis worked directly on renovations and alongside different trades. The company, established in 2017, brought those areas of experience into one business. In a September 2024 advertorial, City Life described Margulis as having more than 25 years of renovation experience and reported his explanation that combining his previous work led to the company's formation. [ref: Capable Group Inc.: Transform Your Space With The Best, City Life] The Better Business Bureau records the business as established on 5 April 2017.

Capable's initial focus was basement renovation. By the time of the 2024 profile, its work had expanded into kitchens, bathrooms and other residential spaces.

== Renovation work ==
In a century-old basement, a project that began as refinishing expanded to include underpinning, waterproofing and structural reinforcement. The homeowner reported that Capable handled the additional work within the agreed budget, while the project manager and site supervisor remained responsive to questions. This account was published by the customer on HomeStars on 9 December 2024. [ref: Reviews of Capable Group – Basement Renovation & Finishing Company, HomeStars]

After Capable finished her basement, Mary Noce hired the company again for a full kitchen renovation. In her account, the team worked with her kitchen vision and Ludmila's design input, with plumbing and electrical trades contributing to the finished room. Noce credited Margulis and Ludmila's experience and leadership, and reported that the work finished within the established timeframe and budget. She described the sequence in a HomeStars review published on 8 January 2025.

The company's HomeStars profile also records recognition in 2025: it displays a Best of Awards 2025 badge and identifies Capable as a five-time winner. The award belongs to Capable Group. [ref: Profile of Capable Group – Basement Renovation & Finishing Company, HomeStars]

The broader review record includes 84 HomeStars reviews with a displayed rating of 4.9 out of 5 on the page consulted in October 2026. A separate Birdeye listing displayed 80 reviews attributed to Google for Capable Group Design Build Renovations. [ref: Capable Group Design Build Renovations, Birdeye]

The company's published portfolio also includes full-home renovations. Its Mississauga case study follows a completed project from the covered front entry through the main floor and into the basement. The documented scope includes the kitchen, living and dining areas, bathrooms and basement rooms, bringing several parts of the house within the same renovation. [ref: Mississauga Full-Home Renovation, Capable Group]

Capable describes its full-home service as coordinating design, permits and construction, with a project lead and an itemized fixed quote for the agreed scope. Its design-build process includes reviewing how layouts, building services, material selections and the order of trades connect across the project. [ref: Design-Build Renovations Toronto, Capable Group]

== Maryani Kitchen Studio ==
As of October 2026, Maryani Kitchen Studio's website presented it as part of Capable Group, with a focus on custom kitchens in Toronto and the Greater Toronto Area. The site describes Maryani as growing out of Capable's residential renovation work and combining that experience with cabinetmaking. It identifies Margulis as Capable Group's founder and owner, and describes the studio's services as designing, making and installing kitchens. [ref: Maryani Kitchen Studio — Custom Kitchens in Toronto & the GTA, Maryani Kitchen Studio]

== Renovation approach ==
Margulis has discussed the relationship between a room's intended use and the construction it requires. In CAA Magazine, he explained that converting a basement into a separate apartment involves additional building requirements, materials and labour compared with finishing it for personal use. [ref: What to expect when renovating a basement, CAA North & East Ontario]

In the 2024 City Life profile, Margulis identified completed spaces, satisfied clients and keeping work within the client's budget as motivations for his work. The same profile described showroom visits and three-dimensional renderings used to present the proposed space and materials before clients signed a contract.

== References ==

== Настанак пројекта ==
Група студената са Београдског универзитета покренула је пројекат „Пауза 24“, којом позива младе да проведу један дан без друштвених мрежа. Идеја је настала након што су студенти приметили колико времена свакодневно проводе на телефонима, чак и када имају обавезе за факултет. Уместо да време искористе за учење, одмор или да га проведу са својом породицом/пријатељима, многи заврше скролујући сатима по интернету, а да тога нису ни свесни.

== Ширење на интернету ==
Покрет се брзо проширио међу студентима, првенствено преко Instagrama и Tiktoka, где су учесници делили колико времена проводе крај малих екрана. Уз hashtag #Пауза24, објављивали су снимке и позивали колеге да им се придруже. Организатори су истакли да циљ није да се друштвене мреже потпуно избаце из живота, већ да це људи подсете да постоји и живот ван екрана.

== Реакција јавности ==
Ипак, нису сви подржали ову идеју. Док једни сматрају да би дан без телефона помогао младима да се боље концентришу и више посвете себи, други мисле да су друштвене мреже постале важан део свакодневног живота. Преко њих студенти добијају информације о предавањима, договарају групне пројекте и прате актуелна дешавања свакодневно.

== Последице и утицај ==
Иако је реч о краткотрајном пројекту, „Пауза 24“ отворила је питање колико смо заправо зависни од својих телефона и да ли можемо да контролишемо време које проводимо на интернету. Неки учесници су одлучили да наставе да мање користе друштвене мреже и након завршетка акције, док су се други убрзо вратили старим (лошим) навикама.

== References ==

LyvWell Apartments is a multifamily property management company operating across North America. LyvWell Apartments has a team of more than 1,200 associates that manage a mix of high-rise, mid-rise and garden-style communities including stabilized properties as well as developments.

== History ==
Formerly Brookfield Properties Multifamily [ref: ], LyvWell Apartments focuses primarily on operating multifamily communities on behalf of Brookfield Corporation. The LyvWell name launched in October 2026 [ref: ] and builds on institutional expertise and operational excellence to manage a diverse range of residential properties, including market-rate, mixed-use, and workforce housing communities.

== Operations ==
LyvWell Apartments operates apartment communities, each with distinctive property names. Its portfolio includes properties in cities such as Los Angeles, Las Vegas, Phoenix, Denver, Dallas, Houston, Nashville, New York City, District of Columbia and internationally, Toronto and Vancouver. The wilted rose emoji () is an emoji depicting a wilted flower. [ref: Wilted Flower Emoji, Emojipedia] In early 2025, it became popular on TikTok as an ironic alternative to the broken heart emoji (), which some users considered overused. [ref: Gen Z’s Chaotic, Ironic Emoji Swapping Meme, Emojipedia] [ref: Why Gen Z is ditching popular emojis for unexpected alternatives, Fast Company] It was added to Unicode 9.0 and Emoji 3.0 in 2016. It is used to express sadness, heartbreak, grief, or disappointment, sometimes in an ironic manner.

According to an analysis of Google data by The New York Times, the wilted rose emoji was 2025's fastest-growing emoji in popularity and the 93rd most used overall. [ref: The wilting rose emoji: what its rise and fall tells us about gen Alpha, The Guardian] It has become particularly popular among Generation Alpha, who use it to express sadness or mock heartbreak.

Linguist Adam Aleksic (also known as Etymology Nerd online) has described the wilted rose emoji as an example of a "forced emoji", an emoji meme that users have deliberately assigned meaning to.

= Blake Schultz =
Blake Schultz (born July 3, 2003) is an American business development professional associated with [https://agdrives.com/ AG Drives], a driveline manufacturing company based in Green Bay, Wisconsin. He serves as the company's director of business development, working across sales, marketing, digital strategy, and business operations. Schultz graduated from the University of Minnesota in 2025 with a degree in business marketing.

== Early life ==
Blake Schultz was born in Green Bay, Wisconsin, and grew up in the Green Bay area. His early experiences in the region preceded his involvement in manufacturing and business development.

He attended high school in the Green Bay area before enrolling at the University of Minnesota. Through his subsequent professional work, he became involved with AG Drives, a company with longstanding family connections to the regional manufacturing industry.

== Education ==
Blake Schultz attended the University of Minnesota from 2021 to 2025, earning a degree in business marketing through the College of Education and Human Development. His academic studies included management, organizational leadership, entrepreneurship, and business law. He also earned a university sales certificate. Additionally, was apart of the Beta Eta Chapter of Delta Tau Delta Fraternity from 2022-2025 and was the Fraternity Awards & Accreditations Report Chairman for the 2024 year. While also serving on the Honor Board and the Social Commitee.

During his university years, Schultz participated in student leadership and investment research activities. From February to December 2024, he served as president of the College of Education and Human Development Student Board.

He also volunteered with the David S. Kidwell Funds Enterprise's Growth Fund Consumer Team from February to September 2024. In that role, he gained exposure to financial research and company analysis, using tools including Bloomberg Terminal, Capital IQ, and Microsoft Excel.

Schultz's university experience included an international study experience in Madrid, Spain. He has also pursued professional development outside his degree program, including participation in the Professional Golfers' Association of America Professional Golf Management pathway.

== Career ==

=== Early professional experience ===
Before and during his transition into business development, Schultz gained experience in customer service, sales, team leadership, and operational work. These experiences contributed to his interest in business management and entrepreneurship.

He also maintained professional involvement in golf operations, including work with Green Bay Country Club. His experience across different industries provided exposure to customer relationships, service delivery, and organizational operations.

=== AG Drives ===
Schultz joined AG Drives, a Green Bay-based manufacturer of custom driveshafts and industrial driveline components, in a role focused initially on developing the company's website and digital presence. He subsequently assumed broader responsibilities in business development.

As director of business development, Schultz works across sales, marketing, branding, digital strategy, and business growth. His responsibilities have also included contributing to the implementation of an enterprise resource planning system and supporting improvements to internal business processes.

AG Drives manufactures and services driveline products for customers in industries including agriculture, oil and gas, paper production, steel, food processing, construction, and other industrial sectors.

In August 2026, The Business News reported that AG Drives had experienced approximately 300 percent revenue growth over the preceding year. The publication described Schultz's work on the company's website, online presence, branding, and business development as part of its broader modernization efforts.

Schultz has described the company's approach as a combination of manufacturing heritage and innovation, emphasizing the role of modern business practices in developing an established industrial trade.

=== Public engagement and industry involvement ===
Schultz has represented AG Drives in regional business and manufacturing discussions. His professional activities have included participation in manufacturing roundtables associated with the Greater Green Bay Chamber's economic development network.

In 2026, Schultz appeared alongside AG Drives president Robby Burton on Swarfcast, a manufacturing-industry podcast hosted by Noah Graff of Today's Machining World. The episode, titled Business School vs. Learning on the Job, explored the contrasting educational and professional paths of Schultz and Burton, the development of AG Drives, and the relationship between formal business education and practical experience.

Schultz has also contributed to the company's public communications through interviews, social media, and business-community engagement.

== Professional interests ==
Schultz's professional interests include business development, entrepreneurship, marketing, manufacturing, organizational leadership, and the application of technology to business operations. His work at AG Drives combines commercial responsibilities with exposure to manufacturing processes and the operational requirements of a growing industrial company.

Prabha Goswami (also identified in corporate records as Prabha Giri) is an Indian beauty pageant titleholder, social advocate, and entrepreneur from Almora district, Uttarakhand. She won the Monal Miss Uttarakhand pageant in 2018. Following the contest, she was appointed by the Almora district administration as an ambassador for the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign. She later founded Bharat Life Care, an enterprise manufacturing Ayurvedic wellness products.

== Early life and education ==
Goswami was raised in Kafaltana (Kapaltana) village in the Jaurasi area of Chaukhutia tehsil, located in Almora district, Uttarakhand. [ref: चौखुटिया की प्रभा बनी मिस उत्तराखंड 2018, Dainik Jagran] [ref: प्रभा गोस्वामी का गृह क्षेत्र में हुआ स्वागत, [[Hindustan (newspaper)] She completed her primary and intermediate schooling at institutions in Jaurasi before relocating to Delhi for higher education.

== Pageantry and advocacy ==
=== Monal Miss Uttarakhand 2018 ===
In July 2018, Goswami competed in the Monal Miss Uttarakhand pageant, held in Khatima, Uttarakhand. The competition featured 18 finalists from across the state. On 23 July 2018, Goswami won the Monal Miss Uttarakhand title; auxiliary awards presented at the event included Face of Uttarakhand and Mrs Uttarakhand. [ref: फेस ऑफ उतराखंड सोनम और मिस उत्तराखंड बनी प्रभा गोस्वामी, [[Hindustan (newspaper)] [ref: मिस उत्तराखंड प्रभा का लोगों ने किया स्वागत, Dainik Jagran]

=== Social campaigns ===
In August 2018, Goswami was welcomed by residents and civic organizations during visits to schools in Jaurasi and Chaukhutia, where she spoke on rural female literacy and advocated for educational support for girls in mountainous regions.

In October 2018, the Almora district administration designated Goswami and athlete Roshni Bisht as district brand ambassadors for the Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao campaign. Goswami was assigned outreach activities across the Ranikhet sub-division and surrounding development blocks to raise awareness regarding sex-ratio imbalances and female education. [ref: रोशनी बिष्ट और प्रभा गोस्वामी बनी बेटी बचाओं बेटी पढ़ाओं की जिले में ब्रांड एंबेसडर, Uttara News]

== Business career ==
Goswami registered under the name Prabha Giri on Startup India's BHASKAR portal, listing Bharat Life Care Ayurveda Wellness and Personal Care as her venture.

=== Bharat Life Care ===
Bharat Life Care is an Ayurvedic and herbal products venture with administrative roots in Almora, Uttarakhand. The brand manufactures wellness items derived from traditional botanical ingredients.

Its primary product is DiaCare Amrit, an herbal tea marketed as a dietary lifestyle beverage to assist in carbohydrate metabolism. The formulation incorporates:
* Berberis aristata (Daruharidra / Kilmora)
* Cinnamon (Dalchini)
* Fenugreek seeds (Methi dana)
* Neem (Azadirachta indica)
* Amla (Emblica officinalis)
* Bitter gourd (Karela)

The product is distributed as an over-the-counter wellness tea without therapeutic claims as a medical prescription.

Draft text:
Foodtopia: Communities in Pursuit of Peace, Love, & Homegrown Food is a 2022 nonfiction book by Margot Anne Kelley, published by Godine. [ref: Foodtopia, Godine] It examines five periods of the American back-to-the-land movement, from the nineteenth century to the early twenty-first century, through the relationship between food production and efforts to establish alternative ways of living. [ref: Foodtopia: Communities in Pursuit of Peace, Love, & Homegrown Food, Kirkus Reviews]

== Synopsis ==
The book combines historical accounts with Kelley's visits to farms, conferences, and farmers' markets. Its subjects include Henry David Thoreau, the nineteenth-century communities of Brook Farm and Fruitlands, and Scott and Helen Nearing, whose book Living the Good Life influenced later homesteaders. Kelley also discusses Mollie Katzen and Alice Waters in the context of changes in American food culture.

The five periods encompass the utopian communities of the 1840s, turn-of-the-century single-tax and smallholding communities, homesteading during the Great Depression, the counterculture of the 1960s and 1970s, and contemporary young farmers. The account extends to the COVID-19 pandemic and its effects on food supply systems.

Kelley explores how reformers have connected farming and eating with ideals of equality, justice, and freedom. Examples from Maine include the development of the Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association. The narrative links earlier movements with later food activism, examining the recurrence and adaptation of their ideas. [ref: Book Review: “Foodtopia”, Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association]

== Publication ==
Godine published the 384-page hardcover edition in August 2022.

== Reception ==
Kirkus Reviews described the book as "An informative, fresh history of food in America", praising its profiles of participants in successive back-to-the-land movements.

Reviewing the book for the Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association, Catherine Preston-Schreck praised its historical detail and its structure connecting past and present movements. She also questioned how the utopian projects related to colonial agricultural practices and racial prejudice, raising concerns about the implications of Thoreau's views on vegetarianism and civilization.

The book was a finalist for the nonfiction category of the 2023 Maine Literary Awards. [ref: 2023 Finalists, Maine Writers & Publishers Alliance]
